Wrap each hot dog piece with 1 piece of bacon and secure with toothpick.

Remove from oven.
Pour barbecue sauce evenly over hot dogs; then drizzle molasses lightly over barbecue sauce. Sprinkle brown sugar over all.

apple pie filling, pineapple and dry cake mix.

Add flour and cook, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Stir in broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is smooth and thickened.
Add pureed vegetables and seasonings to saucepan.

Enjoy!

Boil pineapple and sugar together.
Add Jell-O; when dissolved, add cup water.
Refrigerate until almost jelled; add cheese, Cool Whip and nuts.
Drain artichokes well and chop.
Grate cheese.
Combine with mayonnaise and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve warm with crackers.
Cook the lasagna noodles according to directions.
Drain rinse and separate.
brown the beef and sprinkle the mix over the meat.
Add tomatoes and blend well.
Whip the cream cheese. In a buttered 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Make 2 layers each of noodles, meat & dollops of cream cheese. Bake at 350 degree for 20 minutes or until bubbly.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown beef; drain fat.
Add onion and celery and continue cooking until tender, but not soft.
Add bean sprouts and soup. Heat thoroughly.
Add canned mushrooms if desired.
Serve over chow mein noodles.
Brown beef.
While beef is cooking, cook all other ingredients together. Drain beef, then mix all together in a large pot. Cook for 10 more minutes. Very good!

In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, undissolved yeast and salt. Gradually add water and 2 tablespoons peanut oil to flour mixture. Beat 2 minutes at medium speed of mixer, scraping bowl occasionally. Stir in enough remaining flour to make a soft dough. Knead on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 8 to 10 minutes. Cover and let rest 10 minutes. Roll dough to a 12-inch circle; place on a greased pizza pan. Form a standing rim on crust. Prick dough with fork
randomly. Let rest 10 minutes. Prebake at 450° for 5 minutes.
Mix together m.s.g., cayenne pepper, paprika, white pepper and celery salt.
Rub into turkey cavity and all over the skin.
(Be careful and don't touch your hands to your eyes!)
Separate garlic bud and clean cloves.
Slit holes all over turkey and insert cloves.
Also place cloves of garlic in stomach cavity of turkey. Mix a 4 ounce bottle of shrimp and crab boil with 4 (4 ounce) bottles of water and inject into turkey all over the body.
Place turkey in stainless steel roasting pan and cover with foil. Refrigerate for 24 to 48 hours, occasionally basting with juices in pan.
When ready to cook, heat oil.
Place whole turkey in oil and fry until tender.
Peel the satsumas and cut crosswise into slices.
Sprinkle powdered sugar over satsuma slices.
Drain pineapple.
Mix all ingredients together and let stand in refrigerator overnight (or at least 3 to 4 hours).
To serve, spoon mixture onto lettuce leaves.
Mix together peas, onions, soup, bacon and water chestnuts. Place in casserole dish. Top with Stove Top mix and melted butter. Bake at 350° about 20 to 25 minutes until brown.
Sprinkle 1 envelope gelatin in tomato juice.
Heat, stirring, until dissolved.
Add 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1 tablespoon lemon juice and dash of Tabasco.
Set aside to cool.
In separate saucepan, sprinkle 1 envelope gelatin in chicken stock.
Heat; stir until dissolved.
Remove from heat and add 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
Let cool.
Add chicken, celery and green pepper.
Pour 1/2 of mixture into loaf pan that has been Pam coated.
Chill.
When firm, add tomato aspic mixture.
When aspic is almost firm, spread last half of chicken mix.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce.
Cook noodles.
Cook spaghetti sauce.
Add mix and water.
Cook for 20 minutes.
Layer all ingredients in a casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix and bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Mix all together. Bake in a 325° oven for 30 minutes. Makes 3 layers.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In small bowl, combine flour, baking soda and salt; set aside.
In a large bowl, beat butter, sugar, brown sugar and vanilla extract until creamy.
Beat in eggs. Gradually beat in flour mixture.
Stir in chocolate and nuts.
Drop by rounded measuring tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake for 9 to 11 minutes, until golden brown.
Yields 5 dozen cookies (using tablespoons of dough).

recipes.t: James Earl Jones' Chilean Sea Bass
d: Slice and cook onions in a skillet on low heat until caramelized (between 1 and 2 hours).

Puree all ingredients except olive oil and chicken broth. Heat olive oil. Add ingredients and cook on low for 30 minutes. Add chicken broth as necessary. Season bass with salt and white pepper to taste.
Cover bass with onions and bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Each of 6 servings should include one piece of bass over about 1/6 of the sauce.
Combine the first 6 ingredients in a large bowl.
Place mixture on plastic wrap and form into a ball.
Cover and chill overnight.
Several hours before serving, roll in chopped nuts. Chill until ready to serve.
Bake at 300° for 55 minutes.
Do not bake crust before pouring in the ingredients.
Combine and shape into balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Press into center of hot cookies, 36 chocolate kisses.
Remove to wire rack to cool.
Makes about 3 dozen.
Mix all together by hand until all ingredients are combined. Put in dish and put in oven at 350° for 1 hour.
Top with ketchup. Cook uncovered.
Wash and cut cucumbers in half lengthwise; pack in hot jars with the last 5 ingredients put in each pint jar.
Combine sugar, salt, vinegar and water.
Tie pickling spices in a cheesecloth bag; add to vinegar mixture.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Heat to boiling and pour over cucumbers; leave 1/4-inch headspace.
Adjust caps. Process pints and quarts 15 minutes in boiling water bath.
Yield: about 7 pints.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add sherbet and place in refrigerator until partly set (watch carefully).
Add other ingredients and fold in Cool Whip last.
Chill and enjoy.
Mix all ingredients, except chili sauce, shrimp and parsley. Spread on plate.
Cover with chili sauce, then sprinkle tiny shrimp and parsley flakes.
Serve with crackers.
Blend beer, egg and sugar, then add flour.
Put it in a bread pan and cover with towel.
It rises in an hour or so.
Bake at 350° for an hour.
Cool and slice bread.
Spread real butter on top.
Mmmm!
Good!
Drain all fruit well.
Brown meat and drain, then add seasoning mix, taco sauce and kidney beans.
Let all this get hot, then its ready to eat.
Cream the sugar and shortening.
Add the egg and vanilla. Then the rest of the ingredients.
Roll in balls and flatten. Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Combine ingredients in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with 1/4 cup cracker crumbs and 2 tablespoons butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Chop walnuts.
Beat eggs; gradually beat in sugar, then oil. Combine first mixture, alternating with zucchini.
Stir in raisins, walnuts and vanilla extract.
Turn into 2 greased and lightly floured loaf pans.
Bake at 350° or until loaves test done, approximately 1 hour.
(Bake on lowest rack in oven.)
Let stand about 10 minutes, turn out onto wire racks to cool.
If desired, loaves may be lightly frosted with confectioners sugar, butter and vanilla mixed to a spreading consistency with milk. Makes two loaves.
Freezes well!
Saute onions until clear.
Pour onions into a prepared pie shell.
Add grated cheese.
Beat eggs; add milk and pour over cheese.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Cook the macaroni in boiling water according to package directions.
Drain and set
aside.
Saute
the meat, onion and garlic in oil until the
meat
loses
its
pink
color and the onions are tender.
Add
salt,
pepper,
tomato sauce, catsup, mushrooms, Worcestershire
sauce and Italian seasoning.
Bring mixture to a boil and
then simmer gently for about 5 minutes. Mix in the cooked
macaroni and simmer 5 more minutes.
Yields 8 servings.
Contains 270 calories per serving.
Cook spinach.
Saute onion in butter.
Mix spinach, onion, artichoke hearts, sour cream and 1/4 cup of Parmesan cheese in a casserole dish.
Add pepper and toss well.
Put remaining 1/4 cup cheese on top.
Bake, covered, at 325° for 30 minutes.
Brown onions.
Remove from pan.
Place 1/3 cabbage in pan followed by 1/2 of bell pepper, one tomato and half the browned onion.
Layer with another 1/3 of cabbage and remaining bell pepper, tomato and onions.
Sprinkle remaining cabbage on top and add salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer about 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Saute onion in oil until limp.
Add remaining ingredients. Simmer 30 minutes.
Add cooked meat, if desired.
Combine lime juice, oregano and half the garlic.
Marinate the fish in this for at least 1/2 hour.
Dissolve 1 pint of lime in 2 gallons of water.
Peel, seed and cut cucumbers into strips.
(Use large cucumbers, even the white ones; use the meat only.
You can fix small ones the same way.) Pour lime mixture over cucumbers and let stand for 24 hours.
Drain and rinse cucumbers.
Fill with ice cold water and let stand for 3 hours.
Drain.
Mix vinegar, sugar, salt and spices together.
Pour over cucumbers.
Let stand overnight.
Put on stove next morning and boil for 35 minutes.
Put in jars and seal.
Makes 10 pints.
Mix well the first 6 ingredients; shape into balls.
Brown in the shortening.
Mix the soup with water; pour over meatballs. Simmer 20 to 30 minutes.
Combine rhubarb, apples and strawberries; spoon into a greased 8-inch square baking dish.
Combine sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over fruit.
Set aside.
In a bowl, combine flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut in oleo until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in brown sugar and oats.
Sprinkle over rhubarb mixture. Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes, or until lightly browned. Serve cold or warm with a scoop of ice cream if desired.
Wash and clean peppers.
Parboil peppers for 5 minutes.
Let cool and drain.
Combine rice, meat, salt, pepper and butter; mix well.
Stuff peppers; place peppers in a pan, uncovered, with a little water in the bottom.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour (check after 45 minutes).
Heat can of tomato sauce and serve with peppers.
Combine vinegar and sugar in small saucepan.
Cook over low heat just until sugar dissolves.
Stir in barbecue sauce, water, mayonnaise, mustard powder and red pepper seasoning.
Combine cabbage and carrots in large bowl.
Pour dressing over; toss to combine.
Combine all ingredients but potatoes and mix well.
Add potatoes and mix gently.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Mix all together and pour into greased pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. This
can be frozen and taken out when needed.

Preheat the oven to 375°. Slice about 1/2-inch off the top of the garlic. Wrap it in aluminum foil and bake for 35 minutes. Remove foil and press until all flesh squeezes out. You should have 1 heaping tablespoonful of puree. Mix it with the yogurt, parsley, black pepper and salt.
Melt butter; stir in Eagle Brand milk and Hershey's syrup. For the cake just bake devil's food cake and follow directions on box.
Cut cake and ice cream in squares and pour fudge over top.
Cook pasta according to package directions without adding fat or salt.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
Set aside.
In a large bowl combine tomato sauce, dressing , basil, and oregano.
Add tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and olives.
Stir until coated.
Add pasta and gently toss.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Bake in Magnolite pot.
Pour in cherry filling.
Layer can of crushed pineapple on top of cherry filling.
Sprinkle dry cake mix on top of fillings.
Sprinkle pecans over mixture.
Pour melted margarine over mixture.
Bake for 10 minutes at 450°.
Then turn oven down to 350° and bake for 25 more minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Use 9 x 13-inch pan and 2-quart saucepan.

recipes.t: Sea Scallops With Lemon Butter Sauce
d: Coat 1 lb. sea scallops in flour. Season with salt and pepper. Saute scallops in olive oil & butter in a large skillet over high heat for 2 minutes on each side.	Remove scallops.
Add butter, lemon juice, parsley, salt & pepper and heat.
Serve scallops over rice and top with sauce from skillet.
Bring water, vinegar and salt to boil; let stand 20 minutes. When cool, pour over cukes and green tomatoes, prepared according to preference.
Small tomatoes and cucumbers can be left whole, if desired, and larger vegetables can be cut into chunks.
Cucumbers may be sliced open lengthwise and cut into quarters or eighths. Put vegetables in quart jars; to each jar, add 2 sprigs dill and 2 large garlic cloves, depending on taste.
Cut strawberries in half.
Slice bananas.
Drain pineapple. Cream sugar and cheese together.
Fold in tub of Cool Whip and marshmallows.
Mix together the frozen strawberries, pineapple and pecans.
Add to cheese mixture.
Refrigerate.
Butter pan.
Cover pan with frozen bread dough, then add pudding mix, brown sugar, cinnamon, pecans and butter.
Cover; let sit out on counter overnight.
Cook at 350° for 15 minutes uncovered, then 15 minutes covered.
Mix thoroughly all ingredients. Pour into a greased and floured 9 x 12 3/4-inch oblong pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes in bottom rack of oven.
Combine all these ingredients. Bake at 325° for 30 minutes. Makes about a 3 pound fruit cake.
Preheat oven to 250°.
Place apples in a single layer in a large, flat baking pan. Bake 20 minutes.
Remove from oven, and stir in popcorn and pecans. Mix remaining ingredients in a cup and drizzle over apples, popcorn, and pecans. Return to oven, and bake for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Mix butter, sugar and eggs.
Make a paste of red coloring and cocoa.
Add to creamed mixture.
Add buttermilk, alternating with sifted flour and salt.
Add vanilla.
In small cup, mix soda and vinegar, then add to rest of mixture, blending instead of beating. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350° in 2 (8-inch) greased and floured pans.
Mix Kool-Aid, juice and sugar in a gallon jug.
Add water to fill jug.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes and serve with Triscuits.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift first 5 ingredients in a bowl. Add shortening, eggs, vanilla and corn syrup.
Mix for 2 minutes at low speed; scrape bowl.
Stir in nuts; save some nuts to sprinkle on top.
Pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cook 40 to 45 minutes.
Cook pasta as directed; drain.
Combine curry, yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard and garlic.
Add chicken, red pepper, celery, scallions and sunflower seed.
Toss lightly. Spoon 1 1/2 tablespoons into each shell.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce.
Mix well and cook over medium heat until thick.
Serve over buttered toast or biscuits.
Combine ingredients, except sour cream.
Beat until smooth, blending in sour cream.
Pour into graham or nut crust, trim with reserved crumbs.
Bake in moderate (375°) oven for 35 minutes or until just set.
Let cool with oven door open.
Do not overheat or cool too rapidly.
Chill well.
Peel and slice onions into thin rings.
Saute in margarine until limp or opaque.
Pour half of onions into a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Cover with Parmesan cheese, then crushed crackers.
Repeat layers and bake, uncovered, in 325° oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes.
Delicious with steak!!
Mix jell-O with hot water.
Add pineapple with the juice and the pie filling; mix well.
Place in a 13 x 9 casserole dish.
Let congeal in refrigerator.
In a small bowl mix cream cheese, sour cream and sugar.
Pour this mixture over congealed salad.
Combine chocolate cake mix, butter, water, oil and 1/2 can sweetened condensed milk in mixing bowl.
Mix well.
Pour half of batter into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Combine sugar, oil, buttermilk, eggs, blackberry jam and vanilla in large bowl.
Beat well on low speed.
Add combined ingredients and beat on medium speed to blend well.
Bake at 350° in 2 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans for 40 minutes or until tests done.
Cool completely and frost with Buttermilk Icing.
Mix dates and hot water.
Let cool.
Cream butter and sugar, then beat in eggs.
Sift dry ingredients and add to cream mixture. Add dates, vanilla and 1/2 cup chocolate chips.
Spread batter in greased pan.
Top with remaining chocolate chips and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Mix all ingredients and freeze in a covered container.
When ready to serve, let defrost to a slushy consistency.
Heat applesauce in pan. Stir in gelatin until dissolved. Add orange juice and pineapple. Stir until smooth. Pour into mold and chill.
Melt butter.
Mix all ingredients and roll into balls.
Roll in chopped pecans or coconut, if desired.
Brown ground beef with onions; drain grease.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix sugar, cooking oil and eggs.
Add fruit and nuts; mix well.
Stir in flour; mix well.
Pour in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan. Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Melt oleo in dish.
Combine all other ingredients and mix lightly.
Add to butter and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serves 8 to 10.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Arrange cut cookie dough (1/8 to 1/4-inch) rounds in slightly overlapping pattern on pizza pan. Press dough together to seal.
Bake until puffed and golden, about 10 minutes.
Cool completely.
Mix and store in tightly covered container.
Use 3 to 4 teaspoons mixture in cup of hot water.
Mix the flour with the sugar.
Add the milk.
Mix and pour into 1 pie crust and cover with the second crust.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Lower the heat to 300 degrees, and bake for approximately 15 minutes longer.
Place pastry in pie pan.
Arrange rhubarb.
Mix sugar with flour and add beaten egg yolks and butter.
Spoon mixture over rhubarb.
Bake in hot oven at 450° for 12 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and continue baking for 25 minutes.
Boil potatoes in their jackets until done.
Peel while still hot; let cool.
Slice in thin round slices.
Mix in mayonnaise, vinegar and sugar.
Grate onion and add with salt and pepper.
Mix again.
Chill thoroughly for 3 hours.

Place butter in a shallow dish. In another dish, combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and seasonings. Dip fillets in butter, then coat with crumb mixture. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, uncovered, or until fish flakes easily with a fork.
Cook cauliflower in saltwater 10 to 15 minutes; drain.
In saucepan, cook onion in butter until tender.
Blend in flour.
Add chicken broth, milk and Worcestershire sauce.
Cook until slightly thickened.
Add cauliflower.
Bring to boil; add cheese.
Sprinkle chives over each serving.

Unroll crescent rolls on cookie sheet, but do not take them apart. Bake until golden brown and let cool. Mix cream cheese and dry seasonings together. Spread mixture on baked crescent rolls and sprinkle on all chopped veggies. Let chill and serve.
Mix all ingredients together.
Heat on low until melted and fairly smooth.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Mix all
ingredients and spoon in miniature muffin pan. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Melt butter.
Add brown sugar and water (boiled 1 minute to syrup).
In bowl mix egg yolks, flour and milk; slowly add syrup. Return to stove; boil until thick.
Add vanilla; pour into baked pie shell.
Sprinkle top with crushed graham crackers.
Brown meat slowly.
Spoon off excess fat.
Add next 4 ingredients.
Cover and simmer 40 minutes, stirring occasionally. Salt to taste.
Cook noodles in salted water until tender; drain. Rinse in cold water.
Place half of the noodles in large baking dish.
Cover with 1/3 of the sauce.
Add half of the Mozzarella cheese, then half of the cottage cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with sauce.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes.
Cut into squares.
Boil chicken until tender.
Remove from bone.
Line bottom and sides of greased 3-quart casserole dish with layer of tortillas.
Sprinkle with 2 or 3 tablespoons chicken stock. Layer with 1/2 can undiluted mushroom soup and 1/2 of other ingredients in the order listed.
Cover with another layer of tortillas; sprinkle with 2 or 3 tablespoons chicken stock and remaining ingredients.
Top the last layer of cheese with can of tomatoes with chilies.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake about 45 minutes at 350° to 400°.
In saucepan, dissolve jello in 1/2 cup boiling water and juice from the cherries.
Cool slightly.
In mixing bowl, beat eggs well.
Add sugar; beat well.
Blend in the half and half.
Cut cherries into fourths and add to mixture; stir in vanilla and jello mixture last.
Pour into freezer canister.
Add milk until about 3/4 full.
An electric freezer takes about 15 minutes to freeze.
Melt butter.
Stir in flour and nuts.
Press into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cool.
Combine all ingredients.
Chill.
Serve with assorted vegetables (tomatoes, cauliflower, green pepper, cucumber, celery, etc.).
Unroll crescent rolls and press flat into cookie sheet.
Join all creases.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool in pan.
Mix sugar and cornstarch; add vinegar, oil and water.
Bring to boil.
Add beets and cook over low heat 30 minutes or until thick.
Combine pumpkin, sugars and all spices well.
Beat eggs well with 1/4 cup melted oleo or butter.
Add this to the pumpkin mixture and mix well.
Pour into 10-inch unbaked pie shell. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake 40 minutes longer.
Combine dry ingredients.
Cut in shortening until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add yeast and buttermilk to dry mixture.
Mix well.
Roll out desired amount on lightly floured surface to about 1/4-inch thick.
Cut with 2-inch cutter.
Let rise 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes.
Watch carefully until you get the time right for your oven.
Dough will keep in refrigerator a week in covered container or plastic bag.
Melt margarine; pour over chocolate chips until dissolved. Combine eggs, sugar, vanilla, and nuts.
Mix with chocolate mixture.
Place in deep dish pie crust.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Mix first 4
ingredients like pie dough; roll to size of walnut.
Set on wax paper.
Melt chocolate chips and paraffin in a double boiler.
Leave the pan of water under the melted chocolate while dipping the balls.
Set on wax paper on cookie sheet and cool.
Store in tight container in refrigerator.
Mix together and beat at high speed for at least 5 minutes.
You don't have to toast muffins.

recipes.t: Mushroom-Cheese Souffle("A Favorite From The '76 Cookbook.")
d: Start heating oven to 300°.
With hand beater, beat egg yolks until light and foamy.
Stir milk gradually into flour.
Add to egg yolks and beat well.
Add salt, pepper and cheese and beat until blended.
Gently fold in onion, mushrooms and egg whites, stiffly beaten.
Turn into greased 1-quart casserole.
Bake about 50 minutes or until golden brown on top.
Makes 2 servings.
Place the eggs, pineapple juice, sugar and salt in a saucepan and blend and cook until it boils.
Cool.
In large bowl, combine pears, sugar and pecans.
Set aside for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter and flour large tube pan. Using wooden spoon, stir into pear mixture the oil, vanilla and eggs.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake 1 hour.
Chill broth so fat will raise.
Mix cornstarch and broth together.
Cook on medium heat.
Stir in milk, Worcestershire sauce and mushrooms.
Bring to boil.
Cool and garnish with paprika.
Mix flour, melted oleo and nuts.
Spread in pan; bake approximately 20 minutes at 350° or until light brown.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and 1/2 cup Cool Whip.
Spread over crust.
Mix pudding and milk until thick; spread over 2nd layer.
Spread cherry pie filling over all.
Cover with the balance of Cool Whip. Refrigerate.
Drain tuna.
Mix with cream cheese until smooth.
Add seasoning.
Chill and serve with crackers.
Lightly
grease baking dish.
Flatten breasts and place slice of	chipped
beef
and
shredded cheese on each breast. Roll
up each
breast
with ends down.
Place in baking dish. Combine soup and
sour
cream
and spoon over rolled breasts. Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Saute ground beef and onion in skillet until ground beef is brown.
Stir frequently.
Add chilies, olives, catsup, salt and chili powder and mix well.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Place one slice Colby cheese on bottom half of each loaf.
Spoon ground beef mixture over cheese.
Arrange bacon slice and Muenster cheese slice over ground beef.
Cover with remaining loaf halves.
Wrap loaves with aluminum foil.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Dip chicken pieces in beaten eggs.
Shake chicken in a bag of flour (plus a little cornstarch).
Deep fry until brown.
Place chicken in baking dish, cover with cashews, onion and sauce.
Bake at 250° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Blend all ingredients, except muffins.
Toast muffins until half dark.
Top with mixture and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cut into 4 pieces.
Sprinkle gelatine over cold water.
Stir in sugar, salt, lemon juice and hot tomato juice until it's dissolved.
Add shrimp, celery, onion and olives.
Pour into mold and leave overnight. When ready to serve, set in hot water for a few seconds and unmold on platter. Arrange salad greens around outside and serve with side dish of salad dressing.
Mix sugar, margarine, eggs and flavorings thoroughly.
Measure flour and sift.
Stir flour, baking powder and salt together. Blend well and chill at least 1 hour.
Heat oven to 400°.
Roll dough 1/8-inch thick on a lightly floured board.
Cut with a 3-inch cookie cutter.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for 6 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 4 dozen cookies.
Cut onions, celery, potatoes and add water.
Bring to boil and simmer 15 minutes or until done.
Melt margarine; add flour and make paste.
Remove from pan; put in milk and heat.
Add roux gradually (margarine and flour).
Stir until creamy.
Add potatoes and corn.
Heat and stir.
Don't let boil.
Mix well.
Put in glass baking dish.
Bake for 45 minutes or until brown at 350°.

recipes.t: Parslied Ham And Swiss Cheese Sandwiches
d: Blend the first 4 ingredients and spread on sandwich buns. Fill with ham and cheese slices.
Wrap in foil and bake 15 minutes at 300°.

Sprinkle half of cheese over Crispy Pizza Crust; set aside. Saute vegetables, garlic and Italian seasoning in hot oil 3 to 5 minutes or until vegetables are barely crisp-tender. Spoon vegetables evenly onto pizza. Sprinkle with remaining cheese. Bake at 450 degrees 5 minutes or until cheese melts. Yield: one 12-inch pizza.
In large pot, brown meat and onion.
Cook until onion is tender.
Drain; salt and pepper to taste.
Put in remaining ingredients; stir.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat; simmer, covered, for 15 minutes, or until noodles are tender.
Makes 6 servings.
Let cheese soften at room temperature.
Combine all ingredients with hands and form a ball.
Cook chicken, saving 1/2 cup broth.
Mix chicken, soups and milk.
Pour in a greased glass 9 x 13-inch dish.
Cover with Stove Top stuffing.
Mix 1/2 cup chicken broth with 1/2 stick melted butter; pour over top.
Place in oven and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix until crumbly the first 5 ingredients.
Press 1/2 of crumbs in greased 7 x 9-inch baking pan.
Top with rhubarb.
Then combine in saucepan the next 4 ingredients.
Cook until thick and clear.
Pour over rhubarb.
Top with remaining crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut in squares and serve with whipped cream.
Cut potatoes into small cubes and boil until just tender. Drain and add onion, salt and pepper.
Combine vinegar, 1/3 cup mayonnaise and 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Add mixture to warm potatoes and let cool.
Add green peppers, pimento, celery and the other 1/2 cup mayonnaise to potato mixture and mix well.
Chill.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs.
Sift flour and cinnamon together and add alternately with milk.
Add sherry, nuts and fruit.
Drop on well-greased cookie sheet and bake 20 minutes at 300°.
Makes about 12 dozen.
Bone chicken and discard skin.
Mince the chicken and combine with 1 teaspoon cornstarch and the egg whites, beaten until frothy.
Bring chicken broth to a boil.
Dissolve remaining cornstarch in water and add gradually to broth.
Add chicken mixture, corn, sherry and soy sauce and simmer a few minutes. Serve garnished with ham (boiled, baked or most flavorful and closest to the Chinese, Smithfield ham).
Serves 4.

recipes.t: Chicken, Zucchini And Red Pepper Stir-Fry
d: Cut away tendon and any excess fat from chicken breasts.
Place in freezer just until chicken firms up for easier slicing.
Do not freeze solid.
Meanwhile, insert metal chopping blade in mixer bowl of food processor.
Process garlic (or chop fine with French knife).
Remove chopping blade and insert slicing blade.
Place zucchini in feed tube vertically and process (or cut in slices with knife).
Insert red pepper in feed tube vertically.
Process (or slice into 1/8 inch slices with knife).
Insert scallion vertically.
Process (or slice by hand).
Process water chestnuts (or slice by knife).
Put mushrooms on their sides in feed tube. Process (or cut lengthwise into thirds).
Set aside in bowl.
To process chicken using slicing blade, wedge chicken into feed tube so slicing disk will cut against grain (or cut by sharp knife into 1/4 inch thick slices).

In a glass or enamel pan, bring 4 cups cold water to a boil. Add the tea bags and steep about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Take out tea bags and add the sugar, stirring until sugar is dissolved. Place tea mixture in a 1 gallon container and add frozen juices. Stir until juices dissolve.
Mix ingredients together and pour into pie shells. Bake at 350° until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Finely grind the first 3 ingredients.
Add sugar and whiskey and form into small balls. Roll in colored sugar.
Store in airtight container in refrigerator.
Put first 5 ingredients in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle casserole with paprika and parsley flakes.
Bake in a preheated oven at 300° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Mix well.
Can be mixed in blender, but don't process too much or it will be too runny.
Makes 5 cups.
Beat egg white until foamy.
Brush over the bottom and sides of pastry.
In a small bowl combine flour and sugars.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Sprinkle 2/3 into bottom of pastry.
Top with peaches.
Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until filling is bubbly and peaches are tender.
Dredge chicken breasts in flour to which salt and pepper is added.
Heat mixture of oil and margarine in skillet.
Place chicken in the hot oil, turning to a light brown.
Arrange pieces in a lightly greased baking dish.
Blend and heat all ingredients for the sauce, pour over chicken.
Cover and bake 325 for about 1 1/2 hour or until chicken is tender.
Serves 4.
Mix with electric mixer, margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, vanilla, cocoa and flour.
Blend all together.
Mix sugar and oil in the blender until well blended.
Add the next 3 ingredients and blend.
Add catsup; blend.
You may use more catsup for the taste you desire.
Refrigerate.
Mix together and drop on a greased cookie sheet by spoonfuls. Bake at 400° for about 10 minutes.
Nuts and/or raisins may be added.
Boil the potatoes and process them through a colander, then mash them thoroughly.
Add 6 cups of water.
Brown the flour in the butter and add the potatoes and water with the chopped celery, parsley, thyme, salt and white pepper.
Beat in two egg yolks just before serving.
You will never miss the cow.
Melt a bit of butter in skillet.
Using the rim of a glass, press the center out of the slice of bread.
Reserve center circle. Put slice of bread in pan.
Crack egg into center hole of bread. Turn when egg is set.
Cook over low heat until egg is done. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with bread hole covering egg center (Toad)!
Cook noodles; drain.
Brown hamburger and Italian sausage together; drain.
Put together cottage cheese and Ricotta cheese in bowl.
Put spaghetti sauce in bowl and add meat mixture after browning.
Stir both cheese and meat mixtures good.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Prepare a 9-inch pastry.
Melt butter. Cool.
Beat 2 eggs until foamy.
Add flour, sugar and brown sugar and beat until smooth.
Add melted butter.
Mix well.
Add chocolate chips.
Stir.
Pour batter into pie shell.
Bake for 1 hour.
It's heavenly!
Place dry ingredients (except raisins) in large, deep bowl. Gradually add milk and margarine.
Mix until firm enough to form ball; if still crumbly, add more butter or milk, one tablespoon at a time.
Pat down to an 8-inch circle.
Place on oiled cookie sheet.
Cut the dough in the form of a cross to the depth of 1-inch.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes or until brown.
Cut chicken into nuggets. Batter chicken in egg and then in flour. Fry until golden brown. Dip chicken into teriyaki sauce and place in dish. Cook chicken for 20 to 25 minutes at 325°.
Gradually add milk and lemon juice to softened cream cheese. Add remaining ingredients and mix well. Chill and serve.
Parboil mushrooms.
Mix other ingredients except onions.
Pour over parboiled mushrooms and onions.
Let stand several days (stir occasionally).
Cook until meat is brown; drain.
Add salt and pepper, chili powder, garlic salt, bell pepper and onion.
Put in Dutch oven. Put egg noodles on top.
Don't stir.
Pour water over mixture.
Line an 8 or 9-inch square pan with foil and set aside.
In a heavy saucepan, over low heat, melt chocolate chips and 2 tablespoons butter with sweetened condensed milk, vanilla and salt.
Remove from heat and stir in nuts.
Spread evenly into prepared pan.

Boil potatoes, onion, celery and bouillon in 4 cups water for 10 to 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Add cream of chicken soup and Velveeta. Heat, stirring often, until cheese is melted and soup is smooth. Add broccoli. Continue stirring occasionally until ready to serve.
Mix vegetables.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Drain well.
Cook in kettle for 30 minutes vegetables and vinegar mixture.
Pour in jars and seal.
Melt the butter in a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Mix the next 5 ingredients and pour over butter.
Mix the next 4 ingredients and pour over the batter.
Do not stir.
Bake for 30 minutes in a 350° oven.
Makes its own sauce.
Serve warm.
Beat cheese until fluffy.
Add sugar and peanut butter.
Beat until smooth.
Prepare topping with milk as directed on package. Beat into peanut butter mixture.
Pour or spoon into pie shell. Must be refrigerated overnight to set up before serving.
In saucepan, combine all ingredients except apples.
Melt over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Cool.
Slice apples.
Dip into mixture and serve.
In a heavy pot, bring milk almost to a boil.
Remove from heat and sprinkle in nutmeg to taste.
Beat eggs and to them add sugar, vanilla and a pinch of salt.
Add hot milk to egg mixture.
Pour into unbaked 9-inch pie crust.
Bake in slow oven at 325° to 350° for 30 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Peel apples, quarter and cut in half.
Pat out can of biscuits and put in 1/8 of apple.
Seal apple inside biscuit.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar and 1 stick of melted margarine.
Pour over biscuits and sprinkle biscuits with allspice or spice of your choice.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Good hot or cold with ice cream or plain.

Cook peas according to package directions; drain. While peas cool, break apart cauliflower and slice thin. Combine cauliflower and peas; add celery and onion. Mix together mayonnaise, salt and milk. Mix with the cauliflower mixture. Marinate in refrigerator 6 hours.
Mix soda with sour milk and add to molasses.
Sift together flour, ginger and salt; combine 2 mixtures and add butter.
Bake in greased pan in moderate oven, 350°, for 25 minutes.
Puree the bananas in a food processor along with the thawed lemonade.
Then add the other ingredients and mix well.
This mixture is frozen and will fit in a gallon plastic milk jug. Before serving, partially thaw and add the following:
1 (64-ounce) ginger ale and 1 (64-ounce) lemon-lime soft drink. Yields 50 (1/2-cup) servings.
You can cut the amount of sugar in half.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cream butter gradually beating in sugar. Beat eggs until light; add to butter mixture and beat thoroughly. Add vanilla extract.
Add lemon rinds.
Sift together flour and baking powder.
Carefully blend into butter-egg mixture to make soft dough.
Soften yeast in lukewarm water with honey.
Melt margarine in saucepan.
Cool slightly.
When yeast is bubbly, add 4 more heaping cups warm water, milk, salt, the melted shortening, bran and wheat germ.
Mix and add flours (the total amount will equal almost 5 pounds of flour).
Knead well.
Place in a warm place in greased bowl.
Blend soup and milk.
Add chicken, noodles, pimento and parsley.
Spoon into 1-quart casserole.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake in 350° oven 25 minutes.
This is good served with the main meal and/or as a dessert.
Rub a wooden bowl with garlic and mix the dressing right in the bowl.
Use a variety of fresh torn greens such as lettuce, escarole, spinach, endive and watercress.
Toss well until every leaf is coated with the dressing.
Brown chicken (unfloured) in shortening until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet and make gravy in small amount of shortening.
In same skillet return chicken and lay peppers and onions over gravy covered chicken.	Simmer for 1 hour to 1 1/2 hours.
Drain liquid from one jar of artichokes into pan.
Chop artichokes and set aside.
Add onion to liquid in pan and saute. (Add a little garlic salt.)
Beat eggs; add bread crumbs and seasonings.
Stir in cheese, parsley, artichokes and onion.
Put in greased 9 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Cut into 1-inch squares and serve hot or cold.
Fry bacon; when almost crisp, add onion, squash, salt and pepper.
Cook until tender (about 10 minutes).
Remove from stove; add sour cream and serve.
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Real Mashed Potatoes!(From Potatoes, Not A Mix!)
d: Cut up potatoes and put in a big pot of salted water. Bring to a boil. Put cover on pot and let cook 25 minutes on medium heat. Drain; add butter and milk. Whip using a hand mixer.
Mix together in a baking dish.
Place bacon strips on top. Bake about 30 minutes in a medium oven.
Fry bacon until brown.
Remove from pan.
Chop onion and green pepper.
Saute onion and green pepper in grease.
Add tomato sauce.
Add one can of water.
Mash stewed tomatoes and add to mixture.
Break bacon into bits and add to mixture.
Add Tabasco sauce and salt to taste.
When mixture starts boiling, add shrimp and turn fire down low.
Stir constantly to keep from sticking. Cook until rice dries out.
In top of a double boiler, scald milk.
Slowly add gelatin and honey.
Pour a few tablespoonfuls over egg yolks, then add egg mixture to milk mixture in boiler.
Place over hot water and cook until thick and smooth.
Remove from heat.
Add salt and vanilla, then fold in egg whites.
Pour into a large mold and chill.
The mixture will form 2 layers as it sets.
Dredge beef in flour and brown in Dutch oven.
Add remaining ingredients and cook slowly on low heat for about 3 hours. Thicken gravy if necessary.
Boil potatoes until fork goes through, but not mashes.
Let cool.
Cut up into 1-inch squares.
Whip up mayonnaise, chopped onion, cilantro (use less if using fresh), garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Stir in potatoes and mix well to coat.
Maybe eaten cold or warm.
Combine beans, picante sauce and 1 cup cheese; stir over low heat until cheese is melted.
On serving platter, layer chips, bean mixture, lettuce, sour cream and tomatoes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Makes 8 servings.
Boil chicken.
Pull off bones in bite size pieces.
Add broth and cream of celery soup.
Pour into a greased baking dish.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder.
Gradually add milk, then melted butter.
Pour this over chicken mixture.
Bake at 425° for about 30 minutes.
Chop cranberries in processor or food chopper.
Pour 2 cups sugar over cranberries.
Add the raspberry and orange Jell-O to juice.
Add to cranberries.
Mold in pans.
Cream sugar, eggs, spices and butter at low speed for 1 minute. Add cream and blend. Put in unbaked pie shell. Bake at 350°. Cool until firm.
Mix all ingredients well.
Cook and stir constantly until dough forms a ball and leaves side of pan.
Store in airtight container.
Great for children!!
1st Layer:
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Press in an oblong baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Brown beef.
Add salt, pepper, onion, chili powder, rice, soup and water.
Cook gently for 2 or 3 minutes.
Put cabbage in casserole.
Pour meat mixture over cabbage.
Do not stir.
Bake, covered, for 2 hours at 350° or longer, if desired.
Wash and dry chicken pieces.
Dip into prepared salad dressing.
Spoon crumbs over the dressing to cover.
Place in foil lined pan.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika to taste. Bake uncovered at 375° for 1 1/4 hours.
Remove husks from ears of corn; brush off silks.
Drop in kettle of boiling water to cover, adding 1 teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon lemon juice to each quart of water.
Cover and cook 5 to 8 minutes, or until milk is set and corn is tender.
Cooking time depends on maturity of corn.
Remove from water and serve with butter, salt and ground black pepper.
Mix cream cheese, margarine and sugar. Add eggs, vanilla and cake flour. Bake at 325° for 1 hour in a tube pan.
Melt chips and peanut butter.
Add chow mein noodles and marshmallows.
Mix together and spoon out on waxed paper.
Cook carrots and celery in boiling water until tender.
Cook onion in margarine until tender, but not brown.
Stir in flour. Add milk and chicken broth.
Cook over low heat until thickened, stirring occasionally.
Makes 6 cups.
Soften cheese (I use microwave) on Low.
Add chips and oleo until melted.
Let cool for a few minutes and then add sugar. This recipe can be cut in half, if you don't want as much frosting.
Mix until smooth.
Mix margarine with sugar.
Add vanilla, salt and flour; mix well.
Add chips, nuts and shape into balls and press flat.
Bake at 325° until light brown (approximately 13 minutes).
Heat the cooking oil in a Dutch oven.
Add the meat and cover with the rest of the ingredients.
Salt and pepper to taste. Cover and let cook over low heat for 2 to 3 hours.
Fold in one large container Cool Whip.
Mix hash, onion and egg together.
Prepare muffin mix as directed on package.
Add salt and cheese.
Spread half the batter in greased 8-inch square or round baking dish.
Spread on hash mixture.
Top with remaining batter.
Bake at 400° for about 25 minutes until corn bread is golden brown.
Mix soup, cheese, onion and sour cream.
Mix with vegetables.
Place in a dish.
Sift together in large mixing bowl sugar and flour.
Place in saucepan and bring to a boil butter or oleo, cocoa and water.
Pour butter mixture over flour and sugar; mix well and add buttermilk, eggs, vanilla, baking soda and cinnamon.
Mix and bake on a slightly greased 10 x 15-inch pan at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes. Before cake is done, make icing.
First, mash potato, then add flour.
Next, add powdered sugar and mix until it makes a ball of dough.
Next, take a sheet of wax paper and spread with dough.
Then spread the peanut butter out on the dough.
Roll up like a burrito.
Chill for a couple of hours, then cut in little strips.
Toss all ingredients in a bowl.
Chill until ready to serve.
Mix crumbs and melted butter and press 3/4 of mixture into Pyrex dish.
Cream sugar and cream cheese together.
Mix milk, Dream Whip and vanilla until stiff and add to cheese mixture. Layer on top of crumbs the blueberry filling, then cheese mixture and sprinkle with remaining cracker crumbs.

recipes.t: Penne All'Arrabbiata(Penne With Hot Pepper And Tomatoes)
d: Cut out tomato cores with a sharp knife.
Fill a large saucepan 2/3 full with water.
Bring water to a boil; add tomatoes.
Boil 20 to 25 seconds or until skins begin to split.
Place tomatoes in bowl of cold water.
Peel cooled tomatoes and cut in half horizontally.
Squeeze seeds and juice out of each tomato half. Dice tomatoes.
Heat oil in a large skillet.
Add hot pepper and garlic.
Saute over medium heat about 1 minute.
Before garlic changes color, add diced tomatoes.
Season with salt.
Cook, uncovered, over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in parsley and cook 1 to 2 minutes longer.
Fill a very large saucepan 2/3 full with salted water.
Bring to a boil.
Add penne.
Bring water back to a boil and cook penne, uncovered, until tender but firm to the bite (al dente) 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain penne and place in skillet with sauce.
Toss penne and sauce over medium heat until sauce coats penne, 20 to 30 seconds.
Serve immediately.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix peanut butter and powdered sugar together; smooth into bottom of pie shell.
Make hot pudding by mixing remaining ingredients.
Pour over filling.
Mix all ingredients together.
Form meatballs and brown.
Mix well and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Chop cabbage and steam until limp, not soft. Drain well. Use a shallow baking dish and place in layers 1/2 of cabbage and 1/2 can of soup (spread over cabbage). Crumble 1/2 can onion
rings over this. Then slice Velveeta cheese over all. Repeat layers again. Bake at 350° until bubbly, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Crush Oreo cookies and mix with melted margarine.
Press into 9-inch pie plate and freeze (2 to 3 hours).
Put ice cream in a bowl and stir until smooth. Place in prepared crust and sprinkle with pecans.
Freeze for at least 1 hour (more time in freezer may be needed depending on how much the ice cream has melted).
When ready to serve, slice pie.
Top each slice with hot fudge followed by whipped cream.
Sift and measure flour.
Sift again with soda and salt.
Cream shortening and sugar well.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flavorings.
Add dry ingredients alternately with sour cream.
Bake in a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan at 325° for approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes (time will vary with individual ovens).
Cook spaghetti as directed on box and drain.
In large bowl, add remaining ingredients with spaghetti.
Refrigerate.
Serve cold.
Cook the spinach according to box directions.
Drain well. Mix all other ingredients.
Hollow the center of the bread so it looks like a bowl.
Save the bread from the middle.
Cube into torn bite-size pieces to place around the loaf to use for dip.
In large bowl, combine all ingredients, except 1/2 cup Colby cheese.
Mix well and turn into buttered 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Top with remaining cheese and bake 3 to 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.

Puree the apricots after they have been soaked and cooked according to the package directions; add the sugar and extract. Soak the gelatin in the cold water, add the hot milk and stir over hot water until gelatin is dissolved.
Add this to the puree. Whip the cream and fold it into the puree.
Spoon it into a wet 8-cup mold and chill it in the freezer for about 3 hours. This may be unmolded or served directly from the mold.
Mix salad well and let congeal.
Cream sour cream, cream cheese, sugar and vanilla.
Spread on top of salad.
Sprinkle top with nuts.
Cook the pears and sugar until real thick, then add coconut and pineapple about 1/2 hour before you take it up.
Process in jars for long period of keeping.
In small bowl, combine cream cheese, brown sugar, ginger and vinegar; blend until smooth.
Stir in raspberries.
Serve as a dip or dressing for fresh fruit.
Makes 1 1/4 cups.
In the bowl of an electric mixer with a paddle attachment, combine the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, ground chile and black pepper.
Mix briefly on low speed.

Increase speed to medium and add the water, milk, poblano chile and bell pepper; beat well. Add the eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Change to the dough hook and knead for 3 minutes.
The dough will be very sticky.
Add the butter to the dough, one piece at a time, and continue to knead until dough is smooth and shiny and the butter is completely incorporated, 10 to 20 minutes.
Burn the sugar on stove top on medium heat; set aside to cool. Use an 8-inch cake pan.
Place the last 5 ingredients in blender; blend until smooth.
Pour over burnt sugar in pan.
Steam approximately 1 1/2 hours on very low heat.
Check water level from time to time.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Add nuts.
Combine remaining ingredients; add to dry ingredients.
Stir only until flour is moistened.
Pour into a greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Cut each biscuit into 4 pieces.
Then dip into sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Coat each piece well.
Drop in Bundt cake pan.
Sprinkle over the nuts.
Then melt the butter and brown sugar.
Pour this mixture over biscuits.
Place in cold oven.
Set at 350° and bake for 20 minutes.
Turn pan upside down over plate after removing from oven.
Mix all ingredients together well with mixer; fold in chocolate chips.
Spray Bundt pan with Pam or grease and flour. Pour mixture into Bundt pan.
Bake in the oven preheated to 350° for approximately 1 hour.
After cake is cooled on serving plate, can poke holes in top with toothpick and brush on extra Kahlua.
Dissolve Jell-O in 2 cups boiling water.
Add 2 cups reserved peach syrup (if not enough, add water until there is).
Put mixture in fridge to set a bit (about 1 1/2 hours).
Beat peaches with mixer until very mushy.
Beat the whipping cream, adding the powdered sugar.
Fold in the Jell-O mixture.
Stir very well.
Pour into 13 x 9-inch pan and keep in fridge until set.
Peel and core apples, leaving them whole then slice into 1/2-inch slices.
Set aside.
Mix together the water, sugar, candies and food coloring in a saucepan.
Bring mixture to a boil. Drop in apple rings. Simmer until tender, about 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from syrup.
Serve as an accompaniment to any type wild meat.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease pie plate.
Cook and stir beef and onion; drain.
Stir in seasoning.
Spread in plate; top with chillies.
Beat milk, Bisquick and eggs until smooth.
Pour into plate.
Bake 25 minutes.
Top with tomatoes and cheese; bake 10 minutes longer.
Melt margarine in large skillet.
Add salad dressing mix.
Add chicken and brown slowly until golden.
Place contents of skillet in baking dish.
Blend soup (undiluted), cream cheese and wine until smooth.
Spread over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, 1 hour at 325°.
Serve over rice.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix all ingredients well with hands.
Roll into balls the size of a walnut.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and press with the tines of a fork in a criss-cross pattern.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool on a cake rack. Serve at room temperature.
They freeze very well.
Cook broccoli crisp-tender.
Combine eggs, cheeses, onion, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Arrange broccoli in baking dish; add cheese mixture and sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Add margarine.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Wipe off bologna and
leave
skins
on.
Cut
into 4 or 5-inch lengths.
Pack in jars lengthwise and add 1/2 cup water to each quart.
Cook 1 hour in hot water bath or 30 minutes at 10 pound pressure.
Cream butter, sugars and eggs.
Add vanilla, dry ingredients and M&M's.
Bake 12 minutes at 350°.
Flour and brown steaks in a pan.
Put browned steaks in a casserole dish.
Put chopped onions and cut up mushrooms on steak. Mix soups together and pour over tops of steaks.
Bake for 2 1/2 hours at 350° in a covered casserole dish.

In small bowl, mix flour, melted butter and 1 cup chopped pecans. Press into a 2-quart dish or 10-inch pie pan and bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Cool. Place 1/2 cup chopped nuts in shallow pan and bake in oven with pastry until slightly browned.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 9x13 pan.
Bring sugar, butter and water to a boil.
(Microwave works well.)
Add chocolate and stir until melted.
Add eggs, vanilla and mix well.
Add dry ingredients.
Bake 16-20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in middle comes out sticky.
Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in boiling water. Cool until syrupy and beat in cheese spread and pineapple.
Let congeal to syrupy stage and fold in prepared dessert topping mix.
Refrigerate until set.
Mix well and pour over cake.
Brown sausage, drain and crumble into a 13 x 9-inch dish. Saute hash browns in oleo, then spread over sausage.
Sprinkle cheese over potatoes.
Mix eggs, milk and seasonings.
Pour over mixture.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Combine bread crumbs, brown sugar, chili powder, garlic powder, dry mustard, celery seed and cayenne.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Brush each chicken piece with butter.
Roll in crumb mixture to coat.
Arrange chicken, skin side up, so that pieces do not touch, in a shallow baking pan.
Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 50 minutes or until tender. Do not turn.
Makes approximately 6 servings.
Mix and put in greased casserole. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix together.
Pour into greased dish and dot with margarine. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Blend broccoli, corn, egg, 1/4 cup crumbs, onion, 2 tablespoons melted butter, salt and pepper.
Turn into 1-quart casserole; top with 1/4 cup crumbs mixed with 1 tablespoon melted butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, beat eggs; add sour cream.
Stir in sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, vanilla and salt; mix well.
Stir in apples. Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 375°
for 15 minutes.
Put can of milk in icebox over night.
Add sugar and lemon juice to strawberries.
Beat until berries are a fine pulp.
Spread crescent rolls in a 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Spread hash browns on top.
Fry sausage and drain.
Spread over potatoes. Whip eggs and pour over; top with cheese.
Depending on how many you wish to serve, use six to twelve eggs.
Use sharp cheese. Bake at 350° for one half hour.
Mix liquids and coffee together with pudding mix and beat with hand.
Mix in Cool Whip and put in crust.
Freeze.
Remove and dollop extra Cool Whip on top and sprinkle with toasted almonds.
Serve semi-frozen.
Take out of freezer 10 minutes before serving.
Place first 3 ingredients in saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly until mixture forms soft-ball stage; add vanilla, then coat nuts.
Turn out onto wax paper.
Allow to cool and then separate into pieces.
Place in candy dish.
Saute onion, turkey and celery in margarine.
Add 1 2/3 cups water and seasoning.
Mix. Cook 5 minutes.
Then add stuffing mix and let set.
Use king, silver or red salmon.
Stir all ingredients together.
Shape into roll, ball, log, or leave in bowl.
Chill for 3 hours.
Serve with crackers.
Cream butter, Crisco and sugar.
Beat eggs in one at a time. Add flour, sifted together with salt and baking powder.
Alternate with Pet milk.
Add vanilla and nuts last.
Put a thin layer of dough in a greased angel food pan and sprinkle with cinnamon mixture.
Alternate the layers of dough and cinnamon mixture until pan is filled.
Do not put cinnamon mixture on top.
Bake 60 to 70 minutes in a 350° oven or until done.
Bake cake according to box directions.
Let cool, then crumble half of cake in a punch bowl.
Layer strawberries, pineapple, banana slices and pudding.
Repeat layers and top with Cool Whip.
Add egg whites and salt together and beat until stiff. Add sugar and beat. Add chocolate chips and nuts.
Make crust from first 3 ingredients.
Mix and put in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Cool well.
Mix Cool Whip, cream cheese and powdered sugar together.
Spread on crust.
Mix pudding and milk, cook until thick.
Let cool; pour over cream cheese mixture.
Toast coconut, sprinkle over top and let chill.
Cream first 4 ingredients.
Add eggs.
Mix flour, salt and soda; add gradually.
Blend well.
Stir in 2 cups each chips and pecans.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes for chewy, 11 to 13 minutes for crisp.
Makes 6 dozen (3-inch) cookies.
In a glass 9 x 13-inch pan, combine soup mix, dressing and liquid.
Mix well.
Place chicken pieces in sauce.
Turn to coat each piece.
Cover.
Microwave 9 1/2 minutes per pound at 70% power.
Rearrange chicken piece halfway through cooking time.
Let stand 3 to 5 minutes, covered.
Serve with rice, buttered noodles or stuffing.
Melt butter in deep pan; add farina and cook until golden color, stirring constantly.
Stir in chopped nuts.
Reduce heat. Meanwhile, bring water and sugar to a slow boil.
Cook 3 minutes. Pour syrup slowly over farina, stirring with wooden spoon until halva is slightly thickened.
Remove from heat.
Cover; let stand 10 minutes.
Shape with individual molds or with spoon.
Place on large platters and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Pour hot water over Jell-O.
When dissolved, add sugar.
Cut orange in pieces with peelings and put in blender with cranberries and orange juice.
Blend.
Combine all ingredients and chill in refrigerator overnight.
Cut round steak into thin strips.
Cut onions into chunks. Wrap round steak around onion chunk, then wrap with a piece of bacon.
Secure with a toothpick.
Brown on all sides.
Make broth with bouillon cube and simmer for 1 hour.
Use tongs to pick up.

recipes.t: Spicy Bean Salsa With Tortilla Chips
d: In a large bowl, combine all ingredients except tortilla chips; mix well. Cover and refrigerate several hours or overnight to blend flavors. Serve with tortilla chips as an appetizer. May also serve as a side dish. Makes 12 servings.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Cook on Full power for 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir mixture a couple of times.
Add marshmallow cream and peanut butter.
Stir until it thickens or your arms fall off. Pour into buttered pan.
Let cool.
Enjoy.
Shred beef and mix all ingredients.
Make the night before. Cut top out of loaf bread.
Dig bread out, leaving a 1-inch rim. Pour mixture in bowl.
Cut bread in dip sizes.
When all bread cubes are gone, then cut loaf in bite sizes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In 12-inch skillet, over medium heat, fry bacon crisp; drain on paper towels.
Crumble and set aside.
Prepare cake mix according to package directions.
Add poppy seed and extract.
Bake in 2 (9-inch) layer pans according to directions on package.
Frost with favorite white fluffy icing.

Pour the rest of pudding mixture over crackers.

In a large bowl, combine pancake mix, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, pumpkin, oil, milk and eggs.

Combine next 3 ingredients; set aside.

Beat in chocolate mixture and vanilla extract.
Stir in flour mixture, cracker crumbs and nuts.

Serve hot.

Beat pudding mix with juices you drain off fruit.
Mix in fruit and Cool Whip.
Refrigerate.

Cream sugar and shortening together.
Add boiling water, mixing well, with mixer at medium speed.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.

Turn out on a floured surface and pat into a large rectangle.

Bake 10 to 15 minutes or until nicely browned.

Mix flour, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Add shortening and mix until crumbly.

Wrap each patty in plastic wrap and chill at least 1/2 hour.
When ready to roll, lightly flour both sides of patty and roll on lightly floured surface.

Add the converted rice, mushrooms and onion to the pot without stirring.
