Add the stuffing and walnuts. Sprinkle over broccoli and bake at 400° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Combine the first 3 ingredients.
Place on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes until lightly browned.
Cool.
Simmer onion in oil.
Add tomatoes, paste, sauce and water; simmer.
Do not burn on bottom.
Simmer 1 hour or more.
Parboil sausages slowly to get some fat out, about 20 minutes.
Drain and add sausages to spaghetti sauce.
Heat for 30 minutes at a slow simmer.
Serve with spaghetti.
Mix and scald sugar and milk.
Stir other ingredients into hot milk and cook until thickened and smooth.
After mixture has cooled, add sliced bananas.
Trim and wash cauliflower and break into small flowerets. Combine all ingredients.
Toss lightly and chill well.
Combine half and half with Worcestershire powder.
Dip scallops in milk mixture and roll in bread crumbs.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 5 minutes.
Boil chicken until tender.
Remove skin and bones.
Cut into bite sized pieces.
Reserve 2 cups of cooking broth.
Saute onion in butter until just heated thoroughly.
Add to onion the chili peppers.
Then add and heat chicken broth and soups.
Stir until smooth and heated.
Into large bowl, tear tortillas into bites sized pieces; stir in chicken pieces, soup mixture and 1 cup Cheddar cheese.
Pour into baking dish and top with 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese and crushed nachos (if desired).
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Mix all together.
Bake 1 hour and 20 minutes in large tube pan, greased and floured, at 350°.
Mix all ingredients together and pour into a 2-quart casserole dish.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 300°.
Melt together the bitter chocolate with the stick of butter. Mix the eggs, sugar, flour, vanilla and coffee.
Blend the mixture with the chocolate and butter.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts or marshmallow bits, M&M's or other small edible bits.
Bake about 20 minutes in a 350° oven in an 8 x 14-inch pan.
Test with toothpick for slight moistness.
Refrigerate immediately.
(This keeps them moist.)
Can be frozen.

Cut bacon in small pieces and fry slowly to a golden brown in a large saucepan. Add onion and cook slowly without browning for 5 minutes. Add corn, potatoes and tomatoes in alternate layers. Sprinkle with salt, sugar and pepper, then add water.
Cook slowly until potatoes are tender.
Remove from heat and stir milk in slowly. Serves 6 to 8.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add strawberries and stir until thawed.
Add bananas and nuts.
Pour 1/2 mixture into long dish and put in refrigerator until firm.
Combine pineapple and Cool Whip and spread on layer.
Top with remaining mixture. Refrigerate until firm.
Crumble Blue cheese and mix well with finely grated Cheddar cheese and cream cheese, chopped parsley and grated onion.
Shape into a ball.
Wrap and refrigerate until firm.
Reshape ball and roll in dry roasted peanuts or pecans.
Cream 1 stick of butter and 1 cup of sugar.
Add eggs, flour, chocolate syrup and nuts; mix well.
Pour into greased and floured pan and bake at 325 degrees for 30 minutes.
Top with frosting when cool.
Fry bacon crisp in large skillet.
Pour off drippings.
Cover bottom of skillet with oil.
Saute pepper and onion just until tender.
Meanwhile, cook rice according to directions.
Pour rice over onion and pepper.
Add crumbled bacon and soy sauce.
Stir slightly to mix.
You can add cabbage, carrots, ham, chicken or hamburger meat.
Combine all ingredients in mixer and beat until mixed well, approximately 2 minutes.
Pour into two 9-inch cake pans that have been greased and floured.
Bake at 325° for 35 minutes. Cool before icing with cream cheese frosting.
Combine crab meat, olives, cheese and onion.
Add mixture of mayonnaise and lemon juice; add seasonings.
Fill buttered buns with mixture; wrap each in foil.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Grind dates with a little flour to keep from sticking; walnuts help, too.
Fold in egg whites, stiffly beaten, last.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
In a large saucepan, melt butter and saute onion, celery and apples for 5 minutes.
Stir in curry and flour.
Gradually stir in chicken broth, cream of coconut and half and half.
Stir over moderate heat until sauce bubbles and thickens.
Stir in chicken and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve over rice.
Whip cream to soft peaks; add sugar.
Fold in half and half and vanilla.
Add snow and beat.
Cover and place in freezer.
Place chicken on a rack in roasting pan.
Season with salt and pepper and 1 1/2 teaspoons oregano.
Arrange potatoes around chicken; sprinkle with salt, pepper and oregano.
Pour butter and lemon juice over chicken and potatoes.
Add chicken broth to pan bottom.
Bake at 350° for 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Baste with juices while baking.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine sugar, cinnamon, allspice and ginger.
Add scalded milk slowly to eggs; mix well.
Add sugar-spice mixture and butter or margarine; stir until sugar dissolves.
Combine bread cubes and raisins in buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Pour custard mixture over bread cubes. Place casserole in pan of water.
Bake 1 hour or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Heat 1 cup of the water to boiling; dissolve instant coffee in water.
Stir in remaining water, dry milk, sugar and salt. Refrigerate until chilled 3 to 4 hours.
Place softened ice cream in punch bowl.
Pour chilled coffee mixture on ice cream.
Swirl ice cream throughout coffee mixture.
Beat whipping cream in chilled mixing bowl until very soft peaks from.
Top chocolate mocha punch with mounds of whipped cream.
Sprinkle nutmeg over the mounds of whipped cream.
Melt 1 stick butter.
Crush 1 package Oreos (save some out). Pour butter over cookies in bowl and mix.
Press mixture into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Slice carton of ice cream and layer over cookie dough.
Pour 1 jar caramel ice cream topping over ice cream.
Top with Cool Whip and garnish with leftover Oreos.
Saute onions in butter.
Layer half of onions and butter in casserole dish.
Cover with half of crackers and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Repeat layering.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cover and freeze.
Serve frozen.
Keeps well in refrigerator.
Mix sugar and milk in a large, heavy saucepan.
Slowly bring to rolling boil and boil for 8 minutes.
Then move the saucepan off the heat and add the butter, chocolate chips and marshmallows. Mix only until the chips and the marshmallows are melted.
Add the vanilla and nuts and blend.
Spread the mixture in a large ungreased pan and let it cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt chocolate.
Grease and flour 2 large loaf pans.
Sift the dry ingredients and set aside.
Beat eggs; add sugar, oil and chocolate.
Stir.
Add the sifted dry ingredients and zucchini, then add the nuts.
Pour into 2 large loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown ground beef and drain grease off.
Add Manwich and simmer about 15 minutes.
While waiting for beef and sauce to simmer, make instant mashed potatoes.
Add beef mixture into a casserole dish or pan.
Add corn on top of beef mixture, then add instant potatoes on top of corn, then top with grated cheese.

Combine all ingredients in large mixer bowl. Blend well, then beat at medium speed of electric mixer for 4 minutes. Pour into greased and floured 8 x 4 inch loaf pans. Bake at 350 degrees for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean and cake begins to pull away from sides of pan. Do not underbake. Cool in pan 15 minutes. Remove from pan and finish cooling on racks.
Note:
If you desire to spice it up, add 1/4 cup pepper juice.
Mix all ingredients and bake at 350° for 90 minutes, or until potatoes are done.
Cream the sugar, shortening, salt and nutmeg.
Add eggs and ice water; work in flour.
Roll out on floured board; cut in desired shape.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.
May be sprinkled with sugar while still warm, if desired.
Mix all ingredients in medium-sized bowl.
Pour into a lightly greased 1-quart casserole and bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Heat pineapple juice and lime jello.
Put pineapple, cottage cheese and marshmallows in big bowl.
Cool lime jello and pour over pineapple mixture.
Add whipped cream.
Sets quickly.
Cook beans until mushy.
Dice potatoes, carrots and onions. Add salt, pepper and tomato soup.
Add small amount evaporated milk to thicken and cook until vegetables are cooked.
Mix all ingredients and spread into serving dish or 9 x 13-inch or larger pizza pan.
Top with shredded lettuce, grated Cheddar cheese and chopped tomatoes.
Chill for at least 1 hour. Serve with tortilla chips.
Combine juices and coriander in large pitcher or punch bowl. Just before serving add club soda and stir.
Garnish with orange slices and cranberries.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in 2 greased and floured cake pans.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix together first 5 ingredients.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan. Top with finely crushed crackers and melted oleo.
Bake at 375° until cheese melts and mixture is bubbly.
Serve warm.
Beat butter lightly.
Add part of sugar and mix until smooth. Add remaining sugar and beat until smooth and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in flavoring.
Add dry ingredients alternately with sour cream.
Bake at 325° in greased and floured Bundt or tube pan for 1/2 hour. Reduce heat to 300° and cook 45 to 50 minutes or until cake is done.
Cool cake 5 minutes before removing from pan.
Lightly oil a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Stir together sugar, oil, margarine and eggs.
Mix in nuts and vanilla.
Stir together flour, baking soda and salt; add to sugar mixture.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake in 350° oven about 25 to 35 minutes (until browned and knife comes out clean).
Cut into 32 pieces.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth. Chill and serve with raw vegetables.

Mix flour and baking soda. Cream butter, sugars, vanilla. Add eggs, gradually add flour mixture then stir in chips and nuts. Batter will be stiff. Drop onto ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 375 degrees for 8-10 minutes. For chocolate lovers, use Chocolate flavored instant pudding.
Cook on medium heat in saucepan until thick.
Pour on cake while hot, then place in oven broiler until brown, 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut potatoes in 1/2-inch cubes.
Cover with water; heat to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Drain and cool.
Slice cabbage.
Toss potatoes, cabbage and remaining ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate.
You will need an 8 x 10-inch flowerpot.
Combine all ingredients in a food processor or blender.
Blend until creamy.
Refrigerate, covered.
Will keep for weeks. Yields 2 1/2 cups.
Mix together the mayonnaise and sugar in a small bowl and set aside.
Layer the first 6 items in order listed, then spread mayonnaise mixture over top, sealing edges.
Sprinkle cheese and bacon bits over the top.
Refrigerate and let sit overnight.
Combine all ingredients, except chicken. Mix the night before; let sit out to allow sugar to dissolve. Needs to be at room temperature.
Peel potatoes; cut in slices 3/4-inch thick.
Place in baking dish (single layer is best).
Mix sugar and flour; spread over potatoes.
Heat water and margarine.
Add vanilla.
Pour over sugar and potatoes.
Bake at 350° until potatoes are tender (about 20 to 30 minutes).
Mix together cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip. Spread over the baked crust.
Top with blueberry pie filling.
Cream butter; gradually add 3/4 cup sugar, beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer.
Add egg and lemon rind, beating well.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; stir well. Add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Stir in zucchini and walnuts.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Remove to wire racks. Combine confectioners sugar and lemon juice; stir well.
Drizzle over warm cookies; let cool completely.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in a lightly greased, large, heavy cast-iron skillet.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until browned.
Prepare brownie mix according to directions, using 1 egg method.
Put in pan.
Mix other ingredients and sprinkle over top of brownie mix.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
Brown onion and pepper in margarine.
Cook limas until tender; drain.
Add peppers, onions and celery soup.
Place in a greased casserole dish and cover with bread crumbs and cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Blend dry ingredients.
Cut in shortening until coarse like peas.
Make a well in the center.
Pour in 1/2 cup of milk; toss or mix.
Add egg with rest of milk.
Mix lightly with a fork. Roll or pat to 1/2 or 3/4-inch.
Bake at 400° for 12 to 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Grandma Bella'S Cream Cheese Pound Cake
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream the butter, cheese and sugar until fluffy.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating 3 minutes for each egg.
Combine dry ingredients and beat in alternately with the milk and vanilla.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan lined with waxed paper.
Bake for 1 hour.
Beat eggs until fluffy; put bread in blender, then add apples. Fold in eggs.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cook macaroni shells until done.
Stuff with mixture of cottage cheese, Mozzarella cheese, Parmesan, eggs, spinach, salt and pepper.
Cover with Prego sauce.
Cook at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Arrange chicken parts (or 4 breasts) in 12 x 8-inch baking dish, bone side down, thicker portions toward edges of dish.
Top with 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms.
Stir 1/2 teaspoon dried basil into 2 cups of pasta sauce (onion and garlic is great) and pour over chicken.
Cover with waxed paper.
Microwave High for 17 minutes or until fork can be inserted in chicken with ease and juices run clear, rearranging pieces once.
Serve over cooked pasta.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bring water to boil.
Mix brownie mix, water, oil and egg in large bowl.
Pour into greased and floured 12-inch pizza pan.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, remaining egg and vanilla in small bowl at medium speed until well blended.
Pour over brownies.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Cool.
Top with fruit; drizzle with chocolate.
Grind peppers and onions.
Pour boiling water over them and let stand 2 hours.
Drain and add vinegar, salt, sugar and mustard seed.
Cook until tender.
Jar and seal.
Saute beef, onion and garlic in oil until meat browns.
Add rest of ingredients except rice; bring to a boil.
Stir in rice. Cover; let stand 5 minutes.
Mix all together for 2 minutes.
Put in two loaf pans or one angel food cake pan.
Grease the pans very well and dust with a mixture of cinnamon and sugar.
Bake at 350° for approximately 40 to 50 minutes, depending on the size of the pans.
Wash and dry cucumber and onions.
Chop very fine.
For each package of cream cheese you use, add cucumber and green onions.
Cream sugar, margarine and shortening in mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add flour and eggs; beat well.
Add flavorings; mix well.
Stir in Sun-Drop.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 1/4 hours.
Cool in pan for several minutes. Invert onto serving plate.
Spread frosting over cake.
Yield:
16 servings.
In a large bowl, add pineapple (with juice) and pudding; mix well.
Add fruit cocktail and marshmallows.
Fold in Cool Whip. Put in a pretty glass bowl and top with coconut, chopped nuts and cherries.
Chop onion and bell pepper very fine and cook in small amount of water in frying pan (large).
Add brown sugar, ketchup, mustard, bacon and beans.
Bring mixture to boil.
Pour mixture in baking pan and cook in oven at 350° for 45 minutes to one hour.
Mix hot rice, Cheez Whiz and margarine together until cheese melts. Add rest of ingredients. Put into casserole dish. Bake 20 minutes at 350° until brown.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a jar; shake well.
Combine cauliflower, onion and olives.
Marinate in dressing for 1 hour.
Combine all but nuts and parsley.
Chill.
Shape into ball and roll in nuts and parsley.
Chill again.

In small mixing bowl, blend together soup and milk; set aside. Cook rotini according to package instructions. In large mixing bowl, combine green peppers, onion, chicken, pimiento, cheese and cooked rotini. Pour on soup mixture and mix thoroughly. Pour into 9 x 13 greased casserole. Sprinkle with bread crumbs. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes. Serves 7 to 9.
Thaw peas; add all other ingredients.
Chill overnight. Serves 6.
Peel and dice potatoes and cook until tender.
Drain.
Melt butter in 3-quart pot.
Add carrot and onion.
Cover and cook until tender.
Remove from heat.
Add flour and milk.
Add 1/2 potatoes.
Mash remaining.
Add to soup with seasonings and bouillon.
Heat to steaming hot.
Cook chicken and cut into bite size pieces.
Place in bottom of a 3-quart casserole dish.
Combine sour cream and chicken soup; pour over chicken.
Crush crackers; put over chicken and sauce. Melt butter; put over crackers.
Top with poppy seed until dark; refrigerate for 24 hours.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Sort and soak beans with a pinch of baking soda over night. Next day bring to a boil. Rinse and cover with water and add ham or bacon, onion, salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer
1 1/2 to 2 hours or until tender. Add water as needed during cooking time.
Mix the first 4 ingredients together.
Spray a loaf pan or dish with Pam.
Sprinkle a layer of Pepperidge Farm herb stuffing on the bottom of the pan.
Add squash mixture, then cover with another layer of Pepperidge Farm herb stuffing.
Dot the top of the casserole generously with butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Brown beef and onion in skillet for 5 minutes.
Add salsa, tomato sauce and bouillon cube; bring to a full boil.
Stir in rice; cover and remove from heat.
Let stand 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Mix well and put into 2 graham cracker pie crusts.
Put in refrigerator for 3 to 4 hours before serving.
This is rich and delicious.

recipes.t: Hot Fudge Sauce(This Is A "Mom" Original)
d: Mix cocoa, sugar and salt.
Add butter and milk.
Bring to a boil over medium to low heat; stir constantly.
When sauce thickens, remove from heat.
Cool 3 to 5 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.
Use over ice cream, cream puffs or eclairs.
Put canned milk in a quart jar and fill up with regular milk. Use a double boiler; heat until boiling.
Beat eggs and add to milk.
Add sugar and cornstarch.
Boil until thick, then cool. Strain.
Add vanilla.

Bake potatoes at 400° for 45 minutes or until tender. Cool, then cut into quarters lengthwise. Scoop out pulp, leaving 1/8-inch shell. Reserve pulp for use in other recipes. Increase oven temperature to 500°. Combine butter and soy sauce. Brush on both sides of skins. Place on a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until crisp. Top with coarse salt, sour cream, chives and/or bacon bits. Yield: 6 servings.
Cook pasta as directed on the box.
Drain; rinse with cold water and put in a large bowl.
Add olives, artichoke hearts, celery, dressing and cheese.
Season with salt and pepper.
Toss together.
Cover and let marinate in refrigerator overnight. Makes 8 servings.
Beat the margarine, sugar and vanilla until light and fluffy. Add flour and mix well.
Chill the dough.
Shape about 1 tablespoon of dough around each chocolate kiss.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375° for 12 minutes.
The cookie should be set but not brown.
Cool slightly, then roll in confectioners sugar.
In a 10-inch skillet, brown meat with onion; drain off fat. Stir in gravy and 1/2 cup water.
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and frozen vegetables, breaking apart with fork.
Bring to boiling.
Cover; reduce heat.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Top with biscuits; simmer, covered, 15 minutes.
Sprinkle biscuits with cheese; heat until cheese melts.
Sprinkle with paprika, if desired.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease oblong pan.
Mix egg, butter and cake mix together.
Pat into pan.
Pat flat; do not leave raised edges.
On rack in broiling pan broil steak for 5 minutes on each side; cut into 2- inch pieces and set aside.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs, one at a time, and stir until mixed well.
Add flour and stir until well blended.
Add flavoring.
Stir in whipping cream.
Bake in a Bundt pan at 375° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in a 3-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 30 minutes. Strain if desired. Cover and refrigerate.
Combine peas, tuna fish, corn, pimentos and cream of mushroom soup in casserole.
Top with shoestring potatoes.
Bake.
Reserve stock.
Debone chicken and cut in bite size pieces. Cook spaghetti in reserved stock; drain to just below top of spaghetti.
Saute onion, celery and bell pepper in margarine until tender.
Add cheese to hot spaghetti; stir until melted.
Add all other ingredients together and season with garlic salt.
Stir together well.
Bake in oblong dish or pan at 350° for 30 minutes. Sprinkle parsley flakes on top.
Serves approximately 12 to 15 people.

Mix baking soda and soup in a bowl; set aside. Cream sugar and Crisco. Add eggs and soup mix; mix well. Sift together dry ingredients; mix all together. Bake in 9 x 9 or 8 x 9 greased and floured pan at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Mix well and form into ball.
Mix all together and put in icebox overnight.
When chilled, roll them and cut in star shape.
Bake at 350°.
Mix first 6 ingredients together; stir in 1 cup of any dry cereal.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a piece of waxed paper.
Put a jelly bean in center of each and refrigerate until firm.
Makes 12 cookies.
Mix well.
Use more water if needed for thinning.
Serve over Swedish meatballs.
Arrange fish in a greased 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish.
Pour soup over fish.
Sprinkle with pepper, cheese and paprika.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until lightly browned.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Press evenly into ungreased pan first 3 ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Beat cream cheese in 3-quart bowl.
Add sugar and cocoa gradually.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Pour in vanilla.
Pour into spring-form pan.
Bake at 300° until center is firm, about 1 hour.
Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours.
Prepare topping.
Spread over cake; loosen sides and remove.
Layer the bottom of 9 x 13-inch cake pan with the pecans and coconut.
Pan must be buttered.
Mix cake mix as directed on box and pour over pecans and coconut in pan.
Mix cream cheese, oleo and sugar together and pour over cake mix.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients except for oil; mix well.
Pour about 2 inches of oil into frying pan; get oil hot but not smoking, or use Fry Daddy.
Drop batter by tablespoons, 4 to 5 at a time, into hot oil.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve immediately.
Makes about 24 puffs.
You will also need artificial holly leaves or other garnish.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Use as a dressing for vegetables.
Add water to heavy skillet and immediately add brown sugar also.
Stir continuously over medium heat.
Bring mixture to a rapid boil until it reaches the soft ball stage (120° to 238° on a candy thermometer).
Take off heat.
Stir in pecans until well coated.
Sprinkle cinnamon.
Keep stirring until they cool and dry.
Cut cream cheese into 20 pieces.
Mash biscuits into 3 1/2 inch circle.
Place a piece of cream cheese on each biscuit.
Mix cinnamon and sugar.
Place 1 teaspoon of sugar mixture on each biscuit.
Roll biscuits into balls.
Melt butter and pour into Bundt pan.
Then pour in 1/2 of the nuts into pan.
Then pour 3/4 of what sugar mixture you have left into Bundt pan.
Then put your 20 biscuit balls into the Bundt pan.
Then pour what sugar mixture and nuts you have left over biscuits.
Bake 35 minutes at 350°. Remove from oven.
Turn onto plate.
Let pan remain a few minutes before removing.
Glaze while hot.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake in covered casserole at 350° until hot and bubbly.
Combine sugar, milk and margarine in pot; boil for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; add remaining ingredients. Stir until chips and marshmallows are melted.
Pour into a well buttered pan; let cool in refrigerator for 2 hours.
Cut into 1 inch squares.
Combine the yolks, lemon juice and sugar in the top of a double boiler.
Cook over simmering water until sugar is dissolved.
Add butter; continue to simmer until mixture thickens. Pour in a clean bowl.
Chill.
Mix in order. Drop by ice cream dipper. Flatten with fork. Bake 12 minutes at 350°.
In large saucepan, melt butter.
Remove from heat.
Add brown sugar and mix well.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into 8-inch square greased pan. Bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Drain bacon, reserving 1/4 cup drippings.
Crumble bacon; reserve 2 tablespoons.
Microwave beans as directed on package; drain well.
Add mushrooms and onion to reserved 1/4 cup drippings in skillet.
Cook and stir on medium-high heat 10 minutes; drain.
Add bacon, hot cooked green beans and pepper; mix lightly.
Spoon into 2-quart serving dish. Microwave process cheese spread as directed on label.
Pour over green bean mixture.
Sprinkle with reserved 2 tablespoons crumbled bacon.
Makes 10 servings.
Put all ingredients in blender and mix until fluffy.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drop by spoonful on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375°.
Cook all ingredients on low heat.
Stir constantly to prevent sticking until thickened.
Remove from stove.
Add lump of butter. Cool; ready for use.

Cream butter. Add sugar and other ingredients in order given. When thoroughly mixed, mold and shape into fingers about the size of pecans. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly browned. Roll in powdered sugar when cool. Be sure to mix pecans in by hand. Makes about 7 dozen.
Sprinkle salt over cucumbers and let stand about 15 minutes. Squeeze water from slices and combine with remaining ingredients. Chill.
Bring to a boil and boil, covered, 2 minutes.
Uncover and cook to a soft ball stage.
While cooking, beat 2 egg whites until stiff, but not dry.
Pour the syrup over the beaten egg whites slowly.
Beat with electric mixer until thick, almost stands in peaks.
Quickly add 2 cups pecans and 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla. Drop on wax paper.
Mix ground beef, egg, seasonings and bread crumbs with 1/3 can of tomato sauce.
Add more sauce and/or breadcrumbs until mixture is moist and well mixed.
Place remaining tomato sauce in medium saucepan with sugar and lemon juice.
Mix and place over medium-high heat.
Brown hamburger; drain off fat.
Add pepperoni and pizza sauce.
Mix well and simmer 5 minutes.
Add cheese just before serving.
Spoon onto bun and enjoy.

Grind together peppers, garlic and onion. Put in crock pan (not aluminum). Add salt and add just enough water to cover. Let set 2 hours and drain. Add oil, vinegar and water. Cook 30 minutes. Seal in hot jars. Makes 12 pints.
Melt butter and add chopped onion, oregano, salt and rice. Stir all the ingredients listed and simmer 10 minutes (can use iron skillet or Teflon).
Turn into large casserole and add beef consomme and water.
Add drained mushrooms; bake, covered at 400° for 1 hour.
Saute the shrimp with the butter and seasonings for 1 minute. Add the vermouth and boil for 1/2 minute.
Strew shrimp in pie shell.
Make custard with eggs and milk or cream.
Pour in custard to within 1/8-inch of rim; sprinkle on cheese.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 375° or until puffed and browned.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add onion, egg and milk; mix well.
Drop by spoonful into deep fry; fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Mix flour and sugar together.
Beat egg yolks.
Mix all together and cook over boiling water until thick.
Put in baked pie shell.
Pour peaches and juice into
an 11 x 14-inch pan, which has been greased.
Pour
dry
cake
mix
over
peaches.
Melt margarine and pour over mixture.
Bake
in 325° oven 1 hour or until brown on top.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add spices and
dry
ingredients.
Drop
by spoonful onto greased baking sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool on rack.
Store in refrigerator.
Each cookie contains 55 calories.
To reserved pineapple liquid add enough water to make 1 1/2 cups.
In large bowl combine Eagle Brand milk.
Add pudding mix and beat well.
Add pineapple.
Chill 10 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon 1 1/2 cups pudding into 3 to 4-quart glass serving bowl.
Top with 1/3 each of chocolate wafers, banana and pudding. Repeat layering twice, ending with pudding.
Chill thoroughly.
Cream first 4 ingredients together.
Butter or Pam spray 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer 1 package rolls, filling, 1 package rolls and cinnamon-sugar topping.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder into bowl.
Beat eggs with milk; add melted Crisco and whole kernel corn and combine the two mixtures lightly.
Drop from a teaspoon into deep Crisco heated to 365° (or when an inch cube of bread browns in 60 seconds).
Fry until brown and cooked in center (about 4 to 5 minutes).
Drain on absorbent paper.
Cream margarine and sugar.

Pour into large bowl and fold in Cool Whip.

Clean vegetables with a vegetable brush.

Simmer first 7 ingredients together until done.
Place in crusts.
Cover with lattice work crust or rolled top crust and be creative with designs on top.
Bake 1 hour at 450°.
Makes 4 pies.
Wash and cut up chicken.
Boil chicken in large pot with plenty of water.
Add onion, pepper, salt and butter.
After chicken is done, use broth and pour over corn bread.
Put all other ingredients with corn bread and mix well.
Debone chicken and put pieces in with dressing.
Pour mixture in a greased pan and bake at 350° about 30 minutes or until brown.
Pour boiling water over meal.
Let stand until cool.
Add sugar, salt and beaten egg.

Cover tightly over low heat about 3/4 hour.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill in refrigerator for a couple of hours.
Combine ingredients in order given except use only 1/2 can cherries.
Lastly, fold in last 1/2 of cherries.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Soften yeast in lukewarm water.
Cream shortening, sugar and salt.
Add boiling water and cool to lukewarm.
Add well beaten eggs, yeast mixture and flour; mix well.
Place in refrigerator at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
Make into rolls.
Let rise 2 hours in warm place.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425°.
Mix sugar, cocoa and cornstarch in saucepan.
Add butter, milk, eggs and vanilla; mix well.
Pour into regular pie shell (not deep dish) and bake at 325° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Cream margarine and brown sugar.
Add beaten eggs.
Mix together flour, soda and baking powder.
Add with coconut flakes and oatmeal to mixture.
Add nuts (optional).
Place pecans, cashews and almonds in 1 1/2-quart micro-proof casserole.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt.
Cut butter into 8 pieces and arrange evenly on top of nuts.
Cook, uncovered, on High for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once or twice during cooking.
Combine rice, milk, sugar and salt; cook until creamy (15 to 20 minutes).
Blend milk and egg and stir into rice mixture.
Add raisins and cook 2 minutes.
Add butter and vanilla; sprinkle with nutmeg or cinnamon (optional).
Pick over beans; wash.
Cover with 3 cups water and 1 tablespoon baking soda.
Soak overnight or 8 hours; then add 2 cups water, mustard and next 6 ingredients.
Cover and boil 20 minutes.
Heat oven to 250°.
Cut salt pork into small pieces and place in a bean pot or casserole dish.
Cover with hot beans and their liquid.
Sprinkle pepper on top.
Cover and bake in a slow 250° oven or until tender.
Add 3/4 water when 2/3 done, if necessary.
Cook sugar and water.
Add cranberries.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water, then add cranberry mixture and pineapple and chill slightly.
Fold in celery and nuts.
Put in 5-cup mold or 9 x 9-inch square dish.
Mix jello according to directions. Add pineapple and oranges (drain both).
Chill until set.
Top with whipped cream.
Sprinkle nuts on top.
Thoroughly cream together butter or margarine and sugar.
Add egg; beat until light and fluffy.
Add orange peel and corn syrup; mix well.
Sift together remaining ingredients; stir into creamed mixture.
Chill dough thoroughly.
On lightly floured surface, roll to 1/4-inch thickness.

Bake in 375° oven for 8 to 10 minutes.

Cool on rack.
Decorate gingerbread men with decorating icing and raisins, if desired.

Shape into burgers and fry or grill.

Pour over the broccoli mixture. Stir until all pieces are coated.

Cook until sugar is dissolved.
Add peanut butter; continue cooking until it melts. Add this to cereal.
Mix in large bowl until cereal is coated. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Let set until firm.
Slice a large onion and boil until tender in chicken broth; strain and throw away onion.
Return to heat.

Stir.

Simmer. Pour into cup over a slice of lemon.

Mix cabbage with mayonnaise, buttermilk or sour cream, Tabasco, onion and celery seed.
Refrigerate 1 hour before serving.

In a large skillet, saute broccoli, zucchini, red pepper and snow peas in butter until crisp-tender. Add half and half and black pepper.
Cook briefly until slightly reduced. Serve over pasta. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

Mix the milk, honey, blueberries, baking powder, egg and shortening. Combine flour and salt; add to the first ingredients. Stir just to moisten. Fill greased muffin pans 1/2 full. Bake at 400° for 12 to 15 minutes. Makes 12 to 15 muffins.
Slice squash in half.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and oleo. Cook in microwave until tender.

Mix and put into a greased and floured 8 x 12 pan. Pat on bottom of pan.

Spread evenly. Refrigerate until firm (about 15 minutes).
In a large pot, boil chicken until tender.
Remove from broth and reserve broth.
Debone chicken and put aside.
To the broth add onion, celery, green pepper and oregano.
Salt and pepper generously.
Then add vermicelli.
Stir constantly until vermicelli is done.
Add deboned chicken.
Mix salt, pepper and flour.
Roll individual servings of veal cutlets in seasoned flour.
Brown in hot oil in skillet rubbed with garlic.
Add 1 cup hot water; cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours. Arrange meat on hot platter.
Into gravy left in pan, stir 1 cup cream.
Heat and pour over noodles.
Sprinkle with paprika.

Cook sugar and water to soft-ball stage. Beat egg whites until stiff. Pour 1/2 sugar mixture over egg whites, beating constantly. Place remaining syrup back on heat. Bring to boil, then pour syrup over egg whites. Add cut up marshmallows to icing and beat until consistency to spread on cake.

Melt shortening in a skillet and brown meatballs on all sides.

Add liquid and remaining ingredients, except the beans. Cover and cook slowly for 10 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Add drained beans; cover and heat thoroughly.

Bake at 350° for 13 minutes or until light golden brown; cool.
In small, heavy saucepan over low heat, melt chips.
Spread over oat mixture; sprinkle with nuts.
Refrigerate until chocolate is set.
Cut into bars and store in tightly covered container in refrigerator.
Makes 2 dozen bars.

Cook beef with oil to desired tenderness. Break noodles into 4 sections and cook (save beef seasoning/flavoring packet). Combine cooked noodles, steak sauce, carrot, onion and beef seasoning/flavoring packet. Cook until heated throughout. Add beef. Sprinkle with peanuts. Yield: 4 servings.
Combine all ingredients in a large dish.
Marinate beef, chicken or lamb.

Bake.

Hard boil eggs, let cool and peel.

ingredients.

Serve chilled.

Either simmer on top of stove or place in oven at 375° until all ingredients are bubbly.

Spray a glass baking dish with a nonstick spray. In microwave, melt cheese, butter and cheese. Put sliced potatoes in baking dish. Sprinkle dried onion over potatoes and salt and pepper to taste. Pour cheese mixture over potatoes. Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Combine prepared apples and sugar in large mixing bowl.

Blend oil and egg into apple/sugar mixture.

Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Mix ingredients together.
Use for deep frying vegetables when camping.

Heat pineapple and juice until hot; but not boiling. Remove from heat and add dry gelatin. Mix well. Stir in buttermilk and fold in Cool Whip. Place in 13 x 9 dish and refrigerate until set, congealed.

Add flour.
Add egg yolk and vanilla. Batter will be stiff.

Cook broccoli in boiling, salted water until tender; drain. Arrange broccoli in greased 11 1/2 x 7 1/2-inch baking dish. Place cooked chicken on top.

Sprinkle with cheese.
Combine bread crumbs and butter.
Sprinkle over top.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350° or until thoroughly heated.

Put yams in bottom of baking dish.

Add bread crumbs slowly until mixture is consistency of cookie dough (sprinkle in more crumbs if needed).
Roll into a ball and pat ball into a glass dish (about 8 x 8-inch).

Cream the margarine, Crisco and sugar until light and fluffy. Add eggs; beat well. Sift flour, measure and add baking powder; sift again. Add to the creamed mixture with milk. Add flavoring last and beat well. Pour into well-greased and floured pan.

Preheat oven to 450°.

Add all ingredients except whiskey.

Add to dry ingredients and beat until blended.
Stir in crawfish, rice and green peppers.

Add Tabasco sauce to taste.
Drop batter by tablespoonfuls into deep, hot fat (375°).
Fry until golden, 3 to 4 minutes, turning once. Drain on paper towel and serve with cocktail sauce or tartar sauce. Makes 24 puffs.
Combine flour, sugar, oil, egg yolks, pineapple cinnamon and nutmeg in large bowl.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form. Fold into batter.
Fold in pecans.
Pour into a 10-inch tube pan. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 10 minutes, or until cake tests done. Let cool in pan.

Mix first 4 ingredients together.

Heat oven to 400°. Layer ingredients in casserole pan and bake until done.
Mix all ingredients, except coconut and food coloring.
Shape in about 3 dozen small ovals.

Mix rice and soups together.

Mix together soup, onion, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Add chicken, rice, celery and eggs; toss lightly.
Put mixture in 9 x 13-inch baking dish; top with bread crumbs.
Bake for 40 minutes at 350°.
Boil roast in a large pot on top of stove until extremely tender.

By hand, gradually stir 2 cups flour, Cheddar cheese and 2 to 3 cups more flour until soft dough.
Knead on floured surface until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled in size.
Punch down dough.
Shape into rolls. Place in greased pan.
Cover; let rise 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Wash the unpeeled sweet potatoes.
Cook in a large saucepan in the water with 1 teaspoon salt for about 20 minutes, until tender, but not mushy.

Add the remaining salt, butter, pepper and milk.
Combine cream cheese, sour cream and butter thoroughly.
Add remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Serve with crackers.

Set over night or for several hours in the refrigerator.

Cook over medium-high heat until thick syrup forms on bottom of pan, stirring frequently. Add corn, bacon, pimento, salt, pepper and chiles. Stir to mix and continue cooking until corn is heated through.
("Great for company.")
Use fresh or frozen berries.

Blend until smooth.

Pour chocolate and sweetened condensed milk into bowl; stir until smooth and pour into crust.
Press nuts evenly onto chocolate in the crust and refrigerate 10 minutes.
Pour milk into large bowl and add pudding mixes.
Beat with wire whisk for 2 minutes or until smooth.
Mixture will be thick.
Spread 1 1/2 cups of the pudding over nuts and chocolate layer in crust. Immediately stir half of the whipped topping into remaining pudding.
Spread over pudding in crust.
Top with remaining whipped topping.
Refrigerate 3 hours or until set.
Mix all but Certo.
Boil for 1 minute.
Add Certo and boil for 2 minutes.
Put in clean jars and seal.
Mix well.
Chill. Serve over ice. Serves 75.
Sift flour and cut lard into mixture.
Add sugar and buttermilk; mix well with hands.
Roll out and place apart on baking sheet that has been greased with margarine.
Bake at 450° for about 18 minutes, or until brown on the bottom, then broil tops until golden brown.
Brush margarine over the tops while hot.
Mix butter, sugar, cocoa and milk.
Boil hard for 1 minute. Remove from heat and add vanilla and oats.
Drop by spoon on waxed paper.
Mix well and pour into unbaked pie crust.
Slice 3/4 stick margarine on top.
Bake in 425 degree oven for 30 minutes or till set.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In small saucepan, over low heat, melt chocolate pieces, stirring occasionally.
In medium bowl, beat together next 5 ingredietns.
Slowly add melted chocolate, stirring rapidly with wire whisk or spoon.
Fold in pecans.
In electric skillet, brown roast on all sides in butter.
Pour enough water to cover roast; simmer 2 to 3 hours.
Add more water during simmering if necessary.
Drain water (if any) and place potatoes in skillet with roast.
Pour in pineapple juice.
Cook until juice becomes thick-like sauce and potatoes are tender.
Cook carrots until just tender.
Place carrots into buttered casserole.
Sprinkle raw onions over carrots.
Spread mayonnaise mixed with lemon juice over carrots and onions; pepper to taste. Add grated Cheddar cheese.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cook hamburger and onions until brown; drain.
Stir in tomatoes and juice, green peppers, water, mushrooms, salt, sugar, chili powder and macaroni.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat and simmer about 30 minutes.
If needed, add more water.
Cream butter.
Gradually add sugars.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add dry ingredients. Mix.
Add pumpkin.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Rinse broccoli well and cut flowerets into bite-size pieces. Toss with raisins, onion and crisp bacon pieces.
Combine cream cheese and remaining ingredients in blender.
Pour over broccoli. Mix well.
Serve well chilled.
Use only butter or margarine.
Mix Ragu sauce and Cheddar cheese soup with 2 cups of Mozzarella cheese in baking dish.
Drain grease off ground beef. Mix ground beef in sauce.
Add cooked noodles; mix well.

Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray Pam on a 10-inch tube pan.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Cream together the butter, shortening and sugar.
Add extracts.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Sift flour with baking powder and salt; add to egg mixture alternately with milk.
Blend well after each addition.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Cool 15 minutes before turning gently onto plate.
Bake and cool pie crusts.
Toast chopped pecans and coconut. Mix Cool Whip, condensed milk and cream cheese.
Put a layer of this mixture in bottom of crusts, then sprinkle in pecans and coconut.
Next, drizzle caramel topping over all.
Layer again, starting with cream cheese mixture and ending with caramel topping. Freeze.
Take out about 30 minutes before serving.
Thaw spinach and drain well (squeeze liquid out of spinach, if necessary).
Mix with other ingredients and refrigerate for several hours before serving.
Heat oven to 400.
Grease rectangular baking dish, 13x9x2 inches.
Cook beef and onion in 10 inch skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until beef is brown.
Drain.
Stir in soup, vegetables and milk.
Remove from heat.
Combine water, fruit juice, Minute tapioca, sugar and salt in saucepan and mix well.
Bring mixture quickly to a boil over direct heat.
Stir all the time and remove from heat after boiling.
Do not overcook.
Will be thin.
Put in pineapple and nuts.
Stir occasionally until cool.
Mix well and serve chilled.

8 to 10 servings.
In 2-quart casserole, add oleo, peanut butter and vanilla. Put in microwave on High power for 3 minutes.
Remove from microwave and stir in sugar.
Press in container.
Let cool.
Cut in squares.
Put all in mixer bowl.
Stir on slow to combine.
Beat well.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine shortening and sugar in mixing bowl.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and beat until well blended in peanut butter.
Sift together flour, salt and soda. Combine with peanut butter.
Stir in oats.
Roll dough to form small balls.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet.
With fork, press cookie balls.
If dough sticks to fork, dip in flour. Bake for about 12 minutes.
Cut gumdrops into small pieces.
Cream butter and sugar together.
Add well beaten eggs.
Add flour and applesauce alternately.
Stir in baking soda and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Fold in nuts, raisins and gumdrops (chopped candied cherries and candied pineapple may be added for variety).
Bake slowly in about 250° oven approximately 3 hours.
Will make 4 small loaves or one large tube pan.
I use all orange slices, 2 pounds.
In a large skillet, saute poultry in oil until no longer pink. Set aside.
In same skillet, cook onion, peppers and garlic until tender. Drain. Stir in chili and tomatoes.
Add rice and pepper sauce.
Arrange chicken on top.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Top with shredded cheese.

Saute onion in butter.
Boil squash until tender.
