Add squash, beaten egg and crumbled crackers.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Place mixture in casserole dish and bake at 350° uncovered until light brown on top.
Place chicken in a 13 x 9-inch greased baking dish.
Mix soup and broth.
Pour over chicken.
Break eggs over this.
Chill the evaporated milk, unopened, in refrigerator until icy cold.
Mix all ingredients and allow to marinate for at least 2 hours.
Serve with crackers.
(Better if made 1 or 2 days ahead.)
Slowly melt butter being careful not to burn.
Add brown sugar while butter is still warm.
If brown sugar is clumpy, place with butter in microwave until sugar softens.
Add eggs and vanilla and beat until creamy and of a slightly lighter color.
In separate bowl, mix dry ingredients together and add to mixture.
Fold in chips.
Place 2-inch balls on ungreased sheet and bake at 325° for about 12 to 15 minutes.
Take out and cool for one minute.

Butter bread on both sides. Saut onions in 2 tablespoons butter. Butter 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Layer mushrooms, onions, cheese and bread. Mix soup, milk and soy sauce and pour over top. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix first 3 ingredients and place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle nuts over mixture.
Mix cream cheese and box confectioners sugar and spread over nuts.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
When cool, cut in squares.
Slice cookie dough 1/4 inch thick.
Arrange slices close together in pizza pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until light brown.
Cool completely.
Cook noodles according to directions on package.
Drain.
Stir in tuna, celery, mayonnaise, onion, green pepper and salt.
In saucepan, combine soup and milk; heat through.
Add cheese.
Heat and stir until cheese melts.
Add to noodle mixture.
Turn into 2-quart casserole.
Bake, uncovered, in a 425° oven for 20 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Bake pastry shell 9 to 11 minutes.
Let cool.
Beat 4 egg whites, at room temperature, and cream of tartar at high speed on mixer for 1 minute.
Gradually add 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until stiff peaks form, 2 to 4 minutes.
Combine egg yolks, cantaloupe and next 6 ingredients in a heavy saucepan; stir well.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and bubbly.
Remove from heat; stir in vanilla.
Pour mixture into prepared pie shell.
Spread meringue over hot filling, sealing to edge of pastry.
Bake at 400° for 8 minutes, until browned.
Let cool.
Grease muffin tin very thoroughly.
Sift flour and salt together.
Separate
eggs
and
beat
yolks
until
thick
and creamy.
Whip the
cream
until
it
holds its shape.
Now add flour and whipped cream to the egg yolks alternately beginning and ending with the flour.
Whip egg whites until stiff.
Dump egg batter on
top of whites and mix with your hands until all the white patches have disappeared.
Work quickly.
Spoon into muffin tin, filling half full.
Bake in preheated oven at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Lay cooked chicken pieces in bottom of casserole dish.
Spread mushroom soup over chicken.
Heat 1 can cream of chicken soup with 1 can water or chicken broth.
Add 1 package bread crumbs.
Spread over top.
Bake at 350° for about 35 minutes.
Combine salmon, onions and butter; mix thoroughly.
Add potatoes and mash.
Stir in milk; whip until smooth.
Spread mixture in prepared pastry shells; top with crust and crimp edges to seal.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Pie may be frozen.
Yields 12 to 16 servings.
Boil until syrup reaches 300° on candy thermometer.
Take from heat.
Add 1 tablespoon soda.
Pour on a buttered cookie sheet. When hard, break in pieces and dip.
Combine all ingredients.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°. Serve with crackers.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Cool and crumble.
Cook macaroni according to directions.
Combine macaroni, crumbled bacon and tomato sauce.
Cut cheese up in pieces and mix in with other ingredients.
Put in a 2-quart casserole dish sprayed with Pam and bake at 350° for about 30 minutes, until cheese is melted.
Mix egg, sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt and flour.
Bring water and 1 cup
milk to a boil.
Have batter ready.
Drop into boiling mixture gently.
Turn heat down.
Dumplings go to bottom of pan (cover).
Add butter, corn and 1 cup milk.
Cook until warmed through.

Preheat the oven to 350°. Beat butter at medium speed of an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Gradually add sugar, beating well. Add eggs and molasses, mixing well. Combine flour and next 4 ingredients. Add to butter mixture alternately with hot water, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Mix after each addition. Pour batter into a greased and floured 8-inch square pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serve with whipped cream. Makes 9 servings.
Prepare the night before.
Grease an 8 x 10-inch pan with butter or oleo.
Place 6 slices of bread (crusts removed) in bottom of pan.
Cover each slice with a slice of American cheese. Then spread each with prepared mustard and cover with any of the listed meats.
Butter 6 more slices of bread and place on top, buttered side up.
Blend soups.
Stir in milk and cream.
Heat just to boiling. Add crab.
Heat.
Stir in wine just before serving.
Serves 6 to 8.
Pound cutlets until they reach 3 x 3-inch size.
Dip meat into egg and milk mixture, then dip into 3/4 cup dry seasoned bread crumbs.
Sprinkle freely with Parmesan cheese; allow to stand 15 minutes.
Saute in butter or oil until crisp (2 to 4 minutes, each side).
Place in baking sheet, top with your favorite spaghetti sauce and Mozzarella cheese.
Place in preheated oven until cheese melts.
Serves 4 to 5.
Cook beets.
Peel and cut.
Pour liquid over and bring to boil, then put in jars and seal.
Saut chicken livers and onions until done, but not browned. Cool slightly.
Puree 1 cup at a time in blender.
Stir in salt, dry mustard, pepper and butter.
Refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Frost 1/2 chocolate and 1/2 white frosting.
Put 2 to 3 cups hot water in large stew pan.
Add potatoes, carrots and onions (all peeled and diced).
When halfway tender, add tomato sauce, corn, beef stew mix and hamburger meat.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cook on low heat until ready.

Pour juice off pickles and discard. Rinse with cold water. Put in large bowl or crock and add remaining ingredients. Stir well until the sugar dissolves. Let stand for 4 days, stirring daily. Pack in sterilized jars or put them back in the gallon jar they came in and store in refrigerator.
Drain pineapple and save juice.
Put pineapple in a butter dish.
Mix sugar and flour and sprinkle over pineapple and add 1 cup pineapple juice.
Pour over.
Put a cup of grated cheese.
Melt 1 stick of butter and 2 tablespoons of brown sugar and stir up crushed crackers (Ritz).
Sprinkle over the ingredients.
Bake 40 minutes at 325°.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add vanilla and then salt.
Add egg whites one at a time, beating after each one.
Beat in 2 tablespoons flour.
Add 3/4 cup buttermilk with baking soda added. Add remaining flour and buttermilk alternately.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes in 10 x 15-inch sheet cake pan that has been greased and floured.
Cool and frost with buttercream frosting.
Mix all ingredients and make medium size patties.
Brown in small amount of cooking oil and set aside.
Make the sauce.
Cream first 3 ingredients together.
Add eggs, one at a time. Beat after each egg.
Add cake flour, 1/2 cup at a time.
Beat each time.
Add lemon or almond extract.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour in greased, floured Bundt pan.
Cook and cube chicken.
Mix together all ingredients, except cheese and tortillas.
Put a little of the mixture in the bottom of pan (so they don't stick).
Put 2 tablespoons of mixture in tortilla and some of the cheese, roll and place in pan.
After all are rolled up, spread rest of sauce and cheese on top.
Bake for about 30 minutes at 350°.
Grease 9 x 9 x 2-inch or tube microwavable cake pan with solid shortening and line with waxed paper.
Blend water, egg whites and oil.
Stir in cake mix and pudding until well blended.
Microwave on turntable 9 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Remove from microwave and cool until warm to touch.
Turn out on cake plate and remove waxed paper.
Frost with cream cheese frosting, if desired.
Brown ground beef; drain well.
Combine everything together. Bake in a 9 x 13 inch baking dish at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix sugar and cocoa.
Add milk and margarine.
Bring to a boil for 2 1/2 to 3 minutes.
Add vanilla and oatmeal.
Remove from heat.
Spoon out on wax paper.
Let cool.
Cookies will harden while cooling.
Yield: 2
dozen.
Bring to a boil first 4 items.
Boil 1 minute and remove from heat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Beat until well mixed.
Drop by spoonfuls on wax paper.
Let stand for 30 minutes.
Whip the Dream Whip. Add sugar and cream cheese.
Mix well. In deep dish, put 1 layer of ladyfingers.
Spread with mixture. Cover with pie filling.
Repeat in layers.
Chill at least 3 hours. Serves 10 to 12.
Cream together first 5 ingredients.
Add flour, soda and salt to mixture.
Fold in oats, then corn flakes.
Bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes.
Makes 100 (2 1/2-inch) cookies.
"A dishpan full!"
Mix all ingredients except cheese.
Pour into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Sprinkle cheese on top and bake until melted.
Cut first 7
ingredients
into bite size pieces.
Place meat and vegetables layered
in	a roaster or flat in a casserole with lid.
Mix remaining ingredients together.
Pour over vegetables and meat.
Cover.
Bake
at 250° for 4 hours undisturbed.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Place in bottom of greased, glass baking dish (13 x 9-inch).
Arrange cooked chicken on top.
Mix together soup, mayonnaise, curry powder and lemon juice.
Pour mixture over chicken and broccoli. Top with shredded cheese, bread crumbs and paprika.
Bake 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Stir yeast, salt and sugar into flour.
Heat milk until hot to touch.
Add milk and oil to dry ingredients, beating until well blended, for about 5 minutes.
Then with a spoon, add as much flour as needed.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth. Place into a greased or oiled bowl and cover with a towel.
Let rise until double.
Punch down and turn out onto a floured surface. Roll out; cut with a biscuit cutter.
Put into oiled pan and let rise until double.
Cook at 400° until brown.
Cook chicken until tender.
Debone chicken and reserve 1 quart of chicken broth.
Cook spaghetti in chicken broth until tender, do not drain.
Saute bell pepper and onion in margarine.
Add to spaghetti.
Add other ingredients including chicken and cheese (cut cheese into small pieces).
Pour into 1 large or 2 small casserole dishes.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
This dish freezes well.

Cream margarine and confectioners sugar. Add vanilla, lime juice and zest of limes. Combine flour, cornstarch and salt. Mix into butter mixture. Roll batter onto wax paper. Refrigerate. Slice and bake 12 to 15 minutes at 350°. Coat with confectioners sugar.
Put fat in skillet. Add onions and tomatoes. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and sugar. Add okra and cover; simmer until okra is tender, about 5 minutes. Stir all together. Serve hot.
Put all ingredients in casserole and bake, covered, at 300° for 3 hours.
One hour prior to finish, add the potatoes (cut in halves).
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Frying Dip And Coating For Seafood
d: *For tenderizer trick add a 7 ounce can of beer to the dip.
Blend cheese and milk.
Stir in dried beef, onion and pepper. Mix well.
Add sour cream.
Spoon into 8-inch pie plate.
Sprinkle walnuts over top and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Serve with crackers as a dip.
Combine milk and pudding mix and blend 1 minute.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Fold in 2 cups of Cool Whip.
Add about 1 1/2 cups of strawberries.
In bowl combine sugar and cinnamon.
Butter both sides of tortillas.
Sprinkle one side with the sugar/cinnamon mixture.
Put in 350° oven, sugar/cinnamon side up, only about 2 minutes until bubbly.
Take out of oven and let stand 3 to 4 minutes.
Fill shells with sugar side out.
Top each with Cool Whip and add sliced strawberries.
Lightly spray 8 x 8 pan; place apple in pan and sprinkle with lemon juice and water.
Combine remaining ingredients and cover apples.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until apples are done and brown.
Beat eggs; add sugars, peanut butter, oleo, soda and vanilla. Mix well.
Stir in remaining ingredients; mix thoroughly.
Drop dough on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Spinach should be thawed and drained.
Margarine should be melted.
Mix ingredients together, except Ritz.
Place in casserole dish.
Top ingredients with crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Place blintzes (partially defrost) in baking dish.
Blend remaining ingredients and pour over blintzes.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes (mixture should be set).
Serves 6 to 8.

recipes.t: Red Cabbage - German Style(Sweet And Sour)
d: Cut cabbage in half and slice thin.
Place in a large kettle of boiling water for 10 minutes.
Drain.
Put cabbage back in pot and add all other ingredients.
Pour the boiling water on last. Bring all to a boil and simmer for 2 to 3 hours.
Be sure to use a close-fitting lid.
Cream the cream cheese, sugar and vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add drained pineapple, then add cherries and nuts; mix well.
Pour into crust.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix in 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Peel strip around center of each potato.
Cook potatoes in boiling water.
Drain.
Halve any large potatoes.
In bowl, combine cooked potatoes, lettuce, curly endive, eggs, radishes and green onion.
Mix all dry ingredients together; add eggs and butter.
Add milk.
Put in well-greased dish and bake at 350° until thick, about an hour.
Melt margarine and mix with graham cracker crumbs.
(Before mixing together, set aside 1/4 cup of crumbs.) Press in a 10 x 13-inch pan.
Mix egg and milk; dip steak in and then in flour.
Brown lightly in shortening.
Add onions and green peppers to meat in shortening.
Add water and soup; simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook squash in a little water and salt.
Drain and mix with soup, onion and carrot.
Grease a 9 x 12-inch casserole dish and put in all ingredients.
Put 1/2 package of stuffing over top and bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Prepare potatoes according to package directions.
Heat sour cream but do not boil.
Add mustard, salt and sugar.
Stir to blend and add to hot potatoes.
Stir in onion.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serves 4.
Mix cake according to directions, with the exception of using milk instead of water.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Bring to a boil the pineapple and sugar.
When cake is done, punch holes in it and pour pineapple mixture over cake.
Let set long enough to cool.
Mix pudding according to package directions with the exception of leaving out 1 cup of milk.
Mix softened cream cheese and pudding with mixer.
Spread over top of pineapple mixture on cake.
Slice bananas over cake.
Sprinkle with coconut, pecans and cherries.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add strawberry soda pop and cool completely.
Mix cake according to package directions (do not use cake mix with pudding in it).
Bake in 13 1/2 x 9 1/2 x 2 inch greased and floured pan.
Let cool completely.
After cake is cooled, using potato peeler, poke lots of holes all the way to the bottom.
Pour gelatin and soda pop mixture over cake.
Cover entire top of cake with thick sliced bananas.
Heat beans and water to boiling; reduce heat.
Boil uncovered for 2 minutes; remove from heat.
Cover and let stand 1 hour, or cover beans with water and let soak overnight.
Drain and add 10 cups fresh water.
Add salt meat to beans and water.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer about 2 hours or until beans are tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and simmer 1 hour.
Makes 12 servings; contains 1 gram fat per serving.
Line a Pyrex pie pan or round Corning Ware dish with large size tortilla round.
Pour in a can of peaches, cherries, plums or blackberries, sweeten to taste.
Tear the second tortilla round into pieces and stick down into fruit.
Pat generously with butter.
Cut strips from another tortilla and lay on top. Sprinkle with sugar and again pat generously with margarine.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat
oven
to
Saute
onion rings in 1/4 cup butter.
Combine
remaining
butter
with
cracker
crumbs. Reserve 1/4
of
crumb mixture for topping and layer remaining crumbs into
bottom
of greased 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Spread sauteed onion rings over crumb layer and sprinkle with cheese, salt and paprika.
Combine eggs and milk and pour over layers. Top with reserved crumb mixture and bake 35 to 40 minutes.
In a 2-quart microwave-safe casserole, crumble meat.
Add the green pepper.
Cook in microwave, covered, on High for 2 to 3 minutes until no pink remains in meat, stirring once or twice. Drain off the fat.
Stir in nacho cheese soup, milk, corn, chopped tomato and minced onion.
Cook, covered, on High for 7 to 10 minutes or until chowder is heated through, stirring once.
Makes 3 main dish servings.
Serve with corn chips.
Soak gelatine in cold water 5 minutes.
Beat egg yolks with 1/4 cup sugar.
Add pineapple, lemon juice and salt.
Cook on low heat until consistency of custard.
Add softened gelatine, stir and cool.
Beat egg whites until white and foamy.
Add remaining sugar gradually and continue beating until glossy and holds soft peaks. When mixture begins to thicken, fold in egg whites.
Beat whipping cream and fold in.
Pour into baked pie crust and refrigerate.
Cook all ingredients, except pecans and vanilla, to soft ball stage (240°).
Cake:
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour two 13 x 9 x 2-inch pans.
Prepare cake as directed on package.
Divide evenly in pans.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a shallow 2-quart baking dish. Stir together soup, chicken and vegetables in dish.
Combine flour, milk and butter.
Stir until smooth.
Pour over mixture in dish.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until brown.
Mix ingredients and pour into pie shell.
Bake until center is firm.
Mix all ingredients together and roll out on floured board. Cut out and bake at 350° until light brown on greased cookie sheet, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 14 biscuits.

recipes.t: Willie'S Homemade Boiled Chicken And Rice
d: Boil chicken thighs for 1 hour and 45 minutes.
Stir in 2 cups rice.
Cook, covered, for 20 minutes longer.
Ready to serve.
Add cut-up margarine to flour.
Make well in flour; add egg yolks and sugar that's been mixed together.
Mix with fingers; sprinkle with 2 tablespoons cold water.
Continue to work with fingers.
Make into a ball, wrap in wax paper and refrigerate until chilled.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Take dough out and divide into 2 balls; refrigerate one.
Roll part of dough to about 1/8-inch thickness on slightly floured surface.
Cut into 2 1/2-inch rounds.
Put rounds on slightly greased cookie sheet.
In center of each, put 1/2 teaspoon of apricot preserves and pinch around edge or use fork.
Brush top with mixture of egg and milk. Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes or until lightly brown. Remove from rack.
Cool.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Mix sugar, butter, milk, vanilla and nuts.
Roll into balls and chill.
Drop in melted candy coating.
Spoon onto wax paper.
Cook in 2-quart pan, stirring constantly, over medium heat until mixture comes to a full boil.
Boil and stir 5 minutes. Take off heat; stir in 6 ounces chips, vanilla and nuts.
Pour in greased pan.
Blend well with spoon the oleo, cream cheese and sour cream. Gradually add sugar, continuing to beat until light.
Add egg yolks (slightly beaten with vanilla).
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour sifted with baking powder and salt and mix
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, baking soda and salt.
In a blender, grind 1/2 cup blanched almonds to a fine powder, add to flour mixture.
Cream the sugar, shortening, almond extract, egg and water and add to dry mixture.
Mix thoroughly.
Form into 1-inch balls and place on an ungreased cookie sheet 2 inches apart. Press one of the remaining almonds into the center of each ball while flattening it slightly with fingers.
Brush cookie with beaten egg.
Bake 20 minutes or until light brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream sugars, margarine and shortening. Beat in egg and vanilla.
Gradually add flour, soda, cream of tartar and salt mixture.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts (optional).
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until firm to touch.

Cook macaroni according to package directions and drain. Cut margarine and Velveeta into small pieces. Place in pan, still warm from cooking macaroni, and pour warm macaroni over cheese and margarine. Cheese and margarine should melt quickly. Then add 1/2 cup milk. Mix well. Place mixture in a casserole dish and place slices of American cheese on top. Bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes.
Combine 10 caramel candies; cut each into 4 pieces.
Add 1/3 cup flour.
Add 3 cups (cut into 1/2-inch cubes) Jonathan or Rome apples, 2/3 cup caramel ice cream topping and 2 teaspoons lemon juice.
Mix well.
Bake at 375° on a preheated baking sheet for 40 to 45 minutes.
Store at room temperature.
Grate cheese.
Mix all ingredients.
Roll and pinch off marble size. Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes (do not overbake).
In a 1 1/2-quart casserole, combine gravy and poultry seasoning.
Stir in chicken and frozen vegetables.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes, or until mixture begins to bubble.
Mix all ingredients.
Place in casserole dish.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
In a skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Saute onions until tender.
Stir in potatoes, soup and milk.
Add cheese, green pepper, pimento and 1/2 cup of the cracker crumbs.
Pour in shallow casserole dish.
Top with remaining cracker crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Sort and wash beans.
Combine beans and water in large Dutch oven; bring to a boil.
Cover; reduce heat to medium and cook 40 minutes.
Add next 8 ingredients; cover.
Reduce heat and simmer 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Mash most of beans against side of Dutch oven with back of a spoon; stir well.
Cover and bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-high and cook, uncovered an additional hour or until desired degree of doneness, stirring occasionally. Discard bay leaves.
Serve over hot cooked rice.
Pierce hole in broccoli package and cook 3 minutes in microwave oven.
In a mixing bowl, mix soup, sour cream, lemon juice, garlic powder and soy sauce.
Set aside.
Put rice and broccoli in greased 2-quart casserole dish and add half of the soup mixture.
Add chicken and remaining soup mixture. Top with Parmesan cheese and bread crumbs. Cover with plastic wrap. Cook 8 minutes. Turn dish 1/2 turn and cook 6 to 8 minutes. Serves 6.
Mix together.
Add extra flour if needed.
Roll out; cut into shapes.
Bake for 7 minutes.
Cook rack of ribs in Dutch oven or regular 350° oven for about 2 1/2 to 3 hours or until done.
In a bowl, mix together remaining ingredients.
Pour sauce over ribs and bake, uncovered, until brown, about 20 minutes.
Keep basting ribs with sauce.
Mix together first six ingredients.
Stir in enough cold water for thick batter.
Mix in onion and drop by teaspoons into deep fat.
Flatten patties slightly as you turn them.
Fry to a golden brown.
Beat eggs well.
Add other ingredients.
Stir until well blended.
Pour into unbaked crust.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Salt and pepper chops; brown well in skillet, then put in baking dish.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over chops. Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 1 1/2 hours, or until tender.
Turn chops after an hour.
Have a barbecued taste.
Bake in baking dish covered with foil at 350° for 25 minutes.

Preheat oven to 425°. Sprinkle bacon over bottom of pastry shell. Combine eggs, cream, salt, nutmeg and cayenne pepper in a bowl and beat until thoroughly mixed. Sprinkle cheese over bacon and ladle egg mixture over top. Bake 15 minutes at 425°, lower the heat to 350° and bake another 30 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin and salt in hot water.
Break up cranberry sauce with fork.
Add the gelatin mixture; chill until thickened. Fold in apples and nuts.
Saute celery, bell pepper and onion in margarine.
Combine with tomatoes and steam on low fire.
Mix in soup.
Cook rice according to directions.
Mix rice with tomato-soup mixture.
Add grated cheese and crawfish.
Bake at 350° about 40 minutes or until bubbling.
Don't stir.
Enjoy with salad and French bread. Serves 8.
Brown and cook the ground beef.
Add the salad dressing, spaghetti sauce, and cooked macaroni.
Heat on medium heat.
Top with grated Cheddar cheese.
Serves 4 to 6.
Spread beans on serving platter. Mix sour cream with taco seasoning and spread over beans. Cover with shredded cheese and sprinkle with remaining ingredients.
Put pineapple in 2-quart casserole dish.
Mix flour, sugar and cheese and cover pineapple.
Cover this with cracker crumbs. Drizzle margarine over crumbs.
Bake at 350° until bubbly, approximately 20 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
You will need 2 regular size muffin pans.
Cut steak in strips.
Mix garlic, soy sauce, salt and 1/4 cup water.
Add steak.
Marinate steaks 1 hour (longer if possible) tossing occasionally.
Drain steak.
Save the marinade.
Cut cheese in small pieces or grate and allow to come to room temperature.
In mixing bowl, beat cheese and mayonnaise until smooth and creamy.
Add onion, Worcestershire sauce, paprika and parsley.
Continue to beat until thoroughly blended.
Shape into 2 balls.
Roll in nuts.
May garnish with olives, cherries or parsley.
Freezes well.
Cream margarine and sugar together.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Stir into margarine mixture with milk. Beat until smooth.
Pour into greased baking dish.
On top of the batter, place peach slices close together.
Pour about 1/4 cup of peach juice over the peaches and batter.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°. Serve with milk or ice cream.
Combine broccoli, corn and egg in a bowl; mix well.
Place in a casserole.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 15 minutes longer or until cheese is melted.
Fry bacon until crisp; drain and crumble. Line 2 large baking sheets with foil.
Mix together and store in closed container in refrigerator. Delicious with vegetables.

Preheat oven to 325°. Combine cranberry sauce, dressing and soup mix in small mixing bowl and mix well. Spread half the cranberry mixture over bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Arrange chicken in single layer over prepared layer. Top with remaining cranberry mixture. Bake 30 to 45 minutes until chicken is cooked through. Serve over rice. Yield: 8 servings.
Mix all of the ingredients and divide into 4 separate containers and freeze.
When serving, add 1 quart of 7-up to each container.

In a 13 x 9-inch pan, bake cake mix according to box direction. While slightly warm, poke holes in cake with a wooden spoon handle and press down flatten cake. Pour crushed pineapple, including juice and spread evenly. Prepare pudding according to box directions, but subtract 1 cup milk. Pour and spread evenly over pineapple. Top with Cool Whip and walnuts. Refrigerate 1 hour prior to serving.

Preheat oven to 350°. Saute squash and onions with the margarine until tender. Drain. Add eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Spoon into a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish and top with cheese and crackers. Bake for 20 minutes.
Line bottom of baking dish with 6 slices of Armour dried beef. Top with boneless chicken breasts.

recipes.t: Polly'S Sour Cream Banana Nut Bread
d: Mix first 6 ingredients in bowl, mixing well after each ingredient is added.
In another bowl, sift together salt, soda, baking powder and flour.
Add alternately with sour cream to first 6 ingredients.
Fold in nuts.
Bake in two large loaf pans at 350° for 1 hour.
Saute ground beef with onion in oil in skillet until ground beef is browned, stirring frequently.
Add mushrooms and spinach, mixing well.
Stir in eggs gradually.
Cook until eggs are set, stirring constantly.
Season with salt and pepper.
Yields 6 servings.
Pour pie filling into 8 x 8 x 2-inch square pan.
Mix remaining ingredients with a fork.
Sprinkle over fruit.
Bake at 400° for about 20 minutes or until light brown.
Boil chicken, including heart, gizzard and liver for about 45 minutes.
Use enough water to just float the chicken.
Remove pan from heat.
Take chicken out and let it cool.
Save the pot of water.
When chicken is cool, pick the meat off the bones (don't start too early or you will invent words the dog won't stay around to hear).
Put chicken meat back into the pot of water.
Add the complete soup starter, the vegetables for seasoning and the sliced carrots.
Add any leftover veggies found in the fridge.
Cover pot and simmer at least 2 hours.
Serve with cornbread.
It will fix what ails you!
Fry onions, bacon and mushrooms together, turning frequently until bacon is sufficiently cooked (not crispy).
In a separate frypan, heat vegetable oil on medium-high temperature for 2 to 3 minutes.
Season sliced potatoes with paprika, pepper and salt as listed in large bowl.
Reduce temperature to low-medium; add sliced potatoes slowly to hot oil; turn potatoes frequently.
Fry until light brown color is achieved.
Combine all ingredients in one frypan and cook an extra 10 to 15 minutes and serve.

Cook chicken in seasoned water until tender; reserve broth. Debone. Cook potatoes, celery and carrots in broth until tender. Reserve 3 cups broth. Melt butter and flour; stir a few minutes. Add milk, 3 cups chicken broth, salt and pepper. Mix everything together, including peas. Pour in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish. Shape crusts to fit and put them on top; make a few slits. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Cook the rice following the instructions on the package. This should take about 20 minutes.
Pour the rice into a large bowl to let it cool.
Scramble the eggs in a small pan over medium heat.
chop scrambled chunks of egg into small pea-sized bits with your spatula while cooking.
When the rice is cooled, add the peas, carrots, eggs and onion to the bowl. Carefully toss all of the ingredients together. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium/high heat.
When the butter has completely melted, dump the rice mixture into the pan and add the soy sauce plus a dash of salt and pepper.
Cook the rice mixture for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often.
In a large skillet on medium heat brown pork in oil for 5 minutes.
Remove; keep warm.
In the drippings saute onion and mushrooms until tender, stir in water, mustard and salt; bring to boil.
Return chops to pan; reduce heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until chops are tender.
Remove and keep warm.
Combine flour and sour cream until smooth; add to skillet.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir 1-2 minutes or until thicken.
Serve pork chops and mushroom sauce with noodles.
In a bowl, mix sugar, butter, anise seed, liqueur, bourbon, almonds and eggs.
Beat to blend. Stir together flour and baking powder. Add to butter mixture and blend thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate dough until firm, 2 to 3 hours.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle rice on bottom.
Layer chicken, skin side up on rice.
Sprinkle onion soup mix over chicken.
Mix water with both cans of soup and heat, then pour over chicken.
Cover with foil and bake 2 hours at 325° to 350°.
Fry bacon until crispy.
Remove from skillet and set aside. Into bacon drippings stir, vinegar, water, sugar, salt, onion and egg.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Add lettuce to skillet and toss with hot dressing quickly.
Remove to bowl.
Crumble bacon on top.
Mix flour, baking soda and salt in medium bowl; set aside.
Make potatoes for 2 servings, as label directs, using liquid, omitting butter and seasoning.
Measure 1 cup.
In large bowl, sprinkle yeast over water; stir until dissolved.
Stir in sugar and salt until dissolved.
Add 1 cup potatoes, butter and 3 1/2 cups flour.
With electric mixer at medium speed, beat until smooth, 2 minutes.
Gradually add 4 cups flour, mixing with hands until smooth and stiff enough to leave bowl.
Add remaining 1/4 cup flour, if needed.
Turn out onto lightly floured board.
Knead until smooth, electric, small blisters appear on surface, 10 minutes.
Place in greased large bowl; turn over.
Cover with towel.
Let rise in warm place (85°), until double, 1 hour.
Turn out dough onto lightly floured pastry cloth or board.
Divide in half.
Roll out one-half into a 16 x 8-inch rectangle; roll up from one end.
Press ends even, pinch to seal and tuck under loaf. Place, seam side down, in greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Brush surface lightly with some of the melted butter.
Repeat with other half of dough.
Let loaves rise in warm place, until tops are rounded, 1 hour.
Set oven rack at lowest level.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes or until deep golden brown and loaves sound hollow when tapped.
If crust becomes too brown, cover with brown paper.
Turn out onto wire racks, brush tops with remaining butter.
Cool.
Makes 2 loaves.
Line cookie sheet with sides with foil.
Arrange separated crackers on foil, side by side.
Sprinkle nuts over top of graham crackers.
Bring butter and brown sugar to a boil in small saucepan and pour over crackers evenly.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes in a 350° oven until bubbly.
Remove from oven and let set a couple of minutes.
Cut apart with knife while still warm and cool on wax paper.
Makes about 3 dozen 1 1/2 x 3-inch cookies.
Make and brown small meatballs and drain well.
In large stock pot put chicken broth, soup bone and cleaned giblets on medium flame approximately 1 hour.
Remove soup one, skim off and add vegetables.
After another hour, reduce flame.
Add parsley, meatballs and noodles after 10 to 15 minutes, should be ready.
Mix sugar and water until sugar is dissolved.
Mix remainder and stir well.
Chill.
Just before serving, add 1/2 gallon pineapple sherbet.
Makes 60 (1/2 cup) servings.
Good for wedding and other receptions.
Stir onion, cabbage and celery in water.
Simmer until tender. Add rest of the ingredients and simmer.
Serve the next day. (One pound of ground turkey may be added.)
Beat egg whites at high speed with an electric mixer until stiff peak forms.
Set aside.
Beat butter and shortening until creamy; gradually add sugar beating well.
Add egg yolks, 1 at a time, beating until blended after each addition.
Combine flour, cocoa and baking soda; add to butter mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Beat at low speed until blended after each addition.
Stir in coconut, chopped pecans and vanilla.
Fold in egg whites.
Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 8 inch cake pans.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes our clean. Cool in pans 10 minutes.
Remove cake layers to wire rack and cool completely.
Use wooden spoon to stir up ingredients which are placed into a pot.
Cook until tender.
Combine all and add dressing as much as desired.
There may be too much dressing for this recipe.
Refrigerate overnight.
Combine flour, baking powder and 1 teaspoon of salt; cut in 1/3 cup butter with pastry blender until mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle cold milk (1 tablespoon at a time) evenly over surface.
Stir with a fork until dry ingredients are moistened.
Shape into a ball. Chill.
Drop marshmallows in boiling water, dissolve well.
Add jello and cool.
Add pineapple to cheese and mix well, then add to cooled gelatin mixture.
Add whipped cream and nuts, pour into large pan, 8 x 14-inch, chill well and serve.
May use a large jello mold.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add quick cooking oatmeal to desired consistency.
Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Place in freezer to harden.
(This can be rolled into waxed paper and sliced after hardening.)
Blend together all ingredients except oil.
Turning blender on low speed, add oil very slowly in a steady stream.
Stir in a few extra seeds.
Chill until ready to serve.
Soak beans overnight.
Cook in chicken broth until soft.
Chop onion, celery, cabbage and garlic.
Cook in small amount of oil until soft.
Add to beans.
Add ham, salt and pepper to taste. Cook on low for 30 minutes.
Chill marinated artichokes and shrimp.
Drain and quarter artichokes and combine with shrimp.
Beat together the olive and vegetable oils, vinegar, mustard, chives, scallions, salt and pepper.
Pour over the shrimp and artichokes.
Refrigerate several hours.
Serve with toothpicks.
Crush Oreo cookies in food processor.
Set aside.

dissolve gelatin in boiling water.	Combine cold water

Dip chicken into eggs then into bread crumbs and arrange in a 9
by 13 inch baking dish.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes. Take out and pour pasta sauce over chicken and top with cheese.
Bake 10 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink.
Crush enough corn chips to make 1/3 cup.
Mix ground beef, chips and seasoning mix.
Shape into 6 patties.
Set oven to broil. Broil patties 5 minutes; turn and broil for 3 minutes more. Crisscross cheese strips on each patty and sprinkle with paprika. Broil until cheese is puffed and golden.
Cook veggies and drain well.
Add chicken, oleo, cheese, soup, salt and pepper.
Bake 40 minutes at 350° (also good with ham instead of chicken and cream of mushroom soup instead of cream of chicken).
Melt butter or oleo in jelly roll pan.
Sprinkle on graham cracker crumbs, nuts, chocolate chips, butterscotch chips and coconut.
Pour evenly over top, Eagle Brand milk.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until coconut is brown.
Layer refried beans mixed with taco mix.
Layer sour cream with carton of avocado dip.
Layer grated Cheddar cheese.
Layer green onions and black olives.
Refrigerate until chilled.
Serve with taco chips.
Spread rice on bottom of oblong dish.
Dissolve bouillon in water and pour over rice.
Place pork chops on rice.
Pour mushroom soup and water over chops.
Sprinkle onion soup over all. Cover with foil and bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Chicken can be substituted for chops.
Cook first 6 ingredients for 5 minutes.
Stir in Rice Krispies. Roll in balls.
Then roll balls in mixture of coconut and confectioners sugar.
Makes about 24 balls.
Saute onion in butter, add milk and bring to boil.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Bake in greased 9 x 13-inch dish.
Save 1/2 cup cheese to sprinkle on top and bake 30 minutes more.
Cut in squares to serve.
Good with ham and cole slaw.
May be refrigerated overnight before baking.
Beat egg yolks, salt and 1/2 cup sugar.
Add pineapple syrup and lemon juice.
Cook in double boiler, stirring constantly, until thick.
Add pineapple.
Cool.
In skillet, brown beef.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place ground beef in bottom of glass dish, then pour soup over beef.
Place Tater Tots on top of meat and soup.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until Tater Tots are brown.
Mix together and bake 20 minutes at 375°.
Inexpensive and very good for tuna.
Mix and drop from spoon on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350°. Garnish with pecan halves, if desired.
Combine all ingredients.
Bake at 425° for 45 minutes.
Makes 2 pies.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Sift baking powder and flour together.
Add to sugar mixture with milk.
Fold in egg whites, vanilla and lemon flavoring.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/4 hours.
Saute onions in butter.
Add broccoli and cook until soft. Mix with remaining ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook over low heat first 4 ingredients for 10 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 1/2 cups Rice Crispies.
Add rest of Rice Crispies if needed.
Prepare aluminum foil with part of coconut; spread over to put mixture on adding more coconut as needed.
Cream butter, shortening and both sugars.
Add eggs and beat well.
Blend in flour and soda; mix in vanilla.
Roll in small balls.
Sprinkle with sugar and place on greased cookie sheet. Flatten with glass or refrigerate until firm (overnight) and roll out and cut with cutters.
Color may be added.
Best when soft (before refrigerating).
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.

recipes.t: Artichoke, Potato And Bacon Salad With Fennel Flowers
d: Wash and cook potatoes just until tender.
Cut onion lengthways into quarters and cut thinly crosswise.
Soak in cold water.
Cut peppers into strips, 1/4 x 1-inch long.
Cut artichokes in half.
Slice artichokes crosswise in 1/4-inch slices.
You will need freezer paper and string.

recipes.t: Hot Chicken, Shrimp Or Crab Salad
d: Combine all ingredients except cheese and potato chips; put in casserole.
Combine cheese and potato chips and sprinkle on top. Bake at 350 degrees until hot, 25 to 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Prepare herb stuffing as directed on package.
Set aside. Melt 3 tablespoons butter. Add onion and saute until glassy.
Add soup and cheese, stirring until heated through and cheese is melted. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add the cooked carrots. Turn into greased casserole (2-quart). Cover with stuffing mix.
Drizzle 1/3 cup melted butter over top.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until hot and bubbly. Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients.
If bacon drippings are cold, melt them first.
Pour into ungreased dish.
Bake at 350 for 45 to 60 minutes.
In a bowl, beat eggs and sugar until light and fluffy.
In a double boiler, melt chocolate and butter over hot water.
Add egg mixture to the chocolate mixture.
Combine flour, baking powder and nuts in a bowl.
Add to chocolate batter and stir until smooth.
Put in a greased 8-inch square pan.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes.
Let cool and then cut into squares.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a medium bowl combine 1 1/2 cups flour and 1/2 cup confectioners sugar.
Cut in margarine until crumbly.
Press into bottom of lightly greased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Bake 15 minutes.
Meanwhile in a large bowl combine eggs, granulated sugar, baking powder, ReaLemon and remaining 3 tablespoons flour.
Mix well.
Pour over baked crust for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cool.
Cut into bars.
Sprinkle with additional confectioners sugar.
Store, covered, in refrigerator.
Butter an 8 inch square pan with 2 tsp. butter, set aside. Combine powdered sugar and dry milk, set aside.
In a heavy saucepan combine 1/2 cup butter, sugar and corn syrup; cook and stir until it comes to a boil and sugar is dissolved.
Stir in powdered sugar, about 1/3 at a time until blended.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla.
Continue stirring until mixture thickens and mounds slightly when dropped from a spoon.
Spread into prepared pan.
Cool.
Cut candy into four strips.
Cut each strip in half.
Shape each strip into a log shape.
Wrap in waxed paper, twist the ends.
Freeze or refrigerate until firm.
In heavy saucepan or microwave melt caramels with milk.
Stir often. Roll logs in caramel mixture then in pecans.
Wrap in waxed paper. Store at room temperature in airtight containers.
Cut into slices with serrated knife.
Heat oven to 400°.
Spray 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan with no-stick cooking spray.
Dip chicken in margarine and coat with combined remaining ingredients.
Place in prepared pan.
Bake 20-25 minutes or until tender.
Makes 6 servings.
Heat strawberries, sugar and Jell-O just enough to dissolve Jell-O; stirring constantly.
Let cool.
Mix pudding with milk as stated on package.
Add sour cream to pudding.
Fold in 3/4 of Cool Whip.
Layer cake, pudding mix and strawberries in a large dish, repeating until all is used.
Top with remaining Cool Whip. Refrigerate for several hours.
Mix well.
Pour into ice cream freezer can.
Freeze until firm.
Heat butter and oil in a large heavy skillet.
Add the sliced potatoes; turn them to coat thoroughly in the butter and oil, then cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Turn potatoes often so they cook evenly.
Carefully add 1 cup boiling water to the potatoes in the pan.
Add the scallions, sage, parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Boil, uncovered, for 10 minutes, until water evaporates.
If potatoes aren't done, add 1/3 cup boiling water and cook 5 minutes more.
Serve at once.
Serves 4; 315 calories per serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients, except cheese and chips. Put in a 13 x 9 casserole dish and top with cheese and chips. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix syrup, salt, vinegar, salt and pepper and butter in 2 quart pan.
Stir constantly; bring to a boil over medium heat until mixture reaches the hard crack stage 290°.
Add soda and mix well. Pour foamy mixture over corn.
Cut deer up into small pieces; boil for about 1 hour and a half on medium-high.
Dice onion, potatoes and carrots; add to boiled meat after half hour cooking.
Add all other ingredients and continue cooking for the other hour.
Serves 3 to 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In 13 x 9-inch baking pan, melt butter in oven.
Sprinkle crumbs over butter, then pour condensed milk evenly over crumbs.
Top with remaining ingredients; press down firmly.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool.
Cut into bars.
Store loosely.
Mix together dressing, vinegar and sugar.
Pour over other ingredients.
Recipe can easily be doubled.
Combine the first 3 ingredients. Set aside 3/4 cup.
Press remaining crumb mixture into an ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish. Set aside.
Combine condensed milk and orange juice concentrate. Fold in whipped topping and oranges.
Spoon mixture over crust and sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture. Cover and freeze until firm. Makes 12 servings.
Mix together and chill.
Saute onion and garlic in small amount of oil until golden brown.
Stir in tomatoes and paste; simmer 30 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in oregano and simmer 30 minutes more.
Mix eggs and salt.
Dip eggplant in eggs; then in bread crumbs.
Fry in oil; drain on paper towels.
Mix cheeses together.
Pour 1 cup mixture in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Top with 1/3 eggplant and 1/3 cheeses.
Repeat until used up.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients.
Store in tightly sealed container. Use 2 to 3 heaping teaspoonfuls per cup of hot water.
Mix and roll into two rolls.
Wrap in Saran Wrap and refrigerate 24 hours.
Remove from wrap and place on broiler pan; cook at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.

Brown sausage, ground beef, onion and pepper in large skillet. Drain off excess grease. Put mixture in a large pot; add chili powder, salt and pepper. Stir in tomatoes and beans. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to simmer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Split rolls in half and brush with mixture of butter, poppy seed, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Layer ham and cheese and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Great for parties.
Mix all ingredients, except pecans.
Chill, then roll into ball.
Roll ball in chopped pecans.
Layer lettuce, onion, peas and eggs. Sprinkle with bacon.
Ice top with mayonnaise.
Sprinkle top with shredded cheese.
Spray a 1 1/2-quart casserole with cooking spray.
Combine all ingredients and pour into casserole.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes at 350°.
Saute butter and onion until tender.
Blend in flour. Gradually add chicken broth and cook until it thickens slightly. Stir in wild rice and salt.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Blend in half and half and sherry.
Heat to serving temperature.
Add meat and carrots at this time, if desired.
Mushrooms, water chestnuts or chopped bacon may also be added at this time.
Top with sliced almonds, if desired.
Serves 4.
Combine crumbs and margarine.
Press onto bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
This makes a very large salad.
Combine all ingredients except eggplant, bitter-melon and okra.
Bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer, covered, until beef is tender.
Add eggplant, bitter-melon and okra; cook for 15 minutes.
If using canned bitter-melon, add last 3 minutes of cooking.
Wash fish and place in pan.
Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with lemon pepper seasoning.
Cover.
Broil for 10 minutes, then turn catfish and repeat process, cooking for another 10 minutes or until fish flakes apart.
Cut cabbage in small pieces.
Add 2 cans mixed vegetables (Veg-All).
Add 2 cans chicken broth.
Add 1 large can whole tomatoes.
Add large can tomato juice.
Salt to taste.
You can add green beans, peas, carrots or any canned vegetables.

Prepare cake mix; let cool. Crush Butterfingers; set aside. Melt margarine in saucepan. Mix in sugar and mix well. Remove from heat. Stir in Cool Whip and mix well. Pinch 1/2 of cooled cake into punch bowl or trifle dish. Pour 1/2 of Cool Whip mixture over cake. Sprinkle layer with 1/2 crushed Butterfingers. Repeat layers and chill.
Combine all ingredients and heat.
Serve with egg rolls.
Blend well. Makes 2 (8-ounce) servings.
In a
large kettle, cook potatoes, carrots and celery in water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain, reserving liquid, and setting vegetables aside.
In the same kettle, saute onion in butter until soft.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper; gradually add milk, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Gently stir in cooked vegetables.
Add one cup or more of reserved cooking liquid until soup is desired consistency.
Yield:
8 to 10 servings.
Coat cutlets with mixture of flour, salt and pepper.
Brown in butter and remove as cooked.
Sprinkle 3 tablespoons flour into pan drippings.
(You may have to add more butter to drippings.) Stir in wine, tomato sauce, chicken broth, lemon juice and salt and pepper to taste.
Cook over low heat until sauce thickens.
Skin and bone chicken breasts lengthwise.
Cut chicken into 1-inch pieces; set aside.
Steam potatoes over steamer until sticky and not quite done, still hard.
Include garlic, onion and herbs in steamer.
Turn frequently.
For serving 4, you may want to steam a batch of potatoes, set aside and steam the other half with herbs.
Place Cool Whip in bowl and add lemon juice; mix.
Stir in jello and sugar.
Mix well.
May add more sugar, if needed, for personal taste.

Brown meat and onions. Add your soups, milk, enchilada sauce and chopped green peppers to meat and simmer for about 10 minutes. In a greased (Pam spray) pan, add ingredients as below: Layer of meat mixture, layer of crumbled Doritos and layer of grated cheese, repeating layers until all material is used. Bake at 350° in oven for about 30 minutes or until cheese is melted. All or parts of the casserole can be frozen.
Combine applesauce, oil, egg and sugar substitute.
Combine remaining ingredients and add them to applesauce mixture.
Pour into a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until it tests done.
Mix dates, butter, sugar and boiling water and add remaining ingredients.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until done.
Combine sugar and egg.
Sift together baking powder and flour, then add to sugar mixture.
Toss together nuts and apple, then add to batter.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Mix soup, 3/4 cup cheese, onions and ham together thoroughly.
Now fold in broccoli.
In separate bowl, melt butter and mix in cracker crumbs.
Mix well.
Take half of crust mixture and spread over bottom of baking dish.
Pour in soup mixture.
Take remaining crust and smooth over top.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Bake between 375° to 425° for approximately 30 minutes.
Mix well and put in greased baking dish.
Bake in oven at 325° for 1 hour.
Squeeze excess liquid from spinach.
Place all ingredients in blender-blend till combined.
Butter a souffle dish or 1 1/2 qt. baking dish.
Sprinkle with 1 to 2 parmesan cheese - pour mixture in and bake at 375 degrees for 50 minutes or until puffed and golden.
Sprinkle salt and pepper on all sides of short ribs and put into Dutch oven or a 3-quart covered casserole dish.
In a small saucepan, combine the tomato soup with the molasses, vinegar, liquid smoke and minced onion; bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour over short ribs; cover and bake in a 275° oven for 3 to 4 hours, or until very tender.
Just before serving, spoon off any excess fat.
(If you prepare this dish ahead, refrigerate it and then lift off the solidified fat before you reheat it.)
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Cook all ingredients in skillet for 3 minutes except beans; add beans.
Put in crock-pot and cook until ready or simmer for 25 to 30 minutes atop stove.

recipes.t: Cumber Kimshi(Variation Of Traditional Korean Cabbage Kimshi)
d: Slice cucumbers very thinly and wilt with salt.
Squeeze out water.
Add spices.
This keeps in the refrigerator for weeks.
It gets hotter the longer it sets.
Mix ingredients in order given.
Bake in 8 x 12-inch pan at 350°.
Batter will be thick, depending on how juicy the apples are. If too thick to spread, add 1 or 2 tablespoons water.
No other liquid is necessary.
Make cream sauce of butter, flour, salt, pepper, broth and milk.
This will be thin.
Add chicken and drained peas and carrots.
Put in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Make pie crust; roll thin and cut out like biscuits. Place on top of chicken mixture. Bake at 425° for 30 minutes.
Combine all 7 ingredients and mix well (Jell-O pudding mix last).
Bake 60 minutes at 350°.

Place bread evenly into a lightly greased 11 x 7 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish. Set aside. Stir garlic powder into quiche filling. Pour over bread. Bake at 400° for 20 minutes. Top with pepper rings and bake 5 additional minutes. Let casserole stand 5 minutes before serving.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix all ingredients together into pan and bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Recipe may be doubled to serve 16.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar, cornstarch, salt and ginger.
Add orange juice.
Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Stir in butter and pour over hot carrots.
Stir to coat.
In a skillet cook sausage until well done, drain.
Separate crescent rolls into 8-inch triangles.
Place dough in 12-inch pizza pan, with points toward center.
Press over bottom and sides to form crust.
Spoon sausage over crust. Sprinkle with potatoes.
Top with Cheddar cheese.
In a bowl, stir eggs, milk and 1/8 teaspoon pepper.
Carefully pour over mixture in crust. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake at 375° for about 25 minutes or until set.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix shortening, sugar and eggs together thoroughly.
Sift flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt together.
Mix together.

Combine flour, salt, pepper and paprika. Coat chicken with flour mixture. Melt margarine in heavy skillet. Brown chicken on both sides. Remove from heat. Brown remaining flour mixture in margarine until golden brown, stirring constantly. Slowly stir in water to make gravy. Return chicken to skillet and add onions. Cover and cook on low heat until done, about 25 or 30 minutes.
Mix sugar, vinegar and oil.
Pour over vegetables.
Cover and place in refrigerator.
This salad will keep for weeks and improves with age.
Soak bread crumbs in condensed milk to which the extract and coloring have been added.
Add nuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Top each with a nut half; bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together by hand.
Decorate top with cherries and crushed cashews
Combine chips and milk and microwave for 2 1/2 minutes.
Stir and microwave 2 1/2 minutes more.
Add vanilla and pecans.
Pour into greased glass pan and refrigerate.
Mix sugar, cocoa and flour.
Add eggs and milk, a little at a time, mixing well.
Cook on medium heat, stirring until thick. Add butter and vanilla.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Combine potatoes and 1/4 cup butter, onions, soup, sour cream and cheese.
Place in a buttered casserole.
Mix remaining butter and crushed corn flakes and sprinkle over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Mix together and press into the bottom of a 10 x 13-inch dish the graham cracker crumbs, 1 stick of butter and sugar.

Slice beans in thin slivers. Cook 5 minutes. Cool. Cut onions in thin slices. Add beans along with mixture of salad oil, lemon juice, salt, sugar, pepper and paprika. Chill in refrigerator several hours to develop flavor. Serve as salad or relish.

Make graham cracker crust in 9 x 9-inch dish by combining melted margarine and 2 tablespoons sugar. Refrigerate for 30 minutes, until set. Combine microwaved/soft cream cheese and powdered sugar; mix. Add 1/2 tub Cool Whip; mix. Place next to crust. Cover with chocolate pudding. Finish top off with whipped cream. Chill.
Combine all ingredients.
Fold in whipped cream.
Chill several hours.
Makes 1 1/3 cups.
Brown chopped onions, garlic and salt.
Add drained tomatoes (puncture tomato in strainer to get out most of juice).
Add drained chile peppers.
Cook until all moisture is absorbed, approximately 45 minutes over low heat, stirring occasionally. Add cheese.
Stir constantly until melted.
Serve warm with Dorito chips.
Can be cut in half for small gathering.
In a large saucepan, combine the first 8 ingredients. Cook over medium heat until hot and bubbly.

Place in an 8 x 12-inch ungreased baking dish. Place the refrigerated dinner rolls over hot chicken mixture. Combine the cheese and melted margarine. Spread cheese mixture on rolls. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Cut shortening into dry ingredients.
Very gradually add egg/water mixture while gently mixing with fork.
Don't overwork dough.
Beat egg whites, sugar and vanilla together until stiff.
Add coconut and cornflakes.
Mix until blended.
Drop onto buttered cookie sheet by teaspoons.
Bake at 250° until lightly brown.
Sauce:
Melt margarine in a saucepan.
Stir in flour until well blended.
Slowly stir in 2 cups milk.
When sauce is smooth and hot, reduce heat and stir in cheese.
Season with salt, pepper, Dijon mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Process vegetables in food processor until well chopped.
Mix all with turkey.
Form into burger and bake.
Brown chicken. Remove from skillet and blend soups and paprika.
Add chicken and vegetables.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes or until chicken and vegetables are tender. Serve over rice or noodles.
Layer hamburger, carrots, onions and potatoes in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Pour tomato soup over this and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Set out 1/2 gallon ice cream to soften.
Roll crackers fine. Melt oleo and combine with crumbs, except a handful saved out for on top.
Pat mixture on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat together pudding and milk.
Fold into the ice cream.
Pour over crumb crust.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with crumbs. Set in refrigerator for 8 hours.
Cut in squares.
Fast and easy.
Chop meat and onions (greens only) and mix with cream cheese, soup and sour cream.
Serve with Ritz or Club crackers or with party rye bread.
Place chicken thighs in shallow casserole.
Mix soup with 1/4 cup of water and pour over chicken.
Cover with thin cheese slices, then place Stove Top stuffing on top.
Bake at 325° to 350° for
1 hour.
Freezes beautifully.
Nice served with asparagus or Chinese pea pods.
Serves 8 to 12.
Drain pineapple, reserving 2 tablespoons juice.
Combine brown sugar and butter in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Arrange pineapple slices in pan, cutting slices, if necessary.
Place a cherry half, cut side up, in center of each slice.
Sprinkle with reserved juice and then nuts.
Combine cake mix, Dream Whip, right from envelope, eggs and water in large mixer bowl.
Blend, then beat at medium speed for 4 minutes.
Carefully spoon over mixture in pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes or until top springs back when lightly pressed.
Let stand in pan for 10 minutes and then invert onto serving plate.
Let stand 1 minute, then remove pan.
Serve warm or cold.
May also be topped with Cool Whip.
Empty caramels in saucepan with 1/3 cup of milk.
Melt, stirring constantly.
