Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake at 350 degrees for 35-40 minutes.
In a small bowl with fork or wire whisk, mix mayo, anchovy fillets, Parmesan cheese, lemon juice and black pepper.
Sprinkle chicken quarters on both sides with salt and pepper. Melt butter in small saucepan; add lemon juice, tarragon, chervil and vermouth; brush part over chicken.
Place chicken, skin side down, on rack of broiler.
Broil 6 inches from heat for 20 minutes, basting frequently.
Turn; broil 15 to 20 minutes longer or until nicely browned, brushing with remaining lemon-butter.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook each separately until done. Season with salt. Drain well.
In small saucepan, combine margarine, sugar and water until sugar has dissolved.
Add chocolate chips till partially melted. Remove from heat and stir until chips are totally dissolved and mixture is smooth.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Mix cake mix as directed.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Put pecans in bottom of cake pan; spread cake mix over pecans.
Melt stick of margarine; mix with cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Pour over cake mix.
Bake at 300° for about 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Bake 30-40 minutes at 350 degrees.
Serve with whipped topping or vanilla ice cream.
Wash and scrub each potato; dry with a paper towel.
Cut each potato into eight wedges; arrange peel side down in a shallow baking pan.
Mix the rest of the ingredients and brush over potatoes.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until potatoes are golden and tender.
Brush occasionally with mixture.
Add enough water to reserved vegetable liquid to measure 1 1/2 cups.
Pour into 2-quart saucepan.
Heat to boiling.
Stir in peas, rice, butter, salt and carrot.
Heat to boiling. Remove from heat.
Cover and let stand until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, about 10 minutes.
You will need an iron frying
pan.

recipes.t: Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookie Dessert
d: Mix pudding and 2 cups of milk until smooth.
Add chocolate Cool Whip; set aside.
Crumble 1 box of thin mints in bottom of an 8 x 8-inch dish.
Pour in half of the pudding mixture.
Top with vanilla Cool Whip.
Continue to layer, saving 1/4 cup of cookie crumbs for top.
I use a Tupperware container so I have the cover to store in the refrigerator overnight.
Heat oven to 350°.
Cook and stir onion in margarine in large skillet until tender.
Stir in chicken, 1/4 cup picante sauce and cream cheese; cook until thoroughly heated.
Stir in 1 cup cheese.

Combine potatoes, onions and water in a 2-quart microwave-safe dish. Cook, covered, on full power, 10 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Stir one time. Lightly mash potatoes. Stir in flour. Add milk, salt and pepper. Cover and cook on full power 5 minutes longer, stirring every minute or until soup boils and is thickened.
Mix all together and beat well.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cut steak into bite size pieces; place in bowl.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Place in refrigerator for 2 hours.
Brown flour with butter; gradually add beef consomme soup.
Add mustard, sour cream and catsup.
Bring to a boil.
Set sauce to one side.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Blend in vegetable oil.
Add enough milk to make a stiff dough.
Thinly roll out dough (1/4-inch thick) on a lightly floured board into two 10 x 18-inch rectangles.
Spread on sausage; roll up lengthwise.
Chill well and slice 1/4-inch thick.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake yellow cake mix in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Combine crushed pineapple and its juice and 1 cup sugar.
Bring to boil for 5 minutes.
Punch holes in cake and pour pineapple mixture over cake.
Let cool.
Prepare vanilla instant pudding.
Pour over cool cake.
Slice 3 bananas and layer over pudding.
Spread with 8 once carton Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with nuts and coconut.
Keep in refrigerator.
Cut chicken as for frying, place with seasonings in a large kettle with enough cold water to cover.
Bring slowly to a boil, simmer until meat comes off bones.
Remove bones, cut chicken in fairly large 1/2-inch pieces.
Return to pot; add onions, potatoes and butter beans.
Cook until done; add tomatoes and corn, cut from cob.
Cook slowly for 25 to 30 minutes.
Melt margarine and add sugar.
Stir and let cool.
Add eggs (one by one), flour and vanilla.
Stir.
Add peanuts and chocolate chips.
Stir again.
Pour mix in greased rectangular pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Fill a 9 x 9-inch or 9 x 13-inch pan full of apple slices. (Spray pan with vegetable spray first).
Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of cinnamon and sugar.
Mix flour, honey and salt together.
Add milk gradually.
Add beaten eggs and butter.
Beat for 2 minutes.
Add blueberries, sprinkled with flour.
Layer ingredients in order.

recipes.t: Ms. Carly'S Broccoli And Chicken Casserole
d: Spread cooked broccoli in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Add chicken, salt and pepper lightly.
Mix soup, mayonnaise and lemon juice and pour over chicken.
Top with corn flakes and dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Prepare jello using pineapple juice for cold water.
After thickened, add other ingredients.
Combine French dressing, mayonnaise, salt and pepper to make dressing.
Bake cake according to package directions in 3 layers.
In the bottom of the punch bowl, put the strawberry pie filling.
Add a layer of cake.
Mix pudding according to package directions and add drained pineapple.
Spread on top of cake layer, then add second cake layer.
Top this layer with cherry pie filling and add third layer of cake.
Mix second box of pudding as directed and add 3 bananas, sliced.
Spread on top of third cake layer.
Top with Cool Whip.
Garnish with pecans and cherries.
Dissolve yeast in warm water in large warm bowl.
Add sugar, salt, margarine and 2 1/2 cups flour; beat until smooth.
Stir in enough more flour to make soft dough.
Knead 6 to 8 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; turn to grease top.
Cover; let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes.
Punch dough down; divide in half.
Roll half to 14 x 10-inch, spread half dressing down center third of dough length.
Layer with half the beef, cheese and sauerkraut. Make cuts from filling to dough edges along sides of filling, 1 inch apart.
Alternating sides, fold strips at an angle across filling; place on greased baking sheet.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Cover; let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes.
Brush with egg, sprinkle with caraway seed.
Bake at 400° about 25 minutes.
Serve warm.
Refrigerate leftovers; reheat to serve. Makes 2 loaves.
Cream together sugar, butter or margarine and eggs; mix well. Sift flour and then measure out three cups; add soda and salt and sift again.
Add flour mixture to butter mixture a little at a time letting your batter blend well between each addition.
Add in bananas and nuts and mix well.
Pour into well greased tube or Bundt pan and bake at 300° for 1 hour or until toothpick inserted in middle comes out clean.
Layer ingredients in order in a 13 x 9-inch dish, except Ritz crackers and melted oleo.
Roll Ritz crackers to crumbs; toss with stick of melted butter.
Top with crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° until bubbly and brown on top (20 to 30 minutes).

Heat oil in a large skillet on medium-high heat. Add sausage; cook and stir until lightly browned. Add chicken, onion, pepper, celery and garlic; cook and stir until chicken is cooked through. Stir in tomatoes, okra, tomato sauce and seasoning. Bring to boil. Stir in rice; cover. Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Stir.
Mix all ingredients together.
Shake well.
Serve over spinach salad.
Put in small cake pan in layers:
Bean dip, guacamole (avocados mixed with the mayonnaise), sour cream mixed with taco seasoning, shredded cheese, tomatoes, olives, onions and shredded cheese. Serve with chips.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add egg and mix well.
Add all ingredients and blend well.
Drop with teaspoon on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
* Do not add water.
Thaw pastry.
Mix ground beef, salt, pepper and onion; bind with egg yolks.
Wash and quarter mushrooms.
Cover the bottom of an 8-inch loose bottomed cake pan with the bacon.
Arrange the cheese, herbs and mushroom quarters on top.
Cover the meat mixture, pressing it down firmly and smoothly on the top.
Melt cheese and milk.
Add mustard and vinegar.
Put in container and refrigerate.
Mix all together with hands and shape into a ring. Put strawberry jam or green pepper jam in center and serve with crackers of your choice.
Microwave meat first, or else put in crock-pot and cook until half done.
Add barley and mushrooms, fill pot to within 1 inch of top with stock or water.
Cook 3 to 4 hours until barley is done. Season to taste.
Combine ingredients.
Spread on cake while hot.
Brown under broiler until coconut is brown.
Combine sugar and flour.
Add butter.
Place on floured board; pat to thickness of 1/2-inch.
Cut into shapes desired.
Bake in a moderate oven (325° to 350°) for 25 minutes.
Cream the butter and both sugars.
Add eggs and vanilla; mix together with the flour, oatmeal, salt, baking powder and soda. Add chocolate chips, Hershey Bar and nuts.
Roll into balls and place two inches apart on a cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes at 375°. makes 55-60 cookies.
Put flour, salt and pepper in a bag.
Put pork chops in and shake until flour covers chops.
Put Crisco in frying pan.
One at a time, put chops in pan.
Cook on medium heat until done.
Drain blueberries and pineapple (save juice).
Mix Jell-O with package directions (hot water only).
Add juice from berries and pineapple.
Let jell.
Add pineapple and blueberries to Jell-O. Mix remaining ingredients together.
Top chilled Jell-O mixture and chill.
Mix dry ingredients together and cut in shortening. Store in an airtight container.
Take the amount that you think you need and add egg and water.
Bake until golden brown.
*Add more bread crumbs to taste.
Put oleo, cocoa and buttermilk in saucepan.
Heat over low heat, do not boil; remove and stir in sugar, pecans and vanilla. Beat, then spread while cake is still hot and serve.
Wonderful!
Save 1 cup Mozzarella cheese for topping.
Melt chocolate chips in double boiler; add beaten egg yolk and cool.
Add beaten egg whites, sugar and nuts.
Fold in whipped cream.
Put broken pieces of cake in bottom of pan.
Pour cool mixture over the pieces of cake.
Refrigerate until serving time.
Cook eggs; remove shells and cut each in half lengthwise. Remove yolks.
Mix yolks with rest of ingredients.
Fill each half white of egg with mixture.
Place potatoes in a 1 1/2-quart dish.
Add remaining ingredients and stir to coat potatoes.
Cover tightly with microwave plastic wrap.
Cook on High for 10 minutes in a 600 to 700 watt oven or 15 minutes in a 400 to 500 watt oven, shaking dish to redistribute potatoes.
Potatoes are done when the tip of a small knife easily pierces the potato in the center.
Serves 4 as a side dish.
Combine 1 1/2 cups flour with the sugar, salt and undissolved yeast.
Combine milk, water and margarine in a saucepan.
Warm over low heat to 115° to 120°.
(Margarine does not have to be melted.)
Remove from heat and gradually add flour mixture.
Beat 2 minutes at medium speed, scraping sides of bowl occasionally. Add 1/2 cup flour.
Beat on high for 2 minutes.
Stir in additional flour to form soft dough.
Turn out onto lightly floured board.
Knead 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in greased bowl.
Turn over and grease top.
Let rise 15 minutes. Turn out on a floured board.
Divide dough in half and shape into rolls.
Cover and let rest in a warm place for 15 minutes.
Bake at 425° for 12 minutes or until done.
Mix all ingredients together; pour into a pie shell.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes, or until golden brown and not runny.
Combine boiling water and cornmeal.
Combine 1 1/2 cups unbleached flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour, cereal, sesame seed, salt and yeast; blend well.
Heat milk, oil, molasses and honey until very warm.
Add warm liquid, cornmeal mixture and yogurt to flour mixture.
Blend well.
Stir in rest of whole wheat flour until stiff dough forms.
Knead in 1 to 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour about 8 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; cover loosely with plastic wrap and cloth towel.
Let rise in warm place until light and doubled in size, 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Melt chocolate very slowly in double boiler; add rest of ingredients.
Spread on wax paper; chill.
Break into pieces.
Mix in order.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Bake in a 350° oven. Frost with powdered sugar frosting, flavored with coffee.
Combine mayonnaise, vinegar and sugar to make dressing.
Set aside.
Combine shrimp, carrots, onions and peppers; set aside.
Mix well soup, vinegar, salad oil, sugar and mustard.
Pour over shrimp and vegetables.
Mix lightly.
Refrigerate overnight. Before serving, add cucumber slices.
(You can also add orange or apple slices, dew melon cubes, etc.).
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Potatoes And Tomatoes With Fresh Coconut
d: Peel potatoes, then dice into 3/4-inch pieces and put into bowl of cold water.
Heat oil in heavy 3-quart pot over medium-high flame.
When hot, add finely chopped garlic.
Stir about 5 seconds before adding red pepper and cumin seed.
Stir for another 3 seconds.
Garlic should brown lightly, red pepper should darken and cumin seed should sizzle.
Lower heat to medium.
Add grated coconut and stir for 10 to 15 seconds.

Cream butter and sugar; sift baking powder and flour together and add to butter mixture, alternating with egg yolks. Add lemon extract, fruits and nuts; add stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake at 275° for 2 hours.
Mix all together and freeze.
Stir eggs into pumpkin.
Blend salt, sugar and spices.
Stir into pumpkin.
Add milk and mix well.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan layer chicken.
Melt margarine and add flour until smooth, add sour cream until it just bubbles.
Add soup, chilies and onion salt.
Blend well, pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Add cheese and bake until melted.
Serve over rice.
Brown meat and onion in a large skillet on medium-high heat. Drain.
Stir in water, catsup and mustard; season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice; cover.
Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with fork.
Top with cheese; cover. Let stand until cheese melts.
Makes 4.
Cook, peel and slice fresh beets in a bowl and set aside.

Mix sugar and cornstarch until blended before adding the vinegar. Stir all ingredients together and cook at hard boiling point for 1 to 2 minutes or until clear and slightly thickened. Add butter and pour this sauce over the beets.
Serve warm.
May be reheated, but do not boil.
If there is extra sauce, it may be used later if stored in refrigerator.
A small family would not use 3 cups of beets at one meal.
Soak
beans
in
broth.
Cook down with garlic that has been minced.
Add
onions,
celery
and carrots, all chopped. Add eggplant, peeled and chopped, and olive oil.
Season with herbs. Cook on very low burner until done.
Mix squash, nutmeg, cinnamon and sugar.
Mix thoroughly.
Add eggs and milk.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until done.
(May need to cover edges of pie with foil to prevent overbrowning.)
Mix all ingredients and chill.
Prepare chicken by removing bones and steaming good size pieces (good idea to buy breasts and thighs).
Dip in tempura batter and fry in hot deep oil.
Slice each piece in 1/2-inch to 1-inch slices.
Arrange on a bed of shredded lettuce.
Cover with sauce.
Blend sour cream and dry mustard; set aside.
Slice cucumber and place in shallow dish.
Pour sour cream mix over all.
Chill. Serve cold.
Cook all except vinegar and salt.
Simmer 4 to 5 hours.
Add vinegar and salt when beans are tender (last).
Cook spinach according to directions on package and drain. Combine ingredients; mix well.
Chill.
Serve with assorted vegetable dippers.
Makes 3 cups.
You will also need sticks.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well. Pour mixture into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 325° until golden brown, about 1 hour.
Cut
squid
into
rings or 3-inch pieces.
If tentacles are large,
cut
in half.
Toss the squid in flour mixed with salt and
pepper;
coat
as
you
are
frying, to avoid flour getting soggy.
In a skillet, heat enough oil to measure about 1
to
inches
deep.
When
the oil is hot, add squid. Lower
heat just
a
little
and
continue to fry squid until nicely
golden. Drain on paper towels.
The squid should cook in
to 3 minutes. Place fried squid on platter and garnish with lemon wedges. Makes 2 servings.
In a large saucepan, mix together the corn syrup and sugar and heat slowly until it boils, stirring often.
Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter until it melts.
Then stir in Rice Krispies. Pour mixture into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
When cool, melt chips and spread on top.
Mix together soy sauce, sugar, ginger and garlic powder.
Add meat strips and marinate overnight in refrigerator.
Cook on barbecue grill on bamboo sticks after draining.
Combine the first five ingredients in a bowl and beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth.
If you use a food processor, use the knife blade.
Drain the can of chiles.
Gently stir in the last three ingredients.
Chill well.
If you wish, garnish with chile strip.
Set out at room temperature before serving, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Cook over medium heat until mixture is dissolved.
Cook over high heat for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove from heat and add desired flavoring or cinnamon oil.
Add food coloring if desired.
Pour into cookie sheet; allow to cool completely.
Crack candy and roll into powdered sugar.
Store in airtight container.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pour into a glass pie plate.
Needs no crust.
Bake at 325° until browns on top.
Cook sweet potatoes in boiling water until fork easily pierces potatoes.
Cool slightly. Remove skins. Place cooked and peeled potatoes into a large mixing bowl.
Mix with electric mixer until smooth. There should be 3 1/2 cups of mashed sweet potatoes. Stir in butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Mix in spices, salt and evaporated milk.
Pour into unbaked pie crusts.
Bake in a 425° oven for 20 minutes.
Lower heat to 325° and bake 30 to 45 minutes longer or until knife inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool before serving.
Butter square Corning baking dish. Put bread in dish.
Mix scalding milk, butter, salt and sugar.
Add eggs, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg, stir over bread.
Set baking dish in some water in Pyrex pie plate.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix in dishpan in order given.
Drop by large tablespoon or ice cream scoop and flatten.
Place 6 to a cookie sheet.
Recipe does not call for flour.
Bake for 12 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Makes 77 large cookies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a bowl, combine oil, eggs, water and pumpkin.
Mix well.
In another bowl, sift together flour, salt, baking soda, nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
Gradually add dry mixture to liquids and mix well.
If you wish, stir in 1/2 cup nuts and/or raisins.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake for about 1 hour or until it springs back when lightly touched and sides of the loaf have pulled away from the pan.
Mix like pie crust.
Add egg yolk and yeast mixture.
Divide into 2 parts and roll out on cookie sheet.
Top with cream cheese mixture.
Top with other crust.
Bake at 350°.
Bring all ingredients, except macaroni, to a boil.
Add macaroni and simmer until tender.
Serves lots.
In saucepan, blend sugar, cornstarch and salt.
Add milk. Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly.
Cook and stir 2 minutes more.
Remove from heat.
Stir small amount of hot mixture into yolks or beaten egg.
Return to hot mixture; cook and stir 2 minutes more.
Remove from heat; blend in butter, vanilla, lemon juice and lemon peel.
Pour into sherbet dishes; chill.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
I add 2 red peppers or 1 fresh jalapeno.
Combine cranberries and pineapple.
Mix powdered sugar and sour cream together.
Stir into fruit.
Pour into shallow dish and freeze until firm.
Remove from freezer and let sit a few minutes before serving.
Mix flour and margarine like pie crust, add nuts and press into bottom of a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes; cool.
Cream together the cream cheese and powdered sugar; fold in 1 c. Cool Whip then spread over crust.
Mix the pudding mix using only 3 c. milk, and beat until stiff; spread over the cream cheese mixture.
Top with the remaining Cool Whip and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
Chill well before serving.
Peel carrots and cut into strips.
Cook until just tender; drain.
Add butter, sugar, vinegar and mint or dill.
Cook until transparent.
Serve hot or as a cold relish.
Cut steak in crosswise strips 1-inch wide.
Mix water and vinegar with ketchup and other seasonings; pour over meat.
Let stand several hours, turning meat occasionally.
Lift meat from liquid, saving vinegar mixture.
Place meat in pan, top with sliced onions and add 1/2 of the vinegar mixture.
Cover, simmer gently over low heat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, adding vinegar mixture as required to keep liquid about 1/2-inch deep in pan.
Remove meat and onions to hot platter; strain liquid, then boil hard 3 to 4 minutes, pour over meat and serve while hot.
This should be made just before serving.
Rub the bottom of a small bowl with onion or garlic.
Put in 1/2 teaspoon of salt, a dash of Tabasco sauce and a tablespoon of cold water (to dissolve salt).
Stir until salt is completely dissolved.
Now gradually add, stirring constantly, 6 tablespoons of oil and 1 teaspoon of vinegar or lemon juice.
Beat quickly until well mixed.
Mix butter, flour and chopped pecans.
Press in a casserole dish.
Bake for 15 minutes at 350°.
Mix the cream cheese, sugar and Cool Whip.
Spread on crust.
Add pie filling.
Eat!

Sift flour; add baking soda and salt. Sift again. Combine with brown sugar. Add melted shortening to beaten eggs and combine with dry ingredients. Add nuts and dates. Pour into greased 7 x 11 x 2-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut in bars while hot. Sprinkle or roll in powdered sugar.
1. Have all ingredients measured and ready.
Line a baking sheet with waxed paper or foil; set aside.
Dissolve gelatine in cold water, set aside.
Add pineapple and sugar together in pot on stove.
Bring to a boil.
Add the gelatine mixture to the pineapple mixture.
Stir until gelatine is dissolved.
Add lemon and cherry juice, let cool.
Mash cream cheese and chopped cherries.
Add to pineapple mixture.
Chill to slightly thickened.
Add Cool Whip.
Top with chopped walnuts and cherries, if desired.
Mix with mixer in large bowl.
Beat oil and sugar together.
Add eggs and banana.
Beat well. Add sifted dry ingredients, milk and vanilla.
Mix well and stir in nuts.
Pour into a 9 x 5 x 3-inch pan.
Bake in a 350° preheated oven for 1 hour.
Cool well and store overnight before cutting. Makes 1 loaf.
Place potatoes	in
a
medium bowl.
Cover with boiling water. Let
stand
for
8 minutes or until water is absorbed. Heat skillet
and add bacon.
Cook and stir until bacon begins to crisp.
Add
the
onion
and
mushrooms.
Stir until barely tender.
Add
parsley,
sprinkling	it
evenly
over the bacon mixture and
potatoes.
Toss together lightly.
Adjust heat to low.
In a small mixing bowl, beat eggs with 1/4 cup of water. Add the
salt
and
pepper.
Pour
over vegetables in skillet. Sprinkle with cheese.
Cook
over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes or until eggs are set.
Cover skillet for part of cooking time to help eggs
set on top.
If desired, brown under broiler for 2 to 3 minutes.
Put water and bouillon cubes in pot; boil until cubes are melted.
Add chopped broccoli, onion and celery (celery is a must).
Let boil until soft.
Melt butter and add flour.
Heat half and half in microwave, then add it to broccoli mixture.
Add butter and flour mixture.
Let simmer until it thickens.
Add parsley and dash of black pepper.
No salt is needed.
Combine oats and sour milk. Let stand.
Combine all dry ingredients.
Add egg and melted butter to oat mixture and mix well.
Add dry ingredients and stir only until moistened.
Fold in huckleberries.
Fill muffin cups 3/4 full.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.

Boil potatoes in skins. Peel and slice thin. Cook bacon until crisp, then cook onion in bacon fat. Mix in flour, sugar, salt and pepper. Stir water in gradually. Add vinegar gradually. Cook and stir until it boils for 1 minute. Pour over potatoes. Add the bacon. Cover and let stand until ready to serve.
Add sugar to oil.
Add eggs and pumpkin.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Then add water.
Place in greased and floured pan. Add nuts, if desired.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 2 loaves.
Cream oleo and sugar. Mix 3 beaten eggs. Mix pineapple and 1 tsp. vanilla. Pour in unbaked pie shells. Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
Beat 1 cup sugar and margarine until fluffy.
Mix in egg whites.
Stir in combined flour, oats and baking soda.
On wax paper, press into 16 x 12-inch rectangle.
Spread combined pumpkin, 1/2 cup sugar and spice over dough to 1/2 inch from edge. From narrow end, roll up dough.
Sprinkle sesame seed around roll, pressing gently.
Wrap in wax paper; freeze overnight or until firm.
Combine ingredients in a jar with tightly fitted top. Shake well and refrigerate. Shake well before use.
Cut off tops of green peppers; remove seed.
Cook peppers 5 minutes in boiling water to cover (salt added).
Drain and set aside.
Combine next 7 ingredients.
Mix well.
Fill peppers with meat mixture.
Place in a 2-quart shallow casserole.
Pour tomato sauce over and around the peppers.
Bake at 375° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Grease 2-quart casserole.
Layer sliced zucchini, sliced tomatoes, mushrooms and cheese.
Repeat to fill dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake, uncovered, for 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Cream the cream cheese and nuts; set aside.
Drain juice from cherries and pineapple; bring juice to a boil.
Pour over jello to dissolve.
Let cool; add Coke.
Combine all ingredients and refrigerate.
Combine first 5 ingredients in bowl; mix well.
Cut rolls in half.
Spread sauce over bottom half of roll.
Sprinkle with ham and cheese.
Cover with top half of roll.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
May be frozen and reheated.
Combine tomatoes, celery, salad dressing, green pepper and onion; toss lightly.
Chill.
Add bacon; toss lightly.
Spoon vegetable mixture over shredded lettuce.
Garnish with additional cherry tomato halves and bacon curls.

Cook chicken until tender; allow to cool and cut into bite size pieces. Saute onion and green chilies in butter. Mix soup, milk and Velveeta cheese in large pan; heat until cheese melts. Add onions and green peppers. Stir until well combined. Add chicken and mix well. In a large baking dish, place a layer of tortillas, a layer of chicken mixture and a layer of grated cheese. Repeat layers until dish is filled. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.

Fry chopped meat and drain. Add tomatoes. Saute eggplant in olive oil, then add to meat mixture. Grate cheese. Set aside. Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with crescent rolls. Spread meat mixture on dough. Top with cheese and season to taste.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes or until crust is golden.
Combine cucumbers and onions.
Mix remaining ingredients and then pour over cucumbers and onions.
Stir gently to mix. Refrigerate overnight.
Heat oven to 400°.
Lightly grease pie plate (10 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch).
Beat remaining ingredients after you sprinkle turkey, mushrooms, onions, salt and cheese in pie plate.
Pour into pie plate.
Bake until golden brown and knife inserted halfway between center and edge comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Refrigerate any remaining pie.
Cook chicken; save broth.
Remove chicken from bone and cut in chunks.
Saute chicken and mushrooms in butter or oleo. Add the chicken broth
and	green
beans
and
bring this to a boil.
Stir in Minute
rice, then remove from heat.
Cover for a few minutes before serving.
Pour pie filling into greased baking dish.
Sprinkle top with cinnamon sugar; put dry cake mix on top.
Put pats of margarine on top.
Bake in 350 degree oven for 25 minutes or until top is brown and bubbly.
(Any flavor pie filling may be used.)
Cream butter and sugar; add egg.
Beat 2 to 3 minutes; add nuts and poppy seed.
Beat 1 minute.
Stir in flour and salt. Refrigerate until dough is easily shaped into rolls.
Make 2 rolls.
Roll in sugar; wrap in waxed paper and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.
Cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Bake on ungreased pan at 325° for 20 minutes or until slightly brown.
Store in closed tin.
Heat oil in large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry garlic and onion 2 minutes.
Add broccoli, zucchini and mushrooms.
Stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Add water chestnuts and tomatoes; heat through.
Add Molly McButter; stir until melted in.
Sprinkle with sesame seed, basil and pepper to taste.
Makes 4 (2 cup) servings.

recipes.t: Grilled Salmon Fillets(Easy; See Marinade Variations)
d: Make a marinade by mixing 2 tablespoons oil, ginger, cumin, coriander, salt and cayenne together in large shallow bowl. Add fish and marinate in the refrigerator for no more than 30 minutes. Meanwhile, build a single-level fire. Set grill rack in place. Cover grill with lid and
let rack heat up, about 5 minutes. Rub cooking grate with oil-dipped wad of paper towels.
Make yellow cake according to directions, except substitute double strength coffee for water called for.
Bake in two round layers.
When layers are cool, split them in half.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon whiskey on each cut, except for rounded top.
Spread Cool Whip on each cut surface and top.
Stack layers.
Refrigerate 8 hours (24 is better).
Gently stir together all ingredients in a small bowl until blended.
Put beef, soups, onion, salt and pepper into a large pot. Simmer slowly for several hours.
When the meat is tender, add sour cream and mushroom pieces.
Bring to a boil and immediately serve over hot rice or noodles.
Sprinkle 2 cups cranberries into buttered 10-inch pie plate. Combine 1/2 cup sugar and walnuts.
Sprinkle over berries.
Cook the first 3 ingredients together until thick; let cool. Mix Dream Whip; add to cooled jello-pudding mixture, along with drained pineapple and oranges.
Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine tomatoes and bread crumbs in a large bowl; let stand until liquid is absorbed.
Lightly mix in ground beef, egg, mustard, salt and pepper.
Divide mixture into quarters, then shape into a 5-inch loaf; make a ridge down middle of each with your finger.
Place loaves on a rack in a shallow baking pan.
Bake 30 minutes.
Spoon cheese into hollows.
Bake 10 minutes longer or until cheese melts and loaves are crusty brown. Yields 4 servings.
Heat water to boiling in 3-quart saucepan.
Break block of noodles; reserve seasoning packet.
Stir noodles, chicken, bok choy and carrot into water.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in seasoning packet.
Preheat oven to 250°.
In large roasting pan, spread the popped corn and the dry roasted nuts.
In heavy saucepan, combine the sugar, butter and dark corn syrup.
Cook until mixture boils. Boil for 5 minutes without stirring.
Remove from heat.
Stir in the vanilla and baking soda.
Pour mixture over corn and nuts; stir to coat.
Bake, uncovered, at 250° for 1 hour.
Stir occasionally.
Cool; break apart.
Store in covered container.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Cook chicken and broccoli.
Layer in baking dish. Pour mixture over chicken and broccoli.
Top with bread crumbs and small pats of butter.
Bake at 400° until top is brown and bubbly.
Bring all ingredients to room temperature.
Cream the butter; add sugar and beat.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat.
Add flour and milk.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 40 minutes.
Place the peppers on a roasting tray and put in a 350° oven. Turn the peppers until cooked on all sides (about 1 hour).
When done, place the peppers in a paper bag.
Wait a few minutes and then peel and slice the peppers into strips.
Place in a bowl with fresh garlic and olive oil and let marinate.
Cook bacon; drain and crumble.
In large salad bowl, mix spinach, sprouts, water chestnuts, eggs and bacon.
In a jar, combine oil, sugar, catsup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and onion; shake well.
Sprinkle dressing on salad and toss.
Serve. Dressing refrigerates well and is good on any salad.
Cook chicken (cut into pieces) in water with 1 teaspoon salt. Strain and debone.
Use 2 cups broth to cook rice.
Saute onion and broccoli in oleo.
Mix all together and put in casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly hot.
Cook and crumble meat.
Arrange in layers in casserole dish. Bake at 350° until vegetables are tender.
Combine oat bran, brown sugar, walnuts and baking powder in bowl; mix well.
Combine milk, bananas, egg whites and oil in small bowl; mix well.
Stir into oat bran mixture just until moistened.
Fill paper-lined muffin cups 2/3 full.
Bake at 425° for 17 minutes or until brown.
Yield: 12 servings.
Cut chicken in serving pieces; set aside.
Sprinkle washed rice in bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Pour 2 cups water over rice.
Place chicken on top of rice.
Place parsnips, cut in chunks, around chicken.
Mix soup and milk.
Pour over chicken. It will look very soupy.
Bake, covered, with foil at 325° for 60 minutes.
Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Peel the potatoes (enough to fill a 13 x 9-inch casserole bowl) and slice as thin as possible.
Grate the cheese.
Brown the sausage.
Alternate the layers of each, beginning with a layer of potato slices, then sausage and then cheese.
Add the milk, salt and pepper.
Bake in preheated 350° oven.
You may have to cover with foil.
For softer potatoes you may want to boil them for a few minutes before putting them in the casserole bowl.
Combine beans, milk, soup, pepper and 1/2 can of the French fried onions.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining onions and bake 5 minutes longer.
Place chicken, sliced onion, 2 teaspoons salt and celery in a pot.
Cover with water.
Cook until tender.
Bone and cut chicken into pieces.
Reserve broth.
Combine soup, broth, tomatoes and 1/2 teaspoon salt in pan and heat.
Layer chicken, tortillas, cheese, chopped onion and heated sauce in a casserole dish. Repeat, ending with cheese.
Bake at 250° for 20 minutes.
Lower to 200° and bake for 40 more minutes.
May be frozen.
Mix shredded carrots with combined ingredients.
Refrigerate before serving.
Mix flour, soda, salt, cinnamon, sugar, oil, eggs and undrained pineapple.
Mix only by hand.
Add bananas and nuts and mix again.
Bake in a tube or Bundt pan that has been greased and floured.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour and 5 minutes.
Let cool in pan 1 hour before removing to serving plate.
Heat oven to 450°.
Lightly grease cookie sheet.
Mix flour, mustard and red pepper.
Cut in margarine with pastry blender until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Stir in Swiss cheese, buttermilk and egg until dough forms.
Turn dough onto well-floured board; coat with flour.
Knead lightly 10 times. Roll or pat dough 1/2-inch thick; cut with floured 2 1/2-inch biscuit cutter.
Place on cookie sheet.
Mix egg yolk and water; brush over biscuits.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden.
Serve warm.
Makes 10 biscuits.
Peel and slice potatoes into large pot.
Grate onion very fine and add to pot with celery seed, salt, margarine and water to completely cover potatoes.
Cook until tender, adding water as necessary to maintain level of broth.
Mash about half the potatoes and reduce rest to small pieces.
Cut up cheese into hot potatoes and broth.
Stir carefully until cheese has melted, then add milk.
Simmer over low heat until desired consistency.
Soak macaroons in the rum.
In a double boiler, melt chocolate with water and 6 tablespoons of sugar.
Mix well.
Remove the chocolate from heat and add the egg yolks one at a time.
Let mixture cool.
Beat egg whites, adding 1 tablespoon sugar to make them more dense.
Fold into chocolate mixture gently.
Line bottom and sides of an oiled 7 1/2 or 8-inch spring-form pan with split ladyfingers.
Add half of the chocolate and then the layer of soaked macaroons.
Add the remaining chocolate mixture.
Top with remaining ladyfingers and cool for at least 6 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Combine chicken and apple.
Sprinkle with lemon juice and toss together.
Mix celery with mayonnaise and add to chicken and apple mixture.
Toss lightly.
Chill.
Serve on lettuce or eat as is. Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Place milk, eggs, salt, pepper, cheese, butter or margarine, onion and cubed potatoes in blender container.
Blend on high speed, just until potatoes are grated.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Bake in 375° oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Put tuna in a medium mixing bowl.
Add enough Miracle Whip to make it look creamy or to your taste.
Cut up pickles and put them in (I like lots of pickles).
Stir it all up and put it on the bread or eat with crackers.
Grease large pan.
Mix all ingredients.
Cook 35 to 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients well.
Put in a large baking dish sprayed with Pam.
Cover top with crisp, crumbled bacon.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix together and cook over low fire for 1 hour or 1/2 hour.

Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease sides and bottom of a 10-inch deep-dish pie pan. In a medium mixing bowl, mix together flour, salt, baking powder and pudding mix. Mix in butter, egg and milk. Beat for 2 minutes. Pour mixture into pie pan. Arrange the peach slices on top of the pudding mixture. In a small mixing bowl, beat cream cheese until fluffy.
Add 1/2 cup sugar and 3 tablespoons reserved peach syrup. Beat for 2 minutes. Spoon mixture over peaches to within 1-inch of pan edge.
Mix cornstarch with 1/2 cup milk.
Combine chocolate, butter, remaining milk, sugar, salt and vanilla in a double boiler.
Heat to the boiling point.
Add cornstarch mixture and cook 8 minutes. Let cool and pour into a baked pie shell.
To serve, top with whipped cream.
In mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, soda, cloves and cinnamon.
Add shortening, brown sugar and buttermilk.
Mix until all flour is moistened.
Beat 2 minutes; add eggs.
Beat 2 minutes more; stir in nuts.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes. Frost with Orange Butter Frosting.
Add noodles to boiling water.
Boil according to instructions. Dice onion and saute in butter.
Add soup, milk, tuna, salt and pepper to onion.
Cook together for about 5 minutes; do not boil. Drain noodles.
Add tuna mixture to noodles and stir until combined.
Pour into casserole dish.
Sprinkle top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes until brown.
Mix vegetables and steam until tender.
Transfer to a bowl. Toss with Olive Butter.
Yields 6 servings.
Combine butter, flour and pecans.
Mix well.
Press into 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Cool completely.
Mix sugar, eggs and strawberries.
Bring to hard boil. Remove from stove and add Jello.
Cool.
Whip milk and add to mixture.
Pour into crust.
Chill.
Add a few drops of red food coloring if desired.
Mix
flour, margarine and pecans.
Press in bottom of a 9
x 13-inch
pan.
Bake
for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese,
powdered
sugar and 8-ounces Cool Whip; spread over crust.
Mix chocolate pudding and milk.
Spread over that layer. Top
with
another	8-ounces of Cool Whip and sprinkle chopped pecans on top; chill thoroughly.
Drain pineapple and oranges (use juice as a beverage). Combine pineapple, oranges, banana, grapes, marshmallows, coconut and almonds. Fold in yogurt. Chill. Serves 4 to 6 people.
Cut one pita bread in half.
Spread on ingredients (sauce, cheese, etc.).
Spray a cooking sheet with Pam.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 9 minutes.
Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions.
Drain. Steam carrots, broccoli, cauliflower and yellow squash until tender.
Drain.
To vegetables, add cream of celery soup.
Season with Italian seasoning.
In baking dish, build layers of noodles, vegetables and grated Mozzarella and Ricotta cheese.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake in 350° oven until cheese is bubbly and brown.
Brown beef and drain.
Add 1/2 cup tomato sauce and taco seasoning.
Stir.
Line bottom of 9 x 11 x 2-inch pan with 2 cups corn chips.
Crush remaining chips and set aside.
Spoon meat mixture over corn chips.
Combine remaining tomato sauce with beans and spoon over meat mixture.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese and crushed chips.
Bake 5 more minutes.
Cream butter and sugar until smooth.
Add vanilla and eggs, one at a time.
Add yogurt, mix at medium speed.
Mix in flour, salt, soda and poppy seed.
Put in muffin tins.
Bake at 400° approximately 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 14 muffins.
Place chicken in greased flat 2-quart casserole dish.
Mix soup, sour cream, broth, water chestnuts and almonds.
Heat and pour over chicken.
Top with cracker crumbs which have been tossed in oleo.
Bake at 375° until crackers are browned.
Grease baking dish.
Add crushed pineapple, pie filling, yellow cake mix and nuts in layers.
Pour melted margarine over top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix together; add water.
Makes 2 gallons.
Put croutons in a greased 8 x 12-inch pan; top with cheese. Cook sausage in skillet until brown.
Drain on paper towels. Place sausage over cheese.
Beat egg(s), add sugar and shortening and stir well.
Add soda to your sour milk, then add to other ingredients.
Add sifted flour, baking powder and salt, then add vanilla.
Finally add chips and walnuts (optional) and stir together thoroughly.
Drop on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Select fresh even cucumbers.
Wash and cut ends off.
Place dill in jar and clove of garlic.
(If you wish you can use hot peppers.)
Pack in sterilized jars.
Add 3 level teaspoons of salt in each jar.
Boil 1 quart vinegar and 3 quarts water.
Pour hot over pickles and seal.
Put in cold packer, starting with cold water.
When water comes to a boil, remove jars.
Let stand 4 weeks before eating.
Brown ground beef.
Add taco seasoning and water.
Cook 15 minutes.
Cool.
In separate bowl, chop the lettuce, onion and tomatoes.
Add ground beef.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Before serving, add cheese, dressing and crushed Fritos.
Dissolve yeast in warm water in a large bowl.
Stir in sugar, shortening, beaten egg, salt and 3 cups of the flour.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in enough flour to make dough easy to handle.
Place dough in greased bowl, then turn greased side up.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours or until ready to use.
Dough can be kept up to 4 days in refrigerator at 45° or below; keep covered.
Combine first seven ingredients.
Spoon into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with almonds. Bake at
350° for 20 minutes or until heated through.
Makes 3 cups.
Has 300 calories per 1/2 cup serving.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Cool and enjoy.
(When storing, keep cloves with beets in juice to keep flavor.
Lasts forever!)
About 1 1/2 hours before serving:
In large skillet over medium-high heat, cook bacon until light brown.
Push bacon to one side of skillet.
Mix yeast and water together. Set aside.
Mix all the rest of the ingredients together.
Combine both mixtures. Turn dough on floured board.
Knead. Spread on greased pizza pan.
Let stand 15 minutes. Spread spaghetti sauce on dough, then add cooked hamburger meat, mushrooms, cheese, onions, pepper or whatever you like. Preheat oven to 425°.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes. Eat and enjoy.
Prepare salad 1 hour before using and refrigerate.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water. Add ham and remaining ingredients. Toss well. Chill at least 4 hours before serving.
Mix cream cheese and powdered sugar and fold in Cool Whip. Mix milk and pudding.
When thick, fold into Cool Whip mixture. Put 1/2 of crumbled Oreos in bowl; layer pudding mixture and top with layer of Oreo crumbs.
Melt 1/2 cup margarine in baking dish in slow oven.
Mix potatoes, onion, cheese, sour cream and soup and place in baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix corn flakes and 1/2 cup melted margarine.
Put on top and bake 15 minutes longer.
Serves 8 to 10.
Bake cake in 9 x 13 pan according to directions on box.
When done, poke holes in cake.
While cake is baking, combine pineapple and sugar and boil for 5 minutes.
Pour over cake while hot.
Let cake cool, then prepare instant pudding according to directions on box.
Spread pudding over cake.
Spread Cool Whip over pudding.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add cheese and flour.
Place apples in a 2-quart dish.
Spread batter over apples.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes until bubbly.
Cook the roast with the dried onion soup and Italian seasoning for 12 hours in crock-pot on low.
Cool and slice or shred meat. Save drippings.
To drippings, add the remaining ingredients. Simmer until ready to serve.
Saute oil, onions and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add all ingredients to one pot and cook for 45 minutes.
Add sherry at end.
Serve with Swiss cheese.
Mix and spread on greased and floured jelly roll pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Build in bucket glass with crushed ice.
Float rum.
Garnish with red cherry and orange slice.
Top with French fried onions last 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream the butter.
Gradually add sugar, beating until mixture is light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Combine flour, soda and salt. Add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Stir lemon rind, vanilla and yogurt into batter. Pour batter into
a greased and floured 10-inch Bundt pan. (I just spray with Pam, no flour.) Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan 15 minutes; remove from pan and cool completely on a rack.
Sprinkle cake with powdered sugar, if desired.
Yields one 10-inch cake.
Mix together and set aside while preparing dressing.

Mix vegetables, water chestnuts, cream of chicken soup, onion, and mayonnaise (or sour cream) together. Place in a 9 X 13 glass baking dish. Melt butter and mix with crumbled Ritz crackers. Spread crackers over top of casserole. Bake at 350 for 25 minutes. Serves 8 to 10.
Mix jello and cold water; set for a couple minutes and add 1/4 cup boiling water until dissolved.
Add all ingredients.
Chill!
In fry pan cook chicken with olive oil.
Add diced carrots and broccoli.
Take a 9 inch pie pan and place a bottom crust.
In bowl mix soup with 1/2 c. milk.
In pie pan add your chicken, broccoli and carrots, potatoes.
Pour soup over ingredients.
Put top on pie.
Preheat over 350°.
Cook pie in oven until golden brown or approximately 1 hour.
About 1 1/4 hours before serving, prepare pie crust mix as label directs for 1 crust pie; use to line 9-inch pie plate. Preheat oven to 425°.
In medium bowl, with wire whisk or fork, mix eggs, half and half, salt and pepper until well blended. Sprinkle shredded cheese in pie crust.
Pour egg mixture over cheese.
Bake quiche 15 minutes, turn oven control to 325° and bake for 35 minutes longer or until knife inserted in center of quiche comes out clean.
Makes 6 main dish servings.
Cook bacon until crisp; drain and crumble, reserving drippings.
Set bacon aside.
Saute onion, catsup, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce and mustard in a greased 1-quart casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Yield: 4 servings.
Brush chicken with oil and coat with this coating.
Bake until done.
Cook broccoli.
Drain. Add soup, mayonnaise and nuts.
Mix well. Add eggs and onion.
Pour into greased baking dish. Sprinkle with cheese and top with crumbs. Repeat.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serves 8 to 10.
Cream butter and brown sugar.
Add eggs.
Gradually add flour, soda, allspice and milk.
Fold in candied fruit, nuts and raisins. Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet and bake approximately 15 minutes at 350°.
Makes 3 1/2 dozen.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Add salt and soda.
Stir well.
Add flour and chocolate chips.
Bake at 325° for 8 minutes.
Remove from oven when light brown.
Dehead broccoli and cauliflower.
Put in a 3-quart pot with enough water to cover vegetables.
Cover and steam until done. Drain.
Add 1 to 1-1/2 quarts of milk and 1/2 loaf of Velveeta cheese.
Cover.
Simmer 20 to 30 minutes or until cheese has melted.

Line 9-inch pie plate with 1 crust; set aside. Combine remaining ingredients. Add salt and pepper to taste. Pour filling in pie crust. Top with second crust. Seal and crimp edges. Slit top of crust to vent and bake at 375° for 45 to 60 minutes or until golden brown.
Beat eggs slightly; add sugar, syrup and butter and mix well. Add vanilla; add peanuts.
Bake at 350° for about 45 to 50 minutes or until filling is firm and brown.
Pie may be soft when shaken gently but will firm as it cools.
Bring to a boil.
Turn heat down and simmer 15 to 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
In a medium bowl, mix together flour, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
In a large bowl, using a wooden spoon or an electric mixer set on medium speed, beat together butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Stir in the apples.
Stir flour mixture into the apple mixture until the dry ingredients are just moistened.
Spoon batter into the prepared pan.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 1 hour. Transfer the pan to a wire rack to cool for 10 minutes.
Turn the cake out onto the rack to cool completely.
In a skillet, cook sausage and onion until sausage is brown and onion is tender, drain.
Stir in apples, sauerkraut, water, brown sugar and caraway seeds.
Transfer to a 2 1/2 qt. baking dish.
Cover and bake at 350 degrees for one hour.
Garnish with parsley, if desired.
Make 6 to 8 servings.
Combine sugar and syrup; mix well.
Add eggs, butter, vanilla and nuts.
Mix well and pour into uncooked pie crust.
Bake for 10 minutes at 400°.
Lower temperature to 300° and cook for 35 minutes longer.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix all ingredients, except peas and gravy, and shape into 2 loaves.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam. Place loaves in dish, lightly spray top with Pam to help brown nicely and bake at 400° for 1/2 hour.
Add gravy and bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Then add peas to gravy and steak.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Beat egg yolks, butter and sugar.
Add flour and buttermilk. Cook over low heat until thick, stirring constantly.
Add extract. Pour into baked pie shell.
Top with meringue and brown.
Pour rice
in
a large baking dish.
Add soup and mushrooms and
stir
to mix.	Place 1 stick of margarine in center of dish. Bake
in
preheated oven at 400° for approximately 1 hour.
Mix all but bread cubes and raisins.
Add bread cubes and raisins.
Pour into well oiled baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook shells according to package directions.
Pour marinara sauce into saucepan and heat.
Spoon 1 cup of sauce into bottom of a large roasting pan or 1/2 cup sauce into each of two 2-quart baking pans.
Reserve remaining sauce; keep warm.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Beat egg whites in small bowl; stir in milk, juice, oil and peel. Add to flour mixture.
Stir until moistened.
Stir in cereal. Pour into prepared pans.
Bake 1 hour.
Defrost hash browns and combine in a large bowl with melted butter, salt and pepper.
Add onion, soup, sour cream and cheese. Blend ingredients thoroughly.
Pour into buttered 3-quart casserole dish.
Mix 1/4 cup melted butter with corn flakes. Sprinkle crumbs over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Wash peas and put in 6-quart pot.
Add 6 cups water and 2 onions.
Cook on low heat for 45 minutes.
Add carrots and celery. Cook for an additional 30 minutes on low heat, continuing to be sure it remains boiling.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Store in an airtight container and keep in refrigerator.
This recipe makes 3 cups mix (equivalent of nine 10 1/2 ounce cans of condensed cream soup).
Break eggs into mixing bowl.
Add margarine, molasses, sugar, nutmeg and baking soda.
Cream thoroughly.
Work in flour. Transfer dough to a well floured board and knead until it is pliable.
Roll out and cut with biscuit cutter.
Bake at 400° until light brown.
Yields 3 dozen tea cakes.
Combine dry ingredients in mixing bowl.
Add Crisco and first amount of milk called for.
Beat with mixer at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Add eggs, rest of milk and vanilla.
Beat 2 minutes. Spread batter in 2 well greased and floured 9 x 1 1/2-inch round layer cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes until center springs back when touched lightly.
Cook 10 to 20 minutes, then remove from pans.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add brown sugar.
Cook until blended and slightly thickened, stirring constantly.
Cool slightly.
Add cream.
Beat until smooth.
Add confectioners sugar gradually until right consistency to spread.
Brown beef and onion; add Ragu sauce and heat to boiling point. Beat cream cheese; add cottage cheese, sour cream and olives and mix.
In a 3-quart casserole, layer 1/2 beef mixture, 1/2 noodles, cheese mixture, remaining noodles and top with remaining beef mixture.
Bake.
Combine everything in a large saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer 8 to 10 minutes or until pasta is tender.
Lightly grease 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan. Line bottom with waxed paper; set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Put roast in roasting pan.
Add water, tenderizer and cover.
Cook for 1 hour.
Peel potatoes and cut in half.
Cut celery in half.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover and return to oven for 1 more hour.
At end of baking time, remove from oven.
Place roast on platter and surround with veggies.
Sprinkle flour on cheese.
Pour on butter.
Add salt and red pepper.
Add Rice Krispies.
Knead by hand.
Roll into marble sized balls and bake on ungreased sheet.
Flatten with fork and bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Melt 1/2 stick butter in frying pan.
Salt and pepper pork chops.
Brown pork chops in pan until braised on both sides but not until done.
Remove from frypan and put aside.
Melt rest of butter in frypan.
Add rice and brown.
Add consomme, onion soup and mushrooms.
Bring to a slight boil.
Pour into a 2 to 3-quart casserole dish.
Top with pork chops.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine five ingredients in food processor; process until blended and cheese is fine as you want it.
Add pimiento; process just to blend.
Store in covered container in refrigerator.
Makes 3 cups.
Fill a stemmed glass with hot water, then empty glass.
Refill with boiling water and empty again.
Fill the glass more than half full with the coffee and sugar to taste.
Stir and add whiskey. Spoon on whipped cream and drink hot coffee through cool cream.
Prepare stuffing and let stand 2 minutes.
Add oranges to stuffing.
Place 1/4 stuffing in each ham slice.
Roll ham and place each one, seam down, in a baking dish.
Spoon remaining stuffing around ham slices.
Spoon marmalade over all.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cut slightly cooked potatoes into 1 inch cubes.
In large bowl combine potatoes, onions and salad dressing.
Toss gently. Dust with paprika.
Garnish with chives and bacon bits.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
In food processor, blend strawberries until smooth; pour into saucepan.
Add water, sugar, tapioca and salt; let stand 5 minutes.
Bring to boil over medium heat, stirring constantly; remove from heat and add lemon juice.
Chill; add orange sections just before serving.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly and bake in greased casserole dish at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Cream sugars and butter.
Stir in oatmeal.
Pat into 9 x 13-inch pan or cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.

Fry tortillas in oil in a small frying pan until soft, approximately 2 to 3 seconds on each side. Set aside. Place 1 tablespoon of sauce on each and stack. Brown ground beef and drain the fat off. Add one can sauce and simmer together for about 5 minutes or until the beef and sauce are well mixed. Fill tortillas with beef, 4 ounces cheese and olives. Roll and place into a 9 x 13-inch glass pan. Pour remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle the rest of the cheese and olives on top. Bake at 250° for 10 to 20 minutes until cheese is melted. Makes 5 to 6 servings, depending on how many enchiladas you can make with this recipe. Also great to reheat. You may use Monterey Jack and can use more or less if you like cheesy enchiladas.
In a casserole dish place a layer of peeled, sliced potatoes. Spoon mushroom soup and cubed Spam.
Another layer potatoes, soup and Spam.
Fill up dish.
Add salt and pepper (to taste).
Mix one can water into mushroom soup can; mix.
Pour over potatoes, Spam and soup.
Add more water, enough to fill casserole dish up to top layer of potatoes.
Bake at 400° until potatoes are tender.
Serve hot or cold.
Cook spaghetti and celery in chicken broth to package directions.
Drain, add green pepper, onion and diced chicken to spaghetti.
Set aside.
Prepare cheese sauce, milk, flour and margarine in medium sized saucepan.
Cook until thick, stir constantly.
Add grated cheese and mushroom soup.
Mix cheese sauce into spaghetti mixture.
Pour into large oblong baking dish.
Top with margarine and cracker crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix dry ingredients.
Blend in margarine, buttermilk, and molasses.
Put in unbeaten eggs and mix.
Beat by hand 20 strokes. Butter and flour a 9 x 9 x 5-inch glass pan, or 8 x 12-inch aluminum pan.
Pour in mixture and bake at 340° to 350° heat for 45 minutes.
The bigger the dish, the less heat.
Bring to boil the white sugar and white syrup; add peanut butter and Special K cereal.
Spread on buttered 11 x 16-inch cookie sheet.
Melt the chocolate chips and butterscotch chips. Spread on top of mixture on sheet.
Eggs:
We usually do 12 to 18, depends on size of group you are feeding or the size of your deviled egg dish.
Cook spaghetti and rinse in hot water.
Add beaten eggs and butter; mix well.
Brown hamburger and onions.
Add Parmesan cheese and mushrooms.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour spaghetti sauce over meat and top with Parmesan cheese, Mozzarella cheese and pepperoni.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In large bowl, crumble beef.
Heat in microwave 2 to 3 minutes on High until beef is browned, stirring once.
Drain.
Stir in sauce and water.
Put all ingredients in a mixing bowl and mix for 5 minutes. Pour into a pint jar.
Serve on garden salad.
Have butter and eggs at room temperature.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream butter until soft; beat in sugar and beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flour and sour cream, alternately to creamed mixture, starting and ending with flour. Add flavoring and beat until smooth.
Pour into pan and bake 1 1/2 hours until golden brown, top springs back when touched.
Cool on wire rack before turning out.
Pop popcorn; put into a large pan.
Mix sugar, syrup, water, vinegar and butter in saucepan; boil until it forms a firm ball in cold water.
Pour over popped corn.
Stir until all is covered. Use lots of butter or margarine on hands as you form balls.
Makes 12 large popcorn balls.
Note:
Use 1/4 cup peanut butter in place of 1/4 cup margarine.
Chop artichokes to small pieces. Mix artichokes with rest of the ingredients.
Place in decorative baking dish in preheated oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix the last 3 ingredients and let stand while preparing vegetables.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix creamed corn, whole kernel corn, and melted oleo.
Add Jiffy cornbread mix and sour cream.
Beat egg and add to this mixture.
Add softened Cheez Whiz.
Mix well. Pour into greased baking dish and bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Combine all ingredients together and put in a 9 x 13-inch dish sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.

Press the liquid from the grated potatoes and discard. Combine grated potatoes with the mashed potatoes, egg yolk, salt and pepper. Shape into desired size pancakes and fry until brown and crisp on both sides.
The pancakes are often served with sauerbraten or other substantial meat dishes or as a luncheon dish together with applesauce.
Mix all ingredients and pour over roast.
Turn roast over in sauce and cover all sides.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Bake in slow oven at 325°.
In a large mixing bowl, combine 3 cups flour, cake mix, yeast, salt and warm water.
Mix until smooth, add enough remaining flour to form a soft dough.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead until smooth, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Roll dough into a 9 x 18-inch rectangle.
Spread with butter and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Roll dough jelly-roll style, starting with the long end.
Slice the dough into 1-inch circles, place on greased cookie sheet.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 15 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes.
Frost, if desired. Makes about 18 rolls.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs with melted margarine.
In a larger bowl, combine the corn and sour cream.
Stir in the butter and egg mixture.
Add the corn muffin mix and mix well.
Pour into a well-greased casserole or Pyrex baking dish (9 x 13-inch or smaller).
Bake at 350° for 1 hour (will be lightly browned on top).
Do not overbake.
Pour boiling water over oats; let stand while you cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs.
Mix all together.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Place in pot and simmer until tender.
Fry steak in pan until tender.
Mix soup, gravy and 1/2 of the sour cream in a pan; heat on low.
Cook noodles in boiling water until done.
When steak is cooked, add to the soup mixture.
When noodles are done add to the rest of the ingredients.
Mix well and let stand for a minute or two.
The extra sour cream is for adding before storing leftovers or if it is not moist enough.

Drain off water.
Run through meat grinder or chop in food processor with onion and garlic.

Drop by spoon into shortening or any cooking oil.
Fry until golden brown.
Peel onions. Slice 1/4-inch thick. Separate into rings.
Dip into milk, then into combined flour and salt. Fry until light brown, a few rings at a time, in shallow frying pan.
Drain on paper towel. Sprinkle with salt.
Serve hot.
Great with steak.
Combine cream cheese, confectioners sugar, peanut butter and milk in a large mixing bowl; beat at medium speed with an electric mixer until well blended.
Fold in whipped topping; spoon into crust and sprinkle with peanuts.
Chill 8 hours.
Have ready a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Mix confectioners sugar, cracker crumbs, peanut butter and butter in medium-size bowl until blended.
Scrape into ungreased baking pan and press into an even layer.
Spread melted chocolate over top.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours until chocolate is firm.
Let stand at room temperature 15 to 20 minutes before cutting with sharp knife into bars.
Makes 36 bars at 173 calories per bar.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a 12-cup muffin pan or use paper liners.
Beat together softened margarine and sugar at medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Beat in bananas until smooth.
Mix together flour, salt, baking powder and soda.
Alternately stir in flour mixture and buttermilk into egg mixture until dry ingredients are just moistened.
Stir in nuts and vanilla; do not overmix. Fill cups 2/3 full.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes.

Saute onions in butter until tender. Add dash of Kitchen Bouquet. Add beef bouillon and water. Add sugar and Parmesan cheese. Simmer 1 hour. Add sherry. Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes until golden brown.
Immediately cut into squares along lines.
Cool 2 minutes; remove from cookie sheets.
Cook sliced squash and chopped onion in boiling salted water for 5 minutes. Drain.
Combine soup and sour cream.
Stir in carrots.

Fold in squash and onion. Combine stuffing mix with melted butter. Spread 1/2 stuffing mixture in bottom of a 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish. Spoon vegetable mixture on top. Sprinkle with remaining stuffing mixture. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

Reserve 1/2 cup of mixture.

Set aside.

Fold whipped cream into egg mixture and top with whites of eggs.

Mix margarine, peanut butter and 2 sugars in another bowl.
Add flour mixture to the other bowl.
Mix well. Roll into small balls and roll in sugar. Bake at 375° for 8 minutes or until they start browning.
Place a kiss in each and press down so the cookie cracks. Bake 2 to 5 minutes longer until brown.

Spoon into ungreased 2 cup ovenproof serving dish.

Cream the butter and sugar.

Pour into a 10-inch greased and floured tube pan.
Bake in a 300° oven for 2 hours or until cake pulls away from side of pan.

Place in greased casserole.
Sprinkle bread crumbs and cheese on top.
Bake for about 30 minutes at 350°.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Cream the shortening and gradually add 1 1/2 cups of sugar, continuing to cream until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, beating well.
Add sifted dry ingredients, alternating with milk, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Blend well after each addition.
Cut cream cheese into 1/4-inch cubes and fold into batter along with orange peel.
Turn batter into 2 greased and floured 9 x 5-inch loaf pans or 12 well-greased muffin tins.
Bake at 375° for 50 to 55 minutes for loaves or 20 to 25 minutes for muffins or until golden brown.

Parboil broccoli; arrange on top of rice.
Combine mushrooms, mayonnaise and seasonings.
(For thinner sauce, add 1 cup milk.)
Top rice with sauce mixture.
Sprinkle almonds on top.

Cream sugar, eggs and oleo.
Add flour, meal, vanilla, coconut and pineapple.

Bake slow.
Serve with whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Mix all together and cook until thick; pour into baked pie shell.

Cook green pepper and onion until tender.
Remove from pan and put on the side.
Cook chopped meat, then drain all fat.
Return chopped meat, pepper and onion to frypan.
Mix the 2 cans of tomato soup together.
Pour into chopped meat and mix.
Cook pasta.
Drain.
Return to pot. Add soup mixture and mix well.
Mix well.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet 10-15 minutes at 350 degrees.
To prepare syrup, put honey, sugar and butter in saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Mix cereals and nuts in roasting pan; pour on syrup and toss.
Bake at 275° for 45 minutes; stir once 1/2 way through.
Remove from oven immediately and spread out on a cookie sheet or Reynolds Wrap in a thin layer to cool.
Don't leave in pan or it will stick together.
Store in airtight container.
Combine beef, crackers, onion, green pepper, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, seasoning to taste and 1/2 cup of tomato sauce.
Mix well. Pat into bottom and up sides of a greased 9-inch pie plate.
Toss and brown sausage.
Drain.
Saute pepper, onion and celery in sausage pan.
Drain.
Boil water and add rice and dry soup mix.
Cook until tender.
Mix with first 4 ingredients.
Bake in casserole dish for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle chicken with lemon juice, salt and pepper to taste. Add remaining ingredients. Add more mayonnaise if necessary until chicken barely holds together. Chill before serving.
Spray Pam in glass dish.
Layer pineapple, pie filling or peach slices, cake mix, coconut and oleo.
Bake 1 hour at 350°. Add pecans.
Bake 15 minutes more.
Cool before serving.
Mix together the sugar, salt, flour and rhubarb.
Put into an ungreased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Mix together the oats, cinnamon, oleo and brown sugar; sprinkle this mixture over rhubarb mixture. Bake at 350° until topping is browned and rhubarb is tender, about 35 to 45 minutes.
Cool before serving, then top with Cool Whip.
Use buttered flat 8 x 8-inch pan.
Combine rice, sour cream, chilies, salsa, salt and pepper.
Put a layer of rice combination and about 1/2 pound Jack cheese, shredded.
Finish with rice, top with grated Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 325° for 1/2 hour or 300° for 45 minutes.
Can be combined the day before serving and held in refrigerator for baking.
In skillet, brown bacon until crisp.
Break into small pieces. Add onion and stir until almost done.
Add fresh green beans with 1/3 cup water.
Turn to medium heat and cook, stirring constantly. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes. Add more water, if needed.
Cover and turn heat to low.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes longer. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Serve.
Wash well and thoroughly dry spinach.
Tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and refrigerate.
In a heavy skillet, fry the bacon until crisp.
Drain on paper towel and crumble.
Shake the oil, vinegar, wine, soy sauce, sugar, mustard, curry powder, salt and seasoned pepper together and pour over spinach.
Add bacon and toss lightly.
Top with chopped boiled eggs.

Wash and cut broccoli flowerets into bite-sized pieces.
Add raisins, sunflower seeds and onions.
Mix mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar.
Pour over broccoli mixture.
Mix lightly.
Top with bacon bits.
Serves 4 to 6.

Microwave candy on Roast - a setting that allows sugar syrup to quickly boil and blend into a candy, yet needs little watching. Mix and cook ingredients in a buttered glass mixing bowl or 4-cup glass measure.
Bowl or dish must be 2 or 3 times as large as the volume of the candy ingredients so candy syrup will not boil over. Cover candy during cooking when called for in the recipe.

Use a glass plate or stretch plastic wrap tautly across the bowl or glass measure; pierce plastic wrap so steam escapes during cooking. There is no need to worry that candy will scorch because microwaves cook from all sides, not just the bottom.
Candy syrups are usually stirred once during cooking so heat is equalized and candy cooks smooth.
Do watch candy closely because a microwave oven cooks fast.
When candy is removed from oven, it should register 236° on a candy thermometer.
Do not put a candy thermometer into a microwave oven or it will be damaged.
Combine first 6 ingredients and form into log.
Roll in chopped pecans and Parmesan cheese.
Combine all ingredients in large container, stirring well. Chill and then serve over crushed ice (2 quarts).
In a large bowl, mix well mayonnaise, chili sauce, relish, onion and salt.
Add cabbage and raisins; toss to mix well. Makes 6 servings.
Cake:
Combine flour and sugar in large bowl.
Heat margarine, cocoa and Coca-Cola to boiling.
Pour over flour and sugar; stir well.
Add buttermilk, eggs, soda, vanilla and marshmallows.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix all together.
Break 1/2 stick of Ritz crackers and melted margarine (1 stick) and put on top.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 45 minutes.

tablespoons oil until tender.
Add potatoes; cover with water.
Cook covered 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Blend in soup, milk and salt.
Heat but do not boil.
Serve garnished with bacon and parsley.

Drain fruit.
Add coconut and chill. Stir in sour cream just before serving.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a square 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Blend butter, sugar and vanilla.
Add eggs; beat with a spoon.
Combine dry ingredients.
Add to egg mixture.
Stir in chips.
Spread in pan.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes (slightly less for chewy brownies) or until brownies pull away from the sides of the pan.
Cool completely.
Cut into squares.
Yields 16 servings.
Saute onions in oleo until brown.
Add mushrooms and saute for 5 minutes.
Add rice and saute another 5 minutes.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in water; bring to a boil.
Pour over rice mixture. Cover and shut off heat.
Wash lentils in cold water.
Drain.
Now add lentils to cold water.
Saute bacon and onions until golden brown.
Stir in tomato sauce or tomatoes, add bacon and onions, potatoes and rest of ingredients, adding more water as needed during cooking.
Simmer 30 to 45 minutes; add parsley.
Beats eggs; add shortening and sugar and beat well.
Add remaining ingredients and stir in.
Drop by spoonfuls into hot grease and fry until brown on all sides.
Coat hot do-nut holes in cinnamon/sugar mixture.
Dough can be made ahead and refrigerated.
Mix cake mix, lemon pudding, cooking oil, water and eggs all together.
Mix in a separate bowl the cinnamon and sugar. Set this aside.
Grease a tube pan and sprinkle about 1/2 of the cinnamon and sugar mixture around in pan.
Pour your cake mix in pan and then add the rest of the cinnamon and sugar mixture on top. Stir lightly and bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Brown sausage and drain.
Add cheese and chili to sausage. Heat until cheese has melted.
Stir and serve hot.
Serve with tortilla chips.

recipes.t: Yellow Split-Pea Soup With Kielbasa(My Favorite Winter Soup - A Meal In Itself)
d: In a heavy kettle, cook the onion in the butter over moderately low heat, stirring until it is softened.
Add the split-peas, the sliced carrot, the celery, the kielbasa, the bay leaf and 2 1/2 quarts water.
Bring the liquid to a boil, skimming the froth and simmer the mixture, covered, stirring occasionally for 3 hours.
Discard the bay leaf and transfer the kielbasa with a slotted spoon to a plate.
In a blender, puree the mixture in batches.
Transfer the puree to the kettle and thin it with hot water to the desired consistency.
Cut the kielbasa into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Quarter the slices and add them to the soup. Season the soup with salt and pepper.
Makes about 9 cups before thinning, serving 6.
Note:
May increase potatoes, corn or shrimp.

Combine sugar and water and cook until sugar dissolves. Add peaches and cook rapidly until fruit becomes clear, stirring occasionally. Cover and let stand 12 to 18 hours in a cool place. Drain fruit and pack into hot Ball jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Cook syrup rapidly 2 to 3 minutes or longer if too thin. Pour over fruit, leaving 1/4-inch headspace. Adjust caps. Process half pints and pints 20 minutes at 180° to 185° in hot water bath. Yield: About 6 half pints.

bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

Good luck.
Enjoy!
