Bring to a boil, cover and bake at 375° until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice with a fork.
Put yeast in warm water; add sugar.
Let stand.
Put salt and eggs in warm milk and shortening.
Add yeast mixture.
Stir well. Add flour to make stiff.
Set in warm place; let rise, then make into loaves or rolls.
Let rise and bake at 350° until golden brown.
Combine eggs, salt and sugar.
Add milk and vanilla.
Pour into pastry shell and sprinkle with nutmeg.
Cover top with coconut.
Bake in very hot oven (450°) for 10 minutes.
Reduce temperature to 325° and bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until a knife inserted comes out clean.
Mix together first 4 ingredients and pat into 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.

Preheat oven to 350°. Place alternate layers of sauerkraut and beans in a buttered 8-quart casserole, ending with sauerkraut. Combine water and salt. Mix until dissolved. Add to casserole. Slice sausage roll. Place slices on top of sauerkraut. Bake 40 minutes. Remove from oven. Increase temperature to 400°. Arrange biscuits on top. Bake 10 to 15 minutes until browned.
Cut all vegetables fine.
Cover with water.
Bring to a boil and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Makes a big kettle.
Combine cake mix, pudding mix, club soda, eggs and oil; beat with mixer, then stir in cherries, pineapple and nuts with spoon. Make 3 layers.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until done.
For added color, use 1/2 jar red and 1/2 jar green cherries.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a large bowl.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into a loaf pan or dish and freeze.
Combine brown sugar, butter, vanilla and boiling water. Pour into
x	8-inch	glass
pan.
Pour
boiling water over raisins. Cover and let set while mixing batter.
Cut bread in shape of a triangle.
Place 1 slice of Mozzarella between 2 slices of bread.
Cover them with flour, then dip in egg, then in bread crumbs.
Meanwhile get oil ready and hot so you can fry the bread.
Cut in butter, shortening and sugar, creaming well.
Blend in almond extract and sifted flour, mixing well.
Roll dough into balls, using 1 level tablespoon of dough for each cookie.
Press and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Place on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in a 350° oven.
Cook for 8 minutes.
Mix taco seasoning mix, sour cream and salad dressing together and set aside.
Mix together cake mix, margarine and 1 egg.
Press into greased 9 1/2 x 13-inch pan.
Mix together powdered sugar, cream cheese and 3 eggs.
Pour over first mixture.
Bake at 300° for 60 minutes.
Let cool; cut into squares.
Dust veal strips with flour, salt and pepper.
Saute veal in 2 tablespoons butter, sauteeing quickly.
Remove veal from pan.
In skillet, heat remaining butter and add onion.
Cook until lightly glazed.
Add parsley and sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the flour; stir. Add cream and stock, cooking over low heat until sauce is smooth. Add meat and cook until tender.
Stir in last two ingredients when skillet is removed from heat.
Serves 8.
Drain pineapple; set juice aside.
Mix pineapple, apples, pecans and cheese.
Cook pineapple juice, sugar, flour and egg on medium heat, stirring constantly.
Pour over salad.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients except orange marmalade and whipped cream.
Beat at low speed 1 to 2 minutes. Pour into greased and floured 9-inch baking pan.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Arrange chicken in the bottom of a casserole dish.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Stir together soup and water in saucepan over medium heat to remove lumps.
Remove from heat and add sour cream.
Stir in cheese and 1 1/2 tablespoons poppy seed. Pour over chicken strips.
Mix together remaining poppy seed, melted butter and cracker crumbs.
Sprinkle over chicken and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

Cook potatoes in saucepan. Cover with water and bring to boil. Remove from heat and drain. Transfer to a greased 2-quart baking dish. While potatoes come to a boil, make a white sauce by melting 3 tablespoons butter in saucepan. Stir in flour, salt and pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture begins to bubble. Remove from heat and slowly add milk, stirring constantly. Return to heat and bring to boil, stirring. When sauce is slightly thickened, add cheese and stir until cheese is melted. Pour cheese sauce over potatoes in baking dish. Add ham and mix gently so as not to break up potatoes. If desired, combine 1 cup dry breadcrumbs and 2 tablespoons melted butter in small bowl and sprinkle over casserole. Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine sugar and oil.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well. Stir in vanilla.
Sift together dry ingredients; add to sugar-egg mixture, mixing well.
Stir in pears and pecans.
Batter will be stiff.
Pour into a well-greased and floured tube pan.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350° for about 1 hour or until done.
Cool about 5 minutes and remove from pan.
Freezes well.
Following directions on Knox package, thoroughly dissolve gelatine.
When slighlty cooled, combine with Irish cream and slowly add to heavy cream which has been whipped with sugar and extract until it is almost stiff.
Don't add the liquor too soon, or it might not stiffen.
When combined, pour into crumb crust. Garnish with sprinkles or nuts and extra whipped cream (so dietetic).
For quick setting, place in freezer for a few hours. Can be frozen a few weeks ahead of time and put into refrigerator a few hours before serving.
Select a deep, wide dish that will hold chicken without crowding and have only one layer.
Melt oleo in dish; salt and pepper lightly.
Roll chicken in oleo and arrange in dish. Sprinkle dry rice over chicken.
Sprinkle soup mix over all.
Add water slowly around and over all.
Cover with foil or lid and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
At 45 minutes, lift chicken up and let rice fall under chicken.
Cook all together until kinda thick.
Tear the cake into bite-sized pieces.
Place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
In mixing bowl, combine the pudding mix, milk and sour cream. Beat until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Spread over the cake. Spoon pie filling on top.
Chill until serving time.
Makes 12 to 16 servings.
Mix gently by hand.
Pour into 13 x 9-inch pan (greased and floured).
Bake at 350° for approximately 25 to 30 minutes.
Frost with dark chocolate frosting.
Mix all ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Cover tightly and place in refrigerator overnight.
Bake in a large pan in preheated oven at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
You can add chopped chicken in dressing before baking.
Mix chicken, onions and lettuce. Add sesame seeds, almonds and noodles.
Remove husks from ears of corn.
Spread corn generously with margarine and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Wrap each ear in heavy-duty foil, sealing and twisting foil around ends.
Place on grill for 15 to 20 minutes.
Boil chicken breasts until they are white and tender.
While these are cooking, also cook broccoli by package directions.
When done, debone chicken and cut into bite-size pieces.
Spread broccoli in bottom of Pyrex dish.
Layer with chicken.
Mix soup, curry powder, mayonnaise and lemon juice together and pour over chicken.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Crush crackers and mix with margarine and spread on top.
Bake in preheated oven at 325° for 35 minutes.
Combine all ingredients together and marinate in the refrigerator for 6 to 10 hours.
When ready to dry, remove slices and drain on paper towels; may pat dry.
To dry, spread slices in single layer on oven racks.
Place a pan under racks to catch drippings.
Set temperature at 140° or lowest temperature on your stove.
Open door slightly to allow air to circulate and moisture to escape.
Drying will take 6 to 10 hours.
Turn over after 4 hours.
Jerky is done when meat is shriveled, dark, leathery and chewy.
Cook rice to tender.
Drain and put aside.
Fry onions to light brown.
Add salami, then bread crumbs to absorb oil.
When cool, mix all ingredients, including eggs, pine nuts and cheese, etc.
Shape into meatball size or smaller.
Fill dish with bread crumbs and roll balls to cover.
Fry in deep oil or fry in pan to golden brown.
Drain.
Place turkey slices between two pieces of plastic wrap and pound with edge of heavy saucer until thin.
Remove plastic and coat each side of turkey with flavored bread crumbs, pressing down firmly.
Season each side with a sprinkle of flavored salt, garlic powder and black pepper.
If time allows, refrigerated breaded slices for an hour to set bread crumbs.
In large, heavy skillet, melt 3 tablespoons margarine and begin browning slices over medium-high heat until golden brown.
Remove from skillet and keep warm.
Add remaining margarine to skillet drippings and saute mushrooms until tender.
Add lemon juice and wine or chicken broth and stir to loosen brown particles.
Return turkey to skillet and top with lemon slices.
Simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes until sauce thickens and turkey is tender.
Makes 4 servings.

Heat oven to 375°. Lightly grease cookie sheet or use parchment paper. Beat butter, eggs, brown sugar and vanilla extract until well blended. Add flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. Beat until blended. Stir in oats and brickle with a spoon. Drop dough by rounded teaspoon about 2-inches apart onto prepared sheet. Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until edges are lightly browned. Cool 1 minute. Remove to wire rack. Makes about 4 dozen (large) cookies.
Mix cream cheese and sour cream.
Add taco mix.
Put mixture in round dish.
Layer with lettuce, tomatoes, cheese and olives. Pour salsa over all.
Serve with nachos.

recipes.t: Spiced Apple Rings Or Lime Pickles(Takes 3 Days To Make)
d: Scoop center out of cucumbers. Cut into 1/2-inch rings.
Add lime and enough water to cover all the cukes.
Let stand 24 hours in plastic container. Drain and rinse well.
Cover with ice cubes. Let stand 3 hours.
Drain well.
Chop olives and pecans finely or in a food processor.
Mix in the mayo and softened cream cheese and pepper adding the olive juice to achieve spreading consistency.
Refrigerate.
Serve on crackers or as a sandwich filling.
Mix together peanut butter and sugar until they resemble pie crust mix.
Gradually stir in Cool Whip; mix until smooth and creamy.
Spread hot fudge sauce on bottom of chocolate pie crust. Top with Cool Whip mixture.
Spread more hot fudge sauce on top of pie.
Sprinkle with walnuts, if desired.
Freeze for at least 3 hours before serving.
Stays fresh in freezer.
Cook bacon until crispy, then crumble into small pieces.
Cut broccoli into small pieces; mix all ingredients together.
Chill and serve.
Mix all ingredients and pour over crust.
Cover and let set in refrigerator.
Place bacon on bottom of 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Sprinkle rice over bacon; add chicken, then salt and pepper.
Dilute mushroom soup with milk; pour over chicken.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at
350°. Serves 6.
Brown beef or sausage, cut in small pieces, in oil in 3-quart saucepan; drain.
Add spaghetti sauce and simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook lasagna; drain.
(Separate lasagna and lay out flat on wax paper or aluminum foil to keep pieces from sticking together as they cool.) Spread about half cup meat sauce on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Cover with layer of lasagna.
Add some Mozzarella and Ricotta cheeses and cover with sauce.
Repeat layers of lasagna, meat sauce and cheeses, ending with a layer of lasagna and sauce.
Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese.
Cover dish with aluminum foil.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Remove foil and bake 5 minutes longer.
Allow to stand about 10 minutes before cutting for easier handling.
Melt the butter and chocolate; cool.
Beat eggs with wire whisk; add sugar, chocolate and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add flour and walnuts.
Bake in small coffee cake pan at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Frost or cover with powdered sugar.
Cook broccoli and rice separately.
Place melted butter in bottom of 2-quart dish.
Mix together cooked broccoli, rice, soup, onion, cheese and milk.
Place on top of butter.
Bake at 300° to 350° for 30 minutes.
Simmer about 1 hour or longer.
If you use broth that you have prepared yourself from turkey, put it in the refrigerator until fat has risen to top.
Skim off fat and use only the broth.
Cook broccoli as directed.
Drain well.
Combine soup, mayo, eggs and onion.
Blend in cooked broccoli.
Pour into buttered 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Melt margarine.
Add crumbs and mix well.
Sprinkle over top of cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Microwave on High power.
Mix sugar and syrup and microwave for 4 minutes.
Add peanuts and microwave for 3 to 5 minutes until peanuts are light brown.
Stir in vanilla and butter and microwave 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in baking soda until light and fluffy. Spread on greased cookie sheet to cool 1/2 to 1 hour.
When cool, break into small pieces.
Mix sugar and milk together.
Bring to a boil and boil exactly 9 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in chocolate bits, butter and marshmallow cream. Stir until melted and mix well. Add vanilla and nuts. Yields about 5 pounds.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Beat with mixer 5 to 7 minutes.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes. Sprinkle with confectioners sugar while still warm.
Layer in dish as given, starting with the lettuce.
Chill in refrigerator 6 to 8 hours.
Do not stir.
Mix ingredients and pour into unbaked pie shell. Bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Brown meat; drain.
Mix with sauce.
Layer sauce, noodles (uncooked), sauce, cheeses, noodles, sauce, etc, sauce on top. Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.

recipes.t: Melt In Your Mouth Chicken Pie
d: Place deboned chicken in 9 x 12-inch pan.
Bring to boil chicken broth and soup.
Pour over chicken; mix flour, buttermilk and melted margarine.
Pour over first mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown at 450° for 5 to 10 minutes.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a saucepan, combine beef, onion, garlic and 1/4 cup water; cook until onions are tender.
Spread half of potatoes in a 3 quart casserole.
Top with half of meat mixture, then carrots, then cheese, then remaining meat mixture. Mix soup with 1/2 soup can of water; pour over casserole and top with remaining potatoes.
Bake, uncovered at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
When potatoes are fork tender, combine biscuit mix with enough milk to make a thin consistency; pour over casserole.
Bake 5 to 10 minutes longer or until dough is lightly browned.
Yield: 6 servings.
Mix flour, margarine and pecans together and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix together in a large bowl.
Pour in tube pan.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Dissolve jello in boiling water and cool.
Melt marshmallows in pineapple juice over low heat.
Fold until smooth.
Blend cheese, carrots and pineapple.
When gelatin cools, blend together all ingredients.
Pour into mold and chill several hours.
Select a melon about 20 inches long with a flat base.
The day before serving, cut an 8-inch oval section making a sawtooth edge, out of the top of the melon.
Remove cut portion and reserve. Using a long handled spoon, scoop out pulp; remove seeds.
Place 1/4 of the pulp at a time in blender container or food processor bowl.
Cover, blend or process until pureed.
(Should have 12 cups.)
Place melon shell on a large tray.
Return puree to melon shell; stir in water, lemonade concentrate and grenadine.
Replace cut out portion of melon.
Refrigerate overnight.
Before serving, remove cut portion of melon; pour in lemon-lime beverage to fill 3/4 full.
Stir with an up-and-down motion.
Ladle punch into cups.
Combine all ingredients except almonds.
Simmer about 20 minutes or until liquid is absorbed.
Stir in almonds and serve. Serves 4.
Combine all ingredients in a wok.
(You may use a large pot but is better to use a wok.)
Stir ingredients to keep from sticking.
Cook until warm throughout.
Mix shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, then molasses; blend well.
Sift dry ingredients together; add to first mixture. Combine thoroughly.
Roll balls size of walnuts in white sugar. Bake at 375° for 12 minutes.
Makes about 6 dozen cookies.
Chop artichoke hearts and mix with remaining ingredients. Bake in a small casserole dish at 300° for 30 minutes.
Serve hot with Melba toast rounds.
Pound chicken fillets until thin.
Lay out flat and sprinkle with parsley.
Top each fillet with a slice of cheese, then a slice of ham.
Roll up tightly.
Brush each fillet with mayonnaise and then roll in the bread crumbs.
Spray a baking pan or sheet with cooking spray.
Arrange the chicken rolls, seam side down, in a single layer.
Bake in a 400° oven about 30 minutes.
Wash and drain pork chops.
Dip each chop in prepared mustard. Roll in flour, salt and pepper.
Fry to a golden brown.
Drain off fat.
Using the cans of soup, spoon the rice on top of pork chops and pour the soup around chops.
Cover and simmer until tender.
If more rice is desired, cook the cup of rice and spoon on the chops.
(Use an electric skillet.)
Slice wieners in half lengthwise and place in dish, cut side down.
Pour over barbecue sauce and bake in moderate oven (350°) for 15 minutes.
Baste frequently.

In large pot, boil potatoes until they start to fall apart. Drain some of the water. Cook on low, constantly stirring, until thick. Add salt, pepper, butter and chives. Stir well. Add enough milk to make soup as thick as you like it. Continue to cook on low until hot.
Put all ingredients in a casserole dish and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serves 4.
Mix graham cracker crumbs, sugar and margarine in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Press evenly onto bottom of pan.
Arrange banana slices on crust.
Mix crumbs, sugar and butter in bottom of 9-inch square pan. Combine pumpkin, sugar, salt and spices.
Fold in ice cream.
Pour over crumbs.
Cover.
Freeze.
Cut into squares 20 minutes before serving.
Grease an 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Pour in dry rice.
Lay raw chicken on top of rice.
Mix together mushroom soup, soup can of water and onion soup mix.
Pour this over rice and chicken. Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Yield:
4 to 5 servings.
In a salad bowl, layer the ingredients as follows: lettuce, 1/4 cup dressing, bacon, tomatoes, cheese, turkey or chicken and remaining 1/4 cup of dressing.
Serve immediately or refrigerate overnight.

Put squash in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Drain well. Butter a 1 1/2 quart baking dish. Beginning with a sprinkle of cheese, alternate ingredients by layers. Save a little cheese for topping. Bake in oven at 350 degrees until contents bubble. Sprinkle remaining cheese over top. Brown and serve immediately.
Mix all together except vanilla in heavy saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, as it thickens turn down. Add vanilla and set aside after it thickens.
Let it cool then spoon into baked pie shell or you can pour in while it is warm.
Butter casserole dish.
Mix soup, water and chicken with noodles.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes (covered).
Put apples in baking dish.
Sprinkle jello on top.
Mix sugar, flour and margarine well.
Put on top of apples.
Bake 30 minutes until apples are done.

Sift flour, salt, baking powder & soda. Cream brown sugar and shortening. Add eggs and vanilla. Beat well. Stir in dry ingredients and rolled oats. Chill dough. Form into balls and roll into powdered sugar until heavily coated. Bake in a moderate oven on greased cookie sheet at 375° for 8-10 minutes.
Beat egg slightly with fork.
Stir in milk, pumpkin and butter.
Measure flour; blend in dry ingredients.
Fold in raisins.
Fill cups 2/3 full.
May sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon sugar over each muffin.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes in a 400° oven.

Combine margarine, dry cake mix and 1 of the eggs. Stir together until dry ingredients are moistened. Pat mixture over bottom of well-greased 10 x 15-inch jelly roll pan. Beat in remaining eggs and sugar. Stir in coconut and nuts. Spread evenly over margarine mixture. Bake at 325° for 40 to 50 minutes or until golden brown. Cool pan on wire rack to room temperature. Cut into bars. Makes 4 dozen.
Combine all ingredients.
Marinate meat about 4 to 6 hours. Refrigerate for about 1 hour before grilling.
Mix flour and sugar.
Beat eggs.
Add to flour mixture with milk.
Add chopped rhubarb.
Add to other mixture.
Bake at 300° until brown and crusty on top.
Yields 1 crust pie.
Use big pie pan (do not use nonstick).
Dissolve jello in 1 1/2 cups of hot water.
Reserve 1/3 cup to mix with mayonnaise.
Add canned pineapple and juice.
Stir in cottage cheese.
Mix the mayonnaise with 1/3 cup hot jello and add to the rest of mixture.
Add nuts last.
Set in refrigerator.
Mix all.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix well.
Brush on uncooked meat and let stand for 1 hour. Barbecue and keep moist.
Cover potatoes with water; bring to boil.
Lower flame and simmer until tender.
Drain, peel and cut potatoes into bite size pieces.
Mix onions, celery, eggs and sweet relish with mayonnaise and mustard.
Stir in the potatoes.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Cover bowl and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Serves 4 persons.
Mix flour, sugar and salt; slowly add cream and vanilla.
Pour into unbaked shell and sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes, then at 325° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Dissolve each Jell-O in 1 1/2 cups hot water.
Put in square pan.
Dissolve gelatine in 1/4 cup cold water, then add hot pineapple juice and put in refrigerator and let cool.
Add whipped cream, sugar and vanilla, then fold in cubes of Jell-O.
Take half crust mixture and press in bottom of buttered pan.
Put in filling and sprinkle remaining crust over top.
Put in refrigerator to set for at least 6 hours.
Better if left overnight.
Allow Jell-O to set overnight, then cut into small squares.
Set pan into hot water for 1 or 2 seconds.
Jell-O will slide right out.
Cut meat into serving pieces; score on both sides.
Place meat in shallow pan.
Mix soy sauce, onions, garlic, sugar, oil, sherry and pepper.
Pour over beef and let stand 1 hour at room temperature.
Turn once; drain.
Place meat over medium coals. Grill until desired doneness (allow 15 minutes for medium). Garnish with additional green onion, if desired.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cook grits as directed on box.
Add ingredients as listed. Beat hard after each addition.
Bake in a moderate 400° oven until firm and slightly brown (about 1 hour).
Serve at once.
Good with barbecue.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Wash chicken and pat dry.
Drop in milk and coat with crumbs.
Arrange in single layers in baking pan. Bake 45 minutes or until done.
Chop
and
cook
the
cabbage
just until crisp-tender; drain. To prepare cream sauce, melt margarine.
Stir in flour until smooth and add
milk.
Cook
over
medium
heat and stir until thick. Saute green pepper and onion in oil until tender. Place layer of cabbage
in
a
lightly
greased
baking
dish. Sprinkle with sauteed
onion,
pepper and grated cheese. Cover with cream sauce and bread crumbs.
Bake about 10 minutes in a 350° oven.
Mix mayonnaise and sugar; layer in large bowl first 4 ingredients.
Mix in mayonnaise mixture, top with cheese.
Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Mix
together; add enough French dressing to cover all. Serve on lettuce leaves if desired.
Stir until thick and bubbly.
Combine all ingredients except sugar and water in a quart jar. Boil sugar and water 5 minutes.
Add to other ingredients and shake well.
Store in refrigerator.
Makes 1 quart.

In casserole dish, layer 2 cups peas, tomatoes, onion, bell peppers and salt and pepper to taste. REPEAT LAYERS. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top. Place 6 slices of bacon on top of cheese and bake until bacon is done and onions are tender. You may need to place under broiler to get bacon crispy.
Mix chicken with all ingredients.
Layer the chicken mixture, a layer of Dorito chips, a layer of Cheddar cheese and repeat. Add a little broth on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Use a 9 x 9-inch pan.
You can prepare this recipe and place in the refrigerator to cook when you get home from work.
Brown meat, onions, salt and pepper; drain.
Add beans and soup; mix well.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Peel potatoes and cook until tender; mash, using butter and milk.
Pour meat mixture into casserole pan; drop spoonfuls of potatoes on top. Make sure to leave openings in the middle for steam to escape. Bake at 350° until potatoes start to brown.
Whip Eagle Brand milk and juice of 2 lemons.
Fold in whipped cream with sugar added.
Add pecans and fold in pineapple.
Pour into 2 cooked pie shells (or 2 graham cracker crusts).
Chill.
Slice potatoes into a large piece of foil.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Crumble bacon over potatoes.
Add onion and cheese. Dot with butter.
Wrap loosely and seal well with double fold. Cook in 350° oven for about 1 hour or until done, turning occasionally.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cook broccoli according to package directions; drain.
In saucepan, over low heat, combine mayonnaise, cheese and milk. Heat, stirring until cheese melts.
Serve over broccoli.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix the softened margarine and sugar well.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually add the flour and stir in well.
Add vanilla, chips and nuts.
Combine fruit and juices with brandy.
Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
To serve, fill large stem glasses or goblets half full of fruit and marinade.
Pour the champagne over the fruit at the table.
Serves 6.
Mix in large mixing bowl, chicken, potatoes, cream of chicken & cream of celery. Place in 9 x 11 baking pan. Melt butter & combine with milk and flour. Pour over top. Bake at 350 for 1 hour.
Mix ingredients in order given.
Mix well after each.
Grease and flour angel food cake pan.
Spread in cake pan and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350° or when cake springs up when touched.
Have cheese at room temperature.
Add onion mix and salad dressing to make smooth.
Add pepper and beat with electric mixer. Stir in shrimp.
Chill.

Heat oven to 500 degrees. Grease baking sheet. Combine milk and salt in a small pan or bowl and stir. Dip fish in milk and roll in crushed corn flakes. Place on baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.
Melt butter in medium saucepan; stir in sugar, corn syrup and cinnamon candy.
Bring to boil; continue boiling, stirring constantly, until candy is dissolved completely.
Boil without stirring for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in soda. Gradually pour over popped corn, mixing well.
Allow to cool completely.
Break apart and store in tightly covered container. Makes about 4 quarts.
(Spray popped corn container with Pam.)
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease jelly roll pan, 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch.
Stir together all ingredients, using hands or spoon. Shape mixture into 1-inch balls.
Place in pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until brown.
Immediately remove from pan.
Serve warm with sauce for dipping.
Makes 7 1/2 dozen.
I like barbecue sauce.
Slice zucchini and cut into quarters.
Cook in 2-quart pot in 1 cup of broth.
Cook about 6 minutes or until crispy tender.
Add 3 tablespoons chopped scallion greens one more minute.
Drain broth back into remaining broth and set aside in small bowl.
Peel rest of zucchini and chop.
Chop rest of scallions and their tops. Simmer in butter until soft.
Add broth.
Add heaping tablespoonful of chopped pimento to reserved broth.
Add remaining pimento to pot mixture.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Put through blender; add salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with croutons.
Crush Oreo cookies in 9 x 13 pan.
Leave enough out to sprinkle top of dessert.
Mix butter, cream cheese and powdered sugar well.
May be a little lumpy.
Mix potatoes, cheese, sour cream, and both cans of soup in large mixing bowl. When mixed evenly spread into large casserole dish.
Top with cornflakes place into oven and bake at 350 degrees until cheese is bubbly.
Let stand 10 minutes and enjoy.
Combine sugar, margarine and milk in a heavy saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Boil 5 minutes over medium heat. Stir in chips until melted.
Add Marshmallow Creme, nuts and vanilla.
Beat until blended.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cool at room temperature.
Cut into squares.
Makes about 3 pounds.
Mix Eagle Brand milk, egg yolks, and lemon.
Pour into crust. Whip egg whites and a tablespoonful of sugar until fluffy. Spread on top of pie.
Brown meringue.
Mix together the pudding and milk, then add the sour cream and Cool Whip.
Layer vanilla wafers, sliced bananas and filling until all the filling is used.
Makes 1 (11 x 13-inch) pan full.
Soften cream cheese. Add remaining ingredients and blend. Shape and chill. Serve with assorted crackers.
Put the wafers in a casserole dish; cut the bananas up on top, then spoon on the pudding.
Repeat 2 or 3 times until you use it all up.
Top with Cool Whip.
Arrange the broccoli in a 2 qt. baking dish.
Place the chicken over the top.
In a separate bowl, combine soup and milk and pour over the broccoli and chicken.
Sprinkle with the cheese, combine the butter and breadcrumbs and sprinkle over the top.
Bake at 450°f. 230°c. gas mark 8 for 20-30 minutes or until bubbling.
Brown ribs in a pan for 15 minutes.
Drain fat.
Place ribs in crock-pot.
Combine other ingredients and pour over ribs.
Cook on medium for 4 to 5 hours.

In a 2-cup container, dissolve yeast in 1/2 cup lukewarm water and 1/2 teaspoon sugar. Let stand 1 hour. Cream shortening and 1/2 cup sugar. Add 1 1/2 cups lukewarm water to shortening mixture; add egg and salt. Add part of the flour and mix well, then add the yeast mixture. Add remaining flour and mix well. May have to add extra flour if dough is sticky.
*If you don't have buttermilk, add some vinegar to milk.
In a saucepan, combine brown sugar, water, shortening, raisins, cinnamon, salt and cloves.
Bring to a boil.
Cool.
Add flour and soda.
Pour into loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for one hour and 15 minutes.
For a flat cake, use a greased 8-inch pan.
Mix everything together and use with Tostitos chips or garnish on your favorite Mexican dish.
It's also very delicious on white chili.
In top of double boiler over hot water, melt butterscotch morsels.
Stir in salad oil.
In large bowl, mix noodles, peanuts and butterscotch morsels.
Mix thoroughly with a fork.
Drop mixture onto wax paper by teaspoonful.
Boil ingredients, except beets and onion for a few minutes, then add beets and onion.
For better flavor, make a day ahead.
Mix first 6 ingredients well.
Refrigerate for 3 hours.
Form into 2 logs; roll in finely chopped pecans and sprinkle parsley over top.
Serve with crackers.
Mix all ingredients in a pot.
Bring to a boil.
Boil until a few small drops form a little ball when dropped in a glass of cold water.
Remove from heat.
Ready for cake.
Mix together to make crumbs.
Mix first three ingredients in saucepan.
Heat and thicken with cornstarch until desired consistency.
Serve over pancakes, waffles, French toast, etc.
Cut cheeses into 1 inch squares about 1/2 inch thick.
Cover with dressing and pimentos and marinate several hours or overnight. Serve in shallow serving dish with crackers.
Slice sausage crosswise, about 1/2-inch thick.
Brown in oil in deep saucepan or Dutch oven.
Add garlic, onion, carrots and basil.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add zucchini, tomatoes with liquid, bouillon, cabbage, salt and pepper.
Combine dates, water, soda and butter; let cool.
Beat the egg and sugar; add remaining ingredients.
Mix all together.
Bake in moderate oven (325°) for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Blend ingredients in mixing bowl. Pour into prepared pan.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Place peeled eggs in bowl or jar.
Mix vinegar, beet liquid, sugar, salt, onion and cloves.
Pour over eggs.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 days.
Slice eggs and serve on greens.
Cut tofu into quarters and boil in salted water for 20 minutes.
Drain and crumble.
Combine with the other ingredients and bake for 40 minutes at 350°.

and
scale
carp.

mix with wine. Place fish with butter/wine sauce into aluminum foil, wrapping tightly. (Salt

and
bake	at 350° for 1/2 hour.

Throw away and eat shingle.	Serves all.
Salt and pepper roast.
Coat in flour.
Heat cooking oil in skillet and lightly brown roast.
Wash, peel and cut potatoes into quarters.
Wash and scrape carrots and cut into approximately 1/8-inch slices.
Remove roast after browning and place into a large baking dish.
Arrange potatoes and carrots (and sliced onions, if desired) around the sides of roast.
Sprinkle the soup mix onto roast.
Brown a tablespoon of flour in the oil remaining in skillet after browning the roast.
Pour 1/2 to 1 cup of water over browned flour to make gravy.
Add salt and pepper.
After the gravy has thickened, pour it over and around the roast in the baking dish.
Place the dish into a very hot oven (425°) for about 15 minutes.
Place a piece of aluminum foil very loosely over the dish.
Reduce the heat to 300°.
Cook for about 15 minutes per pound.
(If you have a cooking timer on your oven, you can set it for the estimated cooking time and your lunch will cook while you are away at church.)
Melt margarine in a large saucepan over low heat.
Add marshmallows and stir until completely melted.
Remove from heat. Add peanut butter, if desired.
Add Rice Krispies cereal.
Stir until well coated.
Using buttered spatula or waxed paper, press mixture evenly into buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cut into squares when cool.
Cook onions until soft.
Add artichokes, spinach, soup, eggs and spices.
Pour into greased casserole dish.
Blend cream cheese, Parmesan cheese and milk.
Pour over top of casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Prepare fettuccine as directed on package.
Drain and set aside. Gradually add skim milk to fat-free mayonnaise and garlic in small saucepan.
Heat thoroughly, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat; blend in Egg Beaters.
Toss with fettuccine and mushrooms until well coated.
Add Parmesan cheese and mix well.
Place roast in deep pot or casserole.
Mix sugar, ginger, soy sauce and soup.
Pour over meat.
Cut onions in thick slices. Place slices over meat.
Cover tightly and bake at 300° for 4 hours and 30 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients together except cheese until all is mixed well.
Pour mix in very hot oiled skillet.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Spray 1 large bowl or brown paper bag with Pam.
Place the sugar, butter, corn syrup and salt in a glass bowl; microwave on High until boiling, then cook for another 2 minutes.
Add baking soda; stir well (mixture will become foamy).
Place popped corn in bowl or bag; pour syrup mixture over corn.
Stir well with wooden spoon sprayed with Pam.
Microwave for 1 1/2 minutes on High; stir.
Repeat.
Microwave for 30 seconds on High; stir.
Pour out on cookie sheet.
Spread out and allow to cool.
Mix all ingredients together and blend on medium speed for 3 minutes.
Pour into 3 cake pans that have been greased and floured.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool and frost.
Saute pepper, celery and onion in oleo.
Add cheese (cut into small pieces), soup, mushrooms, pimento and chicken.
Cook noodles in broth where chicken was cooked.
Add noodles to mixture and pour into casserole dish.
Cook in 350° oven (covered) for 25 to 30 minutes.
Remove cover and cook until brown, 5 minutes.
Drain all canned fruits, reserving 2 cups mixed juices.
Layer drained fruit, strawberries, cherries and bananas in bowl. Combine pudding mix with reserved juices in bowl, beating until thick.
Pour over fruit.
Do not toss.
Chill for 2 hours before serving.
Yields 15 servings.
Melt cheese with soup.
Put broccoli in long, flat casserole. Pour cheese mixture over broccoli.
Top with Pepperidge Farm dressing.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut biscuits into fourths.
Fill a small baggie with sugar and 2 tsp. cinnamon.
Shake biscuits in baggies.
Place into bundt pan.
Melt 1 1/2 sticks of oleo and add brown sugar, pecans and 1 tsp. cinnamon.
Pour batter over biscuits.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes and then empty pan.
Cut chicken into large pieces.
In bowl combine onion, soups, salsa and milk, blending well.
In a 1 1/2-quart buttered casserole, layer half the tortillas, chicken, sauce and cheese. Sprinkle with green chilies.
Repeat layers once more ending with cheese on top.
Cover; refrigerate for 24 hours.
Remove cover. Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pack in a buttered loaf tin and bake 1 hour at 350° or moderate oven.
Increase heat during last twenty minutes or so.
Serve with sauteed pineapple slices.
Place broccoli in baking dish.
Mix rest of ingredients and pour over broccoli.
Then place topping mixture on top of broccoli and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Season to taste.
Combine beans, tomatoes and soup.
Line a greased ovenproof dish (2-quart) with tortillas.
Layer half of ground beef, soup mixture and cheese.
Add another layer of tortillas, meat and soup mixture, ending with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted.
Cream Crisco and sugar until smooth.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each addition.
Combine salt and flour.
Add to mixture.
Beat well and stir in vanilla.
Cook in a greased and floured tube pan for 1 hour and 10 minutes at 300° until brown.

Put package of mincemeat, broken, with 1/2 cup water and boil briskly for 1 minute. Cool. Combine the mincemeat, nuts, candied fruit, sweetened condensed milk and egg. Blend well. Stir in flour and baking soda; pour into a loaf pan that has been greased and floured. Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until center comes back when lightly touched.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, salt and baking soda. Set aside. In a small bowl, beat eggs, sour cream and butter. Add all at once to dry ingredients along with apples.
Stir, just until moistened. Fill well-greased muffin tins 2/3 full.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Yields 24 muffins.
In medium bowl combine milk and Jell-O mix, beat until smooth, approximately 1 to 2 minutes.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Fold in chocolate cookies.
Pour mix into pie crust.
Add extra cookies, either whole or crushed, on top for garnish.
Freeze for 3 hours before serving.
A great treat children love!
Put 1 cake layer in bottom of a large punch bowl.
Starting at top of ingredients, layer pudding, cherry pie filling, pineapple, fruit cocktail, coconut, pecans and Cool Whip; put 1 layer of each.
Add other cake layer and start over.
Put cherries on top of cake.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Mix with water and egg.
Use for onions or vegetables.
Cook sugars, syrup, cream and salt over high heat until mixture forms a soft ball (235°) when dropped in water.
Remove from heat. Add flavoring and pecans.
Beat until creamy.
Drop from spoon onto waxed paper.
Brown sausage and hamburger until crumbled; drain excess grease.
In crock-pot, melt cheeses.
Add meat, soup, tomatoes, green chilies and onions; mix well.
Makes a large amount and can be frozen.
Serve with chips.
Serves many.
Make syrup of sugar, water, cinnamon and nutmeg; add butter. Quarter, peel and core apples.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder, then cut in shortening.
Add milk all at once and stir until flour is moistened.
Roll 1/4-inch thick; cut in 5-inch squares.
Put 4 pieces of apples on each.
Sprinkle generously with additional sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Dot with butter and fold corners to center.
Pinch edges together and place 1 inch apart in greased baking dish or pan.
Pour syrup over dumplings and bake in moderate oven at 375° for 35 minutes.
Serve hot with cream.

Cream the cream cheese and add drained green chilies.
Blend well with mixer.
Spread out tortillas; divide and spread out cream cheese evenly over tortillas.
Roll each one like a jelly roll. Wrap and refrigerate.
When ready to serve, cut in thin slices.
In large pot, boil chicken and keep stock.
Bone and skin chicken.
Place back in pot.
Add vegetables.
Salt and pepper. Boil until cooked.
Reduce heat to simmer.
Keep water level high. Add water to flour to make slightly sticky dough.
Roll out 1/4-inch thick and cut 1 1/2-inch squares.
Drop squares into water and let cook until dough is done.
Drain water only as needed to keep from overflowing.
Combine all ingredients in a casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 6 servings.
Heat oven to 250°.
Spray 13 by 9 inch baking pan with non-stick cooking spray.
Combine cereal and pecans in pan.
In large bowl, microwavable, combine sugar, corn syrup and crisco. Microwave on high for 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Stir and microwave again for 30 seconds or until boiling.
Stir vanilla and baking soda into mixture.
Pour over cereal mixture and stir to coat mixture evenly.
Bake 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes.
Spread on baking sheet and cool completely.
Break into pieces.
Store in air tight container.

Brush with melted butter.
Cut in pie shaped wedges.

Bake at 375° for 15 to 18 minutes.

Add salt, tomato sauce, beans and water.
Let simmer 45 minutes.
Mix margarine, sugars, egg and vanilla.
Stir in flour and baking powder.
(If dough is soft, cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour.)
Heat oven to 350°.
Beat egg whites.
While beating, heat water, cornstarch and sugar on stove until it boils, then pour into egg whites slowly and add vanilla.

Note:
Need 24 paper nut cups, 1 1/2 x 1 1/4-inches.

Separate rolls. Sprinkle chicken over the triangles. Roll up, beginning at the large end. Place in a casserole dish. Mix the soup, cheese, milk and chicken broth and pour over rolls. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook potatoes, water and salt until tender.
Cut bacon into small pieces and fry until almost cooked.
Add onion and cook slowly until bacon is completely cooked.
Combine all cooked ingredients in one pot and add milk and clams.
Bring to a boil, however do not boil.
Mix well; stuff bird and bake.
Or, cook neck and back and put the stock over dressing and bake dressing in casserole at 325°. This stuffing can be used to stuff whitefish.
Eliminate giblets.
Mix the pudding mix with the milk.
Add the sour cream and Cool Whip, mixing well.
Layer pudding in 5-quart dish with bananas and the vanilla wafers.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.
Melt butter and brown sugar in a large fryer.
Beat eggs, sugar and vanilla until thick.

Serve plain or with whipped cream.

Cut ham and cheese into squares to fit individual rolls.
Put one of each on each roll, then top with other half of roll package.
Separate rolls and return to original aluminum pan.
Cover with foil and heat at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes.

Mix with just enough milk to pour and beat into hot milk.
Stir until thick.
Set into a pan of cold water and add butter and vanilla and beat well.
When slightly cool, pour into pie shells.
Take whites of eggs and add baking powder and beat until thick.
Add sugar and vanilla and pour into pie shells spreading well and brown under broil.
In large skillet, cook bacon until crisp.
Drain, reserving 3 tablespoons drippings in skillet.
Crumble bacon; set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in drippings for about 5 minutes or until onion is tender, but not brown.
Combine flour, chili powder and salt. Cut liver into thin strips; toss with flour mixture to coat.
Add liver to onion in skillet; brown quickly on all sides.
Stir in crumbled bacon, undrained tomatoes and whole kernel corn.
Simmer, covered, until mixture is heated through.
Serve with tortillas or over hot, cooked rice.

Cook noodles.
Drain and place in large casserole.
Add margarine, cheese, milk and eggs.
Mix well.
Sprinkle another cup of grated cheese on top.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.

Heat in skillet the first 4 ingredients until very hot.

Cover with plastic wrap.

Microwave, uncovered, on High 6 to 9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes.

Add salt and 3 eggs (one at a time), stirring well.
Add 1/4 cup milk. Stir and then add 1 teaspoon vanilla; stir and add pecans.
Mix sugar and butter until creamy.
Add eggs and peanut butter.
Mix soda and flour in with the rest.
Place small balls on cookie sheet.
Press out with fork.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes, or until lightly browned.

Mix shortening, butter, sugars, eggs and vanilla.

Mix 1/2 of your spaghetti sauce with all your ingredients.

Pour the rest of spaghetti sauce over the top of the circular meat loaf.
Cook on High for 12 minutes.
Pour off drippings.
Cook on High approximately 5 minutes more (depending on your microwave).
Serve with peas or another green vegetable in the center.

Add 3 eggs, beating well.

recipes.t: Oven Roasted Chicken In Tomato Sauce
d: Place chicken in baking pan.
Combine all other ingredients and pour over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for about 45 minutes or until chicken is brown.
Before serving, garnish with lemon slices, parsley or cooked green peas, if desired.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Heat all together for 1 to 2 hours. Great at winter get togethers!
Blend together milk, lemon juice, lemon peel and yolks until thickened.
Turn into pie shell.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In heavy 2-quart saucepan, melt butter. Combine bread crumbs and next 4 ingredients.
Dip chicken breast halves in melted butter; roll in bread crumb mixture.
Place in ungreased 9-inch square baking dish.
Bake in center of oven 50 minutes or until golden brown.
Meanwhile, add diced onion to remaining melted butter (1/2 cup).
Saute onion; add wine and chopped parsley.
Pour over golden brown chicken breasts.
Return to oven 3 to 5 minutes more just to heat sauce.
Serve with sauce spooned over breasts.

d: Wash spinach and break into small pieces in a large bowl.
Add bacon, eggs and bean sprouts and lightly toss.
Top with croutons and this dressing:
On floured surface, roll half of pastry into a 12-inch circle. Cut 6 (4-inch) circles.
Repeat with second pastry.
Fit into 12 muffin pan cups.
Fill each muffin cup with some shrimp, green onion, black olives and cheese.
Beat remaining ingredients and pour over mixture in muffin cups.
Bake in 400° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.

Blend well.
Add egg yolks, juice and cooled butter; blend.

Do not boil.
Put into puffed pastry.
In blender, combine peaches, orange juice, rum and lemonade concentrate.

Mix the first 4 ingredients and spread 1/2 batter in 9 x 13-inch greased pan. Mix together the brown sugar, pecans and cinnamon. Sprinkle 3/4 mixture over batter. Swirl with knife. Add remaining batter and top with remaining cinnamon sugar mixture. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Remove and drizzle with the confectioners sugar, vanilla and milk.
Mix applesauce, sugar, butter and egg together and set aside. Combine flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and cloves together. Mix well and add raisins and nuts.
Stir in applesauce mixture. Pour batter into well-greased tube pan and bake in preheated 350° oven for 50 minutes or until done.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine all ingredients, except margarine and shape into 6 equal patties.
In a 10-inch skillet, heat margarine until hot and bubbly.
Add patties and cook over medium heat, turning once, until brown on both sides.

Combine first 8 ingredients in a large shallow dish or zip-top freezer bag; add beef. Cover or seal and chill 8 hours, turning occasionally. Remove beef from marinade and place on rack in roasting pan. Discard marinade. Bake at 425° for 40 to 50 minutes or to desired degree of doneness. Cover loosely with foil and let tenderloin stand 10 minutes before slicing.
Put all ingredients in a pint jar; shake to mix well.
Mix sugar, oil and eggs together.
Add strawberries and lemon juice.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and spices.
Gradually stir dry ingredients into strawberry mixture.
Mix and add nuts, if desired.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Sift flour, soda, salt and cinnamon; set aside.

Remove from heat.
Add sugar; mix well.
Add sifted ingredients, beating well.

Beat well.

Put all together.
Bring to boil for 1 minute.
Set off to cool.
Bake two pie shells.
After mixture cools, add 1 quart of strawberries and put into pie shells.
Top with Cool Whip and refrigerate.

Knead until smooth and elastic, adding more flour (up to 1/2 cup) if necessary to prevent dough from being too sticky.
Place dough in a greased bowl. Cover; let raise in warm place until doubled, 45 minutes to 1 hour. Punch dough down; divide into 12 balls.
Roll each out to form 18-inch rope.
Twist into pretzel shape.
Let rise, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes.
Brush lightly with egg white mixture and sprinkle with salt.
Bake at 425° until well browned, 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients with mixer, except chocolate pie crust. Put mixed ingredients in the chocolate pie crust.
Freeze for 1 hour.
Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with foil. Unroll crescent rolls. Beat ingredients and spread on top of the bottom of the pan. Lay second can of rolls on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

Mix ingredients together in large bowl until well blended.
Put in pan; bake for 25 minutes, until done.
When cool, frost with favorite chocolate frosting (butter frosting suggested).

Layer in greased casserole.
Sprinkle celery over top.
Mix soup and cheese.
Pour over top of vegetables.
Bake at 350° until heated thoroughly. Can top with Ritz cracker crumbs and sprinkle with melted margarine over top.

Brown meat, add minced garlic, onion and celery.
Cook until onion is transparent.
Add corn, salt, chili powder and tomatoes and boil slowly about 15 minutes.
Slowly stir in olives. Put in a greased casserole dish, top with cheese. Bake at 350° about 45 minutes.

Add flour a little at a time; beat well. Add flavorings.

Mix ingredients 3 minutes. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Let cake cool.
Mix brown sugar and butter in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Add vanilla.
Pour mixture over cream cheese and blend thoroughly.
Use as a dip for sliced apples.
Preheat oven at 350°.
Sift all dry ingredients into 8-inch square pan.
Make 3 holes with spoon in dry ingredients.
In one hole, put vanilla.
In another, put vinegar and in last hole, melted butter.
Pour lukewarm water over all.
Stir, mixing well. Bake 30 minutes.
Cool in pan; frost with chocolate frosting.

Add vanilla and eggs; beat until smooth.
Stir in flour mixture until well blended.
Stir in dates and nuts.
Drop by tablespoon onto greased baking sheet.

Very good!
Combine raisins and lemon juice; heat gently until hot. Then set
aside until raisins are cool and plump.

Put into small casserole dish and bake at 325° for about 15 to 20 minutes. Top with slivered almonds. Serve with crackers.
Brown meat after coating with flour, salt and pepper in hot oil.
Add liquid to meat.
Add chopped onion.
Cover and cook 45 minutes.
Add carrots.
Cook until tender.

Stir to mix well.
Melt caramels with 1/3 cup evaporated milk over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Combine remaining milk with cake mix, melted margarine and mix well.
Press half of cake mix into bottom of 9x13 greased pan.
Bake at 350 for 6 minutes.
Sprinkle one cup nuts, coconut and chocolate pieces over crust, pour caramel mixture on and top with teaspoons of remaining cake mix, pressing gently into caramel mix.

Cool slightly, refrigerate (2 dozen).

Roll up towel and cake together.
Put in freezer for 30 minutes.

Pat on bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 400° for 8 minutes.
Mix cream cheese and sugar. Fold in Cool Whip.
Spread on cooled crust.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Add frozen berries. Mix until somewhat thick. Spread over cream cheese mix.
Refrigerate.
Crumble crackers and add sugar and melted margarine.
Use half for crust and half for top.
Mix orange juice, mashed oranges and Cool Whip.
Pour over crust and top with other 1/2 of cracker crumbs.
Place first 6 ingredients in an oblong glass baking dish and broil until vegetables are tender.
In a saucepan, cook spaghetti and set aside.
In another saucepan, combine Velveeta and milk over low heat until Velveeta melts and combines with milk to make a cheese sauce.
Combine shrimp mixture, spaghetti and cheese sauce.

Dredge in flour.
Brown in oil on each side in skillet.
Empty contents of one can of soup over chops.
Cook for 1 hour at 350°.

Heat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Roll 1/4-inch thick on lightly floured cloth covered board.

Stir in sour cream and butter; continue to cook until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla, mixing well.
Stir in chocolate until blended.
Pour mixture into pie crust.

Bring to a boil for 1 minute, 9 cups of water and 2 cups of sugar.
Take off stove and add 1 (12 ounce) can frozen orange juice and lemonade.
Let cool.
Add brandy.
Stir and put in a gallon bucket; put in freezer.
Let sit for 24 hours.

Saute onions, bell pepper and parsley, stirring occasionally until onions are clear.

Cover, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally until potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
Boil macaroni.
Melt butter in saucepan; take off heat and add flour.
Blend well; add milk slowly until blended with flour mixture (no lumps).
Return to heat, stirring constantly until thickened.
