You may substitute bell pepper for celery and chicken soup for mushroom if you desire.
Bring broccoli and water to full boil in medium saucepan on medium-high heat. Stir in rice. Cover. Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes. Add Velveeta. Stir until Velveeta is melted.
Beat eggs in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients.
Beat well.
Pour into an oiled 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° until mixture is set and top is golden, about 45 minutes.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Melt margarine in heavy skillet; set aside.
Layer vegetables in skillet:
carrots, onion, celery, zucchini and green peas.
Top off with cabbage; season and dot with butter.
Cover tightly with lid; bring to boil.
Let simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until vegetables are done.
Best when the vegetables are still slightly crisp.

recipes.t: Squash Pie (Coconut Flavor)(Tastes Just Like Coconut Pie)
d: Mix ingredients; pour into pie crust. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients and form into 1-inch balls.
Press flat on greased cookie sheet with a fork.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Boil artichoke hearts for 5 minutes.
Drain and quarter.
Mix all ingredients, except olives.
Slice olives.
Place on top. Bake, uncovered, 15 to 20 minutes at 450° in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Layer lettuce and chopped vegetables, saving enough lettuce for top layer.
Layer the peas and last layer of lettuce.
Cover with mayonnaise.
Add thick layer of Parmesan cheese and refrigerate a day or two. Crumble 1/2 pound of cooked crisp bacon and spread on top.
Looks pretty in deep glass bowl.
Place ground meat in bottom of casserole dish.
Put green beans on top of meat.
Pour Tater Tots on top of beans.
Spoon cream of mushroom soup over mixture.
Cover with foil and bake in 350° oven for 50 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for 10 minutes.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch pan and sprinkle the wafers over top evenly.
Sprinkle the chocolate chips, coconut and walnuts on top.
Pour the milk over all and bake at 350° for thirty minutes. Cut into squares while warm.
(I doubled the recipe.)
In mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar.
Add vanilla.
Stir in potato chips and chopped nuts.
Add flour.
Blend well.
Form into small balls with hands.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Flatten with floured glass.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Makes about 3 1/2 dozen.
Mix sugar, flour, eggs and butter and put in saucepan.
Cook on low heat until butter melts.
Add coconut and pineapple.
Stir all together and pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until pie is golden brown.

recipes.t: Biscuit Dough(Very Light; For Obstorte, Roll, Cakes And Cheesecake.)
d: Sift flour 4 times.
Beat egg yolks until thick and creamy, lemon colored.
Add water; continue beating until very thick. Gradually beat in sugar, then extract.
Fold in flour, a little at a time.
Beat egg whites until foamy.
Add cream of tartar and beat until they form moist, glossy peaks.
Fold in egg yolk mixture.
Bake in angel food pan in slow oven at 325° for 1 hour. Invert 15 minutes.
Use whatever size pan is needed for: obstorte, cake, cheesecake, etc.
Fill with apricot jam.
Top with cream filling.
Decorate with cake decorator.
In a 2-quart dish, dissolve gelatin in water.
Add pie filling and pineapple.
Chill until firm.
Combine cream cheese, sour cream, nuts and sugar.
Spread over gelatin mixture.
Chill.
In Dutch oven heat water and bouillon until dissolved.
Add broccoli; cover and cook until broccoli is tender.
Add milk, cheese and dash of pepper.
Cook and stir until cheese is melted. Combine 1/4 cup flour with 1/2 cup cold water.
Stir into broccoli mixture.
Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cream shortening; add sugar, beaten eggs, flour, salt and vanilla.
Spread into a 9 x 12-inch greased pan.
Reserve 1 cup batter for top.
After spreading the portion of batter in bottom of pan, spoon pie filling on batter.
Drop the rest of the batter on top of filling, not completely covering it.
When baked, fruit will ooze up through batter.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Bake at 325° if using glass dish.
Put fruit in bottom of pie shell. Beat egg yolks. Add milk. Mix cornstarch with sugar.
Add sugar mixture and butter to beaten egg
yolks, then add vanilla flavoring.
Pour over fruit. Bake at 325° until set.
Let cool.
Cook and debone chicken.
Set aside.
Cook wild rice separately; set aside.
Saute onion in butter; add soup, mushrooms, milk and flour and heat until well blended and hot. Make layers of rice, chicken, sauce and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt oleo and stir into stuffing.
Put 1/2 of this into casserole.
Then put chicken over this.
Pour broth over this. Mix sour cream and soup
togther,
then put over chicken.
Top with rest of stuffing.
Spoon
a little broth over all.
Bake, uncovered, 30 minutes at 350°.
Combine first 4 ingredients in medium bowl; set aside, stirring occasionally.
In large bowl beat together margarine and sugar until creamy.
Add flour, oats and 1/2 teaspoon apple pie spice; mix until crumbly.
Save 3/4 cup mixture for topping. Press rest into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes.
Combine rice and cheese.
Mix well. Add chicken, peas and half of the onions. Mix lightly. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Top with remaining onions and bake 5 minutes longer. Serves 4 to 6.
Mix all ingredients, except Smokies.
Cook on stove top until thick.
Add Smokies.
Serve warm.
Saute beef, onion and garlic until brown and tender.
Combine beans, oregano, chili powder, chiles, tomato sauce and water in separate saucepan.
Bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes.
Cut fillets into 2 to 3 pieces.
In heavy skillet, saute onions in 1/4 cup butter until golden brown, about 20 minutes. Add potatoes, salt, pepper and boiling water.
Arrange fish fillets on top.
Cover and simmer about 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add scalded milk, light cream and 3 tablespoons butter.
Heat until very hot.
Slice tomato and float on top of chowder.
Mix all ingredients with little hands.
Store in Ziploc bag. Add food coloring for more fun.
Melt margarine in bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Put graham crackers on top.
Put chips on top of crumbs.
Put coconut on top of chips.
Put pecans on top of coconut.
Spread Eagle Brand milk over top.
Bake at 350° for about 25 to 30 minutes.

Cook broccoli and dried onion in salted water. Before totally cooked, add undiluted soup, butter and milk. Simmer a little while. Cut cheese into chunks and let melt in soup. Keep stirring as it tends to stick. Serves about 8.
Cream cheese, softened.
Add butter, chicken, mushrooms and Lawry's seasoning.
Flatten rolls with a rolling pin; put 1/8 of chicken mixture on roll.
Roll to form from narrow end.
Dip in melted butter and roll into walnuts, then in bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes, until done.
Thicken chicken broth and use as a side dish to pour over chicken.
Beat the eggs until they are creamy.
Mix sugar, flour and cornmeal.
Add to the eggs, a small amount at a time.
Add liquids slowly in the order they are listed.
Pour into an unbaked pie shell and bake for 40 minutes at 350°.
Mix first three ingredients together first (so mustard doesn't clump).
Mix rest.
Pour over chuck steaks or Spencer steaks. Marinate 2 to 3 hours.
Barbecue or broil.
Brown rice in butter in skillet.
Mix beef broth bouillon soup, French onion soup and browned rice in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Excellent with smothered quail.
I usually double this recipe.
Mix all ingredients, except oil, until thick.
Shape into balls.
Place into hot oil to fry.
Drain and serve warm.
Boil eggs for 15 minutes.
Cool off and peel.
Slice in half. Place yolks in a bowl.
Mash with a fork until smooth.
Add salad dressing, sweet relish, mustard and sugar.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon up and place in center of each egg half.
Sprinkle with paprika and refrigerate.
Melt butter and chocolate in a double boiler.
Cream egg and chocolate mixture with sugar and salt.
Beat until the mixture is light and smooth, then add vanilla.
Sift flour and baking powder. Add the flour and baking powder alternately with the milk into the creamed mixture.
Work in the nuts.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 375° for 8 minutes or until done.
Makes 6 dozen.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease square brownie pan.
Dump cherry filling in pan; add cake mix and pour melted margarine over top. Spread pecans on top.
Bake for 45 minutes.

Combine water, lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl. In a separate bowl, mix flour, paprika and seasoned salt. Preheat electric skillet to 325° of place a heavy skillet on the stove and preheat on medium-high. Dip fish fillets in liquid mixture and then place in flour mixture, covering completely. Shake off excess flour and place fillets, meat side down, in greased preheated pan. Cook 6 to 7 minutes, depending on the thickness, then turn over and cook until firm to touch (about 6 minutes more).
Garnish each with a sprig of parsley and a lemon twist.
Serves 6.
In a large pot, cook ground beef, onion and green pepper until tender.
Season ground beef with salt and pepper to taste.
Add tomatoes, catsup, sugar and Worcestershire sauce.
Let simmer about 10 minutes.
Stir frequently.
Add water.
Bring to a full boil.
Add macaroni.
Cook until macaroni is tender.
Stir often to prevent macaroni from sticking.
Drain the pineapple and reserve syrup, make up to 1 c.

with water. Bring to a boil, dissolve the gelatin in the hot liquid and allow to cool. Gently stir in ginger ale, chill until partially set. Whip the cranberry sauce, stir in pineapple and fold in the gelatin. Turn into a mold and chill until firm. Blend together the Cool Whip and cream cheese, spread over the gelatin mold, sprinkle with pecans.
Boil chicken and break or tear into bite size pieces; discard the skin.
Dice celery ribs into small pieces.
Peel and cut oranges into bite size pieces.
Take 2 quarts of water and add the lemon juice.
Cut up apples into bite size pieces and let soak in water-lemon mixture.
(This prevents apples from turning brown.) Add drained apples, chicken, oranges, almonds, mayonnaise and sugar together in a bowl and mix together.
You may add more mayonnaise and sugar to your own taste.
Heat oven to 400°.
Heat water and butter to boiling.
Stir in Bisquick. Stir about 1 minute or until forms a ball. Remove from heat. Beat in eggs until smooth.
Mix in cheese and Italian seasoning. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes or until puffed and light golden brown.
Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Store in refrigerator until served.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Arrange chicken in baking dish. Combine other ingredients and pour over chicken.
Cover and bake 40 minutes.
Uncover and cook an additional 20 minutes or until brown.
Contains 242 calories, 15 fat and 78 cholesterol.
Soften cream cheese.
Form a ball.
Sprinkle or roll ball in Ranch mix.
Cover with pecans or bacon bits.
Cream margarine, sugar
and
eggs.
Add bananas, mashed through a sieve.
Add
sour milk, in which you dissolve baking soda.
Lastly, add flour,
baking
powder and salt; beat well. Add nuts, if desired.
Bake in a tube pan in moderate oven for 40 minutes.
May ice or glaze if desired.
Dissolve jello and hot water.
Add salad dressing; beat.
Stir in cottage cheese, oranges, pineapple and cherries.
Refrigerate until set.
Mix Jell-O and 1 cup boiling water.
Set aside to cool.
Bake cake as directed on box in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Let cool slightly. Using a fork, poke holes 1-inch apart throughout.
Pour Jell-O over entire cake slowly.
Refrigerate until cool.
Cook pasta and drain.
In a large bowl toss pasta, cheese, onions, radishes, olives and cucumbers.
In a small bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Toss with the pasta and spread evenly. Chill 1 to 2 hours.
Serve.
Bake cake according to directions on package.
Cool cake 15 minutes. Punch holes in top with a fork.
Combine milk, sugar and coconut.
Bring to a boil and simmer one minute.
Spoon over cake. Cool cake completely.
Top with Cool Whip mixed with 1/2 cup coconut or sprinkle coconut across top.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Saute onion, pimento and mushrooms in butter.
Combine macaroni, onion mixture and remaining ingredients; mix well.
Spoon into a lightly greased 2-quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix together soups and sour cream.
Microwave onions on High for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add onions, potatoes and cheese to soup and sour cream mixture.
Add salt, pepper and onion powder.
Place in greased casserole.
Melt margarine and crumble Ritz crackers; mix with hands until all are buttery.
Sprinkle over top.
Sprinkle topping with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Scone dough must be handled minimally and quickly.
As soon as the soda makes contact with liquid the rising action has begun. The object is to get the scones into the oven quickly while the dough is still wobbling so the rising is not wasted.
Mix vanilla pudding mix in fruit cocktail, then add apple, cherries and bananas.
In bowl, mix shrimp and salsa.
Cover and chill 1 hour.
Cook rice and add chilies, scallions, salt and pepper. Mix well. Skewer salsa-coated shrimp; broil or grill.
Place on rice.
Serves 4.
Oil bottom of casserole dish.
Mix all the ingredients.
Pour into casserole; top with bacon strips, very thin ones.
Bake at 350° until done.
Mix the cornstarch, flour and seasonings until well blended. Add beer; mix well.
Cut about 3/4-inch off top of onion; peel onion.
Cut onion into 12 to 16 vertical wedges, but do not cut through bottom (root end).
Remove about 1 inch of "petals" from center of onion.
Dip cut onion in Seasoned Flour and remove excess by shaking; dip in batter and remove excess by gently shaking. Separate "petals" to coat thoroughly with batter.
Mix batter after standing to blend ingredients.
Gently place in fryer basket and deep fry at 375° to 400° for 1 1/2 minutes.
Turn over and fry 1 to 1 1/2 minutes longer or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Place onion upright in shallow bowl and remove center core with circular cutter on apple corer.
Serve hot with Creamy Chili Sauce.
Mix eggs and sugar.
Add other ingredients.
Mix well and pour into unbaked pie shell.
Sprinkle with reserved coconut.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour or until firm.
Preheat oven to 350° and grease cookie sheet.
Place shortening, sugars, egg and vanilla in mixing bowl and beat thoroughly.
Sift together salt, flour and soda and add to shortening mixture.
Mix well.
Blend in oats and drop by teaspoons onto cookie sheet.
If you wish, you may also add 1/3 cup chopped nuts, raisins or shredded coconut to the batter.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until slightly brown at the edges.
Makes 5 dozen.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix together Ricotta cheese, spinach, Parmesan cheese and egg until well blended.
Layer 1 cup sauce, 3 noodles, 1 cup Ricotta cheese mixture and part of Mozzarella cheese in 12 x 8-inch baking dish.
Repeat layers twice.
Cover with foil.
Bake 20 minutes; remove foil and bake 15 minutes longer.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cream oleo, sugar, eggs and spices.
Add rest of ingredients and roll into small balls.
Flatten on a cookie sheet.
Bake at 350°.
Fill with filling.

Cook French fries according to package directions. Place fries on a broiler proof dish or platter. Sprinkle with cheese, onions and bacon. Broil for 1 to 2 minutes or until cheese is melted. Serve with Ranch dressing. Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Combine and pour over meatballs. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
In large shallow baking pan, put 1 layer corn chips (not too thick, as it dries out), 1 layer rice and 1 layer hamburger mixture (hamburger, onion, tomato sauce and chili seasoning).
Sprinkle with grated cheese (Cheddar).
Put in oven to melt cheese.
On top, put 1 layer shredded lettuce and 1 layer cherry tomatoes (or cut up whole tomatoes).

Brown ground beef and onion lightly in skillet, stirring until beef is crumbly; drain well. Layer ground beef mixture, green beans and Tater Tots in 9 x 9-inch baking dish. Combine soup and milk in bowl, beating well. Pour over layers. Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours or until brown.
Place chicken breasts in an 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Pour salad dressing over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 minutes.
Place rice, vegetables and 1/2 can Durkee French fried onions around and under chicken.
Combine chicken broth and Italian seasoning and pour the mixture over chicken and vegetables.
Bake, uncovered, 25 minutes.
Top with remaining onions and bake another 2 to 3 minutes.
Melt butter and brown steak.
Add onions and peppers to meat and add all other ingredients except cornstarch.
Cook on low heat 10 to 15 minutes and then thicken with cornstarch.
Serve over rice.

recipes.t: The Ten Minutes, No Fuss, Healthy Lunch
d: In medium bowl, combine the chickpeas, tomatoes, onion and tuna.
Mix olive oil, vinegar and pepper until blended.
Pour over chickpeas-tuna mixture.
Toss.
Serve with bread.
Serves 3 to 4.
Mix all ingredients good.
Roll into a ball, then roll in toasted pecans or almonds.
Can double ingredients for a larger cheese ball.
Combine all ingredients and mix into boiling milk.
Cook a few minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
In small saucepan, melt chocolate with milk over low heat; stir occasionally.
Remove from heat; stir in vanilla.
In large bowl, beat butter with peanut butter and sugar until blended.
Stir in flour and oats until combined.
Measure out 1 cup and set aside. Press remaining oat mixture into pan.
Spread chocolate over. Crumble reserved 1 cup of oat mixture over top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Grease baking dish.
Place bread in bottom of dish, then sprinkle cheese and sausage over it.
Mix eggs, milk, salt, pepper and dry mustard.
Pour over cheese and sausage.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Drain yams.
Add pineapple, white sugar, cinnamon and 1/4 cup melted butter.
Mash until creamy; spread in glass pan.
Pour remaining butter over top of mixture.
Sprinkle with brown sugar. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Combine drained vegetables, onion, cheese, mayonnaise and soup; mix well.
Pour mixture into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Sprinkle crushed crackers over top of casserole.
Return to oven and bake until crumbs are lightly browned.
Beat cream cheese and all other ingredients with electric beater until blended.
Line a margarine tub with foil and pack in mixture.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Turn out on serving plate and peel off foil.
Add dry ingredients together.
Mix shortening and sugar.
Add beaten egg and applesauce.
Fold together with dry ingredients. Bake 10 minutes at 375°.
Makes 3 dozen.
Slice sausage 1/2-inch thick; brown in Dutch oven with olive oil.
Add onion, garlic, carrots and basil; cook 5 minutes.
Add zucchini, tomatoes and beef bouillon.
Simmer 1 hour.
Add Northern beans and cabbage.
Cook 20 to 30 minutes longer.
Place potatoes in a pot.
Cover with water.
Boil until tender (20 to 30 minutes).
Drain and place potatoes in a bowl. Refrigerate until cool.
Cut potatoes in 1/2 to 1-inch pieces.
Salt and pepper fryer.
Mix rice, water, oleo and soup.
Place chicken on top of rice mixture. Bake at 350° for 2 hours, without lifting cover.
Stir all together and put in refrigerator.
Combine all ingredients well.
Cook broccoli until done.
Drain water.
Add soup and sour cream.
Mix well.
Add mushrooms and Stove Top with juice; add onions and 1/2 of each cheese.
Mix well.
Put in buttered casserole dish.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes at 325°.
Mix Cool Whip and jello powder; stir in all remaining ingredients.
Chill well.
Garnish with extra Cool Whip (optional).
Place broccoli in casserole.
Add chicken.
Mix soup, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Pour over broccoli and chicken.
Top with grated cheese and bread crumbs that have been sauteed with butter.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Combine milk, cornstarch, sugar and salt.
Cook over medium heat; stir constantly.
Add beaten eggs; cook until thick.
Remove from heat.
Line bowl with vanilla wafers.
Layer with pudding, wafers and bananas.
Line a cookie sheet with well buttered foil.
Place saltines, side to side, to cover.
Boil together the butter and brown sugar; pour over crackers.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Sprinkle with the chocolate chips; spread with spatula while hot.
They will melt.
You can also add chopped nuts or coconut on top of the chocolate.
Refrigerate for 3 hours.
Break into chunks when chilled.
Store in refrigerator.
Leave skin on potatoes when boiling.
Put in large bowl when boiled and after drained.
Make the following to pour over while potatoes are still warm:
Italian salad dressing, sliced green onions and chopped parsley.
Pour over the warm bite-size potatoes and let set for about 1 hour to marinate.
Toss several times. Then add the mayonnaise.
Toss until completely covered.
Put in fridge for at least 2 hours.
Better to chill overnight so flavors have plenty of time to blend.
Just before serving, garnish with sliced hard-boiled eggs.
Great!
In deep bowl, using mixer, combine cream cheese, sugar and milk.
Add 3/4 cup Bits 'O Brickle; fold in whipped topping.
Spoon into pie crust.
Sprinkle remaining Bits 'O Brickle over filling. Freeze about 4 hours before serving.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Blend first 4 ingredients in bowl.
Beat until smooth.
Pour into greased and floured 12 cup Bundt pan.
Bake in preheated 350° oven 45 minutes or until cake is done.
Cool in pan 25 minutes, then invert onto cooling rack to finish cooling.
Decorate and serve with 1 can cherry pie filling and Cool Whip.
Mix all and have fun.
Cut chicken in bite size pieces.
Combine fat, flour, salt, milk and broth; cook until thickened.
Add mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Cook broccoli; place in bottom of casserole dish.
Combine chicken and sauce.
Pour over broccoli.
Top with bread crumbs. Bake at 350° until well heated and brown.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Heat onion, soups and Ro-Tel in saucepan, then in casserole dish, put layer of chicken, layer of soup mixture, layer of Doritos and top with cheese.
Bake in slow oven until mixture bubbles.
Heat margarine until melted and remove from heat.
Stir in sugar and eggs.
Beat slightly by hand just until combined; stir in flour.
Remove 3/4 c. of batter and set aside.
Stir melted chocolate into remaining batter.
Spread chocolate batter into a greased 9 x 9 x 2 baking pan; set aside.
Stir peanut butter into reserved batter.
Dollop on top of chocolate batter, then sprinkle with chocolate pieces.
Swirl batter with a knife.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 2-quart casserole.
Cook grits in boiling water.
When almost done, crumble cheese and butter into grits.
Blend eggs and milk together.
Then mix egg/milk mixture with grits.
Pour into greased casserole and bake at 350° for 45 minutes, uncovered.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and bake, uncovered, 15 minutes longer or until cheese is melted.
Sift flour, soda and salt; set aside.
Cream Crisco, peanut butter, sugar and brown sugar.
Add milk, egg and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients to mixture.
Shape into balls.
Roll in sugar and place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press down with fork.
Bake at 375° for 8 minutes.
Makes 3 dozen cookies.
Cook macaroni; rinse and drain.
In large saucepan or Dutch oven, combine juices, lemonade and cinnamon sticks.
Bring to boil; reduce heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add water if desired.
Serve hot or cold.
Mix together ground turkey, egg, Stove Top seasoning, onion and Stove Top dressing.
Make small meat balls.
Brown slowly in butter.
Drain.
Add flour to drippings.
Stir until smooth. Remove from heat and add milk and water.
Cook and stir slowly until gravy is smooth.
Add meatballs to gravy.
Simmer 10 minutes. Makes 6 servings.

recipes.t: Country Bread Pudding With Custard Sauce
d: Heat oven to 325°.
Pour melted butter into approximately an 8-cup baking pan and refrigerate.
Place the bread sliced into a large bowl and pour the milk over them, tossing to let the bread absorb most of the milk.
Tear sliced bread into pieces.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Blend cake mix, oil and eggs.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Place by level teaspoons on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Cook noodles following directions on package.
Combine noodles, tuna, mayonnaise, vegetables and salt.
Blend celery soup and milk.
Heat thoroughly in saucepan.
Add cheese to saucepan and stir until cheese is melted; then add to noodle mixture.
Turn into ungreased 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Bake at 425° uncovered for 20 mins. or until bubbly.
Simmer chicken until tender.
Cool and remove from bones.
Cut chicken into bite size pieces. Mix soup and sour cream.
Add chicken and chopped, boiled eggs.

Mix together flour and sugar; set aside. Grease casserole dish. Pour drained pineapple in dish. Add sugar and flour mixture to top of pineapple. Sprinkle cheese over previous layer, then the Ritz crackers. Slice margarine in small pieces and place on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix all together and keep refrigerated.
Drink at least 2 ounces per day.
This will help to keep your cholesterol down as well as help those with arthritis.
Brown pork chops in lightly greased skillet. Sprinkle with seasoned salt and set aside. Combine soup, milk, sour cream, pepper and 1/2 teaspoon seasoned salt.

Stir in partially thawed potatoes and add 1/2 cup cheese and 1/2 can French fried onions. Spoon mixture into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Arrange pork chops over potatoes. Bake, covered, at 350° for 40 minutes. Top with remaining cheese and onions. Bake, uncovered, 5 minutes longer. Serves 6.
Dissolve yeast in milk.
Sift flour and salt.
Cut in shortening.
Add vanilla and yeast mixture.
Add one egg at a time and beat well after each addition.
Place dough in refrigerator overnight.
Soften tortillas by dipping in hot oil for 2-3 seconds, drain on paper towels and set aside.
In medium size bowl mix sour cream, cottage cheese and green chili; set aside.
Grate 1 cup cheese; set aside.
Cut remaining cheese into 24 slender sticks (about 1/2 x 2
inches).
Taking one tortilla shell at a time, place a stick of cheese and a heaping tablespoon of sour cream mixture on it and roll.
Place the rolled tortillas in a 9 x 13 inch casserole dish.
Cover tortillas with enchiladas sauce.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Put potatoes in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour 3 tablespoons melted butter over potatoes.
Mix soup, cheese, sour cream and onion. Pour over potatoes.
Mix corn flakes, 2 tablespoons butter and 1/2 cup grated cheese over top.
Bake 30 minutes at 300° to 325°.
Cover and cook 10 minutes on High.
Roll chicken livers in flour and saute in shortening until brown.
Arrange asparagus in baking dish.
Top with sauce made from mayonnaise, minced onion and chicken livers.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Brown lightly under the broiler.
The chicken livers and sauce may be prepared in advance, if desired.
Simmer onion and celery in margarine.
Add mushroom soup, cheese and 1/2 cup water, heat until cheese melts.
Combine all ingredients in a greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Prepare Rice-A-Roni according to directions, adding a handful of brown rice to make more (optional).
While rice is cooking, skin and debone chicken and cut it in small pieces.
After rice is soft and dry, spread chicken over the top of rice along with the corn (drained); cover dish with no heat for 5 minutes.
Mix and serve.
Applesauce and biscuits go well with this dish.
Brown chops and arrange in baking dish.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Combine soup, water and thyme.
Heat.
Then add parsley, sour cream and 1/2 can of onions.
Blend and spread over the chops. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until tender. Remove cover, put remaining onions on top and bake 5 minutes more.

In a small, heavy saucepan, melt butter with brown sugar and corn syrup over moderate heat, stirring until smooth. Pour into a 13 x 9 x 2 inch baking dish. Cut bread in 1 inch thick slices, arrange slices in one layer in baking dish, squeezing slightly to fit.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Beat eggs in large bowl.
Stir in cake mix, cherry pie filling and oil until blended.
Spread in pan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes. Cool.
Prepare pudding pie filling as directed on package.
Let stand for 5 minutes or until thickened.
Spread over cake. Garnish with Cool Whip and chopped nuts.
Store in refrigerator.
Mix all ingredients together.
Top with Ritz cracker crumbs. Bake at 350° until crumbs brown.
Peel and cut potatoes into chunks.
Boil until soft.
Drain. Add butter and sour cream.
Beat.
Slowly add milk*.
Continue beating.
Shake on cheese.
Add parsley and pepper.
Whip until creamy.
Combine all ingredients.
Roll mixture into 1-inch balls. Place on a greased cookie sheet.
Store in refrigerator.
Split each cream puff in half.
Combine undiluted soup, curry powder and chopped chicken and heat through over low heat.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Fill bottoms of puffs with the hot mixture and replace tops.
Serve at once sprinkled with paprika, if desired.
Makes 36 appetizers.
Melt butter and sharp cheese.
Add flour, cyapepper and Rice Krispies.
Roll into balls and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Dissolve sugar in water in large container.
Add lemon juice, orange juice and pineapple juice.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Serve over crushed ice.
Yield:
34 servings.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat until fluffy.
Make a paste of vinegar and cocoa and add to mixture.
Sift salt and soda with flour.
Add mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Blend well.
Add vanilla and red coloring.
Mix well.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly after each.
Add flour alternately with 3/4 cup sour cream.
Dissolve baking soda in 1/4 cup sour cream; add to batter and blend well.
Add extract and salt.
Stir.
Bake in pan for 1 hour and 5 minutes.
Cool 20 minutes in pan.
Remove and sift powdered sugar over warm cake.
Serves 10 to 12.
Add yeast to warm water; let rest for 10 minutes.
Mix scalded milk, butter, sugar and salt.
Stir until dissolved.
Cool to 85°. Beat 1 egg and add to yeast mixture.
Add to milk mixture.
Beat in half of flour (sifted).
Beat 2 minutes.
Add remaining flour and mix the dough until it blisters.
Place in greased bowl; cover, place in refrigerator.
To bake, form into two loaves.
Let rise for 1 hour before baking.
Mix first 7 ingredients and place in greased casserole. Combine brown sugar, flour, margarine and pecans and sprinkle on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 325°.
In a large bowl, beat eggs until foamy. Beat in flour, sugar and brown sugar until well blended. Blend in melted butter.
Stir in chocolate morsels and walnuts.
Pour into pie shell. Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Remove from oven.
Serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream.
Cook noodles according to directions.
Grate cheese.
In saucepan, melt butter.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add flour, stir to mix.
Add milk, a little at a time, stirring constantly. Continue until you have added all the milk.
Add grated cheese; melt.
Pour over noodles in casserole dish.
Sprinkle with paprika. Cook on 450° until brown.
Let cool about 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake oblong cake as directed.
As soon as cake is removed from oven, drizzle 1/2 cup honey over top.
Sprinkle with 1 cup coconut and slip under broiler a few minutes to toast coconut.
Best when served warm.
Mix sugar and syrup; bring to a rapid boil.
Add peanut butter and stir until well mixed.
Pour over corn flakes and mix well. Drop by spoonful on waxed paper and cool.
Then hide em.
Cream sugar, oleo and Crisco.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating
after
each.
Add
sifted flour and vanilla.
Fold in 7-Up or ginger ale.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 325° in tube pan.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray 2 large cookie sheets with Pam. In large mixing bowl, combine oat bran, oatmeal, flour, baking powder and allspice.
In blender or food processor, combine oil, egg whites, vanilla, honey and brown sugar.
Blend these liquids into dry ingredients.
Drop by teaspoon of batter onto the prepared cookie sheets and bake 12 to 14 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spray baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
In medium bowl, coarsely mash black-eyed peas. Add rice, onion, bread crumbs, mayonnaise dressing, chili powder, cumin and red pepper.
Divide mixture into 8 (1/3 cup) portions. Shape each portion into a 1/2-inch thick patty.
Cut up and fry bacon until crisp.
Drain and crumble.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Trim cauliflower into small florets. Brush a deep ovenproof dish with melted butter or oil.
Place florets in dish.
Heat oil in frying pan.
Add the fresh bread crumbs and toss over medium heat until crisp and golden.
Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from pan and drain on paper towels. Combine tomato pasta sauce.
Pour over cauliflower in prepared dish.
Sprinkle with combined bread crumbs and cheeses.
Sprinkle with extra pepper.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until cauliflower is tender, cheese has melted and top is brown.
Serves 4. Prep time: 20 minutes.
Total cooking time:
20 to 25 minutes.

Place peaches in baking dish. Sprinkle with lemon juice. Combine flour, sugar, & egg until lumpy. Spread over peaches. Pour butter over mixture. Bake at 375 degrees for 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown.
Put fruit &/or pie filling in bottom of pan.
Pour dry cake mix over fruit.
Pour melted oleo over cake mix.
Bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs.
Add dry ingredients and raisins.
Bake at 350° to 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except pimentos.
Boil slowly for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Add pimentos; boil for 5 minutes more. Pack into jars and seal.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
To this hot mixture, add fruit.
Place half of mixture in oblong dish.
Place in refrigerator and let set.
Then spread evenly and thinly 1/2 pint sour cream.
Spread remaining half of jello mixture and let set.
Mix celery soup, chicken soup and milk; heat.
Add rice to soup mix.
Put
into
greased
9 x 13-inch pan and top with pork chops or
chicken
with
1	package dried onion soup mix. Cover with tinfoil and bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients. Bake in an iron skillet at 350° for 40 minutes or until brown.
After cream cheese has softened, put in a blender or mixer and add each additional ingredient.
Keep refrigerated.
Soften cream cheese and mix with pepper and pimientos.
Stuff mixture into hollow of celery stalk.
Mix first 7 ingredients together and mold into a loaf in baking dish or pan.
Place celery and carrots along sides and at ends of meat loaf.	Salt vegetables and add water; cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for about 2 hours or until done.
Place meaty spareribs in a pan under your broiler until brown on both sides.
Transfer the ribs to a deeper pan and cover with barbecue sauce.
Cover with a tight lid and bake at 350° for 2 to 2 1/2 hours or until tender.
Day 1:	Peel and seed chunk cucumbers to make 8 quarts. Cut into chunks and soak 24 hours in
2 cups lime mixed with 8 quarts cool water.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour loaf pan(s).
Measure all ingredients into a large mixer bowl; beat on medium speed 1/2 minute.
Pour into pan(s).
Bake 55 to 65 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Remove from pan(s).
Cool thoroughly before slicing.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Brown ground beef and onion; drain. Stir in salt. Spread into 9 inch pie plate. Sprinkle with cheese. Stir milk, eggs and Bisquick mix with fork until blended. Pour on top of ground beef and cheese. Bake at 400 degrees for 25 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Chop onion and pickle very small. Mix all ingredients together. Chill.
Put in blender and mix well.
Serve with assorted vegetables.
Melt almond bark.
Add dry ingredients.
Drop by the spoonful on wax paper.
Cream together shortening, sugar, eggs and vanilla. Sift together flour and cream of tartar; add.
Mix together, then roll into small balls. Roll them into cinnamon and sugar mixture. Makes about 5 or 6 dozen.
Bake at 350° for 5 to 7 minutes.
Beat together orange juice concentrate and milk until frothy. Add vanilla pudding.
Beat for 1 minute (should thicken).
Blend in sour cream until smooth.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. Good luck!
Melt oleo.
Saute onion and bell pepper in oleo until tender. Empty the 2 cans of hominy, draining one and draining 1/2 of the other can.
Mix in with the onion and bell pepper mixture.
Stir in Cheez Whiz and pimento until melted and mixed well.
Pour into casserole dish.
Bake until bubbly.
Soften gelatin in water.
Stir over hot water until dissolved. Add all remaining ingredients except apple.
Chill until mixture begins to thicken.
Fold in apples.
Spoon into individual molds or small ring mold and chill until firm.
Makes about 2 1/2 cups, 4 servings.
Shred lettuce and put into a large bowl.
Cut into strips the chicken, ham and cheese; arrange over lettuce.
Top with thinly sliced eggs and scatter over with onions.
Preheat oven
to
Roll out the pastry and line a 10-inch pie
dish.	Combine
the
corn
syrup
and	sugar in a saucepan and
bring to a boil.
Cool, stirring, just until the sugar is dissolved.
Beat the eggs in mixing bowl and gradually add the syrup and sugar.
Add the remaining ingredients and pour the
mixture
into the pie shell.
Bake 50 minutes to one hour or until the pie is set.
Serves 8.
Cut pickles in small pieces.
Grate onion.
Mix ingredients in large mixing bowl.
Beat until well blended (use electric mixer for best results).
Chill.
Mix graham cracker crumbs, pecans, marshmallows and dates together.
Add milk gradually until mixture is moist enough to stick together and roll in logs. Roll logs in graham cracker crumbs.
Place logs in aluminum foil and refrigerate.
Freezes well.
In margarine, saute bell pepper, onion, Worcestershire sauce and hot pepper sauce.
Add soup and water.
Blend shrimp and wild rice into soup mixture.
Add water chestnuts.
Put in large ovenproof casserole dish and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Spoon coffee ice cream into pie crust, spreading evenly. Freeze until firm.
Place candy in plastic bag.
Crush with rolling pin, mallet or hammer.
Spread fudge topping evenly over coffee ice cream.
Sprinkle with 1 cup of crushed candy.
Spoon butter pecan ice cream over, spreading evenly.
Freeze until firm, 2 hours.
Garnish with fresh whipped cream-rosettes around edge of pie.
Put remaining candy in middle.
Delicious!
Mix all ingredients, except peaches.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Pour mix over melted butter.
Add sliced peaches; sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve with or without vanilla ice cream.
Peel and cube eggplant and boil until tender.
Soak bread in milk.
Drain eggplant, add bread and milk mixture.
Mix well. Stir in beaten eggs, onion, salt and pepper.
Place in well buttered casserole dish.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix meat, rice, 1/2 cup water, the onion, salts, garlic powder and pepper.
Shape mixture by rounded tablespoonfuls into balls.
Place meatballs in an ungreased baking dish (8 x 8 x 2-inch).
Cook first 5 ingredients until tender.
Add soup and chopped Velveeta.
Stir constantly until the cheese is melted.
Cream the cheese with mayonnaise and add remaining ingredients; blend together.
Use whole wheat bread for a great tasting treat.
Mix everything except pecans well.
Add pecans; pour into 9-inch unbaked pie shell and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt oleo in 8-inch square pan.
Stir in flour and pecans and beat in bottom of pan to form crust.
Bake at 350° until lightly brown.
Peel and mash ripe avocado pulp.
Add remaining ingredients. Serve as a salad, heaped on tomato slices, or as a dip for chips.
Mix sugar, salt, syrup and milk in a saucepan.
Cook slowly until a boil is reached.
Continue cooking until a soft ball forms when a bit is dropped in cold water.
Or use a candy thermometer, cooking to 260°.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Add sherbet and allow to melt.
Add drained fruit and sliced bananas.
Chill.
Serves 12.

recipes.t: Creamy Cheese Soup(Debbie Loves My Cheese Soup.)
d: Put milk in a double boiler and cook on medium heat.
Melt oleo (this can be done in microwave) and add flour to oleo.
Mix well, then stir into hot milk.
Add cheese, ham and carrots and cook for 20 minutes.
Do not let double boiler boil dry!
Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Beat butter in large bowl until creamy. Add banana and peanut butter; beat until smooth.
Blend in egg, apple juice concentrate and vanilla.
Beat in flour, baking soda and salt.
Stir in chopped peanuts.
Drop rounded tablespoonfuls of dough, 2 inches apart, onto lightly greased cookie sheets.
Top each with one peanut, if desired.
Bake for 8 minutes, or until set.
Cool completely on wire rack.
Store in tightly covered container.
Makes 2 dozen.
Grease potatoes and bake for 1 1/2 hours at 350° or until done.
Brown hamburger meat and mix with taco seasoning mix according to package directions.
(Be sure meat is drained.)
In a double boiler or microwave, melt Velveeta cheese mixed with Ro-Tel tomatoes.
Stir frequently.
To serve, slice hot potato and lightly fluff.
Layer taco meat, cheese mixture, sour cream, green onions and salt and pepper to taste.
Yield:
4 to 6 servings.
Mix ingredients in bowl.
Spread on tortillas.
Fold tortilla and dampen edges.
Cook in oven at 350 about 15 minutes in greased pan.
For bottom layer, stir together first 4 ingredients and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Stir in 6 tablespoons melted butter.
Pat in a 11 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix and put in greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Heat oil in large skillet on medium high heat.
Add chicken, onion and pepper.
Cook and stir until chicken is cooked through. Add corn, broth and salsa; bring to boil.
Stir in rice and cover. Remove from heat.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Sprinkle with cheese.
Let stand 2 minutes. Serve.
Saute onion in margarine until tender. Mix all ingredients together and put in casserole dish. Cover tightly with foil.
Note:
For a fuller pie use the 4 cups of apples, 6 ounces juice and 1 tablespoon cornstarch.
Other ingredients remain the same or can be adjusted to suit your taste.
Cream butter, potatoes and sugar.
Add eggs, milk, nutmeg and vanilla.
Sift baking powder with flour.
Stir in mixture and add more flour to make a soft dough.
Roll 1/4-inch thick; cut and deep-fry.
Drain on paper towels.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Brown ground beef.
Combine with all other ingredients in a crock-pot.
Heat on low for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Dip chicken in buttermilk.
Combine flour, cornmeal, salt and pepper in a grocery sack.
Place chicken in bag, 3 pieces at a time, and shake until well coated.
Mix well and let stand several hours.
Use with a variety of fresh vegetables.
Mix first 5
ingredients together.
Mix next 3 ingredients together to make
dressing.
Pour dressing over salad and let set for at least 2 to 3 hours before serving.
Beat eggs until lemon colored.
Add flour, baking powder, salt, cottage cheese, shredded Jack cheese and melted butter.
Blend smoothly and stir in chilies.
Pour mix into well-greased 9-inch square dish.
Bake in 350° preheated oven 35 minutes or until top is lightly brown and center appears firm.
Cut in squares and serve hot.
Serve with coarsely chopped and sauteed red pepper and green onions.
Accompany with bran muffins.
Cream together shortening, sugar, brown sugar and peanut butter.
Mix together milk, vanilla and egg.
Sift together plain flour, salt and soda.
Mix all ingredients, gradually adding flour mixture.
Shape into balls about the size of a quarter and roll in white sugar.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes. Take out and press a chocolate kiss on top and bake about 1 to 2 minutes longer.
Break bread into small pieces in bowl.
Add remaining ingredients.
Beat until well mixed.
Pour into nonstick muffin cups.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Yields 4 servings.
Mix and bake at 350° for 30 or 35 minutes in loaf pan.
Brown chops in oil; drain.
Place chops in baking dish and top with lemon slices.
Mix catsup, vinegar, water and sugar.
Pour over chops.
Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes or more. Serves 4 to 6.
Can prepare ahead of time and be baked when ready to serve.
Scrub unpeeled potatoes well.
Cut each potato in half lengthwise.
Then cut into even wedges.
Boil potato wedges for 5 minutes in salted water.
Drain.
Pat dry.
Spread wedges in a single layer on a lightly greased baking sheet.
Sprinkle with oil, spices and herbs.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 425° to 450° for another 10 to 12 minutes, or until potatoes are golden brown and cheeses are melted.
Brown salt pork in 3-quart saucepan.
Add onions and saute until they begin to turn yellow.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes, creamed corn and frozen corn; reduce heat and simmer for 35 minutes.
Add salt, pepper, milk and butter; simmer for 5 minutes and serve.
Boil sugar, milk and butter to soft ball stage.
Add peanut butter, salt and vanilla.
Cool to lukewarm.
Beat until it's ready to set.
Spray mold with Pam.
In a saucepan, heat soup, stirring in cheese until smooth.
Dissolve gelatin with water; add to soup mixture.
Add remaining ingredients and blend well.
Pour into mold and chill overnight.
Serves 45.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Beat in molasses, egg and vinegar. Stir flour with spices and salt, then blend with batter.
Chill 3 hours.
Roll out to 1/8-inch and cut with cookie cutters.
Bake at 375° for 5 to 6 minutes.
Frost or leave plain.
Enjoy!
In casserole dish, layer pineapple and cream cheese.
In double boiler, mix flour, sugar, egg and juice.
Cook until thick. Pour over pineapple and cream cheese.
Top with marshmallows. Cook in 350° oven for 15 minutes or until it bubbles good.
Heat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in large saucepan over low heat.
Blend in flour and seasonings.
Cook over low heat, stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly.
Remove from heat. Stir in broth and cream.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute.
Stir in wine, spaghetti, chicken and mushrooms.

recipes.t: Last Of The Garden Green Tomato Chow
d: Grind first 6 ingredients together.
Add salt.
Let stand 2 or 3 hours.
Drain and rinse well.
Add celery seed, mustard seed, sugar and vinegar; mix well.
(No cooking.) Put in jars.
Keep in refrigerator.
Drain Veg-All and mix with other ingredients.
Top with oleo and crackers.
Bake 15 minutes at 375°.
Cream together margarine, cream cheese and powdered sugar. Blend together milk, vanilla, instant pudding and Cool Whip.
Mix both mixtures together.
Crush up Oreos in a blender.
Layer crushed cookies and mixture.
Start with cookies and end with cookies.
You can layer this in a plastic flowerpot and add silk flower in the top.
You can also add gummy worms in the layers or on top, if desired.
Heat oven to 350° (375° for high altitude).
Brown meat and onion.
Drain.
Spoon into ungreased 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Stir in taco seasoning, tomato sauce and corn.
Sprinkle cheese over top.
Stir remaining ingredients until blended.
Pour over beef mixture.
Bake 35 minutes, until lightly browned.
Serve with sour cream, chopped tomato and shredded lettuce.
Arrange washed, dried chicken pieces in a large casserole dish.
Pour Ragu sauce over top, covering pieces well.
Sprinkle Parmesan on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until chicken is very well done.
Serve over hot, buttered spaghetti or fettucine.
Mix all ingredients.
Form into 1-inch balls on greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix dry pudding, Cool Whip and pineapple and juice until well blended. Stir in apples, marshmallows and peanuts or candy bars until thoroughly combined.
Refrigerate until served. Best if eaten within 24 hours. Tastes like a caramel apple.
Microwave sausage and onion, uncovered, in a shallow, 2-quart casserole on High for 4 to 5 minutes, or until sausage is no longer pink.
Stir twice during cooking.
Remove sausage and onion from dish with slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.
Add potatoes to the casserole with the sausage drippings and microwave, covered, until potatoes are cooked, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in 1/4 teaspoon salt and spread potatoes evenly in the dish.
Combine eggs, milk, remaining salt and pepper in a 2-cup measure.
Pour evenly over potatoes.
Mix sausage mixture with thyme and sage in a small bowl and sprinkle over potatoes. Microwave, uncovered on High for 3 minutes.
Lift eggs at edge with spatula to distribute uncooked portion of egg mixture evenly. Do not stir potatoes and sausage.
Microwave, uncovered, at 50% power (Medium) until eggs are almost set, about 8 to 10 minutes. Give dish a 1/4 turn twice during cooking.
Serves 4.
Saute minced onion and green pepper in butter to soften.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Grate first two cheeses and mix with other ingredients.
Make rolls or balls and roll in chili powder and chopped pecans.
Combine all ingredients.
Cool and chill.
At serving time, add:
Mix cake mix according to directions on package.
Fill cupcake pans 2/3 full.
Cream the cheese with sugar, salt and egg; stir in chocolate pieces.
Drop one rounded teaspoon cheese mixture into each cupcake.
Bake as package directs.
When cool, frost with any white buttercream frosting.
Makes 30 cupcakes.
These cupcakes freeze well.
Grate ham or Spam.
Mix with cream cheese.
Add chopped olives, onions, lemon juice, thyme and Worcestershire sauce.
Mix well.
Chill.
Serve on black bread or assorted crackers.
Mix both soups, chunk chicken and Veg-All together.
Pour in casserole dish.
Mix Bisquick, milk and butter.
Pour over chicken mixture and bake 1 hour at 375°.
Melt oleo; add sugars and small amount of milk.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Add corn meal and remaining milk. Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes, then 325° for 30 minutes longer.
Mix all of the ingredients together.
Pour into individual molds.
Chill until firm.
Brown hamburger, onion and green pepper.
Cook noodles according to directions on package.
Drain and mix all ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Use jelly roll pan.
Grease and flour pan.
Whip eggs until thick and foamy.
Add sugar gradually to eggs.
Fold in pumpkin and lemon juice. Sift together all dry ingredients and fold into egg mixture, beating just until batter is smooth (can use electric mixer, low speed).
Pour into pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 375° or until cake springs back when touched lightly.
Immediately loosen cake from edges of pan; invert on towel sprinkled with confectioners sugar.
While hot, roll cake and towel from narrow end.
Cool completely on wire rack.
Coat chicken with flour, salt and pepper; brown well in shortening.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Blend any remaining flour mixture with tomatoes; add Heinz 57 sauce, Parmesan cheese, sugar and oregano.
Pour over chicken.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove cover; top with cheeses.
Bake, uncovered, 25 minutes longer or until chicken is tender.
Skim excess fat from sauce.
Preheat oven at 400°.
Trim crust from bread.
Cut loaf of bread in half lengthwise, then into 8 equal crosswise slices.
Combine butter and garlic; mix well.
Spread on all sides of each 8-inch slice.
Arrange on 15 x 12-inch cookie sheet.
Sprinkle with seed.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Mix all together.
I knead it with hands like bread, as it is stiff.
Form into balls (roll in palm of hands), smaller than walnuts.
Melt together in double boiler 3/4 of 1 block paraffin wax.
Roll balls in chocolate mixture and put on wax paper lined cookie sheet.
I use ice tea spoon with long handle to get them out of double boiler.
If they stick to pan, you can pull them free by pushing them off wax paper by putting your hand under wax paper. Sounds harder than it is.
Makes about 60 to 70.
You will also need baking pans or large foil pans.
Mix jello with 1 cup boiling water.
Add frozen strawberries and stir until separated.
Add drained crushed pineapple and nuts. Put 1/2 mixture in bowl and set in refrigerator 10 to 15 minutes (until slightly gelled).
Remove from refrigerator and spread with sour cream.
Pour remaining jello on top and return to refrigerator.
(Should remaining jello gel, place bowl in warm water and stir until slightly thin.)
Preheat oven to 375°.
Coat 18 (2 3/4-inch) muffin tin cups with vegetable cooking spray; set aside.
Toss first 2 ingredients together and refrigerate overnight. Add remaining ingredients (except shrimp). Refrigerate.
Just before serving, toss in shrimp meat.

Heat oil. Add beef and onion, saute until meat is browned. Add tomatoes. Season to taste with salt, pepper, and paprika. Add bay leaf. Pour in stock, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours or until beef is tender.
Cream butter and sugar.
Beat in 1 egg at a time until 3 have been used.
Then add some flour.
Add 2 more eggs and rest of flour.
Then add buttermilk and blackberries. Bake in loaf pan at 300° to 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Combine cake mix, oleo, evaporated milk and chopped nuts. Press 1/2 of the mixture into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 6 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Pour melted Caramel Sauce over top. Crumble remaining cake mixture over and bake for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cover beans with water plus 2 inches more.
Soak beans 10 to 12 hours.
Put in slow cooker.
Add water to cover beans plus 2 inches more and add chili mix, garlic and onion.
After 4 to 5 hours cooking, add liquid smoke and hot sauce.
When beans are done, add salt.
Do not heat beans in microwave as they get hard.
Drain juice off cocktail and add water to make almost 2 cups. Put jello in and add Coke.
Place in refrigerator and let almost jel.
Pour in pecans and fruit cocktail.
Set in refrigerator until jelled.
In a greased sheet cake pan, spread pie filling.
Spread pineapple on top of pie filing.
Spread cake mix on top of pineapple.
Melt butter and pour over mixture.
Spread nuts and coconut on top.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix sausage, eggs, crumbs, salt and poultry seasoning.
Melt cranberry sauce and mustard.
Mix with meatballs.
Serve warm.
Mix ingredients together.
Put into a greased (Pam) 9-inch pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Shake flour in oven bag; place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Add water, lemon juice, garlic and dill to bag.
Squeeze bag to blend ingredients.
Add fish fillets to bag. Turn bag to coat fish with sauce.
Arrange fish in an even layer; dot with margarine.
Close bag with nylon tie; cut 6 half-inch slits in top.
Bake until fish is tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine ingredients in large bowl, folding together until blended.
Spoon into decorative serving bowl.
Chill.
Makes 12 to 14 servings.
Preparation time: 5 minutes.
Chill time: 30 minutes.
Mix and refrigerate until chilled; roll in balls.
Put 4 pecan halves to make legs.
Bake on greased cookie sheet at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes or until brown.
In a mixing bowl, beat egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form.

Gradually add sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time. After all sugar is added gradually add salt and vanilla. Beat until stiff peaks form and all the sugar is dissolved about 5 to 8 minutes. Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto greased baking sheet. Bake at 300° for 30 minutes or until lightly browned. Cool on baking sheet. Once cooled, remove and store in airtight container. Yield: 4 dozen.
Cook rice in water with oleo until water is evaporated. Cook broccoli
with
onion, celery and green pepper until half done. Do
not overcook; drain, reserving juice.
Mix together broccoli and
rice,
add mushroom soup and 1 can of juice from cooked broccoli.
Put
in
greased
Pyrex casserole, top with Velveeta cheese
and bake in 350° oven until hot and cheese is melted.
Mix egg, milk and poultry seasoning in bowl and set aside. Mix flour, dressing mix, salt, pepper and Accent in large bowl with fitted cover (or gallon Ziploc bag).
Heat 2 cups oil on stove in large frying pan.
Dip chicken strips in egg mixture and then in flour mixture and fry until golden brown, turning once.
Brown beef, onion and bell pepper; drain.
Cook tomatoes, rice and Italian seasoning; let it go to boiling.
Turn down heat; cover and let it simmer until rice is tender.
Mix with beef. Pour into baking pan or dish.
Top with shredded Cheddar cheese and melt in a 350° oven.
Great.
Scrub potatoes; peel onion and melt 2 tablespoons butter in glass baking dish.
Slice potatoes and onion.
Alternate layers of each onto melted butter.
Top with 1 tablespoon butter.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cover with Saran Wrap and microwave 10 minutes (or until potatoes are tender.)
This may also be fixed inside foil and placed on grill just prior to cooking hamburgers.
Prepare pizza dough.
Spread in round pizza pan.
Place pizza dough in oven to rise about 5 to 10 minutes; dough should not be moist at this time.
Layer the following items in this order: refried beans, hamburger (browned), Cheddar cheese and Mozzarella cheese.

Cook on low heat until rice is done.
Stir several times during cooking.
Heat milk in one pan.
Heat tomatoes, tomato soup, butter, flour (mix first in some of the tomatoes) and salt in another pan. When hot, add pinch of soda.
When both milk and tomato mixture are hot, mix together.
Cream butter, shortening and sugar until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each one.
Combine flour and baking powder.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk.
Stir in flavorings.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours in a 10-inch tube pan.
Melt margarine in baking dish or pan.
Mix flour, sugar and milk together.
Pour over melted margarine.
Add vanilla to sweetened fruit.
Pour over batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut orange into eighths, and pierce with whole cloves.
Put all ingredients in a crock-pot.
Cover.
Cook one hour on high, then four hours on low.

Can be doubled for a six-quart crock-pot.
Bake French fries as directed on package.
Fry bacon; pinch into small pieces.

Place back in oven until cheese is melted.

recipes.t: Fresh Corn And Tomatoes With Curry
d: Shuck the corn.
With knife, cut kernels off cobs.
There should be about 2 1/2 cups.
Core the tomatoes and cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Melt butter into skillet.
Add the scallions and curry powder.
Cook, stirring briefly, until wilted.
Add the corn, tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Stir and cook for 4 minutes over medium to high heat.
Do not overcook.
Serve hot.
Sprinkle with coriander.
Yields 4 servings.
Chop pepper, celery and onion.
Cook until done, then add pork and beans, catsup and brown sugar.
Combine first 10 ingredients in punch bowl.
Float sherbet in punch.
Mix jello according to directions.
Beat in cream cheese.
Add pineapple after draining.
Add nuts, if you want.
Sprinkle marshmallow topping on top.
Chill until firm.
Any flavor of jello and fruit combination could be substituted.
*Add more if desired.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add vinegar, lemon juice, water, butter or oleo.
Cook on low heat until thickened, stirring.
Add beaten yolks and cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Cool.
Refrigerate.
Cream sugar with shortening.
Add three eggs, one at a time, beating between each addition.
Add soda, salt, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg and pumpkin.
Add flour and beat well.
Cook in a greased and floured tube or Bundt pan for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix melted oleo and graham cracker crumbs in a bowl.
Then press into 13 x 9 x 2-inch bowl or pan.
Combine softened cream cheese (8 ounces and 3 ounces) milk and vanilla in a medium bowl. Beat until smooth.
Spread the following in order over crust: cream cheese mixture, whipped topping and cherry pie filling. Chill several hours.
Cut into squares to serve.
Cover bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan with rice; add broth plus water if needed.
Layer chicken over rice.
Mix soup, sour cream and poppy seed.
Pour over chicken.
Top with crushed Ritz crackers.
Pour melted butter over top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix first 4 ingredients and microwave until cheese is melted. Spread mixture on muffin halves.
Bake in 350° oven until slightly brown.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake in skillet on top of stove, slowly, until done.

Mix oil, sugar and chicken flavor packet in microwavable bowl for 1 minute in microwave. Add vinegar and stir well. Just before serving, mix first 4 ingredients together. Add Ramen noodles by breaking them up in mixture. Do not cook noodles. Pour the dressing mixture over and stir well. Serve immediately.
Mix Jell-O as directed on package. When it begins to set, add rest of the ingredients. Mix well. Let set. Serve on lettuce with mayonnaise and crackers.
Cook sugar, water, corn syrup and food coloring to very hard crack stage (300°).
Add oil of cinnamon; stir slightly to mix in oil.
Pour onto well-greased cookie sheet, cool.
Crack into pieces.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Melt butter with 1 cup of milk.
Let sugar and remaining milk come to a boil, then add other ingredients and stir until thick.
Make pudding according to directions.
Cool slightly.
Pour into cake mix; add eggs and blend well.
Pour into well-greased 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Sprinkle on butterscotch chips and nuts generously.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes or until done. This is a time saving recipe.
Scrub potatoes and grease with corn oil.
Bake for 5 minutes in microwave or 20 minutes in 400° oven.
Test with fork for tenderness.
Wrap in foil and set aside.
Mix Cheddar cheese, flour, salt and cayenne pepper.
Add egg whites.
Shape into small balls and roll in fine cracker crumbs. Fry in deep oil at 375° until golden.
Serve hot.

Heat butter and oil in heavy, large skillet over medium-high heat until butter is melted.

Add scallops.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, covered, for 4 to 5 minutes, or until scallops are opaque. Stir in remaining parsley; season to taste with salt and pepper. Pour over spaghetti; toss gently to mix.

Brown beef, celery and onions.
Drain off excess fat.
Mix in mushrooms, water chestnuts, bamboo shoots and soy sauce. Dissolve bouillon cubes in hot water; stir in mushroom soup.
Add to beef mixture.
Stir in rice.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 6 to 8.
Delicious.
Mix
ingredients
well	and
roll into small meatballs. Let 1/2
wedge of lard or some Crisco melt in frying pan.
Put in meatballs, let brown on all sides and remove.
Cook potatoes in broth.
Chop celery and add.

The potatoes must be very well cooked, otherwise soup will be gluey.
Put scalded milk in breadcrumbs.
Add 4 egg yolks, sugar, butter and grated rind of lemon.
Bake in 325° oven for 35 minutes.
Beat egg whites into confectioners sugar until stiff. Spread over bread pudding to seal.
Set into a 350° oven for 12 to 14 minutes or until golden brown.
In a large pot, put potatoes and water. Bring to rolling boil. Add salt, pepper, celery salt and onion flakes.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then add butter or margarine. Cook until potatoes are tender.

Let cool, then refrigerate.

Boil water, vinegar and salt (not iodize) for 3 minutes. Pour over pickles while hot.

Let stand for 4 to 6 weeks before use.
Cut butter and cream cheese into flour until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Work with hands to form ball.
Cover and chill 1 hour.
On floured surface, roll half into 11-inch circle.
Cut into rounds with 2-inch floured cutter.
Spread each round with about 1/2 teaspoon of cheese spread.
Top with a few shrimp.
Fold in half and seal.
Put the cereal in a large bowl.
Bring sugar, syrup and oleo to a boil; boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter; stir thoroughly and pour over flakes.
Mix. Spread in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Once the fat has been removed from the chicken, place the chicken in ovenware container.
Season.
Add lemon juice and the chicken broth.
Garnish with paprika.
Cover and cook in oven at 350° for about 40 minutes.
Combine cake mix, fruit cocktail with syrup, 1 cup of coconut and eggs in large mixer bowl.
Blend, then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until cake springs back when lightly touched.
Cook macaroni, omitting salt.
Drain well; rinse in cold water.
Combine the next 4 ingredients and the cooked macaroni.
Cream Crisco, sugar, brown sugar, vanilla and egg in large bowl at medium speed of electric mixer.
Mix all ingredients in a blender, except oil. After all is well blended, add oil very slowly. Blend until thick.
Delicious.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Double recipe for 4 or more people.
Mix with hands, the first 5 ingredients.
Remove 2 cups of crumbs and set aside.
Mix remaining crumbs with boiling water, molasses and baking soda.
Pour into ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

Bake 40 minutes at 375° in loaf pan.

of

recipes.t: Golden Glazed Ham With Cherry Sauce

Heat in a 325° oven for time indicated on label.
One-half hour before end of time, remove ham from oven and score fat in diamonds.
Mix together Cool Whip, cream cheese, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Pour 1/2 of mixture into each pie shell.
Pour 1/2 pie filling on top of each mixture and swish around until white shows through, making swirls.
Refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease (with extra amount of softened butter) and lightly flour a 10-inch tube pan.
Set aside.
Combine the butter and cream cheese in a large mixing bowl.
Beat mixture with an electric mixer until well blended and creamy for 2 minutes.
Gradually add sugar while continuing to beat on medium speed.
Beat until the mixture is light and fluffy for 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating after the addition of each egg until it is thoroughly absorbed.
Sift together the flour, salt and baking powder.
Slowly add this combination to the egg mixture, blending well.
Stir in the coconut flavoring and vanilla flavoring, then the flaked coconut.
Beat well for 1 minute.
Cut potato into quarters lengthwise and dry with a paper towel.
Coat all over with the oil.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Place in a nonstick pan or a Pam sprayed pan and bake at 450° for 20 minutes or until done.
In large saucepan, boil chicken broth and onions.
String beaten egg while stirring.
Add salt and pepper.
Add cornstarch mixture to thicken.
Continue to boil until thickened.
Add corn, if desired.
Serve in bowls.

Let cool.
Add peas, corn, celery, onion, green pepper and pimiento.
Let chill overnight.

Boil 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Stir in peanut butter, vanilla and oatmeal. Drop on waxed paper.

Crush vanilla wafers and chop nuts.
Combine with sugar and cocoa.
Stir in corn syrup and rum.
Wet hands and form mixture into balls (small).
Roll in chocolate sprinkles.
Freeze on flat tray.
When firm put into container.
Marinate 3 hours.
Add one large head of lettuce.
Sprinkle on more Parmesan cheese.
In large bowl, combine flour, 1/4 cup sugar, baking powder and salt.
Using pastry blender or 2 knives, cut in 1/3 cup butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in chocolate chips. Add milk; stir until dough holds a shape.
On floured board, knead dough lightly.
Roll dough into 16 balls.
Cut apples into chunks, but do not peel.

Cover and cook over medium-high heat until apples are very soft, about 30 minutes. Press through a food mill or fine sieve and return to the cleaned pot.
Stir in sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until very thick, about 2 hours.

Add the dry ingredients and mix well.
Add the nuts and cranberries to the mixture.

Cream confectioners sugar and cream cheese in bowl until light and fluffy.
Blend in chocolate and vanilla.
Add walnuts; mix well.
Pour into buttered 8-inch dish.
Chill until firm.
Cut into squares.

Add mushrooms; cook until tender, about 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cook 3 minutes more.
Return shrimp to skillet.
Heat through.
Sprinkle with parsley.

Serve hot with tortilla chips or vegetable dippers.

Mix all ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle on onions towards end.

Mix ingredients, adding eggs one at a time.
Bake in loaf pan at 350° for 30 minutes.
Grease 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan with margarine.
Put coconut and pecans in margarine covered pan.

Pour cake mix over pecan mixture.

Pour over cake mix.
Now bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.

Cover with foil.

Saute until mushrooms are cooked.

Roll over and continue adding, then rolling, pinching each end.

Add chicken.
Refrigerate covered for 30 to 60 minutes.

Add egg, blending thoroughly.
Let cool. Add potatoes to flour-egg mixture and blend well.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Flour hands lightly, shape mixture into tablespoon-size balls.

Pour oil into a deep fryer or large saucepan and heat to 375°.

Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.
