Bake at 350° uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large skillet, brown chops.
Drain on absorbent paper.
In buttered, oblong baking dish, arrange chops, potatoes and mushrooms on top.
In a small bowl, combine water and soup mix.
Pour over other ingredients in baking dish.
Put tater tots in bottom of pan. Brown ground chuck, drain. Put over
tots. Pour soup in layers over ground chuck in any order. Spread cheese and put over soup. Bake at 350 degrees, until bubbly about 30 minutes.
Cut broccoli flowerets into smaller than bite-size pieces. Cut off tough outer layer of stalks and chop the tender part into small pieces.
You need 8 cups of broccoli.
(Do this the day before and store in plastic bag.)
Saute bacon until crisp.
Slice onion lengthwise.
In large bowl, combine the broccoli, onion and raisins and bacon.
In small bowl, mix together mayonnaise, sugar, vinegar and pepper.
Combine dressing with the vegetables; refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
Top with sunflower seeds.
Step 1:
In a large skillet, brown ground beef and onion. Drain.
Remove from skillet.
Set aside.
Mix all ingredients together in bowl and pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Double recipe makes 3 pies.
Extract juice from strawberries.
Combine dry ingredients for cake, then add others.
Pour into greased pans.
Bake at 350°.
Take the cubed steak and set it into the pan (with Crisco) on medium-low.
While steak is cooking, chop the veggies into fine pieces and place them in a bowl (with the cheese).
When the meat is done, put it in with the veggies.
Put the whole jar of Ragu into the pan (simmer with a little bit of water).
Cream sugar and butter, add egg and vanilla. Mix thoroughly. Sift dry ingredients together and stir into first mixture. Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Divide dough in half and roll out on lightly floured pastry sheet.
Roll thin but thick enough to pick up the design in the cookie cutters.
Dip cutter in flour before each cutting.
Cut as many cookies from each rolling as possible.
The least amount of working with the dough gives the best cookie.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake for 7 to 8 minutes or until delicately golden.
Mix all ingredients and beat for 3 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Dissolve all ingredients, except beets; bring to boil.
Add diced or sliced beets until warm.
Put in sterile bottles and seal.
Cold pack 10 minutes.
Combine the sugar, cornstarch, jello, lemon juice and water. Cook until it becomes thick, stirring occasionally.
Allow to cool.
Put berries in pie shell; pour thickened mixture on top. Chill for at least 3 hours.
Serve with whipped topping; garnish with halves or whole berries.
Beat egg
whites
stiff
and add sugar; then add baking powder, vanilla, pecans and crackers.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake
at 350° for 25 minutes.
When cool prepare Dream Whip
as directed on box.
Mix with cream cheese and pineapple
and
spread
over
dessert;
refrigerate.
Will keep several days.
Blend all ingredients in bottom of an 8 x 12-inch baking dish. Add chicken. Cover and marinate in refrigerator for 8 to 10 hours. Turn at least once in marinade.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Baste with pan juices and serve over rice.

recipes.t: Apricot-Blueberry Coffee Cake(A Favorite Of Family And Friends)
d: Combine cake mix, pudding, eggs, oil and sour cream; beat well by hand; add blueberries and apricots.
Combine sugar, cinnamon and nuts; set aside.
Grease and flour a tube pan.
Pour 1/2 of the cake mixture into pan.
Sprinkle with 1/2 of the sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Add the remaining cake mixture, then the remaining sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour. Yields 12 to 14 servings.
Combine cheese, milk, onion, Worcestershire, lemon juice and spices.
Stir in crab.
Halve English muffins with a fork.
Cut halves into fourths and pile each wedge high with crab mixture. Place on baking sheet; dust with paprika and broil until lightly browned and bubbly.
Makes about 40.
Mix together first three ingredients, then add the coconut, pecans and raisins.
Stir well, then add vinegar.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake 40 minutes at 300°.
Blend cornstarch, mustard and salt into ham drippings.
Add water, sugar and raisins.
Cook and stir until clear and slightly thickened.
Blend into vinegar and lemon juice.
Makes 3 cups.
Make 24 hours before serving.
Use large casserole or large glass pan.
Shred or tear lettuce into dish, approximately 1/3 full.
Layer on top of the following (do not stir): green peas, green pepper, celery, red onion.
Frost entire top with the following mixture:
mayonnaise, sour cream and sugar.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Right before serving, sprinkle with bacon.

In a mixing bowl, beat peanut butter, cream cheese and butter until smooth. Add sugar and milk; fold in whipped topping. Pour into the crust. Cover and freeze for at least 4 hours. Remove from the freezer just before serving. Garnish with peanuts and chocolate curls if desired. Yield: 6 servings.
Mix together with a whisk.
Brush on meats or poultry last 20 minutes of cooking or grilling.

Wash and peel potatoes, chop into wedges and place in microwave safe dish. Bake 15 to 20 minutes. Add butter to potatoes last few minutes in microwave. Cook bacon, remove from grease and brown onions. Add to potatoes along with corned beef, place on top and do not stir. Cook until done.
Mix all together real good, then pour in ice cream freezer. Freeze as you would ice cream.
Beat egg yolks and sugar in medium saucepan.
Slowly beat in two (2) cups of the milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until thermometer registers 150°F. or mixture coats the back of a metal spoon.
Remove from heat;
strain into pitcher.
Stir in remaining milk, Jim Beam Bourbon, vanilla and nutmeg.
Cover and chill at least 8 hours or overnight.
Sprinkle with additional nutmeg.
Brown hamburger and onion; drain.
Stir in seasoning and tomato sauce.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread 1 can of rolls onto bottom of pan.
Spread hamburger mixture on top of rolls. Sprinkle both kinds of cheese on top, then top with second can of rolls.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Pare and slice eggplant. Cook in salted water until tender. Drain and mash.
Add other ingredients except cheese slices. Place in a greased 1-quart casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Arrange cheese slices on top and bake an additional 20 minutes.
Yields 4 servings.
Soak cereal in warm milk for 10 minutes.
Beat eggs with fork; add sugar to taste.
Add salt, vanilla and cereal/milk mixture. Spoon into a buttered 5 cup casserole dish.
If desired, sprinkle top with nutmeg.
Set casserole into a pan partly filled with water.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Stir at least twice during the first 20 minutes of baking.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Serve warm or chilled.
Store leftover pudding in refrigerator.
Pinch lettuce in small pieces.
Combine all other ingredients except Fritos.
Add them just before serving.
Place all
ingredients
in a 9 x 13-inch pan and cover. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Spread in ungreased, 9 x 5
x 3-inch pan or casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour to 1 1/4 hours.
Cream together margarine, cream cheese and sugar. Set aside. Mix together pudding and milk until smooth.
Mix in whipped topping.
Mix in cream cheese mixture.
Alternate layers of the crushed cookies and pudding mixture, beginning and ending with cookies.
Put in refrigerator or freeze until firm.
Mix all ingredients and pour into graham cracker crusts. Makes 2 or more pies!
Cook beans until partially tender; drain and saute in olive oil, 1 clove garlic and oregano.
Add salt and pepper.
Cook until tender.
Cook noodles according to package and drain.
Combine tuna, soup, onion, vinegar, milk and Cheddar cheese in a bowl.
Mix well. Stir in noodles. Spoon into 2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Dot shell with Kahlua and set aside.
Slightly beat egg yolks in top of a double boiler.
Add 1/2 cup sugar.
Place over simmering water.
Cook and stir until sugar is dissolved.
Melt chocolate with 1/4 cup water in a small saucepan.
Stir melted chocolate
mixture into egg yolks.
Cook and stir until mixture begins to thicken.
Soften gelatin in 1/4 cup cold water.
Add to thickened chocolate mixture.
Stir well and remove from heat.
Add Kahlua.
Place pan with mixture in a bowl of ice water to cool. In small bowl, beat cream with 2 tablespoons sugar until stiff. In another small bowl, beat egg whites until stiff.
When chocolate mixture begins to thicken, fold in half of the whipped cream, then fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Refrigerate remaining whipped cream.
Turn chocolate mixture into pie shell, chill.
Top pie with remaining whipped cream and almonds.
Makes one 9 inch pie.
Heat oven to 325°. Toss rice and spinach together. Add eggs, milk, Worcestershire sauce, salt and onion. Pour into 2-quart baking dish. Sprinkle butter and cheese over rice. Bake 30 to 40 minutes.
Let cream cheese stand at room temperature for 15 to 20 minutes to soften.
Drain green beans.
Mix all ingredients together in casserole dish and bake at 350° for about 20 to 30 minutes until bacon pieces are done.
Place all ingredients, except walnuts, in a large bowl. Microwave at Medium (50% power) until chocolate chips are melted (about 3 to 5 minutes), stirring once or twice during cooking. Stir in nuts.
Pour into well-greased (8 x 8-inch) square baking dish.
Refrigerate until set (overnight if possible).
Brown the butter; add flour, then milk.
Stir and cook until smooth.
Add cheese and mushroom soup and stir until melted.
Pour over beans.
Heat.
On a breadboard, pound flour into both sides of steak; cut into serving pieces until flour is absorbed.
Preheat frypan to 360°. Add fat and onions; saute until golden in color, about 3 minutes. Remove from fat.
Change frypan setting to 400° and add a tablespoon of fat.
Then brown steak on both sides, about 10 to 20 minutes.
Sprinkle browned meat with salt and pepper; add the sauteed onions, garlic, celery, tomatoes and pepper slices.
Cover and set frypan at 220°.
Simmer until the meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Sprinkle with parsley when serving.
Combine cheese, dates and 1/2 cup pecans.
Cover and chill 30 minutes.
Shape into a ball and roll in remaining pecans.
Serve with apple wedges or gingersnaps.
Makes 2 cups.
Separate eggs.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add 6 tablespoons of sugar gradually.
Put in refrigerator.
Cream butter and add remainder of sugar.
Beat at low speed.
Add 2 egg yolks at a time.
Add milk and flour alternately.
Add flavoring and fold in egg whites.
Pour into greased steeple pan.
Bake 1 3/4 hours in a 300° oven.
Soften bread in water.
Add beef, onion, egg, salt and pepper and mix thoroughly.
Form into patties.
Brown on both sides in butter in heavy skillet.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over meat.
Cook, covered, on low heat for 30 to 40 minutes.
Wash chicken. Push garlic and rosemary under skin and in cavity. Cook in Brown N Bag
1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours at 375°.
Stir whipping cream and sugar together well.
Cook 7 minutes. Stir well, then cook 7 more minutes.
Remove and add butter and pecans.
Stir in 1 teaspoon vanilla (optional), then drop on wax paper.
Cream shortening, butter, sugar and eggs.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into a loaf pan, greased and lightly floured.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix the first 4 ingredients.
Peel off a strip around top of apples.
Place apples in 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish; fill centers with nut mixture.
Microcook, covered, until tender, 5 to 6 minutes; give dish a half turn twice.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
Fry hamburger and onion together until hamburger is brown and crumbly.
Drain off excess fat.
Mix all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake 1 to 1 1/2 hours until carrots are tender at 350°.
Mix wafers, powdered sugar and orange juice and roll in small balls.
Then roll these in the coconut.
Mix sugar, flour, oats, cinnamon, salt and raisins.
Add eggs and mix well.
Add margarine.
Mix soda and vinegar together and add to mixture.
This dough will be stiff, but mix well.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes, depending on how crisp or soft you like them.
Cut squash in half lengthwise and discard seeds.
Slice into 1/2-inch slices crosswise and remove peel. Place in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Heat orange juice in microwave dish. Dissolve candy in the orange juice.
Pour over squash. Sprinkle with salt.
Cover with foil and bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes. Place liquid from baking pan into small saucepan and boil until thick.
Pour over squash. Yields 4 servings.
Has 150 calories, fat free.
Fold in fruit and nuts with mixture.
Freeze in Pyrex dish. Cut into squares.
Fills a 7 x 11-inch dish.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Grease and flour a Bundt pan or tube pan. In large bowl, cream together the butter, shortening, and sugar.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. In another bowl, combine the flour, baking soda, salt, and cocoa. Stir to mix.

Add the flour mixture to the creamed mixture alternately with the buttermilk. Add vanilla and mix well. Stir in walnuts. Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Bake for about 1 hour 10 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted into center of cake. After the cake has cooled slightly in the pan, turn it out onto a cake plate.
Mix all ingredients together and put in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Top with mixture of 1/4 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Brown and drain ground beef, sausage and onion on low heat; add other ingredients.
Cook in a large pot.
Serve with nacho chips.
Keep warm in crock-pot.
Mix cream cheese, onion and Tabasco sauce.
Spread on ham slices.
Roll ham slices and refrigerate overnight.
Slice in one-inch pinwheels after chilled thoroughly.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve.
Cook meat and onion until brown; drain fat.
Add taco seasoning mix to meat mixture.
Add chilies.
Cut tortillas into thirds.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer salsa, meat, cheese and tortillas in that order.
End with layer of tortillas topped with cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes at 350°.
Mix all ingredients and roll in powdered sugar.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Serves 5.
Gather 1 peck dandelion heads.
Do not collect from an area sprayed with pesticides or herbicides.
Wash to remove bugs. Combine dandelion heads with boiling water in a large container. Let the flower heads steep for 24 hours.
Strain the juice.
To the juice, add sugar, yeast and fruit.
The amount of fruit can vary, depending on the flavor you want.
Set it in a warm, dark area to ferment.
Do not stir.
Keep mixture quiet for about 2 weeks.
When the mixture reaches the desired potency, siphon off and filter through cheesecloth.
Refrigerate.
It's ready!
In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and sugar.
Add potatoes, eggs, corn syrup, nutmeg, salt, butter and evaporated milk.
Beat well.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
Yields 8 servings.
Blend softened cheese with capers.
Spread on salmon.
Roll, jelly-roll fashion.
Chill.
Cut in 1/2-inch slices.
Serve on cocktail picks.
Mix Crisco or oleo, powdered sweetener, milk, almond, vanilla and eggs together and add flour, baking powder and nuts.
Make into logs and refrigerate overnight.
Slice and bake at 350° until light brown.
They do not brown like cookies with sugar.
Can also add coconut and substitute unsweetened orange juice for the milk.
Keep in refrigerator.
(Thirteen calories per cookie.)
Brown beef and onion in skillet; drain off fat.
Add soup, beans, green chilies, chili powder, salt and pepper; simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve over rice or with crackers.
Brown the steak.
Mix the remaining ingredients and put on top of the steak.
Bake.
Mix all ingredients well and bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Roll chicken in a mixture of flour, salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Brown in oil.
Place chicken in a 13 x 9-inch baking dish; sprinkle with Parmesan and then Mozzarella.
Pour spaghetti sauce over chicken.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes. Serve with spaghetti or vermicelli.
Serves 6 to 8.
Dip into boiling water the peaches.
Plunge peaches into cold water.
Slip off skins. Cut in half.
Discard pits.
Press peaches through sieve or food mill into mixing bowl.
Stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice and the sugar.

Let stand for 15 to 20 minutes. Combine the heavy cream, vanilla, almond extract and salt. Stir into peach mixture. Fill freezer container 2/3 full of mixture. Cover tightly. Set in freezer tub and freeze until firm.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool in pans 10 minutes.
Finish cooling before adding icing.
Place beaten egg in top of double boiler and add sugar, flour and salt.
Mix well.
Add butter and pineapple juice.
Cook over water until smooth and thickened.
Cool, then add Dream Whip or whipping cream.
Peel eggplant and cook in boiling water 7 to 10 minutes. Drain and season with dash of onion powder and dill.
Mix remaining ingredients with 1/3 cup cracker crumbs and combine with eggplant.
Put in 2-quart greased casserole.
Sprinkle remaining cracker crumbs on top and dot with butter and dash of paprika. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix cornstarch and lemon juice in pan.
Separate 3 yolks from egg whites, set the whites aside.
Add egg yolks to lemon mixture and stir, then add boiling water and cook until thick.
Pour into pie shell.
Beat egg whites and sugar until stiff peaks form for topping.
Spread onto pie and bake at 325° for 15 minutes or until topping is golden brown.
Combine all ingredients; cover and chill at least 2 hours. Serve with vegetables, fish, chicken or tortilla chips.
Yield: 2 cups.
Brown sausage and drain.
Cook onion and celery in oleo until tender.
Mix remaining ingredients together; dump in sausage, onion, oleo and celery.
Stuff a 14 to 20 pound bird or dressing may be baked in pan for 35 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Feeds a hungry family!!
Mix cake mix, melted butter and 1 egg.
Pour and press into lightly greased cake pan.
Mix pumpkin, 2 eggs, sugar, salt, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and milk.
Pour over crust mix.
Mix remaining ingredients until crumbly; sprinkle over pumpkin mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool and serve with whipped topping.
Mix together ground beef, Spatini, cold water and bread crumbs.
Shape into meatballs.
Place on cookie sheet.
Bake in oven for 25 minutes at 350°.
Layer in bowl as listed.
Let sit 8 hours overnight in refrigerator.
Mix ground beef, bread crumbs, egg and poultry seasoning. Shape into about 2 dozen 1 1/2-inch balls. Brown balls slowly in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat. Pour off excess fat.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Blend butter and sugar; add eggs.
Beat well.
Stir in milk and vanilla. Add sifted dry ingredients together with nuts, dates and cut cherries.
Mix well.
Crush corn flakes into fine crumbs.
Shape dough into balls using 1 level tablespoon dough each.
Roll balls into crumbs.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Top each with 1/4 cherry.
Bake at 375° for about 12 minutes or until lightly brown. Yield:
6 dozen 2-inch diameter cookies.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Stir in egg.
Sift together the flour, soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with applesauce.
Add oats and blend well. Stir in raisins and nuts.
Drop by teaspoons onto well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Cook celery in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain.
Drain water chestnuts; reserve liquid.
Slice water chestnuts.
Drain mushrooms and reserve liquid.
Mix celery, water chestnuts, almonds and mushrooms.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add flour and stir until smooth.
Add reserved liquids, milk and broth; cook, stirring until thickened.
Stir in celery mixture; pour into casserole.
Top with crumbs; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in preheated 375° oven until bubbly and brown.
Cream margarine and sugar; add soda and vinegar, then vanilla and flour.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet and bake for about 15 minutes at 300°.
Place tomatoes with juice in bowl, mash tomatoes to desired consistency.
Place jalapenos, onion and garlic in food processor and chop.
In skillet, over low heat, place vinegar, oil and jalapeno mixture until warm to touch (do not boil).
Sprinkle with salt several times.
Add tomatoes, stir well.
Place in jars and refrigerate.
Dice each vegetable into extremely small pieces.
Add oil, then squeeze in the juice of 1 to 2 lemons depending on your taste.
Add the salt, then add lemon, oil and salt based on how much salad you need.
The salad should be tart and refreshing.
In 2-quart casserole, mix all the ingredients.
Microwave on High for 11 to 13 minutes.
Rotate dish 1/2 turn; cook 5 minutes.
Combine jello, pecans and coconut.
Stir in milk and vanilla. Chill 1 hour.
Shape into strawberries.
Roll in red sugar.
If you wish, tint sliced almonds with green food coloring and insert in tops of berries to form leaves.
Makes 1 pound, 3 ounces. Very pretty to use among Christmas goodies.

In a medium-size bowl, put 1/2 cup of coconut, then add 4 tablespoons sugar and 3/4 cup of warm milk. Stir well until mixed. Poke cake all over with fork and then pour the milk mixture all over cake, then allow to cool and frost with frosting made from Cool Whip, sour cream, 1/4 cup of confectioners sugar and 1/2 cup of coconut. Then top with remaining coconut. Chill until time to serve. Cake needs at least 3 hours to saturate, but overnight in fridge is best.
Brown hamburger and drain grease.
Peel, cut and boil potatoes.
Mash potatoes.
Add butter and milk; set aside.
Drain green beans.
Combine tomato soup, green beans and browned hamburger in a greased baking dish.
Layer mashed potatoes on top of hamburger mixture.
Spread evenly.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Let set 5 minutes and serve.
In large bowl, combine all ingredients.
Store in airtight container.
Makes 2 1/2 cups mix (12 to 14 servings).
You will also need one oven baking bag.
Heat apple juice and cornstarch in saucepan until thickened. Remove from heat.
Stir in butter and cinnamon.
Pour over apples in large bowl and mix carefully.
Pour into pie crust and cover with second pie crust.
Bake in oven at 375° for 45 minutes.
Combine spinach or broccoli, cheese spread, bread crumbs and bacon in a 1 1/2-quart saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until cheese is melted.
Unroll dough
and separate into 16 triangles.
Cut each triangle in half lengthwise so you'll have 32 triangles.
Spread each triangle with about 1 teaspoon of mixture.
Roll up, starting at wide end.
Place on greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 375° for 11 to 13 minutes or until golden brown. Makes 32 appetizers.
Whip Crisco, sugar, eggs and vanilla together.
Mix flour, soda, cream of tartar and pinch of salt.
Combine and drop by spoonful on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Butter casserole dish.
Spread ingredients in layers (Chili, cheese, Fritos, onion, tamales, cheese then repeat.)
Cook grits in boiling water for 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and place in greased casserole.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Delicious with ham.
In medium saucepan, combine sugar and water.
Cook over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, stirring constantly.
Cool.
Finely shred enough orange and lemon peel to make 2 tablespoons.
Set aside.
Squeeze juice from the lemons and 1 1/2 cups orange juice. Add juices and peel to the cooled syrup.
If desired, pour over mint sprig, cover and let stand 1 hour.
Strain mixture; pour into jars and cover.
Refrigerate.
To serve, fill glasses or pitcher with ice cubes.
Pour equal amounts of fruit syrup and water over ice.
Stir to combine.
If desired, garnish with lemon slices. Makes 6 cups fruit syrup or 12 (8 ounce) servings of orange-lemonade.
Brown ground beef; drain. Stir in all ingredients. Put in casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Mix
sugar
and
cocoa	in microwave-proof bowl.
Place stick of butter in center of dry mix.
Pour milk over.
Do not try to mix!
In a small bowl or jar with a tight-fitting lid, combine oil, vinegar, garlic, salt and pepper; set aside.
In a large salad bowl, combine all remaining ingredients.
Chill until ready to serve.

Cook ground beef and onion; drain. Add tomato juice, beans and seasoning mix; set aside. Layer casserole dish with chips, chili, cheese, chips, chili, cheese until all ingredients are used. Cook at 350° for 20 minutes or until cheese has melted.
Brown ground beef in frypan or pot.
Remove from heat.
Drain excess fat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Simmer for 1/2 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Coat 12 (2 3/4 inch) muffin tin cups with vegetable cooking spray; set aside.
In small bowl, combine buttermilk, bran and baking soda; set aside.
In mixer bowl, cream sugar, prune puree; beat in egg whites and molasses.
Stir in buttermilk mixture, flour, apple and salt.
Blend thoroughly. Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups, dividing equally.
Bake about 20 minutes until pick inserted into center comes out clean. Cool in pan for 15 minutes.
Turn onto rack to cool completely.
Cream the cheese and sour cream and spread on a platter.
Add the taco seasoning to taste.
Chop and spread on the cream cheese mixture: onion, lettuce and tomato.
Spread the Cheddar cheese over the top.
Use real "nachos" or Tostitos with dip.
Butter a 9 or 10-inch pie dish at least 1 1/2 inches deep. Place peaches in dish.
Spread bread evenly over peaches.
Mix melted butter, sugar, flour and egg together until well blended. Pour evenly over bread, making sure all bread is covered.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes, or until golden brown.
Add water to apples and cook until done.
Add sugar, salt and spices and simmer until jelled.
Refrigerate until used.
Heat oven to 350°.
Turn off and place pan in oven with peanut butter and Candi-Quick.
Mix the next 3 ingredients and drop by teaspoon on wax paper.

recipes.t: Braised Bratwurst With Spicy Mustard Sauce
d: About 30 minutes before serving, with sharp knife, score sausages for even cooking.
In 12-inch skillet, over medium heat, cook sausages in apple cider until cider evaporates and sausages are browned and heated, turning sausages occasionally.
Mix ingredients.
Bake at 350° in oblong pan until cake falls (or about 45 minutes).
Cool and cut into squares.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a large bowl.
Toss well. Combine lemon juice and remaining ingredients in a jar.
Cover tightly and shake vigorously.
Pour over lettuce mixture.
Toss gently.
Yields
4 servings.
Combine first 5 ingredients in saucepan.
Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
When thickened, add apples.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Dot with butter.
Cover with top crust.
Cut slits for escape of steam.
Bake at 375° for about 50 minutes or until crust is brown and juice bubbles through slits.

Grind first 5 ingredients in blender. Add 1/2 cup salt. Let stand for 2 hours. Drain dry or squeeze out. Add vinegar, sugar, mustard seed and celery seed. Mix well; pack into jars and seal. Makes 10 pints.

Place milk, sugar, and butter in iron skillet and cook over medium heat. Stir until mixture turns brown and gets thick and sugary. Add pecans and vanilla flavoring. Pour into well buttered plate. Cut into squares before it is completely cool.
Dissolve yeast and 1-1/2 teaspoons sugar in warm water; set aside until bubbly.
Beat 2 eggs, 2 tablespoons sugar and salt. Add cream and butter.
Beat.
Add yeast mixture and slowly blend in flour.
Mix well and let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide into 5 or 6 parts.
Form into balls.
Press into greased pans, forming a 1/2 inch ridge around outside of the pan.
Let rise 15 minutes.
Pour rice, prune, poppy seed, apple, cherry or any cake and pastry filling over the center.
Top with Cheese topping.
Bake at 350 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook the bacon in iron skillet until crisp.
Add the onion and peppers.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Simmer for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients, except nuts, together with mixer until smooth.
Add nuts.
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes, or until done.
Cut chicken breasts in half.
Mix remaining ingredients together in a shallow pan large enough to hold breasts in one layer.
Place breasts in marinade, turning to coat and rubbing marinade into breasts.
Marinate at least one hour and as long as overnight.
Grill chicken over hot coals or under broiler.
Strain marinade, bring it to a boil and serve it with chicken.
Yield:
4 servings.
Carbohydrate 5 g, protein 21 g, fat 5 g, calories 186.
Brown the pork chops.
Meanwhile, mix remaining ingredients and put into large casserole dish.
Place browned pork chops on top.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix flour and cream of tartar in pan.
Add water, food coloring and oil.
Stir over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes.

Bake as directed.
When has about 15 minutes left in oven, put sugar and pineapple in a saucepan; bring to a boil.
Boil until sugar is dissolved.
Poke holes in cake and pour mixture over entire cake.
Place in refrigerator. Cool completely.
Make pudding and pour over cake.
Use 1/2 coconut and Cool Whip.
Mix together.
Put over cake.
Then top with remainder of coconut.
Then take your hand and push coconut into Cool Whip so it doesn't fall off cake.
Mix together all ingredients as you would for meat loaf.
Form into small balls; brown in frying pan. Drain grease and place meat balls in a baking dish. Cover with jar of spaghetti sauce. Cover with foil. Bake at 400° for 40 minutes.

Preheat oven to 375°. Chop all ingredients, then add sauce mix. Cut biscuits in half, then in half again. Then mix with spaghetti sauce. Put in 13 x 9 pan sprayed with Pam. Bake at 375° for 23 to 28 minutes.

recipes.t: Perpetual Pot Of Fruit With Rum Or Brandy
d: Bring water and sugar to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Cool.
Add lemon juice and rum or brandy (or some of both).
Pour into a large container with cover. Add fruit to the syrup, making sure that the fruit is submerged. Refrigerate, replenishing as needed.
Keeps beautifully.
Bake in oven at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes in uncooked pie shell.
Soften cream cheese.
Beat all ingredients until smooth and even color.
Sprinkle paprika or cut chives on top.
Serve with carrots.

Cream butter; slowly beat in sugar and salt. Add 1 egg at a time and beat briskly. Blend entire mixture. Pour into pastry lined pie pan for 8-inch pie. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 350° and bake until custard sets, about 35 to 40 minutes.
In a bowl, combine softened cream cheese, sugar and 1 egg.
Add almond extract; set aside.
In small saucepan melt chocolate and butter together.
Cool.
Beat 2 eggs.
Add sugar and chocolate mixture.
Beat in sifted and combined flour, baking powder and salt.
Pour half the chocolate mixture into a well-greased and floured square baking pan (8-inches).
Gently spread the cream cheese mixture.
Top with remaining chocolate mixture.
Bake in 350° oven 45 to 50 minutes, until cake tester inserted in center comes away clean.
Cool in pan before cutting into rectangles or squares.
In small saucepan, combine 1 package undrained raspberries and cornstarch; cook and stir until thickened and clear.
Chill thoroughly.
In blender, combine remaining 1 package drained raspberries, Eagle Brand and ReaLemon brand; blend until smooth. Place in large bowl; stir in food coloring if desired.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon half the mousse mixture into dessert dishes; top with equal portions of raspberry sauce, then remaining mousse mixture.
Chill thoroughly.
Garnish as desired.
Refrigerate leftovers.

recipes.t: Tomato Salad In A Bread Bowl
d: Cut a thin slice off top of bread.
Carefully cut out most of the inside of the bread, leaving a shell.
Tear insides into large, irregular pieces.
Toss lightly under broiler.
Set aside.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly grease 8-inch glass baking dish.
Place half of apples in dish; top with corn syrup.
Add remaining apples, lemon juice, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and nutmeg. Combine 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, sugar, salt, butter, flour and oatmeal.
Mix well and press firmly over apples.
Bake 50 minutes. Top with ice cream and serve.
Cream sugars, butter and peanut butter in bowl with electric mixer.
Beat in eggs, milk and vanilla.
Sift together flour, soda and salt.
Stir into egg batter.
Shape into balls; roll in additional granulated sugar.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from oven and immediately press a chocolate kiss into each cookie.
Cool on wire racks.
Makes 7 dozen cookies.
Mix in order given and bake at 350° until lightly browned or until done.
Boil pork chops and potatoes until cooked.
Saute onion in pan and roll in flour.
Add 1 large can of tomatoes and string kraut.
Mix together all ingredients.
Pour into a greased and floured 9x13-inch pan.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
If it gets too sticky, put in a little flour.
Feeds six children.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pour into greased and floured 3 loaf pans size 7 1/2 x 3 x 2-inch.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Very good served with fresh fruit.
Mix the sour cream, marshmallows and coconut.
Use wooden spoon and stir in oranges and pineapple.
Refrigerate overnight. Just before serving, add bananas.
Serves 6.
Soften cream cheese; then add olives and enough salsa to make mixture pink.
Place 1 tortilla on plate (or server) and spread cheese mixture; repeat process ending with tortilla on top.
Cut into small slices like pie.
For garnish, fasten stuffed olive on each slice with toothpick.
Mix all ingredients together and bake 10 minutes at 350°, then 40 minutes at 300°.
Combine all ingredients, except round steak, in a saucepan; bring to a boil.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Pound steak (break tissues).
Cut into serving pieces.
Put in a large pan.
Pour barbecued sauce over meat.
Cover tightly and bake at 325° for 2 hours or until fork-tender.
Drain peas.
Mix Miracle Whip with sugar; add vinegar (enough to make very tart).
Cut up eggs.
Mix all ingredients together. Cover and cool.
Add salt and soybean oil to 1 quart water.
Bring to a boil and add potatoes until fork-tender.
Remove potatoes and add butter, heavy cream, pepper and sour cream.
Mash.
Serves 4.
Cut meat into 1/2-inch strips.
Mix together ginger, chili powder, garlic and lemon rind.
Dip meat into mixture and brown in butter.
Combine sugar, jam, lemon juice, salt and 1 1/2 cups water.
Add meat and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with rice.
Stir flour, 2 tbsp. sugar, baking soda, and salt. Stir in milk and 3 tbsp. of melted butter. Mix until dough forms.
Sprinkle surface lightly with flour. Knead dough 10 times.
Roll dough, with rolling pin into a rectangle 9x5 inches.

Brush with remaining melted butter. Sprinkle mixture of 3 tbsp. sugar and cinnamon. Roll dough up tightly, beginning at narrow end. Pinch end of dough to seal. Cut into 4 equal pieces. Place cut side up on greased cookie sheet. Pat into circle. Sprinkle with more sugar. Bake at 425° for 8 to 10 min. Remove from cookie sheet immediately. Let cool on wire rack.

Combine skim milk, strawberries, orange juice and sugar substitute in container of an electric blender or food processor. Process until strawberries are pureed and mixture is frothy. Transfer mixture to a small pitcher.
Stir in buttermilk.
Pour into individual glasses and serve immediately.
Diabetic Exchange: 1 skim milk.
Each serving amount:
1 cup.
Calories:
Mix all ingredients; pour into casserole.

Cook cream cheese and broth in large saucepan on low heat until cheese is melted, stirring frequently with wire whisk. Stir in chicken, vegetables and salad dressing mixes. Spoon into 9-inch pie plate. Cover with 1 pie crust; seal and flute edge. Cut several slits to permit steam to escape. Cut remaining pie crust into decorative shapes; arrange on crust. Place pie plate on cookie sheet. Bake at 425° for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown. Makes 8 servings.
Melt butter over low heat in a small pan. Add cocoa, conf. sugar and milk. Stir and heat until everything is blended. Pour over cake (leave in pan) and spread.
Combine flour, sugar and cocoa in mixing bowl.
Heat cola and oleo to boiling point.
Pour over flour mixture.
Add eggs, buttermilk, soda and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add marshmallows and stir with spoon until they are coated.
Pour into greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Mix ground beef, bread crumbs, onions, milk, egg and next 3 ingredients.
Make 1/2 to 1-inch size meatballs.
Put shortening/oil in a skillet and cook until golden brown.
Drain grease.
In crock-pot preheat chili and jelly.
After heated place meatballs in crock-pot.
Let simmer approximately 1 1/2 to 2 hours on low.
Makes approximately 5 dozen.
Trim
crust
off top and sides of loaf of French bread. Cut X's across top.
Place Swiss cheese, cut in small pieces, in
X's. In
pan
melt butter, mustard, onion, poppy seed and lemon juice until all is dissolved.
Spoon over bread and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Pour into two 8-inch pie shells or 1 large pie shell.
Bake at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Break graham crackers into sections and line bottom of pan. Bring butter to boil 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour over crackers and add pecans.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Let cool.
First, brown hamburger.
Drain the meat.
Take 13 x 9-inch glass pan and butter both sides and bottom.
Spread biscuits on both bottom and sides.
Put meat on top of biscuits, then put vegetables on top of meat.
Put a little bit of water on top. Bake in 325° oven for 15 minutes.
Pull out and put potatoes and cheese on top.
Put back in oven for 3 to 5 minutes or until cheese melts.

Place rice on bottom of casserole dish. Place uncooked chicken on top of rice. Pour onion soup mix over chicken. Mix milk, soup and 1 soup can of water together. Pour over top of all. Bake at 325° for 1 to 2 hours.
Sift first 5 ingredients together.
Beat eggs; add sugar, oil and pumpkin.
Mix dry ingredients gradually into liquid mixture. Pour into four (1 pound) coffee cans.
Bake at 350°
for 1 hour. Remove while warm and wrap in foil.
Arrange drained peaches in a square baking pan.
Pour lemon juice and spread brown sugar over peaches.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Mix flour, sugar and salt in a bowl; set aside.
Bring the oleo, cocoa and water to a boil and add to the flour mixture.
Mix together the remaining ingredients and add to the other mixture. Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes, in a well-greased cookie sheet pan.
Mix one cornbread mix according to directions on box and add 1/2 can corn.
Put in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer hamburger, picante sauce, cheese and the other cornbread mix, mixed according to directions, adding the other half of the corn. Bake at 400° until golden brown.
Serve immediately.
Cut olives into large pieces.
Cut bacon into 1/4-inch strips and cook slowly until crisp.
When bacon is half done, add onion and cook until soft.
Drain off fat.
Combine bacon and onion with eggs, celery and olives.
Add mayonnaise.
Mix.
Stuff tomatoes and serve on lettuce.
Mix corns with butter and sour cream.
Add eggs and stir in muffin mix.
Bake in a 9-inch pie pan for 35 to 40 minutes at 375° until golden brown.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Combine cake mix, pudding, eggs, oil, 3/4 cup water and bananas.
Mix well.
Pour into greased and lightly floured bundt pan.
Bake for 1 hour. Meanwhile, combine sugar, margarine and 1/4 cup water in sauce pan.
Bring to a boil, and remove from heat.
When cake is done, immediately pour sauce slowly over cake, allowing time for it to be absorbed.
Leave cake in pan for 20 minutes before removing.
Brown meat and onion; drain excess fat and set aside.
Combine cornbread mixes together according to directions on box. Additionally, add 1/3 cup milk and can of corn to the cornbread mixes.

Using a nonstick spray, prepare a 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Pour a small amount of cornbread batter in pan to form a layer. Sprinkle meat mixture on top and then sprinkle grated cheese on top of the meat.
Pour remaining cornbread mix on top of all and bake according to box directions.
Mix cornstarch, sugar, salt and nutmeg; add egg yolks.
Mix. Add sour cream, raisins, lemon juice and nuts.
Cook until thick. Pour into baked pie shell.
Spread meringue on top and brown.
Rinse chicken and pat dry.
In large bag, combine flour and seasonings.
In shallow bowl, beat eggs and water.
Place chicken a few pieces at a time in bag and shake to coat.
Dip in eggs and shake in bag again.
Fry chicken until done.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine cabbage, marshmallows, pineapple, apple, celery and enough salad dressing to moisten. Toss lightly and chill.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl.
Pour into a greased casserole and bake 30 minutes in a 350° oven or until lightly browned.
Put vegetables and salt into ice water; let stand for 3 hours. Drain.
Bring to
boil vinegar, sugar and spices.	Add squash, onions and peppers; boil
for
minutes and put into jars and seal.
Mix ingredients together.
Place in casserole and bake for 50 minutes at 350°.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease 12 x 8-inch (2-quart) baking dish. In large skillet, brown ground beef and onion.
Drain.
Stir in water, pepper, tomato sauce, and tomato paste.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vegetables and 1 1/2 cups cheese.
Spoon mixture into greased baking dish.
Separate dough into 10 biscuits.
Separate each biscuit into 2 layers.
Place biscuits near outer edge of hot meat mixture, overlapping slightly.
Sprinkle remaining cheese in center and around edge. Gently brush biscuits with margarine and sprinkle with oregano. Bake for 22 to 27 minutes or until biscuits are brown.
Mix butter with coffee, salt and chocolate.
Add rest of ingredients and beat thoroughly.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Beat until creamy and frost tops and sides of cakes.
Saute chopped onion in melted margarine until tender.
Add the mushroom soup.
Cut up 1/3 of a small box of Velveeta or American cheese.
Add to onion and soup mixture.
Melt cheese with mixture. Add 2 cups cooked rice and 10 ounces of frozen broccoli (thawed and drained).
Pour in buttered casserole dish and top with cracker crumbs.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Blend first 5 ingredients like pie dough. Put half in 8 inch square pan. Mix remaining ingredients. Spread on crumbs. Put remaining crumbs on top. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix all together and put in a greased loaf pan.
Bake 1 1/4 hours at 350°.
Combine melted butter with dressing mix.
Sprinkle small amount in casserole dish.
Save
enough
to cover top of casserole and combine the rest of crumbs with the other ingredients. Pour into casserole dish.
Sprinkle the reserved crumbs on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly and brown.
Peel shrimp (uncooked) and devein.
Make roux (dark) of flour and oil.
Add shrimp to this for a few minutes, stirring constantly.
Set aside.
Brown beef cubes in oil.
Add water, salt and pepper for seasonings.
Simmer slowly until meat is tender.
Add vegetables and cook 30 minutes or until vegetables are done.
Yield: 6 servings.
Carbohydrate 7 g, protein 11 g, fat 12 g, calories 180. One serving = 1 1/2 meat medium fat exchange, 1 vegetable exchange, 1 fat exchange.
Cream together margarine and sugar, beat egg and add to mixture.
Tear bread slices and add with pineapple to first mixture.
Mix together.
Place in 1 1/2 to 2-quart greased baking dish and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix and pour over carrots.
Refrigerate overnight.
Chop nuts.
Place all nuts, drained cherries and dates in a large bowl.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and sugar together. Coat the fruit and nuts with dry ingredients.
Add vanilla to eggs and pour over coated fruit and nuts; mix well.
Mix sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt together.
Beat egg whites and water until it's meringue consistency.
Add sugar mixture 1 tablespoon at a time.
Beat to a stiff peak.
Fold in pecan halves.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine first four ingredients in a buttered casserole dish.
Put butter on top of applesauce.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Blend all ingredients together.
Pour into a 13x9 inch pan. Top with topping mix.
Dissolve
jello in hot water.
Add sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add cool water.
Set in refrigerator to cool until thick
(soft).
Add ground fruits, nuts and liquids.
Mix then pour into mold and refrigerate.
Toss all ingredients together.
Let egg whites stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Sift flour and salt and set aside.
Coat a 15x10x1 baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Line with wax paper and coat the paper with spray.
In a mixing bowl, beat yolks until slightly thickened. Gradually add sugar and beating until thick and lemony colored. Add orange peel, lemon juice and vanilla.
Add sifted flour mixture and mix well.
Batter will be thick.
In another bowl beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Fold into batter.
Spread into prepared pan.
Bake at 350 for 12-15 minutes or until cake springs back when lightly touched in center.
Cool on wire rack 5 minutes. Turn onto a kitchen towel.
Sprinkle with 1 Tbsp. powdered sugar. Gently pull wax paper off and roll cake up jelly roll style, starting with short side.
Cool completely on wire rack.
Unroll cake- spread marmalade evenly over cake within 1/2 inch of edges. Roll up again, seam side down.
Sprinkle with remaining sugar. Wrap and place in refrigerator one hour.
Servings 8 - 5 Points.
Mix flour and brown sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Cut in the Parkay and add the nuts. Mix in egg and soda. Press half of mixture in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pour into 1-gallon freezer.
Finish filling with whole milk.
Stir and freeze in ice cream freezer.
Simmer tomatoes in large saucepan for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and add 1/4 cup butter, soda, 1 teaspoon salt and sugar.
Let cool during preparation of next step.
Melt the remaining 1/4 cup butter in large kettle.
Add flour and 2 teaspoons salt.
Add milk; heat and stir to boiling point.
Combine the two mixtures and heat slowly.
Add salt, if needed, and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
Blend half and half and mayonnaise.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into greased casserole.
Cover with 1/2 cup bread crumbs.
Dot with butter, if desired.
Bake at 350° approximately 30 minutes.
Use a skillet or wok.
Saute onion, green pepper, salt and pepper in chicken fat.
Place potatoes on top of ingredients in skillet or wok, then chicken breasts on top of potatoes.
Pour in broth.
Cover and simmer gently, about 30 minutes.
Do not stir.
Bring water, gelatine, sugar and pineapple to boil.
Cook for five minutes.
Remove from stove and while hot add cream cheese and cream.
Stir until smooth.
Add pecans.
Pour into mold or decorative bowl.
Chill until firm.
In small bowl, combine all ingredients until smooth.
Chill about 2 hours.
Serve over fresh fruit salads.
Yield: 1 1/4 cups.
Melt margarine.
Add chocolate chips.
Keep over heat until melted.
Add other ingredients.
Pour into two unbaked pie shells. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, sugar, vanilla and egg.
Mix well. Spread on bottom of deep 9-inch unbaked pie shell.
Combine canned or cooked pumpkin, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and salt.
Mix well.
Blend in beaten egg and evaporated milk.
Carefully pour over cream cheese mixture.
Bake at 350° for 65 to 70 minutes or until done.
Cool.
May be topped with Cool Whip or cream.
Cube steak and brown in skillet with garlic and pepper and a little oil.
Add soy sauce and water.
Cover and cook 20 minutes. Add sliced bell peppers and onions.
Cook 10 minutes.
Add 1 teaspoon cornstarch and cold water to thicken.
Serve over rice.
Dissolve red hots in hot water and add Jell-O.	Blend thoroughly and cool.
Add applesauce.
Pour in loaf pan and jell.
Sift flour, salt and baking soda together.
Add brown sugar and rolled oats.
Cut in margarine until crumbly.
Spread half the mixture in a greased 7 x 11-inch baking dish.
Whisk together eggs and 3 tablespoons water until well blended.
Combine bread

crumbs and 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese. Dip the sliced eggplant into the egg mixture, then dredge in the bread crumb mixture. Cook the eggplant in 3 batches in 1 tablespoon hot olive oil (per batch) in a large skillet over medium heat 4 minutes on each side or until tender. Arrange 1/3 of eggplant in a single layer in a lightly greased 11 x 7 baking dish. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese and 1/2 cup Mozzarella cheese. Repeat layers twice. Spoon 3 cups pasta sauce over top. Bake, covered, at 375° for 35 minutes. Uncover and sprinkle remaining 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese and 1/2 cup Mozzarella cheese. Bake 10 more minutes or until cheese melts. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.

recipes.t: Green Bean And Radish Salad In Sour Cream Vinaigrette
d: Bring plenty of lightly salted water to a boil.
Add the beans and cook until just tender, about 6 or 7 minutes.
Drain and run under cold water to stop further cooking.
Transfer the beans to a serving bowl.
Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon vinegar, sour cream and oil.
Whisk the dressing until smooth.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Add the radishes, scallions and dressing to the beans. Toss the salad gently with 2 spoons.
Let the salad marinate at room temperature for 2 hours before serving.
Turn salad to lunch dish by adding smoked turkey, Swiss cheese or smoked ham, cut into julienne strips.
Cut
and
dice	chicken
breasts;
season with seasoned salt, pepper
and
Mrs. Dash.
Cook slowly in slightly greased frying pan; do not brown meat.
Simmer until done; may substitute chicken with
shrimp or beef.
Set aside.	Chop and cook green onions
in slightly greased pan (drain any excess oil); set
aside. Scramble
eggs
with about 1 tablespoon of cooked green
onions; set
aside.
Begin	frying cooked rice (do not boil rice too long) in butter.

Boil potatoes until tender but still firm. Drain and let cool. Peel and shred potatoes. In a buttered 2-quart casserole, place a layer of potatoes. Sprinkle with Lawry's salt and dot with butter. Repeat until all of potatoes have been used. Pour whipping cream on top. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until top is golden brown. Serves 8 to 10.
All spices should be dehydrated.
Mix together and refrigerate.
Mix flour, brown sugar, margarine and nuts until crumbly. Spread on cookie sheet lined with heavy-duty Reynolds Wrap.
Bake in 350° oven for 13 to 15 minutes.
Cool; break apart into crumbs. Line an 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2-inch loaf pan with heavy-duty aluminum foil, leaving a 1 1/2-inch collar around top.
Spread 2/3 of crumb mixture in bottom.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon color; blend in condensed milk.
Add lemon juice and rind; stir until thickened.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold into lemon mixture.
Pour mixture into prepared pan; sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.
Freeze until firm.
When solid, cover with piece of foil the size of the top.
Lift from pan and return to freezer. Slice in bars to serve.

Stir together orange juice, soy sauce and ginger root. Add chicken. Let stand 30 minutes at room temperature. Drain chicken. Reserve sauce. Saute chicken in olive oil. Stir together reserved sauce and cornstarch. Stir into pan and heat until thick and bubbly. Stir in orange sections and cashews.
Mix the ingredients together.
Make into individual crab cakes.
Fry until golden brown.
Combine all ingredients, except almonds, and put in ovenproof dish.
Top with almonds.
Place in oven for 15 to 20 minutes at 375°.
Serve with crackers or nachos.
Combine onion, carrots and hot shortening together; cook slowly for 5 minutes.
Add bread cubes, milk, salt, sage and pepper; mix well.
Layer ingredients in 8-inch square pan, starting with rice. Cover and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
*I use 4 cups corn from my freezer.
Put the ingredients in a Corning Ware dish in the listed order. Do not stir.
Dot 1/2 stick margarine on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Beat first 5 ingredients together until smooth.
Add apple and nuts.
Mix well.
Pour in ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Drain the first three ingredients.
Mix all together and heat.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and flour.
Beat for 10 minutes.
Pour batter into greased and floured tube cake pan. Bake for 1 1/2 hours at 300° until golden brown and toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Great with strawberries and whipped cream or for wedding cakes.
Beat the first 3 ingredients well, then beat in the baking soda, orange peel, salt and flour.
Mix in the apples and walnuts. Bake at 350° in a greased and floured Bundt pan for 50 to 55 minutes. Cake is done when toothpick comes out clean.
Invert onto rack after cooling for 10 minutes.
Serve plain or iced.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix margarine and sugar thoroughly.
Add eggs, pumpkin and water.
Blend in flour, soda, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and cloves.
Stir in nuts and raisins.
Pour into a well-greased loaf pan, 9 x 5 x 3-inch.
Bake 65 to 70 minutes until toothpick stuck into center comes out clean.
Soften cream cheese; add finely chopped onions, beef, garlic and Worcestershire sauce.
Chill; serve on crackers.
Scrub tongue well.
Cover with boiling water and bring to a boil.
Skim, cover and simmer until tender, 3 to 4 hours.
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt per pound when partially cooked.
Remove skin when tender.
To 2 cups strained water in which tongue has been boiled, add the rest of the ingredients.
Blend together to form sauce.
Place tongue in roasting pan; pour over sauce.
Cover and bake 30 minutes at 350°, turning often.
In medium bowl, combine the first 3 ingredients.
Spread cheese mixture on cut side of each bread half.
Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Broil 4 inches from heat for 3 minutes, or until bubbly and lightly browned.
Combine dressing, soy sauce and ginger.
Pour over chicken. Marinate in refrigerator several hours or overnight.
Place wings on broiler pan.
Broil 15 to 20 minutes, turning once.
Brush occasionally with marinade.
Makes 36 appetizers.
Cook the potatoes in their skins.
Cool, peel and cut up in fine pieces.
Cook the eggs and cool, peel and cut up.
Chop up the peeled onion.
Put all together.
Sprinkle the salt, pepper and celery seed over them.
Then mix the salad dressing, vinegar and sugar together.
You may have to add more sugar and vinegar to make it taste real tart.
Mix all together while potatoes and eggs are still warm.
Mix all but lettuce and croutons.
Toss with greens and top with croutons.
Mix all ingredients together and spoon into paper lined muffin cup and freeze.
Remove from freezer a few minutes before serving. Makes 15 servings.
In a frying pan, brown ground beef.
Drain off fat.
Mix in Parmesan cheese, onion, oregano, tomato paste and Mozzarella cheese.
Cut French bread in half lengthwise.
Lay bread, cut side up, on a cookie sheet.
Spread meat mixture evenly over top of bread halves.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until done.
Heat oven to 425°.
Mix mincemeat and apple.
Pour into pastry lined pie pan.
Cover with top crust which has slits in it.
Seal and flute.
Cover edge with 1 1/2-inch strip of aluminum foil to prevent excess browning.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until crust is nicely browned.
Serve slightly warm with whipped cream on top.
Mix well; roll in pecans.
Serve with crackers.
You will also need nonstick spray coating.
Cream butter; add sweetener, vanilla and egg.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Add to mixture.
Add applesauce, dates and nuts.
Bake 1 hour at 350° in loaf pan.
Mix together sugar, milk, cocoa and butter; bring to a boil. Boil for 1 1/2 minutes.
Remove from heat; then add quick cooking oatmeal, vanilla and pecans.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto wax paper.
Pound meat.
Sprinkle with salt.
Dip first in flour, then in eggs and then in bread crumbs.
Fry in butter or oil until brown. Serve with lemon wedges.
Cut up your favorite fruit into a bowl.
Add chopped walnuts and shredded coconut, as desired.
Mix all ingredients in a glass 9 x 13-inch pan and refrigerate overnight.
(If you use an aluminum pan, store ingredients in a glass bowl and transfer just before baking).
Sprinkle crushed potato chips over top and bake in 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours. Serves 12.
Cook onion in butter until transparent.
Add ground beef. Cook, stirring until beef is light brown.
Add the flour, salt, pepper, mushrooms and soup.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the sour cream and simmer for 15 minutes longer.
Serve over cooked rice or cooked egg noodles.
Garnish with paprika.
Makes 4 servings.
In large saucepan, add brussels sprouts, salt and butter to 2 inches of water.
Bring to boil, cover and cook until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain.
Add salad crunches and parsley and sprinkle parmesan to cover sprouts.
Serve warm.
Serves 4 to 6.
Peel the banana.
Cut it in half crosswise.
Cut the pineapple ring into quarters. Place a banana half on a plate.
Place 2 pineapple quarters near the base of the banana.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the cottage cheese around the bottom and eat!
Mix together the wine, soy sauce and seasonings.
Place the steak in a long glass baking dish and pour the marinade over the meat.
Cover and chill at least 12 to 18 hours, turning the meat over once or twice.
Preheat the broiler.
Remove the steak from the marinade.
Pat dry and broil 4-inches from the heat for about 5 minutes on each side.
To serve, cut thin slices diagonally across the grain.
Serve with rice.
Mix in very large bowl Raisin Bran, sugar, flour and salt. Add soda, cinnamon, beaten eggs, oil and 1 quart of buttermilk; mix well.
Stir all the way to the bottom; refrigerate.
Do not stir again.
Fill muffin tins 2/3 full.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 20 minutes.
Keep in refrigerator for 6 weeks.
Use just what you need each time.
Makes 5 dozen.
Heat water to a boil.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cornmeal, sugar and salt.
Add boiling water, stirring gradually into 3 ingredients.
Batter should not be too thin.
Add milk and butter.
Using a small ladle, pour batter onto hot greased griddle forming cakes about 3 inches in diameter.
Fry until browned on both sides.
Serve with maple syrup.
Serves 2 to 4.
Mix pudding mix with cold milk at lowest speed of mixer for 3 minutes.
Remove mixer.
Fold in 1/2 cup whipped topping.
Slice banana into pie crust.
Pour in pudding.
Chill 3 hours.
Top with remaining whipped topping.
Mix well.
Place mixture into one pie shell.
Place the other pie shell on top.
Brush top with butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix and blend well.
Bake at 300° to 350° for 30 minutes or longer.
Grease 2-quart casserole. Mix sugar, flour and salt. Beat in eggs. Add pineapple. Pour in pan. Tear bread or croissants into pieces and spread over mixture.
Pour melted butter over bread. Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour or until it stops jiggling.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a baking pan 9 x 9 x 2-inches.
Mix all ingredients except whipped cream or applesauce in a large mixer bowl.
Blend 1/2 minute on low speed, scraping the bowl constantly.
Beat 3 minutes on medium speed scraping occasionally.
Pour into the pan.
Bake 50 minutes.
Serve warm with whipped cream or applesauce.
Simmer all for 1/2 hour.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking to pan.
Drain corn, peas and beans.
Then mix peppers, celery and pimientos with first mixture.
Bring to boil the oil, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Pour over vegetables; mix well.
Chill and serve.
Keeps for weeks.
Combine preceding ingredients; chill.
Serve with chopped vegetables or cut up dark pumpernickel bread.
Cook ground beef, onions and seasoning mix together until meat turns color; drain.
Put in a greased 8 x 8-inch square pan. Spread beans on top of meat.
Mix Bisquick, milk and eggs; pour over beans.
Bake at 400° until brown.
Sprinkle cheese on top and put back into oven until cheese is melted.
Serve with remaining ingredients.
Mix flour and sugar together.
Stir in corn and all other ingredients.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Bake until thick, but not too dry (approximately 30 minutes at 350°).
Cut up cooked sausage links in small, fine pieces; set aside. Combine cheese spread and Monterey Jack cheese; beat with mixer until well combined.
Stir in sausage.
Spread on bread, bagels or English muffins.
Bake at 350° for 5 minutes.
Cook hen with celery, bay leaves, salt, pepper and enough water to cover.
When the chicken is ready to fall from the bones, remove from broth; set aside.
Sprinkle apples with sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Add vanilla and lemon juice.
Cook slowly for about 25 minutes, stir occasionally.
Mix and bake cake (per directions) and let cool for about 15 minutes.
Poke holes in top of cake.
Mix together milk and cream of coconut.
Pour mixture on top of cake.
Put in refrigerator and let set.
Sprinkle coconut and/or nuts on top.
Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate until time to serve.
Brown slices of country ham in ample grease (I use Crisco). Remove ham.
Brown flour very brown, put a lot of black pepper in pan and add tomato juice.
Add water to desired consistency and simmer.
Fry apples in a frying pan, adding sugar and bacon drippings until done (add a bit of salt).
Add a pan full of steaming hot biscuits that contain chunks of cheese in the center. Together with grits and lots of the tasty tomato gravy you will have a feast incomparable.
Boil potatoes and mash well.
Add lemon juice, oil, salt and hot pepper.
Place a layer of mixture in bottom of serving dish. Saute onion and spread over potato mixture.
May add other cooked, chopped fine vegetables.
Cover with second layer of potatoes. Sprinkle with grated cheese (optional).
Garnish with olives, sliced hard-boiled eggs and serve on lettuce.
Mix together the almonds and sugar.
Blend in butter and flour.
Mix well.
Add egg yolks.
Roll dough to 1/2-inch thick. Save half for cross bars.
Spread on cookie sheet, then spread 1 pound apricot jam over dough.
Make cross bars by rolling out dough and cutting into strips.
Crisscross strips on top of jam to give lattice effect.
Bake in a 350°
oven about 30 minutes, or until light brown.
Great!
Spread pie filling and pineapple in a 13 x 13 x 2-inch cake pan.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over fruit (do not stir).
Top with nuts; add coconut.
Pour melted butter over all and bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Great with ice cream.
Serves 12 to 15.

recipes.t: Broiled Salmon With Herbed Lemon Butter
d: Line broiler pan with foil and place salmon fillets on the well-greased rack.
Combine remaining ingredients; baste salmon with mixture.
Broil 4 inches from heat, allowing 10 minutes cooking time per inch of thickness measured at its thickest part or until salmon flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Do not turn salmon.
Baste several times during cooking.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine and melt over medium heat.
Pour over popped corn. Bake at 250° in two 15 x 9-inch pans for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes and stirring after removed from oven until cooled.
Keeps well in an airtight container or bag.
Can halve recipe.
Also can use the large bags of popped corn but omit salt if you do.
Bake cake mix, following package directions.
Cool.
Crumble cake into very large bowl or pan.
Add fruit to crumbled cake. Make Betty Crocker frosting mix, following package directions. Mix with cake and fruit.
Pack tightly into foil-lined 10-inch tube pan or two 9 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Cover cake with foil and chill in refrigerator at least 24 hours.
Cake should be kept refrigerated.
Slice with sharp knife.
Place bread cubes in 12 x 18-inch nonstick pan.
Combine chicken, onion, celery, chilies, mayonnaise, salt and pepper in medium bowl and spoon over bread.
Tear tortillas into bite-sized pieces and place on top.
Combine eggs, milk, cottage cheese and soup in a small bowl and pour over top.
Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to blend.
Preheat oven to 325° and bake 50 to 60 minutes or until the dish is firm and set.
Remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
Serves 8.
Mix all ingredients but last two.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Top with crushed corn flakes and dot with butter. Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Grease square baking dish.
Layer cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese in dish.
Mix cooked beef, herbs, tomato paste and 1/2 cup Mozzarella; spoon evenly over top.
Beat milk, eggs, Bisquick, salt and pepper with a wire whisk until smooth.
Pour into dish.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Cool for 5 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine 4 tablespoons of mix with 2/3 cup of hot water.
Cut zucchini and squash into fourths lengthwise, then into 1/2-inch sections crosswise.
Dice onion; mince garlic.
Fry onion in enough oil to keep it from sticking.
Add garlic when onion is soft.
Then add squash.
Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture collapses and becomes soft.
Remove from heat and add cheese, the salt and pepper to taste (cheese is quite salty).
Serve over or mix into pasta adding more olive oil as needed.
Serve with green salad if desired.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle each serving with crumbled bacon and green onions.
Makes 1-quart.
Sift flour, soda, salt, nutmeg and cinnamon into a bowl.
Add rolled oats and raisins.
Mix applesauce, oil, egg, vanilla and sweetener together.
Add to dry ingredients; mix just until moistened.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet. Bake at 375° for 10 minutes, or until done.
Yields 2 dozen cookies.
Butter a 2-quart casserole.
Put 1 can of pineapple on bottom of dish.
Mix cheeses together and sprinkle half of cheese mixture on top of pineapple.
Mix flour and sugar and sprinkle on cheese. Follow with second can of pineapple and the remaining half of flour-sugar mixture, leaving remaining half of cheese mixture for top.
Pour 1/2 cup pineapple juice over entire dish and dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbly and brown.
Mix together first four ingredients and form into logs.
Roll logs in chopped beef until well covered.
Can be prepared ahead of time and kept refrigerated several days.
Serve with crackers.
Prepare egg noodles as directed; drain.
Brown hamburger meat; drain.
Combine all ingredients together.
Place in greased 9 x 13-inch dish; sprinkle Mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine Crisco, brown sugar, egg, milk and vanilla in large bowl.
Beat at medium speed until well blended.
Combine oats, flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
Mix into creamed mixture at a low speed.
Stir in raisins.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix all together; drop and bake at 350° to 375°.
Makes lots.
Mix all together.
Spread over tortillas; roll up.
Wrap tightly in plastic.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cut 1/2 to 3/4-inch and serve with salsa.
Whisk together and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Mix both milks, eggs and vanilla until well combined.
Stir in the flaked coconut and pour the mixture into 6 individual custard cups or a larger flan mold.

Place the cups or mold in a large baking pan and fill it with water to a depth of 1-inch. Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean. A flan mold will take longer than individual cups. Allow to cool, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.
Crumble half of cake in bottom of bowl. Layer half of pudding, pineapple and pie filling. Repeat with second layer. Add large Cool Whip on top. Nuts and coconut are optional. Refrigerate overnight.
Cut fillets in 4-inch portions.
Season with salt and pepper. Mix nuts and cayenne.
Dip fillets in egg and water mix; roll in flour.
Fry in butter in skillet or microwave 5 minutes with nut mix sprinkled over fillets.

Melt butter. Add sugar and milk. Bring to a rolling boil, cook for 7 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Add chocolate chips and marshmallows. Stir until dissolved. Pour into 2- 9 x 13 buttered pans. Cool. Cut into squares. Makes 5 lbs.
In large Pyrex casserole, well greased, put 1 cup milk and 1 egg.
Beat with fork until well blended.
Add in layers cooked macaroni, grated cheese, dots of butter, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Arrange sliced tomatoes.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 35 minutes or until thoroughly heated through.
Mix green beans and cream of mushroom soup and top with onion rings.
Place in microwave until steaming hot.
Melt margarine.
Add other ingredients and stir together. Pour into a glass casserole dish and bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix beans, onion and pepper sauce; reserve.
Mix baking mix and sour cream until soft dough forms; beat vigorously 20 strokes.
Gently smooth dough into ball on floured cloth covered board.
Knead 20 times.
Roll dough 1/4 inch thick.
Cut with floured 2-inch cutter.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press a deep indention about 1 1/2 inches in diameter in center of each round with floured hands.
Fill each with generous teaspoon of bean mixture; spread within indention. Top each with chilies and cheese.
Bake until light brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients.
In a large baking pan, shape into a loaf.
Bake 1 hour or until done.
Makes about 8 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Trim off each garlic head to expose the tops of the cloves.
Place heads in shallow baking dish, such as a 9-inch pie plate.
Drizzle garlic with oil and sprinkle with pepper, salt and thyme.
Roast garlic for 30 minutes.
Reduce heat to 250° and cook for 1 hour longer.
Serve garlic with slices of crusty French bread, butter and goat cheese, such as Feta.
Pop the cloves out of the skins and spread on bread.
Yield:
8 servings.
Saute onion and celery in margarine.
Mix all ingredients well and bake in greased 8-inch casserole at 350° for 35 minutes.
Combine dry ingredients.
Beat eggs, add cream, oil and honey.
Stir into dry ingredients until just moistened.
Pour into 9 inch square pan.
Bake at 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes.
In saucepan, combine all ingredients except coffee.
Heat to boiling.
Strain.
Pour liquid over coffee in heatproof container. Stir coffee until dissolved.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Lightly grease a 2-quart casserole. Wash, pare and thinly slice potatoes; measure 8 cups.
Cook potatoes and onions, covered in small amount of boiling water, with 2 teaspoon salt, for about 5 minutes or until slightly tender.
Drain.
Melt butter or margarine in saucepan; remove from heat.
Stir in flour, pepper, paprika and remaining salt until smooth.
Blend in milk.
Cook, stirring, over medium heat to boiling point or until thickened and smooth.
In prepared casserole, layer one-third of potatoes and onions; sprinkle with 1 tablespoon parsley.
Top with one-third of the sauce.
Repeat, then add remaining potatoes and top with remaining sauce.
Bake, uncovered, for 35 minutes, or until top is browned and potatoes are tender when pierced with fork.
Serves 6 to 8.
Microwave chocolate and milk in a large microwavable dish on High for 2 or 3 minutes, until chocolate is melted, stirring half way through heating time.
Stir until chocolate is completely melted.
Stir in vanilla and walnuts.
Spread in a greased 8 x 8-inch pan.
Refrigerate until firm.
Cut into squares.
In a large mixing bowl, mix all the ingredients together.
If you are using broccoli, thaw it in the microwave and drain well before mixing it in.
Place mixture in ungreased casserole bowl and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Remove and stir well during this cooking time.
After it is done, let it stand for a few minutes.
Mix ground beef with sauce, onion and salt.
Shape into patties. Brown on each side.
Put hot potatoes on each patty. Sprinkle with cheese and brown or until cheese melts.
In a 3-quart saucepan, cook beef and onions until beef is brown; drain.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat to a boil over medium heat.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Makes about 7 one cup servings.
Divide noodles into 3
for the 3 layers.
Combine water with sauce in bowl.
Cover bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan with 1 1/2 cups sauce.
Arrange layer of uncooked noodles, slightly overlapping, on top of sauce.
Spread 1/2 Ricotta and Mozzarella over noodles.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons Parmesan.
Add layer of sauce.
Layer noodles with the remaining Ricotta and Mozzarella and 2 tablespoons Parmesan.
Top with layer of noodles. Pour remaining sauce over, spreading evenly to cover edges of noodles. Sprinkle with 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Cover tightly with heavy-duty foil.
Set on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let stand, covered, on rack for 10 minutes before cutting.
Position rack in center of oven and preheat oven to 350°. Line baking sheets with parchment paper or coat with nonstick cooking spray.
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar, applesauce, egg white, oil and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in raisins.
In a medium size bowl, stir together the oats, cake flour, whole wheat flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
Using a wooden spoon, stir the dry ingredients into the wet, mixing just until blended.
Drop the dough by tablespoonfuls onto a prepared baking sheet, spacing cookies about 1 1/2 inches apart.
Bake for about 15 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Transfer cookies to a wire rack; let cool.
Makes 3 dozen cookies.
Place all ingredients except marshmallows and vanilla in top of double boiler over boiling water and beat with a rotary beater 7 minutes or until mixture holds a peak.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and marshmallows.
Continue to beat until well blended and apply to cake.
Line sides and bottom of medium size casserole dish with bread dipped in melted butter or margarine.
Mix other ingredients together and pour into bread-lined dish.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes or until firm.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water; add strawberries, bananas and nuts.
Put 1/2 of mixture in glass bowl or mold and refrigerate until firm.
Spread 1/2 of the sour cream on first mixture of Jell-O and pour remaining Jell-O mixture on top of sour cream. Chill again until firm.
Spread the remaining sour cream on top. Better if made the day before.
Fry garlic and onion in oil until lightly browned.
Add clams with only 1/2 juice, parsley and a little salt and pepper.
Add wine; simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve over cooked linguini.
Combine sugar, corn syrup, milk and cream of tartar in a 2-quart glass measure.
Cook on High for 6 minutes.
Let stand 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly cooled.
Beat vigorously until creamy. Add peppermint extract and food coloring.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto sheets of foil.
Let stand until cool and firm.
Store in airtight container.
Makes about 36 mints.
Mix all ingredients except crackers and margarine.
Place in a 2-quart buttered casserole dish.
Mix crackers with margarine. Sprinkle on top of vegetables. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Thoroughly combine all ingredients and shape into a loaf pan (8 x 4 x 1 1/2-inches).
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Allow meat loaf to stand 5 minutes before slicing.
Makes 6 servings.
Heat oven to 425°.
Prepare pastry for 9-inch crust.
Sprinkle bacon, cheese and onion in pastry-lined pie pan.
Blend remaining ingredients with mixer.
Pour into pie pan.
Bake 15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 300°.
Bake pie 30 minutes longer or until knife inserted 1 inch from edge comes out clean.
Let pie stand 10 minutes before cutting.
Serve in wedges.
Put all the ingredients into blender. Can add roquefort or bleu cheese.
Keeps well.
Combine
all ingredients, except nuts, in top of double boiler over medium heat.	Stir constantly until smooth.
Then add nuts. Spread in 9 x 5-inch buttered pan.	Cool and cut in squares.
Cook spaghetti in 2-quart stock.
If you do not have that much stock, add a little water.
Drain.
Add cubed cheese.
Add mushrooms, onions (cooked in butter), bell pepper and chicken, Ro-Tel and Worcestershire.
Fold in peas last.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake in 300° oven for 30 minutes.
Serves approximately 8.
Combine crumbs and melted butter; place in bottom of an 8-inch square pan.
Combine cream cheese, powdered sugar and whipped cream.
Pour in pan and spoon blueberry filling on top.
Freeze for 2 hours before serving.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, oregano and salt.
Mix well.
Cut in cold margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Blend in cheese, egg and yeast. Turn out on well floured surface.
Knead.
Shape into ball.
Place in well-greased bowl.
Brush top with melted margarine; cover. Let rise until doubled.
Punch down.
Shape as desired.
Brush with melted margarine; cover.
Let rise again until nearly doubled.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Serve warm.
Yield: 1 1/2 to 2 dozen.
Drain crabmeat; press to remove excess fluid.
Flake.
Mix crabmeat, onions, cheese, seasonings and mayonnaise.
Remove stems and scrape gills from mushrooms with a spoon to make deep cups. Heat oven to 325°.
Stuff mushrooms generously with crab mixture. Place in ungreased shallow baking dish.
Bake 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Turn oven to broil.
Broil until golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Combine juices in freezer container.
Mix well.
Freeze for 2 days.
Place mixture in a punch bowl.
Add ginger ale 1 hour before serving.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch loaf pan.
Mix rice and both soups and spread into loaf pan.
Lay chicken parts on top of rice.
Mix onion soup, water and lemon juice and pour over each piece of chicken.
Cover with foil and bake at 300° for 3 hours.
Serves 4 to 6.
Boil sugar and milk to soft ball stage, then add marshmallow, peanut butter and vanilla.
Beat until smooth.
Pour into 9-inch pan, let cool then cut.
Mix all ingredients together very thoroughly and chill.
Use salt and pepper to taste.
Beat egg before you mix in rest of ingredients.
Flour hands and separate dough into 4 sections.
Roll each section into snakes on a floured surface.
Cut 1-inch pieces out of the snakes and, with thumb, press flat.
Fast freeze (about 10 minutes) on a cookie sheet.
When hard, cook in boiling water (salted) for 5 minutes after they rise to the top of the pot.
Serve with spaghetti sauce.
About 4 hours before serving or early in day, preheat oven to 350°.
Grease cookie sheet.
In large bowl, combine first 6 ingredients and 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour.
With pastry blender or two knives used, scissor-fashion, cut in margarine or butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in raisins and caraway seed.
Stir in buttermilk just until flour is moistened (dough will be sticky).
In large skillet, saute onion.
(I like to add garlic, also.) Add venison and cook until browned.
Add mushrooms and brown, then add soup and sour cream.
Cover and simmer 30 to 60 minutes. Electric fry pan works good.
Serve over hot noodles.
Cook macaroni until slightly tender.
Drain.
Set aside. Brown meat and onions in small skillet.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Oil a 1-quart casserole dish; spoon in 1/3 of meat mixture.
Add cooked macaroni and then add remaining meat. Spread cheese soup over all (may be frozen uncooked).
Cover the casserole tightly; bake at 400° until bubbly.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix together and boil for several minutes.
Can add a few marshmallows for a change; let them melt in sauce while hot.
Microwave Directions:
Spread 1/2 teaspoon peanut butter on flat side of each cookie.
Place marshmallow between peanut butter spread sides of cookies, making a sandwich on microwave-safe paper towel.
Microwave on High for 6 to 8 seconds or until marshmallow is slightly softened.
Squeeze cookie together slightly.
Makes 1 cookie.
Wash cucumbers; trim ends.
Cut cucumbers into 1/4-inch slices.
Combine cucumber slices, red pepper, onion and garlic in a
large
bowl;
add salt and stir well.
Pack crushed ice over cucumbers;	cover
and
let stand 24 hours.
Drain well. Rinse cucumber
mixture
