several	times
in cold water; drain well. Remove
and discard garlic.
Pack cucumber mixture into hot, sterilized jars, leaving 1/2 inch headspace.
In heavy skillet brown salt pork in olive oil.
Add vegetables and saute until slightly tender.
Remove pork and vegetables, leaving fat in skillet.
Add 1/4 cup pickle juice to skillet and brown meat.
Baste meat with juice while browning.
Sugar in juice will caramelize and glaze meat.
Turn meat and baste with additional 1/4 cup of juice.
Add more juice as needed.
Juice will cook off as meat browns.
Put all the remaining ingredients in a large covered roasting pan or kettle and cook in 325° oven for approximately 4 hours or cook, covered, on top of stove for 4 hours or until tender.
Pour gravy over sliced meat to serve.
Soak beans overnight. Drain soaking liquid. Cook 1 hour. Rinse and chill beans.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour over with Italian dressing. Will keep several days.

Cook rice and broccoli until tender. Do not salt anything. Saute onions and celery in butter. Combine all ingredients. Pour into 11 x 7 inch casserole dish. Let stand in refrigerator for 12 hours. Bake on 350° for 30 minutes. Serves 8.
Mix and place in loaf pan; add sauce and bake.
Place ham, with pineapple and brown sugar on top in 400° oven wrapped tightly in aluminum foil for about 1 1/2 hours.
Mix everything in a 10 inch skillet.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly until the mixture turns golden brown (about 5 or 6 minutes).
Spread in a greased 8 or 9 inch round pan.
Cool.
Remove from pan and break into pieces.
Mix juices and sugar; stir in beaten egg.
Cook in double boiler for 5 minutes until spoon is coated.
Good on fruits and melons.
Mix ground beef, onion, 2/3 cup chopped pepper and cooked rice.
Add crumbled bread and tomato juice; mix well.
Take seeds out of the 8 sweet peppers and drop peppers in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain and fill with ground beef mixture.
Put in a large pot with lid and pour ketchup over top of peppers.
Add 1/2 cup of tomato juice to pot.
Cover and cook 2 hours in oven at 350°. Uncover and cook 30
minutes.
Place water in a saucepan.
Add cloves and cinnamon.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Add the tea at once; stir to distribute and immerse leaves.
Cover and steep 5 minutes. Strain.
While tea steeps, heat orange and lemon juices, with sugar added, to a boil.
Stir into the hot tea and serve at once in teacups.
Makes 7 or 8 servings.
Prepare stuffing as directed on package.
Do not stuff hens until ready to roast.
Rinse hens with cold water.
Pat dry.
Rub neck and body cavities with salt and pepper.
Lightly stuff cavities with prepared stuffing.
Roast at 400° for 1 hour.
Place any remaining stuffing in a small baking dish; bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
(Meanwhile, heat orange juice and butter; baste hens frequently during the last 30 minutes of roasting.)
Combine all ingredients (except juice, potatoes and hamburger).
Simmer over medium
heat until tender; then discard bay leaf.
Add juice, diced potatoes and partly fried hamburger. Cook until potatoes are soft.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream and taco seasoning all together. Shape into a mound on a plate.
Spread salsa sauce over top. Sprinkle chopped ingredients over top.
Sprinkle cheese over top last.
Serve chilled with corn tortilla chips.
Saute hamburger, pepper and onion together until meat is brown. Add seasonings and keep mixture warm.
Melt cheese and Ro-Tel together.
Keep warm.
In individual salad bowls, layer Fritos, meat, lettuce and tomatoes.
Cover with cheese sauce.
Marinate artichoke hearts in vinegar and oil for 4 to 6 hours; drain and reserve liquid.

recipes.t: Baked Beans With Pineapple And Bacon
d: Mix all ingredients, except bacon in 2-quart baking dish. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook bacon crisp; blot on paper towel.
Crumble up and add to bean mixture before serving.
Very good.
Melt margarine.
Add flour, cream cheese, salt, liquid, chicken, macaroni and pimiento.
Mix well.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes, until slightly browned.
Mix first three ingredients and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese and powdered sugar together and set aside.
Mix Dream Whip together by directions on box.
Fold into cream mixture.
Put in chilled crust and top with blueberry pie filling.
(Can substitute strawberry or cherry pie filling.)
Melt butter in a skillet.
Add rice, toss to coat with butter. Heat on low for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place rice mixture in a 2-quart casserole bowl; add hot chicken broth.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Stir in the remaining ingredients.
Cook 5 additional minutes.
Serves 4.
Blend cheese with butter; add flour, salt and paprika.
Mix well.
Pat olives dry on paper towel.
Mold 1 teaspoon dough around each olive to cover.
At this point you can refrigerate or freeze puffs for up to 10 days.
They hold their shape better if frozen first.
Bake puffs on lightly greased cookie sheet in a 400° oven until lightly golden brown, approximately 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve hot.

Toss all vegetables in enough olive oil to coat; add herbs. Spread out onto 2 cookie sheets and roast in oven at 400° until well done and crispy, about 15-20 minutes, stirring vegetables at least once during baking.
Beat eggs and other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Soak bread in hot milk.
Set aside.
Beat together eggs and sugar.
Add to soaked bread/milk mixture.
Add vanilla, raisins and grated apple.
Add brandy last.
Bake in well-greased pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Grate
carrots.
Place	in
8-inch Dutch oven.	Mix the rest of the ingredients and bake for 30 minutes.
Cook meat, mix in refried beans, taco seasoning mix until hot and blended. Mix enchilada sauce and soup together, warm.
Put meat mixture in middle of tortilla, roll and place in greased baking dish. Pour sauce mixture over rolled tortillas, sprinkle with cheese and bake until bubbly.
Place shrimp in boiling salted water; reduce heat and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Shrimp are done when they are pink and tender; drain and rinse with cold water, then chill.
Combine first 4 ingredients; mix well.
Spoon into uncooked manicotti shells.
Arrange in 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish. Combine picante sauce and 1/2 cup water; pour over manicotti.
Set oven at 350°.
Mix together sugar, butter, egg and vanilla.
Beat with mixer until creamy.
Add baking powder to flour.
Alternate flour and milk to mixture, beating with mixer until well mixed.
Fold in drained blueberries.
Spoon out into muffin tins.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown.
Mix together the sugar, cornstarch, salt, eggs and enough milk to make a smooth paste; add to scalded milk.
When it comes to a boil, boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add remaining milk, vanilla and Grape-Nuts.
Can add Eagle Brand.
Yields 8 quarts.
Okay to use for 6 quarts, just don't add Eagle Brand.
Brown meat. Add all ingredients, except noodles and cheese. Season to taste.
Simmer for at least 3 hours.
Do not skim off too much fat, or lasagna will be dry.
Cook noodles as directed on package, but add 1 tablespoon oil to prevent sticking.
Place in pan as follows:
layer of noodles and layer of cheese.
Repeat, ending with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Prepare crust.
Cool.
Press half of softened ice cream into crust.
In small bowl, stir corn syrup and peanut butter until blended.
Pour half of mixture over ice cream.
Sprinkle with half of peanuts, repeating layering.
Freeze until firm, about 5 hours. Let pie stand at room temperature for 5 minutes for easy cutting.
Mix squash, sugar, flour, nutmeg, vanilla and lemon extract together.
Add beaten eggs.
Add milk to squash.
Stir until well blended.
Pour into an unbaked pie shell.
Bake for 10 minutes at 375°.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes or longer.
Mix oleo with flour, like pie dough.
Add egg yolks, sour cream and vanilla.
Mix together and make 8 balls of dough.
Put in refrigerator for 2 1/2 hours or overnight.
Roll like pies in powdered sugar.
Beat egg whites and 1/2 box powdered sugar together.
Spread egg white mixture over dough; sprinkle with ground nuts.
Cut with pizza cutter like pie in 8 pieces.
Roll outside to center and put on greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes or until brown.
Cream the butter and sugar until light; add the applesauce, raisins, flour, spices, salt, soda and baking powder sifted together twice.
Beat well and bake in a shallow well-greased pan in a moderate oven, 350° to 400°.
Test with toothpick after 40 minutes.
Trim all fat from roast, brown and drain.
Combine 1/4 cup flour, salt and pepper.
Coat meat with flour mixture.
Place all vegetables except mushrooms in crock-pot and top with roast. Cover and cook on low setting for 10 to 12 hours.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Place beef, garlic salt and stuffing in pie pan.
Add milk and mix together with fork.
Spread mixture evenly over bottom of pan with a rim around the edge.
Spread tomato paste over meat. Sprinkle oregano and mushrooms over paste.
Top with cheeses. Bake 20 minutes at 400°.
Mix all ingredients together (except drain and save pineapple juice).
Beat together pineapple juice, water and lemon juice. Then stir into Jell-O until dissolved.
Chill until set.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Mix sour cream and cream cheese.
Spread on a cake plate. Pour picante sauce over and sprinkle cheeses on top.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Mix with spaghetti sauce, drained mushrooms and water.
Layer in 9 x 13-inch pan: meat sauce, uncooked lasagne noodles, cottage cheese, Mozzarella and Parmesan cheese, beginning and ending with meat sauce.
Sprinkle top with Parmesan.
Cover with heavy duty foil and seal tightly.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let stand 15 to 20 minutes before removing foil.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Combine water, butter and salt and bring to boil.
Remove from heat and flour all at once.
Stir vigorously until mixture leaves sides of pan and forms ball around spoon.
(If ball does not form immediately, hold saucepan over low heat and beat briskly a few seconds.)
Cool slightly.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat until smooth and glossy after each addition.
Drop by teaspoonful onto greased baking sheet, leaving 2 inches between puffs.
Bake 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake until no bubbles of fat remain on surface and sides of puffs feel rigid, about 30 minutes.
Cool.
Cut a cap off puff and fill with Pastry Cream.
Replace cap.
Makes 10 large puffs.
Cake:
Mix all together and add 1 cup sour milk.
If you have no sour milk, add 1 teaspoon vinegar.
Add flour and soda.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.

Cream Crisco; add eggs. Add to flour mixture. Mix. Add sour milk. Last add water. Drop by tablespoon and bake 8 minutes at 350°. Cook flour and milk until thickened. Beat in Crisco with powdered sugar until fluffy; add cooled paste and vanilla. Beat until creamy and spread between 2 cookies.
Cream butter, sugar and Crisco.
Add sour cream and blend.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix in vanilla.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Add alternately with milk.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes in 10-inch tube pan.
Brown ground beef and spices in skillet; drain, then add spaghetti sauce and cottage cheese.
While cooking meat mixture, cook noodles and drain.
Put crackers in a large bowl.
Pour on oil.
In another bowl, mix together all dry ingredients.
Mix all ingredients together and store in a container with a lid.
Remove chicken from bone and place in dish.
Heat celery soup and broth and pour over chicken.
Mix flour, milk and baking powder with margarine and pour over chicken.
Bake at 425° for 30 minutes.
In small frying pan, toast sesame seed over low heat, shaking pan often, until golden brown (about 3 minutes).

Transfer seed to blender or food processor and add garbanzos, 2 tablespoons olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and 6 tablespoons reserved liquid. Whirl, adding more liquid if necessary, until hummus is smooth, but still thick.
Season with salt and pepper.
Place in shallow bowl.
Drizzle with remaining 2 tablespoons oil.
Makes 2 cups.
Stir together flour, sugar, salt and baking powder.
In large mixing bowl, combine all-bran and milk.
Let stand about 5 minutes.
Add flour mixture and raisins.
Stir only until combined.
Spray 12 muffin pan cups with no-stick spray.
Divide mixture into 12 cups.
Bake at 400° for approximately 20 minutes. For reduced calories, use 2 tablespoons sugar instead of above amounts.
In small saucepan on low heat, melt butter and chocolate. Take off burner.
Add sugar and mix.
Add one egg at a time, mixing after each.
Add all remaining ingredients and mix.
Grease 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook squash and mash.
Add eggs, milk and other ingredients to squash.
Pour into buttered baking dish.
Sprinkle cheese on top and bake.
Bake 40 minutes at 375°.
Chill and keep in refrigerator for a good long time.

recipes.t: Chicken And Rice In Green Vegetable Broth
d: Remove and discard skin from chicken.
In a large sauce pan, combine chicken broth, water, rice, thyme and pepper.
Add chicken, cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes.
Shred cabbage and spinach.
Remove chicken to a cutting board.
Remove meat from bones and cut into bite size pieces.
Return chicken to broth, add cabbage and spinach, bring to a boil over medium heat.
Boil broth just until cabbage and chicken are wilted and heated through, 1 minute.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs, sugars, dressing and vanilla at medium speed with electric mixer; add flour and baking soda. Set aside 1 cup of batter.
Spread remaining batter into lightly greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool 10 minutes.
Combine crackers with butter and press on bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan, reserving 1/4 cup for topping.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gradually add sugar, salt and vanilla.
Spread egg white mixture over cracker crumbs.
Bake in a 325° oven 10 to 15 minutes.
Cool.
Spread pie filling over top. Beat whipping cream until stiff.
Add powdered sugar.
Spread pie filling and refrigerate.
Cut into squares to serve.
Mix salmon, onion, green pepper (if desired), basil, thyme, salt, pepper, egg, flour and cracker crumbs (if desired).
Form patties and roll in additional cracker crumbs.
Fry in small amount of Crisco.
Makes 5 to 6 patties.
Combine all ingredients, except nuts.
Chill 3 hours.
Shape into ball and roll in chopped nuts.
Chill until firm.
Drain
liquid from fruits.
Combine all ingredients and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours before serving.
Cook sugar, Karo and water together in very heavy skillet or Dutch oven on top of stove until it spins threads.
(Pick up spoon and let it run slowly out into hot syrup.
Watch for threads.)
Or if using candy thermometer, cook to hard crack stage.
Add oleo and raw peanuts.
When candy turns color of peanut hulls it is ready. Remove from heat and quickly add vanilla and soda.
Stir and pour into greased cookie sheet.
Spread as thin as possible using 2 greased forks pulling it to the edges of pan.
Cool.
Break into pieces.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Chill enough so it does not wilt lettuce.
Chop onion and tomatoes.
Cut lettuce to salad size.
In large bowl, combine lettuce, onion, tomatoes and taco mix.
Add beef.
Crunch up the Doritos and add to mixture.
Pour dressing over salad just before serving.
In a 10-inch skillet, brown meat and onion; drain any excess fat (electric skillet at 350°).
Stir in soup, enchilada sauce, milk and chillies.
Reduce heat to 220°.
Cover and cook 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Slice onions and separate into rings.
Make batter of the beaten eggs and milk.
Stir together flour and seasoning.
Dip onions into flour and then in batter.
Drop onion rings into oil and cook until golden.
Serve hot.
Mix the ingredients together and brown in 325° oven until light brown; stir often.
Chop ice cream and sherbet in punch bowl.
Add juice.
Stir. Add ginger ale last.
Serves 25 people.
Mix all ingredients together (except for powdered sugar). Blend well; roll into small balls.
Roll in powdered sugar. Refrigerate.
Combine cold ground beef and remaining ingredients and mix well in a heavy saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until boils, stirring often. Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease pie plate.
Heat salted water; add broccoli.
Cover and heat to boiling.
Cook until almost tender, about 5 minutes.
Drain.
Mix broccoli, onion, green pepper and cheese in pie plate.
Beat remaining ingredients until smooth, 15 seconds in blender on high speed or 1 minute with hand mixer.
Pour into pie plate.
Bake until golden brown and knife comes out clean at 350° for 40 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting.
Place pheasant on aluminum foil in roaster.
Rub interior with butter, then salt, pepper and garlic.
Cover bird with uncooked rice.
Pour apricot juice and apricots over all.
Wrap tightly in the foil.
Bake in 325° oven until pheasant can be easily pierced with a fork.
Serves 2 to 4.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Spray 2 loaf pans with vegetable spray. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat together sugar, oil and eggs.
In a separate bowl, stir together dry ingredients. Add dry mixture to batter and mix just until blended.
Stir vanilla, apples and pecans into batter.
Pour batter into prepared loaf pans.
Bake for 1 hour or until inserted knife comes out clean.
Yield: 2 loaves.
Place chicken pieces in baking dish.
Heat ingredients together in pan and pour over chicken.
Bake 1 hour at 375°.
Slice sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch thick pieces.
Combine with pineapple, butter, sugar and cinnamon in 2-quart casserole.
Place in microwave oven and cook on High 4 minutes.
Stir.
Sprinkle top with pecans and brown sugar.
Continue cooking 2 to 4 minutes.
If dish is not hot and topping melted after 2 minutes, give 1/4 turn before continuing to cook.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Preheat
oven
to
Cook ground sausage and drain off all
fat.
Set
aside.
Spray 9 x 13-inch baking pan with Pam. Line
bottom
of
pan
with bread.	Beat 8 eggs and pour over bread.
Sprinkle dry mustard over eggs.
Sprinkle ground sausage over
eggs.
Sprinkle
Cheddar
cheese
over sausage. Sprinkle crushed corn flakes over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes covered with foil.	Remove foil and bake until brown, approximately 5 minutes.
Cut cheese into cubes in a saucepan; add salsa to keep cheese from sticking.
Brown hamburger; drain.
Salt and pepper to taste. Add Tabasco sauce.
Combine hamburger and cheese.
Excellent dip for nachos or taco salad.
Mix mustard and catsup together first to keep from lumping. Add rest and bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Peel pumpkin and cut into small squares.
Boil until soft. Do not drain water.
Add milk until pumpkin is covered.
Bring to a simmer.
Add salt and pepper.
Beat eggs with fork.
Add flour slowly and keep mixing until it gets a little thick (like dumplings).
Drop this mixture into pumpkin 1/2 teaspoon at a time; let simmer 20 minutes.
Serve.
Combine all ingredients.
Let stand until double in size, about 1 hour.
Knead down and let rise again.
Roll out on floured board until 1/4-inch thick.
Spread with oleo, cinnamon and brown sugar.
Roll up like a jelly roll.
Grease pan with oleo and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Let raise until double in size.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Peel and dice baked sweet potato.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut shortening and potato into flour mixture. Add milk and sugar; stir until well mixed.
Roll out on floured surface 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick.
With knife, cut into squares and bake on greased baking sheet at 400° for 12 minutes.
Makes 12 to 18 biscuits.
In small saucepan, whisk together broth, milk and flour. Insert clove into onion; add to broth mixture along with remaining ingredients.
Bring to just below boiling over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Lower heat to simmer and cook, stirring frequently, for 10 minutes.
Remove onion and bay leaf with slotted spoon.
Makes 1 cup.
(Have
all
cheese at room temperature.) Add garlic and pecans to cheese mixture.
Divide into logs about size as Ritz crackers. Mix
chili
powder,
red cayenne pepper and lots of paprika.
Roll logs
in this mixture on waxed paper.
Wrap in waxed
paper
and chill overnight.
Slice and serve with Ritz crackers.
Pour all ingredients in a bowl.
Melt 3 minutes in microwave. Stir.
Pour in pan.

recipes.t: Bread Pudding And Brown Sugar Sauce
d: Butter dish.
Layer brown sugar on the bottom, then layer the bread cubes over sugar.
Mix eggs, sugar, vanilla, milk and raisins; pour over bread, slowly.
Put in pan of hot water.
Bake at 375° until done, about 1 hour.
Put Velveeta cheese, oleo and vanilla in a large pan on stove and melt together.
Blend in the dry ingredients together in large bowl.
After the dry ingredients are mixed, add the melted oleo and cheese mix with a spoon.
When the mixture is fully combined, place it in a long pan (cookie sheet with wax paper on bottom) and pop it into the refrigerator.
Cut into squares when it is firm and cold.
Keep refrigerated.
Makes 5 pounds.
May be frozen for later use.
Combine croutons and oleo; pat into quiche pan.
Combine 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese and remaining ingredients; mix well.
Spoon over crust.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Cream together shortening and sugars.
Add eggs and mix thoroughly.
Add flour, soda and baking powder with pineapple and vanilla.
Mix.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 350°.
Follow directions on package for bread dough except use cookie sheet.
Spread dough on a greased sheet.
Cook hamburger meat, sausage, onions and green peppers.
Spread tomato sauce on bread dough; sprinkle with garlic salt, if desired.
When meat mixture is about cooked, drain and spread over dough.
Add mushrooms and pepperoni.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.

Combine first 3 ingredients in a heavy saucepan. Combine milk and egg yolks gradually stir into sugar mixture. Cook over medium heat stirring constantly until mixture thickens and boils. Boil 1 minute stirring constantly. Remove from heat, stir in 1/2 cup coconut, butter and vanilla. Pour into pie shell. Cover with meringue sealing edges and sprinkle 1/4 cup coconut on top of meringue and bake in 350 degree oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
Combine the following
ingredients
and boil 8 minutes, stirring constantly:
powdered
sugar, evaporated milk, chocolate chips and 1/2 cup butter.
Add vanilla and cool.
Combine cookies and 1/2 cup melted	butter.
Pat
into 9 x 13-inch pan and freeze until firm.
Sprinkle
peanuts
over
cookie crust. Spread ice cream over	peanuts and cover with cooled chocolate mixture. Freeze until ready to serve.
Serves 16.
Combine the first 5 ingredients; mix well.
Drop by tablespoon onto a waxed paper-lined cookie sheet.
Chill for 1 hour.
Shape into trees.
Brown beef and onion in skillet.
Pour off excess fat; add the rest of ingredients.
Bring to boil and simmer 15 minutes; turn into a large, greased casserole dish (1 1/2-quart).
Boil the potatoes in their jackets until done; peel and mash. Add butter, sugar and lemon extract.
Combine the beaten egg and milk.
Mix with the potatoes until blended.
Pour into the pastry shell and bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Take 1 cup of cracker crumbs and layer the bottom of the casserole dish.
Then be sure you have drained your Veg-All, and put them as your next layer.
Add your celery soup and pour milk over it.
Put margarine and sprinkle salt and pepper over it. Cook for about 25 minutes in 400° oven.
Remove, then spread with rest of cracker crumbs and cheese.
Place back in oven for 5 to 7 minutes, or until cheese melts.
Mix first 6 ingredients together.
Shape into cakes and roll in crushed cracker crumbs.
Fry in hot oil until brown.
Bake the cake in 9-inch pans.
Cool thoroughly and split each layer in half.
Spread the cherry pie filling between the split layers.
Now you have the original 2 layers with cherry filling in between.
Reserve 1/2 cup pie filling to go on top of cake.
Melt margarine in dish you are going to bake in.
Beat eggs, sugar and cornstarch; add vanilla, milk and creamed corn.
Pour into dish over butter.
Bake at 375° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Do not cover.
Grind coriander, garlic and nuts.
Mix all together into batter, adding 2 packages Spanish peanuts.
Scoop batter with a hostess spoon and fry until brown.
Mix, in order, first 8 ingredients.
Chill 2 hours.
Drop on greased sheet and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Cook hamburger; drain well.
Put in crock-pot on low; mix in the rest of the ingredients.
Cook until cheese melts and serve hot with nacho chips.
Boil fryer until tender. Remove from broth and set aside to cool. Mix dry ingredients.
Cut in shortening.
Add beaten eggs and enough milk to make a stiff dough. Roll out really thin on heavily floured board.
Cut into pieces (pizza cutter works great!).
Drop into rapidly boiling broth.
Cover and simmer on very low heat for 5 to 10 minutes. Remove skin and bones from chicken and pull into bite size pieces.
Add chicken to pot and season to taste with black pepper.
I pour about a cup of sweet milk in pot just as it's finished cooking.
Mix sugar, cocoa, baking powder and milk together.
Bring to boil until mixture forms a soft ball.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter.
Stir until mixture thickens, pour onto buttered plate.
Mix together and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all the ingredients and pour into a greased pan. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Mix ingredients together well, then drop by teaspoonfuls on cookie sheet and bake 10 to 12 minutes at 375°.
Mix together all ingredients for patties.
When milk is absorbed, shape mixture into 12 patties.
Cook slowly for 10 minutes or until brown on both sides in a small amount of fat. Mix together all ingredients for Sauce.
Add to the meat in skillet and cook slowly, turning in Sauce.
Combine all ingredients except mayonnaise. Beat well with mixer.
Cook until thick. Remove pan from stove and add mayonnaise. Beat well and cool.
Cut beef with scissors.
Mix all together, then refrigerate.
Place berries in 9 inch square baking dish.
Combine sugar, cornstarch, and salt, mixing well.	Sprinkle mixture over berries. Dot with butter.
Roll out pastry to fit dish.
Place pastry over berries.
Brush with milk, and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 425° for 30 minutes.
Makes 6-8 servings.
Dissolve each flavor jello separately with 1 1/2 cups hot water.
Pour in ice cube trays.
Set until firm.
Mix all ingredients in punch bowl.
Makes 25 to 30 punch cup servings.
Blend all ingredients except oil. Drip in oil very slowly; blend well.
Store in jar in refrigerator.

recipes.t: Alita Darby Arthur'S Classic Pecan Pie
d: Stir together eggs, sugar, corn syrup, margarine and vanilla. Add pecans; mix.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes in 350° oven.
Cool; serve with whipped cream or ice cream.
Mix together and heat in microwave for 8 minutes.
Serve warm with crackers.
Cut dates into thirds, add coconut, nuts and cherries, sprinkled with flour.
Add milk and mix well.
Butter loaf pan and dust with flour.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add the remaining ingredients. Add water to cover 1 inch above ingredients.
Cook for 1 hour on low heat.
Serves 15 to 20.
Mix lobster, mayonnaise, celery and onion.
Serve on bed of lettuce.
Make applesauce with apples.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix all ingredients.
Boil for 1 1/2 hours in the oven or until thick. Put in jars and seal.
Lay slices of rye bread in bottom of Dutch oven.
Place brisket, with fat side down, on top of the bread in Dutch oven. Sprinkle garlic powder and pepper on brisket.
Throw onion slices into pan.
Pour beer over the meat.
Spread the chile sauce over the meat.
Cover Dutch oven.
Melt margarine; add to stuffing mix.
Grease 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Cut chicken into small pieces.
Combine soup, broth and sour cream.
Put 1/2 of stuffing mixture in casserole.
Layer all of chicken on top and pour broth mixture over it.
Top with remaining stuffing mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until bubbling hot.
Mix all ingredients except onion.
Put into skillet, top with onion and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix together
sugar,
corn syrup, water and salt in a 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Cook in microwave on Full power 20 to 22 minutes or	until
hard
ball
stage is reached.
Stir once or twice during
cooking.
While
syrup
cooks,
beat egg whites until stiff peaks form in a large mixing bowl.
Gradually pour hot syrup over
egg	whites until beating at high speed until mixture
is thickened
and
candy
starts
to lose its gloss. Beating
may require about 12 minutes.
Add vanilla and nuts. Drop by
teaspoon on
waxed	paper.	Candy
may be tinted for special occasions.
Sift together all the dry ingredients.
Add egg, buttermilk, and oil.
Mix well and pour into hot iron skillet.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Bake 15 minutes.
Flip in pan and brown.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In large bowl, combine flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon and cloves; set aside.
With mixer at low speed cream oil and sugar until light and fluffy; beat in egg whites and applesauce.
Stir in dry ingredients until smooth. Spray baking sheet with vegetable spray; drop dough on cookie sheet.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes or until brown.
Makes 8 servings.
Wrap cinnamon, cloves and mint in cheesecloth or place in a cloth spice bag.
Place bundled spices in cranberry-raspberry juice; simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove spices and pour juice into a punch bowl.
Cool.
Add ginger ale, orange slices and fresh mint leaves for garnish.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix meat and salt; divide in half.
Pat one half evenly in ungreased 8-inch pie pan.
Mix cream cheese, mustard and horseradish; spread over meat.
Shape remaining meat into 8-inch circle.
Place on cheese mixture; pinch edges together to seal.
Bake 45 minutes.
Place onion rings around meat.
Cut into wedges.
Place pheasant breasts in a steamer and cover.
Steam only until meat can be removed from bone (meat should be rare).
Cool to room temperature and cube.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat egg whites until thick and foamy. Gradually add sugar and beat until stiff. Fold in salt, pecans, vanilla and chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheets covered with brown paper.
Place in oven, close door and turn oven off.
Leave in oven overnight.
Blend the cream cheese, juice of salmon, mayonnaise, sour cream and onion salt well.
Add salmon; blend well.
Serve with vegetables, crackers or potato chips.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease 24 mini muffin cups.
Stir together flour, cheese, mustard and chili powder in mixing bowl. Beat eggs in separate bowl; stir in milk and oil.
Add liquid mixture to dry ingredients, stirring just until blended.
Batter will be slightly lumpy.
Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Drain mushrooms and save juice.
Cook broccoli in mushroom juice.
Drain broccoli and chop.
Saute onion and garlic in oleo until clear.
Put broccoli, garlic and mushroom soup into double boiler.
When hot, add cheese and mushrooms and season to taste with Worcestershire sauce.
Serve with Melba rounds.
Brown hamburger and onion; drain off grease.
Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Mix all ingredients together.
Stir until well blended.
Store in refrigerator in covered container.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and vanilla together and set aside. Mix jello and water together and place in refrigerator and let jell slightly.
Mix all ingredients and serve at once.
Blend ingredients and beat 2 minutes.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes at 350° in greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Sprinkle with sifted confectioners sugar or glaze.
May be baked in loaf pans for banana bread.
Cook yellow squash in water.
Drain water.
Mix ingredients together and cook 30 minutes at 400°.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Beat 1 1/2 minutes at high speed of mixer.
Add remaining ingredients, except chocolate chips. Chips are added last.
Place in 8 x 8-inch ungreased pan and bake at 375° for 20 to 22 minutes.
Slice margarine sticks and distribute evenly over bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Pour dry cake mix over margarine.
Pour peaches, including juice, over cake mix.
Top with coconut.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve warm.

recipes.t: Onion Dip For Veggies Or Chips And Pretzels
d: Boil bouillon cubes with water.
Using an electric mixer, add cream cheese and onion.
Should make a day ahead and refrigerate. Warm to almost room temperature before serving.
Stir well and thin with a little milk if needed.
Sift
flour,
baking
powder, salt and soda into mixing bowl. Stir in milk until all is wet; then add corn oil.
Toss out on floured board.
Sprinkle a little flour on dough.
Then flatten out
and
cut
biscuits.
Grease pan and turn biscuits over in grease and bake at 425°.
Makes 14 large biscuits.
Mix sugar and cornmeal.
Add oleo and cream.
Add eggs, one at a time and beat thoroughly.
Add remaining ingredients to mixture and beat.
Pour in pie shell and place in oven.
Cook at 400° for 10 minutes.
Reduce to 325° and cook 30 minutes longer.

Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a frying pan. Make sandwiches, using 2 slices of bread and 1 piece of cheese for each. Place sandwich in pan and fry until lightly brown; turn over and brown on other side. Fry on medium heat.
Place Brie on large serving plate.
Melt butter and brown sugar in saucepan; add corn syrup and flour, stirring well. Bring to boil; reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; cool to lukewarm.
Gradually stir in milk.
Pour caramel over Brie.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Combine lemon juice and water.
Toss with fruit wedges.
Drain.
Arrange around fruit.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer bread, meat, cheese and onion.
Melt butter and pour over all.
Beat eggs, seasonings and milk.
Pour over.
Chill in refrigerator overnight and bake 1 hour at 350°. Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Mix together the flour, oleo and nuts.
Press in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Cool.

recipes.t: Sour Cream Dressing For Cabbage Slaw
d: Add all ingredients to sour cream.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water.
Chill.
Add remaining ingredients and let set.
Melt chocolate in double boiler over hot, not boiling, water. Remove pan from fire and stir in sugar and corn syrup.
Blend in bourbon.
Combine crushed vanilla wafers and walnuts in bowl.
Add chocolate mixture to it.
Form into one-inch balls and roll in sugar.
Let ripen in covered container for few days or longer. Then wrap and present to your friends.
Makes about 4 1/2 dozen.
Mix cocoa, sugar and salt; add water and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in milk; heat to boiling, but do not boil.
Beat with rotary beater just before serving.
Serves 6.
Melt butter, let cool.
Pour over sugar and grated orange peel.
Add 1 tablespoon orange juice.
Add milk, nuts and coconut; mix well.
Set in freezer to cool.
Blend ingredients in blender until smooth and foamy.
Chill before serving.
Makes 2 shakes.
Shred cabbage and place in
a large pot with 3 tablespoons water and 1 can of stewed tomatoes.
Cook until almost tender.
In a separate pan, melt 1/4 stick margarine.
Mix with 1 teaspoon salt, 2 tablespoons white vinegar and 1 tablespoon flour.
Saute the diced onion in the mixture.
Add this to the cabbage when the cabbage is almost tender.
Heat until desired tenderness is reached.
Add a teaspoon of sugar if needed.
Cook potatoes in jackets and dice.
Mix cream cheese and milk together.
Add all ingredients together in 9 x 11-inch baking dish which has been greased with butter.
Line baking dish with foil.
Arrange chicken in pan.
Add rest of ingredients.
Cover pan with foil and bake at 350° until well done.
Mix sugar, vanilla and cream cheese together.
Make a package of Dream Whip.
Follow directions on Dream Whip.
When you get this mixed up, combine Dream Whip, sugar, vanilla and cream cheese together.
Bake pie crust at 350° for 10 minutes.
Fill pie crust with mixture and top with cherries.
Chill for 2 hours before serving.
Mix all together.
Bake at 350° until squash and potatoes are tender.
Add cheese and melt.
Mix all ingredients and place in Pyrex dish.

Prepare cake mix by directions on package in 2 pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Dribble melted butter over warm cake. Combine sugar, coffee and cinnamon and sprinkle over cake. Chopped nuts may be added if desired.

Boil potatoes in water about 20 minutes until fork-tender. Drain well. Return to pot. In saucepan beat milk and butter over low heat until butter melts. Stir in salt and pepper. Add to potatoes and mash with potato masher or mixer until smooth.
Mix together and refrigerate.
Reduce 1/3 to 1/4 for family.

Brown meat. Mix taco seasoning as directed on package. On a baking sheet, roll out crescent rolls. Add hamburger meat and raw onions. Top with crescent rolls. Cover with cheese. Bake at 350° until brown. Serve with tomatoes, cheese, etc.
Melt margarine in large skillet over medium heat.
Saute onion and pepper until onion is transparent.
Add tomatoes, rice, seasonings and water.
Cook 10 minutes over medium heat.
Cut shrimp in half lengthwise; add to skillet; mix well.
Cook covered, stirring occasionally, until liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes. Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a medium bowl, beat egg yolks; stir in Eagle Brand milk and lemon juice.
Pour into crust; bake 8 minutes.
Cool. Chill 3 hours or overnight.
Dice and cook carrots until tender.
Combine all the rest of the ingredients; heat to near boiling.
Drain the carrots and mix into the sauce; let cool.
Cook chicken and slice.
Cook broccoli.
Heat soup, mayo and curry powder.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place broccoli on bottom.
Place chicken on top and cover with soup mixture and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Three cups cooked rice can also be used as the first layer.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 to 60 minutes.
In large bowl combine all ingredients except confectioners sugar.
With hands, mix until thoroughly blended.
Refrigerate dough 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 375°.
Form dough into 1 1/4-inch balls. Place 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheet; bake 15 to 20 minutes or until set, but not brown.
Let stand 1 minute.
Remove to wire racks; cool partially.
Roll in confectioners sugar while still warm; roll again.
Makes about 20.
Mix all ingredients in medium bowl by hand. Take a small handful and form into patty.
Fry on medium-high with oil just covering bottom of pan. Fry until lightly brown.
Makes 6 burgers.
In large pot on stove, rub a clove of
garlic
and
discard. Bring wine to bubble (not quite boil)
and gradually add cheese (already
cut
and	tossed	with
cornstarch)
stirring constantly.
When cheese is melted, add spices
and
pour
into fondue pot.
If too stringy when eating, increase heat.
Mix dry ingredients until crumbly.
Pat half of mixture into an 8 x 8-inch pan.
Spread pie filling over mixture.
Cover with other half of crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Ann Mcgill Erck'S Sour Cream Coffee Cake
d: Cream
sugar,
butter
and eggs until smooth.
Add sour cream and
vanilla.
Sift
flour,
salt and baking powder and add.
Pour half this batter into greased and floured tube pan. Add half
of topping of cinnamon, brown sugar and pecans.
Add remaining batter and remaining topping.
Bake 1 hour at 350°. Let
stand until
cool
enough
to
handle
and
unmold cake. Freezes well.
Cook chicken.
Cut in chunks and put in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cook broccoli according to directions; layer.
Add cheese. Mix 1/2 cup milk with celery soup.
Pour on top.
Mix dressing according to directions and spread on top.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Cook soup, milk and grated cheese until cheese is melted. Pour in casserole dish.
In each crescent roll, put a strip of chicken and a strip of cheese.
Roll up and place on top of soup mixture.
Cook in 350 degree oven until rolls are brown.

Grease pie pan. Brown meat and onion; drain. Add salt and pepper; spread into pan. Beat milk, Bisquick and eggs. Pour over meat. Bake 25 minutes at 350°, then add tomato sauce and cheese over top. Bake until knife inserted comes out clean, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Cut spareribs into servings.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Place in a roaster pan and cover with onions.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over meat.
Cover and bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Baste occasionally turning ribs once or twice.
Remove cover from roaster during the last 15 minutes of baking to brown spareribs.
Use a large mixing bowl.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Add sugar and cream of tartar very slowly to stiffly beaten egg whites.
Slowly add the nearly unfrozen berries and juice to the egg white peaks.
Beat on high with mixer for 15 minutes.
Put into pie shell of your choosing and freeze.
Add sliced berries and whipped cream for garnish before serving.
Make graham cracker crust.
(Save some crumbs to sprinkle on top.)
Combine ingredients for dessert.
Cook macaroni. Rinse and drain. Combine with remaining ingredients in large bowl. Gently stir in dressing. Cover and chill at least 2 hours before serving.
Mix together and top with 1 cup corn flakes.
Dot with margarine.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 8 to 10.
Cream sugar, shortening and eggs.
Add baking powder, salt and flour.
Stir in chips and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes in a 10 x 14-inch pan.
Sift dry ingredients; set aside.
Cream together all other ingredients; mix well and add to flour mixture.
Add chocolate chips and nuts (optional).
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Stir in chilies and barbecue sauce.
Spoon into 10 x 6-inch baking dish.
Bake in oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve hot with crackers.
Chop the onions, tomatoes, green peppers and pickles and mix with the cornbread and bacon.
Add pickle juice and mayonnaise to taste for the dressing.
In a large saucepan, melt butterscotch flavored morsels and peanut butter over very low heat, stirring constantly until smooth. Stir in cereal.
Press half of the mixture in buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Chill.
Set remaining mixture aside.
Melt over hot (not boiling) water the chocolate morsels, sugar, margarine and water, stirring constantly until smooth.
Spread over chilled cereal mixture.
Spread remaining cereal mixture evenly over top. Press in gently.
Chill until firm (1 hour).
Yields 25 squares (1 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch).
Boil together 3 minutes the first 8 ingredients.
Cool.
Sift together the remaining ingredients.
Add to first part and bake. Can be used at holiday time for fruit cake.
Improves with time. Can be made ahead to season.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Stir together dry cake mix, butter and eggs in a mixing bowl.
Stir in cereal.
Roll dough into 1 1/2 inch balls.
Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet.
bake 8 to 10 minutes until edges are brown.
Cool on cookie sheet before moving to a cooling rack.
Combine the first 6 ingredients.
Spoon into prepared pie crust.
Cover with top crust; crimp edges to seal.
Slit top crust and brush with egg, if desired.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes. Cool 10 minutes.
Make and set aside.
Melt butter (2 tablespoons).
Add flour and seasonings.
Cook over low heat until bubbly.
Slowly stir in milk.
Heat to boiling.
Stir in corn and egg.
Pour into casserole dish; sprinkle with crumbs and butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Melt margarine in an 8 x 11-inch Pyrex pan in oven.
Combine apples, water and 1 cup sugar in a saucepan.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes. Pour apples in pan with margarine.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Mix flour, baking powder, milk and 1 cup sugar.
Pour over apples.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Brown meat, onions and bell peppers in skillet. Drain excess fat. Add rice and diced cooked potatoes. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Chop raisins and walnuts finely.
Melt chocolate.
Blend together butter, sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Stir in raisins, nuts and chocolate.
Mix until well blended.
Brown and drain sausage.
Beat eggs with milk, mustard and salt.
Cube bread and layer with sausage and cheese in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Pour egg mixture over layers; cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake 45 minutes at 350° (20 minutes with foil on and 25 minutes with foil off).
Do not overbake.

In a skillet, saute celery and onion in butter until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in apple. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes. Sprinkle with flour, curry powder, salt and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve immediately. Yield: 4 servings.

recipes.t: Old Fashioned Peanut Butter Pie(Heritage Recipe)
d: Dissolve cornstarch in 1/2 c. cold water, add rest of ingredients.
Cook until thick and pour into baked crust.
Use egg whites for meringue.
Makes 2 pies.
Saute onions and celery in nonstick skillet sprayed with Pam. Combine flour with 1/2 cup of the broth in a small jar with a lid. Shake until there are no lumps.
Add to kettle and slowly add rest of broth and milk.
Stir over medium heat until thickened. Add cooked wild rice and chicken.
Heat to serving temperature. Makes 6 (1 cup) servings.
Preheat oven to 450°.
In 13 x 9-inch baking or roasting pan, blend onion soup mix, butter and pepper sauce.
Add potatoes and turn to coat.
Bake, stirring occasionally 45 minutes or until potatoes are crisp.
Serve with dressing.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix together and refrigerate.
Melt together over low heat or on 50% power in microwave the almond bark and peanut butter.
In large bowl, mix peanuts, marshmallows and Rice Krispies.
Pour melted mixture over and mix all together.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Refrigerate to set.
These freeze well.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Add beans with liquid.
Add salt and taco seasoning to taste.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Drain off all liquids and cool.
Chill before serving.
Gently toss the lettuce, tomatoes, dressing, cheese and chips together.
Stir in meat and bean mixture.
Dump pineapple and pie filling in bottom of oblong pan.
Mix and spread evenly over bottom.
Sprinkle dry cake mix evenly over those.
Pour melted margarine over cake mix.
Sprinkle evenly with coconut and then pecans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
With a 2 1/2-inch round cutter, cut a circle from each bread slice.
Spread about 2 tablespoons of peanut butter on half of bread rounds; top with remaining bread rounds.
Make 2 small indentations on top of sandwiches for "eyes".
Using peanut butter as glue, push one raisin into each indentation.
Into greased casserole, put soup and milk.
Stir and add rest of ingredients; stir.
Store, covered, 3 to 4 hours or overnight in refrigerator.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, uncovering the last 10 minutes to brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine butterscotch morsels and butter; melt over boiling water.
Remove from heat.
Mix boiling water with baking soda and add to butterscotch mixture.
Gradually blend in the remaining ingredients.
Drop by slightly rounded teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Makes 5 dozen cookies.

Mix first 4 ingredients in a large bowl. Pour into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish. Place mandarin orange segments on top of mixed fruit, being careful not to break the segments. Pour mandarin orange liquid over all fruit. Cover with foil and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix the plain salt with enough water to cover cucumbers.
Put a weight on cucumbers to keep under water. Stir every day for 15 days. Remove, wash and slice. Soak overnight in alum water to cover. Rinse 3 times.
Cover with vinegar.
Let set overnight. Remove cucumbers and throw away the vinegar.
Layer cucumbers, sugar and spices in crock.
Cover. In a few days enough syrup will be made to cover pickles.
Put in jars. Do not have to be sealed.
Mix everything with 1/2 of the tomato soup.
Put in loaf pan. Pour rest of tomato soup on top.
Sprinkle with Mozzarella cheese. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Cream butter and sugar together. Beat eggs and combine with butter mix. Add bananas, beat well. Mix all dry ingredients together and combine to beaten mixture. Add nuts. Grease and flour two loaf pans. Divide mixture between loaf pans and bake at 350 degree for about 45 minutes or until lightly brown and done.
Mix in order given.
Spread on greased cookie sheet pan.
Makes 2 (10 1/2 x 15 1/2-inch) pans and 1 (8 x 8-inch) pan or something similar.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Melt Velveeta cheese in saucepan; add salsa.
Melt together, then add green onion (chopped up).
Pour over soft tortillas or chips.
Mix the first 6 ingredients.
Roll into small uniform balls. Chill.
Melt the paraffin and the chocolate chips in double boiler.
Dip balls in this, kept warm.
Chill, then refrigerate to keep for serving.
Break angel food cake in small pieces.
Layer in pan.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Allow to thicken slightly.
Add berries to jello, pour over cake and chill.
Mix instant pudding, then whip together with ice cream.
Pour this over jello cake.
Chill until firm, then cover with Cool Whip.
Delicious!
In medium bowl, beat cream cheese until smooth.
Stir in mayonnaise, cucumbers, green onions, lemon juice, dill and hot pepper sauce.
Cover and chill.
Serve with fresh vegetables, crackers or chips.
Combine soup, water and chicken.
Add dry rice and 1/2 can French fried onions.
Stir to mix.
Pour in buttered casserole. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining onions on top; bake 15 minutes more.
Combine juice, flour and sugar.
Put in cheese and pineapple. Put mixture into casserole dish.
Mix Ritz crackers and melted butter.
Put on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Mix all ingredients. Pour into casserole dish, top with more cracker crumbs. Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Grease loaf pans and line bottoms with waxed paper.
Use 2 regular pans (9 5/8 x 5 1/2 x 2 3/4-inch) or 6 mini pans (5 1/2 x 3 x 2 1/4-inch).
Mix first 6 ingredients together and let stand until you mix and roll out single pie crust.
Fill pie crust and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 425°; turn down temperature to 350° and continue to bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until knife comes out clean.
Place meat in an 8 x 12-inch cake pan lined with foil paper (enough to be able to wrap meat after all ingredients have been put in).
Place on top of meat the onion, green pepper, bay leaves, garlic and mushrooms.
Add tomato soup straight from the can on top of ingredients, then add ketchup.
Wrap meat up with foil.
Bake in oven at 350° for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Tear up angel food cake and lay in bottom of 9 x 13 pan.
In large bowl, cream the cream cheese.
Add pudding and milk and mix for 1 minute.
Stir in drained pineapple.
Pour mixture over cake and top with Cool Whip.
Refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
In a saucepan, mix all ingredients together and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Strain and serve.
Yield: 8 servings, 77 calories.
Mix ingredients and bake at 375° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Cake can be baked in Bundt pan or made as cupcakes.
Thoroughly mix cream cheese, mayonnaise and sugar together. Add marshmallows, pecans and fruit cocktail.
Add desired amount of red food color to the whipped cream.
Fold in colored whipped cream.
Freeze in thin layer in serving dish.
Cut into small squares before serving.
Serve frozen or only partially thawed. (This was served on a restaurant buffet on Sundays.)
In a large skillet cook ground beef until crumbly.
Drain off fat.
Add onions and green pepper.
Cook until they are tender. Stir in tomatoes, rice, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Mix well. Pour into a 2-quart casserole dish.
Mix the first five ingredients together.
Brown hamburger. Drain and mix with taco seasoning mix and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Let cool, then add to salad.
Heat soup to boiling.
Remove from heat and add Jell-O.
Stir until dissolved.
Add cream cheese and mix until well blended. Stir in remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Beat eggs in large bowl.
Add cottage cheese, grated Cheddar, butter, spinach, flour, salt and pepper.
Pour into 2-quart buttered casserole.
Bake on low, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°. Yields 12 to 14 servings.
Slightly cook bacon.
Wrap one piece around each breast. Place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish.
Mix butter and Worcestershire sauce.
Pour over chicken; sprinkle mushrooms and scallions over top.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes, basting once or twice.
Fill a tall glass with ice.
Put in vodka.
Add cranberry juice to top.
Squeeze in lime and stir.
Serves 1.
Drain apricots and pineapple, reserving 1 cup of the combined liquid.
Combine the liquid with the apricots, pineapple and remaining ingredients.
Spoon into cupcake papers put in muffin tins.
Freeze until solid, then package cups in freezer bags. Remove from the freezer 20 minutes before serving to partially thaw.
Makes 30 servings.

In a skillet, cook beef over medium heat until no longer pink; drain. In a bowl, combine the egg, milk and cornmeal until smooth. Add corn, tomatoes, olives, chili seasoning, seasoned salt and beef. Transfer to a greased slow cooker. Cover and cook on high for 3 hours and 45 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese; cover and cook 15 minutes longer or until cheese is melted. Yield: 6 servings.
Dissolve Jell-O in water; let slightly thicken.
Add rest of ingredients.
Store in refrigerator.
Boil the sweet potatoes until tender, about 30 minutes. Remove the skin, mash the pulp.
Add the fruit juice and margarine and whip mixture until fluffy.
Add the nutmeg, brown sugar substitute and cinnamon.
Spray a baking dish with non-stick spray.
Pour mixture into pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Combine first six ingredients.
Spoon into prepared deep dish pie crust.
Place second crust on top.
Seal the edges of the crust.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Remove bones and skin from salmon; mash with fork.
Add potatoes, salt, pepper and beaten egg.
Mix well.
Form into cutlets.
Roll in crumbs.
Heat oil and fry.
Drain on absorbent paper.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Add seasonings to flour.
Add rabbit. Heat oil.
Add rabbit; brown on both sides.
In casserole dish, add rabbit, mushrooms, milk, butter and onion.
Cover with foil; cook for about 1 hour.
Remove chicken from bone.
Cook spaghetti in chicken broth. Remove spaghetti from broth.
Cook onions, pepper and celery until tender.
Pour in tomatoes and cheese.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in large casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream sugars and margarine; add eggs and stir well.
Stir in vanilla.
Add all dry ingredients and mix well.
Shape dough into 2 logs.
Refrigerate overnight.
Slice and bake at 325° for 12 minutes.
Pat crescent rolls onto pizza pan or cookie sheet to look like pizza crust.
Bake as directed on can.
Cool.
Combine all ingredients and pour over chicken.
Soak for 5 to 6 hours or overnight.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Drain marinade and cook at 450° for 15 minutes.
Toast the English muffins (the longer you toast them, the crunchier your pizza "crust" will be).
Add desired amount of pizza sauce to each muffin.
Add toppings and cheese (keep in mind that some meats like sausage or beef should be cooked before you put them on your pizza).

Bake your mini-pizzas for 5 to 8 minutes at 350°, or until your cheese melts, or heat in the microwave. The time will vary based on the number of pizzas you are heating and the amount of topping on each pizza.
Do not heat too long! They should be heated through when cheese is melted.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Layer asparagus, peas and potatoes alternately in an 8 x 8-inch pan.
Melt the margarine, milk and undiluted soup.
Mix well and pour over top. Crumble saltines and sprinkle on top. Sprinkle with a little cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly, about 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
In large bowl combine all ingredients.
Saute onions in a skillet with a small amount of oil.
Add onions to the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Pour mixture into a greased 13 x 9-inch pan or large casserole dish.
Top with cheese.
Bake in oven for 30 to 40 minutes or until firm at 350°.

In a saucepan, dissolve the gelatin in boiling water and stir in the orange rind and cranberry sauce. Refrigerate the mixture until it is thickened. Remove from the refrigerator and stir in the pineapple, celery and pecans. Pour the mixture into a lightly oiled 1 1/2-quart mold. Refrigerate the salad until it is firm. Unmold the salad on the lettuce leaves. Serves 10 to 12.
Boil the peppers in water until soft.
Melt margarine in a large saucepan. Add onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic and parsley. Simmer until tender.
Add ground meat to mixture.
Cook ground meat until brown. Add shrimp and crab meat.
Cook for 15 minutes. Add bread crumbs. Add salt and pepper to taste. Stuff cooled peppers. Sprinkle bread crumbs on top. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Serves 4. Contains 375 calories.
Prepare macaroni as on package; drain.
In large skillet, combine green pepper, garlic and beef; cook until beef is brown and vegetables tender.
Drain.
Stir in tomatoes, sauce, corn, olives and salt.
Add macaroni; mix well.
Stir in cheese.
Serves 6 to 8.

recipes.t: Sesame Curry Sauce(Use To Brush Over Chicken, Meat Or Fish When Grilling.)
d: Combine in a screw-top jar.
Shake well.
Brush over grilled items.
Heat oil in a large skillet on medium-high heat. Add chicken, onion and pepper. Cook and stir until chicken is cooked through. Add corn, broth and salsa. Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice. Cover. Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese. Cover.
Let stand 2 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix in large mixing bowl the sugar, flour and baking soda. Mix the butter, Coca Cola, and cocoa in a saucepan and bring to a full rolling boil.
Add the hot mixture to the dry ingredients and stir.
Add the buttermilk, eggs and marshmallows to the mixture. Mix all well.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 inch baking pan and bake for 30 - 35 minutes at 350°.
Brown hamburger meat.
Season to taste - onions optional to brown with hamburger.
Drain meat.
Place back in skillet.
Layer up with corn (either whole or cream) and green beans (drained). Top with mashed potatoes.
Garnish with cheese on top.
Bake approximately 30 to 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl until well blended.
Roll the dough out on a floured board.
Cut out treats with a dog bone shaped cookie cutter.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until dry.
Saute chicken chunks in oil until firm.
Stir in celery and cook 2 minutes.
(Should be crispy.)
Add vegetables, soup and soy sauce.
Stir in onions.
Heat through and serve over rice.
Top with noodles.
Dissolve Karo and sugar.
Heat thoroughly until blended.
Beat eggs; add butter, pecans and vanilla.
Mix together with Karo and pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake in medium hot oven.
Rinse and pat dry cutlets.
Dip each cutlet in bread crumbs, shaking off excess.
Put breaded cutlets on flat surface and place slice of Mozzarella cheese and slice of ham on each cutlet.
Roll up cutlets and fasten each one with a toothpick.
Bread cauliflower into medium sized flowerets; cook in boiling water until tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain well; set aside.
In saucepan, saute mushrooms in butter.
Blend in flour gradually. Stir in milk.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium heat until thick.
Stir in salt, cheese and pimento.
Place 1/2 of cauliflower in buttered 2-quart casserole.
Cover with 1/2 the sauce.
Add remaining cauliflower and top with remaining sauce. Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Put all ingredients in blender; mix, then pour into two 8-inch pie pans (greased and floured).
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes.
A crust will form on bottom, pie filling in center and coconut on top.
Combine all ingredients in punch bowl and serve.
Yields 25 to 30 cups.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Cover with remaining ingredients mixed together.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Peel and cut potatoes for cooking.
Cook until almost done. Transfer to casserole; add corn and salt and pepper to taste. Cover top with grated cheese.
Bake until brown in a 350° oven.
Combine flour, soda and spices.
Beat butter, sugars, egg and molasses.
Then add dry ingredients.
Use a cookie press on cold ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
In large saucepan, combine potatoes, onion, celery, broth, garlic and marjoram.
Bring to boil; reduce heat and simmer, covered, about 10 minutes.
Stir in milk and oleo.
Combine flour and corn; stir into soup.
Heat, but do not boil, until slightly thickened.
Gently stir in salmon and heat through.
Serves 6 to 8.
Brown ground beef and cool.
Chop lettuce, tomatoes and onion. Mix, then add shredded Cheddar cheese and creamy Ranch dressing. Sprinkle more cheese on top.
Serve with nacho chips.
May be crushed and added to each individual salad or served on the side. Use salsa to suit your taste.
This makes a very large main salad.
Bake at 400° and then at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook broccoli until tender, 10 to 15 minutes; drain.
Put in bottom of baking dish.
Mix the next 7 ingredients.
Place on top of broccoli.
Melt butter and mix with bread crumbs; put on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown sausage and ground meat.
Drain and add melted cheese mixture.
Heat in crock-pot.
Mix all ingredients and mold into a ball; let set overnight. Can roll in chopped pecans.
Spray pie pan with Pam.
Make graham cracker crumbs and mix with margarine, cinnamon and 2 Equal.
Press into pie pan.
Bake 5 minutes at 350°.
Mix water and cornstarch.
Bring to boil (don't boil) and set aside.
Into hot mixture, add Jell-O.
When mixture cools, add 6 packages Equal.
Put aside and cool 30 minutes.
Add strawberries and pour into baked and cooled crust.
Chill.
Makes 4 servings.
Each serving equals 1 fruit, 1 bread, 3/4 fat and 38 additional calories.
Mix milk until well blended with lime juice.
Mix in Cool Whip (may add a few drops of green food color) and pour into pie shell. Chill in refrigerator until set.
Mix sour cream or yogurt with salad dressing.
Serve with veggies.
Melt butter over low heat.
Blend in sugar, eggs and peanut butter; mix until smooth.
Add oats, soda, raisins and chocolate chips (mixture will be sticky).
Drop on greased baking sheet with large spoon.
Flatten slightly.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes for large cookies.
Remove to cooling rack.
Yields 2 dozen cookies.
Bake for about 30 to 45 minutes at 425°.
Mix fruit in flour to coat.
Add salt, coconut and pecans. Add Eagle Brand; mix well.
Drop by spoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 275° for 25 minutes.
Cool completely.
Store in airtight container about 5 days before serving.
Makes 4 dozen.
Mix shredded chicken and 1/2 cup green enchilada sauce in saucepan.
Fry tortillas in vegetable oil until medium fry.
Dip tortilla in green enchilada sauce.
Scoop chicken; sprinkle cheese inside and roll tortilla.
Repeat steps for each tortilla.
Put enchiladas in tray and spread leftover enchilada sauce on top. Sprinkle cheese on top.
Mix cocoa, cornstarch, sugar and salt.
Slightly beat egg yolks.
Add to mixture and milk.
Cook until thick; stir constantly.
Add flavoring.
Pour into pie shell.
Cover with meringue.
Grind raisins and nuts.
Mix with honey and press into sheet 1/2-inch thick.
Cover and place weight on top for 24 hours.
Cut into bars.
Roll in white or colored coconut.
Place shrimp in a single layer in a 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan.
Set aside.
Combine next 8 ingredients.
Pour over shrimp.
Bake at 450° for 5 minutes or until shrimp is done.
Dissolve red raspberry Jell-O in 3 1/2 cups water.
Chill until firm.
Use 9 x 13-inch pan.
Make mashed potatoes with potatoes and part of milk.
Save remaining milk for cheese sauce.
Cook noodles 10 minutes; rinse with warm water and set aside.
Cook margarine, milk, onion and cheese until melted.
In 9 x 13-inch greased pan, add 1/2 of noodles.
Spread in pan.
Add not quite 1/2 of cheese sauce. Spread evenly.
Add mashed potatoes on top of noodles and cheese. Add remaining noodles and cheese sauce.
Bake at 350° until golden brown or 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Quick And Easy Potatoes Au Gratin
d: Peel and cube potatoes.
Place in a well-greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with flour and pour milk to cover.
Stir potatoes with a fork so that all are well coated with flour and milk.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cover with the grated cheese and dot with butter.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 1 hour. Serves 4.
Sprinkle Jell-O over Cool Whip; mix well.
Stir in remaining ingredients; chill.
Mix egg, mustard, salt, sugar, cayenne, tarragon and dill in blender.
Add slowly the oil.
Blend again until thick.
Beat eggs and sugar 5 minutes.
Mix together pumpkin and lemon juice and add to first mixture.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and salt and add.

Spread evenly in a jelly roll pan which has been greased and floured. Line the pan with wax paper. Sprinkle walnuts over the batter. Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes. Sprinkle a dish towel with powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine all ingredients except chicken. Lay chicken in a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
(Use 2 pans, if necessary.)
Pour ingredient mixture over chicken.
Add water, enough water to cover chicken.
Bake in oven for 15 minutes at 400°.
Turn oven down to 350° and bake for another 45 minutes.
Boil chicken quickly.
Separate into serving pieces or strips. Cover with spaghetti sauce mix (I use Giant's brand).
Add vegetables.
Simmer on stove or in oven.
Just before time to serve, add prepared shrimp (the amount and size you can afford that week)!
Cook 3 or 4 minutes.
Serve on rice.
Heat mixture in an iron pot until it starts to boil and lower flame to simmer.
Heat sugar in iron pot until sugar melts. Cook the mixture in an aluminum pot until soft ball stage.
Beat well. Add the nuts and pour into buttered platter.
Mix together butter, cherries, nuts, coconut and powdered sugar.
Form balls; chill.
Melt paraffin and chocolate chips. Dip balls and chill.
Cook carrots and onion in boiling water until tender.
Stir in soup, milk, cheese and Worcestershire sauce.
Stir over low heat until cheese melts.
Garnish with parsley.
Serves 6 to 8.
Bake potatoes
in
a 12-inch Dutch oven for 1 hour with 12 coals on top and 10 coals on bottom.
Cut baked potatoes in half lengthwise.
Scoop	out
potato and mash with milk, sour cream, margarine,	chives,
salt and pepper.
Mound back into shells. Add
grated
cheese
on
top.
Sprinkle with paprika. Place in Dutch oven.
Bake 25 minutes with 14 coals on top and 12 coals on bottom.

Cook cake by directions on package; use 13 x 9-inch pan. While still warm punch holes in cake and pour a can of Eagle Brand milk over cake, then cool and pour 1 cup Coco Lopez over cake. Spread on a large container of Cool Whip.
Sprinkle coconut on top.
Refrigerate.
Mix vinegar, salt, celery seed and sugar until dissolved. Pour over rest and put in covered dish.
Place in refrigerator. Wait 24 hours before eating.
Good for a summer cook out.
Melt butter and mix into all ingredients.
Stir and drop onto baking sheet.
Bake at 400° until browned on top.
If desired, brush on butter and sprinkle with parsley.
Mix fruit, tapioca and sugar; set aside.
Combine the two cake mixes.
Add oil, eggs and water and mix well by hand.
Add fruit mixture and blend well.
(Mixture will be thick and sticky.) Spoon into greased and floured pans (4 round or 2 rectangular) and spread evenly.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Beat the eggs.
Melt the Velveeta cheese and margarine together.
Add to eggs and scramble.
Brown and drain sausage. Saute onion and green pepper together slightly.
Into a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer half of egg mixture, half of sausage, half of onion-green pepper mixture and 1 cup shredded cheese.
(Do this procedure again, ending with shredded cheese.)
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, covered.
Remove cover and bake an additional 15 to 20 minutes, until set-up.
Mix the first 5 ingredients together.
Combine crackers and butter, sprinkle over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 20-25 minutes.
Mix in electric blender.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups.
Melt shortening; mix with oatmeal.
Combine egg with sugar and add oatmeal mixture.
Stir soda into milk.
Add flour to first mixture alternately with milk.
Add flavoring and cinnamon.
Stir in floured nuts or raisins.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake in a 375° oven until lightly browned, about 15 minutes.
Blend eggs, butter, margarine, sugar and vanilla flavoring. Add flour. Blend in applesauce. Roll nuts in flour. Blend in nuts and coconut. Cook at 250° for 4 hours.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease loaf pan.
Blend egg into salmon. Stir in remaining ingredients.
Spoon into pan.
Pat into shape. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until top is golden brown.
Garnish with lemon wedges.
Shape in loaf and bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
In medium saucepot, saute bacon until lightly brown.
Remove bacon and drain.
Saute onion and red pepper.
Cook 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in flour.
Gradually stir in milk, corn, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Bring just to boiling point over low heat; simmer one minute, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle chowder with sauteed bacon pieces.
Peel your eggplant and slice about 1/4 inch thick.
Lightly flour and fry in oil (not a lot).
Drain on paper towels and set aside.
Combine all ingredients and stir well.
Drop by tablespoon into hot oil.
Turn once.
Drain and serve at once.
Brown meat, celery and onion; drain fat.
Add remaining ingredients and stir until well blended.

Brown meat and onions. Add salt, pepper, herb sauce and sugar. Mix sour cream and cream cheese together. Place noodles first in casserole dish, the meat mixture then cream cheese mixture. Keep layering, top with American cheese slices. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes. This dish will make 2 medium-sized casseroles.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Mix taco seasoning, creamed corn and beans with juice into hamburger.
Crumble chips in bottom of long casserole dish (any amount you like).
Pour meat mixture over chips and bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over top and heat until cheese melts.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Combine all ingredients and roll 1/2 inch thick.
Cut with 2 inch cutter.
Bake at 450° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cook onion in oil until soft and golden.
Stir all ingredients together.
Pack tightly into a casserole, greased.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Uncover the last 15 minutes. Allow to stand for 15 minutes before serving.
For a moister loaf, use less crumbs. You can also use more nuts.
Walnuts work well.
Cream margarine, sugar and egg.
Add remaining ingredients. Drop and bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Place chicken legs and thighs in a shallow roasting pan or glass baking dish.
Do not grease pan or baking dish beforehand. Sprinkle salt, pepper and paprika over the chicken in liberal doses.
Bake in 325° oven for 1 1/2 hours until skin is crisp.
Do not turn chicken while cooking.
Serve on bed of watercress or as is.
Combine all ingredients and spread in a 9 x 13 inch greased baking dish.
Bake in a 325° oven for about 25 to 30 minutes or until slightly golden brown.
Serve warm with Fritos, chips of choice, or crackers.

recipes.t: Basic Meat Loaf Microwave Special(Cooking Time 15 To 17 Minutes)
d: Mix ground chuck thoroughly with onion, crumbs, egg, catsup, milk and seasonings.
Mold into a rounded, flat loaf in 9-inch pie plate.
Spread catsup evenly over top of loaf.
Cover with waxed paper.
Place loaf in microwave oven.
Cook 15 to 17 minutes, giving dish 1/4 turn every 4 minutes.
Let loaf stand at least 5 minutes before slicing.
Yields 6 servings.
Add beans and brown sugar to onion cooked in bacon fat.
Mix all and place slices of bacon on top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour (approximately).
Mix first 5 ingredients together.
In separate bowl, mix other 3 ingredients.
Put 1/2 of second mixture in with first mixture. Keep 1/2 for icing.
Bake cake per instructions on box.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add vanilla.
Blend in flour and nuts until like pie crust, crumbly.
Chill 1 hour.
Roll in balls. Bake 15 minutes or until light brown at 325°.
Roll in powdered sugar when cool.
Beat until creamy.
Wrap in wax paper.
Store in airtight container.
In medium saucepan, slowly melt chocolate over low heat, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in marshmallows and nuts.
Spread on buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan. Chill and cut in squares.
Shake Molly McButter on bread.
Add both cheeses and garlic powder.
Broil until brown.
Beat egg well.
Add salt and milk.
Stir baking powder with flour and stir in other mixture. Beat until smooth.
Add blueberries. Drop from spoon and brown both sides.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a medium size bowl, mix cake mix, water and peanut butter until blended.
Roll dough into 1-inch balls.
Put the sugar in a bowl and roll the dough balls in it until covered.
Place dough balls on a cookie sheet about 1-inch apart.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until cookie separates.
Then place chocolate candy on center and press down until cookie separates around edges.
Makes about 5 dozen cookies.
Mix ingredients together.
Chill for 2 hours.
Roll out, cut and bake at 350° until golden brown.
Cool.
Melt butter and cream cheese in top of double boiler.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Serve in a chafing dish. Serve with dip size Fritos or Wheat Thins.
In a bowl, combine cheese, apple, salad dressing and walnuts. Spread on 6 slices of bread and place 2 slices of bacon on each. Cover with egg slices.
Top with tomatoes, if desired, and remaining slices of bread.
Trim fat from round steak on all edges; cut meat in lengthwise strips; coat meat in flour, salt and pepper mixture.
Brown meat in oil.
Add soup mix and 4 cups of water.
Simmer for at least 1 hour; until meat is tender.
Add extra water as needed.
Add bell peppers cut into strips, cook until peppers turn color, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Thicken with cornstarch and water.
Serve over rice.
Add onions and mushrooms to ground beef.
Then brown and drain.
Add remaining ingredients.
Stir and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve over noodles or split hamburger buns.
Crumble both breads into a large pan; pour 2 to 3 cups broth over breads.
Cook celery and onion in remaining broth until tender (oleo can be used instead).
Add this to bread, then sage and seasonings.
Lastly, add eggs and sugar; gradually add soup and broth until desired consistency.
Punch deboned chicken into dressing.
Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Check after 30 minutes.
Remove cover to brown.
Put ingredients into blender and blend about 20 seconds.
Pour into 10-inch pie pan.
Bake until golden brown in a 350° oven for about 30 minutes or until knife inserted in middle comes out clean.
Crust forms at the bottom, custard in the middle and the coconut on top.
Combine first 5 ingredients together.
Bet eggs, sugar, oil and vanilla until creamy.
Add zucchini and stir in dry ingredients, just until moist.
Bake in two 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans at 350° for 1 hour.
Can omit nuts.
Freezes well.
Tear cake into bite size pieces; set aside.
Prepare whipped topping according to package directions; set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese and confectioners sugar.
Fold in whipped topping.
Add cake pieces; stir gently to coat evenly. Spoon into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Top with pie filling. Chill until ready to serve.
Yields 12 servings.
In a large saucepan combine potatoes, water, bouillon, red pepper and black pepper.
Bring to boil, reduce heat.
Cover and simmer about 10 minutes or until potatoes are just tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in 2 1/2 cups of the milk and corn.
Mix well.
A delicious spread for crackers and party snacks.
Brown ground chuck with onion and green pepper in large saucepan, stirring until ground beef is crumbly; drain.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Simmer for 2 hours or to desired consistency.
Chill overnight and reheat to improve flavor.
Serve with corn bread.
Yield:
10 servings.
Place cold water and gelatin in blender and let stand five minutes.
Add hot water.
Cover and blend on medium speed about one minute, or until white and foamy.
Add brown sugar and lemon juice to gelatin mixture and blend until throughly combined.
Add cream and eggs.
Gradually add strawberries.
Place in refrigerator until slightly thickened (15 minutes).
Pour into serving dishes and garnish with dollop of whipped cream and whole fresh strawberries.
Cut bread into oblong shape 2 x 1-inch.
Use a teaspoon and put the condensed milk on each side of the bread.
Mix the coloring and banana flavoring with the coconut.
Spread the coconut over the slices of bread.
Place slices on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 250° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve hot or cold.
Cream butter well; add white and brown sugar slowly and cream well.
Beat eggs, cold water and vanilla.
Mix and sift dry ingredients and add alternately with liquid ingredients to cream mixture.
Chill at least 1/2 hour.
(Can be wrapped in wax paper and left overnight.)
Roll to desired thickness (about 1/8 or 1/4-inch) and bake for 12 to 15 minutes in a 350° oven.
Frost with colored frosting or brush with slightly beaten egg white and sprinkle with colored sugars.
Prepare sausage and peppers.
Combine all the ingredients and mix together.
Pour into oblong shallow pan and bake at 350° until firm.
Serves 8.
In a bowl, cream the sugars and shortening. Add eggs, beating one in at a time.
In second small bowl, add vanilla to the water and add to sugar mixture alternately with sifted dry ingredients. Stir in apples and nuts.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch greased and floured cake pan.
Mix up caramel topping and spread on batter before baking. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Break pretzels into bite size pieces.
Then place pretzels in a large mixing bowl minus any crumbs which will soak up the dressing. Mix ingredients in a separate bowl and pour over the pretzels.
Mix pretzels and ingredients well.
After mixing, put pretzels in a pan, approximately 11 x 9 1/2-inch.
Put in preheated oven at 350° for 5 minutes.
Then take out.
Pour back into mixing bowl and mix well again.
Then place pretzels back in oven 5 more minutes. Remove and drain on paper towel.
Drain pineapple and reserve juice.
Place pudding mix in large bowl.
Add about 4 tablespoons of the pineapple juice to make a soft paste.
Mix well.
Add drained pineapple, whipped topping, marshmallows and chopped nuts.
Mix well until mixture is fluffy and increases in volume.
Refrigerate until chilled.
Soak bread crumbs in milk; add meat, eggs, onion and seasonings.
Mix well.
Form in individual loaves; place in greased muffin pans.
Cover with Piquant Sauce.
Bake in a moderate 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Or form one loaf in 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch pan.
Spread with sauce; bake 1 hour.
*Or whatever you want to use, as long as it is 18 ounces of "something."
To make icing, beat butter or margarine with cream cheese in bowl of an electric mixer until very light and fluffy.

Beat in powdered sugar, followed by vanilla, pecans and optional coconut. To frost the cake, spread a generous amount of filling between and over the top of the layers, leaving the sides of the cake unfrosted.
Or use the icing to generously frost the top of the cupcakes.
Mix soup, milk, sour cream and shredded cheese together and stir into the frozen potatoes.
Bake in glass dish or 1 1/2-quart greased casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, uncovered.
Mix all together and simmer 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°.
Place apples into buttered pan.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Sprinkle over apples.
Bake until brown.
In a 3-quart saucepan, heat potatoes, salt and enough water to cover to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes or until potatoes are fork-tender.
Drain.
While potatoes are boiling, in a 12-inch skillet, heat butter.
Cook onions until tender.
Add sausage, tomatoes with liquid, paprika, caraway seed and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in potatoes and serve.
