Cut the first 5 ingredients into strips or chunks.
After cutting veggies and meat, saute chopped onion and garlic in oil. Stir in remaining ingredients; cook until slightly thickened. Thread meat and veggies on skewers.
Brush with sauce.
Place skewers on grill.
Cook for approximately 10 minutes, or until done.
Baste with remaining sauce while cooking.
Skin and wash chicken breasts.
Pat dry.
Place in a shallow pan.
Mix pineapple juice, soy sauce, oil and ginger.
Cover chicken with marinade and cover.
Refrigerate for 8 hours; turn pieces over once.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Pour off marinade, reserving liquid.
Bake chicken for 20 minutes; baste every 10 minutes.
Turn chicken pieces over and bake for another 30 minutes.
Continue to baste every 10 minutes, until chicken is done.
Serves 4.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Stir in celery and chopped onion; cook until tender.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper, if desired. Gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Add potatoes.
Bring to boil; simmer 15 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
Add bacon and Crab Delights.
Heat 3 to 5 minutes more.
Makes 4 servings.

Thaw and soften bread dough. Blend together melted butter, egg, garlic powder, parsley and salt. Cut off pieces of dough about size of small walnuts. Dip into butter mixture. Place pieces of dough into greased loaf pan until all dough is used. Cover. Let rise until double in size. Bake at 375° for 30 minutes. Brush with melted butter or margarine. Cool on wire rack. Makes 1 loaf.
In large mixer bowl combine chocolate, coffee, butter, brown sugar, egg, sour cream, flour, soda, salt and 1/3 cup coconut. Mix on lowest speed until a dough forms.
Drop by rounded teaspoon onto greased cookie sheets 12 to 15 minutes.
Frost warm. Sprinkle with remaining coconut.
Dissolve sugar in water to make a light syrup.
Mix syrup with next three ingredients and pour into small containers to freeze solid.
Approximately 1 hour before serving, remove containers from freezer and place in punch bowl.
Pour ginger ale over frozen ingredients.
As mixture thaws, rake a fork over ice mixture to make slushy.
In a Dutch oven, bring water to a boil.
After rinsing off sprouts, simmer for ten minutes.
Bias cut celery and onions into semi-large pieces.
Add to sprouts and simmer another five minutes.
While you are cooking the vegetables, cut meat into whatever size pieces you desire.
Combine all ingredients. Mix well and put into baking dish. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Pour water over oatmeal; let stand 10 minutes.
Add sugar and margarine; stir well.
Add eggs.
Sift and add dry ingredients. Add 6 ounces chocolate chips.
Put in greased cake pan.
Sprinkle on top 3/4 cup nuts and 6 ounces chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Put stuffing mix in a greased, flat 3-quart casserole.
Top with cheese, then sausage.
Beat eggs, milk, soup and mustard together, then add mushrooms and pour over other ingredients in casserole.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all together.
Place in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Best if mixed the day before.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown meat in a small amount of oil.
Add chopped onions, water and salt.
Cover and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Add green peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Blend cornstarch with a little water and add to meat mixture.
Cook, stirring, until thick.
Just before serving, add tomatoes and soy sauce; heat. Serve over rice.
Cook squash and onion in salted water, about 5 minutes.
Drain well.
Cook green pepper and meat until meat is no longer pink. Stir in rice.
Blend eggs, soup, sour cream and seasonings; stirring into meat mixture.
Fold in squash mixture.
Turn into a greased 11 1/2 X 7 1/2 X 1 1/2 baking dish.
Top with cheese. Sprinkle with paprika, if desired.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Makes 8 servings.
Do not salt anything.
Brown hamburger in 2 to 3 tablespoons butter, add pepper.
Remove meat from frypan, put in vegetables and cook until tender.
Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of water to keep from burning.
Cook rice, when done add soy sauce and canned soups.
Add meat and rice mixture to vegetables.
Mix ingredients well and put into covered dish and bake 30 to 40 minutes.
A half cup water may be added, if needed.
Can be frozen before baking.
Bring to a boil in 2-quart saucepan in 1 1/4 quarts of water. Add ingredients.
After 3 or 4 minutes, add rice; cut down heat and simmer for 10 minutes or until rice is cooked.
Use bigger pan if needed.
Optional:
Add raisins or chocolate chips if you drop cookies.

recipes.t: Wild Rice Rose(Serve With Lamb Or Chicken)
d: Soak rice overnight; drain.
Wash and drain.
Mix with remaining ingredients.
Place in buttered 2-quart casserole dish. Cover and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 4 to 6.
Combine pancake mix, flour, baking powder and salt in bowl. Add egg and beer; mix until smooth.
Dip fish in batter, coating well.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown; drain.
Yield:
6 servings.
In a saucepan, heat applesauce until it bubbles.
Stir in Jell-O and cook until dissolved.
Remove and cool, then stir in pop, orange juice and peel.
Chill until partially set, then stir in apples and nuts.
Chill until set firm.
Combine flour, salt, pepper and garlic powder in a bag.
Shake the chicken pieces individually until coated.
Brown in the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat, pour off fat.
In a bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Add to skillet and simmer, covered, 25 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Serves 4.
Grease tube pan.
Cut each biscuit into fourths.
Shake in a bag with sugar and cinnamon.
Put a layer of pecans (1 cup) and 1/2 biscuit mixture in pan and repeat this.
Pour mixture of brown sugar and margarine over all of this.
Bake at 350° for about 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix all together, then fix into a roll; freeze.
Slice when ready to serve.
Heat sausage in heavy 8-inch ovenproof skillet according to package directions.
Remove sausage and keep warm.
Saute the onion and green pepper in sausage skillet over medium-high until tender.
Combine eggs and milk in bowl.
Add the onion, green pepper and tomato.
Melt the butter in the skillet over low heat. Add the egg and vegetable mixture and cook until eggs are almost set.
Arrange the sausage on top of eggs.
Place under the broiler and broil until center is firm and top is lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.
Mix all but Fritos in large bowl.
Chill, then make Meat Sauce:
Melt butterscotch chips and peanut butter in the top of a double boiler. Stir in nuts and shoestring potatoes. Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Cool for several hours in the refrigerator.
Yields 2 or 3 dozen.
Heat milk and cream together until film shimmers over surface. Do not boil.
In separate pan, precook oysters and drain.
Add oysters (slice if you prefer) and butter to hot milk and cream mixture.
Heat but do not boil for 5 minutes more.
Add seasonings and serve at once.
Serves 5 to 6.
Cook
beef,
onion
and
garlic.
Add
soups and water; cook. Add 1 package wide noodles, uncooked.
When noodles are done, place
slices
of
cheese, cover and let stand until ready to eat.
This is all cooked in one pot.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add lemonade concentrate and stir to dissolve.
Add ginger ale.
Chill until thick, but not set.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 2 1/2-quart mold. Chill until firm.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Place roast in medium roaster pan and cover with water.
Add chopped onion, celery, salt and pepper. Cover and let cook 30 minutes. Turn oven down to 325°.
Let cook slowly, approximately 4 hours. Check roast to be sure it is covered with water. After 4 to 4 1/2 hours, add potatoes and carrots.
Cook about 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are tender.
Combine all ingredients in blender with 1/2 cup water and enough ice cubes to fill container.
Process until liquified.
Cut off tips of squash and cut in pieces.
Boil until tender. Drain and mash.
Add eggs, bread crumbs and butter.
Then add sugar, salt, onion and pepper.
Bake in greased casserole at 350° until top is lightly browned, about 45 minutes.
Makes 10 servings.
Mix pudding and buttermilk.
Add oranges (I drain 1 can), Cool Whip (I use 16 ounces) and shortbread cookies.
Refrigerate.
Boil first three ingredients 3 minutes.
Then add peanut butter and oats.
Drop on wax paper.
Cook oats in water.
Add butter.
Let cool.
Add sugars, coconut and eggs.
Mix in dry ingredients.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 35 to 45
minutes, until light brown.
Trim fat from meat and bones.
Cut meat into 4-6 serving pieces.
Grease large skillet, season meat on both sides with salt, brown meat thoroughly.
Set meat to the side;
add onion; cook and stir until tender.
Stir in broth, soy sauce and garlic. Cover; simmer for 10 minutes or until meat is tender.
Add green peppers.
Cover; simmer for 5 minutes.
Dissolve yeast in milk.
Mix all ingredients together and roll up to 90 balls.
Cover and set it in the refrigerator overnight until next day.
The next day, roll the balls on powdered sugar, but don't roll too thin.
Put the filling in the center of the cookie; fold one side of the cookie and then overlap the other side on top.
Slightly greased a cookie sheet using two cookie pans. Place 6 or 7 cookies across and 6 rolls down.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Use apricot or nut filling.
Spray crockery with nonstick spray.
Stir in peaches and pour into crock-pot.
Cook on low for four to six hours.
Sprinkle gelatine over ginger ale.
Heat until dissolved.
Do not boil.
Cool.
Mix in other ingredients.
Serves 10 (1/2 cup) servings.
Season veal with salt and pepper, then dip in flour, vigorously shaking off the excess.
In a heavy skillet, melt 2 tablespoons margarine with olive oil over moderate heat.
When the foam subsides, add the veal, 3 or 4 at a time, and brown for about 3 minutes on each side.
When done, transfer them to plate.
Pour most of the fat out of the skillet, leaving only a thin film at the bottom.
Add the Marsala and 1/4 cup of broth and boil briskly over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Scrape in any brown fragments clinging to pan.
Return veal to pan; cover and simmer over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, basting with pan juices until tender. Transfer veal to a heated platter.
Add 1/4 cup broth to sauce in pan and boil briskly, scraping in brown bits.
When sauce has reduced and is syrupy, taste it for seasoning and season as necessary.
Remove the pan from the heat; stir in 2 tablespoons of softened margarine and pour the sauce over the veal.
Cook broccoli and place in 9x13 baking dish.
Debone chicken; place on top of broccoli.
Mix mayonnaise, soup, lemon juice and spread on top of chicken.
Brown bread crumbs.
Sprinkle on top with cheese.
Bake 350 degrees 30 minutes.
Skin chicken breasts (optional for low-fat).
Place into a baking dish the breasts.
Add 1/3 cup water and place into a preheated oven at 325°.
After 30 minutes, add soy sauce.
Continue to cook for another 30 minutes, then add chopped pepper and sliced mushrooms.
Continue to cook an additional 20 to 30 minutes.
Turn breasts several times to allow the soy sauce to penetrate the meat. Brown lightly.
Serve with wild, brown or white rice.
A low-fat dish and low-salt.
Brown beef.
Add onion, green pepper, salt, brown sugar, chili powder, bay leaf and rest of the ingredients.
Cook, covered, until rice and vegetables are done.
Stir often.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cook broccoli according to box directions.
Drain.
Place broccoli in a casserole dish.
Add the butter and Velveeta cheese. Crush crackers and spread over top.
Dot extra butter on top of crackers.
Place in a 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes or until brown on top.
Combine sugar and milk in saucepan.
Add vinegar.
Boil until it forms a soft ball in cold water.
Pour mixture over pecan halves.
Add grated rind of 2 oranges and stir until pecans are coated.
Spread on foil to dry.
Mix the onions, soy sauce and water and put into roasting pan. Put fryer in roaster, skin side down.
Cook 40 minutes and turn; cook 40 minutes.
Serve with Uncle Ben's seasoned long grain and wild rice.
Serves 15.
Shred cabbage.
Cut carrot, cucumber, bell pepper and radishes in rings.
Mix sugar, vinegar and oil and pour over vegetables. Toss and refrigerate several hours before serving.
Salt to taste before serving.
Combine all ingredients except honey in a large bowl.
Beat at low speed of electric mixer.
Fill baking cup lined muffin tins 1/2 full.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. Drizzle with honey. Yields 18 muffins.
Cut bacon into pieces and fry with onion.
Drain off fat.
Add vinegar, sugar, beans and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Serve hot.
Combine chicken, mixed vegetables and soups in bowl; mix well. Spoon into greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Spread topping evenly over chicken mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until brown.
Yield:
8 servings.
Mix all ingredients in a jar and shake well.
Store in refrigerator.
In a medium bowl, beat together butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy, 1 to 2 minutes.
Beat in cocoa.
Add flour and beat until well blended.
By hand, stir in pecans.
Spread evenly in a wax paper-lined 8-inch square glass dish.
Cook in a microwave oven on High for 3 minutes. Turn dish a quarter turn and cook 2 1/2 to 3 minutes longer.
Let cool.
Sift powdered sugar over top.
Cut into 16 or 25 squares.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut in shortening until mixture is like coarse crumbs.
Stir in rolled oats.
Combine egg, milk and brown sugar; beat well.
Stir into dry ingredients; add raisins.
Spoon into paper baking cups in muffin pans.
Combine granulated sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over batter.
Bake in a 425° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 12 muffins.
Combined crushed frosted mini-wheats with flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and brown sugar.
Mix well.
Add margarine mixing until crumbly.
Set aside for topping.
Place apples in ungreased 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle topping evenly over apples.
Bake at 350° for 55 minutes or until apples are tender and topping is browned.
Serve warm with ice cream.
Drain juice from pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Reserve to use with pudding.
Combine juice and pudding in small saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Mixture should thicken and become clear.
Cool to room temperature.
In large bowl, gently combine the pineapple chunks, oranges and fruit cocktail.
Pour pudding mixture over fruit and toss to coat fruit.
Refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.
When ready to serve, add bananas and gently combine. Serve immediately.
Bananas may darken after a while.
Cooked cup of rice is added to all other ingredients.
Mix well.
Serve.

In a large saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Add tortellini; cook until tender, about 6 minutes. Stir in the beans, tomato and basil. Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Add the vinegar, salt and pepper. Serve with cheese.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add baking powder and sugar to egg whites.
Add nuts and crackers.
Mix together.
Pour into greased pie pan.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Set and let cool, then put Cool Whip or whipped cream on top.
Mix shortening, sugar, egg and molasses very well.
Either stir or sift flour before measuring.
Blend all dry ingredients and stir into wet mixture and chill.
Heat oven to 375°.
Roll dough into 1 1/4-inch ball.
Dip tops in granulated sugar.
Place balls, sugar side up, 3-inches apart on greased baking sheet.
Sprinkle each with 2 to 3 drops water.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or just until set, but not hard.
Makes about 4 dozen.
Melt butter and cool.
Beat eggs; add sugar and mix.
Whip the cream.
Add melted butter to eggs and sugar; add whipped cream. Add vanilla and flour.
Use 1 scant teaspoon for each one on Krum-KaKa iron.
Makes about 4 dozen.
Prepare cake mix as directed on package in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Cool completely.
Break cake into pieces.
Prepare pudding mix as directed on package.
In clear glass punch bowl, layer 1/2 of cake, 1/2 of pudding, 1/2 of cherry pie filling, 1/2 of pineapple and 1/2 of Cool Whip.
Repeat layers, ending with Cool Whip. Garnish with maraschino cherries and nuts.
Cover; refrigerate several hours before serving.
Mix ingredients together and pour into a buttered 2-quart dish.
Crush Ritz crackers over top and dot generously with butter.
Bake at 400° for 35 minutes.
Cover if crackers tend to burn.
In ungreased 8-inch cake pan, mix together flour, sugar, soda and cocoa.
Make 3 wells in flour mixture.
Put vinegar in one, vanilla in one and corn oil in 3rd.
Pour water over all and mix with fork until entirely moist.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes until just done.
Ice as desired.
Stir together in order given.
Pour into 2 loaf pans, well-greased.
Bake pie crust and let cool.
It is not necessary to bake graham cracker crust.
Cover bottom of pie shell with banana slices.
Whip cream cheese and combine with Cool Whip.
Spoon over bananas in pie crust.
Top with blueberries.
Chill 2 to 3 hours before serving.

Brown ground beef with onion; drain. Grease 8 x 13-inch baking dish. Place crushed Doritos in bottom. Pour ground beef and onion mixture over Doritos. Mix together the sauce and soup. Pour over mixture. Cover top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until cheese is melted bubbly.
Cook meat, diced onions and garlic.
Mix all well in a casserole.
Grate cheese over top and bake 55 minutes at 350°.
Soften cream cheese.
Preheat oven to 350° (325° for glass dish).
In medium saucepan, melt morsels and margarine.
Stir in crumbs and nuts.
Press 1/2 the mixture firmly into bottom of greased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
In large bowl, beat cheese until fluffy, then beat in sweetened condensed milk, vanilla and egg; mix well.
Pour into prepared pan.
Top with remaining crumb mixture. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool to room temperature.
Chill before cutting into bars.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Combine 2 cups baking mix and milk in a bowl.
Mix well.
Beat vigorously for 30 seconds, adding enough remaining baking mix to make moderate dough. Knead 10 times on floured surface. Roll into 1/2-inch thick rectangle.
Spread with butter.
Mix sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle over butter.

Top with raisins and nuts. Roll as for jelly roll to enclose filling; cut into 1-inch slices. Place on baking sheet. Bake at 450° for 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown. Blend confectioners sugar with a small amount of water.
Drizzle over rolls. Cool for 5 minutes.
Yields 1 dozen.
Pour into 2 greased and floured loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Melt butter.
Add water and dressing.
Put 1/2 dressing in casserole (8 1/2 x 10 x 1 1/2-inch).
Cook and drain beans.
Layer on top of dressing.
Add a layer of almonds, followed with split up chicken breast pieces.
Cover with remaining dressing, then combine the soup and chicken broth; blend until smooth.
Pour soup mixture over entire casserole.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes at 325°.
Heat the oil and gently fry the chopped onion and garlic until softened.
Add the chili pepper and fry gently for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, sugar, salt and pepper to taste and cook on a high flame, uncovered, for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
When the sauce is reduced and thick, check the season.
If you like a smoother sauce, you can pass the sauce through the medium disk of a food mill.
I usually just chop up the tomatoes with a fork and leave the sauce a bit chunky.
Add the chopped parsley just before serving.
Cook the pasta following the directions on the packet very carefully to avoid overcooking.
Mix all dry ingredients together and roll ribs in this mixture until well coated.
Place ribs in greased roaster pan with lid. Blend together tomato soup, vinegar and onion.
Pour this over ribs.
Bake in oven very slowly at 250° to 300° for 3 or 3 1/2 hours.
Stir together sugar, margarine and milk.
Bring to a full boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Gradually stir in chocolate chips until melted.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour into greased pans; cool at room temperature.
Cut into squares.
Mix filling together.
Spread onto tortillas.
Let refrigerate about 1 hour.
Slice into pinwheels and serve.
Great to make ahead and serve.
Mix together.
Bake at 300° until lightly browned, stirring often.
Mix and chill for at least an hour before serving with crackers.
Mix all ingredients and enjoy.
Mix ingredients by hand.
Let mixture set overnight in refrigerator.
Make into patties and cook on slightly greased grill or frying pan.
Cook corn bread to package directions. Cool. It's better if kept for 24 hours, then crumbled. Add all vegetables. Cool in refrigerator about 1 hour. Stir in Miracle Whip. Add cheese.
Beat egg; stir in remaining ingredients, mixing just to moisten.
Pour into 12 greased muffin cups until 3/4 full.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve cool or hot with butter.
Place Velveeta and 1 cup milk in thick boiler and melt.
Add the Kraft package cheese powder.
Beat egg and pour into cheese mixture and stir.
Place boiled macaroni in Corning dish.
Add cheese mixture over this.
Cook in 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cook bacon, crumble and set aside.
In bacon fat, cook onion, pepper and mushrooms until tender.
Stir in flour, chicken broth, cream and pimento.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Add salt, pepper, bacon, chicken or turkey and cooked spaghetti.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Drain pineapple.
Slice bananas and dip in lemon juice.
Mix melted butter and graham cracker crumbs and press into 13X9 pan. In mixer, mix powdered sugar, butter and eggs for 15 minutes. Spread over crumbs.
Cover with crushed pineapple.
Cover pineapple with banana slices.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with nuts and cherries.
Chill overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a bowl, sift together the flour, salt and baking soda.
In a second bowl, place all the other ingredients.
Add the flour mixture to bowl 2 and beat until well mixed.
Batter will be lumpy.
Place in tube pan and bake for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Do not open oven.
When cooled, remove from pan and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Cream sugar, oil and baking chocolate; add eggs and mix.
Add remaining ingredients and mix.
Spray 3 small loaf pans with Pam; pour batter in and fill halfway.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown steak with green pepper and onion and cut into small bite-size pieces.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over egg noodles or rice.
Prepare cake mix according to box instructions.
Generously grease a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Pour 1/2 of cake batter into the pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at temperature recommended on box instructions.
While cake is baking, melt caramels in saucepan with the can of milk.
Remove cake from oven; pour caramel mixture over hot cake.
Sprinkle chocolate chips on top of caramel.
Pour remaining batter evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until top layer is done.
Let cool completely; cut into squares. Makes between 30 to 36 squares.
Pan fry sausage into crumbled pieces and drain on paper towels.
In a large boiler, bring to boil tomatoes, tomato sauce, water (add more or less water according to your liking), salt and pepper, oil and celery seed.
Add sausage and macaroni.
Stir well, turn off, place on lid and leave covered 5 minutes.
Serve with crackers and salad or coleslaw.
Mix and put half of mixture in 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle 1/2 brown sugar mixture on batter and swirl in.
Pour rest of batter in and use rest of brown sugar mixture.
Bake at 325° for about 40 minutes.
Melt butter; set aside to cool.
Mix flour and sugar.
Add milk and eggs.
Stir in vanilla and vinegar.
Add butter and nuts.
Put in crust and bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Cut each onion into 4 thick slices; separate into rings (reserve small rings for another use).
Set aside.
Combine cereal and next 3 ingredients; divide in half and set aside.
Beat egg substitute at high speed with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
Dip half of onion rings in egg substitute; dredge in half of crumb mixture.
Place in a single layer on baking sheets coated with cooking spray.
Repeat procedure with remaining onion rings, egg substitute and crumb mixture.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes, or until crisp.
Serve warm.
Cook cranberries in water until they pop open.
Pour in sugar, marshmallows and cherry jello.
Stir until jello and sugar are dissolved.
Refrigerate until mixture starts to set.
Add the celery, apples and pecans.
Pour in mold and chill.
Put sugar on bottom of double boiler insert.
Add bread.
Mix eggs, milk and vanilla.
Pour over bread.
Place insert over hot water.
Cook until set 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Remove insert and let cool.
When cool, place plate over top of pan and invert pudding. Serve warm or cold.
In a medium skillet, cook bacon until crisp. Remove from fat and set aside.
Add mushrooms to bacon fat. Cook until golden; drain and set aside.
Prepare mostaccioli according to package directions. Drain.
In same saucepan, combine half and half, butter, parsley flakes, salt, garlic and hot pepper sauce.
Heat just until butter melts, stirring frequently. Combine bacon, mushrooms, hot mostaccioli, half and half mixture and Parmesan cheese. Toss to coat.
Place on warm serving platter. Garnish with green onions.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix all together well and spread into loaf pan.
Spread tangy sauce over meat loaf and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.
Put cucumbers in quart jars.
Add garlic, dill weed and peppers.
Mix all other ingredients.
Fill jars with liquid. Store in cool dark place for 2 weeks.

Cut kielbasa into 1/2-inch pieces. Cook in microwave for 5 minutes or until fully cooked. Mix all other ingredients together. Pour mixture over cooked kielbasa and mix together. Heat in microwave 5 more minutes.
Whip cream cheese until soft and fluffy.
Beat in peanut butter and sugar.
Slowly add milk, blending thoroughly into mixture.
Stir in whipped topping.
Pour into prepared crust. Sprinkle with chopped peanuts, if desired.
Freeze until firm and serve.
For storage longer than 4 to 6 hours, wrap the pie well for freezing to prevent dehydration.
Saute sausage.
Drain.
Beat eggs with milk, salt and mustard. Line 13 x 9-inch baking dish with bread.
Top with sausage, then cheese.
Pour egg mixture over all.
Cover tightly.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Serve immediately.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a large bowl; cut in shortening with a pastry blender until shortening is the size of peas.
Add buttermilk and stir with a fork until dry ingredients are moistened.
Turn dough out onto a heavily floured surface and knead lightly 4 or 5 times.
Bake cake as directed for about 25 to 30 minutes in a rectangular pan.
Then remove from oven and punch holes all through the cake with a fork.
Then pour the condensed milk on the cake, covering it completely.
Let cool about 10 minutes.
Then mix the rest of the ingredients together and spread over the cake and store in refrigerator.
Cube Spam into 1/2 to 3/4-inch cubes.
Put into a pan.
Add cooled, cubed potatoes.
Add salt and pepper as desired.
Add chopped onion.
Mix well with sour cream.
Before serving, add croutons (do not refrigerate with croutons, they will get mushy). Serve directly on plate or on lettuce leaf as garnish.
Use 1 part rice to 2 parts water.
Wash rice and drain.
Add water and salt.
Cover microwave dish or Pyrex dish with paper towel.
Place in microwave and cook on High for 18 minutes.
Let set for 4 to 5 minutes.
Combine soup, peppers, celery seed, Worcestershire sauce and salt.
Place over medium heat until mixture is heated thoroughly. Place hominy in greased baking dish; pour soup mixture over hominy; top with crumbs and almonds.
Bake at 300° for 15 minutes.
Yields: 12 servings.
Cream butter and cheese together.
Mix in all spices.
Serve at room temperature.
Can be frozen.
Combine sugar, pumpkin and eggs in large bowl.
Blend well. Add oil.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake 1 hour or until toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Grease baking pans well. Bake at 350°.
Brown meat and onions; add seasonings.
Dip each tortilla in warm oil.
On each one, spoon 2 tablespoons sauce, a generous tablespoon of filling and a sprinkling of cheese; roll up and place together in large pan.
Pour remaining sauce and cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine salmon, sour cream, artichokes, green onion, dill, Tabasco sauce, mustard and lemon juice in a blender.
Process until firmly chopped.
Add remaining ingredients.
Process for 1/2 minute.
Cover and refrigerate overnight before serving.
Makes 4 servings.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube or Bundt pan.
Stir together the poppy seed and buttermilk; cover and refrigerate overnight. Sift together flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs one at a time.
Beat in vanilla and grated orange rind.
Stir in flour mixture alternately with poppy seed mixture, mixing until just smooth each time.
Turn half the batter in prepared pan; sprinkle with sugar, cinnamon mixture; add remaining batter.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour or until inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Place cake on wire rack to cool 10 minutes.
Remove cake from pan to cool completely.
The cake becomes moist when stored in a tightly covered container for several days.
Blend ingredients together and add asparagus pieces last. Mix and pour into casserole dish.
Cook beans as directed, then add all ingredients until done. Cook bacon; crumble on top of beans.
Brown ground beef; add salt and pepper.
Add vegetables in layers without mixing.
Last, sprinkle rice on top (do not stir). Simmer until done (about 30 to 40 minutes).
Mix before serving. Serves 6.
Mix cream cheese, 1 tablespoon milk and sugar in large bowl with wire whisk until smooth.
Gently stir in whipped topping. Spread on bottom of crust.
Pour 1 cup milk into bowl.
Add pudding mix and beat with wire whisk until well blended, 1 to 2 minutes (mixture will be thick).
Stir in pumpkin and spices using wire whisk; mix well.
Spread over cream cheese layer. Refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Garnish with additional whipped topping and nuts, if desired.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook eggplant and onions in water to cover 20 minutes.
Drain and add remaining ingredients.
Place in greased casserole and bake in moderate oven at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown. Serves 6.
With meat mallet, pound cutlets to 1/8-inch thickness.
On waxed paper, sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper.
Add flour and coat cutlets.
In a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat in hot olive oil and butter, cook veal a few pieces at a time until lightly browned on both sides.
Add more olive oil if necessary.
Reduce heat to low.
Into drippings in skillet, stir water, wine, bouillon and 1/2 teaspoon of salt, scraping to loosen brown bits.
Return veal to skillet; cover and simmer 15 minutes until cutlets are tender.
Cut 1 lemon and squeeze out juice.
Thinly slice the other.
Remove cutlets to platter; keep warm.
Stir lemon juice in pan.
Heat until boiling over high heat.
Spoon over cutlets.
Garnish with parsley. Serves 8.
Melt butter in microwave on High; stir in flour until smooth. Microwave 30 to 45
seconds until heated.
Blend in milk smoothly. Microwave 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 minutes until thickened, stirring every minute.
Stir in cheese until melted, 15 to 20 seconds.
Mix in macaroni well.
Microwave 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once.
Cook broccoli according to package directions; drain.
Mix soup with milk; stir constantly while heating.
Don't boil.
Add broccoli, pepper to taste, butter and herb.
Heat to bubbly and serve.
Mix all ingredients, pour into greased casserole dish and bake 35-45 minutes at 350 degrees.
Combine crab, cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Add lemon juice, curry powder, Worcestershire sauce and onion to taste.
Put in 7 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish; top with cheese and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Combine eggs, sugar and cream cheese.
Blend well.
Put in pie crust and bake 20 minutes at 375°.
Cool and add pie filling.
Top with whipped cream.
Chill thoroughly before serving.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Add milk and corn.
Mix again.
Pour into a casserole baking dish about 2 inches deep.
Pour melted butter on top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Sift flour, baking powder, soda, dry milk, salt and sugar. Add pecans; mix well.
Combine beaten eggs, butter, bananas and lemon juice.
Add dry ingredients; mix only until flour is moistened.
Divide into 6 well-greased loaf pans (3 1/2 x 8 x 2 1/2-inch).
Bake in a 325° oven for 40 to 45 minutes, or until done.
Cool thoroughly.
Wrap in foil; store overnight.
Good for freezing.
Preheat oven to 450°.
In a large plastic bag, mix all ingredients except parsley.
Close bag and shake until potatoes are evenly coated.
Empty potatoes in shallow pan.
Bake, stirring occasionally, for 40 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Garnish with parsley.
Makes 8 servings.
Mix and pour into pastry.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until done.
Cook carrots in a small amount of water until just barely tender; drain.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over carrots.
Refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
Combine Miracle Whip, cream cheese and Good Seasons mix. Spread on slices of cocktail rye bread.
Top with a thin slice of cucumber. Sprinkle with dill weed.
Boil hamburger meat, potatoes and onion in water until tender. Add Spanish rice, tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Cook for 20 minutes over medium heat.

Slice potatoes and cube cheese. Mix soup and milk until creamy. Layer potatoes, cheese, ham and onion in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan. Pour half the soup over and repeat the layers. Dot with butter. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Bake pastry shell 10 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Reduce temperature to 325°.
In small saucepan over low heat, melt chips with butter.
In a large mixer bowl, beat chocolate mixture with milk, biscuit mix, eggs and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in walnuts.
Place bananas on bottom of pastry shell. Pour chocolate mixture over bananas.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes or until center is set.
Cool.
Garnish as desired.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Beat the first 7 ingredients 2 minutes. Pour into greased 10-inch pie pan. Drain the peaches and save juice.
Lay peaches on top of batter. Beat the cream cheese, sugar and peach juice for 2 minutes.
Spoon on top of peaches.
Leave a 1-inch margin. Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon. Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Line an 8 x 8-inch pan with sliced banana peppers. (May use other peppers.)
In a large bowl combine eggs, corn and cheese. Mix well.
Pour over peppers in pan.
Bake in a 300° oven for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients and chill overnight.
Beat the first 4 ingredients well and set aside.
Sift together the flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice.
Gradually add dry ingredients to egg mixture.
Add prunes, vanilla and walnuts. Pour into greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Glaze while hot.
Remove caps from mushrooms and chop the stems.
Cut up bacon and fry with mushroom stems.
Add onion, pepper and bread crumbs. Stuff mushroom caps with first mixture.
Place in buttered shallow baking dish.
Salt, cover and refrigerate.
Before baking, sprinkle with the Parmesan and basil.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Grease 6 custard cups or other microwave-safe dishes; set aside.
Place equal amounts of bacon and cheese in each cup.
Break 1 egg into each cup.
In small bowl, mix sour cream, milk and hot sauce until well blended.
Spoon 3 tablespoons sour cream mixture around each egg.
Gently break egg yolks with fork.
Place egg cups in microwave and cover with paper towel.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes on Medium power until eggs are set as desired.
Garnish with chopped green onions or diced tomatoes.
Cut sausage into bun sized pieces.
Cook for 15 minutes; drain.
Slice onions and peppers into 1/2-inch strips.
Mix whole tomatoes, Sweet 'N Low and tomato sauce with 1 1/2 cans of water. Cook for 15 minutes.
Add vegetables and cook another 15 minutes. Add sausage and cook another 15 minutes.
Serve with (soft) sausage buns.
Makes about 20 sandwiches.
Brown ground beef, onion and green pepper; drain.
Prepare rotini noodles according to package directions; drain.
Mix all ingredients together except cheese.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan and cover with cheese.
Bake in 350° oven until cheese is melted.
Saute ground beef, onion and garlic. Stir frequently until meat is no longer pink (do not brown).
Drain fat off. Add remaining ingredients and cook slowly, uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 hours until sauce thickens. Spoon over hot dogs. Top with chopped onions, if desired.
Mix pudding mix with milk.
Let set until thick.
Slice cake very thin.
In an attractive bowl, layer the following:
Put all these ingredients in a bowl and stir together.
Pat dough on sides and bottom of pie pan same as a graham cracker crust.
Bake in 400° oven for about 7 to 10 minutes (not too brown).
In large pan, heat butter and saute cabbage and onions until wilted.
Place half of the cabbage, onions and potatoes in a 3-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with 1 cup cheese.
Put remaining cabbage, potato and onion on top.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in same pan cabbage was cooked in.
Add 1/4 cup flour.
Cook 1 minute.
Add can of broth.
Cook until thickened.
Pour over top of cabbage.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix first five ingredients. Melt shortening in skillet. Dredge pork chops in flour mixture and brown in hot fat, slowly.
Cook raisins in water until dry.
Let cool.
Then mix all ingredients well by hand.
Bake in lightly greased bundt pan or 9 x 13 x 2 inch pan for 55 - 60 minutes at 350.
Cream shortening.
Add sugar gradually.
Add egg and molasses. Add sifted flour, baking soda, salt and ginger.
Roll into balls in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients, using electric mixer.
Use apple wedges, orange slices, banana chunks, pineapple chunks, etc. to dip.
Cook sausage; drain.
Brown beef; drain.
Cook onion and celery in meat fat until tender.
Cook rice and drain.
Mix all ingredients together except cheese and bake at 350° for 1 hour, adding cheese to top during last 15 minutes.
Mix the rhubarb and sugar together and let set overnight.
In the morning, boil the mixture for 5 minutes, then add the Jell-O. Stir well.
Put in jars to seal.
Very good if you like rhubarb strawberry on your toast.
Mix all together and bake at 325° for 2 1/2 hours in a casserole dish, removing cover last 30 minutes.
Cook beef, onion and green pepper in a large skillet over medium high heat until meat is brown, stirring to separate meat. Drain fat.
Stir in sauces; mix well.
Combine spaghetti, Romano cheese, eggs and butter in large bow; mix well.
Place in bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Spread Ricotta cheese over top.
Pour sauce mixture over Ricotta cheese.
Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese over top. Bake in pre-heated oven 350° until cheese melts, approximately 20 minutes.
Combine sugar, seasoned salt and pepper; place mixture in a shaker.
In a shallow pan, arrange layer of meat strips.
Sprinkle with seasonings and cover with liquid smoke; repeat layers to use all ingredients.
Marinate meat for 8 hours.
Place aluminum foil on oven racks.
Arrange meat strips on foil in single layer.
Set oven temperature at lowest possible setting, leave oven door ajar and bake for 4 to 8 hours or until done to taste.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 4 1/2 x 6 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Mix flour and sugar.
Stir in pecans.
Blend eggs, potatoes, milk and shortening.
Add liquid mixture to flour mixture.
Stir until blended.
Pour into pan.
Press pecan halves in top of batter. Bake 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.
Mix and cook sugar, cocoa, flour and milk in saucepan until thick.
Add vanilla and butter.
Pour over hot biscuits.
Drain oranges and pineapple.
Mix all ingredients except gelatin.
Sprinkle dry gelatin over salad and toss lightly.
Break cake and press it in a sheet pan bottom.
Bring juice and Jell-O to a boil, then add can of pineapple, cottage cheese and Dream Whip.
Mix all up in a bowl and pour over cake.
Keep in fridge.
Really good if you are on a diet.
In heavy skillet or wok, saute onion in oil until transparent, but not browned.
Add rice, water, bouillon cubes, salt and pepper.
Bring to a vigorous boil.
Cover and cook over low heat until all water is absorbed, about 25 minutes.
Stir in eggs and green onions.
Cook until eggs are set.
Stir in soy sauce.
Use 3 teaspoons per cup and fill with boiling water.

recipes.t: Granny Little'S Pound Cake(In Loving Memory)
d: Cream margarine, Crisco and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Add flour (presifted with baking powder) alternately with flavoring.
Bake at 325° to 350° for 1 hour.
Mix until thick; pour into pie shell.
In large saucepan fitted with steam basket, bring 1/2 cup water to boil; place vegetables in basket and cook, covered, 4 minutes; remove saucepan from heat.
Toss together all ingredients except almonds and lettuce leaves.
Put almonds on top.
Serve 6.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Sweeten this mixture to your taste. Mix cherry Jell-O according to box directions, but use pineapple juice instead of water.
Let jell until syrupy, then add the cranberry relish.
Let set at least 2 hours.
Best when sets overnight.

Flatten chicken to 1/4-inch thick. In a shallow bowl, lightly beat the egg. Combine cracker crumbs and salt in another shallow bowl. Dip chicken in egg, then in crumbs. Set aside. In a large ovenproof skillet, saute mushrooms in 1 tablespoon butter until tender. Remove and set aside. In same skillet, melt remaining butter. Add chicken; cook over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes. Top with ham, mushrooms and cheese. Broil until cheese is melted.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients, except potatoes. Stir in potatoes.
Pour into ungreased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish or 2-quart casserole.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, uncovered.
Fill a large pot with water to cover ingredients. Add shrimp and crab boil seasoning.
When water comes to a boil, add sausage and corn. Boil 10 minutes.
Add shrimp and boil 3 minutes.
Drain and serve with butter for the corn and cocktail sauce for the shrimp.
Cole slaw and favorite beverage completes the meal.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
While hot, punch many holes with ice pick.
Pour glaze over cake.
Let stand several hours before serving.
Blend all ingredients together except crumbs and cheese.
Spoon into casserole, cover top with bread crumbs and cheese.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
This dish multiplies well for a big crowd.
Serves 6 to 8.
Saute onion, celery and green pepper in butter until tender. Stir in chili sauce.
Combine 1/2 cup this mixture with ground beef, bread crumbs, egg, salt and pepper.
Form into a loaf in shallow baking pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Let stand 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve remaining sauce, cold or hot, over meat loaf.
Yields 6 servings.
Combine all ingredients except dressing, Fritos and cheese Add the French dressing. Allow a few hours to marinate in the dressing.
Add cheese and Fritos before serving.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Cream shortening and butter.
Add sugar and beat at medium speed for 5 minutes.
Add egg yolks and beat until the yolks disappear.
Stir flour, baking powder, salt and cocoa together.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour.
Add vanilla.
Fold in the beaten egg whites.
Pour into a 10-inch tube pan that has been greased and floured.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Let cool in pan for 30 minutes.
Remove from pan.
May be iced with your favorite chocolate icing.
Take each frank.
Wrap 1/2 slice cheese around it.
Take 1 piece bacon and wrap over the frank and cheese.
Wrap 1 biscuit around frank.
Continue until ingredients are used up.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 450° until golden brown.
Serve hot.
Heat butter in pan in 350° oven until melted.
Sprinkle graham cracker crumbs evenly over butter.
Press down with fork. Sprinkle chocolate chips and coconut over crumbs.
Drizzle condensed milk evenly over top.
Cover with marshmallows.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Refrigerate for one hour before cutting into bars.
Combine all ingredients except cherries in a mixing bowl. Blend on low speed of electric mixer 15 seconds; increase to medium speed and blend 30 additional seconds.
Stir in cherries. Pour batter into a greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Bake at 350°
for 1 hour and 10 to 15 minutes, or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in pan; remove to wire rack and cool completely.
Yields 1 loaf.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Beat cheese until fluffy.
Combine mustard with milk and add to cheese with salt, cayenne, crab meat, chives, and almonds.
Mix well and spread generously on bread slices.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika.
Cut each slice in 4 triangles; put on a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until well browned.
Boil potatoes, peel and mash while hot.
Add butter, beat eggs with half of sugar.
Add to potatoes and butter mixture.
Add milk and rest of sugar.
Mix in spices (should be creamy).
Pour into pie shells, bake in oven at 350° for one hour or until custard is set and a toothpick comes out clean.
Makes 2 (9-inch) pies.
Cook butter and onion until tender.
Add flour until mixed well.
Add milk, salt and pepper and cook until thickens a little. Add sherry and crab meat.
Spread sliced apples in 9 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle with water, cinnamon and salt.
Work remaining ingredients together until crumbly.
Use pastry blender, fork or fingers.
Spread over apples.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Follow directions on box for cake mix. Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Cool. With electric mixer, beat cream cheese, milk and pudding until thick. Spread over cooled cake.
Spread drained pineapple over creamed mixture. Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with some chopped nuts and coconut.
Keep in refrigerator until served.
Prepare ribs.
Remove excess fat, wash and pat dry with paper towel.
Place ribs in baking pan; sprinkle with salt and pepper. Cover with chopped onions and chopped celery.
Sprinkle with Worcestershire sauce.
Bake slowly in 325° oven until tender (approximately 1 1/2 hours).
Drain fat and pour 1/2 bottle or more barbecue sauce over ribs and return to oven for 1/2 hour, baste occasionally and remove from oven.

Combine and mix first 6 ingredients. Spread in 9 x 13 baking pan. Sprinkle 2/3 of spice cake mix on top. Sprinkle on top of cake mix the chopped walnuts. Drizzle butter over top. Bake for 50 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Poppy Seed Cake With Anise Hyssop
d: Combine and set aside buttermilk, poppy seed, almond extract and anise hyssop flowers.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks and beat.
Sift together flour, soda, baking powder and salt. Alternately add with buttermilk mixture.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour half the batter in a greased tube or bundt pan. Sprinkle half of the sugar-cinnamon mixture on batter and add the remaining batter and the remaining sugar mixture.
Cut through batter with knife for marble effect.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Put pineapple juice, sherbet and ice cream in large mixing bowl and mix together.
When ready to serve, add ginger ale. Makes 24 servings.
Mix all ingredients together except margarine. Melt oleo and pour into 9 x 12 casserole dish. Pour mixed ingredients over melted oleo. Do not stir. Bake 1 hour in 325° oven.
In a blender, combine canned sliced peaches, dry milk powder, vanilla and cinnamon.
Cover and blend until smooth.
Add five ice cubes, one at a time with the motor running.
Blend until smooth. Makes 4 servings.
Calories per serving:
Diabetic exchanges per serving:
milk 1, vegetable 0, fruit 1/2, bread 0, meat 0 and fat 0.
Cook pasta in boiling water until just done and rinse in cold water.
Add enough salad dressing to thoroughly coat the pasta. Add Parmesan cheese and vegetables.
You may use any other vegetable you choose.
Enjoy!
This makes enough for 10.
Melt chocolate in boiling water; cool.
Sift flour, soda and salt.
Cream butter and sugar well.
Add egg yolks one at a time, beating after each.
Blend in vanilla and melted chocolate.
Add flour mixture alternately with buttermilk, beating after each addition.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour into 3 (9-inch) greased and floured layer pans.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool in pans 15 minutes.
Remove and cool on rack.
Brown ground beef; drain and add seasoning mix.
Let cool. Mix cream cheese and chip dip together.
Spread creamed mix in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer with meat mixture, lettuce, tomato and cheese.
Refrigerate.
Serve with nacho chips.
Beat eggs.
Cook sausage and onion.
Drain grease.
Mix all ingredients and bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
When set in the middle it is ready to eat.
Can be prepared the night before and cooked in the morning.
Sprinkle bacon, cheese and onion in unbaked 9-inch pie shell. In a bowl, add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Pour over the bacon and cheese mixture.
Bake in a 400° oven for 15 minutes.
Reduce temperature to 300° and bake 30 minutes longer or until knife inserted 1-inch from edge comes out clean.
Let stand 10 minutes; cut into wedges and serve.
Brown meat and onions.
In another pan place tomato soup and 2 cans of water.
Add chopped green pepper and olive juice.
Boil for a few minutes.
Add Worcestershire sauce.
Cook and drain spaghetti or vermicelli.
Put in large container.
Add meat, sauce and cheese to spaghetti.
Mix well.
Put in 2 casseroles (13 x 9-inch). Spread can of undiluted mushroom soup on top of each.
Decorate with sliced olives.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients, adding beans last. Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine first 8 ingredients and 2 tablespoons barbecue sauce. Form into 12 thick patties.

Wrap bacon slice around the sides of each patty and secure with a toothpick. Bake on a rack at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes or until done. Baste frequently with barbecue sauce the last 30 minutes. Serves 12.
Mix flour and soda.
Combine butter, sugar and pudding mix in large bowl.
Beat until smooth. Beat in eggs.
Gradually add flour mixture.
Stir in oats and raisins.
Batter will be stiff.
Drop by rounded teaspoon about 2 inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix cream, egg, Parmesan cheese and bacon together.
Toss with cooked spaghetti.
Sprinkle with salt, Parmesan cheese and plenty of freshly ground black pepper.
Serve immediately!

recipes.t: Italian Chocolate Cookies(A Very Old Recipe)
d: Make enough perked coffee to cover raisins.
Pour over raisins and let cool.
Place unpeeled potatoes in a large saucepan and cover with water.
Cook just until tender, but firm.
Drain and cut potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Place in an ungreased 2 1/2-quart baking dish. Add pimientos, onion, garlic and onion salt; toss gently. Sprinkle with cheese.
Place bread cubes on top and pour melted margarine over all.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 30 minutes or until bread is toasted.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
In a mixing bowl, blend cream cheese, mayonnaise and salad dressing mix until smooth.
Slice a thin slice off tops of tomatoes and carefully remove insides.
Invert on paper towel to drain.
Fill with cream cheese mixture.
Yield: 12 to 16 servings.
Do not drain fruit.
Mix and chill first 6 ingredients.
Just before serving, add bananas.
Serve plain or with whipped topping.
In a large saucepan, place all the squash.
Add the onion, garlic, broth, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes or until the vegetables are very tender.
Allow to cool slightly; puree in a food processor or blender with basil, parsley and lemon juice until smooth.
Place in a container, cover and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
When ready to serve, add the buttermilk.
Whisk until smooth and adjust the seasonings with salt and pepper.
Serve chilled and garnished with chopped basil and parsley.
Serves 6.
In shaker jar, combine lemonade concentrate, soy sauce and seasonings.
Shake ingredients vigorously to blend.
Pour half of marinade into shallow pan and add chops in single layer.
Pour remaining marinade over steaks; cover pan and place in refrigerator approximately 24 hours.
Meat should be turned once or twice during refrigeration.
Remove from refrigerator three or four hours before grilling.
Grill over medium coals 40 to 45 minutes.
Baste steaks occasionally with remaining marinade.
Cook
bacon
loosely covered with paper towel in microwave oven
for
to 3 1/2 minutes or until crisp.
Reserve 2 tablespoons
of drippings.
Tear lettuce into small pieces and combine
with onion in salad bowl.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Combine
vinegar,
reserved
bacon
drippings,
sugar, water, salt,
mustard and pepper in 1 cup glass measuring cup. Cook uncovered
in
a
microwave for 1 minute or until mixture boils,
stirring
to
dissolve sugar.
Pour over salad greens, tossing
to coat well.
Garnish with crumbled bacon and radish slices.
Serves 6.
Line bottom of bowl with 1/2 cake that has been broken into pieces.
Mix together milk, cream cheese, and sugar.
Mix in Cool Whip and beat with mixer until smooth.
Pour 1/2 of the mixture over first layer of cake.
Repeat layers.
Pour pie filling on top.
Grease a 10-inch tube pan.
Set aside.
Preheat oven to 325°. In a large mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar until smooth.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Combine flour, baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon soda, cocoa and cinnamon; add alternately with sour cream, beating after each addition.
Stir in vanilla.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake for 75 minutes, or until done.
Cool in pan 10 minutes.
Take off wire rack; cool completely.
Wash squash. Slice in rounds, fairly thin. Salt, pepper and roll in flour.
Have cooking oil medium-hot and fry until crisp and golden brown. Serve while hot.
Mix together.
Add water until soupy.
Stuff turkey.
Put water in bottom of pan with turkey.
Bake 3 hours; 45 minutes at 400° and the balance at 325°.
Mix together oil, Parmesan cheese, salt, garlic powder, paprika and pepper.
Dip potatoes in mixture.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Mix and add 1 roll Ritz crackers (crushed) on top.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Set aside in bowl the nuts, cinnamon and sugar.
Cream butter. Add white sugar.
Add the eggs and beat fast.
Measure flour, baking powder and salt.
Grease and flour Bundt pan.
Add dry ingredients to egg mixture alternately with sour cream and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly.
Put 1/2 batter in cake pan.
Spread filling over the rest of batter.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes. Cool in pan on rack for 1/2 hour.
Freezes nicely.
Thaw covered. Better the older it gets.
Combine vegetables, tossing lightly.
Combine remaining ingredients; mix well.
Pour over vegetables and toss lightly. Cover and chill overnight.
Drain well before serving.
Mix Veg-All, sour cream, mayonnaise and cheese.
Place in casserole dish.
Crush crackers and mix with melted butter. Spread on vegetable mixture and bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Brown and crumble hamburger meat in large skillet.
Chop up onion and bell pepper.
Add to hamburger meat.
Brown until soft. Add tomatoes and enough water to make gravy.
Add seasonings. Cook on low heat 45 minutes.
Add noodles.
Cook 10 minutes or until noodles are done.
Serve with corn bread and salad.
Mix together in blender or food processor until smooth.
Gradually mix the ingredients, except cracker crumbs and melted margarine, together into a large bowl, then pour into a casserole bowl.
Add the crushed crackers evenly on top, then spread the melted margarine evenly on top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Drain sauerkraut.
Add remaining ingredients and toss lightly. Use only enough mayonnaise to moisten the mixture.
Chill well about 1 to 5 hours before serving.
Spread crumbs into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Make pudding and pour over crumbs.
Slice bananas over pudding.
Cover with Cool Whip. Layer on strawberries and pineapple.
Sprinkle on coconut.
Cut sausage in half lengthwise, cut crosswise into 1/4-inch slices.
In 10-inch skillet, combine rice, sausage, tomatoes, water, salsa and beans.
Mix well, breaking tomatoes with large spoon.
Bring to boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer 20 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand, covered, about 5 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
In a bowl, mix all ingredients together except ham.
Remove rind from ham. Score fat with a knife.
Rub mixture over ham. Wrap ham in foil or plastic and refrigerate overnight.
Heat oven to 425°.
Unwrap ham.
Place in a 13 x 9-inch cake pan.
Roast, uncovered, for 20 minutes.
Reduce heat to 325°.
Baste with drippings every 30 minutes for about 4 hours or until meat thermometer registers 160° internal temperature.
Boil chicken breasts until done and cool.
Debone and chop into bite sized pieces.
Save approximately 3 cups of water boiled in.
Chop celery, carrots, onion and garlic into fine pieces.
Rinse lettuce.
Drain well.
Tear into small pieces.
Clean and slice mushrooms.
Rinse cucumber, green pepper, onion and tomatoes, sliced.
Combine all ingredients in a salad bowl. Garnish with green onions.
Chop squash and onion; cook until tender and drain well.
Mix in all other ingredients and stir in saltines.
Place in buttered casserole and bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Brown pork chops on each side; drain.
Arrange potatoes in a 9 x 12-inch casserole, lightly coated with nonstick spray.
Mix water, soup and sour cream in small bowl; pour over potatoes. Arrange pork chops on top.
Season with salt and pepper.
Bake, covered, at 375° for 1 1/4 hours.
Remove	crusts	from bread and spread butter lightly on each side.
Place
in large skillet over moderate heat.	Add a little of	the
remaining	butter.
Brown	bread on each side, drain on paper
towels

eggs slightly.

Toss
romaine,
dressing
and croutons.
Mix carrots, celery and tuna together.
Add mayonnaise.
Just before serving, add noodles.
Serves about 6.
Boil until it forms a ball in cold water, then beat and pour into pan to set.
Mix together and simmer for one hour (covered).
Then add 2 cups of water.
Cook one more hour.
Serve hot.
May be put in containers to freeze, if desired.

recipes.t: Food, Facts And Fancy Cream Of Potato-Vegetable Chicken Soup
d: Dice bacon and place in heavy saucepan.
Cook, but do not brown. Remove extra fat. Add diced onion and diced celery.
Saute 2 to 3 minutes.
Add potato, broth and bouillon.
Cook until potato is almost (soft) tender.
Add frozen carrots and peas, celery slices, mushroom slices, diced chicken, milk, chicken broth and herb blend.
Melt butter. Add flour to make gravy. Add milk to thicken. Once thickened, add cheese. Arrange broccoli stems facing in the middle. Pour cheese sauce over the broccoli.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Stir in marshmallows until almost dissolved.
Add cream cheese.
Fold in rest of ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Put in an 8 x 8-inch Pyrex dish and refrigerate.
Stir jello, sugar and syrup all together.
Bring to a full boil.
Remove from heat and add the baking soda, stirring to mix. Pour over popcorn stirring so all corn is coated.
Grease hands with butter and form into balls.
In large bowl, mix Bisquick, cheese and sausage meat; add salt and pepper.
Mix well and roll in small ball.
Place in refrigerator half a day or night.
Cut bacon in three strips and wrap each ball with a strip of bacon.
Lap ends and stick toothpick in to hold in place.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix together cinnamon and sugar in a small bowl.
In a medium bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg and vanilla until blended.
Sift flour, baking soda, baking powder or salt over sugar mixture.
Stir with wooden spoon to make a stiff dough.
Shape dough into walnut-size balls.
Roll in cinnamon/sugar mixture to coat.
Place balls about 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cool on wire racks.
Keep half of egg whites to put in last.
Bake at 450° for 10 to 15 minutes, then to 375° to finish.
For 2 pies.

recipes.t: Cool Veggie Pizza Or Mexican Siesta Pizza
d: *For Mexican Siesta, add 2 tablespoons of sour cream and 2 tablespoons of taco mix.
Omit mayo and dill.
Cook onions in butter until soft.
Add other ingredients and simmer 15 minutes (preferably 30).
Makes about 2 1/2 cups and will be thick.

Place ribs on baking sheet. With sharp knife, cut meat between bones. Crush garlic and blend with other ingredients. Spoon sauce on both sides and into cuts. Bake in 400° oven for 20 minutes on each side. Serves 4.
Combine all ingredients in covered pan or casserole dish or Dutch oven.
Cook in 300° oven for 3 1/2 to 4 hours.
If it gets too dry, add water to make right consistency.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Bone chicken and chip up meat.
Boil spaghetti in chicken broth.
Cook vegetables in margarine until onions are transparent. Mix chicken, spaghetti and vegetables with mushroom soup.
Cook around 40 minutes in a 300° oven.
Melt chocolate in boiling water.
Cool.
Cream margarine and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks one at a time.
Beat after each addition.
Add chocolate, vanilla, buttermilk and flour to the egg mixture, beating slowly until smooth.
Add the soda mixture and fold in the egg whites.
Bake in layers or in a long, flat pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook cabbage, drain and place in 2-quart lightly greased casserole dish.
Melt cheese in soup, pour over cabbage.
Place corn bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350°
until hot and bubbly or brown.
Peel, core and slice apples.
Mix with cinnamon and sugar. Arrange in 9 x 13-inch dish.
Melt oleo and add to remaining dry ingredients.
Spoon over apple mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Keep covered with foil and last 15 minutes, uncover to crisp up the topping.
Mix cinnamon into sugar; add cream and mix well.
Cook on medium-low heat, stirring constantly; cook to 240°.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Stir until syrup coats nuts.
Spread on wax paper to cool.
Break into pieces.
In medium bowl with fork, beat cream cheese until smooth. Gradually stir in crushed pineapple, 1 cup pecans, green pepper, onion and salt.
Shape into a ball. Roll in remaining nuts.
Wrap in plastic film or foil.
Refrigerate until well chilled, overnight.
Mix fruit, tapioca and sugar.
Pour in ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix other ingredients and drop by spoonfuls on top of fruit. Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Put your sliced cucumbers or any cut up vegetables in mixture. Cover and store in refrigerator.
Eat whenever hungry.
Combine ingredients.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Form patties and coat with seafood breader.
Pan-fry.
Put vinegar and dry ingredients in blender with motor running. Add oil in steady stream.
Add onion, then papaya seed and blend until seed looks coarsely ground.
Chill for 1 hour.
Good on fruit or green salads.

Let cauliflower stand in salted water 20 to 30 minutes and rinse. Cover with water. Add the salt and garlic (if desired). Bring to a boil. Simmer 20 to 25 minutes or until tests done. Drain and place on serving dish. Top with Cheese Sauce and Buttered Bread Crumbs.
Saute onions, zucchini and garlic in margarine or oil. Prebake 1 pie crust until slightly cooked.
Mix together cheese, eggs, milk and dash of Tabasco sauce.
Add sauteed vegetables to egg mixture.
Pour into crust.
Bake at about 350° until set, about 45 to 60 minutes.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top after it is baked.
Mix syrup, sugar, milk and chocolate.
Stir over low heat until sugar dissolves.
Increase heat until soft ball stage is reached. Add butter and put in cool water until mixture is lukewarm.
Add vanilla and beat until candy stands alone.
Add pecans and mix and turn into greased dish.
Position rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees. Butter a 9 x 9 pan.
Cream butter and sugar.
Blend in eggs; add bananas and mix well.
Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture with buttermilk.
Bake for 50 minutes at 350° in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Serves 10 to 12.
Brown onion and garlic in margarine.
Add other ingredients except wieners.
Simmer.
Add wieners and cook 10 minutes.
Mix together cake mix, pie filling, eggs, vanilla and nuts. Pour into 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Mix together flour, sugar, butter and flavoring (will be crumbly).
Sprinkle over batter. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine
first	4 ingredients.	Mix sugar and remaining ingredients.
Bring
to a boil; cover.
Reduce heat and simmer 2 minutes.
Pour
vinegar
mixture
over vegetables and toss. Cover and chill at least 2 hours.
Mix all together. Top with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Blend in blender.
Marinate meat overnight, then barbecue. Also good for chicken.
Before you go to church Sunday morning, cut up and remove the skin from fryer; salt and flour lightly.
Arrange in single layer in slow cooker.
Slice onion; spread over chicken.
Sprinkle over this the seasoning, thyme and celery
and parsley flakes.
Place lid on cooker; turn on.
Come home from church and eat!
In a large pitcher or punch bowl, combine all except sherbet. Stir until all juices are thawed and blended.
Top with scoop of sherbet, if desired.
Makes 18 (4 ounce) servings.
Combine almonds, oleo, crumbs and extract; mix well.
Sprinkle 1/3 of crumbs over bottom of 8 1/2 x 11-inch pan that is lined with foil.
Spoon half of ice cream over crumbs.
Drizzle with preserves.
Sprinkle with crumbs.
Repeat layers.
Store in freezer.
Cut in squares and garnish with whipped cream, if desired.
Heat oil in large skillet.
In large bowl, combine zucchini, potatoes, eggs, cracker crumbs, salt, basil and pepper.
Stir until well mixed.
Drop by heaping tablespoonfuls into heated oil and cook until brown.
Add more oil, if needed.
Serve with grated Parmesan cheese.
Makes about 18 medium pancakes.

Boil chicken; cool and debone. Take bread and tear like you would for dressing. Mix seasoned salt, pepper, salt and onion with bread. Mix soups, broth and chicken. Add to bread crumbs and mix well. Put into two 9 x 13-inch pans. Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Wash wild rice.
Boil rice for 15 minutes and drain; set aside.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove bacon and discard all but 3 tablespoons bacon drippings.
Saute celery, onion and green pepper in drippings, until onion is transparent.
Put in a large kettle and add rice, broth, mushrooms, soup and diced bacon.
Cook on low heat for 1 hour or more.
Do not add salt.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour cookie sheet.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat sugar and eggs for 5 minutes. Add anise and beat well.
Add dry ingredients and mix at low speed.
Make 3 separate long loaves on cookie sheet, 3-inches wide.
Bake 15 minutes, until lightly baked.
Remove from oven and cut into 1-inch cookies.
Put back on cookie sheet, cut side down, and bake 10 more minutes.
Makes 3 dozen.
Heat jello, cream cheese, tomato soup and water until melted and blended well.
Cool well.
Add Miracle Whip, pecans, bell pepper and onion; chill overnight.
Makes about 2-quarts of dip. Good for a large crowd and good with chips or vegetables.
Put rhubarb in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle Jell-O and sugar over rhubarb.
Sprinkle package of dry cake mix over mixture.
Mix butter and water together and drizzle over the top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine apple, celery, nuts and mayonnaise.
Toss and serve on crisp greens.
Serves 4.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a shallow dish.
Dip each chicken breast in milk.
Roll in crumb mixture.
Place chicken in a lightly greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 18 minutes or until done.
Yields 6 servings.
Cream 1/3 of the sugar with butter and salt in a large bowl. Blend extract, 2 tablespoons milk and remaining sugar into mixture.
Gradually stir remaining milk into frosting until desired spreading consistency is reached.
Mix all together.
Put in 2 (5 x 9-inch) greased and floured pans.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Mix flour and sugar.
Spread 1/2 mixture evenly in bottom of pie pan.
Line pan with quartered or halved apples, cut side up. Spread remaining sugar mixture on apples.
Drizzle cream over apples.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Crush crackers fine, then combine with sugar and butter.
Mix well.
Press firmly in unbuttered 9-inch pie plate.
Bake at 375° for 8 minutes.
Place in refrigerator to cool.
Mix milk and lemon juice by hand until thick.
Add strawberries and part of the juice for color.
Arrange in pie shell.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Top with Cool Whip.
Mix eggs, sugar and oil.
Beat into the wet mixture flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, baking powder and vanilla.
Add nuts, dates and zucchini to mixture.
Mix together sour cream, jelly and coconut for dip mixture. Wash and cut fruit.
Arrange on tray.
Use decorative toothpicks to pick up fruit and dip in mixture.
Mix thoroughly. Store in refrigerator.
Serve with vegetables.
Beat together with enough cream to make it smooth.
Mix ingredients in order using 8 to 12 hamburger rolls.
Fill with mixture.
Cover with tops.
Seal each sandwich inside of foil and put on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Serve hot.
Drain shrimp and rinse in cold water.
Gradually blend milk and mayonnaise into cream cheese.
Add seasonings and shrimp.
Mash
bananas
in
mixing bowl.
Add remaining ingredients. Stir until blended by hand.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Beat egg and sugar.
Add milk and vanilla.
Sprinkle cinnamon on and beat.
Set mixture aside. Break bread into bite size pieces in a bowl.
Pour water over bread; make soggy.
Squeeze water out of bread by handfuls.
Put all bread in baking dish.
Pour egg and milk mixture over it. Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 375° for 1/2 hour to 45 minutes.
Cook squash and onion for 10 minutes until soft and drain. Melt butter and place croutons in skillet.
Place them on bottom of cake pan and save the other half for the top.
Grate carrots, and mix with mushroom soup, chicken soup and King sour; mix them with squash.
Grate cheese on top.
Place Italian bread crumbs on top sparingly and bake 30 minutes at 350° or longer.
Cut broccoli into flowerets.
Peel and slice stems.
Cook pasta.
When pasta has about 13 minutes left to cook, heat olive oil and add garlic and red pepper.
Stir one minute.
Add broccoli.
Mix well.
Add salt and 1/2 cup water or defatted broth.
Use less salt if using canned all chicken broth.
Cover with a tight lid.
Cook 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain pasta and mix with broccoli and its liquid.
Serve at once.
Mix and pour into a casserole dish and top with crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Spread crescent rolls on cookie sheet and press together. Bake as directed on can until brown.
Mix remaining ingredients except vegetables and spread over crust. Top with vegetables.
Rub ribs with crushed garlic and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Place in roasting pan, rib side down,in 350° oven.
