Put in a large casserole dish. Add diced up cheese (about 4 slices).
Add pimientos and tomato soup.
Cover with more cheese slices and crumbled up bread on top of casserole.
Bake until cheese melts and bread is brown.
Don't let new small potatoes go to waste.
Scrape them or if you want to do a basketful or more, fill your washing machine with cold water and let it run to clean them.
Pack them in jars; add water and 1 teaspoon salt to each quart.
Cold pack 3 hours.
Prepare rigatoni according to package directions. Melt margarine.
Add flour and cook, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Do not brown.
Stir in milk, salt, pepper and cheese.
Cook until smooth and thickened.
Pour sauce over hot rigatoni and mix gently.
Sprinkle peas on top and place in oven at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix salt, masa and flour into bowl. Add beaten egg, milk and shortening. Drop chili into batter, then drop chili in hot oil.
Combine all ingredients and stir together.
Bake in greased 8 x 8-inch dish in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
After
topping	has been added, bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Potatoes	may be prepared several days ahead and refrigerated.
Topping should not be added until you are ready to bake them.
Mix all together and chill thoroughly before serving.
Put cubed bread on bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt margarine and cheese in double boiler.
Pour over bread.
Beat eggs with fork and add milk and mix.
Pour over mixture.
Place in refrigerator overnight.
Bake one hour at 300°.
Shred cabbage in bowl.
Add pinch of celery seed or more, if desired.
Add cole slaw dressing and stir.
Chill and serve or serve immediately.
Soften yeast in water; let stand while combining sour cream, sugar and baking soda in large bowl.
Add 2 cups biscuit mix, then yeast mixture.
Mix well.
Stir in 3 more cups biscuit mix.
Turn dough onto board dusted with 1/2 cup biscuit mix; knead to form smooth ball.
Shape dough into small rounds the size of a walnut. Place close together in buttered 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Bake rolls 15 minutes, or until done.
Makes 72 bite size rolls.
Cut cabbage, onions and green pepper very thin and sprinkle with salt.
Bring to boil oil, vinegar and sugar.
Let cool.
Pour over vegetables.
(Better if made one day in advance.)
Preheat oven at 200°.
Grease and flour tube cake pan.
Mix ingredients and pour into pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Bring margarine, sugar, cocoa and milk to a boil for about 3 minutes.
Add peanut butter and oats.
Then drop on waxed paper and allow to cool.
Soften butter (don't melt).
Mix powdered sugar, peanut butter, graham crackers, vanilla, coconut and butter in large bowl.
Roll into 1-inch balls.
Bake cake in oblong pan according to directions on box.
This only uses half the cake (you can find someone baking on the same day and share).
Break 1/4 of the cake into large pieces and place in a 2-quart serving bowl.
Pour half the thawed strawberries over the cake.
Spread with half of prepared pudding.
Repeat layers. Chill at least 8 hours.
Right before serving, spread whipped topping on top and sprinkle with almonds.
Spoon into dessert dishes to serve.
Cook noodles as directed on package.
Line a casserole with noodles and make into a nest.
In a large frying pan, saute the shrimp in 1/2 cup clarified butter until pink and tender, about 5 minutes.
Cover noodles with shrimp.
Combine soup, sour cream, mayonnaise and chives; add mustard and sherry.
Pour sauce over shrimp and sprinkle Cheddar cheese over all.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, until
cheese has melted and bubbly.
Serves 6.
Blend Crisco with salt and sugars.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing thoroughly.
Add flour, baking soda and nuts to mixture. Shape into roll about 2 1/2 inches in diameter or 2 smaller rolls. Roll in wax paper and chill in refrigerator.
When ready to bake, slice thinly and place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes, or when delicately brown.
Cook carrots until tender and cool.
Mix remaining ingredients into carrots. Place in refrigerator and let set 12 hours or more. Yields 1/2 gallon or enough for 25 people.
Cook Jell-O, pudding and water until thick and clear.
Chill. Add whipped Dream Whip and oranges.
Sift together flour, soda and salt.
Cream together margarine and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg.
Stir in Baby Ruth pieces and dry ingredients.
Add vanilla and blend well. Chill dough for 30 minutes.
Drop by 1/2 teaspoon onto greased baking sheet.
Bake in oven at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until done.
Remove from baking sheet onto wire racks to cool.
To enhance flavoring, add caramel flavoring.
Mix all together and shape into loaf pan.
Decorate top with pecans and cherries, if wanted.
Can use marshmallows.
Sift together first 5 ingredients.
Cut in shortening.
Add yeast mixture.
Add to dry ingredients.
Dough should be soft and pliable; work 5 minutes.
Roll out; cut with biscuit cutter.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
May refrigerate dough overnight.
Place water on stove for linguini; follow directions on package to cook the pasta.
Place all ingredients, except mussels, into large pot and simmer for 1/2 hour.
While the sausage and sauce are cooking, clean mussels according to package directions.
Add to sauce and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes until mussel shells open.
Serve over linguini.
Serves about 8.
Mix Jell-O with cottage cheese until well blended.
Add fruit; be sure oranges and pineapple are drained well.
Mix well and fold in Cool Whip.
Makes a great low-cal, cool salad.

Peel onions and cut into even thin slices. Heat margarine in large skillet. Add onions; toss until coated with margarine. Do not brown. Add vinegar, brown sugar and curry powder. Blend well. Add parsley. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until glazed. Season with salt, pepper and curry powder. Serve hot as a side dish or cook as an appetizer. Can be used in greens or potato salad.
Beat first 6 ingredients together using only 1 package of pudding for 4 minutes at high speed.
Place in 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Beat together 1 package of pudding and 1 cup milk.
Beat heavy cream until peaks form. Mix with pudding mixture.
Use this to ice cake when cake is cool. Store cake in refrigerator.
Tear lettuce in pieces.
Cook and drain peas.
Layer vegetables in a large salad bowl.
Spread a layer of mayonnaise, sealing the lettuce.
Make a second layer of vegetables.
Seal with mayonnaise.
Top with Parmesan cheese and then black olives. Cover tightly with Saran Wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Toss before serving.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine whole wheat flour and yeast.
Heat buttermilk, molasses, honey, salt and butter until warm.
Add oats, whole wheat flour, yeast mixture and eggs.
Bake at low speed for 3 minutes at medium.
Spread
cream cheese on slice of dried beef.
Put slice of pickle
on
top
and roll up.
Chill, then slice into bite size pieces.
Note:
About 1 cup to 1 1/2 cups chopped pecans for outside coating.
Dilute lemon jello in boiling water.
Add cold water and pineapple juice.
Let cool.
Add the crushed pineapple and 1 cup shredded carrots.
Chill until set.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Put beans in a baking dish and add onions, mustard, brown sugar and bacon.
Stir to mix. Bake at 350 degrees for approximately 1 hour until bubbly and set.
In a large frypan, put layer of Tater Tots to cover skillet. Cook Tater Tots until just about done.
Mash Tater Tots flat with a spatula.
Break open about 4 or 5 eggs over the top of Tater Tots.
Mix eggs in with Tater Tots. Season to taste.
Mix all ingredients together and pour into greased and floured tube pan or make three 9-inch layers. Bake for 1 hour at 325°.

Melt butter over low heat and remove from stove. Add 2 cups sugar. Beat well. Mix in eggs and vanilla; blend well. Sift together flour, cocoa and salt. Add to sugar mixture. Mix well. Stir in coconut. Spread into greased 9 x 13 baking pan.
Mix all in large bowl.
Bake in covered 9 x 13-inch bowl at 350°
for 1 hour.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch cake just as listed.
Sprinkle cake mix over the whole top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Cook onions in melted margarine until limp.
Add thawed broccoli, salt, pepper and savory.
Cook 5 minutes over low heat.
Put spaghetti into greased 3-quart casserole.
Cover with a layer of cheese slices.
Pour in milk. Add a layer of broccoli, then cover with cheese slices.
Bake 30 minutes in a 375° oven.
Cream Crisco and sugar well. Add eggs and beat. Sift dry ingredients together. Add this a little at a time while beating the egg mixture.
Add bananas and nuts. Bake in greased, slightly floured loaf pan at 350° for about 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean. Makes one loaf.

recipes.t: Macaroni Cheese Salad With Dill Weed
d: Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain.
Turn, while still hot, into a bowl that contains butter and Parmesan cheese; toss to coat.
Add celery, cheese, salad cubes, mayonnaise to moisten, salt, pepper, seasoned salt and mustard;
mix well and chill.
Turn out on salad greens, and if desired, 2 cups of slivered ham or 1/4 cup of real bacon crumbs may be added to recipe.
Serves 8 to 10.
Mix first 6 ingredients and form into small balls.
Roll in cornflakes.
Drop in hot grease and fry.
Brown ground chuck; add green pepper and onion.
Cook until tender; drain off fat.
Mix mayonnaise, milk, eggs and cornstarch until smooth.
Add beef, cheese and salt.
Stir until well blended.
Pour into uncooked pastry shell and bake on cookie sheet at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
It's ready when knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Combine drained beans with remaining ingredients.
Heat thoroughly, stirring gently.
Mix together the first 3 ingredients; let stand a while, preparing other ingredients.
Add the flour, soda, salt, cinnamon, dates and nuts; mix.
Add the oil and vanilla; mix well.
Cook in tube pan or loaf pan at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
May be refrigerated, covered, for 1 month.
Makes 5 cups.
Mix ingredients; form into small meatballs.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes uncovered in baking dish.
Add tomatoes and peas. Return to oven for 15 to 20 minutes with cover on.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Chop cabbage into pieces.
Brown sausage, season with chili powder.
Drain sausage.
Bring water to a boil and cook noodles for 15 to 20 minutes.
In large mixing bowl, place peaches, pineapple and fruit cocktail if used with all juices; slice strawberries and add
to other fruit, then add pudding mixes. Do not prepare pudding, just dump in bowl with fruit and mix. Add bananas, sliced or chunk-sizes. Mix all together and refrigerate.
Soak beans overnight.
Place salt pork in the bottom of a bean pot, drain the beans and to pot with all other ingredients.
Cover with hot water and bake at 325° for 5 or 6 hours.
Add more water as needed and reduce temperature to 300° for last hour.
Add more molasses, if desired.
Fork test, done when beans are tender, but not mushy.
Serves 10 hungry people.
Cut cabbage into large chucks.
Put in casserole.
Brown ground chuck and onion; drain.
Add tomato soup (not diluted). Put over cabbage.
Cook in a 350° oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Stir in 1/2 hour.
Mix together beans, brown sugar, barbecue sauce and bacon. Saute onion and pepper; add to other mixture.
Put in baking dish; bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix all together, refrigerate overnight, drain and serve.
Beat eggs and add all ingredients, cooking constantly.
Chill! Fold in egg whites and cream; fold in brandy and rum.
Chill, then add vanilla.
Cream shortening and sugar; add eggs and beat well.
Sift together dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture.
Add vanilla and honey.
Bake on greased cookie sheets at 350°.
Put all the ingredients in mixing bowl.
Mix on low for 15 minutes.
Crush Doritos.
Mix together soup, sour cream, chilies, onion and chicken.
In a 3-quart casserole, layer Doritos, soup mixture and cheese in that order.
Make 2 layers.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Serves 8 to 10.
Brown meat in a large saucepan and drain.
Add next 4 ingredients.
Bring to boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix Ricotta cheese or cottage cheese, egg and Parmesan cheese.
Put a little of the meat sauce in bottom of 13 x 9 baking dish and alternate layers as follows:
noodles, 1/3 meat sauce, half of cheese mixture.
Repeat and then top with remaining meat sauce.
Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese on top and cover with foil. Bake at 350° for one hour or until noodles are tender.
Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
Prepare 9 x 13-inch pan with vegetable spray.
Cook margarine, sugar, chocolate and vanilla in top of double boiler over simmering water until blended.
Add egg; stir slowly.
Cook 5 minutes; stir constantly.
Add vanilla, cracker crumbs and pecans. Press into prepared pan.
Chill 15 minutes.
Cream margarine and Neufchatel cheese until fluffy.
Add vanilla.
Gradually add powdered sugar; beat until smooth.
Add color; pour over cracker mixture.
Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Melt butter and chocolate chips in top of double boiler.
Spread over cream filling.
Refrigerate until firm.
Cut into squares (36).
Place chicken in greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Mix soup and broth and pour over chicken.
Place sliced boiled eggs over soup mixture.
Mix flour, margarine and milk.
Pour over chicken mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until golden brown.
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup water.
Mix potatoes and milk.
Add flour salt, shortening and sugar.
Add 3 more cups flour and knead.
If needed, add 1 more cup flour.
Let dough double itself, then roll out and cut with regular doughnut cutter.
Let rise until twice their regular size.
Cook in deep oil at 390°.
Makes 4 dozen plus holes.
Combine all ingredients thoroughly, except only add 1/2 cup of tomato ketchup at this time.
Mix with hands.
Pack firmly into ungreased baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
At the last 15 minutes of baking time, take the meat loaf out and brush the other 1/2 cup of tomato ketchup over the top.
Put back in oven for rest of baking time.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes before slicing.
Makes 8 servings.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Bake, covered, for 15 minutes in a preheated 425° oven.
Drain broth.
Combine tomatoes, cornstarch, basil or oregano and optional pepper sauce.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Pour heated sauce over chicken.
Top with cheese.
Bake 5 minutes uncovered.
Cook in at least a 4-quart Dutch oven.
Brown the ground chuck and chopped onion until the meat is thoroughly cooked.
Add the salt and pepper for seasoning.
Then add the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil over low heat for 30 to 35 minutes.
Stir often to avoid burning.
No lid is necessary.
Serve hot.
Serves 4.
Combine all the ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth. Chill or serve immediately.
Melt Crisco in small pan; blend in flour.
Add milk.
Cook and stir until very thick and smooth.
Remove from heat.
Pour into bowl and add onion, lemon juice and seasonings.
Stir in salmon. Shape into balls.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Combine egg with water. Dip balls in mixture.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Deep fry until browned, about 3 minutes.
Serve plain or with cream gravy with peas.
Mix ground beef lightly with bread crumbs, egg, milk, onion, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Pack mixture lightly in a 2-quart loaf dish.
Cover with waxed paper.
Cook in microwave 5 minutes at Medium-high.
Top with catsup.
Rotate dish 1/2 turn.
Cook, covered, 15 minutes on High or until done.
Remove from microwave. Cover with aluminum foil and let stand 5 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix sour cream, milk, Bisquick, eggs, pepper and salt together; stir in ham, cheese and chilies.
Pour into deep pie plate.
Cook until inserted knife comes out clean at 400° (40 minutes).
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes before cutting.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Stir in remaining ingredients; beat vigorously 20 strokes.
Let rest about 5 minutes.
Cook okra in boiling salted water 10 minutes; drain.
Brown onion and green pepper in salad oil.
Add tomatoes and cook slowly for 5 minutes.
Add okra and remaining ingredients.
Cook over low heat until vegetables are just tender, stirring as little as possible.
One cup canned tomatoes may be used in place of fresh tomatoes.
Serves 4.
Use a double boiler; heat chocolate chips until melted.
Add can of condensed milk and vanilla.
(Also peanut butter if desired.)
Add nuts.
Pour into a lightly buttered 8-inch or 9-inch square pan.
Cool for 1 or more hours and then cut into squares.
Wash
and
drain
celery.
Cut into pieces three inches long. Fray
ends	if
you
want the celery to curl.
Chill in cold water
overnight.
Mix
and blend sour cream, mayonnaise and pecans.
Drain the crisp celery sticks and fill with this mixture.
Cook sausage and drain.
Cut up celery, onion and bell pepper; add to sausage.
Pour in chicken broth.
Add uncooked rice.
Mix well.
Pour into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 350°.
When cooked, fluff with fork.
Soak cucumbers in lime water for 24 hours.
Rinse in clear water several times.
Soak in clean water for 3 hours.
Drain. Mix the cloves, vinegar, celery seed, salt and mixed spices; pour over pickles.
Let stand overnight.
Heat to boiling and put into jars.
Wash and hull berries; set aside.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and Jell-O.
Add water and syrup.
Cook over medium until thickened. Mixture won't be real thick.
Cool.
When cool, pour over berries and toss lightly.
Pour into baked 9-inch pie shell.
Refrigerate until set, about 3 or 4 hours.
Top with whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs until foamy and white.
Add salt.
Continue to beat, gradually adding sugar until a stiff peak forms.
Fold in morsels and pecans.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet by the spoonful.
Place in oven and turn oven off.
Do not open door until the next morning.
Yields 40 to 60 cookies.
Pour salmon juice into measuring cup and set aside.
Put salmon in mixing bowl and 1 egg.
Break up salmon and mix the egg real good.
Fork in 1/2 cup flour.
Mixture is thick.
Add a little pepper, 1/4 salmon juice and add 1 teaspoon baking powder. Beat with a fork.
It must foam.
Pour into salmon mixture.
Mix with fork.
Scoop with small spoons into hot oil.
Makes brown tidbits.
Stick with toothpick and serve with dip or put a hot sauce over them.
Cook vegetables in one and one-half quarts of water until tender.
Add other ingredients and cook until cheese is melted.
Mix all ingredients, except vanilla, in saucepan and cook until it thickens.
Add vanilla.
This will get thicker as it cools.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients; place in lightly greased 4 1/2 x 8 1/2 x 2 5/8-inch loaf pan or shape in loaf form and place into 1-quart greased baking dish.
Bake for 45 to 60 minutes or until meat is no longer pink in center of loaf. Unmold on platter; top with sliced tomatoes and garnish with parsley, if desired.
Heat oven to 350°.
Heat chocolate in 2-quart saucepan over low heat; stir frequently until melted.
Remove from heat.
Stir in coconut, walnuts and milk.
In a bowl, combine pork, sherry, soy sauce, vinegar, cornstarch, ginger, sugar and chili paste.
Toss to mix.
Marinate 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into a baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Can be served with ham.
Brown hamburger.
Put in bottom of an 11 x 14-inch baking dish.
Cook celery and onion; drain peas.
Spread celery, onion and peas over meat.
Spread undiluted mushroom soup over all. Cover with Tater Tots.
Bake in a 350° oven 3/4 to 1 hour.

recipes.t: Mandarin Pork Chops With Wild Rice
d: In large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon oil and brown chops.
Add water, long grain and wild rice with sauce (original recipe), reserved syrup and green onions.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, 13 minutes or until pork is done.
Stir in oranges; heat through.
Add all ingredients together with enough water to cook until tender and of desired consistency.
Prepare popcorn and add peanuts, if desired, or any kind of nuts you want.
Cook sugar, butter, salt and Karo for 5 minutes. Take from stove and add baking soda.
It will foam, then add vanilla.
Pour over popcorn and mix well.
Spread out onto 2 cookie sheets and bake in 250° oven for 1/2 hour.
Stir after 15 minutes. Pour onto wax paper and spread apart.
Cool and then it can be stored in plastic bags or an airtight container.
It will last a while.
Yield:
8 quarts.
Combine flour, salt, baking powder and soda; set aside.
In mixer bowl thoroughly combine sugar, brown sugar and margarine. Add eggs and vanilla; beat well.
Add Rice Krispies and raisins, mixing until it combines.
Drop cookies on greased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for about 16 minutes or until light golden brown.
Brown meat, pepper and onion in 2 tablespoons oil with garlic. Add tomatoes.
Drain all liquid so mixture is very dry.
Flatten out crescent rolls into 1 sheet, mush seams together so there are no holes.
Place meat and vegetable mixture on one half and bring other side over.
Press edges together.
Cook 35 minutes at 350° until crust is golden brown.
Serves 2 adults and 1 to 2 children. Repeat recipe to make more Strombolis as needed.
Rinse kraut and put in roaster.
Top kraut with onion slices and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Add water so it is almost to the top of the kraut in the pan.
Brown ribs in skillet and lay on top of kraut.
Mix in a large measuring cup ketchup and Worcestershire sauce, and then fill the cup with water so the mixture measures a total of 1 cup.
Mix and pour over ribs and kraut.
Put in oven for 2 1/2 hours at 350°.
Beat egg in large bowl until thickened.
Add marmalade and butter until well blended.
Sift together flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Combine buttermilk and lemon juice. Alternately add dry and liquid ingredients in thirds to egg mixture, stirring until well mixed.
Fold in walnuts.
Pour batter into greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool in pan 5 minutes.
Invert onto wire rack.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix with sugar.
Cut in butter; add beaten egg and mix to make crumbs.
Place 1/2 of crumbs in bottom of greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Distribute cherries evenly and top with remaining crumbs.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) for 30 minutes.
Serve with ice cream or other topping. Sprinkle crumbs lightly with cinnamon.
Cook green beans in water, covered, until tender.
Meanwhile, in a skillet saute mushrooms in butter until tender.
Add onion powder and garlic powder.
Drain beans.
Add to skillet and toss. Season with salt and pepper.
Yield:
6 servings.
Grate potatoes coarsely.
Add other ingredients, except last 2, mix thoroughly.
Press into casserole dish.
Top with mixture of bread crumbs and butter.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Beat egg whites until stiff. Combine all other ingredients in a medium size bowl and mix well. Fold in egg whites.
Heat oil or melt butter in a skillet.
When it is hot enough to sizzle a drop of batter on contact, add spoonfuls of batter.
Fry on both sides until firm and lightly browned. Serve immediately. Serves 4.
Brown hamburger meat with onion and bell pepper.
Drain grease.
Add spaghetti and tomatoes.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Dissolve raspberry Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Stir in pie filling.
Turn into 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Chill until partially set.
Dissolve lemon Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water. Beat together cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Gradually add lemon Jell-O.
Stir in undrained pineapple and whip 1/2 cup whipping cream.
Fold into lemon mixture with one cup of tiny marshmallows. Spread on top of cherry layer.
Top with nuts.
Makes 12 servings.
Remove giblets and neck from chicken, then rinse chicken well under cold water.
Place chicken, breast side down, in an 8-quart kettle.
Add carrots, cut up celery, onion, 1 teaspoon salt, the bay leaf and 1 quart of water.
Bring to boiling over high heat. Reduce heat; simmer, covered, for about 2 hours, or until chicken is tender.
Let stand, uncovered, and frequently spoon broth over chicken for 1 hour, or until cool enough to handle.
Remove meat from bones in as large of pieces as you can.
Pull skin from chicken.
Cut chicken into 1/2 to 1-inch chunks.
Chill.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan and spread frozen potatoes in pan. Saute onion (chopped) in 1/4 cup margarine.
Mix together onion, creamed soup, sour cream and shredded Cheddar cheese.
Pour over potatoes.
Mix together corn flake crumbs and 1/4 cup melted butter.
Pour on top of casserole.
Cover with foil.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.

recipes.t: Hot Cross Buns(A Family Tradition On Good Friday)
d: Combine sugar, salt, yeast and flour in large bowl.
In 1-quart saucepan, over low heat, heat milk and butter until very warm (120° to 130°).
With mixer at low speed, beat liquid into dry ingredients until blended.
Increase speed to medium; beat 2 minutes.
Beat in egg and 1 cup flour to make a thick batter; continue beating 2 minutes, scraping bowl often.
Stir in raisins and flour to make a soft dough.
Put tomatoes, onions, bell peppers and jalapeno peppers through food grinder.
Add seasonings and vinegar.
Bring to a boil.
Simmer about 1 hour, stirring often.
Pour in pint jars and seal in hot water bath.
Make jello with 1 cup of water; let cool.
Cream the cream cheese and add jello.
Add pineapple and nuts.
Fold in whipped cream.
Refrigerate.
(I use a ring mold.)
Serves 10 to 12.
Cream butter well, then add sugar gradually.
Add egg yolks and vanilla, continuing to mix.
Fold in almonds and whiskey.

Add flour and baking powder and mix by hand until dough is formed. Then make small shaped cookies (round balls, flat half moons). Bake at 350° for 20 minutes (almost light gold) on ungreased cookie sheet.
Cool cookies before sifting confectioners sugar on top and bottom.
Sift flour in a large bowl.
Make hole in center of flour and put in all ingredients in the hole.
Work up as you would for biscuits.
When all is mixed together, roll out on floured paper and cut.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Follow directions on cake package mix.
In a separate bowl, mix remainder of ingredients.
Grease and flour a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Pour cake mix into pan.
Pour Ricotta mixture over the batter.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes or 325° if oven is too hot.
Let cool completely before cutting.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Drain and crumble.
Combine bacon with tomatoes, cucumber and onions.
Sprinkle with garlic salt, sweet basil and pepper.
Mix well and chill.
Combine vinegar and salad oil; shake well.
Just before serving, pour over salad and toss.
Serves 6 to 8.
Beat all ingredients together and fill unbaked tart shells. Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Makes about 15.
Bake at 350°.
Gradually add orange juice to confectioners sugar, blending well.
Makes 1/3 cup.
Mix all ingredients in a greased casserole dish.
Top with Pepperidge Farm herb stuffing mix.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Mix
well peanut butter, Rice Krispies, oleo and sugar. Melt chocolate chips and wax.
Roll by teaspoon size in hands. Keep your
fingers
wet
and
then
dip the logs in chocolate mixture. Put on wax paper.
Butter glass baking dish.
Cut buttered bread into triangles; mix fruit with sugar.
Arrange buttered bread, fruit and sugar in layers in the dish.
Beat the eggs with the milk, then pour egg and milk mixture over the bread-butter-fruit and allow this to soak in for 15 to 20 minutes.
Then bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until custard is set and top is lightly browned.
Mix butter, brown sugar and 1/2 cup confectioners sugar. Blend in flour and vanilla. Stir in nuts.
Using about 1 teaspoon of dough, shape into crescents or balls.
Place on ungreased baking sheets. Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350° until lightly browned. Cool. Roll in confectioners sugar.
Melt the margarine and cream cheese over low heat.
Leave all liquid on chilies for spicier flavor.
Mix altogether.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix cornstarch and sugar in small saucepan.
Pour in orange juice and mix well.
Heat, stirring until thickened.
Stir in butter and ginger.
Pour over cooked carrots.
Layer slices of tomatoes and Mozzarella.
Sprinkle with chopped fresh basil, salt and freshly ground pepper.
Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.
Heat oven to 350°. Fry eggplant and drain on paper towels. Cook spinach according to directions and drain.
Mix Ricotta cheese and spincah, don't beat, just blend.
Spread evenly in pan. Layer eggplant on top.
Either slice or grate Mozzarella cheese and layer over eggplant.
Cover with sauce.
Sprinkle grated cheese. Give it a blessing and throw it in preheated oven for 45 minutes until bubbly.
Enjoy!
Mix all together and bake in buttered casserole. Crumble Ritz crackers on top.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain juice and add to water to make 3 cups; boil.
Add Jell-O, fruit and cinnamon.
Let set, serves 8.
Mix nuts, sugar, flour and butter; press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool.
Peel and cut tomatoes in 8 pieces.
Put onions and peppers through grinder.
Put all ingredients in large pot and cook until thick.
Makes about 8 pints.
Soften cream cheese.
Mix in powdered sugar, vanilla and milk. Gently fold in Cool Whip.
In glass bowl, put some of the cake cubes.
Drizzle some of the Cool Whip mixture over cake.
Spoon pie filling over that.
Add another layer of cake, Cool Whip and cherries.
Keep making layers until all ingredients are used up, ending with cherries on top.
Store in refrigerator or make ahead of time and freeze.
This makes a lot!
Cook tortellini to desired doneness as directed on package. Drain; rinse with cold water.
In large clear glass bowl with straight sides or 13 x 9-inch baking dish, layer cabbage, spinach, tortellini, tomatoes and green onions.
Pour dressing evenly over top; sprinkle with bacon.
Cover; refrigerate until serving time. Makes 8 (1/2-cup) servings.
Cook the pasta in boiling water (do not overcook); drain in colander.
Pour warm pasta in bowl and pour Wish-Bone dressing over.
Stir.
Cool at room temperature.
Meanwhile, dice green peppers and thinly slice onions.
Cube the cheese into 1/4-inch cubes.
Add all to pasta except cheese and parsley.
They can be added just before serving.
Serve on a lettuce leaf.
Mix all ingredients and place in dish.
Cover with potato chips, crushed or uncrushed.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Great for after the holiday meals.
Heat raisins and water just until the mixture comes to a boil. Cool.
Add soda and set aside.
Mix sugar, oleo and eggs and beat until smooth.
Add flour, salt, raisins and water.
Beat until smooth.
Bake in loaf pan at 350° until, when tested, the toothpick comes out clean.
In large bowl, mix first 6 ingredients.
In a jar or small bowl, combine sugar and oil.
Pour over vegetables and mix well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours.
Combine soy sauce, marmalade, catsup and garlic.
Brush both sides of ribs.
Place in crock-pot.
Pour in remaining sauce. Cover and cook on low, 8 to 10 hours.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Melt margarine for 1 minute in microwave.
Add sugar and microwave 2 more minutes.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Grease jelly roll cookie sheet.
Carefully break each cracker into 4 pieces and place side by side in a single layer on cookie sheet.
Drizzle pecan mixture over crackers.
(Do 1 pan at a time.)
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from pan while still warm.
Prepare pizza dough according to package directions.
Mix together tomato paste and tomato sauce.
Add dash of oregano and dash of garlic salt. Spread sauce over unbaked pizza crust. Spread browned ground chuck over the sauce.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake on lowest rack for 10 minutes at 500° or
until golden brown.
Makes 1 pizza.
Cook onion and celery in part of broth until tender, then puree.
Crumble cornbread and toasted bread.
Mix with rice, pureed onion mixture and enough broth to make a fairly soupy mixture.
Heat bacon grease in shallow baking pan and add dressing mixture and bake at 400° until brown on top and crusty on edges.
Cut, core and mash fruit.
Add other ingredients and cook until thick. Pour into jars and process 10 minutes in boiling water bath.
Makes 6 (1/2-pint) jars.

Mix flour, sugar, salt together. Then add to egg yolk and milk mixture. stir into heated milk. Cook over medium heat until thick stirring constantly. Add butter, vanilla and coconut, banana or cocoa. Pour into baked 9 inch pie shell.
Line a 15 x 10 x 2-inch jelly roll pan with waxed paper; grease the paper and set aside.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, combine marshmallows, butter and peanut butter.
Cover and microwave on High for 2 minutes; stir until well blended.
Stir in cereal until well coated.
Spread into prepared pan.
In a microwave-safe bowl, combine chocolate and butterscotch chips. Microwave, uncovered, on High for 2 minutes.
Stir; spread over cereal to within 1-inch of edges.
Roll up jelly roll style, starting with a short side, peeling away waxed paper while rolling.
Place, seam side down, on a serving plate.
Refrigerate for 1 hour or until set.
Cut into 1-inch slices.
Makes 10 servings.

recipes.t: Oven Baked Halibut A La Orange
d: Line a 12 x 8 x 2-inch shallow baking dish with foil.
Lightly brush both sides of halibut steaks with oil.

Arrange in dish. Sprinkle with orange peel and dill. Cover dish with foil and bake at 450°, allowing 10 to 12 minutes cooking time per inch of thickness measured at its thickest part or until halibut flakes when tested with a fork.
In a large bowl, blend butter, sugar, flour and salt.
Add the eggs and beat well with a rotary beater or mixer on low.
Stir in the corn and milk.
(If using frozen corn, chop it up a little first to release the milky juices.)
Saute chicken in oil.
Sprinkle with salt; add vegetables and broth.
Bring to full boil over medium heat.
Separate vegetables with fork, stirring frequently.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 3 minutes.
Combine sour cream, flour, and paprika.
Stir into vegetables and heat gently.
Potatoes may be red skinned or other thin skinned; cut in 1/2-inch chunks.
Ham is fully cooked, smoked and cut in small chunks.
Corn may be fresh, canned or frozen.
Combine beans; toss all together.
Chill overnight.
Before serving, toss to marinate beans and drain.
Beat first 3 ingredients.
Add next 3 ingredients; add remaining ingredients and blend.
It's much easier to use Cusinart or blender for carrots.
Lightly grease 2 loaf pans and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown ground beef; drain fat.
Add taco seasoning per package directions and simmer approximately 5 minutes.
Layer beef on bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish; top with refried beans; layer sour cream and salsa to taste and shredded cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts (approximately 10 minutes).
Garnish with diced lettuce, tomato, onion and black olives.
Add salsa and serve with tortilla chips.
Enjoy!
Line crackers on bottom of cookie sheet.
Boil butter and brown sugar for 3 minutes.
Pour sugar and butter mixture over crackers.
Bake 4 minutes at 375°.
Remove from oven and sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Let melt.
Spread with butter knife.
Put in refrigerator for about 10 minutes.
Remove and cut into squares.
Return to refrigerator.
Sprinkle nuts on top, if you desire.
Melt cheese and stir in other ingredients.
Simmer for a few minutes.
Serve with plain tortilla chips.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan or 12 cup Bundt pan.
In large mixer bowl, cream butter.
Gradually add sugar, beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, and flavorings.
Sift together flour, salt and soda.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with sour cream.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake 1 hour and 15 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in cake comes out clean.
Cool about 15 minutes in pan.
Mix by hand and put in jars.
Makes 2 quarts.
Cover with lids (not sealed) and tighten and then loosen a little.
Pickles will work a little so it needs a little "working" space!
Refrigerate. Will keep up to a year.
Combine all ingredients, except apples and pecans, mix well. Fold in fruit and nuts. Bake in well greased tube or bundt pan at 350 degrees for approximately 55 minutes.
Cool in pan. May serve with whipped cream.

Freeze pineapple juice. Take out 1 1/2 to 2 hours before serving time and partially thaw. Put in a large container and mash up. Add lemonade and orange juice, mixed with water as directed on cans. Add ginger ale. Stir and serve.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and set aside.
Run water over broccoli to thaw.
Cook hash browns according to directions.
Beat desired amount of eggs with 2 teaspoons water, then pour over potatoes.
Cook eggs, turning 1 to 3 times.
When eggs are done, put cheese on top.
Cover pan to melt cheese.
Cook in 12 x 14-inch skillet. Five eggs will serve 4 people, 4 to 6 ounce portions.
Toast cracked wheat and coconut by stirring constantly in a dry pan over medium heat for several minutes, until lightly browned.
Place in a saucepan andd remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle with chopped nut, if desired.
Mix all ingredients in
a saucepan and simmer on low for about 20 to 30 minutes. Store in refrigerator.
Layer peeled and sliced potatoes in a 9-inch pan. Mix margarine, flour, brown sugar and water.
Make a hot syrup and pour over potatoes.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Mix thoroughly and bake 16 to 20 minutes at 375° in a 10 x 14-inch pan.
When cool, cut into squares.
Spray pan with Pam.
Slice onion in bottom of pan.
Wash; salt and pepper the roast.
Lay roast on onion in pan.
Cover roast with the undiluted soup.
Cover pan with aluminum foil.
Cook in a 300° oven for 3 hours.
This will make its own gravy.
Wash cucumbers and pack in jars.
To each quart jar add 1/2 bunch dill or more, 1 garlic button and 1 small onion.
Let vinegar, water and salt come to a boil; pour over cucumbers. Seal.
Combine pears and water in a large Dutch oven.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat 40 minutes or until pears are soft, stirring occasionally.
Drain.
Press pears through a sieve or food mill; measure 1 quart of puree.
Combine 1 quart puree with remaining ingredients in a Dutch oven.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, 15 minutes or until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat; skim off foam.
Quickly pour hot pear mixture into hot sterilized jars, leaving 1/4-inch headspace; wipe jar rims.
Cover at once with metal lids and screw on bands.
Process in boiling water bath 10 minutes.
Yield:
2 pints.

Combine the first 4 ingredients for 6 minutes (sugar, salt, butter and evaporated milk). Bring to a boil. Keep at a rolling boil over medium heat. Do not stir. Have a metal or glass bowl ready with the chocolate chips, chocolate squares and Fluff. Pour boiling syrup over this and stir until chocolate is melted. Stir in vanilla and nuts. Pour into buttered 9 x 13 pan. Cool slightly, then place in refrigerator to chill and become firm. Cut into squares with sharp knife.
Mix oleo, sugar, flour and meal.
Add beaten eggs, add other ingredients and pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 350 degrees until it does not shake.

recipes.t: Julienne Of Beets And Carrots Or Carrots And Parsnips
d: Cook beets.
Slip off skins and julienne.
Julienne carrots or parsnips. Cook to desired tenderness.
Melt butter and add to it a little orange juice.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix flour, sugar and cocoa.
Add enough hot water to dry ingredients to wet it.
Add egg yolks, milk, margarine (melted) and flavoring.
Pour into uncooked pie crust and cook until firm, approximately 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In small bowl, blend pepperoni, cheeses, oregano and egg.
Roll apart crescent rolls into 8 rectangles (press perforations to seal).
Spread mixture on each rectangle, making sure to cover to the edges.
Starting at shorter side, roll up and seal.
Cut each roll into 6 pieces.

recipes.t: Tank'S Taco Grande(Mom Or Dad Will Help With Hard Parts.)
d: Preheat oven to 350°.

Spray Pam on bottom and sides of 9 x 13 baking dish. Cook turkey or beef until no longer pink, breaking up chunks to small crumbs. Add taco mix and water (see mix directions). Remove from heat. Add 1 cup of salsa.
Place skinned chicken breasts in 8-inch square baking dish that has been lightly oiled.
Lightly salt and pepper.
Place drained sauerkraut over chicken; top with cheese slices, one over each breast.
Pour dressing evenly over the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake in a 325° oven about 1 1/2 hours or until fork can be inserted in chicken with ease.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley. Makes four servings.
Baked potato skins can also be baked at the same time.
Combine first 2 ingredients in a 2 x 8 x 12-inch dish, mixing well.
Layer with remaining ingredients in order listed.
Serve with Tostitos.
Mix all juices except 7-Up or ginger ale.
Add just before serving.
Cook squash according to directions on the package; drain. Sliver raw carrots on coarse side of grader.
Mix squash, carrots, pimentos, sour cream and undiluted soup in saucepan.
In separate bowl mix herb stuffing and margarine.
Line baking dish with half of herb stuffing mixture.
Pour in squash mixture and top with remaining half of herb stuffing mixture. Salt and pepper to taste. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Yields 8 servings.

Wash lentils and let soak overnight; drain. Saute onions, celery and garlic in olive oil. Put soaked lentils in large pot and fill with 2 quarts water. Add sauteed vegetables, carrots, tomatoes (chopped very coarsely) along with all the puree, oregano, salt, pepper, parsley and bay leaf.
Cream margarine, sugar and eggs together until light and fluffy.
Sift together flour, soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir into creamed mixture.
Stir in oats, raisins and walnuts.
Drop from a tablespoon 2 inches apart on lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for about 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool slightly and remove from pan.
Sift or mix together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Cream the shortening and confectioners sugar.
Blend in the almond extract and eggs.
Measure milk and add alternately with dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
(Begin and end with dry.)
Fold in walnuts and cherries.
Pour into well-greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Cut gently through batter to break air bubbles. Bake at 350° for 60 to 65 minutes.
Remove from oven and while still warm spread on top with butter and sprinkle with a mixture of cinnamon and sugar.
Blend all together with hands until well blended.
Roll into small balls.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for about 15 to 20 minutes or until done.
Combine butter or margarine, sugar and curry powder.
Bring to a boil.
Drain the fruit and arrange in a 2-quart baking dish (about 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch).
Pour hot sauce over it. Garnish with cherries. Bake at 325° until it bubbles (about 30 to 40 minutes). Serve hot.
Very good with poultry, ham and pork.
Serves 8 to 10.
In a 2-cup casserole, slightly beat eggs.
Add sugar and blend.
Pour in milk and blend with salt and cinnamon.
Add raisins and bread cubes.
Dot with butter.
Layer half of cabbage, onions and green pepper.
Sprinkle half of sugar over vegetables.
Repeat.
Let stand while making dressing.
Mix sugar and cornstarch; add vinegar and water from beets. Bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes.
Add beets and simmer 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, bring to a boil and add butter. Serves 4.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350 degrees for one hour.
Makes a large bowl.
Grind cranberries in blender.
Add marshmallows and sugar. Chill, covered, overnight.
Add grapes, apples, walnuts and salt. Fold in chilled, whipped cream.
Serves 8 to 10.
Drain beans and rinse with cold water several times.
Let drain.
Mix other ingredients in a large container.
Pour in beans and mix.
Let stand in the refrigerator 12 to 18 hours.
Mix all ingredients together and sprinkle with paprika.
Serve with Triscuits crackers or corn chips.
Mix sugar and butter.
Add eggs one at a time.
Add flour and milk, starting and ending with flour.
Bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at 325°.
Cook corn and lima beans in a small amount of boiling water for 12 minutes or until tender; drain and set aside.
Cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp; remove bacon, reserving drippings in skillet.
Crumble bacon and set aside.
Saute chopped onion in bacon drippings until onion is tender; remove onion and set aside. Add flour to bacon drippings, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add tomatoes and rest of ingredients.
Heat through.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine first 4 ingredients and beat until stiff.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on foil-covered cookie sheets.
Turn oven off and leave cookies in oven overnight.
Store in tins between wax paper.
May be frozen.
Mix flour, margarine and cream cheese and refrigerate.
Mix brown sugar, eggs, vanilla, salt and margarine.
Cook over low heat.
Watch closely as it burns easily.
Add walnuts.
Roll out dough 1/8-inch thick.
Cut with a scalloped cookie cutter.
Press into 1-inch muffin tin.
Drop 1 teaspoon of filling into each cup about 3/4 full.
They will swell.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Avoid overbrowning.
Mix together 3 cups of hot water, pineapple juice and lemon Jell-O.
Stir until dissolved.
Pour mixture in pan and refrigerate to cool, but not set firm, about 1 hour.
Mix together lime Jell-O and 1.5 quarts of hot water.
Stir until dissolved.
Pour lime Jell-O mixture into a 13 x 9-inch cake pan; chill until firmly set. Mix together strawberry Jell-O and 1.5 quarts of hot water.
Stir until dissolved.
Allow mixture to cool.
In a small mixing bowl, cream the cream cheese.
Add whipped cream.
To this mixture, add the cooled lemon Jell-O mix and whip until blended thoroughly. Pour the lemon mixture on top of the set lime Jell-O.
Refrigerate until firm.
Pour strawberry Jell-O on top of the lemon mixture and let set again, until firm.

recipes.t: Fresh Tomato Sauce For Pasta Or Pizza Crust, Etc.
d: Heat oil in a large skillet.
Add onion and garlic.
Saute 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes and remaining ingredients.
Stir well and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low and cook 10 minutes or until reduced to 4 cups.
Keep in freezer for quick pasta dishes.
Arrange pasta in skillet.
Top with chicken (undrained), frozen peas, carrots and sliced onion.
Pour on broth.
Sprinkle with tarragon.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix all ingredients and pour into pie crust.
Cook in 375° oven for about 1 hour.
Thoroughly cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs; beat well. Add flour, sifted with salt, baking powder, soda and cocoa alternately with milk and vanilla.
Add coffee; mix well.
Fill greased cupcake pans 2/3 full.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.

Mix pudding according to directions. Add eagle brand milk. Put in refrigerator for 5 to 10 minutes until set. While waiting for mixture to set, beat heavy whipping cream (use a mixer) until a soft peek. Fold in to pudding mixture. Start layering in a 2 qt. dish; putting pudding mixture first, then cookies and bananas. Refrigerate overnight so cookies get soft.
Scald milk with margarine.
Add with all remaining ingredients to bread and stir lightly.
Bake at 350° until firm.
Cream sugar and oleo.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Sift flour, cocoa and salt.
Add sugar.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and spread with Marshmallow Creme while hot.
Cool 30 minutes and ice.
Cut off top of loaf of bread and hollow out, forming a crust shell.
Tear enough bread for 2 cups; set aside.
Brown beef and oil; add green pepper, Worcestershire sauce and cheese soup. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in bread crumbs.
Fill in bread crust. Place American cheese slices diagonally on top.
Bake 5 to 10 minutes or until cheese melts.
Mix the cream of mushroom soup and milk together.
Add all other ingredients.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cover and place in fridge overnight (12 hours).
Before baking, sprinkle buttered bread crumbs on top.
Bake, uncovered, 1 1/2 hours at 350°. Grease the pan before adding ingredients.
Mix cream cheese with 1/2 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce and a little lemon juice.
Spread in bottom of pie plate.
Pick shells from large can of backfin crabmeat.
Spread over cream cheese. Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Mix Heinz chili sauce, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire, horseradish and lemon juice and pour over crab. Serve with Ritz crackers.
Mix ingredients in large bowl.
Pour into a 10 x 14-inch pan. Top with cheese crackers and melted butter.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Cook rice as directed.
Set aside to drain.
Put veggies in skillet with small amount of oil.
Stir fry.
Add 3 tablespoons soy sauce.
Add rice.
Stir fry until hot.
Ready to eat.
Mix 1 cup of flour, baking powder and butter; add egg and milk.
Mix.
Press into greased pie pan.
Arrange rhubarb in pie shell
Sprinkle with Jell-O.
Add cup of boiling water to package of jello.
Mix until dissolved.
Add package of frozen berries; stir until thawed.
Add the applesauce and stir well.
Pour into a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Chill in refrigerator until set.
For the topping, fold in 1 cup of marshmallows into 1 cup of sour cream or Cool Whip and spread over the set jello.
Mix all together. Put in pan and bake at 350° until done.
Two days before using, make sauce:
Brown onions in bottom of a large Dutch oven.
Add meat and brown.
Stir occasionally to break it up well.
Add salt, pepper, lots of oregano, garlic powder, 3 cans of tomato paste and can of puree.
Add 1 teaspoon of sugar.
Cover.
Simmer 2 to 3 hours, stirring every 30 minutes or so and taste to season.
When done, put in a large airtight container.
Store in refrigerator at least 24 hours before using.

Blend margarine, sugar and egg. Then add pumpkin and vanilla. Sift flour, cinnamon, baking powder, soda and salt. Add walnuts. Drop with spoon on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for almost 12 minutes.
Cook chicken in water with onion.
Remove chicken; drain and set onions aside.
Chop chicken; salt and pepper to taste. Combine chicken, onion and mayonnaise to taste.
Add celery, lemon juice, pimento, eggs and soup.
Put into casserole dish.
Top with almonds, potato chips and cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
While grits are still hot, add cheeses and margarine.
Allow to cool; add eggs and milk.
Pour into baking dish.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 45 minutes.
This dish can be made ahead of time, frozen and reheated.
Serves 6 to 8.
Sift and measure the flour.
Cut the butter into the flour. Break the egg into a measuring cup, then add enough water to come up to the 3/4 cup line.
Add to the flour; mix lightly with a fork. Drop by tablespoonfuls over boiling meat and broth or into well-greased steamer placed over boiling water.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, or until dumplings are tender.
Combine oil, sugar and eggs; beat at medium speed for 3 minutes.
Combine dry ingredients and add to mixture.
Fold in pecans and apples.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes, or until cake is done.
Dust apples, raisins and nuts with some of the flour; set aside.
Blend oil, sugar and slightly beaten eggs; set aside. Sift together flour, salt and soda; add to egg mixture and add vanilla.
Fold in coated apples, nuts and raisins; pour into a 10-inch greased tube pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 250°.
Grease two 9 x 13-inch pan.
Heat brown sugar, margarine, corn syrup and salt in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly until bubbly around edges.
Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally for 2 minutes longer.
Remove from heat; stir in baking soda until foamy and light colored. Pour over cereal, peanuts and raisins in greased 4-quart bowl. Stir until mixture is coated.
Spread evenly in pans.
Bake 15 minutes.
Stir.
Let stand just until cool, about 10 minutes. Loosen mixture with metal spatula.
Let stand until firm, about 30 minutes.
Break into bite size pieces.
Makes about 10 cups of snack.

recipes.t: Lime Salad Chiffon With Graham Crackers
d: Make the crust with butter and cracker crumbs.
Put into an 8-inch square pan.
Chill.
Mix jello and sugar with 3 cups boiling water.
Stir until dissolved.
Add remaining ingredients.
Put in freezer.
Stir after about 3 hours and every hour thereafter until it is slushy.
Dissolve jello into boiling water. Add sugar and dissolve. Add cold water, pineapple juice and lemon juice. Pour into clean milk or apple juice jugs and chill well or start to freeze.
Beat eggs and mix with flour, salt, cinnamon, soda, vanilla, nuts, sugar, oil, bananas (not mashed) and pineapple.
Do not beat.
Stir until blended.
Pour into greased and floured pan (9 x 13-inch).
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Cook butter and sugar on medium heat, stirring frequently, until temperature reaches 290° on candy thermometer.
Pour onto greased cookie sheet with sides.
Spread out.

Mix the tomato soup, brown sugar and vinegar together well. Bake meat until it has about 20 minutes left. Pour the barbecue sauce on the meat and continue to bake uncovered until the meat is done. This is great on pork chops, some cuts of beef and a great way to dress up leftover meat.
Cream together margarine and sugar.
Sift together, flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Add nuts and raisins to dry ingredients.
Add eggs, sour cream and vanilla.
Mix well.
Bake in bundt pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Sprinkle sugar and cinnamon mixture on top before baking.
Sprinkle on bottom after baking.
Melt butter in a large sauce pan and add all ingredients, except shrimp. Cook over medium heat for approximately 5 minutes. Add shrimp and saute for 4 minutes on each side.
Remove from heat and
ladle butter sauce over shrimp.
Garnish
with fresh parsley and 3 slices of lemon.
Serves two.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Take 1 can of beans; drain 1/2 water; put in casserole dish.
Add cream of mushroom soup, then onions and cheese; mix well.
Sprinkle extra cheese on top.
Cook in oven for 30 minutes or until onions and green beans are tender.
In a saucepan, make a roux with flour and butter.
Add mustard.
Lower heat and add one-half of the milk, stirring so as not to scald.
In a pot, cook pasta until it's half done.
Saute onion and add to roux mixture along with cheeses and rest of milk.
Give each child 3 large marshmallows and toothpick.
Instruct to insert toothpick and to align marshmallows.
Decorate snowmen with raisins, fruit slices and cereal pieces.
Eat as snack.
Slowly cook oil, onions, celery, salt and beef, stirring constantly.
Add potatoes and tomatoes; stir well. Place in casserole dish. Place strips of pastry on top.
Bake at 425° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Blend well and add Hershey's syrup.
Mix together flour, soda and salt. Melt Hershey bars; alternately add buttermilk, Hershey bars and vanilla.
Bake in stem pan at 350° for one hour.

recipes.t: Baked Beans With Green Pepper And Carrots
d: Wash beans, cover with water and cook until soft.
Drain, not too dry.
Add salt and bacon drippings.
Mix in baking dish the beans, brown sugar, onions, green pepper and grated carrots.
Add catsup.
Bake in 325° oven for one hour or until as dry as desired.
In a large kettle, brown sausage, beef and onion.
Drain off any fat.
Add remaining ingredients, except cabbage; mix well. Stir in cabbage and simmer, 15 to 20 minutes or until cabbage is tender.
Serves 8.
Add sugar and water to cherries.
Bring to a boil.
Pour over jello and stir until dissolved.
Place in refrigerator until cool. Remove and add Coke, pineapple and nuts.
Refrigerate until set.
Mix together until smooth. Dip hot dogs into mix and deep fry. Yields 8 to 10 corn dogs.
Mix flour, Crisco, salt and sugar until like coarse cornmeal. Add cold water.
Roll as for pie dough, approximately 1/8-inch thick onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Prick with a fork.
Cut into bite size pieces (1/4-inch squares) with a knife before baking.
Bake in 400° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until very light brown.
Fry onions gently
in
fat
until lightly browned.
Add stock, and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer about 15 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, except vegetables.
Beat until creamy.
Makes about 1 cup.
Use as a vegetable dip.
Cook first 4 ingredients.
Add all other ingredients and bake.
Mix all ingredients together.
In a big bowl mix all ingredients together, except semi-hard rolls, and let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Next day cut the rolls in half, on one side smear a little amount of butter and put on spread.
Close the roll with the other half and mount in aluminum foil.
Heat oven to 350°F and bake for 15 to 20 minutes. If you do not use up all the rolls at once, the rest mounted in aluminum foil can be stored in refrigerator for 2 days.
Stir pudding in pineapple and juice.
Mix in nuts, marshmallows and cherries. Fold in Cool Whip.
Place in an 8 x 8-inch pan. Refrigerate until firm.
Partially thaw vegetables (enough to break apart) and mix with onions, mushrooms and chestnuts.
Place into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix soup and Cheez Whiz.
Heat just enough to be able to mix well.
Pour over vegetables.
Bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
Saute tips in butter; add flour and brown.
Add hot beef stock and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Reduce wine and vinegar to 1/2 and add to above.
Combine the first 4 ingredients and roll into 1-inch balls.
Mix first 5 ingredients into balls.
Brown in butter at 250° in electric frypan or regular pan on medium high heat.
Melt catsup and currant jelly in frypan.
Simmer meat balls and sauce together for 30 minutes.
