Toast nuts at 325° for 15 minutes.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Fold in sugar and salt.
Slowly fold nuts into mixture and mix until coated.
In a Dutch oven cook ground beef and onion until meat is browned and onion is tender.
Drain.
Add the next 8 ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Remove the bay leaf.
Serve over spaghetti.
Yield:
4 to 6 servings (about 1 quart).
Place chilies under broiler after washing; make a small slit in each pepper.
Blister on all sides.
Place in plastic bag for 15 minutes.
Put in cold water; peel and seed.
Cut Monterey cheese in strips and stuff chilies.
Put in casserole dish; sprinkle with Cheddar.
Beat egg, salt, milk and flour until smooth.
Pour over and bake 35 to 45 minutes, until knife blade comes out clean.
Soften cream cheese to room temperature.
Mix all ingredients together.
Shape into round or square shape on waxed paper. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours.
Place on serving dish and remove waxed paper.
Serve with crackers.
Drain oil from artichoke hearts.
Reserve hearts.
Put oil into frying pan.
Heat.
Chop scallions and fry in oil until limp. Drain oil, reserve scallions.
Cook macaroni. Drain. Combine tuna, soup and milk. Fold in macaroni. Bake in 9 x 12 dish at 350° until mixture is bubbly. Sprinkle with cheese and brown. May substitute noodles for macaroni.
In 3 quart saucepan, saute onion in butter until tender. Stir in flour, salt and nutmeg until smooth.
Gradually whisk in milk and water.
Add cheese; cook and stir over medium heat until melted.
Add spinach; cover and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes or until heated through.
Serve with oyster crackers if desired.
Yield: 5 to 6 servings.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Drain.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan. Top with soup.
Add Tater Tots.
Freeze.

Remove and discard the neck, giblets and any excess fat from the chicken. Rinse chicken well inside and out with cold water. Lightly brush or spray chicken with vegetable oil, then season inside and out with the rub mixture. Open the can of beer and pour out half. Set the half full can of beer on a flat surface and slide the chicken over the top so the can fits inside the cavity. Transfer the bird to the grill, keeping the can upright. Grill over indirect medium heat 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours or until the chicken juices run clear and the internal temperature reaches 170° in the breast and 180° in the thickest part of the thigh. Wearing barbecue mitts, carefully remove the chicken and beer can from the grill. Be careful not to spill the beer since it will be hot. Let the chicken set for about 10 minutes before lifting it from the can. Discard beer. Cut chicken into serving pieces. Serve warm. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Cook the squash and onion in boiling water for 5 minutes; drain.
Combine the soup, sour cream and carrot.
Fold in the squash and onion.
Combine the stuffing mix and melted butter or margarine.
Spread half of stuffing mixture in a 9 x 3-inch baking pan.
Spoon vegetable mixture on top of stuffing.
Sprinkle remaining crumbs over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut with spatula.
Serves 10.
Travels well.
Equally good at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and lightly flour two 8-inch layer pans.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add vanilla.
Sift flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternating with water.
Stir in sauerkraut.
Bake in preheated pans at 350° for about 30 minutes or until cake tests done.
Frost with your favorite icing.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In 2-quart ungreased casserole dish with a tight fitting lid, mix rice, salt and pepper.
Dot with butter.
Pour boiling water over rice.
Stir to melt butter. Bake, covered, 45 minutes (do not lift lid).
Add green onions. Mix lightly.
To serve, fluff up rice lightly with fork.
Serves 6.
Brown beef, then add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil and simmer until done.
Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients together. Cover and refrigerate at least a few hours before serving. Best served with Fritos Scoops.
Brown the first 3 ingredients and drain. Stir in the remaining ingredients except cheeses. Take off heat before adding cheeses. Stir until melted and well mixed. Serve with crackers.
Cut and brown bacon with onion and ground beef.
Pour in casserole dish and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cook until thick enough to dribble over cake.
Toss all ingredients together in medium bowl.
Chill before serving.
In a large mixing bowl, beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in condensed milk until smooth.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour into prepared crust.
Chill 3 hours or until set. Top with cherry pie filling.
Ready to serve.
Excellent with coffee.
Makes one 9-inch pie.
Bring to a boil the squash, onion and water. Cover and simmer until tender.
While this is cooking mix cornbread crumbs, cream of chicken soup, margarine and black pepper.
Mix with squash mixture and bake in greased 1 1/2-quart casserole dish at 350° for 45 minutes.
Slice the bread lengthwise and hull out loaf (top and bottom). Brown hamburger and onions, then add catsup.
Spoon into bottom part of the bread.
Put a slice of cheese on top of meat.
Place top of bread on sandwich, then roll in plastic wrap.
Place in oven and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Slice and serve with salad.
Fry bacon; cool and crumble.
Mix softened cream cheese, salad dressing, cheese, bacon bits and onion.
When well mixed, form into ball and chill.
Ball may be rolled in finely chopped walnuts or pecans or parsley flakes.
Blend ingredients; refrigerate if desired.
Heat over hot water before serving.
Yields about 1 cup sauce.
Mix all ingredients together.
Refrigerate overnight.
If desired, add 2 cups of sliced bananas at serving time.
Beat sugar and shortening together.
Then add eggs one at a time and beat.
Add rest of ingredients and beat good.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Combine sugar and milk; bring to full rolling boil.
Boil and stir for 4 1/2 minutes.
Break up chocolate and mix with other ingredients.
Pour hot syrup over all ingredients and stir.
Pour in buttered 9 x 13-inch pan and refrigerate.
Mix and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Mix coconut, milk, sugar and butter together.
Spread in a sheet cake or cookie pan.
Put in freezer for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Remove; cut into bars.
Melt chocolate chips and paraffin in double boiler.
Dip bars into chocolate mixture (I dip them with a toothpick).
Place on wax paper to cool.
Turn on oven and set at 350° (moderate).
Mix first 7 ingredients in a 2-quart bowl.
Stir in potatoes until well mixed. Put mixture into a shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup cheese and paprika over top.
Bake near center of oven about 1 hour or until potatoes are tender.
Cream together shortening, brown sugar and eggs.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix together and drop by tablespoons on greased cookie sheet (for smaller cookie, use teaspoon).
Bake at 375° for 12 minutes.
Brown and drain meat; add onion.
Cook until clear.
Add remaining ingredients except beans and cheese.
Cook until macaroni is tender.
Add beans and cheese.
Cook until heated through and serve warm.
Dice tomatoes, green pepper, cheese and ham.
Cook spaghetti; drain and cool with cold water.
Toss together.
Add Italian dressing.
Mix first 3 ingredients well.
Roll into small balls.
Chill until firm.
Dip in melted chocolate.
Prepare Dream Whip with 1 cup of milk as directed on package, using a large mixer bowl.
Add remaining milk and pudding mix. Blend, then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes, scraping bowl. Spoon into pie crust. Chill for 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Spread in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, turning and mixing every 10 to 15 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then add raisins and any other dry fruit you like.
Store in an airtight container.
Clean crab meat and pick out all bones.
Combine everything and roll in egg, then bread crumbs and fry in deep fat.
Beat cream cheese at medium speed of electric mixer until fluffy; stir in remaining ingredients.
Serve on crackers or bread.
Yield:
3 1/4 cups.
Mix ingredients in a large bowl.
Chill for 1 hour.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, mix all ingredients together.
Chill overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook ground meat until browned.
Drain and add taco seasoning, stirring well. Add tomato sauce and chopped tomatoes.
Stir in corn and simmer over low heat 30 to 45 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Serves 6.
Cook broccoli only until it separates.
Drain.
Mix remaining ingredients in greased casserole dish.
Alternate first broccoli, then mixture.
Repeat.
Crush Ritz crackers over top.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook broccoli according to package directions.
Drain well. Pour broccoli back into pan.
Add salt and pepper.
Stir in cheese and 1/2 stick of margarine until melted.
Pour into buttered casserole dish.
Melt remaining margarine in pan and stir in crushed Ritz crackers, then spread over the broccoli.
Bake at 350° for about 25 minutes.
Combine sugar, tapioca, salt and almond flavor.
Mix thoroughly with fruit and fruit juices before pouring into shells. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes, then at 350° for 30 minutes.
Fry hamburger meat in large skillet.
Drain off fat.
Pour pork and beans in with hamburger meat, then barbecue sauce.
Heat thoroughly.
Cook rice until tender in salted water.
Mix all ingredients. Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup diced Cheddar cheese.
Pour into flat bakeware.
Top with cooking cheese.
Brown cheese in hot oven.
Serve.
Heat skillet.
Put in oil.
Heat and put in garlic, zucchini, salt and pepper. Cook few minutes until tender.
Great taste.
Combine all ingredients; mix well and pour the mixture into a greased skillet. Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cream
oleo,
powdered sugar and vanilla together.
Add flour, salt and nuts.
Put in refrigerator to chill;
roll in balls. Bake
at 400° until done.
While hot, roll in powdered sugar. Cool.
Roll in plain sugar.
Simmer ham in water until ham loosens from bone.
Discard bone and fat.
Add barley and onion.
Cook until barley is tender, about 1 hour.
Serves 2 as a main course.
Grind the cranberries and add sugar.
Let set overnight in the refrigerator.
Dissolve jello in 1 pint warm water and let set until it gets thick as honey.
Add all cranberries, nuts, celery, marshmallows, apples and pineapple.
Add one big cup of Cool Whip. Put in refrigerator for 2 to 3 hours.
Cream together all moist ingredients.
Sift together and add all dry ingredients.
Shape into small balls.
Dip in sugar. Flatten with fork.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake 15 minutes or until very light brown.
Bake at 350°.
Cream shortening with sugar.
Add beaten egg, then molasses, vinegar and cold water.
Sift flour, soda and ginger and add to first mixture.
Stir in as much of the flour as you can and knead in remainder.
Roll out.
Cut in desired shapes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350°.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Cut in butter.
Add milk to make a soft dough.
Turn onto floured board and roll 1/2 inch thick.
Cut into small squares.
Drop into hot liquid.
Cover closely and cook 20 minutes.
Makes 12.
Mix all ingredients excluding confectioners sugar and bring to a boil.
Stir to prevent sticking.
Remove from heat and add confectioners sugar.
Add about 1/3 at a time, and use an electric mixer for beating.
Add vanilla and continue mixing until mixture is of spreading consistency.
Add chopped nuts if desired.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch cookie pan and preheat oven to 350°. Prepare Toll House cookie dough as directed on package of chocolate chips.
Place 3/4 of dough on bottom of pan.
Mix together cream cheese, sugar and beaten eggs.
Pour over top of dough in pan. Glob on the rest of the dough.
Bake for 30 minutes and touch to see if dough springs back.
May need to bake for 40 minutes.
Mix hot water and yeast until dissolved.
Stir warm water and brown sugar.
Slowly add flour.
Mix until smooth.
Roll dough until smooth and 16-inches for each pretzel.
Twist into shape.
Dice fruit and vegetables. Add other ingredients and chill before serving. Serve with tortilla chips.
Blanch asparagus for three minutes in small saucepan.
Melt butter and stir in flour.
Cook, stirring, for one minute. Gradually add cream or half and half and milk.
Cook until thick. Stir in white wine, cream or chicken broth.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in egg yolk, cheese and shrimp.
Put in buttered casserole dish layered: one half asparagus, then one half shrimp. Repeat layer and top with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Chop walnuts and mix with sugar and spices.
Grease an 11 x 16-inch pan with melted butter.
Place 4 filo in pan, brushing each with melted butter.
Sprinkle with thin layer of nut mixture. Cover with 3 filo, brushing each with melted butter.
Continue this procedure until all filo and mixture is used.
Finish with 4 filo on top, brushing each with butter.
Cut into about 75 small squares (before baking).
Bake in slow oven (300°) for 1 hour or longer, until lightly brown.
Remove from oven and cool.
Pour warm syrup over pastry.
Bake 30 minutes at 350° in 8 x 12-inch pan.
In a 2 quart saucepan, add water, lime Jell-O and cream cheese. Heat on medium heat until cream cheese melts.
After cheese melts, add marshmallows.
Stir until dissolved.
Then refrigerate until its almost firm.
Then add pineapple juice, crushed pineapple and Cool Whip.
Beat until mixture is smooth.
Pour into bowl. Sprinkle chopped nuts on top.
Refrigerate until firm.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Work in butter until it disappears.
Add eggs and vanilla and knead until soft and pliable.
Pinch off piece of dough and roll into length of about 4 to 5-inches, twist and place on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brown lamb and onion.
Add beans, ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar and mustard in a large casserole.
Top with bacon.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients.
Mix well, roll out and cut with "bone" shaped cookie cutter.
Bake at 300° until very hard.
Fido will love these!
Mix together the vanilla wafers and 1/4 cup melted butter and pack into an 8 x 8-inch dessert dish.
Cream the powdered sugar and 1/2 cup butter.
Add eggs and beat 10 minutes.
Beat whipping cream until stiff (could use Cool Whip).
Add drained crushed pineapple and nuts (if desired).
Mix the sugar, butter and egg mixture.
Top with pineapple mixture.
Decorate with vanilla wafer crumbs, whipping cream, cherries and nuts.
Refrigerate for 8 hours.
Combine the first 3 ingredients; sprinkle on both sides of steaks.
Combine egg and milk in a shallow bowl.
Dip steaks in egg mixture, then dredge in cracker crumbs.
Pour oil to depth of 1/2 inch into large, heavy skillet.
Fry steaks in hot oil over medium heat until brown, turning once.
Remove steaks; drain off drippings, reserving 3 tablespoons.
In skillet, add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute.
Add broth and 1/2 cup milk; stir constantly until thick.
Add Worcestershire sauce; stir.
Serve gravy with steaks and cooked rice or mashed potatoes.

Combine cornmeal, milk, salt, bacon drippings, eggs, soda and corn in mixing bowl. Set aside. Saute ground beef in skillet. Drain on paper towels. Grease a large black iron skillet and heat. Sprinkle bottom with a thin layer of cornmeal and brown slightly. Pour half of the batter in hot skillet.
Sprinkle cheese evenly over batter, then sprinkle on the meat, onion and peppers.
Pour remaining batter on top. Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes. Serves 8 to 10.
Serve with a tossed green salad, iced tea and fruit dessert for a complete meal.
Cook hamburger with onion until brown, then drain.
Stir in brown sugar, salt, barbecue sauce and pork and beans and heat through.
Place in casserole.
Separate biscuits and cut in half. Sprinkle with cheese, then arrange over hamburger mixture.
Bake in preheated 425° oven until biscuits are brown.
Place butter and one "plop" of oil in a large kettle.
Cut up onions and saute in kettle.
Add salt as desired and 1 spoon sugar for flavor and browning.
When onions are soft and brown, sprinkle 2 spoonfuls (1 at a time) of flour and mix into onions.
It will be pasty.
Add meat and brown, about 30 minutes.
Add 4 cans of broth and 4 cans of water.
Add 3 to 4 bay leaves and a few sprinkles of red pepper.
Bring mix to a boil.
Cover and reduce heat to simmer for as long as you would like.
Serve in bowls with torn pieces of bread and cheese, letting the cheese melt.
Enjoy!
Mix
1 1/2 cups flour, salt, sugar, sour cream and milk in mixer
at
medium
speed until blended.
Dissolve yeast in warm water
and add it along with the melted margarine to the flour mixture; beat until smooth.
Remove from mixer and beat with spoon, gradually adding the remaining flour.
If dough is too sticky
to
handle, add a little more flour and knead for several minutes.
Place
dough in a large pan in a warm place and let rise until doubled in size.
In a large bowl, combine broccoli, cauliflower, bacon, onion, tomatoes and eggs; set aside.
In another bowl, combine mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar.
Mix until smooth.
Just before serving, pour dressing over salad and toss.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
In a large bowl, stir together the first 5 ingredients until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Toss to coat well.
Cover. Refrigerate at least 2 hours to blend flavors.
Makes about 5 cups.
Peel and slice potatoes.
Just cover with salted water and boil until tender.
*Use less sugar if using sweetened coconut.
Boil tapioca, water and salt for 1/2 hour.
Two hours later, add jello and sugar.
When cool, top with whipped cream and fruit. Mix in marshmallows.
Wash lettuce leaves and stack on four salad plates.
Cut the cantaloupe in half and scoop out the seeds.
Cut each half into half.
Place each piece in the "green sea" of lettuce.
Cut the 2 slices of cheese in half diagonally (from corner to corner).
Use a toothpick and make a sail with the cheese and then "raise the sail" on each "boat".

recipes.t: Walt And Roberta'S Favorite Seven Layer Cookies Or Hello Dollys
d: Melt butter in pan.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs over melted butter, then spread crumbs with chocolate chips, then butterscotch chips.
Sprinkle coconut over this, followed by the milk poured evenly over the coconut and add the chopped pecans on top.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool and cut in 1 1/2-inch squares.
Use a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Yields approximately 3 dozen.
Peel and slice potatoes; layer in baking dish with flour and salt and pepper.
Cover with canned milk.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Salt and pepper lightly.
Spray a 9 x 13-inch pan with Pam. Put bread, sausage and cheese into pan.
Pour egg mixture (beat eggs, 2 1/4 cups milk and mustard) into pan.
Refrigerate overnight.
Blend flour, cinnamon and butter with pastry blender. Sprinkle over apples in a 2-quart baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Serve with ice cream.
For 9-inch pie pan, prepare Dream Whip as on package, using vanilla and cold milk.
When topping peaks with blender, add cream cheese, slowly blending.
Add sugar and blend.
Pour into crust. Chill about 3 hours.
Combine all ingredients. Bake at 250° for 45 minutes.
Brown hamburger in
1 tablespoon fat.
Add other ingredients. Cover and
simmer
for
30	minutes.
Add more tomato juice if it is too dry.
Beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in milk until smooth.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour into crust.
Top with lemon topping. Chill 3 hours.
Refrigerate.
Mix soup, dressing and preserves in bowl.
Put chicken in a 13 x 9-inch loaf pan.
Cover with mixture.
Bake uncovered 45 minutes at 350°.
Combine the first 5 ingredients together.
After combined, place uncooked chicken on top of rice mixture.
Spoon soup over the top of the chicken.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours, or until rice is cooked.
Place drained pineapple in baking dish.
Mix flour with sugar and sprinkle over pineapple.
Cover with cheese and top with crushed Ritz crackers.
Cut margarine into small pieces and place on top of crackers.
Bake at 325° until bubbly.
Make tossed salad.
Cut up egg and cheese in salad or add cottage cheese to salad.
Add dressing.
Serves 1.
Mix bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, green onions, parsley, basil and cloves in a bowl.
Stir in melted margarine.
Brush four 12-inch foil squares lightly with oil.
Place 1 fish steak on each square.
Drizzle with olive oil.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Top with crumbs.
Spoon wine around each steak.
Seal foil securely.
Place packets on baking sheet.
Bake at 450° for 8 minutes or until fish flakes easily.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix all ingredients and chill for 4 hours or overnight.
Serve with assorted raw veggies.
Brown spareribs in heavy skillet.
While ribs are browning, make a sauce from remaining ingredients.
Cook all for 10 minutes. Pour over ribs and cook for 2 hours in a 375° oven.
Remove; cover the last half hour to glaze them.
Mix ingredients together; form into small balls.
Bake in oven at 400° for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake cake as directed on box.
Let cool on wire racks.
Put beans in a large pot.
Add the 2 or better quarts of water and soak overnight.
Next day, drain the beans and add more water, more than cover.
Add the ham bone to the beans and water, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Remove the ham bone from pot and chop the meat and return it to the pot.
Then add onion, potato, celery and garlic.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Be sure there is enough water, cook for another hour.
Prepare rice and limas as labels direct. Drain black-eyed peas. Dice red pepper. In large bowl, mix peas, red pepper, parsley, lemon juice, oil, mustard, sugar and salt. Add rice and limas. Chill.
*Favorite meat is to use
ground
moose,
if not available, use ground beef round.
Venison
is
good to mix in with beef and also you can add ground
pork.
You need a total of 6 pounds of meat with the sauteed onion.
In mixing bowl, beat milk, sour cream and pudding mix until smooth.
Place 1/3 sliced bananas into pastry shell.
Top with 1/2 pudding mixture.
Repeat layers.
Arrange the remaining bananas on top.
Cover with Cool Whip.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Sprinkle chicken with salt.
Spread rice on bottom of greased 3-quart casserole.
Layer with mushrooms, then chicken.
Mix undiluted soups with savory and dry soup mix.
Pour over mixture in casserole.
Pour broth around sides to moisten rice.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° about 1 1/2 hours.
Serves 4 to 6.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Combine egg, milk and oil. Add liquid ingredients to dry ingredients.
Fill greased muffin pan 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Yields 12 muffins.
Coat chicken with flour and salt.
Brown in oil for 10 minutes; remove from pan.
Reserve 1/4 cup pan juice.
In pan, stir honey, teriyaki sauce, chives, pepper and juice; heat to boiling.
Boil for 30 seconds.
Add pineapple; heat again.
Pour sauce over chicken.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix thoroughly meat, rice, 1/3 cup water, onion, salts, garlic powder and pepper.
Shape into well rounded tablespoon sized meatballs; place in ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Stir together remaining ingredients and pour over meatballs.
Cover pan with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 15 minutes longer.
Serve with pasta if desired.
Mix sugar and cinnamon together.
Tear small pieces of dough off, dip in melted butter, then in sugar mixture.
Drop into Bundt cake pan.
Let raise to within 1 inch of top of pan.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Spread each cut side with Ranch dressing. Add cheese and broil until lightly browned. Garnish with parsley.
Prepare cake mix as directed on box.
Bake in 13 x 9-inch pan. When done, remove from oven and prick with fork.
Prepare gelatin as on box, then pour over cake.
Prepare pudding and spread over cake.
Put glaze over pudding.
Put Cool Whip on top.
Slice strawberries and place on top.
Prepare angel food cake according to directions.
Just before baking, add red food coloring and stir into cake.
Bake according to directions.
Combine egg whites, sugar and strawberries in top of double boiler; beat with mixer to mix.
Place over rapidly boiling water; beat constantly with mixer.
Cook 7 minutes, or until mixture stands in peaks.
Remove from boiling water; beat until cool.
Fold in 2/3 cup strawberries.
Spread over cake.
With a sharp knife, cut deep pockets between each rib on meaty side of roast.
Combine green peppers, green onion, celery and garlic; stuff deeply into pockets.
Season roast with salt and cayenne pepper.
Insert meat thermometer.
Place roast, rib side down, in a shallow roasting pan.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 2 to 3 hours or until thermometer reads 170°.
Let stand 15 minutes before carving.
Cream butter, sugar and vanilla in a large mixer bowl.
Add eggs and food color; blend.
Combine flour, cocoa and salt; add alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture.
Stir baking soda into vinegar; fold carefully into batter (do not beat).
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9-inch pans.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes.
Remove from pans.
Cream butter and sugar until light.
Beat in egg yolks.
Sift together dry ingredients and add to butter, sugar, egg mixture alternately with the milk and flavoring.
Beat well.
Carefully fold in egg whites.
Bake in a tube pan or
in 2 loaf pans.
Pans should be greased and floured.
Bake in a 375° oven until done.

recipes.t: Peanut Butter Fudge(Small Batch, Can Be Doubled)
d: Remove from heat and add 1/2 stick butter and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Let cool to 135°.
Add peanut butter.
Mix well.
Pour into buttered dish.
It should be getting stiff as you mix it up. It does not take long to set up.
Beat sugar and Karo well.
Add eggs, one at a time and beat well.
Add butter, vanilla and pecans.
Pour in a 9-inch unbaked pie shell and bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until done.
Brown meat in 1 teaspoon oil.
Add onions and garlic.
Cook until tender.
Add bouillon cube with 1 cup hot water, then add stewed tomatoes and green pepper.
Cook 30 minutes, then add cornstarch and soya sauce.
Cook 5 minutes longer.
Serve over rice.
Put meat in shortening, then add chopped onion and garlic. Next, add the kidney beans, tomato soup and seasonings.
Heat thoroughly.
Just before serving, top with cheese and place under the broiler to melt cheese.
Cook macaroni until tender.
Grate block cheese in bowl.
Mix powdered cheese, milk and eggs together.
Layer macaroni, then cheese alternately in casserole dish.
Pour mixture on top.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cook at 450° for 45 to 50 minutes until golden brown.
Mix all together and cook over medium heat until tender.
If cabbage seems to be quite moist, cut water by 1/2 cup.
Combine lemon juice and rind.
Blend in condensed milk.
Beat egg yolks slightly; blend into mixture.
Pour into cooled pastry shell.
Beat egg whites until foamy; add cream of tartar.
Add sugar, one tablespoon at a time, beating well after each. Continue beating until very stiff peaks form.
Pile lightly on pie filling.
Brown in oven (350°) for 10 minutes.
Serves 6.
Brown beef in 12-inch skillet or Dutch oven.
Drain.
Add chicken, broth, mushrooms, rice, onion, green pepper, barbecue sauce and seasoning; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes or until rice is tender.
Add tomatoes; mix lightly.

Cook rice in boiling salted water until tender. Fry 1/2 cup bacon until crisp. Add onion and green pepper; simmer until onion is soft and yellow. Add tomatoes, sugar, salt and pepper. Pour rice into strainer and rinse with hot running water. Add rice to onions, bacon and green pepper mixture. Mix well and pour into greased casserole dish.
Bake about 30 minutes at 350°.

In a large saucepan, cook the cranberries and 1 1/2 cups water over medium heat until the berries pop, about 15 minutes. Stir in raspberries. Transfer to a blender or food processor; cover and process until smooth. Strain and discard seeds, reserving juice. Pour the juice into a 2-quart freezer-proof container; set aside. In a small
saucepan, sprinkle gelatin over remaining water. Let stand for 1 minute. Stir in sugar.
Cook and stir over medium heat until gelatin and sugar are dissolved. Add to berry juice. Stir in ginger ale; cover and freeze.
Boil chicken.
Debone.
Add 2 cans cream of chicken soup to broth.
Add noodle dumplings.
Cook until tender.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine chicken and celery.
Mix salt, onion, mayonnaise and lemon juice. Mix into chicken.
Split buns.
Place, cut side down, on broiler rack.

In a tall, narrow ware pot (Mexicans call it a jarrow), the beans nestle closely together and pack while cooking and it means the heat seeps gently through the jarrow as it should in cooking beans.
In order that the beans pack right, you should use enough to almost fill the pot when they swell, never less than 2 pounds. Use Mexican pinto beans.
Wash the beans; put them in the pot and fill the pot about half full of water.
Never soak pinto beans.
It causes them to be mushy.
Using a medium flame, bring the water to a boil while stirring the beans to keep them from burning.
When the water boils, turn the fire low so it can barely simmer.
It is best if you see a bubbly oozing out now and then.
Throughout the cooking, keep the water level barely covering the beans.
It makes them pack.
Be sure any water you add is boiling.
After an hour of cooking, add several chunks of salt pork.
Some people put a lid on the beans, but I do not.
It chokes off those fine odors and sometimes it causes the juices to boil over.
At the end of the second hour, cut the garlic fine (I use 6 pods).
At the end of another hour, add the oregano and chili pequins, mashed up (I use jalapeno peppers, 2 small ones, with seeds taken out).
Cook another hour.
At the end of 4 hours of cooking, add salt, one level tablespoon per each pound of beans.
Simmer 1 more hour.

d: Fill 1 gallon glass or plastic jug with sliced cucumbers. Dissolve salt in enough water to cover cucumbers.
Let set for 3 days.
Pour off water, rinse 3 times in cold water.
Soak 24 hours with alum in water to cover.
Pour off and rinse 3 times in cold water.
Cover with white vinegar, let set for 7 days.
Drain vinegar off and throw away.
Rinse 1 time.
Heat 1 cup vinegar and 3 cups sugar until sugar is dissolved.
Cool and pour over cucumbers (will not cover pickles), add pickling spice and turmeric (put spice and turmeric in soft cloth tied up).
Let set for 24 hours.

Usually only large fish are cooked this way, but slices of large fish, such as salmon, pike, halibut or carp are also excellent.

Pour over chicken.

Melt butter in large nonstick skillet over medium high heat. Add carrots and saute until carrots begin to brown slightly, about 8 minutes.
Add apple juice and honey and bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until carrots are tender and liquid is reduced to glaze, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Transfer to bowl.
Sprinkle with green onion tops and serve.
Makes 4 servings.
Sprinkle ribs with salt, pepper and Schilling barbecue spice. Place ribs in broiler pan under broiler for 30 minutes to brown and remove excess fat.
Slice ribs into serving pieces and put in crock-pot.
Add onion and pour in barbecue sauce.
Cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours or on high for 3 to 4 hours.
Mix together the cake mix, oil, eggs and lemon extract. Dissolve the jello in the hot water and add to the cake mix; mix well.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 to 45 minutes.
While hot, prick with toothpick and pour on frosting.
Combine applesauce, sugar, rum, grated orange rind and gingersnaps.
Stir until well mixed.
Chill.
Just before serving, fold in whipped cream and pile into sherbet dishes.
If desired, top with additional cream and nuts.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease 12 muffin pan cups.
In large bowl, combine flour, corn meal, sugar, baking powder, salt and red pepper.
In medium bowl, whisk milk, butter and egg.
Stir into dry ingredients just until combined.
Stir in corn.
Spoon into prepared pans.
Bake 20 minutes.
Unmold and serve warm.
Makes 1 dozen.
Place broccoli in casserole.
Cover with chicken.
Spread mushroom soup, then cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until cheese melts.
If using fresh broccoli, cut into spears.
In a 9-inch pie plate or shallow casserole dish, arrange broccoli and top with chicken.
Combine soup and milk; pour over chicken.
Sprinkle with cheese.

Combine butter and bread crumbs; sprinkle over cheese. Bake at 450° for 15 minutes, or microwave by covering with wax paper and cooking on High for 6 minutes, or until hot, rotating dish halfway through heating.
To prepare pan, line 9 x 13-inch pan with wax paper.
Mix sugar and Jell-O together.
Add boiling water; mix well. Add pineapple and orange juice.
Freeze in plastic 1 gallon container or 1 gallon Ziploc bag.
When ready to serve, add ginger ale.
Mix coffee and sugar together and cool.
Add half and half, milk and vanilla. Pour into Ziploc bags or milk cartons and freeze.
Two hours before serving, remove from freezer.
Serve with spoons at a slushy consistency.
Wash beans.
Cover beans with plenty of water and bring to boil.
Boil 2 minutes, set off burner, cover beans and let set for 1 hour.
Drain off water and rinse beans.
Cover with water and cook beans until tender.
Add onion and all other ingredients. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In large bowl, combine meat,
onion soup mix, eggs, tomato sauce, bread crumbs, water and chopped pepper.
Shape into loaf and place in baking pan.
Bake about 45 minutes or until done.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cook pasta to desired state; drain.
Dice green pepper and onion; add to pasta.
Add cooked and drained sausage.
Microwave pepperoni on a few paper towels for 2 to 3 minutes; pat oil off, then add to pasta.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well. Refrigerate until chilled.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan with margarine.
Add hash brown potatoes (slightly thawed by rinsing with water in colander). Pour 1/4 cup melted butter over potatoes.
Sprinkle with onions. Mix together soup, sour cream and milk.
Pour over potatoes.
Top with cheese.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in saucepan and mix in bread cubes.
Spoon over cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 1 hour.
Mix pudding according to package and cool.
Mix pudding and Cool Whip until creamy.
Layer graham crackers and pudding mixture, keep layering until graham crackers are on top.
Top with icing and chill.
Bake 45 minutes at 425° or until golden brown.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into greased and floured pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into buttered casserole dish. Sprinkle 1/4 cup stuffing mix on top and dot with 1/2 stick margarine.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes, uncovered.
Make pudding. Pour whipped cream (8 ounces) in pudding.
Whip mixture.
Put cream cheese in mixture.
Mix mixture and whip.

recipes.t: The Best And Easiest Peanut Butter Cookies
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients well.
Roll into 1-inch balls and place on slightly greased cookie sheet.
Press each ball with fork.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or just until cookies start to turn brown.
Place broccoli spears on bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Lay chicken pieces on top.
Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice and soup together.
Pour over chicken.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
May also top with potato chip crumbs or buttered bread crumbs.
Pound chicken breasts and put in baking dish.
Puree apricots in blender and add lemon juice.
Pour mixture evenly over chicken. Sprinkle with oregano and garlic powder.
Heat Marsala and butter in saucepan until butter is melted.
Pour over chicken.
Place under broiler approximately 30 minutes until glaze is brown. Serve with rice or rice pilaf and green veggie.
Serves 6.
Drain cherries and pineapple thoroughly.
Heat juice in saucepan and add jello.
Stir until dissolved.
Pour into bowl and add Coke.
Place in fridge until it begins to jell.
Add halved cherries, pineapple, pecan pieces and cream cheese chunks.
Combine and place back in fridge until firm.
Preheat oven to 400°. Warm pie crust in oven about 10 minutes while the oven heats.
Shred cheese and place in mixing bowl. Crumble bacon into bits and add to bowl.
Whip eggs with fork and add to mixture.
Add milk, chives, salt and pepper to cheese mixture.
Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour into crust.
Sprinkle surface with nutmeg.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes before serving. Makes one (9-inch) pie.

recipes.t: Pork Chop And Rice Casserole (Or Chicken)
d: Dredge meat in flour.
Cook in a little shortening until brown. Put in 2-quart or larger baking dish.
Brown pepper, celery and onion.
Put in dish with meat.
Add rice on top, then tomatoes. Bake in 350° oven until tender, about 45 minutes.
Might have to add 1/2 cup water when gets dry.
In large bowl, mix oil, eggs and sugar.
In separate bowl, sift dry ingredients.
Add to mixture.
Stir in apples and nuts. Spread into well-greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Distribute chips onto top of cake.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
For best results, bake at least 2 to 3 days before serving.
Mix (except onion and bacon) and put in baking casserole. Slice onion and put on top.
Put chopped bacon on top.
Bake for 1 hour at 400° to cook bacon and onion.
Reduce heat to 275° and bake, covered, for 2 to 3 hours more.
Spread coconut in a large shallow pan.
Bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes, until golden brown.
Turn into a small pie pan. Cool.
Cube tomatoes into bite size pieces.
Spread tomatoes evenly in a casserole dish.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic salt. Sprinkle bread crumbs over tomatoes.
Sprinkle cheese next.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.

Coarsely crush Oreo cookies to equal one cup. In a large bowl, beat egg yolks, stir in condensed milk and vanilla. Fold in cookies and whipping cream. Pour into an aluminum foil lined 9 x 5 inch loaf pan or other 2 quart container. Cover, freeze 6 hours or until firm. Scoop ice cream from pan or peel off foil and slice. Store in freezer.
Crush garlic with salt in small bowl.
Add crumbled cheese, mayonnaise, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, paprika and pepper; stir until ingredients are well blended and dressing is smooth and creamy.
Chill.
Refrigerate in tightly covered container.
Makes 1 1/2 cups dressing.

Combine first 3 ingredients in a small bowl, stirring well; set aside. Combine mayonnaise, lemon juice and hot sauce, stirring well. Brush mayonnaise mixture evenly over both sides of fillets; dredge in cereal mixture. Place fillets in 9 x 13-inch glass cooking pan coated with cooking spray. Bake at 450° for 18 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork. Serve with lemon wedges. Makes 8 servings.
Cream butter, 3/4 cup sugar and vanilla in mixer bowl.
Add 3 eggs, beating well.
Combine flour, baking powder and baking soda. Add dry ingredients to butter mixture alternately with sour cream.
Combine pumpkin, beaten egg, 1/3 cup sugar and pie spice. Spoon half of batter into 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Spread to corners.
Sprinkle half of Streusel over batter.
Spread pumpkin mixture over Streusel.
Carefully spread remaining batter over pumpkin mixture.
Sprinkle remaining Streusel over top.
Bake in slow oven at 325° for 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix chicken soup and milk; reserve half of the mixture.
Mix remaining soup, rice and 1/4 of the onion soup mix.
Pour into ungreased baking dish.
Place chicken breasts on top. Pour reserved soup mixture over chicken breasts.
Sprinkle with remaining onion soup mix.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer.
Peel and halve peaches.
Lay face down in unbaked pie shell.
Mix coffee cream, sugar, cinnamon and flour together.
Pour over peaches.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes until lightly brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook spinach and drain well.
Melt margarine in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix ingredients in any order.
Pour into pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Let stand for 45 minutes. Cut into squares.
Makes a "hit" served cold at receptions. Serves approximately 35.
Fry meats, celery, garlic and onion.
Add other ingredients. Salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
In saucepan, melt margarine; stir in flour and gradually add milk and some of the cheese to make cheese sauce.
May need to use more flour before milk is added or more milk.
Put cooked macaroni in baking dish; stir in cheese sauce mixture.
Add more cheese to taste.
Mix ground beef, eggs, evaporated milk, bread crumbs, onion, salt and pepper together well.
Form balls.
Brown meat balls in small amount of oil.
Mix together hot water, bouillon cubes, mushroom soup and chicken soup and pour over browned meat balls. Bake in 300° oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Grate 10 ounces sharp Cheddar cheese into a 9 x 13-inch buttered Pyrex dish.
Sprinkle 5 tablespoons of finely chopped jalapeno peppers on top.
Grate 8 to 10 ounces Monterey Jack cheese on top of peppers.
Press down.
Pour 6 to 7 beaten eggs onto cheese.
Bake 45 minutes at 325° or until set and golden. Cut into 1-inch squares.
Place pie crust into pyrex pie plate and cook as directed on package.
Cool.
Mix instant chocolate pudding as directed using 1 cup less milk for each box.

When well blended, pour into cooled pie shell. When pie filling is set, spread Cool Whip on top of filling, shave Hershey bar into curls. Sprinkle chocolate curls on top of Cool Whip topping--then sprinkle walnuts on top also.
Simmer ingredients for 5 minutes.
Pour over chicken pieces and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Pour cherry filling in bottom of casserole dish.
Sprinkle cake mix on top.
Pour melted butter next.
Top with pecans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream together butter and sugars, add egg and mix well.
Add remaining ingredients one at a time except pecans.
Mix until combined; stir in pecans.
Form into balls the size of walnuts; place on ungreased cookie sheet and flatten with a fork.
Bake at 325° for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly brown; do not overcook. Allow to cool a few minutes before removing from pan.
Yield: 6 dozen.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water; add cold water and ice cubes.
Cool until partially set.
Stir in all remaining ingredients and pour into molds; chill until set.
Makes 2 large jello molds.
Preheat oven to 250°.
Place crackers in large shallow baking pan.
In a small bowl, combine butter, taco seasoning mix, Worcestershire and salt.
Pour butter mixture over crackers; stir well.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Pour onto waxed paper to cool.
Store in airtight container.
Yields 6 cups snack mix.
Mix Oreo cookies and margarine.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Spread ice cream on top of cookies.
Sprinkle on peanuts and freeze for several hours.
Melt chips and stir in sugar, margarine and evaporated milk.
Bring to a boil.
Boil for 10 minutes.
Cool completely.
Spread cooled fudge on peanuts and freeze.
Put egg, butter, bananas, sugar and granola into blender. Whirl on low until smooth.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Add blender mixture and stir until moistened.
Turn into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 325° for 60 minutes.
Yields one loaf.
Cover squash and onion with water and butter and bring to boil.
Cook approximately 5 minutes, until tender.
Drain.
Melt Velveeta cheese.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Pour over squash. Makes 4 servings.
Flour deer after salting and
peppering.
Fry
in oil to brown.
Meanwhile place a large
skillet
or
pot
on
another burner.
Depending on amount you
cook,
put water in pot.
For one package of deer to feed 4, use about 2 cups of water.
When meat is browned, drop directly
into
water
that is simmering. Do not drain on paper.
Continue
until
all
meat
is browned. Cook onions in oil until tender.
Drain off most of oil.
Brown small amount of flour and brown.
Add
all
this to water.
Add soup. Simmer, adding water if necessary.
In
large
mixing
bowl
stir together dry ingredients. Make well
in
center;
drain pineapple, pressing out liquid. Reserve 1/3 cup syrup.
Add remaining ingredients.	Beat with wooden spoon.
Pour into 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan, greased. Sprinkle with walnuts and brown sugar.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and serve cold.
Keep refrigerated.
Add water as directed on lemonade. Mix together and serve.
Combine salad dressing mix, oil, dill weed and garlic.
Pour over oyster crackers; stir to coat.
Place in warm oven 15 to 20 minutes.
Store in tight container.
Cream together the sugars and margarine.
Combine with remaining ingredients and mix well.
Roll in balls the size of a small walnut.
Place 2 inches apart on greased cookie sheet. Press with the bottom of a glass, dipped in sugar.
Sprinkle sugar generously on top of each cookie.
Bake at 350° about 10 minutes. Makes 100 cookies.
Soak gelatin in the pineapple juice and dissolve over hot water.
Add to pineapple and cream cheese mixture.
Fill green peppers and set in refrigerator to harden.
With a very sharp knife, cut the stuffed peppers crosswise into thin slices.
Serve on lettuce with mayonnaise.
Remove foil from Kisses.
In a large bowl, combine butter, sugars and vanilla. Beat well. Add flour; blend until smooth. Stir in chips. Mold scant tablespoon of dough around each Kiss, covering completely.
Shape into ball and place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until set.
Cool.
Remove from cookie sheet.
Makes 6 to 7 dozen cookies.
Drizzle topping over each cookie (optional).
Dissolve
jello
in
one
cup
hot
water and pineapple juice. Melt
cranberry
sauce
in
saucepan on low heat until smooth and
mushy.
Mix
with all other ingredients and chill until thickened
and then add diced apple.
Spoon into 8-inch square dish,
sprayed with Pam or salad oil for easy removal. Chill until
firm.
Cut
in squares and serve on lettuce with mayonnaise or Cool Whip.
Serves 8.
Cream sugar and butter together.
Add remaining ingredients. Mix together thoroughly.
Add egg whites which are beaten.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes.
Mix ingredients and form in balls; put in Pyrex pan close together.
In blender, mix Jell-O and water.
Add juice, vinegar and milk.
Add cream cheese, one piece at a time.
Add carrots and pineapple.
Pour in 2-quart mold and chill.
Melt oleo, add brown sugar and pretzels.
Spread in a 13 x 9 inch pan.
Bake in 350 degree oven until bubbly (3-5 minutes). Combine cream cheese and white sugar, beat smooth.
Add in 1/2 cool whip, mix.
Spread over cooled pretzels.
Dissolve jello in 1 1/2 c. boiling water, add strawberries.
Mix well, cool.
Pour over cream cheese layer and chill.
Top with remaining cool whip.
Rub steak with garlic; sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
Cut meat crosswise into 4 to 6 serving pieces.
In large skillet, cook bacon.
Drain bacon; reserve 2 tablespoons drippings in skillet.
Place slice of bacon on each piece of meat, roll up and secure with wooden picks.
Coat rolls with flour.
Brown rolls in the reserved bacon drippings over medium heat.
Combine Cool Whip and milk in a large bowl.
Refrigerate one hour.
Add remaining ingredients and stir well.
Then refrigerate overnight.
Mix pulp, sweetener and egg.
Add dry ingredients and a little of the milk.
Blend well.
Add rest of milk and butter.
Bake 55 minutes at 325°.
Chop chocolate coarsely.
Combine with oleo or butter and boiling water in a large saucepan.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until chocolate is melted.
Add sugar and corn syrup. Heat slowly to boiling, lower heat and simmer gently 8 minutes. Watch carefully but do not stir.
Test for thickness on ice cube. Add vanilla.
Refrigerate leftover sauce in screw top jar.
Reheat in warm water (in jar) until soft enough to pour.
Makes 2 1/2 cups.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, cook the beef until browned, stirring to separate meat. Spoon off fat. Stir in soup, water, Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Heat through,
stirring occasionally. Serve on buns.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all the ingredients in a large pot.
Boil it on the stove until the mixture becomes thick and the egg yolks have evaporated and there is no lumps.
Let this mixture cool for approximately 30 minutes.
Put mixture into a ice cream maker until it freezes.
Cook ground beef and then drain.
Pour ground beef in pan (8 x 10-inch).
Stir tomato soup in with the ground beef.
Pour green beans (drained) and then mashed potatoes until it covers the ground beef.
Pour shredded cheese over it.
Heat oven to 350° until cheese melts.
Mix baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and olive spice in small bowl; set aside.
Mix remaining ingredients in large bowl; pour in baking dish.
Sprinkle cinnamon, baking soda, nutmeg, cloves and olive spice over top of cake.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Peel and mash avocado in bowl with lemon juice and salt. Combine sour cream and mayonnaise with taco seasoning in another bowl.
(I use 1/2 of the package of taco seasoning in the sour cream mixture and 1/2 in the refried beans.)
Melt butter in a large skillet.
Add onion and saute until soft.
Add cabbage to skillet.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in caraway seed, salt and pepper.
Combine the first five ingredients.
Place chops in a glass baking dish and pour marinade over.
Cover and refrigerate 3 to 6 hours or overnight.
To cook, remove chops from marinade and grill or broil 4-inches from the heat to desired doneness. Brush occasionally with the marinade.
Serves 6.
Heat oven to 450 degrees.
Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup; level off.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, cinnamon and baking soda.
Using pastry blender or fork, cut in shortening until mixture resembles course crumbs; stir in raisins.
Stirring with fork, add buttermilk until mixture leaves sides of bowl and soft dough forms.
Turn dough onto floured surface and knead lightly until no longer sticky.
Roll out 1/2
inch thick and cut with floured 2 1/2 inch cutter.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet with sides touching.
Bake at 450 degrees for 10 to 15 minutes or until light golden brown.
Cool 5 minutes on wire rack and frost. Serve immediately.
Prepare Rice-A-Roni mix as package directs.
Remove sausage from casing and crumble.
In 12-inch skillet, brown sausage and onion; drain, reserving 1 tablespoon drippings in skillet.
Set aside.
Add zucchini and garlic; saute over medium-high heat 1 minute.
Cover, continue cooking over low heat about 2 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Combine prepared Rice-A-Roni, sausage mixture, 1 1/2 cups spaghetti sauce and basil; spread into 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with 1 cup cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes, or until heated through.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Heat 2 cups of water to boiling, pour over jello in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Mix in cherry pie filling and the crushed pineapple.
Let this mixture jell.
Pick meat from chicken (no skin).
Mix all ingredients, then tear up the bread like for dressing.
Stir all together.
Add enough broth to make all real moist, a cup or more if needed. Pour in large casserole dish or pan and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Add meat, onion, celery and salt to 6 to 7 quarts boiling water.
Boil on medium about one hour.
Add potatoes, carrots, bouillon and hot pepper to taste.
When beef is well done, add tomatoes. Simmer 30 minutes.
Layer the first 5 ingredients.
Sprinkle with sugar, cheese, salt and garlic powder.
Just before serving, add bacon or bacon bits.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Can be made the day before needed.
Shred cabbage (food processor or hand grater) and put into pot with 2 quarts water or broth.
Add the remaining ingredients after the cabbage shrinks down enough to make room for the rest.
Boil on medium-low for a few hours.
Yum!
Melt butter in large skillet; add broccoli and onion.
Cook until broccoli is thawed.
Cut cheese into 1 square.
Mix cheese, soup, milk and rice in large bowl.
Add broccoli.
Mix and bake in oven at 350° for about 30 minutes or until cheese is melted and rice is done.
Fry meat and drain.
Add crunched chips and Tabasco; mix together.
Mix other ingredients in bowl; let meat cool and mix with salad.
Cream together margarine, sugar, egg and molasses until mixture is smooth.
Combine dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture; mix well.
Stir in chopped pecans.
Cover the cabbage with 1-quart boiling water.
Add the salt; boil 5 minutes, drain dry.
In the melted oleo, add flour and stir well.
Add milk and cook until thickens a little.
Put cabbage in baking dish.
Add cheese to sauce and stir until melted.
Pour over the cabbage and cover with buttered crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Mix chocolate cake mix as directed on box.
Bake in two 13 x 9-inch pans for 20 minutes at 350°.
While cake is baking, mix in large bowl 1 cup Pet milk and 1 cup sugar.
Bring to rapid boil and remove from heat.
Add marshmallows; stir until melted.
Add coconut.
Pour over hot cakes; cover completely.
In a saucepan heat to a rapid boil 1 1/2 cups sugar, 1/2 cup Pet milk and margarine.
Remove from heat; add chocolate chips and stir until melted.
Pour over cakes to completely cover.
Sprinkle with toasted coconut if desired.
Cook cabbage and onion together until cabbage is almost done. Cook noodles; drain.
Mix noodles with cabbage, onion and sour cream.
Mix half of the cheese into mixture.
Put in baking dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese and then with bread crumbs.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Dip chicken breasts in yogurt.
Roll in mixture of bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Place in baking dish.
Place tinfoil lightly over dish.
Bake at 350° for approximately 45 to 50 minutes.
Soak sliced cucumbers in lime water for 24 hours, stirring often.
Rinse in cold water until cucumbers are lime free.
Water will be clear.
Combine cucumbers and onions in salted water.
Let stand for 3 hours and then drain.
In a large kettle, combine vinegar and remaining ingredients; bring to a boil.
Add vegetables and heat to simmering.
Avoid boiling the vegetables for this will make them soft.
Pack while hot in sterilized jars and seal.
Makes 3 quarts.
Spray 9 x 13 inch baking dish.
Cut bread into 1-inch-thick slices; arrange closely in single layer in prepared pan.
In large bowl beat eggs, whisk in milk, 3 Tbsp. of sugar, vanilla and salt; pour over bread.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour or over night.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Sprinkle bread with cinnamon, if desired.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes or until golden brown. Remove from oven; sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Slice strawberries place in bowl.
Add lemon zest, juice, and remaining 1 Tbsp. sugar, mix lightly.
Serve over warm French toast.
Yields:
8 servings.
Spray pot with Pam. Combine all ingredients. Stir once. Cook on low 3 1/2 to 4 hours.

Combine cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla in small mixer bowl until blended. Add cocoa alternately with milk, beating until smooth. Fold in topping until combined. Spoon into pie shell and chill until firm or freeze.

recipes.t: Pasta With Vegetables And Goat Cheese
d: Combine broth, wine, shallots and black pepper in large saucepan.

Bring to a boil, add broccoli, breaking florets apart. Add squash and mushrooms, reduce heat, cover and simmer 5 minutes. Add cream cheese, goat cheese and lemon juice, cook on low heat, stirring constantly until cheeses are melted.
Set aside, keeping warm.
Cook pasta according to package directions, drain.
Place in large serving bowl, add vegetable/cheese mixture, toss gently. Garnish with red pepper strips.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Combine dry ingredients and add to butter mixture; mix well.
Add eggs, bananas and pecans. Add 1 tablespoon vanilla (optional).
Grease a loaf pan.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°, then 30 minutes at 325°.
Combine first 5 ingredients
in
a large pitcher.
Fill pitcher with ice and
water.
Serve immediately in salt-rimmed glasses.
In heavy saucepan, cook bacon until crisp.
Drain off all but 2 tablespoons bacon drippings from pan.
Crumble bacon; set aside. Sprinkle both sides of beef with lemon pepper marinade.
Brown beef in bacon drippings.
Combine mushroom soup, dill pickle and Worcestershire sauce; pour over browned meat.
Cover; simmer for about 2 1/2 hours, or until meat is tender.
Remove to warm platter.
Sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Skim fat from gravy; serve with roast.
Cook carrots in small amount of water for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender.
Drain well.
Combine onions, green pepper and carrots in large bowl.
Mix well.
Mix remaining ingredients in second bowl.
Pour over carrot mixture.
Marinate 24 hours in refrigerator.
Place croutons in greased 9 x 13-inch metal pan.
Put grated cheese over croutons.
Brown sausage and place on top of cheese. Beat eggs and mix with soup, mustard, milk and mushrooms.
Pour over sausage.
Bake, covered, with foil in 300°
oven for 1 1/2 hours.
This recipe may be prepared the night before and refrigerated.
Serves 10.
Season pork chops and brown.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add flour and mix well.
Slowly add milk.
Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Alternately place potatoes, onions, pork chops and cream sauce in greased casserole.
Cover.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover last 15 minutes.
Serves 6.
*Bake 1/2 hour at 350°. Cool. Cut into bite size pieces.
Gently add all ingredients to peas.
Refrigerate before serving.
Heat oven to 325°.
Sift the first 5 ingredients together in a mixing bowl.
Make a well; add Wesson oil, egg yolks, water and maple flavoring.
Beat until smooth with spoon or mixer on medium speed.

Add cream of tartar to egg whites in large mixing bowl. Beat until whites are very stiff, then pour egg yolk mixture gradually over beaten egg whites, gently folding with rubber scraper, just until blended.
Pour into ungreased 10 x 14-inch tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 55 minutes, then at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Turn pan upside down on bottle until cold.
Mix salad dressing and ginger together. Add to other ingredients. Serve on lettuce with muffins.
It's delicious.
In a 6-quart saucepan, in hot oil, brown roast on all sides. Spoon off fat.
Stir in mushroom soup, onion soup mix and 1 cup water.
Reduce heat to low; cover and cook for 2 hours.
Add vegetables.
Cover; cook for 45 minutes, or until roast and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove roast and vegetables.
Stir together flour and remaining 1/4 cup water until smooth. Gradually stir into soup mixture.
Cook until mixture boils and thickens, stirring constantly.
Garnish with fresh parsley, if desired.
Makes 8 servings.
Mix confectioners sugar and granulated sugar together.
Heat oven to 325°.
Cream butter and sugars together.
Gradually add the rice and unbleached flour.
Mix with hands until smooth; do not overmix.
Press into baking pan or shortbread mold.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Slice cucumbers, onions and peppers very thin.
Salt overnight, covered with water.
Drain, then cook with remaining ingredients.
Let stand in hot vinegar for a few hours, then reheat and can.
Mix first 7 ingredients.
Add peanut butter (the kind with oil on top).
Mix again.
Add M&M's and chocolate chips, mix well; then add uncooked oatmeal.
Drop by teaspoon.
Bake at 350° on greased cookie sheet.
Boil macaroni according to package directions.
Melt 3/4 stick of butter until slightly burned.
Put in macaroni; mix with some Romano cheese.
Wash peppers; remove tops.
Finely grind peppers and onions; drain.
In large saucepan, combine peppers and onions; cover with boiling water.
Let stand 5 minutes; drain.
To pepper mixture add sugar, vinegar, salt, dill seed and 1/2 cup water.
Boil gently, uncovered, 5 minutes.
Pack into hot half pint jars, leaving 1/2 inch headspace.
Adjust lids.
Process in boiling water bath 5 minutes.
(Start timing when water returns to boiling.)
Makes 10 half pints.
Beat brown sugar, oil or applesauce, egg, milk and banana until well blended.
Stir in flour, baking powder and salt all at once.
Fold in cereal, dates and nuts.
Spoon batter into paper-lined 4-inch muffin tins until 2/3 full.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes at 375°.
Serve warm or cold.
Dissolve jello in boiling water, turn heat to simmer, add marshmallows and dissolve.
Add drained pineapple.
Cool.
Whip milk and cream cheese in large bowl, add cold jello mixture.
mix well.
Pour into greased mold and refrigerate.
Top with whipped cream in mold pattern if desired.
Mix together cocoa and sugar.
Add dash of salt and the water. Bring to boil.
Stir in milk and vanilla.
Remove from heat. Serves 8.
Combine all ingredients but cereal and melt in top of double boiler.
Add cereal, mixing quickly.
Spread in buttered 8-inch square pan.
Chill; cut in 1/2-inch squares.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Wrap individually in waxed paper.
Mix well. Cover. Chill.
Brown onions, bell pepper and beef in large skillet.
Add tomatoes, basil, rice, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Pour into casserole dish and cover with slices of American cheese.
Heat in oven at 350° until cheese melts.
Serve hot.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Drain. Combine all ingredients.
Mix together and cook on low until cheese is thoroughly melted.
Beat cream cheese, 1 tablespoon milk and sugar in medium bowl using wire whisk until smooth.
Stir in lemon peel and juice. Stir in 1 1/2 cups of the whipped topping.
Spread evenly in bottom of crust.
Press strawberry halves into cream cheese layer, reserving several for garnish, if desired.

Mix vegetable/seasoning packet from Stove top Dressing, with hot water, and margarine in large bowl until margarine is melted. Stir in stuffing crumbs just till moistened. Let stand 5 minutes. Mix turkey and green beans in 2 qt. casserole dish. Mix soup and milk in another bowl until smooth; pour over turkey mixture. Spoon stuffing evenly over top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated. Makes 6 servings. Easy and delicious!
Combine the vinegar, the juice from the peaches, sugar, cinnamon and cloves.
Boil until reduced by about half.
Remove the spices.
Stick the cloves into the peach halves and pour the syrup over peaches.
Let stand overnight in the refrigerator.
Cook water and cornstarch (stirring constantly until thick). Remove from heat and let stand until cold.
Add sugar, vanilla and margarine.
Beat with electric mixer until smooth.
Spread on cool cake.

recipes.t: Champignons Bordelaise Mushrooms With A Bordelaise Garnish
d: Rinse the
mushrooms
in cold water and drain well.
If the mushrooms are large, slice them or cut them in half.
In a heavy skillet, heat
the	oil.
When
the
oil is hot, add the mushrooms and
salt and pepper to taste.
Cook over high heat, shaking the skillet
and
stirring so that the mushrooms cook evenly until they
are quite brown and crisp.
They should be almost mahogany colored.
Pour
the mushrooms and cooking oil into strainer
or sieve to drain.
To skillet, add the butter. When
melted,	add mushrooms.	Sprinkle
quickly
with
bread crumbs, shallots and parsley.
Toss and serve.
Serves 4.
Mix crackers and margarine.
Press 2/3 cup of cracker mixture in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Prepare pudding with 2 cups milk; add softened ice cream and blend until smooth.
Pour over crust. Put in the freezer until set.
Remove and spread Cool Whip on the top.
Sprinkle remaining cracker crumbs on top and crushed Butterfinger bars.
In 1-quart casserole, blend soup and milk.
Stir in tuna, egg and peas.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 25 minutes. Top with potato chips, etc. and bake 5 minutes longer.
Makes 3 to 5 servings.
Mix dates in hot water.
Set aside.
Cream oleo and sugar. Add eggs; beat until fluffy.
Sift flour, salt and soda.
Add alternately with date mixture to egg mixture.
Mix well each time. Stir in vanilla and 1/2 cup chocolate chips.
Spread in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with remaining chips and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Drain pineapple well, reserving two tablespoons syrup. Combine softened cream cheese, vanilla and reserved syrup, mixing until well blended.
Stir in 1/4 cup pineapple and 1/2 cup pie filling.
Gradually add sugar to cream, beating until soft peaks form.
Fold into creamed cheese mixture.
Pour into crust.
Top with remaining pineapple and pie filling.
Chill until firm.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In bowl, stir together flour, sugar, cocoa, brown sugar, baking soda and salt.
Cut in margarine until crumbly; add eggs.
Mix well.
Spread in greased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Bake 8 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Top evenly with chips, then sweetened condensed milk and coconut.
Return to oven; bake 20 minutes or until lightly brown.
Remove from oven.
Let cool.
Cut into bars.
Let chicken pieces or steak marinate in this mixture for 6 to 8 hours.
Excellent on the grill.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Blend cream cheese and margarine.
Add chicken, salt, pepper, milk, chives and pimento.
Separate crescent rolls into 4 rectangles; seal perforations.
Spoon 1/2 cup mixture onto center of each rectangle.
Pull 4 corners of dough up to center of mixture and seal.
Brush tops with melted margarine; dip in crushed croutons.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Boil noodles according to package directions.
Drain.
Add drained tuna, soup, a little butter and some milk.
Peas may be added if desired.
Mix well.
Bake in greased casserole at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cream
sugar
and
shortening.	Beat in eggs.
Dissolve soda in	sour milk; add alternately with the flour and baking powder that
has
been sifted together. Stir in vanilla, nuts and	mashed bananas.
Drop
by
spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake in 350° oven 10 to 15 minutes.
Yield: 4 dozen.
Sift flour, soda, salt, cream, 1 cup sugar and shortening. Add eggs; mix well.
Add apples, milk and vanilla.
Mix well. Pour into greased loaf pan.
Combine remaining sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle over batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Note:
Buttermilk can be replaced with 1/2 cup whole milk mixed with 1 tablespoon vinegar.
Mix first 3 ingredients and put into baking dish.
Add the remaining ingredients in the order given.
Bake in 400° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Combine the milk, shortening, sugar and salt.
Cool to lukewarm.
Add yeast which has been dissolved in lukewarm water; add about 2/3 of the flour and beat thoroughly.
Let rise until double; add remaining flour.
Knead well.
Let rise again until double.
Roll dough 1/4 inch thick.
Cut with a 3-inch biscuit cutter.
Brush rounds with melted butter.
Grease thoroughly center with dull edge of knife.
Fold double, pinch edges together and place on well-greased pan, one inch apart.
Allow to rise until double in size.
Brush tops with melted butter.
Bake in hot oven (425°) for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 30 rolls.
Mix dry cake mix, eggs and oil.
Add raisins, nuts or coconut. Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix beaten eggs, sugar and syrup. Add melted butter, vanilla and chopped pecans. Pour into uncooked pie crust. Bake for 20 to 35 minutes at 325°.
Mix cracker crumbs and 1 stick melted margarine.
Press into 13 x 9-inch pan. In mixing bowl, cream eggs, 2 sticks margarine (melted), powdered sugar and vanilla.
Beat with mixer 15 minutes, no less.
Spread over crumbs.
Slice bananas thin, and layer pineapple.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with pecans and cherries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Melt butter and chocolate chips together.
Add powdered sugar. Pour a little milk at a time.
Heat on stove.
Will not get real thick until after it cools.
Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat.
Add beef and onion and cook until brown.
Stir in chili powder and salt.
Cook 1 minute longer.
Add tomatoes, beans and corn.
Cook over high heat until bubbling.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Prepare potatoes as directed on package.
Stir in cheese and cilantro.
Top mixture with 1/2 cup of potatoes and enjoy.
Weigh 7 pounds pickles and put them in salt water that will float an egg.
Let them stand 3 days, then 4th day change to clear water for 3 days, changing the water daily.
Cut pickles in chunks, put them in weak vinegar.
Add a teaspoon of alum to every quart of water to cover them, and let them stand a day.
Make a syrup out of 3 parts water and 3 parts vinegar, 1 tablespoon each cinnamon, cloves and allspice, 1 teaspoon celery seed and 1 tablespoon mustard seed.
Put all spices in a thin cloth and boil it in your syrup for a while.
Then fill your cans and pour the syrup over them and seal cans.

Cut cabbage up like slaw. Set in bowl aside. Saute pan sausage. Drain grease from sausage. Add stewed tomatoes and let simmer for while. Add cabbage a little at a time. Then let all simmer until cabbage is cooked down. May add a cup or two of water if needed.
Spread crushed pretzels on bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Melt margarine or butter with 2 tablespoons sugar and pour over pretzels.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cool.
May want to use tomato juice.

Preheat oven to 450 degrees. Cut four 20-inch long pieces of foil. Divide and layer tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, peppers and potatoes on each foil piece. Place chicken breast on top of vegetables. Mix Worcestershire sauce and pepper in a small bowl. Spoon over each breast. Top with 1 teaspoon margarine and 1 teaspoon honey. Seal packets by bringing opposite sides of foil together and fold over several times. Fold over the other two ends of foil tightly. Pierce top of foil twice with knife to vent. Arrange packets on baking sheet. Bake for about 35 minutes. Can be assembled ahead and refrigerated for up to two days. A great do-ahead main dish for a week-end bar-b-que. Can be grilled as well. Place foil side down about 4-6 inches from heat source for about 15 minutes. Serves four.
Melt butter.
Add rest of ingredients; stir.
Brush top and bottom of bun.
Stack with ham and cheese.
Wrap in foil.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix vinegar and soda and set aside.
Cream sugar and shortening; add eggs.
Add a little food coloring to cocoa to make a paste.
Add to creamed mixture with rest of coloring.
Add flour and salt, alternating with milk.
Add vanilla, then vinegar and soda.
Beat well.
Use 2 (8-inch) round pans (greased and floured).
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
When cooked, split to make 4 layers.
Dissolve jello in boiling water and let cool. Add strawberries, pineapple, cranberry sauce and pecans. Put into a 12 x 8 x 2-inch pan or mold sprayed with cooking spray. Chill until firm.
Add salt and pepper to meat.
Toss all ingredients together and serve.
Leftovers taste good too, only not crunchy.
Mix first 4 ingredients and place in 8-inch glass dish.
Then mix last of ingredients until crumbly.
Sprinkle crumb mixture over top of apples.
Microwave on High for 12 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Can serve with ice cream or whipped topping.
Mix ingredients and top with dressing.
Combine sugar and water. Boil 3 minutes. Cool.
Mash bananas. Add to fruit juices and stir in sugar syrup.
Pour into containers and freeze. When ready to serve, thaw slightly.
Pour carbonated beverage over mixture.
Parboil cabbage to loosen leaves.
Mix meat, rice, onion, egg, salt and pepper.
Roll balls in cabbage leaves.
Place in pan and pour mixture of soup, sauce, vinegar and sugar over.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
To make meatballs:
Combine all ingredients (mixture will be soft).
Shape into walnut size meatballs.
Place meatballs in a single layer on wax paper lined cookie sheets.
Freeze until solid.
Store frozen meatballs in freezer bags until ready to cook.
Makes approximately 80 meatballs.
These are good for something rather quick.
Takes approximately 1 hour baking time.
Boil all ingredients, except honey, for about 3 minutes. Strain through cloth to remove all seeds and lemon rind.
Mix well with honey.
Take one warm tablespoon at a time at 1/2 hour intervals.
In a skillet, brown beef in the vegetable oil.
When browned, add the flour and stir until flour starts to brown.
Add water and stir.
Add the hot sauce, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Stir well.
Bring to a boil.
Now add the carrots, onions, peppers and tomatoes if desired.
If the sauce seems too thin at this point, you can thicken it with a bit of rue which is flour that you have heated in just a slight bit of vegetable oil or you can add just a touch of cornstarch.
Once the vegetables have been added, bring to a boil once again, then cover and simmer until vegetables are tender.
The longer it simmers the better it will taste.
It is great served over noodles or over rice.
Cook potatoes with skins on until just firm.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cook onion, celery and pepper.
Add ketchup, sugar and vinegar.
Warm, then add to meatballs.
Add onion, catsup and dressing into blender or food processor. Add softened cream cheese into mixture and blend until mixed. Refrigerate for a few hours.
In saucepan, mix sugar and flour; whip eggs and add to juices. Cook until it thickens.
Add the macaroni and all the fruit to 3/4 container Cool Whip.
Cool 2 hour.
Saute onion in oil in 2-quart boiler.
Add rice, salt and chili powder.
Pour in broth plus enough water to make 16 ounces liquid.
Bring to
boil and then cover and simmer until rice is done.
Brown hamburger, onion and celery in skillet; drain fat.
Pour hamburger into baking dish, 2 1/2-quart dish.
Add 3 cups boiling water, rice and dry vegetable soup.
Cook 1 hour at 350°.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Roll into balls.
Put into 9 x 13-inch pan or baking dish.
Mix other ingredients and pour over meatballs.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until juice is cooked up.
Blend cheese with margarine.
Stir flour with salt and paprika and mix well.
Wrap 1 tablespoon of mix around each olive. Completely cover the olive.
Freeze in a plastic bag.
To serve, place frozen puffs on ungreased cookie sheet and bake in 400° oven for 10 to 15 minutes until golden.
Olives will be quite hot. Serve on toothpicks.
Mix
milk and lemon juice; add other ingredients.
Pour in crusts.
Chill for 4 hours.
Cream the cream cheese with the sugar.
Add milk and mix well.
Combine with the thawed topping.
Remove the brown crumbs from angel food cake.
Break or cut the cake into small pieces. Mix cake with the creamed mixture.
Combine cherry pie filling with almond flavoring.
Swirl into cake mixture.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch dish or serve from a pretty crystal bowl.
Cream sugar and margarine.
Add eggs one at a time.
Add chocolate syrup, nuts and flour.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix together cake mix, oleo, egg and vanilla.
Put into a greased
and
floured 9 x 13-inch metal pan.
Cream together cream cheese, powdered sugar, eggs, pecans and vanilla.	Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Gather polk greens in spring of year.
Look and wash well. Parboil greens; rinse.
Boil again.
Put 2 tablespoons of soda in water, rinse well.
Squeeze out all the water you can.
Put greens and cut up onion in skillet with fair amount of Crisco.
Cook until onion is translucent.
I like to scramble 3 or 4 eggs, then mix with cooked greens.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Sprinkle cheese in pie crust.
Whisk eggs until frothy.
Add other ingredients and mix.
Pour over cheese.
Bake at 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake an additional 15 to 20 minutes or until center is set.
Mix.
Spread over mix.
Top with remainder of Cool Whip before serving.
Refrigerate.
In a 2-quart saucepan over high heat, bring to boiling soup mix, rice and water.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 25 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in green onions, if used.
Yields 4 servings.
Make cake as directed on box; add poppy seed to cake mix. Stir and bake as directed.
Poke holes in cake and add in holes caramel syrup.
Top with Cool Whip and crushed up candy bars.
Heat 3 to 4-inches of oil to 375° in deep fryer.
Measure 1 1/2 cups flour and the remaining ingredients in a large bowl. Blend 1/2 minute on low speed, scraping bowl occasionally.
Stir in remaining flour. Turn dough onto well floured surface. Roll around lightly to coat with flour.
Gently roll dough 3/8-inch thick.
Cut with floured doughnut cutter. With wide spatula, slide doughnuts into hot fryer. Turn doughnuts as they rise to surface. Fry 2 to 3 minutes or until golden brown. Carefully remove from oil.
Drain.
Serve plain, sugared or frosted. Makes 2 dozen.
Parboil eggplant; drain.
Saute onion, celery and shrimp in butter in skillet.
Add tomato.
Cook to desired consistency.
Add salt, pepper, Tabasco sauce, Worcestershire sauce and bay leaf. Add eggplant.
Spoon into 4 x 7-inch baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Yields 8 servings.
Combine eggs, half and half and cheese.
Cook ham slice and cut into small cubes.
Add to mixture.
Add parsley and garlic powder. Mix well.
Pour into pie crust.
Bake at 375° for approximately 1 hour.
When done, middle should be raised and browned lightly. Cover pie crust edge with foil to keep from overbrowning.
Slice zucchini.
Roll in flour, then roll in milk/egg mixture. Roll in bread crumb/Bay seasoning mixture.
Let set 1 hour before frying in canola oil.
Layer ingredients, starting with lettuce and ending with bacon.
Put meat in roaster.
Add onion soup mix; sprinkle on.
Add potatoes, onions and carrots.
Mix together cream of celery soup, water and catsup.
Pour over stew.
Bake, covered, for 2 to 3 hours.
Combine ingredients; serve with veggies.
Especially good with raw cauliflower.
Dissolve jello in water.
Put in blender or food processor. Add cheese in 1-inch cubes.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in berries and nuts.
Pour into mold.
As jello begins to thicken, stir to distribute fruit and nuts evenly.
Mix together flour, salt, pepper and other seasonings with corn meal.
Fry in hot oil until brown.
Mix first 3 ingredients and bring them to a boil.
Brown the 1/3 cup sugar; add to first mixture while cooking to soft ball stage.
Drop on oil paper.
Slice the meat diagonally against the grain into 1/8-inch strips.
Heat a large nonstick or regular skillet (use 1 tablespoon of oil) and brown the steak quickly over high heat. Push aside.

Fry sausage; drain and crumble into a greased 9 x 13-inch casserole dish. Sprinkle cheese over sausage. Mix well the remaining ingredients; pour over sausage mixture. Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes, until set and browned on top. Cool 5 minutes before slicing.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl; chill.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap.
Combine all ingredients, beating well until spreading consistency.
Place 1/4 teaspoon frosting on each warm cookie.
Mix all ingredients.
Drop by teaspoon into hot cooking oil. Cook until golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Makes 24.
Cook macaroni as directed.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese, set aside.
Combine milk, eggs, salt and pepper, swish lightly until smooth.
Mix as for drop cookies.
Bake in greased 9 x 13-inch pan for 30 minutes or until done. Frost with chocolate frosting.
Slice each hot dog in half lengthwise.
In small bowl, crumble onion rings.
Reserve 2 tablespoons for topping.
Combine potatoes, butter, crumbled onions, salt and pepper in shallow 1 1/2-quart casserole dish and blend well.
Combine soup and milk in small bowl.
Pour 3/4 soup mixture over potato mixture and blend. Arrange hot dogs, cut side down, on top of potatoes.
Sprinkle with reserved crumbs.
Pour remaining soup mixture over onions. Bake 25 minutes at 375°.
Serves 4.
Combine butter, evaporated milk, sugar and salt in medium, heavy saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Boil for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Bring first 4 ingredients to a full boil.
Boil 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add vanilla and beat until thick.
Saute onions in butter until golden.
Separate into rings, if desired.
Add pepper rings and cook until tender.
Combine ingredients in a 2-quart shallow casserole and toss lightly. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or until vegetables are tender, stirring once.
Add chopped onion to mashed potatoes.
Form into patties. Brush with butter.
Fry in butter greased frying pan until golden on each side.
Brown meat and onion; drain and set aside.
Mix soups, Ro-Tel and chili powder together.
