Place Doritos in a casserole dish. Put meat and onion on top of that.
Pour mixture on top of meat. Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly and serve.
Toss chicken in your favorite coating.
Melt 1/2 cup butter in roasting pan.
Roll chicken in butter.
Arrange in pan skin side down.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Melt 1/4 cup butter with honey and lemon juice.
Turn chicken skin side up and drizzle with honey mixture.
Bake another 30 to 40 minutes, basting occasionally.
Serve with steamed rice.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place almonds in shallow pan and bake until golden brown (8 to 10 minutes).
Let cool.
Reduce oven to 300°.
In small bowl, whisk together the eggs, vanilla and extract. In mixing bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking soda and salt. Add egg mixture and mix until blended, about 1 minute.
Cut almonds in half and mix in.
Divide dough in half.
On greased and floured baking sheet, pat out dough into 2 logs, about 1/2-inch high, 1 1/2-inches wide and 12-inches long, spacing them about 2 inches apart.
Bake at 300° for 40 to 50 minutes or until golden brown. Transfer to wire rack.
Cool 5 minutes.

recipes.t: Ground Beef Ragout(With Pate Grand-Pere - Dumplings)
d: Cook beef in margarine.
Add onion, salt and pepper.
Brown, stirring often.
Add other ingredients, mix, cover, and let simmer.
Prepare dumplings (pate grand-pere).
Brown pork chops on both sides in hot fat.
Place apple slices in greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with butter or margarine. Top with browned chops, Cover. Bake in 400° oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Serves 3 to 4.
Brown ground beef; cook macaroni.
Mix all but pizza sauce and mozzarella cheese together.
Place in a 9 x 13 pan, pour pizza sauce over the top, then sprinkle the mozzarella cheese over the pizza sauce.
Bake 350° for 30 minutes.
Cover with foil until the last 10 minutes.
A can of mushrooms can be added to the meat mixture if desired.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix margarine, sugar and vanilla.
Add flour gradually and mix well.
Chill dough.
Form into 1-inch balls and place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until set, not brown.
Roll in confectioners sugar while warm.
Combine cranberry juice cocktail and concentrate.
Stir well; chill.
Just before serving, pour into a 4 quart punch bowl.
Add scoops of sherbet.
Slowly add ginger ale.
Makes about 50 (1/2 cup or 4 ounce) servings.
Cook shells for 14 minutes; drain.
Mix everything else together and add to drained shells.
Pour into greased baking dish.
Bake about 1 hour at 350°.
Simmer first 4 ingredients.
Mix 1 cup into eggs.
Mix back into pan.
Stir over low heat 5 minutes to thicken.
Strain and chill.
Add nutmeg, if desired.
Bring water to a boil.
Add cubes, garlic powder and pepper. Next, add onion, celery, carrots and cabbage.
Boil gently until vegetables are tender.
Add tomatoes; boil gently until all is heated and serve.
In greased baking dish or 2-quart casserole, alternate layers of potatoes, peppers and onion.
Combine remaining ingredients. Pour over.
Cover; bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20 to 30 minutes longer or until potatoes are tender.
Serves 8.
Brown meat in hot oil in skillet then transfer to slow cooker.
Add sauce, green pepper, and onion. Cover and cook on high heat for 4 to 5 hours or until tender. Slice and serve with sauce.
Cook cauliflower in salted water according to package.
Drain. Arrange in a buttered 1-quart casserole.
Drain beans, reserving 1/2 cup liquid.
Add drained beans to casserole.
Melt butter in small saucepan.
Stir in flour.
Add reserved 1/2 cup liquid, milk, onion, salt and hot sauce.
Cook and stir over medium-low heat until sauce thickens.
Pour over vegetables in casserole. Garnish with pimento.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs; beat.
Add remaining ingredients except nutmeats.
Beat thoroughly.
Fold in nutmeats. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Brown and drain meat.
Add spaghetti sauce, onions and green pepper.
Add enough spaghetti sauce to make thinner than usual. Cook slowly until well blended.
Combine grated Mozzarella cheese with cottage cheese and Egg Beaters.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan spread a thin layer of the meat mixture, then the uncooked lasagna noodles.
Top with meat mixture and a layer of cheese mixture. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Continue layering and end with Parmesan cheese topping.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown meat and onion; drain fat.
Add rest of ingredients, except wonton skins.
Put mixture each skin.
Fold in triangle. Wet edges with cold water to seal.
Fry in 1-inch hot oil until golden brown, 30 to 60 seconds.
Drain on paper towel.
Freeze if you wish.
In a large heavy Dutch oven, melt the butter. Mix in flour until smooth.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly, over medium heat.
Blend in the hot chicken broth with wire whip.
Add the cheese and stir until blended.
Pour in whipping cream. Incorporate well.
Add Worcestershire and beer.
Cook over low heat, stirring until thick and smooth, 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve with croutons, bits of ham, freeze dried chives or a sprinkling of parsley.
Mix
together
all ingredients and pour into pie crusts. Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Brown meat and onion.
Drain fat and run hot tap water over meat.
Using a colander makes this easy.
Combine meat mixture, soups and corn; heat thoroughly.
Add noodles and it's ready to serve.
Mix ingredients in the order given, pour into an oiled 2 qt. casserole dish and bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes.
Top with the additional buttered crumbs and bake 20 minutes longer or until center is firm.
Combine juice and water in medium saucepan; bring to a boil. Add rice and cinnamon stick.
Cover.
Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes or until liquid is absorbed.
Yields 3 cups.
Blend first four ingredients thoroughly.
Divide into 24 equal parts and form into balls.
Place a ball into each of 24 miniature muffin pans.
Press thumb into each ball to make a shell.
Beat with a fork the next 4 ingredients until blended.
Place a few ground nuts in each shell and pour filling over each.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Process cottage cheese in a blender until smooth.
Press spinach between paper towels until almost dry.
Put cottage cheese, spinach and remaining ingredients into a bowl.
Blend well, folding ingredients together.
Cover and refrigerate 3 hours.
Yields 3 cups.
Has 14 calories and a trace of fat per tablespoon.
Cream together sugar and butter. Blend in remaining ingredients.
Pour batter into a buttered and floured angel food tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Mix together and chill for about an hour and roll into balls. Leave on a plate or cookie sheet in refrigerator for easy snacking.
Place gelatine, pudding and sugar in saucepan; stir in 1/2 cup water and the eggs.
Blend well. Add remaining water; stir over medium heat until mixture comes to full boil.
Remove from heat and stir in rum.
Chill thoroughly.
Fold Cool Whip into chilled mixture and spoon into graham cracker or chocolate crust.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine all ingredients and pour into baking dish.
Cook for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 250°; continue baking for 2 to 3 hours.
Remove from oven long enough to sprinkle top with 6 strips of bacon cut in strips.
Allow to cook 1 hour or until bacon curls and is crisp.
Beat
egg
yolks; add 1 cup syrup from pineapple, sugar and flour.
Cook until thick.
Arrange in layers in bowl with a
layer of pineapple, a layer of marshmallows, grated cheese, then sauce. Repeat.
Serve at room temperature.
Serves 6.
Soak bread in milk; mix with other ingredients and cook 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Serve hot.
Mix cheese, mayonnaise and mustard until melted.
Pour over cooked cauliflower.
Mix ingredients together and put tiny Tater Tots on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add molasses and egg.
Beat until smooth.
Stir together flour, baking soda and ginger.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk.
Drop by teaspoonful onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake until lightly browned, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and mix well in casserole dish.
Put grated cheese on top or you can use canned onions.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes.
Roll the zwieback into fine crumbs and mix with the melted butter or margarine and 1/2 cup of the sugar.
Pack all but 1/2 cup of this mixture on the bottom and sides of a well-greased 9-inch pan.
In medium saucepan, over low heat, melt chocolate chips and butter, stirring constantly, until blended.
Remove from heat; cool 5 minutes.
Stir in marshmallows and 1 cup nuts; do not melt marshmallows.
Mix and place in microwave.
Bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes on High.
Add 1/2 teaspoon baking soda.
Pour half popcorn in a brown paper bag and pour half the syrup over it.
Add remaining popcorn and syrup.	Fold top of bag and shake well or gently stir with large, long handled spoon.
Microwave 1 1/2 minutes on High. Take out and shake well.
Cook another 1 1/2 minutes on High. Remove and shake well.
Spread on cookie sheets to cool.
Wash escarole thoroughly and boil down.
Saute minced garlic in olive oil in frypan.
Cut up cooked escarole some before simmering with garlic.
(This can be done ahead of time.)
Salt while cooking.
Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt and fat.
Drain; rinse with cold water and drain again.
Drain pineapple, reserving 2 tablespoons juice.
Combine pasta, pineapple chunks, cantaloupe and grapes in a medium bowl.
Cover and chill.
Combine yogurt and reserved 2 tablespoons pineapple juice in a small bowl, stirring well.
Cover yogurt mixture and chill.

Slowly brown ground beef with chopped onion and smashed garlic clove. Drain and put in large pan with soups, tomato paste, herbs, salt, pepper and 2 to 3 cups of water. Add more chopped onion and garlic. Slice cabbage thinly and add along with carrots and green pepper. Simmer for about 1/2 hour. Leave skin on potatoes, cut into quarters and add to soup along with macaroni; simmer for another 1/2 hour. You will need to add water once in awhile as the soup cooks.
Mix thawed and drained broccoli, onion, green peppers and cheese in a greased 10 inch pie plate.
Beat remaining ingredients until smooth, about one minute with hand beater. Pour into pie plate.
Bake until golden brown, about 35-40 minutes at 400°.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting.

Spread half of the crushed wafers in the bottom of a greased 8 inch square pan. Prepare pudding mix according to package directions, spoon hot pudding over the wafers. Slice one banana; place over pudding. Top with remaining crumbs. Chill for one hour. Meanwhile, prepare gelatin according to package directions; chill for 30 minutes or until partially set. Pour over crumbs. Slice the remaining banana and place over gelatin. Spread whipped topping over all. Chill for at least 2 hours. Serves: 9.
Pick carefully through the crab for pieces of shell. Blend the cream cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and mayo until smooth. Fold in the crab.
Spread in a 9-inch Pyrex pie plate.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes until browned and bubbly.
Serve over crackers.
In a 4-quart saucepan, place potatoes.
Add water to cover potatoes.
Over high heat, heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to medium.
Cook 8 minutes or until potatoes are fork-tender.
Drain in colander.

Combine all ingredients, except crackers. Pour into baking dish. Crumble 1 roll of crackers and mix with 1/2 cup melted butter or margarine. Sprinkle generously on top of vegetables. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes until brown.
Mix hash browns, onion and margarine together, then add 2 cans water. Cook 20 minutes. Add remaining ingredients.
Heat to simmer.
Place chicken breasts in oblong pan.
Mix together soups and water.
Heat.
Pour over chicken.
Top with cheese and stuffing mix.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Pat topping down into soup mixture.
Bake 15 minutes more.
Scrub potatoes and dry.
Pierce with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Remove from oven.
Cool to handle.
Cut in half lengthwise; remove pulp to bowl carefully; keep skin whole.
Mash pulp with cottage cheese, salt and pepper.
Scoop mixture back into skins.
Sprinkle with paprika and parsley and bake 20 minutes more.
In saucepan, combine brown sugar, corn syrup, butter, cream of tartar and salt.
Bring to boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Bring to hard ball stage, 260°.
Remove from heat; stir in baking soda, stirring quickly.
Pour over freshly popped corn in large pan.
Bake 1 hour at 200°.
Stir occasionally.
Turn onto waxed paper and break apart.

Saute onion, carrot and celery in olive oil for 15 to 20 minutes. Add meat, cook and crumble. Add white wine to mixture and continue to cook (with lid on loosely) for 1 to 1 1/2 hours. Add tomato sauce, salt to taste and basil. Lightly cover and cook for several hours more. Serve with pasta.
Mix all ingredients.
Serve with boiled shrimp.
Make cream sauce with the first 8 ingredients; when thick add cheese.
Mix in well-drained hominy and undrained chilies.
Pour into buttered casserole.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake, uncovered, 30 minutes at 350°.
Let cream cheese stand to room temperature.
Beat until fluffy and blend in sour cream, salt and sugar.
Fold in fruit, nuts and marshmallows.
Pour into loaf pan or jello mold.
Freeze overnight or 6 hours.

Preheat oven to 350°. Sift flour, baking soda and salt onto waxed paper. Cream margarine and brown sugar with electric mixer at medium speed in large bowl until fluffy. Beat in eggs, 1 at a time, until fluffy. Stir in vanilla. Add flour mixture, 1/3 at a time, until well blended. Stir in rolled oats, rice cereal and walnuts. Drop by teaspoonfuls, about 1-inch apart, onto large cookie sheets, lightly sprayed with nonstick cooking spray. Bake 10 minutes or until cookies are firm and lightly golden. Remove to wire racks; cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In hot oven, melt margarine in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Remove from oven.
Stir in crumbs; spread evenly in bottom of pan.
Pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over crumbs.
Sprinkle with a layer of peanut butter flavored pieces, layer of chocolate pieces and then peanuts.
Press peanuts gently into mixture.
Bake 25 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Chill at least 1 hour before cutting bars.
Makes 36 bars.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Peel potatoes; cut crosswise into 1-inch slices.
Place in pot; cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat slightly; cook for 15 to 20 minutes, or until tender.
Drain.
Peel bananas; cut in half once lengthwise and cut twice crosswise.
Toss with lemon juice.
Place cooked potatoes and bananas in a shallow roasting pan.
Sprinkle with brown sugar, nutmeg and salt.
Drizzle with rum and melted butter.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and puree potatoes, bananas and liquid in a food processor until fairly smooth, leaving a bit of texture.
Pour into an ovenproof casserole and cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serves 10 to 12.
Beat egg white until foamy; brush over bottom and side of pastry.
In small bowl, combine flour and sugars; cut butter into mixture until it resembles fine crumbs.
Sprinkle 2/3 of mixture in bottom of crust; top with peaches.
Sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes or until filling is bubbly and peaches are tender.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients, except shrimp, only using a sprinkle of cayenne pepper.
Rinse shrimp in cold water and drain; fold into mixture of other ingredients.
Mix flour, baking soda and salt and set aside.
Cream butter until fluffy and beat in sugar, egg and vanilla.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Shape into 2-inch balls.
Place 3 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or until lightly brown.
Let cookies remain on sheet until they are firm.
Makes 21 (4-inch) cookies.
(For softer cookies, add an additional 1/2 cup flour.)
Cook margarine, water, peanut butter and vegetable oil until it comes to a boil, then add flour, sugar, milk, eggs, vanilla and soda.
Grease and flour pans.
Bake on 18 x 13-inch cookie sheets. Makes 2.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Meatballs:
Mix hamburger, milk, soup mix and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce together by hand.
Form into meatballs and place on broiler pan.
Broil 12 to 15 minutes (or until done).
Stir together flour, 1/4 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon cocoa powder and baking powder.
Add milk, oil and vanilla. Stir until smooth. Stir in nuts. Transfer batter to a 1-quart casserole. Combine the 1/3 cup sugar and remaining cocoa powder. Gradually stir in boiling water.
Pour evenly over batter.
Bake in a 350° oven about 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean. Serve warm.
Makes 4 servings.
Heat oil in heavy saucepan.
Add onions and garlic; cook 5 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add other ingredients. Simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours, uncovered, stirring occasionally.
Melt margarine and chocolate drops and cool the mixture.
Add the nuts and marshmallows.
Mix and form 4 to 6 logs from the mixture.
Roll in coconut on waxed paper or foil and put in freezer until firm, slice thin.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
In skillet, saute onions and butter.
Set aside.
Mix eggs and milk until well blended.
Add corn and meal mix.
Spread butter into prepared pan.
Spoon sauteed onions over top.
Spread sour cream over onions.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 35 minutes.
Let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Serve warm.
Place chopped apple in an 8-inch square pan coated with cooking spray.
Combine cranberry sauce and orange juice, stirring well.
Spoon cranberry sauce mixture evenly over apple.
Combine oats, flour and brown sugar; cut in margarine with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Sprinkle oat mixture evenly over cranberry mixture.
Coat oat mixture with cooking spray.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes or until apple is tender.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Bottom:
Mix together flour, oleo and nuts.
Pat firmly in bottom of pan and bake at 375° until slightly brown.
Blend margarine and peanut butter.
Stir in brown sugar.
Sift together flour, baking powder, salt and granulated sugar into mixture.
Add 3/4 cup milk and vanilla extract.
Mix until flour is dampened.
Then beat two minutes on electric mixer or 300 strokes by hand.
Add eggs and remaining milk.
Mix, then beat one minute longer or 150 strokes by hand. Bake in moderate oven (375°) for 25 to 30 minutes before removing.
Pour boiling water over mushrooms and let stand 2 minutes; drain.
On 4 skewers alternately thread mushrooms and zucchini. Combine Italian dressing and Worcestershire sauce.
Grill kabobs over medium coals about 12 minutes turning and brushing often with salad dressing mixture.
Thread cherry tomatoes on end of skewers and grill 5 to 10 minutes more until heated through, turning and brushing often with salad dressing mixture.
Yield: 4 servings.
Drain hominy.
Place in 2-quart casserole dish.
Heat soup (undiluted).
Add Cheez Whiz and let melt.
Pour over hominy. Sprinkle chips on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Cut cabbage into 6 wedges, removing core; place in large saucepan.
Add onion, sugar, salt, bay leaf and water.
Bring to boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Add vinegar and apple; cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes or until apple is tender.
Use a heavy pan with cover, heat oil and add uncooked rice. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until rice is browned. Add onion, bell peppers, garlic and ground beef.
Cook and stir frequently until meat is brown.
Add seasoning, soup and water. Cover tightly and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, for about 40 minutes or until rice and meat are tender and liquid is absorbed.
If needed, add more water during cooking.
Blend cake mix, pudding mix, water, eggs and oil in bowl. Beat for 4 minutes.
Stir in coconut and nuts.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch layer pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cool in pans 15 minutes.
Remove and cool on rack.
Cut small French rolls into slices and mound mixture of remaining ingredients onto each slice.
Place under broiler until puffy and slightly browned.
Combine cheese, mushrooms, onions and mayonnaise.
Spread about 2 teaspoons of the mixture on each toast round.
Place pepperoni slice on top.
Place on baking sheet.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes until cheese melts.
Serve immediately, or keep warm in 250° oven.
Sprinkle chicken with salt, pepper and paprika.
In skillet, brown chicken in 4 tablespoons of the butter and transfer to a 2-quart casserole.
Arrange artichoke hearts between chicken pieces.
Heat oven to 375°.
Sprinkle ribs with lemon juice.
Cook for 1/2 hour.
While cooking, combine rest of ingredients.
Bring to boil, then remove.
Pour over ribs and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour (until tender).

Mix together first 6 ingredients and spread on muffin halves. Bake at 350° to 400° until golden brown. Better if baked on wire cookie rack placed in a lipped pan to catch excess margarine. May be frozen up to 3 months before baking.
Pour boiling water over 6 frankfurters.
Cover; let stand 8 minutes.
Slit each frank lengthwise.
Spread with mustard. Combine 2 cups well-seasoned mashed potatoes, minced onion, chopped pimento and chopped parsley.
Spread over split frank. Brown in broiler or oven.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° until done.
Cream shortening and sugars.
Blend in eggs and vanilla.
Sift flour, salt and soda.
Fold into creamed mixture along with the oats, nuts and raisins.
Roll into small balls and place on cookie sheet.
Flatten with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden.
Yields approximately 10 dozen cookies.
Mix Cool Whip and cottage cheese.
Sprinkle orange jello over it and mix well.
Mix pineapple with oranges and add 1/2 box of pudding.
Mix with the mixture of Cool Whip and cottage cheese. Refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight.
In a large bowl, combine sour cream, minced chives, lemon juice, salt, pepper and hot sauce.
Peel and thinly slice cucumbers.
Add and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Mix in large mixing bowl; add to cooled thickened jello.
Pour in molds and let set.
Layer the first 4 ingredients in order in buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat remaining ingredients together and pour over bread in pan.
Cover in refrigerator overnight.
In the morning, make a topping of 2 cups crushed cornflakes and 1/2 cup melted butter. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Beat together cheese and milk.
Add onions and everything but almonds.
Stir well.
Put in 8 x 8-inch glass pan.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Top with toasted almonds.
Serve with crackers.
May be doubled.
Brown bacon, add onion and simmer until tender.
Drain 1 can of beans, add to bacon and onion.
Then add second can with most of the liquid.
Add mushroom soup and simmer until hot.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly spray cookie sheet with cooking spray.
In a large bowl mix flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
In a separate bowl whisk together shortening, applesauce, granulated sugar, egg and vanilla until shortening breaks into pea-sized pieces.
Add flour mixture to applesauce mixture.
Mix well.
Fold in oats and raisins.
Drop rounded teaspoonfuls onto a cookie sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool on a cookie sheet for 5 minutes.
Remove and put on cooling rack.
Makes 36 cookies.
Line angel food tube pan with heavy brown paper (a grocery sack will do). Spray with vegetable cooking spray.
Unroll the crescent rolls and spread on a large greased cookie sheet.
Pat them together into a single piece and bake 10 minutes at 350° so they are brown on top.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake in greased 9 x 9-inch pan at 350° until top browns and sides pull away from pan.
Serve hot or cold, with whipped cream or plain.
Brown onion in butter.
Add flour and then milk.
Add egg yolks and sauce to potatoes; mix well, then fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake in a greased dish in oven about 25 or 30 minutes at 350°.
Place apples in shallow casserole dish.
Cream butter with sugar.
Gradually work in cheese and flour.
Spread over apples and bake at 350° about 30 minutes until top begins to brown.
Grate dried beef.
Mix all ingredients together.
Roll cheese ball in extra grated dried beef.
Blend margarine and cream cheese.
Add sugar, beat well until mixed.
Add eggs 1 at a time, blending until smooth; add vanilla. Sift flour, salt and baking powder 3 times.
Add flour alternately with milk.
Mix smooth after each addition.
Pour into greased and floured 10 x 4-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° about 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Mix well and keep refrigerated in a covered container.
Makes about 2 cups sauce.
Spoon over piping hot hamburgers.
Melt together cream cheese and soup.
(Do not add water to soup.
Put in as is and melt with cheese over medium heat until smooth.)
Mix gelatine with 3 tablespoonfuls of water.
Add to soup mixture.
Add soup mixture with the rest of the ingredients in a bowl.
Refrigerate overnight (or at least a few hours).
Make cake as directed.
When done, blend together cream of coconut and Eagle Brand milk.
While cake is still hot, poke holes in top and pour liquid over cake.
Top with Cool Whip and coconut. Refrigerate.
Drain artichoke hearts well.
Chop artichokes in food processor until smooth.
Add mayonnaise, cheese and garlic; mix well.
Pour into small casserole; bake for 1/2 hour at 350°. Serve with Triscuits or Melba thins.
Mix baking mix, milk and cheese together and drop by tablespoonfuls onto a lightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes at 450°.
Melt butter and add garlic powder.
Brush over warm biscuits.
Bake angel food cake as directed.
When cool, break cake in pieces and place in baking dish.
Cream sugar, cream cheese, and condensed milk together.
Fold in cool whip with electric mixer. Pour this mixture over cake pieces then add pie filling.
Combine the cake mix, cocoa, sugar, oil and cake coloring. Add the eggs and buttermilk.
Mix as any other cake mix in 3 thin layers.
Cook the flour and milk to a thick pudding.
Place in box to cool.
Cream the oleo, Crisco, 1 cup sugar and vanilla. Beat in the pudding mixture and spread on cake. Sprinkle with coconut.
Boil chicken until tender.
Remove from bone and cut into bite size pieces.
Grease 9 x 13-inch dish with margarine.
Sprinkle crushed chips in dish.
Add other ingredients in order listed. Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 20 minutes more.
Cook asparagus in water until tender.
Whip asparagus in blender until smooth.
Saute onions in margarine.
Stir in flour and cook until bubbly.
Add milk gradually, stirring until thickened.
Stir in asparagus puree.
Add chopped parsley and salt to taste.
Do not boil.
Let rise for 30 minutes and knead; cut out with biscuit cutter.
Dip in melted butter; let rise.
Bake at 450° until brown.
Cook first three ingredients for 5 minutes until sugar has dissolved.
Add marshmallow cream and peanut butter.
Mix well. Place in buttered platter to cool.
Mix altogether and serve over cooked steak.
Put some dill and garlic bud or sliced onions in bottom of jar and fill with unpeeled, sliced (not too thin) or make spears of cucumbers.
Add rest of dill and more garlic or onion on top. Fill jars with liquid that has been heated to dissolve sugar. Seal and cold pack just until water begins to boil.
Yields approximately 4 quarts.
Put potatoes, onion, water and oleo in covered dish and microwave 10 to 12 minutes, stir occasionally.
In large bowl, combine milk, flour and pepper (shake flour and little milk to dissolve).
Microwave 6 to 7 minutes, stir often.
Pour over potatoes.
Add ham and cheese, microwave 2 to 3 minutes to melt cheese.
Sift flour with soda and salt; cream butter.
Gradually add sugar; mix well.
Add eggs and bananas.
Blend; add milk and lemon juice.
Add flour mixture and nuts.
Put in a bread pan and cook at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain pineapple and set juice side.
Mix flour and sugar.
Add reserved juice, stirring well.
Beat egg and add to mixture.
Stir in pineapple.
Pour into casserole dish.
Top with bread cube. Pour melted oleo over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
About 1 1/2 hours before serving or day ahead:
Preheat oven to 400°.
In large open roasting pan, arrange chicken pieces, skin side up.
Place carrots and prunes around chicken.
In small bowl, mix brown sugar, lemon juice, white wine vinegar, salt, flour, oregano and pepper until blended.
Pour over chicken.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes, basting chicken frequently with liquid in pan, until chicken is fork-tender.
Arrange chicken, carrots and prunes on large platter or in bowl.
Skim fat from juice in roasting pan; pour pan juices over chicken mixture.
Serve warm or cover and refrigerate to reheat later.
Makes 8 main dish servings, about 335 calories per serving.
Mix all together and boil.
Pour into hot canning jars, already cleaned and prepared.
Seal jars.
Let first 4 ingredients stand 3 hours. Drain. Add sugar and vinegar; refrigerate.
Cream butter and shortening with sugar.
Add molasses.
Add soda to boiling water and add to creamed mixture.
Sift flour with spices and salt.
Add small amount at a time to creamed mixture and work in well.
Work well with hands and knead dough well.
Cover and store in a cold place overnight and longer if you don't want to bake all at one time.
Roll to infinite thinness on board.
(Board should be covered with cloth stretched tight and tacked on edges of board.)
Flour board (cloth) evenly before rolling out cookies. Bake on a greased cookie sheet in 375° oven for a few minutes or just until they begin to brown.
Place peanut butter, cream cheese and honey in mixing bowl. Stir until well blended.
Trim crust from bread.
Cut into animal shapes using cookie cutters.
Spread peanut butter on half the bread animals.
Top with a matching bread animal.
May be covered and refrigerated until ready to serve.
Place flower tips from broccoli and cauliflower in large bowl. Add cheese, bacon and onion.
Stir up.
In separate bowl, mix Miracle Whip, Green Goddess dressing, sugar and vinegar.
Mix until smooth.
Pour over vegetables.
Stir until fully mixed and coated.
Melt butter or margarine in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir in vinegar and dill seed.
Good on green beans and whole kernel corn.
Yield:
1/4 cup.
Do not drain any of the ingredients.
Just pour in crock-pot. Mix all of the ingredients together and cook on low for about 6 hours or let simmer on low on top of stove for 2 hours.
Pepper, salt and add hot sauce to taste.
Melt butter in a skillet; add onion and rice.
Brown, stirring continuously.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in water.
Combine all in a baking dish; add mushrooms, salt and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Grind berries.
Add sugar and let stand overnight.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot water.
Add 1/2 cup cold water.
Mix all together.
Put in dish; let set in refrigerator overnight.
Add 1/2 envelope gelatin.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill.
Serve on little pieces of bread.
Mix well and serve cold or with ice cubes.
Mix together cream cheese and taco sauce with mixer.
Onto 2 plates, spread lettuce, tomatoes and onions.
Add taco dip on top of lettuce, tomatoes and onions.
Spread 1 package of shredded Colby cheese over entire plate.
Serve with taco chips or your choice of chip.
Preheat oven to 425°.
In a large bowl with hand, knead all ingredients until blended.
Mix first 8 ingredients and form into loaf.
Combine Worcestershire sauce and catsup.
Lightly score top and spread catsup over top.
Roast in covered pan at 350° for 60 to 75 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, except cucumber, mixing until well blended.
Stir in cucumber.
Chill several hours or overnight. Serve with chips or as a vegetable dip.
Yields 1 2/3 cups.
Drain beans and bean sprouts; mix with onion and garlic.
Mix salad oil, sugar and vinegar together and pour over beans.
Let marinate for 24 hours in refrigerator.
Cream
butter
and powdered sugar.
Work flour, vanilla and nuts
into creamed mixture.
Form into small crescents or balls. Bake on ungreased sheet in oven at 350° for 30 minutes or
until lightly browned.
Roll tarts in powdered sugar while still warm.
Cream together eggs and oil.
Add dry ingredients.
Blend in vanilla, butter extract, pineapple, carrots and pecans.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Puree together carrots, melted margarine and milk.
Mix together sugar, eggs, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and baking powder. Add pureed carrot mixture to rest of ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 to 1 hour until crispy.
Use a large covered casserole.
Combine all ingredients into the casserole.
Cover and bake 4 hours at 250 degrees.
Do not brown meat beforehand.
Optional - frozen peas.
In crock pot may cook longer until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Cook whole squash in boiling water until tender; drain.
Cut in half lengthwise; scoop out pulp. Reserve pulp and shell.
Mash pulp.
Melt butter over low heat and blend in flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt and dash of pepper.
Remove from heat.
Stir in milk gradually.
Return to heat. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce is thick.

Fill 6 quart Dutch oven with water. Add 1 Tbsp. salt. Bring water to a boil; add Brussels sprouts. Reduce heat to medium. Cook 12 minutes, until crisp and tender. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking. In large non-stick pan, over medium heat, cook bacon for 5 minutes until slightly crisp. Pour off fat. Add onion to bacon in skillet and cook for 5 minutes or until tender. Add sprouts, remaining salt and pepper. Heat thoroughly. Add vinegar and butter, stirring to melt butter.
Using palm of hand, flatten chicken to even thickness.
Dip chicken into egg, then into crumbs to coat.
In skillet over medium heat in hot margarine, brown chicken on both sides.
Add sauce.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheeses.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Parboil the eggplant whole.
Let cool and cut in half lengthwise.
Scoop inside out, leaving about 1/2-inch around side and bottom.
Chop the pulp.
Saute onion, butter, parsley flakes and garlic powder until wilted.
Add shrimp and cook 3 minutes more.
Add eggplant pulp and 3/4 cup bread crumbs and shrimp and ingredients.
Cook on low heat until done, 5 to 10 minutes.
Fill hull and sprinkle rest of bread crumbs on top.
Add a strip of bacon on each one.
Bake in oven until bacon is done and bread crumbs are toasted.
Combine flour, salt, soda and cinnamon; set aside.
Combine eggs, sugar and oil in mixing bowl.
Mix well.
Stir in carrots and pineapple.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Pour batter into 2 greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until done.
Yields 2 loaves or makes 5 miniature loaves.
Combine broth and lentils, onion, uncooked rice, wine and seasonings.
Shred 1/2 ounce cheese and stir into ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole dish and bake, covered, at 350° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until lentils and rice are done, stirring twice.
Cut remaining cheese into strips and uncover casserole.
Top with cheese strips.
Bake an additional 2 to 3 minutes more until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.
Trim spinach; tear in small pieces and refrigerate.
Sprinkle strawberries with 1 teaspoon of sugar or artificial sweetener and refrigerate.
Shake meat with seasoned flour in plastic bag.
Brown meat in shortening in Dutch oven or stew pot.
Add soup and water; cover. Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cover.
Cook 1 hour or until vegetables are tender.
Stir occasionally to thicken.
Uncover and cook to desired consistency.
Serves 5.
Peel potatoes and cut into pieces. Cover with water.
Bring to a boil and boil 20 minutes or until tender. Drain potatoes and mash. Beat egg, cream, salt, sugar and spices together, then beat into mashed potatoes. Whip until fluffy.
Heat oven to 350°. Butter a 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Pile whipped potatoes in baking dish.
Press marshmallows lightly into potato mixture. Bake, uncovered, about 30 minutes or until marshmallows are melted and browned.
Makes 6 servings.

Boil the beef starting on high heat until it comes to a boil. Lower the heat to medium and cook the beef approximately 30 minutes. Add vegetables, stewed tomatoes and V-8 juice. Bring to a boil then lower heat to medium. Cook for approximately 30 minutes, then simmer on low heat until beef is tender but not overcooked. Salt and pepper to taste.

Cook sausage and drain. Mix sausage and eggs together. Put in a shallow baking dish. Pour soup over the top. top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. This can be made the night before and baked in the morning.
*I use my homemade spaghetti sauce with the spices.
Cut kernels of corn off cobs with sharp knife.
Scrape each ear with knife to remove all of corn and milk from each ear.
Melt butter in heavy saucepan or heavy skillet.
Add corn and 1 tablespoon of milk per ear (about 1 cup for 12 ears).
Simmer until tender.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
(I use white pepper.)
Drain fruit.
Add the marshmallows and coconut.
Add sour cream and mix thoroughly.
Chill.
Brown meats and drain.
Melt cheese in microwave.
Stir all ingredients together and heat in crock-pot. Serve with Fritos.
Place chicken pieces in greased casserole and pour taco sauce over chicken according to taste.
Cover casserole and bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, uncovered.
Sprinkle cheese over top of chicken and cover with broken tortilla chips.
Bake, uncovered, until cheese is melted and chips are hot.

Fold in melted margarine.
Pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven and immediately sprinkle with marshmallows.
Do not drain liquid off fruit.
Mix all ingredients together. Chill and serve.
Mix together.
Put into baking dish.
Bake in oven 25 minutes at 325° until brown.
Debone pork.
Cut up chicken and pork into mouth-sized pieces. Preheat a large skillet or paella pan with 1/4-inch coating of olive oil (medium flame).
Toss in chicken and pork; cook evenly. Chop onion into small pieces and add to meat.
Cook with cover on for 20 to 30 minutes (low flame).
Mix cheese and margarine; add flour, salt and pepper, mix well.
Shape into small balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Flatten with fork.
Bake at 375° about 10 minutes.
Combine potatoes, onion and ham.
Chill 1 hour.
Shape mixture into patties.
Combine milk and eggs. Dip patties into this mixture and then in crumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Brown meat.
Add peppers, soups and sauce.
Let simmer.
Put Doritoes on bottom of casserole dish.
Put mixture on top of Doritos.
Put cheese on top of that.
Bake until cheese is melted.
Place hash browns in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt butter and pour over potatoes.
Add salt, pepper and onions.
Mix soup and sour cream; pour over potatoes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Top with crushed Ritz crackers (about 32) and 1/4 cup melted margarine. Bake at 350° for about 35 to 40 minutes.
Melt butter and cook onion until soft.
Stir in flour.
Add potatoes, milk, salt & pepper.
Cook 25-30 minutes.
Add cheese and kielbasa and cook another 2-3 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in a loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or longer.

Place potatoes in a 9 x 13 pan. Pour melted margarine over potatoes and onions (1 stick margarine). Mix soup and sour cream. Pour over potatoes. Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over top to taste. Crush 1 stick of the Ritz crackers and mix with 1 stick of margarine. Spread mix over top. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Cook chicken in the water with 1 tsp. of salt in a covered pot, about 30 minutes, or until chicken is soft.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Save broth and soak tortillas in in it.
Toast sesame seeds and squash seeds in a skillet until they lightly brown.
In a food processor, grind the seeds. add the cilantro, green onions, hot chiles, tomatillos and 1 cup of the broth.
Add the tortillas and process into a smooth paste.
Brown the chicken in a lightly oiled pan for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Add the paste mixture and the remaining broth, about 2 cups.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until the sauce is reduced to a thick, rich, green consistency. Serve over rice if desired.
Makes 4-6 servings.
Whip all ingredients together until smooth.
Grease casserole with butter.
Pour mixture into dish. Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Mix together flour, sugar and salt.
Stir in lemon rind, juice, well beaten egg yolks and milk.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole or 6 custard cups.
Set in pan of water (1-inch deep).
Bake 45 to 50 minutes at 350°. Serve warm or cold.
Good with whipped cream.
Beat butter at medium speed of electric mixer; gradually add sugar, beat well.
Add eggs, one at a time; beat well after each one.
Add the Kahlua and chocolate; beat until blended.
Combine flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt; add to the mixture in mixing bowl; alternate with the milk until all is used (begin and end with flour).
Mix well after each addition.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 23 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool on wire racks for 10 minutes; remove from pan and cool.
Stir 1/2 cup nuts into 1 cup of the frosting; spread between layers.
Frost rest of cake. Sprinkle with reserved nuts.
Combine beef, egg, crumbs, onion, 1/3 cup sauce, salt, oregano and pepper.
Mix well and shape into flat rectangle, about 10 x 12 inches, on waxed paper.
Sprinkle cheese over.
Roll as for jelly roll; press ends to seal.
Bake in shallow baking dish at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain off excess fat.
Pour remaining sauce over roll; bake an additional 15 minutes.
In a large skillet, brown beef with onion, then drain grease. Stir in soup, cream cheese and catsup.
Transfer to a large casserole dish.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Top with biscuits and bake for an additional 10 to 20 minutes, until biscuits are golden brown.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
In a large mixing bowl, cream butter, sugar and anise flavoring; beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add flour mixture and almonds.
Turn out on a floured pastry cloth and knead gently until smooth.
Divide dough in half.
Shape each half into a roll about 1 1/2 inches in diameter.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven until firm to the touch, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
While still warm.
Cut rolls into crosswise slices about 1/2-inch thick.
Place cut side down on cookie sheet.
Return to oven and bake until toasted and dried out, about 10 to 20 minutes, longer if necessary. Turn once to toast and brown both sides.
Cool completely.
Store in a tightly covered tin box.
Makes 3 to 3 1/2 dozen.
Fry chicken in butter (use heavy skillet) for 5 minutes; add onion, garlic and tarragon sprigs.
Sprinkle with flour, stirring to distribute flour evenly.
Add water and carrots.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Remove chicken and keep warm.
Let the sauce cook down, stirring often, for about 5 minutes.
Remove tarragon; add cream, salt and pepper.
Simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in chopped tarragon and serve with rice.
Serves four.
Brown meat;
add
onions.
Combine
first 4 ingredients and add.
Combine next	3
ingredients	and add.
Add 1 cup of the water.
Cook 2
to	2 1/2 hours (until tender).
Mix flour with remaining water
and
add and let thicken.	I add carrots or green beans for variety.	Serves 4.
Saute onion in oleo; stir in soups, mixing well before adding other ingredients.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix sour cream, evaporated milk and 10x sugar together.
Add thawed whipped topping.
Tear angel food cake into small pieces and put into a large bowl.
Add first mixture, stir together.
Mix strawberries (sliced) and glaze.
Put on top of cake mixture. Keep refrigerated.
Rub meat with a cut surface of garlic, salt and pepper.
Place in bowl.
Heat vinegar, water, onion, bay leaves, peppercorns and sugar together, but do not boil.
Pour hot mixture over meat; cover bowl and let stand in cool compartment of refrigerator 4 to 8 days, turning meat each day.
Combine all ingredients.
Spoon into prepared pie crust. Cover with top crust; crimp edges to seal.
Slit top.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Cool 10 to 15 minutes before serving.
Cook potatoes in skins.
Let cool.
Peel and shred coarsely. Over low heat, cook onion in butter.
Add cheese and stir until almost melted. Remove from heat and blend in sour cream, salt and pepper.
Fold in potatoes.
Put in greased 2-quart casserole. Dot with butter and bacon.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
In wok, fry chicken breasts in Wesson oil.
Sprinkle with garlic powder.
Remove excess oil when done with paper towels.
In separate pan, cook Knorr soup and bouillon cubes about 20 minutes. Thicken with cornstarch.
Cut up vegetables and add with the soup to chicken in wok.
Heat together while stirring.
Enjoy.
Layer cake pan with pecans.
Mix sugar and cinnamon together. Roll biscuit in mixture.
Pour over pecans in cake pan.
In saucepan, mix butter, ice cream, granulated sugar and brown sugar. Mix until all is melted.
Pour over biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Flip out on wax paper while still hot.
Mix all ingredients well.
Remove from dressing with slotted spoon and serve on lettuce leaves.
Cook macaroni.
Peel and chop onion.
Preheat oven to 350°. Open can of stewed tomatoes.
In mixing bowl, combine milk, cheese, stewed tomatoes and onion.
Pour cooked macaroni into baking dish.
Pour tomato cheese mixture over macaroni and stir. Bake in oven for 40 minutes.
Add sugar to lime Jell-O and mix by package directions.
Add all to Jell-O.
Let set until firm.
Can be made several days ahead.
Grate cheese in flat dish.
Beat egg and pour over cheese. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add milk to cover cheese.
Pour cooked macaroni into dish; stir.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Beat sugar and oleo together.
Add eggs; mix well.
Add flour, chocolate and vanilla.
Blend well.
Pour into greased Pyrex (9-inch) pie plate.
Bake 25 minutes at 325°.
Serve warm with ice cream.
Mix cream cheese with powdered sugar and 1 cup Cool Whip; stir until smooth.
Spread on cooled crust.
Mix pudding with milk. Spread on top of cream cheese.
Spread Cool Whip on top of cream cheese.
Sprinkle with whatever you have.
Cream shortening.
Add confectioners sugar; add egg whites and beat well.
Add vanilla or other desired flavoring.
Beat until smooth; spread on cake.
Combine all ingredients and let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Garnish with a few red maraschino cherries.

recipes.t: Red Cabbage(A Sweet And Sour Dish With Great Color)
d: In a small saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar and cloves.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 6 minutes.
Remove cloves.
Add onion and water; simmer 5 more minutes.
Place shredded cabbage in a large saucepan and pour hot vinegar solution over cabbage.
Cook until cabbage is hot and crisp-tender (5 to 6 minutes).
Combine egg and milk.
Stir in sugar and salt.
Sift and mix together the flour and baking powder.
Mix all ingredients and use with assorted, raw vegetables.
Mix everything, except butter and corn flakes; place in baking dish.
Top with corn flakes and butter.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Cut raw corn off of cob and measure.
Add water, sugar and salt.
Stir well.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Cool.
Put into freezer containers and freeze.
Blend milk and egg.
Combine flour and seasoning in plastic bag.
Shake chicken in seasoned flour.
Dip chicken pieces in milk-egg mixture.
Shake chicken a second time in seasoning mixture to coat thoroughly and evenly.
Brown onion and ground beef.
Add all other ingredients; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 40 or 45 minutes at 350°.
Serve with tossed green salad and garlic bread.
This is a big hit with men!
Boil and debone chicken breasts.
Place in casserole dish. Undercook broccoli and layer on top of chicken.
Melt together both soups, mushrooms, margarine and cheese.
Pour over broccoli and chicken.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Remove skin and bones and flake salmon.
Add other ingredients except pecans and parsley.
Mix well and chill until easy to handle.
On a sheet of waxed paper, mix pecans and parsley.
Turn salmon mixture onto this and shape into a log.
Serve with crackers.
Scramble eggs in a bowl.
Add ham and cheese.
Mix.
Add a dash of wine and spice to taste.
Pour in a heated skillet.
Flip when lightly golden brown.
Mix.
Pour mixture on top of cake in pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Combine in a large bowl 1 1/2 cups flour and yeast.
Heat buttermilk, butter, sugar and salt until warm and butter is almost melted (120° to 130°).
Add to flour mixture along with eggs. Beat at medium speed for 3 minutes after blending with electric mixer.
Stir in remaining flour with mixing spoon and as much flour as needed to form soft dough.
Knead 6 to 8 minutes on floured surface.
Let rise until double.
Make into desired rolls. Makes 1 1/2 dozen cloverleaf rolls.
Let dough again.
Bake for 15 minutes at 375°.
Roll rabbit in mixture of flour, salt and pepper.
Heat fat or oil, about 1/4 inch deep, in heavy frypan, large enough to hold the pieces without crowding.
Use moderate temperature.
Marinate meat in dressing for several hours or overnight in fridge.
Remove from marinade and brown meat.
Combine meat, marinade and water in a 2 1/2-quart casserole.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Add vegetables and continue baking for 45 minutes.
Place biscuits around edge of casserole; brush with margarine.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake at 475° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Cook fettuccine according to package directions; drain.
Heat butter and garlic in skillet on medium heat until garlic is lightly browned.
Add Crab Delights, half and half and pepper.
Heat about 3 minutes or until mixture just begins to bubble, stirring occasionally.
Add Parmesan cheese; stir for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Toss Crab Delight sauce with fettuccine.
Serve immediately with additional Parmesan cheese, if desired.
Makes four 1-cup servings.
Drain all vegetables before adding to liquid.
Cut onion and bell pepper. Dice small.
Mix vinegar, oil and sugar.
Put in covered bowl and keep in refrigerator.
Combine the dressing, sugar, onion and Parmesan cheese in a large Ziploc bag; refrigerate and let marinate for 8 to 12 hours. Mix remaining ingredients and toss just before serving.
Mix ingredients. Spread in well-greased 13 x 9 x 2 pan.
Mix all ingredients and pour in unbaked pie shell and bake at 350° until done.
Beat (third word in Proverbs 23:14).
Bake in loaf pans at 325° for 50 minutes.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add all other ingredients. Bring to boil; reduce heat.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with grated Parmesan cheese.
Makes about 6 cups.

Preheat oven to 350°. Combine 1 tablespoon margarine, 3 tablespoons flour, the brown sugar and nutmeg. Stir in water. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Add rhubarb and cook until tender. Remove from heat. Stir in pineapple and pour into ungreased, shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish (12 x 7 x 2-inch works well). Combine 1/2 cup sugar, 3/4 cup flour and remaining margarine until mixture resembles coarse meal. Sprinkle over fruit mixture. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serve warm. Makes 8 servings.
Dissolve
jello in
cups
boiling
water.
When completely dissolved,
add	strawberries,
pineapple and nuts. Place 1/2 of mixture into a mold
or
x 13 x 2 1/2-inch pan and let set in refrigerator.
Keep
the remaining half at room temperature.
When first half is
set,
spread
1 pint of sour cream.
Carefully pour remaining mixture over sour cream.
Let set until firm in refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 350°.

Dissolve soda in vinegar; set aside. Cream the shortening. Add sugar and beat well with electric mixer. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in soda mixture. Sift together flour, cocoa and salt. Combine buttermilk, vanilla and food coloring.

Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk mixture, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Bake 25 to 35 minutes. Cool in pans 10 minutes. Remove from pans. Cool on racks. Spread Custard Frosting between layers, top and sides. Sprinkle with coconut flakes, if desired.
After cooking squash, beat in bowl with Mixmaster.
Add other ingredients, including bread crumbs.
Place in shallow casserole; cover with more bread crumbs.
Dot with butter; bake for about 45 minutes at 350°, until brown on top.
Boil 2 to 3 quarts water. Add chicken. Turn flame off and let chicken sit in water.
Steam broccoli.
Make Stove Top according to package directions.
In a bowl, with a wire whisk, mix soup, broth and sour cream.
Lay chicken in bottom of rectangular casserole dish and broccoli.
Pour soup mixture over chicken and broccoli.
Spoon stuffing to cover entire top of dish. Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes at 325°.
Heat until mixed and then pour over potatoes in baking dish.
Mix and pour into ice cream freezer.
Freeze per instructions for freezer.
Beat the one egg; add sugar and beat until very light and white.
Add the milk without stirring.
Then sift 1 pint flour to which has been added the baking powder and salt and nutmeg.
Beat this thoroughly; then add quickly enough flour to make a firm but soft dough.
Roll out 1/2-inch thick; cut into rings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spread pie filling in bottom of a 9-inch square pan.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Combine dry cake mix, nuts and melted butter.
(Mixture will be crumbly.)
Sprinkle over pie filling.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes, until golden brown.
Serve with whipped cream or hot with coffee cream.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Pour boiling water over dates and nuts.
Let them stand until cool.
Mix shortening and sugar.
Add the eggs, without heating. Sift salt with flour.
Now add soda to dates and nuts.
Add alternately to the sugar mixture with flour.
Lastly, stir in 2 to 3 cups cold water.
Bake in two loaf pans at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Mix brown sugar, white sugar, Crisco and eggs in bowl.
Add mincemeat and milk.
Stir, then add soda, baking powder, flour, salt and spices.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Test with toothpick.
Layer 1:
Dissolve lime gelatin in hot water.
Add pineapple and juice-water mixture to gelatin; stir well.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan and place in refrigerator to congeal.
You will need toothpicks or string.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time.
Sift flour, baking soda and salt together.
Alternating, add flour and sour cream to butter mixture.
Add vanilla.
About
1 1/4 hours before serving:
On waxed paper, mix potato flakes,
paprika,	salt, garlic powder, pepper and 1/4 cup grated
Parmesan
cheese.
In
pie	plate, beat egg and 1 teaspoon water.
Dip
chicken
pieces
into egg mixture, then coat with potato flake mixture.
Prepare rice according to directions on bag.
Saute onions and ground beef.
Add chili mix, canned tomatoes, salt and pepper to beef mixture.
Add rice.
Mix milk and cheddar cheese soup together and beat until creamy.
Pour over meat mixture.
Top with cubed fresh tomatoes, shredded lettuce, shredded cheese and Fritos.

Combine all ingredients except broccoli and tortellini. Bring to a boil and then turn to low and simmer for 30 minutes. At 15 minutes, add the broccoli and tortellini and continue to simmer for 15 minutes. Enjoy.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook macaroni according to directions. Drain.
Combine ground beef, onion and seasonings.
Shape into 16 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in oil, turning to brown all sides.
Stir in soup.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in sour cream, macaroni and sweet peas.
Put in greased 2-quart casserole dish and bake 45 minutes. Makes 8 servings.
Combine
Spam,	cheese, mayonnaise, relish and mustard. Pile on open-face buns.	Broil until cheese is bubbly.
In a 2-quart saucepan combine rhubarb, sugar, 2 tablespoons water and cardamon or cinnamon.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Cover and simmer about 5 minutes or until fruit is tender.
Stir together the 1 tablespoon water and cornstarch.
Add to rhubarb mixture.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly.
Cook and stir for 2 minutes more.
Stir in strawberries. Serve warm over ice cream.
