Brown meat in skillet.
Add onions.
Mix soup, tomatoes and milk.
Alternate
meat
and
tortillas.
Pour soup mixture over meat and tortillas.
Poke with knife so soup runs through meat. Bake 30 minutes at 400°.
Top with cheese.
Put back in oven for a few minutes for cheese to melt.
In 1 1/2-quart casserole dish, combine soup and sour cream. Stir in broccoli, ham and rice.
Mix well. In a cup, combine bread crumbs and butter. Sprinkle over casserole.
Heat oven to 350°. Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until hot and bubbly. Serve.
Melt margarine in 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Sift flour with baking powder; beat eggs and season lightly.
Add 5 to 6 drops Tabasco sauce.
Stir in flour, ham, cheese, cottage cheese and most of the melted margarine.
Swirl rest of margarine around in dish to coat evenly.
Pour in egg mixture.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake 10 to 15 minutes longer until puffed and golden brown.
Cut into squares and serve.
Combine milk and soup in a 2-quart, microwave-safe casserole dish.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and microwave on High for 10 minutes.
Stir.
Microwave another 12 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Serves 8.
In saucepan, combine brown sugar, granulated sugar, evaporated milk and butter or margarine.
Bring to full boil over moderate heat, stirring frequently.
Boil for 15 minutes over moderate heat, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Add marshmallow cream, butterscotch chips and chocolate chips.
Stir until chips are melted and mixture is smooth.
Blend in nuts and vanilla. Pour into a greased 9 x 9-inch pan.
Chill until firm.
Makes about 2 1/2 pounds.
Freezes well.

Cut meat into 3 or 4 portions. Mix flour and salt; dredge meat in flour mixture. Set aside remaining flour. Brown meat in small amount of hot oil, about 3 tablespoons. Place meat in shallow baking dish. Blend reserved flour mixture into drippings in skillet. Add tomatoes and green chilies, celery, carrot and onion. Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture boils. Pour over meat. Cover and bake in 350° oven for 1 hour or until meat is tender. Sprinkle cheese over meat.
Process chicken in food processor for 5 seconds, using steel blade.
Add cream cheese, chutney, curry, onion, mayonnaise and pepper.
Process 5 to 10 seconds, until well blended.
Place in an au gratin dish; spread with almonds.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Serve with large corn chips.
Mix oleo and graham crumbs. Put this in the bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Beat the eggs, oleo and 10x sugar for not less than 15 minutes.
Spread on the graham crust and then cover with sliced bananas and crushed pineapple. Cover with Cool Whip. Sprinkle with chopped nuts and some cherries.
Refrigerate for several hours before serving.
Keep refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Cook rice and raisins together.
Beat egg yolks and add sugar, pinch of salt, milk, nutmeg and cinnamon.
Preheat oven to 400°. Cook ground beef. Put in 8 inch baking dish. Top with sauce and cheese. Combine milk, bisquick and eggs. Beat until smooth. Pour over top. Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Brown coconut and pecans lightly in 1/4 cup margarine.
Mix cream cheese and Eagle Brand milk until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip. Put 1/4 cream cheese mixture in each pie crust.
Drizzle 1/4 jar caramel and 1/4 coconut mixture.
Repeat layers.
Freeze (better results if frozen overnight).
Thaw 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
Combine fruit and sugar in a 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix remaining ingredients and sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for one hour or until brown and bubbly.
Beat cream cheese and sugar in mixing bowl until fluffy and well-blended.
Spread on bottom of pie crust.
In skillet, over medium heat, melt butter and add apples.
Cook, stirring, until tender-crisp, about 5 minutes.
Drain well on paper towels.
Drop on greased cookie sheet and bake at 300° for 30 minutes; 275° may be better.
Makes 100 cookies.
Place cranberries, Quartered orange with peel, apple and sugar in food processor.
Chop
until mixture reaches relish consistency.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Mix in walnuts and serve.
In a 1 1/2-quart bowl, stir sugar, cocoa, milk and vanilla together until partially blended.
Place butter over top in center of bowl.
Microwave on High for 2 minutes.
Stir vigorously until smooth.
(Don't worry if all the butter does not melt; it will as mixture is stirred.)
Pour mixture into greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Chill in refrigerator 1 hour.
Cut into squares.
Makes about 36 squares.
Cut ribs into serving pieces. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Place in shallow pan. Bake at 450° for 1/2 hour.
Pour off excess fat.
Reduce oven heat to 350°.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over ribs. Bake for 1 1/2 hours, basting frequently. Makes 4 servings.
Combine sugar, margarine and eggs.
Mix well.
Stir in bananas, buttermilk and vanilla.
Stir in remaining dry ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Heat in crock-pot until cheese is melted.
Serve warm with tortilla chips.
In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil until very hot.
Stir in Sofrito and stir for 20 seconds.
Add rice; stir until all ingredients are well mixed.
Add black beans, water, salt, garlic powder, pepper and envelopes of Sazon; stir and bring to a boil. Add olives and/or Vienna sausages (optional).
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes (until all water is absorbed).
Stir rice once with a large fork after 10 to 15 minutes.
When rice is done, turn off heat and let stand for 5 minutes.
Stir rice once again after 5 minutes and enjoy!
Peel and cube potatoes.
Boil until soft.
Drain, but do not throw water away.
Mash potatoes and butter.
Slowly add water (not too much) and heat, stirring all the time.
Mix leek soup mix with water and add to potatoes.
Heat and stir all the time.
Keep stirring and add 1/2 the cream.
Combine cranberries,
orange
and
apricots and put 1/2 the mixture in	the
blender.
Blend well.
Add the other half of mixture, blend well. Add sugar, ginger, almonds and raisins to mixture.
Refrigerate.
Combine sugar, syrup, water and peanuts.
Measure into custard cup soda and salt.
Cook together sugar, corn syrup, water and peanuts for 30 to 35 minutes after it begins to boil, until it is amber, a little deeper than straw color.
Add soda and salt, mixed.
Remove from heat.
Beat until blended and pour onto heavy buttered aluminum tray.
Pull edges to thin sheets; cut off pieces with kitchen shears.
Cool and store tightly covered.
Put chicken in pan.
Put salt over chicken, then put Pepsi up to the top of chicken.
Then cook 1 hour at 350°.
Then cover with barbecue sauce.
Boil chicken breasts in 1 quart water until tender.
Remove, cool and cut up.
Add cream of chicken soup to broth and bring to rolling boil.
Pour half of the vanilla wafers into about a 1 1/2-quart bowl. Whip cream until stiff and fold in drained maraschino cherries (chopped) and drained crushed pineapple.
Add chopped nuts.
Layer the creamed mixture over the wafers; add the remaining vanilla wafers.
Refrigerate overnight.
In large saucepan, combine 1 1/4 cups of pineapple juice and sugar.
Bring to a boil.
Add apple wedges.
Simmer, covered, 3 to 4 minutes or until apples are tender, but not soft.
With slotted spoon, lift apples from liquid.
Set apples aside to drain.
Blend the remaining 1/4 cup pineapple juice slowly into cornstarch.
Add to hot pineapple liquid in saucepan.
Cook and stir until mixture thickens and bubbles.
Cook 1 minute more.
Remove from heat; stir in butter or margarine, vanilla and salt.
Cover and cool 30 minutes, without stirring.
Mix all of ingredients together and roll into 80 to 100 balls.
Cook rice.
In a large frying pan, heat oil; toss in broccoli and onion.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add cream of chicken soup. Reduce heat.
Stir in cheese, milk and salt; cook until bubbly. Place rice in bottom of 2-quart casserole and add broccoli sauce. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Fold together milk and juice.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into crust and cool for a few hours.
Put water, sugar and pineapple in top of double boiler and bring just to boiling point.
Mix flour and cornstarch and add to pineapple mixture.
Cook until it thickens.
Remove from heat and add vanilla.
When cool, fold in egg whites.
Pour into 2 baked pie shells.
Top with 1/2 pint whipped topping for each pie. Sprinkle with coconut.
Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Place unwrapped ham on rack in large roasting pan. Let stand at room temperature 2 hours.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add cold water.
Pour into individual ring molds or 6 ounce custard cups.
Chill until firm, about 2 hours.
Dissolve jello in water (do not add cold water).
Add ingredients except sour cream.
Stir well or until raspberries separate.
Pour 1/2 mixture in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill until firm enough to spread sour cream over top.
Add remainder of jello mixture and chill until firm.
This can be made with different flavors also.
Example:
strawberry jello and fruit, orange jello and mandarin orange slices, etc.
But raspberry is super!
Layer vegetables in the order listed in a 10 x 10 x 2-inch casserole dish.
Spread mayonnaise evenly over top.
Sprinkle sugar, then Parmesan cheese, then Bac*Os bits over mayonnaise. Layer mushrooms evenly over top and then sliced eggs.
Add croutons on top.

recipes.t: Midwestern Scalloped Corn And Sausage Casserole
d: Brown sausage; drain off all fat except about 2 tablespoons. Add flour and stir until blended, then add milk and stir until mixture boils and thickens.
Add corn, salt and pepper to mixture. Place into shallow casserole.
Arrange thick slices of tomato over the top of sausage and corn mixture.
Top with grated cheese. Place under broiler for 4 to 5 minutes, until tomatoes are cooked and cheese is melted.
Yields 4 servings.
In 1-quart microproof casserole, combine carrots and water. Cover.
Cook on High (maximum power) 6 minutes.
Stir in green peppers.
Cover.
Cook on High (maximum power) 12 to 15 minutes or until carrots are tender, stirring once during cooking time. Drain.
Combine first 3 ingredients and press firmly into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Beat cream cheese, sugar and 2 tablespoons of milk until smooth.
Fold in 1/2 of Cool Whip.
Spread over crust.
Prepare pudding using 3 1/2 cups milk.
Spread over layer of cream cheese. Chill 2 hours.
Spread remaining Cool Whip over pudding layer. Garnish with graham cracker crumbs or semi-sweet mini chocolate chips.
Beat eggs; add butter, milk, sugar and flour all together. Add corn. Bake at 350° until firm, approximately 45 minutes or more. Sprinkle small jar chopped pimentos on top (option).
Cream the butter with sugar.
Mix in egg yolks, then flour, then nuts.
Use hands.
Grease an 8-inch square pan.
Put half of the dough in pan.
Top with 2 tablespoons of apricot preserves. Put the rest of the dough on top of the apricot preserves.
Spread remaining preserves on top.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Lay chicken wings n large pan.
Mix soup, dressing and 3/4 jar preserves and spoon over chicken.
Cover with foil and bake for 1 hour.
Uncover and continue baking for 1/2 hour or until browned at 350°.
Drain shredded zucchini and squash.
Squeeze dry with paper towels.
Set aside.
Coat a medium skillet with vegetable spray. Place over medium-high heat until hot.
Add onions and saute for 5 minutes or until tender.
Combine squash, onions, shredded cheese and next four ingredients in large bowl.
Stir well.
In large bowl, mix buttermilk, mayonnaise, horseradish, sugar, bouillon and dill.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and chill.
Garnish.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Mix oleo and sugar; mix flour, salt and baking powder.
Add 2 mixtures together and add vanilla.
Add enough milk to make stiff dough.
Roll out on floured sheet and cut like biscuits.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.
In a large bowl lightly beat 2 eggs.
Add ham, sausage, bread crumbs, milk, parsley and horseradish and mix well.
Press into a greased 6 cup ring mold.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours.
Toward end of baking time, prepare scrambled eggs with remaining eggs. Remove ring from oven and drain juices.
Unmold onto serving platter.
Fill center with scrambled eggs.
Serve immediately.
Prepare shells and drain.
Cool spinach and pour into large bowl.
Add salt, pepper and cheese (Ricotta or cottage cheese). Mix fried beef and spaghetti sauce.
Stuff cheese mixture into shells.
Pour spaghetti sauce over shells.
Use a 9 x 13-inch pan. Top with shredded cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Drain oranges, reserving 2 tablespoons syrup.
Blend syrup with stir-fry sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in wok or skillet (high heat).
Add chicken, cashews and garlic; stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Remove from pan.
Heat remaining oil in same pan.
Add onion and snow peas.
Stir-fry for 3 minutes and then add chicken, cashews and stir-fry sauce mixture.
Cook and stir to coat all ingredients.
Remove from heat and stir in oranges.
Serve on rice.
Mix all ingredients until well blended.
Pour into unbaked 8-inch pie shell.
Bake 10 minutes at 450°. Then 30 minutes at 350°.
Grind cranberries and apple.
Add the sugar.
Stir and let stand overnight in the refrigerator.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Stir in nuts and orange peel.
Mix egg, orange juice and salad oil in a small bowl.
Add liquid mixture to dry mix and blend well.
Pour into greased loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 55 minutes. Do not overbake. Cool in pan on rack for 10 minutes before removing from pan. Makes 1 loaf.
Bake pie shells at 450° for 6 minutes.	Always prick bottom and sides of crusts with a	fork before baking.
Remove shells from oven; reduce heat to 350°.
Toss ham in 1 tablespoon flour, then sprinkle ham over bottom of pie shells.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over ham.
Beat remaining ingredients together and pour mixture into shells.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean.
In medium mixing bowl, blend cream cheese, lemonade and condensed milk until smooth.
Add a few drops of food coloring. Blend well.
Squeeze 1/2 lemon into mixture.
Add Cool Whip and blend for a few minutes.
Pour into pie crust.
Chill 2 to 3 hours.
In a medium bowl, combine carrot, onion, eggs and salt.
Add salad dressing.
Toss to combine.
Refrigerate about 2 hours to allow flavors to blend.
Yields 4 servings.
Combine softened cream cheese and salad dressing, mixing well. Add cheese and apples; mix well.
Chill.
Serve with apple wedges, crackers and bread.
Makes 1 2/3 cups.
Mix vinegar and sugar; slowly add oil.
Add cooked rotini and green pepper.
Mix corn, eggs and sour cream together.
Add meal.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Makes 16.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Using a large bowl, beat eggs well. Add flour, salt, baking powder and butter to eggs and beat well until all is dissolved.
Add potatoes and onions and mix well. Don't be afraid to use your hands!
Pour into brownie pan and bake for 1 hour.
Enjoy!

Cream oleo, vegetable oil, sugar, powdered sugar, vanilla and eggs. Add flour, salt and soda. Roll a teaspoon of dough into a ball. Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Press lightly with floured fork. Works best if dough is chilled. Bake at 375° for 12 minutes.

recipes.t: Cicoria Fina Agliata(Dandelion Sauteed With Garlic)
d: Clean and wash greens, cut in half.
Place in saucepan.
Cook for 10 to 15 minutes or until tender.
Remove and drain.
Heat oil and garlic in frying pan.
Place greens in pan.
Stir with wooden spoon until slightly dry.
Serve hot.
Serves 6 to 8.
Saute onions until golden in margarine.
Add water; bring to boil.
Add bouillon cubes and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer 1/2 hour, or until ready to eat.
Add grated cheese just before putting in bowls.
In individual bowls, add croutons.
Put Mozzarella cheese over top in each bowl.
Melt cheese in microwave or oven.
Melt 1 stick of butter in a flat casserole dish.
Salt, pepper and flour chicken pieces.
Place in dish and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Turn over and bake for 15 minutes more.
Mix cream of chicken soup with buttermilk and pour over chicken.
Cover and bake for 15 minutes longer.
Serve with rice.
Mix all ingredients together well. Serve over sliced cucumbers.
Mix first 3 ingredients well; let come to boil.
Add jello. Mix and let cool.
Chill milk.
Beat until stiff and add all together.
Pour in crust.
Tenderize meat; brown steak quickly in 3 tablespoons oil.
Add mushrooms, onion soup and water.
Bring to boil.
Mix sour cream and flour.
Add to meat and simmer until sauce is thick.
Combine all ingredients; bake at 350° for about 30 minutes in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Heat oven to 350°.
Butter an 8 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Chop the spinach.
Grate the carrot.
Chop the scallion.
In a large bowl, combine flour, 2 tablespoons Parmesan, sugar, baking powder, salt, thyme and nutmeg.
In a separate bowl, combine the milk, oil and egg.
Stir the milk mixture, chopped vegetables and pimento into the flour mixture until all ingredients are just moistened.
Spoon batter into the prepared pan.
Sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons Parmesan.
Bake until a toothpick stuck into the center comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes. Remove from the pan; cool completely.

Cook cabbage and onion until tender and drain water. Place cooked cabbage in casserole dish sprayed with Pam. In a bowl, mix soup, mayonnaise and salt and pepper. Pour over cabbage. In another bowl, mix crushed Ritz crackers, butter and cheese. Spread over cabbage and soup mixture. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden brown. Do not overbake or cheese gets too brown.
Mix all ingredients together and let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Bake in 350° oven from 45 to 60 minutes.
Serve hot. (If you use a dish that can be taken out of the refrigerator and put right in the oven, that will be the best.)
Combine the first 6 ingredients.
Spoon into prepared pie crust.
Cover with top crust; crimp edges to seal.
Slit top crust; brush with egg, if desired.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes. Cool 10 minutes.
Prepare cookie mix as directed on box.
Spread in pizza pan and bake at 375°
for 12 minutes.
Cool.
Sprinkle with sugar before baking.
Combine flour, baking soda and salt.
Beat butter and brown sugar in a large bowl at medium speed until creamy.
Beat in egg until light and fluffy.
Beat in melted chocolate and vanilla.
At low speed, beat in flour mixture.
Fold in nuts, chocolate and candies.
Grease baking sheets.
Drop dough by tablespoons, 2 inches apart on prepared pans.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool cookies on rack.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
Peel and dice zucchini.
Mix zucchini, Bisquick and oil in bowl.
Mix well.
Then add eggs, one at a time.
Add remaining ingredients and bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Mix together and shape into balls.
Dip into melted chocolate.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Add the juice from the clams, seasonings, condensed cream of mushroom soup and white wine.
Simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 8-inch square baking pan.
In large mixing bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla; beat well.
Stir together flour, crumbs, baking powder and salt.
Add to the butter mixture and beat until well blended.
Press 1/2 dough into pan.
Arrange bars over dough, breaking as needed to fit.
Spread with Marshmallow Creme. Scatter bits of remaining dough over Marshmallow Creme; carefully press to form a layer.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool completely and cut.

recipes.t: Deep Dish Pie (Has No Bottom Crust)
d: You will need 1 greased casserole dish.
Cover pickles and onions with water and salt.
Let soak for 3 hours.
Drain.
Mix together 10 cups water, turmeric, mustard seed, celery seed, vinegar and sugar and pour over pickles.
Heat and put in jars and seal.
Place first 7 ingredients in saucepan; heat to boil.
Reduce heat.
Add sour cream (do not boil after adding).
Place a couple of spoonfuls in the bottom of 4-cup crock-pot.
Layer tortillas, soup mixture and cheese.
Cook on low for the afternoon.
Let stand 10 minutes if there is too much liquid or cook a bit longer. Dinner is ready when lessons are finished.
Serve with tossed green salad.
Beat eggs until fluffy and slowly add remaining ingredients. Pour into 2 well-greased and floured loaf pans and bake in 325° oven for 60 minutes or until done.
Invert and cool loaves on racks.
Heat milk to lukewarm.
Add oil.
Mix yeast and sugar into a small amount of warm water to dissolve yeast.
Add to milk mixture and then dry ingredients. Roll out on floured board and knead well. Cut out biscuits and place in oiled pan.
Let rise 45 minutes or until doubled in size.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until browned.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a covered pan and simmer until vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add cheese, stirring over low heat until cheese is melted.
Whisk in beer and stir until well blended.
Thaw frozen bread dough.
Roll dough into 2 (14 x 8-inch) rectangles.
Beat together eggs, Parmesan cheese and oregano. Spread egg mixture on dough, reserving 3 tablespoons.
Top with cheese and melt.
Roll up from long edge and pinch seams to seal. Place seam side down in greased pan.
Brush top of loaves with remaining egg mixture.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Write fortunes on strips of paper.
Mix sugar into egg whites and blend until fluffy.
Melt butter and let cool until warm.
Add flour, salt, vanilla and butter to the sugar mixture.
Beat until the batter is smooth.
Pour batter from a spoon to form circles on a well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° about 8 minutes.
Lay a message on each cookie; fold in thirds, then bend it gently in the center.
If cookies get too hard to bend, return to oven for about 1 minute.
Mix all ingredients. Store in refrigerator.
Keeps well for several days.

Scald milk. Beat eggs in a bowl until light and frothy. When milk is scalded, add corn muffin mix and beat. Then add eggs. Pour into casserole dish margarine which has been melted. Bake in 425° to 450° oven for 25 to 30 minutes. Leftovers are good with syrup for breakfast.
Mix cream cheese, 1 tablespoon milk and sugar in a large bowl with a wire whisk until smooth. Gently stir in Cool Whip. Spread on bottom of crust.
Combine all ingredients.
Bake in a greased, uncovered container, 45 minutes at 325°.
Separate eggs.
In egg whites, add 1/2 tsp. cream of tartar and beat well until very stiff.
In yolks, add flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, oil, extract, rind and water.
Beat well until creamy.
Fold into egg whites, do not beat.
Pour into 10 inch tube pan.
Do not grease.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes and 375° for 10 minutes more.
Combine sugar, buttermilk, soda, oleo and Karo.
Cook over low heat until candy makes hard ball in cold water, about 45 to 55 minutes.
Add pecans and vanilla.
Start beating by hand until it gets thick and loses its sheen.
Drop on wax paper and cool.
In electric frypan, brown pork chops and onion.
Wash sweet potatoes and microwave 10 minutes on High.
Combine first 4 ingredients
and cook 1 to 1 1/2 hours, the longer the better.
Add frankfurters and cook 30 minutes longer.
Break up angel food cake into bite-size pieces.
Place pieces in bottom of casserole dish.
For ease in mixing allow cream cheese to soften out of refrigerator for a couple of hours.
With wire whisk, blend together cream cheese, whipped topping and sugar until nearly smooth.
Layer this mixture on top of cake pieces. Top dessert with one or both cans of pie filling depending on your liking.
Because of layering, a deep dish is best.
However, if using a shallow pan, at least 9 x 13-inch is recommended.
Fry bacon; break in pieces.
Saute onion and green pepper. Chop cabbage.
Add tomatoes, salt and pepper and vinegar.
Put all in one pot and boil until cabbage is done.
Dissolve jello and salt in boiling water.
Drain pineapple, measuring syrup.
Add water to make 1/2 cup if necessary.
Stir into gelatin with lemon juice.
Blend in mayonnaise.
Chill until very thick.
Fold fruits, nuts and Cool Whip into jello.
Pour into 2 freezing trays or a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Freeze until firm or at least 3 to 4 hours.
To serve, cut in squares or slices.
Makes about 8 servings.
Preheat broiler.
In small mixing bowl, combine margarine, basil and parsley; mix thoroughly.
Onto each slice of bread, spread half of the margarine mixture; sprinkle half of the cheese on each slice of bread.
On nonstick baking sheet, arrange bread slices, herb-side up, and broil until cheese is golden, about 1 minute.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer as follows:
1/2 head shredded lettuce, bacon, eggs, peas, onion, mixed dressing, ham and Swiss cheese.
Press down after each layer.
The dressings will spread thickly over entire surface and top with ham and cheese.
Cover with Glad Wrap and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Grate or shred cabbage and soak in water for an hour Drain and rinse well and pat off water.
Mix sour cream, sugar and cider vinegar well and pour over cabbage and mix well.
If using caraway seeds, spin then in the blender long enough to release the oils and mix in the slaw.

Blend 1/2 of the sugar with cornstarch. Add pineapple with juice. Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is thick and clear. Cool. Blend cream cheese (softened at room temperature) with 1/2 cup sugar and salt. Add eggs, one at a time, stirring well after each egg is added. Blend in milk and vanilla. Spread the cooked pineapple mixture over the bottom of pastry shell. Pour in cream cheese mixture and sprinkle with pecans. Bake at 425° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 325° and bake 50 minutes. Cool before serving. Serves 7 or 8.
Combine sugar and butter.
Beat in electric mixer at medium speed five minutes.
Add chocolate and one egg; beat five minutes. Add other egg, vanilla and salt; beat five minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon in baked pie shell and chill.
Mix all ingredients together and chill.
This will keep covered in refrigerator for a week, a
month
or until all has been eaten.
Prepare your crust.
Cook crushed strawberries.
After cooked until clear, add 1 Knox gelatine dissolved in 2 tablespoons cold water.
Add berries into baked pie shell.
Cut stew meat into small pieces and brown in cooking oil. Remove meat and saute onion and garlic in the oil.
When onion is tender, put the meat back into oil with onion and garlic.
Add flour and toss until blended.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Lower heat and slowly add water until sauce is not too thick.
Add Kitchen Bouquet to darken and simmer on low flame until meat is tender, about 1 hour.
In a large mixer bowl, beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk until smooth.
Stir in ReaLemon and vanilla.
Slice 2 bananas; dip in lemon juice.
Drain and line crust.
Pour over bananas; cover.
Chill 3 hours or until set. Before serving, slice remaining bananas; dip in lemon juice, drain and garnish top of pie.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Mix the first 4 ingredients together.
When ready to eat, add dressing and mix, then add crushed Fritos.
Heat oven to 350°.
Measure all ingredients into a large bowl. Mix 1/2 minute on low speed, scraping bowl constantly.
Beat 3 minutes at high speed, scraping bowl occasionally.
Pour into prepared pans.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
In a mixing bowl beat margarine with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds.
Add about half of the flour, the 1 cup sugar, the egg, vanilla, baking soda, and cream of tartar.
Beat until thoroughly combined.
Beat in remaining flour. Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Combine the 2 tablespoons sugar and the cinnamon.
Roll balls in sugar cinnamon.
Place 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 11 minutes or until edges are golden.
Makes about 36.
Cook pasta. In a skillet, combine all other ingredients and simmer. Drain pasta and combine with heated tomato mixture. Top with Parmesan cheese.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly spray cookie sheet with nonstick spray.
Roll chicken pieces in flour to evenly cover all sides.
Dip chicken in egg white and roll in cornflake crumbs. Place on prepared cookie sheet.
Bake 20 - 30 minutes for boneless breast halves or 45 - 55 minutes for chicken pieces.
Add garlic, onion flakes, basil flakes and mushrooms to olive oil; mix well.
Add tomatoes and cook for 1/2 hour.
Brown crumbled hamburger.
Add eggs to cool rice.
Add hamburger and rice mixture to the tomato mixture.
Put in 2 or 3-quart casserole.
Add salt
to taste (optional).
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle top with Parmesan cheese before serving.
Cook rice as directed on package.
Chop onion, pepper and celery.
Brown sausage and drain, then add vegetables.
Cook until vegetables are limp.
Add rice and soup and pour into greased 3-quart casserole dish.
Cover and bake for 1 hour at 325°.

Mix well first 6 ingredients and place in greased 9 x 13 baking dish. Sprinkle with paprika. Combine 1 1/2 sticks melted margarine and crackers and spread on top of potatoes. Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Cover loosely with foil during latter part of baking to prevent drying out. Serves 12-15.
Bring sugar, cocoa, butter and milk to a boil.
Boil for 2 minutes.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Stir in oatmeal.
Drop by tablespoon onto well buttered wax paper.
Cool.
Layer ingredients (in order listed) in greased 1 1/2-quart casserole. Cover; bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes. Remove cover and bake 5 minutes or until cheese is melted. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Bake pie shell at 375° for 15 minutes.
In bowl, combine condensed milk, sour cream, lemon and extract; mix well. Reserving 6 peach slices, spread remaining filling on bottom of pie shell.
Top with sour cream mixture.
Top with reserved peach slices and almonds.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Cool.
Refrigerate.
In large saucepan or kettle having a lid, brown meat in oil. Add salt, spices and onion soup mix.
Stir in boiling water, tomato sauce and soy sauce.
Cook and simmer about 15 minutes.
Mix fried hamburger and seasoning.
Put in bottom of baking dish.
Heat refried beans and spread over top.
Mix sour cream, chili dip and cheese.
Spread over beans.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Heat Tostitos and serve.
Brown sausage and drain.
Beat eggs and add milk.
Add salt and mustard.
Cube bread; stir into eggs.
Add cheese and sausage. Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan for 45 minutes at 350°.
Heat all ingredients in a double boiler.
Serve warm with crackers.
Simmer raisins and water in saucepan over low heat until raisins are plump, 20 to 30 minutes.
Drain water into measuring cup.
Add water to make 1/2 cup.
Heat oven to 400°.
Cream shortening, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Stir in raisin liquid. Blend flour, baking powder, soda, salt and spices.
Stir in.
Add rolled oats, nuts and raisins.
Drop rounded teaspoonfuls 2-inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix beaten eggs, syrup, sugar, peanut butter and vanilla together. Pour in unbaked pie shell. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes until crust is brown.
In large saucepan, boil/steam broccoli in 1/2 cup water. Remove about 1/4 of the broccoli and set aside.
Put remaining broccoli in blender and puree until smooth.
In large saucepan over medium heat, combine flour, butter and 1 cup of water until creamy.
Pour mixture from blender into flour mixture.
Rinse blender with 1/2 water and cream or evaporated milk and pour in flour-broccoli.
Stir and season with spices.
Microwave Cheez Whiz and stir into soup.
Chop broccoli that was set aside and add to soup.
Heat thoroughly.
Lightly brown beef, onions and celery; add remaining ingredients and stir well.
Pour into greased casserole dish. Bake for 1 1/2 hours in 350° oven.
Mix broth and soup together.
Heat until mixed well.
Pour over chicken.
Mix seasonings and brown sugar.
Brush steaks with oil. Sprinkle seasoning mixture over both sides; press into steaks. Place steaks on medium-hot grill.
Grill 6 to 8 minutes on each side or until cooked to desired doneness.
In large bowl, cream together oleo and sugar.
Add eggs; beat until light and fluffy.
Add almond extract.
Stir in flour and baking powder.
Mix until smooth.
Butter a 13 x 9-inch cake pan. Pour batter in pan.
Spoon pie filling with the cake mixture in different places.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes, or until golden and cake tests done.
Filling will sink into the cake while baking.
Serve warm with sweetened whipping cream or Cool Whip.
*Or 1 pound large, cleaned and deveined shrimp or 8 ounces boiled breast of chicken, minced.
Spread refried beans on serving dish.
Then layer on green chiles.
Mix taco seasoning mix with 1/2 of the jar of chunky salsa sauce.
Layer this on serving dish.
Add grated Cheddar cheese.
Layer sour cream.
Spread the chopped green scallions. Then sprinkle remainder of salsa sauce on top.
Keep refrigerated. Can use corn chips or tostadas to scoop the dip up.
Use 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish or round plate.
Cream sugar and oil together.
Add eggs and pumpkin; mix well. Sift together dry ingredients, add alternately with water to pumpkin mixture.
Pour into 2 well-greased and floured 9 x 5-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or until tests done.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Remove from pan to cool.
Boil potatoes until tender (approximately 30 minutes).
Remove skins.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Lightly spray a 1-quart baking dish with vegetable spray.
Mash potatoes.
Add pineapple juice, oil and whip until fluffy.
Add pineapple, cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice.
Mix well.
Place in baking dish.
Spread molasses over the top.
Dot with margarine.
Bake, uncovered, for 15 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Line bottom of dish with 1/2 crushed cookies.
Then spread pudding.
Then spread rest of crushed cookies.
Spread Cool Whip and then nuts.
Combine cocoa and sugar.
Add to pudding mix and prepare as directed on package.
Cool; add vanilla.
Whip cream and fold into chocolate mixture.
Pour into peppermint stick ice cream shells. Freeze.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Add oil and vanilla.
Beat until smooth.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add sugar and blend together.
Fold into batter.
Add nuts and apples.
Pour into greased tube pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Brown pork sausage.
Drain and crumble.
Mix all other ingredients together.
Put in greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes until set and brown.
Serve hot.
Serves 6.
In large bowl, dissolve the gelatine in water.
Heat soup and add to gelatine.
Add rest of ingredients; mix and mold (i.e., Tupperware jello mold container).
Chill 6 hours.
Unmold.
Serve with crackers.
In a bowl, whisk together buttermilk, 1 tablespoon flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
Immerse tomato slices in mixture.
In a heavy skillet, heat over moderate heat until candy thermometer registers 350°.
While oil is heating, whisk together the remaining flour, salt and pepper.
Dredge tomatoes (1 at a time) in seasoned flour, shaking off excess and fry in batches of 6 (do not crowd in skillet) until golden brown on both sides. Transfer slices to paper towel to drain.
Sprinkle with salt.
Place cheese on dish.
Pour 3/4 sauce over cheese.
Place shrimp on top and add rest of sauce.
Sprinkle with green onions. Place crackers around dish.
Cook squash until tender, drain, mash lightly and drain again. Make stuffing according to directions.
Layer 1/2 of stuffing on bottom of 9 x 12-inch casserole dish.
Mix rest of ingredients together, layer and then top with remaining stuffing.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Brown ground beef with onion, bell pepper and season to taste. Layer in dish with frozen vegetables and mushroom soup.
Add a layer of Velveeta cheese. Top with a layer of Tater Tots and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt marshmallows in milk over low heat; pour jello in, stirring until dissolved.
Combine softened cream cheese and mayonnaise, mixing until well blended.
Gradually add jello mixture, mixing until well blended.
Stir in pineapple.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour into 2-quart mold; chill until firm.
Unmold if you like.
Makes 12 servings.
Press 1 can of crescent rolls into a 13 x 9-inch pan, sealing perforations.
Cream 1 cup sugar with cream cheese and vanilla. Spread this over dough.
Top with remaining can of dough.
Brush with egg yolk.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/4 cup of sugar and pecans.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Best when served same day at room temperature.
Cut off tips of broccoli only and steam or boil until almost done.
Meanwhile, mix soup, eggs, onions, mayonnaise and cheese and put in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Cream sugar and cream cheese. Add strawberries and juice, pineapple and bananas, nuts, Cool Whip and lemon
juice.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch pan or 24 muffin paper cups. Freeze.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add bell pepper, onion, celery and ground chuck.
Cook slow until done.
Mix in spaghetti mix, Ragu sauce and tomato sauce.
Simmer 20 minutes.
Boil spaghetti. Rinse with cold water.
Add to the meat sauce.
Cook for 10 more minutes.
Cover with cheese.
Put lid on pot.
Turn off heat. Serve with salad or cold slaw and garlic bread.
Cook fettuccini to desired doneness as directed on package. Drain; rinse with hot water.
Keep warm.
In large skillet over medium-high heat, heat oil.
Saute onions for 1 to 2 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Reduce heat to medium.
Stir in sour cream, milk, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cook, stirring constantly, until hot.
Do not boil.
Stir in turkey ham, egg wedges and fettuccini; toss gently.
Makes 4 (1 1/2 cup) servings.
Prepare apples.
Put a little lemon juice over them; set aside and cover.
Add sugar and
eggs
to
oil; mix well at low speed until creamy and
smooth.
Sift
flour and measure.
Sift again with salt, soda and
baking powder.
Add flour mixture to creamed mixture a little at
a
time.
Fold
in well after each addition; add vanilla.
When
batter
is stiff, remove beaters and finish mixing by hand.
Fold in apples and nuts.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 55 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Grease and flour tube pan. Put 1/2 batter in pan. Mix sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle most over batter.
Also, sprinkle most of nuts.
Add rest of batter and sprinkle rest of nuts and sugar-cinnamon.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 to 45 minutes, sometimes longer.
Crush vanilla wafers. Cut candied fruit into pieces.
Leave nuts whole.
Mix all ingredients except milk and marshmallows. Melt marshmallows in milk and mix with other ingredients.
When mixed well, pack in angel food pan or 3 small loaf pans.
When cool, remove from pan and wrap in wax paper at room temperature.
Heat oven to 375° and grease an 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan. Place applesauce in the bottom of the pan.
Mix remaining ingredients in mixing bowl and sprinkle on top of the applesauce. Bake until golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes and serve warm.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Mix well; pour into pie shell. Bake at 350° until firm.
Prepare the cranberries and apples in a food processor or blender.
Mix together the oranges, sugar and dry Jell-O, then combine all ingredients together.
It is best to let the relish set a couple of days before you use it.
The relish can also be frozen.

d: *Vary the number of chilies according to your "heat tolerance" or just don't use them.
I prefer at least 3.
Combine 2 cups flour and yeast.
In saucepan, heat milk, shortening, sugar and salt until warm.
Add to dry mixture.
Add egg and pumpkin.
Beat at low speed 1/2 minute.
Beat 3 minutes on high.
Stir in enough remaining flour to make soft dough.
You will also need 4 (18 x 12-inch) pieces heavy aluminum foil.
Mix sugar and flour; add cream, egg, vanilla and nutmeg.
Mix well with eggbeater or wire whisk.
Put rhubarb in pie shell; pour cream mixture over rhubarb.
Push the rhubarb pieces down so they will be well coated with the cream mixture.
Flute edge of pie crust.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and continue baking 40 to 45 minutes or until done.
Mix dry ingredients thoroughly, sifting 3 times.
Add cream and milk to make a medium dough ball.
Divide into 4 equal parts and knead 25 to 30 minutes.

When dough is smooth and free from bubbles, roll out with rolling pin onto metal baking sheets. Measure with ruler 1-inch (prick with fork) the width of cooking sheet, all the way across (1-inch prick, 1-inch prick).
Bake in slow oven 12 to 15 minutes at 375° until light brown.
Cut apart lengthwise with sharp knife.
Mix both kinds of corn, sour cream, cheese, corn meal and butter together.
Then add eggs (slightly beaten) and salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Bake in 1 1/2-quart casserole at 325° for about 40 minutes or until center is set.
If desired, you may add a cup of cooked chicken.
Saute onions in oleo until tender.
Add sour cream, 1/2 cup of Cheddar cheese, dill weed and salt.
In a separate bowl, mix corn bread mix, milk, egg, corn and hot sauce.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Top with onion mixture.
Top this with 1 1/2 cups Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
(Very good leftover!)
Fry mushrooms in butter pan about 10 minutes; do not brown. Fry medium onion in butter.
Combine ham, cheese and mushroom mixture.
Place cooked noodles in greased oblong casserole.
Place ham and cheese mixture over noodles.
Pour half and half over top. Cover and bake at 350° for about 40 minutes.
Cut cooked eggs into pieces. Stir in other ingredients. Refrigerate.
Into a medium mixing bowl, sift together flour, soda, cloves, ginger and sugar.
Add margarine, egg and molasses.
Beat until smooth and stir in oats.
Drop by level tablespoon 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in a 375° oven, until lightly browned; let stand a minute before removing from pan.
Mix all ingredients; chill overnight for best flavor.
Combine first 6 ingredients; stir until blended.
Spoon into a greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes. Top with cheese and bake 5 minutes.

Saut celery, onion and garlic in vegetable oil until tender; add the taco seasoning and 1 cup water. Stir until mixed well. Add tomatoes and all beans with juice except pinto beans (rinse and add). Bring to a boil and simmer on low for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
In a bowl combine cream cheese and milk, whisk until smooth.
Add flour and salt, mix well.
In a separate bowl gently whisk eggs then add cream cheese mixture, mix well.
Pour in a long cookie sheet (parchment paper may be used). Bake for 30 to 33 minutes or until eggs are puffy and golden. Meanwhile, finely chop ham.
Remove omelet from oven, immediately spread dijon mustard, and sprinkle 1/2 of cheese, ham and green onions.
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese and roll up, (like a jelly roll).
Let stand 5 minutes allowing cheese to melt.
Slice and serve.
Mix all ingredients except salt.
Add salt last to taste. Store in sealed container in refrigerator for at least 1 hour prior to serving.
Serves 10.
Cream the oil and sugar together.
Add the egg and beat until light.
Blend in the vanilla and applesauce.
Stir the flours, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, oats and raisins into the creamed mixture.
Blend well.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a lightly oiled baking sheet.
Bake in a 375° oven for 10 minutes. Cool on a wire rack.
Makes 24 cookies.

Cream together butter, sugar, and eggs. Sift together all dry ingredients. Add dry ingredients and pumpkin to creamed mixture. Add pecans and vanilla. Mix well. Bake for 55 to 60 minutes in greased and floured 9 x 13 pan
at 350 degrees.
Drain green beans; place in casserole dish.
Warm soup and water in saucepan; pour over beans.
Cook in oven 20 minutes. Top with onion rings.
Cook 10 more minutes.
Chill cream.
Wash and slice cucumbers.
Sprinkle with salt and sugar; add vinegar.
Allow to stand 10 minutes.
Add sweet cream and mix.
Chill 15 minutes before serving.
Combine ingredients and beat until smooth.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake in greased 8 x 8-inch pan for 30 to 35 minutes.
Pour into bowl the cake mix and jello.
Add oil, nectar and well beaten eggs.
Mix at low speed, then beat for 2 minutes at number 4 speed.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Cool in pan.
Mix together soup, lemon juice and mayonnaise.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Place in bottom of casserole.
Top broccoli with chicken, then pour soup mixture over all.
Sprinkle top with cheese and crumbs.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes in 350° oven.
Layer lettuce and then onions in large bowl.
Mix mayonnaise with sugar and stir in peas (drained).
Add cheese and top with bacon bits.
Mix all ingredients in saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and let simmer for 20 minutes.
Brush sauce on meat the last 20 minutes of grilling.
Pour stewed tomatoes, water and spice in a large pot with garlic, pepper and crushed red pepper.
When mixture comes to a boil, stir in onions, zucchini and yellow squash.
Stew (boil) for 2 hours, stirring every 15 minutes.
Serve in individual bowls; garnish with freshly grated cheese.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Serve with crackers (Ritz are best).
Hard-boil eggs and peel.
Boil all ingredients, except eggs, in a saucepan.
Simmer for several minutes.
Cool until just warm and add shelled, boiled eggs.
Keep refrigerated a day or so to blend spices.
Mix together the first 3 ingredients in
9 x 13 baking dish; spread out for crust. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and cool.
Press shredded carrots between paper towels to remove excess moisture; set aside.
In large bowl, combine cheeses and minced onion.
Stir in shredded carrots and broccoli.
Cover tightly. Refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Shape mixture into a ball; wrap with plastic wrap.
Makes one cheese ball.
Mix all together and chill.
Cook shrimp in boiling water with a little salt about 10 minutes and peel.
Cook the rice in shrimp water.
Saute onions and bell pepper (chopped) in margarine.
Add rice and stir.
Add Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper to taste, then shrimp. Serve hot.
Melt margarine in saucepan; remove from heat.
Stir in lemon peel, flour, dill weed and salt.
Blend in half and half; cook and stir over medium heat until mixture thickens and comes to a boil. Remove from heat.
Blend a small amount of hot mixture with egg yolk; blend back into hot mixture.
Stir well; cook for 1 minute longer.
Serve over cooked vegetables.
Mix sugar, cocoa and salt in iron skillet.
Add milk, oleo and Karo.
Cook on high until when dropped in cold water the candy won't separate, makes a ball in bottom of cup of cold water.
Take off heat; beat.
Add vanilla and beat until it looks shiny.
Pour in buttered platter.
Can add pecans, peanut butter or coconut.
Combine cauliflower, broccoli, onion and water chestnuts; toss well.
Combine remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Pour over vegetables and let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Put chocolate chips, sugar, vanilla, egg and salt in blender. Heat milk to just boiling.
Pour into blender.
Blend 1 minute or until thoroughly blended.
Pour into 6 individual serving cups. Chill and serve with whipped topping.
Mix ingredients in crock-pot.
Cook on high until melted, then on low for 2 to 3 hours.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet and pour off excess fat. Add taco seasoning and water.
Simmer until reduced.
Place equal amounts of taco meat on each tortilla.
Add some refried beans, if desired.
Put some salsa in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Roll up tortillas and place seam down in pan.
Top with more salsa and the cheese.
Put in oven at 300° for 20 minutes or microwave 6 to 8 minutes until cheese melts.
Mix dry pudding mix, pineapple with juice, marshmallows and pecans. Add Cool Whip and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours before serving.
Mix the sugar, cocoa, vanilla, peanut butter and nuts together.
Melt the butter or margarine.
Add to mixture.
Put into a 9 x 13-inch pan, lightly buttered.
Refrigerate and cut.
Mix well shortening, brown sugar and eggs.
Add buttermilk and stir in flour.
It will be easier to work with if you chill dough overnight.
Drop by teaspoon on baking sheet and bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, or until done.
Yields 7 dozen.
Cook cabbage in
salt water until tender.
Drain off all of water.
Put cabbage in casserole dish.
Mince the garlic.
Wash the mushrooms quickly, then trim and slice them.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
When the foam subsides, add the mushrooms, the minced garlic, 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5 minutes.
Taste for seasoning and add salt and pepper if needed.
Sprinkle with parsley before serving.

oven

Combine other ingredients, except crackers to make sauce.
Combine sauce with broccoli.
Pour into casserole.
Sprinkle top with cracker crumbs.
Bake in 400° oven for about 30 minutes.

In a microwave-safe glass bowl mix first 3 ingredients together and cook on High for 7 to 9 minutes, until mixture bubbles and peanuts are brown.
Quickly stir in margarine and vanilla.
Cook on High for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add baking soda, stirring quickly until mixture is foamy.
Pour onto a greased cookie sheet.
Let cool for 15 minutes, until firm.
Break into pieces or cut.

Bring water to a boil; add jello.
Stir until dissolved.
Add frozen berries; continue to stir until berries are thawed apart. Add applesauce.
Stir until well mixed.
Set in refrigerator until set.
Cover the bottom of shallow baking dish (10 x 6 x 2-inch) with spinach.
Break eggs around outside edge of dish.
Pierce egg yolks twice and egg whites several times with a toothpick.
Mix soup, pepper and onion flakes.
Pour around eggs.
Cover spinach completely.
Cover and cook on High for 7 to 8 minutes or until eggs are almost set.
Sprinkle cheese.
Let stand covered 5 minutes.
Serves 6 people.
Mix all ingredients, but ginger ale, the day before.
Fill ice trays with mixture and put 1 cherry per cube (optional).
Freeze until ready to serve.
Mix ginger ale and ice cubes in large punch bowl.
Lightly mix and form into loaf.
In skillet over medium heat, in 1 tablespoon hot margarine, cook chicken 10 minutes or until browned on both sides.
Remove chicken; keep warm.
In same skillet, in remaining margarine, cook broccoli, carrots and mushrooms 5 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in soup, milk and pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Return chicken to skillet.
Reduce heat to low; simmer 5 minutes or until chicken is fork-tender.

Let cream cheese soften. Spread on bottom of dish. Spread 2 cans of green chilies, then chopped onion, then chili. Layer second set of green chilies. Cover with cheeses. Bake at 350 for approximately 30 minutes. Serve with chips.
Cook
sausage
and drain.
Separate rolls into 8 triangles. Place triangles onto pizza pan.
Press to form sides of crust. Seal
perforations.
Spoon sausage over dough.
Sprinkle with hash browns and Cheddar cheese.
Mix together thoroughly.
Put into loaf pan and cover with two strips of bacon.
Pour one can (8 ounce) tomato sauce and bake at 350° about 1 hour.

and
shortening.

beaten eggs, cocoa, soda and salt.

Add chicken, rice, peas and hot pepper sauce.
Return to boiling; remove from heat.
Cover.
Let stand 5 minutes or until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice with fork before serving.
Makes 4 servings.
Trim brisket well.
Place in large deep roasting pan.
Heat Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke and margarine. Pour over brisket.
Cover tightly with heavy-duty aluminum foil.
Cook in oven at 250° for 1 hour per pound. (Or cook at 425° for 1/2 hour, then reduce heat and cook at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes per pound.) Meat is done when fork inserts easily.
Cool for 30 minutes and cut with electric knife into thin slices.
Place sugar and spices in basket of percolator.
Place juice and water in lower part of coffee pot and allow to perk just like coffee.
Melt cream cheese and milk, stirring constantly.
Add remaining ingredients. Pour into buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, uncovered.
Combine first 5 ingredients and set aside.
Saute celery and onions.
Cook rice by directions, adding water chestnuts, celery and onions.
Into a large buttered Corning casserole, put layer of rice, then layer of chicken mixture and then sprinkle with cheese. Alternate layers until all is used.
A little Tabasco sauce can be added.
Garnish with small pieces of chicken, cheese and paprika.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Mix sugar, cream of tartar and cinnamon.
Pour in boiling water.
Boil until soft ball stage.
Remove from fire.
Add vanilla and pecans.
Stir until mixture sugars.
Turn out on waxed paper and separate pecans.
Combine oleo, sugar and syrup.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until sugar is dissolved (do not boil).
Let cool slightly.
Add to beaten eggs, vanilla, salt and pecans.
Pour in unbaked pie crust.
Bake in 325° oven for about 40 minutes or until brown.
Combine first 6 ingredients in bowl.
Mix at low speed until smooth.
Combine baking soda and flour in sifter.
Sift in dry ingredients.
Pour into 13 x 9 baking dish and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt butter; blend in flour and add milk, all at once.
Stir until thickened.
Add grated cheese, salt and pepper.
Continue to cook and stir until cheese is melted.
Remove from heat and spread 1/2 of the cheese sauce on the bottom of a shallow 2 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Place potatoes on top of cheese sauce, sprinkle with onions and bacon. Add remaining sauce over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, until potatoes are tender.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Meanwhile, press biscuits into 12-inch round greased baking sheet or 12-inch pizza pan, pinching edges of biscuits together to seal.
Bake 10 minutes.
Gently boil the mushrooms for 1 minute, drain.
The heat will help the marinade to absorb into the mushrooms.
Serve hot or cold.

and

Add apples and onions to	Dutch

Mix and boil salt, vinegar, pepper, sugar, oil, and water. Cool mixture and pour over remaining ingredients premixed in a large bowl. Set for several hours in refrigerator.

recipes.t: Truthahn Brust In Zwiebelrahm Sosse(Turkey Breast In Onion Sauce)
d: Set oven at 350°.
Lay turkey slices in shallow baking dish (spray with nonstick coating).
Mix together whipping cream and soup mix; pour over turkey.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove cover and bake another 30 minutes. Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Grate potatoes, add salt and egg and mix well.
Drop by tablespoons in well-greased frying pan, spreading real thin.
Fry slowly until browned on each side.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together three times. Cream sugar and shortening; add milk, stiffly beaten egg whites and vanilla. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Frost with your favorite frosting.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients and spoon into 9-inch pie plate or shallow ovenproof dish.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly browned.
Sprinkle with sliced green onions and chopped tomatoes, if desired.
Serve with tortilla chips or crackers.
Makes 2 cups.
Preparation time:
10 minutes.
Cook time is 25 minutes.
Wash and cut chicken into 1-inch chunks.
Also cut sirloin into chunks.
Marinate chicken in teriyaki sauce for 1 hour.
Marinate steak in Worcestershire sauce for 1 hour.
Cut and wash peppers and onion into large chunks.
Put peppers and meat on skewer alternating.
Cook on grill until done.
Serve over rice with extra sauces, sauteed mushrooms and pineapple chunks.
Do not use the sauce that the meat marinated in.
Use fresh sauces.
Boil syrup, butter, sugar and salt together for 5 minutes at medium-high.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and soda; return to heat and cook 2 more minutes.
Pour over Rice Chex, almonds and coconut; mix well.
Pour out onto greased cookie sheet (large). Cool, cut and eat.
Blend together in blender, then chill.
Combine all ingredients in large 3 gallon pan; cook until mixture comes to rolling boil.
Turn heat down until sauce is barely boiling and cook for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Stir often, but sauce must be stirred constantly almost all of the last hour to keep from sticking.
Store in 12 (1/2 pint) Mason jars.
In large bowl stir together flour, cocoa, salt, baking powder and soda.
In mixer bowl beat together butter and sugar on low speed of electric mixer until fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla; beat well.
Gradually add dry ingredients to cream mixture; beat until well blended.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press down center of dough with thumb.
Drain cherries and reserve juice.
Place a cherry in center of each cookie.
In saucepan, combine chocolate chips and condensed milk. Heat until chocolate is melted.
Stir in 4 teaspoons of cherry juice.
Spoon about 1 teaspoon frosting over each cherry, spreading to cover cherry.
Bake at 350° about 10 minutes.
Remove to wire rack and cool.
In a large skillet or wok, heat the oil until quite hot.

Add the walnuts and saute for 1 minute. Add the broccoli and cook over medium heat, tossing frequently, until tender and crisp, about 4 minutes. Add the soy sauce and cook 1 minute more. Serve immediately, garnished with red bell pepper.
In a 1 1/2-quart greased casserole, combine soup, milk, soya sauce and pepper.
Add beans and 1/2 of the onion rings.
Stir. Bake in a 350° oven for 25 minutes until hot and bubbly.
Stir. Top with remaining onion rings.
Bake 5 minutes more.
Beat eggs and shortening.
Add dry ingredients and enough milk to make a stiff dough.
Knead dough on floured surface.
Roll out very thin, cut in strips and drop into boiling broth with a teaspoon of Accent seasoning. When dumplings are almost done, add a few drops yellow food coloring and 1 cup of cream.
Layer chicken pieces in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle salt, pepper, garlic and onion powder to your taste.
Place in microwave oven and cook chicken until done (around 30 to 40 minutes depending on your oven).
Remove chicken and place on heated outdoor grill.
Baste barbecue sauce over it and put lid down.
It only has to stay on the grill for a few minutes to get the smoked flavor without all of the time and trouble of regular grilled chicken.
Barely cover the ingredients in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat until tender.
Sauce will be kind of thick.
Cook dry beans in water until softened (1 1/2 to 2 hours). Drain and put into crock-pot.
Add all remaining ingredients; mix well.
Cover and cook on low 10 to 12 hours or high 4 to 6 hours.
Note: Ingredients listed are for each pastie.
Combine soup, milk, and beaten eggs.
Stir until well blended, add squash, 1 c of the cracker crumbs, and 1 c of cheese, stir until blended.
Pour into a buttered 1 1/2 quart baking dish.
Mix together the remaining cheese and cracker crumbs.
Sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve 8.

Beat until smooth and frothy.
Add pineapple and vegetables.
Pour into bowl; let set.
Also good with orange-pineapple jello.
Blend until consistency wanted.
Make sandwiches or serve on crackers.
Mix sausage, beef, pepper, onion, mushrooms and pepperoni in skillet and brown.
Add sauce and sugar.
Salt and pepper to taste.

Brown bacon in heavy 3-quart pot with a tight fitting lid. Remove bacon and brown onions in drippings until transparent. Remove pot from heat and add paprika, beef, salt, caraway, bacon and half green pepper and tomato.
Return to heat and cover tightly.
Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, and add small amounts of water as needed.
Cook 1 1/2 to 2 hours until meat is tender.
Add garlic, potatoes, the rest of peppers and tomatoes.
Add enough water to completely cover meat and vegetables.
Bring to a boil; simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with very small bow tie egg noodles.
Blend well and chill before serving with cucumbers, carrots, cauliflower, celery, etc.

Preheat oven to 325°. Mix Egg Beaters with sugar, vanilla and salt. Gradually add scalded milk and pour into ovenproof dish. Sprinkle with nutmeg and place dish in a warm-water bath. Bake in slow oven 1 hour or until set.
Boil lemon and orange rinds with cloves and cinnamon bark for 5 minutes.
Strain; add juices, sugar and the tea.
Serve piping hot. Makes 3 quarts.

Add the tea bags to the boiling water in a large glass bowl. Let cool. Stir in sugar and water. Add frozen orange juice and lemonade. Stir well. Finally, stir in whiskey. Freeze in a container with a lid. Serve in a glass with Sprite.
Drain green beans and chestnuts.
Mix together the soup, sherry, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss in green beans and chestnuts.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Nice if topped with "canned" onion rings or slivered almonds.

Add flour and spices; mix well.
Stir in rhubarb.
Pour into greased pan; add topping.
Peel carrots; cut in 1/4-inch thick diagonal slices.

Drain.

Stir well.
Add to carrots in saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes longer.
Mix mayonnaise, vegetable oil, grated onion, Worcestershire, Tabasco sauce, dry mustard and eggs and serve over green beans.
Mix all together.
Pour into casserole dish and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Put everything in bowl. Mix together. Place in pan. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Melt 1/4 cup or less margarine in 9 x 13-inch glass pan.
Beat the eggs, then gradually mix in the remaining ingredients one at a time in order.
Pour in the 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for approximately 40 minutes.
Mix first 8 ingredients; melt fat in skillet and brown meatballs.
Mix sugar, water and vinegar.
Spoon over meat. Simmer for 30 to 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
In a bowl, combine cracker crumbs and peanuts.
Stir in 1/4 cup butter and 2 tablespoons peanut butter; mix well.
Set aside 1/2 cup for topping.
Press the remaining crumb mixture into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, in a mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and 1/2 cup peanut butter until smooth.
Beat in sugar and vanilla.
Fold in Cool Whip; spoon over crust.
Drizzle with chocolate; sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture.
Cover and freeze for up to 3 months. Remove from the freezer 15 minutes before serving.
Mix all ingredients in saucepan.
Cook on high heat for 2 minutes,
stirring	constantly.
Cook

Add eggs and applesauce. Gradually stir in flour mixture.

Fold in raisins.
Spoon batter into a nonstick 12-cup fluted pan.

Invert onto a wire rack for cooling. Drizzle sugar and lemon juice over cake.

Cut cheese in pieces, then add to hot milk.
Heat 5 minutes on 1/2 power until cheese is soft. Mix until smooth.

Beat until well mixed.

Remove the chicken with a large spoon and remove the chicken bones and skin.
Skim fat oils from the top of the broth, put the chicken meat back into the pot, add tomatoes and boil for 15 minutes.

Press into an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan.

Add first five ingredients.
Process until smooth.

Mix all other ingredients.

Mix salt with flour; cut in shortening.
Separate egg; save the white.
Add yolk to 2/3 cup water and beat.
Add to flour mixture.
Mix into soft ball stage.
Divide dough in half.
Cook onion and zucchini in salt water for about 5 minutes, then drain well.
Pour into well-greased casserole.
Add Italian seasonings.
Pour tomatoes over top of zucchini and onion.

Stir flour, salt, baking powder and spices together.
Cream sugar, margarine and egg until light.
Add prunes, buttermilk, molasses and vinegar and beat to combine.
Dissolve soda in boiling water.
Stir in flour mixture and soda water.
Drop onto greased baking sheet and bake for 15 to 17 minutes at 350°.

Mix all ingredients (except bread).
Cut top off bread (keep for lid).
Dig out center of bread (keep bread for dipping).
Fill bread with mixture.
Replace top of bread.
Triple wrap bread with foil and place in 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours (or until cheese is melted and mixture is hot all through).

6 servings.

Blend all ingredients with spoon, then hands. Line molds with fine sugar. Press in fondant. If no molds are available, roll into 1 inch or 1/2 inch balls, then flatten with fork or bottom of glass dipped in powdered sugar. May make ahead and freeze.

Mix in remaining ingredients.

Top with more grated cheese and crushed tortilla chips.

Slowly pour into the egg mixture while the blender is running.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Enjoy.

Press a pecan half in the center.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.

d: Drain all fruit.
Add sugar and curry to melted butter. Arrange fruit and nuts in layers in casserole; pour butter mixture over all and bake at 325° for 1 hour.

Add cognac and carefully ignite by touching edge of pan with match flame.
(Always use caution when flaming!) Allow flame to completely die out after several minutes.
Add cream and cook over high heat until mixture reduces and thickens, coating back of spoon.
Stir in cayenne, tarragon, dash of salt and lemon juice.
Arrange chicken on a platter and pour sauce over to serve.
Serves 4.
Cut sausage into 1-inch pieces; saute in oil in large skillet until lightly browned.
Remove from heat.
Saute cut up peppers and onions until tender.
Add sausage and other ingredients. Stir; cook 15 to 20 minutes on low heat.
Serve over noodles, rice or rolls.
Mix all the ingredients together.
Roll into small balls. Flatten and deep fry in oil.
Cook until brown.

Cook broccoli; drain. Spread it in a 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Mix chicken, soup, mayonnaise, mushrooms, curry powder and 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese in medium bowl. Spread chicken mixture over broccoli. Sprinkle 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese over top. Bake in preheated 350° oven for 40 minutes or until heated through. Makes 6 servings.

recipes.t: Cajun Chicken Casserole With Cornbread Crust
d: Combine chicken, soup, celery, green pepper, onion and pimentos in a large bowl.
Stir well.
Pour into a 9 x 14-inch pan or individual casserole dishes.
Combine cornbread mix, chicken stock and melted butter in a large bowl.
Stir well.
Sprinkle over casserole.
Bake in a 350° oven until crust is golden and casserole is bubbly, for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Yields 10 servings.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add mushroom soup; beat and blend with milk and soy sauce.
Mash tofu coarsely, and combine all ingredients; mix well.
Bake in oiled loaf pan, set in a pan of hot water, at 350° about 45 minutes, or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let stand 10 minutes before unmolding.
Brown meat and onion together.
In crock-pot, add all ingredients.
Bake at 300° for about 2 hours (low setting on crock-pot).
Can be baked in a large Corning Ware dish in oven.
To the cooked pasta add the Italian dressing and salad season mix.
Mix well and refrigerator overnight.
Just before serving add the green peppers and tomato.
Mix with mustard or mayonnaise until smooth.
You will need a 3 to 4-quart pot (Dutch oven) and 1 empty Coke bottle.
Combine flour, Crisco and salt.
Cut shortening in flour until it is gravel size.
Put vinegar, egg and water in another bowl and beat, then add to flour mixture.
Flour your hands and form crust into a ball.
Wrap in wax paper and refrigerate for 2 hours before rolling into pie crust.
In large bowl mix onion soup mix, bread crumbs, chili powder, cumin, thyme and pepper.
Dip chicken in bread crumb mixture; coating well.
In large skillet heat 1/2-inch oil and cook chicken over medium heat turning once until tender.
Drain on paper towel. Serve warm and could be served with assorted mustards.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Preheat
oven
to
Mix flour, margarine and powdered sugar in small
bowl.
Press
evenly in bottom and about 5/8-inch up sides of square	pan,
8 x 8 x 2-inches.
If dough is sticky, flour
fingers.
Bake
minutes.
Beat remaining ingredients in a medium
bowl
on medium speed until light and fluffy.
Pour over hot
crust.
Bake	about
25 minutes.
Let stand until cool and cut into small pieces.

Preheat oven to 350°. Grease a 12-cup Bundt pan. Mix cake mix, oil, water and eggs together with mixer on low speed until blended, about 1 minute. Scrape bowl and beat for 2 minutes, still on low speed. Add the container of frosting and continue beating on low speed for about 2 minutes. Pour into pan and bake until a cake tester inserted in cake comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes. Cool cake in pan. Invert onto a plate and cool completely before slicing. No frosting is needed.
Wash celery and cut into small pieces.
Fill celery with cream cheese and add raisins.
Children can assist with this activity.
Peel, core and chop apples.
Cook apples slowly (do not add water).
Cook
in
crock-pot on low temperature for 7 to 8 hours. Makes about 3 pints.
Mix all ingredients together in casserole dish.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Top with remaining Durkee onions.
Broil until crisp and brown.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown sausage; drain.
Add onions, carrot and green pepper; cook until tender. Stir in flour until smooth.
Gradually stir in milk; cook, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and begins to boil. Stir in Worcestershire sauce and sage.
In 3-quart baking dish, combine beans and sausage mixture.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Serve hot with crackers. Makes 10 servings.
Mix first 5 ingredients thoroughly and make a well in center. To well in flour mix and add remaining ingredients.
Mix until no lumps remain.
Pour in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Doesn't need to be greased.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Frost with Peanut Butter Frosting.
In a 2-quart casserole, combine onion and ground meat. Microwave 4 minutes on High (100%).
In a separate bowl, combine the remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Add to meat and onion, stirring to blend.
Cover and microwave 8 minutes on High (100%) or simmer on stove.
Serves 6 to 8.
Grate
corn
from
cobs into a bowl and measure correct amount.
Beat
eggs
vigorously
and
stir
in onion, salt and cayenne.
Heat
milk
until
a
film forms; skim and stir into corn mixture.
Pour
into 6 buttered custard cups and place in a shallow
pan containing about 1 inch of boiling water.
Bake in a preheated 325° oven for 50 to 60 minutes or until a knife inserted in center of custard comes out clean.
Combine half of all the ingredients in electric blender; process until smooth.
Repeat with all the remaining ingredients. Combine mixtures.
Pour into individual glasses.
Makes about
4 cups.
Cream sugar, butter or oleo and eggs (one at a time).
Add flour, baking powder, soda, vanilla and sour cream or buttermilk. In small bowl, mix cinnamon, chopped nuts and sugar.
Pour half of batter in cake pan; put half of topping onto cake, then add remaining cake batter and top with remaining topping.
Bake in greased 13 x 9-inch pan in 350° oven for for 45 to 50 minutes.
Spread rolls on 9 x 13-inch pan.
Saute onion and zucchini in oleo until soft.
Pour over rolls.
Pour eggs over zucchini and onions.
Sprinkle cheese over all.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour to 45 minutes.
Cut in squares.
Mix together all ingredients.
Bake in covered 2-quart casserole dish 1 hour or until done.
Serves 6.
Sift flour, measure 7 cups and sift with soda, salt and spices.
Sift 1/2 cup flour and set aside to use only if needed. Measure sugar, butter and molasses.
Turn molasses into small pan and warm slightly; add brown sugar and stir until melted.
Add butter, blending in well.
Stir in eggs, one at a time.
Batter is smooth.
Add orange peel.
Stir in dry ingredients.
Gradually add sufficient flour to make a soft dough that can be kneaded.
Knead until smooth.
Keep tightly covered and refrigerate overnight. Roll out and cut in desired shapes.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Beat egg.
Stir in poultry seasoning, salt and cheese; mix with rice.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Shape by rounded teaspoonfuls into 1-inch balls.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Heat 2 to 3 inches of oil.
Fry rice balls until golden brown; drain.
Makes about 15 rice balls.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cinnamon. Mix one egg, 1/2 cup milk and 3 tablespoons oil; stir into flour mixture.
Turn into well-oiled 9-inch pan.
Mix all ingredients and pour in a greased pie plate (use a bigger pan and make thinner for an appetizer).
Bake at 400° for 35 minutes.
One and one-fourth hours before serving, cook yams in boiling, salted water for 25 minutes or until tender.
Drain and cool.
In a 1-quart saucepan, mix cornstarch, nutmeg or cinnamon, salt and granulated sugar.
Stir in water.
Cook over low heat until sauce is clear.
Stir in lemon juice and brandy.
Heat oven to 375°. Peel potatoes; slice crosswise, 1/4 to 1/2-inch thick.
Put into buttered shallow baking dish.
Pour on sauce, then bake 30 minutes or until glazed, basting occasionally.
When glazed, sprinkle with miniature marshmallows and broil until golden, if desired.
Using large glass or plastic bowl that has flared top, layer vegetables in order named; do not mix.
Spread mayonnaise over top to seal.
Sprinkle sugar, then cheese over this.
Seal with covering of plastic wrap or tight fitting lid.
Refrigerate 8 to 12 hours.
When ready to serve, sprinkle top with crumbled fresh fried bacon or artificial bacon bits.
Serves 10 to 12.
Brown ground beef and drain well.
Add to other ingredients in crock-pot.
Stir well, cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours (high for 2 to 3 hours).
Serve with tossed salad and crusty French bread for a quick and easy meal.
Cook potatoes in boiling water for 14 minutes or until tender. Drain.
Mix mayonnaise and mustard in a large bowl.
Add potatoes, bacon and chives.
Mix lightly.
Refrigerate until serving (at least 1 to 2 hours).
Makes 6 servings.
Heat oven to 400°.
Generously grease 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Cook beef and onion in 10-inch skillet until beef is brown; drain.
Stir in soup, vegetables and milk.
Stir baking mix and water in baking dish until moistened; spread evenly.
Spread beef mixture over batter.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Blend filling together (cream cheese, butter, sugar, 1 egg, cornstarch, milk and vanilla).
Beat at high speed until smooth. Set aside.
Mix the first 3 ingredients with mayonnaise.
Add pimiento, salt and sugar.
Blend cake mix, egg and 1/3 cup water in square pan, 8 x 8-inch.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Mix remaining ingredients and gradually pour over brown sugar.
Bake until cake springs back, 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes.
Spoon into dessert dishes.
Serve warm; whipped cream optional.
Cream eggs, sugar and Crisco.
Add milk, baking powder, flour, vanilla and coconut.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Heat the brown sugar and butter in a medium-size saucepan over medium-low heat until the butter has melted.
Dissolve the coffee in the hot water and stir into the butter mixture.
Let cool to room temperature.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter an 8 x 11-inch baking pan.
When the butter mixture is cool, beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Stir into the butter mixture with a wooden spoon.
Stir in the walnuts and chocolate.
Spread evenly in the pan with a rubber spatula. Bake 25 to 30 minutes until light brown.
Cool and cut into bars. Frost and sprinkle with nuts, if desired.
Makes 20 brownies.
Boil the first 5 ingredients until clear.
Pour over slightly beaten egg white; continue to beat until spreading consistency. Add vanilla.
Grease a 2-quart souffle dish.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Cook grits in milk and water according to package directions.
Add salt.
When grits are cooked, add pepper, nutmeg, Tabasco and all but 1/2 cup of cheese.
Mix well and then allow to cool slightly. Add egg yolks.
Beat egg whites stiff and add half of them to the grit mixture; beat well.
Fold in remaining egg whites with a rubber spatula.
Spoon into the souffle dish and sprinkle remaining cheese over the top.
Bake 25 minutes.
Melt chocolate in a double boiler pan.
Stir in instant coffee.
Cool.
Beat egg yolks and fold in chocolate mixture. Beat egg whites, fold in chocolate mixture. Beat whipping cream with salt and fold in mixture.
Mix together carrots, cream cheese, Parmesan cheese and fines herbes.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Peel and chunk potatoes.
You can also add chopped onion to taste.
Put in small casserole with tight fitting lid.
Don't add any water.
Cook on high for 3 minutes.
Add small pat of oleo.
Stir well to coat the potatoes.
Then add any of the seasonings and cook, covered, for 1 more minute or until tender.

Layer chicken, onion slices and Velveeta cheese in order listed in 11 x 14-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with 1/2 of chips. Pour mixture of tomatoes and soups over chips. Top with remaining chips. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. (Does best if covered with foil during baking. Uncover last 10 minutes to brown top.) Makes 12 servings.
Pour the liquid from the pears into a saucepan with the 2 packages Jell-O.
Heat just before it boils.
Blend pears, cream cheese and Cool Whip in blender.
Fold in Jell-O.
Pour mixture into 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish sprayed with Pam.
Let set in refrigerator until firm.
Cut into squares.
Combine chicken, celery soup, mushrooms and liquid, celery, green pepper and steak sauce in a large skillet.
Heat slowly, until bubbly hot, about 10 minutes.
Saute pork steak; salt and pepper to taste.
Brown hamburger; salt and pepper to taste.
Put Ro-Tel and tomatoes in blender and blend about 30 seconds.
Cut jalapenos into small pieces.
Put all ingredients into large soup pot, add 1/2 jar of minced garlic and cook (simmer) for about 1 hour or so.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Wash chops and season on both sides. Beat together egg and milk.
Dip chops in mixture, then coat on both sides with crushed cornflakes.
Place in baking dish and bake at 350° about 45 minutes or until the meat is cooked through and the juices run clear.
It is not necessary to turn chops during cooking.
Serve in sandwich or with baked potato or other vegetable.
Beat margarine and sugar until creamy.
Add remaining ingredients, except powdered sugar; mix well.
Cover.
Chill 30 minutes.
Cream together butter and oil.
Add sugar and beat until mixture is smooth.
Add egg yolks and beat well.
Combine flour and soda and add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk. Stir in vanilla.
Add coconut and nuts.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into mixture.
Pour batter into three greased and floured 8-inch pans.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool and frost with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Put roast in baking pan.
Add onion, garlic and soup.
Add bouillon cubes to water; pour over.
Cover with foil; bake at 350°.
May need to add more water.
Slice roast; serve on French bread with gravy.
Mix
sugar,
salt
and	cocoa.	Add
eggs and mix well. Stir in vanilla and milk.
Add melted oleo, then coconut.
One cup of nuts may be added, if desired.
Pour into 2 unbaked pie shells. Bake at
350° for 40 minutes or until firm.
Cool and serve.
Brown meat; drain.
Add seasoning and water.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
Prepare rice.
Melt cheese and Ro-Tel tomatoes; mix well.
Combine meat, rice and cheese dip.
Top with chips.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
*Weight Watchers makes a fat-free Parmesan cheese.
Peel orange, remove white membrane.
Chop rind and pulp fine. Chop or grind cranberries.
Combine apples, oranges and cranberries and drain well, reserving the juice.
Pour juice in measuring cup and add enough water to make two cups.
Heat one cup juice and sugar in a small saucepan, stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Pour over gelatin in bowl, stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in remaining juice and cool thoroughly.
Add drained fruits, nuts and celery.
Pour into mold and chill until firm.
Unmold on lettuce greens with pink gelatin cubes and pink mayonnaise.
Dilute Jell-O in hot water and let set slightly.
Add crushed pineapple; let set until firm.
Mix Dream Whip according to package; add cream cheese.
Whip together and put over set Jell-O. Cook until thick the eggs, sugar, flour and juices.
Cool, then spread over Jell-O and cheese topping.
Butter 1 side of each bread slice; lay 6 slices flat, buttered side down, in a lightly buttered 13 x 9-inch pan.
Mix ingredients. Pour into greased casserole dish. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes. Serve with tortilla chips.
Combine sugar, nuts and egg and mix.
Using 1 rounded teaspoonful per cookie, shape into balls.
Bake on lightly greased cookie sheet in a preheated 300° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Breakfast Stuff(Stuff:  An Unspecified Material Substance Or Aggregate Of Matter
d: Brown sausage and drain well.
