Mix Bisquick, milk and eggs. Spread mix in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine sour cream, poppy seed, salt and eggs.
Spread this mix over the sausage.
Sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Homemade Chicken Soup(The Kind That Cures The Flu)
d: Cook chicken in large stockpot; cool, debone and cut up into small pieces.
Return to pot in which broth from chicken was cooked.
If more broth is needed, you may use clear, canned broth. Add clean, cut up carrots and celery.
Add onions which have been chopped and chopped fresh parsley tops and stems.
Cook in broth until tender.
You will need to salt and pepper to taste.
May serve over cooked rice or noodles.
Prepare pasta according to package directions; drain.
In large bowl, combine pasta and remaining ingredients; toss to mix. Serve immediately or cover and chill.
Stir gently before serving. Refrigerate leftovers.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Bring 1 cup cider to a boil; add gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Stir in remaining cider.
Chill until consistency of unbeaten egg white.
Fold in apple, celery and pecans.
Pour into a 4-cup mold.
Chill until set.
Unmold on a lettuce lined plate and top with a dollop of mayonnaise.
Brown meat in butter.
Add: soup, rice and water.
Cover and cook for about 5 minutes or until rice is done.
Mix all ingredients and form into 1-inch balls; chill.
Dip into chocolate and place on wax paper to set.
Mix all ingredients.
Stir well, cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.
Serve with vegetables or Snackwell pepper crackers.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Cook broccoli according to package directions to tender-crisp.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large, heavy skillet over moderate heat.
Stir in garlic, basil leaves, onions and parsley.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Turn off heat and gently mix in with cooked broccoli.
In a casserole dish, place crumbled angel food cake in bottom and cover with crushed pineapple with juice.
Prepare pudding mix according to package directions and pour over pineapple.
Place sliced bananas over pudding; cover with Cool Whip.
Let chill before serving.

In a large kettle, cook potatoes, carrots and celery in water with bouillon cubes until tender. Saute onions in butter until soft. Stir in flour and salt and pepper, gradually add sour cream, stirring constantly until desired consistency. If too thick, add plain milk.
Yield: 2 1/2 quarts.
Saute onion in margarine.
Mix soup and Cheez Whiz.
Add cooked and well drained broccoli.
Top with onion rings or cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Cut up the chicken and cover with 3 quarts water.
Add the salt and saffron and stew until tender.
Remove chicken from stock and set aside the legs and breast for chicken salad.
Take the rest of the meat from the bones and return meat to broth.
Add the corn and noodles to soup.
Season with pepper.
Cook 15 minutes longer.
Before serving, add parsley and chopped eggs.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Beat eggs in a large bowl on high until foamy.
Beat in flour, sugar and brown sugar.
Beat in butter.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts.
Pour into pie shell and bake for 55-60 minutes.
Serve warm with ice cream or cool whip.
Boil a whole chicken in a Dutch oven pot with water.
(Cover chicken over half way with water) after chicken is done, take out of broth to cool.
Mix flour and shortening in together first. Then add all other ingredients.
(I beat my egg in with the 5 tablespoons of chicken broth.) After mixing all ingredients, mixture should be a soft dough.
Roll out dough very thin and let stand for about 10 minutes.
Then cut into strips and drop into boiling broth.
Simmer about 15 minutes, then add deboned chicken to dumplings.

Preheat oven to 350°. Melt butter and chocolate in saucepan. Remove from heat and stir in sugar. Add eggs and vanilla. Stir in flour, baking powder and salt. Add morsels. Spread mixture in a 9-inch square pan. Bake 25 to 30 minutes. Cool and cut into squares. Store in airtight container.
Mix, chill and serve with apples, grapes, bananas and other fruit of your choice.
Mix sugar and shortening until light and creamy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add milk and flour alternately.
Stir in flavorings.
Start baking in cold oven at 275° in tube pan for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Mix well.
Refrigerating overnight makes it better.
In a large pan, brown ground beef; drain.
Add tomato sauce, mushrooms and onion; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Prepare noodles according to package directions.
Prepare 24 hours ahead.

recipes.t: Copy Cat Cheese Biscuits(Similar To Those Served By A Popular Seafood Restaurant
d: Preheat oven to 450°.
Mix baking mix, cheese and water.
Drop by large spoonfuls onto greased baking sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes.
After baking, while hot, brush with melted butter, mixed with the parsley, garlic and Italian seasoning.
Serve hot.
Makes about 12 biscuits.
Place the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, cream the shortening and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat the eggs and add to the creamed mixture.
Mash the bananas (3/4 cup banana pulp) and mix with the sour milk and vanilla.
Add the banana mixture alternately with the dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Pour the batter into 2 greased 9-inch round layer pans or a 9 x 13-inch pan and bake 1/2 hour at 375° for the round pans and 40 minutes at 350° for the 9 x 13-inch oblong pan.
Cut English muffins in half.
Set aside.
In large bowl mix together olives, cheese, onions, mayonnaise and salt.
Spread mixture evenly over 12 muffin halves.
Place on baking sheet. Broil 3 to 4 minutes or until cheese is bubbly and melted.
Cut in half before serving.
Garnish with parsley sprigs.
You will need 1 (8 x 20 x 3-inch) pan with cover.
Cut sweet potatoes in half crosswise.
Cook in boiling water to cover, for 10 minutes.
Drain and cool.
Cut crosswise into 1/2 inch slices.
Mix together flour, sugar, cocoa, salt and baking soda. Combine shredded zucchini, vanilla and oil.
Mix with dry ingredients.
Add nuts.
Spread into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
May frost or serve as is.
Very good!
Combine all ingredients, mixing well.
Place in a greased 5 1/2 cup ring mold.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 45 minutes. Unmold and serve on platter with cooked peas in the center.
This makes a very pretty vegetable to serve with chicken, fish or beef. You may make the ring and freeze.
Reheat, fill with peas and serve immediately.
Pack first four ingredients in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add vanilla ice cream.
Keep frozen until ready to serve.
Heat oven to 350°.
Cut fish into serving size pieces. Arrange in greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with parsley, basil, oregano and pepper.
Top with spaghetti sauce, then sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until fish flakes easily at the thickest part.
Cream together eggs, sugar and oil.
Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Add alternately with baby food.
Bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes.
For icing, combine cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla and butter or oleo.
Combine
vinegar,
sugar and salt in saucepan, stirring until sugar
dissolves.
Bring to a boil.
(If you desire, add ajinomoto when
liquid
becomes clear.) You can make a larger "batch" at a time and keep it on hand, making it handy to make sushi,
inari, maze-gohan, California roll, etc., frequently. The "su"
is
also very
good to make "sunomono" or for other salads.
Spread 1 cup whipped topping on bottom of pie crust.
Combine milk and pudding mix. Blend with wire whisk or mixer for 1 minute. Fold in 1 1/2 cups whipped topping.
Spread over whipped topping in crust. Spread remaining whipped topping over top, leaving a 1-inch border and forming a depression in center of the whipped topping.
Spoon cherry pie filling in the center. Chill 3 hours.
Place dry beef in
bottom
of
dish.
Wrap bacon around chicken.
Spread soup over top of all.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 300° for 2 hours, then 350° for 1/2 hour, uncovered.

Sift flour; measure and resift 3 times with baking powder and salt. Cream butter and shortening; blend in sugar gradually. Add beaten egg and beat until smooth and fluffy. Add flour mixture alternately with milk, beating well after each addition. Spoon into buttered muffin pans, filling about 2/3 full. Bake at 400° for 25 minutes. Makes 24 muffins.
Sift together the flour, soda and salt.
In separate bowl, cream together the butter, shortening, sugar and vanilla.
Add egg to creamed mixture and beat until fluffy.
Add dry ingredients plus milk to creamed mixture and stir until smooth.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Flatten with bottom of glass which has been dipped into sugar.
Bake in a preheated 350° to 400° oven for about 12 minutes.
Cool.
Yields 5 1/2 dozen 2-inch cookies.
Mix ingredients together; roll into walnut size balls.
Bake on cookie sheet at 350° until done (approximately 30 to 45 minutes).
Prepare the sauce while meat balls are baking.
Combine dry ingredients.
Add cold milk to egg yolk.
Add this mixture to scalded milk (total 2 1/2 cups milk includes all).
Cook very slowly until thick and creamy.
Add vanilla.
Cool.
Pour into unbaked cooled pie crust, 8 or 9-inch.
Add meringue by beating 3 egg whites (room temperature) with 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar until foamy.
Gradually add 3 tablespoons sugar and beat until stands in peaks.
Put on pie.
Brown in 350° oven 12 minutes.
Cool out of draft.
Mix cake mix, cinnamon, almond extract and vanilla.
Bake at 350° and let cool.
Bake potato.
Grill bacon until crisp.
Drain, leaving 3 tablespoons grease.
Add onion and saute slowly.
Remove from heat.
Cut shallow lengthwise strip from potatoes and scoop out inside and add to skillet.
Add cheese, crumbled bacon, sour cream and seasonings.
Mix and mash with spoon to blend.
Return to low heat and heat through.
Stuff into potatoes.
Drizzle with melted butter and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly grease cookie sheets.
Cream the butter with sugars in a large bowl until blended.
Add egg and vanilla.
Beat until fluffy.
Combine flour, cocoa, baking powder and baking soda in a small bowl.
Stir into creamed mixture with oats, chocolate chips, raisins and nuts.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto prepared cookie sheets.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned around edges.
Remove to wire racks to cool.
Makes about 4 dozen cookies.
Let margarine get to room temperature.
Add Crisco and sugar, beat well.
Add eggs one at a time, beating 1 minute after each, alternately with milk.
Add other ingredients.
Bake at 350° until done.
Cook beans for 15 minutes. Layer on tray and let cool. Mix taco mix and add cream cheese. Layer on top of beans. Chop pepper, tomato, onion and lettuce and layer in order. Serve with chips.
Marinate the meat according to directions. Grill the vegetables until tender-crisp.
Remove and keep warm.
Grill meat until preferred doneness.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Mix together soup, broccoli, rice, process cheese spread, half the onions and water. Spoon into 1 quart casserole dish. Bake 35 minutes. Top with remaining onions. Bake 5 minutes more.

recipes.t: Cabbage Casserole In A Rice Cooker
d: Brown ground meat and sausage together.
Drain oil when cooked.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl; then transfer into rice cooker.
When cooked, leave in cooker for 10 minutes before serving.
Saute peppers and onions in small amount of oil.
Blend all ingredients together.
Pour into casserole.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
In skillet, brown frankfurters and cook onion in butter until tender.
Add soup, beans and water.
Bring to boil.
Pour into 2-quart shallow baking dish (12 x 8 x 2-inch).
Combine corn muffin mix, milk and egg.
Spoon around edge of baking dish.
Bake in 400° oven for 20 minutes or until done.
Makes about 5 1/2 cups.
Bring cheeses to room temperature.
On a sheet of wax paper, roll out Velveeta.
Divide the cream cheese into small portions and put on top of Velveeta.
Roll again.
Spread the green chilies over cheeses.
Roll up as for a jelly roll.
Divide into 2 rolls. Serve with crackers.
Mix all ingredients well, then chill overnight.
Serve with chips or raw vegetables.
Roll pork chops in flour and onion mixture.
Brown pork chops in oiled skillet.
Add whole tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Cover with tomato sauce and simmer until tender.
Cook hamburger meat and onion until done; drain.
Add chili powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper and red pepper.
Cook for a few minutes.
Add Cheez Whiz and cook until melted.
Spread meat on flat tostada shells.
Shred cabbage on top of meat (may want to sprinkle red pepper on if you like hot stuff).
Place another tostada shell on top of cabbage.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In a bowl, combine flour, oats, sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Add butter.
Mix well.
Cream butter.
Add sugar and beat well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each addition.
Dissolve soda in persimmon pulp.
Mix into creamed ingredients.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves.
Stir into creamed mixture.
In a large bowl, combine pudding mix, whipped topping and salad dressing; mix well. Fold in remaining ingredients. Leave in bowl. Serve immediately or chill.
Cook until soft ball stage the sugar, Karo and water.
After soft ball stage, add peanuts.
Cook until dark.
Remove from burner.
Add baking soda, vinegar and salt.
Mix together and pour onto a buttered cookie sheet.
Cool, then break apart.
Put in all ingredients and blend until smooth.
Put in Dixie cups or popsicle molds.
Put plastic spoon or popsicle stick in middle and freeze until frozen.
Cut bread; add a little butter.
Beat eggs with milk, salt and mustard.
Layer bread, sausage and cheese.
Pour egg mixture on top and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Brown ground beef and onions; drain.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce and seasonings.
Add the two cheeses.
Let simmer while you cook and drain macaroni; add to other ingredients and let simmer 10 minutes.
Pour into two oblong; greased baking dishes and cook at
350° for 20 minutes.
This can be frozen for use at a later date.
Mix all ingredients together and pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into unbaked deep dish pie shell. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until solid.
To Cream Soup Base, add corn, milk, onion, chervil, salt and bouillon cube.
Heat to simmering, cooking long enough to dissolve bouillon cube.
Serve garnished with parsley and paprika.
Combine all but lettuce and egg.
Toss lightly, cover.
Chill at least 1 hour.
Just before serving, add lettuce and egg.
Toss.
Combine sugar, corn syrup, water and salt.
Cook to very hard ball stage (260°).
Slowly pour syrup in a thin stream over beaten egg whites, beating constantly.
Beat until mixture holds shape (about 4 to 5 minutes).
Stir in vanilla.
Drop by heaping tablespoonfuls on waxed paper, lifting and twirling spoon to form a peak.
If divinity becomes too stiff for twirling, add a few drops hot water.
Makes about 1 1/2 dozen.

recipes.t: Beef Casserole(From The Files Of Louella Scott Williams)
d: Lightly brown the ground beef, onion and green pepper in oil, then add the soups, water, garlic and cooked spaghetti.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and top with grated cheese.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Beat eggs until fluffy.
Add oil, sugar, vanilla and zucchini. Mix well.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Add raisins, pineapple and nuts.
Blend.
Wash eggplant; pare and cut in 1/2-inch slices.
Or wash squash and cut crosswise in slices.
Dip slices in well seasoned flour.
Saute slowly in butter for 10 to 15 minutes, or until crisp and browned, turning occasionally.
Serve hot.
Makes 6 servings.
Boil potatoes in jacket until done.
Peel and mash.
Add butter, sugar, vanilla, sprinkle of nutmeg & cinnamon.
Combine the beaten eggs and milk.
Mix with potatoes until well blended. Pour into pie shells.
Bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients for 2 minutes with electric mixer. Fold in nuts.
Bake in greased tube pan 50 to 55 minutes at 350°. Cool before serving.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Blend dry ingredients and 1/2 sour cream.
Mix well all remaining sour cream.
Beat well.
Bake at 350° until done.

recipes.t: Pumpkin Cake(This Cake Is So Tasty It Doesn'T Need Frosting)
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together and beat well.
Bake in tube or Bundt pan for 1 hour.
May sprinkle with confectioners sugar, if desired.
Mix all together. Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Place ham, cheese and croutons in the bottom of a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix remaining ingredients; pour this mixture over crouton mixture and refrigerate overnight.
Cook until barely tender carrots, potatoes and celery.
Add dinner cuts, onions and a dash of salt.
Add mushroom soup.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cover with pie crust.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Cook chicken slowly in covered nonstick skillet on both sides. Add a little water if it wants to stick.
Blend cake mix, pudding mix, water, eggs and oil in large mixer bowl; beat for 4 minutes.
Stir in coconut and walnuts. Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cool in pans for 15 minutes.
Remove and cool on racks.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Line cupcake pans with paper liners. Place vanilla wafer in bottom of each liner.
In small bowl beat next 5 items until light and fluffy.
Fill liners 3/4 full with mixture.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until set.
Top each with spoonful of filling and 1 teaspoon nuts.
Chill.
Serves 24.
Cut up cabbage, onion and carrot.
Mix.
Add sugar and salad dressing.
Mix.
This is so easy and so great to have on hand in the freezer. Toasts like a dream or serve with cream cheese.
Melt 1 stick butter, mix 1/2 cup powdered sugar and graham cracker crumbs.
This makes first layer of cake.
Press mixture into bottom of loaf pan.
Layer ingredients in order listed in a microwave-safe pan. Microwave on High for 5 minutes or bake in oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix sugar and cocoa.
Add corn syrup and milk.
Stir.
Cook on medium heat, stirring often, until it reaches a soft ball stage (235° on a candy thermometer).
Add butter and vanilla.
Let cool. Beat until it thickens and loses its shine.
Pour into greased pan to harden.
(Nuts may be added just before pouring into pan.)
Mix flour, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Heat margarine, Coke and cocoa in pan to boiling.
Pour over mixture. Add eggs, buttermilk, soda and vanilla. Stir in marshmallows.
Batter will be thin; marshmallows will float.
Cook in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan for 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Frost cake while hot.
Beet greens may be prepared in the same ways that you prepare spinach or Swiss chard, but they must be young and small to be tasty.
Try cooking the greens in boiling salted water for 5 to 8 minutes.
Drain, chop and add the butter or margarine.
Toss with a fork until butter is melted.
Add the horseradish and lemon juice; mix well.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serves 4.
Blend first seven ingredients for two minutes.
Put into greased 9 or 10-inch pie plate.
Arrange peach slices on top. Blend cream cheese, juice and 1/2 cup sugar together.
Beat until creamy and place in center of peaches; spread out to about 1 inch from edge of pie plate.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Can be served warm or cold.
Place all ingredients in a blender and mix until smooth. Serve over various lettuce salads.

recipes.t: Waldorf Turkey Toss With Apple Dressing
d: Combine applesauce, honey, vinegar, poppy seed, paprika and lemon peel. Gradually add oil, beating with electric mixer until slightly thickened.

recipes.t: Glad'S Own Custard Pie(Ed'S Very Favorite)
d: Beat eggs; add sugar.
Scald milk and add to mixture.
Add nutmeg; pour into unbaked crust.
Bake at 350° until filling is firm.
Top with meringue.
Brown slightly.
Sift dry ingredients into mixing bowl. Stir in orange rind and nuts. Beat eggs in small bowl. Add orange juice and oil.
Mix well. Add to flour mixture.
Mix until moistened.
Fill greased tins 2/3 full. Bake at 425° for 18 to 20 minutes. Makes 18 muffins.
Melt
butter
in
oblong baking pan.
Pour out and save for later.
In	pan,
put
pie	filling on bottom and top with crushed pineapple	and
juice.
Cover
this with the dry cake mix.
Top off with reserved melted butter.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°
Prepare enough grits to serve 12.
Mix all ingredients in grits while hot.
Bake at 350°.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brown sausage meat; drain.
Press one can crescent rolls in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch casserole dish.
Top with sausage and cheese.
Beat eggs; add salt and pepper.
Pour eggs over sausage and cheese.
Bake in a 375° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Saute
shrimp in oil
until
pink.
Remove
shrimp
and saute onion, celery and bell
pepper.
Add
rice to shrimp and eggplant mixture.
Pour into
buttered 2 1/2 quart dish.
Pour soup over top.
Top with grated cheese and then buttered bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
You will need one 8-inch clay flowerpot.
Melt butter.
Add brown sugar and corn syrup and blend.
Pour mixture into bottom of 8 x 8-inch or 10-inch round pan.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Peel and slice apple.
Spread apple slices on top of nuts.
Dip each refrigerated roll in sugar-cinnamon mixture (one side only).
Place sugar side down in the pan.
After placing all rolls in pan, sprinkle remaining mixture over all.
Bake in 375° oven and turn out onto a large plate or tray.
Let sit for 30 seconds, then lift off and serve warm.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease cookie sheets.
Combine first four ingredients and mix well with spoon.
(Dough will be thick.)
Add vanilla chips and nuts.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Let stand on cookie sheet 1 minute before removing to wire rack.
Yields 2 dozen large or 4 dozen small cookies.
In a medium saucepan over very low heat, melt chocolate, stirring constantly; remove from heat.
Add butter, stirring until melted; stir in liqueur and orange peel, if desired.
Transfer to a medium bowl; cover and refrigerate until mixture is fudge-like, about 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cut a 3-inch round from each slice of bread.
Brush inside of 2 miniature muffin tins generously with butter.
Gently fit bread rounds into each mold to form a cup. Bake 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and cinnamon; set aside. Cream shortening and sugars; add eggs and beat. Add flour mixture and oats. Drop onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Simmer all ingredients and then add cheese.
Stir until completely mixed.
Serve with tortilla chips and quesadillas.

Preheat oven to 350°. To cook chicken, you can either boil for 20 to 25 minutes or place in a microwave-safe dish; cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on High. Turn and cook another 2 to 3 minutes or until cooked through and no longer pink inside. Let cool. Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. In a 9 x 13-inch baking dish, combine chicken, salt, pepper, rice and soup. Mix well. Top with cheese, then with bread cubes. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbly and golden brown.
Combine all ingredients, except the bread.
Use some of the reserved clam fluid to thin it.
Cut the top off the bread.
Break out the insides and set aside.
Mix cake mix, vanilla pudding, 1 cup water, 1/2 cup oil and the eggs together on medium speed until well blended.
Fold in the poppy seed.
Prepare Bundt or tube pan by greasing with butter and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes. Cool 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put 4 to 6 slices of bacon on top and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or until juice cooks down.
Place potatoes in casserole dish.
Mix soup and milk.
Pour over potatoes.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts and is bubbly.
Bring first three ingredients to a boil. Take off heat and add peanut butter, vanilla and oats.
Drop by spoonful onto wax paper.
Mix sugar and eggs.
Beat.
Mix all dry ingredients.
Add to eggs and sugar mixture alternately with oil and coffee.
Beat well. Add raisins, apples and nuts.
Cook at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Let cool.
Add Cream Cheese Icing.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add sugar, syrup, butter, salt and vanilla.
Continue to beat until thoroughly blended.
Stir in peanuts.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 45 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.
May be topped with whipped cream or ice cream.
Mix sugar, milk and soda thoroughly and cook over medium heat until small amount tested in cold water forms small ball.
Add butter and return to heat until butter has melted.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and beat until mixture begins to thicken.
Add pecans; mix thoroughly and drop in thin patties onto waxed paper or foil.
Yields 20 to 24 pralines.
Blend eggs, margarine, sour cream and corn.
Add salt and muffin mix.
Pour into greased 9 x 12-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
This is best when served hot.
Simmer onion and drippings.
Add beef and simmer until brown. Mix all other ingredients.
Add beans last so they will not be mushy.
Add all ingredients to meat and bring to a boil.
Simmer 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together in order given.
Beat well. Chill dough 1 hour.
Shape into small balls.
Put on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Do not overbake.
Let cool on cookie sheet before removing.
In a large bowl, cut broccoli into bite-size pieces.
Crumble bacon into broccoli and add chopped onion.
In a small bowl, mix mayonnaise, vinegar and sugar.
Stir well.
Stir into broccoli gently until broccoli and bacon are well coated.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add remaining ingredients. Pour into container and chill until firm.
Prepare German chocolate cake mix as directed on package, substituting Egg Beaters and applesauce for eggs and oil.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan, sprayed with low-fat cooking spray, as directed.
Pour condensed milk over hot cake (in pan).
Let cool. Spread caramel topping.
Sprinkle Grape-Nuts.
Top with Cool Whip. Refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Delicious and guilt-free!
Use meat mixture to fill and roll about 12 to 15 flour tortillas.
Place rolled tortillas in cooking dish.
Heat oil in wok or large skillet until hot.
Add cabbage, onion, pepper, garlic powder, sugar, salt and pepper.
Stir-fry until cabbage is just tender and light green, about 3 minutes. Add water and cover; remove from heat.
Let stand 3 to 5 minutes. Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Combine first five ingredients.
Stir in pecans.
Combine remaining ingredients and add to flour mixture, stirring until dry ingredients are moistened.
Spoon batter into 2 greased and floured 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool in pan 10 minutes and remove and leave on wire racks.
Mix first 4 ingredients, then add flour to thicken slightly. Add the next 3 ingredients and mix.
Add flour until right for punching.
Lard sides of pan.
Knead a few minutes more.
Let rise 2 times.
Make into large 3-inch buns.
Let raise.
Bake at 350° and let cool.
Slice each bun in 2 or 3 slices.
Dry in low oven until crisp.
Drain all canned vegetables. Mix oil, vinegar, sugar and pepper. Pour over vegetables and mix well. Best if refrigerated overnight.
Boil together margarine or butter and milk.
Cream together eggs and sugar with a pinch of salt.
Beat well.
Add flavoring. Add flour.
Beat in warm milk.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Chop cabbage and green onions.
Add almonds, sesame seed and cooked chicken breasts.
Combine Top Ramen flavor packets, salt, pepper, sugar, vinegar and oil.
Pour over salad and add crushed Top Ramen noodles.
Melt margarine and marshmallows in pan over low heat.
Chop dates and nuts.
Add to margarine-marshmallow mixture.
Spread about 1 cup graham cracker crumbs on wax paper.
Shape mixture into long roll.
Lay on graham crackers and roll up.
Chill; slice thin.

Let cream cheese soften at room temperature for about 1 hour. Using plastic gloves, mix cream cheese, ham or turkey (use as much as desired), green onions, red pepper and Worcestershire sauce; mix well and form into a ball. Roll in pecans until covered and store in refrigerator. Serve with your favorite crackers.

recipes.t: Frosty Orange Nog Without Ice Cream
d: Place ingredients in blender and blend until smooth.
Heat milk and sugar to rolling boil in 2-quart saucepan, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Add chocolate and salt.
Stir until chocolate melts, then beat with rotary beater until smooth.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and vanilla. Keeps well in jar in refrigerator (if the family doesn't find it).
Dissolve jello in water and stir in strawberries until thawed. Add a little water.
Add bananas.
Pour half of this mixture in a pan.
Chill until firm.
Spread evenly with the sour cream.
Pour remaining jello on top.
Chill until firm and cut in squares.
Top with dollops of sour cream.
Serves 6.
Mix well and shape into loaf; cook in covered pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Last 10 minutes, remove foil and let meat brown.

In a saucepan, combine sugar, eggs, lemon juice and salt. Cook and stir over medium heat until temperature reaches 160° until mixture is thickened. Cool completely. Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Drain and rinse in cold water. Place in a large bowl. Drain pineapple, reserving juice. Pour juice over the spaghetti. Stir in apples. Toss gently. Drain. Stir in the egg mixture. Add pineapple. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Fold in whipped topping just before serving. Garnish with walnuts and cherries.
Place half of the sliced apples in a buttered casserole dish. Cover with half of the carrot slices.
Combine dry ingredients; sprinkle half of the mix over carrots.
Repeat the layers; pour orange juice over the top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Bake pie crust 7 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Reduce oven temperature to 325°.
In medium bowl, combine milk, light brown sugar, cognac, light corn syrup, pumpkin pie spice and salt.
Add canned pumpkin and beaten eggs.
Blend well. Slowly pour pumpkin mixture into prepared pie shell.
Bake in a 325° oven until filling is barely set in the center, about 40 minutes.
Cool.
Garnish with whipped cream, if desired.
Makes 8 servings.
Wash cauliflower and
separate into flowerets; set aside.
In a large saucepan, melt butter.
Saute onion until soft and transparent.
Stir in garlic.
Saute briefly, being careful not to burn.
Stir in rice and coat with butter.
Add pepper to broth; bring to a boil.
Lower heat to simmer.
Leave uncovered and cook 20 minutes.
Add cauliflower; cover.
Simmer 5 to 10 minutes until cauliflower is just tender.
Sprinkle with cheese and parsley. Serve hot from the pot.
Serve in wide rimmed soup bowls.
Add extra cheese, if desired.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Mix well.
Shape into 2 logs; wrap in foil.
Store in refrigerator.
Cut into slices. Yields 4 dozen.
Sift flour and salt.
Put cream cheese and butter in a bowl and blend.
Add sifted ingredients; blend and cover.
Chill.
Heat oven to 350°.
Divide dough into small portions.
Roll on floured board about 1/8 inch thick and 3 inches square.
Place a scant tablespoonful of preserves in center of dough and fold 2 opposite corners to center.
Pinch and seal.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake 20 minutes until edges are lightly browned.
Put 1/2 crumbs in casserole.
Add shrimp, mushrooms and 1/2 cheese.
Top with remainder of bread and cheese.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add seasonings and milk; mix.
Pour over the casserole. Bake at 325° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
(May be prepared ahead of time and refrigerated.)
Combine flour, salt and pepper; dredge chicken pieces.
Heat oil in large skillet; add chicken and brown well on both sides. Turn chicken skin side up and add water.
Bring to a boil; cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Place chicken on platter and keep warm. Add vegetables to skillet.
Bring to a full boil over medium heat, separating vegetables with fork.
Stir until sauce cubes are blended.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in catsup and serve over chicken.
Makes 3 servings.
Bake potatoes.
Let cool.
Peel and cube.
In large skillet, fry bacon.
Remove bacon and allow to cool, then crumble.
Saute onions and peppers in bacon drippings.
Add potatoes and stir, heating thoroughly.
Add bacon last.
Serve while hot.
Mix and pour into a tube pan and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Heat butter over low heat until golden brown.
Remove from heat.
Beat in sugar, milk, vanilla and salt.
Blend in Jif. Frosts one 9 x 13-inch cake.
Stir together sour cream, sugar, parsley, vinegar, onion and dill.
Fold in cucumbers; cover and chill for 2 hours.
Cut bananas into 1-inch pieces.
Place lemon juice, sour cream and coconut in separate bowls.
Dip bananas in lemon juice.
Roll in sour cream and then in coconut, making sure all sides are coated.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Makes about 24 pieces.
Mix all ingredients.
Roll out; cut.
Cook gently in boiling broth.
Mix oleo and other ingredients with a fork or fingers.
Roll into balls about 1-inch.
Place on cookie sheet and press with fork crisscross.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cut onion, celery and carrots finely.
Fry in oil until lightly brown.
Add small amount of grated cheese, garlic and parsley.
Add clean shrimp, tomatoes, tomato paste and 1/2 cup water.
Cook until done.
Use more water, if needed.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over spaghetti.
Beat eggs until light and foamy.
Add sugar, oil, zucchini and vanilla to eggs and mix lightly but well.
Combine flour, salt, soda, baking powder and cinnamon, then add to the egg/zucchini mixture.
Stir all until well blended, then add nuts and pour into two 9 x 5 x 3-inch greased loaf pans.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven. Remove pans from oven and cool on a rack.
Place apples in bottom of a 11 x 7-inch baking dish or pan. Sprinkle cinnamon and nutmeg over apples.
Cover with slices of white loaf bread with crust removed.
Mix sugar, margarine and egg.
Pour over bread.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until brown.
Mix eggs, sugar and shortening together.
Add vanilla, bananas, buttermilk and baking soda.
Mix well.
Add baking powder, flour, salt and nuts.
Beat until fluffy.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cool.
Mix 1 package of banana instant pudding according to box directions.
Spread over cake. Spread Cool Whip over this.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Cook rhubarb in water for 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove and add Jell-O, sugar and juice.
Chill slightly.
Fold in apple and nuts.
In a 1 1/2-quart casserole; stir together peanuts, sugar, syrup and salt.
Cook 8 minutes on High in microwave oven, stirring well after 4 minutes.
Stir margarine and vanilla. Microwave 2 minutes longer.
Add baking soda and quickly stir until light and foamy.
Immediately pour into lightly greased baking sheet.
Spread out.
Combine sweet potatoes, sugar, eggs, vanilla, milk, margarine and marshmallow cream with electric mixer until smooth.
Spoon into a greased 2-quart shallow dish.
Combine brown sugar, flour, 1/3 cup margarine and pecans.
Sprinkle over top of casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cream Crisco and sugar well. Beat in eggs. Add flour, vanilla and coconut. Bake at 350° until done.
Slice all but 4 berries.
Mix cream cheese, milk and confectioners sugar until smooth.
In 4 goblets, layer half of sliced berries, then half of cheese mixture.
Repeat.
Garnish with whole berries.
Shave the chocolate bar.
Top each goblet with 1 ounce shaved chocolate.
Layer in a 9 x13 inch pan.
1st layer, put crushed cookies in dish and pour melted butter on top.
2nd layer, mix cream cheese and powdered sugar; spread on top of cookies.
3rd layer, sliced strawberries.
4th layer, pineapple. 5th layer sliced bananas. Top with Cool whip.
Scramble eggs and set
aside.
Fry bacon and set aside. Fry hash browns and set aside.
Drain pineapple thoroughly; reserve syrup.
Add enough water to make 1 cup syrup.
Combine with sugar and cranberries and bring to full boil.
Remove from heat.
Drain cranberries and reserve syrup. Combine drained cranberries, pineapple, banana, pears and lemon juice and chill.
Melt butter and blend in cornstarch.
Add cranberry syrup and stir over medium heat until it boils and thickens.
Reduce heat and stir a little hot mixture into egg. Return to hot mixture, stirring constantly.
Cook over low heat 3 minutes.
Cool to lukewarm.
Fold fruit, marshmallows and whipped cream into cool mixture.
Freeze.
Can be frozen in muffin tins and used as needed.
Will thaw quickly for eating.
In a large bowl, thoroughly mix 2 cups flour, dry milk solids, sugar, salt and yeast.
Add oleo.
Gradually add tap water to dry ingredients and beat 2 minutes at medium speed of electric mixer, scraping bowl occasionally.
Add 3/4 cup flour.
Beat at high speed 2 minutes, scraping bowl occasionally.
Stir in enough additional flour to make a stiff dough.
Turn out onto lightly floured board; knead until smooth and elastic (8 to 10 minutes).
Place in greased bowl, turning to grease top.
Cover; let rise in warm place, free from draft, until doubled in bulk, about 45 minutes.
Drain spinach (squeeze dry) and combine with other ingredients.
Put bowl in freezer until hard enough to roll.
Roll out into 1-inch balls and put on cookie sheet in freezer.
After frozen, they can be stored in bags.
Cook at 350° for approximately 20 minutes (until golden brown).

recipes.t: Sherry'S Soft And Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
d: Preheat oven to 375°.
Sift together flour, baking soda and salt and set aside.
Combine butter or shortening, sugar, brown sugar, vanilla and water.
Beat until creamy.
Beat in eggs.
Add flour mixture; mix well.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by well rounded teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix all ingredient together and pour into a greased and floured jelly roll pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Spread peanut butter immediately from the oven; cool in refrigerator.
Melt chocolate chips in a double boiler.
Spread over cooled cake. Cool in refrigerator.
Cook meatballs as directed (see recipe).
Mix brown sugar and cornstarch in skillet.
Add meatballs; stir in pineapple (with syrup), vinegar and soy sauce.
Heat to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat.
Add meatballs.
Cover; simmer, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Stir in green pepper. Cover; simmer until crisp-tender, 5 minutes.
Boil raisins and water for 2 minutes.
Cool and add soda to raisin mixture.
Add remaining ingredients to raisin mixture.
Drop on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 7 to 10 minutes.
One egg and 1/2 cup bread crumbs can be added to stretch hamburger.
Mix sugar, mustard, salt and vinegar.
Add oil slowly; beat constantly until thick (or use blender).
Add poppy seed and beat a few minutes longer.
Delicious over fruit.
Cook pasta according to package directions and drain. Meanwhile, in large saucepan, melt butter.
Add broccoli, green pepper and mushrooms.
Cook just until tender.
Add hot pasta and remaining ingredients, heat thoroughly, stirring occasionally. Sprinkle with cheese, if desired.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Cook bacon and onion in a skillet until bacon is crisp, stir constantly.
Stir in sauerkraut and brown sugar, add potatoes and apples.
In a cheese cloth bag tie peppercorns, juniper berries, cloves, parsley and bay leaves; add to sauerkraut.
Add pork chops and smoked kielbasa pieces, pour chicken broth in, stir well.
Heat to boiling, then reduce heat, cover and simmer until meat is done, potatoes are tender for about 45 minutes.
When done remove spice bag.
With a slotted spoon remove sauerkraut, potatoes and apples to a large platter.
Arrange meat and kielbasa in the center of the platter.
Serve with fresh sourdough bread.
Brown
ground
beef and onion;	drain good.
Mix ground beef, onion,
sugar
and pork and beans.	Put in a long Pyrex dish.
Put bacon
on top of beans and top with ketchup.
Cook until bacon is cooked.
Bake in oven at 400°.
Cut pork into thin strips.
Dredge in the flour.
Cook quickly but thoroughly in the hot oil.
Remove meat from skillet.
Add remaining ingredients to drippings and cook 2 minutes until crisp but tender.
Stir pork strips in and serve.
Cut ingredients and marinate overnight in Kraft Italian dressing.
Put ground beef, rice and peppers in green peppers in 2 inches of water and cook covered for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Combine corn meal, shortening and 2 cups of milk in a pan over medium heat.
Bring mixture just to a boil, stirring constantly.
Blend beaten eggs, salt and remaining milk.
Add to corn meal mixture.
Mix well.
Stir in baking powder.
Pour into greased 1 1/2 to 2-quart casserole.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve hot with butter.
Spread chips in casserole dish.
Place boned chicken on top of chips.
Saute onion and pepper in butter until tender.
Add all other ingredients except for the cheese.
Mix well.
Pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Top with cheese the last few minutes.
Bake cake as per directed in a large oblong pan.
While hot, cover with crushed pineapple.
Brown ground meat with chopped onions, chili powder, ground comino and salt.
Drain.
On the side, pour about 1/2 can Wolfe's chili into a bowl or Pyrex pie dish; add small amount of water (make it a little runny); stir and warm in a microwave.

Dip flour or corn tortillas into warm chili; add a couple of spoons of meat, onions and cheese, then roll it up and place into an oblong pan. When all are rolled up, pour any remaining chili on top; add cheese and onions.
Cook at 400° to 425° until cheese melts.
Crush wafers to fine crumbs.
Add to nuts and chopped cherries.
Mix well in milk.
Pour coconut on waxed paper.
Form rolls by rolling and shaping on coconut.
Wrap in foil. Refrigerate.
Layer the sausage and cheese in order in the pie shell.
Beat the eggs and milk together.
Add to the pie shell.
Sprinkle with sharp cheese.
Bake for 35 minutes in a 350° oven.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Cut into chunks.
Add all ingredients; mix well.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Place all ingredients in a heavy pan and cook 45 minutes (high heat).
Stir
every 10 minutes until all sauce is gone. Turn to low heat; fat becomes oil.
Cook carrots in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain.
Combine carrots, zucchini and tomatoes in rectangular dish.
In saucepan, stir cornstarch, milk, 1/2 cup cheese and butter until smooth and thick.
Pour sauce over vegetables.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and almonds.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 6.
Cook beef until brown and crumbly.
Turn into a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Arrange thawed peas over meat, then cover with celery. Mix together soup, cream, seasonings and onion.
Pour over celery. Sprinkle with chips or flakes.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine apples and sugar in mixing bowl.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Blend oil, vanilla and egg with the apples, then combine the dry ingredients and mix in well.
Stir in the raisins.
Pour into greased 8-inch square cake pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Yields 9 servings.
In a small saucepan, melt margarine; stir in Worcestershire sauce and seasoned nuts, cereals and pretzels.
Pour margarine, sauce over mixture.
Mix lightly about every 20 minutes.
Spread out on absorbent paper or heavy brown paper to cool.
Keep crisp by storing in airtight container.
Chunk squash.
Par-boil, drain and mash.
Leave skin on.
Put in baking dish.
Beat egg yolks lightly.
Add all ingredients except egg whites.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Fold into vegetable mixture.
Bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.
Makes 8 servings.
Heat pineapple juice and cherry juice together.
Mix Jell-O with juice.
Cool thoroughly (this is very important).
Add Cokes, pineapple, nuts and cherries.
Pour in molds or Pyrex pan and chill until firm.
Mix in order given and our into unbaked pie crust. Bake in moderate oven 25 minutes.
You may use an orange instead of lemon; it's very good.

Cut up stewed tomatoes and combine in saucepan with onions, fresh tomato, salt and pepper. Bring just to a boil. Boil hard 1 minute and remove at once from heat. Put half of mixture through blender just to mince fine, but not to puree. Return to remaining half of mixture. Cool and refrigerate in tightly covered container to use within a few weeks. Freezes well to use within 6 months.
Melt butter.
Add sugar and curry powder.
Drain fruit well. Arrange in a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Add butter mixture.
Bake for 1 hour at 325°.
Serves 12.
Mix together bread crumbs, celery, green pepper and onion. Add lemon juice and clam juice and mix well.
Season with garlic salt, oregano and pepper and mix.
Add this mixture to the chopped clams.
Spoon into cleaned clam shells and top with bacon pieces. Bake at 350° until bacon is crisp.
Serve with lemon wedges. Serves 8.
Cook grits.
Add cheese, butter and garlic.
Stir until blended.
Beat 3 eggs in measuring cup.
Add half and half to eggs to measure 1 3/4 cups total.
Add to grits.
Put in casserole. Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 10.
Prepare rice mix using package directions.
Season chicken with salt and pepper in skillet.
Brown slowly in butter.
Spoon rice into 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with chicken, skin side up.
Add soup to skillet.
Slowly add Sauterne, stirring until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to boil.
Pour over chicken.
Cover and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tender.
Serves 6.
Combine all ingredients and cook over medium heat until it comes to a full boil.
Pour into a 9x13 pan lined with vanilla wafers or crackers.
Using high speed of the electric mixer, cream butter, sugar and vanilla until soft and creamy.
Sift together salt and flour; add gradually to butter mixture.
Blend well on low speed.
Add noodles, stirring in by hand.
Chill until firm.
Pinch off small pieces of dough and shape into fingers.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cool; dust with powdered sugar.
Yield:
5 to 6 dozen icicles.
Cook bacon until crisp; drain and reserve 1/4 cup fat from bacon.
Cook onion in the fat until tender.
Blend flour, sugar, salt and celery seed; add vinegar and 1 cup water and cook until thickened.
Add bacon, potatoes and eggs.
Empty can of pineapple with juice in a 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan.
Spread pie filling over pineapple.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over pie filling.
Sprinkle chopped nuts over cake mix. Generously dot with margarine.
Never stir mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes until top is brown.

recipes.t: Zucchini Parmesan(Can Substitute Eggplant For Zucchini)
d: On wax paper, combine bread crumbs with oregano.
Cut zucchini lengthwise.
Brush with mayo; coat with crumb mixture.
In 2 1/2-quart casserole dish, arrange zucchini, crumb side up.
Cook, covered with wax paper on High for 12 to 15 minutes, until tender, rotating halfway through cooking time.
In small bowl, cook spaghetti sauce on High for 1 to 3 minutes, until hot.
Meanwhile sprinkle 1 1/2 cups Mozzarella cheese over zucchini.
Spoon sauce over cheese; top with remaining Mozzarella cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Cook on High for 2 to 4 minutes until cheese melts.
Cream Cheese:
Mix above ingredients until smooth.
Fold gently into whipped cream.
Mix 1 stick of margarine (melted) with the first 5 ingredients.
Mix half of dressing with rest of ingredients. Leave half of dressing to top the mixture.
Bake for 25 minutes at 350°.
Season meat with salt, brown in hot fat.
Arrange alternate layers, onions, potatoes and meat in a 2-quart casserole.
Pour soup over layers.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Sprinkle cheese over casserole about 10 minutes before it's done, if desired. Makes 6 servings.
Cook cauliflower in 1-inch boiling salt water until tender-crisp; drain.
Separate into flowerets.
Start heating oven to 350°.
Combine soup and milk in a 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish.
Add cauliflowerets, ham, savory and 1/2 cup cheese. Sprinkle 1/2 cup cheese on top.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Serves 4.
Pie Shell:
Mix cracker crumbs, butter and sugar in bowl. Press into pie pan to form crust.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°; cool.
Fry together bacon and hamburger; drain.
Add 3 cans of beans and juice.
Mix with onion, catsup, brown sugar, prepared mustard and vinegar.
Mix together in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Slice beef across the grain into very thin strips.
In skillet over high heat in 1 tablespoon margarine, cook 1/2 of beef and 1/2 of onion until beef is no longer pink and onion is tender.
Set aside and repeat with remaining margarine, beef and onion.
Return meat mixture to skillet.
Stir in soup and paprika.
Heat through, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to very low.
Stir in sour cream.
Gently heat through.
Serve on hot noodles.
Boil together the brown sugar and hot water for 10 minutes. Cool and add the butter, flour, milk, salt and eggs.
Cook all together in a double boiler until thick and smooth, stirring constantly.
Cool and add 1 teaspoon vanilla extract and 1/2 cup pecan meats, chopped.
Put 2 tablespoons of mixture in prepared (baked) tart shells.
Garnish with 1/2 cup whipped cream, sweetened with 1 tablespoon of powdered sugar and put a whole pecan on top.
Fills about 1 dozen shells.
Delicious!
Mix all together and bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 45 minutes at 325°.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Mix with egg and milk.
Spread over bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with spaghetti sauce, grated cheese and pepperoni or other toppings.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Cook noodles and drain.
Combine soup, milk, water and cheese and heat to boiling, stirring.
Combine first 8 ingredients in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs, Parmesan and parsley. Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Microwave until butter melts; take out and stir fast!
Put into pan.
Let cool, then cut.
Mix chicken broth, soups, chili powder, Ro-Tel, onions and bell pepper.
Place half of the chicken in casserole dish.
Pour half of the soup mixture on top.
Crumble half of the Doritos on top. Layer again in this order.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Serve topped with sour cream and black olives. Makes 1 large or 2 small casseroles.
Grease muffin pan and press biscuit half in pan cups up the side as far as you can.
Divide sausage and place on dough.
Mix cheese cottage cheese eggs and pepper; pour over sausage and dough.
Bake 375° 15 to 20 minutes.
Wipe muffin pan, grease and make the rest of the muffins.
Cut about 1 1/2 inches from tops of melons.
Scoop out seeds. Wipe cavity with paper towels.
Drain pineapple, reserving syrup. Add water to syrup to measure 1 1/4 cups.
Heat syrup-water mixture to boiling.
Pour over gelatin.
Stir to dissolve.
Cool to lukewarm.
Stir in milk and pineapple.
Chill to consistency of unbeaten egg whites.
Spoon into cantaloupe cavities.
(Depending on cavity size, there may be enough gelatin mixture to fill a third cantaloupe.)
Chill in upright position at least 3 hours, or until firm.
Slice into 1-inch rings to serve.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix shortening with brown sugar cream.
Add egg.
Sift together soda, salt, flour, milk rolled oats.
Finally add raisins, nuts, vanilla.
Bake at 375 till golden brown.
Cook all ingredients together.
On the farm, we used fresh corn and tomatoes.
This was one of Claude's favorites.
Slice onion about 1/8-inch thick then chop slices finely.
In a pan add about 2 tablespoons of butter and the onions.
Saute until transparent.
Add the chicken broth.
Dice the potatoes and add to the broth.
(The potatoes should double the volume of liquid in the pan.)
Cook until potatoes are tender.
While still on the heat, mash the potatoes.
Cook a little longer and mash again.
At this point you can add the sour cream and serve.
Bake cake according to package instructions.
Mix jello with 2 cups boiling water.
Add frozen strawberries to jello and break up. Add 1/4 cup cold water and stir.
Jello has to be jelled until a little thick.
Brown ground beef with onion in skillet, stirring until ground beef is crumbly; drain.
Stir in taco seasoning mix, tomato sauce and water; mix well.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 8 1/2 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Brown meat with salt, pepper and onion.
Drain.
Add taco mix and 2 cups water.
Cook on medium heat until mixture is hot.
Let simmer on very low heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture is thick.
Add drained corn and olives (if desired); heat.
Grate each kind of cheese separately.
Spray baking dish with vegetable spray. Fill each separated shell with small amount of pepper, cheese and meat.
Roll shells and lay in dish (side by side) and pour rest of meat sauce over rolled shells.
Cover the tops of shells with grated cheese (Cracker Barrel).
Bake at 400° for 5 to 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
*This will not work with the round American type eggplants.
Boil new potatoes until partly cooked.
Remove from pan and cut potatoes into halves.
Pour melted butter over potatoes in a baking dish and sprinkle with dry Italian dressing.
Finish baking until done.
Do not cover.
Step 1:
Remove 1 cup cake mix and cut in 1/2 stick margarine with 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Set aside.
Blend peppers and vinegar.
Add with sugar and boil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add pectin.
Boil for 1 minute.
Add food coloring; strain out pepper pieces, if desired. Can in 4 pint canning jars.
Serve over cream cheese with crackers.
Split Twinkies long wise and lay in cake pan, filling up.
Mix vanilla pudding and milk together and set aside.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream and Cool Whip.
Add to pudding and spread over Twinkies. Top with cherry pie filling.
In a frypan with a small amount of melted margarine, grill 2 slices of sandwich bread on one side only of each slice.
Then remove one slice from pan and set aside.
Heat oven to 350°.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Put into mixing bowl.
Add salsa, chili powder, Miracle Whip and corn.
Layer 1/2 meat in dish.
Add 1/2 chips and cheese on top.
Layer rest of ingredients.
Measure and sift dry ingredients.
Beat until light and fluffy the sugar, shortening, eggs, milk and vanilla.
Blend in the dry ingredients.
Add nuts, dates and cherries.
Blend well and chill. Shape into small balls.
Roll in crushed corn flakes.
Place on greased baking sheet.
Press 1/4 maraschino cherry in each.
Bake in moderate oven (375°) for 10 minutes.
Brown and drain the sausage.
Add remaining ingredients. Spread on party rye bread.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Mix all ingredients and pour into 2 well-greased and floured cake pans.
Frost with 7-Up frosting.
Cut the white of the egg up into the cream cheese and salad dressing.
Keep the egg yolk separate and mix all the rest together.
After that's done, smash the egg yolk and sprinkle on top.
If you want a big dish, use 8 ounces cream cheese and 2 hard-boiled eggs.

recipes.t: Next Best Thing To Robert Redford Cake
d: Mix together flour, nuts and butter and put in 13 x 9 x 2 pan. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Dissolve each (cherry, orange and lime) package jello in 1 1/2 cups hot water and place in long dishes.
When jelled, cut into small squares.
Dissolve 1 package plain gelatin in 1/4 cup cold water.
Add to 1 cup hot pineapple juice.
Chill to a syrup.
Whip 1 pint whipped cream; add 1/2 cup sugar.
Mix well the whipped cream, juice mixture and jello squares.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan lined with crust.
Mix ingredients together.
Pour into casserole dish.
Bake at 350° until hot.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease baking dish.
Place beef in baking dish.
Toss with gravy and flour.
Set aside.
Spray 12-inch skillet and cook mushrooms, celery, onion and garlic about 6 minutes or until tender, but crisp.
Transfer to baking dish along with carrots, wine, beef broth, thyme, marjoram, salt and pepper. Bake, covered, about 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Uncover to stir occasionally until beef is tender and vegetables are cooked through.
Replace cover after each stirring.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients.
Fill buns; wrap in tinfoil.
Heat in preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Let cream cheese set out until it's room temperature.
Mix crabmeat and cream cheese; shape into a ball.
Pour cocktail sauce over it and refrigerate until you're ready to serve.
Serve with crackers.
In a 12-inch skillet add 1/2 cup Crisco to get it to the melting stage.
Add 1 or 2 bags of corn with your 2 teaspoons salt and pepper, frying to let the whole kernel corn get golden brown.
Combine gelatin and water and cook over medium heat until dissolved.
Beat cream cheese, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Add milk and softened gelatin; beat until mixed.
Refrigerate until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes.
Stir in cream cheese mixture until smooth; fold in whipped cream.
Pour into ungreased mold.
First, flatten meat to tenderize and make larger.
(This can be done by pounding meat with the flat side of meat cleaver or plate edge.)
Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder and spread with mustard.
Dip meat in egg on both sides and then dip in bread crumbs.
Melt margarine in skillet at medium-high heat.
When margarine is hot, add meat and fry until brown on both sides.
If egg is left over, scramble and place on top of meat.
Mix all ingredients except bacon in casserole.
Top with bacon slices and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine crumbs, cocoa, sugar and margarine.
Press firmly on bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Pour Eagle Brand evenly over crust.
Top evenly with remaining ingredients in order listed.
Press down firmly.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Cool; chill thoroughly, if desired.
Cut into bars.
Store, loosely covered, at room temperature.
Mix
dry
ingredients.
Combine egg, milk and water and stir into
dry
ingredients
until they are moistened.
Spoon batter into
a
greased loaf pan (9 x 5 x 3-inches).
Bake at 350°
for 55
to 60 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.
Combine milk, rice, pudding mix, raisins and egg in saucepan. Stir over medium heat until mixture just comes to a boil.
Cool 5 minutes, stirring twice.
Pour into dessert dishes or serving bowl.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Serve warm.
Makes 10 servings.
Grate American cheese and set aside.
Chop onion and saute in butter.
Cook frozen broccoli in water.
Combine onion and broccoli using all liquid.
Add bouillon cube and stir until dissolved.
Add garlic powder, dash of pepper, half and half and grated American cheese.
Heat until cheese is melted, stirring constantly.
Grind or chop "chicken"; add cheese and green chilies, set aside.
Wrap tortillas in damp paper towels; microwave at High 15 seconds or until hot.
Brush both sides of tortillas, one at a time, with vegetable oil (keep remaining tortillas warm).
Place a scant 1/2 cup of "chicken" mixture just below center of each tortilla.
Fold in left and right sides of tortilla to partially enclose filling.
Fold up bottom edge of tortilla; fold into a rectangle and secure with a wooden pick.
Repeat with remaining tortillas and "chicken" mixture.
Place on a lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes or until crisp and lightly browned.
Serve with shredded lettuce, salsa and sour cream. Yields 4 servings.
Combine all ingredients.

Add olive oil to moisten to taste. Use as filling for spinach turnovers (in roll mix dough) or excellent as: pizza topping, dip for raw vegetables, to spread on French bread or crackers, to stuff boneless chicken breasts or to toss with hot pasta.
Slice sausage into 1/4-inch thick; brown over medium heat in Dutch oven or heavy kettle.
Remove sausage with slotted spoon and reserve.
Drain away excess fat.
Add celery, onion, thyme and salt.
Cook until onion is tender.
Stir in flour.
Cook 1 minute.
Mix corn meal, flour, milk, egg and oil.
Beat with fork. Roll hot dogs in flour, then roll in batter.
Deep fry in oil until brown.
Mix all ingredients and pour into buttered casserole dish; sprinkle paprika on top.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.
In 3-quart oblong baking dish, mix soup, milk, thyme and pepper.
Stir in vegetables.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes or until mixture begins to bubble.
Meanwhile, cut each biscuit into quarters.
Remove dish from oven.
Stir.
Arrange biscuits over hot chicken.
Bake 15 minutes until golden brown.
Mix and blend first 4 ingredients and blend well.
Pour over the two packages of oyster crackers.
Mix well and place in air-tight container for storage.
Combine fruit and lemon juice in 4-quart saucepan.
Cook, stirring until it is almost tender.
Stir in sugar, powdered pectin, butter and food coloring.
Bring to a rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Boil for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from heat and skim off foam.
Ladle into sterilized jars, leaving 1/2-inch space at top.
Seal with paraffin.
Makes 8 (6 ounce) glasses.
Heat grill.
Cut loaf into 1-inch slices.
Lightly spread one side of each slice of bread with margarine.
Place, margarine side down, on ungreased cookie sheet.
Sprinkle cheese, bacon and parsley evenly on bread slices.
When ready to barbecue, place slices, margarine side down, directly on gas grill over medium-high heat or on charcoal grill 4 to 6-inches from coals.
Cook 4 to 6 minutes or until bottom of bread is toasted and cheese is melted. Makes 8 servings.
Press shredded cucumber between paper towels to remove excess moisture.
Beat cream cheese until fluffy.
Stir in cucumber and other ingredients.
Spread between party rye or wheat bread, or as a spread for open-faced sandwiches.
Pour boiling water over dates, soda, salt and butter.
Cool. Add eggs to sugar and then add other ingredients.
Combine the 2 mixtures.
Bake at 350° in greased and floured loaf pan for 1 hour or until done.
Mix in blender and serve.
This will make 4 to 6 servings.
Combine first 3 ingredients and mix well.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Combine the last ingredients and beat well.
Pour over crust in pan.
Bake in 375° oven 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool, then cut into squares.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Mix well with pastry cutter; divide into balls large enough for 4-inch fried pie.
Put eggs, milk, corn bread mix and onion soup (one package) into blender container.
Mix until blended.
Mix above ingredients.
Eat with your favorite fruit!
Cook broccoli according to package directions, then drain well. In saucepan, melt margarine.
Add a few onion flakes, flour and water.
Blend and let boil a bit.
Add Cheez Whiz, broccoli and eggs.
Mix gently.
Turn into buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Dot with cracker crumbs and/or crumbled croutons and 2 tablespoons margarine.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Combine vegetables, chicken and seasoning; mix well.
Stir in mayo to moisten.
Spread mixture in 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Melt chocolate; set aside.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Beat in eggs and blend in chocolate, vanilla and flour.
Add 1/2 almonds and spread in 8-inch pan.
Sprinkle remaining almonds and bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes.

Place the chocolate sauce, milk and ice cream in a blender. Blend until it turns a chocolate milk color. Pour in a cup. Top with whipped cream and sprinkles. Place the piece of chocolate on top of the whipped cream.
In a 13 x 9-inch glass Pyrex dish, pour a layer of olive oil. Cut up about 10 plum ripe tomatoes in halves.
Sprinkle on top lots of fresh garlic, salt and pepper, basil or spice and oregano (optional).
Bake in 350° oven until the tomatoes get a little soft or to the consistency you like (approximately 35 minutes). It doesn't look like tomato sauce.
Cook up linguini and add to the Pyrex dish that the tomatoes are in.
Toss and serve.
Mix with hands until crumbly.
Form into small balls.
Place on baking sheet.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Can be frozen before ready to bake.
Serves 5 to 6 dozen.
Peel and cut apples; arrange in an oblong baking dish.
Mix remaining ingredients in bowl; sprinkle over apples.
Bake in 375° oven for 30 minutes.
Cool before serving.
Serves 12.
Mix well and keep in refrigerator.
Will keep up to a week.
Arrange veal in 12
x
8-inch
baking
dish.
Top
with sliced mushrooms.
Cover
with
wax
paper.
Microwave
at 50% (Medium) 7 to 10 minutes or until veal is tender and no longer pink; rearrange once,
leaving
mushrooms on top.
Set aside. In small bowl
blend remaining ingredients.
Increase power to High. Microwave 2 to
minutes or until thickened, stirring with wire whip once
or
twice.
Pour
sauce over veal;
cover with wax paper.
Reduce power to 50% (Medium).
Microwave 2 to 4 minutes or until heated through.
Melt margarine in a large skillet and saute garlic, onion, celery and mushrooms until tender, not browned.
Add rice and stir until each grain is coated.
Add chicken broth, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Transfer to buttered 2-quart casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until rice is tender and all liquid absorbed.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Combine all ingredients.
Place pineapple rings on top.
Pour a little juice over top.
Cover.
Bake at 325° for 2 hours.
Blend soup into 1 package broccoli (do this 3 times).
Mill all together; add lemon pepper.
Refrigerate.
To serve, heat mixture with half and half until hot.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Line a 9 x 12-inch Pyrex with crushed saltine crackers. Place a layer of onions over crackers.
Sprinkle with a layer of grated cheese.
Repeat until onions and cheese are used.
Wash and drain lettuce.
Break into small pieces in a large salad bowl.
Add tomatoes which have been cut into small pieces. Add Ranch Style beans.
Just before serving, add corn chips and Catalina dressing.
Toss well and serve.
For small servings, this recipe can be halved.
Cook sausage in half lengthwise.
Cut crosswise into 1/4-inch slices.
In a 10-inch skillet, combine rice, sausage and remaining ingredients except optional toppings.
Mix well, breaking up tomatoes with large spoon.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Remove from heat; let stand covered 5 minutes.
Top as desired and serve with additional salsa or picante sauce.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix well sugars, oil and margarine.
Add eggs, vanilla, salt and soda; mix well.
Add flour; mix well.
Add oatmeal or cereal and chocolate chips.
Blend well.
Bake at 350° on ungreased cookie sheet for 10 minutes until light brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Set aside. Mix buttermilk, egg and vanilla together.
Add to dry mix and mix well.
Add nuts and broken Heath bars.
Stir just enough to mix. Pour into 8 x 10-inch or 2 bread loaf pans (greased well or wax paper lined makes easier clean up).
If greased, also flour well. Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Turn out while warm (after cooling about 1/2 hour).

Preheat oven to 350°. Grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan. Set aside. Combine crumbs, chips, coconut and walnuts in medium bowl. Stir to blend. Add milk. Stir with spoon until blended. Spread batter evenly into prepared pan. Bake 15 to 18 minutes or until edges are golden brown. Let pan stand on a wire rack until completely cooled. Cut into 2 1/4 x 2 1/4-inch bars. Store, tightly covered, at room temperature or freeze up to 3 months.
Chill all juices first.
In punch bowl with ice ring, add already mixed cranberry, pineapple and sugar.
To this add ginger ale and serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients and pour into a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Mix chicken, soup, mayonnaise and curry powder.
Pour over broccoli in casserole dish.
Mix cheese and bread crumbs; put over top.
Bake at 350° until hot through and brown.
Mix cream cheese, pineapple, bell pepper, onion and seasoning salt (by hand) until well blended.
Add 1 cup pecans and mix well. Shape into ball.
Roll in 1/2 cup pecans and refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients together until fluffy.
Refrigerate at least 24 hours for flavors to blend.
Soften at room temperature for 1 hour before serving.
Brown ground beef and sausage and drain well.
Mix spaghetti sauce with meat.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer with noodles, sauce, cheese and pepperoni.
Repeat with remaining ingredients, ending with cheese and pepperoni.
Bake at 350° for approximately 25 minutes, until cheese is bubbly.
Heat milk and marshmallows in a double boiler until marshmallows are melted.
Add lemon jello; stir until dissolved. Mix crushed pineapple with cream cheese with mixer.
Add to jello mix.
Add nuts.
Cool.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Form in flat shallow dish and let set in refrigerator.
Make red jello using drained pineapple juice for part of liquid.
When beginning to set, pour over cold bottom layer.
Heat 1 tablespoon cooking oil (any variety) in large frying pan.
Add onion and cook until clear.
Add chicken and cook until thawed.
Add broccoli and mushrooms and cook about 5 minutes until heated through.
Add bean sprouts and water chestnuts.
Mix stir-fry seasoning according to package directions and pour over stir-fry.
Add soy sauce to taste.
Be careful not to cook too long, bean sprouts will become soggy.
Serve immediately over hot cooked rice.
Mix together gelatin and hot water.
Add orange juice concentrate; cool.
Add orange slices and crushed pineapple.
Let congeal.
Place chips on the bottom of a glass casserole dish.
Scatter the chicken pieces on top of chips.
Mix soups and chiles together and pour over all.
Top with tomatoes; sprinkle cheese over top. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Garnish with sour cream and guacamole before serving.
Cut cabbage into wedges.
Cook in salted water until tender; drain.
Mix soup and milk together and set aside.
Grease casserole dish. Layer alternately the cabbage, soup and cheese. Top with bread crumbs.
Dot with butter.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Layer bread slices on cookie sheet.
Put a teaspoon of dressing, then a piece of corned beef, sauerkraut and top with a small piece of Swiss cheese.
Put under broiler for 3 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, stirring well; spoon into a greased 13x9x2 inch baking dish.
Bake at 350 for 40 minutes.
Yield:
12 to 15 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Mix lightly with a fork.
Shape into a loaf and bake in a greased 8-inch square pan for one hour.
Cream butter and sugar. Add lemon juice and beaten egg yolks; mix.
Stir in flour and milk.
Fold in egg whites that have been beaten stiff.
Pour in unbaked pie shell and bake at 450° for first 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 325° and bake until set as custard, about 45 minutes.
Add red hots to water and bring to boil.
Red hots should be dissolved.
Pour over jello.
Add applesauce and nuts.
Let set in refrigerator.
Bake cake as directed in two 8-inch round cake pans.
Place one layer in the bottom of a punch bowl.
Add pineapple.
Layer with bananas (sliced), 1 1/2 cans vanilla pudding and 1 layer Cool Whip.
Add the other layer of cake.
Layer with strawberries, 1 1/2 cans vanilla pudding and Cool Whip.
Cover with maraschino cherries and nuts.
On large microwavable platter, start layering as follows: tortilla chips, Cheddar cheese, refried beans, hamburger, sour cream, tomatoes, green onions and black olives.
After completing first layer of everything, begin with second layer in same order. When ingredients are gone, top with guacamole and jalapeno peppers.
Entire platter can be heated in microwave.
Serve immediately.
Great party snack (but a little messy)!
Pour boiling water over bran.
Stir well and let cool.
Mix all ingredients.
This will keep in refrigerator 6-8 weeks.
Bake 20 min. at 400 degrees in greased muffin pan.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in heavy skillet.
Add onions and cook, stirring frequently, for 7 to 8 minutes.
Stir in sage and cook 2 to 3 minutes longer or until onions are limp and slightly colored. Set skillet off heat.
Blend with mixer until smooth.
Frost one layer.
Can be used for Whoopie Pies.
Cook roast along with 2 diced onions and 2 cups water in crock-pot for 8 to 12 hours on low. Drain. Shred meat and add 1 diced onion and barbecue sauce. Cook 1 to 3 hours on medium.
Crumble sausage in medium skillet; cook over medium heat until brown, stirring occasionally.
Drain well.
Line bottom of buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish with crescent rolls, firmly pressing perforations to seal.
Sprinkle with sausage and cheese. Combine remaining ingredients; beat well and pour over sausage. Bake at 425° for 15 minutes or until set.
Let stand 5 minutes. Cut into squares and serve immediately.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
In medium saucepan over medium heat, melt butter and saute shallots lightly. Stir in flour and cook for 3 minutes. Add broth and sherry.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in ham, chicken, asparagus and cream.
Pour chicken mixture into an ungreased 9-inch pie pan.
Preheat oven to 425°. Cut an 8-inch circle from crust.
Cut hearts out of extra dough with a cookie cutter, if desired.
Place circle on a cookie sheet and moisten with cold water.
Pierce with a fork and brush with egg.
Decorate with hearts which are also brushed with egg.
Bake crust and full pie plate for 10 minutes, reduce heat to 350° and bake another 10 to 15 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is hot and set.
With a spatula, place pastry over hot filling and serve.
Makes 4 servings.
In top of double boiler, beat egg yolks and 1/4 cup sugar with mixer for 5 minutes.
Set over simmering water; add Marsala and continue beating for 6 minutes.
(Keep beater on high speed.) Remove, set aside and cool.
In separate bowls, beat Mascarpone cheese (which is available in delis with imported cheeses) until smooth and whipping cream until it has soft peaks.
Fold together Mascarpone, whipping cream, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Mix together coffee and rum.
Layer one package of ladyfingers in flat bottom casserole and brush with 1/3 of the coffee mixture.
Spread 1/3 of the Mascarpone mixture on ladyfingers and top with 1/3 Marsala mixture.
Repeat with remaining ladyfingers, making 3 layers.
Sift cocoa powder evenly on top.
Cover lightly and refrigerate 3 hours.
Serves 10 to 12.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan. Sprinkle 1/2 cup chopped pecans in pan.
Set aside.
Cream the butter or margarine and cream cheese.
Add brown sugar and cream until light and fluffy (about 5 minutes).
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Fold in flour just until combined.
Do not overmix.
Stir in vanilla and remaining 1 cup chopped pecans.
Spoon batter into prepared pan and place on baking sheet in oven.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours or until wooden toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool in pan 10 minutes. Remove to rack to cool completely.
Yields 16 servings.
Saute onion and celery in oleo.
Cook rice and broccoli according to package directions.
Combine celery, onion, soup and cheese.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in cooked rice.
Add broccoli.
Pour into a 3-quart dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a large skillet, heat oil and brown okra until tender (about 10 minutes).
Add onions and tomatoes to mix.
Cook until onions are translucent.
Put all remaining ingredients in large pot along with mixture in skillet.
Bring to boil, then simmer for about 45 minutes.
Mix cut squash, Ro-Tel tomatoes (do not drain) and 1 1/2 to 2 cups water in a large pot. Stew on medium heat for about 20 minutes or until squash is tender.
Preheat oven to 350°.

In a baking dish, spoon in layer of squash mixture, dob with butter, sprinkle with handful of bread crumbs and layer of cheese. Continue layering until all mixture is used. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Combine crackers, sugar and oleo.
Spread 3/4 mixture in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix Eagle Brand milk and orange juice.
Fold in Cool Whip and oranges.
Fold in Cool Whip and oranges.
Spread in crust. Top with remaining cracker mixture.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: The Original Berlin Fair Clam Chowder
d: Use a coarse grinder for all ingredients.
Cook salt pork and onions just a little.
Add about 2 or 3 cups or more water, then the potatoes.
Cook until nearly done.
Add clams and the juice, salt, pepper and a little sugar (about 1 teaspoon).
Simmer about 1 hour uncovered.
This recipe can to me from my sister-in-law, Marion France.
Use 1/2 bag of chips mixed in with all the ingredients.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Put rest of chips over all.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top and bake at 400° for 20 minutes. (Put in cake pan or casserole.)
You can use canned chicken or cook a whole one and use it.

Sift flour, cream of tartar, soda and salt together. Put aside. Cream butter and flavoring together until butter is soft and smooth. Add sugar, gradually creaming until fluffy. Add egg yolks one at a time. Next, add dry ingredients to creamed mixture, beating until well-blended. Form dough into 1-inch balls and place about 2-inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Mix first 7 ingredients together to form batter.
Roll or dip frankfurters in mixture and fry in deep fat.
Mix all ingredients; will be stiff (better to mix with hand). Bake at 350° on a well-greased cookie sheet about 8 minutes.
Saute celery and onion until tender.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in a 1 1/2 qt. greased casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove and sprinkle chinese noodles over top. Bake for an additional 15 minutes.

Cream butter, margarine, cream cheese and sugar until thoroughly creamed. Add vanilla and salt; alternate eggs and flour. Beat until well blended. Bake in a lightly greased and floured tube pan at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Chop onion fine.
Combine ground meat, chopped onion and rice in a large bowl.
Form into medium size meat balls and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Drain salmon and flake into bowl; stir in onion, egg and bread crumbs.
Mix.
Form into 1/2 inch thick patties; fry in a little oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Turn only once while frying.
Serve with lemon.
Beat well the zucchini, pulp, soda, sugar and shortening.
Add egg and beat well.
Sift flour and spices.
Add dry ingredients with nuts and raisins.
Drop by teaspoons onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
In a medium bowl, beat together eggs, corn syrup, sugar, butter, vanilla and salt.
Arrange walnuts on bottom of pie shell. Carefully pour egg mixture over walnuts.
Bake on bottom rack of preheated 400° oven until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool on wire rack. Serves 6 to 8.
Pour all juices into a large goblet half filled with ice cubes.
Top with ginger ale.
Decorate with slices or oranges and lemons.
Cut meat into strips 1/8-inch thick.
Soak meat in mixture of ingredients for 6 hours. Dry in oven or on stovetop until crisp.
Combine soup and margarine; stir well.
Drain mushrooms and water chestnuts, reserving liquid.
Add enough water to reserved liquid to equal 1 1/3 cups.
Add all ingredients and mix well. Pour into a lightly greased baking dish.
Cover and bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Mix all together.
Let set for awhile to blend.
Spread on crackers.

recipes.t: French Toast With Bananas 'N Brandy Coulis
d: Slice baguettes diagonally into 3/4-inch thick slices. Mix buttermilk, milk, eggs, vanilla and cinnamon thoroughly. Soak slices in mixture for 10 minutes or so. Lightly spray griddle with nonstick vegetable coating. Over medium heat, cook slices on griddle until golden brown. Keep in warming oven (covered with a sheet of aluminum foil) at 200° until just ready to serve.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Add taco sauce and simmer.
Put lettuce, tomatoes, kidney beans, onions and cheese in a bowl.
Add meat and French dressing.
Mix.
Add chips just before serving.
Mix all ingredients together.
Spread on bread.
Cut diagonally.
Put about 1 inch oil in frying pan and heat.
Place bread with filled side down and fry 15 seconds.
Turn and fry other side until golden brown.
