Drain on absorbent paper.
Cream together egg, sugar, shortening and molasses.
Add rest of ingredients.
Roll in small balls, then roll in sugar.
Bake at 375° for about 10 minutes.
Boil together sugar, honey and water until syrup spins a thread.
Slowly pour syrup over stiffly beaten egg whites, beating continuously.
Beat until mixture holds in shape.
Blend in extract and coconut.
Drop from teaspoon onto waxed paper or spread in a buttered 9-inch square pan; cool and cut into squares.
Blend well in blender and keep in refrigerator.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add to pineapple.
Stir in eggs and butter.
Mix.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together well, except bread.
Spread over entire slice of bread.
Broil on cookie sheet until bubbly.
Serve warm.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients, except bread; mix well.
Slice loaf into 1/2-inch slices, cutting but not through bottom of loaf.
Spread one side of each slice with margarine mixture.
Wrap in foil; bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.

Remove husks and silks from corn. Cut corn from cob, scraping cob to remove pulp; set aside. Cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp; remove bacon, reserving drippings. Crumble bacon and set aside. Saute corn in bacon drippings until golden brown. Add water to cover, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil; reduce heat, cover and simmer 30 to 45 minutes. Stir in crumbled bacon.
Line a 12-cup bowl with 2 pieces of wax paper, one on top of the other.
Let each piece extend over opposite edges of bowl so all edges are covered; paper will be wrinkled.
Set bowl aside. In a large bowl, sprinkle gelatin over cold water.
Let stand 5 minutes to soften.
Add boiling water; stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in granulated sugar, salt, orange juice concentrate, lemon juice and peel.
Refrigerate 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until partially set and mixture mounds when dropped from a spoon.
In a large bowl, whip 1 pint cream until it forms soft peaks.
Fold gelatin mixture into whipped cream.
Spoon a small amount of lemon mixture into bottom of prepared bowl.
Scatter several pieces of angel food cake over lemon mixture.
Continue alternating cake and lemon mixture until all is used.
Cover with plastic wrap and foil.
Refrigerate 1 to 2 days before serving.
May also be frozen.
Combine first 8 ingredients.
Shape into 4 patties.
Coat grill rack with cooking spray, place on grill over medium-hot coals.
Place patties on rack and cook 8 minutes on each side or until done.
Serve on buns.
Makes 4 servings.

In small bowl, whisk oil, garlic, rind and juice, vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper. Pour half into large storage bag; add beef. Seal; refrigerate 1 to 2 hours. Divide steak, peppers, onion and mushrooms into 6 equal portions. Thread each portion onto large metal skewers. Heat broiler. Place skewers on large broiler-pan rack. Brush with some of remaining marinade. Broil 5 minutes. Turn over; brush with remaining marinade. Broil 5 minutes. Serve with rice.
Mix mayo, cream cheese, and soup in small pan until warm.
Add gelatin.
Mold.
Chop and mix all ingredients together.
Pack in pan with oil paper.
Cover tightly.
Store in cool place.
Keeps good for several years in freezer.
Store in cool place for 2 to 3 weeks before cutting.
Boil sweet potatoes until tender. Add sugar, butter and flavoring. Mix and place in refrigerator overnight.
Place sugar, peanut butter and margarine in a glass bowl. Microwave 2 minutes on High. Stir a few times during the 2 minutes. Remove and stir in vanilla.
Pour into a 9 x 9-inch buttered dish.
Chill 30 minutes and cut in squares.
Brown ground beef in oil in a large skillet, stirring to crumble.
Drain off pan drippings.
Stir tomatoes, tomato paste and seasonings into meat. Bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
Drain.
Place half of noodles in lightly greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish, slightly overlapping lengthwise edges.
Spoon 1/3 of meat mixture over noodles.
Add 1/2 shredded Mozzarella cheese, cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Repeat layers and spoon on remaining meat mixture. Arrange Mozzarella slices on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Saute onions in butter, then blend in salt and flour.
Add sour cream until smooth.
Bring to boil, add corn and cook until heated through.
Add 1/2 bacon.
Pour in greased dish and top with parsley and bacon.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Night Before:
Cook spaghetti and rinse under cold water. Refrigerate.
Peel, deseed and chop cucumber.
Chop green pepper and green onions.
Deseed and chop tomatoes.
Add spaghetti.
Add salad dressing (all of it).
Add salad dressing now or just before.

Brown hamburger and drain. Add taco seasoning, cheese, and Ro-tel tomatoes. Stir together in skillet over low heat until cheese is melted, keep warm. In large bowl mix the salad mix, tomatoes, and Doritoes. When ready to serve, mix everything together and serve immediately to keep chips from getting soggy.
Sprinkle chicken on both sides with salt and pepper.
In a large frypan, place oil and heat to medium temperature.
Add chicken and saute about 4 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Turn chicken, cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook 10 minutes or until fork can be inserted in chicken with ease.
Remove chicken and keep warm; drain off oil and discard.
Arrange in square or round pan the cut fruit.
Sprinkle with mixture of flour, sugar and cinnamon.
Dot with butter or margarine.
Sift together into bowl the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add oil, milk and egg.
Stir with fork until blended.
Drop by spoonful over fruit.
If desired, dough may be spread with spatula.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes in preheated oven at 350°.
Cook until bubbly and light brown.
Serve warm.
Combine egg, milk, salt and pepper.
Soak the fish in this mixture for 15 minutes.
Dip each fillet in the bread crumbs. Melt butter in skillet.
Add fillets and saute on both sides until brown.
Let butter or margarine, eggs and cream stand at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours.
Cook bacon in skillet until browned.
Remove and drain on paper toweling.
Beat together eggs and cream just until blended.
Cook pasta until al dente (tender), about 15 minutes.
Drain thoroughly; do not rinse.
Toss pasta with butter.
Pour egg mixture over and toss until pasta is well coated.
Add bacon, cheese, pepper and parsley; toss to mix. Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 350°. Mix and bake 15 to 20 minutes. Remove cover. Top with 1 stick oleo, melted, and add Progresso bread crumbs, Italian-style. Bake 15 to 20 minutes more and serve.
Press cookie dough onto a greased pizza pan.
Cook as directed.
Do not overcook.
Let cool.
Mix softened cream cheese with 3/4 of the container of Cool Whip.
Spread onto dough.
Cut up fruit onto pan.
Spoon heated preserves onto pizza.
Let chill in refrigerator 2 to 3 hours before serving.
In a bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and baking soda.
Add egg, milk and corn; stir just until mixed.
Beat eggs and egg white until creamy.
Add milk and cream. Sprinkle in salt and pepper.
Stir in meats and cheese.
Pour into an unbaked pie shell.
Add mushrooms; layer tomatoes.
Sprinkle with additional cheese, if desired.
Bake for 10 minutes at 425°, then for 10 additional minutes at 350°.
(You can also add 1/4 cup sauteed onions for more flavor.)
Serves 8.
Cream butter, sugar and vanilla in large bowl. Gradually add flour. Beat on low until well blended. Chill 1 hour.
Mix oil and dry ingredients.
Pour over oyster crackers; blend well. Dry on paper towels.
Dissolve flour in the milk.
Add salt, sugar and eggs. Combine with corn and mix well.
Pour into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
When done, knife will come out clean.
Mix ingredients all together.
Form into a loaf.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes.
Have cream cheese at room temperature.
Combine with all ingredients except nuts.
Form into ball or log.
Place in refrigerator and chill.
Take out and roll ball or log in nuts. Wrap in waxed paper or foil and place in refrigerator until time to serve.
In large bowl, cream butter and 2 cups sugar until fluffy. Add vanilla, then eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
In separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Add sour cream to butter and egg mixture; mix well. Slowly stir in flour mixture until batter is smooth.
Spoon 1/2 of batter into a greased 10-inch tube pan.
Combine cinnamon, nuts and remaining sugar; sprinkle 1/2 over batter in pan.
Spoon in remaining batter and top with cinnamon/nuts mixture.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes until tested done.
Cool 15 minutes before removing from pan.
Makes 16 to 20 servings.
Mix together the shortening, margarine and sugar.
Add gelatin, eggs and vanilla.
Blend in dry ingredients.
Roll into small balls; place on cookie sheet.
Flatten with bottom of a glass that has been dipped in sugar.
Make sure glass has a bottom design on it that goes on cookie when pressed.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Line an 8-inch square pan with cherry pie filling.
Mix margarine, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, flour, salt and milk. Pour 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water over the batter.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes at 400°.
Beat eggs.
Add flour and sugar.
Mix well.
Add pineapple. Pour into greased casserole and cover with white bread (cubed). Pour melted butter or margarine over all.
Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Delicious!
Beat together with a fork and press into the bottom of greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix together yogurt, Cool Whip and puddings.
Fold in pineapple and oranges.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Peel and cut potatoes into 1/2-inch crosswise slices.
Cook in boiling water until almost tender.
Melt butter in shallow 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add single layer of potatoes, turning once in butter.
Mix remaining ingredients and sprinkle over potatoes. Bake 1/2 hour or until done and tops are crisp.
Serve hot.
Bring first 4 ingredients to a boil in a large sauce pan. Gradually stir in grits.
Return to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat, and simmer, stirring occasionally for 5 to 7 minutes until thickened. Add cheeses and hot sauce or red pepper, stirring until cheeses melt.
Serve immediately.
Combine crumbs and butter; press onto bottom and sides of 9-inch pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Can use ready made vanilla wafer crust.
Beat egg whites stiff.
Combine all ingredients in large bowl (including egg whites and yolks).
Mix thoroughly.
Use round deep pan.
Start in cold oven; bake at 300° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Saute onion in butter.
Stir in sour cream, dill weed, salt and half the Cheddar cheese (1/2 cup).
In a separate bowl combine corn, milk, dry muffin mix, egg and hot pepper sauce.
Put corn mixture in a buttered 9 x 13-inch dish.
Spread onion mixture over top.
Top with remaining Cheddar cheese.
Bake in a 425° oven for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Brown hamburger.
Layer in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan or large casserole dish with potatoes and onions.
Combine soup, tomato sauce, milk and spices.
Pour over potatoes and hamburger.
Cover with foil or cover casserole and bake at 375° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Remove cover.
Place on top a few slices of Mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes, until browned.
Keeps well in refrigerator.
Reheat in oven or microwave.
Mix beef, rice, salt, pepper and onion together.
Form into 1-inch balls.
In large skillet, mix soup and water; bring to a boil.
Add meatballs gently.
Cover; simmer for 25 minutes, turning once.
Spread each ingredient in a large pan in the order that it's written.
Bake about one hour at 350°.
Steam broccoli and drain.
Put half of it into a casserole dish.
Beat 1 egg until light, add undiluted mushroom soup and mayonnaise; mix well.
Pour 1/2 of this mixture over broccoli in the casserole and also half of the grated cheese.
Repeat with layers of broccoli mixture and cheese.
Melt 1/4 cup butter.
Mix with crumbled crackers and sprinkle over entire casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Recipe can be doubled.
In large saucepan, combine water, broth, soup, chicken, onion, garlic, basil and oregano.
Bring to a boil; simmer uncovered 30 minutes.
Add tortellini and vegetables.
Simmer 10 minutes. Serve with cheese.
Beat together the peanut butter, sugar, vanilla and butter. Roll into small balls and chill them for about an hour.
In top of double boiler set over hot water, melt chocolate and paraffin. Dip chilled balls into the mixture and place on wax paper to cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, cream together milk, shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well.
Mix dry ingredients together.
Slowly add milk, while stirring.
Cook over medium heat until it comes to a boil.
Boil 1 minute and add oleo and vanilla.

In medium saucepan, bring 3 cups milk and broccoli to the boiling point, then simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes. Stir in Lipton chicken noodle soup mix and flour blended with remaining milk.
Bring to the boiling point, then simmer 10 minutes or until soup is lightly thickened and broccoli is tender. Makes 4 servings.
Mix together and chill overnight.
Mix all the ingredients together, except butter and bread crumbs, and pour into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs and drizzle the butter over crumbs.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Bring butter and cheese to room temperature.
Beat together the butter and cheese until well blended.
Combine flour, oregano, salt and cayenne; add to cheese mixture, gradually.
Add water; mix until well blended.
Form dough into a ball.
Roll out on floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into 3 x 3/4-inch strips or cut into shapes with small cookie cutters.
Bake on ungreased baking sheet in 400° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Serve warm or cold.
Makes about 40.
Saute onion in butter until clear.
Add broth and cut up squash; cook until tender.
Puree squash when cool; season and add cream when cold.
Sprinkle top with chives.
Can be served hot or cold.
Boil chicken and debone.
Cut in bite size pieces. Save 1 cup of broth. Cook noodles in remaining broth. Combine remaining ingredients and add chicken and noodles. Bake in casserole dish at 350° for 30 minutes.
Blend the ingredients and run through food processor.
Once combined-refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients together and freeze in an 8 x 8-inch pan. To serve, let stand about
15 minutes and cut into squares.
Serve on a bed of lettuce.
Serves 9 to 12.
Mix; add ingredients and pour into crust.
Top with Cool Whip (optional).
Combine all ingredients and add salad dressing (amount desired).
Refrigerate.
Combine brown sugar, sugar and sour cream in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until it boils.
Cook
to the soft-ball stage (240° on candy thermometer).
Stir in salt and vanilla.
Pour hot candy over walnuts in a mixing bowl.
Mix until walnuts are evenly coated.
Spoon out onto waxed paper.
Separate nuts.
Allow to cool and set.
Heat the gravy.
Add the canned roast beef.
Just before serving, add the yogurt and mix.
Serve immediately over cooked egg noodles.
Clean rind by removing red meat and green outer part of rind. Cut rind and lemon into small pieces.
Mix fruit and sugar; let set overnight.
Cook mixture for about 1 hour, until thickened. Remove mixture from heat.
Add 1/2 cup pectin and enough food coloring to give an attractive color.
Seal preserves in jars.
Cook broccoli until tender; drain.
Chop into small pieces. Combine soup, mayonnaise, egg, onion, salt and pepper.
Add to the broccoli.
Pour into casserole dish and cover with cheese and cracker crumbs.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix sauce well and pour over thin sliced beef.
Let marinate at least 4 hours.
Place strips on wire rack over cookie sheet. Bake at 150° for 11 to 12 hours.
Blot excess grease.
Store in container with a lid at room temperature.
Mix altogether in large bowl.
Chill and serve.
Mix first 5 ingredients well.
Shape into balls.
Dip in well beaten egg; roll in crumbs.
Fry in deep fat until crispy.
In a large skillet, fry meat in salad oil until tender.
Add garlic, onion and rest of ingredients.
Cook until desired tenderness.
Serve mixture on warm tortillas topped with salsa and sour cream to your taste.
Bake cake as directed on package in three 9-inch layer cake pans.
Boil sugar, milk, marshmallows and coconut until marshmallows melt.
Cool.
Put between layers.
Use frosting on top and sides.
Make jello according to directions.
Chill until slightly set. Chop cranberries, apples and oranges in food processor. Add sugar according to taste. Add nuts and mix with jello. Chill.
In a large bowl, gently toss together pineapple, apple, celery, grapes, walnuts and kiwi.
In a small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, yogurt and honey.
Fold gently into fruit mixture. Cover and chill for 2 hours.
Makes 6 to 8 servings, each containing 210 calories and 2 grams saturated fat.
Mix crushed wafers and butter.
Press into a 9-inch pie plate. Cover with softened ice cream.
Top with hot fudge.
Freeze for 10 minutes.
Top with Cool Whip and almonds.
Freeze any leftovers.
Put pears in mixer.
Add 1/4 cup Crisco oil and cake mix. Beat, then add eggs, one at a time.
Beat well.
Bake in tube pan at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
Cook rice.
Add chopped onion and pepper.
Cook sausage until done.
Add with remaining ingredients to rice mixture.
Place in casserole and bake until bubbly at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Wash potatoes, but do not peel them. Cut them into quarters.
Wash the carrots and cut them into 2-inch chunks.
Peel onions and cut into wedges.
Spread pie filling in bottom of 9 x 11-inch pan.
Pour crushed pineapple over filling.
Sprinkle cake mix over fruit mixture. Pour melted butter over all.
Bake in 350° oven until top is brown, about 1 hour.
Serve warm with ice cream.
Blend well.
Put in Pyrex casserole dish.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with crackers or French bread.
Combine eggs, sugar, corn syrup and butter.
Cook over low heat until butter melts.
Remove from heat and add vanilla and pecans.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine water, cracker crumbs and salt.
Add beef and mix well.
Press into a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan lined with waxed paper.
Cover and refrigerate overnight. Cut the meat into 12 squares. Coat each square lightly with flour. Brown in oil in skillet, a few pieces at a time. Drain. Remove waxed paper from the baking pan.
Spread the soup in bottom of pan. Place meat squares in a single layer over soup. Bake, uncovered, at 300° for 35 to 40 minutes.
To serve, spoon some soup over each meat square.
Yields 12 servings.

Add butter, milk and egg.

Return to oven and bake until cheese melts (about 15 to 20 minutes).

Drain.
Drain juice from butter beans and kidney beans.
Add the 4 beans and salt and pepper to taste.
Add a pinch or two of chili powder and bring to boil. Then turn to low and let simmer.

Stir in cereal.
Shape by level tablespoonfuls into logs.
Roll in peanuts.
Place on waxed paper.
Melt chocolate chips and paraffin wax in double boiler over hot water, stirring.
Drizzle over logs.
Chill until serving.

Mix well.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until golden brown ontop.
Mix orange juice as directed.
Mix 1/2 of orange juice, 1/2 of
Ginger ale, and 1/2 gal. pineapple sherbet.

Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until light brown.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar while warm.

recipes.t: Shrimp Mousse(Appetizer For A Large Crowd.)
d: Rinse shrimp well.
Set aside.
Dissolve gelatine in boiling water.
Set aside.
Bring tomato soup to a boil.
Add cream cheese. Let it melt into soup.
Add mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Add celery, onion, chives, parsley and shrimp.
Stir well.
Pour into prepared ring mold or fancy fish mold that has been sprayed with Pam vegetable oil.
Place into refrigerator overnight.
Unmold onto platter or tray that has been lined with lettuce leaves.
Serve with crackers.
Melt butter in skillet.
Saute onion and broccoli until tender (about 20 minutes).
Combine rest of ingredients.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into lightly greased loaf-baking dish.
Bake about one hour at 350°.
Serves about 20.
Stir well, but do not use electric mixer.
For variety, add desired amount of one or more of the following ingredients: apples, nuts, raisins, dates, chocolate chips, cocoa or drained fruit cocktail, or up to 4 bananas (overripe).
Bake in a floured and greased Bundt pan at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool on a rack for about an hour.
Turn over onto serving plate.
In a bowl, mix together 1 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons flour and diced rhubarb.
Pour into an 8 or 9-inch baking dish and dot with butter.
Blend milk gradually into cream cheese.
Stir in lemon juice, shrimp, Worcestershire sauce, garlic salt and dill.
Cover; refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
Serve with crackers.

Brown ground chuck in a skillet; drain. Add spaghetti sauce and oregano; heat until warm. Put 8 ounces of sauce on bottom of a 13 x 9 x 2 or equal size pan. Remove from oven and let stand 15 minutes before serving. Good with garlic bread and tossed salad.
Place steak flat in shallow baking dish.
Mix all ingredients and pour over steak.
Let stand all day, turning occasionally or refrigerate overnight.
Barbecue 5 minutes on each side or broil 2 minutes on each side.
Cut diagonally into thin strips.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat shortening until creamy and glossy.
Gradually add sugar, beating until light and fluffy after each addition.
Add eggs and beat until thick and pale lemon color.
Sift dry ingredients; add alternately with bananas.
Blend thoroughly after each addition.
Mix together and bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Stir again and serve.
Serve with any vegetables.
Boil spaghetti for 9 minutes; drain.
Add milk and beaten eggs; mix well.
Put into buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Brown ground beef until crumbly; drain and place on top of spaghetti.
Pour pizza sauce on top of ground beef.
Layer onion slices, pepper slices, mushrooms and pepperoni.
Sprinkle with Mozzarella cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Provide each child with covered margarine tub.
Have available various measuring cups and spoons.
Instruct children to make a snack mixture by using various measuring tools.
Encourage them to compare amounts measured.
Combine pretzels, cereals and nuts in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Cook and stir brown sugar, oleo and corn syrup in a medium saucepan over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil.
Let the mixture boil without stirring for 4 minutes.
Remove heat.
Brown ground beef and onions in skillet.
Drain any grease and add tomatoes, corn and tomato paste.
Put in bottom of 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine flour, salt, paprika and pepper.
Roll chicken in flour mixture to coat very lightly, shaking off excess.
Spoon 2 tablespoons oil from top of artichokes into skillet and heat. Place chicken in pan and saute, browning slowly over moderate heat. Turn to brown on all sides.
Add onion when chicken is almost browned.
Spoon off any excess fat.
Add wine, heat to boiling, then cover.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes or until chicken is tender. Saute nuts in butter until lightly browned.
Set aside.
Add artichokes to chicken.
Mix cornstarch with remaining marinade, then gently stir liquid into skillet.
Simmer 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Remove chicken and artichokes to serving dish. Spoon liquid over chicken and sprinkle with toasted nuts.
Add pepper and cheeses to hot white sauce; stir until cheese melts. Combine sauce and potatoes and pour into 2-quart casserole. Toss crumbs with margarine and sprinkle over potatoes. Bake at 350°
for 35 minutes.
Garnish with chopped olives.
Bring first 3 ingredients to a boil; let cool.
Whip Pet milk; add sugar, celery, apple and nuts.
Add Jell-O mixture and refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into greased jelly roll pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Let set a minute.
Cream the sugar with the butter.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Shape into two rolls; chill until firm.
Cut 1/4-inch thick and bake 30 minutes at 300°.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar while warm.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, two at a time; beat well after each.
Add flour and sour cream alternately, beginning and ending with flour.
Add soda and extract last.
Bake in greased and floured large tube pan for 1 1/4 hours at 325°.
Mix syrup, sugar, salt, butter and vanilla.
Add eggs; pour into 9 inch unbaked pie shell.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients and bake at 400 degrees until brown.
Spray saucepan with nonstick cooking oil.
Place onion over medium heat.
Saute onion until clear.
Add all ingredients, except shrimp.
Stir well.
Add shrimp; cover and cook on very low heat for 35 minutes.
Uncover and toss rice.
Cover again and cook very slowly until rice is done.

Combine bread and milk in a small bowl.
Beat egg in large bowl; add oregano, salt, pepper and garlic.
Add beef and cheese; mix well.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Cook 3 or 4 pieces of bacon until crisp.
Crumble cool bread and crumble; add remaining ingredients.
Toss lightly and moisten with Miracle Whip.
Cheese is good in this.
Mix all but bacon in with Miracle Whip, then pour over bread and bacon.
Toss.

Cook chicken, debone and reserve broth.
Cut chicken in approximately 1-inch pieces.
Put in large pan the potatoes, carrots, onions, peas and celery; cook until tender.
Add 1 to 2 cups of broth and mix with cornstarch.
Mix vegetables and 3 cups of cooked chicken.
Pour broth, etc., over all and put in large baking dish.
With mixture hot and bubbling, put biscuits on top and bake at 400° for 15 to 25 minutes or until biscuits are done and browned.
Pound chicken to 1/2-inch thickness.
Place flour in plastic bag.
Beat eggs in shallow bowl or pie plate.
Combine cornmeal, cumin, salt and cayenne pepper in another pie plate.
Place chicken, 2 pieces at a time, in bag with flour and shake to coat. Remove chicken and dip in egg.
Roll in cornmeal mixture, pressing to coat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook until brown and cooked through.
Place on platter; top with sour cream and picante sauce.

Add water, stirring.
Serve over ice in glasses and garnish with lemon slices.

Pour over salad.
Top with remaining cheese.

Grind cranberries fine.
Add pineapple and sugar.
Stir well. Let stand in refrigerator overnight (covered).
Two hours before serving, whip cream.
Add nuts.
Place in a serving bowl and chill.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease 10-inch skillet.
Brown sausage and onion; drain well.
Combine eggs, cornmeal, corn, milk and oil.
Pour half of mixture into skillet.

Pour remaining batter over top.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes before serving.
Melt butter in a saucepan.
Pour in light brown sugar.
Mix together.
Add eggs, flour and flavoring.
Add as many pecans as you like.
Pour in a 9 x 13 pan and bake at 350° for about 20 minutes.
When middle of bread falls, take out of oven.
If you don't take out of oven when it falls, it won't be as moist.

Make your coffee as you usually do, but then add a quarter teaspoon of almond extract.
Voila!
In a large mixing bowl, combine sweet potatoes, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and salt.
Add eggs; with a fork, lightly beat eggs into sweet potato mixture.
Add the evaporated milk; mix well.
Place a pastry lined 9-inch pie plate on oven rack; pour in sweet potato mixture slowly.
Cover edge of pie with foil.
Bake in a 375° oven for 25 minutes.
Remove foil.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes more or until a knife inserted off-center comes out clean. Cool on wire rack.
Cover and chill to store.

Mix all ingredients together and put into greased casserole. Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Beat white syrup, sugar, salt, butter and vanilla. Add eggs and pecans. Pour into unbake pie shell. Sprinkle pecans over all. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.

Sprinkle some crackers over top.

Cook lasagne according to package directions; drain. (Separate lasagne and lay out flat on wax paper or aluminum foil to keep pieces from sticking together as they cool.)
Mix well and place heaping teaspoonful of mixture on cookie sheet.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Turn oven off and put in cookies for 2 hours or overnight.
Store in airtight container.
Mix chicken, almonds, pineapple and celery with enough Miracle Whip to make it hold together.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and Greek seasoning.
Mix with a fork all ingredients, except parsley flakes.
Roll into ball and roll in parsley flakes.
Chill and serve with crackers.
Combine corn, sugar, eggs, milk, pepper and 3/4 cup of cracker crumbs in casserole.

Bake at 400° for 20 to 30 minutes.

Place fruits in a bowl. Add Fruit-Fresh and orange juice concentrate, stirring gently.
Let stand for 1 hour or longer. Arrange fruits and marshmallows on skewers. Sprinkle each kabob with a small amount of sugar.
Fry hamburger, bacon and onion.
Drain off fat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Cut tenderloin(s) in half.
Blend remaining ingredients together.
Marinate pork in mixture for 10 minutes.
Grill or broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning when needed.
Serve with hot cooked rice, if desired.

Makes enough sauce for 5
- 3 1/2 to 4 lb. whole fryers split down the breast and cooked over a charcoal fire.

Makes 3 servings.
Mix all sauce ingredients together and pour over ribs.
Bake for 1 hour or until done.

Cover; cool to room temperature and whisk.
Fold in Cool Whip, Amaretto and brandy.
Serve with any type of cut-up fresh fruit.

Serve warm with ice cream or plain anytime.

Add spices and Worcestershire sauce.
Melt cheese with meat over low heat.
Serve on party rye.
(Place on cookie sheets and freeze. Reheat 8 to 10 minutes at 350°.)

Combine.
Stir with a spoon, putting into 3 greased and floured pans.

Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture starts to boil.
Continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Remove caramel mixture from
heat; pour over popcorn.
Toss quickly to coat.
Bake the caramel-coated popcorn in a 300° oven for 15 minutes.
Stir popcorn.
Return to oven; bake 5 to 10 minutes more, or until well coated.
Gently stir in the peanuts, if desired.
Turn caramel popcorn out onto foil. Cool; break up into 1-inch pieces.

Put first 3 ingredients in a large bowl and mix well with a fork.
Add shortening and mix with a fork until ingredients are crumbly.

Wrap each in plastic or waxed paper and chill at least 1/2 hour.
Dough may be left in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or frozen, until ready to use.

Remove ginger and lemon strips with a slotted spoon and discard. Place tea bags in a tea pot. Immediately add simmering water mixture. Cover and let stand 3 to 5 minutes. Remove tea bags and discard. Serve immediately in mugs. If desired, garnish with lemon slices.
Combine flour, salt, pepper and paprika; stir well.
Cut in butter until mixture looks like coarse meal.
Add cheese; stir well.
Roll dough to 1/3-inch thick on floured surface.
Cut with a 1 3/4-inch biscuit cutter.
Place on greased baking sheet.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Yields about 4 dozen.

Heat oven to 375°. In large bowl, combine contents of seasoning packet, poultry seasoning and water; mix well.

Add soup; blend well. Add potato slices, turkey, carrots, celery and onion, stirring until thoroughly combined. Spoon mixture into ungreased 2-quart casserole dish. Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Mix and pour over crackers.
Let sit several hours.
*Blueberry may be substituted for cherry.
In 10-inch skillet, place asparagus spears; add enough water to cover.
Bring to a full boil.
Cook over medium heat until asparagus is crisply tender (5 to 7 minutes).
Drain; return to skillet.
Add remaining ingredients, pushing asparagus to side just until butter is melted.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through (5 to 7 minutes).

Cook sugar and syrup until boils, then remove from heat.
Add peanut butter.
Stir peanut butter in sugar and syrup.
Pour mixture over corn flakes.
Press corn flakes and mixture into a sugar pan.
Let cool, cut in squares and eat.

Ad eggs. Beat well with spoon.

Spread into pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes.
Cool and cut into squares. Makes 16 brownies.

Brush with 1/2 of the mayonnaise mixture.
Grill 5 minutes, turn.
Brush with remaining mayonnaise mixture.
Grill an additional 5 to 8 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork.

Combine remaining ingredients in baking dish over ribs.

Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Spray casserole with Pam.
Slice potatoes; add salt and pepper.
Heat and bring to boiling; boil 3 to 4 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, water and oregano; dot with oleo.
Sprinkle shredded Mozzarella cheese on top.
Place sliced pepperoni over cheese and bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until potatoes are soft.
Boil chicken breasts in enough water to cover them completely.
Add 1 tsp. salt and either 1 stalk of celery diced or a couple dashes of celery salt and a couple slices of onion, diced up (optional).
You can also add one hot banana pepper to be taken out later (optional).
We like our food spicy.
Combine chicken, pineapple, almonds, ginger, garlic powder and mayonnaise.
Separate dough into 4 rectangles.
On ungreased baking sheet, press each piece of dough into 8 x 5-inch rectangle. Firmly press perforations to seal.
Cut each rectangle in half to make squares.
Place about 1/4 cup chicken mixture in center of each piece of dough.
Pull 4 corners of dough to top center of chicken mixture.
Twist ends and seal edges.
Brush with melted margarine and sprinkle with sesame seed.
Makes 8 sandwiches.
Combine beans in a pan with water and onions.
Bring to a boil, cover and remove from heat for 2 hours (or soak beans in cold water overnight).
Return to heat, bring to boil and simmer slowly until beans are very tender, about 3 hours.
Mash beans with a potato masher and add bacon drippings, butter or lard.
Mix well and continue cooking, stirring frequently until beans are thickened and fat is absorbed.
Salt to taste.
Serve or reheat.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Melt one pat butter or margarine in small bowl in microwave, on High for 30 seconds.
Add eggs and Ranch dressing (Marzetti Garden Ranch works the best).
Beat thoroughly.
Cook on High for one minute.
Fold in outer edges.
If desired, place cheese slice over top of eggs.
Cook again for 45 seconds on High with cheese, or 30 seconds without, until cheese is melted and eggs are not runny in center.
Serves one.
Sprinkle chicken breasts with salt and set aside.
Combine egg, flour and milk, stirring until smooth.
Dip chicken in egg mixture. Roll in cracker crumbs.
Fry chicken in 1-inch hot oil until brown. Drain on paper towel.
Yields about 3 dozen.
Layer chips in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix Ro-Tel tomatoes, cream of chicken and hamburger together.
Layer this on the chips.
Layer Cheddar cheese on the soup mixture.
Layer chips and then another layer of cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
In medium bowl, beat cheese until fluffy.
Add Eagle Brand milk; blend thoroughly.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour into crust.
Chill 2 hours or until set.
Top with desired amount of pie filling before serving.
Pour grape and orange juice into the container, then take the measuring cup and fill it with sugar.
Take the spoon and stir it for about 1 to 2 minutes.
And then you put it in the refrigerator for about 3 to 4 minutes.
Boil and debone chicken.
Mix the soups together on the stove with the broth.
Line a 12x13 pan with Doritos, put the chicken on top of the chips, pour soups on chicken and sprinkle with the onions.
Top with grated cheese.
Cover with foil and bake at 375 degrees for 30 minutes.
Soften 1 package dry yeast in 1/4 cup very warm water.
Cut butter and Crisco into flour and salt mixture until particles are the size of small peas.
Blend in the beaten eggs, sour thick or commercial cream, vanilla and the softened yeast.
Mix thoroughly. Cover; chill at least 2 hours.
Dough may be stored in refrigerator up to 4 days and baked as needed.
Combine all ingredients and store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
Mix sugar, cocoa, margarine, milk and salt.
Bring to a quick boil, stirring constantly.
Boil 1 1/2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add oats, peanut butter and flavoring.
Mix well and spoon onto wax paper to cool.
Beat all ingredients together. Bake in unbaked pie shell like a custard pie until knife comes out clean (450° for 10 minutes; reduce heat to 300° and bake 50 minutes or until done).
Blend together and serve with cut up fruit.
Melt butter, add flour, brown sugar, and nuts.
Spread in a 9 by 12 inch pan.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.
(Stir 3 or 4 times.)
Cool.
Set aside 1/2 for top.
Melt margarine.
Combine eggs, sugar and vanilla flavoring with margarine. Gradually add flour and cocoa. Add 1/2 cup pecans to mixture. Pour mixture into 9 x 11-inch greased pan.
Add remaining pecans, sprinkling on top. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
They are done when it rises and falls back down.
Mix all ingredients together. Cook in stew-pot or crock-pot. Cook until melted and hot.
Cook pork in lightly salted water over low heat 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Drain, reserving 1 cup broth.
Cut pork into thin slices and place in a large shallow baking pan.
Combine salt, reserved broth and remaining ingredients.
Mix well and pour over pork slices.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Heat oven to 450°.
Generously grease 6-ounce custard cups or 8 medium muffin cups (2 1/2 x 1 1/4-inch).
Beat eggs slightly in medium bowl; stir in remaining ingredients with fork or wire whisk just until smooth (do not overbeat).
Fill custard cups half full or muffin cups 3/4 full.
Bake 25 minutes.
Decrease oven temperature to 325°.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes longer or until deep golden brown.
Immediately remove from cups.
Serve hot.
Yields 6 to 8 popovers.
Combine sugar and oil, beating until smooth. Beat eggs slightly.
Add to sugar and oil, beating until creamy.
Add vanilla, soda and salt.
Alternate, adding flour and milk.
Add poppy seed and nuts.
Bake in well greased pan at 325° for approximately 1 hour.
Wash and rinse kraut; add vegetables.
Mix dressing and pour over mixture.
Let stand overnight.
Mix first 4 ingredients well.
Spread mushroom soup over casserole and bake 1 hour in 375° oven or until done.
Sprinkle cheese over top.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease a 15x10x1 inch jelly roll pan.
Line top and sides with waxed paper.
Grease waxed paper.
Beat eggs and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in pumpkin, stir in dry ingredients. Pour into pan, spread evenly, sprinkle with nuts.
Bake for 13-15 minutes.
Invert onto towel dusted with powdered sugar.
Peel off waxed paper, roll up cake and towel together from short side. Place seam side down on wire rack.
Cool completely, unroll cake.
Using a clear 3-quart salad bowl, layer lettuce, onion, tomatoes, avocado and olives.
Top with shrimp and cheese.
Sift flour, spices and soda.
Dredge fruit and nuts in additional flour.
Mix dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Add eggs and milk.
Fold in fruit and pecans.
Bake on greased cookie sheet for 15 minutes at 300°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Remove excess fat from chops and place in baking pan.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Then on each chop, spread catsup about 1/8-inch thick.
Sprinkle 1 1/2 to 2 teaspoons brown sugar on each chop, then place a slice of lemon on each chop.
Sprinkle a little more brown sugar.
Bake for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, depending on the thickness of the chops, basting occasionally.
Blend all ingredients until well blended. Spread in nonstick loaf pan, baking dish or individual molds.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes in loaf pan, 20 minutes if use individual molds.
Spread almonds in single layer in shallow pan.
Bake at 300° for 15 minutes, stirring often until almonds are toasted. Split each nut in half when cool.
Combine softened cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Add bacon, onion, dill and pepper.
Mix well.
Cover and chill overnight.
Form cheese mixture into shapes of two pinecones on serving platter. Beginning at narrow end, press almonds at slight angle into cheese mixture in rows.
Continue overlapping rows until all cheese is covered.
Garnish with clean, washed pine sprigs.
Serve with crackers.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
Grease a 9-inch pie pan.
Sprinkle in veggies, onion and cheese. Beat remaining ingredients and pour into pan over veggies. Bake at 400° for 35 minutes.
About 4 hours before serving, in Dutch oven over medium heat, in hot salad oil, brown the meat well on all sides.
Add remaining ingredients with 1 1/2 cups water and heat until boiling.
Reduce heat; cook until fork-tender.
Serve meat with pan liquid.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Put all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Fill 8 well-greased muffin tins or custard cups.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes, then lower oven temperature to 350° for 20 minutes longer.
Serve warm with butter and jam.
Put the cottage cheese through a food mill to make it smooth. Beat the mashed potatoes into the cottage cheese.
Beat in sour cream, eggs, salt and cayenne.
Stir in scallions.
Spoon into pastry shell.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake at 425° for 50 minutes or until golden brown.
Combine first
5 ingredients in blender and mix well.
Turn into ungreased deep dish 9-inch or regular 10-inch pan.
Add meat, shellfish or vegetables, poking into batter.
Top with onions, mushrooms and cheese.
Bake until top is golden brown, about 45 minutes at 350°.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Mix in a bowl the bell pepper, onion, tomatoes, green onion and bacon.
Mix in a separate bowl the sweet pickles, pickle juice, mayonnaise and Miracle Whip salad dressing.
Layer cornbread, vegetables and dressing alternately.
Refrigerate overnight.

Preheat oven to 350°. Beat egg in large bowl; add remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly, but do not overwork the mixture. Pack into 5 x 9-inch loaf pan. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes or until done. Spread with ketchup during the last 10 to 15 minutes of baking.
Combine chili, salsa, mushrooms, Parmesan and Italian seasoning.
Mix cottage cheese and parsley flakes.
Layer noodles, cottage cheese, chili and Mozzarella.
Repeat to make 3 layers. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Sift flour and salt into bowl.
Drop eggs into a well in center of flour and pour in milk.
Beat until smooth.
When roast is done, remove from oven
and keep warm.
Increase oven heat to 450°.
Pour beef drippings into 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan and heat until sizzling hot.
Pour batter over hot drippings.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until puffy and golden.
Serve in slices with roast beef.
Peel the potatoes and slice about 1/4 inch thick.
Bring to a boil for 10 minutes in salted water.
Drain.
Cook butter, sugar and milk on low heat for 10 minutes.
Add chocolate chips, marshmallow, prunes, nuts and vanilla.
Cook on low for 10 minutes.
Put in a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
When it gets cool, cut.
Mix all ingredients except grated cheese.
Put in large shallow casserole dish.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

Saut beef and drain excess fat. Add to onions, garlic and mushrooms. Continue cooking while adding remaining ingredients. Bring to a slow boil for 30 minutes to thicken. Lower heat with lid on and cook 30 more minutes. When serving, top with sour cream or grated cheese.
Combine zucchini and seasonings in casserole.
Cover.
Place in oven and cook 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and continue cooking for 10 minutes.

Coat the beef strips in 1 tablespoon flour and salt. Brown beef in butter; add mushrooms, onion and garlic. Cook until onion is crisp and tender. Remove mixture from pan and blend in 2 tablespoons flour and beef broth. Cook and stir until thick and bubbly. Stir in dairy sour cream and dry white wine. Return beef mixture to pan and mix. Spoon about 3 tablespoons of mixture into center of unbrowned side of crepe. Fold over; place seam down into 13 x 9 x 2 pan. Cover and bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes. Serves 6.
Brown chicken in oil until lightly browned; remove from pan. Add vegetables and stir for 2 or 3 minutes.
Add chicken broth mixed with cornstarch to pan.
Return chicken to pan.
Cover and cook slowly for 20 minutes.
Serves 2.
Mix the first 4 ingredients and pour into a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Mix next 3 ingredients well and pour over other mixture in pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Combine 1st 5 ingredients in small mixing bowl and beat 3 minutes with heavy duty mixer at medium speed.
In large mixing bowl, combine flour, shortening, sugar and water and mix thoroughly.
Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Cover and let dough rise in warm place, 85° free from drafts for 3 hours or until doubled in bulk.
Punch dough down; cover; refrigerate overnight.
With lightly floured hands, shape dough into 1 1/2-inch balls; place in 3 greased 9-inch cake pans.
Let rise in warm, draft free (85°) place approximately 2 hours or until doubled in bulk.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Yields 2 1/2 dozen large rolls.
Dough can be stored in refrigerator in greased and covered bowl 5 to 6 days.
Sift dry ingredients.
Cream together butter, shortening and sugar.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Beat in vanilla and egg.
Add flour mixture; beat until smooth.
Blend in milk.
Drop by teaspoon onto lightly greased baking sheet.
Flatten with glass dipped in sugar.
Bake in a 400° oven for 12 minutes.
Set oven to 350°. Peel, core and slice 12 to 15 apples in a 9 x 13 cake pan. Use good cooking apple (Jonathan, Ida Red or Yellow Delicious).
Sprinkle with 3/4 cup of white sugar and lightly sprinkle with cinnamon. Add 1/3 cup flour.
Line 9 x 13-inch pan with a layer of graham crackers.
Mix dry pudding and milk until completely mixed.
Add Cool Whip.
Mix thoroughly.
Spread 1/2 pudding mixture over crackers.
Add another layer of graham crackers.
Spread remaining pudding mix over crackers.
Add final layer of graham crackers.
Spread frosting over crackers.
Chill for 3 hours before serving.
Melt the first three ingredients.
Then add the minced clams, crabmeat, garlic salt to taste and a pinch of "accent."
Serve warm on crackers.
Prepare white sauce while combining Butter Buds, flour, salt and pepper and slowly add skim milk.
Stir with wire whisk until smooth and thickened.
Set aside.
Place 1/2 cooked macaroni in the bottom of a 2-quart casserole dish that has been sprayed with nonfat cooking spray.
Sprinkle with 1/2 onion, salt, pepper and cheese.
Repeat.
Pour sauce over casserole.
Drizzle liquid Butter Buds over top.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over top. Sprinkle stuffing over top.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes longer.
Have children mix all ingredients after chopping. Add enough grape juice to bind mixture.
Serve on matzoh.
In butter, saute onion and pepper.
Drain all vegetables.
In baking dish, layer hominy on bottom, then corn, mushrooms, pimientos and last the onion and pepper in the butter.
Over all, pour the Cheez Whiz.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix together in bean pot or casserole. Bake at 300° for 2 hours. Serves 10 to 12. It may be necessary to add a little water if cooked in casserole.
Makes 1 (9-inch) pie.
Preheat oven to 250°.
Combine coconut and butter; press into 9-inch pie plate.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, or until evenly browned.
Cool.
In medium saucepan, combine chocolate morsels, pumpkin, marshmallows and salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until morsels and marshmallows melt and mixture is smooth.
Cool; beat with wire whisk.
Fold in whipped cream. Spoon into crust.
Chill.
Combine oats, wheat germ and cinnamon. Mix oil and honey and add to first mixture.
Mix well.
Spread in shallow pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Watch carefully so it does not scorch.
Remove from oven and add raisins.
Makes 3 cups.
Mix ingredients together.
Heat and stir together until sugar is dissolved and flavors are well blended.
Simmer about 5 minutes. Pour over 1 to 3 pounds of cooked, shredded beef which has been cooked with 1 small chopped onion.
Dissolve yeast in warm water; mixture will be thick.
Sift together flour and sugar in large bowl; cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Add buttermilk and yeast mixture; stir well.
Turn dough onto well floured surface.
Roll out to desired biscuit thickness.
Cut out with biscuit cutter and place on baking sheet.
Brush tops with melted butter.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes until golden brown.
Makes about 2 dozen biscuits. Dough can be stored in an airtight container in refrigerator for 1 week.
Thicken the flour and milk.
Add cheese and melt.
Add the rest of the ingredients; simmer for 15 minutes.
Slice or julienne all vegetables.
Stir-fry vegetables in olive oil for 5 minutes; remove from heat.
Cover with lid for 2 minutes.
The heat and steam will make vegetables tender.
Can be served over rice or pasta.
Optional:
A can of crushed tomatoes may be added for a heartier meal.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In a large bowl, mix turkey, peas, corn, gravy, 2 tablespoons of the chives and the thyme.
Turn into shallow 2 1/2 to 3-quart baking dish; set aside.
Warm potatoes and mix in remaining chives.
Cover turkey mixture with potatoes. Bake at 400° for about 25 minutes, until turkey mixture is bubbly and potatoes begin to brown.
Makes about 6 servings.
Cook macaroni as directed and drain.
In large skillet, cook and stir onion, green pepper and butter, until onion is tender. Stir in macaroni and remaining ingredients.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole and cover.
Bake at 400° fo 30 minutes.
Pour chili into greased 8-inch square baking pan.
Combine remaining ingredients in order listed; blend well.
Pour batter over chili.
Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes or until done. Cool 5 minutes.
Combine first four ingredients.
Scald milk.
Cool to lukewarm. Crumble yeast into milk.
Add sugar.
When bubbling, add to cream in which the egg yolks have been beaten.
Mix well.
Add to flour mixture.
Mix thoroughly and refrigerate overnight.
Next morning, divide into 6 equal parts.
Roll each into a thin roll and twist two together (makes 3 rings).
Place each in greased pie pan and let rise for about 2 hours.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° for about 20 minutes.
Pit and peel avocados; mash pulp in medium bowl to chunky consistency.
Add lime juice, scallions, jalapeno chiles and tomatoes, then fold in cheese, bacon and coriander.
Season to taste with salt.
Serve as soon as possible to keep bacon crisp. Use your favorite chips for dipping.
Mash the sweet potatoes.
Add sugar, spices, butter or margarine and salt.
Beat until light, then stir in raisins and nuts.
Rinse chicken.
Pat dry.
Cut into thin strips.
In a skillet saute chicken in half the butter until lightly browned on all sides.
Remove from pan.
Sprinkle with flour, stir to combine. Add half and half, a little a time, until sauce is smooth and creamy.
Cook, stirring from time to time, for 10 minutes.
Add sherry; season to taste with mustard, salt and pepper.
Cook fettucini in salt water according to directions on package.
Drain well.
Place fettucini in hot individual serving bowls.
Ladle chicken with sauce over noodles.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and parsley.
Serve immediately.
Bake pie shell for 5 minutes and set aside.
Mix flour, sugar and salt.
Beat eggs and add to flour mixture.
Add all other ingredients, saving margarine for last.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cook all ingredients together until thick, then thin with sweet cream when ready to use.
Pour into muffin pan lined or cupcake wrappers.
Wrap and freeze.
Makes about 15.
Put a slice of tomato on each pork chop.
Season with salt and pepper.
Put a slice of onion on top of the tomato and dot with butter.
Bake in a moderate oven at 375° for 45 minutes.
Gravy may be made from the pan drippings.
Slice a layer of raw potatoes in bottom of greased casserole dish, then put a layer of raw onion with layer of hamburger.
Pour in cooked tomatoes, then season each layer to your liking with your favorite seasonings; season each layer.
Bake 1 hour in oven at 350° or until tender.
Salt chicken; dredge in flour or add salt and pepper to about half a bag of
a plastic bag (the kind that you get from the supermarket
with your vegetables).
Shake your drummettes in the bag (no
mess).
Deep
fry chicken.
Dip, while hot, in sauce made with remaining ingredients.
Weigh nuts and place them in a baking pan.
Melt 1/3 stick of margarine for each pound of nuts.
Add a very small amount of salt since the margarine contains salt.
(Since the nuts are a little greasy, more salt can be added after nuts are roasted.)
Pour the margarine mixture into the pan of nuts and stir thoroughly before placing in the oven.
Place nuts in the oven; turn control to 300°. Do not open oven at any time and do not stir nuts.
When temperature reaches 300° (light goes off), turn oven off.
Still leaving the oven closed, allow nuts to remain for another 20 minutes before removing.
Nuts will not seem roasted when you first remove them, but probably will please you after they are completely cool.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Combine next 3 ingredients. Combine all ingredients.
Put tea, juices and sugar in large pan and heat with spices. Serve warm.
Pound chicken breast to 1/2-inch thickness; salt and pepper and set aside.
Put potatoes, 1/2 cup sugar, 4 tablespoons butter, salt and vanilla in a mixer bowl.
Beat until mixture is very light and fluffy (this is the secret of the dish).
Pile mixture into a greased 2-quart casserole.
Mix together pecans, 1/2 stick butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar and cornflakes to make a crumbly topping. Spread over sweet potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes or until mixture is hot and topping browned.
Sift flour with baking powder, salt and soda.
Cream butter. Gradually add sugars; cream until light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla.
Beat well.
Add flour mixture in 4 parts, beating just until smooth after each addition.
Mix in rolled oats and coconut. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets.
Sprinkle with additional coconut and bake at 375° for 9 to 12 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.

recipes.t: Fancy Flounder Roll-Ups(A Great Dish For Those Whose Favorite Meal Is Fish.)
d: Divide broccoli among fillets, placing across and wrapping/rolling fillet around; secure with toothpick.
Arrange in 2-quart shallow baking dish (12 x 8 x 2-inch).
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix
all ingredients together;
heat to boiling, but do not boil.
Place in sterilized jars and seal.
Melt caramels with 1/3 cup evaporated milk in top of double boiler or barely simmering water or microwave.
Stir.
Grind the following ingredients: onions, cabbage, green tomatoes and green peppers.
Pour salt over mixture and let stand 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients.
Let set in refrigerator overnight in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In food processor or blender, chop onions, peppers, Romas and other tomatoes.
Add seasonings.
Serve with tacos, tortilla chips and Mexican dishes.
Soak bread crumbs in milk.
Add beaten eggs, sugar, butter, salt, cinnamon or nutmeg and vanilla.
Pour in greased dish or pan; bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Let cool.
Serve with sauce that follows.
Trim excess fat from beef.
Heat oil in 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook beef in oil about 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until brown on all sides.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Place onions in 3 1/2 to 6-quart slow cooker.
Place beef on onions.
Mix remaining ingredients; pour over beef and onions. Cover and cook on low heat setting 8 to 10 hours or until beef is tender.
Remove beef and onions from cooker using slotted spoon. Cut beef into slices.
Skim fat from beef juices in cooker if desired.
Serve beef with juices.

recipes.t: Michael'S Danish Chocolate Chip Tart A' L'Orange
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine Ricotta, eggs, sugar, butter and vanilla; beat well.
Stir in chocolate chips. Spoon 1/4 cup into each crust (mini).
Place on cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes (center will be soft).
Cool completely.
Brown steak in frypan with 1 teaspoon butter (margarine or Pam), garlic and ginger.
Put into crock-pot with all other ingredients except green peppers.
Cover and cook on high 3 to 4 hours or low 6 to 8 hours.
Add peppers and cook for 1 more hour.
Preheat oven to 350° (depending on your oven).
Bake for about 45 minutes.
Brown the hamburger meat in skillet.
Spread browned meat in bottom of a casserole dish.
Cover the meat with mushroom soup. Cover the soup with the sliced cheese, then top with the Tater Tots.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Grind veggies with coarse blade.
Sprinkle with salt and let stand overnight.
Drain off juice and cover with mixture of sugar, celery seed, prepared mustard and vinegar.
Mix all together and put in jars; seal.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes, carrots, parsnips and onions with rosemary and garlic.
Drizzle with margarine.
Arrange in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Bake at 450° for 40 to 45 minutes or until fork-tender, stirring constantly.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine first 7 ingredients.
In a medium bowl, whisk together remaining ingredients.
Add egg mixture to dry ingredients; stir until batter is moist.
Pour batter into 3 greased 3 x 5 1/2-inch loaf pans.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pans 10 minutes.
Turn onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Store in airtight container.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs, flavorings and buttermilk alternately with flour, salt and soda mixture.
Next, add melted chocolate and blend well.
Use 9-inch tube pan, greased and floured or Bundt pan, I prefer the latter.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 300°.
Remove from cake pan.
Place cake under tight cover until cool.
This cake is very moist and light in texture.
You will need aluminum foil (for baking sheet).
Combine the flours, wheat germ, dried milk powder, sesame seed, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Stir in the water well.
Butter four 1 pound shortening cans.
Pour in the batter.
Smooth tops.
Cover each tightly with foil.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes or until tops are golden brown.
Immediately remove bread from cans.
Cool on racks.
Cook bacon, hamburger, onion, green pepper and mushrooms until meat loses its color.
Add remaining ingredients.
Let simmer. Cook 1 pound spaghetti according to package directions.
Add to sauce and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve with grated Parmesan cheese.
Serves 8.
Mix together and cook until spinach is tender.
Serve warm with chips.
Combine tapioca pudding and vanilla pudding with water.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add orange Jell-O, stirring until dissolved.
Then add Cool Whip, stirring until dissolved.
Put in Mandarin orange segments, reserving a few for the top.
Chill until firm.
Soften cheese and margarine. Defrost in microwave from 1 to 1 1/2 minutes.
Blend with salt, pepper and seed.
You may use a food processor.
Add flour and process until soft enough to put through a cookie press.
Press strips onto a jelly roll pan that has been sprayed lightly with Pam.
Cut into desired length and bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Slice bananas into a blender.
Process until pureed.
Cream sugar and butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs and lemon peel until blended.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Beat dry ingredients into wet ingredients alternately with the pureed bananas.
Repeat twice, ending with dry ingredients.
Stir in poppy seed.
Pour into a well-greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 60 to 70 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Remove and place on a wire rack to complete cooling.
Mix Jell-O and water.
Cool.
To cake mix, add 4 eggs, oil and Jell-O water.
Beat as directed on box.
Put into Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Poke holes in cake with toothpick.
Pour over cake a mix of 1/2 cup lemon juice and 2 cups 10x sugar.
Cool 25 minutes.
Flip and put on plate.
Sprinkle 10x sugar over the top.
In medium saucepan, add water.
Place over high heat.
Add carrots.
Cover pan and cook for 10 minutes.
Add zucchini.
Cook 5 minutes.
Remove pan from heat and drain.
Puree vegetables until smooth in food processor.
Transfer pureed vegetables in large saucepan.
Add skim milk and place over medium heat uncovered.
Stir constantly with wire whisk.
Sprinkle in flour, cinnamon and pepper.
Add chicken bouillon.
Continue stirring until dissolved.
Makes 4 servings.
Calories 117, cholesterol 2 mg, fat 1 gram.
Mix butter, flour and nut meats together and put in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Cool.
Low-fat products may be substituted.
Heat oven to 375°.
Put rice in 9 x 13-inch casserole dish that has been sprayed with light cooking oil.
Place chicken (that has had the skin removed) on top of rice.
Mix cream of mushroom and cream of celery soups together and pour over top of chicken and rice.
Cover with foil and bake for 1 hour at 375°, then remove foil and bake for 15 minutes.
In mixing bowl, toss together the graham cracker crumbs and the melted 1/2 cup butter.
Press crumb mixture onto bottom of a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Use all of this in amounts to serve 6 people.
Steam on stove top on low heat 1 1/2 hours.

Set oven at 400°. Cream together butter, sugar, vanilla and flour. Mix well. Beat in eggs one at a time. Stir in Kahlua, corn syrup, milk and pecans. Mix well and pour into chilled crust. Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce heat to 325° and bake until firm (about 40 minutes). Chill. When ready to serve, garnish with whipped cream and pecan halves. Serves 8 to 10.
Place margarine in skillet and add steak strips and brown lightly.
Add other vegetables and cook until desired tenderness over medium heat.
(If needed, add a little vegetable oil while cooking.)
Mix dry ingredients.
Add beaten eggs, water, oil, pumpkin and nuts.
Mix well.
Bake in 3 ungreased loaf pans for 1 hour at 350°.
Press Hungry Jack biscuits into circles.
Mix well mayo, Parmesan cheese, tarragon, basil, green onions and garlic clove. Spread onto biscuit circles to 1/4-inch of edge.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 13 minutes.
Melt over low heat.
Spread on cooled crust.
Saute onions in margarine.
Add Cheez Whiz; mix thoroughly. Add thawed frozen chopped broccoli.
Add cream of mushroom soup and cooked rice.
Add milk and mix thoroughly.
Pour into baking dish and bake about 35 minutes at 350°.
Mix the Bisquick, cheese, salt, pepper and parsley together, then add the eggs, oil and butter.
Add the zucchini and the chopped onion.
Mix well.
Put the ingredients into a 10-inch pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until the toothpick comes out clean.
Melt butter in 10 inch baking dish.
Combine flour and sugar. Add milk.
Pour into the middle of melted butter.
Do not stir. Pour fruit into middle of dish.
Do not stir.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 min. to 1 hour, depending on depth of dish and oven.

Combine all ingredients except brown sugar and ketchup. Mix well. Press evenly in loaf pan. Combine ketchup and brown sugar in a small bowl. Mix well and spread over meat mixture. Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour.
Cut lettuce into small pieces.
Cut tomato into cube.
Add mayonnaise, mix well.
Chill until ready to eat.
Combine and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Place marshmallows on top after baking and brown just before baking.
Amount of marshmallows depends on the cook.
Mix all ingredients except Cheez Whiz.
Add 1 can of water and cook until tender.
Put in baking dish and cover with the Cheez Whiz. Bake in oven at 350° just until cheese melts.
Cook eggs.
While they are hot, mash them up in casserole dish with butter.
Put crab meat in.
Add salt and pepper, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and milk.
Stir.
Sprinkle top with cracker crumbs and dot with butter.
Cook at about 375° for approximately 30 minutes.
Be sure to pull crab meat apart.
Combine the ground beef, salt, pepper and onion together.
Add the tomato sauce and bread crumbs to the ground beef.
After cooking the meat until brown, put the meat into the green peppers. Boil the green peppers for about 2 minutes before you put the meat into them.
Sift flour.
Add brown sugar and salt.
Cut in shortening until fine crumbs are made.
Put in greased 6 x 10-inch pan and bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Blend the first 3 ingredients together and add the eggs, vanilla, oatmeal and Post Toasties. Sift together and add the flour, baking soda and baking powder.
Stir in the chocolate chips and pecan halves (optional).
Use ice cream scoop to put dough onto large cookie sheet (6 to sheet).
Bake at 350° for 18 minutes.

recipes.t: Lemon Scones(Flaky, Tender Biscuits With A Twist!)
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and margarine.
Cut with pastry blender until fine.
Stir in 1 egg, raisins, lemon peel and enough milk until dough leaves sides of bowl.

Peel and cut up eggplant; boil in salted water until tender then drain. Cook ground meat in a skillet with fat and seasoning. Add onion, garlic, and bell pepper; mix. Add rice and eggplant and mix thoroughly. If too dry, add a little water. Place in a greased casserole dish and cover with crumbs. Bake in a moderate oven, until golden brown.
Mix tomatoes, onion, parsley, basil and garlic.
Cut bread in oval slices.
Pour olive oil on bread slices and spread 1 to 2 tablespoons of mixture on top.
Put in oven at 375° to 400° for 10 minutes to toast.
Watch it!
Enjoy as a wonderful pupu!
Blend liquid ingredients into dry ingredients; do not overmix. Bake in greased muffin pans for 20 to 25 minutes at 425°.
Wash pickles of brine.
Slice or split lengthwise and put into pint jars.
Bring remaining ingredients to a boil, stirring.
Let cool.
Pour over pickles.
Let stand 30 days.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Layer in buttered casserole (9 x 12-inch) in order:
rice, green chilies, 1/2 of cheese, zucchini, tomatoes and salt as desired.
Mix sour cream, garlic salt, oregano, green onions and green pepper.
Spread over tomatoes and top with rest of cheese.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Melt butter in bottom of pan.
Mix flour, sugar and milk.
Add syrup and peach pieces.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix cream cheese, Worcestershire and garlic salt.
Spread on glass tray about 1/2-inch thick.
Cover with cocktail sauce. Crumble crabmeat on top of cocktail sauce.
Serve with crackers.
Boil for 5 minutes. Pour over beef. Put in fridge at least 2 hours. Best if left overnight.
Shake to mix occasionally. Fix beef as desired.

Brown meat with onions, drain grease. Put in crockpot. Add all remaining ingredients, (do not drain juice). Cook on High 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, then switch to low, to keep warm for serving. Can also be cooked in a large pot on stove.
With electric mixer at medium to high speed, cream butter and shortening until soft.
Add cheese; mix well.
Sift flour, salt, mustard and cayenne pepper together.
Add in 3 additions.
Mix well after each addition.
Pipe cheese mixture on a cookie sheet; bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350° or until just starting to turn golden brown at edges.
Carefully transfer cheese straws to a wire rack for cooling as they are very crisp and break easily. Sprinkle with paprika, if desired.
Makes 8 to 9 dozen.
Parboil zucchini about 7 minutes.
Cool.
Cut in half.
Scoop out pulp.
Chop pulp.
Mix with cheese (reserving 1/2 cup), eggs, rice, onion, bread crumbs and salt.
Stuff shells with mixture. Sprinkle with bacon.
Bake in greased baking dish at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Top with cheese the last few minutes of baking.
Fry bacon. Saute hamburger and onion. Crumble 10 slices of bacon into hamburger. Add the remaining ingredients.
Put into a baking dish. Crumble the last 2 slices of bacon on top of dish. Bake at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt margarine or butter and dip chicken breasts.
Mix flour and salt and dip chicken in this.
Beat egg with water and dip chicken.
Mix bread crumbs and cheese and roll chicken in this. Place chicken in baking dish and bake 45 minutes in a preheated 350° oven.
Place raw eggs in the mixer.
While beating, add salt and mustard.
Slowly add the oil, then remaining ingredients.
Store dressing in covered jar.
In a large skillet, saute sausage, bell pepper and onion.
In a boiler, bring water, salt and rice to a boil and cook only 10 minutes.
Do not cover.
Remove rice and water from heat.
Add the packages of soup.
Mix well.
Add this to sausage mixture and add cheese.
Pour all this into a casserole dish.
Bake 30 minutes at 325°.
Do not grease.
Do not cool.
Preheat oven to 475°.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl. Combine the syrup and milk, adding this to flour mixture.
Stir with a fork until thoroughly mixed.
Do not overwork the dough. Shape the mixture into a ball and place it between two pieces of wax paper that have been dusted with flour.
Roll the pastry into a circle large enough to fit in a 9-inch pie pan.
Spray pan with a nonfat cooking spray.
Arrange crust in pan.
Cut off the edge that hangs over.
Prick the bottom with a fork.
Bake 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool before adding filling.

If you are making a pie where the filling needs to be cooked with the shell, simply bake at 350° for 45 minutes or however long the recipe calls for. Wrap foil over edges while baking so the crust won't get overbrown. Remove last 5 minutes.
Yield:
1 pie crust (8 servings).
Per serving:
Fat 0.13 g, calories 54, protein 1.7 g, cholesterol 0.24 mg, carbohydrates 11.3 g, sodium 3.4 mg.
Prepare rice as directed on package.
Mix in mayonnaise.
Mix apple with lemon juice.
Stir into rice mixture with remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Jimmy Dean is a good sausage for this.
For 2 whole chicken legs, make 3 cups of White Sauce.
Use the numbers in parentheses.
Melt butter in saucepan over low heat. Blend in flour, salt and pepper.
Cook over low heat, stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in milk.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Cut fryer in quarters, wash, cover and cook in water with salt and celery.
Let stay in broth until cooled.
Remove and debone chicken, saving broth.
Saute peppers and onions in oleo.
Do not brown.
Cook spaghetti in broth.
Add water if necessary.
Do not drain.
Add onions, peppers and chicken.
Mix together well, then add Ro-Tel and diced Velveeta.
Mix lightly until cheese melts. Add peas with juice.
Be careful not to mush up peas while stirring.
Good made a day ahead.
Scald milk.
Pour over bread crumbs and eggs.
Add butter, sugar, raisins, fruit, slivered almonds and spices.
Pour into well-buttered ovenproof dish (1 1/2-quart).
Set in hot water about 1 to 1 1/2 inches deep; bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
(Try center; should come out dry.)
Dot with butter and cinnamon-sugar if desired.
Serve hot or cold with whipped cream or wine sauce (optional).
Drain juice from the pineapple and put in a large bowl.
Add the milk, cherries and nuts; mix well with a spoon.
Fold in the unfrozen Cool Whip.
Cover and refrigerate.
The salad sets well when refrigerated the night before or 4 hours before serving.
Combine butter and flour. Let cook until butter melts. Add milk and cook until thick. Add at least one cup of chicken. Serve over biscuits or rolls.
Cook beef, onion and garlic; drain fat.
Add tomatoes, water and bouillon.
Bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
Add orzo and mixed vegetables.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Enjoy.
Mix all above ingredients together.
Put into a 9 x 13 baking dish.
Sprinkle crushed corn flakes on top of the mixture (about 1 1/2 to 2 cups).
Pour melted butter on top (1/2 stick).
Bake at 350 for about 1 hour.
Simmer ingredients 2 hours and serve with toothpicks.
Slowly pour milk into pudding in a saucepan, stirring constantly over low heat to keep smooth.
Add softened butter or margarine.
Continue cooking over low heat, stirring constantly, until it begins to boil.
Remove from heat.
Gradually beat in the sifted confectioners sugar.
Add vanilla and cool.
If the frosting is too thick, a little milk may be added to spread easily.
This will frost and fill a 9-inch layer cake.
In a large skillet, cook the ground meat.
Brown with the onion, then drain.
Add taco seasoning mix.
Add the Hidden Valley dressing mix.
In a large pot, add the kidney beans, pinto beans, hominy, stewed tomatoes and Ro-Tel.
Add 4 cans water.
Simmer. Serve hot with chips or crackers.
Grease	9
x 13-inch cake pan.	Spread 3 cups marshmallows
on bottom of pan. In small saucepan, cook rhubarb, sugar and
water. Remove
from
heat. Stir in strawberry jello mix. Cool.
Mix cake according to directions on package.
Pour cake mixture
over marshmallows,
very
gently,
then pour rhubarb mixture
over the cake mixture, very gently.	Bake at 350° for 45 to	50 minutes. Cool in pan. When serving, turn cake pieces upside down and top with Cool Whip.
Drain and rinse crab or shrimp.
Spread cream cheese over platter or dish, top with sauce and then with shrimp or crab.
(If desired, sprinkle lemon juice on top.)
Serve with crackers or chips.
Cook chopped onion in melted margarine.
Add other ingredients; mix well.
Bake in casserole dish at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Grease Bundt pan. Cut loaf into 7 sections.
Put in pan.
Mix sugars and cream together.
Pour over rolls. Cover and put in refrigerator overnight.
Next morning, preheat oven to 350°.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes. Remove and let stand until caramel sets, approximately 30 minutes.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar and flour.
Add remaining ingredients. Mix well.
Pour in unbaked pie shell.
Bake slowly until firm at 300° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt chocolate chips and margarine in double boiler, stirring until smooth. Stir in raisins and nuts. Drop by tablespoons onto wax paper.
Cool.
Mix all ingredients together and spread mixture over bread. Broil until toasted; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Serve hot.
Combine 3 cups water, uncooked rice and next 4 ingredients in a medium saucepan.
Bring rice mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 3 cups milk.
Combine remaining 1/2 cup milk and egg, stirring with a wire whisk.
Gradually stir about 1/4 of the hot rice mixture into the egg mixture.
Add back to the rice mixture; stir well.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Discard lemon rind and cinnamon stick.
Stir in vanilla and raisins.
Serve warm or chilled.
Yields 6 servings.
In a medium bowl, combine the confectioners sugar and peanut butter.
Mix to a crumbly consistency (like a streusel) and remove about 1/2 cup of the mixture; set aside.
Pour the remaining mixture evenly over the pie crust.
Make pudding according to package directions; pour pudding over the crumb layer, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
Mix first five ingredients.
Add ginger ale and soda water last.
Makes 40 to 50 (4 ounce) cups.
(Easy.) Dissolve yeast	in warm water, then add buttermilk, oil and sugar.
Mix
baking
powder,
salt and soda into flour. Pour into
liquid
ingredients.
Stir well with wooden spoon. Doesn't have
to
rise.
May store in refrigerator and use as needed.
Keeps several days.
Combine cereal, raisins and peanuts in large container; mix well.
Combine margarine, chocolate morsels and peanut butter in saucepan.
Heat until melted, stirring constantly.
Do not boil. Add vanilla and let cool.
Pour over cereal mix and mix until well coated.
Pour into large brown paper bag.
Add confectioners sugar and shake.
Store in tightly covered containers.
Yields 12 cups candy.
Note:
This works well in double boiler.
Combine soup and milk in a medium saucepan.
Stirring with a wire whisk, add tomatoes and cheese.
Cook over low heat until cheese melts and soup is hot.
Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with bacon.
Yields 4 2/3 cups.
Toast each english muffin half.
Lightly spread with butter. Place two paper towels atop two coupled paper plates.
Separate pepperoni and place atop paper towels.
Microwave on High for 20-30 seconds (do not blacken).
Remove from microwave and dab off excess oil with paper towel.
Spread 1/2 tsp. salad dressing on each muffin half.
Place 1 slice tomato and 5 slices of pepperoni on each muffin half.
Top each with 1/4 c. of cheese.
Place muffins on non stick cookie sheet.
Broil on high for 5 minutes or until browned (no more than 8 minutes).
Cool 1 minute.
Serve.
Simmer chicken breasts until tender.
Save a little broth. Shred chicken.
Mix soup ingredients (soups, salsa, milk and broth).
Grease 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Cut tortillas into quarters and start layering tortillas on the bottom, then chicken pieces, then soup mixture and top with cheese.
Repeat layers. Cover with foil and refrigerate 24 hours.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until bubbly.
Cook broccoli, drain and set aside.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bubbly.
In a large bowl, thoroughly mix 1/2 cup of the Prego sauce, beef, bread crumbs, onion and egg.
In 12 x 8-inch baking pan, firmly shape meat into 8 x 4-inch loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours or until done.
Break up tuna.
Add egg and bread crumbs.
Mix well.
Form into patties and fry or grill lightly.
Layer apples and yams in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
In a saucepan, combine remaining ingredients. Cook, stirring, until thick.
Pour sauce over yams and apples. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Heat butter in heavy saucepan.
Add onions and cook until soft.
Add rice and stir.
Add water, seasoning, bay leaf, thyme, salt and pepper.
Boil.
Cover and let simmer for 20 minutes.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Dissolve soda in milk; add eggs. Sift flour twice and add to milk mixture.
Add remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Drop on greased cookie sheets.
Bake in 350° oven for about 10 minutes or until lightly brown.
Combine first 4 ingredients; chill well.
Make dressing with remaining ingredients (except croutons); shake well to blend. Pour over greens, a little at a time and toss (it doesn't take all of the dressing for 1 salad).
Add croutons just before serving. Serves 8.
In a large 9 x 13 Pyrex dish, place the above ingredients in order given.
Bake at 400° for about 40 minutes.
Layer lettuce, onion, peas and eggs.
Sprinkle with bacon bits. Ice top with mayonnaise.
Sprinkle top with cheese.
Mix together the cream cheese, mushroom soup, tuna, onion, mustard and milk.
Add macaroni.
Top with the bread crumbs and melted margarine.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix the first 4 ingredients together; let stand about 5 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Beat all together.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes at 400°.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, celery seed, onion, milk, bread crumbs, egg and Worcestershire sauce.
Shape into a ball and place in a baking pan.
Combine the brown sugar and catsup and pour over the top of the meat loaf.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Snap off tough ends of asparagus.
Remove scales from stalks with a knife or vegetable peeler, if desired.
Cover asparagus; cook in a small amount of water 6 to 8 minutes, or until asparagus is crisp-tender.
Drain.
Combine remaining ingredients in a jar; cover tightly and shake vigorously.
Place asparagus in a shallow container; pour marinade over asparagus.
Cover and chill 8 hours. To serve, drain off marinade.
Yields 8 servings.
Combine evaporated milk, marshmallows, morsels and salt in saucepan; stir over medium heat until thick.
Line bottom of 9-inch pie pan with vanilla wafers.
Spoon out 1/2 quart vanilla ice cream over wafers.
Cover with half the chocolate mixture. Repeat again.
Put pecans on top.
Freeze 3 to 5 hours.
Serve. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Prepare hamburg your way.
Make small meatballs.
Mix chili sauce, jelly and water.
Bring to a boil.
Add meatballs.
Cover and cook for 1 hour.
Mix every once in a while.
Serve over rice.
Season chicken with salt and Accent.
Cover with beaten egg for 2 to 4 hours.
