Cook enough potatoes that when mashed makes about 2 1/2 quarts.
Add margarine and enough milk to thin.
Add mayonnaise, mustard, pickles, onion and eggs.
Mix well.
Top with egg slices. Serve hot or cold.
To the crushed crackers, add the melted oleo, sugar and gelatine.
Mix all together and put in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pat down and chill.
Cook margarine, sugar and dates over low heat, stirring constantly until melted.
Remove from heat.
Stir in 1 teaspoon vanilla flavoring.
Add 2 cups Rice Krispies and 1 cup chopped nuts.
Let cool.
Roll into small balls in confectioners sugar. Makes approximately 3 dozen.
Mix well and bake at 350°.
Bake in 3 layers or an oblong pan.
Cool.
Spread icing over cake.
Take 2 big rolls frozen cookie dough.
Slice it thin.
Put on cookie sheets by loving hands of all the G.A.'s touching the cookies.
Bake at 350°
for 4 to 7 minutes.
Cool and put in Baggies to give to a lonely person.
Combine corn, cream cheese, and mushroom pieces in saucepan. Heat over low heat until creamy.
Stir continually, will scorch easily.
Cream sugar, butter, egg yolks and lemon extract.
Add flour and baking soda mixture.
Mix well.
Fold in fruit and nuts that have been dredged in flour.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into batter.
Wash and drain mushrooms.
Hollow out and chop enough of the pieces to make 3 tablespoons.
Cook pieces with onion, garlic and 1 teaspoon extra virgin olive oil.
Stir in crab, shrimp, Prosciutto and cheese, along with catsup.
Stuff into mushroom crowns; sprinkle with fine soft bread crumbs.
Bake at 425° for 6 to 8 minutes.
Cook fettucini in boiling salted water.
While cooking pasta, prepare sauce.
Melt butter and cheese over low heat.
Gradually stir in cream, walnuts and wine.
Bring to boil then whisk a bit of the sauce into the egg yolk.
Return the mixture to the sauce and stir continuously over gentle heat until thickened, do not allow it to boil.
Stir in the parsley and pour mixture over cooked and drained pasta.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.
Makes 2 to 4 servings.
Mix all together.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Bake in 350° oven for one hour.
Stir after 1/2 hour and take the lid off for the last half hour.

Cream 1/4 cup softened butter. Gradually add the sugar alternately with the bourbon, beating until thick and smooth. Shape measuring 1/2 teaspoons of mixture in small balls using sugar on hands if necessary. Press a pecan half on each side of ball and chill. Melt chocolate with 1 1/2 teaspoon of butter in top of double boiler. Dip one end of each candy in the chocolate and put on cookie sheet covered with wax paper. Chill. Makes about 2 1/2 pounds.

Cook macaroni and set aside. Mix cottage cheese and sour cream with a little under half the bag of cheese. Then combine mixture with macaroni. Spray a 13 x 9 pan with cooking spray and pour macaroni mixture into pan. Top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese bubbles or turns golden brown, whichever is preferred. Enjoy!
Cook green pepper and onion in a saucepan coated with vegetable spray over medium heat, stirring constantly 5 minutes or until tender.
Stir in broth, chopped potato and pepper.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 5 to 7 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Combine cornstarch and milk, stirring until smooth. Gradually add to potato mixture, stirring constantly.
Stir in corn.
Boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Serve immediately.
In a small bowl, combine flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
In a large bowl, cream margarine, granulated sugar, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Gradually beat in flour mixture. Stir in oats and butterscotch morsels and drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 7 to 8 minutes for chewy cookies, 9 to 10 minutes for crispy cookie.
Cool for 2 minutes and remove from baking sheets.
Fry pork chops.
Put in slow cooker or drain oil and leave in skillet.
Add soup, water, green pepper and onion. Salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and cook until pork chops are tender.
Preheat oven to 350°. Combine the margarine, sugar, egg yolk, eggs, buttermilk, baking soda, flour and vanilla. Mix well. Pour into three greased layer pans. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake potatoes for 1 hour or until tender.
Cut shallow, lengthwise slice from 1 side of potatoes and scoop out pulp, reserving shells.
Combine pulp with butter, milk, chives, seasonings and half the cheese.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Spoon pulp into reserved shells.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Cook meat with seasonings except salt and pepper in Dutch oven.
Bring to a boil, then cook on low heat 3 to 4 hours until done.
Add salt and pepper to taste during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Place sliced green peppers on top of beef and steam until tender.
Remove meat from broth and cool.
Slice beef thin and return to broth.
Serve on Italian bread.
Dissolve gelatin in cold water.
Combine and gradually heat other liquids.
Pour in gelatin and stir.
Let liquid cool.
Oil mold.
Sprinkle onions, celery and olives on bottom (chopped very fine).
Works great to chop vegetables in blender with some water added, then strain, pressing out water.
Pour cooled mixture in mold.
Chill until firm.
(I mix vegetables right into liquid and pour in a bowl; works fine.)
Excellent for the holidays or anytime.
Serve a little dab of mayo on top.
A real tradition in the Roseberry family!
In heavy skillet, cook onions in heated butter until slightly browned.
Sprinkle with flour and cook over low flame until golden, never allowing them to become dark brown.
Add consomme and water. Bring to boil, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, then simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Spoon into casserole or individual bowls. Place slices of bread on top.
Sprinkle generously with cheese. Add pepper.
Sprinkle with melted butter.
Brown quickly under broiler flame.
Serves 4 to 6.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients, except cracker crumbs.
Pour into square, well-buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle crumbs on top.
Cook for 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Grease bottom of Bundt pan.
Sprinkle half of nuts on bottom; arrange rolls on top of nuts.
Combine margarine, sugar, cinnamon, pudding and nuts; pour over top.
Let set in a cool oven overnight.
The next morning, tuck rolls back inside pan and remove from oven.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, then turn upside-down on plate.
Brown beef and onion. Put in casserole dish, mix squash, cheese, crackers, eggs, tomatoes with beef and onion. Bake in oven at 350° for 30 min.
Pack okra tightly in jars.
Add a few hot peppers and a button of garlic to each pint.
Bring to a boil the water, vinegar, salt and sugar.
Pour over okra in jars and seal.
Let age about 3 weeks.
Add water to raisins and boil 5 minutes or until liquid decreases to 1/2 cup.
Cool.
Cream shortening, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add other ingredients alternately to cream mixture. Drop by 2 heaping teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 400°.
Makes 40 large cookies.
Salt eggplant and leave for 30 minutes to drain.
Pat dry. Heat 6 tablespoons olive oil in a large heavy pan. Add eggplant. Brown on all sides. Remove. Drain on paper. Add more oil. Cook zucchini until moisture has evaporated.
Remove. Drain. Cook peppers. Remove. Drain. Add onions.
Cook until soft, not brown. Stir in tomatoes, garlic, sugar, parsley and thyme.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the rest of the vegetables. After 5 minutes, remove from heat.
Mix in basil. Refrigerate overnight.
Combine first 5 ingredients; beat with an electric mixer just until smooth.

Place a well-greased muffin pan in oven at 450° for 3 minutes or until a drop of water sizzles when dropped in pan. Remove pan from oven; pour 1 tablespoon of batter into each cup. Sprinkle each with 1 teaspoon cheese; fill each cup 3/4 full with remaining batter.
Bake at 450° for 25 minutes.
Cook noodles.
Pour in bowl.
Mix in soup and tuna.
Add cheese on top.
Cook in oven until cheese is melted and warmed up.
Soak wheat in cold water for 45 minutes.
Change water several times.
Use sieve; press to squeeze dry.
Chop parsley, mint leaves and tomatoes very fine.
Add wheat, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Serve with fresh lettuce leaves or serve in pita bread.
Serves 6.
Grease and flour Bundt pan.
Mix together cake mix, pudding, poppy seed, oil and water.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix well. Pour into prepared Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Combine cookie crumbs and butter.
Press firmly into bottom of a 9-inch spring-form pan.
In a large mixer bowl, beat cream cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk until smooth.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Mix well.
In a small bowl, toss 1/2 cup chips with flour to coat; stir into cheese mixture.
Pour into crust.
Sprinkle remaining 1/2 cup chips evenly over top.
Bake for 1 hour, or until it springs back when lightly touched.
Mix cheeses, garlic and green chilies together.
Stir in nuts. This is really good on Club crackers.
You may roll it into a ball and roll in nuts, if you wish.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Cover and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Uncover and continue baking an additional 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 10 to 12 easily.
Combine first four ingredients and mix thoroughly. Shape into balls about the size of a quarter.
Brown on all sides in a dry skillet; drain on paper towels.
Drain fat from skillet, then add remaining ingredients.
Stir well.
Return meatballs to sauce. Refrigerate until time to use.
When ready to use, reheat, simmering for 20 minutes.
Serve in a chafing dish with cocktail picks.
Yields 36 balls.
For a party of 50, triple recipe.
Mix all together in micro-safe dish and heat until cheese melts.
Stir and serve with tortilla chips.
Decorate top with chopped olives.
Teens love it!
Brown ground beef and onions in large pan.
Then add catsup, brown sugar, vinegar, salt and mustard; mix well.
Then add beans. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Makes large casserole or several small ones.
Freezes well.
Thaw and reheat.
Sprinkle chicken breast with tenderizer, garlic salt and seasoning salt.
Fold chicken breast in half around slice of cheese and wrap with slice of bacon.
Top with soup and bread crumbs.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Pour lemon juice over crushed bananas and mix all.
Pour into cups and put in freezer for 1 hour.
Top with maraschino cherries. Freeze overnight.
Makes 25 (5 ounce) cups or 35 (3 ounce) cups.
Beat eggs; add sugar, cooking oil and vinegar.
Sift flour and soda together.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Bake in a tube pan for 40 minutes at 350°.
Test with a toothpick.
Grind cranberries and apples and mix with sugar.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water or juice.
Add cold water and refrigerate until Jell-O thickens, then add fruit mix.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drop by spoonfuls on wax paper.
Put broth and water into a 10-cup saucepan over medium heat. Mix next 8 ingredients together and form into small meat balls (1-inch size) and drop into boiling liquid.
Let simmer 3/4 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In lightly greased 9 x 12 inch baking pan, spread pineapple and top with pie filling.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over this.
Slice margarine into 12 slices and dot over top. Cover all with coconut.
bake for 1 hour or until golden.
Serve with ice cream or whipped cream if desired.

In mixing, beat cream cheese until smooth. Add 1/2 c sugar, salt, 1 egg, and 1 tsp vanilla. Beat just to combine. Spread mixture on bottom of pastry. Sprinkle pecans over cream cheese mixture. Lightly beat 3 eggs. Add 3 tbsp sugar, syrup, melted butter, and 1 tsp vanilla. Place pie on a baking sheet on oven rack. Slowly and carefully pour syrup mixture over pecans. Cover edge of pie crust with foil. Bake at 375° for 20 min. Remove foil. Bake at 325° for 20 min. Bake at 325° for 15 to 20 min. more, till knife inserted in center comes out clean. Cool before serving. Refrigerate leftovers. Serves 6 to 8.
Cream shortening, butter, sugar and eggs.
Beat well dry ingredients, add to creamed mixture and add nuts. Drop by tsp. about 2 inches apart. Bake at 350° for 12-15 minutes. Makes 5 dozen.
Season and brown
chops.
Place
over rice in casserole dish. Place onion and
pepper
on top of each chop.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour
consomme
over all.
Bake for one hour at 325°.
Boil the sugar, lemon rinds and 1 quart water for 5 minutes. Cool, then add remaining ingredients, except ginger ale.
Chill. When ready to serve, add ginger ale.
Cook macaroni as directed on package; drain.
Pour in casserole dish.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Melt margarine.
Saute whole cloves until brown.
Remove garlic.
Mix sour cream, yogurt and Parmesan cheese and put in skillet with butter.
Heat oven to 400°.
Generously grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish. Cook beef and onion in 10-inch skillet until beef is brown. Drain. Stir in soup, vegetables and milk.
Stir baking mix and water in baking dish until moistened.
Spread evenly. Spread beef mixture over batter. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 30 minutes.
Drain the vegetables.
Combine with onion, celery and pimentos.
Pour dressing over vegetables.
First mix ground meat, pepper, salt, and water.
Cook the meat in a pan on the stove for one hour.
Put the meat on the buns.
Set jello using water and 1 cup juice.
Add drained fruit before jello sets.
Let set.
Cook 1 cup juice, sugar, flour, egg and butter.
Let cool.
After it cools, mix 1 envelope Dream Whip according to directions on package.
Carefully fold into cooked mixture.
Spread on top of jello and fruit.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Date Nut Bread(Made In Soup Cans)
d: Put chopped dates in a saucepan and add cup of water.
Bring to a boil.
Set aside to cool.
In another bowl, beat eggs.
Add sugar and vanilla or rum and mix well.
Then sift together flour, baking powder, salt and soda.
Combine the ingredients and place into pie crust.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes two pies.
Put hash browns in 9 x 13-inch baking dish and let thaw. Combine remaining ingredients and pour over hash browns.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa and soda.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour into ungreased pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Melt margarine and saute onion until tender.
Add soup and heat.
Add cream cheese and melt.
Add half jar pimento.
Fill tortillas with mixture and fold over.
Pour rest of mixture and pimento over them.
Top with other cheese.
Heat in oven until hot and melted.
Melt butter or margarine and stir in sugar.
Add juice and rind.
Heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Stir in the oats and nuts.
Chill mixture for an hour.
Shape into balls.
Roll balls in coconut flakes.
Makes about 30.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Melt butter and chocolate squares.
Cool slightly.
Blend in sugar and one egg at a time and beat one minute.
Add walnuts and dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Chill at least 30 minutes.
Shape into balls using 1 teaspoon of dough for each.
Roll in sugar.
Place on greased baking sheet.
Bake at 300° for 18 to 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Freeze It And Forget It Fruit Salad
d: Combine syrup, egg, sugar, salt, flour and vinegar in saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened.
Cool.
Add fruit to cooked mixture.
Chill Carnation in refrigerator tray until soft ice crystals form around edges of tray (10 to 15 minutes.)
Add lemon juice; whip very stiff (1 minute.)
Fold into fruit mixture.
Spoon into 6 cup mold.
Freeze until firm about 5 to 6 hours.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease 1 to 1 1/2 quart casserole. Arrange potatoes in casserole.
Mix sugar, cornstarch, salt, cinnamon and orange peel in heavy quart saucepan.
Add apricot nectar and water.
Cook on high until mixture comes to boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in apricots and margarine.
Pour evenly over potatoes.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes (uncovered).
Mix potatoes, onion and bacon in casserole dish.
Mix soup and milk; pour over potatoes.
Cook in microwave for 10 minutes.
Mix in Cheez Whiz.
Cook 10 minutes longer or until potatoes are done.
Mix all ingredients except chocolate together.
Spread by hand into a greased 10 x 15-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Do not overbake.
While cookies are still warm, spread chocolate over them.
Prepare spaghetti sauce mix according to directions.
Add oregano and parsley.
Melt butter in frying pan and add bread dressing.
Toss until brown.
Put zucchini in bottom of casserole. Spoon part of sauce over it.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and bread crumbs.
Top with Mozzarella and tomato slices.
Add remainder of sauce and rest of bread; top with cheese.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes in 375° oven.
This recipe makes 3 or 4 pie crusts.
Dough may be frozen in a freezer bag for future use.
Soak crumbs in milk with powdered sugar and salt for 1/2 hour. Fold whipped cream and vanilla into softened macaroons.
Fill paper baking cups in cupcake tins.
Decorate with maraschino cherry bits.
Freeze without stirring.
Combine all ingredients and chill.
Serve with raw vegetables.
Cook shells and drain.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Saut mushrooms in butter.
Mix all ingredients together and simmer over low heat.
Add salt, pepper and garlic powder to taste.
Mix and store in a glass jar.
Keep lid on tight.
This will keep for years.
Mix all ingredients; spread on buns.
Wrap in foil and place in a shallow pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, until heated through and the cheese melts.
Mix the ingredients well in large bowl.
Roll out and cut into star shapes.
Bake at 350° for 9 to 10 minutes.
Makes 2 to 3 dozen.

Place onions in an 11 x 8 1/2 x 2-inch (28 x 21.5 x 5-cm) dish. Cook, uncovered, at 100% for 2 minutes in a 650 to 700 watt oven. Stir in rice and cook, uncovered, for 1 minute or until rice is milky-white, but not browned.
Mix ingredients well.
Add 2 to 3 slices of tomatoes.
Chill at least 4 hours and better if overnight.
Mix cake mix according to instructions on box.
Bake in 12 x 18-inch or 11 x 15-inch pan.
When done, let cool completely before adding the rest of the topping.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Meanwhile, chop celery.
Drain salmon. Break into large chunks.
In a 1 1/2-quart casserole, combine celery, condensed soup, milk, frozen broccoli, lemon peel and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Add salmon and uncooked noodles, then toss lightly until well mixed.
Bake, covered, in a 350° oven about 50 minutes or until noodles are tender, stirring once after 25 minutes of cooking.
Sprinkle salmon-noodle mixture with cheese.
Bake, uncovered, about 5 minutes more until cheese is melted.
Makes 4 servings.
Contains 244 calories.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together, then work in the shortening.
Take out 1 cup for topping.
Add the cinnamon, brown, sugar, vanilla, buttermilk and soda.
Stir all together.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle on the topping.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients together in large glass measuring cup. Microwave on High until it comes to a boil, stirring every minute.
Stir in vanilla and butter.
Serve over vanilla ice cream.
Select good firm ripe tomatoes; scald and strain through a coarse sieve to remove seed and skin.
When cold, add to each gallon tomatoes the other ingredients; let simmer slowly for 3 hours.
Seal in bottles or jars.
In a saucepan, combine oil, vinegar, 2 tablespoons of water, onion, sugar, garlic, 1/2 teaspoon salt, celery seed and dash of pepper.
Bring to boiling.
Add artichoke hearts.
Cook until tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Cool.
Stir in pimento.
Chill.
Mix all ingredients.
Roll into golf size balls.
Cook for 12 to 15 minutes at 375°.
Pour 3/4 cup hot water over soda in small bowl. Stir to dissolve. Beat in molasses and egg yolk, combining well.
In medium bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt and spices, mixing well. Add butter.
Using fingers, rub into flour mixture to make crumbs. Sprinkle 1/4 crumb mixture in bottom of pie shell. Top with 1/3 molasses mixture.
Continue layering, ending with crumb mixture on top.
Preheat oven to 350°. Bake pie for 35 minutes or until filling is firm to the touch when lightly pressed with fingertip. Serve pie warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream, if desired.
Cream
sugar,
butter
and
Crisco.
Add eggs, one at a time. Beat
well.
Sift
together dry ingredients.
Alternate dry ingredients with milk into mixture;
add vanilla.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.

Cream together margarine, sugar and vanilla. Blend flour and cocoa together and add to this mixture. Refrigerate 1 to 3 hours. Mold a scant tablespoon of dough around each chocolate drop. Shape into balls. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until set. Cool. Roll in 10x sugar. Makes 4 1/2 dozen.
Put water and margarine in a large pot; bring to boil.
Beat eggs and sugar; stir in salt, milk and corn meal.
Add to boiling water; stir and cook until thick.
Pour into 9 x 9-inch baking dish or pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix dry jello with cottage cheese and Cool Whip.
Add all fruit which has been well drained. Mix well and refrigerate for several hours.
Mix all ingredients together and serve chilled.
Serves about 8 people.
Spread cheese on ham.
Roll up on pickle.
Chill about 1 hour. Slice.
Cook 3 to 4 hours on low in a crock-pot.
Crumble sausage and fry; drain well.
Spread bread with butter. Cut into cubes and cover bottom of 9 x 14-inch pan (sprayed with Pam).
(Frozen bread slices are easier to work with.)
Sprinkle drained sausage over bread.
Beat eggs well, then add evaporated milk and salt.
(I use garlic salt.)
Beat until fluffy then pour egg mixture over sausage and bread.
Cover with grated cheese.
(I also put some of cheese into egg mixture before pouring onto bread and sausage.)
Refrigerate overnight (covered with foil).
Bake next morning for 35 to 40 minutes in 350° oven.
In 3-quart saucepan, cook the noodles according to package. Drain well.
In same saucepan, melt butter.
Stir in herbs and noodles.
Cook over low heat until heated through, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in Parmesan cheese.
Brown beef and onions about 10 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce, kidney beans, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Break taco shells in 1/2 at fold.
Arrange on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Spoon meat mix over tacos and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or until hot.
If desired, top with lettuce and tomatoes.
Put butter, Rice Krispies, pecans and coconut in bowl; mix well and put in oven for 10 minutes or until butter melts.
Remove from oven; add sugar and mix well.
Place layer of sugar mixture in bottom of dish, then place layer of soft ice cream over that, then another layer of sugar mixture, etc., with layer of sugar mixture being on top.
Cover with foil and re-freeze ice cream. Take out of freezer 30 to 45 minutes before serving.
In a large frypan, put olive oil to cover pan.
Heat pan first. Put fresh rosemary in first and then pork chops.
Cook hot and then sprinkle wine to cool pan down.
Move chops around so they don't stick.
Repeat many times.
Heat up.
Cool down with wine.
Turn over.
Should be caramel color on chops.
Cook until white inside. Serves 4 to 6. Temperature:
Medium-high.
Cooking Time:
35 minutes.
In a skillet, saute the red pepper and onion in butter until tender.
Add the soup, milk, worcestershire sauce and hot pepper sauce; stir until smooth.
Stir in the green beans and water chestnuts.
Transfer to an ungreased 1 1/2 qt. baking dish. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake, uncovered at 350° for 15 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted.
Cook onion, garlic and curry powder in butter until onion is tender.
Stir in soup, milk, shrimp and peas.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes; stir frequently.
Serve over rice.
Serve with fruit salad.
Soften bread crumbs in milk.
Combine remaining ingredients. Shape into a loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat. Combine milk and flavoring.
Add flour alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour.
Fold in coconut.

Place all ingredients, except pork loin, in a saucepan and bring to a low boil, stirring until sugar is melted and ingredients are blended. Use caution since this boils over easily. Let cool. Reserve 1/3 cup of the marinade and refrigerate. Marinate pork for no less than 4 hours; overnight works best.
Mix syrup, oleo and boiling water.
Slowly add sugar and milk. Mix until well blended.
Makes 1 1/4 cups.

recipes.t: Crazy Aunt Moo'S "I Married A Greek" Orzo Salad(Yield:  10-12 Servings)
d: 1. Cook box of orzo, set aside.
Whip together lemon juice and Eagle Brand milk.
Whip cream and sugar.
Add flavorings.
Mix well with milk mixture.
Pour into baked pie crust.
Refrigerate.
Very, very good.
Brown sausage; drain off fat.
Separate crescent rolls and place into ungreased 12-inch dish.
Press together making bottom crust and sides.
Spoon sausage over the crust.
Sprinkle with potatoes.
Top with cheese.
Beat together eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Pour over crust.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cream butter, sugar and brown sugar in a large mixing bowl. Add quick-cooking oats.
Mix well; press into a 2-quart utility dish.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes until slightly firm to touch. Place chocolate morsels and peanut butter in a double boiler over boiling water.
Stir until melted.
Spread melted chocolate mixture over warm oat mixture.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Cook spaghetti; drain.
In medium skillet, heat margarine with garlic.
Add carrots, zucchini and onions.
Cook and stir until vegetables are tender.
Blend refried beans with taco mix.
Spread in 9-inch pie plate.
Mash avocados and combine with sour cream and lemon juice. Spread mixture over beans.
Sprinkle with cheese, tomatoes, chilies, olives and green onions.
Peel and
cut
up the potatoes.
Add water to cover and boil until tender.
When
cooked,
mash potatoes with a potato masher. Cook bacon until
brown,
then
add onions.
When the onions are brown, place
bacon,
onions
and potatoes in large pot (12 quart) and
combine
the
mixture.
Add
tomato juice, tomatoes and ketchup and
bring to a boil.
Add Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, salt
and
pepper.
Simmer
for
30 minutes. Add fish and bring to
a rolling boil.
Turn down the heat and let simmer.
Put sugar, corn syrup, 1 cup cream and butter together.
Stir and cook to a vigorous boil.
Gradually add the other cup of cream. Do not allow the mixture to stop boiling while cream is being added.
Cook until thermometer reads 250°, stirring gently. Without a thermometer, cook to hard ball stage.
Remove from fire; add chocolate, nuts and vanilla.
Beat until chocolate is melted.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease round layer pan, 9 x 1 1/2-inches or square pan, 8 x 8 x 2-inches.
Prepare topping.
Mix baking mix, sugar, egg and water.
Beat vigorously 30 seconds.
Stir in apples.
Spread batter in pan. Sprinkle with topping. Bake until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Refrigerate any remaining coffee cake.
May substitute dried venison for beef.
Combine first five ingredients in top of double boiler.
Beat 1 minute, then place over
boiling water and beat constantly for 4 minutes.
Remove from boiling water, beat 1 minute more while you add vanilla.
Spread on cake.
Steam broccoli stems for 10 minutes, then put in bottom of casserole.
Fry sausage very little and pour off grease. Alternate broccoli tops, sausage, onion and cheese in casserole with soup.
Put croutons on top and pour on butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix together.
Put into a greased and floured Bundt or angel food pan and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Sift flour and powder together in a bowl, set aside.
Cream butter and shortening.
Gradually add sugar while beating.
Beat until light.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla and lemon, mix well.
Add dry ingredients, alternately with milk.
Mix well.
Spoon batter into a greased tube pan.
Place in cold oven.
Turn on oven and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours, or until done.
*May substitute all ground beef.
Combine all ingredients, except oil and cheese, and mix well. Divide batter into 4 patties.
Mix ingredients (except egg white and almonds) together well. Pour in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat egg white.
Pour over top.
Place sliced almonds on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cut into squares.
Saute bacon, green pepper, onion and mushrooms 5 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook until brown. Add salt and pepper to taste. Add tomatoes (break up).
Combine with spaghetti.
Pour into large baking dish and bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Top with cheese, if desired.

recipes.t: Brown Sugar Cake With Maple Flavor
d: Cream butter and sugar, then add egg yolks one at a time and beat.
Mix milk and buttermilk together.
Take 1/3 cup out.
Add soda to 1/3 cup of milk.
Add flour and milk to mixture.
Add flavorings.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix 2 tablespoons milk into peanut butter in a large bowl. Gently stir in whipped topping.
Pour 2 cups milk into a large bowl.
Add the pudding mix.
Beat with wire whisk 1 to 2 minutes or until well blended.
Spoon whipped topping mixture and pudding alternately into glasses. Refrigerate 1 hour.
Makes 6 servings.
Melt
margarine;
add	sugar,	syrup
and
salt.
Stir constantly until sugar is dissolved.
Let boil over low heat 5 minutes; do not stir.
Remove from heat;
add soda and flavoring. Stir real good;
this will be foamy.
Pour over corn and mix real good.
Bake
in
250° oven for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes. Let cool and break apart.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Mix cheese and pineapple together; then add all ingredients to gelatin mixture and congeal. Yields 10 servings.
Heat sugar, water and cornstarch until clear, stirring all the time. Add jello. Cool. Clean and halve strawberries.
Fold into cooled jello mixture.
Spoon into pie crust and refrigerate until set.
Serve topped with Cool Whip.
Combine all ingredients except butter and stuffing mix.
In a large bowl, mix thoroughly and then spoon into a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish, lightly buttered.
Combine stuffing mix and butter and sprinkle on top.
Bake 1 hour at 350° or until bubbly and brown.
May be made ahead and stored covered in refrigerator.
Fold together the sour cream, cream cheese, chilies, olives, onions and garlic powder.
Smear on flour tortillas and roll into a log.
Cover individually with foil and refrigerate overnight to set.
Cut into pinwheels or 2-inch sections.
For variation, layer tortillas and cut into wedges.
Brush liquid smoke on brisket and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Soak overnight in cold coffee and wine.
Add onion and bay leaves.
Bake in a covered roaster or roasting bag for 5 to 6 hours at 300°, fat side up.
Remove fat after 4 hours and drizzle with barbecue sauce.
Slice across grain and add more sauce, if desired. Keep in low oven (200° to 250°) until ready to serve.
Add milk to onion mix to make 1/2 cup milk; mix.
Heap onto tablespoon, forming into a ball.
Drop into deep, hot fat and fry until golden brown.
In a small mixing bowl, cream butter; add 1/3 of the sugar and beat well.
Add egg, vanilla, salt and cream; beat until smooth. Gradually add remaining sugar, beating until smooth.
If frosting is too thick, additional cream may be added.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine flour with seasonings.

Layer macaroni, cheese and flour mixture in alternate layers in a baking dish until all are used. Pour milk over all and top with crushed cracker crumbs, if desired. Bake about 45 minutes or until golden brown on top.
Preheat oven to 350°. Mix all ingredients in order listed. Pour into lightly floured Bundt pan. Bake 1 hour. Remove from oven to rack. Cool completely.
In bottom of dish, put the lime jello, 1 cup hot water and 1 cup crushed pineapple.
Let this set.
Wash chicken; remove skin and dip chicken in beaten egg. Place chicken in crushed potato chips and press both sides so chicken is evenly covered.
Place chicken in pan after putting a little oil in pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 5 servings. Good with Easy Potato Bake.
Mix the first 5 ingredients and place in a large roaster or foil turkey pan.
Pour oleo and taco mix over mixture and bake in 250° oven for 45 to 55 minutes.
Stir every 15 minutes.
Cool and store in airtight containers.
Serve with apple slices.
Use a heavy saucepan large enough to hold all ingredients. Brown beef in the pan.
Drain.
Add package of beefy-onion soup to one cup of hot water in a small saucepan, then add this to the beef.
Add the tomato soup.
Peel and dice potatoes and onions to suit.
Add all vegetables, salt and pepper to suit.
Cook until done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Melt butter in saucepan over low heat.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining ingredients (sugar, honey, egg, flour, soda, cinnamon, salt, oats, coconut and nuts).
This mixture will be thick.
Press in prepared pan.
Bake 20 minutes.
Cool in pan. Cut into 32 bars.
Saute ground meat, onion, salt and pepper.
Simmer with cover on.
Cook until meat turns white.
Add water and bring to boil. Add garlic powder, red pepper, paprika, Italian spice mix, chili blend, tomato sauce, cream of mushroom soup and cheese soup. Simmer for at least 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Makes large amount. Can be divided and frozen.
Combine all ingredients except buns.
Spread mixture between buns.
Wrap each in foil.
Place on baking sheet.
Heat at 250° to 300° for 30 minutes.
Serve warm.
Makes 10 servings.
Peel and cube cooked potatoes.
Add chopped onion, pickles and egg whites.
In a coffee mug, add egg yolks, pickles and juice (about 1/8 cup) and finish filling mug with mayonnaise (about 3/4 cup).
Pour to consistency over other ingredients.
Brown meat with salt, pepper and onion; add tomato paste, water and spaghetti sauce mix and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
In a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan, alternate layers of meat sauce, Cheddar cheese, noodles and Mozzarella cheese until all ingredients have been used.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before serving.
Crush garlic and salt in a mortar and pestle or small bowl until a paste forms.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Have cooked rice ready.
Have onion, parsley, bell pepper, celery, green onions and garlic chopped and ready.
Mix well and refrigerate.
Using a rolling pin, crush pretzels between waxed paper.
Mix together pretzels, margarine and 3 tablespoons of sugar.
Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 8 minutes at 400°.
Let cool completely.
Brown and strain meat.
Stir in next 5 ingredients.
Pour into an 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Prepare corn muffin mix according to package directions except add 1/2 can onions.
Spoon around outer edges of casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 minutes.
Top corn bread with Cheddar cheese and remaining onions.
Bake for 2 to 3 minutes.
In medium skillet, saute butter and chicken livers for 2 minutes.
Add onion and apple and stir for 5 minutes until apple softens.
Stir in brandy and cream.
Transfer mixture to blender and blend 2 to 3 minutes or until smooth.
Refrigerate this mixture for 1 hour.
In
skillet
mix
hamburger, onion, green pepper, salt, pepper,
chili powder and sugar.
Let hamburger brown with all these ingredients.
Add tomato ketchup and let simmer 30 to 45 minutes.
Spread refried beans on serving dish, mix sour cream and taco mix.
Spread on top of beans. Top with lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, and peppers.
Beat flour, baking powder, soda, pudding, butter and egg for 2 minutes at medium speed, then pour into 8-inch deep dish or 10 pie pan.
Drain the can of peaches, saving juice.
Put peaches on top of mixture in pan.
Beat cream cheese, sugar and peach juice. Spoon onto the top of peaches within 1 of edge.
Mix 1 Tbsp. sugar and cinnamon, sprinkle over cheese mixture.
Bake 350° for 30-35 minutes until crust is golden brown - filling appears soft.
Keep refrigerated.
Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise and package of Good Seasons. Mix well and spread mixture on bread and top with a cucumber. Refrigerate a couple of hours before serving.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Brown ground beef mix in seasoning package.
Drain very well. Break up chips and toss all ingredients together.
Pour dressing over salad and mix well.
Serve immediately.
Dissolve Jell-O in 2 cups boiling water.
Add 1 cup cold water and pie filling.
Mix well and pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill until set.
Spread Dream Whip over top of set Jell-O.
Wash cucumbers, any size.
If they are solid, 2 gallons.
Make a brine of 2 cups salt to 1 gallon water; boil and pour over cucumbers in a stone jar.
Weigh down; let stand 7 days.
Drain; wash and cut into chunks.
For next 3 days, make a solution daily of 1 tablespoon powdered alum.
Pour over cucumbers which have been drained and old liquid discarded.
On 4th morning, heat 6 cups white vinegar, 5 cups sugar, 1/3 cup pickling spices and 1 tablespoon celery seed (may tie spices in a cloth).
Heat to boiling and pour over pickles.
On 5th morning, drain liquid into a pan.
Add 1 cup sugar.
Reheat.
Pour over pickles.
On 6th morning, drain in pan.
Add 1 cup sugar.
Pack pickles into sterilized jars and fill to within 1/2-inch of top of jar with boiling liquid.
Seal at once.
Boil all ingredients, except mangoes.
Add mangoes when mixture is cool.
Store in jars and refrigerate.
Drain vegetables; mix with celery and onions, add salt and pepper.
Heat vinegar and sugar; pour over vegetables. Refrigerate until well chilled before eating.
Mix eggs, oil, salt and pepper together.
Add flour and about 3/4 cup water.
Work dough until you can roll it easily.
Do not have it stiff.
Roll as thin as possible.
Cover with dishcloth and let sit overnight.
Put chicken broth in a large pot.
Let come to hard boil and begin to put in dough cut in small pieces, keeping dough covered.
Boil until pastry is done.
If broth gets too low, add water so pastry doesn't become dry.
With a big spoon occasionally lift pastry from bottom to top.

recipes.t: Rice And Deviled Eggs With Tuna
d: Cook green pepper and onion in butter until glossy.
Combine soup and milk. To 3/4 of the soup mixture, add rice and tuna. Place in a casserole. Top with deviled eggs and refrigerate.
Heat oven to 350°.
Stir peanut butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla in a bowl until blended.
It will be sticky.
Roll into 1 1/4-inch balls.
Then roll in sugar and place on cookie sheets about 1 1/2 inches apart.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes until cookies look dry and tops are cracked.
Remove from oven and immediately press chocolate kiss in center of each.
Cool on cookie sheets.
Mix dry ingredients; beat eggs and oil together.
Beat in dry ingredients.
Stir in carrots.
Can bake in a Bundt pan at 350° for 1 hour or in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 45 minutes.
Grease a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Drain corn.
Put in casserole dish. Add rest of ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until set. If you want a little more custard, add 2 extra eggs, slightly beaten, and 1 more cup of milk.
Mix flour, cornmeal, baking soda, pepper, garlic salt and egg. Slowly add milk to make a thick, smooth batter.
Try not to make it too runny.
Use less milk if you need to.
Cut onions into rings.
Prepare oil by heating to frying temperature.
Dip onions into batter and put immediately into oil.
If oil is hot, the rings will start frying immediately.
Let the rings fry until golden brown.
Remove and place on paper towel to drain.
Serve with catsup or barbecue sauce.
Serves 6 to 8.
Variation:
Eliminate tomato sauce, use a little more oil to coat potatoes and add oregano and green pepper rings.
Mix sugar, margarine, milk and dates in saucepan; cook until thick or makes a ball in cold water.
Beat until it begins to get thicker.
Add pecans and beat some more.
When it gets so thick you cannot beat it, put in a damp cloth and roll it up.
Let set for at least 2 hours, then slice into pieces.
Beat together margarine, sugars and eggs until creamy.
Then add salt and flour, coconut, chocolate chips and pecans.
Pour in two 9-inch cake pans, greased and floured.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Let cool and sprinkle with powdered sugar or leave plain.
Cut each apple lengthwise in half and remove core.
Arrange apple halves cut side up in 12 x 8-inch baking dish.
Toss cheese in flour.
Combine 3/4 cup cheese, 1/2 c.
almonds and remaining ingredients, except pastry.
Mix well.
Roll pastry into 15-inch square.
Fit pastry into 11 3/4 x 7 1/2-inch baking dish.
Trim 1-inch beyond edge.
Fill with turkey mixture.
Top with remaining cheese and almonds.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 400°.
Combine gelatin, sweetener, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir in milk, egg yolks and yams.
Mix well.
Cook 10 minutes. Chill. Beat egg whites until stiff.
Stir in Sweet 'N Low.
Fold into gelatin mixture.
Pour into pie shell.
Chill.
Cut top from peppers; remove seeds.
Brown meat in skillet; stir in garlic salt and salt.
Add 1/2 cup of tomatoes and the cereal.
Fill each pepper with 1/2 cup meat mixture.
Place in a greased shallow baking dish.
Pour on remaining tomatoes.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Spread 1 teaspoon of refried beans on each tortilla chip.
Top with 1 teaspoon of cheese and one olive slice.
Place 8 in circle on paper plate.
Heat on full power for 30 to 60 seconds, or until cheese is melted.
Serve warm.
Repeat with remaining chips.
Place potatoes in a Dutch oven; cover with water and bring to a boil.
Cook 8 minutes or until tender.
Drain; place in large bowl. Add onion and next 4 ingredients; toss gently.
Combine sour cream and next 5 ingredients; stir well.
Pour over potato mixture; toss gently to coat.
Cover and chill.
Combine ingredients at last minute before serving.
Layer ingredients in order listed:
lettuce, celery, pepper, onion and peas.
Mix sugar and Miracle Whip together and spread over top layer.
Then sprinkle cheese and bacon bits on top.
Let salad marinate for 24 hours, if desired, or serve when prepared.
Mix all and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix all except cheese and tortillas.
Fill tortillas.
Put remainder of mixture on top.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix together 1/2 cup margarine, salt, pepper, onion, soup, sour cream and cheese.
Add thawed potatoes and blend.
Pour into buttered 3-quart casserole.
Mix 1/4 cup melted butter and corn flakes.
Put on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together flour, 1/2 cup sugar, cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Add milk, oil and vanilla; stir until smooth.
Stir in nuts.
Turn into a ungreased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Combine the 3/4 cup sugar and the 1/4 cup cocoa; gradually stir in boiling water.
Pour liquid mixture evenly over batter in pan.
Bake in a 350° oven about 30 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Serve warm or chilled. Sprinkle with sifted powdered sugar.
Serves 8.
Heat oven to 375°.
Cook ground beef in preheated large skillet over medium heat until no longer pink.
Pour off drippings.
Add spaghetti sauce and tomatoes with liquid to skillet.
Stir and set aside.
Meanwhile, combine Ricotta, egg, Parmesan and basil.
Spread 2 cups beef sauce over bottom of 11 x 7-inch baking dish.
Arrange 3 lasagna noodles in single layer, pressing into sauce.
Spoon cheese mixture on top of noodles. Sprinkle with 1 cup Mozzarella and top with 2 cups sauce.
Arrange remaining noodles in a single layer, pressing lightly into sauce. Top with remaining sauce.
Spread evenly.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until noodles are fork-tender.
Sprinkle with remaining Mozzarella; tent lightly with foil.
Let stand at least 15 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook noodles and drain.
Cook chicken.
Roll in bread crumbs. Place in casserole and add cooked noodles.
Dice cream cheese. Mix in sauces and seasonings.
Pour over noodles.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes in a 350° oven.

In a mixing bowl, combine first seven ingredients. Beat until well blended. Slice bread in one inch pieces. Spread on one side of each slice of bread and place on ungreased baking sheet. Broil 4 inches from heat for 3 minutes or until cheese is melted and lightly browned.
In a large capacity food processor or blender, combine all the ingredients except whipped topping.
Blend thoroughly 1-2 minutes. Remove blades and pour into a large bowl.
Gently fold in the whipped topping.
Soften yeast in 1/4 cup warm water; let stand 10 minutes. Combine cottage cheese, oleo, salt, sugar and baking soda.
Stir. Add onion, dill, egg and softened yeast.
Beat well.
Add flour gradually.
Cover with wet cloth.
Let raise in warm place until double in bulk.
Stir dough down, knead and pinch into loaf pan proportions.
Let rise 30 to 40 minutes.
Combine ingredients and put cheese on top.
Bake in greased, covered casserole for 30 minutes.
Pepper, but do not salt, chicken breasts.
Wrap slice of bacon around each.
Place a layer of dried beef in bottom of baking dish.
Place bacon wrapped breasts in dish.
Cover with mixture of chicken soup, sour cream and cream cheese.
Cover with foil. Place in 325° oven for 2 hours.
When tender, remove foil and let brown slightly.
Serve on bed of rice.
Blend all ingredients in big pot.
Add chicken and cook on medium heat until chicken is fully cooked; stir often.
It takes about 45 minutes.
Serve with rice and tossed salad.
Tear lettuce in bite-size pieces into a large bowl.
Add browned, drained and cooled hamburger.
Add beans, cheese and crumbled chips.
Combine mayonnaise and taco sauce; add to salad. Mix well.
Brown ground beef and diced onions.
When beef and onions are brown, add spaghetti sauce, tomato paste, and diced whole tomatoes. Drain all juice from tomato can.
Prepare noodles per package instructions and drain noodles.
Combine with sauce and enjoy!
Peel cucumbers and cut in small pieces.
Mix together yogurt and water until smooth.
Add cucumbers, garlic, salt and mint. Place some ice cubes in a bowl and refrigerate a few hours.
Stir well just before serving.
Beat together eggs, oil and sugar.
Add grated zucchini.
In a large bowl mix together flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add zucchini mixture and blend.
Add nuts, raisins and spices.
Mix well.
Pour into two greased loaf pans and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Rinse peas and boil with water and ham hocks.
Reduce heat to a slow boil; cover and cook 45 minutes.
Add to pot, cut up vegetables and seasonings.
Simmer for 2 hours.
After 2 hours, remove ham hocks and set them aside.
Place smoked sausage in soup and cook for 1/2 hour longer over low heat.

recipes.t: Lo-Fat Triple Layer Chocolate Silk Pie
d: In large bowl, mix cream cheese, sugar and 1 tablespoon milk with wire whisk until smooth. Gently stir in 1 1/2 cups Cool Whip; spread in bottom of crust. In 2nd bowl, stir pudding mix into remaining milk and mix well. Immediately stir in whipped topping. Spread this over cream cheese mixture.
Place chops in baking dish.
Combine bread crumbs, onion, 1/2 water, margarine and poultry seasoning.
Spoon onto each chop. Cover chops with gravy made with mushroom soup and 1/3 cup water. Bake 1 hour, uncovered, at 350°.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook skinned chicken in water until tender.
Remove from broth and cut into chunks.
Strain broth and measure.
Add water to equal amount called for to cook rice.
Cook rice according to directions. While rice is cooking, saute celery in small amount oleo until partially tender.
When rice is done, combine rice, chicken, celery, water chestnuts, soups, mayonnaise and onion soup mix. Pour into large flat casserole (approximately 4 quarts).
Cover with stuffing mix.
Drizzle with melted oleo.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Remove cover and bake 20 to 25 minutes longer until golden brown and heated through.
Serves 10 to 12.

Dissolve and pour over cucumbers (gallon glass jar); let stand for 2 weeks. Wash off brine water and cover with cold water. Add 2 tablespoons alum powder and let stand for 24 hours. Drain off alum water. Pour vinegar to cover and add 2 teaspoons pickling spices (tied in a bag) and leave for 24 hours. Drain off vinegar and throw away. Add 3 cups sugar for 3 mornings straight. These pickles do not have to be sealed. The whole process is done in the gallon glass jar.
Combine egg
whites,
sugar, salt, water and corn syrup in top of
double
boiler.
Place over rapidly boiling water, beating constantly	at high speed of electric mixer.
Beat for 7 minutes or until frosting will stand in peaks.
Remove from boiling water; add vanilla and beat at high speed until thick enough to spread.
In heavy skillet, melt butter; add sliced apples.
Fry until tender.
Add sugar and cinnamon to taste.
Fry until caramelized but still juicy.
Spoon onto warmed flour tortillas.
Mix together Kool-Aid, sugar and water.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add pineapple juice. Chill.
When ready to serve, add ginger ale.
Pour in punch bowl over an ice ring.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pack into loaf pan and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Cut in oleo.
Spread 2/3 of mixture in a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Spread 1 can of pie filling on top. Sprinkle remaining ingredients on top of pie filling.
Bake 30 minutes in a 375° oven.
Top with vanilla ice cream or whipped topping.
Thaw frozen juices.
Pour in orange juice, lemonade and apple juice.
Stir while pouring in ginger ale.
Scoop on sherbet. Serve immediately.
Add more sherbet later as first scoops melt.
Brown meat; drain.
Add taco seasoning, water, corn, pepper and sauce.
Pour in casserole dish.
Mix package of muffin mix and pour over mixture.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes.
Add cheese and bake for 5 more minutes.
Mix together the corn meal, salt and soda and blend.
Stir in shortening, sour cream, corn and eggs and mix well.
Add chiles and cheese; stir.
Pour mixture into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Thoroughly mix together the cream cheese, bacon, celery salt and onion salt.
Cut off tops of cherry tomatoes and remove pulp. Stuff with cream cheese mixture.
Sprinkle tops with parsley. Chill.
Sprinkle sugar over berries.
Pour cake mix over pineapple, blueberries and sugar.
Melt and pour margarine over cake mix. Sprinkle chopped pecans over top.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch buttered dish or pan for 45 minutes at 350°.
Mix all ingredients together and chill.
Serve with raw vegetables.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
Marinate beef and vegetables for at least 2 hours.
(Use a plastic Ziploc bag or plastic bowl with lid.
Keep cold in cooler.)
Alternate items on toasting stick.
Cook over the coals until done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine cake mix, eggs and oil; stir until well blended.
Mix in chocolate chips.
Spoon onto cookie sheet.
Bake for 9 to 12 minutes.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Combine corn, beans, cheese and onion.
Combine mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce.
Fold into corn mixture. Turn into 1-quart casserole.
Melt butter; toss with crumbs.
Sprinkle over casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven 350°.
Grease large shallow baking dish.
Combine water and milk and heat to simmer.
Add: Cornmeal, salt, sugar and butter.
Stir over medium heat until the mixture is thickened (about 5 minutes).
Remove from heat.
Mix and bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Melt butter over medium-high heat.
Brown hamburger, onion and green pepper.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Mix and serve with Triscuits.
Shell a quart and one-half of chestnuts.
Put them in hot water and boil until the skins are soft, then drain the water and remove the skins.

Replace the chestnuts in water, and boil until soft. Take out a few at a time, and press through a colander while hot. Season the mashed chestnuts with two tablespoonfuls of butter, two teaspoonfuls of salt and one-quarter of a teaspoon of pepper.
Mix the gelatin with the cottage cheese.
Add the pineapple, marshmallows and shredded coconut.
Add the whipped topping and mix well.
Refrigerate overnight before serving.
Mash drained sweet potatoes.
Mix with beaten egg, margarine, salt, brown sugar and nutmeg.
Arrange slices of pineapple in a lightly greased shallow baking pan.
Mound the sweet potato mixture on each slice.
Brush with additional margarine, if desired.
Bake at 425° for about 15 minutes.
Trim fat from roast.
Place into crock-pot.
Add dry soup mix, mushroom soup, tomato soup and water.
(I find it easier to mix the ingredients before pouring over roast.)
Turn crock-pot on high until cooking well.
Turn to low and let cook 10 to 12 hours, or until desired doneness.
Cut all vegetables into chunks.
In a deep frying pan or wok, add oil, chicken and vegetables.
Cook on medium high for 5 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Add oregano, salt, pepper and garlic powder and simmer for 10 minutes or until chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Serve over white rice and enjoy!
Serves 5.
Measure cereal into large bowl.
Butter 13 x 9 x 2-inch rectangular pan.
Melt only 5 cups of marshmallows, corn syrup, magarine and chocolate chips in medium saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly; remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla.
Pour over cereal.
Mix quickly until completely coated with chocolate. Stir in 1 cup of marshmallows.
Make squares by pressing mixture down into buttered rectangular pan with buttered back of spoon. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Then cut into 2-inch squares.
Yields 24 squares.
Slice top off of the French bread; scoop out and crumble the inside bread, leaving about 1/2 to 3/4-inch shell.
Brown ground beef, onion and pepper.
Add all of the remaining ingredients to the crumbled bread; stuff the shell.
Top with sliced American cheese; replace top of loaf.
Heat in oven for about 10 minutes.
Beat all ingredients with mixer until well blended.
Put in refrigerator.
Best if made the day before needed.
Mix all ingredients; shape into loaf in 9 x 5 x 3-inch long pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

Combine beans and corn. Mix rest of ingredients (except oleo and crackers) in with vegetables. Pour into greased casserole dish. Dot with oleo. Crumble crackers on top. Bake at 350 degrees for 35 to 40 minutes.
Trim off the tough ends of the watercress and discard.
Rinse the leaves and tender stems.
Drain well.
Put mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper in salad bowl.
Blend with wire whisk.
Add oil, beating with whisk.
Add watercress, chopped egg and onion.
Toss and serve.
Mix all ingredients together well.
Store in airtight container.
Enjoy!

recipes.t: Quick Cherry Cheese Pie Or Fruit Dip
d: With an electric mixer, mix lemon juice, cream cheese and marshmallow cream together until smooth. Pour into already prepared graham cracker crust and top with chilled cherry pie filling. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Place chicken breasts, one at a time, between 2 sheets of waxed paper.
With flat side of mallet, gently pound breasts until each is about 1/4 inch thick; set aside.
In a rimmed plate or pie pan, combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, 1 teaspoon of oregano, garlic salt and pepper; set aside.
Clean shrimp.
May leave tail on.
Melt butter/margarine in frying pan.
Saute garlic and shallots until clear.
Add everything except parsley and shrimp.
Bubble one minute.
Place shrimp on broiler pan.
Pour half sauce over shrimp.
Broil 5 inches from heat for 3 minutes.
Turn over and pour remaining sauce on shrimp and broil additional 3 minutes.
Turn out onto serving dish; garnish with parsley.
Serve with white rice. Instead of broiling may also just add shrimp to frying pan with sauce and cook until shrimp are done.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Prepare macaroni by package directions in medium saucepan.
Melt butter; stir in flour, dry mustard and salt.
Gradually stir in milk; cook and stir until mixture thickens slightly and bubbles.
Remove from heat.
Add 1 cup of shredded cheese and stir until melted.
Add macaroni.
Mix together chicken, soups, stock and vegetables. Add a little pepper and poultry seasoning to taste. Add 2 to 3 tablespoons melted butter; stir together. Pour in greased 9 x 13 baking dish.
Place apples, sugar and cranberries in baking dish.
Mix melted oleo, sugar, oatmeal and flour together and pour over apple mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Saute onion in margarine in skillet until tender.
Dip steaks in milk; coat with a mixture of crumbs, salt and pepper.
Brown quickly in the hot skillet from which the onions have been removed. Place in a baking dish.
Add tomato sauce to skillet; heat for several minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add mushrooms now and pour sauce over steaks.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with cheese.
Let stand, covered, for a few minutes to melt the cheese.
Great served with rice pilaf.
Combine all ingredients; blend well.
Chill for 15 minutes. Form into 1-inch balls.
Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Melt honey, butter and brown sugar in pan.
Mix dry ingredients together in large bowl.
Pour honey mixture over dry ingredients and stir to coat.
Bake in jelly roll pans for 25 minutes at 325°.
Lay out on aluminum foil to cool.
Store in closed container.
Melt 1 stick butter and cheese (separately) in microwave; drain carrots and add to cheese in 1-quart casserole.
Crumble bread into the melted butter.
Sprinkle bread over carrots.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.

recipes.t: No Bake Chocolate Cookies(Aka:  Mississippi Mud Cookies)
d: Put sugar, cocoa, milk and margarine in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Stir well and boil 1 minute.
Turn off heat and add vanilla.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoon on waxed paper.
Allow to set.
Makes 4 to 5 dozen cookies.
Arrange lettuce on
large
tray.
Arrange fruit so that no two colors are next to each other.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Put all ingredients in bowl and mix well for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour into pan; bake for 40 to 45 minutes.
Brown meat.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce and chili sauce mix. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in corn and olives.
Cut tortillas in half or quarters according to bowl size.
Layer tortillas and meat in casserole bowl, ending with tortillas.
Sprinkle with cheese. Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Garnish, after baking, with lettuce and avocados.
Mix together all ingredients.
Pour into a 1-quart casserole. Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Tie cloves and cinnamon in a cheesecloth bag.
Place spice bag and remaining ingredients in a large kettle; stir well.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
Remove the spice bag.
Yield:
1 1/2 gallons.
Dip chicken pieces into 1/2 cup Pet milk.
Roll pieces in flour, salt and pepper.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Put chicken, skin side down.
Bake, uncovered, near center of 425° oven for 30 minutes.
Turn chicken over.
Pour mixture of 1 can cream of chicken soup, 3/4 cup Pet milk and 1/4 cup water over chicken.
Bake 30 minutes longer, or until drumstick is tender when pierced.
Place chicken on serving dish.
Stir gravy well and serve with chicken over mashed potatoes.
Serves 6.
Drop on cookie sheet.
Bake 10 minutes at 325°.
Combine chicken, soup, mushrooms and Cheddar cheese in a 2-quart casserole dish.
Add rice, mixing well.
Sprinkle with potato chips and Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese melts.
Dissolve each of the jello flavors in 1 cup boiling water and 1/2 cup cold water.
Pour into 3 (8-inch) square pans and chill until firm.
Blend pineapple juice, water and sugar; bring to a boil.
Add lemon jello and stir until dissolved.
Chill mixture until it's consistency of unbeaten egg white.
Whip this mixture, then whip the cream, then whip together.
Cut the 3 jello flavors in 1/2-inch cubes and fold through the lemon mixture.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Dissolve jellos in boiling water and add thawed lemonade and limeade.
Chill until partially set.
Whip until foamy.
Add Cool Whip and mix well.
Stir in pineapple and pour into an 8 cup mold. Refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients, except whipped cream, and pour into pie shell.
Bake at 375° for 50 to 55 minutes, until top is crackly brown and filling just quivers when you nudge the pie plate.
Cool and garnish with whipped cream and nuts.
Mix margarine and graham crackers and pat into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Make pudding according to package directions; cool slightly. When cool, spread over graham cracker crust.
Add layer of banana slices, then layer of pineapple.
Cover this with Cool Whip. Sprinkle chopped pecans and cut up maraschino cherries over the top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cut into squares.
Serves 12 to 15.
Peel, dice and boil potatoes until tender.
Mash potatoes, then add margarine, cream cheese, sour cream, salt and pepper. Mix until smooth and well blended.
Pour into a buttered 2-quart casserole dish and bake at 400° until lightly brown.
Serve.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Beat for 10 minutes.
Add vanilla and lemon
flavoring.
Beat 2 minutes longer.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Place ground beef in skillet.
Season with garlic powder, salt, black pepper (use quite a bit of black pepper) and chopped onion.
Cook until done.
Drain and add soup.
Simmer until heated thoroughly.
Serve on noodles.
Combine crumbs and butter; mixing well.
Line muffin pans with paper liners.
Spoon graham cracker mixture into each liner. Press into bottom.
Beat cream cheese until light and fluffy. Gradually add sugar.
Mix well.
Add egg and vanilla, beating well.
Spoon into liners.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Butter casserole dish.
Place sole on bottom. Top with crab and shrimp.
Then with tomato and garlic butter.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix together; use only enough broth to make moist. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbling.
Melt butter and saute onions.
Add cheese and soup.
After cheese has melted, add crabmeat, salt, pepper, and Tabasco sauce. Serve in chafing dish.
Prick pie shell with fork and bake 5 minutes at 450°.
After filling, bake 45 minutes or until brown and puffy at 350°.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 1 1/4-inch pie plate.
Beat all ingredients except nuts until smooth for 2 minutes in blender on high, stopping blender occasionally to stir, or 2 minutes with hand beater.
Pour into pie plate.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool 5 minutes.
Serve with ice cream, if desired.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Drain.
In a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, pour Doritos first, then layer beef and onion and beans.
Pour Ro-Tel over mixture.
Top with cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° until cheese is melted, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Cream butter; slowly add sugar.
Cream thoroughly.
Add well beaten eggs and soda, dissolved in a little hot water, and cocoa, mixed with a little hot water.
Alternately add sour milk and flour.
Mix to smooth batter.
Add vanilla.
Bake in moderate oven 35 to 40 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a 9-inch cake pan with margarine.
Cook potatoes in skins until tender.
Drain and peel.
Cut potatoes into bite size pieces in a large bowl.
While potatoes are still warm, sprinkle with vinegar.
Add celery, eggs, pepper, onion, pickle, salt and pepper.
Blend mayonnaise and mustard together.
With 2 forks, gently toss all ingredients.
Add more mayonnaise, if needed.
Avoid mashing potatoes.
Cover and chill.
Cream together butter, sugar and eggs. In separate bowl, combine flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Add flour mixture gradually to butter mixture. Mix well. Add vanilla and almond extracts.
Simmer chickens with salt until tender.
Bone and chop fine. Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Chill.
Serve on a lettuce leaf with green stuffed olives and small whole dill pickles.
Melt butter.
Add sugar, milk and cocoa.
Stir together. Bring to a boil and boil for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Mix in oatmeal and any optional ingredient.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in 9-inch square pan.
Mix 1/2 cup butter; add 1/2 cup sugar and beat until light.
Add egg and beat well. Sift flour, baking powder and salt and add to first mixture with milk, beating until smooth.
Carefully spread on berries.
Bake in oven (375°) about 30 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes; turn out on serving dish.
Serve at once with cream if desired.
Mix ground beef, crackers, salt and water.
Form into balls and refrigerate overnight.
Next day, slice meat and brown in a skillet.
Place slices in covered baking dish.
Mix cream of mushroom soup, flour, steak sauce and second cup of water and pour over meat.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours. Very good.
Mix milk and pudding until smooth. Add spice and pumpkin.
Mix until blended. Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into baked pie shells. Refrigerate until served.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Cut chicken into 1/2-inch chunks and place in marmalade for approximately 6 to 8 hours.
Wrap each chicken chunk with 1/2 slice of bacon.
Thread chicken, mushrooms and onions on shish-kabob skewers alternating chicken, mushrooms and onions.
Cook 30 to 35 minutes, baste while cooking with leftover marmalade.
Chop cabbage in bite size pieces.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Saute beef and onions.
Put over cabbage.
Mix tomato sauce, water and rice.
Pour over contents.
Top with kraut.
Bake 20 minutes uncovered.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
Combine milk and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Stir in cranberry sauce, pineapple and nuts; fold in whipped topping. Spread in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Freeze until firm.
Remove from freezer 10 minutes before cutting.
Return leftovers to freezer.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour square pan, 9 x 9 x 2-inch.
Measure all ingredients into large mixing bowl.
Blend 1/2 minute on low speed scraping bowl constantly.
Beat 3 minutes on medium speed scraping bowl occasionally.
Pour into pan.
Bake for 50 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.

Put everything except the gelatin into a pan and cook over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes stirring every so often. Now sample a little to see if it needs more sweetener. Sprinkle the gelatin ever the mixture and stir until completely dissolved.
Brown beef and onions in skillet; drain.
Add Worcestershire sauce.
Stir in flour and mix beef well.
In large pot, cook egg noodles and drain.
Add to noodles, ground beef, mixed vegetables (drained) and 1 1/2 cups tomato juice.
Combine all ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate 4 to 6 hours. Stir occasionally.
Broil shrimp and marinate 4 to 5 inches from heat in preheated oven for 7 minutes.
Then shrimp and broil another 10 minutes.
Serve shrimp with the marinade.
Serves 4.
Mix sugar, water, salt, flour, butter and vanilla and cook until thick.
Add 1 tablespoon vinegar.
Cool.
Add to apples (sliced thin).
Place in pie shell and bake at 425° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Dip chicken breasts in egg batter; add salt and pepper.
Roll in bread crumbs.
Fry lightly in oil.
Place in a greased baking dish.
Cover with spaghetti sauce and bake at 350° for 1 hour. Put Mozzarella cheese on chicken 5 minutes before it's done.
Slice peaches into a greased 8-inch baking dish.
Add lemon juice.
Mix sugar, flour and egg and crumble over top of peaches. Pour margarine over top and bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes or until browned and bubbling.
Mix well all ingredients, except butter and pie shells and Cool Whip, in a saucepan.
Add the butter last and cook over medium heat until thick, stirring constantly.
Pound turkey if necessary between two sheets of waxed paper to uniform thickness.
Place in a large bowl.
Pour the apple juice, soy sauce, sherry, garlic and thyme over the turkey and mix gently.
Cover and refrigerate overnight or for 3 to 4 hours. Remove turkey and reserve the marinade.
Heat butter and oil in large skillet.
Quickly brown turkey on both sides.
(Be careful not to overcook.)
Add the plums and reserved marinade.
Cover and simmer gently 10 to 15 minutes.
Garnish with fresh thyme and dusting of pepper and serve.
Place thawed potatoes in large bowl.
Mix soup, cheese, sour cream, onion, salt and pepper.
Pour mix over potatoes.
Toss until coated.
Brown meat well in a large skillet. Drain. Add green pepper, onion, salt and pepper. Brown a few more minutes.
Add tomatoes. Place in a large bowl in this order: lettuce, tomatoes, corn chips, hot meat mixture and hot cheese mixture.
Mix about ingredients and chill until set.
Top with lite Cool Whip.
Combine sugar, syrup and vinegar in 2-quart bowl.
Cover with plastic wrap and microwave on High 3 minutes.
Stir well. Microwave, uncovered, on High 4 to 10 minutes, until thickened (300°).
Test by dropping in cold water.
Remove the threads; if they bend, cook more.
It is done if it is very brittle.
Quickly stir in soda and mix well.
Pound steak to 1/4-inch; cut into serving-size pieces. Sprinkle with seasonings.
Dredge in flour; dip in milk.
Dredge in flour again.
Brown coated steaks in hot oil.
Remove and drain.
Reserve 3 tablespoons pan drippings.
Add 1/4 cup flour to drippings.
Cook over medium heat until bubbly, stirring constantly.

Stir in 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Add 2 cups milk, slowly cook until thick, stirring constantly. Add steak to gravy; cover, reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes. Remove cover and cook an additional 5 minutes.

recipes.t: Cowboy Cookies(Great Family Recipe, Many Cookies To A Batch)
d: Sift flour, soda, salt and baking powder; set aside.
Blend together margarine and sugars.
Add eggs and beat until fluffy. Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Add oatmeal, vanilla and chips.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Gale Cirocco'S Broccoli And Spaghetti Soup
d: Saute onion and garlic in butter.
Pour in chicken broth and broccoli.
Heat over medium burner.
Add milk and Cheez Whiz.
Heat on low so the milk does not curdle.
Cook spaghetti separately according to box directions.
Drain and add to the soup.
Combine 2 cups flour, salt and undissolved yeast.
Heat water, milk, molasses and margarine over low heat until liquids are 120° to 130°.
Add to dry ingredients; beat 2 minutes at medium speed, scraping bowl occasionally.
Add eggs, oatmeal and 1 cup flour. Beat at high speed 2 minutes.
Stir enough flour to make a stiff dough.
Turn into floured board, knead 8 to 10 minutes.
Place in greased bowl; grease top.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Punch down; knead in pecans.
Divide into 3 equal pieces; shape into loaves.
Place in 3 greased 8 1/4 x 4 1/2 x 2 1/2-inch loaf pans.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Remove from pans; cool on wire racks.
Combine chicken, celery and nuts.
Add soup, mayonnaise and eggs, mixing well.
Add most of potato chips, salt and pepper. Put in greased casserole.
Sprinkle with remainder of chips.
Bake at 450° for 12 to 15 minutes, covered.
Mix all seasonings.
Add cabbage and chill thoroughly. Garnish with sliced olives.
Serves 4.
Combine meat, vegetable juice and 1 well beaten egg.
Add oatmeal and mix until really moist.
Add remaining ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine noodles, soup and milk.
Add chicken, broken into small pieces.
Put in casserole dish, cover and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 400°.
Sprinkle with cheese during last 5 minutes of baking.
Sift together flour, nutmeg, cinnamon, baking powder, salt and baking soda.
Beat eggs until thick and lemon colored; gradually beat in sugar.
Add melted shortening, milk and vinegar, then add flour mixture.
Mix well.
Chill for a time, then turn out on floured cloth.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix in dishpan.
Drop on greased cookie sheet and flatten.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes (do not overbake). Makes 300 to 400 cookies.
Slice 5 slices of bread.
Melt the butter and cook the bread in the butter.
Mix the rest of the ingredients and place in a casserole.
Place the bread on top.
Bake 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Slice chicken breasts.
Combine honey, lime juice and mustard. (I use a combination of Kosciusko and a stone-ground mustard.) Place chicken in a baking dish.
Pour marinade over chicken, turning to coat.
Let stand for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once.
Drain pineapple well.
Squeeze to remove all liquid.
Blend softened cream cheese with pineapple.
Add other ingredients and shape into ball.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Reshape and roll in additional cup of finely chopped pecans.
Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl well.
Pour into a large Bundt cake pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Heat oven to 350°.
Prepare crust (if needed) and press into pan.
Soften cream cheese in large bowl.
Beat in 3/4 cup sugar. Add eggs one at a time, beating until smooth after each one.
Beat in lemon peel and juice.
Pour into crust.
Bake 30 minutes or until center is firm.
(Do not turn oven off.)
Remove from oven. Allow to stand 5 minutes.
During this time, combine sour cream, 1 tablespoon sugar and vanilla.
Spread over top of pie.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Return to oven.
Bake 2 minutes or until sour cream is set.
Cool.
Chill about 4 hours before serving.
Mix cake mix, brown sugar, pecans, margarine and eggs.
Spread evenly on pizza pan and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool. Mix container of whipped cream and softened cream cheese and spread over crust.
Arrange fruit on top of filling in alternating rows of fruit.
May use "Fruit Fresh" to keep fruit from turning. Chill to serve; slice like pizza.
Mix vegetables, water chestnuts and mayo.
Pour into casserole. Top with cheese.
Spread butter and crackers (mixed together) on top.
Bake at 350° about 30 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin and 3/4 cup of water on medium heat until dissolved.
Put in blender.
Add cottage cheese until very smooth. Add cream cheese, yogurt and lemonade.
Mix well for 2 minutes. Put in refrigerator for 3 hours.
Eat with lots of fruit.
Brown beef in large heavy kettle; drain and add onions.
Cook until onions are tender.
Add remaining ingredients except cheese; simmer for 15 minutes.
Ladle into bowls; top with the grated cheese. Yields 6 to 8 servings.

Roll out pastry and line a 9 inch pie plate and refrigerate. Stir fry cabbage and sliced onion in butter until barely tender. Whiz cottage cheese and scallions in blender or food processor. stir into cabbage mixture along with tarragon.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Distribute half of cabbage in pie shell.
Arrange sliced eggs on top, cover with rest of cabbage.
Cover with top pastry, crimp edges.
Cut 2 or 3 slashes in top and bake at 400 degrees for 15 minutes.
Reduce temperature to 350 degrees and bake 20 to 25 more minutes.
Crust should be lightly browned.
Makes 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream margarine, shortening and sugar. Add eggs, one at a time.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk and vanilla.
Pour into tube pan and bake for 1 hour and 25 minutes.
Bring berries (1 cup), 3/4 cup sugar and lemon rind to boil in saucepan.
Combine remaining sugar (1/4 cup) and 1/4 cup water with cornstarch.
Stir into boiling berries.
Cook about 1 minute, until thickened.
Cool to room temperature.
Pour in other 4 cups berries, stir to coat.
Pour in baked pie shell.
Chill until completely set.
Decorate with whipped cream or Cool Whip and a few berries.
Rub salt, pepper and celery salt into brisket.
Lay brisket on heavy-duty foil, fat side up.
Pour liquid smoke, Worcestershire sauce and lemon juice over brisket.
Seal in foil and let marinate overnight.
Bake for 10 hours at 225°.
Bring 1 quart of water to a boil.
Steep with 1 family size tea bag.
While still hot, add sugar, cinnamon, orange juice and lemonade.
Add an additional quart of either hot or cold water (more or less to taste).
Transfer chicken to plate; set aside.
Add to skillet the oil, onion, salt, oregano and pepper.
Brown until golden.
Add chicken, tomatoes and wine or water.
Bring to boil.
Cover; reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Remove meat; keep warm.
Boil sauce over high heat 3 minutes to thicken slightly.
Spoon on top of chicken.
Serve over rice.
Combine apple juice, allspice, cloves, ginger and cinnamon sticks.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Drizzle ham with 1/2 honey.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Drizzle with other 1/2 honey.
Baste with apple juice mixture every 20 minutes until done.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Wash and wedge potatoes. Soak wedges in cold water for 1/2 hour.
Mix together dry ingredients.
Coat wedges with mixture.
Place in pan on top of melted butter.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes, turning once after 20 minutes.
Combine the first ingredient in a large bowl.
Combine corn meal and all other ingredients; pour into cream-style corn.
Place in an 11 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° until a knife inserted in middle comes out clean.

recipes.t: Blue Owl Restaurants Chicken Salad Pie
d: Combine all ingredients except the cheese.
Place in pie crust.
Bake at 375 degrees for about 30 minutes.
Top with cheddar cheese and bake an additional 10 - 15 minutes.
Heat chocolate and 2 tablespoons milk in saucepan over low heat.
Beat sugar in cream cheese; add remaining milk, the chocolate mixture and peppermint and beat until smooth.
Fold chocolate mixture into whipped topping.
Spoon into crust and freeze.
Soak fish in buttermilk overnight or for 4 to 6 hours.
Wash well, removing buttermilk.
Drain on paper towels.
Squeeze lemon juice over fish.
Roll in mixture of cracker meal, flour and small amount of cornmeal if desired.
Fry in heavy skillet (cast-iron) in enough Crisco plus 1 tablespoon butter to cover bottom of pan well.
Pour boiling water over tomatoes, red peppers, green peppers and onion; let stand 5 minutes.
Drain and add sugar, vinegar and canning salt.
Mix and cook 15 minutes.
Mix salad mustard with cornstarch and cook 15 minutes longer.
Stir to keep from sticking.
Remove from stove and add salad dressing.
Stir thoroughly and put in pint jars; seal.

Drain pineapple and reserve juice. Add water to juice to make 2 cups and heat to boiling point. Add Jell-O, pineapple and cranberry sauce; stir until cranberry sauce is completely melted. Stir in nuts and refrigerate until set.
Marinate steak in oil and vinegar overnight.
Place a little oil in pan and saute over very high heat so meat sears.
Add 2 tablespoons green peppers, salt, pepper and garlic.
Cook until meat is done.
Put orange juice, sugar, dry milk, ice cubes and banana or strawberries in blender.
Blend on high speed for 1 minute or until ice is chopped and mixture is smooth.
Pour into individual glasses.
Garnish with orange slices.
Cook ground chuck until brown; drain through strainer until all fat is gone.
Finely crumble meat with hands, then put in 6-quart slow cooker.
Add all remaining ingredients, then stir to mix thoroughly.
Cook on high 2 hours, then simmer for 2 hours, then enjoy the best chili in world.
Mix all ingredients in large serving bowl, adding the 7-Up last.
Add ice cubes or frozen ice ring.
Serve and enjoy.
Heat chocolate chips and condensed milk in microwave until melted.
Pour over 1 cup Rice Krispies and stir to coat.
Press on buttered pizza pan.

Place the prepared Stove Top stuffing on top.
Bake, covered, at 375° for 40 minutes. Remove the lid, reduce the heat to 350° for 20 to 25 minutes more. Serves 4.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl and add salt and pepper to desired taste. If you desire a hot taste leave all seeds in peppers. If you desire a milder taste, cut peppers in half and take out all seeds.
Grease and flour regular tube pan or fluted tube pan.
Combine cake mix, sugar, oil, eggs and sour cream.
Blend with electric mixer at low speed until ingredients are moistened.
Beat at medium speed 2 minutes.
Stir in pecans.
Pour half of batter into prepared pan.
Combine cinnamon and brown sugar.
Sprinkle over batter.
Pour remaining batter into pan.
Bake 45 minutes at 350° or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Allow cake to cool 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare Rum Sauce, then pour over cake.
Cool at least 1 1/2 hours before turning out of pan.
Mix together cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Add prepared Dream Whip.
Spread on top of prepared cake.
Top cake with cherry pie filling.
Enjoy!

recipes.t: Pasta With Sausage And Cream Sauce
