d: Melt butter in skillet; stir in sausage and fry until brown. Drain grease.
Stir in cream, wine, 1 tablespoon parsley, nutmeg and 1/2 cup Parmesan.
Simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Cool slightly; set aside. Beat the cream cheese until smooth.
Gradually add gelatin, beating well.
Stir in pineapple and baby food.
Fold in whipped topping.
Pour mixture into a 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish.
Cover; chill until firm.
To serve, cut into squares and serve on lettuce. Serves 12.
Grease 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Spread half the bread cubes evenly in dish.
Add the ham and both cheeses, then cover with remaining bread cubes.
Mix eggs, milk, onion, salt and mustard.
Pour evenly over bread cubes and refrigerate overnight. Combine cornflakes and butter for topping.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Makes 10 servings.
In large bowl, stir together 1 1/2 cups flour and yeast.
In saucepan, heat milk, sugar, shortening and salt to 115° to 120°. Stir constantly.
Add heated mixture to flour mixture; add egg. Beat with electric mixer on low 1/2 minute.
Beat 3 minutes on high.
Use spoon and stir in enough remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Place dough in greased bowl, turn once to grease surface. Cover and refrigerate dough until chilled.
(Chill overnight and fry for breakfast.)
Mix all together and put chips on top.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix dry ingredients.
Stir in remaining ingredients until moistened.
Turn pancakes when bubbles appear.
Tis helpful to sift dry ingredients together.
Tis better not to beat the egg.
Tis best not to overstir the batter.
Double the ingredients and you'll have batter good for 2 days!!
Mix cream cheese and butter until blended.
Blend in yolk and vanilla.
Add cake mix (dry), 1/3 at a time, mixing well after each addition.
If mixer is used, add last 1/3 by hand.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°.
Drop by teaspoons onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until light brown.
Cool slightly before removing from sheet.
Put everything into a 6-quart crock-pot. Fill with water to 1/2-inch of top. Cover. Cook on low 6 to 8 hours or until done. Adjust salt.
Serve with hearty bread and a salad.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add sugar, stir until dissolved.
Add cold water.
Prepare orange juice and lemonade according to package directions.
Add pineapple juice.
Add jello mixture.
Pour into jars, cover and chill for 24 hours.
Part of jello mixture may be poured into jello mold.
Freeze for 24 hours. Place ice ring in punch bowl, add rest of punch.
Bring a 3-quart saucepan full of water to a boil.
Add mostaccioli noodles and simmer until tender.
Drain and set aside. Brown ground chuck in a skillet and drain off any grease.
In a large saucepan, add tomato paste, water, sugar, salt, pepper, oregano and basil.
Heat and simmer.
Add browned meat mixture. Simmer the tomato-meat mixture for at least 1/2 hour.
Next, add noodles and serve with Parmesan cheese and buttered garlic bread.
Chop green onions using half of green tops.
Cut beef fine or chop fine.
Soften cream cheese and add onions, beef and accent. Put small amount of pecans in and keep the rest to roll cheese ball in.
Mix thoroughly; then roll ball in remaining nuts. Refrigerate.
Will make 2 small balls or 1 large ball.

Mix first 5 ingredients. Divide into 6 portions. Flatten and shape meat mixture around boiled eggs. Dip meat coated eggs into egg whites and bread crumbs. Deep-fry in hot oil until brown and crusty, about 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from oil and drain. Cut crosswise for 2 round nests. Spoon tomato sauce around nests. Makes 12 servings.
Mix and bake in a 13 x 12-inch pan at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes; do not overcook.
Add black-eyed peas to onion.
Cover and cook over low heat 8 to 10 minutes.
Put bacon on top.
Melt margarine in skillet on medium-high heat.
Saute onion, green pepper and garlic 3 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients. Stir 3 minutes.
Add cooked fettucini; toss and heat through. Serves 4.
Marinate meat all day or overnight, especially with a thicker cut of meat.
Cream oleo, sugar and eggs, one at a time. Add flour, alternately with milk. Add candy, dates, nuts and coconut.
Mix well. Mixture will be thick. Grease and flour tube pan.
Bake 2 1/2 hours at 250°. While cake is still warm, add glaze while still in pan.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cream the butter and 1/2 cup of the sugar; add beaten eggs gradually and then the grated lemon rind.
Add flour and milk alternately.
Put peaches into the pastry shell; sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup of sugar.
Spread batter over the peaches and bake in a 375° oven for 20 minutes.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350° and bake for an additional 20 minutes.
In a colander, rinse cooked macaroni with cold water; drain well.
In a large bowl, combine the pasta and salad dressing. Toss to coat.
Add the cucumber, green pepper, onion and snipped parsley to the pasta mixture.
Toss gently.
Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours.
Before serving, stir in the cherry tomatoes.
Makes 4 servings.
Sift dry ingredients into large bowl.
Mix water, vinegar and vanilla.
Make a "well" in dry ingredients.
Add water mixture and applesauce all at once.
Mix well.
Grease 10 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350°
for 35 to 45 minutes.
Batter will be very thin.
Wash peas.
Put in water to boil.
Simmer 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Cover and let stand 1 hour.
Add ham bone, vegetables, bay leaf and thyme.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, 2 1/2 to 3 hours or until peas are soft.
Remove bone. Cut off meat and dice.
Return meat to soup.
Season to taste with pepper.
Makes about 2 quarts.
Cream butter and sugar until lemon colored.
Beat in eggs one at a time.
Add vanilla.
Sift together flour, salt and baking powder.
Add to egg butter mixture.
To the raisins, add the cup flour and be sure each one is coated.
Put in large cake pan and cook about 3 hours between 250° and 275°.
Spray 6-inch deep oven safe pot or dish with Pam or spread margarine around dish.
Layer cherry pie filling, coconut, pineapple, cake mix, pecan halves and cut up margarine over top. Bake on 350° approximately 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients; let sit overnight in the refrigerator to blend flavors.
Mix all ingredients well and pour into 2 nine-inch pans.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Combine gravy and next 6 ingredients.
Add spaghetti and mix well.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle top with remaining 1/4 cup cheese and paprika.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes or until bubbly and lightly browned.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Makes 4 servings.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 2 round 9-inch pans or 1 (13 x 9-inch) pan.
Beat all ingredients in a large bowl on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Scrape bowl occasionally.
Pour into pans and bake 35 to 40 minutes or until wooden toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes and remove from pans.
Cool completely.
Frost cake.
Mix sweet potatoes, evaporated milk, sugar, eggs and margarine with electric mixer until smooth.
Pour into oblong dish sprayed with Pam.
Heat in 400° oven for about 15 minutes or until heated thoroughly.
Remove any white membrane surrounding roast.
Place roast in a shallow dish.
Combine wine, onion and seasonings; pour over roast. Cover and marinate 8 hours in refrigerator, turning meat occasionally.
Cook linguine.
Finely chop vegetables.
Put 1/4 shaker of Salad Supreme into drained linguine.
Add rest of shaker to Italian dressing and stir.
Pour over linguine.
Add vegetables and toss lightly.
This is better if prepared the night before. Makes 12 to 15 servings.
Boil onion.
Cook chicken and cut into bite size pieces.
Mix everything together in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Make biscuits and place on top of mixture (make biscuits very thin).
Bake at 475° until biscuits are done.
Before you start, check the rum to make sure the quality is good.
Select a large measuring bowl, measuring cup, etc. and check the rum again.
With an electric mixer, beat 1 cup butter in the fuffy bowl.
Add 1 teaspoon sugar and beat.
Meanwhile check the rum again.
Add 3 large eggs, 2 cups fried druit and beat unitl very high.
If druit sticks in beaters, pry out with a screwdriver. Taste the rum again.
Add 3 cups baking powder, one pint of rum, one seaspoon of tada and one cup of pepper.
Stir in 1/2 pint lemon juice and fold in the chopped buttermilk and strained nuts.
Add one bablespoon of scrown sugar or whatever color you have.
Check the rum again.
Turn pan to 350 degrees, grease oven and pour the whole mess in.
Sample rum while waiting.
Let first 5 ingredients stand in the refrigerator for several hours.
Then add 1 package of Dream Whip without vanilla, 1 cup chopped nuts and 3 cubed bananas.
Fold all this together and put into paper cups placed in muffin tins.
Place into freezer until firm, then you can place in Ziploc bags.
Sprinkle ribs with garlic salt (optional).
Mix ingredients, coat
ribs on both sides and put in glass pan to marinate overnight.
Fill
the bottom of a broiler pan with water, cover pan rack
with
aluminum
foil
and
put
ribs
on rack.
Cover loosely with
foil,
bake at 350° for 1/2 hour per pound. Baste with sauce frequently.
Towards end of cooking, remove covering foil.
Cook
spaghetti according to package directions.
Drain and mix together with other ingredients. Reserve 1 cup cheese. Pour in	greased
casserole dish.
Spread remaining cheese on top. Bake
at
for
about 30 minutes or until cheese is melted and lightly browned.
Mix flour and oleo until crumbly; press into bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool.
In a medium saucepan, slowly combine the vinegar and mustard, whisking to make a smooth mixture.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Add sugar and eggs; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil.
Cook for about 30 seconds or a little more, until mixture coats a spoon.
Remove from heat; pour into hot, sterilized jars.
Cool.
Cover and refrigerate.
If this is stored for a long time, it may need stirring before using.
Place pineapple in a saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Add gelatin, stirring until completely dissolved.
Stir in buttermilk, coconut and pecans. Cool.
Fold in whipped topping.
Pour into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan or dish.
Chill until firm.
Yields 15 servings.
Cover limas with water and bring to a rapid boil.
Stir in baking soda; water will turn green.
Pour off; add fresh water. Parboil 3 times or until water boils clear.
Add chopped onion, meat and pepper to taste.
Do not salt until beans have cooked long enough to taste saltiness of meat.
Cook until beans are tender, about 1 hour.
Pour off excess stock and save for adding to leftover beans or soup.
Lift tomatoes from juice in can, chop and add to beans.
To about 2 quarts of cooked beans, add 2 tablespoons vinegar and 2 heaping tablespoonfuls brown sugar.
Salt and season to taste.
Pour into baking dish, cover with sliced ham or bacon, sprinkle with brown sugar and dot with butter.
Bake 1 hour in moderate oven.
Add tomato juice to excess bean stock for soup.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in boiling water.
Pour into 20 x 14-inch oven cooking bag.
Add rice, carrots, celery and onion. Place bag in baking pan.
Evenly spread out rice mixture. Sprinkle chicken with marjoram, salt and pepper.
Place on top of rice, close bag and make slit in top of bag.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Cook over low heat to 238° or soft ball stage.
Pour in greased 8 x 8-inch pan; cut into squares when hard.
A nicer alternative is to get the small brown candy cases from See's and plunk a spoonful into each one.
This makes the candy easier to serve or to package for mailing.
Soften cheese; mix all together.
Serve with thinly sliced apples.
Beat together milk and pumpkin.
When smooth, add vanilla pudding, pumpkin spice and cinnamon.
Beat well.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into graham cracker pie shell or regular pie shell that has already been baked and cooled.
Cook sweet potatoes to just tender, about 30 minutes.
Drain, cool and peel.
In large bowl, mash potatoes.
Stir in oleo, sugar and raisins.

Put broiler pan 8 to 10-inches from heat and preheat broiler. In a shallow bowl, combine oil and mustard. Dip steaks into mixture, then into the onions, coating completely. Place steaks on a rimmed baking sheet and broil for 3 to 4 minutes on each side.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Break bread into pieces as if for stuffing unless you are using cubed plain stuffing pieces.
Add soup, 1/2 stick melted margarine and eggs and blend well. Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan that has been greased.
Sprinkle crushed potato chips and 1/2 stick margarine (or butter) over casserole. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until set.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 10-inch pie plate.
Beat all ingredients until smooth.
Pour into plate.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean (50 to 55 minutes).
Garnish with whipped cream if desired.
Sprinkle steaks with salt and pepper.
Brown in shortening in large iron skillet; drain.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour around chops.
Bake in 350° oven 45 minutes or until tender.
Stir gravy.
Makes 4 servings.
Saute onions, bell pepper and celery in margarine until tender.
Add shrimp or crawfish.
Cook 7 minutes.
Add 2 cups of water.
Bring to a boil.
Add noodles; cook 7 minutes.
Add seasoning to taste.
Melt Velveeta and add the half and half to noodles.
Simmer celery, onions and chicken broth 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix with chicken, soup and butter.
Top with noodles and nuts.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Boil and stir margarine, sugar and dates for 3 minutes.
Add Rice Krispies and pecans.
Form into small balls and roll in powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Combine 1 cup of corn flake crumbs with milk.
Mix in remaining ingredients.
Form into 1-inch balls. Roll in remaining corn flake crumbs.
Place on greased pan and bake 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat skillet and add butter or oil.
Saute carrots for 10 minutes.
Add juice, spices and raisins.
Cover and simmer until carrots are tender and most of the juice is absorbed.
Heat over medium heat the first 4 ingredients, stirring constantly.
Cook until mixture turns amber colored and begins to emit a light smoke.
(This usually takes between 10 or 15 minutes.)
Cube or shred cabbage; add cubed ham, cream, flour and seasonings.
Cook just until tender.
You may add a little milk if more liquid is needed.
Slow heat is the secret.
In a large, heavy pan, cook onion and garlic with basil in butter until tender.
Stir in golden mushroom soup and water.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and cook ten minutes or until noodles are done.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add beaten eggs, 3 cups flour, salt and
baking powder.
Mix 1 cup flour with nuts and fruit. Mix with other ingredients.
Bake 3 hours at 250°.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Pour Miracle Whip, sugar and vinegar over ingredients.
Mix well.
You may add additional Miracle Whip to suit your taste.
Beat egg whites until stiff,
adding sugar gradually.
Beat in baking powder.
Fold in crackers,
nuts and vanilla.
Spread in greased 9 inch pie plate.
Bake 40 minutes at 300°.
When cool, top with peach slices and whipped cream.
Mix well and pour into shallow casserole.
Top with cheese and mixture of crumbs and butter.
Sprinkle with almonds.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Blend in the milk and vanilla. Stir in the flour, cherries and pecans.
Form dough into two 8-inch rolls.
Roll in flaked coconut, coating outside.
Wrap in wax paper or plastic.
Chill 2 hours.
Cut into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Bake at 375° for 12 minutes on ungreased sheet pan.
Bring syrup and sugar to a boil in a small saucepan.
Slowly pour over beaten eggs, beating constantly to blend.
Add butter; stir until melted.
Stir in salt, vanilla, lemon juice, cereal, coconut and milk.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 375° about 30 minutes or until top is set and lightly browned.
Serve warm or cooled with or without whipped topping.
Spray Bundt pan well with Pam.
Take rolls (thawed) and spread in pan.
In layers, pour brown sugar, nuts, dry butterscotch pudding and melted butter over rolls.
Cover with cloth and let sit out overnight.
Bake the next morning for 35 minutes at 350°.
Put in large bowl; make a stiff mix of ingredients.
Put a little oil on top.
Cover; let rise overnight or until double in size.
Punch down.
Knead 50 times.
Divide in half.
Roll 1/2 as flat as you can.
Spread softened cream cheese.
Spread over entire area.
Spread pie mix of your choice over cream mix.
Fold over the sides of dough to cover pie mix.
Let rise again.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix powdered sugar and small amount of milk.
Spread over cake.
Sprinkle toasted almonds over cake. Take remaining dough and make into rolls; let them touch each other.
Rise until double.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Spread crescent dough on a greased cookie sheet.
Press to form crust.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Pare apples and slice thin.
Combine Sugar Twin, flour, spices and salt.
Mix with apples.
Line pie plate with pastry.
Fill with apple mixture and dot with butter.
Adjust top crust. Sprinkle with Sugar Twin.
Bake at 400° for 50 minutes or until done.
Roll pork chops into flour; brown until golden.
Cook potatoes until almost done.
Put in bottom of baking dish.
Mix sour cream and mushroom soup; thin with milk.
Pour over potatoes.
Combine eggplant, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper and water. Cook on medium-high until cooked down and most of the water has evaporated.
Mix butter with cracker crumbs.
Spray casserole pan with Pam or lightly grease.
Place 1/2-inch of cracker crumbs in baking dish. Add eggplant and crackers, leaving enough crackers for a top covering.
Mix egg and milk and pour over top of casserole.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake an additional 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Cream sugar with shortening.
Add eggs and beat well.
Add pecans, soda and milk.
Add flour, salt, vanilla and bananas.
Mix well.
Bake in loaf or layer pan at 350° about 35 minutes.
Chop up 3 to 4 cups lettuce.
Place in large bowl or oblong pan.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and approximately 1 teaspoon sugar.
Layer with sliced hard-boiled eggs, salt and pepper. Sprinkle peas (I never use whole box).
Layer remaining lettuce. Top with bacon bits and then Cheddar cheese.
Seal top of salad with mayonnaise.
Decorate with scallions.
Cook green string beans until still firm.
Pack in jars.
To each pint jar, add 1/4 scant teaspoon red pepper, 1 clove garlic and 1 head dill or 1/4 teaspoon dill seed.
Heat vinegar, water and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Pour into jars.
Seal.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking pan; set aside.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine chocolate chips and butter in a large saucepan. Melt over low heat, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat. Combine eggs, salt and sugar; blend well.
Add to chocolate mixture.
Stir in flour, baking powder and vanilla until well blended.
Stir in nuts, if desired.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake for 25 minutes or until brownie begins to pull away from edge of pan.
Let stand until cool.
Cut into bars.
Combine all ingredients.
Store in an airtight container.
Use 2 to 3 teaspoons per cup of hot water.
Combine fruits; sprinkle with lemon juice.
Chill.
Fold whipped cream into mayonnaise.
Fold into fruit mixture.
Serve on greens.
Top with coconut.
Cook ham and potatoes until potatoes are almost done.
Add noodles and cook for 12 to 15 minutes.
Then add tomato juice and sauce and simmer until done.
Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil in large skillet.
Add meat, bell peppers, and onion.
Cook over medium-high heat 5 minutes or until meat has browned.
Add chili powder, cumin, and tomatoes.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in beans and heat through.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water; add sherbet and stir until blended.
Add other ingredients.
Fold in whipped cream last.
Add 1 cup chopped nuts, if desired.
According to what vegetables you decide to use, blanch mixed vegetables for 3 minutes and cook squash in boiling water for 10 minutes.
Drain well.
In saucepan over heat, melt butter, then add flour and stir in milk.
Cook until thickened.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Beat egg yolks until fairly stiff and add to sauce.
Add seasonings and mix well.
Add vegetables of choice. Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into mixture.
For 6:00 p.m. serving time:
Mix and drop by teaspoon into cupcake pans prepared with oil. Bake at 425° until light brown.
Spread muffins with mixture.
Set on cookie sheet and freeze. When frozen, wrap until ready to serve.
Broil until bubbly.
Cut into four pieces.
Marinate chicken wings anywhere from 6 to 24 hours.
Remove from marinade and bake in a 350° oven for 60 minutes.
You can also use marinade for pork or beef.
Delicious!
Yield:
24 wings.
Brown diced bacon in large skillet.
Remove bits from drippings and reserve for garnish.
Saute onion in bacon grease until tender.
Add remaining ingredients and stir until mixture begins to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 30 minutes. Garnish with bacon before serving.
Mix together in a medium bowl all the ingredients except the cocktail sauce.
Shape into a ball.
Place in middle of a serving dish and cover with clear wrap.
Refrigerate.
To serve, pour the cocktail sauce over the ball and decorate dish with crackers.

Beat butter, sugar and vanilla in large bowl until creamy. Stir together flour and cocoa; gradually add to butter mixture, beating until blended. Add pecans; beat until well blended. Refrigerate dough about 1 hour or until firm enough to handle.
Trim ends of zucchini.
Cook, covered, in boiling, salted water for 5 to 8 minutes.
Drain and cut in half lengthwise. Scoop out centers; chop.
In a 9 x 13 x 2-inch Pyrex, layer bread cubes, cheese, bread cubes and cheese.
Top with sausage that has been fried, crumbled and drained.
Brown stew beef in oil about 5 minutes.
Add water, salt, pepper, potatoes, turnip, carrots, celery, onion, bouquet sauce, bouillon cube and bay leaf.
Cook over medium heat for about 1 1/2 hours or in oven at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix flour and 1/2 cup water (cold).
Add to stew beef to thicken for gravy.
Cover and cook onion in margarine in 3-quart saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally, until tender, 20 to 30 minutes.
Add beef broth, water, bay leaf, pepper and thyme.
Heat to boiling and reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Set oven on broil and/or 550°.
Place bread slices on cookie sheet.
Broil with tops about 5 inches from heat until golden brown, about 1 minute. Turn; broil until golden brown.
Place bread in 4 ovenproof bowls or individual casseroles.
Add broth; top with Swiss cheese. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Place bowls on cookie sheet. Broil with cheese about 5 inches from heat just until cheese is melted and golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve with additional French bread if desired.
Makes 4 servings.
Bake pie shell.
Mix sugar, water and cream of tartar, let come to boil.
Drop in crackers; let boil 2 minutes.
Put in pie shell. Put margarine and cinnamon on top.
Bake in 350° oven and let brown.
Combine beans and garlic in food processor, using on-off motion until smooth (do not puree).
Transfer to bowl and stir in salsa.
Serve with vegetable crudites or toasted tortilla pieces. Makes 4 servings, about 1/2 cup each.
Cook broccoli in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and place in baking dish.
Combine soups; pour over broccoli.
Sprinkle with cheese and stuffing.
Pour melted butter over top.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Put 1 cup warm water in a large bowl.

Sprinkle in 2 packages of yeast and 2 tablespoons of sugar. Let stand until yeast rises. Put remaining 1 1/2 cups of water in small pot and then add 3 tablespoons of butter, 1 level tablespoons salt and 4 tablespoons of sugar.
Simmer until all ingredients are melted.
Cool until lukewarm.
Cream together shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well. Add flour to creamed mixture alternately with banana.
Blend well. Stir in nuts.
Pour into well-greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes, or until done.
Remove from pan.
Cool on rack.
Place whole ribeye on baking pan.
Rub both sides heavily with chopped garlic.
Cover both sides with black pepper, then lightly salt both sides.
Bake with fat side up at 350° for 45 minutes, then lower temperature to 175° and cook for 4 hours for medium-rare, 6 hours for medium-medium well.
Mix all ingredients together.
Refrigerate overnight to blend flavors.
Cream butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
Add beaten egg yolk, vanilla and sifted flour.
Spread on 12 x 17 1/2-inch cookie sheet and bake at 350°.
Combine all ingredients; shape into very small balls (scant teaspoonfuls).
Brown in shortening.
In mixing bowl, cream butter, sugar and eggs.
Stir in cocoa, flour, vanilla and salt.
Spread into a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until brownies test done.
Cool.
Spread marshmallow cream over top of cooled brownies.
In small saucepan, melt peanut butter and chocolate chips over low heat, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; stir in the cocoa.
Spread over marshmallow layer.
Chill before cutting.
Makes 3 dozen.
Combine rice and cheese.
Drain asparagus and reserve liquid. Add asparagus to rice and cheese.
Blend together egg, mayonnaise, 3 tablespoons asparagus liquid and seasoned salt.
Stir into rice mixture.
Pour into a greased 1-quart casserole.
Sprinkle paprika over the top.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Trim excess fat from roast.
In Dutch oven or large skillet, slowly brown meat on all sides in hot shortening.
Add next 7 ingredients.
Cover.
Cook slowly 2 1/2 hours or until meat is tender.
Place biscuits on meat. Sprinkle with parsley.
Cover tightly and steam 15 minutes or until "dumplings" are done. Remove meat (pot roast) and "dumplings" to warm platter. Make pot roast gravy if you want to.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Thaw frozen fish.
Clean and dry fish.
Brush inside of fish with lemon juice and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Wrap each fish with bacon slices.
Place fish in a hinged wire grill.
Cook about 5 inches from moderate hot coals for 10 minutes.
Turn and cook for 10 to 15 minutes longer or until bacon is crisp and fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Serves 6.
Cook chicken until tender.
Cool and cut into bite-size pieces. Take fat off the cooled broth, blend fat with flour, 1 teaspoon salt and pepper.
Slowly add 2 cups broth and heavy cream, stirring constantly.
Cook over low heat until thick.
Combine cornbread crumbs, celery, 1 teaspoon salt, pepper to taste and butter. Arrange cut up chicken and dressing alternately in large casserole. Cover with sauce and bake 50 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Mix together the cheese at room temperature.
Roll in chopped parsley or paprika.
Put chicken in large pot and add about 1/2 gallon water; cook until tender.
Remove chicken from broth and let cool; remove from bone.
Reserve broth.
Mix milk, Crisco and flour.
If not thick enough, add a little more flour.
Put broth on stove and add cans of chicken broth; bring to boil.
Add chicken into broth.
Drop dough a teaspoon at a time into broth and cook 10 minutes covered.
Mix all ingredients. Shape into a ball. Serve with ritz crackers.
Mix oil, dill, garlic salt and Ranch salad dressing.
Pour over crackers.
Mix well.
Let stand for at least one hour. Store in plastic container.
Cream together the cream cheese and sugar.
Stir in the strawberries, crushed pineapple and thawed topping; gently fold in bananas and walnuts.
Spoon into a 9 x 13-inch pan and freeze. Let stand at room temperature for 1/2 hour before serving.
Mix all ingredients together well.
Bake at 375° in a loaf pan about 40 minutes, or until done.

recipes.t: Cream Of Broccoli Soup(Makes 7 Cups; Low In Cholesterol)
d: Heat broth in large saucepan to boiling.
Add broccoli, onion and garlic.
Cover.
Simmer for 7 to 10 minutes or until broccoli is tender.
Remove from heat.
Cool for 5 to 7 minutes.
Puree vegetables and broth in blender or food processor until desired consistency.
(Process in two or three batches if necessary.) Return to pan.
In 2-quart glass measuring cup with handle, combine sugar, sour cream, corn syrup, butter and salt.
Microwave at High for 5 minutes.
Stir well until sugar dissolves.
Microwave at High for 6 minutes or just until mixture reaches 236°.
Let stand 15 minutes; do not stir.
Add vanilla; beat until mixture starts to lose its gloss (about 6 minutes).
Stir in cherries and walnuts. Quickly pour into buttered 8 1/2 x 4 1/2-inch loaf pan.
Cool and cut into squares.
Makes about 1 1/2 pounds.
Combine flour, sugar, cocoa, soda, baking powder and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Add eggs, coffee, buttermilk, oil and vanilla. Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
(Batter will be thin.)
Pour in greased and floured 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook squash and onion in salted water and drain. Add bread crumbs and cheese and put mixture in a baking dish. Add rest of the ingredients and bake at 375° until top starts to brown.
In a large skillet in a little oil, brown steak on one side. Remove steak.
Mix oatmeal in oil that the steak was browned in. Add a little water, if needed. Spread oatmeal mixture on one side of steak.
Put sliced onion on top of oatmeal.
Fold over steak. Add more onions, Worcestershire, salt and pepper to taste on top. Put a small amount of water in pan.
Cover and bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Brown ground chuck and drain.
Add remaining ingredients to ground chuck and place in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° until bubbly, usually about 20 to 30 minutes.
Grease baking sheet.
Combine sugar, corn syrup and salt in 3-quart casserole.
Stir in peanuts.
Microwave on High, until light brown, for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once.
Stir in remaining ingredients until light and foamy.
Spread on greased cookie sheet as thin as possible.
Cool and break into pieces.
Mix sugar and flour together.
Stir until smooth.
Add cocoa; blend well.
Add all other ingredients and cook over low heat until thick.
Pour into a baked pie shell.
Top with meringue.
Cut squash in half lengthwise; remove seeds.
Bake, cut side down, in shallow pan at 350° for 45 minutes or until tender.
Fry diced bacon.
Add beef, onion, 1/2 teaspoon salt and dash of pepper.
Cook until beef is browned.
Pour off excess fat.
Remove squash from shells (reserve shells).
In small mixing bowl, whip squash with 1/2 teaspoon salt; add milk as needed to make mixture fluffy.
Combine with beef mixture.
Return to squash shells.
Top with crushed potato chips.
Continue baking at 350° for 15 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Dip apples in 1/2 cup lemon juice to prevent browning.
Mix dressing ingredients in separate bowl until blended and pour over veggies.
Chill for several hours.
Mix the cake mix, 2 eggs and melted oleo together and press into 9 x 13 pan.
Mix the cream cheese, 2 eggs, powdered sugar and vanilla together.
Spread on top of cake mixture and bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts and reserved powdered sugar.
In medium skillet, heat dressing and saute green pepper and onion.
Stir in tomatoes with liquid and simmer, covered, 15 minutes.
Add shrimp, red pepper and sugar.
Simmer, covered, an additional 15 minutes or until shrimp turn pink.
Serve over hot rice.
Combine margarine and sugars together.
Add Egg Beaters and vanilla.
Mix well.
Brown beef in skillet and drain off fat.
Put all ingredients in crock-pot (3 1/2 or 4-quart model).
Stir thoroughly.
Cover and cook on low 7 to 9 hours (high 3 hours).
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown sausage and drain. Stir in pizza sauce. Set aside. Line greased muffin pan with biscuits. Spoon sausage mixture into biscuits.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until brown. Add cheese on top and let it melt.
Mix together.
Cover and chill.
Before serving add 1 quart carbonated water or ginger ale.
Makes 10 servings.
Heat oven to 375°.
Separate crescent dough into 4 rectangles. Press perforations to seal.
Brush each with margarine.
Combine cheese and oregano; sprinkle over dough.
Cut each rectangle crosswise to form 2 squares.
Place a sausage link on each square; roll up.
Cut each roll into 3 or 4 pieces.
Secure each with a toothpick.
Place, cut side down, on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Brown beef in skillet; drain fat.
Add Ragu.
Heat to boiling. Mix Ricotta, eggs, parsley, salt, pepper and some Parmesan cheese (save some to sprinkle on top).
Put meat sauce in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Put layer of noodles, 1 cup cheese mixture, meat sauce, noodles then cheese sauce.
Spread remaining meat sauce on top and sprinkle the rest of Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Peel eggplant and dice in small cubes.
Saute pepper and onion until tender.
Add tomatoes, eggplant, salt and pepper; cook 15 minutes.
Place in a casserole dish.
Melt oleo in a skillet. Add bread crumbs and stir.
Sprinkle bread crumbs over eggplant. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes, or until eggplant is tender and crumbs are brown.

Grind the first 4 ingredients all together. Drain off juice. Add the salt; let set overnight. Add the water and cook 10 minutes on simmer. Drain well and rinse with water to remove salt. Mix the sugar, vinegar and mustard. Stir in vegetables and cook 12 minutes. Then mix the cornstarch with cold water. Add to vegetables and cook 3 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and let cool 10 minutes. Add the salad dressing. Stir well. Put in pint jars and seal. Hot water bath for 5 minutes.
Peel and devein shrimp; chop.
Place shrimp, 1 cup of chicken broth and the Casera sauce in blender.
Cover and blend on high speed until smooth.
Heat shrimp mixture, the remaining broth, salt, saffron and pepper to boiling.
Mix cornstarch and water; stir into shrimp mixture to thicken.
Heat to boiling; cook and stir for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir in half and half. Garnish with parsley.
Yields 5 cups.
In medium bowl, combine cream cheese and sour cream; mix well. Stir in chilies, onions and jalapenos.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread tortilla with about 1/4 cup cream cheese mixture; top with another tortilla.
Continue spreading and stacking tortillas until stack is 4 tortillas high.
Top with another tortilla that has not been spread with cream cheese mixture. Make another stack with remaining 5 tortillas.
Wrap tortilla stacks in plastic wrap.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Cut each stack into 18 wedges.
Arrange pinwheel fashion around cup of salsa, picante sauce or salsa verde.
Makes 36 appetizer servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Spoon into small muffin tin. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Pour boiling water into blender container.
Add gelatin; blend at low speed until dissolved, about 1 minute.
Combine cold water and ice cubes to make 1 cup.
Add to gelatin; stir until ice is almost melted, then blend in yogurt and vanilla.
Chill in dessert glasses for 1 hour, or until set.
Makes 5 servings.
Each serving contains 35 calories.
(Optional:
Add 2 c. walnuts or pecans.)
Cook beans for 1 hour over medium heat with salt, pepper and drippings.
Add garlic, onion and pepper.
Cook 1 hour and add sausage in 1/2-inch slices.
Cook another hour.
Serve over rice.
Brown sausage.
In crock-pot put sausage, beans, onion and green pepper.
Mix together tomato soup, tomato paste and brown sugar.
Pour into crock-pot and mix with beans.
Use crock-pot on high for 1 hour, then low for 2 hours.

Boil squash and onion together in salted water until tender. While squash is cooking, saute crushed crackers in 1/2 cup margarine until brown and crisp. Set aside. Make white sauce with 1/4 cup margarine, half and half and cornstarch. When white sauce is smooth, add Velveeta cheese cubes and heat until melted. Drain squash and place in an oblong casserole dish; pour cheese sauce over squash and top with the crackers. Bake for 25 minutes at 350°. Cover with foil for the first half of baking time to keep crackers from browning too much.
Mix all the ingredients with enough Miracle Whip to hold together.
Shape into a ball.
Cook zucchini 10 minutes until clear, using some of pineapple juice in the cooking.
Then add 2 cups pineapple, lemon juice, sugar and box of Sure-Jell.
Bring to rolling boil.
Boil for 5 minutes; remove from heat, then add orange jello.
Stir well; put into jars and seal.
Mix milk and pudding together.
Fold in sour cream and 1/2 of Cool Whip.
Place layer of vanilla wafers in large dish.
Then a layer of bananas, and a layer of pudding.
Repeat.
Top with remaining Cool Whip.
Refrigerate.
Will serve a lot.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Add milk.
Knead the dough until it has a rubbery texture.
Roll it out on a lightly floured surface until it is 1/2-inch thick.
Cut into squares.
Fry in oil until brown.
They will puff up and cook quickly.
Drain on paper towels.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with honey, if desired.
Set aside walnuts.
Using your hands, blend ingredients together.
Shape into ball.
Roll in chopped walnuts.
In double boiler, melt Hershey bars and marshmallows in the milk.
Allow to cool.
Add the whipped cream.
Pour into crust and top with additional whipped cream.
Chill about 4 hours.
Mix the other ingredients in a small container and pour over the tomatoes.
Broil the tomatoes 3 to 5 minutes or until cheese is slightly brown.
Serve immediately.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Add flour and salt.
Cut in butter and mix until blended.
Roll 1/2 at a time into rectangle. Beat cream cheese, sugar, lemon and orange rind.
Beat until fluffy.
Spread 1/2 on each rectangle.
Sprinkle walnuts.
Roll as jelly roll.
Place seam side down on greased cookie sheet.
Slit lengthwise 3/4 of the way through.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Slice at an angle. Makes 24 cookies.
Mix ingredients well and serve with veggies!
Brown meat and onion.
Salt to taste.
Add soup and 1/2 can water.
Mix.
Place in 2-quart casserole dish.
Place Tater Tots on top of mixture.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes at 375°.
Makes 8 servings.
Cut clams up with sharp knife and fork.
Peel and dice potatoes; combine with onions, pepper, Texas Pete, Worcestershire, oregano, parsley flakes, salt and black pepper in large saucepan. Cover with clam juice and water.
Add mixed vegetables and boil slowly 1 hour.
Dice salt pork and fry crisp.
Add meat and grease to clam
mixture.
Continue cooking.
Mix pie crust and roll out. Using 13 x 9-inch pan, line sides with crust.
Add clam mixture. Cover with strips of crust.
Bake in 400° oven until crust is browned.
Mix well.
Mix 1 package vanilla, reduced calorie, pudding "dry" with fruit (family size).
Stir well.
Weight Watchers count as 1/2 cup equals 1 fruit and 5 optional calories.
Brown the hamburger meat with diced onions and green pepper until meat is brown.
Add can of mushroom soup and can of tomato soup (undiluted).
Add catsup, water, salt, pepper and chili powder.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the whole can of drained kidney beans.
Add juice from can as needed.
Stir well.
Serve with raw chopped onion.
Add more chili powder to make hotter.
Mix and refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.
Combine sugar and cornstarch in saucepan.
Add butter, lemon rind, lemon juice and egg yolks.
Stir in milk and cook over medium heat, stirring until thick.
Cool, then fold in sour cream. Spoon into baked shell.
Cool at least 2 hours.
Serve topped with whipped cream and chopped walnuts or pecans.
Mix peanut butter, powdered sugar, margarine and graham crackers together.
Roll into balls.
Refrigerate.
Melt together paraffin wax and chocolate chips.
Dip balls with toothpicks in chocolate.
Drop on wax paper to cool.
Remove core from escarole and wash under cold water until completely cleaned.
Discard discolored and tough outer leaves. Place in a large pot with salt.
Cover with water and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and boil gently 8 - 10 minutes.
Drain.
In same pot, heat oil and saute garlic 3 minutes.
Add cannellini beans. Simmer 5 minutes. Add escarole and toss to mix.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cook another 2 minutes and serve.
Put all ingredients into a blender and blend well.
Allow to stand, covered, in the refrigerator for 2 to 3 hours before serving.
Makes about 2 1/4 cups.
Great as a party dip with fresh veggies.
Put all but the shrimp into a saucepan.
Hold out the sherry until later.
Over medium heat bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Just before serving, add shrimp and sherry.
Serve over rice.
Beat cream cheese, 1 1/3 cups sugar, 1 egg, vanilla and salt until thick and creamy.
Beat 3 eggs.
Add 1/4 cup sugar, Karo syrup and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Spread cream cheese mixture in bottom of unbaked pie shell.
Then sprinkle nuts on top of pie. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook spinach according to directions on package and drain. Blend soup mix, sour cream and salt. Add to drained spinach. Place entire mixture into a 2-quart casserole.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Spray baking dish with Pam.
Layer ingredients as listed, except for cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Place cheese on top as soon as removed from oven.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease baking sheet.
In bowl, mix crabmeat, onion, egg, celery and bread crumbs.
Remove stems from mushrooms and finely chop.
Add to crabmeat mixture.
Fill each mushroom and place on baking sheet.
Bake for 5 minutes to remove water from mushrooms.
Mix pretzel crumbs, butter and 3 tablespoons of sugar.
Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Cool.
Mix the first 4 ingredients.
Mix in enough Italian dressing to hold the mixture together.
Very good served with Club crackers.
Cook broccoli until done, drain.
Add sour cream or yogurt and cream of celery soup.
Add meat and onion mix.
Place in 3-quart casserole dish.
Cover with shredded cheese.
Bake at 350°. Yields 4 servings.
In a buttered casserole dish, layer the first 4 ingredients top with a little stuffing.
Add the water and dot with butter. Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Uncover the last 10 minutes to brown topping.
Mix well.
Spread dough in bottom and 1/2-inch up sides of a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Cut in shortening.
Moisten dough with enough water to give it the right consistency for rolling.
Roll dough out on lightly floured surface.
Cut into 6-inch saucer size circles.
Mix together cooked macaroni, ham, Cheddar cheese, cooked frozen peas and salad dressing.
Add salt and pepper to your taste.
I also add a little prepared mustard.
Mix well and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Place tomato slices in a shallow dish.
Mix remaining ingredients and marinate tomatoes.
Just mix and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Saute the onions in the margarine until tender.
Add the squash, chicken broth, white pepper, celery salt and tarragon and cook over low heat until tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the milk.
Process in blender until smooth.
Serve hot or cold.
Can be frozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Line bottom and sides of a 9 x 11-inch pan with waxed paper.
Mix pumpkin, milk, sugar, cinnamon and eggs; pour into pan.
Pour dry cake mix over mixture.
Top with nuts and cooled margarine.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes.
Invert on tray.
Combine sugar, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper.
Mix with remaining ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.

recipes.t: Hidden Valley Ranch Chicken Stir-Fry(Dinner In Ten Minutes Or Less)
d: Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in large skillet or wok.
Add chicken, cut into thin strips.
Stir in Hidden Valley original Ranch salad dressing.
Mix to coat chicken.
Add thawed vegetable medley and 2 tablespoons water.
Stir-fry about 2 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Roll crackers.
Add melted butter.
Mix well and line the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Place in refrigerator using 1/2 graham cracker mixture.
Prepare vanilla pudding as directed and put in pan.
Let set until cool.
Cover with remaining crumbs. Prepare chocolate pudding the same and put in dish.
Set overnight.
Add whipped cream just before serving.
Cut in wedges.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Pour pecans in bottom of tube pan. Pour batter over nuts.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Combine all ingredients except beans and bacon, mixing well until sugar is dissolved.
Gently stir in beans (with juice) and place in oblong baking dish.
Layer bacon across top.
Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Remove from oven; turn bacon slices and spoon off grease.
Return to oven and bake 45 minutes longer.
Bake in Bundt cake pan for approximately 40 minutes at 350°.
Put all ingredients into blender and puree.
May substitute mint chocolate chips for plain chocolate chips.
Marinate meat in marinade and/or vinegar for about 1 hour. Preheat vegetable oil in wok or large pan on stove.
Add meat and marinade to pan and quickly brown outside of meat, stirring so all sides brown.
Cover and steam for about 3 minutes.
Add vegetables; stir until coated with liquid.
Cover and steam for 5 minutes or until vegetables are desired tenderness.
Add brown sugar and soy sauce to taste.
Serve over rice.
Blend together eggs, sour cream and salt.
Stir in cheese. Add ham if desired.
Pour egg mixture into greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Drizzle butter over top.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 20 minutes or until set.
Mix
all
together
and pack firmly in a loaf pan lined with foil.
Let set in refrigerator three days before cutting.
Put all ingredients in large bowl and mix well with electric mixer.
Grease and flour 2 loaf pans.
Divide batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients together (except wings), then add chicken and let marinate 4 hours or more.
Remove chicken from marinade and bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
In a bowl, blend together the oil, vinegar and Italian dressing.
In a large bowl, combine other ingredients.
Stir. Pour dressing over and stir.
Chill.
Keeps good in refrigerator. May add other vegetables such as onions, carrot slices, cauliflower, etc.
Mix all ingredients except cookies.
Chill.
When ready to serve, add the cookies.
Bake cake according to directions in 4 layers.
Add bananas and 3 tablespoons of Cool Whip with about 1/4 cup sugar.
Frost between 3 layers with bananas.
Frost top and sides with rest of Cool Whip.
Place the meat of your choice in the bottom of a pan.
Mix dry ingredients and pour over meat.
Then mix liquids and pour over meat and dry seasonings.
Marinate at least two hours.
This is better if you marinate your meat overnight or at least for several hours.
Turn once when marinating. Now, grill!

recipes.t: Chicken Breast With Sage And Nutmeg
d: Trim any fat from chicken.
Combine next 5 ingredients. Dredge chicken in flour mixture and set aside.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Add chicken and cook 7 to 8 minutes on each side until browned.
Add vermouth and bell pepper; reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Transfer chicken to serving platter; spoon sauce over chicken and garnish with fresh sage leaves.
Combine potatoes, onion, water and salt in saucepan.
Cover and boil until potatoes are done, about 20 minutes.
Then add milk and margarine and pepper.
Heat for 5 minutes until hot.
Then while this is heating make Rupples.
Mix well.
Refrigerate until ready to use.
Lightly grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan; set aside.
Stir flour, baking powder, salt and baking soda in a mixing bowl.
Stir thoroughly.
Cream sugar and shortening until light and fluffy. Add eggs and orange peel; beat well.
Mash banana in a bowl with a fork; stir in milk.
Add flour mixture and banana mixture alternately to cream mixture.
Beat until smooth after each addition.
Fold in nuts.
Pour batter in prepared pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 45 to 50 minutes.
Turn out and cool on a wire rack.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in 8-inch square microwave dish, covered with plastic film, vented on one corner. Microwave on 50% power for 6 minutes.
Stir.
Microwave for additional 6 minutes.
May be served warm or cold.
Combine onions and butter in 3-quart microproof casserole. Cover.
Cook on High for 10 to 12 minutes or until onions are transparent, stirring once during cooking time.
Stir in remaining ingredients, except cheese.
Cook on High for 10 to 11 minutes or until hot.
Serve in bowls with cheese sprinkled on top.
Stir-fry zucchini and garlic in oil for 3 to 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Reduce to low heat.
Add parsley, margarine and half and half.
Cook until butter melts.
Add cheeses, linguine and oregano.
Serve.
In a small saucepan, combine all ingredients.
Cook and stir over low heat until hot.
Serve with vegetables, poultry, fish or eggs.
Makes 1/2 cup or 8 (1/2-tablespoon) servings.
Brown meat and onion together.
Stir in peas, corn and stewed tomatoes.
Add a dash of lemon pepper, black pepper or cayenne to taste.
When macaroni and cheese mix is ready, mix all together in a large skillet until heated through.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
In large pot, combine all, except cheese and chips.
Bring to a boil using medium heat.
(Can mash tomatoes, if desired.)
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; set aside.
In mixing bowl whip cream until soft and peaks form; gradually fold in sugar.
Combine water and extract; add alternately with flour mixture, gently folding ingredients together after each addition just until combined.
Fold in egg whites.
Spread into greased and wax paper-lined 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until cake tests done and is lightly browned.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.
Remove from pan; cool completely.
With fork, break cake into 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 inch pieces; set aside.
Melt butterscotch coating.
Add peanut butter; stir and melt. Stir in noodles and peanuts.
Drop into large candy cups and let set at room temperature.
To make sour milk mix about 1/2 teaspoon white vinegar to the 1 tablespoon of milk and let stand until curdles.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten egg and salt.
Add flour and bananas alternately.
Dissolve soda in little tepid water and mix with the sour milk.
Add to batter.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Bake in greased loaf pan very slowly at 250° for 1 hour and 25 minutes.
Brown 10 minutes more if needed.
Toothpick test and let stand overnight before use, having turned out to cool.
Mix together; put on cake and place under broiler a few minutes until brown.
Do not have to put under broiler, can just leave as is.
Cook chicken and shred into small pieces.
Put all ingredients in crock-pot or large pot and cook for approximately 2 1/2 hours on low to medium heat.
Serve over rice.
Sprinkle gelatin over milk.
Let stand 5 minutes, then heat until dissolved.
Separate eggs.
Beat egg whites to peaks.
Beat yolks in large bowl.
Pour gelatin mixture into egg yolks (slowly), then pour back into pan and add sugar.
Cook until custard coats spoon (8 to 12 minutes).
Add vanilla.
Pour custard over egg whites and cool.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Gradually add other ingredients, adding pecans last.
Lightly grease and flour 9x13 pan.
Spread mixture evenly.
Bake 30-35 minutes at 325°, or until toothpick inserted in middle comes out dry.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Mix salad dressing, whipped topping and sugar.
Pour over apple mixture and toss gently.
Combine all ingredients; stir well.
Cover and chill 3 hours. Serve with fresh vegetables.
Makes 2 cups.
Cream the sugar and shortening. Add cocoa, eggs and sour milk. Mix well. Add flour.
Mix. Add boiling water with baking soda and vanilla. Beat.
Go heavy on wet ingredients.
Light on dry ingredients. Bake 45 to 55 minutes at 350° in long pan or 8-inch.
Mix the first 5 ingredients.
Place mixture in loaf pan to chill thoroughly and cut into slices.
Roll in flour and brown quickly in frying pan.
Place fried slices in casserole.
Mix mushroom soup and 1 can of water; pour over meat.
Cover to bake. Bake 1 1/2 hours at 300°.
Combine juice, sugar and condensed milk; add whipped cream. Tear cake into small pieces and place in casserole dish or individual compotes.
Pour mixture over cake and blend together slightly.
Chill 24 hours before serving.
Pound cake can be used. Yield: 8 to 10 servings.
Cut broccoli in bite-size pieces.
Chop green onions.
Cut tomatoes in half.
Mix all ingredients in medium-size bowl.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Coat with mayonnaise.
Toss until well coated.
Mix ingredients in blender.
Pour into pie shells.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Prepare cake batter according to package directions; set aside.
In saucepan over low heat, melt peanut butter chips with milk, stirring constantly, until blended.
Add peanut butter mixture while warm to cake batter.
Beat on medium speed of electric mixer until blended, about 2 minutes.
Fill ice cream cone cup 2/3 to 3/4 full with batter.
Place upright in regular muffin cups or 2 inches apart on a cookie sheet.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until wooden pick inserted comes out clean.
Cool completely.
Frost as desired.
Decorate with chocolate or colored sprinkles.
Makes 24 cones.
Brown ground beef.
Cook noodles following box directions. While noodles are cooking, add pepper, onion and tomato soup to ground beef.
Simmer about 15 minutes.
When noodles are done, layer half of the noodles and half the ground beef.
Mix: 1/2 tomato wedges and 1/2 cheese.
Repeat with the remaining, ending with cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes, until cheese is melted.
Place 1/2 the lima beans in bottom of nonstick baking pan. Top with a layer of corn, then top the corn with 1/2 of the tomato slices, the onion and garlic.
Top with another layer of lima beans and corn; end with tomato slices.
Pour tomato juice over all.
Cover and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Brown beef
and
onion, then add all the other ingredients. Simmer for 1 hour.	Serve with a salad.
Brown bottom of pie shell slightly.
Cook broccoli according to package directions.
Saute mushrooms and onion in butter.
Beat egg slightly and mix with broccoli, mushrooms and onion.
Place mixture in cooked shell.
Place cheese slices on broccoli mix.
Mash yams or sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon butter and water in can and place on top of cheese and broccoli.
Cut top of pie crust in strips, lattice top.
Bake at 350° until top crust is brown.
Beat cheese until light and fluffy.
Blend in remaining ingredients.
Then chill.
Mix oil, vinegar and seasonings.
Simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
(If you increase, don't add more salt or poultry seasonings, but simmer longer.)
Marinade chicken overnight.
Grill over low heat until done.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Slice each potato length into 1/4-inch ovals, then slice each oval lengthwise into matchsticks.
Coat a baking sheet with 3 sprays of vegetable oil.
Combine egg whites and Cajun spice in a bowl.
Add the matchstick potatoes and mix to coat.
Pour the coated potatoes onto the prepared baking sheet and spread them out into single layer, leaving a little space between. Place the baking sheet on the bottom shelf of the oven.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the fries are crispy, turning them every 6 to 8 minutes with a spatula so that they brown evenly.
Serve immediately.
Brown hamburger and chop onion; drain.
Put in 8 x 8-inch casserole dish.
Add green beans and green pepper, if desired. Mix water and mushroom soup.
Pour over mixture.
Add a layer of cheese slices.
Place tatoes on top.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until tatoes are done and cheese is melted.
Melt
oleo
in
heavy
saucepan.
Stir
in brown sugar. Cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and add cornflakes, nuts and coconut.
Toss until well mixed.
Pour out on cookie sheet and cool thoroughly.
Crumble and serve over ice cream.
Bring the syrup of vinegar, sugar, salt, celery, mustard seed and turmeric to a boil.
Boil 5 minutes.
Pour over cucumber slices and seal.
Cook 5 minutes in hot water bath.
Combine milk and lemon juice; stir well.
Fold in pineapple and topping.
Spoon into pie shell and chill.

recipes.t: Aunt Betty'S Nephew'S Famous Spaghetti Sauce
d: Brown onion and garlic (cut up in 1/4-inch pieces).
Add ground meat and brown.
Add sauce and paste with 1 to 1 1/2 cans water; add sugar, salt and pepper.
Cook well and let simmer for two hours.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add frozen berries and break apart.
Break up angel food cake in jello mixture.
Mix slightly. (Cake will absorb juice and jello.)
Pour into a 13 x 9-inch pan and refrigerate.
Serve in squares, topped with whipped cream.
Cut loaf of Velveeta into slices and put in a large bowl. Saute vegetables in 1/4 cup of oleo until tender.
Add to cheese. Add 3/4 to 1 cup picante.
Place bowl in microwave and heat, stirring occasionally until melted to a medium consistency.
Serve with your favorite nacho chips.
Heat all ingredients in a Teflon skillet, uncovered.
Stir gently until well heated.
Makes dinner for one with a 4-ounce portion of limited vegetables (pea pods or bamboo shoots).
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water, then add pie filling and crushed pineapple with juice.
Cool Whip may be added, when set if desired.
Combine onion, mustard and water.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Wipe fish with damp cloth and arrange in baking dish.
Sprinkle with salt.
Combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, onion and mustard mixture and black pepper.
Pour mixture over fish.
Bake in preheated oven at 500° for 12 to 17 minutes or until done and lightly brown. Garnish with paprika.
Serves 6.
Place ingredients in order given in a large mixing bowl.
Beat with electric mixer; start on low speed, then move to medium and finish with about 10 minutes on high speed.
Batter should be smooth and liquid.
Grease and lightly flour a round baking pan 10 inches in diameter and 3 inches high.
Pour batter into pan; bake for 1 hour in preheated 350° oven.
Leave cake in oven, with door closed, for an additional hour after heat is turned off, then cool on rack.
Refrigerate for storage.
Makes 20 servings.
Lightly boil
first
ingredients until peas are soft (45 minutes).
Cool
a little and remove bay leaf.
Blend with remaining ingredients.
Return
to pan and simmer until thick. Stir occasionally.
Makes 1 quart.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook and drain pasta shells. Brown and drain ground beef.
Combine picante sauce, water, tomato sauce and taco seasoning.
Chop chilies and grate cheese. Stir 1/2 cup sauce into ground beef along with chilies, 1/2 cup cheese and 1/2 can fried onions.
Pour remaining sauce into bottom of 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Stuff cooked shells with ground mixture. Arrange shells in dish.
Pour remaining sauce over shells.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 25 minutes.
Top with remaining cheese and fried onions.
Bake, uncovered, for 5 minutes.
Cut off ends of bread and cut in half.
Spread with soup directly out of can.
Roll bread up like crescents.
Cut bacon in half.
Wrap a slice of bacon around each slice of bread.
Secure with toothpick.
Bake on foil lined cookie sheet at about 425° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix ingredients together and simmer until blended, about 2 hours.
Pour melted butter into jelly roll pan.
Combine flour, cheese, salt and pepper in plastic bag.
Drop in potato slices; shake to coat with flour mixture.
Place in a single layer over the butter.
Bake at 375° for about 30 minutes.
Turn slices; sprinkle with Italian seasoning.
Bake 30 minutes more, or until tender.
Line pan with foil.
Put onion, halved, and 2 cloves of garlic in pan on each side of roast with 1 inch of water.
Pile salt on top.
Bring water to a boil in a large saucepan and cook noodles. While noodles are cooking, melt the butter in a skillet.
Add the mushrooms and zucchini.
(It may be more convenient to use separate skillets for the mushrooms and zucchini.)
If possible, check
temperature of warm water with thermometer.
Sprinkle yeast over water in a large bowl; stir until dissolved.
Stir in sugar and salt until dissolved.
Add eggs, squash, 1/2 cup softened butter and 3 cups flour.
Separate 1 egg and beat until frothy.
Brush pie shells with white, but do not saturate.
Bake pie shells.
Brown sausage and drain.
Cook broccoli according to package and drain.
Combine whipping cream, Velveeta and Cheddar cheese and microwave 3 to 4 minutes.
Beat eggs and combine with cheese mixture.
Combine all ingredients in a 1-quart casserole dish.
Cover. Microwave 10 to 12 minutes on High or until water is absorbed. Fluff with fork.
Mix eggs, cornmeal, milk, oil, soda, salt and corn.
Place half of mixture in skillet or pan that has been sprayed with Pam. Top with ground beef, onions, grated cheese and jalapeno peppers. Put remaining cornbread mixture on top.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes at 375°.
Cook spaghetti according directions; drain.
Should have approximately 3 cups of spaghetti.
Add the Parmesan cheese and eggs.
Pat spaghetti mixture into a buttered, 10-inch pie plate to make crust.
Saute onion in 1 tablespoon of butter.
Blend in flour. Gradually add milk.
Stir constantly until thickened.
Add cheese. Stir until melted.
Stir in corn and 1/4 cup bread crumbs.
Arrange broccoli in an 11 3/4 x 7 1/2-inch dish.
Pour cheese sauce over broccoli.
Toss remaining crumbs and butter over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 8.
Let cheese set to reach room temperature.
Beat cheese until creamy, add remaining ingredients.
Roll into small balls.
Serve with toothpick.
Saute onion in butter.
Add hamburger, salt and pepper, heating through but not browning.
Spread half the shredded cabbage in a 2-quart baking dish.
Cover with meat mixture.
Top with remaining cabbage.
Pour undiluted tomato soup over top; stir.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 6.
Saute cabbage, peppers and onion together until transparent. Add oleo and zucchini.
Saute until transparent.

In 4-quart pot, add chunked potatoes and onion. Cover with water and cook. Stir all other ingredients together in pot, warming slightly to blend well. Add to potatoes and onions and water. Heat slowly, stirring often. Add milk if it's too thick. Refrigerate leftovers (5 to 7 days).
Bring to a boil sugar, water and pineapple.
Remove from heat. Dissolve Jell-O into mixture.
Chill until slightly thickened. Add cheese, milk and pecans.
Stir well.
Chill until set.
Melt butter in a large skillet.
Add coconut and chopped pecans.
Cook until golden brown, stirring frequently.
Set aside. Combine cream cheese and sweetened condensed milk.
Beat until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Layer 1/4 of the cream cheese mixture in each shell.
Drizzle 1/4 topping on each pie.
Sprinkle 1/4 of the coconut mixture over each.
Repeat layers.
Freeze.
Remove from freezer about 30 minutes before serving.
Additional caramel sauce may be served with the pie.
If making individual serving pies, will make approximately 36.
Beat eggs in large bowl; stir in remaining ingredients except pastry shell.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake in 400° oven for 15 minutes; reduce heat to 350° and continue to bake 35 to 45 minutes longer.
Filling will be moist in center.
Cool.
This kitchen-tested recipe makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients and shape into a ball.
Roll cheese ball into the reserved chopped beef.
Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Beat together cream cheese and 1 teaspoon vanilla until soft and fluffy.
Stir in nuts; set aside.
Cut bread into 10 to 12 (1 1/2-inch) slices.
Cut pocket in top of each.
Fill with 1 1/2 tablespoons cheese mixture.
Beat together eggs, whipped cream, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and nutmeg.
Dip bread slices into egg mixture. Cook until golden.
Heat together orange juice and preserves; drizzle over toast when done.
Combine Jell-O with 2 cups boiling water.
Add undrained pineapple and let cool.
Whip cream cheese.
Add to Cool Whip; add sugar, then blend with Jell-O mixture.
Pour into large pan.
Add marshmallows and nuts.
Let chill thoroughly.
Brown beef; drain.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, uncovered, at 400°.
Stir once during baking. This freezes well.
Use 3 small or 2 large pans.
Cream together margarine, eggs, sugar and red food coloring.
Sift together cocoa, flour, salt and cinnamon.
Have buttermilk and vanilla ready.
Mix all ingredients, alternating 3 mixtures, until all are used and mixture is smooth and velvety.
Stir in vinegar and soda.
Pour into prepared pans.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes and test for doneness.
Cake is bright red.
Serves 24.
Blend together the cheese, butter, paprika and salt.
Stir in flour.
Chill dough for easier handling.
Wrap a small piece of dough around each olive, sealing well.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake in 400° oven for 15 minutes or until lightly browned. Serve warm.
Makes 24.
Melt ingredients together, mixing well.
Stir in a large jar of dry roasted peanuts.
Stir well and drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Seal jars.
Process 5 minutes in boiling water.
Remove from water immediately after 5 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°.
In 10-inch skillet, brown ground beef, onion and garlic and drain.
Return beef mixture to skillet and stir in Ragu and water.

In 13 x 9-inch baking dish, layer 1/3 sauce mixture, 1/2 of uncooked lasagna noodles, 1/2 of combined Ricotta or cottage cheese and 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese and parsley. Repeat these steps in layers, ending with sauce on top. (Everything will be 1/2, except sauce and it will be thirds in order to end up with enough to cover the top lightly.)
(I add Monterey Jack cheese to mine, optional.)
Cook for 1 hour tightly covered with aluminum foil.
Let set 10 minutes before serving.
Cook broccoli and set aside.
Saute onion and celery in butter.
Add soup and heat.
Then add Cheez Whiz.
Add cooked rice and salt and pepper to taste (and dash of Tabasco, if desired). Layer chicken, broccoli and rice mixture in casserole dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° until hot, 30 to 40 minutes. Serves 6.
Heat oven to 350°.
Generously grease and flour 2 round pans. Drain peaches, reserving sauce.
Add enough water to reserved sauce to measure 1 1/4 cups.
Prepare cake mix as directed on package, except substitute sauce mixture for water.
Pour batter into pans.
Bake and cool as directed on package.

recipes.t: Ham And Swiss Cheese Finger Sandwiches
d: *Deli ham and cheese work best for this recipe, but are not required.
The ham should be sliced "sandwich thick."

Place first 3 ingredients in a double boiler. Cook over hot water until thick. Then add 1/2 to 1 cup of hot water to the cooked milk and chocolate. Add the butter and the vanilla. Serve hot or cold over ice cream or use as fillings for cakes. Makes 2 cups.
Brown hamburger with salt, pepper, brown sugar and onion.
Add tomato soup.
Cook egg noodles and drain.
Add chicken soup. Layer hamburger mixture and noodle mixture in casserole dish with processed cheese between layers.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Heat oil in a heavy saucepan and brown the beef cubes until deeply colored.
Remove from pan and brown sliced onions until golden brown.
Return beef cubes to pan and add beef bouillon and dry red wine.
Simmer until beef cubes are almost tender.
Add small onions and cook until tender.
Add mushrooms and heat through; adjust seasonings.
Mix cornstarch and water, add to beef stock and boil for one minute, or until sauce is thickened and clear.
Serve with rice or noodles.
Place potatoes in bottom of greased casserole.
Add celery, beef, onions and peppers.
Salt and pepper each layer.
Pour tomatoes over mixture.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot water.
Add 1 cup cold water.
Add strawberries, pineapple and bananas.
Mix well.
Pour half into container and chill until firm.
Spread sour cream over Jell-O and add remaining Jell-O and chill.
Cook Boston butt in crock-pot for about 4 1/2 hours on high until tender.
After it cooks, trim off fat.
Cut in chunks and put in food grinder.
Use 1 cup of stock and cut up potatoes, chopped onion and a little more water to cover potatoes.
Cook until tender but not mushy.
To this, add meat, tomatoes, corn, hot sauce, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for a while.
Mix graham cracker crumbs and 1 stick melted butter.
Press into bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cream eggs, 2 sticks butter, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Beat with mixer approximately 15 minutes.
Spread over crumbs.
Slice bananas over mixture.
Cover with large container of Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with chopped pecans. Decorate with cherry halves.
Cover and chill overnight.
Slice tomato in thin wedges.
Slice onion also in thin wedges, using as much or as little as you want. Add salt and pepper and toss lightly.
Set in refrigerator for at least 1/2 hour.
Pour dressing to taste just before serving.
Wash okra, trim and drain.
Place in shallow dish.
Pour buttermilk over okra, set aside.
Combine next 5 ingredients, mixing well.
Remove okra from buttermilk and carefully roll in cornmeal mixture.
Drop into hot oil (375°).
Fry 3 to 5 minutes, turning and browning on all sides.
Drain on paper towels.
Brown hamburger, then drain grease off.
Place back on heat and add other ingredients, continually stirring.
May add ketchup and brown sugar to taste.
Add chili powder to taste, also.
Cook on low to medium heat for 30 minutes, then serve hot.
Add dry gelatin to cream cheese and combine.
Add boiling water, celery and pineapple.
Fold in whipped topping.
Pour into square baking dish and refrigerate until cold and firm.
Put flour, salt and cut up chicken in brown sack.
Close tightly and shake chicken pieces good.
Fry in hot shortening or oil of your choice.
When browned, remove to paper towel on platter.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Dip each piece of chicken into sauce while hot.
Then place in roasting pan.
Leave open. Bake for 20 minutes in 375° oven.
Cook squash and drain.
Melt 1/2 stick margarine in dish. Reserve 1/2 cup crumbs with the rest of margarine to sprinkle over the top of casserole.
Mix all other ingredients in dish with margarine.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Boil noodles in salt water until tender.
Drain very dry.
Put in large bowl.
Melt butter in hot noodles.
Add 9 beaten eggs. Add both cans of fruit with juice.
Add vanilla, sugar, raisins and orange juice.
Put 3 tablespoons butter in 2 (9 x 12-inch) baking pans.
When butter is melted, in a 350° oven, divide the mixture between the 2 pans and bake 1 hour at 325° or until slightly brown.
Can divide recipe in half.
In large mixer bowl combine 1 1/2 cups flour, yeast, wheat germ and salt, mix well.
Add water, molasses, shortening and egg. Beat 3 minutes at medium speed.
By hand gradually stir in remaining flour to make a stiff batter.
Cover.
Let rise in warm place until light, about 45 minutes.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes until deep brown.
Remove from pan, cool.
Line 10 x 13-inch pan with crust mixture, pressing firmly to bottom and sides.
Put sugar, milk and corn syrup into saucepan.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture begins to boil.
Clip a candy thermometer to side of pan.
Cook for about 12 minutes or until mixture reaches 234°, soft ball stage.
Remove from heat.
Add butter and almond extract.
Beat until fudge begins to thicken. Quickly stir in walnuts and cherries.
Beat until fudge is no longer glossy.
Score into squares while warm.
Brown hamburger; add other ingredients.
Season to taste. Cook until cabbage is done.
Mix all ingredients, except 1/3 cup catsup.
Pack into loaf pan; spread catsup over loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Spread the chiles in the bottom of a greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Cover with cheese.
Combine eggs, cream and pepper and mix well. Pour over cheese.
In large skillet put oil and brown ground beef.
Stir in soup mix, beans, catsup, water, mustard and vinegar.
Simmer until ready to eat.
Combine milk, sugar, yolks, butter and vanilla.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add nuts and coconut.
Beat until cool.
Melt 1 stick margarine in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix sugar, flour, baking powder, salt and milk.
Pour into pan with butter or margarine.
Pour fruit over top of batter.
Do not stir!
Bake at 350` for 30 to 45 minutes.
Sprinkle chicken with salt.
Brown in butter in skillet. Remove chicken and butter into large baking dish.
Mix apples with chicken.
Sprinkle with sugar and nuts.
Add cider; cover.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Serve with mound of steamed rice.
Cook broccoli until almost tender.
Put well drained broccoli in greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Mix flour, salt, baking powder and shortening; mix in milk. Roll out dough in rectangle.
Spread with apples and sprinkle with a little cinnamon and sugar.
Roll up like jelly roll and slice about 1 1/4 inch thick.
Place in 9 X 13 pan.
Boil sugar, water, cinnamon and butter.
Pour over dumplings.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream.

Cream granulated sugar and shortening. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Sift flour, baking powder and salt together. Add the mixture alternately with buttermilk or sour milk. Add coconut extract and flaked coconut. Place in a greased and floured tube pan (a 2 piece pan works best). Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes. Remove from oven. While still hot, punch holes in cake and slowly pour the glaze over cake, allowing it to seep into holes and down sides and middle. Cool thoroughly before removing from pan. Cake will cut better if allowed to firm up overnight.
Combine all ingredients and simmer until done.
More water can be added, if too thick.
In buttered casserole dish, place thinly sliced onions, potato chips and grated cheese.
Do this in layers.
Pour over mushroom soup and milk.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix ingredients.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch dish.
Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Mix and chill. Serve with crackers.
Slice potatoes; put in ovenware dish.
Mix sugar, flour and salt; sprinkle over potatoes.
Mix lemon juice and water; pour over top.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes covered.
Brown the beef, onion and garlic.
Drain the grease.
Add cream cheese and melt into the meat mixture.
Add the other ingredients.
Serve warm in a crock-pot or fondue pot with corn chips.
Grease pan.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Sprinkle chopped pecans in bottom of pan.
Combine cake mix, eggs, oil and water. Mix for 2 minutes until smooth.
Add icing to batter; mix well and pour into pan on top of pecans.
Bake at 350° for 55 minutes or until brown.
Mix all ingredients together, except chicken and cheese.
Pour over top of chicken.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Remove from oven; sprinkle cheese on top.
Return to oven and bake until cheese melts.
Combine corn, onion, cheese, soups and sour cream.
Place in a greased 8 1/4 x 4 1/4-inch or 9 x 5-inch casserole dish.
Mix together crackers, almonds and melted margarine.
Spread topping over vegetable mix.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
May be made ahead and refrigerated.
Broil skinless breast of chicken until done.
When cooled, cube chicken into bite sizes.
Layer Tater Tots in the bottom of a greased casserole dish and add cubed chicken.
Mix soups and milk and pour oven chicken and Tater Tots.
Sprinkle cheese over top. Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
In a large bowl, mix all ingredients (except pecans).
When batter is smooth and sugar is dissolved, add pecans.
Bake in two 9x9 pans for 40 minutes at 350°.
(I line the bottom of pans with wax paper and grease and flour sides.)
Melt butter.
Stir in peanut butter, graham crackers and powdered sugar.
Pat in cookie sheet.
Pick beans and cover with cold water.
Soak 1 to 2 hours. Pour off water and rinse beans.
Add all ingredients.
Cover beans with cold water and simmer until tender.
Pour into baking dish. Bake at 375° until crusty on top.
Enjoy!
Spray oblong pan
with	nonstick spray.
Put cherry and pineapple in pan
and
mix with each other.
Sprinkle dry cake mix evenly over
this
mixture.
Cut up margarine all over the top of this.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes until brown on top.
Place ingredients in springroll shells according to package diagram.
Deep fry with temperature of 140° to 150°.
Turn on both sides, ready when golden brown in color.
Blot excess oil before serving.
Mix all ingredients and marinate overnight.
Remove meat from juice and dehydrate.
If you do not have a dehydrator, place in oven on 140° with oven door cracked open so meat will dry out without being cooked.
If meat is thin enough, it should dry out overnight.
Melt margarine in a large, nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add chicken and onion; cook, stirring constantly, 3 to 5 minutes, or until chicken is browned.
Add mushrooms; cook 1 minute.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add milk and next 4 ingredients.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Cut each slice of toasted bread into 4 triangles.
Serve chicken mixture with 4 toast triangles; sprinkle with paprika.
Crush graham crackers, 1 stick butter and sugar. Mix.
Put in a square dish.
Beat powdered sugar, egg and butter at medium speed for 15 minutes.
Put on top of crumb mix.
Slice bananas.
Put on top. Put drained pineapple between bananas. Put Cool Whip onto that. Put nuts and cherries.
Set overnight.
In pitcher, combine pineapple juice, tomato juice, sugar and hot pepper sauce; blend well.
Pour over ice cubes in glass. Squeeze lime juice into each drink, if desired.
Garnish with dried red pepper, ripe olive and lime peel.
Makes 4 servings.
Marinate chicken in egg at least 1 hour.
Roll in bread crumbs and brown in butter.
Place in baking dish.
Top with mushrooms, then cover with cheese; add chicken broth.
Bake at 350°, covered, for 30 minutes. Remove cover and bake 30 to 40 minutes more.
Make cake mix according to directions only at the part for water add 3/4 cup lemon juice and the rest water (this is what makes your cake moist).
Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Place on round cake plate, cool.
Heat 1-inch salted water to boiling. Add broccoli (or cauliflower).
Cover and heat to boiling.
Cook until stems are almost tender (10 to 12 minutes). Drain.
Place broccoli (or cauliflower) in ungreased 1 1/2-quart round casserole dish.
In Dutch oven, cook hamburger with garlic and seasoned salt until brown; drain.
Add onion, celery and dill weed.
Add water (just enough to cover ingredients).
Cover and simmer for at least 2 hours.
Add water if needed.
Add potatoes, along with more water, to cover ingredients.
Cook until potatoes are tender (not mushy).
Add milk; stir and skim off fat.
Great with French bread and butter.

recipes.t: Pasta And Ricotta Stuffed Red Peppers
d: Chop the onion.
Mince the garlic.
Grate the Mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cut tops off peppers.
Remove the seeds and ribs.
Cook peppers in a pot of boiling salted water just until soft, about 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Note:
Allow butter, eggs and milk to get room temperature.
Cut corn from cob and scrape cob; set aside.
Melt butter in large skillet.
Add chopped onion and cover. Stir once or twice until onion is translucent.
Add corn and milk if corn is dry. Cover and heat through.
Season to taste.
Sprinkle with cheese if desired.
Spread refried beans in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Brown meat and remove from heat.
Add taco mix, enchilada sauce and taco sauce.
Mix well and pour over beans.
Spread cheese on top.
Heat in 400° oven 15 to 20 minutes or until bubbly.
Spread sour cream over cheese and return to oven for 5 minutes.
Use spoon to dip and serve with nacho chips.
Cut up Velveeta cheese in small pieces,
Add Chili Con Carne, salsa and canned chilies.
Unwrap and cut up the tamales in bite size.
Mix all ingredients well and place in a deep dish and bake for 30 -35 minutes in a 350° oven.
Serve with chips or crackers.

Heat skillet; add oil. Mix all the rest of ingredients and dump into skillet. Pack down in skillet. Lower heat. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes. Turn when golden brown and cook other side. Invert onto plate. Garnish with parsley. Serve with broiled meat.
Mix together cake mix, eggs and fruit pie filling.
Spread in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with mixture of butter, flour and brown sugar.
It should be crumbly.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
