Sweeten blueberries to taste and place in melted butter.
Cover with crushed pineapple (do not drain).
Pour cake mix on top of this mixture (do not stir).
Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Serve with ice cream or whipped topping.
Flour meat and season with salt and pepper.
Brown in butter. Place meat in casserole dish. Cook onions until tender but not brown; add soup, milk and mushrooms.
Heat to boiling.
Pour over steak.
Bake, covered, at 325° for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until tender.
Mix cream cheese and crabmeat thoroughly.
Shape into ball or log in serving dish.
Chill until ready to serve. At serving time, pour cocktail sauce over seafood ball and sprinkle top with parsley flakes.
Serve with Triscuits or crackers.
Brown beef in shortening on top of stove.
Add remainder of ingredients. Simmer 1 hour until tender. Serve over or with cooked white rice.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Cool.
Add evaporated milk.
Chill until slightly set.
Blend mayonnaise and softened cream cheese.
Add to thickened Jell-O mixture.
Drain pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Add fruits to Jell-O mixture.
Pour into mold.
Does well in Tupperware mold.
Cut chicken breasts in one-inch pieces.
Marinate in lemon juice, oil, oregano, salt and garlic.
Unwrap phyllo dough; place on wax paper and keep covered to keep moist.
Cut dough in half lengthwise forming 2 strips each 6-inches wide.
Fold in half crosswise; brush with melted butter.
Put two pieces of chicken at short end and roll; form a package.
Brush with melted butter and bake at 400° for about 15 minutes.
Cut snapping turtle meat into steaks (thick as possible) and batter down with hands.
Saute in butter and season to taste. Serve with jelly or appropriate sauce.
Heat oven to 350°.
Blend cake mix, pie filling and eggs in a large mixing bowl.
Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Combine sugar and cinnamon.
Spread half cake mixture in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle with 1/2 sugar mixture.
Repeat with remaining batter and sugar mixture.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cream oleo, oil and sugars.
Add beaten egg and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients, oatmeal, Rice Krispies and coconut; mix well. Roll into balls from tablespoon.
Flatten with glass dipped in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 9 to 10 minutes on a greased cookie sheet.
Melt 1/4 pound butter in each of 2 skillets.
In one, brown the bread cubes until crisp.
In the other, stir-fry onions and celery until soft and translucent.
Mash the potatoes, adding the milk, eggs, salt and parsley.
Fold in the celery and onion mixture and the bread cubes carefully so the cubes remain whole. Pour into a large baking dish and bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
Combine cream cheese and honey, mixing until well blended. Stir in nuts.
Chill.
Great for topping pumpkin muffins!
Mix in order given and bring to boil. Simmer 15 minutes. Pack into sterilized jars and seal at once.
Combine kraut, onion, parsley and seed in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan. Top with 2 cups cheese and 2/3 cup dressing.
Layer beef slices. Add rest of cheese and dressing.
Toss bread cubes with margarine and spread on top.
Bake in 375° oven for 35 minutes.
In large bowl, tear bread into dime size pieces.
Mix both turkey and hamburger with bread.
Add all remaining ingredients except 1/2 cup Worcestershire and 1 stick margarine or butter. Make into patties.
Melt butter or margarine in large frying pan; add 1/2 cup Worcestershire on medium to medium-low heat; fry slowly covered, approximately 10 to 15 minutes each side or until no longer red in middle.
Let sausage and cheese stand at room temperature before making.
Mix together with Bisquick and sauce.
Form into small balls and place on ungreased pans and bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Cool and freeze.
Reheat before serving.
Cook butter and sugar over low heat until bubbly.
Cool and add eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly.
Add vanilla and cream, then sifted dry ingredients and coconut.
Mix thoroughly.
Nuts may be added.
Spread in shallow pan (greased) and bake at 350° for about 25 minutes.
While warm, cut in squares.
Beat butter, sugars, vanilla, water and eggs until light and fluffy.
Mix flour with soda and salt; blend into butter mixture. Stir in nuts and chips.
Drop 2 inches apart from teaspoon onto greased baking sheets or pour onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes, or until golden brown.
In large shallow baking dish, add shrimp to all other ingredients.
Bake at 450° for 5 minutes.
Turn to broil for additional 5 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Cook zucchini and onion in boiling salted water for 5 minutes; drain well.
Mix sour cream, soup, carrots, garlic and Tabasco sauce; set aside.
Combine stuffing and melted margarine.
Put half of this crumb mixture in 8 x 11-inch or 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Add the zucchini to the sour cream and soup mixture; pour over crumbs.
Cover with remaining crumbs.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook fettucine in salted water to desired doneness.
Drain and rinse with hot water.
In large skillet melt margarine; saute onion and garlic until tender.
Add shrimp and saute 2 to 3 minutes. Remove shrimp from skillet; keep warm.
Add 2 tablespoons margarine and whipping cream to skillet; heat until margarine melts.
Stir in cheese, salt and pepper.
In large saucepan combine fettucine, broccoli, and cream mixture; cook until thoroughly heated.
Place on warm serving platter; spoon shrimp over top.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Soak beans 4 to 8 hours, then cook by bringing to a boil. Simmer until done.
Cook rice by instructions on bag.
Cook beans with coriander, cumin and garlic.
Place beans in a large casserole dish.
Add rice, then chopped tomatoes with juice.
Add cheese and olives.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown the meat, onions and garlic.
Drain off excess fat.
Add the 2 cans of soup and a small amount of water, bring to boil and let simmer while cooking the macaroni shells.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add flour, liquid from asparagus and cream of asparagus soup; heat until creamy.
Combine milk and cornstarch; add this to mixture and cook until thickened.
In casserole dish, layer with 1/2 of the English peas and 1/2 the asparagus, then covered with half of thickened sauce and repeat with remaining peas, asparagus and sauce.
Top with grated cheese and bake at 350° until heated throughout and cheese is melted, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Watch closely.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Cool to lukewarm.
Whip cheese until soft and fluffy.
Beat in sugar and peanut butter. Slowly add gelatin mixture.
Fold in whipped topping.
Pour into pie shell.
Sprinkle with peanuts until firm.
Refrigerate and leave 1 to 2 hours.
I always do overnight as the longer, the better the flavor.
Yields:
6 to 8 servings.
Blend these ingredients and pour over vegetables.
Refrigerate and marinate 48 hours.
(Shake or stir occasionally.)
Keeps for several days.
Beat cheese until smooth; gradually beat in sugar.
Blend in sour cream and vanilla.
Fold in whipped topping.
Blend well. Spoon into crust.
Chill until set, at least 4 hours.
Garnish with fresh strawberries.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients.
Mix well.
In a large, shallow baking dish, shape into a loaf.
Bake 1 hour.
Cook tortillas in oil.
Fill with chicken, onions and cheese.
For syrup, bring to boil the sugar and water; add cranberries and cook until they pop.
Dissolve Jell-O with 2 cups boiling water.
Add to Jell-O the cooked berries, pineapple and nuts.
Put in refrigerator to jell.
Cook first four ingredients until thickened.
Then add last four items.
Mix together gently.
Pour into pie crust.
Top with whipped cream.
Makes 2 pies.
Mix Jell-O in water. Let it dissolve, then add all other ingredients. Mix well. Put in refrigerator and let it jell.
Mix all ingredients (except coconut) well with mixer.
Add coconut and mix with spoon.
Pour into oven baking dish.
Top with topping.
Drain canned beans.
Combine beans, mushroom soup, milk, bacon bits, salt and pepper.
Turn mixture into a 1-quart casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with French fried onions.
Continue baking about 5 minutes.
Mix flour, baking soda, cream of tartar and salt together and set aside.
Mix together sugars, margarine and almond extract. Stir in oil and eggs.
Mix with electric mixer until well mixed. Add flour mixture one cup at a time.
Use electric mixer until mixture becomes very thick, finish mixing with a wooden spoon. Chill dough.
Roll chilled dough into walnut-sized balls.
Place on cookie sheet.
Press with fork or a tumbler dipped in sugar.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Red Snapper With Honey Mustard Sauce
d: Rinse fish and pat dry.
Place in a baking dish.
Combine first 7 ingredients.
Stir with a wire whisk until well blended.
Pour mixture over fish, cover and marinate 30 minutes to an hour in refrigerator.
Remove fish from marinade.
Coat grill with vegetable spray and grill fish over hot coals or broil 6 minutes on each side or until fish flakes.
Baste with extra marinade.
Spray Bundt pan with Pam.
Sprinkle a few nuts in bottom of pan.
Stand up biscuits in circle of pan.
Mix Jell-O pudding mix, brown sugar and nuts.
Sprinkle mix over and between biscuits. Pour the melted butter or oleo over top and bake at 350° for 30 or 35 minutes.
Turn out onto plate and serve while warm.
Heat oven to 300°.
Melt butter, salt and hot sauce.
Add pecans.
Stir to coat.
Bake 20 minutes, stirring every 2 to 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with the Worcestershire sauce.
Combine softened cream cheese or margarine, mixing until well blended.
Add flour; mix well.
Shape into ball; chill.
Cut sausage links in half crosswise.
Simmer in water 2 minutes; drain.
Cool.
Divide dough in half.
On lightly floured surface, roll out each half to 12-inch square.
Cut each square into 16 (3 x 3-inch) pieces.
Spread each piece with mustard to within 1/2 inch of edge.
Roll around sausage half; seal ends.
Dip each roll in seed.
Place seam-side down on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly browned.
Blend flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and shortening like pie crust.
Add milk and mix thoroughly until forms a soft dough. On a floured surface, pat dough, then roll out to a rectangular shape with 1/4-inch to 1/2-inch thickness.
Spread softened margarine over the dough.
Sprinkle cinnamon, sugar, apples, and more cinnamon and sugar.
Roll up like a jelly roll.
Cut in 2-inch slices and place in 9 x 13-inch pan (sprayed).
Pour Syrup (recipe follows) over slices.
Bake at 425° for 30 minutes or tops are golden brown and center is firm.
Serve warm or cold.
Combine first five ingredients.
Then add the liquids.
Stir well.
Pour into 9 x 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon uncooked oatmeal over top of batter.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 17 minutes for chewy brownies.
Yields 16 pieces.
Has 68 calories.
Exchange:
1 starch.
Mix all the ingredients together.
Grease a 9-inch glass pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or more.
Check for doneness. You can double this recipe.
Cook until mixture has some thickness; cool.
Add all kinds of fruit (canned or fresh).
Also you can add nuts or coconut.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
In a medium bowl, beat egg.
Add sour cream, Parmesan cheese and garlic powder.
Drain spaghetti.
Add to egg mixture with cheese, spinach and half of onions.
Pour into a greased 2-quart baking dish. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining onions. Return to oven for 5 minutes.

Boil potatoes until soft, then drain. In the meantime, brown beef and onion. Mix in beans and soup and add salt and pepper to taste. Spread meat mix in a Dutch oven. Mash potatoes and mix in milk, eggs, salt and pepper to taste. Spread mashed potatoes on top of meat mix, leaving edges open for bubbling. Bake at 350° for approximately 30 minutes until top browns.
In a skillet, brown the ground beef and drain.
Stir in 1/2 cup salsa.
Spread 1/4 cup salsa in a glass baking dish.
Top with 3 or 4 taco shells.
Top with half of each:
beans, meat mixture, sour cream and cheese.
Repeat layers; cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with lettuce and remaining salsa.
This dish will serve 6 to 8 people.
Cook potatoes and turnips in boiling salt water to cover in 3-quart covered saucepan over medium heat, about 20 minutes. Drain.
Return to pan.
Shake pan over low heat a few seconds to dry.
Mash vegetables.
Add remaining ingredients.
Beat with fork until fluffy.
Mix all together.
Refrigerate for 24 hours.
Cook hamburger, onion, celery and green pepper in bacon grease until brown. Drain hamburger (if needed).
Add other ingredients and cook 2 hours at 350°.
Mix sugar and margarine well.
Mix together dry ingredients and add.
Mix until well blended.
Put in a bread tin and bake in a preheated 300° oven for 1 hour.
Cook beef and green peppers in electric skillet until done. Add both cans of soup, water and soy sauce. Stir until celery soup is thinned out. Simmer. Pour over rice.
Heat skillet until almost smoking.
Turn burner down to low. Mix 1 to 1 1/2 cups corn meal mix, milk and egg.
May also add chopped onion and/or sour cream.
Add water if needed to make batter thin like cake batter.
Pour into hot skillet and place lid on.
Then turn batter and let cook.
Crack lid to let the steam out so cornbread will not be soggy.
One bag of self-rising corn meal is used.
Thoroughly cream shortening, sugars, eggs and vanilla.
Stir in peanut butter.
Sift dry ingredients and stir into creamed mixture.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls on ungreased cookie sheet. Press with back of floured fork to make crisscross.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Blend butter with flour.
Add tomato soup and sour cream.
Cook spinach with onion according to package directions.
Line baking dish with this mixture.
Cover with raw rice, then crab meat and add sauce.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° until thoroughly hot and cheese melts, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Season to taste. Serves 4 to 6.
Melt butter.
Fry onions in butter, then add flour.
Stir and add milk.
In separate pan, boil water and add bouillon cube.
Add to first mixture.
Cube potatoes and mix with green beans.
Pour cream sauce over both.
Bring to a boil the sugar, oil, vinegar and salt.
Add remaining ingredients and let stand 12 to 24 hours in refrigerator.
Will keep for days.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Add remaining ingredients.
Chill for several hours or until firm.
Cook all together until tender.
Process for 5 minutes in water bath cooker.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease 2-quart casserole.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
Brown meat and drain.
Put into casserole and mix in 1/2 can of onions.
Prepare gravy mix according to package directions, except increase water to 1 1/4 cups.
When thickened, add 1/2 cup sour cream, mixing well.
Drain noodles.
Return to pan.
Pour and stir in the gravy mixture. Spread this over the meat/onions in casserole.
To remaining sour cream, add egg and seasoned salt, mixing well with a fork.
Pour over noodles, making sure all are covered.
Bake for 25 minutes, uncovered.
Top with remaining onions and bake 5 minutes more. Serves 4 to 6.
Pierce chuck roast; cover with meat tenderizer and pepper well. Mix marinade of vegetable oil, ketchup, vinegar with garlic and a few shakes of Worcestershire sauce.
Cover roast and marinate at least 12 hours.
Grill and baste with marinade.
Roast has better texture when room temperature before grilling.
Melt lard in heavy pot.
Add hamburger, salt, pepper and chili powder.
Chop onion fine and add.
Stir in tomato juice.
Let cook 1 hour or until thick as desired.
Cream butter, then sift sugar.
Add to butter a little at time, until all is used.
Then add egg yolks, beaten until light. Add flour gradually and last add beaten egg whites.
Fold whites in lightly.
Pour into a greased loaf pan or tube cake pan and bake 45 minutes in a moderate oven.
Do not open oven door until cake has been in oven 40 minutes.
A pan of water in bottom of stove helps.

recipes.t: Honey Baked Sweet Potatoes(Over 50 Years Old)
d: Place potatoes in a baking dish.
Combine butter and honey and pour over potatoes in a hot (400°) oven, 15 to 20 minutes, basting frequently.
Wipe ribs with wet towel or with damp cloth.
Place ribs in a single layer in a shallow roasting pan. Roast ribs at 450° for about 20 minutes, turning once.
Bake crusts with pecans on top; cool.
Cream the cream cheese with 2 cups powdered sugar.
Put a layer in each crust.
Beat Dream Whip (2 envelopes) with cold milk.
Put a layer in each crust.
Divide pie filling on each pie.
Garnish with remaining Dream Whip.
On English muffin, spread chili sauce, add a slice of cheese, a slice of bacon and season with poultry seasoning.
Broil in oven approximately 7 minutes.
Boil chicken and cut in bite size pieces. Chop onion and saute in butter in large skillet. Add green chilies, soup and water. Mix and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.

In medium sized bowl, beat cream cheese until light and fluffy. Gradually add sweetened condensed milk and stir until well blended. Stir in lemon juice and vanilla. Turn into crust. Refrigerate (not freeze) 2 to 3 hours. Garnish with chilled cherry pie filling before serving.
Combine the first 7 ingredients.
Make a dressing with the remaining ingredients.
Pour over salad.
Needs to set in refrigerator at least overnight.
Will keep up to 6 weeks.
Mix cream cheese and Miracle Whip.
Add other ingredients. Chill.
Serve with crackers.
Mash cheese and crisco; cream well. Add flour and salt; Mix well. Roll into small balls; chill 1 hour. Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Balls will flatten as they cook.
Cook until thick when dropped in cold water.
Beat all the time.
Add the Marshmallow Fluff after removing from fire.
Beat until thick.
Pour over nuts.
Bake cake mix as directed on package.
Cool.
Beat whipping cream and powdered sugar in a chilled bowl until stiff.
Fold in cherries, juice and nuts.
Frost cake.
Refrigerate.
Blend cream cheese into hot potatoes.
Beat and add eggs and chopped onion.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Serves 12.
Cut meat into 1/4-inch strips.
Works better if meat is a little frozen.
Mix ingredients.
Marinate strips of meat overnight, mixing once or twice. Turn oven on to slowest temperature. Dry on oven rack for 3 or more hours or until meat is dark and cracks when it is bent.
Remove and cool.
Store in airtight container.
Cut tenderloin lengthwise to within 1/2 inch of opposite edge, leaving edge intact.
Open tenderloin out flat.
Place heavy-duty plastic wrap on tenderloin; pound meat to flatten.
Remove wrap. Spread mustard; sprinkle sage, green peppercorns and 1/2 tablespoon each of black and white ground peppercorns.
Fold tenderloin back over and tie with string at 3-inch intervals. Spread butter on top of tenderloin; sprinkle rest of peppercorns. Place on rack.
Can bake at 425° for 30 to 45 minutes, or until meat thermometer inserted at thickest part of meat reads 140° for rare, 150° for medium or 160° for well done.
Can also cook on gas grill.
Serves 8.
Cream butter and Crisco with sugars.
Add eggs, one at a time. Add flour, soda and powder.
Mix well.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
(It's okay if they are light in color.)
Grease cookie sheets first time only and drop in small/medium sized clusters.
Cream together the butter and sugar.
Add eggs.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Sift together the flour and soda.
Add alternately to creamed mixture with 1/2 cup of lemonade.
Drop from teaspoon onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for about 8 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove from baking sheet.

Beat cream cheese, margarine, milk and vanilla in medium bowl with electric mixer on low speed until smooth. Gradually beat in powdered sugar on low speed, one cup at a time, until smooth. Frosts 1 (13 x 9-inch) cake generously or fills and frosts one 8 or 9-inch (2-layer) cake.
Stir topping, rum and cinnamon in 12-inch skillet.
Quarter bananas by cutting in half lengthwise and crosswise.
Cut again in half lengthwise to form 8 pieces per banana.
Add bananas to topping mixture; heat thoroughly.
Mix together and stir well.
Pour into ovenproof dish. Sprinkle generously with Mexican style Velveeta on top.
Cook at 350°, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes more.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook lasagna noodles and cool.
Brown ground beef with garlic salt and pepper.
Add mushrooms, onion and green pepper.
Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Mix well.
Can use a blender.
Mix all together by hand or electric mixer (mixer is faster and more thorough).
Bake in loaf pans (greased), one pound coffee cans or other cans.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 1 hour. Springs back to touch when done.
Brown pork chops in skillet.
Season with salt and pepper. Blend soup, sour cream, water and parsley.
Fry sausage until done.
Drain.
Add other ingredients.
Mix well.
Shape into loaf and put in loaf pan or on baking sheet. Keep drained. Bake at 375° until done.
Combine first 7 ingredients.
Pour into buttered 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Combine corn flakes (or Chex) with melted 1/4 cup butter; top casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Poke holes in cake.
Pour crushed pineapple with juice over cake and spread evenly.
Make pudding and spread over pineapple. Slice bananas and place over pudding mixture.
Spread Cool Whip over bananas, and sprinkle with coconut.
Shred cheese.
Add crackers and pimento.
Mix dry mustard, sugar and eggs.
Add milk.
Add vinegar very slowly.
Cook over medium heat until thick.
Add cheese mixture; stir well.
Bake in cheese ring or baking dish at 350° for 1 hour.
In 9-inch round or fluted microwavable dish, place water and butter.
Cook covered on High 3 minutes or until butter melts. Stir in stuffing crumbs and 1/2 can onions.
Press stuffing mixture into dish as above.
Reduce milk to 1/2 cup.
In large microwave bowl, combine soup, milk, turkey and peas.
Cook covered 8 minutes.
Stir turkey mixture halfway through cooking time. Pour turkey mixture into stuffing shell.
Cook uncovered 4 to 6 minutes.
Rotate dish halfway through cooking time.
Top with remaining onions; cook uncovered 1 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Mix milk, potatoes and butter.
Mix together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and soda.
Mix all together.
Turn onto a floured board; knead 30 seconds.
Roll 1/2-inch thick and cut with biscuit cutter.
Bake in a 425° oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
In a large kettle, combine strawberries, rhubarb, sugar and pineapple.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat;
stir in gelatin until dissolved. Pour into jars or frozen containers, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Top with lids; refrigerate or freeze.

recipes.t: Peanut Butter Play Dough(Play Dough You Can Eat.)
d: Mix all ingredients until smooth.
Let kids make critters of their choice out of the mixture.
Decorate with peanuts, raisins, chocolate chips or coconut and eat.
In a large bowl, beat together oleo, brown sugar, eggs, flour and milk.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Turn off oven and leave pie in for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Bake pastry shell 5 minutes.
Mix ingredients; pour into pastry shell.
Bake 45 minutes.
Let stand 10 to 12 minutes until firm before cutting into wedges.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix all ingredients except meat in pan and bring to boil.
Add the hamburger meat.
Crumble until well mixed with other ingredients.
Boil 10 minutes, then simmer 20 minutes.
Serve on hot toasted buns.
Mix together and form into a loaf.
Place in a pan (loaf) and pour on can of Campbell's tomato soup over it.
Bake 1 hour in oven at 375°.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place into a baking dish with cover.
Top with Mozzarella cheese and bake 20 minutes at moderate heat.
Serve hot.
Mix dry ingredients.
Cream butter and gradually add dry ingredients.
Mix and chill 1 hour.
Roll into balls and place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press with finger.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes in a 350° oven.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Mix soup, 1/4 c. milk, pepper, vegetables and chicken in 9 inch pie plate.
Mix remaining milk, egg and baking mix.
Pour over chicken mixture.
Bake until golden brown.
Melt chocolate and margarine.
Set aside.
In large bowl with mixer, beat 4 eggs and 2 cups sugar.
Add chocolate to margarine mixture and mix well.
Gradually add flour.
Add vanilla and 1 cup chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Allow cheese to soften at room temperature.
Blend all ingredients together until smooth (except nuts).
Chill for 2 hours.
Shape into a ball and roll in chopped nuts.
Refrigerate.
In an 8 x 8-inch pan, put your spinach or green beans on bottom, then pour the can of cream of mushroom soup over the top of the spinach or green beans.
Sprinkle the top with the dried onions.
Bake about 30 minutes at 350°.
In a small, chilled bowl, whip cream until almost stiff. Gently fold in the yogurt and vanilla.
Chill in a covered container at least 2 hours to allow flavors to blend.
Use as a topping for berries, other fruits and desserts.
Combine cranberries, marshmallows and sugar together.
Chill overnight.
Add apples, grapes, walnuts and salt.
Add cream to mixture when ready to serve.
Melt margarine in jelly roll pan at 325°.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Add sugar and salt; beat into meringue.
Fold in nuts and spread over melted butter in pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes, turning with a spatula occasionally until all butter is absorbed.
Cool.
Store in airtight container.

Drain juice from fruit and measure 4 cups juice. Pour juice into pan. Add the dry jello, dry pudding mix and tapioca. Cook until thick. Let cool completely. Pour over fruit in large bowl. Will keep in refrigerator up to 3 weeks.
Mix together in casserole dish.
Keep enough cheese to top. Sprinkle with parsley and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes or until it bubbles up in the middle.
If potatoes start to look dry, cover to finish baking.
Chop garlic and brown in skillet with olive oil.
Shuck clams, reserving the juice.
Chop clams and add to garlic and oil.
Cook for 3 minutes.
Add parsley and pepper; simmer for 5 minutes. Serve over freshly cooked linguini.
Brown rice in oil until golden brown.
Add onion and garlic. Saute.
Next add tomato sauce, water, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then lower to the lowest heat possible for 20 minutes. Turn off heat and keep covered for 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix pudding and milk until it starts to thicken, then add the cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Layer in dish:
wafers, bananas and filling.
Top with Cool Whip.
Mix butter and flour, then add cream.
Roll out and cut in strips.
Shape in figures of an 8.
Brush with egg white and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes, checking often.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine butter/margarine, confectioners sugar, 2 cups flour and salt.
Mix with a pastry blender or two knives until mixture is well blended.
Pat evenly into a 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan and bake 20 minutes.
Beat eggs lightly. Stir in granulated sugar, 6 tablespoons flour, lime juice and rind. Mix well and spread over baked crust.
Bake 25 minutes longer. Remove from oven and sift confectioners sugar over the top.
Let cool and cut into squares.
Drain pineapple well.
Melt butter in pan (9-inch round or 8 or 9-inch square).
Remove from heat and stir in brown sugar. Arrange pineapple and cherries in sugar mixture.
Prepare crumb cake and pour over all in pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes until tests done.
Fit the steel knife into the work bowl of a food processor. Combine flour, orange juice, mustard, baking powder, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Process 10 seconds, until well mixed.
Pour batter into a deep bowl.
Cut bread and ham into 1/2 inch cubes. Place a cube of bread, a cube of pineapple and a cube of ham on wooden pick.
Repeat to make 30 appetizers.
Pour oil into a large deep skillet to the depth of 2 inches.
Heat oil to 325°.
Dip each appetizer into batter to coat completely.
Carefully lower wooden picks into hot oil.
Deep fry for about 5 minutes, until golden brown.
Serve warm.
Yield:
30 appetizers.
Carbohydrate 15 g, protein 3 g, fat 2 g, calories 82 g.
Line baking pan with silver foil.
Melt butter, honey and mustard.
Stir in salt and curry powder.
Brush on chicken before and during baking.
Bake 1 to 1 1/4 hours at 350°.
Mix shortening and sugar until creamy.
Add egg, cloves and apple butter.
Sift in flour with baking powder, soda and cinnamon. Add raisins.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake in 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes.
Sprinkle chicken with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Mix mustard, yogurt and sour cream in a bowl.
Dip chicken in mixture and cover with mixture.
Place dipped chicken breasts in baking pan.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Makes 4 servings.
Chop cabbage fine.
Add chopped green pepper, onion and shredded carrots.
Whip cream until stiff.
Add sugar, pineapple, vanilla and marshmallows (gently).
Add food coloring last.
Chill very thoroughly before serving.
Amount: 6 to 8 servings.
Mash cheese and blend in sour cream, onion and pepper to taste. Cut a slice from top of tomatoes and scoop out centers.
Fill tomato shells with cheese mixture.
Makes 3 to 4 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°. Mix ingredients in a large bowl in the order given, adding water last. Stir only until moistened. Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan sprayed with Pam.
Bake for 30 minutes. Cool on rack.
Serve with chilled peaches and whipped topping or ice cream.
Boil potatoes; cool and peel.
Melt the margarine and quarter the potatoes.
Put into shallow baking dish and pour the margarine over them.
Turn each section of potato to coat with margarine well.
Sprinkle with minced onion and seasoned salt.
Top generously with Parmesan cheese and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Grease 13 x 9 pan. Mix first 3 ingredients and set aside. Combine cake mixture and rhubarb mixture; pour into cake pan. Pour marshmallows on top. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown meat; add salt, pepper to taste and kidney beans. Simmer 15 minutes.
Cool.
Add rest of ingredients.
Doritos and lettuce when serving.
Wash potatoes; cut into wedges or 3/4-inch chunk slices. Drain.
Place in a bowl; sprinkle with oil and toss lightly. Combine spices and cheese.
In a separate bowl, put half of the potatoes in.
Sprinkle half of the spice mixture over and toss lightly.
After placing these potatoes in a single layer on a lightly oiled 10 x 15-inch pan, sprinkle spices over the remaining potatoes.
Bake at 425° to 450° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Blend well in blender.
Serve over fresh vegetable salad.
In large skillet, brown sausage; drain off excess fat.
Add bell pepper and onion; cook until tender.
Stir in tomatoes and tomato sauce (cut up the tomatoes with fork).
Add sugar, salt and chili powder.
Mix.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Cook large shell macaroni according to directions on package; drain thoroughly.
Add cooked shell macaroni to sauce.
Stir in sour cream; heat thoroughly.
Pass the grated Parmesan cheese.
Mix and let stand for 1 hour or longer.
Add milk to soup.
Heat to boiling.
Add onion, cheese, salt and pepper.
Arrange alternate layers of soup mixture and cooked potatoes in buttered casserole dish.
Sprinkle corn flakes on top. Melted brown butter may be added to the top.
Bake at 350°
for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix chicken, sour cream, enchilada sauce, green chiles and chicken broth in pan and heat.
Fry tortillas until softened. Layer in shallow pan the sauce, tortillas and onion and top with cheese.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Put nuts in mixture and coat.
Spread nuts on baking sheet and bake in 250° oven for 1 hour.
Turn nuts every 15 minutes.
Simmer broccoli, onion and butter until soft.
Add soup and cheese.
Mix well.
Add rice.
Mix well.
Bake at 350° until real hot and brown.
Line two large cookie sheets with wax paper.
In top of double boiler, combine marshmallows, butter or margarine, vanilla and food coloring.
Heat over boiling water, stirring frequently, until marshmallows are melted.
Gradually stir in cornflakes. Drop by rounded, greased teaspoonfuls onto lined cookie sheets. Shape into 2-inch wreaths.
Decorate with red candies.
Store between layers of wax paper in refrigerator.
Makes about 2 1/2 dozen, about 60 calories each.
Mix cream cheese and confectioners sugar; add whipped topping and strawberries and mix well by hand.
Put in crust and garnish with strawberries.
Chill.
Mix well.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Spread bean dip in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix lemon juice, avocado, garlic salt, sour cream, mayonnaise and taco seasoning together.
Spread on top of bean dip.
Layer tomatoes, onions and cheese dip.
Top with black olives.
Mix well the oil, sugar, vanilla and eggs.
Then add flour, soda and apple pie spice.
Mix well.
Last, add apples and nuts. Mix well.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Mix ingredients thoroughly until smooth.
Form into 2 balls and roll in chopped nuts.
Chill 2 hours.
Mix water, oil and pudding mix. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Blend with cake mix and poppy seed.
Place in a Bundt pan, greased and floured or sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Allow to cool in pan for 15 minutes.
Mix sugar, oil and water.
Add cake mix, instant chocolate pudding, eggs, and sour cream.
Mix well.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Pour into a greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Cool in pan a few minutes and then turn out onto serving plate.
Either sprinkle with powdered sugar or ice immediately while still hot with Chocolate Frosting.
Mix soups, milk, sour cream, seasonings and hash browns.
Pour into a 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Boil water, sugar, cloves and cinnamon for 5 minutes in 4 to 6 quart pot.
Add remaining ingredients and bring to boil and let simmer for 30 minutes.
Makes 1 gallon.
Cut cookie dough into 1/8-inch slices.
Arrange cookie slices slightly overlapping on foil covered 14-inch pizza pan.
Press edges to seal.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cool and remove from foil onto serving plate.
Combine cheese, sugar and vanilla, mixing well.
Spread over crust; arrange fruit on cream cheese mixture.
