Cook over low heat for 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Cut chicken into serving pieces.
Soak pieces in buttermilk overnight in refrigerator.
Drain.
The next day, dip in flour, salt and pepper.
Fry as usual.
Mix together; beat until smooth.
Bake at 450° until done.
Combine cake mix, shortening, eggs and water in a large bowl; blend
thoroughly.
Stir
in oats and raisins.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls
onto
ungreased
cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix Cool Whip, sour cream and sugar; add all other ingredients.
Freeze.
Take out 1 hour before serving.
Put rice in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and place chicken on top of it.
Mix together the water and cream of mushroom soup.
Pour over the chicken.
Sprinkle with onion soup mix; cover with foil and bake at 350° for about an hour.
Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.

Butter bottom of 9 X 13 pan. Spread pie filling evenly over bottom of pan. Sprinkle cake mix evenly over top of filling. Sprinkle nuts and butter over top. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes. When completely cooled, spread with cool whip. Keep refrigerated.
In a large saucepan, bring margarine or butter and 3/4 cup water to boiling, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Add baking bar; stir until melted.
Stir in buttermilk, eggs and rum extract; set aside.
Sir together 1/2 cup of the flour and the pecans; set aside.
In an extra bowl, stir together remaining 3 cups flour, sugar, coconut, soda and powder.
Stir in margarine mixture.
Fold in coconut mixture.
Stir in margarine mixture. Fold in pecan mixture.
Boil chicken
until tender; debone and cut into pieces.
Mix chicken,
soup, green chilies, and sour cream together.
Mix all ingredients with enough mayonnaise to hold together (not too much).
Spread evenly over bread or buns.
Place under broiler until melted.
Place drained peas on bottom of 9 x 12-inch casserole dish. Spread chicken over this.
Make sauce of soup, mayonnaise and water.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle on almonds.
Tear bread into small pieces and place on top.
Drizzle melted margarine over bread.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Beat yolks and whites separately.
Add 1/2 cup sugar to yolks while beating.
Add 1/4 cup sugar to whites after beaten stiff. Mix yolks and whites, add milk, whipped cream, whiskey and rum. Let set for at least 2 hours.
Stir before serving.

In a large bowl, combine the first nine ingredients. Beat egg yolks; stir into potato mixture. In a small mixing bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form; gently fold into potato mixture. Transfer to a 2-qt. souffle dish coated with nonstick cooking spray. Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 40 - 45 minutes or until golden. Serve immediately.
Wash eggplant; cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
In 1/2 cup hot oil in large skillet, saute eggplant until tender and golden brown. Remove eggplant and set aside.
In 2 tablespoons hot oil in same skillet, saute onion and celery until tender, about 5 minutes. Return eggplant to skillet.
Stir in tomato sauce; bring to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes.
Add vinegar, sugar, capers, salt, pepper and olives.
Simmer, covered, and stirring occasionally, 20 minutes longer.
Refrigerate eggplant mixture, covered, overnight.
Heat oven to 325°.
Mix in saucepan 1 cup brown sugar, water and butter.
Boil 5 minutes.
Pour into 9-inch square pan.
Mix in bowl 1 cup brown sugar, milk, Bisquick, raisins, nuts and vanilla. Spoon batter on top of mixture.
It will sink into liquid and spread as it bakes.
Bake 45 minutes.
Serve warm, plain or with whipped cream.
This recipe serves 9.
Heat oven to 400°.
Put chilies evenly in greased 8-inch square pan.
Sprinkle cheese over chilies.
Pour eggs over cheese and bake until firm in center, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Place on wire rack and cool 5 minutes.
Cut into bite size pieces. Delicious served on crackers.
Melt almond bark.
Add all other ingredients.
Drop on wax paper.
This is a flat bread.
Sift flour and salt, adding 2 tablespoons oil and 2/3 cup water.
Stir to form a ball.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 3 minutes.
Divide into 12 equal pieces and form into balls.
Roll into circles 6 to 7-inches; keep covered.
Heat a cast-iron skillet and cook in ungreased skillet 1 minute on each side.
Stack and cover with towel.
Serve immediately.
Mix all the ingredients together, except cornflakes.
Pour into baking dish and top with crushed cornflakes.
Melt 1/2 stick oleo and pour over slivered almonds on top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Delicious with cooked rice.
Mix chicken and eggs together; put in bottom of casserole dish.
Mix broth and soup together; pour over chicken.
Mix flour, milk and melted margarine; pour over casserole.
Do not mix.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix eggs, milk, salt and mustard.
Blend well.
Pour in an 8 x 12-inch greased casserole.
Add bread crumbs, sausage and cheese. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine raisins, water and baking soda.
Let stand overnight (10 to 14 hours).
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix by hand with spoon.
Grease cans (not too large) and fill each can 1/2 full. Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Let cool in cans, when cool, remove from cans.
Wrap in plastic wrap or freeze.
You may use soup cans or any other size you wish.
Mix all ingredients together well and spoon onto cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together in a casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Grate cheese.
Mix in other ingredients.
(Black pepper, garlic and mayonnaise are used to your taste.)
Cream together oleo and sugar.
Add eggs, beating well after each.
Mix together the remaining ingredients and stir in.
Bake in greased and floured Bundt pan for 1 hour at 325°.
Make in large frying pan.
Put soup, water and rice in pan. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add all ingredients except onion rings, and simmer 10 minutes.
Heat onion rings in oven.
Dish up chicken hot dish into serving bowl and put onion rings on top.
Saute onions with margarine in large skillet for 15 to 20 minutes on medium heat.
Place half of onions in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with half of crackers and half of Parmesan cheese.
Repeat with remaining ingredients.
Bake, uncovered, in a 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Brown onions in 2 tablespoons oil.
Add meat and seasoning. Heat until meat loses color.
Put in casserole dish over green beans.
Add tomato soup.
Top with mashed potatoes.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.
Mix all ingredients; pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
More spices can be added to taste.
Pans should not be over 1/2 full.
Melt butter and beat eggs.
Drain the whole kernel corn. Combine all ingredients together, adding the muffin mix last.
Pour mixture into a greased 7 X 11-inch baking dish.
Bake ate 375 degrees for 35-40 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cook the pasta (macaroni, twists or shells) and drain.
In large bowl, stir together mayonnaise, parsley, cheese and lemon juice until blended.
Add pasta, beans, peas and carrots; toss to coat well.
Cover and refrigerate until well chilled.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Beat in salad dressing with mixer.
Stir in cottage cheese and add salt.
Chill until thick and syrupy.
Fold in peas, radishes, green peppers and onion. Pour into lightly oiled mold.
Chill until set.
Prepare instant pudding according to package directions.
Fold in half the whipped topping while pudding is still soft.
Spread 1/2 of bread cubes in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Mix chicken, celery, onion and mayonnaise and spread over cubes. Cover with remaining cubes.
Combine eggs and milk and pour over top.
Let stand overnight, refrigerated.
Mix soup and 1/2 can of milk and pour over top before baking.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Sprinkle cheese over top for last 10 minutes of baking.
Cook noodles per package directions.
Rinse under cold water. Add remaining ingredients and toss gently.
Mix stuffing and butter together.
Press half of mixture in lightly greased 9 x 13-inch baker.
Mix the remaining ingredients together and pour over stuffing.
Sprinkle remaining stuffing on top.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Melt chocolate in water over double boiler until chocolate melts; cool.
Sift flour, soda and salt; set aside.
Beat egg yolks with sour cream, adding sugar gradually, and beat vigorously until thick.
Add chocolate mixture and vanilla mixing well.
Add flour, soda and salt to sour cream mixture.
Beat until smooth. Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Bake in paper lined 13 x 9 1/2 x 2-inch pan at 350° for 45 minutes.
Frost with chocolate butter cream frosting.
Mix together and let congeal.
Heat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease jelly roll pan.
Mix oleo, sugar and egg yolk.
Blend in flour and cinnamon.
Pat into pan. Beat egg white and water; brush over dough.
Sprinkle with nuts. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cut immediately into strips.
Mix sugar and oil; add eggs and crushed pineapple.
Beat well. Mix dry ingredients together and add to other mixture.
Add carrots and pecans and beat well.
Bake in three 9-inch greased and floured pans about 40 minutes at 350°.
Wash and cut rhubarb into small 1-inch pieces.
Beat egg; add lemon juice, sugar and flour.
Mix together and pour over chopped rhubarb.
Stir until well coated.
Pour into unbaked 9-inch pie crust.
Dot with oleo.
Cover with top crust.
Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar and prick holes with fork.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes and then at 350° for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Boil shredded cabbage for 7 minutes. Grate the cheese.
Make white sauce with the margarine, flour, milk and salt.
Line buttered 13 x 9-inch baking dish with finely crushed potato chips. Add 1/2 of the cooked cabbage, 1/2 of the white sauce mix and sliced hard-boiled eggs.
Spread 1/3 cup grated cheese over mixture. Repeat steps, ending with the remaining chips. Bake at 325° for 40 minutes.
Cream together margarine and sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Mix together the berries, sour cream and nuts.
Add alternately the dry ingredients to the liquid ingredients.
Grease and flour loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until done.
Makes 3 loaves.
Drain olives; save liquid.
In small saucepan, combine 1 cup olive liquid, chili powder, garlic, bay leaves, olive oil, pepper and onion.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat; simmer 5 minutes, uncovered.
Stir in pimientos.
Place olives in a large jar; pour seasoning mixture over.
Cover.
Refrigerate.
Make at least 3 to 4 days prior to serving.
Makes about 3 cups.
Mix wafers and butter and spread in a 13 x 9-inch pan. Arrange sliced bananas over crust.
Beat together milk and lemon juice until thick.
Add sour cream.
Pour over bananas.
Mix together pineapple and Cool Whip and spread over sour cream mixture.
Sprinkle with pecans, coconut and cherries.
Refrigerate 24 hours.
Place onions in skillet; add sugar, mustard, garlic salt, salt and vinegar.
Cook 20 minutes, covered.
Add onion mixture to beans.
Add bacon.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serves 12.
This fills a 3-quart casserole.
If you have difficulty finding yellow rice, use white rice.
Prepare spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
In medium skillet, cook sausage until no longer pink.
Drain, reserving 2 tablespoons drippings.
Add cabbage, onion, apple and garlic.
Stir-fry just until tender.
Stir in next 4 ingredients. Add spaghetti.
Cook and stir until hot.
Remove from heat.
Add cheeses; toss to mix.
Arrange on warm serving platter.
Garnish as desired.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Mix together meat, egg, bread crumbs, salt and pepper.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Simmer catsup, water and cookie crumbs for 5 minutes.
Add brown sugar, salt and sauerkraut.
Heat to boiling. Add meatballs; lower heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Chop tomatoes, peppers and onions fine.
Boil all together slowly, then add spices and sugar and boil 3 to 4 hours.
Bottle and seal while hot.
*You can use half ground beef and half sausage.
In a mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time,
beating well after each addition.
Beat in vanilla. Combine flour and cocoa; add to creamed mixture just until combined.
Stir in walnuts.
Spread into an ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Bake at 350° for 23-28 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Butter a 13 x 9-inch Pyrex dish.
Line with graham crackers (not crushed).
Mix together pudding and milk.
Fold in Cool Whip. Pour half of this mixture over graham crackers.
Place another layer of graham crackers over this and pour rest of the pudding mixture over crackers.
Lay a third layer of graham crackers on top.
Frost top layer with Fudge Frosting and let set all day or night in refrigerator.

Heat oven to 375°. Grease 1 1/2-quart casserole dish. Toast bread; crumble and mix with butter. Combine cheese and soup. Heat slightly to melt cheese. Add almonds. Place half the asparagus in prepared dish. Cover with slices of 1 egg and half of the soup mixture. Repeat layer. Sprinkle buttered bread crumbs over all. Bake until bubbly and browned, about 30 minutes.
Cook broccoli in boiling water just enough to separate.
In bowl, combine soup, mayonnaise, beaten eggs, onion and salt and pepper to taste.
Pour this into broccoli, mixing well.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Melt margarine and mix into stuffing; sprinkle on top of broccoli mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine cream cheese and 1/2 cup milk, beating on low speed until well blended.
Add remaining milk and pudding mix.
Beat on low speed 1 minute.
Layer wafers, bananas and pudding mix until all used, ending with top layer of pudding.
Cover with a layer of Dream Whip.
Serves 8 to 10.
Place chicken in shallow pan and pour other ingredients over chicken.
Cook covered in oven at 375° for 1 hour.

Heat enough oil in a skillet to cover the bottom. Salt tenderloins. Dredge in flour. Lightly brown both sides in oil. Pour off some of the oil before next step. Generously sprinkle tenderloins with lemon pepper seasoning. Mix soup and 1/2 can of hot water and pour over tenderloins. Sprinkle with a little more lemon pepper seasoning. Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes. Serve with rice or mashed potatoes.
Brown in skillet walnuts, Ramen noodles, butter, and almond slices.

Set aside and cool. In a large salad bowl, combine broccoli, romaine lettuce, chopped green onions. Mix together oil, sugar or Splenda, vinegar, soy sauce, and salt and pepper to make dressing. To romaine mixture add nut mixture and toss.
Pour dressing over salad mixture and toss.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Prepare cake as directed on box. Combine water, orange juice and food coloring.
Add grated orange peel; mix.
Bake and cool as directed on box.
In a large bowl, combine water, yeast, sugar and salt.
Stir until dissolved.
Add flour (dough will be wet).
Place dough onto floured platter.
Place each chicken breast in the center of a 12-inch square piece of aluminum foil.
Fold sides of foil up so the lemon juice won't run out.
Halve the lemons and squeeze the juice of 1/2 lemon over each chicken breast, then sprinkle each with 1/4 teaspoon tarragon and black pepper.
(I also add 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of wine, poured over each piece of chicken.)
Fold foil together and seal well.
Bake wrapped chicken in shallow baking dish at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt butter.
Add onion and garlic.
Cook and stir 5 minutes or until onion is transparent. Stir in oregano and sausage and cook about 5 minutes more.
Stir in potatoes, salt and pepper until potatoes are well coated with butter.
Place mixture in slow cooker.
Cover and cook on High 3 to 4 hours or on low for 6 to 8 hours, stirring every hour if possible.
During last 30 minutes of cooking, add cabbage and peppers.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese before serving.
Makes 6 side dish servings or 4 main dish servings.
Blend all ingredients well. Pour into greased pie tin.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 8.
Brown
ground
beef in a large skillet.
Drain.
Mix in can of	tomato	sauce,	corn,
green
beans, new potatoes and spices. Let simmer on stove for 30 to 45 minutes.
Serve with corn bread.
Mix the crumbs, butter and seasonings.
Sprinkle a layer of crumb mixture 1/2 inch thick in the bottom of a buttered baking dish.
Cover with oysters.
Add a little milk, then a layer of crumb mixture.
Repeat until all the mixture has been used.
Be sure a layer of crumbs is on top.
Bake 35 minutes in a moderate oven.
Mix all and shape into 1-inch balls.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 11 minutes on ungreased baking sheets.
"Do not overcook."
Cool on wire rack.
Makes 3 1/2 dozen.
Drain pineapple and save syrup.
Combine the syrup with the jelly or preserves, ketchup, cloves, cinnamon and salt.
Heat to boiling.
Mix all ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Place in ice cream churn to freeze.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sift the dry ingredients and add to the cream mixture, mixing well.
Fold in the mashed bananas, vanilla and walnuts.
Pour into the prepared pan.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 2 minutes, then invert on a rack.

Spread pineapple in a lightly buttered 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; sprinkle with cake mix, blueberries and sugar. Drizzle with butter and top with pecans. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Put onions and oil into 3-quart casserole. Cover tightly and microwave on High for 2 to 3 minutes. Wash rice briefly in a sieve under cold, running water; drain well.
Add to onions in a casserole along with rest of ingredients, except almonds. Cover tightly
and microwave on High for 7 minutes; stir.
Cover and microwave until liquid is almost absorbed, 8 to 10 minutes longer. Stir. Cover and let stand 10 minutes.
Stir again and top with almonds.
Combine first 4 ingredients in small bowl; spread on 1 slice of bread.
Top with remaining bread to form a sandwich.
In small bowl, beat egg with water.
Transfer to small, shallow pan and soak sandwich, turning occasionally, for 10 minutes or until all egg is absorbed.
Melt margarine in small skillet; add sandwich. Cook until bottom is golden brown; turn and brown other side.
Top with strawberry spread and serve.
Serves 1.
Bring vegetables, spices, sugar and vinegar to a boil and fill 10 pint jars.
Seal.
The liquid that you drain off can be put in tomato juice if making it the next day.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with 1/4 cup of the graham cracker crumbs.
Beat egg whites, water and milk to stiff peaks.
Add egg yolks, lemon zest and lemon juice; beat 1 minute, gradually adding sugar.
Spoon into pie plate.
Sprinkle remaining crumbs over top. Freeze at least 2 hours.
Leave cream cheese at room temperature. Mix with onions that are chopped real fine.
Cut up corn beef with scissors and mix in. Add Accent and Worcestershire sauce.
Roll ball in chopped pecans.
Refrigerate.
Mix sugar and cornstarch.
Gradually add milk, stirring until smooth.
Add eggs, corn, butter and salt.
Mix well.
Pour into greased 1-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Place in pan of hot water.
Bake at 300° for 1 3/4 hours.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
*Choose any 1 vegetable or combine several.
Vegetables should total 1 pound before cooking.
Cut the vegetables into chunks.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix all ingredients in shallow baking pan in a single layer.
Bake for 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden brown, stirring occasionally.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook hamburger, bell peppers and onion.
Add cheese.
Add to meal, corn, oil, milk and salt.
Mix all together and bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes or until brown.
*The more celery, peppers and onions the better.
Mix sugar and syrup and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter mix.
Add cornflakes and stir until all are coated with syrup mixture.
Drop by teaspoon into wax paper.
Cool and serve.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs, one at a time.
Dissolve soda in milk; add flour alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture.
Roll nuts, candy and dates in extra flour, then add coconut.
Add to cake batter.
Bake in tube pan at 250° for 2 1/2 hours.
Mix 2 cups white sugar, and 1 cup orange juice; pour on cake while hot.
Store cake in pan overnight.
Can also bake in loaf pans.
Drain squash and combine all other ingredients.
Set aside enough stuffing or topping.
Bake in casserole dish 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Butter two large cookie sheets.
Beat egg whites and cream of tartar until soft peaks form.
Add sugar, 2 tablespoons at a time, beating constantly until stiff and glossy.
Fold in vanilla, nuts and chocolate chips.
Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto a buttered cookie sheet.
Put in preheated oven, then turn oven off.
Leave in oven for several hours or overnight until crisp.
Sprinkle tenderloins with salt and pepper.
Brown in skillet in butter about 5 minutes per side.
Remove.
Cook onion and celery in same skillet until tender; add more butter if needed. Remove.
Add flour and 1 Tbsp. butter to skillet.
Stir over medium heat until paste forms.
Add chicken broth to skillet. Bring to boil, stirring constantly.
Stir in celery and onion. Layer rice in casserole.
Layer chicken pieces over rice.
Pour thickened celery broth over meat.
Cover and bake for 1 hour in 350° oven.
Put cabbage and onions in large bowl.
Heat remaining ingredients in saucepan, bringing to a boil.
Pour over cabbage and onions; toss.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cook chicken and have noodles cooked and drained.
Melt butter. Blend in flour and seasonings.
Add broth.
Cook, stirring until thickened.
Stir in mushroom soup, chicken and stuffing mix.
Add cooked noodles and mix.
Bake at 350° about 20 minutes or until bubbles.
Spread brown sugar in pie crust; sprinkle with flour.
Pour milk over it.
Dot with margarine.
Do not stir.
Sprinkle pie with cinnamon or allspice.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes until set.

Press 1 package rolls in 9 x 13 greased pan. Beat cream cheese, 1 cup powdered sugar and flavoring until smooth. Smooth cream cheese mixture over rolls. Cover with the other package of rolls. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, Cheddar, onion, mayonnaise and Worcestershire sauce.
Spread on bread that has been cut lengthwise.
Add ham and roast beef slices.
Mix all ingredients in a large stockpot.
Cook at high temperature for half an hour; then simmer for an additional hour.
Brown chops in little portion of bacon drippings.
On top of each chop, place 1 small onion (sliced) and 1 lemon (sliced) and salt and pepper.
Mix and pour over chops: tomato soup and water. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray a loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda and cinnamon and set aside.
In a larger bowl, whisk together applesauce, sugar, egg whites, banana and vanilla.
Add flour mixture all at once and stir gently to blend.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake 50 to 60 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Cool bread completely.
Combine all ingredients.
Let stand for 20 minutes in greased loaf pan.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In small bowl, beat butter, orange peel and orange juice until well blended. Refrigerate to chill.
Pour boiling water over dates and 1 teaspoon baking soda; let cool.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten eggs, then add cooled mixture.
Sift together the flour and 1/4 teaspoon soda; add to creamed mixture.
Mix well.
Pour into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan that has been greased and floured.
Mix the last 3 ingredients; spread on top of cake.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cook pasta until tender.
Drain.
Shake together vinegar, olive oil, salt, pepper and Parmesan cheese.
Mix together remaining ingredients; add pasta and pour dressing over, tossing to coat.
Chill.
Mix together pie filling and almond flavoring in microwave-safe dish.
Cook on High 3 to 4 minutes until bubbly. Sprinkle on top of sauce
the cake mix, then slice butter or margarine on top.
Combine pecans, cinnamon and nutmeg. Sprinkle over sliced butter. Cook on High 12 to 13 minutes or until cake is firm.
Brown together, onions, pepper and celery.
Pour off grease. Add remaining ingredients and bake in casserole 1 hour at 350° or until thick.
Cream shortening and sugars in a large mixing bowl.
Add flour and crumble together.
Set aside 1 cup of this mixture.
Mix eggs, salt, soda and yogurt together in small mixing bowl.
Add this to the sugar mixture and combine (seems better if not completely smooth) and pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan. Bake about 40 minutes at 350°.
Sift in large mixing bowl the flour and sugar.
In a saucepan, put cocoa, cold water, oleo and shortening.
Bring to a boil. Pour over flour and sugar; add eggs, buttermilk, soda, cinnamon and vanilla.
Bake in large 11 x 17-inch pan at 350° for 20 minutes or less.
Combine orange and onion in a large shallow dish.
Pour vinegar over mixture and toss.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Cover and refrigerate 4 hours; stir occasionally.
Toss gently.
Serve over mixed greens using slotted spoon.
Makes 3 servings.
Cook noodles per directions and set aside.
Melt butter and saute onion and sausage 8 to 10 minutes.
Add cabbage and saute 5 minutes. Stir in caraway seed, salt and pepper.
Stir in noodles and sour cream.
Heat through 5 to 10 minutes.
Brown steak on both sides in oil in frying pan.
Combine salt, pepper, dry mustard, minced onion, water and vinegar and pour over steak.
Cover tightly and cook about 1 1/2 hours over low heat. Drain orange sections and pineapple chunks, reserving 3 tablespoons liquid and blend in brown sugar and cornstarch.
Put steak on platter to keep warm.
Put fruit and sugar mixture in pan with drippings and cook 2 or 3 minutes.
Pour over meat and serve.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a loaf pan.
Soak apricots in warm water for 30 minutes.
Cream butter, sugar and eggs well. Stir in orange juice.
Combine dry ingredients and add to egg mixture.
Drain apricots well.
Add with nuts to batter.
Bake approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Tips:
Use more carrots (makes sweeter) or garlic or oregano if you like more herbs; whatever you desire, it's always good.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Use a 2-quart casserole dish, greased. Combine ham, rice, peas, 1/2 cup cheese, salt, pepper and cayenne. Spoon into casserole dish.
Add remaining cheese to the whipped cream.
Spread over top of rice mixture.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes.
Heat tomato juice. Add spices. Do not bring to a boil, but simmer gently. Serve with thin slice of lemon to garnish each serving.
Mix all ingredients together.
Form into a ball and roll on floured board. Cut with cutter dipped into flour.
Bake on greased cookie sheet in a moderate oven until brown.
Mix first four ingredients with electric mixer.
Shape into ball and then roll in pecans.
Mix sugar and flour.
Add vinegar and mustard.
Cook in double boiler until thick.
Add butter.
In saucepan, combine the cranberries, sugar, tapioca, water and orange peel.
Bring to boil, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and stir in apples.
Cool.
Pour into unbaked pastry shell that has been coated with 1/4 cup flour and 1/4 cup sugar mixed together.
Top with uncooked pastry or lattice strips of pastry.
If using a full top crust, cut a few slits in top crust. Slice a few slices of margarine and place on top and sprinkle sugar over top.
Bake at 375° for about 50 minutes.
Heat 1 1/2 cups water to
boiling.
Add cranberries and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add sugar, gelatin soaked in the other 1/2 cup of water, nuts and apples.
Pour
into mold.
Place in circle on bed of crisp lettuce and
fill	center	with cottage cheese seasoned with salt and paprika.
Serves 6.
Saute garlic and onion in oil; add shrimp.
Sprinkle with lemon juice; add mushrooms, wine and salt.
Cook until shrimp turn pink (about 4 minutes).
Serve over rice or pasta.
Add green salad and crusty French bread for a flavorful menu.
Saute the eggplant (cubed) with minced garlic in olive oil. Stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Toss with basil, cubed Mozzarella and rigatoni.
Combine Jell-O, orange juice, water and pineapple; let congeal.
Beat lemon pudding and milk until smooth; whip cream until firm.
Fold in pudding and whipped cream.
Spread over congealed Jell-O mixture.
Dice hot peppers and onion.
Add milk until right consistency. Mix in blender.
Combine and mix ingredients.
Pour in a pie shell and bake at 400° for about 45 minutes.
Arrange chicken in lightly oiled 13 x 9 x 1-inch baking dish. Top with cheese slices.
Combine soup and water; stir well.
Spoon sauce evenly over chicken; sprinkle crumbs on top.
Dot with butter or margarine.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Cook broccoli as directed on package.
Saute onions and celery in oleo.
Mix all ingredients.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top. Bake 20 minutes at 350°.

In a skillet over medium heat in hot margarine, cook onion until tender. Add remaining ingredients, except parsley. Heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low. Cover; simmer 5 minutes or until hot and bubbly. Garnish with parsley. Makes 4 servings.
Melt margarine and cocoa together. Stir together.
Let it cool for a few minutes. Add sugar.
Add eggs all at one time.
Beat with a mixer. Add milk and vanilla. Beat until well blended.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix dressing, cheese, sugar and onion in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients; mix lightly.
Refrigerate.
Makes 8 servings.
Put rice in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix all liquids together.
Pour 1/2 of liquids over rice and mix well.
Place chicken, uncovered, on top of rice.
Cover with remaining liquids.
Sprinkle cheese and almonds on top.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cut kielbasa into bite size pieces.
Combine chili sauce, brown sugar, pineapple and juice.
Pour into a casserole dish. Bake at 250° for 45 minutes.
Mix pie filling, pineapple, condensed milk, banana and lemon juice well.
Fold in container of Cool Whip.
Pour into oblong pan and cover.
Put in freezer.
Take out about 10 minutes before serving.
Melt butter in top of double boiler.
Add dry ingredients; stir until smooth.
Add liquids slowly; cook until thick and smooth. Add cooked beets; let set over low heat for at least 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix flour, salt and baking soda.
Set aside.
Mix fat and peanut butter.
Add both kinds of sugar.
Mix well.
Add eggs and beat well.
Stir flour mixture into peanut butter mixture.
Drop dough from a teaspoon on baking pan.
Flatten with a fork.
Bake at 375° (moderate oven) for 10 to 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Makes 4 to 5 dozen cookies.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Boil noodles until firm but done. Drain.
In casserole dish, combine soups and tuna.
Add drained noodles.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes or until done.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Mix sour cream, dry onion soup mix, mushroom soup, lemon juice, and mustard.
Heat sauerkraut in drippings from cooked sausage.
In baking dish alternate layers of potatoes, cream mixture, and sauerkraut.
Put bread crumbs on top. Bake at 350°F. for 20 to 25 minutes or until bubbly and light brown on top.
Butter 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Mix all ingredients, one at a time.
Bake, uncovered, for approximately 60 minutes at 350°, until set, brown and crusty.
Crush Oreo cookies, reserving 1 cup.
Mix with margarine and put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cream the cream cheese with confectioners sugar.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Spread cream cheese mixture on crumbs. Spread cooled pudding on top.
Sprinkle cookie crumbs over all.
Fry in patties dropped by spoonfuls into a small amount of cooking oil.
Serve hot.
Cook sugar, marshmallows, salt, milk and butter over medium heat.
Boil for 8 minutes.
Take off heat.
Add chocolate chips, vanilla and nuts.
Makes 3 pounds.
Mix the above ingredients in a large bowl, add enough mayonnaise to hold ingredients together.
Chill at least one hour and can be chilled overnight.
Sprinkle with paprika and sliced hard boiled eggs before serving.
Cut chicken into bite-size pieces in a frying pan, cook chicken with the lemon juice and water.
When the chicken is done, add the 2 packages of dressing mix and simmer for at least 5 minutes.
Cook rice as directed.
Serve the chicken mixture over rice.
Mix thoroughly sauerkraut, bean sprouts, celery, diced pepper, chopped onion and celery seed.
Blend together sugar, salad oil and vinegar.
It is best when this mixture is heated and then left to cool.
When cool, pour mixture over vegetables.
It's better after it stands a few days.
Keep in the refrigerator.
Brown chicken in a little oil.
Put in casserole dish.
Blend soup with milk and add pepper.
Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle with paprika (optional) on top.
Bake at 400°, covered, for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Check after 45 minutes for doneness.
Serve with rice or noodles.
Mash liverwurst to make smooth.
Blend in all of rest of ingredients, except add only 1/3 of the cream cheese.
Pack into a 2-cup mixing bowl lined with foil or plastic wrap.
Chill several hours until firm.
Turn out and frost with remaining cheese. Chill well.
Serve with crackers.
Put crackers in brown paper bag.
Sprinkle all dry ingredients onto crackers.
Shake well. Pour oil onto crackers and shake again.
Let bag set in sink 1 hour before storing in Tupperware. Sack will absorb excess oil.
Combine all ingredients.
Mix with electric beater about 5 minutes at medium speed.
Pour the batter into a greased bundt pan or angel food cake pan.
Bake at 350° about 45 minutes or until done.
Cool about 25 minutes before turning onto a rack.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Cook sugar and milk, stirring until mixture makes soft ball in cold water.
Add marshmallows and peanut butter, stirring until all is dissolved and begins to thicken.
Pour in buttered dish or pan. Slice when cold.
Mix first 3 ingredients together and heat until dissolved. Add rest of ingredients and mix together.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Cook as a syrup the sugar, orange juice, rind and salt to soft ball stage.
Stir well, then add nuts.
Stir until creamy.
Lift out pecans, one at a time, placing them on wax paper until dry.
Cook onions slowly with butter and oil in heavy covered 4-quart saucepan for 15 minutes.
Stir in salt and sugar.
Cook, uncovered, over moderate heat, 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often until onions are a deep golden brown.
Sprinkle with flour; stir 3 minutes.
Remove from heat; add boiling bouillon and water to onion mixture.
Blend well.
Add wine and seasonings.
Simmer partially covered, 35 minutes.
While soup is simmering, place 1 layer of French bread slices on cookie sheet and bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until they are dried and golden brown.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Combine dissolved yeast, eggs, 2 1/2 cups flour, shortening, sugar and salt in a large mixer bowl.
Beat until smooth at medium speed, scraping sides of bowl for 2 minutes.
With wooden spoon, stir in remaining flour to make soft dough.
Cover.
Let rise until double in bulk, about 1 hour.
Punch down.
Refrigerate overnight.
Melt the oleo, butterscotch chips and peanut butter together in microwave for 4 minutes.
Pour over the Rice Chex; mix well. Put Chex mix in paper grocery bag with the powdered sugar.
Fold top over and shake.
Coat all well.
Pour out and let dry on cookie sheet.

In a bowl, whisk melted ice cream and pudding mix for 2 minutes. Pour into crusts. Freeze until firm. Pies may be frozen up to 2 months. Remove from the freezer 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with whipped topping, if desired. Yields 2 pies, 6 to 8 servings each.
Cook macaroni in salted water; rinse and drain.
Add macaroni to a bowl containing salad oil and vinegar.
Mix together, then add remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Brown sausage; drain. Bring water to boil; add rice and Lipton onion soup mix. Boil 7 minutes. Add celery, green pepper, sliced water chestnuts and browned sausage. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix milk, soup, salsa and onions.
Chop tortilla into pieces. Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer ingredients and top with cheese. Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Cook carrots and drain.
Melt the butter and cheese together, then mix with the carrots.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt butter and mix with the crackers.
Sprinkle over the carrots and cheese. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes (until cracker mixture is brown).
Saute the onion (chopped fine).
Add the tomatoes and green chilies. Cook until most of the liquid is gone.
Add and heat the milk. Add the Velveeta (cubed) and heat until melted.
Mix well and serve.
In a saucepan mix the sugar and cornstarch very well. Gradually stir in water.
Cook over medium heat and stir constantly until mixture gets thick.
Boil 1 minute.
Stir a little of this hot mixture very slowly into the egg yolks.
Then blend this mix into the hot mix in saucepan.
Return to heat and boil about 1 minute more, stirring constantly until smooth and thick.
Blend in butter.
Stir to melt and then add lemon juice and stir well.
Pour into baked shell.
Cover with meringue.
Be sure to seal meringue to crust so it doesn't shrink.
Bake in a 400° oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until light golden brown.
Cook noodles as directed, then drain.
Brown ground beef; add soups and Velveeta.
Mix well.
Add noodles.
Put into casserole dish.
Sprinkle Cheddar on top.
Bake at 350° until hot through, 20 to 30 minutes.
Scrape the peel off of the potatoes.
Wash well.
Cover with cold water; cover and bring to a boil.
Cook until fork tender, approximately 15 minutes after they come to a boil.
Add bacon drippings and butter and stir.
Mix cornstarch with 1 cup of half and half and add to the potatoes stirring well.
Add the rest of the half and half, salt and pepper.
Stir frequently to keep from sticking and scorching.
Cook until smooth and it thickens. Garnish with chopped green onions and crispy fried bacon.
In a saucepan, combine brown sugar, cornstarch and mustard. Stir in water, raisins, vinegar, lemon juice and peel until blended.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
Stir in butter until melted.
Serve warm over sliced ham.
Yield: 2 cups.
Cut ends of eggplant; peel skin with potato peeler.
Slice into 1/4 or 1/8-inch slices.
Scramble 3 eggs in a bowl.
Pour bread crumbs in another bowl.
Dip eggplant in egg, then in bread crumbs.
Fry in olive oil to lightly brown on both sides.
Cover bottom of baking pan with tomato sauce.
Place a layer of eggplant, overlapping edges in pan.
Cover lightly with sauce; spread evenly.
Cut or break American cheese into squares, 1 for each serving, and place over eggplant.
Put an even coating of Kraft Parmesan over it.
Do another overlapping layer of eggplant, sauce, American cheese and Parmesan.
Put sauce on each piece of American cheese so it won't burn.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Drain kidney beans thoroughly.
Pour off liquid from wax and green beans.
Empty beans into a large bowl.
Add onions. Dissolve sugar in vinegar and add salt, pepper and Crisco oil to beans.
Stir gently to blend.
Marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
Serve beans, thoroughly drained, on lettuce.
Sift flour, salt and soda together. Add lemon juice to apples. Mix oil, sugar and eggs together; add dry ingredients alternately with apples. Add nuts and vanilla.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake 1 hour at 350°. Leave in pan and cover with glaze.
Steam or microwave the cauliflower until soft. Puree in food processor adding the butter and half & half to taste. Season with salt and pepper.
This has 5 grams carbohydrates.
Grease 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie plate.
Cook and stir ground beef in skillet until brown; drain.
Stir in onion and seasoning mix. Spread in plate.
Sprinkle with tomatoes and corn.
Beat eggs, milk, baking mix and cornmeal until smooth.
Pour into pie plate. Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
In one bowl, mix together flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and baking soda.
In another bowl, mix together oil, eggs, sugar, vanilla and chocolate chips.
Add flour mixture to bowl and mix all ingredients well.
Divide batter in well greased and floured loaf pans (9 x 5 x 3-inch).
Bake in a 350° oven for 60 minutes. Pick test; cool in pan 10 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.

recipes.t: Oven Baked Or Crock Pot Stew
d: Cut vegetables in large pieces.
Combine all ingredients in large pot or crock pot.
Cover and bake for five to six hours at 275° in pot; or low in crock pot.
Mix all but biscuits and place in baking dish.
Top with flaky biscuits and bake at 350° until done.
Cream butter and cheese.
Add flour, nuts and flavoring.
Make into 2 rolls.
Chill overnight.
Cut into 1/4-inch slices or make into small balls and press down on cookie sheet with fork.
Bake at 350° until slightly brown.
Bring to a boil ginger ale and catsup.
Pack and roll meat mixture into firm balls.
Add to boiling mixture.
Cook about 3 hours.
Chill and remove fat from top; reheat.
This makes a good dish to freeze or prepare ahead.
Serve with noodles or pasta.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine first six ingredients.
In medium bowl, combine next four ingredients.
Combine the two mixtures.
Spray pan with non-stick spray.
Spread batter in pan. Bake 25 minutes.
Cool and cut into 16 bars.
Calories per serving:
Heat soup to lukewarm.
Stir in water.
Slowly sprinkle gelatine into mixture.
Add onion, mayonnaise and shrimp.
Fold in soft cream cheese.
Pour into mold.
Chill overnight.
Serve with crackers.
Use cupcake liners as needed.
Drain green beans, leaving a little water in each can. Saute onion in bacon drippings. Add chili sauce, beans and bacon. Chill overnight. Heat to serve about 20 minutes at 350°.
Mix half the recipe at a time.
Mix together well all the ingredients.
Roll into 4-inch balls, then refrigerate 2 to 3 hours or put in freezer for 1/2 or 1 hour, then take out of refrigerator or freezer.

Take 1 ball out of refrigerator at a time, then roll out ball on board with flour or powdered sugar and cut with diamond cookie cutter and fill with 1 teaspoon apricot mixture with ground walnuts in center, then bring two corners together and seal.
Put 1/2 toothpick in cookie to hold together. Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 425° for 10 minutes or until lightly golden brown.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar when cool.

Cook macaroni as package described; rinse and set aside. Mix well cottage cheese, sour cream, eggs and sharp cheese (save 2 cups for topping). Add macaroni and stir well. Pour into lightly greased (Pam) 2-quart casserole. Top with shredded cheese and a dash of paprika. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Makes 2 standard size layers.
Mix all dry ingredients.
Add mayonnaise, water and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Steam the squash, zucchini and lemon.
Cook them, but still firm.
In a saucepan, heat just to boiling the cream of mushroom soup, bouillon cube and sour cream. Add the grated carrot. Drain the vegetables well and add them to the sauce.
Prepare the stuffing.
Cover bottom of a casserole dish with 1/2 of the stuffing. Add vegetable/sauce mixture, then top with remaining stuffing.
Bake at 300° for about 1/2 hour.
In a large nonstick skillet, saut the zucchini, corn, green pepper, leek and seasoned salt in oil until vegetables are tender. Add tomatoes; heat through. Yield: 4 servings.
Place shredded cabbage in sterile jars.
Use 1 teaspoon salt per quart and 1/2 teaspoon salt per pint.
Cover with hot water and place lids on tight.
Store in a cool, dark place for one month before tasting.
In large saucepan, heat bouillon in 1/4 cup water until dissolved.
Add cabbage, carrots, onion, 1/2 teaspoon salt and dash of pepper; toss to mix.
Cook, covered, 5 to 10 minutes or until tender.
Combine butter, mustard and pecans and pour over vegetables; toss to mix.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Serves 6 to 8.
About 2 hours before serving, preheat oven to 325°.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, heat milk until tiny bubbles form around the edges.
Blend all ingredients in a large bowl, then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Bake in a greased and floured tube pan at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes or until cake springs back when touched lightly.
Cool for 15 minutes right side up.
Remove from pan.
Combine all ingredients.
Serve with snack crackers.
Makes 1 2/3 cups.

recipes.t: Vermicelli With Spinach And Pasta Sauce
d: Cook spinach in olive oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add salt, pepper, Ricotta and skim milk. Cook over low heat until mixture is heated through.
Do not allow to boil.
Simmer pasta in sauce in a small pan; heat through. Cook vermicelli according to package; drain.
Variations:
Ham, onions, green peppers and/or Cheddar cheese may be added.
In large bowl stir together first three ingredients until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients; toss to coat well.
Chill.
Mix together in saucepan and bring to boil.
Use sauce on ribs, chicken, etc.
Mix all ingredients together.
Saute onions in margarine until limp but not brown.
Add tuna, green beans and mushroom soup.
Stir until well blended and simmer for a few minutes.
If too thick, add a little milk or water. Bake biscuits according to printed directions.
Serve creamed tuna over biscuits.
Toast may also be used instead of biscuits.
This makes a good evening meal as it is light.
Beat sugar, sour cream, condensed milk and vanilla well.
Add 2% milk and fruit. Pour in freezer and freeze.
Sift flour, brown sugar, salt and soda.
Bring to a boil the butter, cocoa and water.
While still hot, add to flour mixture. Add eggs, vanilla and milk.
Pour into sheet pan that has been lined with tinfoil and that has been greased.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, no longer.
Frost with Texas Sheet Cake Frosting.
Cut thin slice from top of tomatoes and scoop pulp out with large spoon.
Mix pulp with remaining ingredients and let stand. Place tomatoes carefully in 8-inch greased baking dish.
Fill carefully with mixture.
Top with bread crumbs and butter or grated cheese.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cook until it turns white and seal relish up in a jar.
This does not take long to prepare.
Mix together and refrigerate.
Mix tea, pineapple juice, lemon juice and orange juice. Boil cinnamon sticks in cup of water for 10 minutes. Add to tea mixture. Heat and serve.
Combine flour, cinnamon, and pecans in a large bowl.
In a separate dish, combine oil, eggs, sugar, pears, and vanilla.
Add to dry ingredients, stirring just until moistened.
Spoon mixture into two greased loaf pans.
Bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Put chicken broth in saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Immediately reduce heat to simmer.
Dissolve cornstarch in water; add to chicken broth, stirring until slightly thickened.
Add onion and stir.
Add egg very slowly, stirring to break it up.
Serve immediately.
Mix all ingredients in large dish, except pork chops.
Lightly brown the chops and place on rice mixture.
Cover and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
To prepare the batter, sift 1/2 cup of the flour and the salt into a deep mixing bowl.
Stir in the beaten egg and butter and then the milk and continue to stir until the batter is smooth.
Do not beat or overstir.
For the best results, set the batter aside at room temperature and let it rest for an hour or so, although it may be used at once if it must.
In either case, the egg white should be beaten with a whisk or rotary beater until stiff and then folded into the batter just before using it.

Dissolve jello as directed on package, add sugar while jello is hot. Add pineapple juice and frozen lemonade diluted to make 1 quart. Add limeade diluted as directed. Add ginger ale immediately before serving.
Drain peas well.
In medium mixing bowl, mix all listed ingredients.
Season to taste.
Cover and set in refrigerator to chill.
Serves 4 persons.
Mix together.
Put in casserole and pour 1/4 cup melted butter over this.
Bake 1 hour in a 350° oven.
Serve.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add coffee and egg.
Stir in dry ingredients and raisins.
Chill 1 hour.
Bake in 13 x 9-inch pan until done in center.
Cut into bars and glaze with powdered sugar glaze.
Whip whipping cream.
In a large bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk, crumbs, peaches and extract.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour into a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Cover.
Freeze 6 hours or until firm.
Grind the cranberries.
Add the sugar and pineapple.
Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
When ready to serve, mix in the marshmallows, nuts and Cool Whip.
Mash cheese until creamy.
Blend remaining ingredients except celery and onion.
Fold in vegetables and combine with cheese. Mix well.
Refrigerate.
Use with crackers or raw vegetables.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a jar; cover tightly and shake vigorously.
Rinse endive lightly; pat dry and trim ends.
Arrange on salad plates; top with watercress.
Drizzle dressing over top and sprinkle with toasted walnuts.
For Crock-Pot:
Arrange ribs in shallow microwave dish.
Salt, pepper and rosemary each rib.
Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Drain fat.
Add ribs, carrots, celery and wine to crock-pot.
Stir together butter, flour, chicken broth, beef broth and bouillon until smooth.
Add to the ribs in crock-pot and cook on high for 6 hours.
Dissolve yeast in water; add melted butter, egg and sugar with mixture.
Add flour.
Store in airtight container and refrigerate. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Melt margarine and stir in 1/2 of the crackers.
Add the other ingredients.
Mix.
Pour into a Pyrex or other glass dish; top with remaining 1/2 cup crackers.
Bake, uncovered, for 15 minutes at 400°.
Combine all ingredients and pour into medium size casserole dish.
Dot top with cracker crumbs and butter.
Bake at 325° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Brown beef and onion in large saucepan; drain grease.
Salt and pepper to taste and add all spices (sugar, garlic powder and Italian seasoning).
Add tomato wedges, tomato paste and 1 can water.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Boil noodles according to box; don't over boil.
Drain.

Make layers starting with 1 thin layer of sauce, 4 noodles laid lengthwise, layer of sauce, layer of cottage cheese, layer of Mozzarella cheese, noodles, sauce, cottage cheese, Mozzarella, sauce, noodles, sauce, cottage cheese, Mozzarella and last 2 or 3 tablespoons Parmesan.
Bake at 350° until cheese really bubbles, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Serve with tossed salad and garlic bread!
Sift everything together, except meal.
Stir in meal.
Then add remaining ingredients.
Beat 1 minute. Bake in greased pan 20 minutes at 425°.
Cut steak into thin strips.
In a large skillet (ovenproof if desired), brown meat in oil, using high heat.
Add onions; saute until tender-crisp.
Blend soup, water and garlic salt; pour over steak.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, or until steak is tender.
Or, cover and bake at 350°.
Serve over beds of fluffy rice.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix together and make into meatballs.
Fry.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Add raisins
and walnuts. Combine egg, vanilla and melted shortening. Dissolve soda in pineapple and add.
Stir just enough to mix well. Pour into greased loaf pan and bake 1 hour or until done at 350°. Wrap in foil for freezing.
Briefly puree 8 ounces kiwi and pour into bowl.
Whip cream into soft peaks.
Whisk egg whites until stiff; sprinkle with sugar toward end and beat to incorporate sugar.
Stir melted gelatin into puree.
Fold in whipped cream, then egg whites.
Pour half the mousse into a round 8 x 3-inch mold.
Refrigerate 15 minutes.
Pour tea over cake and let absorb.
Put cake in mold in 1 piece.
Add remaining mousse.
Freeze 4 hours.
Garnish mousse with kiwi.
Heat oven to 375°.
Beat eggs, shortening and half of the cake mix (dry) until smooth.
Stir in remaining cake mix, oats and chocolate pieces.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls, about 2 inches apart, onto ungreased baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes. Cool slightly before removing from baking sheet.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Dice the bacon and fry.
Drain bacon and cook onion in grease. Beat egg; add salt, onion, bacon and corn.
Pour into a greased baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Peel eggs, slice lengthwise, remove cooked yolks.
Put other ingredients in bowl with yolks and mix with mixer until well blended, not lumpy.
Put filling mixture into egg whites and sprinkle with paprika.
Measure water into a large mixing bowl.
Sprinkle in yeast and stir until dissolved.
Add margarine, sugar, salt and 2 cups flour. Beat for 2 minutes with electric mixer (medium speed).
Blend in remaining flour.
Cover; let rise until double.
Stir down and spread in greased loaf pan.
Let rise until double.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until loaf sounds hollow.
Makes 1 loaf.
Cook ground chuck with onion and pepper and drain.
Mix all other ingredients.
Bake in a 2 1/2-quart baking dish at 350° for 1 hour.
Place chicken and celery in a large bowl.
Combine mayonnaise and curry powder.
Add to chicken mixture and mix well.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Before serving, add the pineapple, bananas, oranges and coconut.
Toss gently.
Serve on salad greens, if desired.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Cut tips off wings and section pieces.
Combine margarine, soy sauce and other ingredients until melted.
Sprinkle wings lightly with garlic salt.
Pour mixture over wings and marinate 4 hours or overnight.
Remove from marinating sauce and bake at 350° until done.
Mix first four ingredients.

Layer in 9 x 13-inch casserole: thin layer of sauce, 3 raw noodles, all of raw ground beef, 1/2 Jack cheese, 1/3 sauce, 3 noodles, spread all Ricotta cheese, rest of Jack cheese, 1/2 remaining sauce, 3 noodles and rest of sauce. Cover loosely.
Cook on 1/2 power (5) 10 minutes, turn 1/4.
Cook 1/2 power 10 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Turn 1/4, cook on High (10) 7 minutes.
Add cheese (Mozzarella and Parmesan).
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Saute garlic and onion in margarine over low heat until tender.
Add chicken broth, carrots and celery; cook until just tender-crisp.
Blend flour into milk; add to chicken broth and cook, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Stir in cheese.
Add salt and Tabasco to taste.
Serves 4.

Make 2 packages Jell-O, using only 3 cups of water instead of the usual four (I use the pineapple juice which was drained from the crushed pineapple and the rest water making up the 3 cups water, 1 boiling and 2 cold.)
Allow Jell-O to begin to jell; add the other ingredients.
Chill until Jell-O is completely firm and set.
Moosh together at room temperature.
Prepare cake mix according to directions on box.
Bake in two 9-inch round cake pans.
When layers are cool, cut each in half, making a total of four layers.
Cook garlic, peppers
and onions in vegetable oil until soft, then add tomato
paste,
oregano, basil, sugar and salt. Simmer all together until
it
comes
to
a
boil.
Bottle and seal.
Combine.
Add 1/3 to 1/2 cup per mug of boiling water.
In small bowl sprinkle gelatin over cold water; let stand 1 minute to soften.
Add boiling water and stir to dissolve.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 2-cup mold or individual dishes.
Chill until set.
Makes 4 servings.
Wash potatoes.
Cut lengthwise wedge across top of potatoes, 1-inch wide and 1-inch deep.
Remove wedge.
Place bacon and green onions in corner of wedge.
Add butter.
Replace wedge and wrap in foil.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour or until potato is done.
Mix soups, onions and green chilies with a dash of salt. Layer the pan with tortillas dipped in oil.
Layer that with chicken.
Pour 1/2 soup mixture, then top with cheese.
Repeat. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Place eggplant in a baking pan and bake in oven at 375° for about 30 minutes.
Remove eggplant and let cool; split open and scoop out pulp; set aside.
Beat eggs slightly.
Then add corn syrup, sugar, margarine and vanilla and mix well.
Add pecans.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Pour into pie crust.
Bake on cookie sheet for 50 to 55 minutes.
Mix dry ingredients together.
Beat in egg, then add buttermilk until batter is proper consistency.
Slice onions thick and dip in batter.
Fry in peanut oil until light brown.
Saute onion and celery in butter.
Mix all ingredients.
Cover with 2 cups potato chips or 1/2 package sliced almonds.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cut bacon in 1-inch pieces; cook until crisp.
Drain on absorbent paper.
Spread on bottom of pie shell.
Beat eggs, cream and seasonings just enough to blend.
Stir in cheese; pour into pie shell.
Bake at 375° for about 35 minutes or until pie shell is golden brown and filling is firm.
Serves 4 as an entree, 8 to 12 as an appetizer.
Melt chocolate chips and 1 cup canned milk in heavy saucepan, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
In another bowl mix wafer crumbs, marshmallows, pecans, powdered sugar and salt.
Reserve 1/2 cup chocolate mixture for glaze.
Stir remaining chocolate mixture into crumb mixture and mix well.
Press into greased pan (9-inches).
Stir remaining canned milk into the reserved chocolate mixture until smooth and spread over mixture in pan.
Chill until glaze is set, then cut into 36 squares.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; set aside.
In large bowl combine sugar, oil, eggs and extract.
Add dry ingredients alternately with buttermilk; stir just until moistened.
Fold in coconut and walnuts.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 8 1/2 by 4 1/2 inch loaf pans.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until bread tests done.
Cool 10 minutes in pans before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.
Combine soup, cheese and onion in pan.
Heat until cheese melts, stirring.
Blend in mayonnaise.
Remove from heat.
In small saucepan, sprinkle gelatin over water.
Over low heat, stir until dissolved.
Stir into soup mixture.

one loaf.

4 protein exchanges, 1/2 fat exchange plus herbed margarine (1 teaspoon = 1/2 fat).
