Place a clean towel over container. Store at about 70°.
On the third day, drain salt water and discard.
Rinse cucumbers and re-scald container; cover and weight. Return cucumbers to container.
Add 1/4 cup salt to 2 quarts fresh water and boil.
Pour over cucumbers.
Replace cover and weight; recover with a clean towel.
On the fifth day, drain salt water and discard.
Rinse.
Makes 5 to 9 pints.
Cook chicken until tender.
Cool and debone.
Cut chicken into bite size pieces.
Saute onion until tender.
Combine chicken, soup, tomatoes and onion.
Layer Doritos, chicken mixture and cheese.
Bake in moderate oven until cheese is melted and the dish is thoroughly heated.
Fry bacon until it starts to brown.
Add chopped onion.
Fry until onion browns; set aside.
Do not drain grease.
Add this to potato mixture.
Grate potatoes into cold water.
Stir well. Drain.
Add eggs, milk, salt, pepper and Accent.
Stir well.
Add bacon and onion.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Wash cucumbers.
Pack into sterilized jars.
Place 1/2 clove garlic and 1 head dill in each jar.
Heat vinegar, water, and salt substitute in saucepan, until boiling.
Cover cucumbers with hot liquid, leaving 1/2 inch head space.
Adjust lids.
Process 15 minutes in boiling water bath.
Allow 5 days to ripen.

recipes.t: Shepherd'S Pie(A Meal In One Dish)
d: Brown ground beef.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Stir in tomato sauce and heat until bubbly.
Put in bottom of a casserole dish.
Put green beans (or corn) on top of meat.
Put prepared instant potatoes on top of green beans (or corn).
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook fettuccine as directed; set aside.
In a large pot, melt butter and saute onion and bell peppers for 15 minutes.
Add garlic, crab and shrimp and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in cream and then cheese, stirring gently until cheese is melted.
Stir in fettuccine.
When thoroughly mixed, pour into a 9 x 13-inch dish. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine sugar, flour cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Mix lightly through apples (sliced 1/4 inch thick).
Heap in pastry-lined 9-inch pie pan.
Dot with butter.
Adjust top crust and flute edges; cut vents. bake in hot oven (425 degrees) 50 to 60 minutes, or until crust is browned and apples are tender.
Pour boiling water over raisins and soak 5 minutes; drain. Combine sugar, shortening, egg and lemon extract in mixing bowl; beat well.
Stir in carrots and drained raisins.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt; add to first mixture and blend well. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Makes 3 dozen.
Cream shortenings; gradually add sugar and cream well.
Beat eggs in one at a time.
Add flavoring.
Mix in milk and flour (with salt) at 3 different times.
Mix well.
Put in greased and floured tube pan and place in cold oven.
Bake at 300° 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cream oleo and sugar.
Add eggs.
Add dry ingredients.
Add chopped fruits and nuts.
Bake at 325° on greased and floured cookie sheet.
(Drop dough with a tablespoon.) Remove from oven when desired brownness is
reached, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Combine and bake at 350° till done.
Cool.
Soften butter and mix with flour and spread in square baking pan.
Then, sprinkle pecans over the top of that.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes, then cool.
Then mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip.
Spread on cooled crust.
Chill in refrigerator. Mix pudding and milk and spread over the top of the cheese mixture.
Top with Cool Whip and sprinkle pecans on top, if desired.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Pour into 2 baked 9-inch pie shells. Top with nuts.
Refrigerate.
Mix sugar and cornstarch.
Add and mix remaining ingredients. Pour into a greased 1-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with nutmeg. Place casserole in pan of water and bake of 300° for 1 hour and 45 minutes.
In a bowl, mix together the flours, sugar, salt, milk powder and baking powder.
Cut in shortening with a pastry blender until well mixed.
Mix water and egg whites to blend, but do not beat. Add to dry mixture, stirring just to blend.
Mixture will be lumpy.
Fold in blueberries.
Spoon into paper-lined muffin tins. Bake at 350° for 25 minutes until nicely browned.
Makes 12 muffins.
Add sugar to beaten eggs.
Continue beating until thick.
Set aside.
Bring water to a boil in a large saucepan.
Add broccoli. Cover, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, or until broccoli is tender.
Stir in soup and milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thoroughly heated.
Stir in pepper.
Pour into serving bowls.
Top each serving with 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese.
Yields 1 quart.
Chop onion; brown in butter.
Add beef.
Let brown well and add tomatoes (put through sieve), peppers and garlic.
Add beans which have been cooked for 1 hour.
Simmer about 6 hours.
Heat through until thick.
Add pepper and garlic salt to taste.
Cool completely before wrapping mixture in egg roll skins and seal rolls with egg yolk.
Deep-fry in wok.
Add 1 large onion thinly sliced.
Cook carrots not too soft; drain.
Marinate overnight.
Can be served cold but best when hot.
Dissolve gelatin and salt in hot water; add cold water, vinegar, onion and pepper.
Chill until slightly thickened. Combine vegetables and fold into gelatin mixture.
Chill until firm.
To fill a 9 x 13 dish, double this recipe.
Mix all together.
Freeze in ice cream freezer.
Brown the onion, beef, salt and pepper, chili powder and tomatoes; set aside.
Cook the water, 1 teaspoon salt and corn meal on the stove, stirring constantly until thickens.
Pour the corn meal mush into baking dish; pour meat mixture over that. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Top with shredded cheese.
Combine sugar, salt and cornstarch in the top of a double boiler.
In another bowl, beat egg yolks with 1/2 cup of the milk. When well mixed, add remaining 1 1/2 cups of milk and mix well. Add milk and egg mixture to sugar mixture.
Before starting to cook the pudding, layer your wafers and sliced bananas in a 2-quart casserole.
Brown beef and saute onion in oil until tender.
Stir to separate beef.
Pour off grease.
Add soup and seasonings and cook 5 minutes.
Serve on buns.
Drain and rinse the hominy.
Generously butter a 3-quart casserole.
Layer the ingredients in this order: hominy, green chilies, salt, pepper, sour cream, butter.
Repeat the layers ending with a layer of hominy.
Dot the top with butter and pour cream over all.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 15 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Combine water, butter and chocolate in saucepan; bring to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Stir in combined flour and sugar.
Add eggs, sour cream, soda and salt; mix well.
Pour into greased jelly roll pan.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Frost while warm with milk chocolate frosting.
Cook pasta as directed on package; drain.
In same saucepan, heat Alfredo sauce over medium heat, stirring frequently.
Stir in cooked pasta, chicken and peas.
Cook 5 minutes more.
Makes 4 servings.
In large bowl with fork, beat butter and sugar until creamy, then blend this mixture with soft shortening.
Combine flour and salt with fork; blend with butter mixture.
Gradually stir in water until mixture cleans sides of bowl.
On lightly floured surface, knead dough until just well mixed.
Chill.
Divide into thirds and roll out crusts.
Bake at 450° for 13 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In medium skillet saute mushrooms in butter.
Remove and drain well.
In blender or food processor (metal blade), blend eggs, sour cream, cottage cheese, Parmesan cheese, flour, onion powder, salt and Tabasco sauce.
Pour mixture in large bowl.
Stir in sauteed mushrooms, Jack cheese and crab meat.
Pour into 9 or 10-inch quiche pan.
Bake 45 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Quiche should be brown (golden) and puffed.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Cut in wedges.
Serves 8.
Place squash in a saucepan; add water to cover and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer 6 minutes or until tender but still firm.
Drain.
Cut squash in half lengthwise, leaving stems intact.
Remove pulp, leaving 1/4-inch thick shells.
Mash pulp; add chilies and next 5 ingredients.
Stir well.
Spoon mixture into shells.
Sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Arrange squash on a rack in a roasting pan coated with vegetable cooking spray.
Broil 5 1/2-inches from heat for 8 minutes or until browned.
Serves 4.
Fill pie crust with crumbled bread.
Cover bread with sugar. Fill with milk.
Dot with little chunks of butter and cover with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook water, sugar and syrup until it reaches soft boil stage. Add 1/2 of the syrup mixture to stiffly beaten egg whites.
Cook other half of syrup to crack stage when dropped into cold water. Add this to egg whites, beating all the time.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Stir with a large spoon until it loses its gloss.
Pour into buttered pan.
Heat water and dates together until mushy.
Cream oil and dates.
Add other ingredients in order given.
Beat thoroughly. Add nuts or raisins.
Bake on lightly oiled cookie sheet at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain syrup from fruit cocktail; add enough water to make 1 1/2 cups liquid.
Heat to boiling; add gelatin.
Dissolve and let cool. Stir in fruit.
Blend cream cheese, mayonnaise and lemon juice and add nuts.
Pour half of the gelatin mixture into fruit mold and let set.
Spread cream cheese mixture over first layer and pour in remainder of gelatin.
Return to refrigerator until firm.
Serve on lettuce.
Mix all ingredients except cornflakes and margarine.
Pour into a greased casserole dish.
Top with crumbled cornflakes and margarine.
Bake 1 hour at 300°.
Dissolve yeast and salt in warm water using a large mixing bowl.
Add whole wheat flour; stir and add the 6 cups white flour. Knead thoroughly right in the bowl.
Cover and let rise for 2 hours.
Make dough into 3 round flat loaves about 1-inch thick (use a rolling pin).
Lay on a cloth to rise for 35 to 40 minutes. Cover with a cloth.
Test dough by pressing lightly with finger. If the impression stays, it is ready to bake.
If not, let dough rise a little longer.
In large microwave bowl, combine popcorn, cereal and nuts.
In 4-cup microwave bowl, combine brown sugar, margarine, syrup and salt; microwave on High for 1 1/2 minutes.
Stir, microwave on High for 45 seconds to 2 minutes, or until mixture comes to rolling boil.
Stir in vanilla and baking soda (mixture will become foamy). Pour over popcorn mixture and toss to coat.
Spread 1/2 of mixture in ungreased 12 x 8-inch pan.
Microwave on High for 2 to 3 minutes or until popcorn is evenly coated, stirring every minute.
Spread on foil to cool.
Using same dish, repeat with remaining popcorn mixture.
Allow to dry for 2 hours.
Store tightly in covered container.
In bowl, combine flour, milk, 1/2 c. sugar, baking powder, vanilla, egg, and cook and serve pudding together.
Mix well and pour into a 10-inch deep dish pie pan or 8x8-inch square sprayed with non-stick spray.
Place peaches over the batter.

In a small bowl, beat well: cream cheese, peach juice, and 1/2 c. sugar. Drop by large spoonfuls over the peaches as evenly as possible. Spread out over the peaches as evenly as possible, keeping at least 1 inch from the sides.
In small bowl mix together 1 Tbsp. sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle over the top.
Bake at 350° for 35-40 minutes.
In skillet cook meat and onions until meat is browned.
Drain off fat.
Stir in tomato sauce, uncooked rice, water, olives, chili peppers, garlic salt, pepper and hot pepper.
Bring to boil.
Turn into a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Cover and bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until rice is tender.
Add cheese cubes, stirring just until cheese is distributed.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Mix and place ingredients in 8 x 8-inch pan and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Combine dry ingredients.
Beat eggs lightly; add with sugar, oil and vanilla and add to dry ingredients.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.

recipes.t: Knock Your Socks Off Carrot Soup
d: Saute the chopped carrots and onion over medium heat in butter for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the stock or bouillon and rice and bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and simmer for 25 minutes or until the carrots and rice are tender.
Put soup into blender jar and puree on low speed for a minute.
Then turn to high speed until the soup is really smooth.
(If the soup is too thick for pureeing, add a little extra stock.)
Layer in a large glass bowl in order given.
Cover and refrigerate overnight or several hours.
Beat egg.
Add sugar, and then Wesson oil and vinegar.
Sift flour and soda together.
Add to mixture.
Add buttermilk slowly. Add vanilla and cake coloring.
Bake in 3 greased and floured 9 inch pans for 30 minutes at 350.
You will also need heavy-duty aluminum foil.
Melt the chocolate and oil together.
Beat in the sugar and eggs.
Stir in the flour, baking powder, salt and nuts.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin according to directions on box.
Add sugar while hot.
Add remaining ingredients and chill.
Place chicken breasts in bottom of casserole dish.
Place one slice of cheese on top of each breast, or sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Pour soup and wine over top of chicken.
Combine stuffing mix and margarine.
Sprinkle on top.
Bake 350 degrees for 55 - 60 minutes.
Evening:
Place starter in a large bowl and add these ingredients.
Make into stiff batter.
Rub with oil.
Cover with plastic wrap and leave on counter overnight to rise until doubled.
Brown meat in pan.
Crumble up and drain off fat.
Chop or tear bread into small pieces.
Grate cheese.
Beat eggs; add milk and salt.
Spray 9 x 12-inch pan with Pam.
Combine meat, bread, cheese and egg mixture in large bowl.
Pour into pan.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 12 servings.

recipes.t: Black Cake(This Cake Will Keep Up To A Year.)
d: Preheat oven to 250°. Take 1/2 cup of flour and dredge raisins and currants in it; set aside. Cream butter and sugar thoroughly. Beat eggs until light. Sift remaining flour with mace, cloves and nutmeg. Add flour alternately to batter with beaten eggs. Stir in brandy and fruit. Pour into baking pan. Bake in 250° oven for 2 or more hours. Makes 36 servings. Preparation time: 2:50.
Brown meat, adding onion, chili powder and garlic salt to taste.
Drain off grease.
Add meat and soup to crock-pot to heat through.
Add milk, using 1 soup can.
When heated, serve with white tortilla chips.
Combine eggs, mincemeat, condensed milk, fruit and nuts.
Fold in dry ingredients.
Bake slowly in a tube pan (250° or 300°)
for 2 hours.
Heat oven to 425°.
Stir together sugar, flour, nutmeg, cinnamon and salt.
Mix with apples.
Put in ungreased baking dish.
Dot with butter.
Put pie crust over fruit.
Put slits in crust. Bake 1 hour.
Skin and dress elephant; cut in bite size cubes.
Peel vegetables and cut into cubes.
Put rabbits in; cut in half.
Put in large pot; simmer gently for 24 hours.
Place neck bones in bottom of soup pot.
Add potatoes, salt, onions, parsley, garlic and Worcestershire sauce.
Place string beans on top.
Add water to cover ingredients.
Cover and cook slowly until done.
Peel eggplant and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Boil in salted water 10 minutes or until soft. Drain and mash.
Mix with eggs, salt, pepper, milk, melted oleo and 3/4 cup cracker crumbs.
Add oysters and pour into greased baking casserole. Cover with remaining cracker crumbs. Dot with oleo and bake at 350° until brown.
Cut bell pepper in half, seed & clean.
Mix all ingredients together and stuff bell peppers.
Place in microwave glass dish 2-inches deep.
Cover with wax paper and cook 19-20 minutes. Uncover, spread ketchup on top of peppers, return to microwave and cook uncovered for 2-5 minutes.
Serves 6.
Combine and cook first 4 ingredients until it has a sugary look or makes a small soft ball when dropped in cold water.
Add vanilla flavoring; stir in nuts to coat.
Spread on wax paper to cool.
Store in airtight container.
Cook celery 8 minutes in salted water.
Drain.
Mix celery, chestnuts, pimento and soup.
Place in a buttered 2-quart casserole.
Melt butter.
Pour over bread crumbs.
Add almonds. Sprinkle over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Beat egg in a butter casserole dish.
Heat corn and milk, then gradually stir into beaten egg.
Add salt, bread crumbs and cheese.
Mix thoroughly.
Place directly on the rack of a moderately low (325°) oven and bake uncovered for 30 minutes or until custard test done.
First Day:
Let cucumbers and salt set in 1 gallon boiling water for 24 hours.
Start with your hot rice (with that onion already cooked in it, remember?).
Then add your cheese to the rice so it melts and coats the rice.
Does it look like a golden field?
Well, then you're ready to add the cauliflower and the weenies and serve this nice and hot.
If you have a bear sitting at the table while you eat this, the calorie count is cut in half.
But don't expect to have no calories just because you invited two bears.
And you can't subtract calories just because you have three bears there.
Get the drift of this yet?
Gently brown garlic in oil and butter.
Be careful not to burn garlic or it will taste bitter.
Add broccoli and stir as you heat pan.
Add chicken broth; cover and simmer until broccoli is just al dente (still a little firm).
Cook rigatoni pasta until al dente; drain.
Add half the fresh basil and mix together with the broccoli.
Top with parsley, pepper, cheese and basil.
Prepare and cook potatoes to make 3/4 cup.
Drain.
Add salt and mash.
Melt oleo; add potatoes, coconut and sugar and mix well. Turn into a buttered jelly roll pan.
Spread evenly.
Refrigerate and allow to harden.
Cut into squares and dip in coating.
Mix all together 24 hours ahead.
About 1 hour before serving, add 5 bananas, quartered.
Wonderful.
Combine all ingredients; mix thoroughly.
Bake in tube pan at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix butter and milk; add peanut butter,
flour and powdered sugar.
Shape into small eggs.
Lay on wax paper overnight.
In a 3-quart pan, make scalloped potatoes.
Leave out butter (hamburger takes place).
Fry hamburger and strain.
Add to potatoes.
Strain peas and add to potato and hamburger.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients together.
Make into balls.
Melt paraffin wax and chocolate bits.
Dip balls in this and lay out on wax paper to dry.
Combine ingredients.
Pack into greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let stand 10 minutes before unmolding. Servings: 8.
Calories: 1 serving, 221.
Exchange per serving: 1 bread, 2 1/2 low-fat meat.
Boil chicken and take off bone.
Cook spaghetti in broth.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Brown green pepper and onion in oleo.
Add cream of celery soup and mushroom soup.
Mix well.
Pour in casserole dish.
Cover with cheese.
Cook at 350° for 50 minutes.
Use just enough canned milk to be able to form graham crackers into dough.
Add dates, nuts and Marshmallow Creme.
Mold into 1 large roll or several small ones.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cut Italian bread crosswise into 1-inch slices.
Do not cut through bottom crust.
Cut Mozzarella cheese into 1/4-inch slices.
Place cheese slices and olives between bread slices.
Then place the bread on a cookie sheet and bake for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted and the bread is hot. Sprinkle loaf with oregano.
With a knife divide loaf into slices. Serve hot.
Cook turnips and onion in saucepan in a little water until tender.
Drain and mash.
Add next four ingredients to turnips and mix well.
Spoon mixture into lightly greased 2-quart casserole. Sprinkle with cracker crumbs and cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
*Use if you want them a little spicy.
Wash beans and rinse.
Simmer beans in 2-quarts water, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Saute onion.
Add onion, tomatoes, lemon juice and flavor packet to beans.
Simmer another 30 minutes.
Add sliced sausage the last 10 minutes of simmering.
Serve with crusty pumpernickel bread.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In skillet, saute beef and onions until meat is fully cooked.
Drain fat.
Stir in tomato sauce and other seasonings.
Spoon into 1 1/2-quart shallow baking dish.
Spread mashed potatoes on top.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, uncovered, or until cheese is melted and casserole is bubbly.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Wash and cook apples until tender, then run in blender until smooth.
Put in saucepan; cook with cider vinegar, sugar and spices on low heat about 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Pour at once into jars and seal.
Process 10 minutes in boiling water bath at simmering temperature.
Mix all together except soups.
Make into 12 large balls or more small ones if preferred.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan or any baking dish.
Mix soups together and pour over.
Cover with foil or glass top of baking dish.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
This can be made the night before and put in the refrigerator.
Can be served with rice or potatoes.
Cook, crumble and drain sausage.
Layer ingredients in order listed in 9 x 13 glass baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes until firm.
Serves 10 to 12.
In covered blender, combine ingredients and blend until smooth. Pour over ice into four 10-ounce glasses.
Garnish with sour cream.
Yields 4 cups or 6 servings.
In a large mixing bowl, combine ground beef, eggs, bread crumbs, water and garlic salt.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Shape beef mixture into 1-inch balls.

Salt each steak; dredge in flour and beat with a mallet or edge of saucer. Saute onions in the fat, then remove onions and reserve. Brown steaks well in fat on each side over medium heat. Be careful not to overcook it.
Serve with onions on top.
Make gravy with the drippings and 3 tablespoons flour. Serve in a separate bowl or return steaks and onions to gravy pan and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve with rice or hot biscuits or mashed potatoes.
Shake chicken in bag with flour, salt and pepper.
Melt butter and dip floured chicken pieces into butter.
Roll chicken in potato chips.
Place in foil-lined pan; cover with foil.
Bake at 400° for approximately 1 hour.
Just before removing from oven, remove foil and brown.
Arrange broccoli in a shallow baking dish.
Arrange mushroom slices over this, then arrange olives, then pimento strips. Sprinkle lightly with oregano and garlic powder or garlic salt.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease bottom of loaf pan and lightly flour.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Gradually add sugar, beating all the time.
Add to flour mixture, then add lemon juice.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Peel carrots and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Boil until tender (20 minutes).
Remove from heat, drain and add butter. Stir to coat all carrots.
Add maple syrup and put mixture in a baking dish.
Add pecans and cover.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Stir to coat.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Place chocolate, sugar, milk, Spry, butter, corn syrup and salt in a saucepan.
Bring slowly to a full, rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Boil briskly for 1 minute.
(On a rainy day or very humid day, boil mixture for 30 seconds more.)
Cool to lukewarm. Add vanilla and beat until thick enough to spread.
Combine all crackers and margarine; mix and put 2/3 of the mix in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Saute vegetables until tender.
Add soup, cheese, pimento, salt and pepper.
Stir in crab meat and shrimp.
Add Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° until brown, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Dot with butter before baking.
Brown hamburg, onions and bacon.
Mix in sauce and beans. Cook in crock-pot.
Boil sugar and water until it spins a thread.
Do not stir. Add egg whites and vanilla to thick syrup.
Beat by hand until stiff. Roll out on powdered sugar board and spread with peanut butter about 1/2-inch thick all over.
Roll like jelly roll. Slice and eat.
Combine the sour cream, milk, chives, salt and pepper.
Add potatoes; mix.
Spread in a 15 x 10-inch baking pan.
Combine cheese and corn flakes; sprinkle over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Sprinkle with chives, if desired.
Combine soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and melted butter until smooth.
Place broccoli in casserole dish.
Add chicken and pour sauce on top.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
In greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish, combine chicken, broccoli and 1 cup cheese.
Blend soup and 3/4 cup milk; pour over casserole.
Bake, uncovered, 15 to 20 minutes or until biscuits are golden brown.
Top with remaining cheese and onions and bake 2 to 3 minutes.
Cook broccoli until dry.
Combine with cottage cheese.
Add eggs.
Add flour.
Add margarine.
Stir well after each ingredient. Place in glass casserole.
Spread cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Cream the sugar and shortening. Add eggs, one at a time. Combine flour, soda and salt. Add alternately with the buttermilk. Add flavoring. Bake 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Mix all ingredients and let set overnight.
Will keep for up to 10 days.
Also the longer it sits the hotter it will be. Excellent with pinto beans and cornbread.
Cream together sugar, margarine and shortening.
Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating after each one.
Mix together soda and buttermilk; add alternately with flour to first mixture.
Add nuts, coconut and vanilla.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into mixture.
Blend shortening and sugar thoroughly.
Add eggs, beating until smooth.
Sift flour with salt; add to mixture, beating vigorously.
Add flavoring.
Drop from spoon onto lightly greased cookie sheet, about 3 to 4 inches apart.
Place nut in center of each cookie.
Bake in a 350° oven for 10 minutes.
Mix together thoroughly, braunschweiger, ketchup and mayonnaise.
Form into loaf with damp hands as it will stick. Chill for 1 hour.
Frost with softened cream cheese (Philadelphia).
Cream cheese should be frosting consistency; thin with mayonnaise.
Serve with any type cracker.
Makes 20 (1 ounce) servings.
Very good to serve for weddings.
Enjoy!
Combine oats, flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Combine remaining ingredients and add to dry mixture.
Stir until moistened.
Fill paper-lined cups 3/4 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in food processor.
Puree thoroughly. Cover.
Chill overnight.
Serve with croutons.
Serves 6.
Cream jello and cream cheese and set aside.
Bring pineapple and sugar to a boil, then add cream cheese and jello.
Mix until dissolved.
Add cold water and put in refrigerator until thickened around edges.
Add Cool Whip and celery and refrigerate until solid.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in 9 x 13-inch pan that has been lined with crushed vanilla wafers.
Sprinkle vanilla wafers on top.
Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Mix all ingredients in large bowl.
Pour into greased pan and bake at 400° until brown!

Fry ham slowly, being careful not to overcook. Remove from pan. Make gravy in the pan ham was fried in. Pour a small amount of coffee or cream right from the pot. Add a little water and bring to a boil.
Toss all ingredients lightly except crumbs.
Place in buttered casserole; sprinkle crumbs on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°. (Freezes well.)
Combine flours, sugar, baking powder, salt and spices.
Add butter, cut in with pastry blender until coarsely mixed.
Make a well.
Add cream, milk and lemon zest.
Stir.
Add cranberries; stir until dough coheres.
Shape into ball.
Place in center of greased baking sheet.
Pat into a 9-inch disk.
Score deeply into 8 wedges.
Brush top with 1 tablespoon of cream and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Cut apart at score marks and serve hot.
Stir together bread pieces, white sugar, egg, 1 tablespoon flour and milk. Bake in oven until dry.
Stir together biscuit mix, oats, sugars and peel.
Beat together eggs, milk, juice and vanilla with rotary beater; add to flour mixture.
Stir until blended; let stand 5 minutes.
For each pancake, pour about 1/4 cup batter onto hot, lightly greased griddle.
Cook over medium-low heat for about 3 minutes until golden brown, turning once.
Cream margarine; add sugar and egg.
Combine dry ingredients and add to margarine mixture.
Stir in water, vanilla and chopped apples.
Spoon into greased pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until done.

recipes.t: Green Tomato Mincemeat For Pie Filling(Low Calorie!)
d: Chop tomatoes fine.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon salt over them and let stand 1/2 hour.
Drain.
Add chopped apples and raisins.
Cook until done.
(Tomatoes, apples and raisins may be ground in a meat grinder or chopped in a blender.) Add vinegar, cinnamon, cloves and sugar before cooking.
Drain potatoes very well and mash.
Add sugar, eggs, milk, 1/2 cup butter, coconut, vanilla and nutmeg.
Pour into a greased 9 x 12-inch casserole.
Combine brown sugar, flour, remaining 1/2 cup butter and nuts.
Sprinkle over mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Melt margarine in saucepan. Add onion and saute. Add broccoli with 1/3 cup water.
Cover and slowly bring to a simmer. Continue simmering until broccoli is thawed. Add soup and Cheez Whiz and simmer again.
Add rice; stir and pour into buttered baking dish. Bake at 325° approximately 45 to 50 minutes.
Mix all together.
Bake in greased casserole at 350° for 15 minutes.
Remove from oven and add bread crumbs and slivered pecans.
Return to oven for 15 minutes more to brown crumbs. Serve at once from the oven.
Cut up cabbage and boil until tender. Fry ground pork until brown; add seasonings, Ro-Tel tomatoes and cabbage.
Cook for about 45 minutes.
Add salt and black pepper to taste.
Add 1/2 cup bread crumbs to mixture. Cook about 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour into baking dish and sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° until bread crumbs are brown.

Place chocolate chips, condensed milk and butter in a large microwave-safe bowl. Microwave at Medium (50%) until chocolate chips are melted, about 5 minutes, stirring twice during cooking. Remove from microwave.
Stir in flavoring and nuts. Pour into a "Pam" sprayed 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Refrigerate until set.
(If you don't eat it all the first day, refrigerate any leftovers.)
Cook artichoke hearts as directed on package.
Rinse with cold water and cut each heart in half.
Chill.
Prepare remaining ingredients, keeping each separate.
Lightly toss together lettuce, half of the cauliflower, half the tomato and all the chives in a large salad bowl.
Arrange remaining ingredients in vertical rows over top of salad.
Dice vegetables.
Cover with chicken stock.
Add seasonings. Simmer until vegetables are soft.
Spoon vegetables into a blender and puree.
Return to chicken broth; add 1 can Cheddar cheese soup, undiluted.
Stir until smooth.
Adjust seasonings to taste; bring to boil.
Sprinkle each serving with a little shredded Cheddar cheese and paprika.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine liver spread, chopped pickle, mustard and margarine. Trim crust from bread.
Cut into 9 long slices; spread with oleo and 2 tablespoons mixture.
Place gherkin strip across narrow end of each slice and roll up like jelly roll.
Wrap tightly in damp linen towel.
Chill 2 hours.
Slice each strip into 8 pieces.
Mix Jell-O with water.
Add 7-Up.
Soften cream cheese.
Beat in pineapple, vanilla and sugar.
Mix Jell-O with cheese mixture and nuts.
Add desired amount of food coloring to give light green color.
Pour in 8 oiled Jell-O molds or in an 8 x 8-inch pan.

Remove kernels with paring knife and place in large bowl. Add tomato, onion and green pepper. Toss to combine. Add lime juice and olive oil. Snip cilantro and add to mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Serve.
Combine all ingredients in large bowl.
Mix well.
Chill for 1 hour.
In a large bowl, mix together the beef, rice, onion, egg, salt and pepper.
Shape into 6 patties.
Brown patties on both sides in oil.
Drain vegetables, reserving liquid.
Combine 1/2 cup of liquid and gravy.
Stir in gravy and drained vegetables and thyme. Pour over browned patties.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes.
In order given, layer ingredients in greased 2-quart baking dish.
Season each layer with salt and pepper.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 6 servings.
Shred cabbage.
Add other ingredients and mix.
Layer pineapple, nuts, cherry filling and coconut. Sprinkle dry cake mix on top. Drizzle melted margarine over cake mix. Bake at 350° until lightly browned.
Mix and bake at 475° about 15 to 20 minutes until brown.
In Dutch oven brown meat on both sides in hot oil.
Remove from heat; add onion, carrots, wine, garlic, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 1 3/4 to 2 hours or until meat is tender.
Meanwhile, pour 1 1/2 cups hot water over prunes and apricots.
Let stand while roast is cooking.
Drain, reserving liquid.
Place fruit atop meat.
Cover and cook 30 to 40 minutes more or until meat is tender.
Remove meat and fruit to warm platter.
Pour pan juices into measuring cup; skim off fat.
Add reserved fruit liquid to pan juices to make 1 1/2 cups.
Return to Dutch oven; blend together flour and 1/2 cup cold water.
Stir into juices.
Cook and stir until gravy is thickened and bubbly.
Spoon some gravy over roast; pass remaining gravy around.
Place pork chops in roaster.
Combine remaining ingredients. Pour over chops.
Cover.
Bake at 300° or until meat is tender and gravy thick.
Combine meat, green pepper, onion, chili powder and oregano; cook until meat is browned.
Drain off excess fat.
Remove from heat and add soup, water, enchilada sauce and garlic salt, combining well.
In a greased 9 x 12 x 3-inch casserole dish, place a layer of tortillas, then meat mixture and the cheese. Layer any remaining ingredients, ending with the meat mixture on top.
Refrigerate casserole for 24 hours or, if desired, freeze. To serve, bake at 350° for 45 minutes (longer if frozen).
Serves 10.
Combine all ingredients in saucepan and cook until candy is dissolved and mix is thick, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Pour into hot jars and seal.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch dish as listed.
Use the mayonnaise to seal in the vegetables.
Cover and chill 8 hours.
Add the bacon bits after chilling.
Crush Ritz crackers and spread in bottom of casserole dish. Melt butter and drizzle over crackers, mixing well.
Mix chicken broth, sour cream and cream of chicken soup together; boil, stirring until smooth.
Add cut up chicken to sour cream mixture and pour over Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° until sides are bubbly.
Prepare pastry shells as directed on package.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, melt margarine and cook half of chicken until browned; stir often.
Remove and cook remaining chicken. Reduce heat to medium-low, add 1 tablespoon margarine, cook broccoli and mushrooms until tender and liquid has evaporated, stir often.
Stir in soup, milk and mustard.
Heat to boiling. Return chicken to skillet.
Heat through, stirring occasionally. Spoon over pastry shells.
Serves 6.
Cook chicken until done. Tear into small pieces and line the bottom of a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Mix chicken soup with milk.
Pour over chicken. Put stuffing on top of soup mixture. Melt 1/2 stick of margarine and mix with 2/3 cup chicken broth. Pour over stuffing.
Bake for approximately 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Boil boneless, skinless chicken breast in water.
Cook until tender.
Chop into bite size pieces and mix together with the other ingredients.
Add salad dressing as you desire.
Serves 12.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Sift all but C, F and K together in a mixing bowl.
Add F and K; stir thoroughly with spoon.
Add C and mix.
Place heaping tablespoon in well-greased muffin pans.
Bake 15 minutes.
Mix chicken, soups, and bread crumbs to consistency for sandwiches.
Bake at 350° until hot.
Bake cake according to directions on box.
Cool.
Crumble 1 cake layer in large serving bowl.
Make pudding using the 3 cups milk.
Pour 1/2 pudding mixture over cake.	Spread 1/2 of pie filling over pudding.
Next spread 1/2 of pineapple, 1/2 of Cool Whip and 1 package of coconut.
Repeat all layers.
Place margarine in baking dish; melt in oven.
Heat peaches, 1/2 cup sugar and water in saucepan until sugar is dissolved, then bring to a boil.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt, remaining 1/2 cup sugar and milk in mixing bowl; stir until smooth.
Remove baking dish from oven; add batter, then peach mixture.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Crust will rise to top and brown.
In a large saucepan mix contents of soup can with equal amount of water.
Bring to a boil.
Fill can with Minute rice and add to boiling soup.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups cooked vegetables (broccoli, peas or green beans), 4 slices American cheese and 1 1/2 cup cooked meat or fish.
Stir, cover and remove from heat.
Let stand 10 minutes for rice to cook.
Beat the egg with a fork.
Bring the broth to a simmering point.
Remove from heat and slowly drizzle in the beaten egg, stirring slowly.
The egg should become stringy-looking rather than making the soup appear milky.
Garnish with parsley.
Serve hot.
Combine all ingredients except peaches.
Mix at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into well-greased deep dish pie plate.
Pour drained peaches over mixture.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Beat together oil and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating until well mixed.
Add vanilla.
Add flour and milk alternately, mixing well after each addition.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cool for 15 minutes before removing from pan.
Blend in blender until smooth.
Mix thoroughly all ingredients and serve.
May be used to make mock turkey, stuffing, etc.
Thaw puff pastry for 20 minutes.
Combine apples, raisins, cinnamon, sugar, nuts and crumbs.
Unfold and roll out each pastry square to 13 x 10-inch rectangle.
Place half the apple mixture along center line of pastry (lengthwise).
Brush edges with beaten egg yolks.
Fold dough over filling, pressing edges together to seal.
Place seam-side down on greased rimmed baking sheet. Repeat with remaining pastry.
Brush tops with egg yolks.
Brown beef or sausage. Stir in seasoning blend. Cook for 5 minutes. Add broth, soup and potatoes. Simmer for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Put everything together in a pot except the rice.
After it has boiled abut 45 minutes, add rice.
Boil until it gets thick. Add some water, if needed.
Also taste for salt.
Serves 2 or 3 people.
Cook and drain macaroni.
Mix together cream of mushroom soup, cream of chicken soup and milk until hot, then add seasonings and butter.
Mix together with macaroni and chicken.
Place in greased casserole.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Mix brown sugar, margarine, water and vanilla.
Stir in flour and salt until dough holds together (if dough is dry, stir in 1 to 2 teaspoons of water). Cut caramels into fourths.
Shape dough by teaspoonfuls around caramel pieces.
Press dough into center of each pecan half.
Bake until done, 12 to 15 minutes.
Cool.
Prepare cake mix as directed on package.
Chop 2 squares of the chocolate into cake mix.
Bake cake in 4 layers.
Trim semi-frozen meat and slice 1/8 to 1/4-inch thick strips. In bowl, combine all ingredients except meat.
Stir until dissolved.
Add meat; coat thoroughly.
Let stand 1 hour or refrigerate overnight.
Meat will absorb liquid.
Remove excess liquid.
Arrange strips close together on oven or cake racks in shallow pans.
Dry meat on lowest temperature (150° to 200°) until it turns brown and feels hard (4 to 7 hours).
Pat off beads of oil.
Cool and store in airtight bags or jars.
Keeps indefinitely.
Makes 1/2 pound.
Can also be dried on top of wood stove on racks and pans.
Turn strips often though.
Very economical.
Prepare apples, core and chop up.
Cut up peaches.
Add dates. Blend slow in blender until smooth.
Very good!
Combine flour, salt and pepper and pound into steak.
In large skillet, brown steak in hot oil on both sides.
Add chopped vegetables, tomatoes or soup mixture.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours or until tender.
Serve over mashed potatoes or rice or egg noodles.
Saute the onion in the oil in a medium size saucepan until tender.

Add the tomato paste, tomato sauce, water, oregano, basil, salt and pepper. Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes. Preheat the oven to 375°. Stir gently to mix. Turn into the prepared casserole.
Add the remaining tomato sauce. Sprinkle with the remaining Mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until the cheese is melted and browned.
Wash eggplant and saute in oil with onions, tomato and garlic. Steam artichokes until done.
Stuff with eggplant mixture and serve hot.
Mix sugar and flour in large microwave bowl; gradually add milk (evaporated milk can be used).
Stir in eggs real well. Microwave 3 minutes.
Stir.
Cook in microwave 2 additional minutes.
Stir.
Cook until creamy or until desired thickness. Crumble vanilla wafers into pudding and add sliced bananas.
Top with whole vanilla wafers.

Enough for two and company, too.

orange juice
Mix well.
Heat oil in skillet.
Dip bread slices into egg mixture. Fry in oil until lightly browned on each side.
Serve with syrup, powdered sugar and apple butter.
Let bread thaw and rise, as per the package instructions. Roll as flat as possible.
Top with butter, cheese and pepperoni. Roll up like a jelly roll.
Spread egg over top and seal.
Bake on foiled cookie sheet at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cook noodles. Lightly brown hamburger and onion; stir in noodles. Pour into casserole. Mix 1 cup bread crumbs with 3 tablespoons butter. Sprinkle on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Coat bottom of 9 x 5-inch loaf pan with vegetable cooking spray. Dust pan with 1 teaspoon flour.
Set aside.
Layer in a shallow Pyrex dish in order. Put in microwave for 5 minutes (longer for some microwaves). Serve with chips.
Season the steak and place it on a well floured cutting board. Cover the	steak
with
flour and pound it with a meat hammer. Continue

up by the steak.
Peel, core and chop apples into bite size pieces (sprinkle with lemon juice so they won't turn brown).
Add celery, raisins, cherries and 3/4 cup pecans.
Mix well.
Add 1 tablespoon sugar to mayonnaise and beat until smooth.
Pour over mixture and toss. (You might have to use more or less mayonnaise.)
Place mixture in serving dish and sprinkle the top with celery seed and the remainder of the pecans.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients except cheese. Make 1/2 loaf.
Lay cheese on top of meat.
Top with remainder of meat and cheese.
Bake for 1 hour.
Combine honey, mustard and lemon juice in mixing bowl; beat thoroughly.
Grill ham steaks slowly over charcoal or cook under broiler. Brush frequently with honey sauce until brown and glazed on both sides.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Combine picante sauce, water and tomato sauce.
Stir 1/2 cup ground beef along with chilies, 1/2 cheese, 1/2 cup French fried onions and mix well. Pour 1/2 of remaining sauce mixture in bottom of a 10-inch round or 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Rinse beans well, trim stem ends and cut beans lengthwise (French-style).
Melt butter or margarine in medium-size skillet over medium heat; stir in chicken broth.
Add beans; bring liquid to boil.
Reduce heat and cook (covered) about 18 minutes.
Add bell pepper, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cook, uncovered, an additional 5 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Add sliced squash and water.
Cook, covered on low until done.
Scorching slightly adds to taste!
Salt and pepper to taste.

pie
crust.

dough
into cookie press and form dough in long lines on cookie sheet.

separate slightly.

Shake first 3 ingredients in bag with chicken until coated. Saute in oil until golden brown.
Mix remaining ingredients in bowl and add to chicken.
Simmer until chicken is cooked.
Serve with rice.
Cube 3 to
bananas,	sprinkle with lemon juice.
Add Eagle Brand milk, Cool Whip, cherry pie filling and nuts.
Mix and freeze.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray a 13 x 9-inch pan with nonstick coating.
Spread chilies in bottom of dish.
Cover chilies with cheese.
Mix remaining ingredients in blender until well blended. Pour mixture over chilies and cheese.
Bake 45 minutes in a 350° oven.
Serves 6 to 8.
Also good cold, cut into 1-inch squares for hors d'oeuvres.
Cream the cream cheese with sugar and mayonnaise.
Add pineapple (drained) and cranberry sauce.
Use mixer to mix well. Add Cool Whip.
Put into cupcake liners and freeze.
Or can be frozen in any dish desired.
Thaw slightly before serving.
A good way to store in freezer is to let mixture freeze and put into Ziploc bags.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Butter and flour a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Place sugar, butter and water in a heavy saucepan and bring just to a boil; remove from heat.
Add chocolate chips and stir until smooth; blend in vanilla.
Transfer to a large mixing bowl and beat in the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix all ingredients. Bake 350 degrees till done. When cool top with frosting:
Simmer tomatoes in a large skillet for 10 to 15 minutes or until tomato liquid is reduced by about half.
Add shrimp; simmer just until they begin to turn pink; sprinkle with cheese.
Cover skillet; simmer about 5 minutes longer or until shrimp are cooked and cheese is hot.
Spoon rice onto a large serving platter; top with shrimp mixture.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Put blueberries in bottom of 8 x 8-inch pan.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, melted shortening, 1/2 cup sugar and milk. Spread over berries.
Mix 1/2 cup sugar, cornstarch and water. Pour over mix.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serve warm or cold with whipped topping.
Place patties in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Heat the water, white sugar and brown sugar.
Heat until sugar is melted good; pour over patties.
Dot with butter and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° until syrup is thick and they are bubbly.
Mix all ingredients and bake in greased and floured Bundt pan at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.t: Pork Tenderloin With Sherry And Cream Gravy
d: Tie 2 pieces of tenderloin together in 3 or 4 places.
Season with Worcestershire sauce, poultry seasoning and garlic powder. Place in baking pan (use meat thermometer).
Cook at 350° until thermometer reads 180°.
(Well done pork reading on thermometer.) Remove from pan when done.
Let rest 10 minutes.
Slice and put on serving platter.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Grease a 2 inch muffin tin. Combine bran and milk in a bowl and let sit for 5 minutes.
Then mash with the back of spoon.
Sift together the flour and sugar and add to bran.
Add the beaten egg and the melted butter and stir until well blended, Do not beat.
Stir in the nuts and raisins. Divide batter amount the muffin cups.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes. Makes 12 muffins.
Put jello in bowl; add hot water and stir until jello is dissolved.
Add cold water.
Drain cherries and pineapple and add juice of both to jello.
Cook broccoli according to package directions.
Meanwhile, cook bacon and garlic until bacon is crisp.
Add vinegar; heat. Brown bread crumbs in butter.
Pour sauce over hot broccoli and sprinkle with crumbs.
Makes 3 servings.
Cook macaroni in boiling salted water; drain and rinse. Combine the mushroom soup, milk, onion and seasoning.
Alternate layers of macaroni, soup and cheese in greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° about 45 minutes.

Top with cheese.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

Put in a casserole dish.
Top with crushed potato chips.

Mix together margarine, cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Mix pudding with milk and vanilla in a separate bowl.

Layer cookies, then pudding, cream cheese mixture, ending with crushed cookies.

Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Stir in pineapple.
Fold in bread cubes.
Turn into greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 1 hour.

Brown meat and onion.
Layer in dish hamburger, cheese, pepperoni, cheese and so forth, ending with biscuit mix on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Thoroughly mix all ingredients except margarine and crackers. Place the vegetable mixture in a 9 X 13 casserole dish.

Spread evenly over the vegetable mixture.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.

Shape into a loaf.
Mix the remaining ingredients and pour over meat loaf.
Bake, covered, for 1 1/2 hours and
uncovered for 1/2 hour at 350°.
Blend on high speed in blender, chopped cucumber and chicken broth 2 minutes.
Add sour cream.
Continue to blend 2 more minutes at high speed.
Chill before serving.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Mix eggs, milk and vanilla and add to dry mixture.

Uncover and continue baking 20 to 30 minutes more.

In another bowl, beat yolks until foamy.

Put first 3 ingredients in microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave 45 to 60 seconds or until melted (shiny).
Stir until well blended. Stir in nuts.
(You can use any nuts.)
Drop by teaspoons onto a wax paper-lined cookie sheet.
Place cookie sheet in refrigerator for about an hour.
Remove candy and place in Tupperware or tin with wax paper between layers.
Keep in refrigerator.
Delicious!
Layer crushed chips in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread diced chicken over chips.
Sprinkle onion and pepper.
Mix soup, undiluted, and spread.
Pour Ro-Tel over top.
Bake 25 minutes.
Last 10 minutes, cover with Monterey Jack or Cheddar cheese.
Boil chicken and save at least 1 1/2-quarts broth.
If not enough broth, use 1 can of chicken broth with water to make 1 1/2-quarts.
Saute onion, bell pepper and celery in butter.
Mix sugar, syrup and peanut butter.
Add cereal and shape mixture into balls.
Roll in confectioners sugar or coconut.
Place peeled, sliced apples in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour water over the apples.
Mix sugars, flour and margarine as for pie crust.
Spread
on	top
of apples.
Bake until apples are done. Serve with ice cream or whipped cream.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 10-inch pie pan or 9-inch square pan.
Cook spaghetti to desired tenderness; drain and set aside. Brown the beef with celery; drain.
Stir in spaghetti sauce and mushrooms; simmer 15 minutes.
Combine spaghetti, eggs, Parmesan cheese and garlic salt; toss.
Place mixture in the prepared pan. Press evenly over bottom and up sides, forming a crust.
Pour meat mixture over spaghetti.
Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese.
Prepare stuffing according to package.
Combine milk and meat. Make patties and pat to 6-inch circle.
Top with stuffing.
Draw meat up and over to cover stuffing.
Place in casserole and pour remaining ingredients (combined) over all.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 minutes.

recipes.t: New Potatoes With Black Peppercorn Butter
d: Combine broth and peppercorns in a small sauce pan.
Cover and simmer until reduced to 1/4 cup.
Add Brandy and simmer until reduced to about 3 Tbsp.
Cool.
Blend peppercorns, butter, lemon juice, shallots and Thyme in processor until peppercorns are finely chopped.
Cook potatoes until tender, and quarter.
Place in a large bowl.
Add green onions and 1/4 c. peppercorn butter. Reserve remaining butter for another use.
Toss gently.
Season with salt.
Prepare Cobbler Topping.
In large mixer bowl, beat together eggs and sugar.
Add cream, pudding mix, vanilla and salt; beat well.
Mix in pie filling.
Pour into 4 to 5-quart ice cream freezer.
Add milk.
Freeze according to manufacturer's directions.
Remove dasher.
Add Cobbler Topping and stir until well mixed.
Ripen ice cream.
Makes 4 quarts.
Make stuffing on stove according to directions.
Set aside.
Separate crescent rolls into three layers.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
Mix crab mixture together and spoon onto layer of crescent rolls.
Bake 10 minutes in 400° oven.
Makes 36 appetizers.
Cook onion and celery in butter until tender.
Stir in flour, gravy or cream, salt and chicken.
Roll out dough on lightly floured surface to about 1/8-inch thickness.
Cut dough into 4-inch squares.
Spoon chicken mixture onto 1/2 of each square and fold over to make triangles.
Press edges of dough together to seal.
Stick top with fork to let steam escape.
Bake in greased pan at 425° about 30 minutes until browned.
Melt butter and chocolate; blend in cocoa and sugar.
Stir in cream.
Bring to a rolling boil for 10 seconds.
Makes 12 ounces.
Combine flours, sugar, poppy seed and baking soda; stir.
Add yogurt, egg white, vanilla and nuts.
Pour in muffin cups sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Bake at 350° for 16 minutes.
Fry sausage with onion.
Put into casserole dish.
Drain sauerkraut and put on top of sausage.
Make mashed potatoes and, while whipping potatoes, add grated Cheddar cheese.
Put on top of sauerkraut; sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Bake for about 30 minutes at 375°.
Enjoy.
Brown meat and drain.
Mix soup mix in water and pour over meat.
Mix well and let simmer for about 30 minutes.
Serve over noodles, rice or creamed potatoes.
Mix all dry ingredients first.
Add liquid ingredients.
Cook on top of stove until mixture becomes firm.
Pour into pie shells already browned.
Save egg whites for icing to go on top of pies. This recipe makes 2 pies.
Whip soup and milk in a 2-quart bowl.
Stir in remaining ingredients except 1/4 cup cheese.
Cover with lid or vented plastic, wrap and refrigerate 12 hours or overnight.
Microwave on High for 15 to 17 minutes.
Sprinkle reserved cheese on top. Let stand 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Serves 4.
Place potatoes and water in 3-quart casserole.
Cook, covered, on power 20 to 25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir halfway through cooking.
Drain.
Beat together cream cheese, onion dip, salt, pepper and garlic salt in large mixing bowl until well blended.
Add hot potatoes one at a time, beating until light and fluffy.
Spoon potatoes in 2-quart casserole.
Dot with margarine as desired.
Heat, covered, on full power 4 to 6 minutes or until heated through.
Sprinkle with paprika as desired before serving.
Brown hamburger meat with onions; pour off drippings. Add tomato sauce; rinse can with water (1/2 cup more or less).
Use this water. Add chili powder, butter, vinegar and sugar. Simmer 15 minutes, then add beans and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more. Salt to your taste.
Place chicken in an oblong dish.
Top with cheese.
Stir soup according to directions.
Spread over cheese.
Combine butter and stuffing.
Sprinkle on top of soup.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes or until chicken is done.
Serve over rice.
Garnish with oregano.
Beat egg in a saucepan.
Add vinegar, salt, pepper and mustard.
Cook slowly over low heat, stirring constantly (don't curdle).
Add currant jelly and catsup.
Heat.
Serve on ham. (This is a tangy, delicious sauce.)
Melt butter in 9 x 12 x 2-inch brownie pan.
Spread crumbs over it.
Sprinkle coconut over that.
Sprinkle chocolate morsels over that.
Sprinkle peanut butter morsels over that.
Pour canned sweetened condensed milk over that.
Top with nuts.
Bake in 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cut into squares while still warm.
Use large mushrooms.
Wipe clean with paper towel.
Never wash or peel.
Break stems off and cut them up.
Saute chopped onion and celery until tender in butter.
Add chopped mushroom stems when onion and celery mix is partially done.
Saute until golden. Use plenty of butter.
Add Italian seasoned bread crumbs and mix. Stuff raw mushroom caps and cook or freeze.
Don't cook before freezing.
In Dutch oven, saute onions and garlic until golden.
Add brown sugar and cook until caramelized.
Add other ingredients and simmer 15 minutes.
Add meat.
Bake, covered, for 5 or 6 hours at 325°.
Uncover last half hour.
Remove from oven and shred meat with 2 forks and return to sauce.
Can be frozen.
Mix all ingredients except bread.
Slice off top 1/4 of bread and hollow out carefully.
Make sure there are no weak points. Fill shell with mixture.
Put bread top back on.
Wrap in foil and bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours or at 350° for 1 hour.
Bread from the top and inside are used as dippers.
(You will need additional bread.)
Shell
and,
if necessary, devein shrimp.
Slice garlic and ginger
into
thin	slices;
add to butter in frying pan. Cook
on medium
heat.
Add
peppers and, lastly, the shrimp. Cook only until shrimp turns red; do not overcook.
Break large head of lettuce into bite size pieces.
Put in
a large bowl.
Add celery, onion, green pepper and peas.
Salt lightly.
Spread with one pint Thousand Island dressing.
Be sure to cover all ingredients well.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Add cheese. Add bacon.
Cover with aluminum foil and refrigerate for at least 8 hours.
In a mixing bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add eggs, milk and oil.
Blend just until moistened.
Spoon into a greased baking pan (8 or 9-inch square). Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spread pie filling in bottom of 9-inch square pan.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Combine dry cake mix, nuts and melted butter.
Mixture should be crumbly.
Sprinkle over pie filling.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes, until golden brown.
Serve with ice cream, whipped cream or serve warm with coffee cream.
Melt oleo; pour over the bread.
Beat eggs; add sugar and pineapple.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Good with ham.
Drain beans and corn.
Mix all ingredients together, except crackers and margarine.
Pour into greased casserole.
Crush crackers and toss with melted margarine.
Top casserole with crackers and margarine mix.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Spread English muffins with butter or margarine.
Sprinkle with garlic salt.
Top generously with Parmesan cheese and sprinkle on some dried oregano.
Place under broiler flame until browned.
These can also be cut into fours before being put under broiler and served as party tidbits.
Mix all together and fold in Cool Whip.
Spoon into graham cracker crusts.
Chill until firm.
Makes 2 pies.
Mix cake mix as on package; pour 1/2 of batter in 13 x 9-inch greased and floured pan.
Bake for 15 minutes at 350°.
Trim fat from meat.
Cut into 1-inch cubes.
In skillet, brown meat in shortening.
Pour off fat.
Add remaining ingredients, except beans.
Cover; cook over low heat 1 hour.
Stir now and then.
Remove bay leaf.
Chill overnight.
Melt together chocolate and butter.
Add eggs and sugar; beat well.
Add milk, flour, nuts and salt.
Pour into well-greased and floured pan and bake 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Turn out on waxed paper and do not disturb until cold.
Cut and roll in powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Prick and bake pastry 5 minutes.
Use quiche pan or standard pie plate.
Cook bacon crisp.
Remove from skillet.
Pour off all but 1 teaspoon of fat.
Cook onion in fat. Crumble bacon over crust with onion and cheese.
Mix soups, milk, mushrooms and pimento.
Fold in cooked chicken; let stand about 12 hours.
Add noodles; place in buttered casserole and sprinkle with almonds.
No salt is needed.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Makes 12 servings.

recipes.t: Our Best Brownies(A Delightful, Chewy Treat)
d: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease and flour an 8-inch square pan.
In a medium bowl, combine eggs, vanilla and Brownie Mix.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in nuts. Pour into prepared pan. Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until edges separate from pan.
Cool.
Cut into 2-inch bars.
Sprinkle or frost with Brownie Topper of your choice.
Makes 16 brownies.
Combine sugar and flour; blend in margarine (melted).
Add egg yolks, milk and water and cook until nice and thick.
Pour into pie shell.
In a mixing bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix in the corn meal and sugar.
Add, mixing only until dry ingredients are moistened, the oil, eggs, milk, zucchini, cheese and onion.
Mix all ingredients together.
In small baking paper cups, drop heaping teaspoonful in cups.
Place cups on baking sheet and bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350°.
Mix the mayonnaise, sugar and pickle juice.
Toss all together and serve.
Melt butter; blend in cornstarch.
Add honey, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture boils.
Add glaze to sliced carrots and grapes.
Stir to mix.
Brown onion and green pepper in 1 tablespoon cooking oil.
Add ground beef.
Cook until beef is done.
Drain well.
Put back on heat; add Ragu, mushrooms and sauce mix.
Simmer at least 1 hour or longer.
Layer cottage cheese and lasagna (cooked until soft) in casserole dish until 1/2 inch from top.
Top with Mozzarella cheese.
Cook for 30 minutes at 400°.
Mix first four ingredients.
Sift flour and add baking soda and baking powder.
Mix into other ingredients and add vanilla and nutmeg.
Refrigerate dough overnight.

recipes.t: Tangle Britches(An Old York County, Pa Recipe)
d: Cream together the butter and sugar.
Add eggs, beating well. Sift in the cinnamon and enough flour to make a stiff dough.
Roll out the dough very thin on a floured board to about 1/8 inch thick.
Cut into rectangular pieces (3 x 5-inch).
Make 5 cups lengthwise in the dough 1/2 inch apart and 4 1/2 inches long so that the rectangle remains on one piece.
Fry in hot, deep fat (360°) for 2 minutes or until they bob up to the top of the hot grease.
When dropping them into the fryer, pick up the first, third and fifth strips and pull them upward.

Let the second, fourth and sixth sag downward so that in frying, they get all tangled or as the Dutch say, "all through each other." Dust with powdered sugar or dribble molasses over them and eat hot.
Combine
ground
beef,
onion,
garlic and pepper; cook until meat
loses
its
redness.
Stir in soup, mushrooms and salt; stir
well and cook until bubbling.
Stir in sour cream and heat. Serve over noodles or rice.
Peel sweet potatoes or yams. Cut into thick slices.
Rinse in cold water.

Cover sweet potatoes or yams with water (use small amount of water as potatoes already have water in them). Bring to a boil (30 minutes). Add all the ingredients except for the marshmallows and butter.
When potatoes are done, sprinkle with marshmallows and butter and heat until marshmallows and butter are melted slightly.
Whip all ingredients, except for vegetable oil, flour and powdered sugar.
Slowly add flour until the batter is satiny. Roll out on a well floured board (the thinner the better).
Cut into long strips, then cut strips into 4 to 5-inch strips.
Slit these strips in the center and pull one end through to make a bow tie.
Deep fry these, about 6 to 8 at a time.
When golden, remove from hot oil.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Enjoy!!
Put a layer of cake squares into bowl.
Put a layer of cherries, layer of French vanilla pudding and a layer of pineapple.
Keep alternating the layers until all ingredients are used.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 4 to 6 mini loaf pans.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
With pastry blender or two knives scissor fashion, cut in shortening until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Let hash browns thaw completely.
Mix in order given.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, uncovered, in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cream together the sugar and margarine until well blended. Add the eggs and beat well. Add the remaining ingredients and mix until blended.
Pour into a greased loaf pan and bake in a 375° oven for 1 hour.
Place all ingredients in mixer; beat 4 minutes.
Pour into 3 pans (8 or 9-inch).
Bake at 350° for about 35 to 40 minutes.
Pick through crab to remove shell.
Put it in a 2-quart casserole dish and set aside.
Saute onion in butter.
Remove from heat and add flour.
Set back on heat and add milk immediately. Stir constantly until mixture thickens and comes to a boil.
Add shredded cheese and stir quickly until it melts.
Remove from heat.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Gently mix it with crabmeat in the casserole dish.
(Top with buttered bread crumbs.)
Bake at 325° for 30 to 45 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Can sprinkle with paprika before baking.
Soften onion in sherry or water.
Add to cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Chop finely the smoked beef and olives. Add to cream cheese mixture.
Mix well.
Form into ball or log. Chill.
Serve with crackers.
Mix sugar, soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic and ginger until smooth.
Pour over chicken and marinate several hours or overnight.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into lightly greased casserole dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Brown meat and chopped onion; drain.
Place meat mixture and the rest of ingredients in a large kettle or Dutch oven.
Simmer for 1 hour.
Stir occasionally.
Mix milk and egg together; pour ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Put all ingredients into a blender.
Whip it up and there you have an imitation of the brand name prepared item.
Saute chopped onion and garlic in vegetable oil.
Add chopped tomatoes and tomato sauce.
Add salt, basil, oregano and sugar. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine first 5 ingredients.
In small bowl, combine remaining ingredients, except lettuce.
Pour over chicken mixture; mix well.
Cover and chill at least 3 hours.
Line serving bowl with lettuce leaves; spoon salad over lettuce.
Makes 4 servings.
Each serving provides:
1 bread exchange, 4 vegetable exchange, 2 fat exchange, 3 calories optional exchange and 3 protein exchanges.
Use a 4-quart nonmetal container.
Mix lemonade and lime concentrate, powdered sugar and egg whites with a whip.
Add crushed ice and club soda.
Serve in salt rimmed glasses.
Add to the eggs the salt and melted butter, then add the milk and flour, sifted with baking powder.
Stir in the well beaten corn.
Fry in small spoonfuls in plenty of hot lard.
Chill a small mixing bowl.
Soften gelatin with 2 teaspoons cold water, then add the boiling water, stirring, until gelatin is completely dissolved.
Cool until tepid.
Place ice water and nonfat dry milk in the chilled mixing bowl.
Beat at high speed until the mixture forms stiff peaks.
Add the sugar, still beating, then the oil and the gelatin.
Place in freezer for about 15 minutes, then transfer to the refrigerator until ready for use. Stir before using to retain a creamy mixture.
Yield: 2 cups.
May substitute regular hash browns for hash browns O'Brien with onions and peppers.
This would eliminate the oleo and onion. May also use Fiesta Cheddar cheese soup with peppers, instead of the regular Cheddar cheese soup.
In a saucepan, combine pineapple and cornstarch. Stir. Add honey, soy sauce and cider vinegar.
Heat ingredients for 5 minutes until thickened.
This sauce is poured over sliced ham when it is served.
Do not pour over ham when it is baking.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour Bundt cake pan, shaking out excess.
Combine first 7 ingredients in large bowl and beat thoroughly.
Pour into pan.
Bake until tester inserted in center comes out clean, about 50 to 60 minutes.
Let cool 5 minutes in pan, then invert onto rack.
Heat oil in large skillet.
Add onion and garlic, cook and stir until tender but not browned.
Stir in beans, tomatoes, water and oregano.
Bring to boil.
Stir in rice.
Return to boil. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Recipe can be doubled.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In small saucepan, combine sugar, butter, water, salt and lemon juice.
Bring to a boil; cook briefly until syrupy.
Add zest.

Lightly smear a Pyrex (not aluminum) baking dish with butter (it's best to choose a dish you plan to serve it in, because transferring baked bananas is a tricky job). Split bananas in half lengthwise and place in dish so that they are cut side down and not overlapping.
Immediately cover bananas with syrup and pop in oven.
Bake for a total of 30 minutes.
After 10 minutes, baste them with syrup.
Repeat 10 minutes later.
Mix and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Let it boil 1 minute, then add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Mix well for 1 minute. Serve warm.
Put all ingredients into a baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Run cold water over vegetables to separate.

Cook meat and onions until meat is brown; drain. Stir vegetables and 1/4 cup water into meat. Cook, covered, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in soup and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Put mixture in 1 1/2-quart casserole. Prepare potatoes according to package directions.
Put over top of meat mixture.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Sprinkle cheese over top the last 5 minutes of baking. Serves 4.
Heat oil in a seasoned cast-iron skillet at 350°.
Mix the remaining ingredients together.
Remove the hot oil from the oven and add oil to the mix.
Pour mixture into hot skillet and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Melt oleo.
Add garlic salt,
basil and parsley.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Cut buns into quarters, then half the quarters.
Brush with oleo mixture on cut side.
Place on cookie sheet and bake until crisp and lightly browned, about 30 minutes.
Store in tightly closed container.
Enjoy!
Place garlic, basil, tomatoes, olive oil and Parmesan cheese together in large bowl.
Cook pasta according to directions and drain well.
While still hot, toss pasta with other ingredients. Cover and cool.
Best when eaten warm.

Mix the crumbs and baking powder; set aside. Beat the egg whites until stiff, then gradually add the sugar. Fold in the cracker crumbs. Add the vanilla and nuts. Place in paper muffin cups and bake until very light brown at 325°.
Be very careful not to overbake. Top with whipped cream and cherries.
Melt cream cheese in double boiler.
Add milk; stir until smooth.
Add garlic, salt and Parmesan cheese.
Stir again. Serve with dry French bread.
Cut into squares or strips.
Saute onion in small amount of oleo.
Add chicken broth and potatoes.
When potatoes are done add Velveeta, salt, pepper and sugar (1 teaspoon).
Thin with milk if desired.
Combine sugar and cornstarch in saucepan. Blend in butter and boiling water.
Add chocolate. Cook, stirring constantly, until chocolate melts and mixture becomes thick and smooth. Remove from heat. Blend in 1/2 tsp. vanilla.
Cool to lukewarm. Frosts 1 eight or nine inch layer cake.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Shake flour in oven bag and place in large baking pan.
Add barbecue sauce and chili powder and squeeze bag to blend.
Add onion and beef; turn bag to coat.
Tie off bag and bake for 45 minutes.
Divide mixture evenly onto rolls.
Mix together ingredients and cover with barbecue sauce.
Cook in crock-pot for 5 to 6 hours.
Prepare and bake cake mix as directed on package for 13 x 9-inch cake.
Remove from oven.
Poke holes at once down through cake to pan with round handle of wooden spoon.
Holes should be at 1 inch spaces.
After holes are made, combine pudding mix with sugar in large bowl.
Gradually stir in milk.
Beat with electric mixer at low speed for not more than 1 minute.
Quickly pour half of thin pudding over warm cake and into holes.
Let rest of pudding sit for 1 minute, then spoon and swirl over cake.
Chill in refrigerator.
Mix all ingredients except for cheese.
Pour half of mixture in hot skillet.
Sprinkle half of cheese on top.
Pour rest of mixture on top of cheese.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake at 375° until brown.
Mix first 3 ingredients together.
Roll out thin.
Cut in 2 or 3-inch squares.
Put 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of raspberry, strawberry or apricot jam on each.
Fold over to make triangles.
Seal edges. Or use a donut cutter and cut circles for bases and circles with holes to go on top.
Seal edges and put jam in centers.
This method makes very attractive cookies.
Be sure to seal the two layers together and use only 1/2 teaspoon of jam on each cookie or the jam will "boil over."
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove and put on brown paper to absorb oil.
Yields 3 1/2 dozen.
Dissolve yeast in the warm water.
Stir in 5 cups of flour, then stir in the rest, little by little, adding only enough to make a dough.
Turn out on floured board and knead until dough is smooth and elastic and doesn't stick to your hands.
Pat into a ball.
Pour 1/2 teaspoon of oil into palm of your hand and roll dough ball around until it is coated.
Put in bowl; cover with towel and let rise until doubled, 30 to 40 minutes.
Punch down and divide into two portions.
With your hands, flatten out each portion to a plate-size round.
Brush rest of oil on top of rounds.
Sprinkle one with sesame seed and the other with Italian seasoning.
Put on baking sheets; cover with bowls and let rise until doubled, about 30 minutes.
Bake in preheated 400° oven for 20 to 30 minutes until golden on top.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook sausage, onion, celery, green pepper and garlic until meat is no
longer pink and vegetables are tender; drain. Add cream cheese, green onion and parsley. Cook and stir over low heat until cheese is melted. Set aside.
Chill all ingredients.
Combine each one finishing with ginger ale.
Makes 2 1/2 quarts.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly in bowl.
Bake at 375 degrees for 1 hour in loaf pan covered with foil.
Uncover and bake for 10 more minutes to brown top.
Dissolve Jell-O.
Add cranberries, apples, sugar and nuts.
Add celery and crushed pineapple, if desired.
Pour into individual cups, decorative mold or 9 x 9-inch pan.
Let set.
Place crushed Rice Krispies cereal and seasonings in large plastic food bag.
Shake to blend well.
Brush chicken on all sides with mayonnaise.
Place one piece at a time in bag; shake to coat well.
Place on rack in broiler pan.
Bake at 425° for 40 to 45 minutes or until golden brown and tender.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix butter, sugar, vanilla wafers and cocoa.
Mix well.
Add oats and mix.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Roll in 36 balls and roll them in powdered sugar.
Store in fridge.
Brown beef and drain.
Add tomato paste and sugar.
Mix eggs, Parmesan cheese, parsley flakes and pepper.
In 13 x 9-inch pan, layer beef mixture, noodles, cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese. Repeat layers.
Cook for 30 minutes at 350°.
Toss the oranges and spinach.
Add desired rice vinegar and olive oil.
Sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Whip egg whites while gradually adding sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold in vanilla.
Stir in chips and nuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto parchment lined baking sheets.
Put into oven and IMMEDIATELY TURN OFF OVEN.
Leave overnight or at least 8 hours in turned off oven.
Do not open oven door during this time.
Crush cookies; add melted margarine.
Mix well.
Grease a 9 x 13 pan and line with cookie mixture.
Soften ice cream at room temperature and spread on top of cookies.
Melt 1/4 cup margarine and unsweetened chocolate.
Add sugar and evaporated milk.
Cook and stir for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Drizzle over ice cream.
Freeze overnight.
Serves 12.
Combine tomato sauce, water, onion, green pepper, butter, salt, sugar, mustard and pepper in saucepan.
Cover and bring to a full boil.
Stir in rice.
Remove from heat; cover and let stand 5 minutes.
Stir with a fork.
Makes 3 1/2 cups or 4 servings.
Cream sugar and Crisco. Add milk and flour alternately. Add soda; mix well. Add eggs (one at a time). Add flavoring. Grease and flour tube pan. Bake 1 hour in 350° oven (in a cold oven).
Mix, form into small meatballs and place in casserole dish.
Cut broccoli into bite size pieces.
In salad bowl, mix broccoli, onion, cheeses and bacon.
Mix mayo, sugar and vinegar and add to broccoli mixture.
Toss well.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients, except tomato and avocado.
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Just before serving, stir in tomato and avocado.
Has 120 calories.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth. Makes a great healthful treat with virtually no fat.
Add any fruits to make different combinations.
Combine all ingredients except the spinach and strawberries. Toss with the spinach and strawberries just before serving.
Mix all ingredients in bowl.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Brown and crumble meat.
In a large mixing bowl, combine 2 cans of enchilada sauce, tomato soup and 1 tomato soup can of water; mix well.
Lay one side of tortilla in sauce and then drop meat and cheese on that side.
Roll it up and put, seam side down, in a rectangular 13 x 9-inch pan that has been greased.
When pan is full, pour remaining sauce over enchiladas.
For more sauce, use other can.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Cover pan with foil; cook at 350° for about 1 hour.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add oil, eggs, water, apples and nuts. Bake 1 hour at 325° in greased and floured pan.
Blend together butter, garlic powder, minced onion and set aside.
Combine pumpkin, sugar, oil and egg in a large mixing bowl. Beat well.
Combine remaining ingredients except walnuts.
Add to pumpkin mixture, mixing well.
Stir in walnuts.
Spoon into a 9 1/4 x 5 1/4 x 2 3/4-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Yields 1 loaf.
Cook potatoes in skins.
Cool, peel and shred coarsely.
In saucepan, melt butter over low heat.
Add cheese and stir until almost melted.
Remove from heat and blend in sour cream, salt and pepper.
Mix with shredded potatoes.
Bake in a 2-quart casserole and sprinkle with paprika for color.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until heated through.
Best if made day before and stored in refrigerator until ready to bake.
Press crescent rolls into 15x10x1 inch baking sheet.
Bake at 350 degrees for 12 - 15 min.
Cool before adding topping.
Combine cream cheese and next 3 ingredients, spread over cooled crust, top with chopped veggies.
Sprinkle top with salad supreme (Mrs. Dash).
Combine spinach, cream, Ricotta and salt and pepper to taste. Heat over medium heat in saucepan.
Pour over cooked pasta and sprinkle with pine nuts.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add just enough soup to make moist.

Working from the front, lift the skin from the turkey breast and slide 2 strips of bacon beneath it on each side. Secure the loosened skin with toothpicks. Place the onion and apple inside the body cavity. Cook about 4 hours in a smoker, using damp hickory, apple, pecan or cherry wood to provide smoke and flavor. Check for doneness every 30 minutes, beginning at 2 1/2 hours, by pricking deeply with a cooking fork. When juice running from the hole is clear, not pink, the bird should be done. (Depending on the bird's size and the smoker's temperature, cooking time will vary considerably.) Keep the fire low and smoky, so the turkey cooks and throughout without drying too much on the outside. A small pan of water placed inside the smoker helps keep the bird moist.
