Roll in extra flour; shake off as much flour as possible. Add to batter.
Mix with hands until all fruits are well covered. Drop on greased pan.
Bake in slow 350° oven for about 18 minutes.
In small saucepan over medium-high heat, heat oil.
Add onion and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, about 3 minutes.
Add tomato sauce and oregano; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer, stirring occasionally about 15 minutes.
Place water, sugar and yeast in small bowl and set aside.
Add all the rest in a large bowl, then add items in small bowl.
Mix all together and set in fridge for 15 to 20 minutes.
Bake what you want now and leave rest in fridge; will stay good for a week.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine and mix well all ingredients. Press firmly into ungreased loaf pan (2 if needed).
Bake at 375° about 1 hour.
Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before slicing.
Core and quarter unpeeled apples; cook in large heavy saucepan until soft, about 30 minutes.
Press through food mill.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Heat milk to lukewarm; add honey.
Stir to dissolve.
Add to ingredients.
Stir in dry milk and oil.
Stir in flour and cooked rice.
Pour dough onto floured surface; knead in flour (dough is slightly sticky because of rice).
Place in greased bowl.
Cover.
Let rise in warm place until double.
Turn out on lightly floured surface.
Knead well. Place in 2 loaf pans.
Let rise until double.
Turn out on lightly floured surface.
Knead well.
Place in 2 loaf pans.
Let rise until double.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes until lightly brown. Brush with butter while still warm.
This dough does not raise very fast.
Mix broccoli, mushroom soup, Miracle Whip or mayo, egg, onion and sharp or Cheddar cheese together and put in buttered 2-quart casserole dish.
Melt oleo and toss in Pepperidge Farm stuffing. Place stuffing on casserole.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Place ribs on a rack in large shallow roasting pan.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Meanwhile, combine sugars and cornstarch in medium saucepan.
Stir in catsup, vinegar and water; bring to boil.
Cook and stir until thickened and clear.
Remove ribs and rack from pan; discard fat.
Place ribs back in roasting pan.
Pour about 1 1/2 cups of the sauce over ribs.
Bake 30 minutes longer.
Cut ribs into serving size pieces.
Brush with remaining sauce.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Boil potatoes, eggs and onion.
Fry bacon and crumble.
Mix altogether using equal amounts of sour cream and creamy Italian dressing.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix together margarine, sugars and peanut butter.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and soda.
Add to mixture; beat well.
Add milk and vanilla.
Bake in tube pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool.
Frost with Peanut Butter Frosting.
First Layer:
Crush cookies; save out about 3/4 cup to sprinkle on top layer.
Melt margarine; add to cookies, then press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Saute garlic,
bacon and cut up cabbage strips in olive oil for
minutes in frying pan.
Then add chicken broth and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add noodles and simmer for 15 more minutes.
Serve with corn bread or muffins.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In mixer, cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in egg yolks, flour, salt, milk and lemon juice.
In bowl, beat egg whites until fluffy, then add to mixture.
Bake 15 minutes at 375° then 45 minutes at 300° until lightly golden.
Mix Pet milk and marshmallows together and melt, stirring constantly.
Add nuts, fruit and crumbs.
Mix well and press in pan or dish and store in refrigerator.
Combine 2 teaspoons sugar and 1 tablespoon cornstarch in saucepan.
Add 1/2 cup water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thick and clear.
Cool.
Beat egg whites with salt and vanilla until soft peaks form.
Add 4 tablespoons sugar after adding cornstarch mixture.
Beat until it stands in stiff peaks.
Spread on pie.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Boil and debone chicken to bite-size pieces.
Set aside. Prepare rice as directed.
Set aside.
Saute onion in butter or margarine until soft; blend in flour, soup and milk and add mushrooms.
Combine all ingredients.
Shape into loaf or ring mold.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave at Medium for 15 to 16 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Blend eggs, milk, onion and peppers in a blender. Add to dry ingredients. Fry in deep fat.
They will turn over by themselves when 1 side is done.
Flake tuna and add salad dressing, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and horseradish.
Fill croustades or shells; top with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake in moderate oven until brown.
Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients together, make into 6 patties and fry until done.
Can also be microwaved, power High for 5 minutes. Rearrange patties and cook 5 more minutes at power 7 or until done.
In saucepan, combine sugar, cornstarch, and salt.
Gradually add cherry juice, stirring until thick and clear.
Add butter and extract.
Cool.
Line 9 inch pie plate with pastry.
Add cherries to cool cornstarch mixture.
Pour into pastry lined pie plate. Top with crust.
Crimp edges high.
Fold strip of aluminum foil around edge of pie.
Bake in oven (425°) about 40 minutes.
Remove foil 10 minutes before end of baking.
I roll the crust between 2 sheets of wax paper.
I fold it and put it in the pan, on the top crust I spread canned milk on top crust, then cut holes and put bits of oleo in the holes.
Then sprinkle sugar on top of crust.
Preheat oven to 250°.
Melt butter in a large oven pan.
Add remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Bake at 250° for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Store in an airtight container.
Combine in double boiler the oil, chocolate and sugar.
Beat in eggs one at a time.
Add vanilla and flour.
Chill.
Drop into sugar and shape.
Bake on wax paper in moderate oven (375°) for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 6 dozen.
Mix honey and eggs together.
Add baking powder and flour sifted together, then add chopped nuts, dates and flavoring.
Bake at 350° on cookie sheet for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mixture should be 1/4 inch deep.
Cut in strips (1/2 x 3-inch).
Roll in powdered sugar before serving.
Yields 60 to 72.
Mix all the ingredients. Place mixture in a casserole dish. Top with grated cheese. Cook at 375 until cheese in melted well.
*Use light variety bread.
Spread and flatten 1 package of refrigerated peanut butter cookie dough in a pizza pan.
Bake according to directions.
If it bakes over the edge of the pan, trim some away.
Cook completely.
Marinate marshmallows in pineapple with juice.
Add whipped cream and cheese.
Moisten gelatine in cold water and dissolve in 1/4 cup hot water.
Add to mixture, then add pecans.
Pour into mold.
Sprinkle some grated cheese on top and chill overnight.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Soften butter in a bowl.
Add spices and salt.
Mix well. Add sugar.
Mix well.
Beat 5 of the eggs, one at a time. Stir in flour and the last remaining egg. Grease only the bottom of a 9-inch tube cake pan and flour lightly.
Place in a cold oven.
Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours or until well done.
Cool at least 20 minutes before turning out.
Sift flour, baking powder, cocoa and salt.
Beat Crisco and sugar good.
Add eggs, one at a time, and beat well.
Add milk and dry ingredients alternately and beat well after each addition. Add vanilla.
Bake in tube cake pan at 325° for 1 or 1 1/2 hours.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Add the rest; mix until flour is dampened.
Fill oiled cans a little more than half full.
Place in cold oven.
Bake at 325°.
Bake about 40 minutes.
Let set a little before you loosen them.
Run a serrated knife around the sides and they will slowly slide out.
Makes 7 cans.
Tastes better the longer it sets.
Can use more nuts, prunes and raisins.
Combine all ingredients in a large casserole dish; mix well. Bake, uncovered, for 40 to 45 minutes in a 350° oven.
In a medium-size saucepan melt butter or margarine and saute onions.
Combine all the other ingredients and let it simmer until your ribs are ready.
Cut potatoes into wedges; cook until tender.
Drain.
Layer baking dish with potato wedges, slice butter and place on top of potatoes.
Add salt, pepper and garlic salt (may use seasoned salt as well).
Place in oven on broil until golden brown.
Mix onion, Ro-Tel tomatoes, green chilies and soup in blender. Brown ground beef and drain.
Break 6 tortillas in pieces and spread in bottom of 9 x 12-inch pan.
Put half of the ground beef, half of the sauce and half of the cheese over the tortillas. Place other 6 tortillas on top of the cheese (do not break up these tortillas).
Put rest of meat, sauce and cheese over the tortillas.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add pineapple juice, lemon juice, crushed pineapple, grated carrots and celery.
Pour into molds and chill until firm.
Mix
all
ingredients
together.
Make into 1-inch meat balls. Cut
bacon
slices
in half and wrap each slice around meat ball.
Hold
together with toothpick.
Bake in 400° oven for 30 minutes, or until bacon is crisp.
Remove toothpick and serve hot.
Remove all fat from the meat and grind with a meat grinder. Mix the ground meat with bread crumbs, egg, parsley, green onions, green pepper, garlic powder and basil.
Salt and pepper to taste and shape into patties.

Soften oleo and gradually add powdered sugar, then the frozen, thawed strawberries. Be careful not to add too much berries; it may not take the full 1/2 cup. Blend and spread between layers, sides and top of cake.
Mix sugar, water and cherry juice together.
Bring to a boil. Add Jell-O and mashed cherries.
Let stand 5 minutes; add pineapple and nuts, then Coke last.
Chill and serve.
Peel potatoes, slice or cut into 1/2-inch pieces and boil in salted water just until tender.
(Be careful not to overcook or the potatoes will become mush.)
Meanwhile cut bacon into small pieces. Cut onion into small pieces or green onions into thin slices.
Mix together vinegar, water, sugar, pepper and salt.
Fry bacon in skillet until crisp, then scoop bacon out of skillet into vinegar mixture, leaving drippings in skillet.
Saute onion in drippings. Add flour to onion in skillet and stir until smooth and thickened. Drain potatoes (when tender) and pour into skillet.
Add bacon/vinegar mixture and stir gently to mix evenly.
In heavy saucepan, mix all ingredients except pecans.
Stir thoroughly and cook to 238°.
Stir often.
Cool to 170° and add pecans.
Stir until thick.
Pour onto a buttered platter and cut into squares.
Melt butter in saucepan; mix in celery and onion.
Arrange fish fillets on top.
Cover and simmer until fish is done, about 20 minutes for frozen fish, 10 minutes for fresh.
Break up the fish with a spoon into bite size chunks.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Slice garlic cloves.
Mix with olive oil.
Set aside for at least 4 hours.
Wash potatoes.
Cut into quarters.
Place into microwavesafe covered dish.
Add water.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes on High in microwave or until tender.
Drain water.
Place on grill; brush with olive oil mix.
Turn occasionally until slightly crisp. Serve immediately.
Combine bran flakes, milk and carrots; let stand 5 minutes. Add remaining ingredients, stirring until particles are moistened. Line each muffin tin with two paper liners; fill half full.
Bake in 400° oven for 20 minutes.
Put cranberries and oranges, including rind, through grinder. Add celery, nuts and sugar.
Make Jell-O using only 1 1/2 cups water.
Add other ingredients.
Place in refrigerator until thick. Serve with whip cream.
Crush Oreos in food processor.
Beat together cream cheese and margarine.
Mix pudding and milk.
Blend the two mixtures.
Add Cool Whip.
Layer cookies and pudding mixture in a bowl.
(For children's parties, fill clear, plastic cups and garnish with gummy worms.)
Refrigerate for one hour.
Slowly cook meat, onion, celery and bell pepper until celery and onion are tender.
Add uncooked rice and tomatoes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer about 45 minutes.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Heat until thickened.
Add to beaten egg yolks.
Bring to a boil.
Thicken and remove from heat and add vanilla flavoring.
Pour this over banana and vanilla wafers which have been layered.
Top with meringue and brown lightly.
Heat large heavy pot.
Add meat.
Brown on all sides without oil.
Pour off any fat.
Sprinkle onion around meat.
Cover tightly.
Cook over low heat for 1 hour.
Remove from heat.
Keep covered and let meat cool to lukewarm.
When cool, slice across grain for serving.
Return meat to pot.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer 1 to 2 hours longer or until tender, turning slices once.
Combine flour, oats, brown sugar, lemon rind and soda in mixer bowl; mix well.
Stir in margarine.
Reserve 1 cup flour mixture. Press remaining flour mixture into 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Spread cranberry sauce over baked layer. Sprinkle with
mixture of reserved flour mixture and pecans.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes longer or until golden brown.
Cool. Cut into bars.
May be frozen up to 12 months.
Drain oranges; save juice.
Add enough water to make 1 cup. Dissolve jello in 2 cups boiling water.
Add sherbet and stir until melted.
Chill until thickened.
Then add orange sections and chill until you are ready to serve, about 2 hours.
Wash and drain beans; cover with water.
Add salt; soak overnight.
In morning drain beans and add 2 quarts water and ham hock with ham shreds.
Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 3 hours. Cut ham off bone; return meat to pot.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 30 minutes more.
Enjoy!!
Cream shortening, sugars and vanilla until light and fluffy. Add eggs and beat well.
Add flour to mixture.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen.
Mix together and drop by rounded spoonfuls.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Add sugar and shortening to boiling water.
Cool in mixing bowl.
Add yeast that has been mixed with lukewarm water.
Add cold water, eggs and salt.
Add flour 2 cups at a time.
Place dough in bowl and rub with vegetable oil.
Refrigerate overnight.
Mix butter and cheese, then add soup mix and flour.
Blend and shape into ball and chill.
Roll out on floured board.
Cut into desired shapes.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Makes about 5 dozen.
(If difficult to roll out, add more flour.)
In 3-quart saucepan, combine water and broth; bring to a boil. Meanwhile, cut chicken into 1/2-inch chunks.
Add to liquid with carrots, celery and potatoes.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms, onions and thyme.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper.
Serves 4 to 6.
Peel and coarsely grate cucumbers.
Wrap in a paper towel and squeeze gently to completely remove juice.
Dissolve gelatin and salt in boiling water.
Add cold water and vinegar. Fold in sour cream and chill mixture until thickened.
Fold in cucumbers, onion and pepper.
Pour into greased mold and chill until firm. Serves 6.
Prepare cake mix as directed on package.
Bake batter in 2 greased and floured 9-inch pans.
Remove cake layers from pans and cool on rack.
Place 1 cooled layer on serving plate.
Spread half can of cherries on first layer.
Top with second layer.
Combine sugar, vanilla, orange rind, and cream.
Whip cream mixture until cream holds its shape.
Spread on second layer and sides.
Spread half of cherries on top of whipped cream.
Sprinkle with chocolate shavings.
Chill until ready to serve.
Mix together in order listed.
Pour into unbaked pie crust. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until center is firm.

Melt butter, peanut butter and chocolate chips in large pan over low heat. After completely melted, pour box of cereal into pan and coat each piece. Be careful not to break up cereal. After coated, pour box of powdered sugar into trash bag, then pour cereal over it and shake bag until cereal is coated.
Place apples in pie shell, then sprinkle with the sugar.
Mix together the flour, oleo, nutmeg and brown sugar and sprinkle over the top of the apples.
Bake at about 375° until apples are tender.
Dissolve 1 package lime jello with 1 1/2 cups boiling water. Blend cream cheese to jello.
Add remaining ingredients. Refrigerate.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs.
Pour milk over crackers.
When soft, add to mixture.
Add remaining ingredients. Bake in 2 layers at 375° for 25 minutes.
Put together with whipped cream or topping.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix first 5 ingredients (dry) in bowl with fork; stir in rest.
Pour into ungreased 8 x 8-inch pan. Bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Cake can be mixed in pan.
Recipe can be doubled and made in 13 x 9-inch pan, but should be mixed with mixer.
Mix and beat ingredients 5 minutes.
Bake in 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes in well-greased Bundt pan.
Can be made 2 days in advance.
Frost or glaze as preferred.
Cream shortening and sugar, then eggs.
Add honey, sour milk and vanilla.
Beat well and add dry ingredients.
Chill and form into balls.
Roll in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Place tomatoes in a 1 1/2 to 2-quart casserole and add wine. Cook over low heat 20 to 25 minutes.
Strain and discard liquid. Add the mushrooms (wash them first!), pepper, bay leaf and olive oil to tomato pulp.
Cook 30 minutes over low heat.
Correct seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve cold.
Serves 4.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook entire package of noodles.
Let sit in water for 1 hour or overnight.
Separate eggs.
Beat egg yolks, sugar and vanilla until thick and lemon colored.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Mix yolk mixture with drained noodles.
Add any optional ingredients.
Cook
broccoli
30 minutes.
Drain water.
Mix together cheese, egg, soup, mayonnaise and mushrooms.
Pour over cooked broccoli and stir well.
Cover with cracker crumbs and drizzle butter on top.
Mix all ingredients except mushrooms and sour cream.
Bake at 350° until meat is tender.
Add mushrooms and juice before serving.
Add sour cream.
Serve over rice or noodles.
In a 3 1/2-quart saucepan, mix sugar with dry gelatin.
Add milk, corn syrup, chocolate and butter.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, to 238° on thermometer.
Remove from heat; pour into a large mixing bowl.
Stir in vanilla.
Cool about 25 minutes or to 110°.
Beat with wooden spoon until candy thickens. Stir in walnuts.
Spread into prepared pan.
Let cool.
Cut in squares.
Makes about 2 1/2 pounds.
Trim excess fat from steak and discard.
Press peppercorns into both sides of steak with heel of hand.
Melt butter in pan large enough to hold steak.
When butter is sizzling, brown steak on one side, turn and brown second side.
Reduce heat and finish cooking steak.
(To test, make a small slash with a sharp knife to see if steak is as done as you want it to be.)
Season with salt to taste.
Obviously, makes one serving.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Combine first seven ingredients; mix well.
Reserve one cup; press remaining on bottom of prepared pan.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until light brown; cool 10 minutes.
Top with nuts and chocolate pieces.
Cook and stir chicken in hot oil until lightly browned.
Add broth, tomato sauce and seasoning mix.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Add corn and red pepper.
Bring to a full boil.
Stir in rice.
Cover.
Remove from heat.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork.
Serve with cheese sprinkled over it, tortilla chips and sour cream, if desired.
Beat eggs, sugar, soda and salt.
Add oil and mix.
Add flour and vanilla.
Mix all together.
Add apples and pecans.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 to 50 minutes.
Pour into unbaked pastry shell.
Bake slowly for 40 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a baking pan.
In a bowl beat butter until creamy.
Beat in 1/2 cup confectioners sugar and then work in 2 cups flour to make a smooth dough.
Press dough in an even layer in the prepared pan.
Bake 15 minutes until slightly puffed.
Next, beat eggs in a bowl with a wire whisk.
Beat in granulated sugar, lemon peel and juice.
Sift remaining 1/4 cup flour over egg mixture and stir in.
Prick top of crust with a fork about an inch away from each other all over.
Pour egg mixture over crust and bake 30 minutes until egg mixture is set. Remove from oven.
Cool and sprinkle top with 1 1/2 tablespoons confectioners sugar.
Heat juice and dissolve jello.
Add water and cool until slightly thickened.
Stir in celery, onion and horseradish.
Add sliced stuffed olives and shrimp if you like variation.
Pour into ring mold or individual molds.
Bring the first 5 ingredients to a boil and add the peanuts. Stir constantly until peanuts are golden brown.
Remove from stove and add the soda.
Stir until foaming almost stops.
Pour on greased sheet pan.
Use heavy pan, use wooden spoon and make on a clear, cool day.
Drain rice on cloth.
Add eggs, salt, pepper and parsley. Chill.
Fry in deep oil until light brown.
Cut potatoes in quarters lengthwise.
Mix with olive oil. Sprinkle with pepper, salt, garlic powder and cayenne pepper. Bake at 450° for 20 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and roll into 1-inch balls. Chill for 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate chips with paraffin. Using toothpicks, dip chilled balls into chocolate.
Cook pasta according to package directions, adding broccoli to water last 2 minutes of cooking time; drain well.
Add process cheese spread and milk to pasta mixture in saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until process cheese melts.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Dissolve jello in 2 cups boiling water.
Add ice (to make 2 cups).
Stir until melted.
Let set 5 minutes.
Add pudding and oranges and mix with mixer.
Add cool whip and mix with mixer. Refrigerate.
Tastes great and it's quick!
Brown beef and onion; drain off fat.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook squash and onion in enough water for simmering (about 1 1/2 cups) until tender.
Drain, reserving 1 cup liquid.
Return 1 cup liquid to squash.
Mix all ingredients.
Place in 2-quart buttered casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until light golden brown.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Prepare potatoes, onions and celery.
Place in saucepan, add water, salt and pepper.
Cover and turn to high heat.
Bring to rolling boil, switch to simmer and cook for 20 minutes.
Then add milk and bring almost to a boil, again using high heat.
While this is heating, measure flour into bowl and add egg.
Stir with a fork until thoroughly mixed.
Stir in egg, flour mixture and butter.
Switch to simmer for at least 15 minutes.
Begin your platter with a bed of lettuce on a round platter. Add thick slices of tomatoes and thin slices of onion around edge of platter.
Place pieces of avocado on tomatoes.
Make spokes with raw cucumber sticks or celery sticks.
Fill center of dish with radish roses and carrot curls.
Cream butter and sugar real good.
Add eggs and flour alternately, adding flour first and last.
Cut fruit and nuts fine and mix with a little flour.
(This keeps all the fruit from going to the bottom of cake.)
Add vanilla.
Mix nuts and fruit with batter.
Bake in tube pan at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Beat the first 7 ingredients together until blended.
Stir in coconut and pineapple.
Pour into pie crust.
Bake for 5 minutes at 425°.
Reduce oven temperature to 325°; bake for about 1 hour longer.

recipes.t: Lemon Herb Chicken With Hollandaise Sauce
d: Dip chicken breasts in bread crumbs.
Place the fillets on microwavable dish and cover with a domed, microwavable cover.
Cook fillet on High for 4 minutes.
Rotate dish 1/4 turn and continue cooking on High for 4 additional minutes.
Add 1/8 cup of water to the frozen broccoli in microwavable dish and cover.
Microwave broccoli for 3 minutes on High.
Separate the broccoli and microwave for 3 additional minutes on High.
Divide broccoli and place each portion with a chicken breast.
Pour Hollandaise Sauce equally over both portions and serve.
Boil potatoes in skins just until tender.
Chill in refrigerator.
When chilled, grate potatoes.
Mix sour cream, cream cheese, milk, margarine, 3/4 cup grated cheese, salt, pepper, onion and grated potatoes.
Put in 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with 3/4 cup grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Saute onion and celery in butter.
Add flour, then cheese (cut up cheese into chunks, so it will melt quickly).
Then add mushrooms and soup.
Cook broccoli according to directions on package.
Drain.
Add to mixture.
Heat the dip well, then pour into chafing dish and keep hot.
Serve with Fritos.
Mix melted butter with dry cake mix; set aside 1 1/2 cups. Press rest into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread mixed Marshmallow Creme and peanut butter on top.
Crumble rest of cake mix on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Let cool and cut.
In a small bowl, soak the gelatin in the cold water for about 5 minutes.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg yolks.
Add 1/4 cup of sugar and cream.
Mix the first 3 ingredients, then add the next 2.
Mix and add the next 4 ingredients and stir in the last 4 ingredients.
Drop by spoonfuls on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes. Makes 5 dozen.
Mix soup, mayo, milk and lemon juice.
Heat and stir.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan, broccoli on bottom, some sauce, cut up chicken, remainder of sauce, grated cheese, bread crumbs on top. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt butter.
Add chips and melt.
Add remaining ingredients. Mix.
Pour into two unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Stir well.
Bake in greased muffin pans or a 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° until done.
Cut up vegetables; grind in food chopper, using coarse blade. Add salt.
Cover; refrigerate overnight.
Rinse in cold water. Drain well.
Reserve 4 berries for garnish.
Puree other berries and banana in blender.
Add jam and milk.
Blend.
Freeze.
Cream butter, gradually adding sugar.
Beat eggs in creamed mixture, one at a time.
Combine flour, cocoa, soda and salt.
Add alternately the dry ingredients and sour cream to creamed mixture, mixing well after each addition.
Add boiling water and vanilla. Mix well.
Bake in a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Check after 70 minutes with toothpick, ovens may vary.
Do not overbake.
Cool for 15 minutes.
Mix lemonade and ice water.
Add pineapple juice and Hawaiian Punch.
Stir thoroughly.
Add 7-Up.
Scoop sherbet into punch bowl.
Pour punch over sherbet very slowly.
Punch will be very frothy.
Serves 100 four ounce servings.
Mix
eggs, oil and water.
Blend in cake mix and peanut butter.
Drop
by
teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Mash down with spoon.
Bake at 350° for 15 or 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Cream Of Carrot Soup With Homemade Croutons
d: Melt butter in a pan and saute the onions, potatoes and carrots for ten minutes on med low heat.
Add stock and sugar and bring slowly to a boil.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
In a food processor, puree soup.
Return to pan and add half and half. Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Cook all ingredients, thicken to consistency you desire.
Top with biscuits.
Mix all until well blended. Roll in nuts and chill.

recipes.t: Cabbage Rolls Or Pigs In The Blanket
d: Cook cabbage 25 to 30 minutes.
Peel leaves. Combine hamburger, rice, onion soup mix, onion, egg and 1/2 can tomato soup.
Roll meat mixture up in cabbage leaves.
Secure with toothpicks.
Place cabbage rolls in a large pan and cover with remainder of tomato sauce and soup. Bake 1 hour at 375°.
Cook macaroni according to directions on box.
Drain and put into crock-pot.
Add other ingredients in this order: oil, milk, butter, eggs and pepper.
Top with the grated cheese and cook for 4 hours on low.
Turn off after 4 hours.
Cook pasta according to directions.
Drain; rinse with cold water.
Chop onion, cucumbers and tomatoes.
Combine ingredients for dressing.
Pour over pasta, onion and cucumbers.
Add tomatoes last.
Refrigerate for several hours, overnight, if possible. Will serve at least 12.
Brown ground beef with onions.
Drain off grease.
In mixing bowl, combine cabbage, carrots, salt and pepper.
Add ground beef mixture to this and toss to mix well.
Pour uncooked rice into a 3-quart casserole.
Pour cabbage and ground beef mixture over rice.
Pour beef broth and water over mixture.
Cover casserole and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Combine vinegar, water, sugar and salt.
Bring to a boil and set aside to cool.
Wash, peel and slice cucumbers rather thick. Place onion and garlic in jars.
Add cucumbers, filling jar to top. Fill jar with vinegar mixture; seal.
Refrigerate for 3 days before serving.
(Liquid makes about 3 quarts.)
Wash and trim sprouts.
Thoroughly wash four 1-pint canning jars and lids.
In each jar, place 1 garlic clove, 1 teaspoon dill seed, 1 teaspoon peppercorns and then fill with Brussels sprouts.
Microwave chocolate squares and 2 tablespoons of milk until almost melted, stirring 1/2 way through.
Stir until completely melted.
Beat in cream cheese, milk and sugar until well mixed. Refrigerate 10 minutes.
Stir in whipped topping until smooth. Put mix in pie crust.
Freeze until firm (3 to 4 hours).
Garnish with chocolate curls or shavings.
You will need wooden skewers.
Choose five of the fruits (grapes are a must) and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Put a piece of each fruit on a wooden skewer, alternating with grapes.
A strawberry on top always adds color.
Refrigerate until serving time.

Preheat oven to 375°. Butter 9-inch square pan. Mix all ingredients together, combining them well. Spread mixture in pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes or until dry on top and almost firm to touch. Cool for 10 to 15 minutes. Cut into 2-inch squares.
Fry bacon until crisp; drain and set aside.
Brown onion in the bacon drippings.
Add bread, cheese and potato.
Crumble bacon and add to mixture.
Beat eggs; pour into mixture.
Season to taste and cook until set, stirring occasionally.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine oats, flour, brown sugar, soda and salt; mix well.
Stir in margarine. Reserve 1 cup and press remaining onto bottom of pan.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until light brown; cool 10 minutes.
Top with chocolate pieces.
Wash, peel, core and slice apples.
Sprinkle lightly with hot water and a few drops lemon juice.
Also a few tablespoons of sugar, salt and cinnamon.
Arrange apple mixture in bottom of large greased baking pan.
In mixing bowl, add melted butter; keep adding remaining sugar and flour to form crumbly mixture, working with a fork.
Sprinkle butter-flour mixture evenly over sliced apples.
A few chopped walnuts, pecans or wheat germ give an added crunch to topping.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 35 minutes or until apples are tender and crumb topping is golden brown.
Serve warm with whipped cream or softened vanilla ice cream.
Cook shrimp according to package directions.
Thaw crab meat. Cook rice according to package directions using seasoning in package.
Mix all ingredients except bread crumbs.
Pour into a 1 1/2-quart greased casserole.
Top with buttered bread crumbs. Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Assemble 3 lasagna strips into a buttered 9x12 inch baking dish.
Mix cheese into hot mashed potatoes.
Add 1/2 potato-cheese mixture.
Layer 3 more lasagna noodles and repeat with potato and cheese mixture.
Saute oleo and onions until golden.
Pour over casserole.
Bake 20 minutes a 350 degrees uncovered.
Place rice in bottom of flat baking pan.
Lay washed chicken breasts on top of rice; sprinkle lemon pepper and salt on chicken and rice mixture.
Place onion slices on top of mixture and pour the water over rice.
Bake uncovered at 275° for 3 hours.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
Drain well and return to the pan.
Add remaining ingredients, tossing lightly to coat the noodles.
Good with veal and poultry.
Serves 4.
Combine first three ingredients and heat until sugar is dissolved.
Do not boil.
Remove and add the remaining ingredients. Mix thoroughly.
Bottle to store.
Beat cream cheese and sour cream in bowl until blended.
Stir in Monterey Jack cheese, olives, onion, salt and garlic powder. Cover and refrigerate 2 hours.
Place beans in food processor or blender; process until smooth.
Spread each tortilla with a thin layer of beans.
Spread thin layer of cream cheese mixture over beans.
Roll up tortillas lightly.
Wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate until chilled.
Cut 3/4-inch slices and serve with salsa.
Cream together cream cheese, sugar and butter; add eggs, one at a time.
Mix well.
Add flour last and one package of Dream Whip.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix first 5 ingredients, then add strawberries.
Bake in greased and floured pan per directions on box.
Spray a 1-quart casserole dish with nonstick coating.
Mix all ingredients in a mixing bowl except potatoes.
Gently stir in potatoes.
Spoon onto prepared baking dish.
Heat oven to 350°. Bake casserole 45 minutes or until slightly puffed and top is lightly browned.
In skillet or slow cooking pot with browning unit, cook meat until crumbly.
Drain.
In large bowl, mix cornmeal, milk and egg. Add meat, dry chili seasoning mix, seasoned salt, tomatoes, corn and olives.
Put in slow cooker or crock-pot and cook on high for 3 to 4 hours.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Cover and cook for another 5 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Beat Egg Beaters and add remaining ingredients. Pour into a large cast-iron skillet already sprayed with cooking spray.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Cream butter and sugar together. Add egg, molasses, ginger and cinnamon. Sift the flour, baking soda and salt.
Add sifted dry ingredients to the creamed mixture alternately with the cold water. Drop by spoonful (large) onto greased baking sheet and bake 8 to 10 minutes in moderate hot 375° oven.

Cook bacon, hamburger and onions in frypan. Add vinegar, brown sugar and mustard. Simmer for 15 minutes. Stir in the beans. Put meat mixture in bean pot or 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake 1 hour at 350° or slow cooker on low for 4 hours.

Place chicken in large Ziploc bag(s) with lemon juice. Marinate overnight, turning bags occasionally. Next day, pat dry chicken with paper towels. Dredge in seasoned flour. Fry in oil until golden. Drain on paper towel.
Place potatoes in large bowl. Add cold water. Let stand 30 minutes. Dry potatoes. Spray pan with nonstick spray. Place potatoes in pan. Spray potatoes with nonstick spray.
Sprinkle with pepper and salt. Bake for 20 minutes at 425°. Using spatula, turn potatoes. Sprinkle with garlic. Bake until golden potatoes.
Partially crush one cup Caesar Croutons.
Add one Tbsp. each chopped chives and parmesan cheese and two Tbsp. melted butter. Cut three medium tomatoes in half (cross-wise).
Season with salt and pepper.
Top with croutons mixture.
Broil until brown.
Serve with roast.
Combine first 5 ingredients and set aside.
Combine Bisquick and onions.
Combine 2 beaten eggs and milk, then add to Bisquick mixture.
Stir only until the mixture is moistened.
Heat milk and water in saucepan.
Add rice; stir.
Add sugar, salt and butter and stir, then let simmer for 50 minutes.
Beat 2 eggs in separate bowl and slowly add hot mixture.
Beat constantly.
Add vanilla and stir gently.
Ladle into dessert dishes and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Refrigerate.
Serves 8.
Mix all the ingredients except steak in a 10 x 13-inch dish. Score steak on both sides.
Marinate for several hours.
Grill.
Dip chicken in eggs. Roll in bread crumbs. Brown in olive oil and garlic (both sides). Grease casserole.
On bottom, layer spaghetti sauce, chicken, Mozzarella cheese, garlic, oregano and Parmesan.
Layer more spaghetti sauce and top with more Parmesan.
Mix first six ingredients together until fluffy.
Separately mix the flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Then add these to the first six ingredients.
Mix well.
Roll into 1 inch balls and roll each ball in sugar.
Place about 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 10 - 11 minutes, remove quickly from oven.
Place one chocolate candy kiss into the center of each cookie pointed side down.
Bake for exactly one minute longer.
Remove from oven and immediately spread chocolate over each cookie.
You may want to leave the cookie as is or you may place a butterscotch chip in each one.
Freezes well.
Makes 6 - 7 dozen cookies.

Cream the butter. Add sugar gradually, then rum flavoring very slowly. Add well beaten egg yolks and milk or cream. Cook over hot water until it thickens as a custard. Pour onto beaten egg whites. It is delicious on bread pudding.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put into a casserole dish.
Put casserole dish in a pan of water and bake 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Brown meat with onion and garlic.
Drain off any excess grease.
Combine with remaining ingredients (except Mozzarella) and place in 3-quart casserole dish. Top with Mozzarella and bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 475°.
Scrub potatoes, cut into long strips about 1/2-inch wide.
Dry strips thoroughly on paper towels.
Toss in a bowl with oil as if making a salad.
Toss with optional spices.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a cookie sheet and place in preheated oven for 35 minutes.
Turn strips periodically to brown on all sides.
If a crispier, browner potato is desired, run under broiler for a minute or two.
Sprinkle with salt. Yield: 6 servings, 80 calories per serving.
This is a low cholesterol, reduced fat recipe.
Soften cream cheese with milk.
Drain pineapple and mix with cheese.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Serve on rounds of nut bread or Ritz crackers.
Makes 12 servings.
Mix sugar, oil, vinegar, water, and flavor packets.
Set aside.
Crush dry noodles.
Mix noodles with almonds, sunflower seeds, onions, and slaw.
Drizzle with dressing and toss.
Cut pita bread into 8 pie-shaped pieces (like pizza).
Split sections open and pull apart.
Drizzle olive oil on "rough" side of bread.
Sprinkle with seasonings as desired.
Bake on ungreased baking sheet at 350° for approximately 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.
Combine sugar, butter, syrup and vanilla.
Bring to boil over medium heat.
Remove and stir for 10 minutes.
(Turns to light caramel color.)
Mix together.
Cut 3 slices of Italian bread.
Place 3 ounces of ham and 1 slice of Swiss cheese on first piece.
Top with another slice of bread, 3 ounces turkey and 1 slice American cheese.
Top with remaining slice of bread.
Dip sandwich into egg wash and grill like French toast.
Microwave or bake until hot through.
Heat milk chocolate chips, oleo and syrup.
Add vanilla and powdered sugar and mix.
Add Rice Krispies.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Set in refrigerator.
Cut into small squares to serve.
(May melt chocolate chips in microwave or double boiler.)
Wrap rinsed chicken livers with strips of uncooked bacon. Place on cookie sheet.
Baste with butter and Worcestershire sauce mixture.
Broil in oven, turning once.

Put eggs in pot and cover with water; heat just until the water boils. Remove pot from heat and cover. Let stand 15 to 18 minutes; remove shells from eggs. Cut eggs in half and remove yolks. Put the yolks in a small bowl and mash with fork. Add rest of ingredients and mix. Fill the egg whites with mixture, heaping it up slightly. Hint: Set pot in sink and run cold water over them to cool eggs down quickly. This makes them easier to peel.
Heat milk and corn gradually.
Stir in egg.
Add next four ingredients and dash of pepper.
Mix well.
Pour into greased 8-inch round baking dish.
Top with buttered crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Serves 6.
Combine flour and salt in a medium bowl.
Mix oil and milk together with a fork.
Add to flour and mix with hands until just mixed.
Add a little cold water if more liquid is needed.
Split dough into two balls.
Chill 10 minutes.
On a dry floured counter, press dough into a flat circle with hands.
Brown and drain meat.
Then dump together and season to taste: a little Tabasco, chile powder and garlic.
Great on a cold day. Serve with corn bread.
In large mixing bowl, combine Eagle Brand milk and water.
Add pudding mix; beat until well mixed.
Chill for 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon 1 cup pudding mixture into 2 1/2-quart round glass serving bowl.
Top with 1/3 each of vanilla wafers, bananas and pudding mixture.
Chill thoroughly.
Garnish as desired. Refrigerate leftovers.
Chop celery, carrots and onion.
In large saucepan, break eggs in peanut oil.
In separate corners of pan, place celery, carrots and onion.
With spatula, chop egg up and flip as it cooks and stir other vegetables.
Add rice and soy sauce and mix all together, stirring and flipping until rice is brown.
Serves 4 to 6.
Make cake according to directions.
Pour into greased and floured 13 x 9-inch pan.
In bowl, mix cream cheese, sour cream and sugar.
Add eggs one at a time, then add vanilla and flour.
Mix until smooth and pour over chocolate batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Combine bananas, oats and milk in bowl; set aside.
Cream butter or oleo and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition.
Combine dry ingredients, adding alternately with banana mixture to creamed mixture.
Spoon into two greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour.
Remove from pans; cool on wire rack.
Yields 2 loaves.
Can be frozen up to 3 months.
Sift flour with cornmeal, baking powder, salt and sugar; set aside.
Combine eggs, milk and oil in a large bowl.
Beat until smooth.
Add yams and beat until blended.
Add flour mixture, stirring only until flour mixture is moistened.
Spoon into 2 greased 8-inch square pans.
Bake at 425° for 35 to 40 minutes or until breads test done.
Cut into squares.
Serve warm with butter.
Mix first 3 ingredients. The ginger ale is to be added just before serving. Sherbet can be added if desired.
Saute garlic in olive oil.
Add basil and oregano; stir frequently and do not overcook.
Add butter; let melt.
Continue to stir.
Meanwhile, water should be brought to a boil.
Add tortellini.
Cool and toss.
Heat oil in skillet; brown meat; set aside.
Drain pineapple and combine the juice with the water, vinegar, brown sugar, cornstarch and soy sauce.
Mix well.
Cook sauce in the skillet until clear and slightly thickened.
Add meat and cook over low heat for about 55 minutes.
Add green pepper, onion slices and pineapple chunks and simmer about 5 more minutes.
Serve over steamed rice.
Place bacon slices in skillet and cook until crisp; remove from skillet to cool.
For fresh corn, cut off cob (it is better cut off cream style).
Mix corn, salt and sugar; pour
into bacon drippings in skillet.
Crumble bacon strips into corn.
Add 1/2 cup water.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes over low heat.
Stir often.
Combine brown sugar and flour.
Add egg yolks and water and beat with
electric
mixer
until creamy and smooth.
Heat the can of
milk
until
hot and add the creamy mixture.
Cook until thickened; stir constantly.
When thickened, remove from heat. Add butter and vanilla.
Pour into an 8-inch pie shell. Top with meringue.
Cook the chicken in enough water to cover until tender.
Pick off bone, return chicken to broth.
Bring to a boil.
Thicken with flour mixture.
This amount depends on the thickness you want. Cook and stir well.
A few drops of yellow food coloring adds color.
Serve over biscuits or mashed potatoes.
Mix all together and heat thoroughly.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, spread the can of blueberry pie filling followed by the can of crushed pineapple.
Sprinkle the box of yellow cake mix over top (don't mix).
Pour the butter over the cake mix and sprinkle with chopped pecans if desired.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Mix brown sugar, sugar, oats and butter.
Pat in buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Melt chocolate chips.
Add peanut butter.
Spread over cooled bars.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: French Toast With Brandied Lemon Butter
d: In a shallow dish, beat eggs, sugar, salt, milk and vanilla. Soak bread in mixture.
Heat butter over medium-high heat and cook each slice until lightly browned on each side.
Serve with maple syrup or Brandied Lemon Butter and lemon slices.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Serves 6.
Saute onion in bacon drippings until tender.
Add okra and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add remaining ingredients, stirring well.
Cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes or until corn is tender.
Yields 6 servings.

Peel fresh carrots and cut into chunks or use frozen carrots. Boil carrots until extra soft. Drain very well. While carrots are warm, add sugar, baking powder and vanilla. Whip with mixer until smooth. Add flour and butter. Mix well. Whip eggs and add to carrot mixture. Pour mixture into a 9 x 13-inch buttered baking dish. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until top is lightly brown. Add powdered sugar to top and serve.
Place the whole wheat flour in a large mixing bowl and set in the oven at the lowest temperature for 20 minutes.
While the flour is warming, dissolve the yeast in 1 cup warm water.
Add the honey to the mixture and set it aside.
Then dissolve the molasses in 1 cup water.
Set aside while the flour is being warmed.
This short time period will give the yeast mixture time to work before you combine it with flour.
Put vegetables in 9 x 12-inch casserole dish in microwave with 1 tablespoon water.
Cook until tender, then set aside to drain. Debone chicken breasts; cube and season to taste.
Brown in oleo. Remove chicken when brown, leaving remaining oleo.
Saute onions. When ready, add cheese.
When melted slowly, add milk and stir. Then add vegetables.
Stir until well coated with cheese.
Add noodles and chicken; stir gently again.
Put in same 9 x 12-inch dish and top with bread crumbs.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8 people.

recipes.t: Feather Cake(From Cookbook Given To Flora A. P. Engle, Christmas 1902.)
d: (No directions were given; follow cake procedures.)
Unroll dough into rectangles; press onto bottom and sides of 15 x 10 x 1-inch jellyroll pan to form crust.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Combine remaining ingredients; mix well.
Spread over crust.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with thin red pepper strips.
Brown meat and onion, add seasonings and tomato sauce.
This may be made ahead and used when ready.
In casserole (round) alternate layers of tortillas, sauce, olives and cheese.
Add water, cover and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
May be frozen before adding water for later use.
Serves 5 to 6.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Saute onion in butter.
Add broccoli, cheese, mushroom soup and mushrooms.
Heat thoroughly. (Good in crock-pot.)
Serve with plain Doritos.

recipes.t: Cauliflower Au Gratin With Almonds And Cheese
d: Boil cauliflower in salted water until tender (about 20 minutes).
Drain.
Make cream sauce.
If desired, add part of cheese to sauce.
Reserve other and sprinkle over top of cauliflower.
Place whole cauliflower (or broken into flowerets) into casserole.
Pour sauce over cauliflower.
Just before serving, sprinkle with grated cheese and almonds.
Brown in moderate oven for about 10 minutes.
Serves 4.
Use a tube pan.
Cream margarine, sugar and eggs together. Sprinkle flour over nuts and fruit, covering good.
Add to batter and add vanilla.
Bake at 250° for 3 hours.
Mix the first 5 ingredients and add ground beef.
Make meatballs the size of a silver dollar and place in casserole dish. Mix the next 3 ingredients and pour over meatballs.
Combine 3 cups flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking soda. Heat liquids until very warm.
Add to dry mixture and beat well. Stir in enough remaining flour to make a stiff batter.
Spoon into two 8 1/2 x 4 1/2-inch pans that have been greased and sprinkled with cornmeal.
Sprinkle top of batter with cornmeal.
Cover, let rise in warm place for 45 to 60 minutes.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Turn out of pans while bread is still warm.
Bake cake as directed in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Meanwhile, combine pineapple and sugar in saucepan.
Cook over medium heat 20 minutes.
Poke fork into done cake.
Pour on pineapple mix; spread evenly.
Cool completely.
Blend all ingredients.
Add enough water to make 1 1/2 gallons.
Add large bottle ginger ale or more if you need to make more.
Beat egg with fork.
Add mayonnaise and chicken soup; blend well.
Stir in broccoli, onion and cheese.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart oblong dish.
Sprinkle crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Beat butter, eggs, sugars and vanilla until light and fluffy. Add dry ingredients; blend well.
Stir in chips and nuts.
Drop from teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake in a moderate oven (375°) for 7 to 9 minutes.
Makes about 7 dozen.
Mix together first 6 ingredients.
Place in casserole dish; sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Drain pineapple, reserving the syrup.
In a saucepan, combine rice, water, pineapple syrup and salt.
Mix just to moisten the rice.
Bring quickly to boiling, reduce heat, cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Add marshmallows, pineapple, banana and lemon juice. Stir and then allow to cool completely.
Fold in cream.
Chill before serving.
Combine broth, broccoli and butter.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients and let simmer 20 minutes.
Beat eggs until thick.
Add sugar to eggs slowly, 1/2 cup at a time.
Stir in vanilla.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Stir in flour mixture 1/2 at a time.
Fold in apples. Stir in walnuts.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cook meat, onions, pepper and seasoning in skillet until meat is brown. Put about 1/2 cup of cheese in the bottom of an unbaked pie shell.
Pour drained, cooked meat mixture over cheese in shell.
Mix mayonnaise, milk and eggs and pour over meat mixture. Sprinkle rest of cheese on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, then cool for 10 minutes.
Place dough on a large cookie sheet on foil.
Pat out with hand, then sprinkle cheese.
Spread pepperoni on dough and sprinkle with olive oil and oregano.
Fold into thirds, seam faced down, on cookie sheet.
Pinch ends closed.
Bake around 20 to 30 minutes at 350°, in preheated oven, until golden brown.
Can brush crust with egg white.
Slice and serve.
Mix well.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Put into mixing bowl the yellow cake mix, vanilla pudding, sour cream, eggs and oil.
Beat as directed on package. Put half of batter into greased pan.
Mix first three ingredients in blender.
Add remaining ingredients and blend well.
Keep refrigerated.
Pare and slice enough potatoes to equal 2 cups; set aside. Cook onion in 1/4 cup margarine until tender.
Blend in flour and seasonings.
Gradually add milk, stirring until smooth.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture is slightly thickened.
Place half of sausage in bottom of 2-quart ovenproof casserole.
Add half of potatoes, half of peas and half of sauce.
Repeat layers with remaining ingredients, ending with sauce.
Combine crumbs and margarine; sprinkle over sauce.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until crumbs are lightly browned.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine all ingredients in deep casserole dish (1 quart size). Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours.
Bake covered at 350° for 1 hour.
May sprinkle little paprika on top.
In skillet over medium heat, brown meat and onions.
Cook until done; drain.
Stir in corn, tomato sauce, rice, steak sauce and pepper.
Set aside.
In a large saucepan, combine all ingredients except salt and pepper.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until thoroughly heated.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Chill milk in freezer several hours.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add lemon juice and undrained pineapple.
Chill until slightly thickens.
Whip margarine, cheese and sugar until fluffy.
Fold into jello.
Whip milk until it peaks.
Fold into mixture.
Butter dish and sprinkle with 1/2 of crumbs.
Pour cheese mixture.
Put remainder of crumbs on top.
Chill several hours.
Mix sauces, spices and pork together and simmer.
Into a 9 x 13-inch pan, pour the can of pineapple.
Over it, spread the cherry pie filling.
Spread the coconut over this, then sprinkle the dry cake mix over all these layers.
Top with nuts. Put thinly sliced oleo over top.
Bake for 1 hour in a 350° oven.
Cream margarine and brown sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Mix flour, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Add to creamed mixture. Add the raisins, juice and nuts; mix.
Drop by spoonfuls onto cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° about 10 minutes.
This is a nice moist cookie.
Layer the ingredients as stated in an 8 x 8-inch baking pan. Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes or until bubbly.
Serve with Tostitos or a heavier chip.
Stir gelatin into boiling water until dissolved.
Let stand until cool.
Add carrot, celery and pineapple.
Also add cheese if used.
Refrigerate until gelatin is firm.
Serves 6.
Put shanks in covered ovenproof casserole.
Mix all other ingredients and cut large onion and put slices on top of shanks. Pour all over shanks and cover your dish.
Potatoes and carrots may be added to dish.
Bake 3 hours in 300° oven.
Beat eggs in bowl.
Add corn muffin mix, sour cream, corn, melted butter and sugar.
Grease an 8 x 8-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
In a
1 1/2-quart microwave-safe bowl, combine sugar, corn syrup and salt; mix well.
Microwave on High for 4 minutes.
Stir in almonds; microwave on High again 4 minutes.
Add butter and vanilla; microwave on High 1 to 1 1/2 minutes.
Stir in baking soda.
As soon as the mixture foams, quickly pour onto a greased metal baking sheet.
Cool completely.
Break into 2-inch pieces. Melt chocolate in microwave.
Drizzle over top.
Yield:
About 1 pound.
Mix dry ingredients together well.
Pour enough boiling water just to mix well.
Add shortening.
Form into palm size pones. Deep fry until golden brown.
Using a mortar and pestle, crush the fennel seed, mustard seed and pepper.
Set aside.
Mix all ingredients well.
Fill large, clean sausage casings with mixture.
Boil in salt water or place in baking dish; bake at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Beat: 6 eggs, add salt and pepper.
Fry as pancakes.
Chop raisins and boil water and raisins for 5 minutes in a 2-quart pan.
Remove from heat and add apples, chocolate and margarine.
When mixture is cool, stir in flour, baking powder and soda.
Add egg, liquid sweetener (Sweet 10) and vanilla.
Beat 1 minute by hand and stir in nuts.
Bake in 9 x 9-inch pan for 40 minutes at 350°.
Cut into pieces, wrap and store in freezer. Contains 175 calories per piece.
Do not drain the pineapple.
Mix flour, pineapple, sugar, eggs, nuts and baking soda well. Pour into a prepared 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 to 45 minutes.
Mix the powdered sugar, butter, cream cheese and vanilla.
Beat until smooth. Spread immediately over hot cake and let cool.
Cook and chop chicken.
Combine and chill.
A must for Christmas.
Mix juices, lemonade and sugar.
Let stand until ready to serve.
Then add ginger ale, strawberries, sherbet, ice cubes and rum.
Enjoy!
Dredge peaches in flour.
Add next 5 ingredients and mix well. Set aside.
Roll 3/4 of pastry to 1/8-inch thickness on a lightly floured surface.
Fit into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Spoon in peach mixture.
Roll remaining pastry out to 1/4-inch thickness on a lightly floured surface.
Cut into 1/2-inch strips.
Arrange in lattice fashion over peaches.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Cook chicken breasts until tender, 30 to 40 minutes.
Cool and remove bones.
Cook eggs approximately 10 minutes and slice. Combine milk and flour together and pour into chicken broth.
Add chicken and eggs for a delicious dinner.
Salt and pepper to your taste; serve over hot biscuits.
Serves 2 to 4.

recipes.t: Godmother'S Flag Cake(4Th Of July Tradition)
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 2 (15 1/2 x 10 1/2-inch) jelly roll pans.
Prepare 1 package of cake mix, substituting orange juice for water.
Spread batter evenly in cake pan.
Bake 20 minutes.
Cool cake for 15 minutes in pan.
Invert on rack.
Repeat steps for second cake mix.
Slice 1 pint of strawberries.
Cut remaining strawberries in half.
Beat the whipped cream, powdered sugar, vanilla and salt until stiff peaks form.
Put one cake layer on a flat serving board.
Spread with about 2 cups whipped cream and top with sliced strawberries.
Put the second cake layer on top.
Put remaining whipped cream over top and sides of cake.
Wash eggplant and cut in half lengthwise.
Carefully remove pulp, leaving 1/2-inch of the outer shell.
Dice pulp.
Dust chicken with flour.
Melt oleo in heavy skillet and add chicken.
Cook over moderate heat about 15 minutes on each side. Pour mushrooms with broth into saucepan. Add bouillon cube and heat.
Blend wine and cornstarch (to mushrooms) until thickened. Allow sour cream to come to room temperature.
Place in bowl, stir until smooth.
Add to sauce.
Remove chicken to warm place.
Pour sauce into skillet.
Heat and serve over chicken and rice on platter.
Stir ingredients until dissolved.
Beat until smooth (will be thin but will thicken later on).
Keep in refrigerator.
Layer first 3 ingredients in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix together milk, eggs, salt, mustard, pepper and onions.
Pour over dry ingredients.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake 1 to 1 1/2 hours in 350° oven.
In large pot, brown hamburger.
Open macaroni and cheese box, reserve cheese package until later.
Add 2 cups water, spinach and macaroni (only, not cheese) to hamburger and bring to boil. Reduce heat, simmer 10 minutes.
Add cheese package, Cheddar, partially drained kidney beans and garlic salt to taste.
Stir well.
Let "sit" 10 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
May be doubled.
Mix together and freeze until a mush.
