Combine dry ingredients in a bag; add chicken and shake. Cook in butter 8 to 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Butter 8 muffin cups.
Mix oat bran, baking powder, cinnamon and salt (optional) in a bowl.
Stir in almonds.
In separate bowl combine milk, egg, honey and chopped apple.
Make a well in dry ingredients and add milk mixture.
Stir just until moistened.
Spoon into prepared muffin cups.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Serves 8.
Place ground beef in casserole dish with onion.
Place potatoes on top. Mix cream of chicken soup with 1/2 can of water; pour over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients except milk.
Add enough milk to form balls.
Drop from teaspoon into hot fat.
Cook until well browned and cooked through.
Serve hot.
Cook macaroni.
Mix other ingredients with macaroni.
Sprinkle with crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix syrup and milk in a large bowl; add potatoes.
Beat eggs and butter.
Combine 2 mixtures.
Add other ingredients and mix. Pour into greased 2-quart casserole dish and bake 1 hour at 350° or until done.
Serves 12.
Preheat oven to 3325 degrees.
In large mixing bowl beat eggs until foamy.
Beat in flour, sugar, and brown sugar until well blended.
Beat in softened butter.
Stir in chocolate morsels. Pour into pie shell and bake 55 to 60 mins.
Mix all the ingredients together, except margarine and crackers.
Mix the melted margarine and the crushed Ritz crackers. Put this mixture on top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Put in icebox to set.
Mix butter, sugar and syrup. Bring to a boil over low heat. Beat eggs gradually. Add syrup mixture. Mix in nuts, salt and vanilla. Pour into crust and bake about 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.
Toss ingredients together.
Serve on a bed of lettuce with dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, cream margarine and brown sugar.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Beat in vanilla.
Combine the flour, baking powder and salt; gradually add to the creamed mixture. Stir in the chocolate chips and pecans.
Spread into a greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack.
Yield: 2 dozen.
Mix and bake at 350° until set.
Grease a 2-quart casserole. Spread rice on bottom.
Mix flour, chili powder, salt and pepper.
Spread over rice.
Dot with 1/2 tablespoon butter.
Mix beef and onions and put over rice. Repeat. Pour over the layers the tomatoes with liquid. Spread corn on top and dot with butter. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes. Serves 6.
Melt margarine in a large skillet. Add onion and cubed pork. Cook until pork is tender. Add other ingredients.
Season with garlic salt and pepper to taste.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into a large baking pan.
Cover with crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes, until golden brown.
Serve hot.
Put margarine and cheese in bowl; microwave until soft.
Drain crab.
Mix all ingredients together.
Spread onto English muffins; partially freeze them.
Cut into pieces and freeze for appetizers. When ready to eat, broil until golden and eat.
Mix sugar, butter, corn syrup and salt in pan.
Boil and cook 5 minutes (candy thermometer, 250°) and add vanilla.
Pour over popcorn and mix well. Bake in a 225° oven for 1 hour, stirring at 15 minute intervals.
Mix all ingredients together and form it in small loaves in shallow pan.
Mix brown sugar, water, mustard and vinegar to make a sauce.
Pour sauce over; cover with aluminum foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Remove foil.
Baste a couple times with sauce.
Put all
of the ingredients into a blender and mix well until ice cubes are crushed.
Soak cucumbers for 24 hours in lime and enough water to cover. Drain and soak for 3 hours in clean clear water.
Drain.
Simmer for 2 hours in 1 cup white vinegar, red food coloring and enough water to cover.
Drain.
Dissolve each box of jello in 1 cup of hot water and 3/4 cup of cold water and pour into square cake pans; let set.
Cut in 1/2 inch cubes.
Soften gelatin in cold water and dissolve in hot pineapple juice; let thicken slightly.
Whip cream, add sugar and vanilla, combine with gelatin and pineapple juice and fold in jello cubes.
Brown beef; add all ingredients and warm.
Serve on hamburger buns.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook chuck with onion and pepper until done; drain off fat. Add remaining ingredients.
Pour into a crock-pot; turn on high until well heated, then turn on low and cook 4 to 5 hours.
Saute mushrooms with butter or margarine.
Add the cream and salt to taste.
Thicken with flour (mix flour with water). While cooking, add the Worcestershire sauce to hot mixture and then refrigerate overnight to thicken.
Use to make tea sandwiches.
Drain pickle slices and return pickles to jar. Boil sugar, vinegar and celery seed. Pour over dill slices. Refrigerate at least 24 hours before serving.
Melt cheese in soup in top of double boiler or crock-pot.
Add remaining ingredients.
Serve warm with tortilla chips.
Yields approximately 3 pints.
Using a large skillet, fry bacon until crisp.
Drain on paper towel.
Use 1 tablespoon grease to saute onion.
Add Worcestershire sauce, horseradish and catsup and stir.
Add lima beans, tomato soup and bacon bits.
Stir well.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole and bake at 325° for 1 hour, uncovered.
Serves 6 to 8.
Very tasty.

Cover onions with cold water. Let stand 1 hour, changing water every 15 minutes (this takes the bite away from raw onion). Drain. Mix rest of ingredients. Put into 2-quart covered dish or jar. Chill at least 24 hours, stirring occasionally to mix well. Makes 2 quarts. Good with steak and good in sandwiches.
Combine all together.
Pour in unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 350°.
Later cover with egg whites.
Mix together brown sugar, cinnamon and pecans.
Set aside. Mix together cake mix, eggs, oil, sugar and sour cream.
Pour half of mixture into 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Pour half of brown sugar/cinnamon mixture over cake batter.
Add remaining cake batter and then remaining brown sugar mixture.
With fork, swirl brown sugar/cinnamon mixture into batter several times.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix powdered sugar, milk and vanilla; pour on top to glaze.
Cover bottom of an 11 x 17-inch ungreased pan with rolls spread out flat.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cool.
Mix the cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise and salad dressing mix; spread over baked rolls.
Mix diced vegetables together; sprinkle over the cream cheese mixture. Cover with plastic wrap; press vegetables down into cream cheese. Keep covered.
Chill 3 to 4 hours.
Cut into small bars.
Mix all ingredients together.
Makes 3 - 8 inch layers, 2 - 9 inch layers or 1 - 9 x 13 2 cake.
Bake at 325° until done.
Cool cake well before icing.
Keep in the refrigerator.
Bake your choice of yellow cake.
While cake is baking, put evaporated milk, flavoring and sugar in a measuring cup.
Add enough water to make 2 cups.
Whip by hand.
Beat shortening, sugars, vanilla, water and egg until light and fluffy.
Add flour, soda and salt.
Stir in nuts and chips. Drop from a teaspoon on greased baking sheets.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 100.
Brown hamburger and sausage in frying pan.
Drain off fat. In saucepan, melt the Velveeta.
Once melted, add soup and Ro-Tel. Pour ingredients from saucepan to a crock-pot.
Stir in meat mixture and chopped onion.
Serve hot with tortilla chips.
Mix pudding, pineapple and juice.
Add rest of ingredients. Mix well and chill.
Dump above ingredients in order into a ungreased 11x13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream the cream cheese.
Drain pineapple and add to cream cheese.
Use 7-Up to mix Jell-O in place of cold water.
Mix cream mixture in Jell-O.
When Jell-O begins to harden (or congeal) sprinkle nuts on top or in cream mixture.
Place in refrigerator until firm and ready to serve.
Orange Jell-O is also good with this.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Blend in shortening and water.
Beat 2 minutes on medium speed with electric blender. Pour batter into a 9-inch pie pan.
Do not spread.
Pour favorite pie filling in center of batter.
Do not stir.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes in a 425° preheated oven.

Preheat oven to 350°. Mix flour, sugar, and cocoa in ungreased 2 quart pan (9 x 9). In a small bowl mix milk, butter, and vanilla; add to flour mixture and stir with a fork until mixed and smooth. Stir in nuts and spread the dough evenly in the pan. Sprinkle with brown sugar and 1/4 cup cocoa. Pour hot water over batter. Do not stir. Bake for 40 minutes.
In saucepan or large skillet, add oil and garlic; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add all other ingredients, except scrod and angel hair; simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
Wash scrod in cold water and towel dry.
Add to tomato mixture.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Pour into small greased and floured loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Bring to a boil the water and salt.
Add tapioca.
Bring back to good boil again, cover and turn off heat.
Let set covered an hour or longer, until balls are clear.
Add Jell-O and sugar. Stir until dissolved.
Chill.
When ready to serve, add whipped cream and any fruit desired.
Makes 12 to 15 servings.
In a 2-quart saucepan, stir together 1 cup sugar and cornstarch.
Gradually stir in water until smooth.
Stir in egg yolks, stirring constantly.
Bring to a boil over medium heat and boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir in next two ingredients. Pour into pastry shell and top with egg whites, beaten stiff.
In a bowl, combine beans, corn, soup, sour cream, cheese and onions.
Pour into an ungreased 2-quart baking dish.
Mix 1/4 cup warm water with yeast and let stand about 1/2 minute before mixing in the flour.
Then add all ingredients, mix well and knead for about 10 minutes.
Make small rolls and let rise in warm place for about 4 hours.
Roll out small pieces of dough by hand into size of a cigarette and about 16 to 18 inches long, twist and make round circle's and brush with beaten egg. Bake in 375° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mix together oil, dill weed, lemon pepper and dressing.
Add crackers.
Put in large bowl; stir occasionally.
Store in airtight container.
Very easy!
Just combine ingredients and serve surrounded by crackers.
Japanese rice crackers are the best.
I love this dip!
Spread each tortilla with cheese; heat until melted.
In a bowl, toss chicken with salsa, peppers and onions.
Spoon 1/2 cup mixture into each tortilla.
Roll up tightly.
Makes 24.
In small skillet, melt margarine over medium-low heat.
Add almonds.
Cook until light golden brown, stirring constantly. Remove from heat; cool.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 250° for 30 to 40 minutes, then at 350° until done.
Cook lasagne noodles until tender.
Drain on paper towel. Brown meat; drain off excess grease.
Add spaghetti sauce and oregano.
Blend eggs and cottage cheese together.
Spread thin layer of meat mixture in 8 x 11-inch pan.
Layer of noodles, all of egg mixture, noodles, then rest of meat mixture.
Top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Layer 3/4 stick of margarine, hash browns, onion, sour cream and chicken soup (mixed together) and cheese.
Toss the corn flakes with 1 stick of margarine and use for top layer.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Empty boxes of sugar into large bowl. Mash out the lumps, then add milk and melted butter; mix well. Add coconut.
(May be easier to mix with hands.) Place in freezer for 1 hour, then roll into small balls. Put back in freezer for 30 to 40 minutes.
Beat all ingredients together for 5 minutes.
Use a 9 x 13-inch pan, greased and floured.
Pour
1/2 of batter in pan, then add 1/2 of topping, then remaining batter, then remaining topping.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
In covered 5-quart Dutch oven, over medium heat, simmer potatoes, onions, celery, cloves, garlic, salt, bay leaf, dill seed and 1 cup water for about 25 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Discard cloves.
Add fish, 1 cup water and remaining ingredients.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat to low.
Cover, simmer 5 to 10 minutes until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork. Garnish with parsley.
Fry unbreaded Wingflingers according to directions.
Melt margarine and stir in remaining ingredients.
Coat cooked Wingflingers with sauce and bake 10 minutes in oven at 350°. Serve with Blue cheese dressing, celery sticks and carrot sticks.
Beat cream cheese at room temperature until fluffy.
Add reserved juice from cherries.
Add remaining ingredients and fold together.
Chill in refrigerator 6 to 8 hours.
Cook diced Chicken until tender, let cool for 1 hour.
Combine Chicken, Celery, Eggs, Onion, Relish, Mayonnaise, Salt and Pepper. Toss together.
Cut the tops off the Tomatoes, scoop out a portion of the pulp and discard; fill each tomato with a portion of the Chicken Salad and put each Tomato on a portion of the shredded Lettuce.
Chill for 1/2 hour in the refrigerator before serving.
Mix all ingredients together well and bake until firm and brown.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Layer in microwavable pie pan; soft shell, beans, Cheddar cheese, Mozzarella cheese and picante sauce.
Layer again and cover with shell.
Microwave for 10 minutes or bake 10 minutes at 350° for 20 minutes.
Top with more picante sauce; serve.
Boil chicken; remove from broth and cool.
Save broth.
Debone chicken.
Cook 12 to 16 ounces spaghetti in chicken broth until tender.
Do not drain.
When spaghetti is tender, add onion and green pepper which have been sauteed in butter.
Add Ro-Tel tomatoes and Velveeta cheese which have been cubed.
Add chicken. Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° until bubbly.
Combine first 6 ingredients in deep 3-quart casserole.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave on High for 4 minutes.
Stir well. Microwave again for 2 1/2 to 4 1/2 minutes, or until soft ball stage.
Add pecans and stir to coat.
Spread on wax paper and cool.
Cream margarine, butter and sugar until light and smooth.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Fill sugar box with flour (to rim).
Add to above mixture and beat well.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Grease tube pan.
Add batter; shake down. Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until done.
Remove from pan immediately.
Mix together and pour into 9 x 13 pan.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.

In a 3-quart saucepan, cook onion, carrots and garlic in hot oil until tender, but not brown. Add undrained tomatoes, sugar, salt, oregano, pepper and red pepper. Bring to boiling; reduce heat. Simmer, uncovered, for 45 to 60 minutes or to desired consistency.
Cook pasta in large amount of boiling salted water until tender; drain well. Serve with tomato mixture. Serves 8.
Combine first 8 ingredients.
Dry frankfurters and dip into combined ingredients.
Fry until golden brown.
Serves 10.

recipes.t: St. Louis Style Peanut Butter Pie
d: Cream together peanut butter, sugar and
cream	cheese. Blend in 2/3 carton Cool Whip. Pour into pie
shell.
Drizzle chocolate syrup over top.
Refrigerate for 2 hours until firm. Top with remaining Cool Whip.
Cook squash and onion in a little salted water for 5 minutes; drain.
Combine soup and milk; stir in carrots.
Fold in drained squash and onion.
Combine stuffing and butter.
Spread half of stuffing mixture in bottom of 12 x 7-inch baking dish.
Spoon vegetable mix on top.
Sprinkle remaining stuffing mix over vegetables.
Bake at 350° for 25 or 30 minutes or until heated.
Saute green onions in butter.
Stir in flour.
Add crawfish tails and fat; continue to saute.
Stir in mushrooms and seasoning.
Fold in sour cream just before serving.
Keep hot in chafing dish.
To freeze, omit sour cream and add when ready to serve.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Chill until ready to serve.
Makes 1 cup of sauce.
Mix together the first 5 ingredients.
Add egg, buttermilk and onion.
Mix well.
Drop batter by rounded teaspoons into deep hot grease (375°).
Cook, turning frequently, about 3 to 5 minutes until golden brown.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Beat with
mixer.
Very good on rye bread.
Can be made ahead of time and refrigerated.
In 9 x 13-inch Pyrex pan place 1/2 of cubed bread.
Mix crab, onion, mayonnaise, almonds, celery and green pepper.
Put over bread.
Put rest of bread on top.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Combine sugar, cornstarch and dash of salt.
Cook until clear. Add jello.
Stir until dissolved.
Cool.
Add strawberries. Pour into baked pie shell.
Refrigerate.
Serve with whipped cream.
Preheat oven to 325°. Grease cookie sheets. Work butter in a bowl until creamy.
Add sugars and beat well.
Add egg and vanilla. Beat well.
Blend in water and peanut butter.
Gradually add dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Drop by teaspoons onto cookie sheet, 2-inches apart. Crisscross with fork.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes or until light brown.
Break up saltines.
Mix all other ingredients except cracker meal.
Let stand until crackers are moist.
Add crabmeat; roll in cracker meal.
Makes about 2 1/2 dozen medium crab cakes.
Let stand in refrigerator at least an hour before frying.
Mix margarine and cheese with a mixer.
Add remaining ingredients. Shape into small balls and place on ungreased cookie sheet, flattened with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix soup and cream cheese.
Heat and stir until cheese is melted. Add mayonnaise and mix well.
Add remaining ingredients. Serve with chips or crackers.
Trim off thick part of each cabbage leaf.
Cover leaf with water; soak 2 minutes.
Mix beef, onion, rice, tomato juice and pepper.
Place about 3 tablespoons meat mixture on each cabbage leaf.
Tuck in sides and roll up.

Mix the buttermilk and soda and let stand. Beat egg whites until stiff. Cream sugar, oleo and shortening. Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each. Add buttermilk alternately with flour to creamed mixture. Stir in vanilla. Fold in beaten egg whites. Gently stir in nuts and coconut. Bake in 3 or 4 layer pans at 325° for 25 minutes.
Melt butter and chocolate; cool.
Beat eggs, salt and sugar. Add chocolate.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bake at 325° for about 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool.
Beat egg white until bubbly.
Blend in butter, sugar, flavoring and coloring.
This should be like cookie dough.
Knead well, then roll into balls.
Let sit on wax paper; press down with a fork.
Cook clams and bay leaf for 5 minutes with just enough water to cover.
Remove bay leaf.
Saute onion, celery and green pepper in butter and add to clams and clam juice.
Add the thickened milk, potatoes and bacon bits; cook gently until potatoes are done.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic.
Bake in oven at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Then, when cool, top with whipped topping.
Stew chicken and cook pasta in broth.
Mix dressing, mayonnaise, cheese and olives.
Cut chicken into bite sized pieces and mix all together.
Store in tightly covered bowl.
Will keep up to two weeks.
Into a 2-quart pot, first add sauteed onion.
Brown and drain the meat; add to pot.
Then add tomato soup and chili powder. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add kidney beans, stewed tomatoes, catsup and sugar.
Mix together and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve.

recipes.t: Grilled Sausage And Scallops With Peppers, Lemon, Basil And Garlic
d: Blanch the scallops in boiling, salted water for 1 minute. Drain and allow to cool.
Cook the sausage in boiling water until completely cooked, about 5 minutes.
Drain and allow to cool. Thread the scallops, sausages and vegetables on skewers and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the skewers over a medium fire until all the ingredients have attained some brown crusting, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Slide the ingredients off skewers into a large bowl.
Add basil, garlic, oil, lemon juice and balsamic vinegar.
Shake the bowl until everything is well mixed.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add sugar and then cold water and all juices.
Yields 60 (4-ounce) servings.
Grind in food grinder or blender the cranberries, apple and orange.
Dissolve jello in hot liquid.
Combine all ingredients and store in refrigerator.
Keeps well for days.
Start with beans and layer each item in a glass dish.
Serve cold.
Chop cauliflower, broccoli, onion and tomatoes.
Mix mayonnaise, sugar, vinegar, sauce and lemon juice; stir over vegetables.
Allow to set in refrigerator overnight before serving.
Thoroughly mix sugar, salt and cornstarch in top of double boiler.
Add cold water and milk; blend until smooth.
Stir constantly over direct heat until mixture boils and becomes transparent-looking.
Place over boiling water, cover and cook 15 minutes.
Cook macaroni for 2 minutes less than the box calls for. Drain.
Put under cold running water until macaroni is completely cool; drain.
In saucepan, place cut up chunks of Velveeta, butter, milk and flour.
Heat slowly, dissolving cheese and flour. Add all grated Cheddar cheese, except for 1/2 cup.
Pour over macaroni in a 2 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Top with 1/2 cup cheese and bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook sausage and drain.
Combine eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Mix well.
Layer pie shell with cheese and sausage.
Pour egg mixture over this and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Saute onion and celery in oil.
Add remaining ingredients. Pour into pie shell.
Put on top crust.
Moisten bottom crust around edges to seal.
Prick with fork.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
Other vegetables such as green peppers or onions may be used or included.
Mix the first 6 ingredients together well.
Roll into ball or log shape.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Refrigerate overnight to blend all flavors.
Serve with crackers.
Stays well in refrigerator several weeks.
Boil eggs, cool and peel. Place eggs in jar, fill with remaining ingredients. Top with onions and fill jar with vinegar, seal, leave untouched for 24 hours.
Cook onions in melted butter until tender. Add Ro-Tel. Simmer for 7 minutes. Add corn. Cook on low for 12 minutes. Add salt to taste.

In skillet, cook sausage fully, then add onion until transparent. Drain well. Add to sausage mixture the next 7 ingredients; mix well. Chill for at least 2 hours. May do ahead and chill overnight. Then shape into small meatballs and roll in flour. Beat together milk and eggs. Dip meatballs into mixture, then roll in bread crumbs. Fry in oil until golden brown. Change oil when needed. Bake in 375° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Bring cream to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Continue to boil while sifting flour into cream slowly, beating vigorously until mixture becomes heavy and butter starts to form.
Remove butterfat as it appears.
Add about 1 quart hot milk gradually and beat until smooth and the consistency of cooked cereal.
Add salt to taste.
Serve hot with butterfat, sugar and cinnamon.
Tie spices loosely in bag and boil in water.
Add tea tied loosely in bag and steep 5 minutes; remove bags.
Heat frui juices and sugar; add to tea and serve.
Serves 25.
Combine the mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon juice.
Layer 1 cup beans, 1/2 cup peas, 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice, 1/2 of the onion and 1/2 of the water chestnuts.
Spread 1/2 of the mayonnaise mixture and repeat.
Top with crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes. Serves 8 or more.
Layer first 5 ingredients.
Mix Miracle Whip and sugar together and spread on top. Cover all with cheese and chill several hours or overnight.
Serves 20.
Place beans in large kettle and cover with water.
Add salt to beans and water; soak overnight.
Next morning, drain and add 2 quarts water.
Add some ham or chicken pieces.
Boil slowly for 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Add the rest of ingredients.
Simmer another 30 minutes and serve with cornbread or crackers.
Poach chicken breast in water seasoned with black peppercorns, a little salt, celery tops and sprinkle of garlic salt.
Cook 5 minutes and turn off stove.
Allow chicken to sit in broth until completely cooled.
When the chicken is completely cooled remove from broth and cut into small dices.
Combine sour cream and mayonnaise.
Mix chicken, celery, apples, walnuts, and sour cream/mayonnaise mixture well.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours (or overnight).
Serve on butter croissants with leaf lettuce or serve alone with slices of fresh fruit in the summer for a cool evening meal.
Blend all in an electric blender for about 1 minute.
Spread thin sandwiches with this and freeze or else freeze.
Spread in small amounts.
In a medium skillet, saute celery and onion in 2 tablespoons butter until tender.
Add bread cubes and stir until lightly browned.
Stir in potatoes, parsley, salt, pepper, milk and egg. Mix well.
Spoon into a greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Dot with remaining butter.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 30 to 40 minutes or until lightly browned.
Garnish with additional parsley. Yield:
6 to 8 servings.
Heat water, 1 tablespoon vinegar and 1 teaspoon salt to boiling.
Add beets.
Cover and heat to boiling; cook 30 minutes or until tender.
Drain.
Cut beets into slices.
Mix olive oil, 1/4 cup vinegar, sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, cloves and onions.
Pour over beets and marinate overnight.
Thaw potatoes in 9 x 13 baking pan. Mix with other ingredients. Top with 1/2 cup crushed corn flakes and 1/4 cup melted butter. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Wash and peel peaches.
Drop peeled peaches into cold salt and vinegar solution (2 tablespoons salt and 2 tablespoons vinegar, 1 gallon water) immediately to prevent discoloration.
Mix sugar and vinegar and hot water; add spices (tied loosely in cloth bag). Boil and skim.
Wash peaches in cold water and drain.
Drop drained peaches into boiling syrup and cook 5 to 6 minutes.
Pack in preheated jars.
Cover with boiling spiced vinegar or let stand overnight in syrup, then pack in jars.
Cover with boiling vinegar.
Seal and process 30 minutes in hot water bath at simmering temperature.
Press crescent rolls in a cookie sheet and bake for 10 minutes (as on package).
Let cool.
Mix the next four ingredients and spread on crust.
Chop all the vegetables fine and press on cream cheese mixture.
Next, press 1 cup shredded cheese on top of the vegetables.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Cherry Bread Pudding(With Almond Cream Sauce)
d: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Combine the bread with the 4 cups of liquid. Mix well. Beat together the eggs, sugar and almond flavoring. Combine with bread mixture and then stir in the cherries. Melt the butter in a 9x13x2 inch baking pan. Pour bread pudding mixture into pan and bake for about an hour. Serve with Almond Cream Sauce.
Combine sugar, syrup, milk and salt.
Cook until it forms a soft ball.
Remove from heat; add butter and vanilla; set aside until lukewarm.
Beat until it thickens and is creamy.
Combine Jell-O, water and pineapple and boil gently together for 10 minutes.
Add cream cheese as soon as you remove boiling mixture from heat.
When cooled and beginning to thicken, add celery and nuts.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour mixture into ring or mold and chill thoroughly.
Mix the first 5 ingredients together.
Toss; stir in dressing and chill.
Combine all ingredients.
Beat until smooth and of a spreading consistency.
Chill.
Makes about 2 cups.
Mix together all ingredients while fish is warm.
Place in refrigerator in a covered jar for at least 3 hours.
The haddock will absorb the juice and taste from the lobster.
Serve as a salad or lobster roll.
Grease 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Quarter biscuits and place in bottom of pan to cover.
Mix hamburger and sauce and then pour on top of biscuits.
Bake for 25 minutes at 400°.
Top with cheese and bake an extra 5 to 10 minutes.
Beat eggs slightly.
Add rest of ingredients and pour into 9-inch unbaked deep dish pie shell or 2 small shallow pie shells. Bake slowly in 350° oven for 55 to 60 minutes or until slightly set.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Cover and chill overnight.
Stir on low flame sugar, water, butter and bananas (mashed) until butter melts.
Set aside to cool.
Beat eggs and vanilla; add to bananas.
Sift flour, salt, baking powder and soda.
Add to batter and stir until blended.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in a greased loaf tin.
Cream well the sugar and butter.
Add egg and pulp.
Sift dry ingredients.
Mix all together. Add in raisins and nuts.
Mix. Drop onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 12 to 15 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients.
Top with fried, crispy bacon.
Mix sugar and mayonnaise and spread over bacon.
Let set in refrigerator covered 2 hours or longer before serving.
In large bowl, mix sugar, flour and salt.
Add and mix by hand the
shortening (oil), unbeaten eggs, vanilla and baking soda dissolved in buttermilk.
Add pecans and bananas.
Pour into 2 loaf pans or a large ring mold.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut chicken into bite size pieces.
Roll into Italian bread crumbs until completely coated.
Place in baking pan.
*The hot and spicy is particularly good.
Heat oven to 475°.
Grease cookie sheet.
In a large bowl, mix the hot water and yeast.
Add water (warm) and sugar slowly.
Add 5 cups flour.
Stir until smooth (not sticking to sides); knead it.
Form dough into golf ball size balls and shape each into pretzels.
Fill a frying pan with water.
For each cup of water used, add 1 tablespoon baking soda.
Place pretzels in gently boiling water for 30 seconds.
Take out of the water and place on cookie sheet.
Salt pretzels.
Bake for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Can be frozen before baking.
Remove	bone
from crab.

Spread evenly over bread in pan.
Blend together soup and eggs, pour over sandwiches.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until set and lightly browned.
Stir together sugar and oil.
Beat in eggs and pumpkin.
Add and mix in dry ingredients.
Pour into a greased bread pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Coat chicken lightly with melted margarine and dredge in seasoned dry bread crumbs.
Place in an ungreased shallow baking pan.
Oven fry at 425° for 5 to 9 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through.
For crisper chicken, coat pan with 1 tablespoon melted margarine or vegetable oil and preheat oven for 5 minutes before adding chicken.
Whip up cream cheese with fork until creamy.
Put in all ingredients except 1 cup pecans.
Mix and form in ball and roll in remaining pecans.
Wrap in aluminum foil and let set overnight (so flavors will not be so strong).
Serve with Ritz crackers.
Place chicken in bottom of casserole dish.
Slice eggs over. Dilute soup with 1/2 can chicken broth.
Pour over above.
Spread dressing mix over this.
Pour 1 1/2 cups broth over dressing mix. Put pats of butter on top and sprinkle with black pepper.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Blend cream cheese with sour cream (with electric mixer).
Add taco seasoning and mix.
Pour in dish.
Drain salsa sauce well and sprinkle over mixture.
Place shredded lettuce on top, then fresh tomato and then shredded cheese.
Serve cold with taco chips. Serves 10.
Mix all ingredients together.
Spoon into muffin pan sprayed with Pam.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Makes 6 muffins.
Cream sugar and butter together.
Add eggs and zucchini.
Add flour, soda, baking powder and cinnamon, sifted together.
Add zucchini mixture, blending well.
Add nuts and raisins.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients, except ground beef.
Mix well.
Add ground beef; mix lightly but thoroughly. Place in loaf pan and bake 1 hour.
Let stand 5 minutes before slicing.
Peel potatoes and slice.
Boil in salted water until tender. Drain potatoes.
Mash thoroughly and add eggs.
Mix well.
Add sugar and butter and milk and flavoring.
Mix well.
Pour into unbaked pie crust and bake on 350° until done.

Press into ungreased 9x13 inch pan.
Combine all ingredients.
Shape into patties.
Bake at 450° for 1 hour.

Layer first 4 ingredients in order (tuna on toast, with the onion over tuna and the eggs over onion).
Mix the soup, milk, parsley and lemon juice together.
Pour over sandwiches and broil 5 to 10 minutes.
Makes 4 sandwiches.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cover peeled and diced eggplant with water; add 1 teaspoon salt and simmer over low heat until tender, 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain and set aside to cool.
Combine eggplant with remaining ingredients and mix.
Pour into square or round baking dish sprayed with nonstick cooking spray and bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Recipe makes 6 servings.
Ultra low-fat.

In large skillet, saute onion in butter until tender. Stir in remaining ingredients. Bring to boil. Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, for 3 minutes or until sauce is slightly thickened, stirring occasionally. Yields 4 servings.
Cut up
onion
and
celery.
Brown in butter.
Add rice and brown.
Place in casserole; add salt, pepper, consomme and water. Cover and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix the first 3 ingredients to a soft dough. Drop by teaspoon on greased baking sheet. Bake 10 minutes at 450°.
Melt the last 3 ingredients. Brush mixture over biscuits immediately out of the oven!
Pound steak 1/4-inch thick; cut into serving pieces.
Blend egg and milk.
Dip meat in egg mixture, then in crumbs.
Slowly brown meat in hot oil, turning once.
Cover; cook on low heat for 45 to 60 minutes, until tender.
Season to taste.

Cook rhubarb until done.
Add sugar and Sweet*10.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Pour this mixture over jello.
Stir until jello is dissolved.
Cool.
Put in jars.
Enjoy the preserves!
Brown meat with onions.
Add tomatoes, beans and rice.
Pour into casserole dish.
Top with crushed Fritos and grated cheese. Bake in 350° oven until cheese is melted and bubbly.

Put milk, onion, lemon juice, Tabasco, celery salt, garlic salt, salt, pepper, and egg in a bowl. Add salmon that has been boned and dark skin removed. Flake with a fork. Add oleo and crumbs. If dry, add salmon juice. Pour into a buttered casserole dish and bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 45 minutes. Serves 4-6.
Mix dry Jell-o, pineapple and sour cream. Mix cool whip, nuts, and marshmallows. Combine Jell-o mixture with cool
whip mixture. Chill in mold or bowl for at least 2 hours before serving.
Stir-fry chicken in oil for 4 minutes.
Combine chicken and vegetables; stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup mayonnaise and soy sauce to taste.
Mix
together rice, chicken, broccoli, cream of chicken soup, water,
salt,
pepper
and poultry seasoning.
Top this with dabs of butter.	Sprinkle cracker crumbs on top.
Drizzle melted butter over
the	crumbs.
Bake
at
350° until top is brown.
Toast Chex crumbs in a 300° oven for 10 minutes; set aside. Combine egg, seasoned salt and taco sauce.
Stir in ground beef and Chex.
Shape into 4 oval patties to fit bread loaf.
Broil or grill for 10 to 12 minutes, or until done.
Turn midway.
Place, end to end, on split French bread.
Spoon on additional taco sauce.
Top with tomato, lettuce and cheese.
To serve, place top on loaf and slice crosswise.
Mix mustard and peppers with enough water to make a smooth paste.
Add sugars and vinegar.
Bring to a boil, stirring continuously.
Add butter and stir until melted.
Add a little of the hot mixture to the eggs; mix well. Pour this into hot mixture in pan.
Continue to stir.
Bring to a boil again over medium heat.
Pour into jar.
Cool and refrigerate. This is guaranteed to open your sinuses!!!
Brush one side of one slice bread with melted butter.
Spread Russian dressing on other side of bread slice.
Place corned beef on dressing, put sauerkraut on top of corned beef and then the cheese on top of that.
Cover with other bread slice.
In a skillet, melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter; place sandwich in skillet and cook until browned and cheese is melted.
Serves 1.
Put each vegetable through food chopper, using coarse blade. If vegetables are covered with liquid, drain off and discard liquid.
Measure each vegetable after chopping.
Beat eggs gently with sugar.
Add oil, water and pumpkin.
Add flour, soda, salt, cinnamon, dates and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in 2 loaf pans.

Bake squash in oven or microwave until nearly tender. Saute apple and celery in butter for 5 minutes. Stir in crumbs and salt and pepper. Fill squash with mixture and top with cheese. Bake 15 minutes longer until tender. Serves 2.
Let stand at least an hour before serving.
Yield: 2 1/2 cups.
With mixer, mix sugars, oleo and oil, then beat in eggs and vanilla.
Sift together the flour, baking soda and cream of tartar.
Add them to mixture.
Cover and place in refrigerator for several hours or overnight.
Form into small balls and roll in sugar.
Flatten with fork.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix first 8 ingredients in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour in hot pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill overnight.
Roll into balls the size of a quarter and bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Place sausage in iron skillet and bake at 500° until done.
Saute onion for a few minutes in olive oil and butter, then add bell pepper.
A couple of minutes later, add corn, stirring all the while.
This mixture should just be about done, then add diced tomatoes.
Cook about 2 more minutes, then season with salt, pepper and sugar.
Makes 6 servings.
Melt butter and mix in next 4 ingredients.
Add both milks. Bring to boil and boil for 1 minute or until thick.
Stir in Parmesan cheese and parsley flakes.
Boil potatoes and cut in cubes; place in casserole dish.
Cut up wieners and add to potatoes; mix in sauce.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt shortening in skillet; add beef, onion, salt, pepper and flour.
Cook until meat loses its red color, stirring occasionally.
Drain off excess fat.
Stir in water, Worcestershire sauce and ketchup; simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 20 minutes or until of desired consistency.
Serve in buns.
Makes 8 sandwiches.

Blend softened margarine and grated cheese. Add flour, salt and cayenne pepper. Knead dough, finally adding Rice Krispies. Roll in small balls, then flatten with hand on cookie sheet. Bake at 350° until done, approximately 10 to 12 minutes, depending on the oven.
Combine egg, milk, flour, salt and garlic salt in bowl; mix well to form batter.
Dip each zucchini round into batter; fry in deep fat.
Batter zucchini when ready to fry so each piece is coated.
Fry until crisp and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix cottage cheese and Cool Whip, then add fruit cocktail and jello.
Let set for 2 hours before serving.
Keeps in refrigerator for 2 weeks.
Place all ingredients in blender except for oil and poppy seed.
Process for 15 seconds in blender.
Then add oil and seed. Mix well.
Serve with salad of spinach, mushrooms, bean sprouts, mandarin orange, small red onion, fresh strawberries and sunflower seeds.
Follow directions on mixing from the back of cake box.
Use the pineapple juice in place of water.
If pineapple juice is not enough just add water for the right amount required.
Cook cake by using directions from cake box.
Mix cream cheese, vanilla pudding and milk (that's required on pudding box).
Add sugar to taste. Next, spread whip topping.
Then place cherries for the finishing touch.
Add pecans if desired.
Keep refrigerated until served.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown sausage; drain.
In 2-quart baking dish, combine sausage, sauce, noodles and 1/2 of Mozzarella cheese.
Mix well.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake 25 minutes or until heated through.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix first 3 ingredients and line cake pan with mixture.
Beat egg whites, butter and powdered sugar for 10 minutes and spread over cracker mixture.
Add pineapple, slice bananas long ways and place over pineapple.
Top with whipped cream, nuts and maraschino cherries.

Add marshmallows.

the chocolate and peanut butter. Add all ingredients and mix

Let cool and place in a tin.

Beat the butter, sugar, orange peel, and vanilla until smooth. Beat in the egg. Mix in the flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix until dough comes together. Mix in the cranberries and coconut. Shape into balls and place on a greased baking sheet. Bake at 350 for 10-15 minutes. Let cookies cool... and then enjoy!
Combine ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate 6 hours.
Serve with assorted fresh vegetables.
Yield: 2 1/4 cups.
Combine all ingredients except chicken. Stir well. Pour over chicken.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Good with rice or mashed potatoes. Makes lots of gravy.
Let pie crust stand out of refrigerator for 1 hour.
Crush vanilla wafers in blender, also nuts and coconut.
Mix all together, form in balls and roll in powdered sugar.
Cook noodles in salted water.
Brown meat and onion in oil. Drain.
Add oregano and sauce to meat.
Simmer for 15 minutes. Layer noodles, cottage cheese, meat sauce and Mozzarella cheese in pan.
Repeat.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Mix vegetables.
Combine remaining ingredients and bring to a boil.
Simmer until well blended, then cool.
Pour over vegetables.
It will stay crisp for several days.
Cook macaroni.
Drain and cool.
Mix all ingredients and chill at least 4 hours.
(Can use yellow or red bell peppers.
Some of each looks pretty.)
Combine strawberries and sugar in bowl.
Stir in white wine. Chill several hours.
Spoon sauce and strawberries into four 6 ounce goblets.
Pour champagne over each.
Combine all ingredients in order given.
Mix thoroughly until moist. Pour into two greased bread pans.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar and 1 tablespoon of butter.
Mix until crumbly and sprinkle on top.
Bake at 350° for about 1 1/2 hours.
Combine fruit.
Add marshmallows and mix well.
Chill slightly and mix again.
Fold in whipped topping and chill overnight.
Melt caramels with water in microwave bowl, stirring occasionally.
When ready, spoon over apple slices.
Boil chicken until tender.
Use water from chicken for soup. Shred the chicken, add other ingredients and enough water to cover everything good.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Blend eggs and milk for 2 minutes.
Heat sugar in pan over very low heat until caramelized.
Immediately put caramel into large container, add remaining ingredients on top of caramel. Cover container and place into a larger pan filled with water. Heat over medium-low heat until ready.
Soften yeast in the warm water.
In a large bowl, combine shortening and hot water.
Add the sugar, salt and soup mix and stir well.
Add yeast mixture.
Gradually add the flour to make a stiff dough.
Knead on a floured board until smooth and elastic. Let rise in a warm place until double in bulk.
Punch down and let rise again 1/2 hour.
Shape in 2 loaves; it makes nice round ones in 8-inch cake pans.
Let rise until light and bake 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.
Brown beef and drain.
Place in greased 9 x 13-inch dish.
In layers on top of hamburger, put cheese, chopped chilies and onion. Pour on cream of mushroom soup and put on Tater Tots in rows. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix ingredients together and store in an airtight container for up to 6 months.
Mix in baking dish and pour 1 can mushroom soup over top. Bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Dissolve cocoa in 1 cup hot water.
Mix well.
Bake in greased and floured pan at 350°.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
Fry hamburger and drain.
Mix together hamburger, sauce, chilies, onion, salt and pepper.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Combine spaghetti and sauce; mix well.
Layer two 9 x 13-inch baking dishes with half the spaghetti; top with half of the cheese and cover with remaining spaghetti and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
(Half recipe fills one 9 x 13-inch pan.)
Melt fat; add hamburg, onion and pepper.
Cook until meat is lightly browned.
Add tomato sauce; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add kidney beans, chili and salt.
Simmer.
Beat egg whites until stiff enough to hold in points.
Add 8 tablespoons of sugar gradually and beat until fluffy.
Fold in remaining sugar, salt, candy and chocolate bits.
Cover cookie sheet with unglazed paper and drop mixture by spoonfuls onto sheet. Bake at 275° for 30 to 35 minutes, until delicately browned, firm and dry.
Remove from paper immediatley.
Kisses should be used within one week after baking, unless frozen.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
Mix sugar and cranberries together and let stand overnight or several hours.
Add gelatin to boiling water.
Stir until dissolved.
Add other ingredients and chill.
Use the pineapple juice and less water if desired.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix ground beef, half of the dry bread crumbs, 1/4 cup cream of mushroom soup, egg, thyme leaves, salt and pepper.
Press mixture evenly against bottom and sides of an ungreased 9-inch pie pan.
Cover meat mixture with the French-style green beans.
Spread remaining cream of mushroom soup over the green beans.
Bake uncovered for approximately 35 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in mixing bowl.
Cut in butter or margarine with pastry blender until mixture resemble coarse crumbs.
Add buttermilk.
Mix quickly to make a soft dough.
Turn out onto lightly floured surface.
Knead a few times to make a soft dough; don't overknead or the biscuits will turn hard and dry.
Roll out to a 6 x 6-inch square.
Place on ungreased baking sheet.
With knife, cut dough into 12 even portions; do not separate.
Bake at 400° about 15 minutes.
Dust with flour and melted butter.
Dissolve gelatin dessert mix in boiling water.
Stir in cold water and spices.
Chill until very thick.
Fold in the remaining ingredients and chill until firm.
Good with hard sauce or whipped cream.
Combine beef and 1/4 of barbecue sauce, eggs and salt.
Mix lightly and divide into 16 portions.
Gently shape into thin round patties.
Place 1 teaspoon each:
barbecue sauce, cheese, relish and onions on 8 of the patties.
Top them with remaining 8 patties.
Press edges together; broil or fry 4 minutes on one side, turn, baste with remaining barbecue sauce and cook 4 minutes longer or until meat is done.
Serve on buns.

mixture

beat until stiff peaks.
Pour filling in baked pie shell. Top

Combine all ingredients in a blender. Cover and blend until smooth. Press fruit mixture through a fine mesh strainer over a bowl to extract juices. Discard solids. Pour mixture into 3-ounce paper or plastic drink cups or pop molds. Cover with foil. Cut a slit in the foil and insert wooden sticks. Freeze several hours until pops are firm.
Mix the first 4 ingredients.
Slice each tray of rolls through the middle.
Spread sauce on both halves of each tray.
Place ham on bottom halves.
Top with remaining halves.
Cover trays with foil.
Bake at 350° to 400° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Best served hot.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, white sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Stir in the milk, oil and vanilla until smooth.
Spread in an ungreased 9 x 9 square baking pan. Combine brown sugar and remaining cocoa.
Sprinkle over batter. Pour hot water over all.
DO NOT STIR.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Serve warm.
Top with whipped cream or ice cream if desired.
Mix all but garnish and then top around edges or center of spread with them.
Bake at 350° until bubbly, about 30 minutes, but check off and on.
Serve with favorite cracker.

recipes.t: Holiday Ham And Chili Cheese Ball
d: In a small bowl, combine cheeses, deviled ham, scallions and chilies; mix well.
Shape mixture into a ball.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Wrap in plastic wrap; chill.
Remove from refrigerator to soften slightly before serving.
Serve with your favorite crackers. Makes 1 (2-cup) cheese ball.
Split hot dogs lengthwise.
Place in shallow pan.
Combine onions and potatoes.
Put on top of hot dogs.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes at 400°.
Serves four.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Mix in 9 x 13-inch greased pan with egg, 1 cup cheese, milk and garlic salt.
Pour spaghetti sauce over spaghetti.
Add 3 cups cheese and arrange pepperoni on top. Bake in oven at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes before serving.
Combine soup, 1/2 cup cheese, pepper, salt, mushrooms and onion in a bowl.
Gradually add milk.
Stir in potatoes.
Place in a greased shallow 1 1/2-quart baking dish. Top with remaining cheese and butter.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour. Serves 6.
*Brandy, rum or sherry to taste may be used in place of vanilla.
Heat tomato juice and sugar almost to a boil.
Dissolve flour in milk; mix to a thin paste and add to tomato juice.
Stir until smooth and thick, cooking thoroughly.
Mix all ingredients except crab meat with mixer, then add crab meat and mix with a spoon.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes in Pam sprayed pan.
Sprinkle extra cheese on top and return to oven to melt.
Prepare pudding mix according to package directions.
Mix with Cool Whip and nuts.
You can use a serving dish or individual dishes.
Place angel food cake on the bottom of dish.
Put pudding mixture on top of cake.
Pour cherry pie filling over this and refrigerate.
Mix well in blender.
Serve as a fresh dip for vegetables.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 50 minutes or until golden brown.
Use 8 x 8-inch greased pan.
Drain salmon; reserve 2 tablespoons salmon liquid.
Flake salmon and set aside.
Combine and blend cream cheese, salmon liquid, lemon juice, horseradish and liquid smoke.
Fold in salmon and green onions.
Refrigerate until chilled to allow flavors to meld.
Makes about 3 cups.
Cook macaroni as directed, drain and rinse with cold water. Combine macaroni and other ingredients.
Mix salad dressing and pour over salad.
Beat eggs.
Add brown sugar and Bisquick mix; mix well.
Add vanilla, nuts and coconut; mix well.
Pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes. Cake is real chewy.
Saute onion and pepper in the oleo.
In a separate bowl, mix the eggs and corn.
Mix the sauteed onion and pepper with sour cream and corn bread mix.
Add eggs and corn to the mixture and spread in a greased 7 x 12 inch baking dish.
Cover mixture with shredded cheese and bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes.
Beat butter and shortening at medium speed with an electric mixer about 2 minutes or until soft and creamy.
Gradually add sugar, beating at medium speed for 5 to 7 minutes.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating just until yellow disappears.
Grease 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Spread half the bread cubes evenly in dish.
Add the ham and both cheeses, then cover with remaining bread cubes.
Mix eggs, milk, onion, salt and mustard.
Pour evenly over bread cubes and refrigerate overnight. Combine corn flakes and butter for a topping.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Serves 10.
Combine last 4 ingredients.
Unroll each crescent roll.
Place triangles of dough on greased cookie sheet with large ends of each triangle in the middle, overlapping slightly, with small ends pointing outward to edges of cookie sheet.
Effect will be of a large sunburst with open circle in center.
Place hash mixture in ring over base of triangles.
Fold points over filling and tuck under the base of the center with filling showing between slits of the ring.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Can be served with scrambled eggs, stewed tomatoes or celery soup if desired.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In a 9 inch pie plate, mix chicken, vegetables and soup.
Mix milk, egg and baking mix.
Pour over chicken mixture.
Bake 30 minutes or until golden.
Melt butter and allow to cool.
Follow package directions to activate yeast.
Sift flour, sugar and salt.
Combine with egg. Add butter and milk.
Add yeast last.
Beat well.
Return to bowl and let rise covered for one hour or until doubled.
Shape into two loaves and let rise in pans.
Brush with melted butter.
Bake at 350° until golden brown, approximately 30 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and mix lightly.
Press into an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Drain.
Let set for 5 minutes before serving.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Add cold water.
Let set until partially thickened.
Add remaining ingredients. Refrigerate until firm.

Remove fat from meat and brown.
Cut steak into bite-size pieces.
Add mushrooms and gravy.
Cook noodles and drain.
Serve steak and gravy over noodles.
Excellent with rolls and tossed salad.
Cream together margarine, sugar and Pet milk.
Cook on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add marshmallows and stir until melted. Remove from heat and add crumbs, coconut and nuts.
Drop on waxed paper.
Mix all of the ingredients and let stand for bread crumbs to absorb liquid.
Mixture should be moist.
Fill the half clam shells.
Sprinkle each with bread crumbs and dot with butter. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cut rhubarb into 1-inch pieces and put into saucepan with sugar and 1/4 cup water.
Cover and cook about 15 minutes.
Blend cheeses with 2 tablespoons maple syrup. Shape into a ball.
Brush on the remaining syrup and coat with pecans.
Serve with assorted crackers.

Stir 1/2 bouillon into cooked rice and place in casserole.
Place chicken on top of rice and pour remaining bouillon over all.
Bake for 1/2 hour in a 325° oven.
Combine all ingredients; stir well.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls 2-inches apart onto lightly greased baking sheet. Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Yield:
6 dozen.
Soften yeast in water; mix all ingredients well.
Add 2 1/2 to 3 cups flour.
Mix into a soft dough.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Work one half at a time.
Roll out on a floured surface. Sprinkle with a mixture of the cinnamon and sugar.
Roll up from the small end.
Cut into half-inch pieces and put into a greased pan.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly browned.
May be frosted with a drizzle of powdered sugar and milk.

Add meat and simmer about 45 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes in greased loaf pan.

may
be
in
suction

tender
but
not
brown.
Add
octopus and saute until octopus

with
spaghetti

Spread on cake.

In a saucepan, combine the sugar, flour and salt. Drain juice from oranges and pineapple into a 1-cup measuring cup; cover and refrigerate fruit. Add enough water to the juice, if needed, to measure 1 cup; stir into the sugar mixture until smooth. Cook and stir over medium-high heat until thickened and bubbly.

Reduce heat; cook and stir 1 minute longer. Remove from heat. Stir a small amount of hot mixture into egg; return all to pan, stirring constantly. Bring to a gentle boil; cook and stir 2 minutes longer. Remove from heat. In a bowl, combine the macaroni and cooked dressing. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight.
Thinly slice pork into bite-size strips; set aside.
Preheat wok or large skillet to high heat.
Make sauce in a bowl by stirring together teriyaki sauce, cornstarch and seasoning package from frozen vegetables.
Set aside sauce.
Add oil to skillet. Stir-fry pork over heat for about 3 minutes or until it is no longer pink, then remove from skillet.
Add frozen vegetables, undrained pineapple and water to skillet.
Add sauce.
Cook and stir over medium-high heat until thick and bubbly.
Cook 2 minutes; stir in meat and cook 30 seconds.
Serve over chow mein noodles.
Cook broccoli and onion until tender.
Put in the bottom of a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
In saucepan, melt half of the butter. Blend in flour, salt and a dash of pepper.
Add milk.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened and bubbly.
Reduce heat; blend in cream cheese until smooth.
Pour over broccoli and onion. Place cheese on top and then use other half of butter; melt and toss bread crumbs in and put on top.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Melt butter in frying pan; add clams, crabmeat and bread crumbs.
Refrigerate mix, then prepare in shells (real or aluminum) and bake at 350° until lightly brown.

In large, glass casserole (cake pan is too big), melt margarine.
Add celery and onion.

Pour in batter.

Set chops on top of rice.
Pour mixture over rice and chops.

(Mash ripe bananas first.) Grease a loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until a toothpick comes out clean.

Mix into Jell-O mixture.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Beat chilled topping mix (Dream Whip) according to directions on package.
Fold into Jell-O mixture along with oranges, nuts and cottage cheese.
Turn into lightly oiled 9 x 13 x 2-inch salad dish or pan.
Cook brown sugar, butter, syrup and salt for 5 minutes at slow heat.
Do not boil hard.
Remove from heat.
Add soda, pour over popcorn and stir well.

Roll olive in flour, beaten egg and then bread crumbs (Italian seasoned or plain dry bread crumbs may be used).

Cook pasta according to package directions.
Serve shrimp over noodles. Serves 4.

place meat into the taco shell, a dab of hot or mild sauce and sprinkle a little shredded cheese.

4 servings.

6 patties.

Cream shortening and sugar thoroughly; add eggs.
Beat until smooth.
Add flour, baking powder and salt; mix well.
Add vanilla; blend well.
Spread 1/2 dough in 9 x 13-inch pan which has been greased.
Place apples and blueberries with a little juice over dough.

When thick as medium white sauce, remove from heat.
Add softened gelatin and stir until dissolved. Chill until mixture thickens and mounds.

Add water and eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
