Sprinkle cheese over broccoli. Dilute soup with milk.
Pour over broccoli.
Microwave 6 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle onion rings over casserole.
Return to oven and microwave for 2 1/2 minutes.

recipes.t: Pie Crust Recipe(Makes Top And Bottom Crusts For A 9-Inch Pie)
d: Mix all ingredients together with a pastry blender in a shallow bowl.
Work quickly; don't mix too much!
Dough should still be crumbly.
Divide into 2 dough balls.
Roll out for top and bottom crusts.
For best results, roll on pastry canvas sprinkled moderately with flour.
A cloth sleeve on the rolling pin helps, too.
Roll outward from the center of the dough ball; roll lightly in all directions.
Overworking crust will make it tough instead of flaky.
Place cherries in large flutes of greased Bundt pan.
Drain pineapple, reserving syrup.
Combine 1/2 cup drained pineapple, brown sugar, melted butter and 3 tablespoons of pineapple syrup. Spoon into Bundt pan on top of cherries.
Prepare pound cake mix according to package directions, using pineapple syrup for liquid. Stir in lemon peel, vanilla and remaining crushed pineapple.
Spoon into pan.
Bake at 325° for 60 to 65 minutes.
Cool in pan for 5 minutes.
Turn out on wire rack or serving plate to complete cooling.
Mix all ingredients until smooth.
Spread on cookies when cool.
Top each cookie with a nut.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and mace.
Stir in egg nog, butter, egg and rum.
Stir just until flour is moist.
Fold in pecans and mixed candied fruit.
Pour into 9 x 5-inch pan or two smaller loaf pans.
Spray pans with cooking spray.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean.
To caramelize sugar, place a heavy skillet over low heat. Stir constantly until melted and brown.
Place granulated sugar and cream in a double boiler and heat to boiling point.
Add caramelized sugar and stir until well blended.
Remove from heat; add butter and vanilla.
Beat thoroughly.
May be reheated over hot water.
Store in jar in refrigerator.
Spread butter in a 3-quart baking dish.
Line the dish with corn chips.
In a saucepan, combine chili and beans.
Heat. Alternate layers of chili beans, onions, peppers, corn chips and cheese.
Put layer of cheese last.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Yields approximately 7 to 8 servings.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch dish the first 5 ingredients.
Mix together the mayonnaise and sugar and spread over vegetables.
Top with shredded cheese and Bac*Os and refrigerate overnight.
Drain spinach.
Combine all ingredients (except bread) in bowl and mix well.
Chill 2 hours.
Cut bread into bite size pieces and use for dipping.
Put 60 Ritz crushed crackers mixed with melted butter in 13 x 9-inch cake pan.
Mix vanilla instant pudding with milk until thick.
Add softened butter pecan ice cream.
Add Cool Whip on top.
Top with toasted coconut.
Peel and dice potatoes.
Rinse well.
In medium-size pan, boil potatoes until tender; drain.
In mixing bowl, combine potatoes, butter and milk.
Blend with mixer until creamy.
Add sour cream and cream cheese.
Pour ingredients in a Pam-sprayed baking dish. Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Brown beef.
Add water, salt, pepper, barley and bouillon cubes.
Simmer for 30 minutes, covered.
Add carrots, celery, onion and tomato sauce.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Add frozen lima beans and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Brown meat in skillet.
Add bean dip, stirring occasionally. May add a little water if it gets too dry.
Let simmer about 15 to 20 minutes.
When ready to eat, put Fritos on a dinner plate.
Pour meat mixture over them, then add lettuce, tomato and onion on top of meat mixture.
Quickie meal.
Serves 5 to 6.
In 4-quart bowl, combine artichoke hearts, salami, olives and Parmesan cheese.
Add olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss well to coat ingredients evenly with dressing.
Add Fontina cheese; toss again.
In bowl, put 2 eggs, beat slightly.
Add sugar and mix well. Add syrup and mix well.
Add melted margarine and pecans; mix well.
Pour into crust.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, then turn oven temperature down to 325° and bake 30 additional minutes.
Cook squash until tender; drain.
Mash squash and add remaining ingredients.
Put mixture in ungreased 1-quart casserole.
Bake, uncovered, 20 minutes at 400°.
Add boiling water to jello.
Stir well.
Add cranberries and mix well.
Add drained crushed pineapple and pecans.
Let set 6 to 8 hours.
Whip cream cheese.
Mix in confectioners sugar.
Blend in Cool Whip.
Spread in pie shells.
Top with pie filling.
Spread 1 side of each ham slice with 1 tablespoon cream cheese.
Place 1 pickle on edge of each ham slice.
Roll ham slice around pickle; press edges to seal.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour. To serve, cut each pickle into 6 slices.
Makes 48 appetizers.
Melt butter in 10-inch glass pie pan in 400° oven.
Mix next 6 ingredients and pour into pie plate.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Dust with confectioners sugar.
Serve with syrup or jam.
Melt butter in saucepan; saute onions over medium heat until clear.
Reserve 3 tablespoons of cracker crumbs for topping and place remaining crumbs in bottom of lightly greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Remove onions from pan with slotted spoon.
Add soup and onions, alternating layers.
Combine eggs and milk; pour over onions.
Top with cheese and cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until brown and bubbly.
Mix the first 6 ingredients together until well blended. Combine flour, baking powder, soda and powdered ammonia; mix in the egg mixture.
Chill at least 2 hours or overnight.
Roll out and cut with cookie cutter.
Place on cookie sheets and bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until light brown.
Makes 7 to 8 dozen.
Combine salsa, currants, water, honey, cinnamon and cumin and mix. Heat oil in skillet. Cook almonds for 1 to 2 minutes. Set aside.

Add garlic. Cook for a minute or less and then add chicken, cooking until browned on both sides. Add the salsa mixture to the chicken. Reduce heat and put on cover. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken is done. Add almonds and stir. Serve with rice or couscous. Serves 4.
About 3 1/2 hours before coat meat with flour.
Pound with saucer.
In hot salad oil, brown meat on both sides in 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add onions, etc.
Heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 3 hours, turning once. Serve over hot noodles, rice or potatoes.

Combine egg and milk; set aside. Combine flour and Parmesan cheese; set aside. Dip pork chops into egg mixture and sprinkle evenly with salt and pepper; dredge in flour mixture. Heat oil in large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat; add pork chops and brown on both sides. Transfer to a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; top with cooked apples. Cover with aluminum foil; bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Place in large boiler and mix well.
Cook to soft ball stage and add vanilla and nuts.
Beat until thick and pour in greased pan.
Steam green beans over water for 5 minutes, until just tender, or cook frozen beans as package directs.
Combine the cooked beans with remaining ingredients in a large saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for about 15 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender.
Dissolve Jello in 1/2 cup of water.
Mix with cake mix and Wesson oil.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Soak matzo in water.
Drain.
Beat eggs with salt, sugar, butter and cinnamon.
Add to matzo.
Stir in nuts, apples and raisins.
Put in greased Pyrex pan.*
Dot with butter.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°, until golden.
Yield:
6 servings.
Combine and heat slowly until soup is thawed.
Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
This is a general base and tastes great.
Feel free to add garlic and/or onion salt and any other spices you prefer.
Brown beef and sausage with onion.
Melt cheese.
Add mushrooms and soup.
After cheese has melted, pour cheese mixture over browned meat.
Add garlic powder.
Serve hot.
Mix together well.
Bake at 400° in muffin tins.
Unbaked batter will keep in refrigerator for about 3 weeks.
Scrub potatoes; boil in skins until done.
Then peel and cut into slices or cubes.
Add onion, apple, peas and pickles; mix oil, vinegar, water, salt, pepper, sugar and parsley well.
Pour over warm potatoes.
Serve warm or chill for 1 hour and serve cold. Substitute with bacon fat from 4 slices of bacon.
Crumble bacon and add to salad.
Serves 4.
Combine all-bran, milk and molasses.
Let stand until most of the moisture is taken up.
Add egg and shortening; beat well. Stir in raisins.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt. Add to all-bran mixture, stirring only until combined.
Fill greased muffin pans 2/3 full. Bake in a 400° oven for about 20 minutes.
(Yield:
12 muffins 2 1/2-inches in diameter.)
Bake at 375° until light brown.
Combine first 7 ingredients in blender few seconds.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle bacon and sausage.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes until knife comes out clean.
Serves 8 to 12.
Mix first 5 ingredients together.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over top.
Sprinkle bacon bits on top of cheese.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan for 2 hours at 350°, uncovered.
Boil salt and cabbage for 10 minutes; drain well.
Mix milk, oleo, cheese and flour; cook until butter and cheese is melted, stirring often.
Pour over cabbage and bake 15 to 30 minutes in 325° oven.
Serves 6 to 8 people.
Brown beef and onion; drain.
Fix soup according to directions.
In a casserole dish, layer ground beef, frozen Tater Tots, cheese and soup. Keep layering until you end up with cheese on top.
Bake at 350° until bubbly and cheese is melted.
Spread half of the onion over bottom of large bowl.
Cover with separated crab lumps and then remaining onion.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Pour oil, vinegar and ice water over all. Sprinkle sugar on top.
Cover and marinate in refrigerator for 12 to 24 hours.
Toss lightly before serving.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Add strawberries and stir to thaw.
Add pineapple and bananas.
Pour half the mixture into 6 cup mold.
When set, blend sour cream into remaining room temperature Jell-O mixture and pour into mold.
Refrigerate overnight or until firmly set.
Mix all together well; form into ball and chill 1/2 hour. Roll in chopped nuts.
Spread bread cubes evenly in 8-inch round dish.
Sprinkle evenly with brown sugar, nutmeg, salt, then raisins.
Measure milk into 1-quart measuring cup.
Add butter.
Microwave at High for 4 minutes, until butter is melted and milk is warm.
Rapidly stir in eggs with a fork and mix well.
Pour over bread cubes in dish. Microwave a Medium-high for 9 to 12 minutes.
When cooked, center may still be slightly soft but it will set up as pudding cools. Serve warm or chilled.
Makes 6 servings.
Blend all ingredients in large mixer bowl.
Beat for 4 minutes at medium speed.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch pans. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Combine hamburger and soups.
Heat together in skillet.
Then put in casserole dish and completely cover with American cheese slices.
Then completely cover with a layer of Tater Tots.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes or until Tater Tots are done.
Mix all ingredients together.
Let stand in refrigerator 12 to 24 hours.
Boil sweet potatoes until done.
Mash with fork and cool. Take large marshmallows and around each, press the mashed potatoes.
Use just enough to cover the marshmallow completely. Dip in melted butter and roll in graham cracker crumbs.
Bake at 300° for 15 to 20 minutes.
The balls will crack slightly when done.
Make School Roll Dough, or use any yeast bread dough.
Roll out in rectangular shape (approximately 8 x 11 inches).
Put 1/2 of ham slices and 1/2 of cheese slices along middle of dough, leaving an inch on each end uncovered.
Sprinkle with seasoning; fold one side of dough over ham and cheese.
Repeat ham and cheese layer on top of fold, using remainder of ham and cheese.
Sprinkle this layer with the Italian seasoning.
Leave 1 inch on each end to seal.
Fold dough over; seal all edges.
Bake at 350° until done.
Cream together oil and sugar; add beaten eggs.
Add sifted dry ingredients of flour and spices to mixture, alternating with buttermilk.
Fold in prunes and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in tube pan.
Ice with Buttermilk Frosting.
Good when stored for a few days wrapped or sealed in cake taker.
In a large bowl, combine oats, flour, 1 cup dark brown sugar. Cut 1/2 cup butter into mixture till coarse and crumbly.
Press into a 13x9-inch baking pan.
Place pecans evenly over crumb mixture.
Mix until blended well.
Good on pork, chicken and beef.
Also, if you like onions, chop 1/4 cup fine and add to sauce.
If you add onions, cook until onions are tender.
Drain beans well.
Mix all ingredients well, scraping bowl thoroughly.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours.
Place sugar, cocoa, butter and milk in saucepan and boil for 2 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter and vanilla.
Then pour into oatmeal which has been placed in a large bowl.
Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Let cool.
Prepare jello with cream cheese.
Let jello mixture cool and beat together until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Put in a ring mold and serve with mayonnaise in center of ring or use individual molds and top with mayonnaise.
Bake at 375°
for 45 minutes. In 10-inch skillet over medium heat, cook beef until brown, stirring to separate meat.
Spoon off fat.
Add spaghetti sauce; heat through, stirring occasionally.
Pound chicken breasts until 1/4 inch thick.
Mix bread crumbs and parmesan cheese together in a shallow pan or bowl.
Melt butter in fry pay over medium heat.
Dip chicken pieces in egg, then in bread crumbs mixture and fry in butter about 5 minutes per side or until done.
Remove from pan.
Serves 4.
Whip the first 4 ingredients until smooth, then add 1 small can crushed pineapple.
Bake in graham cracker crust 20 minutes at 350°.
Cool until glaze forms on top.

Prepare stuffing according to directions only using 1 tablespoon margarine. Set aside. Saute chicken cubes in pan sprayed with Pam until no longer pink. Add soups and milk. Pour into a sprayed 9 x 13 pan and sprinkle with poultry seasoning. Top with prepared stuffing and bake 30 minutes at 325°. Let stand 10 minutes before serving. Serves 6.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat 5 minutes.
Stir in carrots and chill.
Mix ingredients and pour into buttered baking dish.
Cover and let set in refrigerator overnight (until it is a mush).
Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Thaw a loaf of frozen bread and roll out on floured surface into a large triangle.
Spread with mustard and put the baked ham, Provolone cheese, salami and Mozzarella cheese down the center of the dough.
Fold sides and pinch.
Brush top with melted butter and sprinkle with oregano.
Mix all ingredients and place in square pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Blend
cream
cheese and mayonnaise. Add other ingredients. Mix well.
In a small bowl, combine all ingredients until well blended. Turn into 1 1/2-pint baking dish.
Bake uncovered in preheated 375° oven for 15 minutes.
Stir often.
Serve warm with crackers. Yield:
6 to 8 servings.
Prepare salad dressing mix with vinegar, water and oil as directed on envelope.
Mix greens, oranges, onion and pecans in large salad bowl.
Add dressing; toss well.
Place zucchini slices in bottom of 1 1/2 to 2-quart casserole. Combine all other ingredients, except cheese; mix and pour over zucchini.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cover and bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Combine cake mix and sugar in large mixing bowl.
Add vegetable oil and next 4 ingredients.
Beat at medium speed with electric mixer for 6 minutes.
Stir in poppy seed.
Pour batter into a 10 count Bundt pan, sprayed with cooking spray.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.
Cool in pan on a wire rack 10 minutes. Remove from pan and drizzle with lemon glaze.

Slice strawberries. Sprinkle with NutraSweet. Mix cornstarch and water in saucepan. Bring to boil and cook until thickened. Add gelatin. Combine mixture and strawberries. Pour into pie crust. Chill at least 3 hours with whipped cream.
Mix ground beef, onion, pepper and milk together.
Cook rice and mix with ground beef.
Take cooked cabbage, leaf by leaf, and roll with ground beef inside.
Place into baking pan and pour tomato soup over.
Bake at 350° to 400° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

Prepare cake mix as directed on box. Let cool, then split both layers (can make 3 layers). Combine sugar, sour cream (reserve 1 cup sour cream for frosting) and coconut. Blend well. Chill. Spread between layers. Combine reserved sour cream with whipped topping. Blend until smooth. Spread on top and sides of cake. Seal cake in airtight container and refrigerate for 3 days before serving.
Slice corned beef into tiny pieces.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill overnight.
Best served with squares of rye bread.
Place corn in a 1 1/2-quart glass jar.
Remove seed portions of tomato; dice and add to corn.
Cover with Italian dressing and marinate 12 to 24 hours in refrigerator, turning jar occasionally to be sure all vegetables are covered.
Drain before serving. Diced bell pepper and/or chopped green onions may be added for color and/or flavor.
Whole kernel yellow corn may also be added for color.
Pour in milk, oil, salt, baking powder and sugar; mix well. Add flour.
Add more flour if needed.
Flour hands, take 1 tablespoon dough and knead in hand until not sticky; place in pan. Pour 1 tablespoon plus oil in baking dish.
Turn biscuits in oil in pan.
Bake at 450° for 20 minutes.
Makes approximately 10 biscuits.
Delicious.
Mix all together.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Spread cream cheese on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch cake pan, top with chili, cover chili with cheese.
Heat in 350° oven until cheese is melted (and hot).
In large bowl mix together corn, tomatoes, onions, green peppers, salt, pepper, corn meal and cheese.
Let mixture set 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Place egg yolks, Sucaryl and next 4 ingredients in blender and blend 2 seconds.
Add apples.
Blend until fine.
Pour into buttered pie plate.
Bake at 450° for 25 minutes.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Add remaining ingredients and process along with 1 teaspoon Sucaryl.
Put meringue on pie, spreading to edges.
Brown at 350° until golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Serves 6, 155 calories per serving.
Bring all ingredients, except cabbage and onions, to a rolling boil.
Mix 1 cup salad oil into this.
Pour over cabbage and onions and refrigerate overnight.

recipes.t: Cube Steak With Gravy In Crock-Pot
d: Dip steak in flour; fry until brown.
Place in crock-pot.
Add water, soup and gravy mix.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours. Serve hot over rice.
Brown ground beef, onions and bell pepper. Drain. Add soup, salt and pepper.
Pour into casserole dish. Top with potatoes. Bake at 400° for 30 minutes. When making creamed potatoes, add a teaspoon of mayonnaise.
Add baking soda to buttermilk.
Mix eggs, bananas, sugar, milk an shortening.
Add dry ingredients.
Mix together and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Grease and flour pan.

Preheat oven to 425°. Combine curry powder, cinnamon, cayenne, salt and flour in a plastic bag. Add chicken and shake well to coat. Put chicken on baking sheet and spray with cooking oil. Bake 20 minutes. Turn the chicken over and continue baking until golden brown, about 15 minutes longer.
Mix flour, brown sugar and
butter or oleo as crumbs.
Measure 2 3/4 cups into 10 x 15-inch pan (ungreased).
To rest of crumbs, add the rest of ingredients.
Stir in apples.
Spread over crumb base.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool.
Serve
with
ice cream,
whipped cream or sprinkle powdered sugar on top.
Use casserole dish large enough for amount desired.
Put margarine in dish, then layer potatoes, onion and pork chops on top so that they will brown.
Salt and pepper ingredients.
Bake at 350° until done.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease bottom only of 13 x 9-inch pan. In large bowl, combine all ingredients.
Beat 50 strokes by hand. Spread in greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Cool completely; cut into bars.
Makes 24 bars.
Cream the shortening, sugar and salt. Beat in egg
until very light.
Add baking soda to sour milk and stir into egg mixture alternating with flour. Fold in rhubarb and candy sprinkles.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle with topping. Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Combine all ingredients, but meat.
Mix well.
Pour half in an 8-inch iron skillet that has been heated in the oven with oil. Then put on layer of meat, layer of cheese and then remaining mix. Bake 30 minutes at 450°.
Cook macaroni according to directions. Rinse in cold water and chill. Mix all other ingredients and thin with 1 tablespoon pickle juice, if necessary. Chill until served.
Mix flour and soda.
Combine eggs, mincemeat, condensed milk, fruit and nuts.
Fold in dry ingredients.
Bake in tube pan (greased and lined with wax paper) at 300° for 2 hours.
(I have baked this in 2 loaf pans.)
Decorate top with cherries and nuts. Freezes well.
In a small bowl, combine all ingredients.
Stir until well mixed.
Place in covered container.
Chill until ready to serve.
Brown beef
and add taco seasoning, according to directions on package.
Place
flour
tortillas in baking dish and fill with
2 heaping
tablespoons
ground
beef mixture.
Add lettuce, tomato and
onions.
Fold over and close with toothpicks.	Heat enchilada
sauce and Velveeta cheese.
Pour over the tortillas and
top
with
grated Cheddar cheese.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°. Serve with picante.
Place Velveeta cheese in between 2 sheets of Saran Wrap.
Roll Velveeta with a rolling pin into a circle or oval, 1/4-inch thick. Remove top piece of Saran Wrap.
Spread cream cheese on top of Velveeta.
Sprinkle pecans, pimentos, green onions and green pepper on top of cheeses.
Roll into a log and place, seam down, on platter.
May be prepared with light cream cheese and Velveeta for less fat.
Dissolve jello in 2 cups boiling water (save 1/4 cup of dissolved jello).
Add frozen strawberries, pineapple and bananas. Put in refrigerator to congeal.
When congealed, mix cream cheese, confectioners sugar, vanilla and reserved jello.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Spread this mixture over congealed jello.
Sprinkle with nuts, if desired.
Combine beans, milk, soup, pepper and half of onions.
Pour in casserole and bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining onions and bake 5 minutes longer.
Cream of chicken soup may also be used.
Drain 1/2 juice from carrots.
Mix apple filling and carrots. Put in a baking dish, sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake about an hour in 350 degree oven.
Prepare macaroni according to package directions and drain. Pour into a 2-quart baking dish and set aside.
Mix dry ingredients thoroughly; add milk and beaten egg yolks (reserve egg whites for meringue); mix well.
Cook in a double boiler to the desired thickness.
Add vanilla.
Pour into a ready baked crust.
Cover with meringue and bake in moderate oven at 350° until lightly brown.
Blend milk, eggs and spices.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Layer 7 to 8 slices of bread.
Cover with half of cheese and half the egg mixture.
Repeat, using balance of ingredients.
Refrigerate overnight or all day.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Let set a few minutes.
Cut into squares.
In a large saucepan, cook and stir bacon and onion until bacon is crisp and onion is tender.
Stir in reserved clam liquor, the potatoes, water and celery.
Cook, uncovered, until potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add clams, tomatoes and seasonings. Heat to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Makes 6 servings.
Place cheeses in small mixing bowl; let stand at room temperature until softened.
Add onion and Worcestershire sauce; blend on low speed.
Beat on medium speed until fluffy, scraping sides and bottom.
Cover and chill for 8 hours.
Boil potatoes with jackets.
Cool, peel and grate.
Mix everything but 1 cup
cheese in a cake pan.
Sprinkle remaining cup of cheese over casserole and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight. Bake at 350°
for 45 min. to an hour or until cheese on top is bubbly and casserole is hot completely through.
Serves 6.
Cook rice.
Brown onion in butter until transparent.
Add cooked rice, sour cream, green chilies, salt and pepper.
Grease a large 2 1/2-quart casserole or baking dish and layer: one-half of rice mixture, 1/2 cottage cheese, 1/2 Cheddar cheese.
Repeat layers.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Can be made ahead and frozen.
Cook zucchini and onion in water for 5 to 10 minutes.
Drain. Place 1/2 package herb stuffing in bottom of greased 12 x 9-inch baking pan. Cover with zucchini and onion mixture. Combine grated carrots, soup mixes and melted butter.
Spread over top. Cover with sour cream.
Sprinkle remaining stuffing on top. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Prepare stuffing mix according to instructions.
Combine beef and milk.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Make patties and hollow out center.
Fill with stuffing.
Be sure stuffing is covered with beef to make bundle.
Place in greased cake pans, etc.
Heat soup, catsup and Worcestershire sauce until bubbly.
Pour over bundles. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt together.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored.
Add sugar and continue beating for several minutes.
Add lemon juice.
Stir in flour mixture, warm milk and vanilla.
Mix until batter is smooth.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry, and fold carefully.
Pour onto greased 11 x 15-inch pan, lined with waxed paper.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Quickly turn upside-down on dishtowel sprinkled with confectioners sugar. Pull off paper.
Roll up, folding in long side, using towel to keep rolled.
Let cool.
Unroll and spread with lemon pie filling or your favorite jelly.
Reroll and sprinkle top with powdered sugar.
Combine beans, Bisquick and water in bowl; mix well.
Spoon mixture into greased 9-inch pie plate; form shell.
Cook beef until brown.
Drain; spoon over bean mixture and top with sauce. Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake 5 minutes.
Cut into wedges.
Top with sour cream and serve.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cook macaroni; toss with oil.
Add all other ingredients. Pour into lightly greased crock-pot; stir.
Cover and cook for 3 to 4 hours on low.
Mix together.
Top with 1 package slivered almonds.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with corn chips.
In large heavy skillet, pour 1/2 cup oil.
While oil is heating, season pork chops.
Coat on both sides with crushed garlic.
Brown pork chops on both sides; drain.
Serve with rice and favorite stir-fry vegetables.
Grease baking dish.
Put in first 3 ingredients.
Sprinkle oatmeal on top.
Mix sugar, flour and oleo together.
Sprinkle over top and bake until apples are tender.

In a greased 13 x 9 baking pan, arrange rhubarb. In a mixing bowl, combine sugar and gelatin; sprinkle over rhubarb. Then sprinkle the dry cake mix over the gelatin mixture. Pour hot water over cake mix, but do not stir. Top with coconut and almonds; drizzle with butter. Bake in 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Beat eggs, add oil, then cake mix and Jello.
Beat well, then add strawberries and beat well.
Bake at 325 degrees until done. Bake in 3 layers.
Saute onion in the olive oil on medium heat until onion is transparent.
Add flour to the saute and gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
When the ingredients are blended together to a smooth and creamy consistency, add the diced meat, salt and pepper.
Continue to stir constantly until the mixture begins to boil.
Cook for about 3 or 4 minutes more.
The mixture should separate easily from the skillet.
Then pour into a shallow pan or platter and allow to cool for several hours.
You can refrigerate the mixture since the cooler it is, the easier it is to handle. When the mixture has cooled, spoon small amounts and roll into bite size croquettes.
Then bread the croquettes, using bread crumbs, eggs and bread crumbs again, and fry to a golden brown.
Brown and loosely drain hamburger. Add soup and Cheez Whiz; blend with water. Add dry, uncooked noodles and diced onion rings. Mix well. Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Mix first 5 ingredients and melt over hot water and remove from stove.
Place shedded wheat on fork and dip in chocolate mixture and place on waxed paper.
Cool 1/2 hour.
Mix ingredients in large bowl; beat 2 minutes.
Bake in 13 x 9-inch pan at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
After cake has cooled, cover with topping.
Wash broccoli thoroughly and cut tops into bite sized florets (save stems for another use).
Combine with Swiss cheese and green onions.
Stir together mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar and add to broccoli mixture.
Let marinate overnight or up to several days in refrigerator.
Just before serving, toss with bacon.
Sprinkle some on top.
Serves 6.
In bowl, stir together soup and milk.
Fold in remaining ingredients (except pastry).
Spoon into ungreased 2-quart rectangular baking dish.
Roll out pastry to 1/8-inch in thickness. Cut into 3/4-inch strips.
Twist strips about 4 times each and arrange in a crisscross pattern over ingredients in dish.
Bake in a 400° oven for 40 minutes or until pie is bubbly and pastry is golden brown.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Mix together Chex, crushed, cheese and butter.
Separate biscuit dough into 10 biscuits.
Cut each in half.
Press each half in crumb mixture to coat both sides.
With hands, roll each piece to form an 8-inch stick (crumbs will work into dough).
Gently tie to form a knot.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes or until light brown.
Serve immediately.
Makes 20 servings.
Brown meat, onion and bell pepper.
Add tomato sauce, Ro-Tel tomatoes, Mexicorn, salt and noodles.
Cover with cheese and bake 15 minutes at 400°.
Sprinkle chicken with lemon juice and salt and chill for several hours.
Add remaining ingredients and toss lightly.
Combine cranberries and sugar; mix thoroughly to dissolve sugar.
Sprinkle gelatin over pineapple juice to soften.
Place over medium heat; stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Add to cranberry mixture; mix well.
Stir in fruits; fold in sour cream and Cool Whip.
In a large pot, about a 3-quart size, combine potatoes, onion, water and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Keep covered about 10 minutes. Add milk, crabmeat, corn, parsley and other seasonings.
Cook over low heat until piping hot.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cut french bread into eight 1 1/2-inch slices.
Make a pocket in each slice by cutting a slit from top of bread to bottom. Combine jam, cream cheese, strawberries and banana in a small bowl to make filling.
Place heaping Tbsp. of filling into each pocket. Press back together.
Brown beef and add salt and pepper to taste.
Chop onion and add to beef 1/2 way through browning.
Slice potatoes.
Dissolve bouillon cubes in one cup water in microwave (approximately 1 minute or until dissolved).
Layer in a 2-quart casserole a layer of potatoes, half of beef, another layer of potatoes, half of beef and another layer of potatoes.
Pour bouillon mix over meat and potatoes.
Cover and microwave on High for 15 minutes or until potatoes are soft.
Crush vanilla wafers; mix with melted margarine.
Hold out one cup of crumbs.
Press the rest of the crumbs in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Mix partially melted ice cream with the Cool Whip and pour over crust; drizzle topping over top and cover with remaining crumbs. Freeze overnight.
Beat egg whites with salt and cream of tartar until frothy. Gradually add sugar, while beating, and continue beating until mixture gets very stiff and holds shape.
Add vanilla.
Fold in chocolate and nuts.
Drop by teaspoon on foil covered cookie pan. Turn oven on for 30 minutes at 350°.
Turn off oven after 30 minutes and place cookies in oven.
Leave in cooling oven for 5 hours or overnight.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
Thaw and drain spinach; squeeze dry.
Cook onion and margarine.
Stir in spinach; cover and cook 5 minutes.
Add salt, milk and margarine.
Slowly add eggs while stirring.
Blend in bread crumbs and cheese.
Place spinach mixture in mold which has been lined with waxed paper.
Top with a few crumbs.
Bake about 60 minutes at 325°.
If desired, serve topped with tiny cocktail tomatoes.
Brown beef with onion and garlic powder.
Drain well. Add soup and cheese.
Continue cooking over low heat on stove, stirring until cheese melts.
Add cinnamon and beans. Coat warm macaroni with margarine. Serve meat sauce over macaroni.
Serves 4 to 6.
In large pan combine ingredients.
Bring to boil, reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes or until done.
Stir often.
Makes 7 cups.
Mix all ingredients (except for melted chocolate) well.
Press out on large cookie sheet or in large pan.
Let set until hard. Ice with melted chocolate and let stand about 15 more minutes before cutting.
Heat oven to 425°.
Cut squash in half and remove seeds. Place cut side down in shallow baking pan.
Pour in 1-inch water. Bake, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes.
Boil vinegar, salt, mustard, celery and oil for 3 minutes. Pour over shredded cabbage, onion and bell pepper.
Sprinkle sugar over all and mix.
Put in an airtight container in fridge for 24 hours.
Mix cream cheese, egg yolk and 1/4 cup of sugar until creamy. Trim crust from bread and roll each slice with a rolling pin to flatten.
Spread each slice with cream cheese mixture and roll like a jelly roll.
Melt butter. Mix together remaining sugar and all the cinnamon.
Dip each bread roll in melted butter and then roll in cinnamon/sugar mixture.
Bake at 400 degrees for 10 - 12 minutes.
Place trout in a 12 x 8-inch baking dish.
In small bowl, combine crumbs, onion, pepper, mushrooms, salt and pepper.
Spread over fish; top with lemon slices.
Cover with wax paper. Microwave at High 5 to 7 minutes, or until fish flakes easily. Let stand 3 to 5 minutes.
Contains 133 calories per serving.
Peel, put and mash avocados in a medium bowl with lemon juice, salt
and	pepper.
Combine sour cream, mayonnaise and taco
mix in	bowl.
Mix flour and salt. Add oil and mix with a fork. Sprinkle water over mixture and mix one tablespoon at a time. Shape into a ball and place between two sheets of wax paper and roll out.
Combine raisins, nuts and baking soda in boiling water.
Allow to cool.
Add flour, sugar, mayonnaise and vanilla.
Mix well. Pour into cupcake pans and bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until done.
Makes 2 dozen.
Bake ham in 3 cups water for 2 1/2 hours at 350°.
Take ham out of water.
Saute in skillet beef, onion and celery until tender; drain. Add water, tomato paste, salt and paprika.
Reserve 1 cup for biscuits.
Add beans to largest portion of meat mixture and simmer while you prepare biscuit dough.
Pour 1/2 cup of water into skillet; add onion and cook until tender.
Add ground beef.
Stir until ground beef is browned. Drain excess grease from skillet.
Add margarine and stir until melted.
Add tomato paste or sauce and salt and pepper.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook spaghetti per box instructions.
Rinse spaghetti under cold water to separate spaghetti and put in large bowl.
Pour ground beef mixture onto spaghetti and mix well.
Serves 4 to 6. Serve with green beans, buttered potatoes and barbecue bread.
Place asparagus and peas in an 8 x 8-inch buttered dish.
Add soup; layer almonds on top.
Sprinkle cheese, then cracker crumbs. Pour melted butter over top.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix Sugar, Cinnamon, Nutmeg, Flour and Lemon Juice in mixing bowl.
Mix in sliced Apples, then place in bottom Pie crust.
Place top crust over mix making sure to seal the edges.
Poke holes in crust with fork.
Sprinkle water on top of crust and top with dabble of sugar.
Bake in oven at 400 degrees or until golden brown and bubbly.
Grease and flour a 9-inch tube pan.
Slice apples and in separate bowl mix 4 teaspoons sugar and the cinnamon.
Mix orange Jell-O and boiling water; chill.
Add remaining ingredients.
Save some of the coconut to sprinkle on top.
Pour in a large flat container.
Chill overnight.

Mix bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, oregano, salt and pepper and set aside. In a hot skillet, add some butter and saute garlic. Next melt remaining butter. Now roll each piece chicken in butter, then roll in mixture. Put in 13 x 9 baking dish. Bake at 350° for 55 minutes. Just at done, place 2 slices Mozzarella cheese on each chicken breast; put back in oven until it melts.

In a large skillet, brown roast in hot oil. Place roast in a 3 1/2 to 4 qt. electric crockery cooker, cutting if necessary to fit. Add the water to cooker. Sprinkle roast with 2 tsp. of the fresh dill weed or 3/4 tsp. dried dill weed, salt and pepper. Cover and cook on high heat setting for 5 to 6 hours or on low heat setting for 10 to 12 hours, until meat is tender. Remove roast from cooker, reserving liquid; cover roast and keep warm. Measure liquid from cooker; skim fat. Reserve 1 c. of the juices. Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, stir together yogurt and flour until well combined. Stir in the 1 c. reserved cooking liquid and remaining dill weed. Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minutes more. Serve meat with sauce and noodles. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Bake cake mix as directed on box in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cream first three ingredients together well.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup boiling water.
Refrigerate until cold, not thick.
Pour into cheese and sugar mixture.
Add juice of lemon.
Stir in Cool Whip and mix lightly.
Pour lemon mixture into a graham cracker crust.
Top with cherry pie filling.
In blender, combine chocolate bits, egg yolks and Kahlua at medium speed.

In saucepan, heat cream until it comes to a boil. With blender on low speed, pour hot cream into top of blender. Blend on high for 1 minute (the hot cream will melt the chocolate bits and cook the yolks).
Pour mixture into pie shell and chill for 3 hours.
Do not freeze.
Very rich; will serve 12 easily.

Boil chicken until tender. Remove from broth. Cook spaghetti in broth. Cut up cheese. Remove spaghetti from heat; if soupy, drain a little. Mix cheese and spaghetti slightly. Add Ro-Tel, peas and cream of mushroom soup. Put in casserole and bake in oven until bubbly. (If more liquid is needed, add broth you drained from chicken.) Bake about 30 minutes at 350°.
Sift flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Cut in shortening; add milk and mix lightly.
Roll and cut.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Soak toast in cold water for 7 or 8 minutes and then press dry.
Combine with all the other ingredients.
In a bowl, work together until thoroughly blended.
Form in 12 medium sized balls and fry slowly in about 2 tablespoons hot shortening until brown on all sides.
Do not turn meat balls until absolutely done.
Combine all ingredients in a 13 x 9-inch greased pan.
Top with bread or cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Drain.
Add taco seasoning and follow directions on package.
Mix in corn.
Layer 1/2 of tortillas in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Then spread 1/2 meat mixture and 1/2 cheese.
Repeat.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Melt oleo in 9 X 13 pan.
Stir in both cans of corn and cornbread mix.
Add eggs and stir with fork.
Drop sour cream and cheese by spoonfuls on top, then fold in gently.
(Optional:
may add 1 can of chopped green chilies)
Saute clams for 10 minutes and leave juice.
Saute pepper and onion with margarine, adding lemon to taste, for 10 minutes. Combine above ingredients and add 1 cup bread crumbs.
Season with parsley and oregano.
Mix well; top with shredded Cheddar cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Boil fast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Beat until creamy.
Mix and stir with fork.
Just before serving, add celery.
Can be prepared day before, but do not add celery.
Cut vegetables into bite size pieces. Mix together vinegar, water and dressing mix and pour over vegetables.
Marinate in refrigerator overnight, stirring occasionally.
Serve cold.
Put all ingredients into a bowl and mix well.
Combine the first 6 ingredients, mixing well.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Cook meatballs in hot oil in a large skillet until lightly browned; drain meatballs on a paper towel and discard drippings.
Combine chili sauce and jelly in skillet; cook over medium heat until jelly is melted.
Add meatballs; simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Transfer to chafing dish; keep warm.
Sprinkle with chopped green onion, if desired.
Yields about 5 dozen.

recipes.t: Linda Poor'S Ground Beef And Cabbage Casserole
d: Brown ground beef.
Mix in onion, salt, pepper and rice; cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Add soup and water; mix thoroughly.
Remove from heat.
Place cabbage in casserole (2-quart size).
Pour meat mixture over cabbage.
Do not stir.
Cover and bake in a slow oven at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Combine all ingredients except the last 2 and form into small balls.
Melt chocolate with paraffin in double boiler; dip each ball into chocolate.
Remove and place on wax paper.
Grease and line the base of 7-inch round deep cake pan.
Blend the egg yolks with the sugar until mixture is thick and creamy. Whisk half of the orange peel and all of the lemon peel into the egg yolks.
Mix the juice from both oranges and the lemon with the ground almonds and stir into the egg yolks.
The mixture will become quite runny at this point.
Fold in flour.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff and gently fold into yolk mixture.
Pour mixture into pan and bake in preheated oven at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and springs to the touch.
Let cool in pan for 10 minutes and then turn out.
It will sink slightly at this stage. Whip cream to form soft peaks.
Stir in remaining orange peel, cinnamon and sugar.
Once cake is cold, cover with the toasted almonds and dust with confectioners sugar and serve with cream. Serves 8.
Combine flour, butter and chopped nuts.
Spread on bottom of 9 x 13-inch greased pan (glass).
Bake mixture at 350° for 30 minutes; cool.
Combine powdered sugar and cream cheese.
Spread on top of cooled nut mixture.
Layer lemon pie filling on top. Top with Cool Whip.
Refrigerate overnight.
Boil potatoes, onion, celery, salt, pepper and water about 20 minutes.
With hand masher, mash potatoes.
Add milk and butter.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs.
Add sifted dry ingredients.
Fold in blueberries by hand.
Pour into greased muffin tin and sprinkle top with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
With mixer, beat cheese until fluffy. Gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk until smooth.
Add egg and vanilla and mix well.
Toss chips with flour.
Stir into cheese mixture.
Pour into pie crust.
Bake 35 minutes or until center springs back when lightly touched.
Cool and top with glaze.
Serves 8.
Line bottom of a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan with rolls, pressing firmly to seal perforations.
Sprinkle on sausage and cheese. Combine remaining ingredients.
Heat well and pour over sausage. Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Cut into squares for serving.
Boil chicken until done.
Mix soup and broth.
Remove chicken from bone.
Melt margarine in casserole dish.
Add layer of chicken, layer of soup and broth mixture and layer of stuffing mix.
Repeat layers, ending with stuffing.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Cut cake into 1/4 inch slices; arrange half the slices on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
In large mixer bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk, water and extract; mix well.
Add pudding mix; beat well.
Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream. Spread half the cream mixture over cake slices; top evenly with 1 can cherry filling.
Top with remaining cake slices, cream mixture and cherry filling.
Chill 4 hours or until set.
Cut into squares to serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Mix together pineapple, nuts, pie filling and milk.
Fold in Cool Whip and pour into pie crust and chill.
Makes 2 pies.
This is great to freeze.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles according to the package directions.
Brown beef and drain.
Layer 1/2 noodles, 1/2 meat, 1/2 sauce, and cheese.
Repeat for top layer.
Bake 25 minutes.
Brown meat and onion.
Add rice, tomatoes and other ingredients.
Stir to blend.
Cover and simmer until rice is tender.
Stir occasionally.
Cook about 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add strawberries, pineapple with juice and salt.
Pour half gelatin mixture into a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Chill until set.
Pour over beets and boil for 10 minutes.
Cool and serve.

Place potato wedges in a plastic bag; add cooking oil, cheese, garlic powder and pepper. Close bag and shake to coat. Arrange wedges in single layer on a nonstick baking sheet. Preheat oven to 425°. Bake 30 to 35 minutes, turning once or twice.

With 3-inch biscuit or doughnut cutter, cut one round from each slice of bread. Set rounds aside. Tear remaining bread scraps into 1-inch pieces; spread evenly in a 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Sprinkle the Cheddar cheese evenly over the bread. Then layer the asparagus over the cheese. Combine the cooked ham and chopped onions and layer this mixture over the asparagus. Arrange the bread rounds on the top.
Cut broccoli and cauliflower into small flowerets.
Add celery, radishes, onion, salt and pepper into a bowl.
Grate cheeses and add chilies in a bowl.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Mix together remaining ingredients and fold into egg whites.
Pour over cheese mixture; mix with a fork.
Pour into a greased round casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Serves 8.
Mix 2 cups Mozzarella (reserve 1 cup for topping), cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese in a bowl; set aside.
Add 1/2 to 3/4 cup spaghetti sauce to meat mixture in bottom of crock-pot.
Add a layer of noodles, broken to fit without overlapping.
Continue layering 1/3 of sauce, 1/3 pepperoni and 1/3 of the cheese mixture.
Repeat with noodles, sauce, pepperoni and cheese mixture until you use it all.
Pour water around edges of crock-pot.
Top with cheese.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 3 to 4 hours.
Brown sausage and onion.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in casserole.
Sprinkle crushed potato chips on top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix oil and vinegar, sugar, pepper and soup seasoning packet (from Ramen noodles) and refrigerate.
In a large saucepan, combine water, wild rice mix and salt. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes or until rice is tender.
Stir in frozen mixed vegetables during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Combine and mix first 4 ingredients until well blended. Add the last 3 ingredients; mix well, then place in the pie crust. Bake at 450° for 15 minutes and then at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook onions in salted water in saucepan until partially tender; drain.
Place in casserole.
Top with soup, cornflakes and margarine.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Yield:
8 servings.
Combine all ingredients except salt and pineapple.
Chill several hours.
Serve salad on a bed of lettuce.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt.
Top with pineapple tidbits.
Sift flour and salt into a bowl.
Add milk, oil and egg.
Beat until smooth.
Separate onion into rings.
Dip each ring into batter.
Fry 2 to 3 minutes in heated oil (375°).
Drain; sprinkle with salt.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In a large skillet, cook ground beef, onion and bell pepper. Drain and discard grease.
Combine cooked macaroni, tomatoes and 1/2 of the grated cheese with the ground beef mixture.
Transfer to baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top and bake in 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Combine first 6 ingredients and cook 10 minutes.
Cool completely.
Cool hard-boiled eggs completely or eggs will be tough.
Place all in gallon glass jar.
Refrigerate overnight before using.
In large skillet, heat butter and oil.
Fry the garlic, red pepper and
paprika
about
1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the shrimp and cook over medium heat until they turn pink. Stir constantly about 3 minutes.
Stir in parsley, lemon juice and salt.
Serve immediately.
Serve with bread for dipping.
Mix all ingredients and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Separate eggs and beat egg yolks.
Add sugar to yolks and beat until smooth.
Combine flour, cornstarch and cocoa.
Stir a little of the milk into flour, cornstarch and cocoa mixture to make a smooth paste.
Scald remaining milk and stir a little of it into each of the mixtures.
Slowly combine egg mixture and cocoa mixture together with scalded milk.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Add vanilla.
Pour into baked pie shell and cover with meringue.
Bake at 300° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Boil cabbage until tender and drain.
Meanwhile, saute onion in butter and mix with cabbage.
Add cheese, bread crumbs, celery seed, milk, salt and pepper.
Bake in 1 1/2-quart dish at 350° for about 15 minutes, until cheese is melted.
Serves 6.
Melt butter in a medium skillet over low heat.
Add onion, garlic and parsley.
Saute until golden, about 10 minutes.
Add shrimp and stir until pink.
Remove shrimp and place in ovenproof dish.
Cover and keep warm.
Add wine and lemon juice to skillet. Simmer about 2 to 3 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Pour over shrimp.
Serve over rice.
Serves 4.
Mix together all ingredients except bread crumbs and margarine.
Put into Mother's "Yeast-Riz" Crust (recipe follows). Blend bread crumbs and margarine.
Sprinkle over the chicken mixture in crust.
Mix together in pan on stove or in crock-pot.
Stir until cheese has melted.
Keep warm and serve with tortilla chips.
Brown ground chuck, onion and green pepper.
Add mushrooms. When browned well, drain.
Add Spanish rice, barbecue sauce, Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder.
Stir and, when heated, serve.
Makes 4 portions.
Combine broccoli and onion; cook according to package directions.
Drain and add remaining ingredients, stirring well. Pour into greased 2-quart shallow casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Disjoint wings; save tips for broth.
(Cover with water and boil for 1 hour.)
Roll rest of wing pieces in cornstarch, then in 2 beaten eggs.
Brown in oil.
Place in single layer in baking pan.
Pour sauce over and bake at 375° for 1 hour; turn and cover the last 30 minutes.
Beat softened cream cheese and Cheddar cheese.
Blend in onion, Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder.
Beat on medium speed until fluffy.
Add celery, bell pepper and pimentos and mix well.
Cover and chill 3 to 4 hours.
Shape into ball and roll in chopped pecans.
Wrap and refrigerate until ready to use.
Recipe can be prepared a day ahead for better taste.
Spray baking dish with nonstick spray or lightly grease with fat.
Mix all the ingredients and put in nonstick muffin pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Soak bread in milk.
Crumble into ground beef and mix well with egg, salt, pepper and onion.
Form small balls.
Roll balls in flour and then simmer in broth and bouillon for an hour or longer.
You might use an electric frypan at 200°.
These freeze well.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Add peas.
Put in greased casserole pan. Spread mushroom soup on top, then cream of Cheddar cheese soup over top.
Cover with Tater Tots.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Combine first 8 ingredients in a small bowl.
Arrange fillets on sheet pan or sizzle platter that has been coated with cooking spray.
Pour catsup mixture over
fillets; cover and marinate in refrigerator 30 minutes, turning once.
Remove fillets from marinade, reserving the marinade.
Bring marinade to a boil in a small saucepan for 2 minutes.
Place fillets on rack of broiler pan that has been coated with cooking spray.
Broil 6 inches from heat 10 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork, basting occasionally with marinade.
Transfer to a serving platter.
Contains 156 calories.
Yields 6 servings.
Beat cake mix, eggs, pudding and oil together.
Then add fruit and nuts.
Bake in a greased Bundt pan at 350° from 40 to 60 minutes.

Select the flavored yogurt that would go best with your fruit combination. Strawberry and banana use strawberry yogurt, pineapple (crushed) and coconut use pina colada, mandarin orange slices with lemon yogurt. Mix ingredients together; pour into pie shells and refrigerate 2 hours.
Serve.
Mix ingredients together and form into balls.
Place on a jelly roll pan about 1/2-inch apart.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 36 meatballs.
Bake sesame seed and almonds for 10 minutes.
Boil chicken breasts with ginger and enough water to cover until done.
Take out of water and let cool completely.
String chicken.
Chop lettuce
and onions; mix well.
Add chicken, chow mein noodles, sesame seed and almonds.
Unroll crescent rolls and place in bottom of an ungreased 15 x 10 x 1-inch jellyroll pan, pinching edges together to seal.
Brush dough with beaten egg.
Bake at 375° for 11 to 13 minutes and cool completely.
Mix all and bake for 45 minutes in 325° oven.
In heavy pot, cut cabbage.
Add ham and all ingredients.
Cook until done.
Cut or break the cauliflower and broccoli into bite sizes. Mix dressing until smooth, then mix with the vegetables. Refrigerate.
Make at least 24 hours before serving.
Bring the first 3 ingredients to a boil. Put the jello in the mixture. Chill the milk, then whip it stiff.
Mix all the ingredients and pour into the graham cracker crust.
Ready to eat after slightly chilled.
Combine all ingredients; mix gently, but well.
Bake at 300° uncovered for 5 to 6 hours, covering the last hour.
Or cook in crock-pot on low overnight.
Saute onion and pepper.
Mix all together and place in greased casserole.
Add cheese cubes to the top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in wok.
Add beef and onion.
Stir-fry over high heat until beef is done.
Drain excess fat.
Add chili powder, corn, tomatoes, sugar, oregano and dash of salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in cheese until melted.
Spoon over shredded lettuce and top with corn chips.
Mix all together thoroughly.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes, or until done.
Boil small potato with peeling.
Cool and peel.
Mash with a fork.
Add vanilla.
Add powdered sugar until you can knead it like bread.
Roll with rolling pin.
Spread peanut butter, chill and slice 1/2-inch thick.
Spread with cinnamon, English walnuts or candied cherries.
These are variations you can use.
Cream together Crisco and sugar.
Add eggs and beat very well.
Add cake flour then vanilla flavoring.
Beat very Well! Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Thaw crabmeat if frozen; combine crabmeat, celery, mayonnaise, onion, green pepper, Worcestershire sauce and salt.
Place in a well-greased 2-quart casserole or individual shells.
Combine bread crumbs and cheese; sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated and lightly browned.
Beat your deer meat, then mix flour, Greek seasoning, garlic salt, pepper and salt.
Shake deer meat in the mixture.
Have grease real hot.
Cook until brown like you want.
Drain on paper towel.
Heat oil in large skillet.
Add shrimp, onion, pepper and ham. Cook and stir until shrimp are pink.
Stir in tomatoes, tomato sauce and hot pepper sauce.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 5 minutes.

Drain potatoes and place in 13 x 9 casserole dish. In saucepan over low heat, combine chicken soup, milk and cheese, stirring until cheese melts. Remove from heat and fold in sour cream, chives and parsley. Pour mixture over potatoes. Bake at 350 degrees for 25 - 30 minutes.
Combine first 4 ingredients, then add pecans (halves or chopped).
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes.
Cool before serving.
Cook macaroni in salt water.
In microwave melt butter or margarine.
Add flour; stir well until smooth.
Add pinch of salt. Add 1/2 cup of milk; microwave a few seconds.
Add 2 more cups of milk and sharp Cheddar cheese.
Microwave until cheese is melted.
Pour over macaroni; sprinkle top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Beat sugar and Crisco together.
Add eggs and beat well.
Sift flour, salt, soda, baking powder and cinnamon together.
Add to egg mixture.
Add vanilla and mix well.
Beat in bananas and soak until plump.
Drain well.
Add nuts and raisins to batter.
Mix all ingredients with a wooden spoon.
Pour into a greased bread pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Fry onion and margarine.
Boil pepperoni 10 minutes and remove excess fat and drain.
Add all other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook in buttered casserole at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients and divide into two loaf pans.
Bake for 40 minutes.
Make graham crust in large oblong pan.
Mix Jell-O with 1 cup hot water.
Chill to egg white thickness.
Mix cream cheese with sugar.
Whip Carnation milk until thick.
Mix all together and pour over graham cracker crumb crust.
Spread cherry or blueberry pie filling on top (optional).
Mix margarine or butter and sugar in a large bowl until smooth and creamy. Stir in beaten eggs and peanut butter.
Mix well. Stir in remaining ingredients and mix well. Shape into 1-inch balls and place 2-inches apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Flatten by pressing crisscross with tines of fork. Bake in a 350° oven for 10 to 12 minutes. Cool on baking sheet 2 to 3 minutes before removing with spatula.
Makes 5 dozen cookies.
Brown meat; drain.
Stir in salsa, corn, dressing and chili powder.
Layer 1/2 each of the meat mixture, chips and cheese in 2-quart casserole.
Repeat layers.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Top with shredded lettuce and chopped tomato, if desired.
Crush crackers; add margarine.
Place 1/2 of mixture into casserole.
Spread chicken pieces on top.
Mix all other ingredients and pour over chicken.
Spread other half of crackers on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Bake it rather thin; use 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Put one slice onion in bottom of slow cooker.
Top with roast and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Arrange remaining onions on roast and add water.
Cook on low 8 to 10 hours or until tender. Discard most of juices.
Break pork into pieces, removing fat. Pour barbecue sauce over pork and stir.
Let heat through, then serve over buns.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease a square baking dish (8 x 8 x 2-inch).
Cook and stir ground beef and onion in a 10-inch skillet until beef browns.
Drain.
Stir in seasoning mix; spoon into plate.
Beat Bisquick, milk and eggs with wire whisk or hand beater until almost smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour into plate. Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, about 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese; bake 2 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes. Garnish with lettuce, tomato, olives and sour cream.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Brown hamburger with finely diced onion, if desired, until all red has disappeared.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add can of mixed vegetables (do not drain) and 1 can of mushroom soup (do not dilute).
Cover top with Tater Tots and bake at 350° until nicely browned.
Clean and cut artichokes. Snip pinchers off.
Soak in salt water. Rinse and drain. Chop garlic.
Place clove in each, around leaves.
Mix bread crumbs and cheese.
Spread artichoke leaves and spoon mixture into each leaf. Tuck parsley in.
Place in Dutch oven, standing up.
Pour small amount of olive oil over each. Fill pan with water up to middle 3/4 of bottom row of leaves. Boil slowly 2 to 3 hours. Enjoy!

recipes.t: New Orleans Red Beans And Rice
d: Soak beans in water overnight.
When ready to cook, combine all ingredients, except rice, and fill pot with water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer a few hours until soft enough to puree.
Puree 1 cup of beans in blender.
Stir into pot and mix so beans are slightly soupy.
Salt and pepper to taste (never cook beans in salted water!).
Serve over fluffy white rice as a main course with French bread and green salad.
Place chicken in baking dish.
Bake, covered, for 15 minutes in a 425° oven.
Drain.
Combine tomatoes, cornstarch and basil. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Pour heated sauce over chicken; top with cheese.
Bake 5 minutes, uncovered. Serve with noodles or spaghetti.
Serves 4.
Beat egg with one teaspoon water.
Mix pecans to coat with egg and water mixture.
Mix sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Add pecans to mixture.
Stir thoroughly.
Spread on large cookie sheet. Bake at 250° for 60 minutes, stirring once.
Mix together all ingredients and top with Pepperidge Farm dry stuffing mix.
Top with butter and heat in a microwave to serve.
Combine butter, flour and pecans; mix well.
Press in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Cool completely.
Combine soup and cheese, add milk, mayo and egg.
Pour over broccoli.
Melt butter and pour over bread crumbs.	Sprinkle over top of casserole.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1/2 cup water.
Put in frozen raspberries (break up with fork).
Add 1 cup cranberry-orange relish.
Chill about 5 to 10 minutes.
Add 1 cup lemon-lime soda.
Brown onion, and hamburger.
Add other ingredients and simmer.
Cut up fruit and nuts.
Mix flour and sugar, fruit and nuts. Beat egg whites until they stand in peaks.
Add to mixture with vanilla and salt.
Mix and chill in refrigerator.
Drop by teaspoon or form into small balls on greased cookie sheet. Flatten each cookie.
Bake 12 or 15 minutes at 350°.
Grease a 15 x 10-inch jellyroll pan; line with waxed paper. Grease and flour waxed paper; set aside.
Beat eggs in a large bowl at high speed until thick; gradually add 1 cup sugar and beat 5 additional minutes.
Stir in pumpkin and vanilla.
Combine flour, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder and salt.
Gradually stir into pumpkin mixture.
Spread batter into prepared pan; sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix well. Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Drain Kosher dills; cut into strips and rinse well in clear water; drain.
Put back into jars.
Mix the rest of ingredients in kettle; boil one minute.
Let cool.
Pour over dills.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator before using.
Will get crisper with age.
Mix melted butter, Worcestershire sauce and salt in large bowl.
Mix in Chex and nuts.
Mix well until pieces are coated. Place in shallow pan and place in oven.
Stir every 15 minutes. Bake at 250° for 45 minutes.
Combine first 6 ingredients, stirring well.
Spoon into a lightly greased 1-quart casserole or souffle dish. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes. Garnish with parsley, if desired.
Serve with toast points or Melba rounds.
Yields 3 cups.
Melt butter in 4-quart saucepan over low heat.
Add onions and saute until lightly browned.
Add flour and cook an additional 5 minutes until butter and flour are well blended.
Slowly add milk and chicken stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Season with salt and pepper, continuing to stir until soup thickens. Whisk in egg yolk slowly and add cheese.
Simmer for another 5 to 10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
Remove from heat and serve immediately.
Bring to boil:
sugar, milk, syrup, butter and salt.
Add dates.
Stir until forms firm ball in cool water.
Place pan in cold water and beat until thickened.
Add nuts and pour out on wet cloth (brown domestic works best).
Roll up and let set until firm.
Unroll and cut into slices.
Shred meat from chicken breasts into strips.
Place 5 tortillas on ungreased baking sheet.
Sprinkle each with half of cheese mixture.
Top with chicken strips, peppers and onions.
Use jalapenos for desired spiciness.
Top with additional cheese and top with another tortilla.
Bake at 350 degrees for 15-18 minutes or until crisp and heated through.
Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream and salsa.
Serves 6-8 as appetizer.
In a large plastic pan, cover with cold water and let set overnight the cucumbers and lime.
Then wash several times with cold water.
Next, combine sugar, salt, pickling spices and white vinegar.
Pour over washed cucumber slices and let set for 3 hours.
Then bring to a boil for 30 minutes.
Put in jars and seal.
Makes 9 pints.
Melt margarine in large container.
Stir in graham crackers and all other ingredients, except chips and paraffin. Mix well. Roll into balls, put on waxed paper on cookie sheet and freeze for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Dice eggs and add with onion, salt and pimento to chilled green beans.
Pour over whipped sour cream to which sugar has been added.
Serve at once.
Heat olive oil in a medium size pan.
Saute zucchini and yellow squash.
Add green pepper, red onion and mushrooms.
Saute until tender and add minced garlic, salt, pepper and frozen peas. Steam for 5 minutes.
Pour in a little bottled marinara sauce and toss with favorite pasta.
Amount of ingredients depends on size of family.
Mix first three ingredients.
Let stand.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Then mix both batches together.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 325°.
Layer ingredients as they are listed.
Place in a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook the brown sugar and heavy cream on medium low heat in saucepan.
Cook to soft ball stage on candy thermometer.
Remove from heat and add vanilla and butter.
Let set until cool enough to stick your finger in.
Beat until thick.
*Add pepper to taste, I like it hot.
In a saucepan, melt butter or margarine over low heat.
Stir in flour until smooth.
Gradually add milk; cook and stir over medium heat until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat.
Add salt, Cheddar cheese and Parmesan cheese; stir until the cheeses melt.
Add potatoes; stir gently to mix.
Place in a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Combine ingredients.
Drop from a teaspoon on a well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly brown.
Makes about 30 cookies.

recipes.t: Banana Split Pie(Not For The Calorie Counters!)
d: Mix the first 4 ingredients together.
Press in pie pan.
Bake crust until golden brown.
Salt and pepper chops.
Brown in small amount of oil in hot skillet.
Place in shallow greased baking dish.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over chops.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until tender.
Break potatoes into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix next 5 ingredients. Pour over potatoes.
Mix 3 cups corn flakes and 1/4 cup margarine; spread over mixture.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Cook and chop up chicken.
Chop finely, almonds, celery and eggs.
Dissolve gelatin in 1/2 cup cold water and add to hot chicken stock.
Stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Add mayonnaise and mix well.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Season to taste. Place in molds or pans and chill.
Serve on lettuce leaves topped with stuffed olives.
Serves 16 to 18.
Mix all ingredients, except buns.
Shape beef mixture into 4 patties, about 1/2-inch thick.
Cook in 10-inch skillet over medium heat, turning once, about 10 minutes for medium or until desired doneness.
Serve on hamburger buns with chili and cheese spread.
Quarter the pork lengthwise into 4 large strips.
Pierce the meat with a fork.
Whisk the other ingredients together in a bowl. Line a roasting pan with heavy-duty aluminum foil.
Arrange the pork or chicken in a single layer.
Pour the marinade sauce over the meat and allow it to marinate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Remove toys from countertop.
Measure 2 cups of flour.
Get baking powder.
Remove kids' hands from flour. Get baking powder.
Remove kids' hands from flour.
Put flour, baking powder and salt into sifter.
Vacuum mixture the kids spilled on kitchen floor.
Get an egg.
Answer the phone. Separate egg and warm baby's bottle.
Help daughter figure math problem.
Grease pan.
Answer the doorbell.
Take 1/2 inch of salt from greased pan.
Look for kids.
Put mess in wastebasket and dishes into dishwasher.
Call the bakery.
Take an aspirin.
Cook broccoli in chicken broth 15 min.
Saute onion in margarine until tender.
Add flour and stir.
Add milks and cook until thick.
Add broccoli, broth, paprika and cheese.
Stir until cheese melts.
Turn to simmer for 30 min. stirring often.
In microproof baking dish, arrange lamb chops in one layer. Sprinkle with onion and garlic.
Cook, covered, on High (maximum power) for 5 minutes.
Combine remaining ingredients and spread over lamb chops.
Cover with waxed paper and cook on 60 (Bake) for 15 minutes or until lamb chops are tender.
Mix cocoa in hot water, pour in with all the ingredients and beat with mixer.
Bake at 350 degrees until done.
Spread with favorite icing.
Slice and dice all fruit.
Mix all ingredients and refrigerate.
Mix until thick. Spread over cream cheese layer. Top with remaining Cool Whip. Chill several hours. Decorate with sliced lemons and pecans.
Combine all ingredients, except crabmeat and Parmesan cheese. Mix very well by hand, then mix in crabmeat.
Place in small baking dish.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Serve with Triscuits.
A holiday favorite!
Fry bacon in saucepan.
Drain.
Saute onions and garlic in bacon fat until onions are golden brown.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 60 to 90 minutes.
Add water as necessary while cooking.
Combine ingredients; mix well.
Pour into well floured pans. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Beat eggs.
Add corn, sugar, flour, salt and milk.
Mix together and bake in greased 1 1/2-quart dish at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all the ingredients together. Top with 1 package Town House crackers (crushed) and margarine.
Put half of the top mixture in with the other ingredients and save the rest to put on top of the casserole.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes.
After beating separately, mix the cream cheese mixture and Dream Whip.
Slice cake thin and line bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking dish; spread 1/2 of mixture over pieces of cake.
Put another layer of cake and spread remaining mixture.
Spread 1 can of strawberry pie filling on top.
Refrigerate.
In bowl, combine butter, sugar and salt; blend well. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in vanilla, flour, cream and pecans.
Pour mixture into pie shell. Bake at 350° until done.
Serve slightly warm with whipped cream.
Thaw juices and mix all ingredients.
Drink 2 ounces daily.
Combine everything; spoon onto cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Cut out tops of bell peppers.
Wash peppers.
Set aside to drain.
Mix ground beef, eggs, stuffing, rice, onion and salt together thoroughly.
Fill peppers with ground beef mixture. Place peppers in pan.
Pour spaghetti sauce over peppers.
Cook slowly for 6 to 8 hours.
I cook mine in a slow cooker.
Preheat oven to 350° (325° for glass).
In a medium bowl, combine flour and sugar and cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse cornmeal.
Press firmly on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes.
You will need a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Grate 4 tsp peel and squeeze 3/4 cup of juice from the tangerines or oranges.
In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt and 1 cup sugar, whisk in the oil, egg yolks, peel and juice until smooth.
Drain salmon off.
Mix 8 ingredients in large bowl.
Use small dipper or tablespoon shape like hush puppies.
Deep-fry until golden brown.
Cook tomatoes down until all juice is gone; add all other ingredients.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Mix together flour, butter and nuts.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 400° for about 15 minutes.
Cool completely.
Mix cream cheese and powdered sugar; spread on baked crust.
Then, mix pudding with milk until thick and spread over cream cheese.
Cover with beaten heavy cream or you may use Cool Whip.
Shave a chocolate bar on top of cream or Cool Whip.
Delicious!
Brown ground beef and sausage in a large skillet.
Drain off fat.
Melt Velveeta slowly over low heat.
When cheese is melted, stir in salsa.
Serve warm with nacho chips.
Mix first 5 ingredients to form a cookie batter.
Line a cookie sheet with wax paper and grease well.
Spread dough evenly and sprinkle with nuts.
Put 3 cups water and 3/4 teaspoon salt on stove to boil while mixing noodles.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise, then cut each half into thirds.
Scoop out potato pulp, leaving skin intact.
Use potato pulp for mashed potatoes or hash browns.
Sprinkle skins evenly with butter, then bacon and onion, if used.
Sprinkle with cheese. Bake in a 350° oven for 15 minutes or until crisp.
Serve hot. Makes 48 servings.
Boil rotini in large amount of water.
Brown ground beef and onion in microwave or skillet.
Pour off fat.
Add tomato soup to beef mixture.
Drain noodles; add to beef mixture.
Add cheese to beef and noodles.
Season with salt, pepper and chili powder to taste.
Heat in microwave 10 minutes or in skillet; serve immediately.
Serves 8 to 10 people.
Two generations of children's favorite!
Mix first two ingredients until crumbly.
Measure 2/3 cup of that mixture and mix that with cinnamon and brown sugar.
Set aside.
Take remaining mixture and press into ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan (press hard to make crust).
Layer that with apples (1 layer).
Combine first 4 ingredients in a Dutch oven, bring to a boil. Add apples and return to boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer 12 minutes or until apples are tender.
Remove apples to 2-quart casserole dish.
Bring syrup to a boil and cook 10 minutes or until reduced to about 1 cup.
Pour syrup over apples, cool. Cover and refrigerate.
Serve cold.
Mix together.
Form into 2 balls (put half of mixture into Saran Wrap or wax paper and form into ball).
Cool, then roll in chili powder.
Heat butter and cocoa.
Do not boil.

Add cocoa and butter.
Add flour and nuts.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

all ingredients gently with fingers.
Heap lightly into 8 crab

or
small
casserole.
Top with a dab of mayonnaise and
sprinkle
with
paprika.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Serve with baked potato and Caesar salad.
Cream shortening, brown sugar and sugar until fluffy.
Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Sift together flour, salt, soda and baking powder.
Add alternately with buttermilk.
Combine brown sugar and cinnamon.
Pour half the batter into prepared loaf pan.
Sprinkel with 2/3 of the brown sugar mixture.
Add remaining batter. Sprinkle with the remaining brown sugar mixture.
Swirl with knife.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes or until bread tests done.

Steam squash.
In a mixing bowl, combine the soups, mayonnaise, salt, pepper, garlic and Parmesan cheese.
Drain squash and add to the soup mixture.
In a saucepan, melt butter and add stuffing crumbs. Cook on low heat until crumbs are saturated with butter.
Stir frequently.
Line a greased casserole dish with half of the bread crumbs.
Pour squash mixture over crumbs. Top with remaining bread crumbs. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Combine butter and water in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Add white chocolate, stirring until chocolate melts.
Stir in buttermilk, eggs and vanilla; set aside.
Combine 1/2 cup flour and pecans, stirring to coat; set aside.
Rinse and scrub squash.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place in a 3-quart microsafe casserole.
Add 2 tablespoons of water. Microwave on High power for 5 to 6 minutes, until just tender-crisp.
Stir twice.
Drain and place in bowl.
In same casserole, combine olive oil and green onions.
Microwave on High power for 3 minutes.
Stir once.
Add basil, oregano, thyme, rosemary and vinegar.
Pour over the squash.
Toss thoroughly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Put in a jar and shake.
For first layer, put in ground beef and onion.
Add green beans or corn for second layer.
Combine soup with milk and spread for third layer.
For the fourth layer, sprinkle with shredded Cheddar cheese and add Tater Tots for fifth layer.
Beat cream cheese until smooth. Add next 4 ingredients and mix well. Stir in onion and cucumber. Spoon into covered container. Chill until ready to use.

Heat oil in a nonstick pan.
Add potatoes and cook on medium heat.
After a few minutes, add the onions.
Saute until potatoes are tender and onions are transparent.
Add salt and pepper.
Beat eggs in a bowl and then add them to the pan.
Increase heat slightly.
After a few minutes, turn omelette over and cook a few minutes longer.
Chill evaporated milk in freezer until icy cold.
Dissolve jello in hot water and chill until partially set; whip until fluffy.
Stir in limeade and lemon juice.
Whip evaporated milk and add sugar; fold jello and evaporated milk mixtures together. Combine chocolate wafer crumbs and butter.
Press into bottom of 13 x 11-inch pan.
Pour lime mixture on top.
Drain beans in colander and rinse well.
Mix sugar, oil and vinegar in covered jar.
Shake well.
Chop fine or mince pepper and onion. Mix all ingredients well in bowl.

Beat all the ingredients together.
Beat egg whites stiff and fold into mixture.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake in very hot oven at 450° for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 375° and bake until knife comes out clean.
Mix pistachio mix and milk.
Add other ingredients.
Better to refrigerate.
Sprinkle chicken with lemon juice and salt; chill several hours.
Add celery, grapes, chopped eggs, mayonnaise and almonds; toss lightly.
Season salad with salt to taste.
Serve in lettuce-lined bowl.
Saute onions and bell peppers.
Add ground beef and brown. Remove from heat.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Bake for 30 minutes in 400° oven.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with sharp cheese, if desired.
It is better when made ahead of time. Very good for a picnic or covered dish to take out.
Mix peanut butter, chocolate syrup, milk and Cool Whip with a mixer until blended.
Pour into pie shell and freeze for about 2 hours to set.
Serve frozen!
Combine cabbage, carrot, green pepper, radishes and enough salad dressing to moisten.
Garnish with green pepper rings, if desired.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Peel, core and dice apples.
Pour vinegar over them; set aside. Pour remaining ingredients in saucepan; heat over medium heat, stirring constantly so as not to burn or scorch, until thickened. Pour over apples.
Chill and serve.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pumpkin, 1/2 carton whipped topping, pudding mix and spice.
Beat at low speed until well blended, 1 to 2 minutes.
Spread into crust. Top with remaining whipped topping. Quick chill in freezer for 10 minutes or until ready to serve. Dust with additional spice, if desired.
Mix marshmallows and milk; heat until melted.
Cool.
Whip the whipping cream and fold into marshmallow mixture.
Add drained pineapple.
Alternate layers of crushed graham crackers with salad in 2-quart glass serving bowl.
Combine corn, egg, onion, milk, crackers, salt and pepper. Pour into greased casserole dish.
Dot with butter.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Prepare potatoes as directed on package, except skimp on milk.
Add onions, cottage cheese and sour cream.
Mix well and place in baking dish.
Put lots of butter and paprika on top. Bake until hot.
Brown ground beef.
Drain fat.
Add salsa and taco seasoning. Heat thoroughly over medium heat.
In casserole dish, spread even layer of smashed tortilla chips, then layer of meat.
Next, spread tomatoes evenly and sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with sour cream (optional).
Combine all ingredients and place in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
I use enough water in gravy mix to almost cover meat.
I break whole bay leaves into pieces.
Cook pork in hot oil until brown.
Add onion, celery and green pepper.
Cook 4 to 5 minutes.
Combine cornstarch with a little water, then stir in remaining water and bouillon cube.
Add to vegetable mixture.
Cook until just thick.
Add bean sprouts, water chestnuts and soy sauce.
Heat.

Blend well.

Serve with fresh vegetables or Fritos.
This keeps well and freezes well also.
Saute onion in oil.
Add water, potatoes and seasonings.
Cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Mash potatoes slightly.
Add corn and milk.
Heat until simmering.
Be careful soup does not boil.
Serve with parsley garnish, if desired.
Use a big pan or electric skillet.

Add eggs and milk.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cocoa and salt.
