Frost, if desired.

recipes.t: Apple Pie With A Touch Of Butterscotch
d: Heat oven to 425 degrees.
Mix sugar with apple pie filling and pour into bottom pie crust.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and dot with butter.
Place second crust over filling; press together and seal. Sprinkle a small amount of sugar over top of second crust. Cut small slits in top of crust to vent.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes. Let cool; top with pecan halves and zig-zag small streams of butterscotch over pie to decorate.
In a large skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter.
Add chicken and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until pieces are browned, about 5 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining butter, rice and garlic to skillet and cook, stirring constantly, until rice is lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and green onion.
Continue cooking, stirring constantly, until mushrooms are tender, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and basil.
Bring to a boil; cover and simmer 15 minutes. Gently stir in chicken.
Continue simmering until chicken is heated through and rice is tender, about 5 minutes.
Top with cheese and serve immediately.
Serves 6.
Saute onion, celery and potato in butter.
Add clams and juice.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add potato soup.
Simmer for 1 hour; stir often.
Do not boil. Add evaporated milk and half and half.
Bring to a high simmer without boiling.
Add pepper and Texas Pete.
Serve hot.
Serves 8.
Freezes well.
Place Tater Tots in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine margarine, garlic salt, marjoram and oregano.
Mix. Pour over 1/2 mixture on Tater Tots.
Take 3 whole chicken breasts, split in half, debone, remove skin and fat.
Pound flat; on each flattened chicken breast, lay one slice thin ham, one slice cheese, roll up.
Put seam side down on Tater Tots.
Pour rest of herb butter over each chicken breast. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Uncover.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes more.

Blend all remaining ingredients except pie shell together and mix with chocolate.
Pour into the pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Saute beef, onion and green pepper.
Add tomato soup and other ingredients.
Turn heat down to simmer and allow to heat 1 hour. Add water as desired.
Pour over cooked pasta.
Cook cornbread per package.
Cool and crumble into bite-size chunks.
Drain artichoke hearts and chop.
Mix with mayonnaise and cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Serve with Melba toast, sliced fresh bread or unsalted crackers.
Cook grits in water & salt until thickening.
Add rest of ingredients, stir well. Pour in greased 7x11 casserole.
Bake at 350 degrees, uncovered for 30 minutes, or until set.
Cream sugar and shortening; add peanut butter, egg and milk. Add dry ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
Combine first five ingredients in a small bowl.
Stir with a wire whisk until blended.
Cover and chill.
Brown sausage in a skillet; drain off excess fat.
Add peppers, onions, mushrooms, seasonings and garlic.
Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
Top each muffin half with 2 tablespoons meat sauce; sprinkle with cheese.
Broil until cheese melts and filling is hot.
Serve immediately.

Mix all ingredients together.
Beat extra well (3 or 4 minutes).
Bake at 350° for 35 - 40 minutes in a bundt pan or 45 minutes in a tube pan.

recipes.t: Mashed Potatoes With Cream Cheese And Onion Dip
d: Boil potatoes and mash.
Add cream cheese and onion dip.
Whip as usual.

Lastly, add flour, folding in gently.

Mix together the honey, peanut butter and mayonnaise.
Fold in the raisins, celery, walnuts and apples.

Pour boiling water on bouillon cubes.
Let set until dissolved.
Then pour over cabbage and onion.

Simmer until really soft.

Melt cream cheese in mushroom soup (no water) over low heat. Stir until cheese melts.
Mix all ingredients together except water and gelatine.
Whip cream cheese, milk, powdered sugar and Cool Whip until smooth and pour over crust.
In skillet, cook bacon until crisp.
Remove and crumble.
In drippings over low heat, cook rice and onion until rice is browned and onion is soft, stirring constantly.

Salt and pepper to taste.
In a saucepan, combine caramels and water, cooking and stirring over low heat until smooth.
In a pastry shell, layer apples and caramel sauce.
In a mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar and cinnamon.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in nuts.
Sprinkle crumb mixture over apples and caramel sauce.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes, until apples are tender.
Cool.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Bake potatoes at 375° for about 1 hour or until soft.
Cut a thin slice off the top of each potato.
Scoop out the pulp and put into a bowl.
Separate eggs; add yolks to the potato pulp.
Blend until smooth.
Add butter and cream.
Season with salt and pepper. Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Fold into potato mixture.
Fill shells with mixture.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake in oven at 375° for about 15 minutes or until heated through.
Blend flour and butter together.
Pat into the bottom of a pie pan.
Press the pecans into the pie crust.
Bake until golden brown at 350°.
Set pie crust aside to cool.
Then cream together the powdered sugar and cream cheese.
Spread this into the cooled crust.
Slice the bananas and place on top of the cream cheese mixture.
Cover with the Cool Whip.
Spoon the cherry pie filling on top of the Cool Whip.
Refrigerate until it is served.
Melt butter with chives and parsley.
Brush corn with butter mixture, salt and pepper.
Wrap in foil and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Grease large casserole dish or roasting pan.
Layer ingredients in the order they are listed.
If tomatoes don't have much liquid, add some water to keep casserole moist.
Bake at 325 ° for 1 hour, covered.
Then 10 to 15 minutes uncovered if ground beef not browned.

Wash beans. Put in a 6-quart kettle with 3 quarts water and simmer for about 4 hours. Mix remaining ingredients with beans and water. Place in a 4-quart casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 2 to 3 hours. Add more water if necessary. Yields about 10 servings.
Preheat broiler.
Rinse steaks or fillets; pat dry with paper towels.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread 1 to 1 1/2 tablespoons mayonnaise over top of each steak or fillet.
Sprinkle 1 1/2 teaspoons cheese on top of each.
Place on broiling pan. Broil 4 to 6 inches from heat, 5 to 8 minutes or until top is puffed and brown and fish tests done.
Serves 4.
Melt butter, add chopped onion and cook until tender.
Add paprika, pepper, sugar, mustard, sauce, catsup and vinegar.
With sharp knife cut a 3 inch slit in each frankfurter.
Place frankfurters in a flat baking pan, slit side up.
Pour sauce over all and bake in a moderate oven 350° for 20 minutes basting frequently.
Place frankfurters in split, toasted, buttered buns. Serve extra sauce separately.
Melt the chocolate squares in the Eagle Brand. Add the cold water, vanilla and pinch of salt. Use small pan. Stir constantly until mixture thickens and becomes shiny. Pour immediately over cake.
Combine cream cheese and sugar with electric mixer, mixing until well blended.
Stir in 1 cup pie filling and 1/4 cup pineapple.
Fold whipped topping into cream cheese mixture.
Pour into crust.
Top with remaining pie filling and pineapple.
Chill until firm.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Mix crumbs with butter and sugar.
Press into the bottom of a 9-inch square pan.
Combine pumpkin with sugar, salt and spices. Fold in ice cream.
Pour into crumb-lined pan.
Cover.
Freeze until firm.
Cut into squares about 20 minutes before serving. Top with whipped cream and pecans.
Makes 9 (3-inch) squares.
Sift flour, sugar,
baking
powder
and salt into bowl. Drop in Crisco.
Add about 2/3 cup milk, then vanilla and beat until smooth.
Add
egg whites; mix thoroughly.
Add remaining milk and beat until well
blended.
Pour
batter
into 2 (8 or 9-inch) pans which have
been
greased
and
floured.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Use desired frosting.
Separate dough into 10 biscuits.
Flatten into 5-inch circles. Press each into the bottom and up sides of a greased muffin pan; set aside.
Rub liberal amounts brown sugar into both sides of the flank steak.
Don't be stingy!
Lay the steak into an oblong container and cover with soy sauce.
Remember to lift the steak so the sauce gets underneath.
Cover and marinate for 1 hour.
Turn the steak over, re-cover and marinate for 1 hour more.
Mix liquid ingredients with melted butter and bouillon.
Add olives, mushrooms and (last) the rice.
Cook, covered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Place the chicken pieces in a large saucepan and cover them with the water.
Add the celery, bay leaf, onion, salt and peppercorns.
Place the pan over high heat and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan and simmer for 2 hours.
Beat eggs at high speed for 5 minutes.
Gradually beat in sugar.
Stir in pumpkin and lemon juice.
Combine flour, salt, baking powder and spices.
Fold in flour mixture.
Pour into a greased and floured (or Pam sprayed) jelly roll pan.
Spread evenly.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle powdered sugar on a soft towel, loosen cake and invert onto towel.
Roll up cake in towel.
Cool cake completely.
Unroll and spread with filling.
Combine lettuce, broccoli, cauliflower, onion and cucumber with mayonnaise.
Blend well, making sure everything is covered with mayonnaise.
Pour bottle of Italian dressing over mixture and garnish with tomatoes and shredded cheese.
Mix together, except chocolate chips and nuts, and beat 5 to 10 minutes.
In another bowl, mix chocolate chips and nuts.
Brown sausage meat; put aside.
In a heavy saucepan, combine the tomatoes with juice, cream, garlic and tarragon; bring the liquid to a boil, breaking up the tomatoes.
Add sausage; simmer mixture for 25 to 30 minutes or until sauce is thickened.
Cook penne 12 to 15 minutes in boiling water; drain well.
Toss with tomato sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and serve.
In skillet, saute onions in oil or margarine.
Combine with hash browns, soup, sour cream and cheese.
Spread in lightly greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Combine cornflakes and melted butter. Sprinkle over top.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425° and bake for 25 minutes.
In heavy saucepan, stir grits slowly into boiling water.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Allow grits to cool.
Mix well with beaten eggs.
In greased 1 1/2-quart baking dish, alternate layers of grits and cheese.
Pour milk over top.
Sprinkle with bread crumbs and paprika.
Bake in preheated oven at 325° for about 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Boil chicken until it falls off bone.
Reserve 4 cups broth. Take chicken off bone.
Combine broth, chicken and all other ingredients in large pan.
Cook over low heat until spaghetti absorbs most of liquid.
(If you want more spaghetti, cook it first, then add remaining ingredients.)
Beat egg whites, salt, vanilla and water until foamy.
Add cream of tartar.
Beat until slightly stiff.
Add 1 cup sugar gradually, then fold in flour and sugar mixture gradually.
Bake at 375°.
Dip tomatoes in boiling water to remove skins.
Chop all vegetables and put in large pot or dishpan.
(I use food processor for peppers.)
Cook on medium heat for 20 to 30 minutes or until starts to thicken.
Dissolve 3 tablespoons cornstarch with 1/2 cup water.
Add to salsa; cook a few minutes longer to thicken.
Put in hot jars to seal.
Makes about 14 pints.
Wash beans in cold water and drain.
Mix beans, bell pepper and onions.
Mix vinegar, oil, sugar, pepper and salt.
Pour over beans and toss lightly until well mixed.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Serves 12 to 15.
Remove tortillas from refrigerator.
Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise, onions and olives.
Spread thin layer of mixture on tortilla.
Arrange four slices of ham over cheese.
Tightly roll up tortilla.
Wrap individually in plastic wrap.
Place in refrigerator at least 3 hours or overnight.
To serve, cut into 3/4-inch slices.
Makes about 64 appetillas.
Mix together first 3 ingredients.
Press crust ingredients into a 9-inch pie plate; chill.
Brown meat; drain off excess fat.
Add onion, green pepper and garlic.
Cook 1 minute.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, water, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Serve with spaghetti noodles.
Line a 9-inch pan with foil; butter the foil.
Arrange marshmallows in pan.
In a double boiler or microwave-safe bowl, melt chocolate chips, peanut butter and butter.
Pour over marshmallows.
Chill completely.
Cut between marshmallows. Yields 3 dozen.
White chocolate chips can be substituted.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Stir in lemonade.
Add cold water and cranberry juice.
Pour over ice in punch bowl; slowly pour in 28 ounce bottle of ginger ale.
Chill.
Yield:
12 cups.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, and taco mix.
Spread on 8 inch pie plate.
Layer refried beans, then salsa.
Top with cheese, lettuce and olives.
Refrigerate up to 1 hour then serve with crackers or tortilla chips.
Conventional Oven:
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix together gravy mix, curry powder and water.
Place in large size brown-in-bag. Place in a 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Season chicken with salt, pepper and paprika.
Place in single layer in the bag.
Cut slits in the bag and bake for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in a small serving bowl and set aside for the flavors to meld, about 3 hours or overnight is best. Keeps about 1 week. Good on almost everything.
Makes about 2 cups of salsa.
Cream margarine, shortening
and
sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time and beat.
Alternate
adding flour and cream (divide into thirds).
Cook at 300°
at
least 2 hours or until brown. Start in a cold oven!
"Makes a crusty, delicious cake."
Place chicken in buttered baking pan; place sauerkraut over chicken.
Top with cheese.
Pour dressing evenly over cheese. Cover with foil.
Bake at 325° about 1 hour.
Serve sprinkled with chopped parsley.
Serve over white rice.
Mix all ingredients and pour in crock-pot.
Cook on low for 3 to 4 hours.
Mix vinegar, sugar and mayonnaise and pour over broccoli and cauliflower.
Chill before serving.
Combine cucumbers and onions in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix sour cream, vinegar and seasonings.
Pour over cucumbers and onions.
Mix lightly.
Let stand one hour before serving.
Serves 6.
Combine all ingredients and let set overnight.
Serve with king size chips.
Melt margarine in casserole dish.
Add rice; lay chicken in rice.
Sprinkle soup mix over all.
Pour 2 cups water.
Spread can of soup over chicken; add can of water.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend well.
Use as sauce for fish or make beef/lamb/onion and parsley patties and use as sauce for them.
Butter a tube pan.
Cut each biscuit in half and roll into a ball.
Place 1/2 of them in pan.
Bring rest of ingredients (except nuts) to a boil.
Add nuts.
Pour 1/2 of mixture over biscuits that are in the tube pan.
Put remaining biscuits on top of first layer.
Top with remaining mixture.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Combine first 4 ingredients and cook about 1 minute.
Add the remaining ingredients and stir 1 minute.
Drop by spoon onto wax paper.
Mix all ingredients together.
(Drain mandarins and discard juice.)
Refrigerate.
Sift together flour, salt and baking powder; set aside.
Melt margarine and add to brown sugar.
Mix well and let cool slightly. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Stir in nuts and chocolate chips.
Bake in large 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 3/4-inch greased jelly roll pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
In large skillet heat oil.
Saute onion and garlic for 1 minute.
Add zucchini, yellow squash and bell pepper.
Saute 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in reserved tomato juice, tomato paste, water, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in tomatoes and basil and simmer 1 minute.
Mix first 3 ingredients in small deep bowl.
Add boiling water. Beat to stiff peaks with eggbeater or electric beater.
Spread between layers and on top and sides of 8-inch cake.
Sprinkle with coconut.
Simmer butter, onion, pepper and red pepper; mix together soup, corn and Ro-Tel.
Put ham, potatoes and spaghetti in casserole dish.
Then pour over soup.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Then put Velveeta cheese on top.
Put in oven for 5 minutes.
Drain liquid off grape leaves.
Put leaves in 3-quart pan of cold water.
Heat to boiling; drain.
Bring juice to a boil; add gelatin, stirring until gelatin dissolves.
Combine pineapple and milk in blender; blend well. Add gelatin mixture, almond extract and ice.
Mix thoroughly in blender.
Pour into dessert dishes.
Chill until set, about 1 hour.

recipes.t: D.P. Whitmer'S Blueberry Muffins(This Recipe Won Third Place In "Connecticut Pos
d: Lightly spray the inside of muffin tins with nonstick spray. With a paper towel or tissue, gently wipe the spray inside each muffin cup.
Spread soft butter around inside of each muffin cup liberally.
Set aside tins in cool place.
Into a bowl, put 1/3 cup flour, 1/3 cup confectioners sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; mix well, then add the fresh or hard frozen berries and mix well. Reserve at room temperature.
Excellent on all meats.
Mix all ingredients together by hand.
Roll in chopped pecans.
Mix all ingredients in a crock, except cucumbers.
Wash cucumbers and add as they are available.
Put plate over cucumbers in crock.
Put large rock on plate to hold cucumbers under mixture until cucumbers lighten up.
They are then ready to eat.
Mix sweet potatoes with sugar, milk, salt and orange rind. Scoop up about 1/4 cup potato mixture and shape into a ball around a marshmallow, using more, if needed, to cover.
Roll in corn flakes (or pecans).
Place on baking dish sprayed with Pam and freeze, covered.
Combine cake mix, club soda, pudding mix, eggs and oil.
Beat with mixer.
Stir in (by spoon) the cherries, nuts and pineapple. Make three layers.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until done.
Spray an 8 x 8 or 9 x 9 microwavable dish with nonstick spray. Place chocolate chips and Eagle Brand milk in dish.
Stir. Microwave approximately 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir.
If using nuts, add those in.
Microwave at 30 second intervals until chocolate chips are completely melted.
Refrigerate.
Takes approximately 4 to 6 hours to set up.
In a large skillet over medium heat, saute onion, celery and broccoli in butter for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in cheese, soup and milk until smooth.
Place rice in a greased 8-inch square baking dish.
Pour cheese mixture over; do not stir.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Fry together.
Drain hamburger and onions.
Mix together in a large kettle sugar, vinegar, juice, tomato puree, chili powder, pepper, catsup, sauce, Worcestershire sauce and garlic salt.
Add hamburger and onion to this mix.
Salt to taste.
Simmer over low heat for 1 hour.
Cool; run it through a meat grinder.
One pint makes 8 or 9 Coneys.
Mix soup, milk, sour cream, chilies, jalapeno and 1/4 teaspoon cumin in blender.
Mix cream cheese, onion, chicken and 1/4 teaspoon cumin in large bowl.
Roll mixture in flour tortillas. Place in a 13 x 9-inch pan and pour liquid mixture over top. Sprinkle cheese over top.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 25 minutes, then uncovered for 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to
350°.	Put all 3 cans of soup in large deep baking dish;
pour in cup of rice and stir together.
Lay chicken pieces on
top;
cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Lightly grease to large baking sheets with butter or vegetable shortening.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg.
Using a pastry blender or two forks, work the margarine into flour mixture until
thoroughly mixed.
Mix the chopped walnuts with the oatmeal.
Stir into flour mixture.
Beat in egg and bananas.
Mix well.
Drop rounded teaspoonfuls of batter onto baking sheets, about 2 inches apart.
Bake for 12 - 15 minutes, or until the cookies have browned around the edges.
Remove from oven.
Cool cookies for 2 - 3 minutes and transfer to wire racks to cool completely.
Mix all ingredients together except the last 3 and bake in an oiled meat loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Bake walnuts for 15 minutes at 375°.
Combine sugar, water, cinnamon and salt in saucepan; cook over medium heat to soft ball stage.
Do not stir.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and nuts. Stir until mixture becomes creamy and sticks to the nuts.
Dump on cookie sheet and spread as it cools.
In a large mixing bowl blend all ingredients on low setting, then beat 2 to 3 minutes on medium.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan at 350°.
Cool.
Combine all ingredients in a heavy saucepan.
Cook over low to medium heat until mixture reaches 240 degrees on a candy thermometer.
Remove from heat and add butter and vanilla.
Beat until fudge starts to thicken and turns dull.
Pour into buttered pie pan.
Make gelatin as directed on package.
Add rest of ingredients except ginger ale and mix thoroughly.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Sherbet may also be added when ready to serve.
Brown meat; drain.
Add onion and green pepper; cook until tender.
Stir in Cheez Whiz and chili powder.
Layer tortillas and meat mixture in two stacks in 13 1/2 x 8 3/4-inch baking dish. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Top with tomato; cut into wedges to serve.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix cream cheese and sugar in a small bowl until smooth.
Set aside.
Drain pineapple and mix in large bowl with banana pieces, strawberries, nuts and whipped cream.
This should be well mixed. Add cream cheese/sugar mixture and mix well.
Spread in a 9 x 11-inch pan and freeze for 3 hours before serving.
This can be stored in the freezer for at least 3 weeks and can be used as either a salad or dessert.

recipes.t: "Grumbire" Soup(Hearty And Filling On Cold Winter Days.)
d: First:
Cover potatoes and onion with water and cook until soft.
Add milk and heat through, stirring gently.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Mix soy sauce, cooking sherry, garlic and ginger for a marinade.
Add meat, tossing to coat evenly.
Cover tightly. Refrigerate at least four hours or longer.
Mix sour cream and brown sugar together and let set overnight in refrigerator.
In the morning, add other ingredients and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes one regular bread pan loaf.

Brown meats, garlic and salt, add next 5 ingred. Then add 1 tsp each of chili powder, thyme, tarragon, basil, marjorum, oregano, celery salt, 1-2 bay leaves, sugar to taste, seasoning salt romano or parmesan. Simmer for 2-3 hrs.
In a mixing bowl, combine the first 6 ingredients.
Peel the apple and grate it into another bowl.
Stir in the yogurt and the sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the egg, molasses, oil and 1/4 cup water.
Stir the flour mixture into the yogurt mixture until just combined.
The muffin batter will be lumpy.
Spoon into prepared muffin pans.
Bake at 400° until edges start to brown, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Make ahead and freeze.
Great for breakfast.
Mix well and drop in greased muffin tins.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 450°.
Mix and spread real thin on buttered cookie sheet (press and spread with palms of hands).
Brush top with slightly beaten egg white.
Sprinkle with finely chopped pecans.
Cook in 300° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cut in sticks 1 x 3-inches while hot and cool in pan.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Using electric mixer, mix sugar, margarine, Crisco and eggs; mix very well.
Be sure to use whipped margarine; it's the secret to the cake because no baking powder or soda is used.
Add flour and milk, then flavoring.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Mix eggs and cream.
Stir in cheese and sausage.
Pour in greased casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and bake at 350° until rice is tender.
Mix dough.
Roll out to about the same thickness as pie crust, prick dough with fork & cut into 2 inch wide strips then break into pieces about 2 inches long.
Add enough water to broth to make about 2 qts.
Bring broth to boil, add chicken & dumplings & salt & pepper to taste.
This makes enough to serve 8-10 people.
Combine garlic salt and pepper. Rub over roast. Place roast on rack in roasting pan and roast in a 350° oven for 40 minutes per pound.
Put all ingredients into a blender or jar.
Cover and blend or shake until mixed well.
Makes 3 servings.
Cook in crock-pot on low for 18 hours.
Remove peppers.
Use a fork and shred roast.
Place in deep plate or bowl and pour juice over. Serve.
Clean mushrooms.
Remove stems.
Chop stems finely.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in skillet.
Saute mushroom caps briefly on both sides. Remove to shallow baking dish.
Melt remaining butter and saute stems and onions.
Remove from heat.
Add bread crumbs and remaining ingredients.
Toss to mix.
Spoon into caps.
Bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Heat soup and milk; dip tortillas in this mixture.
Place small amount of onions, chicken, green chilies and cheese on each tortilla.
Roll up and place in casserole dish.
Pour soup mixture over tortilla.
Sprinkle any remaining ingredients over top.
Bake at 350° until bubbly hot.
Mix ingredients together.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.
Mix 1 cup sugar, flour and cornstarch.
Stir in scalded milk; then very gradually, blend in beaten egg yolks.
Add the half stick of margarine, cut in several pieces.
Cook in double boiler until thick.
Stir in vanilla.
Cool.

recipes.t: Chinese Whatsit(Or You Name It Casserole)
d: Saute beef; add salt and pepper to taste and a dash of sugar. Place cooked beef in a 9 1/2 x 13-inch baking casserole.
Combine celery and onion and layer evenly over beef.
Break up frozen peas and make another layer.
(Celery, onion and peas may be combined to make 1 layer together.)
Spread crushed potato chips over vegetables.
Dilute soup with water and pour over all ingredients. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Lightly brown sausage in frying pan, breaking into pieces. Remove sausage to absorbent paper and reserve 1/4 cup drippings.
Brown steak or boil chicken.
Saute onions and pepper.
Mix all ingredients together and bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cook, covered.
Mix first 4 ingredients and refrigerate overnight.
Roll into balls and roll in small box of Jell-O.
(Use red for Christmas; orange for Thanksgiving.)
Saute green onions in hot oil in a large skillet until tender. Add rice and next 5 ingredients.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Garnish with a green onion fan.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Sift dry ingredients.
Add milk, egg and margarine.
Beat well and bake in an 8-inch greased pan in a hot oven, 400°, for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pour into shell and bake at 300° until knife comes out clean when inserted in center.
Pie should be brown.
Mix all ingredients well, adding sugar slowly.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Makes a 1 pound loaf.

Mix together, 3/4 pkg. of chipped beef, (chopped) with cream cheese, onion, garlic powder and accent. Make into a ball and roll in reserved 1/4 pkg. chipped beef. Refrigerate until about 1/2 hour before serving. Serve with crackers.
Cream sugar and oil.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Sift flour and mix with salt and soda.
Add to egg mixture.
Add the remaining ingredients and beat until well blended.
Bake in 3 greased layer pans at 350° until tested done. Let cool and frost.
In saucepan, combine egg yolks, sour cream, granulated sugar, flour, vanilla and salt.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened (about 5 to 10 minutes).
Pour into baked pie shell. Set aside.
Combine all ingredients and cook down until thick.
Then can. Let set for 30 days before use.

recipes.t: Country Sausage And Potatoes Au Gratin
d: Cook and stir sausage and onion in oil in 10-inch or 12-inch skillet until onion is tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in potatoes, sauce mix, water and pepper.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, 10 minutes.
Stir in carrot strips; cover and simmer until carrots are crisp-tender and potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in broccoli and cheese.
Cover and cook until broccoli is heated through and cheese is melted, 5 to 10 minutes.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Toss
all
ingredients and place in crock-pot.	Cook on low-medium for
8 hours.
Mixture will thicken and be ready to eat!
Mix eggs, sugar, shortening, butter and vanilla until smooth. Add flour and beat on high for 10 minutes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Sift all dry ingredients together.
Add oil, eggs and vanilla. Mix well and add pears.
Bake in greased and floured Bundt pan at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
No icing needed for this moist cake.
Great way to use up pears during pear season.
Fry bacon crisp.
Set aside, keep drippings in pan.
Cut corn off with sharp knife, cutting first a thin layer off tops of kernels.
Repeat twice, getting all kernels off cob.
Microwave on High for 5 minutes; stir and return if needed to melt cheese thoroughly.
Can also be used as topping for broccoli, cauliflower, etc.
Season chicken to taste.
Place in ovensafe pan.
Mix soup, milk and mushrooms.
Pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Chill grapefruit and crab meat in cans.
Drain grapefruit. Flake crab meat, removing bony tissue.
Alternate grapefruit and crab meat in cocktail glasses.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over grapefruit and crab meat.
Serves 8.
Cream shortening and sugar; add eggs.
Make a paste of red coloring and cocoa; add to creamed ingredients.
Then add vanilla. Mix buttermilk in same cup where red coloring was mixed.
Use all clinging coloring.
Sift flour, salt and soda together and add to mixture.
Beat well; then fold in vinegar.
Pour into 2 cake pans lined with greased waxed paper.
Bake at 350° for 25 or 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown meat in large pan; drain grease.
Celery and onion may be cooked at this time.
Add water, seasoning and tomatoes.
If using any fresh vegetables or rice, add at this time.
Cook until tender.
Add more water as needed.
More seasoning may be needed, depending on taste.
Cook for about 30 minutes.
Serve with cornbread or biscuits.
Mix flour, salt, cold water and shortening like for pie crust. Cut up apples and place in center.
Add butter, sugar and cinnamon.
Shape the dough around apple.
Jag around sides and top with fork.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Could possibly even take 1 hour. Keep checking.
Mix all ingredients together and chill for several hours before serving.
Combine soup, milk and Velveeta in top of double boiler.
Heat until cheese melts.
Add chilies and pimientos.
Set aside.
Brown meat; season with a little cumin powder and pepper, if desired. Layer torn tortillas, meat, onion, Velveeta sauce and grated cheese.
Repeat layers.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Enjoy!
Line a baking sheet with foil.
Draw six (3-inch) circles on the foil.
Set aside.
In a small mixer bowl combine egg whites, vinegar and salt.
Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until soft peaks form (tips curl).
Gradually add the 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating on high speed until very stiff peaks form (tips stand straight) and sugar is almost dissolved (about 4 minutes).
Use the back of a spoon to spread the meringue over the circles on the foil, building the sides up.
Bake in a 300° oven for 35 minutes.
Turn off oven.
Let meringue shells dry in oven, with door closed, for at least 1 hour.
Remove from foil.
To serve, spoon fruit into meringue shells.
Top with whipped topping.
Makes 6 servings.
Marinate the chicken breasts in lemon juice and herbs de Provence for 8 to 24 hours.
Cover the broiler pan with aluminum foil, then oil the foil.
Heat the broiler.
Arrange the chicken on the oiled foiled pan; broil
it on one side, then turn it over and broil it on the other side.
Cook frozen broccoli according to package directions.
Drain well and set aside.
Cook rice (not instant) and set aside.
Saute chopped celery and onion in melted margarine over low heat.
Stir frequently until wilted.
Add cream of chicken soup and milk. Simmer until well mixed.
Add Cheez Whiz and stir well until melted into mixture.
Add rice, broccoli and salt and pepper to taste with 3 good dashes of Tabasco sauce.
Stir until mixed.
Pour into large casserole.
Top with breadcrumbs and grated mild Cheddar cheese (optional).
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bubbly and hot. Uncover last 15 minutes.
Rinse turkey thoroughly inside and out.
Using your hands, rub turkey completely with vegetable oil.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Place bread in bottom of roasting pan.
Put turkey, breast side down, on the bread.

Add eggs, cheese, mushrooms, onion and dash of salt and pepper.

Stuff with hamburger mixture and layer in bottom of baking dish.

Cook pack of noodles in broth.
Saute mushrooms, onions and green peppers in butter and garlic.
Stir into noodles and broth.
Add stewed tomatoes and cheese.
Stir until melted.

Add to other ingredients.
Serve with salad and rolls.
Enjoy!!

Mix baking mix, milk, brown sugar, oleo and nutmeg.
Spread in ungreased square 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan.

Add zucchini to remaining ingredients after they are tossed together.
Mix well. (It may be runny.)
Dump into a 9-inch pie crust and bake 40 minutes at 400° or until golden brown.
(You'll think you are eating apple pie, but it's more delicious.)
Mix all of the ingredients together.

Dice potatoes and onion; cook in grease from bacon slices until tender.

Crumble bacon on top.

Combine squash,

Serve immediately.

In a large bowl, mix together potatoes, oleo, salt, pepper, soup, ham, onion and sour cream.
Pour into 2-quart casserole.
Crumble with Topping.

Works well in tube pan or layers.
Rub the inside of 8 x 8-inch glass baking dish with the cut garlic clove; let it dry.
Then smear the inside of the dish with butter or margarine.
Cut potatoes into slices no thicker than 1/8-inch.
Arrange slices in dish in rows, slightly overlapping both slices and rows.
Lightly salt each layer.
Do not fill dish more than 2/3 full.
Pour milk into dish until potatoes are about half covered; then just barely cover the whole mixture with the half and half.
Finally, sprinkle all liberally with the bread crumbs and some butter shavings.
(Note:

Cook meat; drain.
In a large pot, add additional ingredients for 30 minutes.
Serve with cornbread.
Put celery, pepper and onion in melted oleo in a skillet.
Cook until almost done.
Cook 2 cups rice which will make 4 cups cooked rice.
Mix chicken, rice, soup and cooked items together.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°.
The last 10 minutes, put cheese on top; bake until melted and a little brown on top.
Combine pineapple and sugar in saucepan (don't drain).
Boil and remove from burner.
Add jello and stir to dissolve.
Add the cold water and slightly congeal.
Fold in ground cheese.
Add the Cool Whip and nuts, folding.
Put in casserole dish and chill.
Brown beef, bacon and onion; drain off fat.
Add beans, brown sugar, white sugar, vinegar, mustard, catsup, salt and pepper. Place in baking dish and bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.

In the bottom of a serving dish spread the bean dip, set aside. Mix together the avocado dip, lemon juice and picante sauce and spread over the bean dip. Mix together the mayonnaise and sour cream, spread this over the avocado mixture. Then sprinkle with the seasoning. Top with tomatoes, onions and cheese.
Heat oven to 350°.
Beat together sugar, peanut butter and margarine until light and fluffy. Blend in water, egg and vanilla. Add combined dry ingredients.
Mix well. Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Flatten to 1/4-inch thickness with bottom of glass dipped in sugar.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until edges are golden brown.

Baste turkey with magarine.
Stuff if desired.
Put water, onion and apple in roaster.

Cover roaster.

Turn oven off.
Do not open oven door at all all night.

Spread over peanut butter mixture.

Put tomatoes, vinegar, sugar and spices in pot.
Add red pepper and bring to a good boil. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring well.
Pour into jars and process in the recommended manner.

Slightly beat the eggs in a blender.
Add pumpkin, sugars, salt and spices.
Add milk last and beat until mixed.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake in hot (425°) oven for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 375° and continue baking for 30 to 35 minutes.

Add canned vegetables as stated.
Simmer.
Add flour and water in separate bowl, make it pasty.
Add salt and pepper.
Add to stew, stirring constantly until thickened.
Let simmer; serve.

Add shrimp to baking dish and mix thoroughly. Combine bread crumbs with reserved butter sauce and sprinkle over shrimp.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes.

Pour this batter over dredged fruit and nuts.

Add milk and vanilla.

Add milk mixture.
Stir in canned peaches. Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until browned.

Bake 15 minutes in 350° oven.

350° for 1 hour in tube pan.
Frost with cream cheese icing.
Mix salt, vinegar and water and pour over vegetables and let marinate a couple of hours or overnight.
More salt and vinegar can be added to suit taste.
Fry ground beef and drain; add spaghetti sauce, let sit.
In large bowl, mix cottage cheese, Mozzarella cheese, Parmesan cheese, eggs, parsley, salt and pepper.
Pour 1 cup of sauce in 9 x 13-inch pan and add layer of uncooked lasagne.
Cover with 1 1/4 cups of sauce and 1/3 of cheese mix.
Continue with layer of lasagne, sauce and cheese mix.
Cover with aluminum foil; bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes before cutting.

Cut chicken into bite-size pieces. Set aside. Mix chicken soup, chilies and sour cream. Place a layer of tortillas (whole or strips) in bottom of a 2 1/2-quart casserole dish. Spoon on soup mixture, then chicken pieces. Sprinkle with cheese. Repeat all layers. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Serves 4 to 6.

Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and cool. Drain artichokes, reserving 1/4 cup liquid; set aside. Cut artichokes into fourths. Set aside. Combine pasta, artichokes, reserved artichoke liquid and remaining ingredients in a large bowl; toss gently. Cover and chill. Yield: 6 servings.
Peel and cut raw potatoes into quarters and then into 1/2-inch slices.
Put in pot and barely cover with water.
Add onion, parsley, salt, caraway, marjoram and bay leaf.
Cook until potatoes are soft.
Make a roux from the butter and flour and add a little water from the cooked potatoes to thin.
Add this back to the potato mixture to thicken.
Stir in vinegar as desired for taste.
Cook sugar, corn syrup and water to 242° or medium ball stage. While this mixture is cooking, place the Karo syrup and egg whites into a bowl.
Beat slowly until mixed, then beat hard until light and fluffy.
Pour the first mixture into this in a fine stream.
When the mixture is completely combined, beat hard for 3 minutes.
Add vanilla and store in jars or cans.
Do not cover until mixture is cold.
Saut celery in butter until tender. Combine soup and cheese in large bowl. Mix in broccoli and rice; pour in dish. Bake 350° for 30 minutes until bubbly.
Melt butter in blazer pan or chafing dish.
Add garlic and cool slightly.
Add shrimp; cook, stirring frequently, until shrimp are tender.
Stir in wine and parsley.
Heat to boiling. Serve with rice.
Combine ingredients.
Chill for at least 1 hour.
Serve in hollowed out round bread loaf.
Cook spaghetti. Mix together soups, chicken and cooked spaghetti. Top with cheddar cheese and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook pasta just enough so it is soft enough to roll.
Don't overcook.
Drain and lay flat on foil to cool.
Combine Ricotta cheese, 1/2 cup of Mozzarella cheese, egg, Parmesan cheese, salt and pepper in bowl.
Spread cheese filling on each noodle.
Top with a little sauce, then roll them up.
Place in baking dish seam side down.
Top with more sauce.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Top with remaining Mozzarella cheese.
Continue to bake until cheese melts.
Mix flour and salt.
Place in shallow dish.
Dip eggplant slices in egg and then in flour mixture.
Brown slices until golden in hot oil.
Drain well on brown paper.
Place one layer of eggplant in glass 8 x 8-inch baking dish; top with half of Parmesan cheese, Italian sauce and Mozzarella.
Repeat.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese is completely melted.
Mix margarine, flour, brown sugar and oats.
In separate bowl mix cranberry sauce and sugar.
Grease cake pan with a little melted butter.
Spread 1/2 of oats mixture in cake pan.
Spread cranberry sauce mixture over oats mixture, then cover cranberry mixture with remaining oats mixture.
Bake in 375° oven until golden brown.
Sift together flour, soda and salt.
Set aside.
In a large bowl beat oil, sugar, eggs and vanilla at medium speed for 3 or 4 minutes.
Gradually add flour mixture; beat until smooth.
Fold in pecans and apples.
Pour batter into a greased and floured Bundt pan.
Bake in a preheated 325° oven for 1 hour and 20 minutes or until cake tests done.
Cool on a wire rack for 20 minutes. Dribble with brown sugar topping while warm.
In a medium bowl, combine dates and raisins.
Pour boiling water over mixture.
Set aside to cool slightly.
Stir together flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
Spread crescent rolls in a 17 x 11 x 1-inch pan and pat together. Bake at 350° until light brown, 10 to 11 minutes.
Cool.
Bake cake mix as directed in oblong pan.
Put crushed pineapple on baked cake.
then add vanilla pudding.
Add sliced bananas, then add Cool Whip (spread across bananas), cherries (drain juice and crush), pecans (crushed) and coconut on top (optional).
Keep refrigerated.
Butter bread placing buttered side on bottom of pan.
Layer the Cheddar cheese, Velveeta cheese and ham, sausage or bacon on top of bread.
If bacon or sausage is used, brown and fry.
Mix the rest of ingredients together and pour on top.
Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake 1/2 hour, covered, then 1 hour uncovered in a 350° oven.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
Brown tenderloin.
Place in 275° oven until done, slightly pink in middle.
In separate pan, heat 1 tablespoon butter or oil. Saute onion until caramelized.
Add raisins.
Mix wine and cornstarch.
Add to onion and raisins.
Cook until thick.
Slice tenderloin; place on sauce.
Serve with vegetable and potato or rice.
Sift together flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder and salt, then add milk, shortening and vanilla.
Beat well until fluffy.
Mix in nuts and pour into well-greased and floured pan (about 7 x 10-inch pan).

recipes.t: Fettucini With Tomatoes, Basil And Feta Cheese
d: Mix tomatoes, Prosciutto, basil, olive oil, vinegar and garlic in large bowl.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Set aside for 1/2 hour.
Cook pasta in boiling water until tender.
Drain.
Add pasta to tomato mixture.
Top with Feta cheese.
Serve immediately.
Whisk dressing and soy sauce together and set aside.
In large bowl, combine remaining ingredients (except chow mein noodles). Pour dressing over salad and toss well.
Chill until ready to serve.
Serve topped with Chinese noodles.
(This is really good over hot white rice, too.)
Layer spinach,
lettuce,
eggs, bacon and peas in order listed in a large salad bowl.
Combine lettuce, carrot, and onion in large salad bowl.
Cook bacon slices and save bacon grease for later.
Crumble bacon into small bits.
Mix ramen noodles and almonds on a cookie sheet. Lightly coat the noodle/almond mixture with the bacon grease. Brown the mixture in toaster (or conventional) oven.
Make dressing by combining vegetable oil, vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce in a sauce pan.
Simmer sauce until sugar is dissolved.
Set aside to cool.
Add bacon bits and the toasted ramen noodles and almonds to salad in bowl.
Mix and serve.
Keep dressing separate from salad until salad is served.
(Salad will not keep very long once dressing is added.)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Slice top off of loaf and set aside. Remove bread from interior of loaf, leaving enough on the sides to form a shell.
Tear the bread you removed into small pieces in a mixing bowl.
Brown the ground beef and drain well.
Return to pan and add onion; cook until onion starts to get soft.
Add green pepper (and celery if using) and mix well.
Add Worcestershire sauce and seasonings.
Add meat mixture to bread pieces in bowl. Mix well; mix in the undiluted soup.
Taste test and adjust seasoning.
Stuff bread loaf shell with mixture.
Top with cheese. If desired, spread butter or margarine on the top slice you removed.
(You can also sprinkle it with garlic powder or more of the cheese.)
Heat stuffed loaf (and top) on a cookie sheet in preheated oven approximately 15 minutes, or until cheese is melted.
Slice and serve.
Use an 8-inch square glass baking dish or similar size.
Cut half of the cake and cut it in half.
Using 1/4 of the cake, break into bite size pieces and make a layer of cake pieces in the bottom of the dish.
Sprinkle 1 cup of raspberries over the pieces of cake.
Mix all together.
Add tiny marshmallows and refrigerate. When serving, add 3 to 4 bananas.
Have pastry shell ready; heat oven to 425°.
Cream the butter and sugar, beating well at medium speed.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt and add to creamed mixture, gradually adding milk, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Mix after each addition.
Add flour and mix.
Pour into 3 greased 9-inch pans and bake at 350° for 23 to 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate in a bowl over hot water.
Remove bowl from hot water and whisk in butter.
Next, whisk in egg yolks.
Add rum, cognac or liqueur.
Place bowl over cold water and beat vigorously until chocolate is thick and smooth.
Chill until workable.
Form into balls with 2 teaspoons; roll in unsweetened cocoa.
Place on a chilled plate until firm.
Roll in cocoa again and keep chilled in a covered container until served.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add coconut (not to edge of pan). Next, add pecans on top of coconut.
Mix boxed cake according to directions; pour over coconut and pecans.
Mix the butter, cream cheese and powdered sugar; spoon over cake batter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Place 1/2 c. water with bananas & strawberries in blender and process till smooth. Stir in rest of ingredients except ginger ale. Refrigerate and serve with ginger ale.
Melt marshmallows with 1/4 cup milk in double boiler.
Let cool.
Add creme-de-menthe and heavy cream.
Combine all ingredients.
Mix well and stuff into casing. Great baked, broiled or fried.

Preheat oven to 300°. Spray an 8 x 8 casserole dish with cooking spray. Combine the first 6 ingredients with 1 cup of Swiss cheese. Place slices of French bread over mixture and sprinkle with parsley. Bake, uncovered, 30 to 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Cream together the butter, sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla.
Add the flour, salt, baking soda and cream of tartar.
Roll into small balls.
Press with a fork dipped in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat oil in pan.
Brown chicken in hot oil on all sides.
Set aside and continue cooking until all pieces are done.
As last of chicken browns, add remaining ingredients.
Cook slowly for 40 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Add sherry, if desired.
Serve with pasta and a salad.
Serves 4 people.
Coat a medium saucepan with cooking spray. Melt butter over medium heat.
Add noodles constantly stirring over low heat until noodles become golden brown.
Add rice.
Coat with butter.
Meanwhile bring water or broth to a full boil.
Add at once to rice.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Put on a tight fitting lid and simmer until water is absorbed.
If brown rice is used, add more water and cook longer.
Cook broccoli and spinach in water until completely thawed (but not cooked).
Stir in remaining ingredients except bread crumbs.
Place in large casserole dish and cover with seasoned bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Makes 12 servings of 1/2 cup at approximately 85 calories per serving.
Cook macaroni as directed on package.
Rinse in cold water and drain.
Stir in tomatoes, onions, garlic, parsley, oil, salt, basil and pepper.
Cover and refrigerate about 2 hours or until chilled.
Makes 6 servings.
Brown sausage in skillet; add vegetables.
Cook until just tender.
Lightly toast pita bread.
Use spoon to open while warm. Fill with sausage and vegetables.
Heat all ingredients, except liqueur, in a large saucepan to boiling.
Reduce heat; simmer, uncovered, stirring frequently, until mixture thickens, about 45 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in liqueur.
Refrigerate, covered, 4 hours or overnight.
Serve slightly chilled.
Yields 8 cups.
Mix cake mix, 1 egg and melted butter well.
Reserve 2/3 cup of this batter.
Spread the rest into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
Mix ingredients together and refrigerate overnight. Serve next day chilled.
In a large bowl, whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar, chili oil and vinegar.
Cook vermicelli in boiling water until barely tender (probably less than a minute).
Drain, rinse with cold water and drain again.
Combine ingredients and place in saucepan and place on heat. Bring to a boil.
Turn down heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
This is very hot, so use pepper as you desire.
Saute 1/2 cup chopped
onion
and
1/2 cup celery until limp. Add Velveeta cheese.
Parboil
frozen spinach and drain thoroughly.
Add spinach, cream
of mushroom soup and half the bread crumbs to the pan;
blend
thoroughly.
Put
this
in
a baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining
bread crumbs on top and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Spread hamburger in bottom of a square baking dish.
Cover with chopped onions; top with Tater Tots.
Spread Cheddar cheese soup on top.
(If you mix a little milk with the soup, it spreads much easier.)
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Prepare frosting mix.
Combine dry cake mix and 1/2 of prepared frosting, water and egg; stir by hand (stiff).
Put into greased 9 x 13-inch pan, greased on bottom only.
Combine sour cream and remaining frosting mix and spread over mixture in pan. Sprinkle with chocolate chips.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes. Cool and cut into bars.
Chop eggs; add to other ingredients.
Mix well.
Mix all ingredients and pat out like a hamburger and fry in butter and oil until brown.
Good with pintos or green beans.
Lightly spray casserole dish with Pam.
Do not brown or salt meat.
Put meat in dish.
Pepper to taste.
Cover with chopped onion.
Mix both soups and mushrooms with juice in bowl.
Spread soup mixture over meat and onions.
Bake, covered, at 275° for 3 hours or at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Serve over rice, noodles or mashed potatoes. Yield: 6 servings.
Remove turkey breast from package.
Blot dry, using paper towels.
Combine flour, salt and pepper; dust turkey slices with seasoned flour.
Add 2 tablespoons butter in heavy skillet over medium-high heat; brown flour dusted turkey slices about 2 minutes on each side.
Remove to warm platter.
Add remaining butter and almonds, if used, to the pan.
Brown almonds over medium-high heat and turn almonds out onto platter with turkey breasts.
Add sherry to pan.
Bring to a boil and scrape pan to bring up brownings. Add cream; boil for 2 minutes.
Pour sherry-cream over turkey breasts.
Serve immediately.
In heavy saucepan, melt white chocolate with milk.
Remove from heat; stir in salt, vanilla, cherries for color and walnuts. Spread evenly onto wax paper-lined 8-inch square pan.
Chill 2 or 3 hours.
Turn fudge onto cutting board.
Pull off wax paper and cut into squares.
(Store at room temperature.)
Combine water or broth with contents of potato mix, including seasoning packet.
Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in tuna, milk, broccoli and salt.
Heat 5 to 10 minutes more, until mixture is heated through.
Makes 5 servings, each with 196 calories, 4 grams fat and 15 milligrams cholesterol.
Microwave Directions: Toss apples with 1/4 cup wheat germ and flour.
Layer apple mixture, ice cream topping and raisins in 8-inch square glass baking dish.
Microwave at High 6 to 7 minutes, stirring after 3 minutes.
Separate crescent rolls into 2 rectangles.
Stretch dough over apples to edge of dish.
Drizzle with margarine; sprinkle with combined remaining 1/4 cup wheat germ and cinnamon.
Microwave at High 6 to 7 minutes, or until apples are tender.
Let stand on countertop for 3 minutes.
Serve with vanilla ice cream, if desired.

Clean and wash vegetables and chop fine. Wash and soak wheat 10 minutes. Squeeze water from wheat and add vegetables. Add lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and mix well. Serve with lettuce, grape leaves or cooked cabbage leaves.
In 3 to 4 quart saucepan combine all ingredients.
Heat to boiling; remove from heat.
Combine 1/2 stick of melted margarine and catsup; split chicken breasts just enough to fold.
Salt and pepper.
Brush each piece with the mixture.
Place the pieces of chicken in a shallow baking dish.
Bake 1 hour at 350°, turning and basting occasionally with the mixture.

recipes.t: Birthday And Special Occasion Cake Frosting
d: Beat until smooth.
Use for frosting and decorating.
Half will do a sheet cake.
Combine 1 1/4 cups sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt in heavy saucepan.
Whisk to remove lumps.
Gradually whisk in milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and comes to a boil.
Boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Beat the egg yolks until thick.
Stir 1/4 of the hot mixture into the yolks.
Add remaining yolks to hot mixture.
Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the butter and vanilla.
Combine celery, onion, eggs, chicken broth and mushroom soup. Add chicken and mix.
Place in buttered casserole.
Top with cracker crumbs and cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a Dutch oven, brown beef and drain well.
In same Dutch oven, saute onion and musheroms with garlic and pepper.
Stir in meat and spaghetti sauce.
Heat until bubbly.
Spread meat mixture over both halves of Italian bread and top with cheese.
Broil 6 inches under low flame for 10 minutes.
Cream butter until light.
Mix in powdered sugar, then vanilla. Work in the flour.
Knead dough on unfloured surface until smooth. Use a shortbread pan or jelly roll pan.
Spray lightly with nonstick spray.
Put ball of dough in the middle of pan and spread to sides.
Prick entire surface with a fork, then bake at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes until very lightly browned.
Be sure middle of shortbread is completely cooked.
Cool 10 minutes, then loosen with a knife and flip onto a cutting board.
Cut while still warm into desired shapes.
Top with Lemon Curd, jelly or jam or dip in chocolate.
In a large bowl beat eggs until frothy.
Add oil, sugar and vanilla.
Beat well.
Stir in zucchini and pineapple.
Cook wild rice in 4 cups of water for about 45 minutes; drain. Saute onion and celery in 2 tablespoons butter.
Mix all soups together.
Blend all ingredients.
Season to taste (lemon pepper, parsley flakes, garlic powder, salt and pepper are what I use). Put in buttered casserole dish.
Top with crushed potato chips or cornflakes.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In an 8 x 12-inch baking dish, layer the rhubarb, sugar, dry gelatin and dry cake mix in that order.
Pour water over all and scatter the pieces of oleo over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes, until cake is lightly browned.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine turnips, carrots, onions and 8 whole garlic cloves in a 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Drizzle vegetables with 3 tablespoons of olive oil.
Sprinkle with savory. Season with salt and pepper and toss well.
Bake until vegetables are almost tender, about 45 minutes.
Rinse turkey and wipe dry; rub with oil, then salt and pepper. In a large bowl, combine stuffing mix with oil and vegetables; stir in broth.
Mix lightly.
Stuff loosely into neck and body cavities.
Skewer neck skin to back; tuck legs under skin band. Twist wings under turkey.
Place turkey breast-side up on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.
Place a tent of foil over turkey. Roast at 325° for 3 1/2 to 4 hours (180° to 185° on meat thermometer).
Remove foil last 1/2 hour.
Cornbread stuffing can be cooked separately, the last 45 minutes.
Blend all ingredients together using 10 oz. of A-1 steak sauce. Pack into a loaf pan and top with remaining A-1 sauce. Bake at 350 degrees for 1 1/2 hours.
Heat oven to 325°.

Butter jelly roll pan (15 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch). Heat brown sugar, corn syrup, margarine and salt in 3-quart saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir in cereal and nuts until well coated. Spread in pan and bake 15 minutes. Cool until slightly firm, 5 to 7 minutes.
Loosen with metal spatula.
Let stand until firm, about 1 hour.
Makes 8 cups.
A candy thermometer is necessary for this recipe.
Thoroughly
mix
margarine,
sweetened
condensed milk, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Divide and add desired flavorings and colorings.
Roll into little balls.
If balls are too soft to handle, freeze them.
Then coat with melted chocolate.
In a large bowl, mix together all ingredients until smooth. Chill for 1 hour.
For dipping, serve with assorted fresh or blanched vegetables and pickled baby corn.
Makes 1 1/4 cups.
Combine ingredients in bowl.
Let set a couple hours before serving.
Grease square baking dish.
Spread mustard on one side of each slice of rye bread.
Cut bread in 1/2-inch cubes.
Scatter over bottom of dish.
Crumble corned beef over bread.
In large bowl, mix sauerkraut, soup, water and relish until blended.
Spoon over corned beef.
Cover with microwave paper.
Microwave on High about 8 minutes (turning twice).
Place cheese on top and warm until cheese melts.
Let stand 5 minutes, then serve.
Mix together all but the cheese.
Form into patties.
Fry in oil until nicely browned.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese when done.
In small saucepan, over low heat, melt chocolate in water; stir.
In large bowl, beat sugar and shortening until fluffy. Beat in egg yolks and vanilla.
Stir in chocolate mixture.
In medium bowl, combine flour, baking soda and salt; add to batter alternately with buttermilk until blended.

Cream the shortening and sugar. Combine remaining ingredients. Mix until well blended. Pour into greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Bake in preheated 350° oven for about 55 minutes. Cool on rack before slicing.
Makes 1 loaf.
In double boiler, over boiling water, dissolve cornstarch in water; stir in sweetened condensed milk and egg yolks.
Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Remove from heat; add margarine and vanilla.
Cool slightly.
Arrange 2 bananas on bottom of prepared pastry shell.
Pour filling over bananas; cover.
Chill 4 hours or until set.
Spread top with whipping cream that you have whipped and add sugar and vanilla; garnish with remaining banana slices.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Brown meat; add onions, celery, soups, water, mushrooms, molasses, rice, salt and pepper.
Bake 2 hours, uncovered, at 325°.
In a casserole dish, melt stick of margarine in a 375° oven; in same dish, add the remaining ingredients and bake 30 to 35 minutes.
Top with ice cream.
Fast and easy dessert!
Grate cabbage and onion and green pepper (optional).
Combine oil, vinegar, sugar and salt.
Pour over cabbage mixture. Refrigerate overnight.
Will keep 2 weeks or more.
Combine pineapple and sugar; bring to a boil.
Add orange jello. Stir until dissolved.
Add cold water and let stand until almost congealed.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Add Cheddar cheese and nuts.
Measure
flour;
add
baking powder, salt, baking soda, sugar and
spices.
Combine
eggs
and
oil.
Pour into flour mixture, stirring just enough to moisten the dry ingredients. Add pumpkin and vanilla, mixing well.
Stir in raisins.
Spoon batter
into greased or paper-lined medium-sized muffin pans, filling each
cup 2/3 full.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or
until
a
wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Makes about 18 muffins.
Mix all ingredients well.
Chill in covered dish for 2 or more hours.
Roll or shape into balls about the size of walnuts. Freeze or refrigerate until ready to use.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Makes 60.
Cut 6 asparagus spears into 4 inch lengths and marinate with cherry
tomato halves in 2 tablespoons Italian dressing; cover and refrigerate.
Cut remaining asparagus into 1/2 inch pieces; reserve.
Grease tube pan.
Cut roll dough pieces in half (while still mostly frozen) and place in pan.
Sprinkle brown sugar over dough pieces and sprinkle nuts and cinnamon over brown sugar.
Pour melted margarine over all.
Cover with a tea towel and leave on countertop overnight.
In morning, heat oven to 350°.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes or until browned and done.
Invert on a plate and remove pan.
Soften cheese and margarine.
Mix with the other ingredients. Spread cheese mixture on bread.
Layer into 3 layers.
Cut into thirds, finger size.
Seal each slice with cheese mixture (like icing on a cake).
This is messy!
Place on a cookie sheet and quick freeze.
After they harden, place in plastic bags in the freezer.
Stir listed items together to form stiff dough.
Add 1 or 2 tablespoons more juice if needed.
Mix well and pour over wings.
Refrigerate and marinate for 3 to 5 hours.
Broil and add a little sauce at a time.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes or until crisp.
Mix stuffing and melted oleo.
Use about 2/3 of it to line the bottom of a casserole.
Mix soup, sour cream, grated onion and carrots.
Stir in remaining vegetables and place over stuffing layer.
Sprinkle remaining stuffing mixture on top.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Serves 12 to 15.
In large skillet quickly brown chops in oil; drain fat. Combine pineapple chunks and juice with ketchup.
Add onion, salt and pepper and pour over chops.
Cover.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Turn chops.
Add green pepper cut into chunks.
Cover; cook another 15 minutes.
Thicken sauce with cornstarch and water.
Combine all ingredients except cheese.
Pour into a greased 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Top with cheese if desired.
Mix well and pour into baking dish.
Bring sugar and milk to a boil and boil 3 minutes.
Turn off heat and add dash of salt, vanilla, marshmallow cream and peanut butter.
Mix and press into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cut when cool.
Mix well crushed vanilla wafers, sugar and nuts.
Add orange juice and melted margarine.
Mix well.
Form into small balls and roll in coconut.
Store in a cool place.
Yields:
Saute onion and garlic.
Add tomato paste, stirring constantly.
When mixed well, pour into very large pot and add crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, parsley and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil and then simmer for 2 hours and 45 minutes.
Add sugar and Parmesan cheese.
Continue to simmer for 15 minutes.
Let cool and store extra sauce in freezer.
Makes a lot!
Preheat oven to 375°.
Press crescent rolls out on a jelly roll pan. Bake 10 to 15 minutes. Cool. Combine cream cheese, mayonnaise and dip mix.
Spread over cooled rolls.
Top with finely chopped vegetables, then top with grated cheese. Cut in squares and serve as an appetizer.
Combine all ingredients.
Divide batter.
Place in two 9 x 13-inch pans.
Bake at 450°.
Yields two 9 x 13-inch pans.
Put oil and flour in pot.
Slowly brown flour, stirring constantly (flour should be very dark, but not burned).
Add onions, celery, parsley and garlic, lightly saute.
Add tomato paste, 5 cups water and other seasonings.
Cook for 3 hours on very low temperature.
Add raw shrimp.
Cook 30 minutes before serving.
Just before serving, add eggs.
Serve over hot rice.
Mix all
together;
put in freezer.
If you wish to put in fresh
strawberries, put strawberries into blender; strain and add juice to the mixture.
Mix dressing according to directions.
Add raisins and celery. Press in bottom of buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix chicken, mushrooms and three soups and put on top of dressing.
Crush crackers.
Mix cheese and butter into crackers.
Sprinkle cracker mixture over hot dish.
Cover with foil.
Bake in 325° oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Take off foil for last 15 minutes.
Brown ground beef; add salt, pepper and any other spices to taste.
Drain.
Blend together next 5 ingredients.
Place beef in pie shell.
Pour milk and mayonnaise mixture over meat.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs in a large bowl; add both kinds corn, cornbread mix, sour cream and butter.
Mix well.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake for 45 minutes.
Cream all ingredients; roll in chopped nuts or celery.
Shape into a ball.
Chill.
Melt butter.
Add remaining ingredients in order.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Boil chicken, bone it and cube meat.
Boil broth in saucepan, stir in flour to thicken, add cheese and let melt.
Add noodles and chicken.
Pour into casserole.
Put buttered bread crumbs on top.
Pour evaporated milk over top.
Bake at 350° for 30- minutes.
(May be made ahead and baked when ready.)
Cook peeled Irish potatoes in pan of water until just tender. While potatoes are cooking, chop onion, bell pepper, boiled eggs and sweet pickle in bowl.
Drain potatoes and pour into onion mix. Add salad dressing and salt and pepper to taste.
Cut skinned potatoes into thin slices.
Pour soup and milk over layered potatoes in a deep baking dish.
Place dabs of butter and bake for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes.
(Cover pan with foil.)
In a separate large pan, add chopped dates, orange slices, nuts, salt and flour.
Melt margarine and cream in sugar; add eggs and 1 cup of buttermilk.
Add soda to remaining 1/2 cup of buttermilk and add to mixture of oranges, dates, flour, nuts and salt.
Mix well with hands.
Bake in tube cake pan for 3 or 4 hours at 275°.

Boil chicken breasts until done; debone and shred. Cook spaghetti in remaining broth. Saute pepper and onion in butter. Mix spaghetti and soup with cheese. Add remaining ingredients; mix well. Bake in buttered casserole dish at 350° until bubbly.
Fill blender container to top-cup marking with vegetables. Add cold water just to cover vegetables.
Cover container; follow manufacturer's instructions or run just long enough to chop vegetables, about 3 to 4 seconds.
Pour mixture into strainer; drain thoroughly.
Repeat with remaining vegetables.
Brown the meat; add onions and cook a few minutes.
Add soup, sauerkraut and rice.
Bake covered 1 hour at 300°, then 1 1/2 hours, uncovered.
Serve with rye bread.

Mix squash, carrots, onion, sour cream and cheese. Add stuffing mix to butter. Grease dish with butter. Spread small amount of stuffing mixture on bottom of dish. Pour squash into dish and top with remaining stuffing mixture. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Boil chicken and then shred. Add chicken and 1/2 of each of the ingredients and roll into tortillas.
Bring cranberries, sugar and water to a rolling boil.
Add jello; stir until dissolved.
(To make sweeter, you may substitute strawberry jello instead of cherry.)
When mixture is cool, add celery, nuts and apples.
Mix well and pour into a 9 x 12 baking pan.
Let set.
Serve by cutting into squares.
Enjoy!
Brown and crumble sausage (hot or mild; we prefer the hot); drain and cool.
Set aside.
Beat eggs and milk together with beater a couple of minutes.
Add salt and mustard and beat again. Trim crust off white bread and break into small pieces.
Add bread to egg mixture and stir until softened.
Stir in cheese, mushrooms and sausage.
Pour into a greased (with butter) 9 x 13-inch glass baking dish.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight. Bake at 350° uncovered for 40 to 45 minutes.
Let stand a few minutes before cutting.
Great luncheon dish as well!
Slice French bread in thin slices.
Set aside.
Saute scallops, lemon zest and garlic in butter, then add dill.
Let cool.
Add Swiss cheese and mayo.
Place on slices of French bread.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 15 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Cream softened oleo and cheese.
Blend in flour and chili powder.
Work it with hands and shape into small balls; press on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Makes 4 dozen.
Combine all
ingredients and put half of the mixture in the bottom of
a
x	13-inch
pan.
Place chicken pieces on rice. Add
balance
of
rice mixture.
Parmesan cheese and/or Mozzarella cheese may	be
added.
Bake
1/2 hours at 250°, uncovered. May be baked 1 hour at 375°.
(I prefer the slower cooking.)
Cream butter and add sugar gradually; cream until fluffy.
Add vanilla and flour with soda mixed in; add oatmeal.
Chill 30 minutes and then roll dough in log shape.
Then roll log in chocolate decors or shots.
Cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Bake on foil covered cookie sheet at 325° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.
Mix the fruit and nuts together and drain.
Mix Cool Whip, Eagle Brand milk and lemon juice together.
Stir fruit into milk mixture and pour in pie shells.
Refrigerate overnight or 4 to 6 hours.
Makes 2 large pies.
Process sugar, water, sherbet, bananas, pineapple juice, orange juice, Hawaiian punch and lemon juice about 1/3 at a time in blender.
Pour into 1 large or several small freezer containers.
Freeze until firm.
Let large container stand at room temperature for 1 hour or smaller containers for 30 minutes or until slushy; do not thaw completely.
Pour into punch bowl.
Add lemon-lime soda to slush mixture just before serving.
Garnish with fresh fruit of choice.
Break taco shells or Doritos in bottom of a 13 x 9-inch greased pan. Brown beef and onion in skillet.
Add taco mix as directed. Add beans and simmer.
Pour over chips.
Top with grated cheese.
Put in a 325° oven just until cheese is melted.
Serve with layered salad.
Put in greased casserole.
Top with Pepperidge Farm dressing and bake 20 minutes at 325° or until brown on top.
Good with Ritz crackers.
In saucepan, stir together all ingredients.
Stirring frequently, bring to a boil; reduce heat and boil gently 15 minutes to thicken.
Brush on meat, turning frequently during last 20 minutes of cooking.
Makes 2 cups.
Mix together in a large bowl the hash browns, soup, sour cream, 3/4 of the melted margarine, cheese, onion, salt and pepper.
Pour into a 9 x 11-inch glass Pyrex dish.
Mix the remaining margarine with the corn flakes and top the hash brown mixture.
Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Cream shortening.
Add sugar gradually.
Add well beaten egg and applesauce (Use a little of the flour to dredge fruit and nuts).
Sift remaining flour mixture alternately with the water to the creamed mixture.
Add flour, raisins and nuts.
Cook manicotti according to package directions.
Mix next 10 ingredients together.
Stuff into cooked manicotti.
Place into a 13 x 9-inch baking pan into which 1/2 of the sauce has been poured.
Pour remaining sauce over the manicotti.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Let stand for 5 to 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Can be made ahead, freezes well before or after baking.
Sift together flour, cream of tartar, baking soda & salt. Set aside.
Combine all ingredients and blend well.
Refrigerate before serving.
Mix margarine, 3 cups flour, vanilla, water, sugar, eggs and lemon extract to make batter.
Dredge fruit, nuts, raisins and coconut in 1 cup flour.
Add to batter mix.
Put into Bundt pan. Put pan of water in oven on shelf under cake.
Cook 1 hour at 325°, then remove water from oven.
Continue to cook cake until knife comes out clean.
Melt butter.
Stir in flour and slowly add chicken broth. Cook and stir until thick.
Stir in milk, sherry, salt and pepper. Gradually add cheese.
Stir in cooked chicken cubes and peas. Serve over rice.
Makes 2 1/4 cups gravy.

Let the cream cheese soften. Mix the soften cheese together with the pineapple, onions, and ham. Form into a ball. Roll in the nuts to coat the cheese ball. Place on an attractive serving dish, place in the refrigerator until it is well chilled and serve with party crackers.
Drain salmon; reserve 1/4 cup liquid.
Break meat apart.
Add flour and slightly beaten egg.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add baking powder to liquid; beat until foamy.
Pour into salmon mixture.
Drop by teaspoon in deep fryer half full of oil.
Remove from oil as soon as brown.
These are very crisp and light.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, beat margarine and sugar until fluffy.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating well after each addition.
Stir in jam and preserves.
Stir together all dry ingredients.
Add alternately with buttermilk to jam mixture. Bake for 40 minutes in 3 well-greased cake pans or Bundt pan. Cool for 5 minutes and remove from pan.
Mix together and freeze and keep frozen.
Use ice cream scoop and fill glass 3/4 full.
Add 7-Up and stir.
Add cherry.
This will keep frozen for a long time.
Combine eggs, sugar, salt and flour.
Beat until creamy.
Add corn syrup, butter and extract.
Stir in pecans.
Pour in pastry shell.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine crumbs, marshmallows, nuts and sugar. In a saucepan, melt chocolate chips and milk over low heat, stirring often until blended smooth.
Remove from heat.
Add extract, if desired.
Set aside 1/2 cup.
Pour remaining chocolate mix over crumb mix; mix until well blended.
Pour batter onto greased 8-inch square baking pan.
Press down evenly.
Frost with reserved chocolate mixture.
Chill for an hour.
Cover chicken with water, salt and pepper and cook until done. Take chicken out of broth to cool.
Chop potatoes, onion and celery.
Add to the chicken broth along with the corn.
Add crushed pepper flakes.
Cook until done.
Pick chicken off bones and add to soup.
This can be used as is or thicken with rice, noodles or rivels.
If you use any of these, cook again until done.
Place chocolate
morsels,
milk
and
butter in top of a double boiler;
bring
to
a
boil.
Reduce
heat to low;
cook until
chocolate and butter melts, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat, and stir in pecans and marshmallows.
Spread mixture into a waxed
paper lined 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Cut into 1 1/2 inch squares, store in refrigerator.
Yields 4 dozen.
Mix ingredients together and chill.
Mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and milk.
Spread on top of cool pie crust.
Slice half of the strawberries on top of the cream cheese mixture. Cook the other half of the strawberries, cornstarch and lemon juice until it thickens.
When cool, spread on top.
In bowl, beat potatoes with the sugar.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Combine with potato mixture.
Stir in the raisins, then add milk and spices.
Beat well.
Pour into a greased loaf tin.
Bake in a 325° oven for 1 hour.
Allow to cool.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Butter and flour a 9 x 4 1/2-inch loaf pan.

recipes.t: Low Calorie Beef And Potato Casserole
d: Grease a 2-quart casserole.
Arrange diced potatoes in bottom and sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon crumbled oregano, 1/4 teaspoon salt and some freshly ground pepper.
Crumble ground chuck over potatoes in an even layer.
Sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon more oregano, 1/4 teaspoon salt and some more pepper.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients.
Roll into balls the size of quarters. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes until lightly browned.
Cool.
Roll in confectioners sugar. Yields 36 cookies.
Slice, peel and cut centers out of cucumbers.
Soak overnight in lime water.
Drain and soak overnight in ice water; leave in icebox the next day for 4 hours.
Next, mix sugar, vinegar, alum, salt, red hots, food coloring and cinnamon sticks; bring to boil. Reduce heat and boil gently for 30 minutes.
Can in jars.
Mix 1/2 of margarine and cream cheese with hot spinach.
Add egg; mix well.
Pour into 9 x 9-inch dish.
Mix rest of margarine (melted) with bread crumbs.
Sprinkle on top.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Simmer sauce and grape jelly while meatballs are baking.
Use crock-pot.
Mix first 8 ingredients and marinate chicken breasts overnight. Roll chicken breasts in bread crumbs and bake for 1 hour and 20 minutes in foil covered pan at 325°.
Open foil for last few minutes of baking time.

Mix dry ingredients together. Blend in remaining ingredients, adding more milk if mixture is too thick. Sprinkle additional cornmeal on bottom of hot greased iron skillet. Bake in preheated 450° oven 20 minutes or until brown.
Combine the first 4 ingredients.
Add the water and eggs and mix until well blended.
Spread in a 15 x 10-inch pan.
Sprinkle with chopped nuts combined with sugar.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool before cutting in squares.
Place drained pineapple in casserole dish.
Mix sugar and flour and sprinkle on top of pineapple.
Add grated cheese followed by crushed crackers.
Pour melted margarine on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes, uncovered.
Serve warm.
In
measuring
cup,
break
in eggs plus enough milk to make 1 cup. In mixing bowl, cream shortening with sugar.
Beat eggs with milk slightly and add to shortening and sugar.
Sift flour
and salt together.
Add baking powder.
Add to creamed mixture
and mix until all is well mixed at a low speed.
Then add
cup milk,
some
lemon
rind or vanilla.
Mix for 2 minutes at medium speed.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Place dry cake mix in a bowl.
Put eggs in measuring cup and add enough water to make 2/3 cup.
Add to brown sugar and beat until well blended. Spread in greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle chips and marshmallows on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.

Combine all ingredients, except walnuts, in greased casserole. Sprinkle nuts around outside edges. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Remove from refrigerator to warm. Bake, uncovered, 40 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix cracker crumbs and 4 tablespoons butter; press into 8-inch pie plate.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter. Saute onions until tender.
Beat other ingredients, except cheese, together.
Pour onions over cracker crust. Pour other mixture over onions.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and dot with paprika or parsley flakes.
Bake 35 minutes.
Mix the tomato paste with an equal amount of water.
Add herbs, salt and sugar; simmer on low heat to a boil.
Cut the eggplant in one-inch slices, lengthwise.
Pour oil in casserole and alternate layers of eggplant slices with cheese, finishing with the cheese.
Pour the tomato sauce over it and bake in preheated oven at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.

Mix all ingredients together and roll out dough on well floured towel to about 1/4-inch deep. Cut with doughnut cutter or in strips, if desired. Fry in deep fryer until golden brown. Makes about 7 dozen.
Mix in order given and fry in deep fat.
It is extremely important that you mix the ingredients in the order given or the results will not be as good.
Cook beef until brown.
Drain and add remaining ingredients. Bake for 1 hour, uncovered.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Let set until completely dissolved, stirring occasionally.
Add to Bisquick.
Stir vigorously 2 minutes.
Pour onto a floured sheet of wax or plastic wrap.
Knead until smooth.
Cover with mixing bowl and let rest 10 to 15 minutes.
Press down and cut out biscuits with a 2-inch biscuit cutter.
Place in a greased baking dish and let rise for at least 30 minutes.
If using a glass baking dish, bake for 18 minutes at 425°.
Yields 15 biscuits.
Brush with butter after baked.
Grease and flour a 13 x 9-inch Pyrex pan.
Grate zucchini and chop onion.
Beat eggs.
Add oil and Bisquick; blend thoroughly. To this mixture, add remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Pour into baking dish and bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Mix milk and soup.
Microwave on high 2 minutes.
Stir.
Add green beans.
Microwave on high 2-3 minutes.
Add onions and almonds.
Microwave on high another 2-3 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and dust with flour a 17 1/4 x 11 1/2 x 1-inch baking pan.
In a medium mixing bowl, beat eggs for 5 minutes on medium speed.
Add all other ingredients one at a time, in any order, mixing well after each addition, until entire mixture is creamy smooth.
Blend cheese, butter and margarine well in mixer.
Add sugar. Beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and flour alternately (mix as follows:
one egg, 1/2 cup flour, continue).
Blend well.
Add vanilla.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Start cake in cold oven.
