Turn oven to 300° and bake for approximately 1 1/2 hours or until golden brown.
Remove from pan immediately.
Cake stays fresh over a week and freezes well.
Gently wash mushrooms; remove stems.
Finely dice stems; set aside.
Place mushroom caps, open end up, in a large flat casserole.
Melt approximately 1/2 of the stick of the butter. Add the onion and mushroom caps.
Lightly saute until golden. Remove from heat; add the diced pepperoni and bread crumbs, mixing well.
(I usually use 1 cup of crumbs first to see how well the mixture holds together.
If I need more, I use more.)
Stir in the shredded cheese.
Stuff the mushroom caps; drizzle with the remaining melted butter.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 12 to 15 minutes, or until cheese melts in topping and mushrooms are light golden brown.
You can also broil these appetizers at 425° for about 5 to 8 minutes.
Serves 16 to 25.
Mix well. Delicious poured over grapefruit sections and sliced avocado on lettuce.
In a 4-cup glass measure, blend soup and milk; cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring halfway through cooking time.
Add garlic powder and nutmeg; stir to blend.
Blend in cheese.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring every minute, until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately.
Blend first 4 ingredients in processor or blender. With machine running, gradually add oil in thin steady stream.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Prepare 1 day ahead.
Cover and chill. Bring to room temperature before serving.
Combine lettuce, onion and croutons in a large bowl. Toss with enough dressing to season to taste.
Sprinkle with cheese and serve.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine cooled black-eyed peas, rice and chicken.
Add remaining ingredients; blend well and pack into an oiled 5 1/2 cup mold.
Refrigerate until set.
Unmold and spread with Avocado Topping.
(Don't like molds?
Just use a casserole dish.)
Mix first 4 ingredients. Let set. Once congealed top with cool whip and marshmallows. Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over marshmallows.
To large casserole dish, add cooked potatoes, cooked carrots and frozen broccoli.
Cover with margarine, parsley and onions. Top this with pork chops.
Pour onion soup mix and water over pork chops.
Cover with foil and bake for 2 hours at 400°.
Mix well; chill and serve.
You can substitute peach pie filling for apricot pie filling and can of apricots for can of peaches.
You can top with Cool Whip, if desired.
Salad will last longer without bananas in it.
Combine all ingredients in a 2-quart casserole.
Bake, uncovered, in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In an 8 x 8-inch glass baking dish combine undrained tomatoes (chopped), mushrooms (optional) and 4 tablespoons Village Saucerie.
Place chicken over sauce mixture. Sprinkle remaining 2 tablespoons Village Saucerie over chicken; spread evenly.
Cover dish with foil.
Bake 30 minutes.
Uncover; sprinkle chicken with Mozzarella and Parmesan cheese.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes until cheese is melted and lightly browned.
Mix together and bring to a boil. Simmer 1/2 hour.
Cool. Baste meat.
Blend together first two ingredients in a blender.
Then add the next four ingredients and blend until smooth.
Then fold in last 2 ingredients and pour into large baking dish.
Refrigerate until firm.
Cut into slices and serve.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix all ingredients, except 1/2 cup of the cheese and croutons.
Spoon into 1 1/2-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with reserved 1/2 cup cheese and croutons.
Bake for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.

Cream sugars and shortening in mixer. Add eggs. Beat well. Add oats, flour, coconut, soda and vanilla. Blend until mixture is moistened. Drop onto greased baking sheet using #40 dipper. Bake in a 18 x 26-inch pan at 350° for 10 minutes or until lightly browned around edges. Do not overbake. Yield: 200 cookies.
Place crushed cereal in a shallow dish; stir in paprika.
In another dish, beat egg and milk slightly.
Add flour, salt, pepper and poultry seasoning.
Mix until smooth.
Beat cream cheese until smooth.
Stir in the sour cream, sugar and vanilla.
Fold in the whipped topping.
Spoon the mixture into the prepared crust.
Chill at least 4 hours.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add onions and saute.
Add ground beef and brown.
Drain well if needed.
Add remaining ingredients. Stir well.
Turn heat to low and simmer covered for 30 minutes. Serve over toasted bread or hamburger buns.
Great served with a green salad.
Use first 3 ingredients for each pint jar.
Place 1/2 teaspoon dill weed in bottom of jar.
Wash okra; place in jar.
Add other 1/2 teaspoon dill.
Bring remaining ingredients to a boil.
Pour over okra in jar.
Seal and allow to stand for 2 weeks before eating.
Combine fruit and vegetables, mix with mayonnaise and lemon juice and season.
Serve on lettuce.
Combine all ingredients, except kielbasa, in medium saucepan; stir well.
Cook over low heat 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add kielbasa and cook until thoroughly heated.
Serve warm.
Cream the shortening.
Add sugar gradually; cream until light and fluffy.
Beat egg yolks; add to creamed mixture.
Sift together the soda, nutmeg, cloves, cinnamon and flour.
Combine jam and sour milk.
Add dry sifted ingredients and jam mixture to the creamed mixture.
Add raisins.
Beat egg whites until stiff; fold into batter.
Divide the batter equally into 2 (8-inch) cake pans.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Combine all wet ingredients and sugar; mix all dry ingredients together.
Add wet ingredients to dry and mix.
Add nuts and chips.
Bake in a greased and floured loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour. Make 1 large or 2 small loaves.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Cook chicken and cut in pieces.
Mix soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder.
Put broccoli on the bottom of a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Place chicken on top of broccoli. Put soup mixture over that.
Spread shredded cheese on top of dressing.
Sprinkle lemon juice on top.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Saute
hamburger until brown.
Drain fat.
Add tomatoes and simmer
for
minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add Veg-All, soup mix and orzo.
Sprinkle with parsley flakes, oregano and garlic salt.
Lower heat and simmer 1 hour.
Serve with grated Parmesan cheese.
Mix well in bowl the sugar, shortening, honey, egg and vanilla.
Sift together in another bowl the sifted flour, soda and salt.
Combine first five ingredients in a large bowl and make a well in center of mixture.
Combine rest of ingredients and add to dry ingredients, stirring just to moisten.
Spoon batter into greased muffin pans, filling about 2/3 full.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 18 to 20 minutes or until muffins are lightly browned. Remove muffins from pan immediately.
Saute parsnips, leeks, onions and garlic in olive oil over medium heat; do not allow this mixture to brown.
You can mix a little butter with your olive oil if you like.
Layer mixture alternately with Parmesan cheese into crust.
Some times we mix in some sauteed spinach as well.
Season to taste.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Top with sliced tomatoes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Beat egg, milk and oil together.
Dip turkey slices in egg mixture, then in crumbs.
Place in a single layer in greased baking pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 425°, turning once.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Garnish with lemon slices.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Cream butter, brown and white sugar.
Add eggs, salt and chocolate (melted in boiling water).
Alternately add buttermilk and dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Add vanilla.
Bake in layers or 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan at 350°.
Scoop egg yolks from egg.
Mix all ingredients except paprika. Fill egg whites with yolk mixture.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Combine all ingredients except candy kisses in large mixing bowl.
Mix on lowest speed of mixer until dough forms.
Shape dough into balls using 1 rounded teaspoon for each.
Roll balls in sugar. Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Top each cookie immediately with kiss.
Press down firmly so cookie cracks around edge.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Combine flour and baking powder.
Add grated cheese and chopped nuts; mix well.
Add eggs, milk and oil.
Batter will be lumpy.
Pour batter into pan and bake for 1 hour.
Turn out on rack to cool.
Melt chocolate and margarine in a heavy pan.
Add butter flavoring and pecans and stir to coat pecans.
Remove from heat. Combine sugar, flour, eggs and vanilla; mix only until blended. Do not beat.
Add chocolate-nut mixture and again mix carefully without beating.
Pour into 18 baking cups in muffin pans.
Bake at 325° about 30 to 35 minutes.
Slice angel food cake in bottom of 13 x 9-inch cake pan. Layer fruit next.
Cover with one box instant vanilla pudding, mixed with 2 cups milk and 8 ounces sour cream.
Cover with carton of Cool Whip.
Chill.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl. Refrigerate.
Saute green pepper, celery and onion with sausage in a tablespoon of butter.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, 2 cans water, sugar and spices.
Bring to a boil and add rice. Reduce heat. Cover and let simmer for 20 minutes or until all the liquid is absorbed.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix sugar and Cool Whip and put into 9 x 13-inch spray coated baking dish.
Sprinkle chopped pecans over mixture.
Cut each biscuit into quarters and place tightly together over mixture and nuts.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes.
Let cool for a few minutes before turning baking dish over onto a flat dish or cookie sheet.
Pecan rolls will drop easily onto dish or cookie sheet.
Cover bottom of skillet to 1/4 to 1/2-inch of oil.
Heat. Lightly salt and pepper steak pieces.
Roll steak in flour until covered.
Fry breaded steak in oil until browned on both sides. Drain well.
Put meat in gravy.
Mix all together and refrigerate 24 hours. Will keep in refrigerator 2 weeks.
Cut oleo into flour with pastry cutter.
Add nuts and cut again.
Pat into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 20 minutes at 350° and chill.
Mix cream cheese and sugar.
Mix in Cool Whip and spread on pie crust.
Chill.
Precook chicken and broccoli separately.
Spread broccoli in a casserole and place chicken on top.
In separate bowl, combine soup, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Pour over chicken and broccoli. Sprinkle cheese and bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Serve over cooked rice.
Trim fat from steak.
Combine rosemary and pepper; sprinkle over steak.
Coat a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray; add margarine and place over medium heat until margarine melts.
Add steak and cook 6 minutes on each side or to desired degree of doneness.
Remove steak from skillet; transfer to a serving platter and keep warm.
Combine yogurt, mustard and Worcestershire sauce in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thoroughly heated (do not boil).
Spoon sauce over warm steak. Sprinkle with parsley.
Mix Bisquick and water.
Roll out and spread with 2 tablespoons margarine.
Sprinkle with 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Roll up and cut into slices.
Melt 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons margarine and add brown sugar.
Place spoonfuls of mixture in bottom of muffin cups.
Place a slice of dough in each cup.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Simmer all ingredients in large pot, uncovered, for 1 hour. Make paste of 6 tablespoons cornstarch and 2/3 cup water.
Add to sauce and simmer to thicken.
Preheat the oven to 425°.
In a large bowl, combine the oat bran cereal, nuts, raisins and baking powder.
Stir the brown sugar or liquid sweetening.
Mix the milk, egg whites and oil together and blend in with the oat bran mixture.
Line muffin pans with paper baking cups and fill with batter.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes.
Test for doneness with a toothpick; it should come out moist but not wet.
Makes 12 muffins.
Mix ingredients together and bake in a 10 x 15-inch pan for 45 minutes at 300°.
Take from oven and spoon into bowl of powdered sugar and roll.
When taken from oven, dip with 1 teaspoon and use another to roll.
Makes about 60 cookies.
Mix ingredients well.
Makes 2 loaves.
Put sauce on top of loaves before baking.
Heat to dissolve pineapple juice and lime Jell-O.
Cool until slightly thickened.
Cream the cream cheese and Miracle Whip.
Add this to whipped cream and crushed pineapple.
Mix all together and put in a mold; chill.
Green food coloring may be added for a little more color.
In a large bowl stir

the above ingredients together and transfer to nutmeg pie crust. Dot with butter and top with nutmeg pastry. Cut 12 slits in top of pastry to allow steam to escape. Cover pastry edge with foil. Bake at 375 degrees for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake 20 to 25 minutes longer until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly in the center.
Mix milk and lemon juice thoroughly.
Add pineapple, Cool Whip and nuts.
Pour into 3 prepared graham cracker shells.
Chill 3 or 4 hours.
May be frozen.
May garnish with red or green cherries.
Makes 3 pies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a bowl; beat until smooth, using a wire whisk.
Layer half of cooked macaroni in bottom of a greased 9-inch square baking dish, sprinkle with 1 2/3 cups cheese and layer remaining macaroni on top.
Pour milk mixture over macaroni; sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Bake uncovered for 50 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and continue baking 5 minutes longer or until set.
Serves 6 to 10.
Mix and add raisins.
Add 2 eggs, beaten.
Cook for 30 minutes at 375°.
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot water.
Mix well, then add 1 cup juice.
When partly congealed, add pineapple, celery, nut meats and cream cheese that has been creamed well.
Then fold in whipping cream.
Chill.
In 6-quart
pot, boil potatoes until tender, not mushy. Drain. Saute celery and onion in a little oil and butter; set aside. Put
potatoes
into pot; mash coarsely.
Add onion and celery. Add
hot
milk,
salt and pepper.
Add chicken broth. Stir well. If	too
thick,
add
more	milk
to thickness you desire.	We like it thick.
Dissolve Jell-O in water with lemon juice.
Add remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Chill.
Beat
the
butter
at medium speed with electric mixer, about 2
minutes, until creamy.
Gradually add sugar, beating at medium speed
to
minutes.
Add
eggs, one at a time, beating
just until
yellow
disappears.
Combine
flour
and baking
soda. Add
to
creamed
mixture alternately with sour cream, beginning and ending with flour mixture.
Mix at lowest speed just
until blended
after
each addition.
Pour batter into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake 1 hour and 20 minutes at 325°. Cool
in
pan on wire rack 10 to 15 minutes; remove from pan and let cool completely on wire rack.
Saute meat, onions and peppers until done.
Fill shells; add tomatoes and cheese.
Wrap and pour picante sauce over them or some people like to put picante sauce inside shell.
Prepare grill for indirect method.
Brush turkey with oil. Combine remaining ingredients and sprinkle over turkey.
Place turkey on grill.
Cover grill and cook according to package directions.
Wrap in foil and let stand 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove netting from turkey and slice turkey.
Melt the white chocolate and butter in a small saucepan, stirring constantly.
Set aside. Beat egg yolks, sugar and liqueur until the mixture forms a slowly dissolving ribbon when the beaters are lifted.
Pour the mixture into the top of a double boiler and cook, whisking constantly, over simmering water until very thick, about 3 minutes.
Remover to a large mixing bowl. Whisk in the white chocolate mixture and stir until smooth and cool.
Beat the cream until the peaks are stiff.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine honey and sour cream.
Just before serving, drizzle over individual fruit cups.
Makes 1 to 1 1/4 cups.
Brown sausage and pour off grease.
Add onion, garlic, celery and green pepper to sausage; simmer until tender.
Wash rice and add to mixture along with soups.
Bake in oblong 9 x 13-inch dish for 1 hour at 350°.
Wash the fruit; remove grapes from stems.
Remove skins from pulp.
Cook pulp until soft; strain to remove seeds.
Place the skins and strained pulp into a preserving kettle.
Extract the juice from oranges and lemons; add juices and rind to the grape mixture and cook about 1 hour.
Measure the sugar and grape mixture to equal amounts.
Add nuts and salt.
Continue to cook until thick.
Pour into sterilized jars.
Cool and pour melted wax on top.
Mix all ingredients with mixer.
Grease and flour 3 layer cake pans.
Pour batter into pans and bake at 375° for 18 to 20 minutes.
Place everything into a roaster or large crock-pot.
Cover with the V-8 juice and cook 1 1/2 hours at 350° in the oven or 6 hours in the crock-pot.
In a 3-quart pan, combine potato mix, amounts of water and milk called for on potato package, clam juice, onion and pepper. Cover and cook until potatoes are cooked.
Add clams, milk and butter.
Bring to boil and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve hot. Season to taste.
Put everything except marshmallows in saucepan.
Place over medium heat and stir constantly until it comes to a boil. Continue cooking 1 to 1 1/2 minutes until bubbly.
Drop in 10 marshmallows.
Take off heat and beat
with beater until smooth and ready to spread.
Mix the first 3 ingredients thoroughly.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle the butterscotch chips on top. You can also sprinkle nuts on top. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Chop the tomatoes into 1/4 inch pieces.
Toss with 2 Tbsp. garlic in a bowl.
Add the basil, vinegar, 1/3 c. olive oil, salt and pepper and mix well.
Let stand at room temperature for at least 15 minutes.
Rub bread with the cut side of the garlic halves and brush bread with 1/4 c. olive oil.
Place on grill rack.
Grill for 5 to 8 minutes or until toasted.
Arrange the bread on a serving plate and top with the tomato mixture.
Serve immediately.
Combine soup, stuffing, celery, onion and paprika.
In 9-inch greased pie plate, spoon stuffing.
Arrange chops on stuffing, pressing lightly into stuffing.
Combine sugar and mustard. Spread mixture evenly over chops.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until chops are no longer pink.
Garnish with celery leaves if desired.
Serves 4.
Saute onions in iron skillet in margarine until tender. Combine corn meal, sugar and sage in mixing bowl.
Mix onions into corn meal mixture.
Saute a little minced onion and garlic in a little oil, then add drained green beans.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook slowly for about 5 to 10 minutes, then add a small amount of water saved from can and a little grated cheese.
Mix strawberries and sugar; chill.
Mix sour cream and almond flavoring.
Put strawberries in parfait glasses or serving dishes. Top with sour cream mixture.
Garnish with mint.
Yields 4 servings.
Mix flour, sugar and Crisco together; take out 1 cup.
Add egg, milk, soda and molasses; pour into 9 x 9 pan.
Sprinkle 1 cup flour mixture on top and bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Place lettuce in salad bowl and top with Mandarin oranges, pecans and onion rings.
Combine the next seven ingredients and pour over salad just before serving.
Boil squash, onion and salt until tender.
Drain and mash. Add margarine, soup and most of the crumbs.
Pour into buttered casserole.
Sprinkle remaining crumbs.
Dot with additional butter.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.

Mix together first 4 ingredients. Spread into a well-greased 13 x 9-inch pan. Cream and mix together last 3 ingredients. Pour on top of cake mixture. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Cool thoroughly for 1 hour before cutting into squares.
Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of salt over cabbage and let stand 1 hour. Squeeze out fluid.
Mix cabbage, celery and green pepper.
Put cabbage in boiling water; cook until slightly soft. Drain.
Brown ground beef and onions until onions are clear and beef loses its pink.
Drain.
Add tomato soup, tomato sauce and water to meat.
Prepare Minute rice as directed on package.
Add meat and tomato mixture.
In an 11 x 15-inch baking pan, layer cabbage and meat-tomato mixture; repeat once more.
Cover with aluminum foil; bake in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Heat 3 tablespoons butter and the oil in a large skillet.
A few at a time, brown the chicken pieces well in the hot fat; remove them to a side dish as they are browned and season with salt and pepper.
Pour out the fat from the skillet; let the pan cool for 5 minutes.
Cut 1 ounce Sorrento string cheese in half (or keep whole, optional).
Dredge each piece of string cheese in flour, dip in egg and then coat with bread crumbs.
Place on a plate in a single layer.
Refrigerate uncovered for one
hour.
In a medium saucepan combine marshmallow cream, sugar, evaporated milk, butter and salt; cook over medium heat.
Bring mixture to a boil for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
After boiling for 5 minutes, add chocolate morsels and remove from heat. Stir well until smooth.
Add vanilla and nuts.
Pour into 8-inch square pan.
Refrigerate about 2 hours.
Makes 2 1/4 pounds. Enjoy!
Cook mixed vegetables according to box.
Drain and cool. Combine with remaining vegetables.
Prepare dressing.
Sift flour, salt, baking powder and cocoa.
Add butter, eggs and nuts.
Bake in two greased oblong pans, 8 x 12-inch or smaller ones.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Melt in top of double boiler marshmallows and milk.
Pour hot over lime jello and stir until dissolved.
Add cream cheese and stir to dissolve.
Add crushed pineapple.
Cool.
Blend in whipped cream.
Cream butter and sugar.
Mix flour, salt and baking powder. Add to creamed butter and sugar; mix well.
To this add the eggs, one at a time, slightly beaten.
To this add candied pineapple first, dates, cherries and pecans.
Bake in moderate oven at 250° for 2 or 2 1/2 hours.
Let cool in pan overnight.
Cook in square pan lined with wax paper.
Spray with Pam.
Cook this several days before using.
Slice wieners approximately 1/2-inch thick.
In skillet, mix all ingredients.
Cover and simmer slowly 10 minutes.
Beat margarine and sugar together.
By degrees, add dried milk.
Flavour with vanilla and beat until very smooth.
(GE)
Shred lettuce and fill bowl half way full.
Mix together celery and onions.
Sprinkle over lettuce.
Add peas.
Spread mayonnaise 1/4-inch deep.
Sprinkle cheese and top with bacon bits.
Cook sugar and light corn syrup in a 3 qt. saucepan over medium heat until mixture boils.
Remove from heat.
Stir in peanut butter.
Mix in Rice Krispies.
Press into buttered 13 x 9 inch pan.
Let harden.
Melt over hot water (double boiler) semi-sweet chocolate morsels and
butterscotch morsels.
Stir to blend. Spread over Krispies mixture.
Chill until firm in refrigerator. Cut into bars.
Yield: 48 2 x 1 inch bars.
Mix all ingredients and saute.
Pour over ribs and bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Bring to a boil, stirring.
Mix flour, sugar, walnuts, soda and salt together.
Combine bananas, butter, egg and milk and vanilla in separate bowl.
Add banana mixture to dry ingredients, mixing until just combined. Bake until toothpick comes out clean, about 25 minutes at 350°.
Mash butter and sugar together.
Beat in eggs.
Add sweet potatoes, spices and milk.
Pour in greased pan and sprinkle top with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Bake in a 375° oven for 20 minutes. Serves 6.
Crumble beef into a 4 to 5 quart Dutch oven.
Add onion and cook over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often until beef is lightly browned.
Quarter and core cabbage.
Cut crosswise in one-inch wide strips.
You should have about 8 cups.
Add to meat mixture.
Cover and cook over medium heat 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally until cabbage wilts.
Stir in tomatoes, sugar, vinegar and salt.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally for 10 minutes or until cabbage is tender.
Serves 4.

Place coffee and cinnamon in filter basket of coffee maker. Add water and brew. In a saucepan, blend milk, chocolate syrup and sugar, stir over low heat until sugar dissolves. Combine milk mixture and brewed coffee. Stir in vanilla. Pour into cups to serve. Top each serving with whipped cream with ground cinnamon sprinkled on top.
Line 13 x 9-inch pan with foil.
Grease bottom and sides of foil-lined pan.
Place graham crackers on bottom of pan, cutting crackers to fit.
Microwave chocolate and 2 tablespoons butter in microwavable bowl on High 2 minutes.
Stir until melted.
Spread 1/2 of the melted chocolate over graham crackers.
Microwave remaining 4 tablespoons butter in 4 quart microwavable bowl on High 45 seconds or until melted.
Add marshmallows.
Mix to coat. Microwave 1 1/2 minutes or until melted, stirring after 45 seconds. Add cereal.
Mix to coat well.
Press firmly over chocolate-coated graham crackers in pan.
Drizzle with remaining melted chocolate. Cool.
Cut into squares.
Makes 24.
Cook meat and onions; drain. Add taco seasoning according to package. Add corn, beans, tomatoes and water.
Simmer 10 minutes. Serve with grated cheese and chips.
Lay crescent rolls flat on large cookie sheet.
Bake until done (watch carefully).
Cool.
Mix cake according to directions.
Add 1/4 cup water and donuts.
Stir well and pour into 12 x 18-inch shallow pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Bake unpicked pastry with 2 layers of foil for 5 minutes at 450°.
Remove foil; bake 5 to 7 minutes more (keep warm).
Cook sausage, onions and garlic until meat is done.
Drain.
Stir in chili peppers.
In another saucepan, combine cheese and flour; add cream.
Cook and stir until cheese is melted.
Add hot sauce. Blend hot cream mixture into beaten eggs slowly.
Add meat mixture.
Pour into pastry.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes or until a knife comes out clean.
Let stand.
Serve with picante sauce, sour cream and guacamole.
Combine all ingredients, except pecans and pie crust.
Mix well.
Pour into pie crust.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

recipes.t: Pears With Spicy Lime, Chile And Peanut Chutney
d: Cut each pear lengthwise into quarters.
Using a melon baller, create a well in the center of each quarter.
In a small bowl, prepare chutney by mixing together the next seven ingredients. Spoon chutney into hollowed out section of pear quarters.
Add a sprig of mint for garnish.
Place on serving tray.
Bring pineapple to boiling point.
Add Jell-O and stir until dissolved.
Refrigerate until it begins to set.
Stir in cream cheese.
Fold in whipping cream and nuts.
Add cherries, if desired.
Mold.
Serves 8 to 10.
Dissolve gelatin in cold water.
Put over heat and add vinegar, onion, salt and paprika.
Chill until about to set.
Beat the gelatin mixture into the stiffly whipped cream.
Fold in the cucumbers.
Rinse individual molds, fill them with mousse.
When they are thoroughly chilled, invert them onto a garnished plate. Serves 4.

Mix hash browns with sour cream and margarine. Add 1 cup of the grated cheese, onion, salt and pepper. Slowly mix in the can of soup. Pour into a 13 x 9-inch baking dish. Mix remaining 1 cup cheese with corn flake crumbs. Sprinkle on top of potato mixture in dish. Bake 40 to 60 minutes at 350°, uncovered.
Combine eggs, sugar, syrup and butter.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until butter melts and mixture is steaming. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and pecans.
Mix well.
Pour into pie crust and bake at 325° until set.
Saute celery and onion in margarine.
Add all three soups, undiluted to make a sauce.
Mix all ingredients together and pour in casserole dish.
Place drained broccoli on top and sprinkle with paprika and grated cheese.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Mix first
ingredients
in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan. Put cheese on top and dot with butter.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Heat oven to 400°.
In large bowl, beat 1 1/2 cups sugar and margarine until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla and eggs; blend well.
Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup; level off.
Stir in flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt; mix well.
In small bowl, combine the 2 tablespoons each of sugar and cinnamon.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls; roll in sugar and cinnamon mixture. Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes, or until set immediately.
Remove from cookie sheets.
Makes 4 dozen.
Cook ground beef and sausage until brown and crumbly.
Add Ro-Tel and cheese and melt on low heat.
Serve with corn chips.
Heat margarine until melted.
Blend in flour, salt and pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until bubbly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in broth and milk.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into ungreased 2-quart casserole or 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Cook uncovered in 350° oven until bubbly, 40 to 45 minutes.
Combine ground chuck, onion, soy sauce, mushrooms, pepper and mix lightly.
Shape into patties 1 1/2-inch thick.
Wrap each patty with one slice bacon.
Secure with pick.
Grill 3 to 6 minutes or to desired doneness.
Mix sugar, corn syrup, water and salt in saucepan. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Cover and bring to a boil.
Cook for a minute or two to wash down sugar crystals.
Remove cover. Cook, without stirring, until syrup reaches hard ball stage, 260°, or until syrup is slightly brittle when dropped in cold water. Beat egg whites until frothy.
Continue beating, adding Jell-O slowly. Beat until candy is creamy. Stir in nuts. Candy sets quickly.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto wax paper.
Yields 5 dozen.

Preheat oven and roasting pan to 350°. Salt and pepper 1 side of the roast. Place seasoned side of roast down on preheated pan. Bake for 20 minutes. Season top side of roast. Turn roast over and decrease oven heat to 325°. Roast for about 2 1/2 hours at 325° (longer time will be needed if larger roast). Turn roast over and add vegetables around base of roast in pan, with potatoes on bottom, covered by the carrots and at least 2 pieces of the apples on top of the roast. Cover the roasting pan after adding the vegetables. Add hot water to depth of about 1-inch. Bake for an additional hour or hour and 15 minutes or until vegetables are done and meat shreds easily. Remember to check water level occasionally. You don't want it to go dry.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 13 x 9 inch pan.
Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup, level off.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and lemon peel.
Using pastry blender or fork, cut in margarine until mixture is the consistency of coarse meal.
Add milk, eggs, and vanilla; stir until well blended.
Pour 3/4 of batter into prepared pan.
Top with blueberries.
Spoon remaining batter over blueberries.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool 30 minutes.
Break chocolate into heavy (large) mixing bowl.
Add whipped marshmallow, chopped walnuts and vanilla.
In a large pan, heat to melt butter and margarine.
Then bring to a rolling boil once boiling starts.
Let boil for exactly 6 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add to mixture in bowl.
Mix well.
Put in 9 x 13-inch pan. Chill overnight and enjoy.
Roll biscuits in butter, then roll in brown sugar.
Sprinkle on cinnamon.
Blend all ingredients in shallow pan.
Marinate steak, turning occasionally, several hours or overnight.
Broil 5 to 6 minutes on each side.
Slice on diagonal.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Stir in sugar, salt, oleo, eggs and flour to make stiff dough.
Grease top; cover and let rise until double in bulk.
Punch down.
Form into balls and cover. Let rise until double in size again, about 45 minutes.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes or until done.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan or 12 cup Bundt pan.
Beat butter and cream cheese together in mixing bowl until well blended.
Add sugar and cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beat well.
Blend in vanilla. Sift flour and salt together and blend into cream mixture.
Spoon batter into prepared pan.
Bake 1 hour and 15 minutes.

In saucepan, combine preserves, lemon juice, cornstarch and cinnamon. Cook and stir until well blended and slightly thickened. Stir in franks and pineapple. Heat through. Just before serving, stir in apples and oranges. Serve warm.

recipes.t: Chicken Breast With Honey Chutney And Pears
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine pears and lemon juice. Melt margarine in skillet.
Add chicken; saute. Transfer to shallow glass baking dish.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over chicken.
Place pears and lemon juice combination on top.
Bake 30 minutes or until done.
Place nuts in the bottom of Bundt pan.
Cut biscuits into quarters.
Roll each piece in sugar and cinnamon, mixed together. Put in greased Bundt pan.
Melt butter; add brown sugar, water and remaining cinnamon and sugar.
Boil 2 minutes.
Pour over biscuits.
Bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Turn out on plate; serve warm.
Add mayonnaise to grated cheese.
Add chopped ripe olives and green onions.
Mix and spread on English muffins.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
Cut into fourths to serve.
Freezes well.
Mix everything in saucepan and cook until mixture thickens. Cool and store in refrigerator.
Mix cream cheese, bacon and mushroom caps. Broil about 10 minutes or until clear liquid seeps from mushrooms.
Serve hot.
Melt oleo; saute onion and celery.
Add undiluted soup, squash, cornbread soaked in milk and sage.
Pour in greased casserole dish.
Sprinkle with 1 cup cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Drain and crumble.
Stir-fry onion in bacon drippings for 2 minutes.
Add rice and stir-fry for 7 to 8 minutes.
Add soy sauce, water and crumbled bacon.
Reduce heat to medium-low.
Pur eggs on top of rice mixture.
Stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes or until eggs are cooked.
Beat flour, baking soda, salt, sugar, margarine and eggs 2 1/2 minutes on high.
Add sour cream and beat on low.
Add bananas and vanilla and beat on low.
Optional:
Add walnuts and beat on low. Add raisins; cover raisins with sugar and drop in batter that has been poured into loaf pan.
Push raisins into batter individually with knife.
Butter and flour bottom of pan.
Bake at 350° for 60 minutes.
Cook macaroni as directed, drain.
Rinse with cold water, drain. Mix mayonnaise with lemon juice, salt and sugar.
Combine with macaroni, celery seed, tomato, celery, pimiento and green pepper.
Serve on salad greens, garnish with radish roses. Serves 6.
Combine 2 1/2 cups water, vinegar, sugar, salt, cloves, peppercorns and
bay leaves in saucepan;
bring to boil.
Pour over sliced
onions;
cool.
Stir
in oil.
Pour marinade over steak; refrigerate
to
hours,
turning
at least once. Remove steaks from marinade to absorbent paper; pat dry.
Heat drippings to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together and put in covered 2-quart dish and bake at 300° for four hours.
Delicious!

recipes.t: Mama Crow'S Raisin Nut Jam Cake
d: In large mixing bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs well, then add jam.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with dry ingredients and beat well after each addition.
Stir in raisins and nuts.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans.
Bake 40 minutes at 300° (or until toothpick inserted in center of layer comes out clean).
Cool completely on racks.
Place pork chops in a large skillet and cover with water. Brown the chops.
Remove from skillet and brown the onions.
Put chops back in the skillet with the onions and add vinegar, brown sugar, and ketchup.
Add water to cover.
Cook over high heat until it starts to boil.
Reduce heat to low, let simmer until gravy thickens, about 2 hours.
Mix well and place in casserole dish.
Sprinkle top with 3/4 cup grated Swiss cheese and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

In microwave, melt chocolate, butter and shortening. Stir until smooth. Place in miniature foil baking cups in miniature muffin pan. Put 1 teaspoon chocolate mixture in each cup. Microwave peanut butter until melted. Spoon into cups and cover with chocolate mixture. Refrigerate. Makes 1 dozen.
Melt margarine.
Add onion, broccoli and celery. Cook over low heat a few minutes, then add soup, cheese and rice.
Pour in baking dish and bake for 25 minutes at 350°.
(This may be cooked in microwave.)
Heat oven to 350°.
Line 8 or 9-inch square baking pan with foil, extending edges over sides of pan.
In a small mixing bowl, beat butter, 1/2 cup sugar and salt until smooth.
Stir together flour and cocoa; gradually add to butter mixture, beating until soft dough is formed.
Press dough onto bottom of prepared pan. Beat cream cheese and remaining 1/2 cup sugar until smooth.
Add eggs and vanilla; blend well.
Prepare and bake cake in 13 x 9-inch pan according to package directions.
While cake is still warm, poke holes (about a dozen) across top of cake with the end of a wooden spoon.
Let cool slightly.
Pour sweetened condensed milk and topping into holes and over cake.
Let stand a few minutes, then spread with Cool Whip. Sprinkle crushed candy bars over top.
Serves 12 to 16.
Combine sugar, cream cheese and margarine.
Mix at medium speed until well blended.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Blend in pumpkin.
Add combined dry ingredients, mixing until just moistened.
Fold in nuts.
Mix all ingredients and bake in a 325° oven for 30 to 35 minutes.
You can use either a 13 x 9-inch rectangle pan or a Bundt pan.
To cherries, add 1 cup sugar and the flour.
Cook in saucepan until thick; refrigerate to cool.
Cream the cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Add the vanilla and a little cream to make it smooth.
Whip the cream and fold into cream cheese mixture.
Fill the cooled pie crust with cheese filling.
Pour cherry mixture on top.
Keep refrigerated.
Cook cornbread as directed on package. Crumble and let cool. Chop pepper, tomato and onions. Add to cornbread, then add about 3 cups of Miracle Whip. Chill.
Brown hamburger and onion; drain off grease.
Add taco seasoning.
Spoon half of hamburger into 2-quart casserole, then beans, then cheese, then chips.
Repeat.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Form into logs. about 2 inches long and about 1/2 inch in diameter.
Put them into freezer till frozen.
Oh about an hour or so.
Melt 1 package of chocolate chips. 1/2 bar of wax.
Dip logs into chips and wax.
Put logs onto wax paper.
Its a lot easier to store.
Mix first four ingredients in a large pan until it is crumbly. Place 1 egg, 1 teaspoon of vinegar in 1 cup and mix.
Fill remainder of cup with milk to make 1 cup.
Mix with flour until it will come off of your hands.
Preheat oven to 375°. In bowl,

combine Ricotta cheese, 1 cup Mozzarella cheese, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese and eggs. In 13 x 9-inch baking dish, spread 1/2 of one jar of pasta sauce. Layer 4 uncooked noodles, then 1/2 jar of pasta sauce and 1/2 of the Ricotta cheese mixture; repeat. Top with remaining 4 uncooked noodles and rest of pasta sauce. Cover tightly with aluminum foil and bake 1 hour. Remove foil and sprinkle remaining cheeses. Bake, uncovered, an additional 10 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Brown meat in onion; stir in tomato sauce, chili powder and garlic powder.
Simmer.
Line 9 x 13-inch pan with biscuits, combine half of the cheese, sour cream and egg; then mix with meat.
Spoon the meat mixture over the biscuits.
Sprinkle the rest of cheese on top of the meat mixture.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Combine veggies, soup, 1/2 c. cheese, sour cream, pepper and 1/2 can Durkee fried onions.
Pour into the 1 qt. casserole dish. Microwave on high 10-12 minutes or until bubbly.
Remove and sprinkle remaining onions over top.
Microwave until cheese is melted.
Wash chicken and cut into cubes (approximately 1 to 2-inch in size).
Set aside to drain on paper towels.
Mix beaten egg, milk, salt and sesame seed in medium size bowl.
Add chicken to egg mixture.
Coat each piece of chicken with flour.
After all chicken is coated with flour, heat shortening on medium until ready to fry.
Add nuggets a few at a time to keep them from sticking together, turning them 2 or 3 times until they are tender and golden brown.
Serve with sauces such as barbecue, honey mustard or sweet-n-sour.
In a bowl, blend together cream cheese, sour cream and taco mix.
Spread over dinner plate.
Layer the remaining ingredients on top.
Chill until ready to serve.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Place chicken in crock-pot or casserole dish.
Mix other ingredients and pur over.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or in crock-pot all day.
Serve with rice.
Mix flour, celery salt, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Mix in butter until even particles are formed.
Add milk and blend.
Cook until tender in chicken broth.
Soak gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
In top of double boiler, beat egg yolks; add 1/2 cup sugar, lemon juice and salt. Cook over hot water, stirring constantly, until smooth and thickened.
Add softened gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Remove from heat, add lemon rind and cool.
Beat egg whites until stiff, but not dry.
Gradually add 1/2 cup sugar, beating until stiff. Fold in cooled lemon mixture and then pour into the pie shell. Refrigerate until set.
Spread with whipped cream just before serving.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine the scallions, fresh tomatoes and peppers in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in the pureed tomatoes, water and lime juice. Stir in the oil and parsley; season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate, covered, until ready to serve.
Serve with your favorite corn tortilla chips.
A great summer dip!
Yields 8 cups.
Mix well.
Salt, pepper and sugar to taste.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Stir when half done.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all together well; put in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour covered.
Stir every 20 minutes.
Heat 2-inches deep of oil in skillet.
Heat oil until hot, but not smoking.
Take batter, pour it through funnel into hot oil, moving in a circular motion, then crisscross until you've made a cake the size of a plate or smaller.
When lightly browned, remove and drain on paper towels.
Dredge or sprinkle in powdered sugar and sprinkle with cinnamon powder.
Best when eaten warm.
Remove tips from chicken wings.
Combine pineapple juice, beer, soy sauce, brown sugar, onion, ginger and garlic.
Stir together until sugar is dissolved.
Add chicken, stirring to coat well.
Cover and marinate at room temperature for about 1 hour. Drain chicken; reserve marinade.
Melt margarine in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add chicken and cook, browning on all sides.
add 1/2 cup reserved marinade to chicken.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, over low heat for about 15 minutes or until fork can be inserted into chicken with ease.
Keep chicken moist by using additional marinade as needed.
Cream butter; add sugar and beat until fluffy.
Add beaten eggs.
Sift dry ingredients together and add alternately with milk to butter mixture.
Fold in pecans.
Bake in a well-greased lightly floured tube pan (9-inch).
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until straw inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan 10 minutes before removing.
This can be baked and stored for a couple of days.
Keep cool.
Dissolve jello and water.
Add pineapple.
Chill
until slightly thickened.
Soften and blend cream cheese and sour cream. Stir in jello mixture.
Add nuts and chill.
In large pan, heat chili.
Cut cheese into small squares and add to chili.
When cheese is melted, add sour cream and sauteed onion.
Mix well and serve hot with chips.
Cut stems off eggplant and slice 1/2 to 5/8-inch thickness. In a bowl, beat in egg.
In second bowl, mix cracker crumbs, seasonings and 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.
Spread butter in a 10 x 15-inch baking dish.
Dip each slice of eggplant in egg.
Drain briefly, then coat with cracker crumbs.
Arrange slices in single layer in pan.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once, in a 425° oven.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drop onto cookie sheet or put in pan.
Bake at 325° for 10 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen.
Whip the cream and add sugar and preserves.
Put mixture into pie crust; sprinkle top with coconut and refrigerate.
Crumble and brown sausage; drain.
Beat eggs; add milk, salt and mustard and mix.
Stir in bread cubes, cheese and sausage and mix.
Put in 8 x 12-inch glass baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Let it set for 15 minutes before slicing.
In large bowl combine beaten egg, Lipton onion soup mix, water, bread crumbs and ground meat.
Shape into patties.
Grill or broil until done.
Makes 8 servings.
Cream the butter; gradually add the sugar and beat 10 to 15 minutes at medium speed.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Strain green beans and artichoke hearts.
Cut or mash green beans into small pieces.
Cut artichoke into small pieces.
Mix all ingredients together, and place in casserole dish.
Sprinkle top with additional bread crumbs and dot with butter.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut dates in quarters and pour boiling water over them.
Add shortening, sugar and salt.
When cool, add beaten egg, flour sifted with soda and cream of tartar, nuts and vanilla.
Beat well.
Pour into greased and floured bread pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours.
Watch oven; do not get too hot.
Combine corn, eggs and milk.
Add crushed rusks and mix well. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix all together and bake for 40 minutes at 350°.
Combine ingredients in small saucepan; cook over medium heat until hot.
Serve with warm bread sticks and chips.
Makes 1 3/4 cups.
Wash peas and place in large pan with cold water.
Bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover and let sit for 1 hour.
Fry bacon slowly until brown, drain.
Add Tabasco sauce, bacon and salt to peas.
Bring to a boil, lower heat and simmer, stirring frequently for 30 minutes or until rice is tender. Should be moist, but not wet.
Makes 6 servings.
Scrub and peel potatoes; cut lengthwise into quarters.
Cut each quarter into 3 strips.
Roll in melted butter; then roll in combined remaining ingredients.
Place potato sticks in a single layer on a cookie sheet.
Drizzle melted butter over potatoes. Bake at 400° for 30 to 35 minutes or until potatoes are tender. Yield:
6 servings.

After popping corn, sift through to remove unpopped kernels. Melt caramels, water and butter together over medium-low heat, stirring constantly so it doesn't burn. When melted, pour over corn. Stir so it is well coated. Shape into balls and store in airtight containers.
Cook the drained sauerkraut for 5 minutes with the diced onions and 2 tablespoons butter.
Mix corned beef with relish and mustard.
Spread on slice of party bread.
Top with heaping tablespoonful of sauerkraut mixture and slice of Swiss cheese. Broil until cheese melts.
Serve as an appetizer.
In microwave, sprinkle gelatin over 1/4 cup cold water.
Let stand 1 minute to soften.
Microwave on high 20 seconds, stir; rotate cup 1/4 turn;
microwave high 20 seconds.
Prepare pudding with skim milk following package directions.
Add unflavored gelatin and vanilla to pudding, stir until blended.
Place 8 graham crackers in bottom of 11 X 7 inch dish.
Spread with 1/2 the pudding.
Place 1/2 the banana slices on pudding.
Repeat layers ending with bananas.
Refrigerate 4 hours.
To serve cut into 8 squares.
Top with 1 tub whipped topping.
Roll in balls, then dip in chocolate with 1/2 block to pack.
Beat egg whites and vanilla to soft peaks; gradually add sugar.
Beat until stiff peaks form.
Mix crumbs, nuts and baking powder; fold into beaten egg whites.
Spread evenly in greased and floured 9-inch pie plate.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes. Cool completely.
Whip the cream or use Cool Whip.
Cut pie. Serve topped with cream.
Serves 6.
Wash and core tomatoes.
Cut them up and put them through a juicer (should be about 6 quarts of juice).
Put juice in a large heavy kettle and add remaining ingredients.
Cook until thick and volume is reduced to about 1/2 the original measure.
Ladle into hot pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace.
Cover with lids and bands and process in a boiling water bath canner for 35 minutes. Makes 6 pints.
In a 10 x 13-inch pan, layer chopped lettuce, onion, celery, peas and chestnuts.
Spread on mayonnaise, covering all ingredients.
Sprinkle salt, pepper and sugar over top of mayonnaise.
Sprinkle Mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses over mayonnaise (Parmesan first).
Cover tightly with Saran Wrap or pan lid and refrigerate 24 hours.
When ready to serve, top with bacon and tomatoes.
Serves twelve.
Marinate seafood in soy sauce 15 minutes. While seafood is marinating, melt butter in saucepan. Add parsley and crushed garlic. Remove seafood from sauce.
Place in a shallow casserole or baking dish. Top with mushrooms, water chestnuts and bean sprouts.
Pour butter mixture on top.
Bake at 350° for about 25 minutes.
(Test shrimp for doneness.)
In 13 X 9 baking dish place both cans of corn.
Mix 2 eggs with corn bread mix. Set aside.
Saute onions.
Layer on top of corn.
Place corn bread mixture on top.
Drizzle melted butter over top and bake for 40 minutes at 400.
Mix egg substitute, salt and pepper.
Dip onion rings into egg mixture and coat with bread crumbs.
Place in single layer on greased baking sheet.
Bake 10 minutes at 450°.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine all ingredients in saucepan.
Cook until all is mixed well.
Butter 2 1/2-quart casserole dish and pour in.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Cut unpeeled zucchini into thin slices and boil until tender but still crunchy.
Drain thoroughly.
Melt cheese and butter and mix with garlic powder and zucchini.
Put in a baking dish and crumble crackers on top.
Bake for 25 minutes in 350° oven until golden brown.
Serves 6.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Brown beef, drain and add taco seasoning mix along with the water, and cheese. Place crescent rolls in a ring around a large round stone with the pointed end facing right overlapping each other then place meat mixture in the center of the crescent rolls. Take the end of each crescent roll and wrap around the other end until circle so complete. Bake in the oven until the rolls become golden brown, about 10 minutes. Use the rest of the ingredients to garnish with.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda, salt and sugar; add 3/4 cup shortening, brown sugar and buttermilk.
Add bananas, eggs and vanilla; beat for 1 minute.
Fold in 3/4 cup chopped pecans dusted with flour.
Bake in a tube pan.
Make a thick paste of confectioners sugar and enough sour cream to dribble over cake for frosting.
Bake chicken breasts topped with margarine at 400° for 1 hour and 15 minutes, turning every 15 minutes.
Pour off margarine and chicken fat.
Cover chicken with half the barbecue sauce and bake 30 minutes.
Turn and cover other side and bake 30 minutes.
Bake cake in three layers. Place 1 in bottom of bowl.
Mix pudding mix and place 1/3 on cake layer.
Top with blueberry filling.
Mix pecans with Cool Whip.
Put 1/3 on top.
Place second layer cake.
Add drained pineapple, 1/3 of pudding mix and 1/3 of Cool Whip.
Put third layer with rest of pudding mix, strawberry mix and Cool Whip.
Mix cranberries, apples and sugar.
Melt margarine.
Add Rice Krispies, brown sugar and flour.
Fold into cranberry mixture. Sprinkle with nuts over the top.
Bake in a large buttered casserole (9 x 13-inch), uncovered, for 45 minutes or until thickened and bubbly, at 350°.
Serves 8 to 10 people.
Beat eggs well.
Add sugar and vinegar.
Cook over boiling water until thick.
Cool slightly.
Beat in cheese.
Grate in green pepper and onion.
Add pecans.
Let season 2 hours.
Good for potato chips or Fritos.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix potatoes, sauce mix and water in ungreased 2-quart round casserole; stir in milk.
Bake, uncovered, 30 to 35 minutes or until top is golden brown and potatoes are tender.
Heat oven to 350°.

Measure butter, shortening, 2 cups sugar, egg, liqueur, almond extract and 2 cups flour into a large mixer bowl. Blend 1/2 minute on low speed, scraping bowl constantly. Beat 1 minute on medium speed, scraping the bowl occasionally. Stir in remaining flour.
Knead until smooth. Shape 1-inch pieces of dough into crescent shapes.
Place 1-inch apart on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake until cookies are light brown on bottoms, 15 to 20 minutes. Sprinkle powdered sugar on cookies while hot.
Cool on wire racks. Flavor mellows after 2 or 3 days. Store cookies in airtight containers at room temperature no longer than 9 days or in freezer no longer than 2 months.
Makes about 11 dozen.
Cream sugar and margarine.
Beat eggs, one at a time, into mixture.
Add additional ingredients.
Combine broccoli, onions, cheese, sunflower seeds and bacon. Mix mayo, sugar and vinegar.
Stir in broccoli mix.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all with electric mixer well.
Chill and enjoy.
In large skillet, saute onion and pepper in oil until tender. Add remaining ingredients and cook over medium heat 15 minutes. Stir frequently.
Serve immediately.
Yields 8 servings.
Drain juice from pineapple and add enough water to make 2 cups of liquid.
Heat this and add jello.
Dissolve.
While still hot, add marshmallows; cool.
Add cottage cheese, pineapple, nuts and cherries.
Whip cream and fold other ingredients into this.
Chill until firm.
Cut rind off ham.
Combine dry ingredients and add enough juice to make a dough that can be rolled over fat.
Cover part of ham with dough.
Put in cold oven.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes per pound, 4 or 5 hours for a 15 pound ham, basting every 30 minutes.
Take dough off and finish with brown sugar or any favorite way of browning ham.
Cook zucchini in boiling water until just tender.
Drain.
In large bowl, beat eggs.
Stir in mayonnaise, onions, green pepper, cheese, salt and pepper.
Add zucchini; toss.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Dot with butter and sprinkle with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Serves 6.
Soften cream cheese.
Add all ingredients.
Bake 30 minutes at 350° or 5 minutes in microwave.

In large bowl, combine cake mix, eggs, orange juice, oil and pudding mix. Blend at low speed of electric mixer 1 minute, then high speed 3 minutes. Pour 2/3 of batter in nonstick (Pam sprayed) pan or greased and floured Bundt pan. To remaining 1/3 of batter, add chocolate and blend.
Pour over top of batter in pan. Marbelize with knife. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until cake tests done. Cool in pan 10 minutes, then turn out onto plate to cool completely. Glaze if desired.
Mix all ingredients together.
Beat well.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes.
Butter pie plate (10-inch Pyrex).
Cook rice and set aside.
Melt butter in skillet, add onion and broccoli.
Simmer until onion is transparent and broccoli is tender.
Add soup, Cheez Whiz and milk.
Mix well and remove from heat.
Add rice.
Bake in buttered pan, covered, for 30 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients.
Chill until ready to serve.
Serve with crackers.
Put all in blender and mix. Put corn in last.
Blend it very little.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes until knife comes out clean.
Melt butter in heavy covered skillet.
Brown chicken on both sides.
Remove chicken and drain excess fat.
Stir in soup and loose pan drippings.
Add sour cream, stirring until well mixed. Add chicken.
Cover and simmer over very low heat until tender, about 50 to 60 minutes.
Stir in mushrooms last couple of minutes. Serve over pasta or rice.
Brown hamburger meat with chopped onion; drain grease.
Tear tortillas and place in 13 x 9-inch dish.
Heat soup and tomatoes. Layer tortillas, meat, beans and soup mixture.
Continue layering until all is used up.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake in 350° oven until bubbly.
Prepare lemonade concentrate with water according to the directions on the can.
Add chilled cranberry juice cocktail and ginger ale.
Add ice and mix well.
Float scoops of sherbet on top.
Serve as is or over ice cubes, if desired.
Yields 25 (6 ounce) cups.
Beat until smooth.
Pour into 3 cake pans.
Bake at 325° until done.
Using palm of hand, flatten chicken to even thickness.
Dip chicken into egg, then into crumbs to coat.
In skillet, over medium heat, in hot margarine, brown chicken on both sides.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Reduce heat.
Cover.
Simmer 10 minutes. Sprinkle with cheeses and parsley.
Cover.
Simmer 5 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.
Fry chicken (which has been skinned), coated with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.
Put fried chicken in large pan with 1/2 cup of frying oil.
Add olives, mushrooms and peppers to chicken.
Add 1/2 cup wine for flavor.
Cook for at least 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with rice.
Drain tomatoes, reserving 1 tablespoon oil.
In food processor, place oil, tomatoes, cheese and garlic.
Process until well blended, stopping once to scrape down sides.
Serve with pita chips or bagel chips.
Also good with raw vegetables.

Beat together eggs and milk. Stir in hash browns, onion, salt and hot pepper sauce. Stir in 1 cup of the cheese and half of the bacon. Pour into a greased 9-inch pie plate or quiche dish. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes until center is set. Sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon over the top. Continue to bake 3 to 4 minutes until cheese is melted.
Beat eggs slightly in mixing bowl.
Add other ingredients. Cover bottom of a 6-inch skillet with peanut oil and heat skillet. Pour 1/4 of the mixture in this and cook over low heat until brown on one side.
Turn carefully and cook until brown on other side.
Serve with Brown Sauce.
In large saucepan, melt peanut butter, 1 cup of sweetened condensed milk and 2 tablespoons butter; stir occasionally. Remove from heat; stir in peanuts.
Spread mixture into wax paper-lined 8 x 8-inch pan.
If necessary, singe and clean the goose.
Pat dry.
Rub the cavity with salt.
Combine the other ingredients and stuff into the goose.
Secure the opening with skewers and truss.
Prick the skin thoroughly with a fork so that fat will run out.
Put goose on rack in a roasting pan, breast side up.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Roast in 350° oven for 3 1/2 hours.
At the end of one hour, add a cup of water to the pan and baste every half hour with the drippings.
Serves 8.
Season the ground beef according to your family preference. I use black pepper, seasoning salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. Put all ingredients into a skillet, stir and heat.
Combine popcorn, pretzels and cereals in a large pan or Dutch oven that has been sprayed with a nonfat cooking spray. Combine sugar, Butter Buds, syrup
and lite salt in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil and boil 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Quickly stir in baking soda.
Pour over popcorn mixture and stir together quickly.
Mix until well coated. Spread on 4 cookie sheets that have been lined with foil and sprayed with a nonfat cooking spray. Bake at 250° for 30 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool until hardened.
When cool and hardened, break apart and store in an airtight container.
Stir together cocoa and boiling water in small bowl until smooth; set aside.
Cream butter, sugar and vanilla in large mixer bowl.
Blend in eggs.
Combine flour, soda and salt.
Add alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture.
Blend in reserved cocoa mixture.
Mix 2 whole eggs with milk, sugar and cornstarch.
Mix cold and cook until thick (like a pudding).
Stir constantly to avoid lumps.
Cool.

Beat egg whites with cream of tartar until stiff. Add sugar, vanilla and nuts. Pour into an 8-inch greased pie pan. Mold sides up to form a pie shell. Bake at 300° for 35 minutes. Melt chocolate in water and cool. Beat whipping cream until thick. Mix vanilla into cooled chocolate and fold together with whipped cream. Pour into cooled meringue pie shell. Chill.
Melt cheeses and oleo.
Add half and half.
Add salt; put frozen potatoes in a large casserole.
Pour cheese mixture over the potatoes.
Let set 1 hour.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Peel potatoes; boil until soft.
Mash with butter and sour cream.
Add green onions and salt; blend until potatoes are fluffy.
Put into a casserole dish; sprinkle with more of the salt to taste, if desired.
Add slices of Velveeta cheese to cover top. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients except crackers and cheese and put in a casserole dish.
Sprinkle combined crackers and cheese on top. Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt 1/2 stick oleo in casserole dish.
Mix well all ingredients.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes or until brown.
Beat eggs with a fork.
Add vanilla, sugar and flour, beating with a fork.
Add the date mixture, mixing just to blend.
Pour into a greased loaf pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour or until done.
Thoroughly blend peanut butter and honey.
Stir in 1/2 c. Corn Flake crumbs.
Form into 24 small balls and roll in remaining Corn Flake crumbs.
Chill.
Combine smoked ham, fresh pork, eggs and bread or cracker crumbs and form into loaf.
Place in roasting pan.
Make sauce of remaining ingredients and pour over loaf.
Bake in 350° oven about an hour, or until done.
Place all ingredients on crust then fold and seal.
Dot with butter and make three slits in crust to allow the steam to escape. Bake in center rack at 400° for 1 hour.
Serve with brown gravy or catsup.
In a blender, puree the watermelon pieces and strain the puree through a very fine sieve set over a pitcher, discarding the solids.
(There should be about 2 1/2 cups juice.)
Stir in the vodka, the Triple Sec and the lime juice; pour the cooler into long-stemmed glasses filled with ice and garnish each drink with a watermelon slice.
Makes 4 to 6 drinks.
Combine all ingredients, except tortillas.
Spread tortillas with mixture, almost to end, and roll up.
Slice into 2-inch lengths.
Cut the broccoli into small bite-sized pieces.
Cut cauliflower into bite-sized pieces.
Add onion and cheese.
Add dressing (*), then bacon bits last, and toss.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Place in an oiled 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Serve with lemon wedge or tomato sauce.
Yield:
6 servings.
Approximate calories/serving:
Coat veal with flour.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add veal; cook about 2 minutes on each side or until lightly browned.
Add apples and pecans.
Cook and stir until apples are tender-crisp.
Add honey and brown sugar.
Cook and stir until warm.
Can serve on large croutons by cutting out white bread with large cookie cutter, sprinkle with salt and pepper and bake on cookie sheet 10 minutes at 350°.
Put all the ingredients except the sour cream in electric mixer container.
Mix on low speed 5 to 7 minutes until sugar has dissolved completely and emulsifed.
Add sour cream and mix 1 more minute.
Chill. Serve with whole berries for garnish.
Makes 6 servings.
Dissolve Jell-O in 2 cups hot water.
Stir well.
Add cold water, salt and vinegar.
Stir.
Cool to jellied stage.
Stir in horseradish and whipped cream.
Pour into an oiled mold.
When thoroughly set, unmold.
Garnish with parsley leaflets.
Excellent with ham.
Beat eggs in separate bowl.
Take first 4 ingredients and place onto counter top lined with wax paper.
Take a rolling pin and roll ingredients into a crumblike mixture.
Cover all pieces of fish in egg mixture and then cover fish with crumb mixture to create batter taste.
Cook fish in skillet of oil for 6 minutes. Serves 3 to 4 people.
Very tasty!
Mix all, except chips.
Let the mixture soak together for 10 minutes, then press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with crushed potato chips, then bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Chop basil leaves.
Mince garlic.
Shred cheese.
Drop tomatoes in boiling water for about 10 seconds.
Peel and chop tomatoes. Mix tomatoes, basil, garlic and cheese with oil; let stand in covered bowl at room temperature for at least 3 hours.
Cook pasta and drain.
Add tomatoes to hot pasta and mix well.
Serve warm.
Heat oven to 325°.
Beat the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla together.
Place the bread pieces in a buttered baking dish (approximately 8 x 1 1/2-inches round).
Pour milk mixture over the bread.
Sprinkle on the raisins.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until a knife inserted comes out clean.
Sift together flour, baking soda and salt; set aside.
In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks, one a a time, beating well after each.
At low speed, gradually beat in yogurt, milk and vanilla.
Gradually add dry ingredients; beating until fluffy.
Scrape bowl as needed.
Stir in chopped walnuts.
Mix butter and mustard; then spread on one side of each slice of bread.
Cut bread into cubes.
Beat remaining ingredients with wire whisk until uniform.
Stir in bread cubes.
Pour into a well greased baking dish.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Cream sugar and shortening.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients.
Bake	until
light and brown, 10 minutes at 325°.
Cook broccoli in water until cooked.
Melt butter to liquid. Beat eggs.
Add all the ingredients together, stir it thoroughly. Bake at 350° in any baking pan until top is browned and casserole is lightly moist.
Trim bone and fat from steak and cut into 1-inch strips.
Brown steak in oil in skillet on top of stove.
Mix steak and all other ingredients in a covered casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Serves 8.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Stir in cheese and onion.
Spoon into a 1-quart souffle dish.
Bake at 325° for 25 minutes or until puffed and golden.
Serve immediately with crackers.
Makes 3 cups.
In a large pan or Dutch oven, place oil, ground turkey, chili powder, salt and pepper.
On medium heat, stirring often, cook until meat has changed color.
Add tomato juice, picante sauce and pork and beans.
Simmer for 2 hours.
Put ice cream and sherbet in punch bowl.
Pour juice and ginger ale over it and mix.
Serves 24.
Core cabbage and put in plastic bag; cook in microwave for approximately 25 minutes (if not fully cooked, put in for approximately 5 minutes more).
Let cool.
In microwave dish, prepare rice according to instructions on package; let cool.
Take sauce and put about 1 inch on bottom of lasagna dish.
Separate cabbage leaves, pulling off one at a time.
Take 1 loaf of cabbage.
Spread out and put on 1 large spoon of rice and 1 teaspoon of sour cream.
Flop in sides and roll.
Do this until all leaves are rolled and place them in the dish with sauce. Cover them with the rest of the sauce.
Sprinkle cheeses on top and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Mix ingredients in large pot.
Heat on medium heat until mixture is hot (do not boil).
Serve hot.
Leftover juice can be refrigerated and reheated.
Cream butter and shortening; add sugar.
Cream until fluffy. Add eggs one at a time and beat well after each.
Sift flour and baking powder; add a little at a time with milk.
Stir in flavoring.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add milk to eggs.
Add sifted dry ingredients.
Add currants.
Mix and chill.
Mix jello and boiling water.
Add pineapple.
Let congeal a little then add pie filling and pecans.
Crumble and saute sausage.
Remove sausage from skillet.
Keep tablespoon of drippings.
Add squash and onion, saute.
Add all other ingredients and 1/2 cup water.
Put sausage on top.
Cover. Cook for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine raisins, fruit and water in saucepan.
Cook, uncovered, until water is evaporated and fruit is soft.
Set aside to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, baking soda, salt, nutmeg and cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, combine eggs, applesauce, sweetener, oil and vanilla.
Add nuts to fruit mixture.
Stir into dry ingredients and blend thoroughly. Pour into greased fluted tube pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes or until cake tests done.
Layer in clear glass bowl.
Brown meat, drain grease.
Add onion and cook till onion almost done.
Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer on medium to low heat until done.
Fill cupcakes 3/4 full of batter.
Mix egg, cream cheese, sugar and chocolate chips in middle of batter.
Sprinkle with nuts and sugar over top.
Bake as directed on cake box.
Cook macaroni, rinse in cold water and drain in colander. Dice olives, pimiento and onion.
Toss in salad bowl.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add mayonnaise to moisten.
Cut up cooked chicken.
Mix all ingredients together, except Miracle Whip.
Refrigerate.
Spread in pan.	Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix bacon with chipped ham, chili sauce and relish.
Put a tablespoon of ham mixture on a sliced burger bun.
Top with a slice of cheese.
Close bun and wrap in foil.
Heat 20 minutes in 350° oven.

recipes.t: Bread Pudding With Apples And Raisins
d: Beat together eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and salt. In a round baking dish, add bread, apples and raisins.
Pour egg mixture over all.
Bake in 325° oven for 40 to 60 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean.
For a change, add the melted butter and sugar on bottom of dish.
Make bread pudding with apples and raisins as directed.
Cool.
Turn dish upside down over another dish.
The pudding will have a caramel type topping. Serve with whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Enjoy.
Cook potatoes until done. Add celery, onions and eggs. Mix mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar and sugar. Toss over potatoes. Garnish with paprika.
Stir into drained meat the beans, and taco sauce.
Heat. Layer:
meat mixture, sharp grated Cheddar cheese, 1 cup sour cream, chopped onion, olives, tomatoes and green peppers.
Mix together and press on a cookie sheet.
Chill overnight or put into freezer until firm.
Cut into 4-inch squares.
Roll in flour and brown on both sides in hot oil.
Place pieces in a baking dish.
Cover with 1 can mushroom soup and 1 can water mixed.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix ingredients and stuff in manicotti shells which have been boiled for 10 minutes.
Pour spaghetti sauce over and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook macaroni; drain.
Combine first 6 ingredients with 1 cup mayonnaise, sour cream and 1/2 cup milk.
Blend well.
Add macaroni and toss.
Refrigerate, covered, several hours.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Stir into salad.
Soften cream cheese and mix with the dried beef and horseradish. This is great on pumpernickel bread.
Sprinkle half of stuffing over bottom of 10 x 13-inch casserole.
Layer rest in order given.
Blend soup and milk, pour over top.
Moisten remaining stuffing with melted butter and water, put on top.
Bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until hot.
Cut cucumbers into sticks.
Pour boiling water over and let stand overnight.
Next day, drain.
Pack solidly into jars.

recipes.t: Caribbean Fudge Pie(Kraft General Foods, Inc.)
d: Preheat oven to 375°.
Beat butter and sugar in large bowl until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add chocolate (melt in microwave or in double boiler), instant coffee and rum extract.
Mix well.
Stir in flour and 1 cup chopped walnuts.
Pour into unbaked pie shell. Decorate top with 1/2 cup walnut halves.
Bake in lower third of oven for 25 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Top with whipped cream or ice cream. Serves 8 to 10.
Mix all dressing ingredients and pour over lettuce.
Add croutons and stir once more.
Use Parmesan cheese before serving, if desired.
Grease and flour one loaf pan.
Mix ingredients and bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Saute the onion and zucchini in margarine until tender.
Add broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Pour into blender, 1/3 at a time, and whip until smooth. Add milk, dill, salt and pepper.
Clean and cook whole green beans.
Place them in a sterile pint jar.
Boil the water, vinegar, sugar and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Pour over beans and seal jar.
You may double recipe.
Heat rhubarb with sugar until soft.
Add Jell-O and stir.
Add pineapple juice and lemon juice. Refrigerate until partially set. Add the rest of the ingredients and refrigerate again until completely set.
Melt margarine in a 9 x 12-inch pan.
Pour cracker crumbs over margarine and spread.
Pour coconut on top and spread.
Pour chips on top and spread.
Pour nuts on top and spread.
Pour Eagle Brand milk over top and bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Let cool before cutting in squares.
Combine all ingredients except stuffing.
Sprinkle stuffing over top.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until it begins to bubble.
Break up biscuits in a lightly greased or buttered dish.
Beat eggs.
Add other ingredients.
Pour in dish.
Bake at 350° for about 35 or 40 minutes or until lightly brown.
Brown flour and onions in butter.
Add about 2 cups broth and simmer.
Use layer of chicken, then a layer of vegetables.
Pour 1/2 of the gravy over the chicken and vegetables.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Pull biscuits apart and place on top of cheese. Pour remainder gravy over the biscuits.
Bake until biscuits are browned, about 30 minutes at 375°.
Fill slow cooker with meatballs. Combine sauce and jam. Pour over meatballs. Cover. Cook on low 4 hours, stirring occasionally.
Mix all ingredients in jar and shake well. Store and keep indefinitely.
Good on chicken, beef and pork.
Combine butter and water; stir until butter melts.
Pour over seasoned stuffing crumbs; toss lightly.
Stir in 1/2 can French fried onions.
Spoon stuffing mixture into a 9-inch shallow baking dish (1 1/2-quart) or pie plate.
Press stuffing across bottom and up sides of dish to form a shell.
Mix condensed celery soup, milk, turkey and peas together, then spoon into prepared baking dish. Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining onions and bake, uncovered, for 5 more minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix well and spoon into shaker.
Makes 1/3 cup.
Recipe from Hills and Pines Garden Club, Raleigh, North Carolina.
Saute onion and celery in margarine in a Dutch oven until tender.
Add flour and cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually add milk, stirring until mixture boils.
Stir in corn and next 3 ingredients.
Reduce heat; simmer 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spoon into bowls; sprinkle with paprika.
Yield:
3 servings.
Mix and cook, stirring constantly over medium heat until thick.
Put in a 9-inch unbaked pie shell with lattice top.
Bake for 40 minutes at 400° or until done.

Fry tortillas until lightly fried, not crisp, in oil and dry, using paper towels. In a separate container, put cheese. Set aside. Mix together remaining ingredients in another large mixing bowl. Separately fill each tortilla with a small amount of "mix" and a small amount of grated cheese. Place "bed-fellow" style in a large baking dish. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.

Combine cream cheese and peanut butter in a large mixing bowl; beat at medium speed of electric mixer until light and fluffy. Gradually add whipped topping and powdered sugar and continue beating until smooth.
Spoon filling into prepared crusts.
Freeze at least 8 hours or overnight.
Garnish with chocolate shavings, if desired.
Makes two 9-inch pies.
Soften yeast in warm water.
Mash potatoes while hot, then cool. Add potato water, scalded and cooled milk, salt, sugar and melted shortening to potatoes. Add softened yeast, then stir in flour.
Mix thoroughly, using only enough flour to make a stiff, kneadable dough.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Place in lightly greased bowl. Cover and let rise until doubled in bulk. Punch down and let rise again for about 1 hour.
Shape into 2 loaves.
Let rise in greased bread pans.
Bake in hot oven at 400° for about 50 to 60 minutes or until done.
Turn bread out onto racks to cool.
Makes 2 loaves.
Mix all ingredients well.
Shape into balls.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Serve with sour cream, if desired.
Makes approximately 40 (3-inch) balls.
Cream sugar and butter and add sifted dry ingredients.
Add milk, eggs and apples.
Pour in a bottom oil and floured 9x12 pan.
Mix sugar, corn syrup and vinegar in saucepan.
Cover tightly; bring to a boil.
Uncover; place a candy thermometer in the pan. Without stirring, cook over medium heat to 300°.
Gradually lower heat as mixture thickens to prevent scorching.
Remove from heat; quickly stir in the baking soda and vanilla.
Turn into a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Do not spread; candy will spread itself.
Cool; break into pieces.
Cream Crisco and sugar; add eggs, 1 cup flour with baking powder and salt.
Add vanilla; beat well.
Cut fruit and nuts. Sprinkle the other cup flour over fruit and nuts.
Pour batter over fruit and nuts.
Mix with hands.
Line pan with heavy brown paper (grocery bag works fine).
Put in cold oven and bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Reduce heat to 250° and bake for 2 1/2 hours. Place pan of water under cake while cooking.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix meat, rice, water, onion, salts, garlic powder and pepper.
Shape mixture by rounded tablespoons into balls.
Place meatballs in ungreased baking dish 8 x 8 x 2-inches.
Stir together remaining ingredients; pour over meatballs.
Cover with aluminum foil; bake 45 minutes.
Uncover, bake 15 minutes longer.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Frosting:
Grate peel and squeeze juice from lemon; mix confectioners sugar and add juice.
Boil sugar, syrup and water until it spins a thread.
Then add peanuts and stir continually.
After peanuts are added, cook until it turns a light yellow.
Remove from heat.
Add soda, salt and butter.
Spread thin on buttered cookie sheet.
Break into pieces.
Cut four thin lemon slices; squeeze 2 teaspoons juice from remaining lemon.
Set aside.
In skillet, in hot oil, cook chicken 10 minutes or until browned.
Remove; set aside.
Spoon off fat. In skillet, combine soup, milk, reserved lemon juice and pepper. Heat to boiling.
Return chicken to skillet; top with lemon slices. Cover; cook over low heat 5 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink, stirring often.
Garnish with fresh thyme if desired.
Saute onion and garlic in margarine in small skillet; add paprika.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Roll in onion mixture.
Arrange in 11 x 15-inch casserole.
Spoon remaining onion mixture over chicken.
Bake, covered, at 375° for 40 minutes.
Stir in all ingredients except milk until moist and smooth, then add milk.
On medium heat, cook until thick and boiling.
In large bowl, put in alternating layers of vanilla wafers and bananas and pudding.
Layer potatoes, celery, ground hamburg steak, green pepper, onions and tomatoes.
Sprinkle on each layer separately:
2 teaspoons of salt and 1 teaspoon pepper.
Dot with butter.
Cover. Bake for 2 hours in moderate oven at 350°.
Cook celery and pepper in chicken broth.
Put noodles and all other ingredients in pan.
Add some grated cheese on top.
Cook in oven at 350° for 30 minutes or until cheese is golden brown.
Icing: Bring sugar and water to a boil. Continue
boiling until mixture spins a thread and remove from heat. Beat egg whites while sugar mixture cooks. Egg whites
will form a peak. Add vanilla and heated sugar mixture to egg whites. Mix well.
Add sugar, chocolate and milk together and bring to a boil. Add peanut butter and stir until melted.
Remove from heat and add oatmeal.
If mixture seems too dry add a little more milk.
Drop by spoonful on wax paper and refrigerate until cookies have hardened.
Blend cream cheese and 1/2 cup butter.
Stir in flour and chill 1 hour.
Heat oven to 325°.
Roll dough into 24 (1-inch) balls and press into 1 1/2-inch muffin tins.
Beat egg, brown sugar, 1 tablespoon butter, vanilla and salt together.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup pecans on dough in tins.
Add egg mixture and sprinkle with remaining nuts.
Bake at 325° about 25 minutes or until set.
Cool in pans.
Makes 24 tarts.
Pour 2 cups
hot water over bran and let it stand while mixing muffins.	 Mix
wet
ingredients	together.
Add	wet ingredients to dry ingredients.
Add soaked bran and mix well. Store in
refrigerator.
Will
keep
weeks. Bake at 350° in oiled muffin tins
or
cup	cases,	15
to 20 minutes.
Do not overcook.
Yields 6 dozen.
Drain beans and sprinkle with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Mix all ingredients together with 1/2 cup salad dressing.
Add all ingredients in serving bowl and mix well.
In Dutch oven or heavy saucepan, heat shortening and brown meat well.
Stir in Lipton onion soup mix, tomato paste and water. Simmer, covered, 1 1/2 hours or until meat is tender, adding more water, if needed.
Serve over noodles.
Crush graham crackers in a medium size bowl.
Add sugar and margarine;	mix well.
Spread in bottom of large cake pan, evenly. Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven and cool.
Toss together all ingredients.
Serve with your favorite no or low-fat dressing.
Makes 6 cups.
Brown hamburger and Italian sausage.
Squeeze sausages out of skins.
Add seasonings.
