Add tomato sauce, paste and water; stir. Simmer, uncovered, for 3/4 hour.
Make enough pasta to serve 6 to 8.
Make crust with first two ingredients.
Crush crackers fine; add to softened stick of margarine.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan and refrigerate.
With electric mixer beat next 4 ingredients for 20 minutes.
Must be 20 minutes!
Pour over crust.
Prepare Dream Whip according to package directions.
Fold in well drained crushed pineapple and sliced bananas.
Spread evenly over top. Keep refrigerated.
Mix all ingredients together using broth from boiled chicken. Cook until light brown on top. Serve with cranberry sauce or giblet gravy.
(I suggest you double this recipe.
I make 2 or more at a time. They don't last long.)
Put all ingredients in a 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Cover; bake in a 350° oven for about 45 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix ingredients together, except corn flakes and 1/2 cup melted butter.
Pour into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
May be prepared the night before and refrigerated.
Arrange potatoes in pan.
Mix eggs, milk, 1/3 stick butter, white sugar, vanilla and orange juice; pour over potatoes. Combine brown sugar, flour, 1/3 stick butter and pecans.
Sprinkle over potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cook onion in a little oil until tender, but not brown.
Add tomatoes, zucchini and salt and pepper to taste.
Cook slowly, adding small amount of water if needed.
Add bay leaf, if desired.
Put a little olive oil in bottom of pan.
Brown onion and garlic.
Add both cans of tomatoes and sugar.
Top with oregano, black pepper and salt to taste.
Simmer 1 to 2 hours.
Use a 3-quart baking dish.
Stew chicken, cool and debone. Reserve 2 cups of broth.
Combine soups with 1 cup of broth.
Pour over chicken.
Mix melted butter with second cup of broth and mix in stuffing.
Spoon over chicken.
Cook at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until brown.
Brown onion in cooking oil and add ground beef, chili powder, tomato sauce, corn and olives.
Place in mixing bowl and add 1 1/2 cups milk and 1 cup corn meal.
Place in a greased baking dish and top with 1/2 pound grated Cheddar cheese.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes at 350°.
Heat first 6 ingredients until milk is scalding.
Stir in potatoes.
Cook until smooth, stirring constantly.
Mash avocados.
Peel tomato and dice to fine pieces.
Chop onion into fine pieces.
Mix these together and add salt and very finely chopped jalapeno peppers to taste.
Sprinkle lemon juice over top of mixture.
This helps it from turning brown.
Chill and serve.
In large bowl combine undrained pineapple chunks, undrained mandarin orange sections and undrained fruit cocktail with the flaked coconut and lemon juice.
Sprinkle the instant lemon pudding mix over the fruits and toss lightly to combine.
Chill. Just before serving, peel and slice bananas; fold into fruit mixture.
Serve in dessert dishes; top with approximately 2 1/2 tablespoons Cool Whip.
If desired garnish with tiny bit of grated lemon or grated orange peel.
Serves 9.
Cream butter, sugar, salt and flour.
Add egg yolks and lemon juice; beat until fluffy.
Stir in milk.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites with a wire whisk, gently, until well blended.
Cream butter, honey and molasses; add egg.
Sift dry ingredients.
Mix together.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 375°.
Scrape filling off 1 roll Oreos; crush and save.
Mix pudding, milk and cream cheese in mixer.
Stir in Cool Whip.
Crush 2 rolls Oreos, and stir into mixture along with filling from first roll. Spoon into plant pot.
Sprinkle crumbs from first roll on top. Cover and refrigerate.
Place flower in pot when ready to serve.
Mix and bake at 400° for 40 minutes.
Mix oil, eggs, sugar and vanilla together.
Sift together flour, soda, cinnamon and salt.
Mix well into egg mixture. Blend in apples and nuts.
Pour into a greased and floured tube pan.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
If necessary, remove casing from bacon.
Place bacon, fat side up, in ungreased baking dish.
Stir together pineapple (with syrup), honey, ginger and water.
Pour over bacon.
Roast, uncovered, for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Baste occasionally.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Wash peppers and drain well.
Place peppers on cookie sheet and bake about 20 minutes or until the skin of the peppers become blistered and charred.
Turn the peppers every 5 minutes with tongs.
Place hot peppers in a large kettle; cover kettle and let them stand 15 minutes.
Peel off charred skin with sharp knife.
Cut each pepper into quarters.
Remove the ribs and seeds and cut out any dark spots.
In large bowl, combine oil, lemon juice, salt and garlic.
Put the pepper mixture, with or without anchovy fillets, into a 1-quart dish or jar, covered. Refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Serve as an appetizer, a side dish or use in a tossed salad.
Makes 1 quart.
Excellent with lasagne or other Italian meals.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Beat eggs; add oil, sugar and vanilla.
Mix well, then add zucchini and pineapple.
Add dry ingredients.
Pour into loaf pans.
Bake at 325° for 50 minutes. Makes 2 loaves.
Combine cheese spread, seasonings, butter, mayonnaise and crab meat in bowl; mix well.
Spread on muffin halves.
Freeze just until firm.
Cut into quarters.
Store, wrapped, in freezer. Preheat oven to 350°.
Place on baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.
Strain all fruit and cut up in small pieces.
In a large bowl, place all strained and cut fruit.
Add sour cream and mix thoroughly.
Add miniature marshmallows and mix.
Combine the first 5 ingredients.
Add remaining ingredients. Bake in 2 loaf pans lightly greased at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Select a melon that has a thick rind.
Remove outer green skin and pink flesh; use only the greenish white part of the rind.
Cut rind into 1 inch cubes. combine rind and cold water; soak overnight in refrigerator.
Drain; cover with water and boil 30 minutes. Drain.

For basting sauce, saut onions and celery in the butter until soft. Add tomato puree, vinegar and molasses. Blend well. Place meat on a roasting rack in pan. Brush with part of the sauce. Bake at 350° for about 1 1/2 hours or until pork is tender and juices run clear when pierced with a fork. Do brush the pork from time to time during cooking for best flavor. Cooking time depends on thickness of meat. Makes 4 servings.
Beat eggs lightly in a large mixing bowl.
Add sugar, oil and vanilla.
Beat until creamy.
In another bowl combine flour, baking soda, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and nuts; set aside. Add zucchini and pineapple to egg and sugar mixture.
Add dry ingredients, stirring only until dry ingredients are moistened. Spoon batter into 2 well-greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine margarine with brown sugar.
Add cornflakes and pecans.
Sprinkle over the cooked mixture.
Place maraschino cherries over top and return to oven for about 10 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, well beaten.
Add flour with baking powder.
Sift in.
Add milk and soda mixture.
Add 4 mashed bananas and vanilla.
Bake at 350°.
Do not grease pan.
In a shallow baking dish, combine all ingredients except for shrimp.
Cook, uncovered, in microwave at High for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring twice.
Stir shrimp into butter sauce.
Cover.
Microwave at High for 5 to 7 1/2 minutes or until shrimp are opaque.
Let stand, covered, for 3 to 5 minutes before serving.
Beat cheese and apple juice in small mixing bowl until smooth. Cover and chill at serving time.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Serve with fruit dippers.
Makes 1 1/3 cups.
Mix all dry ingredients and apples by hand in large bowl until apples are well coated.
Combine with wet ingredients.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 1 hour, or until toothpick comes out clean, at 350° (may be less than 1 hour).
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Good with
whipped cream or ice cream.

In a medium sized saucepan, mix the 1 cup sugar, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and cornstarch. Beat in the egg yolks and then the sour cream and raisins. Cook over low heat about 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until well thickened. (Mix will thin on heating and then thicken again.) Remove from heat and cool 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to
Melt
butter in a shallow 1 1/2 quart baking dish.
Combine
flour,
1/4 cup sugar and milk in mixing bowl;
stir
to
blend.
Pour batter evenly over melted butter. Stir together
berries,
remaining
1/2 cup sugar and water; spoon evenly over batter.
Do not stir.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes or until golden brown and bubbly.
In a large crock-pot, add the ingredients.
Cook on low 2 hours before serving.
Serve with chips.
Mix
hamburger,
onions,
bell	pepper,
eggs,	cracker crumbs, potatoes,
salt
and
pepper.
Mix	2/3
can of tomato sauce. Bake
for approximately 1 1/2 or 2 hours at 350°.
When done, take out of skillet. Add 1 1/2 cups of water and 1/3 can of tomato sauce.
Thicken with flour for gravy.
In a bowl, cream sugar and butter.
Add the eggs and banana and mix together.
Sift together the flour, salt and soda.
Combine with the creamed mixture; add walnuts and mix again.
Pour into 2 greased and papered loaf pans.
Bake 1 hour in a 375° oven.
Line bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan with graham crackers.
Mix 2 packages jello pudding mix with 3 1/2 cups milk.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Spread 1/2 jello mixture over graham crackers.
Top with another layer graham crackers and spread other half of jello pudding mixture over that.
Cool in refrigerator at least 2 hours. Do not cover pan with Saran Wrap or waxed paper.
Spread frosting over top and refrigerate.
Should be made at least 24 hours ahead of time.
In punch bowl, combine cider, ReaLemon and sugar.
Stir until sugar dissolves.
Chill.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
When mixed well enough to work with, add cheese.
Knead this and put on floured board.
Roll out and cut biscuits.
I melt some margarine in my pan and see that top and bottom of biscuits have margarine on them.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes or until brown.
Saute celery and onions in margarine.
In a separate pan, cook broccoli according to directions; set aside.
Cook rice.
Combine soup, water chestnuts, Cheez Whiz, rice, celery and onions until the cheese melts.
Add broccoli and pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Set cheese out until soft; add garlic powder, red pepper and pecans.
Mix well with hands.
Roll into two rolls.
Sprinkle with chili powder.
Refrigerate; slice when cool.
Make jello and mix but substitute 1 pint of sour cream for 1 cup of water.
(Beat some cream with some jello to avoid curdling) and then add 1 can crushed pineapple, drained.
Let set and unmold.
May garnish with avocado slices.

Mix salt and cabbage; let stand 1 hour. Squeeze excess moisture from cabbage. Add carrot and green pepper. Mix together in saucepan the vinegar, water, mustard seed, celery seed and sugar. Boil 1 minute. Cool to lukewarm; pour over cabbage mix and serve. This slaw freezes very well. Make a double amount and freeze half for a future meal and picnic.
Spread on cake platter in order given.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Cook lasagna noodles according to package while browning one pound of hamburger.
Drain hamburger.
Drain lasagna noodles and run cold water over noodles.
Then spread 3 of noodles in a cake pan making a layer.
Spoon Ragu sauce over the noodles.
Sprinkle the hamburger over the sauce.
Then sprinkle the Mozzarella cheese over the hamburger.
Combine all ingredients, except nuts, in top of double boiler. Place over simmering water and stir until smooth.
Add nuts and mix.
In a large bowl, combine crushed cookies, nuts and coconut. Add sweetened condensed milk and rum; mix well.
Chill 4 hours. Dip palms of hands in powdered sugar and shape batter into 1-inch balls.
Roll in powdered sugar; cover and store in fridge.
If desired, reroll in powdered sugar before serving.
May be made ahead and stored in fridge for several weeks.
Line bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking dish with strips of bacon. Crumble raw ground beef over bacon.
Slice potatoes and place over ground beef.
Peel and slice carrots and put on top of potatoes.
Slice onion and put on top of carrots.
Pour 1 cup water over all.
Bake at 350° for
1 hour.
Cook all ingredients except onions on top of stove for 3 to 4 hours in covered pan.
During last 1/2 hour, remove meat; slice thinly with electric knife.
Return sliced meat to broth.
Add sliced onion and cook another 1/2 hour or until onions are soft. Serve as roast or make sandwiches when served on kaiser rolls.

Pour 4 cups boiling water over the tea leaves and orange rind in a heat-proof bowl and let the mixture steep for 10 minutes. Strain the tea into a pitcher; add the orange juice, the lemon juice and the sugar, stirring until the sugar is dissolved and chill the mixture.
Add the ginger ale; pour the mixture into tall glasses filled with ice cubes and garnish each drink with one of the orange slices.
Makes 8 drinks.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake 4 to 5 hours at 250°. (Can be made in a crock-pot 4 to 5 hours.)
Preheat oven to 425°.
Prepare a fire so you will have hot coals on the hearth.
Put dry ingredients unsifted in bowl.
Mix in buttermilk and egg.
Add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil and mix thoroughly.
Put remaining oil in 9-inch cast-iron skillet. (If baking in fireplace, use cast-iron skillet with legs, called spider pan.)
Heat skillet in oven or over coals for 5 to 10 minutes.
In oven, pour batter into skillet and bake 25 to 30 minutes or until brown.
Cut into wedges and serve with butter.

Slice potatoes, pepper and onion in strips. Layer 1/2 the potatoes, onions and pepper on a sheet of foil. Add 1/2 the butter and garlic powder. Layer the rest of the vegetables, add the rest of the butter and garlic. Wrap in aluminum foil. Bake in 350° oven 1 hour or until tender. Also great, cooked on the grill.

recipes.t: Roast Turkey Breast With Mushroom Gravy
d: Heat oven to 350°.
Place turkey in shallow roasting pan. Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over turkey.
Cover and bake until done (165° to 170° on meat thermometer), about 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours.
Cut turkey into slices. Serve gravy with turkey and, if desired, with boiled or mashed potatoes.
Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Cream butter, sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Sift flour and salt together; add to creamed mixture.
Mix well to make soft dough.
Stir in walnuts (pecans).
Break off pieces of dough size of walnut; shape into balls.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove from cookie sheet with spatula. Cool slightly and roll in powdered sugar.
Makes 4 dozen balls.
Scrub, pierce and bake potatoes at 425° for 1 hour or until tender.
Cool slightly.
Break in half lengthwise and scoop potatoes into a large bowl.
Beat in butter, salt, pepper and sour cream.
Refill shells.
Sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 or 40 minutes.
Freeze or refrigerate as desired. Serves 6.
Remove outer leaves, quarter, core and shred cabbage.

Core and slice unpeeled apples. Combine cabbage, apples, bacon fat, salt and pepper in heavy saucepan. Add enough boiling water to cover. Cover pan and simmer until cabbage is tender, but still somewhat crisp (20 minutes).
Drain off liquid, reserve and keep hot.
Dissolve Knox gelatine in water.
Warm cream of mushroom soup and mix with the dissolved gelatin.
Add the remaining ingredients and stir.
Pour into 1 quart mold.
Remove crust.
Cut in cubes.
Soak in water and squeeze out. Place in 2-quart baking dish; mix and add milk.
Put in hot oven. When it starts to bake well, then turn down heat.
Stir often for 2 hours.
Serve hot or cold with whipped cream.
In a bowl, combine cream cheese, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
Spread on the bottom of a greased 9-inch pie plate. Combine cheeses; sprinkle half over the cream cheese layer.
Top with the pizza sauce and peppers.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheeses.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Serve warm with tortilla chips or breadsticks.
Boil chicken until done, let cool and cut into small chunks. Fry bacon until very crisp, crumble into bacon bits.
Chop celery medium fine.
Crumble pecans under each half, is in about 6 pieces.
Open canned mushrooms and drain.
Put in large bowl: chicken, bacon bits, celery, pecans and mushrooms.
Add sour cream, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Mix thoroughly and serve.
Melt margarine in two 9 x 1 1/2-inch round cake pans in 325° oven.
Stir in brown sugar.
Spread mixture evenly in pans.
Blend cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Bring 1 cup of juice to a boil; add to Jell-O, stirring until dissolved.
Add 4 tablespoons hot liquid to cheese mix and blend.
Add to Jell-O mix and blend well.
First Layer:
Spread 2 cans of bean dip.
Combine all ingredients.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add to meatballs.
Cook in crock-pot on low for 6 to 8 hours.
(Italian meatballs can be gotten from Sam's.)
Brown meat and drain. Add all ingredients. Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes. Serve with tostado chips or corn bread.

Steam broccoli until done. Drain. Saute onion and pepper in butter. Mix broccoli, rice, onion, pepper and mushroom soup together. Salt and pepper to taste. Pour into casserole dish. Top with grated cheese. Put in oven at 350° long enough to heat through and melt cheese.
Boil potato in	slightly
salted
water
until	cooked. Mash hot potato, adding as much powdered sugar as it will hold to make dough that can be rolled out.
Add vanilla during this process. Roll out
on
powdered
sugar to 1/4-inch thickness. Spread with peanut
butter
generously.
Roll
up
and	slice. This candy keeps very well.
Brown hamburger in skillet.
Cook macaroni until done in large pot.
Put macaroni and hamburger in square 9 x 9-inch pan or larger if serving large crowd.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over top.
Place in microwave or in oven at 350° until cheese melts.
Cook and drain broccoli. Mix other ingredients together. Set aside. Put broccoli in 9 x 11 baking pan. Pour mixture over it. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes, uncovered.
Preheat oven to 275°.
Lightly grease a 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat butter, brown sugar, granulated sugar, egg yolk and nutmeg until light and fluffy.
Add flour; stir to combine.
Pat dough over bottom of prepared pan.
Get the round steak cut a little thicker than the regular round steak.
Cut meat into pieces.
Pour some flour on it and pound flour into meat.
Have oil hot in pan; brown meat.
Add green pepper, celery and tomato juice to meat.
Salt to taste. Let simmer until well done.
Add a little water if meat isn't done and the tomato juice is used up.
Combine all and serve over ice.
Roll a scoop of ice cream (any flavor) in crushed corn flakes. Freeze.
Roll out a canned biscuit or pie pastry and wrap ice cream, being careful to seal all edges.
This may be returned to freezer until ready to fry.
Heat oil to 400° and drop ice cream in for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Drain.
Top with maple syrup and nuts.
Most any kind of ice cream topping will do fine.
Serve at once.
You will need toothpicks.
Bake pie crust according to directions on package.
Heat milk in double boiler.
While it is heating, mix sugar, salt, cornstarch and cocoa well; set aside.
Beat egg yellows slightly, adding 1/3 cup of the warmed milk.
Pour egg mixture back into milk in double boiler.
Add sugar mixture.
Stir constantly over medium heat until thick.
Remove from heat.
Add butter and vanilla.
Allow to cool slightly.
Pour into cool baked pie shell.
Top with meringue.
Beat eggs; add garlic, pepper and diced onions.
Dip chicken breasts in mixture.
Fry chicken until brown, then bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Add vegetables to chicken and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Take chicken out of the oven and sprinkle the avocado over it before serving.
Serves 4.
Mix all ingredients and shape into small meatballs.
Roll meatballs in paprika.
Lightly brown in 1/4 cup margarine.
Drain grease and cover meatballs with cream of mushroom soup mixed with 1/2 can water.
Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Tear bread into pieces and put in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Cook sausage and drain.
Put over bread.
Put cheese over sausage.
Cook Jell-O and pineapple juice for 5 minutes after it comes to a full boil.
Cool.
Mix Cool Whip, cottage cheese and pineapple together.
Add Jell-O mixture.
Blend well.
Pour in mold and chill.
Combine carrots, water and salt in saucepan.
Bring to a boil. Cover and reduce the heat.
Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, until carrots are crisp-tender; drain.
Combine orange juice and cornstarch and stir into carrots.
Stir in raisins and sugar. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until smooth and thickened.
Serves 4 to 6.
Beat first 3 ingredients until creamy.
Beat in water, egg and vanilla.
Add combined dry ingredients.
Mix well.
Cover; chill about 2 hours.
Heat oven to 350°.
Shape into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet; flatten with tines of fork dipped in granulated sugar to form crisscross pattern.
Bake 9 to 11 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Cool 1 minute on cookie sheet. Remove to wire rack.
Cool completely.

almonds.
Serve
with apple and banana slices. Yields 3 cups.
Mix all ingredients in mixer. Serve with carrot sticks, cucumber sticks, celery sticks, green pepper sticks or cauliflower. Children love it with potato chips.
Beat sweet potatoes with mixer until free of lumps.
Add remainder of ingredients and beat well.
Pour into one 9-inch unbaked crust and bake in preheated oven at 450° plus 10 minutes. Lower baking temperature to 350° and continue cooking for 30 minutes.
Grind cranberries and apples; add drained pineapple.
Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in boiling water, then add cold water.
Put all ingredients together and mix well.
Pour into containers or Jell-O molds.
Makes 4 to 5 pints.
May be frozen or stored in refrigerator for a couple weeks.
Melt butter
and
let
stand
until cool.
Beat at high speed until light and fluffy (1/2 hour).	Add 1/4 cup powdered sugar, egg
yolk
and
whiskey;
beat
thoroughly.
Add baking powder to flour
and	sift
together.
Use
low speed and add flour to butter mixture. Add a little at a time until you have a soft dough.
Shape
and	place on cookie sheet; bake at 325° for 20 minutes.
Do
not brown.
Place on waxed paper and sift powdered sugar over cookies.
Cream shortening; add sugar gradually and cream well.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add mashed bananas, nuts and sifted dry ingredients.
Pour into greased bread pan.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Slice onions and peppers in rings.
Brown lightly in oil. Remove from heat and remove them from oil.
Remove all fat from steaks.
Pound steaks to tenderize.
Mix flour, salt and pepper. Cover steaks in flour, shake off excess and brown both sides in oil used for peppers and onions.
Pour off oil.
Place onion and pepper rings on top of steak, then spread soup over all.
Add water to almost cover meat.
Simmer for 2 hours adding water as needed to keep meat nearly submerged.
(Can be done in slow cooker.)
Bring ingredients to a boil.
Reduce heat; simmer for 15 minutes.
Defrost spinach and drain.
Soften cream cheese.
Stir in spinach, Parmesan cheese, mayonnaise, dill and garlic powder. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Warm to serve.
In a large skillet, cook sausage, onion, pepper and celery until halfway done.
Do not drain.
In another skillet, add 3 tablespoons of oil and cook rice slowly until browned.
Add other cooked ingredients in a large pot and add tomatoes and chicken broth; cook for 30 minutes.
Add to mixture to thicken.
Season to taste with ground red pepper, garlic powder, seasoned salt and pepper.
Fold sweetened condensed milk and lemonade concentrate into whipped topping.
Spoon into crusts.
Freeze until firm.
Garnish pies, if desired.
Yield:
Two 9-inch pies.
Freeze for 8 hours.
Combine ingredients in jar.
Cap and shake well.
Makes 2 servings.
Contains 18 calories a serving.
Peel and parboil 2 to 3 pounds sweet potatoes.
Mash and add salt, pepper and brown sugar to taste.
Put in casserole; add 1 small can crushed pineapple.
Cover with marshmallows.
Bake in a moderate oven until the marshmallows are toasted.
Cook ground beef. Drain. Fry bacon crisp and crumble.
Combine the rest of the ingredients in crock-pot and cook all day.
Cook diced eggplant until mushy in salted water.
Mash eggplant and combine with other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Place chicken breasts, one at a time, between 2 sheets of wax paper and gently pound with mallet until 1/4-inch thick.
In a rimmed plate, combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, 1 teaspoon of oregano, garlic salt and pepper; set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together softened butter, parsley and remaining oregano.
Spread about 1/2 tablespoon of the herb-butter mixture across each breast about an inch from lower edge; lay a strip of Jack cheese over butter mixture.
Fold lower edge of breast over filling.
Fold insides and roll up to enclose mixture.
Dip each bundle into melted butter and drain briefly; roll in bread crumb mixture until evenly coated.
Place bundles, seam side down, in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Cover and refrigerate 4 hours.
Bake, uncovered, in a preheated 425° oven for 20 minutes, or until chicken is no longer pink when lightly slashed.
Makes 4 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients, except noodles.
Cook in 350° oven for 40 minutes or until bubbly.
Sprinkle chow mein Chinese noodles over top and cook for about 5 minutes more.
Heat shortening in pan.
Add onion, garlic and mushrooms; saute until onion becomes pale yellow.
Add meat; stir until brown.
Add tomatoes, parsley and seasonings.
Cover.
Simmer about 45 minutes.
While meat is cooking, cook macaroni in boiling water 7 to 10 minutes.
Drain well.
Toss in margarine.
Turn macaroni onto hot platter.
Pour sauce over; sprinkle with grated cheese.
Trim deer steak of all fat, etc.
Soak in combination of milk and Worcestershire sauce for 2 to 3 hours.
Cook egg noodles and drain.
Mix mushroom soup with egg noodles
and put in a casserole dish.
Brown hamburger and drain. Mix together hamburger and Pizza Quick.
Place this mixture in casserole dish on top of noodles.
Sprinkle cheese on top and bake at 350° until cheese is melted.
Combine the vegetables in a pot.
In a bowl, stir the tomato sauce and broth together until smooth.
Stir in oregano or basil, then add to mixture in pot and simmer, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix melted oleo, egg yolks and milk very well.
Add flour; work in well.
Divide dough into 6 parts.
Cool dough in refrigerator overnight or at least for an hour.
Roll out on a floured cloth.
This should be about as thin as you would roll out noodles.
Sprinkle well with cracker crumbs, sliced apples (very thin), sugar and cinnamon.
Dribble melted oleo over all this about 3/4 of a stick.
Roll up.
Grease well with melted oleo. Bake at 375° for 1/2 hour until golden brown.
Again, grease well with oleo and sprinkle with sugar.
Different things one can put with apples include raisins, coconut and pecans.
Use 1/2 cup sugar.
Spray a tube pan with cooking spray and drop in frozen rolls. Mix pudding mix and brown sugar.
Dump over rolls.
Mix white sugar and cinnamon; dump over rolls.
Add nuts.
Pour on butter and let stand, uncovered, overnight.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Invert onto pie plate.
Mix cornstarch, sugar and salt and dilute with cold water, pineapple juice and boiling water.
Cook in double boiler, stirring constantly until mixture thickens.
Cool slightly; add lemon juice, pineapple and beaten egg whites and pour in molds to chill and set.
Serve with custard or whipped cream.
Heat oven to 350°.
Coat a 13 x 9-inch pan with vegetable cooking spray.
Put milk in a shallow dish.
Mix remaining ingredients except chicken in a medium size bowl.
Dip each piece of chicken in milk, then in crumbs, pressing so crumbs adhere to form a thick, even coating.
Arrange meaty sides up in a single layer in prepared pan.
Bake 1 hour or until browned and juices run clear.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix potatoes, sour cream, soup, onions, cheese and 1 stick butter.
Pour into a large casserole dish.
Mix 1/2 stick butter with crushed Ritz crackers. Sprinkle over top of casserole. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until top is brown.
Sift flour and measure 1 cup.
Add 1/2 cup sugar and sift 4 times.
Separate eggs; measure egg whites.
Place in large bowl and add 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Beat until foamy.
Add cream of tartar and beat until stiff peaks.
Gradually add 1 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons at a time, beating after each addition.
Fold in vanilla.
Fold in flour mixture 1/4 cup at a time.
Place in 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Sprinkle chicken with the salt and pepper and arrange on a rack in a baking pan.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until the juices run clear when the chicken is pierced with fork.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the mustard and oil.
In another small bowl, combine the crumbs and sage.
Preheat the broiler, setting the rack 6 inches from the heat.
Brush chicken with half of the mustard mixture and sprinkle with half of the crumbs. Place under broiler for 1 minute or until golden brown.
Turn the chicken the chicken, coat it with the remaining mustard and crumbs and broil for 1 minute or until golden brown.
Serve with corn-on-the-cob and steamed green beans or broiled tomatoes.
Serves 4.
Roll sugar cookie dough onto 2 pizza pans. Bake each for 10 to 12 minutes. Cool completely. Mix together cream cheese, sugar and vanilla. Spread onto cooled sugar cookie crust. Top with sliced fruit.
In large pan, simmer pork chop cubes in salted water (enough to cover) 45 to 60 minutes.
Add more hot water; enough to make as much curry as you want; then put in onions, carrots and potatoes. Salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to boil, lower heat and simmer 2 hours, stirring occasionally, covered.
Add the green pepper and simmer another 15 minutes.
Add flour to water to make sauce for thickening.
Stir into vegetables.
Add curry powder.
Serve over regular cooked rice, not instant.
Leftovers freeze nicely.
Mix all ingredients
and bake one hour at 325° or until done.

Beat persimmon pulp, soda, sugar and margarine until creamy. Beat in egg, then add flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and salt. Fold in walnuts and raisins. Drop by spoonfuls on greased baking sheet. Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes about 3 dozen.
Melt the butter in a large pan.
Spread brown sugar evenly in skillet and arrange pineapple slices on sugar, filling in spaces with nuts.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Beat egg yolks until light, adding sugar gradually.
Add pineapple juice and sifted flour.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Pour batter over pineapple.
Bake in moderate oven (375°) for 30 to 35 minutes.
Turn upside down on cake plate.
Serve with whipped cream, if desired.
Bring this mixture just to a boil.
Let cool and pour over cabbage mixture.
Place in airtight container and let stand for 24 hours, stirring occasionally.
In a bowl, combine crumbs and cheese.
Add seasonings and mix well to blend.
Melt butter.
Dip chicken into butter, then into crumbs.
Arrange chicken in lightly oiled ovenproof baking dish. Bake chicken at 375° for about 30 minutes or until brown and done. Chicken should be tender.
In a bowl, sift first 2 ingredients, add butter and nuts, and mix all together.
Take out 1 cup, set aside.
Add to bowl the rest of the ingredients.
Beat well and put in greased square pan 9 x 9-inch, then sprinkle the cup of crumb mixture on top.
Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Heat oleo in small saucepan until melted.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper, sugar and onion.
Add sour cream.
Stir until smooth. Cook, stirring constantly until mixture comes just to boiling point.
Fold in broccoli.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart greased baking dish.
Toss together Chex cereal and cheese and sprinkle over broccoli mixture.
Bake in preheated 350° oven about 20 minutes or until bubbly.
Serves 6.
Mix until smooth.
Place dip in center of serving tray and surround with vegetables of your choice.
Boil together and cool.
Pour over cucumbers packed in jars and seal.
Makes about 8 quarts of pickles.
Brown ground beef and chopped onion.
Mix meat and onion with ketchup.
Add other ingredients.
Place in casserole dish and bake covered for 45 minutes at 350°.
Combine cornstarch, cinnamon and salt in small saucepan.
Stir in orange juice and cranberry sauce.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thickened.
Set aside.
Drop by spoonful on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool and ice.
Put brown sugar icing on top.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In small bowl, blend first 4 ingredients.
Separate crescent dough into 8 rectangles.
Firmly press perforations to seal.
Spread about 1/4 cup pepperoni mix on each rectangle.
Start at shorter side and roll up; seal.
Cut into 6 pieces.
Place, cut side down, onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes at 375°, until golden brown.
Arrange apples in a greased oblong baking dish.
Sprinkle granulated sugar over apples.
Mix brown sugar, flour, pecans and margarine; pour over apples, patting to cover entire surface. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes a sweet, gooey apple pie. Serves 6 to 8.
Rinse mushrooms, pat dry and remove stems.
Chop stems (makes about 1 1/2 cups) and set aside.
In large skillet, saute bacon until crisp; drain on paper towel, crumble and set aside.
Pour bacon drippings from skillet.
In the same skillet, melt butter. Use about 4 tablespoons of melted butter to brush the outsides of the mushroom caps and place in large shallow 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
To the butter remaining, add onion and saute, then add mushroom stems and saute 2 minutes longer.
Remove from the heat. In bowl, combine eggs, cream, cheese and salt.
Stir in bacon and mushroom mixture.
Fill caps.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix together and roll into balls.
Chill.
Brown meat and onions.
Drain fat. Add remaining ingredients and simmer 1 hour.
Grate cabbage and small carrot.
Add celery seed, salt and pepper to taste.
Combine vinegar and mayonnaise; add to cabbage. Use more or less vinegar, depending on how sour you like it.
Prepare cake mix according to package directions, baking in two 8 or 9-inch pans.
Once layers are cooled, slice in half, making 4 layers.
Preheat oven to 425°.

Combine the frozen hash browns, cheese and onion in a large bowl.	Combine the milk, beef stock, half of the melted butter, garlic powder, salt and black pepper in another bowl and mix until well blended.
Pour over hash browns and mix well.
Heat the remaining butter in a large, ovenproof skillet over high heat.	When the skillet is hot, spoon in the hash brown mixture.

Cook the hash browns, stirring occasionally, until hot and all of the cheese is melted (about 7 minutes).	Put the skillet into the oven and bake for 45-60 minutes or until the surface for the hash browns are dark brown.
Heat vinegar, sugar and seasonings to boiling.	Arrange sliced cucumbers,
onions and green pepper in jars.
Pour hot liquid over and cool.
Store in refrigerator.
Place all ingredients in a crock-pot and cook on high until mixture boils.
Then turn to low and simmer for 6 to 8 hours. Chop cooked meat and serve on sandwich rolls.
Put bacon in a 2-quart casserole.
Cover with paper towel. Microwave 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until crisp.
Remove paper towel and bacon; leave drippings in casserole.
Crumble bacon and set aside. Add clams, liquid, potato, onions and water.
Cover and microwave 8 minutes on High, stirring every 3 minutes.
Add milk, bacon, seasonings and butter.
Cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it comes to a boil.
Let stand 2 minutes.
Serves 3 to 4.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, beating into mixture one a a time.
Add soda, baking powder, graham cracker crumbs, milk, coconut and nuts.
Grease and flour 3 (9-inch) cake pans.
Pour into 3 layers.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Melt butter, add condensed milk and cocoa and heat gently until combined.
Remove from heat and add chopped fruit, coconut and crushed/crumbled cereal.
Stir well and press into a Swiss roll tin.
When cool, ice with lemon icing.
Drain cherries and raspberries; reserve 1 1/4 cups juice and set fruit aside.
In a saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch; gradually stir in juice.
Cook and stir over medium heat until the mixture begins to boil.
Cook and stir 2 minutes longer.
Remove from the heat; stir in butter, extract and food coloring.
Gently fold in the fruit.
Cool slightly.
Pour into pie crust and top with a lattice crust.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until bubbly. Cool and serve plain or with ice cream.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Drain.
Add remaining ingredients and stir.
Serve or chill and serve.
Grind beets in a food chopper.
Measure 3 2/3 cups pulp and juice and add lemon juice.
Add Sure-Jell and bring to a boil.
Add sugar.
Stir and bring to a full boil again.
Boil for one minute. Put in glasses and cover with paraffin.
Roll flowerets in flour, dip in egg to which water has been added.
Roll in bread crumbs and fry in deep fat.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain well. Cool; rinse with cold water to cool quickly.

Combine Italian dressing, mayonnaise, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Blend well. Add cooled macaroni, cauliflower, celery, green pepper, radishes, carrots, tomatoes and parsley to the mayonnaise mixture.
Toss lightly until pasta and vegetables are evenly coated.
Chill for 8 to 10 hours to enjoy.
Combine all the ingredients, except the cilantro, in a 2-quart casserole.
Cover tightly and cook on High for 8 to 10 minutes, or until heated through.
To serve:
Spoon the soup into 4 cups and sprinkle with cilantro.
Bake pie crust as directed on package.
Prepare Dream Whip also as directed.
Mix together sugar and cornstarch.
Add water. Cook over medium heat until thick and clear.
Color with yellow food coloring.
Add almond extract.
Pour over peaches and stir lightly.
Pour into pie crust; top with whipped cream.
Mix all together except chocolate chips.
Beat 4 to 5 minutes. Mix (by hand) the chocolate chips into the batter.
Pour into a greased and floured Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes. Cool.
Ice with chocolate frosting.
In large, deep skillet, fry Spam until brown.
Add vegetables, tomato sauce and spices.
Simmer until potatoes are tender to fork.
Serve with French bread or sourdough bread.
In medium bowl, beat together eggs, milk and soup.
Stir in croutons, flaked salmon, green pepper and onion.
Pour into buttered 11 3/4 x 7 1/2 x 1 3/4-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until set in center.
Dice cooked potatoes.
Add bacon and onion.
Stir in mayo. Put in casserole and top with shredded Velveeta.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Mix mashed sweet potatoes, sugar, melted margarine and vanilla together.
Mix with mixer until fluffy.
Pour into casserole dish.
Clean and cut potatoes.
Cut all vegetables up into pieces. Combine ingredients in baking pan.
Pour in 2 cans of broth.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake at 300° for 3 hours.
Butter each ear of corn and sprinkle with curry powder.
Wrap each ear of corn in a sheet of aluminum foil.
Place on grill for approximately 10 minutes, or until cooked.
Heat oil and saut the onion.
Add the chicken, tomatoes and taco seasoning.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Layer 4 corn tortillas on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch glass pan.
Layer 1/3 chicken mixture, olives and cheese.
Repeat layers 2 times, ending with cheese.
Bake, uncovered, in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Combine any commercial barbecue sauce or your own with oil, bay leaf, garlic and lemon and pepper seasoning.
Pour over cleaned quail and marinate at room temperature for about 1 hour before cooking.
Broil over charcoal, turning once or twice, until done, about 20 minutes.
Do not overcook as this will dry out the tender white meat of the quail.
Serve barbecue sauce separately. The legs make delicious hors d'oeuvres.
Cream sugar with Wesson oil.
Add eggs 1 at a time, beating after each.
Mix flour with spices.
Beat in flour and milk alternately.
Add nuts, prunes and raisins.
Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Saute onions in oil until tender.
Stir in catsup, water, vinegar, mustard, pepper, sugar and wieners.
Bring to boil, stirring occasionally.
Turn down heat, simmer for 20 minutes.
Brown meat and onion.
Add salsa, tomato sauce and bouillon cube.
Bring to a full boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare rice as directed on package.
Put rice on the bottom of serving dish or casserole dish.
Top with meat mixture.
Put raisins in large saucepan.
Cover with water, plus that amount of water also.
Simmer until raisins are plump.
While raisins are cooking, mix together the sugar, egg, flour and cornstarch.
Pour small amount of hot liquid into the sugar-egg mixture, then gently pour all this into raisins.
Stir constantly; it will thicken quickly.
Remove from heat.
Let cool while fitting crust in pie pan.
Place sugar, vegetable oil, eggs, pumpkin and water in a bowl and mix.
Sift flour, baking soda and salt in raisins and spices. Add to first mixture and mix.
Stir in raisins and walnuts.
Place in paper liners in cupcake tin.
Bake at 400° approximately 15 minutes.
Blend shortening with sugar until creamy.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to the creamed mix, blending well. Add mashed bananas, lemon juice and nuts.
Bake in 3 well-greased No. 2 cans (average size can in the home).
Fill cans only 1/2 full.
Bake at 350° for about 50 minutes.
Cover dried peaches with water.
Cook in boiling water for 30 minutes until tender.
Drain and cool.
*No cream style corn?
Substitute 1/4 cup milk, buttermilk
or yogurt,
a
pinch of baking soda and corn kernels to make 1 cup.
Mix sugar, flour and salt together.
Add all remaining ingredients, except coconut.
Mix well.
Cook over medium heat until mixture thickens, stirring with wire whip to prevent sticking.
Add coconut and pour into pie shell.
Top with meringue.
Cream the butter and sugar. Add water and vanilla. Mix well. Blend in flour, salt and nuts. Chill for 4 hours.
Shape into crescents or fingers, using about 1 tablespoon of dough per cookie. Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes. Remove from pan.
Cool slightly.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Makes about 3 dozen cookies.
Mix together the above and pour into greased 8-inch round baking dish.
Mix together thoroughly shortening, sugar and eggs; stir in applesauce.
Sift together flour, soda, baking powder, salt and spices; stir into sugar mixture.
Mix in raisins and nuts.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Place 1/4 maraschino cherry on top for decoration.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 375°.
Grease casserole dish.
Pour pineapple (drained) in dish. Sprinkle sugar and flour mixture over pineapple.
Sprinkle cheese over sugar and flour mixture.
Mix cracker crumbs and melted margarine.
Pour over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Make rice according to package directions.
Saute onions and mushrooms in margarine until tender.
In large casserole, combine cooked rice, mushrooms and onions and soy sauce.
(Add more soy sauce to taste.)
Mix well.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Combine chicken, grapes and almonds. Combine mayonnaise and remaining ingredients. Add to chicken mixture and mix well.
Cook bacon; drain and crumble.
Combine half the Swiss cheese and the other ingredients.
Mix completely.
Pour into deep dish pie shell.
Cover with the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until firm in center.
This is very good, even if you are not a lover of spinach.

recipes.t: Weight Watchers Raspberry Mousse With Strawberries
d: Drain raspberries, reserving juice.
Combine gelatins in small saucepan; stir in half the orange juice and raspberry juice.
Let stand 3 minutes.
Stir over medium heat until gelatin is dissolved.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan (greased and floured).
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Mix pretzels, 3 tablespoons sugar and margarine.
Press into a 13 x 9-inch dish.
Bake for 10 minutes in preheated 350° oven. Cool.
Brown ground beef with chopped onion; drain.
Add catsup and mustard; simmer for 5 minutes.
In 2-quart casserole, layer beef mixture and slices of cheese.
Top last layer of cheese with biscuits.
Follow baking directions on can.
Serve with salad or fries.
To make each turtle, use 1 whole (head) and 2 halves (4 legs) pecans.
Place pecans in form and place softened caramel over pecans to make body.
Pour a tablespoon of chocolate chip mixture over that and chill until firm.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs. Mix in flour and spice. Pour brandy over chopped up fruit and nuts.
Add to cake mix. Refrigerate for 1/2 day before cooking.
Grease cookie sheet. Cook for 15 minutes at 300°.
Combine cheese food, softened cream cheese and margarine; mix until well blended.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Mold into bell shapes using the Cracker Barrel container coated with margarine. Chill until firm.
Remove.
Yields 2 bells.
Warm milk, sugar and Crisco. Dissolve dry yeast in the warm water. When dissolved, add to milk mixture. Add flour and beat with electric mixer. Set aside until double in size.
Sift together baking powder, salt and baking soda.
Add to mixture and enough flour to make a stiff dough (enough to handle; I use my hands.)

Make out your rolls (use greased muffin tins or whatever kind of roll you are making) and let rise. (I make two balls in muffin pan.) Bake at 425° for 7 to 8 minutes. The dough can be placed, covered, in the refrigerator for several days.
You can make a dozen at a time.
Combine first 5 ingredients in heavy saucepan.
Cook over medium heat.
Stir constantly until thick and smooth; set aside to cool.
Scald milk and add sugar.
Set aside to cool.
Mix yeast and warm water; let it sit for a few minutes.
Cut butter into flour and add eggs.
Combine flour, yeast and milk mixtures. Dough will be moist.
Divide in half.
Roll each half out on a floured surface to fit the bottom of a jelly roll pan.
Spread cooled pineapple filling and cover with second half.
Seal edges; snip surface of dough to let steam escape.
Cover with clean towel and let rise in a warm place for about one hour.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Frost with confectioners sugar frosting.
May want to use 2 cans of canned pie filling or substitute other canned fruit or fresh fruit or pineapple.

recipes.t: Fat-Free Pumpkin Bran Muffins(Tasty Muffins Without The Fat.)
d: Spray 12 (2 1/2-inch) muffin cups with cooking spray.
In medium bowl, combine pumpkin, cereal, milk, corn syrup and egg whites.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add pumpkin mixture; stir until well blended.
Stir in raisins.
Spoon into prepared muffin cups.
Bake in 400° oven 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan 5 minutes.
Remove; cool on wire rack.
Toast oats in shallow baking pan in preheated 350° oven for about 15 minutes or until golden brown.
Line a 9-inch square baking pan with aluminum foil and butter.
Melt marshmallows, peanut butter, honey and butter in medium saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in toasted oats and raisins.
Place in prepared pan, spreading evenly.
Chill until firm.
Remove from foil and cut into small squares. Refrigerate in sealed container.
In saucepan, combine beans and oil.
Bring to boil.
Let cool and drain off liquid.
Add eggs, onions, pickles and salad dressing.
Cover and refrigerate.
Cream together butter and sugars.
Add eggs, half and half and vanilla.
Pour into pie shells that have been baked 4 to 5 minutes in a 350° oven.
Sprinkle lightly with nutmeg and pecans.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve with whipped cream.
Soften cream cheese and mix remaining ingredients in order given.
Chill and use as spread for crackers or party bread.
Wash meat.
Cut slits in meat and put in slivers of onion. Drizzle vinegar over meat.
Cover tight and place in refrigerator overnight.
Next day, drain off vinegar and wipe dry.
Put meat in heavy pan and brown both sides in oil.
Pour coffee and water over meat. Add salt and pepper.
Cover and bake 5 to 6 hours in low degree oven until meat is fork-tender.
Make drippings into gravy.
Mix all ingredients together; chill, but add 7-Up just before serving.
Stir all ingredients together.
Heat, but do not boil.
Serve hot.
Serves 16 to 18.
Boil to softball.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Stir until creamy syrup, then add peanut butter.
Put in buttered 8 x 8-inch pan.
Toss apple slices in lemon juice.
Add nuts, raisins, salt, Sugar Twin and cinnamon; mix well.
Lay out 1 sheet of fillo dough on waxed paper and brush carefully with 1 teaspoon melted margarine.
Sprinkle with 1/2 tablespoon bread crumbs.
Place second sheet on top of first and repeat the process.
Now you are ready to fill and roll the strudel.
Spoon 1/2 of the apple mixture in one strip along the edge of the fillo sheets that are nearest you.
Using the waxed paper to help you get started, roll the dough like a jelly roll.
Lay on greased baking sheet, seam side down and brush top with remaining tablespoon margarine. Score at 1-inch intervals.
Repeat process with other two fillo sheets.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until lightly brown; be careful not to let it burn.
Cut into slices when cool.
Cream butter; gradually add sugar, beating well.
Add egg and beat well.
Combine flour, spices and salt; add to creamed mixture, mixing well.
Combine persimmon pulp and soda; stir well and add to creamed mixture.
Stir in raisins and pecans.
Drop dough by level teaspoonful onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes or until done.
Yields 3 dozen.
Wash beans, trim ends and string.
Place beans in a 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Add water.
Cover with heavy-duty plastic wrap and microwave at High for 12 to 14 minutes or until crisp-tender, stirring after 6 minutes.
Let stand covered 2 minutes.
Drain.
Combine dressing and remaining ingredients in a small bowl.
Stir well.
Pour mixture over beans, cover and refrigerate 6 to 8 hours.
Serves 6.
Heat cider, cloves, allspice, cinnamon and sugar to boiling; cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Strain punch and pour into punch bowl.
Float oranges in bowl.
Makes 32 servings (about 1/2 cup each).
Preheat oven to 400°.
Dip chicken in oil, then in flavored bread crumbs, flavored with garlic powder.
Place 1 slice of cheese on cutlet, then roll.
Put in pan sprayed with Pam.
Cover with foil.
Bake 50 minutes at 400°.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Add taco seasoning mix; stir.
Add refried beans and water; stir.
Layer beef and bean mixture into a large oblong casserole dish (13 x 9 x 2-inch). Spread sour cream over mixture.
Top with Cheddar cheese.
Add taco sauce and jalapenos, if desired.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes, until cheese melts.
Mix together lemon juice, oil, salt, pepper, sugar and basil. Add sliced onion and mushrooms.
Marinate overnight in refrigerator.
Use a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Form ingredients into a loaf. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix tomato paste and water and put on top of loaf.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes more.
Thaw potatoes for 30 minutes.
Mix with remaining ingredients. Pour into 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine first 5 ingredients in saucepan and bring to a boil. Cook 2 minutes, remove and cool.
Place remaining ingredients in bowl and add cooled mixture and blend.
Chill.
Keeps for days in refrigerator.
Great for 2 people.
Cook squash until tender; saute onions and bell pepper in small amount of margarine.
Mix all ingredients, reserving 1/2 of cheese for top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix the first 4 ingredients together.
Cut fish into pieces to fit in jar.
Fill about 1/2 full, then add 3 tablespoons of mixture.
Finish filling jar with fish.
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt to each pint.
Do not add water.
Pressure cook for 90 minutes. Yields 4 pints of fish.
In 10-inch baking dish, layer each ingredient; potatoes on bottom, onions, ground turkey, uncooked rice and kidney beans. Spread tomato soup on top.
Pour water over all and cover tightly. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Saute onion with garlic for 1 minute; set aside.
In a separate bowl, mash beans.
Add cracker meal (enough to make a ball).
Add cider vinegar, egg white, onion and garlic.
Grill or bake for 2 1/2 minutes on each side.
Scald the milk in the top of a double boiler over direct heat. Mix the cocoa, sugar and add the 1/4 cup cold milk slowly, stirring all the time, to make a smooth paste.
Combine the scalded milk with the other ingredients and cook over hot water, stirring constantly until the pudding thickens.
Remove from the fire and chill before serving.
If you use milk, for each half cup of pudding that you eat, subtract a half a cup of milk from your daily allowance of milk.
Dissolve cornstarch in water.
Beat eggs until fluffy.
Fold eggs and cornstarch into pineapple.
Add salt and sugar.
Put in baking dish.
Cover mixture with cinnamon.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour or until golden brown all over.
Serve with ham, like a vegetable.
In a bowl, mix the cream cheese, sugar and peanut butter with electric mixer.
Fold in cool whip.
Pour the mixture into pie shells and chill several hours before serving.
Garnish with reserved cup of cool whip.
Spray a 9 x 13 dish with vegetable spray.
Layer ham slices on bottom, then add potato slices.
Mix cream of mushroom soup with milk and pour over potatoes.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Can add Vidalia onion if desired.
In medium skillet, saute (with 1 tablespoon butter) mushrooms, leeks (cut into pieces) and garlic.
Add wine.
Boil gently until wine evaporates.
Stir in chives and rice.
Set aside.
Fry
each
tortilla
in 1/4 inch of hot oil until crisp and golden, turning once.
Drain and place tortillas on paper towels. Sprinkle
each
tortilla
with
combined cheese, then tomato pieces and sprinkle of dried cilantro.
Microwave each tortilla approximately 1 minute until cheese is melted.* Using scissors cut tortillas into quarters.
Serve warm.
Combine soup and cream and put half in bottom of baking dish. Lay chicken pieces over the mixture.
Put other half on top of chicken.
Salt and pepper chicken.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Combine ingredients in large casserole or a roaster.
Cover and bake at 300° for 3 to 4 hours.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Put first 4 ingredients in large dish in layers with lettuce on the bottom.
Mix mayonnaise and sugar and put on top.
Mix. Add shredded cheese and Bac*Os or bacon.
Can substitute boiled eggs, onions and cauliflower.
Saute the onion, green pepper, celery, mushrooms and pimento. Add wine and turkey or crab.
Put pasta on bottom of casserole and Parmesan cheese on top, then sauteed mixture. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Layer in order given.
Bake at 350° about 35 minutes.
May use 2 cans favorite pie filling in place of pineapple.
Cook contents of rice and seasoning packet according to package directions.
While rice is cooking, melt butter in a large saucepan.
Add onion and cook over low heat until tender.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper.
Gradually stir in half and half and chicken broth.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Stir in chicken, pimiento, parsley, almonds and cooked rice.
Pour into a greased 2-quart casserole.
Bake uncovered in 400° oven for 30 minutes.
Melt margarine.
Add corn, sour cream and Jiffy corn muffin mix.
Mix good and bake in a greased casserole.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake at 350° until top is lightly brown.
Mix cake mix according to directions. Add water, oil and eggs.
Combine sugar and butter; cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Add flour alternately with milk, beating well after each addition.
Add flavorings.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 40 minutes.
In large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice, salt and baking powder.
In second bowl, stir together remaining ingredients until well mixed.
Add pumpkin mixture to flour mixture and stir until all ingredients are well moistened. Pour batter into 2 (9 1/4 x 5 1/4-inch) greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 65 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes, then remove.
Cool, then drizzle with glaze.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Heat olive oil in a large saute pan. Saute sliced onions until soft, but not browned.
In a separate pan, heat butter and saute shallots briefly.
Add to onions and continue cooking until the mixture is tender.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg; let cool.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
In large bowl, combine cake mix, 6 tablespoons butter and 1 cup rolled oats.
Mix until crumbly.
Reserve 1 cup crumbs for topping.
To remaining crumbs, add 1 egg and mix until well blended.
Press into prepared pan.
Pour cherry pie filling over crust.
Spread to cover.
To reserved crumbs in large bowl, add remaining 1/4 cup rolled oats, 2 tablespoons margarine, nuts and brown sugar.
Beat until thoroughly mixed.
Sprinkle over cherry mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden brown.
Add whipped topping, if desired.
Cook meat and onion until browned. Drain and stir in beans. Arrange half of chips on each of two 12-inch plates.
Layer half the meat-bean mixture, olives and cheese on top of chips for each plate.
Bake at 350° for 5 to 7 minutes until cheese melts.
Toss all ingredients. Chill and serve.
Cream the pudding, milk, Cool Whip and sour cream together in a large bowl.
Layer the pudding mixture, bananas and cookies in a big dish.
Put pudding mixture on bottom and layer, finishing with cookies on top.
Enjoy!!
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly.
Beat in eggs, 1 at a time, beating thoroughly after each.
Add flour, reserving 2 tablespoons.
Add sour cream.
Mix 1/4 teaspoon soda mixed with 2 tablespoons flour.
Add to mixture with flavorings.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Remove from pan when comfortable to handle.
Cook and debone chicken (reserve broth).
Saute onion until soft.
Cook spaghetti and drain.
Add milk, broth and 1/2 of the Velveeta cheese to spaghetti.
Heat until cheese melts.
Add bite size pieces of chicken and sauteed onion to mixture.
Put into casserole dish and cook, covered, until it bubbles in the middle. Grate remaining Velveeta over top.
Melt and serve.
Melt margarine in pie plate.
Mix all ingredients well and pour into pan.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Cook broccoli 5 minutes until tender; drain.
In saucepan over medium heat, cook soup and cream cheese, stirring constantly. Alternate broccoli and soup/cream cheese mixture in casserole. Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Mix thoroughly and drop by teaspoonful on cookie sheet. Bake at	325°
for 10 to 15 minutes.
This does better if let set for a couple hours in refrigerator before cooking.
Melt butter in soup pot.
Cut off tough green tops of leeks and wash thoroughly to remove sand.
Slice leeks thinly. Simmer slowly in butter until transparent. Dice potatoes and add to leek with broth. Simmer 1/2 hour.
Puree in blender. Return to heat. Season and stir in milk.
Heat through.
Do not boil.
Serve sprinkled with fresh parsley.
Arrange all fruit, except cherries, in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish or 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Combine brown sugar, butter and curry powder; sprinkle over fruit.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour. Garnish with maraschino cherries.
Serve immediately.
Fruit can also be served from chafing dish.
Serve with ham.
Makes 12 servings.
Cut potatoes in wedges and put in ice water for 30 minutes. Combine oil, garlic powder, paprika and salt and pepper.
Coat potato wedges with mixture and lay in shallow baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, mixing lightly.
Turn into baking dish and bake at 350° to 360° for 20 to 25 minutes or until brown.
Mix together flour, salt, pepper and paprika; sprinkle over beef.
Toss floured beef in oil that has been put in 3-quart casserole dish. Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 30 minutes.
Melt margarine in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle the next five ingredients in the order given, in layers on top of the melted margarine.
Pour the sweetened condensed milk over the layered mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cool and cut in squares.
Sprinkle yeast into the water and stir until dissolved.
Stir in sugar, salt and oil.
Add 2 cups flour and beat until smooth, then gradually stir in the additional 1 1/2 cups flour.
Dough should be as soft as biscuit dough.
Turn out on lightly floured board and knead until smooth and elastic.
Place in greased bowl and brush top with soft shortening.
Cover and let rise in warm place (85°), free from draft, until doubled in bulk.
Punch down and divide in half.
Form each half into a ball and place on greased baking sheet.
Press out with palms of hands into circles about 12-inches in diameter, making edges slightly thick.
Mix first 5 ingredients and beat 2 minutes.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Pour in greased and floured Bundt or tube pan. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
A frosting is not necessary, but I usually put a chocolate frosting or glaze on top.
Mix Jell-O and hot water; let stand about 10 minutes.
Add pie filling and pineapple; stir until blended.
Pour 1/2 of mixture into 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish and chill until firm.
(Let other half of mixture stand at room temperature until needed.)
Cook onion, celery
and
pepper
in water until tender. Drain. Mix all ingredients with squash and bake at 400° until firm and slightly
brown.
Put
cheese
evenly
across
top of squash and cover casserole
with
lid to melt cheese.
(Do not return to oven.)
Combine all ingredients except shrimp.
Mix well and place in covered dish in refrigerator to chill.
Remove crusts from bread; cube bread slices.
Layer bread, broccoli, ham and cheese in a 9 x 13-inch buttered pan.
Beat eggs, milk, onion, salt and mustard.
Pour over bread, etc., in pan. Sprinkle paprika and parsley flakes on top.
Bake 50 minutes at 325°.
Cool 10 minutes.
Cut and serve; great for brunch.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Mash cranberry sauce until fine.
Add pineapple, jello, orange juice and nuts.
Put in long size Pyrex dish and let gel overnight.
Good anytime, with meats or as a salad with crackers.
In a large skillet
or	wok, stir-fry chicken and white onions in oil until
chicken
is
completely cooked and onions are clear. Then mix
cooked
rice, green onions and mushrooms in skillet with chicken and onions.
If
rice	is too dry, add 1/4 cup water in skillet or chicken broth.
Sprinkle soy sauce over rice mixture to taste.

Brown pork chops in lightly greased skillet. Sprinkle with seasoned salt and set aside. Combine soup, milk, sour cream, pepper and 1/2 teaspoon seasoned salt. Stir in potatoes, 1/2 cup of the cheese and 1/2 cup of the French fried onions. Spoon mixture into 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Arrange pork chops over potatoes. Bake, covered, at 350° for 40 minutes. Top with remaining cheese and onions and bake 5 minutes longer. Makes 6 servings.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt; stir in eggs. Add to mashed eggplant, mixing well. Drop batter by tablespoons in deep hot oil and fry until golden brown, turning once.

Cook hamburger and onion and put in casserole dish. Put soups on top and cover with French fries laid in rows. Bake at 350-375° for 20 minutes. You can put the hamburger in the casserole raw and then cook for 1 hour or until done.
In large bowl of electric mixer combine sugars and butter. Beat until well mixed.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Continue beating until mixture is creamy.
Next, add flour, soda, baking powder, salt, vanilla, crushed pineapple and nuts and mix on medium speed for a minute or two.
Do not overbeat.
Drop by teaspoons on greased cookie sheet and bake for about 10 minutes or until lightly browned.
Do not overbake.
Bake at 375°.
Place on cookie rack to cool.
Take one large field, a half dozen children, two or three small dogs, a pinch of brook and some pebbles.
Mix the children and dogs together and put them on the field with flowers.
Spread over all a deep blue sky and bake in the sun.
When brown, set away to cool in the bathtub.
Yield: Many years of memories.
Use cheaper cut of meat; cut in small chunks.
Mix with Gebhardt's chili powder, garlic and flour.
Melt fat and suet in deep pot; fry onion until tender; add meat mixture.
Cook 15 minutes, add salt; gradually pour in hot water.
Simmer 45 minutes or until tender.
If chili with beans is desired, add Gebhardt's Mexican-style beans, heat thoroughly; serve.
In medium saucepan, combine milk, egg yolks and butter.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture comes to a boil.
Remove from heat; add remaining ingredients.
Cool until thick enough to hold shape, stirring occasionally.
Frosts two 9-inch round layer cakes.
Mix all together.
Bake 1 hour at 450°.
Mix poppy seed with hot water and let stand.
Combine all other ingredients and mix with electric mixer on low.
Add poppy seed and water; continue mixing on low for 1 minute.
Then, mix on high for 3 or 4 minutes.
Pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 325° for 35 minutes (or in Bundt pan at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes).
Put flour in a brown paper bag.
Add about three pieces of chicken at a time and shake until chicken pieces are well coated with the flour.
Dip chicken in melted butter and place on a cookie sheet; salt and pepper to taste.
Cook in oven at 375° for one hour or until golden brown.
In saucepan, blend cream of chicken soup and milk.
Add remaining ingredients.
Heat.
Stir occasionally.
Makes about 7 cups.
Serve with crispy bread.
Make a simple syrup by dissolving sugar in hot water.
Add lemon juice; let cool.
Dilute syrup with water to taste.
Just before serving add apples.
Serve over ice.
Cream shortening, 1/4 cup margarine and sugar in mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Sift flour and salt together.
Add to batter alternately with orange soda, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in extracts.
Spoon into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 325° to 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool in pan and remove to wire rack to cool completely.
Combine cream cheese, 1/4 cup margarine and confectioners sugar in mixing bowl.
Mix until smooth.
Spread over cake.
Blend soup and sour
cream.
Stir in milk.
Add chicken or tuna, parsley, pimento,
seasonings and noodles.
Pour into 1 1/2 quart shallow baking
dish.
Top
with
crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Makes 3
to 4 servings.
All you need to complete the meal is tossed salad, rolls and dessert.
Dissolve sugar, kool-aid, and concentrates in water.
Add ginger ale just before serving.
Combine sugar and syrup.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat. Add peanut butter.
Pour mix over corn flakes.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoon on wax paper.
Let cool.
Place ground beef in the bottom of a casserole.
Top with a layer of sliced raw potatoes, then a layer of onions.
Pour can of beans over this.
Cover with tomato soup.
Cook in 350° oven for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Uncover and brown for 30 minutes.
Combine chicken, cheese, almonds, celery and pineapple in bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, salt and soy sauce in bowl.
Add to chicken mixture; mix well.
Mix bananas, soda and water; set aside.
Mix shortening, sugar, eggs and milk.
Add flour and baking powder mixture alternately with banana mixture.
Add nuts; mix well.
Grease and flour pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Crumble together the 1 cup flour, 1/2 cup butter and 1/4 cup powdered sugar.
Press into an 8 x 8-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Peel and slice avocado and put in blender.
Add heavy cream, lemon juice and salt.
Blend until smooth.
Place in soup bowls and sprinkle with oregano.
Serves 2.
Pt in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with remaining stuffing mix. Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Grease an 11 x 7 x 1 1/2-inch pan.
Sift dry ingredients. Beat eggs, sugar, cooking oil and molasses.
Add dry ingredients to egg mixture and mix until smooth.
Blend in boiling water. Stir lightly and quickly.
Batter will be thin.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Grease and flour tube or Bundt pan.
Preheat oven to 350°. Combine cake mix, sugar, oil, eggs and sour cream.
Blend with electric mixer at low speed until ingredients are moistened.
Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Stir in pecans.
Pour half of batter into prepared pan.
Combine cinnamon and brown sugar. Sprinkle over batter.
Pour remaining batter into pan.
Bake 45 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven and allow to cool in pan 10 minutes.
While cake is still in pan, pour Rum Sauce over cake and allow to cool 1 1/2 hours before turning out on cake plate.
Serves 12.
Brown the chops in a small amount of fat.
Sprinkle rice between the chops and over the top.
In bowl, dilute soup and add seasonings, then pour over the chops.
Bake, covered, in oven at 350° for 45 minutes or until the rice has absorbed moisture.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease an 8 x 4 x 2-inch loaf pan.
Beat eggs in a large bowl. Stir in water. Add biscuit mix and beat. Add mustard and 1 cup cheese.
Mix thoroughly.
Turn batter into pan. Sprinkle with remaining cheese and dot with butter. Bake 45 minutes. Cool in pan 15 minutes.
Remove and cool on rack before slicing.
Serve sliced, buttered and toasted with a green salad, soup or chili.
Also makes delicious croutons.
This bread will freeze well.

Boil water and oleo (margarine); stir in flour while on the stove until it pulls away from the side of the pan and forms a ball. Remove from heat; add eggs one at a time. Put in a 9 x 13 pan. Bake at 400° for 30 minutes. Lower heat to 350° and bake an additional 10 minutes. Let cool.
Blend the cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Add the ham, parsley, onion, mustard and hot pepper sauce.
Blend until mixed good. Chill.
Serve on bread or crackers.
Boil eggs until hard-boiled.
Cook; peel and slice in half. Take yolk and mix other ingredients with yolk.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Put yolk mixture into egg halves.
Mix all ingredients together and sprinkle with paprika.

recipes.t: Low-Fat Quick And Easy Vegetable Soup
d: Cook meat and onion in a Dutch oven over medium heat until beef is browned, stirring until it crumbles.
Drain beef mixture and pat dry with paper towels.
Wipe drippings from Dutch oven with a paper towel.
Return beef mixture to Dutch oven.
Stir in vegetable juice and remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil; cover, reduce heat and simmer 1 hour.
Simmer all ingredients over low flame.
Stir frequently to prevent sticking. When thick, pour into bowl. Sprinkle top of pudding with cinnamon.
Chill.
(Remove cinnamon stick and rind prior to chilling.)
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Add egg, vanilla, salt and cream of tartar.
Sift and add flour, soda and chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for about 8 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine lemon juice, water, vegetable oil, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, ginger, coriander and fennel seed (optional); mix well.
Use to marinate chicken, fish or veal. Remove meat and boil marinade for 3 to 5 minutes until thickened. Brush over meat before cooking.
Makes 1/2 cup.
Melt oleo and saute bell pepper, onions, celery and green onions until tender.
Add tomatoes, wine and seasoning.
Cook slowly on medium heat for 20 minutes.
Place fish in baking dish. Pour sauce over fish.
Add sliced lemons over fish and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Baste fish with sauce.
Fish should be tender when stuck with a fork.
In large bowl, combine butterscotch chips and peanut butter. Microwave at 7 for 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes or until melted, stirring every 30 seconds.
Add cornflakes and peanuts.
Stir until coated.
Drop by rounded teaspoonful onto wax paper.
Chill until set.
Batter with flour and fry in oil.
Serve with tossed salad.
Beat eggs with half and half.
Stir in corn, asparagus, 1 cup cheese, flaked ham and onion.
Add salt and pepper.
Carefully pour filling into 10-inch pastry shell.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over top.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 45 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Serves 8.
Heat oven to 450°.
Mix all ingredients until soft dough forms.
Turn dough onto surface generously dusted with baking mix; gently roll in baking mix to coat.
Shape into ball; knead 3 or 4 times.
Roll dough 1/2-inch thick.
Cut with 1-inch round cutter dipped in baking mix.
Place with edges touching on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes about 2 dozen 1-inch biscuits.
For mini drops, use teaspoon and drop dough on cookie sheet.
Brown ground beef and onion in skillet; drain grease.
Mix spaghetti sauce and water in with this mixture.
Mix the egg into the container of cottage cheese.
In large oven pan layer sauce mix and lasagna noodles.
Spread cottage cheese on the noodles, then the Mozzarella and Cheddar.
Make 2 to 3 layers and top with Parmesan cheese.
Cook in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Be sure to put aluminum foil over the pan.
Cut peppers in half, lengthwise or remain whole.
Remove seeds and parboil for five minutes.
Remove casing from sausage; crumble and brown with onions in butter until both are lightly browned. Add dissolved tomato paste; salt to taste.
Clean fresh vegetables, then cut up in bite size pieces.
Put in a bowl (a glass bowl looks nice).
Then pour Italian dressing over this (I prefer Good Seasons packets).
Then you just marinate overnight, turning occasionally.
Tie spices in cheesecloth bag.
Combine all ingredients; stir to mix.
Let stand until sugar dissolves.
Return 1/2 of the pickles to jar.
Add spice bag.
Add rest of pickles and syrup. Refrigerate 3 to 4 days before serving.
You may remove the spice bag after a week.
Mix margarine, brown sugar and pecans together; pat into unbaked pie crust.
Bake at 400° until pie crust is brown and praline mixture is bubbly.
Cool.
Next, add butterscotch pie filling to 2 cups cold milk.
Mix until thick.
Fold in Cool Whip and pour into cooled pie crust.
Refrigerate.
Serve with a scoop of ice cream.
Beat the eggs; add sugar.
Then add flour and vanilla.
Scald the milk and melt margarine in the milk and add to the other ingredients.
Pour into greased jelly roll pan.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Spread peanut butter on cake while its hot.
Cool.
Heat beef broth in large kettle. Saut onions, celery and carrots in butter and oil until just tender.

Transfer with slotted spoon to broth and simmer. Use same oil and butter to saut mushrooms. When done, pour mushrooms and liquid into soup. Add wine and bring to a boil. Combine cornstarch and cold water, then add to soup. Heat until slightly thickened and serve.
Serves 6.
Place layer of crumbs in bottom of greased casserole dish. Layer with cheese.
Layer 1 can of asparagus and 1/2 of soup and liquid mixture on top.
Repeat layers.
Reserve some cheese and cracker crumbs for topping.
Pour melted butter over topping. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brown meat and season with next 7 ingredients.
Add tomatoes. Simmer 3 hours or until thick.
Add beans with liquid.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and vanilla at medium speed with electric mixer until well blended.
Add eggs; mix well.
Pour into crust.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until center is almost set. Cool.
Refrigerate 3 hours or overnight.
Yields 8 servings.
Can be served with fruit sauce on top.
Flake salmon.
Combine salmon, cheese, lemon juice, onion, horseradish and liquid smoke.
Chill 6 to 8 hours.
Shape salmon mixture into a ball.
Combine pecans and parsley; roll the salmon ball into the mixture.
Chill at least 4 hours.
Serve with crackers.
Makes 3-inch salmon party ball.

Place 1/2 of drained pineapple in buttered 10x6 pyrex dish. Mix flour, sugar, and salt, sprinkle half of this over pineapple. Dot with butter. Spread 1/2 of mixed cheese over this. Repeat in same order. Bake at 325°-350° for 30 minutes.
Remove and sprinkle with pecans. Bake 5 more minutes.
Pour cereal into very large bowl; set aside.
Slowly bring to a boil, stirring constantly, chocolate chips, margarine and Karo syrup.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and stir.
Pour chocolate over cereal.
Toss until well coated.
Fold in marshmallows. Spread mixture into greased 9 x 13-inch pan or shallow baking dish.
Chill one hour and cut into squares.
Brown onion in hot oil.
Stir in tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon.
Add other ingredients.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
In large pan, over low heat, saute onion in 1/2 cup butter until soft, but not brown.
Add cubed bread.
Sprinkle salt, pepper, sage, thyme and parsley over bread and then stir well. Simmer uncovered until bread becomes slightly browned and crispy, stirring every few minutes.
Add 1/4 cup butter, melted and mixed into 1/2 cup water; mix well.
Remove from heat and serve or refrigerate to reheat in the microwave before serving.
(Can be made the day before.)
Heat orange juice to boiling; add gelatin.
Stir until dissolved.
Break up cranberry sauce with a fork.
Add to jello. Add water and lemon juice.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Fold in the whipped topping and pour into a 5-cup mold.
Chill until firm.
Enjoy!
Cook sausage and onions.
Mix with cheeses and eggs, salt and pepper.
Spread one pizza dough in the bottom of 9 x 13 inch baking pan.
Top with sausage mix.
Spread second tube of pizza dough on top of sausage mixture.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Peel, core and slice pears (approximately 5 cups). In mixing bowl combine sugar, flour, orange peel and cinnamon.
Add pears and cranberries; toss to coat.
Set aside.
Mix ingredients together and pour over meat.
Bake at 350° for 3 to 4 hours.
Remove bone and fat and mash.
Serve on buns.
Break or cut cauliflower into small bite size florets.
Fry bacon to a crisp and crumble.
Slice green peppers and cut into small pieces.
Chop onions fine.
Mix all ingredients, except Miracle Whip.
Mix all ingredients in order.
Pour into prepared pans and bake at 400° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Sift flour and baking powder.
Cream sugar.
Add jello and sugar.
Cream well.
Add egg and vanilla; beat well.
Add flour to butter mixture.
Mix until smooth.
Cook on ungreased cookie sheet at 400° for 10 minutes.
Boil eggplant; drain and mash well.
Add eggs to canned milk; beat well.
Add butter, grated cheese and onion.
Turn into greased casserole.
Prepare pudding with 3 cups of milk; fold in 1/2 of whipped cream.
Reserve vanilla wafers and 1 banana.
Arrange in layers of wafers and bananas.
Spread 1/4 of pudding over wafers; top with banana slices.
Place wafers around sides of dish.
Cover and chill 3 hours.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Mix first 7 ingredients together.
Pour into greased 8 x 12-inch pan.
Spread sour cream over the top.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Enjoy.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Lightly grease a cookie sheet. To make cookie crust: In a large mixing bowl, cream together 1/2 cup butter or margarine and white sugar. Add egg, evaporated milk and vanilla. Mix well. In a separate bowl, mix together flour, salt, cocoa powder, baking soda and baking powder. Add flour mixture slowly to sugar mixture while stirring. Mix just until all ingredients are combined. Drop the dough into greased cookie sheet by rounded tablespoonfuls. Leave at least 3 inches in between each one; dough will spread as it bakes. Bake for 6 to 8 minutes, until firm when pressed with finger. Allow to cool at least 1 hour before filling.
Melt margarine; add flour.
Mix well.
Add remaining ingredients.
Put in large baking dish and cook in slow oven until thick.
Serves 8 to 10.
Heat 2 cups water to boiling.
Add broccoli, celery and onion. Cook until tender.
Do not drain.
Heat margarine until melted. Stir in flour until smooth.
Add 1 1/2 cups water until boiling. Add cooked vegies, broth, bouillon, salt and pepper.
Heat until just boiling.
Stir in cream.
Heat but do not boil.
Marinate cubed cutlets in egg in refrigerator overnight (at least 4 hours).
Then mix in breadcrumbs; brown in skillet in margarine.
Mix all ingredients and set overnight.
In a saucepan, cook green onions and lettuce in oil over low heat for 5 minutes.
Combine flour with broth.
Add to lettuce mixture and stir until thickened.
Put in the cooked peas, sliced water chestnuts and seasoning.
