Bake for 1/2 hour at 350°.
Serve with Tostitos chips.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Place butter in casserole dish and melt.
Add all ingredients, except biscuits, and mix well. Top with biscuits and place in a 400° heated oven.
Bake until mixture bubbles and biscuits are browned.
Cut Crisco into flour and salt.
Sprinkle in cold orange juice and "stir" only until dough leaves sides of bowl.
The secret is, do not handle the dough very much.
Divide dough into two equal parts and roll out, one at a time on well floured area.
Place in pie plate and flute, poke holes in it and bake for your one crust pies.
Bake at 425° until lightly brown.
*May use finely minced onions instead of garlic.
In large skillet, heat oil, margarine and garlic powder and cook shrimp over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until shrimp turns pink.
Remove and set aside.
Add water and milk; bring to boiling.
Stir in noodles and sauce; reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, 8 minutes or until noodles are tender.
Stir in shrimp and green onions.
Heat through.
Makes about 2 servings.
Put eggs in a large saucepan with enough water to cover 1/4 to 1/2 inch above eggs.
Bring to a boil.
Set timer for 10 minutes, drain.
Run cold water over eggs to cool.
Peel and slice eggs lengthwise.
Separate yolks.
Mix yolks, mustard and mayonnaise.
Stuff into whites with spoon and fork.
Garnish with paprika.
Mix all ingredients, except cheese and paprika.
Place in buttered casserole dish.
Top with grated cheese and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake 25 minutes in 350° oven until bubbly.
Serves 8 to 10.
Heat crushed pineapple just to boil.
Stir in 6 ounce box of apricot jello.
Add sugar.
Blend well.
Let cool until partially set.
Add softened cream cheese. Fold in Cool Whip.
Put in a 9 x 13-inch pan and refrigerate.
Cook and cool noodles.
Mix vegetable oil, vinegar, sugar, Accent, salt and pepper.
Pour mixture over slaw, noodles, almonds, onions, green pepper and sunflower kernels.
Let stand in refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold.
Blend the first 4 ingredients with wire whisk.
Tear or cube bread into 8-inch round baking dish.
Add sweets.
Pour custard over all.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until near set in center.
Serve warm or cold.
Dissolve jello, Kool-Aid and sugar in boiling water.
Add cold water.
Pour into ice cube trays, small paper cups or popsicle molds.
Freeze until firm, 2 to 3 hours.
Makes 20 to 24.
Spread over salad and top with chopped nuts.
Freeze steak for 1 hour.
Slice thin, cross grain.
Combine remaining ingredients in shallow dish.
Add steak slices. Marinate for 1/2 hour.
Place on broiler rack.
Broil 4-inches from heat.
Cook for 7 to 9 minutes or until brown, turning to other side.
Serve immediately.
Divide bread into thirds.
Butter baking dish.
Layer 1/3 bread, 1/2 cheese, repeat with bread on top.
Add eggs to milk and salt.
Pour over bread and cheese mixture.
Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Before baking, pour melted butter over top.
Set casserole in pan of hot water.
Bake at 325°, uncovered.
When brown and crusty, put on cover and continue to bake for 45 minutes.
Cook squash and onions until tender.
Drain.
Mix in rest of ingredients, except for bread crumbs.
Place in greased baking dish.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except almonds and corn flakes.
Turn into buttered casserole dish.
Top with flakes and almonds and bake in 375° to 400° oven for 30 to 40 minutes or until bubbly.
In a skillet brown meat.
Drain off fat.
Stir in pizza sauce, mushrooms and olives.
Simmer ingredients while you cook macaroni. Drain macaroni and add 2/3 cup milk.
Combine first three ingredients and set aside. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time. Stir in bananas and milk.
Add dry ingredients all at once, stirring just until all are moistened. Turn into greased loaf pan. Bake at 350° for about 40 minutes or until done.
Remove from pan and cool.
Brown and drain hamburger.
Place in crock-pot.
Add in layers the Ranch Style beans, minestrone soup and Ro-Tel tomatoes.
Add water and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer in crock-pot.
In a 4-quart saucepan, place tomatoes, chopped, and liquid from the can.
Add 1 cup of water and 1 cup chicken broth.
Deskin as much chicken as you want meat in the stew.
Add onion, salt and pepper to taste and 1 teaspoon of sugar.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer about 1 hour.
During the last 30 minutes, add the diced potatoes.
Remove the chicken; cook and take meat off the bones.
Chop the meat and return it to the pan.
Add the corn and butter beans and continue cooking until the beans are done.
Slice tomatoes; do not peel.
Put slices between paper towels to absorb liquid.
Mix batter of eggs, corn meal, chives, water, salt and pepper.
Fry in an iron skillet after battering each slice.
Don't over heat oil.
Turn to brown each side.
Brown meat; add onions, seasoning, tomatoes, corn and bouillon.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in green peppers.
Boil again. Stir in rice and remove from heat.
Cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
Serves 4.
Cook 1 hour at 325°.
Saute celery and onion in butter.
Add soup, milk and 1/3 jar Cheez Whiz.
Make layers of rice, asparagus, chestnuts and soup mixture in a buttered casserole dish. Add remaining Cheez Whiz on top of last layer in teaspoonfuls.
Bake, covered with foil, 25 to 30 minutes in a 350° oven.
Looks messy.
Beat, beat and beat until mixture is smooth and creamy!
Put on cooled cake.
Place onions, vinegar, sugar, mustard, garlic powder and salt in a skillet.
Cover and cook over low/medium heat for 20 minutes (onions should become transparent).
Combine all beans (do not drain the baked beans).
Combine both mixtures in a casserole. Bake in 350° oven, covered, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients together; chill and serve.
Heat beef stew and put in casserole while hot.
Mix buttermilk biscuits with the water.
Drop on hot stew.
Bake in a 450° oven for 10 minutes or until biscuits are done.
Boil water and add jello and gelatin.
Stir until melted.
Add cream cheese to hot mixture and dissolve well.
Chill until partially congealed.
Add rest of ingredients.
Pour into mold and refrigerate.
Mix well and chill before serving.
Use a 9 x 13-inch buttered baking dish.
In a 3-quart pan, cook sugar, corn syrup, nulomoline, cream and lecithin.
Stir often at beginning to dissolve sugar.
Bring to a boil and cook for 3 minutes. Add broken pieces of butter and cook to 230°. Continue to cook and stir until mixture reaches 246°.
Remove from heat. Add salt and vanilla. Gently stir with wooden spoon.
Pour into buttered pan. Add nuts, if desired.

In blender container, combine sour cream, milk and mayonnaise. Process until thoroughly combined, scraping down sides of container as necessary. Stir in remaining ingredients. Transfer to a bowl or jar with tight fitting cover. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Just before serving, stir well.
Makes
8 servings.
Add lemon juice to a bowl of cold water.
Clean shrimp and devein under cold running water.
Remove tail shell as well.
Split shrimp along vein cavity, but do not separate.
Place in bowl of lemon water and let set.
Put all ingredients into pie shell.
Cover and bake 20 minutes at 350°.
In blender or food processor, combine first 3 ingredients; mix until blended.
Remove cap and pour melted butter in slow, steady stream until mixture is thoroughly mixed.
Keep warm over hot, boiling water.
Cut the sweet potatoes and apples into 1/4-inch slices.
Layer in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
In a saucepan, bring syrup, cider, butter and salt to a boil.
Pour over potatoes and apples.
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more or until tender.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Put all ingredients into food processor; chill to serve. Will keep well.
Drain pineapple.
Save juice.
In saucepan, mix juice, 1/2 cup water and lemon juice.
Heat to boiling; remove from heat and add gelatin.
Stir well.
Break up cranberry sauce with fork.
Stir into gelatin mixture.
Refrigerate until mixture begins to gel. Stir in pineapple, celery and apple.
Pour into 4 cup mold.
Chill until firm.
Mix well and serve with assorted vegetables.
Boil chicken until tender; remove from bone and cut into small pieces.
Reserve liquid for stock.
If necessary, add enough water to stock to make 2 quarts.
Add soup, butter, salt and pepper. Make dumplings according to directions; cut into strips.
Drop dumplings into boiling chicken stock.
Boil 2 to 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Fold in chicken and eggs.
Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix ingredients with mayonnaise.
Season to taste (use Nature's Seasons blend and Accent flavor enhancer).
Mix well peanut butter, soft butter, corn syrup, vanilla and salt.
Stir in powdered sugar and nuts.
Knead well.
Spread into buttered cookie sheet.
Press smooth.
Refrigerate.
Sprinkle cucumbers and onion with salt.
Let stand 1 1/2 hours. Drain and rinse.
Mix but do not heat dressing.
Pour over cucumbers and onions in jars.
Let stand in refrigerator, the longer the better.
More cukes and onions can be added to the same solution several times.
Preheat broiler.
Split pita breads.
Combine butter and dill weed; blend well.
Spread dill butter on pita; cut each half into 4 wedges.
Broil until crisp.
Combine caramel candies each
cut into 4 pieces and 1/3 cup flour.
Add apples,
ice
cream
topping
and lemon juice. Mix well.
Pour mixture
into a frozen regular 9-inch Pet-Ritz pie crust and sprinkle with
cup
pecan
pieces.
Bake at 375° on a preheated baking
sheet for 40 to 45 minutes.
Store at
room temperature.
When using a Pet-Ritz deep dish crust, please substitute
caramel candies, 1/2 cup flour, 5 cups apples, 1 cup caramel ice cream topping and 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
Light grease 10-inch pie plate.
Mix together first 4 ingredients.
Put into pie plate.
Put remaining ingredients into blender and blend until mixed well.
Pour liquid mixture over ingredients already in pie plate.
Bake at 400° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Lightly grease a 15 x 12 x 1-inch cookie sheet.
In a large bowl, cream the 1 cup of butter.
Gradually add the sugar, beating until fluffy.
Broil ground beef until rare and crumbled.
Combine with egg white and dill weed.
Shape into 24 equal sized meatballs.
In a large nonstick skillet saute meatballs until browned on all sides. Add green pepper and onion to skillet.
Cover and steam 1 minute. Stir in tomatoes and salt.
Then stir in beans and macaroni.
Cover and cook over medium heat about 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Serves 4.
Combine pretzels, 2 teaspoons sugar and margarine; press into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake for 7 minutes at 400°.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese, confectioners sugar and whipped topping; spread on pretzel mixture.
Dissolve strawberry and lemon jello in boiling water. Add pineapple and strawberries.
Allow mixture to cool.
Spread jello and fruit on cream cheese mixture.
Refrigerate.
Cut into squares.
Serves 16.
Mix all.
Pour into a casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for approximately 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Mexican Dip(This Dip Can Also Be Made Into Roll-Ups.)
d: Mix all ingredients (except for tortillas) together. To make roll-ups, spread dip mixture over tortillas. Roll up and slice into 1 inch pieces. Place on tray and garnish with cilantro.
Cook dates, sugar, butter and egg together until soft.
Cool slightly and add vanilla, Rice Krispies and nuts.
Separate biscuits; cut each in half.
Brush biscuits with mayonnaise.
Combine sugar, cinnamon and pecans; roll biscuits in mixture.
Place 2 pieces in each greased muffin cup.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden.
In food processor, crush cookies until they resemble dirt.
Set aside.
Cream together cream cheese, margarine and powdered sugar. Mix pudding and milk until well blended.
Fold pudding into cream cheese mix.
Fold in whipped topping.
In an 8 - 10 inch plastic flowerpot, alternate layers of cookie dirt and pudding mixture. End with dirt.
Top with worms.
Chill several hours.
Serve with sand shovel.
Blend cheese and butter until soft.
Add flour; blend well and chill well.
Roll into small balls.
Bake at 500° for 7 minutes, or until brown.
Makes 40.
May be frozen.
You may stuff olive in the cheese ball before baking.
Mix all ingredients, except water or milk with fingertips. Add enough water or milk to make dough stiff enough to be rolled out.
Roll out dough fairly thin.
Sprinkle surface of dough with additional sugar.
Cut dough into rounds.
Place on greased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 10 minutes or until brown.
Makes about 3 dozen cookies.
Combine sugar, milk, syrup and salt in saucepan; mix well. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until mixture boils and sugar dissolves.
Cook to 238°, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat.
Add butter and vanilla.
Cool to 110° without stirring. Beat until mixture loses its gloss and a small amount dropped from a spoon will hold its shape.
Quickly stir in pecans, coconut and cherries.
Pour into slightly greased pan, 8 x 8 x 2-inch.
Let cool and cut into squares.
Let cream cheese stand until it is room temperature.
Add seasonings and mix.
Spread on slice of beef.
Roll and put in foil and freeze.
When ready to serve, cut into bite-sized pieces and serve with toothpicks.
Drain cooked broccoli and spread in a casserole dish.
Place chicken on top and pour sauce over both.
Can be made ahead. Before serving, crush 2 cups of Pepperidge Farm dressing and add about 2 sticks margarine.
Cover casserole with dressing crumbs and cook at 350° for 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook for 15 minutes more.
This may be frozen to heat and use later.
Gather ingredients in a large bowl and mix in the order they are listed.
Cook steak in small amount of oil until slightly browned.
Add onions, cook until transparent.
Add soy sauce, sugar and 2 cups water.
Cook until meat is tender, 1 1/2 to 2 hours, adding water as necessary.
Add mushrooms and celery.
Cook for 15 minutes longer and thicken with desired amount of cornstarch mixed with water.
Serve on rice.
Mix the drippings, flour, sugar, salt, water, vinegar and egg thoroughly and boil 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour over bowlful of mixed lettuce and onions.
Stir in bacon bits and serve immediately.
Mix all ingredients in a saucepan, cook slowly, constantly stirring until cheese is melted and smooth.
Cook until thick and then cool, use with cauliflower, broccoli, celery, carrots and radishes.
Beat eggs into cake; mix powder.
Add almond extract.
Add 20 ounce can cherry pie filling and mix well.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour mixture into pan.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Place peach halves, cut side up, in baking dish.
Combine allspice, orange rind, brown sugar and chopped nuts.
Sprinkle mixture over peaches.
Broil in preheated oven about 5 minutes or until sugar mixture is bubbling.
Makes nice accompaniment for meats.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook noodles in boiling water until al dente (still a little firm); drain and place in a large bowl.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine the Ricotta cheese and half the Mozzarella cheese; add to the noodles and mix.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Cover bottom of dish with half the spaghetti sauce.
Spoon the noodle mixture over the sauce.
Cover with the remaining sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and the remaining Mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and let stand for 20 minutes for easier serving.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Soak in water the chipped beef to remove salt.
Drain and chop. Mix mayonnaise, sour cream and all spices.
Remove center of loaf of rye leaving a bread "bowl".
Cube bread removed plus second loaf.
Fill center of bread bowl with mayonnaise mixture.
Arrange bread cubes around bread bowl for dipping.
Melt cheese and oleo.
Pour over mixed sugar, cocoa, vanilla and nuts.
Mix and pour into pan.
Cut in squares after it hardens.
Cut biscuits in 1/4 pieces.
Dip in margarine, roll in sugar. Put in Bundt pan in layers.
Sprinkle nuts and raisins on each layer.
Repeat process until 1-inch from top of pan.
Drizzle remaining margarine (mixed with cinnamon and sugar) over top. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until top is brown.
Saute first 4 ingredients.
Add next 5 ingredients.
Mix in cheese and bread crumbs.
Shape into patties and dredge lightly with flour.
Saute in small amount of oil until crisp or put in flat shell dishes and heat in oven.
Drizzle with lemon juice or serve with lemon slices.
Very good stuffing for flounder.
Cook cabbage with enough water to cover cabbage and onion until tender.
Drain and add soups.
Gently fold together. Crumble sausage in pan and fry out grease.
Drain thoroughly and chop or break up larger chunks real fine.
Put on top of cabbage and serve.
May need to reheat before serving.
Brown beef, garlic and onion in small amount of olive oil. Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Just cook until everything is hot.
Recipe can be doubled for larger crowd.
In 5-quart Dutch oven, combine all ingredients; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer approximately 2 hours or until chowder has thickened, stirring occasionally.
Makes 8 (1 1/2 cup) servings.
Mix and chill.
Best to set overnight.
Cut meat in approximately 3 x 3-inch pieces.
Pound with meat tenderizer.
Chop onion and fry with chopped bacon, until almost done.
Put spoonful of drained bacon and onion in each steak piece.
Roll up and put toothpick through.
After you have done all meat, dip in flour and salt and pepper.
Brown in skillet. Remove and make a gravy out of drippings, adding mushroom soup with some milk.
Put meat in pot, pour gravy over, cover and bake in oven for 1 1/2 hours at 350°, or until tender.
Place bananas in large bowl and mash with electric mixer.
Stir in the sugar and let stand 15 minutes.
Add the applesauce and eggs and beat well.
Beat in the baking soda, baking powder, salt and vanilla, then gradually beat in the flour, mixing thoroughly.
Pour into a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan that has been coated with nonstick spray.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center of the loaf comes out clean.
Remove from oven and let stand 10 minutes before removing from the pan.
Makes 1 loaf.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease 9 x 9-inch pan.
Cream together sugar and butter until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and blend well. Stir in the rest of the ingredients except the blueberries. Spread half the dough in the pan.
Spoon the pie filling on the top; spread the other half of dough over the pie filling.
Bake about 40 minutes or until cake tests done.
In skillet in hot oil, cook chicken for 10 minutes, or until browned.
Combine soup and milk; stir in lemon juice and pepper. Pour over chicken; top with lemon slices.
Reduce heat to low. Cover; simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Bake cake according to directions, adding 1 tablespoon Kahlua to batter.
Bake in 2 (9-inch) pans and cool.
Split layers into 4.
Melt chocolate bits over water.
In large bowl, combine cream, milk and 2 tablespoons Kahlua.
Slowly add instant pudding until thickened.
Lay cake, cut side up.
Spread 1/2 raspberry preserves.
Cover 1/4 pudding.
Next, add 2nd layer of cake and 1/2 chocolate.
Next, 1/4 pudding mix.
Repeat layers, ending with chocolate layer on top.
Decorate with fresh raspberries and chocolate curls.
In a large bowl, sprinkle yeast over warm water and let stand for 5 minutes to soften.
Stir in sugar, oil and salt.
Add whole wheat flour and 1 1/2 cups all-purpose.
Mix to blend.
With a heavy-duty mixer or wooden spoon, beat until dough is elastic. Stir in wheat germ and 1 cup all-purpose flour.
Turn out onto floured area with remaining flour.
Knead until smooth.
Place in greased bowl.
Cover and let rise.
Punch dough down; turn out onto floured surface and divide in half.
Shape into loaf shape.
Place on greased baking sheets; cover lightly and let rise.
Bring cornstarch mixture to a boil.
Brush loaves while mix is warm. Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until browned.
Cool on wire rack.
Coat a 2-quart shallow casserole with nonstick spray; set aside.
In a large bowl, toss together the onion, crumbled salmon, celery, bell pepper, mustard, parsley and bread crumbs.
Place milk in a 2-cup measure.
Blend in mayonnaise.
Pour over the salmon mixture and thoroughly combine.
Spoon mixture into the prepared casserole.
Bake in the preheated 350° oven for about 35 minutes.
Cook Polish sausage in skillet to brown a bit.
Drain off fat. Cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Mix with other ingredients and cook in microwave for 5 minutes.
Then cook 15 minutes more at Medium power.
Stir occasionally.
Serve warm with toothpicks or on small plates.
Mix together all ingredients except ketchup.
Shape into a loaf in a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf dish.
Spread ketchup over top. Cover; microwave on medium-high for 22 to 24 minutes or until no longer pink.
Allow to stand, covered, for 5 minutes, before serving.
Pour cold water in cup and sprinkle Knox on top.
Set aside. Crush graham crackers and place them in a buttered 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
In a double boiler, cook next 6 ingredients until very smooth, stirring occasionally.
Add Knox mixture and stir until dissolved.
Pour over cooled crust. Refrigerate to set.
You can add a small can of drained, crushed pineapple.
Arrange layer of ladyfingers in attractive dish or serving bowl, 1-quart size.
Sprinkle ladyfingers with sherry.
Make up Jell-O according to package directions; pour Jell-O over ladyfingers.
Chill until set.
Cream shortening, sugar and flavoring.
Add 1 egg at a time. Sift flour, soda and salt together.
Add alternately with milk. Add bananas and nuts.
Bake at 325° in greased and floured cake pans until toothpick comes out clean.
Place potatoes in a buttered 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Add bell pepper and pimentos.
Mix lightly.
Combine milk and salt and pour over potato mixture.
Cover with foil.
Bake in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove foil.
Cover with mixture of bread crumbs and cheese.
Drizzle 1/3 cup butter over top.
Continue baking for 15 minutes or until cheese melts.

recipes.t: One Of A Kind Meat Loaf
d: Mix all ingredients well.
Mold into loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Serves 4 hungry people.

Boil chicken until cooked thoroughly, cool and separate. Preheat oven to 425°. In a large casserole dish, combine all ingredients and mix well. Sprinkle top with 1/2 cup of both cheeses and bake for about 30 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Melt the butter in a
small skillet.
Add the onion and cook until transparent.	Put into a casserole dish and add the soup and rice.
Stir and bake for one hour at 375°.
Sift together in large bowl the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add shortening, bananas and 1/3 cup buttermilk; stir to dampen flour.
Beat at medium speed 2 minutes with mixer or 300 hand strokes.
Add eggs, vanilla and remaining buttermilk.
Beat 2 minutes longer (or 300 more strokes).
Fold in chopped nuts.
Pour into 2 paper lined 9 x 1 1/2-inch round pans. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool and frost as desired.
Mix and stir all ingredients in order given:
flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
These can be sifted once if you prefer.
Add beaten egg and mix well with vegetable shortening, peanut butter and Sweet 'N Low.
Add dry ingredients.
Drop by large teaspoonful on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
About 30 minutes before serving or early in day, cut yellow peppers into 2 x 3/4-inch pieces.
Cut celery diagonally into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Remove stem and strings along both edges of each pea pod.

In nonstick 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, in 1 tablespoon hot olive or salad oil, cook yellow peppers, celery, 3/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, stirring frequently, until vegetables are tender and lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Remove vegetables to bowl.
In same skillet, in 2 teaspoons hot olive or salad oil, cook snap peas, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, stirring frequently, until peas are tender-crisp, about 4 minutes.
Stir pepper mixture into snap peas in skillet.
Spoon vegetables onto platter.
If not serving right away, cover and refrigerate to serve cold later.
Garnish with basil sprig if you like.
Makes 6 accompaniment servings.
Mix and bake at 375° for 12 minutes.

recipes.t: Hot Crab, Artichoke And Jalapeno Dip With Pita Triangles
d: In a small heavy skillet, cook the bell pepper in the oil over moderate heat, stirring, until it is softened and let it cool.
In a large bowl, combine the bell pepper, artichokes, mayonnaise, scallions, pimiento, Parmesan, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, jalapeno peppers and celery salt.
Blend the mixture until it is combined well and stir in the crab meat gently.
Mix all ingredients well.
Bake in greased and floured 8 or 9-inch pans for 35 minutes.
Bake and remove from pans.
Frost cake with 7-Up Cake Custard.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl.
Add onion and water.
Beat with rotary beater for 2 minutes.
Dip hot dogs in batter, holding with kitchen fork or tongs.
Drain off excess batter over the bowl. Fry in hot, deep fat (375°) for 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain on paper towel.
Insert wooden skewers.
Serve with mustard.
Thaw frozen spinach at room temperature for 2 hours.
Drain and chop into small pieces.
Heat oil and saute scallions until soft and wilted.
Add spinach and simmer until moisture evaporates. Rinse feta in cold water, drain and crumble it into bowl.
Blend in pot cheese, parsley, pepper and dill.
Add beaten eggs and mix well.
Add spinach and scallions and mix well.
Butter 11 x 14 x 2-inch pan and line it with about 12 to 15 sheets of phyllo, each sheet individually brushed with warm melted butter.
Spread spinach and cheese mixture on top.
Cover with about 12 to 15 more individually buttered phyllo sheets on top of one another.
Roll or push edges of phyllo down all around the pan to hold in mixture. Brush entire top and edges with warm melted butter.
Combine cooled margarine, sugar, eggs, buttermilk and vanilla in a bowl; mix well.
Stir in coconut.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 325° for 35 to 45 minutes or until set.
Yields 8 servings.
Open crescent rolls and flatten on cookie sheet, pinching seams together.
Bake until brown.
Mix Miracle Whip, cream cheese and salad mix together; spread on baked rolls.
Chill overnight. In blender, chop vegetables.
Put vegetables and cream cheese over baked rolls about 1 to 2 hours before serving.
Mix in frying pan.
Add water.
Cook until rice is tender.
Puree all ingredients in blender. Chill.
Serve in well chilled soup bowls.
Pass as a garnish croutons, finely diced cucumbers, onion and green pepper.
In small bowl, combine all ingredients.
Spread evenly over top of hot 8-inch or 9-inch square cake.
Run under broiler, 4 inches from heat, 2 to 3 minutes, or until topping is bubbly and golden.
Cool cake in pan on wire rack; serve slightly warm.
After sauteing meat and onion together, add other ingredients. Cook over medium heat or in a crock-pot for approximately 1 hour.
Grease a 9 x 5 x 3-inch pan.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Heat the milk with the herbs and let steep until cool.
Drain beans and peas.
Add onion, pepper and pimento.
In a saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar, salt and chili powder.
Mix and bring to a boil.
Simmer.
Mix vegetables and sauce together and refrigerate.
Peel and slice eggplants; boil with onion and bell pepper until done.
Drain and mash.
Add oleo, beaten egg and milk; mix, then add soup and stuffing mix.
Put into casserole.
Cover; bake at 350° for about 35 minutes.
Top with cheese; bake until cheese is melted.
Mix rum, 7-Up, sugar, lemonade and limeade concentrates and water together.
Place in a large plastic container; cover and freeze.
When ready to serve, spoon some of mixture into glass and add the same amount of extra 7-Up.
Combine all ingredients in order given, combining baking powder with the flour.
Use just enough hot water to dissolve the soda. Bake at 350°.
Crumble 1/2 of cake in punch bowl.
Add chocolate pudding and cherries.
Crumble remaining cake and add vanilla pudding.
Spread blueberries over vanilla pudding.
Spread Cool Whip on top. Garnish with pecans.
Mix peanut butter and sugar together until very crumbly.
Put layer of Jif and sugar mixture in bottom of baked pie shell.
Add pie filling, then layer of Jif and sugar mixture.
Top with Cool Whip or whipped cream.
Add rest of Jif and sugar mixture on top of pie.
Keep refrigerated.
Cream together shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well.
Blend in flour and vanilla; mix well.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Place in cold oven.
Turn oven to 325°.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Do not open oven door during baking time.
If desired, add 1 teaspoon lemon or butter flavoring instead of vanilla flavoring.
Break head of lettuce in small pieces.
Place in bottom of dish.
Dice onion.
Layer on top of head of lettuce.
Dice bell pepper.
Layer on top of onion.
Grate carrots.
Layer on top of bell pepper.
Dice celery.
Layer on top of carrots.
Layer peas on top of celery.
Grate the eggs and layer on top of peas.
Mix sugar with Hellmann's mayonnaise.
Cover salad with mayonnaise.
Sprinkle fancy shredded cheese over the mayonnaise.
Finely grate cheese.
Blend with butter and flour.
Roll in small balls and put on cookie sheet.
Flatten with spatula. Refrigerate for 4 hours.
Bake 7 minutes at 350°.
Makes about 24.
Place pan under broiler for a minute to brown them.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Add milk and Minute rice.
Add cream of chicken soup.
Stir in grated cheese.
Place in greased casserole dish and bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Mix sugar and oleo; add eggs one at a time.
Mix flour and soda.
Add to sugar and egg mixture.
Add bananas, milk and vanilla.
Mix well; pour in greased and floured tube pan.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
In bowl, combine soup, eggs and milk.
Stir in muffin mix just until blended.
Fold in sausage.
Spoon mixture into a greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 400° for about 20 minutes or until lightly brown.
Heat oven to 350°.
In small bowl, stir together all ingredients except mushrooms.
Stuff each mushroom cap with 1 tablespoon filling.
Place in buttered 13 x 9 baking pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until tender.
Mix sugar, cornstarch and salt in saucepan.
Blend milk and egg yolks.
Gradually stir into sugar mixture.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and boils.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Remove from heat and blend in butter and vanilla.
Place plastic wrap onto filling in saucepan and cool to room temperature.
Combine pineapple and juice, salad dressing and onions in baking dish.
Place chicken in mixture.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Stir once.
Other pieces of chicken can be used.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place the zucchini in the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Top with onion.
Sprinkle uncooked rice over the onion.
Cut 1 tablespoon margarine into pieces and dot over casserole; top with yellow squash.
Add tomatoes, spices and juice. Dot with 2 tablespoons margarine.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 50 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Remove foil and top with cheese. Bake an additional 5 to 10 minutes until the cheese is melted.
Cook the spaghetti; drain, rinse and set aside.
Saute onions lightly in butter or margarine in pan; stir in flour.
Stir in broth, milk and half and half.
Cook, stirring, until thickened. Take off heat.
Mix all ingredients together. Form into oblong mini loaf pans (about 8).
Bake on High or full power in your microwave for 8 minutes. Remove and drain grease. Turn loaves over and cook another 5 minutes.
Remove and let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Grate cheese and let soften.
Blend in butter and paprika. Work in flour until smooth and deep yellow color.
Let stand for 15 minutes.
Pinch 1 teaspoonful off; roll in palm and flatten. Place around a well drained olive.
Chill for 10 minutes or freeze.
Heat at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes, 30 if frozen.
Chop stuffed olives in blender.
Place beef, olives and tomatoes in a Dutch oven.
Simmer until beef falls off the bones. Skim off any fat and remove bones.
No additional seasoning is needed.
Heap on buns or French rolls.
Serve with a salad and beans, if desired.
Mix everything until it bubbles.
Put in the oven in a round mold.
Sprinkle with butter. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Wait until it is cold to put it on a plate.
Preparation time:
10 minutes.
Melt margarine or butter.
While butter is melting, hand beat 6 eggs.
Add the eggs to sugar, then margarine.
Mix buttermilk well, then coconut and vanilla flavoring.
Makes 2 pies.
Put in unbaked pie crusts and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Cover squash with enough water to cover.
Boil until tender and add salt and pepper.
When tender, drain and add 2 eggs and butter.
Mix ingredients with enough crushed crackers to make the mixture into patties; then roll in crushed cracker crumbs, and you're ready to deep-fry in hot oil.
Cook until golden brown and serve.
Mix the first 5 ingredients.
Beat 2 minutes.
Fold in nuts. Pour into a greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Mix all in covered casserole.
Bake at 350° for 3 1/2 to 4 hours.
Serves 4.
Good with corn bread.
Cut sausage any length desired.
Pour wine and water over it. Cook in a 450° oven until done.
Mix all ingredients well.
Shape into loaf.
Bake in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water to which you have added the sugar.
Let stand till yeast is thoroughly dissolved.
Add syrup, honey, brown sugar, molasses, rye flour, shortening and salt together in large mixing bowl.
Add warm water and stir till well mixed.
Add enough white flour to make a soft dough.
Pour onto pastry sheet and knead till dough is still sticky when touched by hands.
Dough should not be to stiff.
Place in large mixing bowl and cover.
Let rise in warm place till double.
Place on pastry sheet and pinch of enough to make a round ball.
There should be enough for 5 or 6 balls.
Let stand for 10 minutes shape into loaves.
Place in a well greased pans and set in warm place to rise till doubled in bulk.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Remove from pans and cool on cake racks.
This should make 5 or 6 loaves, depending on size of pans. 9 1/2 x 5 1/2 is about right.
This bread freezes well and makes delicious toast.
Combine 3 cups flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking soda.
Heat liquids until very warm (120-130 degrees F).
Add to dry mixture, beat well.
Stir in enough flour to make a stiff batter.
Spoon into 2 (8 1/2 x 4 1/2) pans that have been greased and sprinkled with cornmeal.
Sprinkle tops with cornmeal.
Cover and let rise in warm place for 45 minutes.
Bake at 400 degrees for 25 minutes. Remove from pans immediately and cool on racks.
Cook sugar, flour, milk, salt and egg yolks in a double boiler until it starts to thicken.
Then add lemon juice; cook until it thickens.
Cool.
Fold in sour cream and place in a pie crust. Add topping of Cool Whip and chopped pecans.
Mix all ingredients until very smooth.
Heat skillet; spray with Pam.
Pour 2 tablespoons of mixture in skillet and spread over bottom of skillet.
Brown crepe on both sides.
Spread crepe with butter, jelly, syrup or fresh fruit.
Can be rolled up like jelly roll and sprinkled with nuts and powdered sugar.
Mix the first 3 ingredients with 1 3/4 cups boiling water. When partly set, add the remaining ingredients.
Mix everything together and refrigerate until set.
Cook asparagus as directed until barely tender; drain.
Melt butter in a small pan; stir in flour, salt and pepper, blending until smooth.
Add milk and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and bubbly.
Turn half of the asparagus into a 1-quart casserole.
Top with half the eggs.
Pour half the sauce over the asparagus.
Repeat with remaining asparagus, eggs and sauce.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes at 325°.
One pound fresh or one pound drained canned asparagus can be used.
Remove seed from peppers and wash.
Combine salt, pepper, rice, browned ground beef, milk and onion.	Stuff peppers lightly and place in pan.
Add tomato soup and water, then cover.
Cook for 30 minutes at 300°.
Brown meat strips in 1/4 cup butter.
Push meat to one side; add mushrooms and onion.
Cook just until tender.
Add broth. Heat to boiling.
Blend sour cream and flour; stir into broth. Cook and stir until mixture thickens (sauce will be thin).
Season to taste.
Serve over rice or buttered noodles.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Melt margarine in baking dish.
Combine sugar and flour; stir in milk.
Add baking powder, salt and egg, mixing well.
Pour into baking dish.
Add 1 cup fruit in center of batter.
Bake at 400°. Yield:
6 servings.
Cream together brown sugar and shortening.
Add bananas, vanilla and egg.
In separate bowl combine soda, flour, salt and baking powder.
Add sour milk to brown sugar/banana bowl and stir thoroughly.
Add nuts if desired.
Pour into bread pan after spraying generously with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until toothpick inserted in middle comes out clean.
Brown chili meat and drain grease.
Add all other ingredients and cook slowly for 3 hours.
Brown hamburger and onion and season with salt, pepper and garlic.
Drain hamburger of grease and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cook noodles; drain and add enough milk and butter to keep moist.
Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Combine in saucepan the cornstarch and sugar.
Mix well; combine and add egg yolks and syrup from pineapple and cocktail. Blend well.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Cool thoroughly.
Fold in cream, walnuts, marshmallows, crushed pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Cover and chill overnight.
Just before serving, you may add bananas.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Cook the first 4 ingredients in 3 tablespoons oil until soft, but not brown.
Add meat and stir until meat loses red color.
Add tomatoes, tomato sauce and tomato paste.
Cook for 1 hour.

Cook squash in small amount of water until tender. Drain well and mash. In a separate bowl, beat eggs. Saute onion in margarine. Add squash, eggs, milk, brown sugar and salt to onions. Mix well. In buttered 2-quart casserole dish, put 1 layer of crackers, 1 layer of squash mixture and 1 layer of cheese. Repeat 3 layers; top with cracker crumbs and dot with butter. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Stir milk into soup until well blended and remaining ingredients.
Pour into well greased 1 1/2 qt baking dish.
Store covered in refrigerator 3-4 hours or overnight.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 1 hour.
Serves 4-6.
Melt butterscotch morsels over hot water in double boiler. Add oil, marshmallows and noodles.
Drop by spoonfuls on cookie sheet or wax paper.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix about half the cake mix, the peanut butter, margarine, water and eggs in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in remaining cake mix.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Roll balls in chopped peanuts.
Place about 3 inches apart on cookie sheet sprayed with Pam.
Press thumbprint deeply in center of each ball.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool.
Fill thumbprints with jelly. Makes about 6 dozen.
Saute chopped vegetables in oleo for about 20 minutes on medium heat.
Add soups, Ro-Tel and seasonings.
Cook 15 minutes on low heat, stirring frequently.
Add seafood and cook 20 minutes.
Just before serving, add parsley.
You may also add chopped green onion tops.
Serve over rice.

Preheat oven to 350°. Sift flour, sugar, soda, salt and cinnamon in electric mixer on "blend" speed; add eggs, bananas, oil, vanilla, nuts and pineapple. Bake in two 10-inch layer cake pans 1 hour and 20 minutes. Cool and frost.
Brown the rice with the margarine.
When it is as brown as you like it, add the onion, bell pepper, garlic and cilantro.
Also add salt and pepper to taste.
Continue to stir until the onion becomes clear looking.
Add the tomatoes; stir.
Cover; let simmer until rice is done.
You may want to add water, also.
Just don't add too much; otherwise, you will lose the flavor and it will be flat. Continue to watch it so it does not scorch.
Heat soup.
Add dissolved gelatine while stirring constantly. Mash the cream cheese and add soup mixture.
Add mayonnaise and mix. Add shrimp and crab meat, then other ingredients.
Mix well (with a mixer).
Pour into a greased mold and chill.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add flour mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Add one grated orange rind and vanilla.
Bake at 325° to 350°.
Bake in tube pan.
Saute green onions (use blades, too) in a little butter or oleo and olive oil.
Mix spinach (drained) into skillet.
Stir 2 beaten eggs into the mixture and stir until eggs are done.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Mix together and refrigerate.
In a greased 9 x 2 x 13-inch pan dump undrained pineapple and spread evenly.
Dump dry cake mix evenly over pineapple.
Cut margarine into thin slices and cover cake mix.
Sprinkle pecans over top and then sprinkle brown sugar.
Bake at 375° 50 minutes approximately.
Mix all ingredients and cook over medium heat until done. Pour into cooked pie shell.
Top with beaten egg whites and brown.

recipes.t: Mary Frances Glass' Chicken And Rice Salad
d: Combine cooked chicken, rice, dressings and chopped ingredients.
Prepare and refrigerate 12 to 24 hours before serving.
Serve cold.
Dissolve roux in water and boil about 1/2 hour.
Add chopped onions.
Cook additional 1/2 hour.
Add okra.
Add salt and pepper to taste with crawfish boil added.
Add tomato sauce and seafood. When gumbo comes to boil, lower heat and cook 15 to 20 minutes. Add file if desired.
Serve over rice.

Beat egg whites with electric mixer until foamy. Sprinkle salt and cream of tartar over top and continue beating until point that egg whites will stand upright. Add sugar gradually, beating meanwhile. Add vanilla and mix well.
Fold in pecans. Drop by spoonfuls on lightly greased baking sheets. Bake in preheated oven at 275° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Yields approximately 5 dozen. Store in airtight container.
Sift flour and salt together. Add powdered sugar, margarine and vanilla. Add nuts. Chill dough. Roll into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased sheet.
Bake until set but not brown. While still warm, roll in powdered sugar.
Cool. Roll in sugar again. Bake in a 400° oven for 10 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.
Mix ingredients well.
Bake or fry in pones (small cakes) until light brown.
If baking, bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Combine oil and sugar, beating well. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, soda, salt and cinnamon.
Mix well.
Gradually add to creamed mixture, mixing until blended.
Stir in peaches and pecans.
Spoon into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch glass pan.
Bake at 325° for 40 to 45 minutes. Serve with whipped cream.
Melt the chocolate and margarine over low-medium heat.
Add sugar, flour, eggs, vanilla and salt.
Pour into a greased and floured 9-inch pie pan.
Top with pecan pieces.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Makes a brownie-like pie.
Good served with a dollop of ice cream.
Mix red devil sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire and soy sauce and pour over chicken.
Chicken should be face down. Put in fridge overnight.
In 13 x 9-inch pan layer broccoli and sliced Fri Chik that has been sauteed with chopped onion.
Mix together next 5 ingredients and pour over broccoli and Fri Chik.
Layer on grated cheese and cover with buttered crumbs.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Serve over rice.
Melt the oleo and cocoa in saucepan.
In a medium bowl, mix sugar, flour and eggs.
After mixed, add nuts and melted mixture. Chill for 30 to 60 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes in half crosswise.
Gently squeeze the pieces to remove the excess juice.
Place cut-side up in a small casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the bread crumbs, Parmesan, parsley, lemon juice, oil and garlic powder.
Carefully spoon the mixture over the tomatoes and into the cavities left by the seeds.
Bake for 15 minutes or until the tomatoes are softened and the crumbs are lightly browned.
Cook pasta and drain.
Place into large bowl and add other ingredients.
Chill.
Melt butter in microwave.
Mix in cocoa, flour, 1 1/2 cups sugar and egg yolks.
Add milk.
Microwave on High for 3 minutes; stir.
Microwave on High 4 more minutes.
Stir in vanilla; pour into prepared pie crust.
Whip egg whites on high.
Gradually add 1/4 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla; whip until peaks.
Fold into pie.
Bake at 375° for about 5 minutes.
Mix shortening, water, vanilla and egg white.
Mix in cake mix, nuts and chips until dough holds together.
Shape dough into balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in a 375° oven until almost set.
Dip tops in powdered sugar.
Pound meat with the dull edge of a cleaver to tenderize it. Slice into strips about 2 x 4-inches.
Mix ingredients with water needed for Kool-Aid, lemonade and orange juice.
Chill.
At serving time, add 7-Up, Sprite or ginger ale.
Serves 50.
First, peel and slice potatoes thick and put in kettle. Bring to boil.
Remove immediately and drain.
Grease crock-pot and layer them in there; cook until done.
Sprinkle paprika on top and always end up with soup on top.
You can also bake this in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 15 minutes, uncovered and cook for 45 minutes at 375°.
In food processor bowl with metal blade or blender container, combine all ingredients except tomato.
Blend until smooth.
Spoon into serving dish.
Cover.
Refrigerate 1 or 2 hours to blend flavors.
Brown beef in 3 quart saucepan; drain fat.
Add sauce and water, simmer about 10 minutes.
Combine remaining ingredients, except noodles, for filling.
Pour about 1 cup of sauce on bottom of 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Lay 3 pieces of uncooked lasagne on top, followed by about 1 1/2 cups sauce.
Spread half of cheese filling over sauce.
Repeat layers of lasagne, sauce and cheese filling.
Top with layer of lasagne and remaining sauce.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° 55 to 60 minutes.
Remove foil; bake about 10 minutes longer.
Allow to stand about 10 minutes before cutting for easier handling.
Freezes well.
Serves 8 to 10.
Heat oven to 450°.
Saute onion and green pepper in oil. Remove from heat.
Blend in flour.
Stir in milk and soup gradually.
Cook over low heat 1 minute, stirring constantly. Remove from heat.
Stir in ham and lemon juice.
Combine all ingredients, except candy, in a large bowl.
Mix on lowest speed of mixer until dough forms.
Shape dough into balls, using rounded teaspoonful for each.
Roll balls in sugar. Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
In medium saucepan, add cooking oil and elbow macaroni. Brown macaroni lightly. Add water and tomato sauce. Add seasonings.
*Alternate fruits may be used: 20 ounces frozen strawberries (thawed), fresh or frozen blueberries, fresh or frozen blackberries.
Combine yogurt, mustard and horseradish in a large bowl.
Add potato, celery, cucumber, onion and chives. Toss lightly to mix well. Chill.
Makes 8 servings.
Each serving has 60 calories, 2 vegetable and 2 fat exchanges.
Cut baked potatoes lengthwise.
Scoop out potatoes and save the skins.
Beat the potatoes with all ingredients, except crab and paprika.
Fold in crab meat.
Refill potato shells and sprinkle with paprika.
Heat about 15 to 20 minutes in a 350° oven before serving.
Grated cheese may be sprinkled on top.
Very good.
Blend sour cream, soup and eggs.
Add rice, spinach, cheese, onion and sliced mushrooms.
Put in buttered baking dish.
Bake covered at 325° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Blend softened cream cheese and 2 tablespoons oleo until smooth.
Add next 6 ingredients.
Mix well.

recipes.t: Hot Fudge Sauce For Ice Cream
d: Melt the butter; mix in sugar and cocoa.
Add
milk slowly. Simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.

recipes.t: Vegetable Casserole(Cream Corn And Green Pepper)
d: Saute green pepper in butter until soft.
Pour green pepper into a 1 1/2 qt. baking dish and add corn, pimento, egg and 1/2 cup onions.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes till firm.
Add remaining 1/2 cup french fried onions to top.
Bake 5 minutes more.
Mix all ingredients (except cranberry sauce) in a bowl.
Roll into bite size balls and insert toothpicks. Bake in oven at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes (golden).
Slice Twinkies in half and lay in bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan. Mix pudding and spread on top of Twinkies.
Spread pineapple on pudding.
Slice bananas on top of pineapple.
Top with Cool Whip. Spread nuts on last.
You may put cherries on top and drizzle caramel, chocolate or strawberry topping on top of Cool Whip.
Bake chicken at 350° for 1 hour in a casserole dish.
Cook rice; set aside.
Take chicken out; set aside.
Put pan over burner until it sizzles and stir in sour cream.
Put the flame on low to keep warm.
Serve and put sour cream gravy on rice and chicken.
Enjoy.

recipes.t: Lemon Tartlets With Coconut Crusts(Makes 8 Tartlets)
d: Process coconut and sugar in food processor until coconut is minced.
Blend in egg whites.
Press mixture into well-greased 4-inch tartlet pans with removable bottoms.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden.
Remove from pans.
In a large stock pot, put in game (it doesn't matter how much of what you have, I find that about 3 or 4 pounds of meat is good). Fill pot 3/4 full with cold water, add the seasoning.
Bring to a boil 1/2 hour.
Add onion, celery, carrots and potatoes and simmer about 2 to 3 hours.
Pull meat from pot and debone.
Add meat to pot and boil; add pot pie bows or make your own dough and add to pot.
When noodles are done, serve.
Cream sugar and cream cheese; add vanilla.
Mix Dream Whip by instructions and combine with cheese and sugar mixture.
Mix margarine with crumbs.
Layer crumbs in a clear bowl, then cream cheese, Dream Whip mixture, then pie filling.
Repeat layers and top with crumbs.
Chill 24 hours before serving.
This is very pretty in a glass bowl.
Combine cucumber and onion slices in a bowl.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over slices.
Toss.
Serve immediately.
Mix all ingredients with mixer until mixed well.
Cook ground meat until all red color is removed, but do not brown; drain.
Mix other ingredients and add meat after it has cooled.
This salad is best while lettuce is still very crisp.
It keeps well in refrigerator for another meal.
Combine cake mix, oil, water and jello in mixing bowl.
Add eggs, one at a time; beat well.
Add strawberries; mix well.
Pour into three greased 9-inch cake pans or greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, or until done, at 350°.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar and pineapple juice.
Cook until thick, stirring often.
Remove from heat and add Jell-O.
Put into refrigerator to chill.
Beat milk until it stands in peaks. Gently fold Jell-O mixture to milk.
Pour into 2 vanilla wafer pie crusts.
Keep refrigerated.
Trim excess fat from steak.
Pound flour into the meat. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
In a large skillet heat oil.
Add steak and brown meat on both sides over medium heat.
Place steak in baking dish, about 12 x 8 x 2-inch.
Mix all ingredients except butter.
Cook until firm ball forms when dropped into cold water.
Remove from heat.
Add butter. Beat until spreading consistency.
Frost 3 layers or 1 pound cake.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix peanut butter, Crisco, brown sugar, milk and vanilla in large bowl.
Beat at medium speed until well blended.
Add egg; beat together.
Add everything else on low speed, until blended.
Spoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Press with fork.
Bake for 7 to 8 minutes.
Combine all except potatoes and peas.
Bake, covered tightly, in a 325° oven for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Stir and add potatoes and peas.
Continue baking 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are done.
Place spinach and tomatoes in salad bowl.
Arrange eggs, onion and cheese on top.
Puree all ingredients in blender until thick.
Makes 2 servings.
Contains 181 calories, 10 gm protein, 2 gm fat and 27 gm carbohydrates.
Sift flour 4 times and set aside.
Beat the first 5 ingredients until real fluffy.
Add flour and milk in four parts, blend well.
Place in large greased tube pan and bake at 325° for approximately 1 hour and 45 minutes.
Have cheeses at room temperature.
Combine with other ingredients.
Roll into a ball.
Roll in chopped pecans or parsley.
Good with Triscuits.
Brown meat.
Add rest of ingredients and cook 10 minutes.
If not thick enough, add more flour.
Spoon on buns and top with grated cheese or thinly sliced.
Bake at 375° until cheese is melted.
Boil sugar, water and syrup until spins a thread; add peanuts. After adding peanuts, stir continually until syrup turns golden brown.
Remove from heat; add remaining ingredients.
Stir until butter melts.
Pour quickly on 2 cookie sheets with sides.
As mixture begins to harden around edges, pull until thin.
*Use an electric blender or chop very fine.
Cook noodles according to pkg. directions.
Add cooked noodles to other ingredients.
Stir well.
Put in a 9 x 13 dish, crumble potato chips on top and bake at 350 for about 20 min. or until golden brown.

Preheat oven to 425°. Spray 8 x 8-inch pan with vegetable cooking spray. Peel, core and thinly slice apples. In a large bowl, toss apples with lemon juice, cornstarch, cinnamon, nutmeg and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Arrange mixture in baking dish. In a medium bowl, combine flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt. With pastry blender, cut in butter until coarse and crumbly. Sprinkle flour mixture over apple mixture. Bake 40 to 45 minutes until crust is golden and apples are tender. Immediately sprinkle with sweetener. Serves 9.
Blend all the above together.
Put in mushroom caps.
Bake until golden brown at 325°.
Combine condensed milk, lemon juice, lemon flavoring and egg yolks.
Pour into pie crust.
Top with Cool Whip.
Mix all together and beat 4 minutes.
Pour into prepared Bundt pan.
Bake at 350° over 50 minutes.
Let cool 15 minutes before turning out.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Combine milk, eggs and mustard.
In large oblong dish, layer bread, sausage, cheese and mushrooms.
Pour liquids over all.
Let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Before baking, spread 1 can cream of mushroom soup diluted with 1/3 can of milk.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until firm.
Mix dill weed, lemon, pepper, garlic powder and dressing mixes and shake in bag with pretzels.
Pour oil and hot sauce over pretzels.
Mix well.
Bake at 300° for 10 minutes.
Stir and bake 10 more minutes.
Cool and keep in airtight container.
Cook chopped zucchini in water.
Drain and add onions cooked in 1 tablespoon butter.
Add corn, cheese, salt and eggs.
Mix well.
Pour in greased dish and top with mixture of Parmesan cheese, melted butter and bread crumbs.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Brown in skillet beef, onion and pepper.
Add remaining ingredients and heat to boiling.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is tender.
Flatten the boneless chicken with a kitchen mallet Season with lemon pepper seasoning Sprinkle equal portions of the chopped ham and cheese on 1/2 of each chicken breasts.
Fold the chicken breast in half making a "sandwich", again sprinkle with lemon pepper seasoning.
Place in lightly greased pan place in oven cook for approx. 30 min or until completely cooked.
Remove from pan cover with hollandaise sauce.
Excellent when served with new potatoes and asparagus.
Cream shortening and sugar well.
Add molasses and rhubarb sauce and blend together.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to first mixture.
Add fruit and nuts and bake in a greased loaf pan in a moderate oven at 350° for about 50 minutes or until done.
Heat oven to 350°.
Place
half
of the ham in a 2-quart casserole.
Cover with half the potatoes and half of the onion. Sift half of the
flour
over;
season
with
salt
and pepper. Repeat layering ham, potatoes and onion.
Season with additional salt and pepper.
Sift remaining flour atop.
Pour milk over all. Bake, covered, in oven
for
to
1/4 hours or until potatoes are nearly tender.
Uncover.
Combine bread crumbs and melted butter;
sprinkle
atop
casserole.
Top
with
parsley. Bake 15 minutes more.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Boil chicken broth and water.
When boiling, add bok choy. Return to boil; cook, uncovered, for 4 minutes.
Add noodles. Cook chicken.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms and pea pods and heat through.
Season to taste and serve.
Brown sausage in skillet, stirring until crumbly; drain. Combine with remaining ingredients in 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Bake, covered with foil, at 375° for 40 minutes.
Cook macaroni until done.
Drain macaroni, then rinse in cold water.
Then let drain real good.
Then add all ingredients.
Add 1 cup boiling water to gelatin and stir to dissolve. Drain peaches.
Use juice and enough cold water to make 1 cup, add to gelatin mixture, stir, add peaches and pour into 8-inch square dish and refrigerate for 45 minutes to 1 hour until gelatin begins to set.
Then fold in freshly cut apples and banana.
Chill 2 hours until set.
Serves 8.
Recipe can be used in many fruit and gelatin combinations.
Mix all ingredients. Roll into logs. Roll logs into powdered sugar and sprinkle with grated chocolate.
Line a 9-inch square pan with whole graham crackers.
Mix pudding and milk.
Allow to stand for 5 minutes.
Blend in whipped topping.
Spread half over crackers; top this with a layer of cherry pie filling.
Add another layer of crackers.
Add remainder of the pudding mixture, then top with a final layer of pie filling. Chill for 3 hours.

Boil peeled and quartered potatoes in small amount of water. When cooked, do not drain. Mash the potatoes in the water and add the farina and potato starch mixture. Mix well.
