Combine with remaining ingredients.
Place in the casserole dish provided in the church office.
There is no need to bake it as it is baked before serving at the soup kitchen.
You can easily prepare this ahead and freeze it!
In a small saucepan, stir together the 3/4 cup sugar and the cornstarch.
Stir in water and orange juice.
Cook and stir over medium-high heat until the mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Add the fresh or frozen rhubarb pieces; cook and stir until the mixture returns to boiling.
Remove from the heat.
Cover the mixture to keep warm.
Melt butter and add three soups and water.
Remove 1 cup of the mixture and reserve for topping.
To the remaining soup mixture, add 1 cup uncooked brown rice.
Spread rice mixture on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place chicken pieces on top of mixture and top with the 1 cup reserved mixture, Parmesan cheese and almonds.
Bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Cube the rhubarb and spread on bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle dry Jell-O over rhubarb, then scatter marshmallows on top.
Prepare yellow cake according to box directions; pour over top.
Bake according to box directions.
Serve warm, plain or with whipped cream or ice cream.
Cook broccoli as usual and lay broccoli on bottom of greased casserole.
Combine 1/2 pint sour cream and mayonnaise.
Break fried bacon into small pieces over broccoli.
Pour sour cream mix over broccoli.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese.
Sprinkle paprika.
Cook 30 minutes at 350°.
Place pork fat side up in slow cooker (crock-pot).

Combine water and liquid smoke; pour over meat and sprinkle with salt. Cover and cook on medium 8 to 12 hours; remove pork butt from cooker and shred, then add the juices from the cooker (at least 1 cup; the flavor is in the juice).
Ready to eat.
Combine ingredients and put in well-buttered casserole.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Saute celery and onion in a bit of oil.
Combine all of the listed ingredients, except cheese crackers.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole.
Combine 2 cups crushed cheese crackers and 1/4 cup melted margarine.
Stir in 1/2 cup grated Cheddar cheese.
Spread over vegetable mixture in casserole.
Bake in 300° oven for 30 to 40 minutes.

Boil chicken breasts for about 30 minutes. Put eggs in same pot with boiling chicken and boil for an additional 15 minutes. Drain water from chicken and eggs. Spray cool water on chicken and eggs to help cool faster. Spray rectangular casserole dish with Pam. Tear chicken breasts into small pieces and layer the bottom of rectangular casserole dish. Take hard-boiled eggs and remove shells. Press eggs with fork to make smaller pieces. Layer egg pieces on top of chicken and then season the top of chicken and eggs with salt and pepper. (You may also add a pinch of garlic.) Put cream of chicken soup (or chicken broth) on top of the layer of chicken and eggs and smooth with spoon. Mix flour, butter and milk together. Pour onto the top of chicken and eggs. Bake in oven at 375° for about 45 minutes or until the top is golden brown.
Melt butter; add sugar and curry powder.
Drain fruits. Arrange fruit in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and pour sauce over fruits.
Bake at 325 degrees for 1 - 1 1/2 hours.
Serve with sour cream if desired.
Mix the cake mix, eggs and vanilla pudding.
Stir in poppy seed with a spoon.
Bake in tube pan at 350°.

Remove outside leaves from cabbage, cut into wedges. Place in pan with one inch of salted water, cover and heat to boiling. Reduce heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes. Fry bacon until crisp, remove from pan and crumble. Discard all but 2 tablespoons of bacon drippings. Add flour, salt, pepper and cayenne, stir until well blended, then add milk and water. Cook until thickened, stirring constantly. Add cheese, stir until melted. Drain cabbage, place on platter and spoon sauce over wedges, sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Soften ice cream until you can mix in broken cookies and top with crushed cookies.
Put in the freezer to harden.
Heat sauce and serve on pie.
Peel chayotes.
Chop first seven vegetables and put in large kettle.
Put 1/2 cup salt on these.
Mix well and let stand for 3 hours.
Mix once or twice.
Cook linguini. Drain and cover to keep hot.

Melt 1 tablespoon butter in skillet. Add mushrooms, scallions and garlic. Saute until tender. Add scallops, broth, dash of salt, thyme and pepper. Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until scallops are tender. Add parsley.
Soften butter or margarine in large bowl.
Sift together flour, sugar and baking powder.
Add butter and milk.
Beat 2 minutes at medium speed.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Beat 2 minutes more.
Turn into a greased and floured 9-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool; split into 2 layers.
Drain peaches. Whip the cream.
Spread half of cream and peaches between layers. Spread other half of cream over top; arrange remaining peaches sunburst-fashion over cream.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Let stand, the longer, the better.
Coat cheese with flour.
Dip in beaten egg, then in crumbs. Add salt to hot oil.
Fry in oil 20 to 30 seconds.
For variation herbs and seasonings can be added to crumbs.
Cover chicken with water and add the celery salt and onion salt. Boil chicken until tender. Remove chicken and debone. Add chicken soup to broth.
Mix all ingredients together and bake in greased pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown hamburger meat in 2 tablespoons fat.
Grease casserole dish.
Place tortillas in bottom of dish.
Add small amount of onion, hamburger meat, cheese and chilies.
Repeat layers.
Dilute soup with milk and pour over stacked tortillas.
Bake at 225° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Brown beef in skillet. Cut all vegetables in chunks.
Mix all ingredients in large roasting pan.
Cover tightly with foil; bake for 3 hours at 325° or for 4 hours at 250°.
Don't peek until after 2 hours; re-cover and finish baking.
Cook bacon; drain, crumble and set aside.
Slice onion and saute in bacon drippings.
Add potatoes; cover with water and cook until tender.
Add crumbled salmon and milk; scald until hot. Salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish individual servings with bacon and cheese.
In a large skillet brown chicken pieces on both sides in hot oil about 15 minutes.
Remove from skillet and set aside, reserving the drippings.
Add tomatoes and onion slices to pan drippings.
Stir in red pepper, thyme and salt.
Bring to a boil. Return chicken legs to skillet.
Spoon tomato mixture over chicken.
Return mixture to boiling, reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 35 to 45 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Skim off fat.
Serves 12.

Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Meanwhile in a bowl, combine chicken, 1 cup cheese, soup, milk, pimentos, salt and pepper. Drain spaghetti; add to chicken mixture and toss to coat. Transfer to greased 13 x 9 x 2 baking dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese. Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes or until heated through.
Add a touch of Greek home cooking love, put ingredients in a small jar and shake thoroughly.
Chill before serving.
Always shake before serving.
Combine all ingredients except 2 tablespoons of margarine, cheese and crumbs.
Use 1/2 to 2/3 cup of potato mixture for each log to be formed.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons of margarine; stir in crumbs and cheese.
Roll potato logs in crumb mixture.
Place in shallow, greased baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Sweet Potato Casserole With Crunchy Topping
d: Combine potatoes, sugar, salt, margarine, milk, flavoring and eggs.
Turn into greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with topping made by blending topping ingredients.
Mix in large bowl; beat cheese, ReaLemon, Worcestershire and garlic powder until fluffy; stir in onion.
On serving plate spread cheese in a 6-inch circle.
To with chili sauce and crab meat.
Cover and chill.
Serve with crackers.
Makes 12.
Put enough oil in skillet to cover bottom about 1/8 inch. Have good and hot.
Take garlic and crush with side of knife blade.
Add to oil. Cut 1 lemon in half.
Squeeze juice of half into skillet.
Add chicken breast and quickly brown on both sides. Slice second lemon into slices and lay in bottom of 7 x 9-inch baking dish after spraying.
Place chicken breasts on lemon slices.
To skillet add juice of half lemon, honey and seasonings. Bring to boil and pour over chicken.
Bake at 375° until chicken is done.
First Layer:
Mix flour, margarine and 1/2 cup nuts for first layer.
Cream together and press into 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Cool completely.
Brown meat in hot fat.
Add onion.
Cook until golden.
Add tomato soup, water and noodles.
Cook until noodles are tender, stirring frequently to taste.
Add corn and 1/2 cup grated cheese. Pour into greased casserole.
Sprinkle remaining cheese.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Cook first 5 ingredients until forms a small ball in cold water. Add peanut butter and heat until smooth and spreadable.
Cut up elephant into 1-inch cubes.
Be accurate.
Use ruler. Place cubes in kettle containing 2,315 gallons of water.
Simmer 3 days.
Add assorted vegetables.
Do not use rutabagas.
Rutabagas hate people; that's why they taste the way they do.
Simmer 6 more days over low heat.
Saute onions, peppers and celery in butter until tender.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Arrange broccoli in bottom of a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine sauteed vegetables and other ingredients. Spoon over broccoli.
Bake, uncovered, at 375° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs with mixer.
Add oil, sugar and maple flavor.
Continue beating until mixture is thick and foamy.
Stir in zucchini.
Combine flour and remaining ingredients, except sesame seed.
Stir gently into mixture just until blended.
Preheat
oven to 450°.	Grease	a
9-inch
baking
pan. Beat egg in mixing
bowl.
Add
remaining ingredients and stir until blended.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 12 servings.

recipes.t: Shredded Beets With Horseradish And Sour Cream
d: Brown onion lightly in butter in large saucepan 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix in beets, horseradish, salt, dill weed and pepper. Cover; lower heat and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Smooth in sour cream and bring just to serving temperature, do not boil.
Beat together eggs and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients. Pour into 2 (8-inch) pie shells or 1 (10-inch) and bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Mix ingredients.
Slice a loaf of French bread in half. Spread mixture on both halves.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Add cheese on top the last 5 minutes.
Cook all together, except pecans, in 4-quart pan.
Cook to 236° (soft ball).
Stir frequently with wooden spoon.
Remove from heat.
Add chopped pecans.
Cool and beat until creamy.
(After it cools, it sets up pretty fast.)
Drop by spoonfuls onto waxed paper.

Cut up the chicken meat either diced or in strips, chop lemon grass and kaffir leaves in food processor or hand chop finely. Cut the shallots to 1/4 inch strips, cut scallions to 1 inch pieces, chop cilantro with stems, no roots.
Peel and slice the galangal root in thin strips 1/2 inch long.
Heat pan on medium, add the kaffir, lemon grass, shallots, whole dried chilis, and galangal, stir until light brown.
Add the chicken broth and increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Add chicken, coconut and milk, fish sauce and 1/2 teaspoon chili paste.
Add the chili paste in increments and taste before adding the second half.
Heat almost to boiling, remove from the heat, add lime juice, cilantro and scallions.
Serves 4.
Drain pickles.
Add remaining ingredients.
Refrigerate for a week, turning upside down 2 or 3 times a day.
Spray mini muffin pan cups with Pam.
Mix the first 6 ingredients in a medium bowl with a wire whisk.
Mix bananas, yogurt, egg substitute and vanilla well.
Stir the flour mixture into the banana mixture until well moistened.
Add marshmallows and milk together over heat.
Remove and add all other ingredients.
Mix well and pack into dish.
Refrigerate.
Heat oven to 400°.
Cook lima beans as directed on package; drain.
Turn into ungreased 4 1/2-quart bean pot or casserole. Add baked beans and kidney beans.
In covered skillet, simmer sausages in small amount
of water for 5 minutes.
Drain liquid and fry until brown on all sides.
(Do not prick sausages.)
Cut each sausage into 2 or 3 pieces.
Add sausage pieces and ham to beans.
Stir together remaining ingredients; pour over beans and gently mix.
Bake uncovered 1 hour.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Brown sausage and onions.
Add remaining ingredients except bread crumbs.
Mix all and make into small balls; roll in flour and dip in milk/egg mixture.
Roll in bread crumbs and deep fry.
Can freeze.
Mix all ingredients with mayonnaise except cheese.
Sprinkle cheese over top and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Scald milk; cool to lukewarm.
Cream butter with sugar and salt.
Measure warm water into a large mixing bowl.
Sprinkle yeast in water.
Stir in lukewarm milk and cream mixture.
Add beaten eggs and about half the flour.
Beat until smooth.
Blend in fruits, almonds and lemon peel.
Add enough flour to make soft dough.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Cook and stir onions in oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the potatoes, sauce and water.
Reduce heat and cook 10 minutes.
Cook the carrots and broccoli; add to potatoes.
Slice the sausage and add, heating everything together until good and warm.
Add the cheese on top before serving.
Mix together and place into buns. Wrap individually in foil and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Brown ground chuck in medium skillet.
Add mushrooms and onion; saute for 3 to 4 minutes.
Drain off any excess fat.
Stir in water, sauce, bouillon and salt.
Bring to a boil.
In a small bowl, stir together the sour cream and flour; stir into meat mixture.
Cook and stir over medium heat until thick and bubbly; cook and stir for 1 minute more.
Serve over noodles.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Brown ground beef in a large skillet and drain.
Stir in picante sauce until heated.
Put on serving dish.
Drizzle melted cheese on top, then sprinkle lettuce and tomato on top.
Garnish with sour cream.
Serve along side of white corn chips.
Mix chili powder and flour; brown meat in large skillet.
Add powder and flour while browning.
When brown, add water, garlic, oregano and salt.
Simmer slowly for 2 hours.
Combine butter and mustard. Spread on hamburger buns.
Make up sandwiches with ham and cheese. Wrap individually in foil. Bake in foil at 375° for approximately 20 minutes.
(These also freeze well!)
Crush the graham crackers in the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan. Pour the melted oleo over and mix with the crumbs and sugar. Press into the bottom of the pan.
Soften the cream cheese and whip.
Mix in the powdered sugar and whipped cream or whipped topping.
Spread over crumb crust.
Pour the pie filling over the cream cheese mixture.
Sprinkle a few cracker crumbs on the top and chill overnight.
Mix meat, milk, bread crumbs and garlic salt with a fork.
Pat mixture evenly in bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate or 8 x 8-inch pan firmly.
Spread tomato paste over meat mixture.
Drain mushrooms.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over paste, then mushrooms, then oregano and grated cheese.
Lay Mozzarella cheese over top of pie.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 5.
Nice with a salad.
Spread beef with 2 tablespoons of softened butter.
Bake in 425° oven for 15 minutes or until filet is brown all over.
Remove from oven and allow to cool completely.
Reserve pan juices.
Chop onion and mushrooms into fine pieces.
Saute in 2 tablespoons butter until tender.
Cook the liquid down and cool.
(Both of these may be done the night before.)
Combine all ingredients except cheese.
Put in a casserole dish a layer of meat, cheese and meat.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Melt margarine in medium saucepan.
Chop celery and onion finely and saute in margarine.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1/2 to 1-inch cubes; add to pan.
Add spices and just barely cover with water.
Cover and boil for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add canned milk, reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent scorching.
Cream shortening and margarine with sugar.
Add egg yolks, one at a time.
Beat well. Add flour and baking soda alternately with buttermilk.
Add vanilla, coconut and nuts; fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake in two or three 8 x 8 x 2-inch layers at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Chop eggs, crab meat, onion, cabbage, and greens. Mix everything together. Add mayonnaise.
Mix the graham crackers and 6 tablespoons melted oleo into pan.
In bowl mix cake mix with margarine and half or evaporated milk.
Using electric mixer blend at low speed.
Batter will be stiff.
In saucepan over medium heat or in 1 to 2-quart container in microwave, melt caramels with remaining 1/3 cup evaporated milk, stirring frequently on stove or twice during microwave melting.
Keep warm.
Place half of cake batter into ungreased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Spread evenly.
Bake at 350° for 6 minutes.
Let cool 2 minutes.
Dribble melted caramel over top carefully.
Sprinkle chocolate chips and nuts evenly over caramels.
Drop remaining cake mixture by spoonfuls all over surface, spreading together carefully with spatula.
Return to oven and bake 18 to 20 minutes. Let cool in pan at least 15 minutes before cutting into bars. Makes about 24 (2 1/4 inch square) brownies.
Heat tomato soup.
Add lemon jello.
Beat cottage cheese until smaller consistency.
Add vinegar and mayonnaise to cottage cheese.
Chop onion and celery into small pieces.
Add the cottage cheese, vegetable and shrimp to soup.
Pour into serving dish.

Saute crumbled sausage, mushrooms, onions, salt and pepper. Drain well on paper towels. Combine eggs and sour cream in blender for 1 minute. Pour eggs in greased 7 1/2 x 11 1/2-inch baking dish. Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes until set in middle. Spoon hot sauce over eggs and add sausage mixture. Layer the 3 cheeses, beginning with the Velveeta. Casserole may be refrigerated or frozen at this point and baked later. Bake, uncovered, at 300° for 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and let set for 5 to 10 minutes before cutting and serving. Serves 6 to 8.
Mix well and put in pan to cook.
Beat eggs; add melted butter, syrup, corn and seasoning.
Pour into buttered baking dish.
Bake 1 hour at 375°.
Eat while hot (it falls).
In large skillet, cook beef until lightly browned.
Add onion and green pepper, cook until tender.
Drain fat, add remaining ingredients.
Mix well, bring to a boil. Cover and simmer 35 minutes, stirring once until rice is done.
Mix together all ingredients; then add 1 teaspoon lemon and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Mix well.
Put vanilla wafers in bottom of cupcake papers.
Fill 3/4 full; bake and then cool.
Top with whipped cream after cooled.
Mix crushed Oreos and butter.
Reserve 1/3 of the Oreo mixture.
Spread remaining mixture in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Slice ice cream and place on top of crumbs.
Pour Hershey's syrup over the ice cream.
Spread Cool Whip over syrup. Sprinkle with reserved Oreo mixture. Freeze.
Cook all vegetables until done.
Brown meat in skillet.
Add meat and stew mix.
Simmer 15 minutes then add barbecue sauce. Add as much water as desired.
Sliced okra can be added if desired.
Fresh vegetables may be substituted.
Saute bacon and diced onion into large saucepan.
Add milk, red pepper, potato and corn.
Let cook on medium heat until it thickens.
Let it simmer until ready to eat.
Cook celery, onion and pepper in small amount of oil until tender.
Add tomato sauce, seasonings and mushrooms.
Pour over chicken and bake at 350° until chicken is done, about 1 hour.
Prepare dinner as directed on package, except use only 1/2 cup milk.
Add cottage cheese and celery, mix lightly.
Spoon into 10 x 6-inch baking dish.
Arrange sausage links on top of dinner mixture.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Combine peas and water.
Bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Cover and let set for 1 hour.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to boiling point.
Reduce heat and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours or until peas look creamed and ham hock is tender. Remove ham hock.
Trim meat from bone and dice.
Return meat to soup.
Heat thoroughly and serve.
Additional water or milk may be added to soup for a thinner consistency.
In small bowl, combine cream cheese and sugar together; stir in mayonnaise.
Fold in cranberries, pineapple and pecans.
Fold in whipped cream.
Freeze in loaf pan.
When ready to serve, let sit 15 minutes.
Cut into slices, or scoop out into fancy dishes. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients and bake at 350° until top is browned.
Combine taco mix with refried beans.
Spread out in a circle on a glass plate.
Layer remaining ingredients in order given. Garnish with taco chips (make a circle).
Mix the cream cheese and sour cream and place in bottom of dish.
Place salsa on top.
Shred lettuce and put on salsa. Place on top of lettuce, cheese, olives and tomatoes.
(Leave tomatoes whole or cut in half.)
Serve with corn chips.
Combine undrained pineapple, thawed whipped topping and pudding mix.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Cut cake lengthwise in thirds. Drizzle with liqueur.
Spread 1/3 of pudding mixture over bottom layer of cake.
Top with second layer.
Repeat layering with pudding.
Chill 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with toasted, sliced almonds.
Serves 12.
Brown meat in hot skillet and drain.
Add pork and beans, tomatoes and salt.
Pour half the mixture in a baking dish, add layer of sliced onion and cover with remaining beef mixture.
Top with strips of bacon and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
In a large bowl mix pudding crushed pineapples.
Add cool whip and marchmallows.
Mix well and chill before serving.
Keep refrigerated.
Serves 8 to 10.
Simmer the chopped onion, celery and parsley in 1 tablespoon butter.
Do not let it brown.
Then mix the crab meat, bread crumbs and chopped eggs together.
Add to the mixture 1/2 tablespoon red pepper and 1/4 tablespoon salt.
Cook beef and onion in large pan until beef is browned and onion is tender.
Stir in 3 cans condensed soup, beans, water, celery, Worcestershire sauce and oregano.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
This makes a large amount and is very good warmed over and freezes well.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Brown beef and drain.
Combine all ingredients except onions. Pour into greased 2-quart casserole dish and cover.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In skillet, brown slowly
in
salad oil, one fryer, cut up. Place in 12 x 8
x
2-inch
baking dish.
To skillet, add onion and celery; cook until tender.
Add catsup, water, lemon juice, brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and prepared mustard. Simmer 15 minutes
and
skim
off
excess fat.
Pour over chicken. Bake, uncovered, at
for
1/4 hours or until done, basting 3 or 4 times.
Serves 4.
Mix all ingredients together (except chicken).
Take 2 pounds chicken pieces and make slits on the sides.
Pour marinade over chicken and mix well.
Marinate at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to
350°.	Trim
crust
from the bread and roll very thin.	Cream together the egg yolk, cream cheese and sugar. Spread the	mixture
on bread and roll up.	In a separate bowl mix the
brown
sugar	and
cinnamon.	Dip rolls in butter, then in sugar
and	cinnamon mixture.
Place rolls on well-greased cookie sheet.
Freeze
for
5 to 10 minutes.
Cut into thirds.
Refreeze in	plastic
bags
until ready to use. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook vegetables as directed.
Make stuffing.
Mix all together and bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Combine in top of double boiler the brown sugar, white sugar and oleo.
After this is heated and mixed well, take off and cool. Add the remaining ingredients.
Bake in greased and floured 8-inch square pan for 30 minutes at 325°.
Cool before cutting.
Preheat oven and baking sheet to 400°. Partially bake pie crust for 10 minutes; cool. Reduce oven temperature to 350°. Brown ground chuck and onion in a skillet; drain fat.
Stir in taco seasoning mix and a little bit of water.

Combine refried beans and 1/2 cup taco sauce in a mixing bowl. Layer 1/2 meat mixture in bottom of pie shell, then half of bean mixture. Sprinkle cheese on top. Bake 25 minutes. Remove from oven; cool, then top with lettuce, tomatoes and sauce. Makes 6 servings.
To prepare the rice, follow instructions on the rice box. Saute onions in melted butter.
Season fish to taste with McCormick Season-All salt, Goya adobo all-purpose seasoning and Sazon Goya. Bake until tender at 400°.
Mix fried onion and cooked rice together.
Place in pan or dish.
Place baked fish on top.
Combine beef, bread crumbs, milk and seasonings.
Place 1 tablespoon of mixture onto palm of hand.
Flatten.
Place an olive in center of meat.
Mold meat around olive.
Place 1 dozen on shallow baking dish.
Cook in microwave oven 3 minutes.
Insert a wooden toothpick into each meat ball before or after cooking time 3 minutes (for 1 dozen).
Mix all ingredients, except for the pecans, stirring well. Make into a ball and chill in the refrigerator.
When cold, roll in pecans.
Serve with your choice of crackers or bagels.
Slice eggs in half lengthwise and remove yolks.
Position knife blade in food processor bowl.
Add yolks, cream cheese and remaining ingredients.
Process until smooth, stopping once to scrape down sides.
Spoon or pipe into egg whites.
Heat all ingredients except carrots in a saucepan until all ingredients are dissolved.
Cool.
Pour over carrots and refrigerate.
Keeps at least two weeks.
Wash potatoes.
Dry.
Do not peel.
Cut into wedges.
Pour mixture over potatoes and toss until potatoes are covered with mixture.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 400°.
Combine cranberries, apple and sugar.
Dissolve jello in hot water; add syrup.
Chill until partially set.
Add cranberry/apple mixture, grape halves and nuts.
Chill until firm.
Serve on sliced pineapple and lettuce leaf.
Soak mustard and vinegar 12 hours, covered.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook in double boiler for 10 to 25 minutes.
Beat until custard consistency.
Makes 2 cups.
Grease a 9 x 10-inch pan.
Mix soft butter and sugar until crumbly (electric beater).
Add melted chocolate; beat until well blended.
Add 3 eggs; beat until almost smooth.
With wooden spoon, beat in vanilla.
Add sifted flour and salt and remaining egg; beat well.
Add nuts.
Pour into pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Do not overbake!
Bon appetit!
Mash squash.
Add onion, soup, sour cream, carrot, salt and pepper.
Butter casserole; sprinkle layer of crumbs in bottom. Add squash mixture.
Cover with crumbs and generous dots of butter on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Crumble bread into large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients and stir.
If mixture is dry, add mayonnaise.
Place in refrigerator 2 to 3 hours to chill.
Bring sugar, water and syrup to a boil.
Add peanuts and food coloring.
Cook until hard ball stage.
Remove from heat; add butter and salt.
Beat until mixture turns cloudy.
Spoon out on waxed paper.
Prepare carrots and cut into small slices.
Boil in water with salt and white sugar until tender; drain.
Melt butter in saucepan with brown sugar and orange juice.
Bring to a boil; add carrots. Do not overcook.
On one slice of bread, put mustard, bologna, American cheese, onion and pickles.
On the other piece of bread, put mayonnaise, ham, Swiss cheese, lettuce and tomatoes.
Cut in half.
Serve with corn chips and dip.
Place apples in greased dish; sprinkle with lemon juice. Blend dry ingredients; combine with butter.
Sprinkle crumb mixture over apples.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes or until apples are tender.
Yield:
6 servings.
Sift flour in bowl.
With spoon, mix in Crisco and milk.
Just before kneading, add cheese and mix until thoroughly kneaded, using extra flour as needed.
Roll out to about 1/2 inch and cut out or make small biscuits by hand.
Place on greased baking sheet and bake at 500° for 10 minutes.
Mix first 4 ingredients; press into a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Mix remaining ingredients; add to crust.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Mix sugar and flour.
Do not use mixer.
In a saucepan put margarine, water, shortening and cocoa.
Bring to boil and pour over flour mixture.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Add to batter and blend thoroughly.
Cook 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350° to 375°.
Use a 9-inch pie pan.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into pie pan.
Bake for 20 to 40 minutes until brown.
Boil first 2 ingredients 1 minute.
Add the peanut butter (I prefer crunchy) and butter or margarine; stir well.
Pour over 3 1/2 cups corn flakes, stir well and add another 3 to 3 1/2 cups corn flakes.
Put in buttered pan, press lightly and cut in squares.
Wash turkey thoroughly; pat dry.
Season with salt, pepper and/or garlic salt.
Place turkey in oven cooking bag in pan, breast side up, add 1 cup of hot melted butter and water in cavity and 1 cup of water to the inside of cooking bag.
(Following directions for cooking bag.)
Cook in 325° oven until meat begins to loosen from leg.
(22 pounds, approximately 6 hours and 12 pounds, approximately 2 to 3 hours)
Cook spaghetti; drain and rinse.
Combine diced cucumber, pepper and chopped onion.
Add 3/4 jar salad seasoning, 2 diced tomatoes and 16 ounce bottle Italian dressing; mix well.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.

Combine wine and sugar in large saucepan.
Bring to boiling, stirring.
Bring until sugar dissolves.
Lower heat; add pears.
Cover.
Simmer 10 minutes or until tender but still firm.
Let pears cool in syrup. Refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Drain pears.
Blend 2/3 of sauce with cream cheese.
Pat down in pie pan. Top with remaining fudge sauce and nuts.
Cut apples in wedges for dipping.

Simmer all ingredients (except orange juice) for 20 minutes in a large Dutch oven. Add orange juice. Strain and discard spices. Serve hot in punch cups or mugs. Makes 4 quarts or 32 (4-ounce) servings.
Layer.
Bake at 350° or until bubbly.
Add the first 5 items; simmer until potatoes are tender.
Add beans; simmer until soup and beans are hot.
Good cooked all day in a slow cooker.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Shape ground beef into 4 patties.
Brush both sides of patties with soy sauce mixture. Grill to desired doneness.
Top each burger with Cheddar cheese. Cook until cheese is melted.
Serve on buns and top as desired. Recipe may be doubled or tripled.
First cover bottom of pan with tomato sauce completely.
Then add ground meat and cheese.
Cover with lasagna noodles (about 4). To start the second layer cover the noodles with tomato sauce, meat and cheese.
Repeat this process until you have run out of meat, cheese and noodles.
All seasonings and vegetables are to be cooked with meat.
Your top layer should be covered with meat, cheese and plenty of sauce so the noodles won't get hard.
Cover and bake at 450° for 45 minutes or until cheese is melted thoroughly.
Feeds 6 to 8 people.
Peel carrots; cut in fourths lengthwise.
Place in heavy skillet and add remaining ingredients.
Cover and cook over low heat, turning often, until tender and glazed.
Cook 2 chickens; cool.
Cut up.
Cook spaghetti in chicken broth, leaving broth even with spaghetti.
Mix ingredients together except Parmesan cheese and add to spaghetti.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch greased baking dish and top with desired amount of Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes or until casserole is bubbly.
Peel, boil and then drain potatoes.
Mash with Carnation milk, margarine, salt and pepper.
Put in a large baking dish. Brown hamburger and onion and drain. Add ketchup, salt and pepper.
Put hamburger in "well" you have made in middle of mashed potatoes. Bake in preheated 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together until smoothly mixed.
In a 9 x 13-inch cake pan, melt 1/2 cup margarine.
When melted, pour in the egg mixture.
Bake in oven at 450°
for 35 minutes.
Serve with syrup, cinnamon sugar or powdered sugar.
Line oven dish with potatoes.
Spread cheese and bacon on potatoes.
Dot butter evenly over.
Pour milk, salt and pepper. Repeat layers until potatoes are used.
End with bacon-cheese layer.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes or until tender.
Partially freeze steak, then slice across grain into 2 x 1/4-inch strips.
Dredge steak in flour.
Melt butter in a large skillet.
Add meat and onion; cook until meat is browned.
Stir in consomme, soup, mushrooms, salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes, or until meat is tender. Stir in sour cream; cook just until thoroughly heated.
Serve over noodles.
Yields 8 servings.
With mixer, blend cream cheese, confectioners sugar and butter.
In another large mixing bowl, blend milk, pudding and Cool Whip.
Blend the two mixtures together.
Crush the bag of Oreos.
In desired serving dish, layer cookies and pudding mixture.
*Your choice of variety: ham, salami, bologna, spiced luncheon meat.
Melt butter.
Mix butter, sugar and syrup together.
Beat eggs separate.
Add eggs to sugar mixture.
Stir, then add coconut. Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
In a large pot, melt butter.
Add onions and simmer until onions are soft.
Add shredded cabbage.
Salt and pepper to taste. Simmer, covered, stirring occasionally about 45 minutes or until cabbage is very tender.
Add brown sugar.
Mix thoroughly.
Add prepared noodles.
(Depending on your taste as little or as much noodles can be added to cooked cabbage.)
Clean mushrooms; break out stems (set aside).
Place caps on cookie sheet.
In large bowl, place stick of butter and melt in microwave for approximately 1 minute.
Add finely chopped mushroom stems, fresh peppers, onion and black pepper; mix.
Microwave on High for 5 minutes.
Remove; add crushed Ritz cracker crumbs.
Mix well and stuff caps.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Enjoy.
Brown meat with onion, place in bottom of casserole dish. Place cooked potatoes on top of meat.
Place cheese on top of potatoes.
Pour mushroom soup over mixture.
Separate biscuits and place biscuits on top.
Cook until biscuits are brown and casserole is hot and bubbly.
(Amount of each ingredient depends on number of servings needed.)
Heat olive oil in deep 12-inch skillet and saute garlic until tender, but do not burn.
Cut tomatoes into small chunks and add to skillet. Add basil, oregano, parsley, salt and pepper and bring to a low boil for 3 minutes.
Add wine and cook on moderate heat for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand for 15 minutes. Serve over 1 pound of pasta.
Mix all together, then baste turkey.
Set 2 days in refrigerator.
Deep fry in peanut oil 3 1/2 minutes/lb. at 375°.
In a saucepan, bring rhubarb and water to a boil.
Remove from the heat.
Add gelatin and stir until dissolved; cool.
Stir in sliced strawberries; chill until it begins to thicken.
Prepare whipped topping according to package directions; fold half into rhubarb mixture.
Pour into crust.
Chill 2 hours or until firm. Top with remaining whipped topping and whole strawberries.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Set oven to 375°.
Beat eggs slightly in 2-quart bowl.
Stir in sugar, corn syrup, melted butter and pecans.
Pour into unbaked shell.
Bake near center of oven 35 to 40 minutes or until filling is slightly firm. Center of pie may look soft when pie is gently shaken, but will become firm when cool.
Sift flour and baking powder into bowl.
Cut in butter, cheese and red pepper as for pie crust using a pastry blender or 2 knives.
Add water and mix well.
Fill cookie press, using star plate.
Form straw on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for approximately 8 to 10 minutes in a preheated 375° oven.
Remove from cookie sheet immediately to cooling rack.
Chop fine the onions, pepper and garlic.
In saucepan, saute veggies in small amount of oil; add sausage.
Cook, mashing finely to separate.
Cook until done, drain off grease good and add Pizza Quick.
Mix well and cook 10 minutes.
Set aside.
Take rolls from package and slice into 4 or 5 slices each.
Place on cookie tin and put about 1/2 teaspoon pizza mixture on each slice.
Smooth to edge of bread.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
After cookie tin is filled with pizzas, place in hot oven at 400° or broiler to melt cheese.
Remove from oven and serve hot or cold.

recipes.t: Boiled Raisin Cake(My Mother'S Recipe, Mrs.  Granville Carey)
d: Combine the shortening, salt, water, raisins and sugar. Add the
nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves and allspice.
Boil mixture for
5 minutes;
cool.
Add together, then mix with the raisin mixture, the
vinegar
and baking soda.
Add the flour.
Bake for about 1 hour.
Brown meat and add seasonings; set aside.
In separate pan, cook onion in small amount of margarine (or spray).
Add tomatoes, soups, milk and chilies to onion.
Line a greased 9 x 13-inch casserole pan with tortilla pieces (enough to cover bottom), then add a layer of soup mixture, a layer of cheese and a layer of meat.
Add another layer of tortillas and continue layering ingredients until all are used.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix catsup, sugar, vinegar and onions.
Pour over ham.
Bake 1 hour in oven, until hot.
Could be heated on top of stove also. Serve on buns.
Pick over the arugula and discard any tough stems.
Rinse well and shake off excess moisture.
Core tomatoes and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Put all the ingredients into a salad bowl.
Toss well and serve.
Makes 4 servings.
First Layer:
Mix the flour, oleo, sugar and nuts.
Press into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool.
*Kasseri cheese may be purchased at R. Hirts Eastern Market in Detroit.
Or ask your butcher to order it.
Brown pork chops in oil.
Combine catsup, water, honey and steak seasoning.
Pour over chops.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes, turning chops once.
This sauce is also good for outdoor cooking.
Makes 4 servings.
For extra spicy, increase poultry seasoning to 1/2 teaspoon and black pepper to 2 teaspoons.
Cut butter into flour until resembles coarse meal.
Stir 1/2 cup nuts into flour mixture.
Press pecan mixture into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Combine cream cheese and powdered sugar; beat until fluffy.
Fold 1 cup whipped topping
into cream cheese mixture.
Spread over crust. Chill. Combine pudding mix and milk at low speed.
Spread over cream cheese.
Spread
remaining
whipped
topping
on pudding. Sprinkle with pecans or walnuts.
Yields 15 servings.
Mix first 6 ingredients together well. Shape into balls, placing 1 cube of Mozzarella cheese in the center of each.
Coat meatballs with flour.
Brown in frying pan. Spoon off grease.
Add pizza sauce.
Reduce heat to a simmer and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Cool cooked spaghetti by running cold water over it.
Add all remaining ingredients and mix.
Serve chilled.

Bake pie shell according to directions. Place bananas in bottom of crust. Mix Dream Whip and cream cheese until smooth. Pour over bananas. Let chill until firm, then pour pie filling on top. Keep chilled.
Mix cheese, sugars and peanuts well to form dip.
Slice apples thin and arrange around the dip.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add to a casserole dish; bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Spoon onto bread, buns or favorite crackers.
Heat oven to 350°.
Layer chili, corn and cheese.
Put crushed chips on top.
Mix Cool Whip and milk together.
Fold in lemon juice.
Drain oranges; cut oranges in small pieces and fold into mixture.
Pour into pie shell.
Cook lasagne noodles according to package directions. Mash the potatoes.
Add cheese to the potatoes and beat with mixer.
Saute onion in margarine until soft. Add 1/3 of the onion and margarine to the potato mixture and salt to taste. Generously butter a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Place a layer of lasagne noodles in dish, then a layer of potato mixture. Repeat, ending with noodles.
Pour butter and onion over all.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° until heated through.
Saute first three ingredients.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 1 hour.
Serves 6.
Brown onion and hamburger together.
Add other ingredients and stir.
Pour into casserole dish.
Bake for 30 minutes at 425°.
Remove all fat from roast and put roast in slow cooker. Combine all remaining ingredients except bread and pour over roast. Add water to almost cover roast.
Cover and cook on low for 10 to 12 hours or until tender.
Remove meat from broth; reserve broth. Shred meat with a fork.
Cut rolls in halves, spread with butter and grill until brown.
Place meat on rolls; dip in reserved broth while eating.
Note: I use 1 teaspoon baking powder.
Prepare gravy according to package directions; stir in horseradish and mushrooms.
Set aside.
Heat a heavy, nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Add steaks and cook 1 minute on each side.
Steaks will be rare.
Place in a lightly greased 1 quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour gravy over steaks; bake at 350° uncovered, for 15 minutes or until desired degree of doneness.
Garnish, if desired.
Cream butter, peanut butter and sugar.
Add eggs and cream for 5 minutes.
Add vanilla.
Mix dry ingredients together.
Add buttermilk alternating with dry ingredients.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan at 325° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cut crust off 3 slices of bread.
Spread cheese between each slice and top.
Cut in quarters.
Spread on side of each.
Put toothpicks in each one and put on cookie sheet and freeze.
When frozen, put in plastic bag and keep until needed.
Cook frozen for 20 minutes at 350°.
Mix flour and
1/2 cup sugar until smooth and there are no lumps in
flour.
Add
milk,
margarine and egg yolks; cook over medium heat until
it
begins
to thicken.
Add chocolate syrup and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Pour
in baked pie shell.
Beat the 3 egg whites with
cup
sugar until stiff peaks form. Put on top of filling and bake at 300° until golden brown.
Melt cheese in crock-pot on low heat.
While cheese is melting, brown meat and drain.
When cheese is melted, add picante sauce and meat to crock-pot.
Cook on low heat for about 30 minutes.
Mixture can be kept warm in crock-pot for as long as needed.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Mix potatoes, soup, salt, pepper and onion.
Pour in greased baking dish.
Bake at 350° until potatoes are tender.
Add grated cheese and bake until cheese is melted.
Combine butter and sugar; cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and sour cream, mixing well.
Combine next 5 ingredients and add to batter; mix well.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Put beans in large bowl.
Brown in skillet the hamburger seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic and chopped peppers and chopped onions; drain grease off.
Add to beans.
Pour in tomato soup and mustard.
Stir and put in big baking dish.
You can use whatever amount of beans you need.
Bake at 350° until desired doneness.
Add ingredients together and put into baking dish.
Add broccoli, onion, raisins and bacon to a bowl. Mix mayo, sugar, vinegar and lemon juice. Pour over mixture in bowl.
Brown meat and onion; drain.
Add tomato sauce and remaining ingredients, except noodles and cheeses. Simmer 15 minutes. Cook noodles until tender.
Layer 3 noodles and half of the hamburger mixture.
Sprinkle with half of each cheese.
Repeat.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Form into balls.
Roll in sesame seed. Eat!!
Mix all ingredients into a food processor and mix until smooth.
Refrigerate for several hours. Serve on crackers, pita bread, or raw vegetables.
Mix all together and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Mix all of the ingredients (except margarine) in a glass bowl. Place the margarine on top of the mixture.
Microwave on High for 2 minutes.
Stir until smooth.
Press into a small baking dish. Refrigerate until cold and firm.
Prepare cornbread mix (with eggs and milk); add celery and onion.
Bake 15 minutes at 450°.
Crumble cooked cornbread mix in large bowl.
Add reserved broth, salt, pepper, bread and seasoning.
Stir in chopped egg.
Spoon half of mix into greased shallow dish, spreading evenly.
Arrange chicken pieces on top. Spread on remaining dressing.
Top with soup and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Use sugar-free gelatin, lite cottage cheese and low-fat mayonnaise to reduce calorie count.
In a shallow 10-inch baking dish, combine gelatin with water, stirring until completely dissolved.
Stir in remaining ingredients until well blended. Chill until firm and serve on lettuce leaves.
Serves 6 to 8.
Saute squash and onion in butter until tender.
Stir in corn, salt, pepper, garlic and paprika; mix well.
Spoon mixture into casserole dish.
Top with croutons or bread crumbs and grated cheese.
Bake at 300° for 30 minutes.
Mix margarine, peanut butter and sugars until creamy.
Add water, vanilla, eggs, soft flour and soda.
Add to creamed mixture.
Mix in chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Allow to cool slightly before removing from pan.
Cool further on wire rack.
Cream
shortening
and	sugars.
Add
eggs and vanilla. Beat well.
Add flour, cinnamon, ginger and cloves.
Mix well. Add oatmeal and mix.
Add nuts and chips.
Mix well.
Bake 10 minutes in a 350° oven.
Put sugar and cornstarch in large shallow pan.
Stir, mixing well.
Add vinegar, cloves, ketchup, oil, salt and vanilla.
Stir again well.
Add beet juice from can.
Cut beets into bite size and put into pan.
Cook over medium fire 3 minutes, stirring constantly until it thickens.
Serve over rice.
In small saucepan, combine all ingredients, except Cheddar cheese.
Cook over low heat, stirring until cream cheese is melted.
Add Cheddar cheese and stir until melted.
Serve warm with vegetables and/or bread sticks.
Makes 1 3/4 cups.
Cut cake into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Arrange half the slices on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
In large mixer bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk and water; mix well.
Add pudding mix and beat until blended.
Chill 5 minutes.
Stir in extract; fold in whipped cream.
Pour half the cream mixture over cake slices; arrange half the peach slices on top.
Repeat layers, ending with some peach slices for garnish.
Chill 4 hours or until set.
Cut into squares to serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Pour 7-Up in pan and boil.
Pour over jello and cheese.
Stir until dissolved.
Cool until jello begins to thicken.
Fold in pineapple, Dream Whip and nuts.
Pour into mold and refrigerate until firm.
Makes 8 servings.
Beat eggs gently (don't overbeat).
Add sugar, salt, nutmeg and vanilla; blend.
Add cubed bread, cookies or cake; stir. Place saucer on pudding for few minutes so dry ingredients don't float and soak up liquid.
Cook in top of double boiler with water barely simmering; cook until table knife stuck in center comes out clean.
Serve with scoop of ice cream for each serving.
Combine and place in a greased 9x13-inch pan.
Over the top sprinkle 1 box of yellow cake mix.
Drizzle over that, one cube of melted butter and the chopped pecans.
Gently press the pecans into the mixture.
Place thawed potatoes in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Mix together next 6 ingredients and spoon over potatoes.
Top with crushed corn flakes and drizzle with butter.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 12.
Melt chocolate; set aside to cool.
Cream margarine.
Gradually add 2 cups sugar, beating well.
Add 3 eggs, beating well after each.
Stir melted chocolate into margarine mixture.
Add flour, salt, pecans and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Set aside.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Make 3 hamburger patties.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes, carrots and onions.
Tear off 3 big pieces of foil.
In the center of each piece, put a hamburger patty, potatoes, carrots, onions, salt and pepper.
Bring 4 corners of foil up and fold edges.
Will resemble a Hershey's Kiss.
Put on cookie sheet and bake for 1 hour at 375°.
Serves 3.
Combine all ingredients.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan for 45 minutes at 350°.
Bring Jell-O, water and soup to a boil and set aside to cool. Stir rest of ingredients into Jell-O mixture.
Pour into mold or in flat cake pan.
Chill.
Serves 10 to 12.
Mix oleo, nuts and flour together.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Cool.
Mix together cream cheese, powdered sugar, and 1 cup Cool Whip.
Spread on cooked, cooled crust.
Mix 2 packages of pudding and 4 cups cold milk.
Spread this layer.
Top with remaining Cool Whip.
Freeze until served.
Cook broccoli 8 minutes.
Make sauce using cheese, butter, milk, salt and pepper.
In baking dish, place a layer of crackers, a layer of broccoli and then pour some sauce.
Repeat until all ingredients are used.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, except ice, in electric blender. Process until smooth.
Add ice; process until frothy.
Serves 4.
Sprinkle pecans and coconut in buttered 9 x 13-inch pan. Prepare cake mix as per package directions.
Spoon over nuts and coconut.
Combine remaining ingredients in mixer bowl until smooth.
Spoon evenly over cake, leaving 1-inch edge.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Cream cheese mixture will sink to bottom to form frosting.
Cool in pan.
Cut into squares.
Makes 16 servings.
Mix thoroughly.
Divide in 4 balls, roll each into roll and wrap in foil.
Refrigerate 24 hours.
Bake at 325° for 2 hours. Puncture foil so fat can drip out.
Slice thin and serve on crackers or sandwiches.
Marinate first 4 ingredients at least 2 hours.
Add to desired amounts of lettuce and fresh spinach just before serving.
Follow directions on package of meat marinade except replace water with 4 ounces wine; increase oil amount to 4 ounces.
Add wine vinegar and minced garlic.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Scrub potatoes and make shallow slits around the middle as if you were cutting them in half lengthwise. Bake until done 45 to 60 minutes, depending on size.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Put fish in flat casserole dish. Saute onion and green pepper; add tomatoes, ginger and spices; boil.
Spoon over fish.
Bake 30 minutes or until just done. Don't overcook.
Serve with rice.
Preheat oven to 425° F (220° C).
Combine all ingredients except chicken in a small bowl.
Blend well.
Dip chicken pieces in batter and place on a baking sheet.
Bake, uncovered, 40 to 50 minutes, until golden brown and tender.
Or, if desired, dip chicken pieces in batter then fry in hot oil.
Completely
thaw
pork	butt.
Preheat	oven
to
375°. Slice pork
butt in four sections about halfway through, then rub
down with
salt	and liquid smoke.
Wrap with a piece of banana leaf, then in ti-leaves.	Wrap tightly with foil; place in
a
baking pan.
Bake for 2 hours, then lower heat to 350° and
bake
another 2	hours.	Delicious
by
itself
or
with cabbage!
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cook noodles according to package; drain.
In large skillet, brown meat and stir in tomatoes and salt.
Heat through.
Combine with noodles; put into a 3-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Pour peaches and juice in baking dish. Cover with bread. Mix sugar, butter and eggs and pour over peaches and bread. Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.

In a skillet, cook bacon over medium heat for 5 minutes or until partially cooked; drain on paper towels. Roll out dough to 1/2 inch thickness; brush with 1 Tbsp. oil. cut into 1 inch pieces; place in a large bowl. Add the bacon, cheese, dressing mix and remaining oil; toss to coat. Arrange pieces in a 9
X 5 inch oval on a greased baking sheet, layering as needed. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 30 minutes. Cover with foil; bake 5 to 10 minutes longer or until golden brown.
Place peaches with juice in baking dish.
Mix sugar, flour, salt and baking powder with fork.
Add beaten egg.
Spread over fruit.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Top with whipped cream or ice cream.
To hot, drained spinach, add Tabasco, salt, butter and cream cheese that has been softened with milk.
Stir until butter has melted and ingredients are blended.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Add eggs and oil until moist. Do not beat.
Stir in vanilla, pineapple, 2 cups bananas and walnuts.
Spoon batter into three 9-inch greased and floured cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool in pan 10 minutes. Remove from pans to cooling rack to finish cooling.
Frost when completely cool.
Mix cottage cheese and jello.
Add pineapple and Cool Whip. Refrigerate.
Melt butter in 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Pour melted butter into bowl with all other ingredients and mix.
Pour back into casserole dish; bake at 400° until lightly browned, about 40 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Broil drumettes 20-25 minutes. Combine margarine, hot sauce & vinegar in saucepan. Heat until melted and blended.
Add chicken. Toss to coat evenly.
Put 1/2 the noodles on bottom of casserole.
Layer chicken, mushrooms, onions, celery and water chestnuts.
Mix chicken soup, mushroom soup and milk.
Pour over mixture.
Top with remaining noodles.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
Serves 8 to 10.
This cake keeps well and is very moist.
Place ribs in a large heavy pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and simmer gently until tender.
Place in pan and baste with sauce.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes, basting frequently.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix sugars, peanut butter, margarine and vanilla.
Beat in water and egg.
Mix in flour, soda and salt. Stir in peanuts and candies.
Spread dough in a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake until light brown, 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool and cut into bars.
Spread cookie dough on round pizza pan.
Bake until done, slightly brown.
Let cool.
Cream together cream cheese and sugar, then blend in Cool Whip.
Put fruit in a ring around on top until you get to center.
Chill one hour.
Saute onion in shortening; add seasonings and chicken and saute about 10 minutes. Add water, cover and simmer slowly until chicken is tender.*
Add sour cream to pan and mix well. Heat through and serve with mashed potatoes or dumplings. Serves 4.
Do not overcook noodles.
Use bacon drippings; fry noodles and saute onions.
Add tomato pieces.
Scramble eggs.
Add to noodle and onion mixture.
You may add frozen peas.
Mix ingredients in order named.
Spread it thin on a greased and floured pan.
Bake at 375° until done, not allowing the edges to become hard.
Cut into 1-inch squares and roll between your palms into ball shapes. When cool, ice each and roll thickly in shredded coconut.
Drain and wash all the beans and the corn.
Finely chop the peppers, onion and celery.
Mix all ingredients together.
Add the sugar, vinegar and dressing.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine water, butter and sugar.
Cook until butter melts and mixes with other ingredients.
Stir in pecans.
Cut biscuits into quarters.
Stir and coat each quarter in mixture.
Bake in tube pan at 400° until biscuits are done.
Cook and stir meat, onion and pepper until meat is brown and onion is tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients, except spaghetti. Cover; simmer 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Cream together eggs and sugar; add zucchini, oil and vanilla. Sift flour, baking powder, cinnamon, baking soda and salt into wet ingredients.
Cook at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine chiles, sour cream and salt. Spread 1 cup cooked rice in a 2-quart casserole.
Top with a layer of 1/3 of the sour cream mixture, then 1/3 of the cheese.
Repeat layers.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes longer. Makes 6 servings.
Combine the first 4 ingredients in saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Pour over sugar, flour and marshmallows in bowl; stir until marshmallows melt.
Stir in remaining ingredients; mix well.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes, or until cake tests done.
Cool in pan.
Spread Coca-Cola Frosting over top of cake.
Combine milk, chuck, crackers, onion, salt and cheese in a mixing bowl; mix well.
Cut hamburger buns in half.
Toast lightly.
Spread meat mixture evenly over top of each bun.
Cook sausage; crumble and set aside.
Separate dinner rolls and arrange in oblong pan; press sides together to form crust. Bake at 375° for 5 minutes.
Crust will be puffy.
Reduce oven temperature to 350°.
Spoon sausage over dough; sprinkle with cheese.
Mix pie mix, eggs, sugar and milk; pour into cake pan. Sprinkle dry cake mix over the pumpkin mixture.
Pour melted butter over cake mix; top with pecans.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Slice the tomatoes 1/2-inch thick.
Do not peel or core. Drain well between paper toweling until most of the moisture of the tomatoes is absorbed.
Beat the eggs until light.
Mix in cornmeal, water, chives, salt and pepper.
Dissolve jello in 1 1/2 c. hot water.
When cool add strawberries, which have been thawed, and lemon juice.
Whip cream and add to mixture.
Put a layer of mixture in bottom of pan. Break cake into small chunks.
Alternate layers of cake and mixture until all is used.
Chill.
Slice and serve with whipped cream.
Season tomato juice to	your
liking
with
seasonings. Melt gelatin in small amount of tomato juice over medium heat. Mix with remainder of juices
and
grated
onion.
When
this mixture begins to congeal, add
sliced
or	chopped olives and celery. Slice in squares when
congealed.
I add more gelatin (about 2 teaspoons).
It slices
or	unmolds better.
Yield: 2 Pyrex dishes, 10 x 6-inches.

Place rhubarb in a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Sprinkle with the gelatin, sugar and marshmallows. Prepare cake mix according to package directions. Pour batter over marshmallows. Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes. Invert cake onto a serving platter. Serve with whipped topping, if desired. Yield: 12 to 16 servings.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Place sweet potatoes in large mixer bowl and beat until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients except egg whites; blend until smooth.
Beat egg whites in small mixer bowl with clean beaters at medium speed until stiff but not dry.

Spread in greased jelly roll pan (11 x 16-inch) and bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.

Bake in a tube pan at 325° for at least an hour.

Butter baking dish.

Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.

Spread evenly over top.

Add broccoli; stir until thawed.

Cover and let stand five minutes.

Cover each with topping of crushed corn flakes and other stick of melted margarine.
