Slit top crust and brush with egg, if desired.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes. Cool 10 minutes before serving.
Mix sugar, Milnot and oleo together and cook until mixture comes to a boil, stirring frequently.
Boil for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in chocolate chips and Marshmallow Creme.
Stir ingredients until mixture is creamy and smooth.
Pour into a buttered 9 x 9-inch pan.
Allow to cool and cut as desired.
Makes 2 1/2 pounds.
Mix
all ingredients except milk with soup.
Make small patties and roll in flour.	Brown patties in skillet and place in baking
pan.
Pour	soup
and
milk
mixture
over	top
of patties.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In large bowl, cream first 3 ingredients.
Add the rest of ingredients to first 3 and hand mix well.
Pour into 8 x 8-inch pan.
Bake at 350° 40 minutes.
Recipe may be doubled and bake in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Heat fat from chicken or butter.
Add onions and celery and cook just a little.
Add flour, pepper and sage.
Cut up boiled egg and add.
Add meat of chicken or you can use liver.
Cook until thickens.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in refrigerator to firm up. Make into a ball and roll in pecans.
Melt chocolate in double boiler.
Then add 3 cups crushed potato chips to chocolate.
Add pecans.
Drop on wax paper to cool.
Crust:
Mix butter, flour and nuts.
Pat firmly in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes at 325°.
Cool.
Boil chicken breasts; cut up in medium pieces.
Set aside. Reserve broth from chicken.
Put dry rice into a large, covered, heavy baking pan.
Add the soup to the broth and mix well.
Put cut up chicken on top of the dry rice.
Add all other ingredients and pour broth and soup mixture over the rice.
Bake for 1 hour or until rice and chicken is tender.
In a skillet over medium-high heat cook beef or chicken and garlic until browned.
Add onion; cook 5 minutes, stirring often. Stir
in
soup, water and soy sauce.
Heat to boiling. Add broccoli.
Reduce
heat,
cover
and simmer until desired doneness of broccoli.
Serve over noodles.
Brown hamburger, drain grease.
Combine all ingredients.
Cook on low for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Mix the first 2 ingredients for 2 minutes on medium speed or until thick.
Add the Cool Whip. Mix until well blended.
Add the marshmallows.
Layer in bowl as follows:
layer of pudding mix, layer of vanilla wafers, layer of bananas.
Repeat until all pudding mixture is gone.
It's good to start with pudding mix and end with it on top. Sprinkle top with vanilla wafer crumbs.
Saute garlic and oil, pour clam juice in with garlic and oil, put cubed potatoes in and when almost cooked, put clams in and then parsley and milk.
Cook a few minutes longer.
Cook zucchini and onion with margarine for 10 minutes, stirring.
Stir in parsley, salt and pepper, basil and oregano. Beat eggs with Muenster cheese.
Add zucchini mixture with eggs. Mix well and place in pie shell.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes in 370° oven.
Cool 5 to 10 minutes.
Spray a large pan.
Place 1/2 gallon of vanilla ice cream in a bowl to soften.
Crush 2 sleeves of crackers.
Add sugar and stick of melted oleo.
Mix together and press in bottom of pan.
Mix softened ice cream with 1 cup milk and 3 boxes coconut cream instant pudding.
Spread over the crust - Freeze for 4 hours.
Top with Cool Whip and toasted coconut (optional).
May be refrozen.
In a large bowl, beat eggs.
Add sour cream.
Stir in sugar, 1 tablespoon of flour, vanilla and salt; mix well.
Stir in apples. Pour into pie shells.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Barbecue chicken on grill; don't cook completely.
Chop chicken up into bite size pieces.
Cook noodles; combine chicken, celery, onion and soup.
Place in greased casserole dish.
Top with cheese, followed by cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° just to heat through (approximately 30 minutes).
Serves 4 to 6.
Grease 13 x 9-inch Pyrex dish.
Line bottom of dish with white bread.
Brown sausage; drain.
Spoon sausage over bread; sprinkle with a lot of grated sharp cheese.
Beat eggs and milk together; pour into baking dish.
Cover with aluminum foil; refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 or 40 minutes.
Soften cream cheese until smooth.
Add pineapple, pepper, onion, nuts and salt.
Roll in nuts and parsley.
Wrap in waxed paper and refrigerate.
Beat 1st three ingredients
well.
Blend others.
Place in unbaked pie shells.
Bake at
350° for 40 minutes in 9-inch deep pie shell.
Season the lobster pieces with salt, white pepper and paprika.
Melt 2 ounces of the butter in a saucepan.
Fry the lobster pieces gently about 2 minutes.
Add the brandy and the sherry.
Let simmer until liquid is reduced by half.
Add cream. Let simmer again until creamy.
Add remaining butter ( do not allow the lobster to boil while adding butter).
Rectify seasoning.
Serve over freshly made toast.
Serves 8 to 10.
Bake cake as directed in 9 x 13-inch pan; cool cake.
Crumble 1/2 of cake in punch bowl.
Mix pudding with milk, as directed on box.
Spread 1/2 pudding on crumbled cake in bowl.
Drain pineapple and put 1/2 pineapple over mixture in bowl.
Spread 1 bag glaze on pineapple, begin with outside edge (needs to be touching sides of bowl to look pretty from outside).
Next layer, spread 1 cup Cool Whip.
Repeat layers beginning with cake.
Last layer, use rest of Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with nuts and maraschino cherries, as desired.
In a medium saucepan, place celery, onion, carrot, potato, garlic, salt, curry powder and 1 cup of the chicken broth.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, until vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
Pour half of the vegetable mixture into blender and blend until smooth.
Remove and repeat with remaining vegetable mixture.
Return all the pureed vegetable mixture to the saucepan.
Add condensed skim milk and chicken broth to make desired consistency. Heat only until hot.
Do not boil.
Do not drain fruit.
Mix fruit and instant pudding. Fold in the Cool Whip and add the miniature marshmallows. Chill before serving.
Mix eggs (or Egg Mates), pumpkin, salt, sugar, ginger, cinnamon and cloves together.
Pour into pan.
Sprinkle dry cake mix on top.
Drizzle melted butter substitute over mix.
Top with chopped nuts.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cut into squares desired number of squares while still warm.
Thinly slice angel food cake.
Place on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place blueberry pie filling over cake.
Beat instant pudding with 3/4 cup milk.
Add and fold in sour cream and Cool Whip.
Mix until smooth.
Place cream mixture over blueberries and refrigerate.
Always a hit!
Arrange chicken pieces in lightly buttered baking dish.
Top with sliced cheese.
Combine soup and wine.
Spoon sauce over chicken.
Sprinkle with stuffing mix.
Drizzle butter over crumbs. Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Fill an 8 or 9-inch pan 3/4 full of sliced apples.
In a bowl, combine sugar, flour and baking powder.
Add the beaten egg and stir to form crumbs.
Melt oleo and pour over top.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Make a sauce by adding butter, flour and salt.
Add cheese and cook over slow heat until melted.
Pour
off liquid from can of vegetables and place in casserole dish.
Pour sauce over vegetables and bake 40 minutes in 375° oven.
Heat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease and flour round pans (8-inch or 9-inch).
Drain peaches, saving juice.
Add enough water to juice to make 1 1/4 cups.
Prepare cake mix using the juice water mixture.
Bake and cool as directed.
Cut peaches into small pieces.
Mix yogurt, topping and peaches together.
Use as icing between layers of cake on on top.
Brown sausage.
Drain and remove from pan.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Put meats back in pan and add cubed Velveeta cheese. Stir over low heat until cheese melts; add spices and stir again. Spread on party rye.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In small bowl, combine chicken and 2 tablespoons cheese.
Separate crescent dough into 8 triangles. Place about 3 tablespoons chicken mixture on wide end of each. Roll up, start at shortest side; roll to opposite side.
In medium saucepan, combine soup, milk and 1/4 cup cheese.
Heat until cheese melts.
Pour half of soup mixture into ungreased 8 or 9-inch pan (reserve remaining soup mixture for sauce).
Arrange filled crescents over hot soup mixture.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden brown.
Sprinkle with remaining tablespoon of cheese.
Return to oven for 5 to 10 minutes, until cheese is melted.
Serve with remaining sauce.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Cook and drain squash.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Mix sour cream, soup and onion in a small bowl.
In another bowl, pour melted butter over dressing; mix well.
Alternate layers (2) of squash, soup and dressing in casserole dish.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Cook noodles, uncovered, in boiling water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Combine soup, milk, water and Cheddar cheese in 3-quart saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until cheese melts and sauce is hot; stir constantly.
Stir in cooked noodles, turkey, peas, carrots and pimento.
Spoon mixture into greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Mix all ingredients (except peppers).
Chop peppers (with rubber gloves on) and add to mix.
Stir well and bake in well-greased pan at 350° for 1 hour or so.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Beat in eggs.
Beat in 1 cup of the apples.
Add dry ingredients.
Fold in remaining 3 cups apples and nuts.
Place in large greased pan such as broiler pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Blend onion, celery and bell pepper.
Saute in butter until clear.
Add crab meat, cream cheese, red pepper and salt.
Serve hot.
Combine all ingredients and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt butter in large skillet.
Add remaining ingredients; cover.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes or until squash is tender, stirring occasionally.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine all ingredients.
Bake in a greased 13x9 pan at 350 for 40-45 minutes.
Cook rice and broccoli according to package directions.
Cube the cheese.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours in 2-quart casserole.
Mix all together in bowl.
Do not beat.
Put in small muffin tins with liners.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cut and mix fruit, add nuts and 2 cups flour; mix well. Separate
eggs
and
beat
whites and yolks well.
Mix butter, sugar
and	both
parts
of egg together.
Mix 2 cups of flour into
this.
Add
cake
mixture and fruit mixture together and mix well.
Pour in greased pan and bake at 250° for 3 hours.
Combine sugar, flour, salt and nutmeg.
Add fruit, mixing well.
Let stand for 20 minutes.
Spoon into pie crust and dot with butter.
Put on top crust.
Bake at 400° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Brown ground beef.
Add onion, catsup, water, brown sugar, celery, vinegar, dry mustard, Worcestershire sauce and salt and pepper.
Mix together.
Serve on warm hamburger buns.
Line an
x	13-inch cookie sheet with aluminum foil and spray with vegetable oil spray.
Place 36 saltines side by side. Boil
sticks
butter
and
brown sugar for 3 minutes (watch clock).
Pour
mixture over saltines and bake 7 minutes at 350°. Remove
from
oven	immediately
and while hot, pour chocolate morsels
over and spread with a knife.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Cut or break into pieces.

Boil egg noodles until tender. Put 3/4 of noodles on the bottom of a casserole dish. Layer chicken, peas and soup on top of noodles. Lay cheese slices on top of last layer. Put remaining noodles on top of cheese. Cover.
Drain beans.
Save 2 or 3 slices bacon for garnish and crumble remaining 4 or 5 slices.
In a large bowl, mix beans with crumbled bacon, condensed soup, mushrooms, soup mix and oregano.
Mix all ingredients as usual.
Combine jello and water first. Use 12 x 8 x 2-inch Pyrex pan.
Put half of strawberry mixture in pan.
Refrigerate until set.
Spread top with sour cream.
Spread remainder of jello mixture.
Refrigerate.
Soften cream cheese and blend with milk, juice and 2 tablespoons Cool Whip.
Pour into pie crust.
Top with 8 ounce container of Cool Whip and chill.
Heat oven to 350°.
Cut each baked potato lengthwise into halves; scoop out centers, leaving 1/2-inch border.
Reserve pulp for another use.
Brush halves with 2 tablespoons of the butter. Arrange potatoes on cookie sheet and place in preheated oven. Bake until shells are hot, 5 to 7 minutes.
While potatoes are baking, cut chicken breasts in halves.
Flatten each half by pounding between 2 pieces of waxed paper.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat; add chicken, herbs, salt and pepper.
Cook until chicken is golden, 3 to 4 minutes on each side.
Cut chicken into 1/2-inch strips. Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the cheese into each potato half; top each with 1/4 of the chicken and 1 tablespoon cheese.
Bake until cheese melts, about 5 minutes longer.
Serve hot.

recipes.t: Scrabble Mix(You'Ll Never Want To Eat Store Bought Chex Mix Again!!)
d: Combine dry cereals, pretzels and nuts in large roasting pan. In small saucepan, slowly heat butter and bacon drippings until melted.
Add Worcestershire and Tabasco sauces and blend.
Pour over cereal mixture.
With a rubber spatula, gently stir ingredients to distribute the butter mixture.
In small dish, combine the seasonings and sprinkle over cereal mixture.
Again, stir gently to distribute all ingredients.
Toast in slow over 250 degrees for 1 hour.
During the hour, remove from oven every 15 minutes and stir.
Cool.
Store in tin canisters.
Combine ingredients and add enough milk to make 1 gallon. Freeze in ice cream freezer.
Mix, form into loaf in baking dish.
Bake at 375° to 400° for about an hour.
Add sugar, soda, butter, dates and nuts.
Pour boiling water over ingredients and let stand 5 minutes.
When cool, add remaining ingredients.
Pour into a greased bread pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Freezes well.
Whip together sweet potatoes, pineapple, egg, butter, salt and cinnamon.
Swirl in cranberry sauce.
Spoon into greased 8 x 8-inch dish.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.

recipes.t: Blueberry Nut Bread(My All Time Favorite)
d: Sift together dry ingredients. Stir to mix. Set aside.
In another larger bowl, beat together eggs and oil. Stir in blueberries.
Stir in dry ingredients only until moistened (do not overmix).
Pour batter into 2 or 3 well-greased bread pans. Bake in preheated 350° oven approximately 50 minutes or until tests done with knife inserted in center that comes out clean.
Let cool.
Immediately upon shredding raw potatoes, put in salted ice water; let stand 15 minutes.
Drain thoroughly and add sugar and milk.
Turn into a long baking dish.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and dot with bits of margarine.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until done.
Mix all ingredients together; pour into greased baking dish. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Cream the shortening and peanut butter together, gradually beating in the sugar, egg, vanilla and milk.
Add the dry ingredients that have been mixed together.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto a cookie sheet.
Indent the center of each cookie with your thumb.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes. When cookies come out of the oven, place a Kiss in the center of each cookie.
Mix together thoroughly.
Store in airtight container.
Place strawberries in a large bowl and set aside. Mix sugar, cornstarch and water in sauce pan.
Cook until thickened, remove from heat, stir in gelatin until dissolved.
Pour over berries, mix well. Pour into pie shell, refrigerate until set.
Top with whipped cream if desired.
Mix potatoes, 1/3 cup melted margarine, sour cream, onion, salt, pepper, soup and cheese.
Put in large casserole dish.
Mix 1/3 cup melted margarine and dressing mix; pour on top evenly. Bake in 375° oven for 20 minutes or until golden on top.

recipes.t: Rouladen(A Beautiful Make Ahead For A Buffet; I Serve This At Christmas.)
d: Have meat cutter cut roast (across grain) into wafer thin slices.
Put meat and Italian dressing in Ziploc bag.
Marinate overnight, turning several times.
Remove meat; discard marinade. Flatten each slice of beef and place several pieces of carrot and celery on beef.
Roll up and secure with toothpick.
Place in Ziploc bag containing about 1/3 cup flour; shake to coat meat evenly.
Put sausage and meat roll-ups in a 300° electric frypan or large Dutch oven.
Brown all meat, then add remaining ingredients.
Simmer for 2 to 3 hours.
Serve with noodles or potatoes.
Layer in an 8 x 8-inch pan.
Do not stir.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Brown ground beef, stirring until crumbly.
Add garlic, onion and green pepper.
Cook until tender, stirring frequently.
Drain excess fat.
Stir in pepperoni, mushrooms and spaghetti sauce.
Mix all ingredients together and beat well. Bake at 350° until done. This makes three 9-inch layers. Let completely cool before icing.
Dissolve baking soda in warm water.
Mix all ingredients together.
Roll into a log, approximately 1 1/2 inches in diameter.
Refrigerate overnight.
Slice thin.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cut chicken into pieces; cut up garlic and celery into small pieces.
Put in frying pan with margarine and brown.
Add 1 cup of wine vinegar, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat. Later, remove cover and let vinegar cook down until chicken is cooked.
Sprinkle bottom of pastry with 1 tablespoon each of sugar and flour.
Combine the remaining sugar and flour; stir in honey and cream.
Pour mixture over apples.
Mix gently until slices are well coated.
Spoon apples into pie shell.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg and dot with butter.
Bake at 425° for 45 minutes.
Cut top off bread and scoop inside out, leaving about 1-inch sides and bottom.
Fill with all ingredients (mixed) and place top back on.
Wrap in foil and bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Remove from oven and place on platter.
Remove foil and place pieces of bread around loaf.
Use to dip into mixture.
Cover refried beans with sour cream.
Drizzle with Ranch dressing.
Then drizzle with salsa to cover.
Cover with shredded lettuce.
Then sprinkle with onion, black olives and Cheddar cheese.
Layer in order listed.
Serve.
Whip all ingredients for 10 minutes.
Pour into graham cracker crust; refrigerate overnight.
Brown onion and garlic in butter.
Add crawfish and crab meat, 1/2 of bread crumbs, water and lemon juice.
Cook over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until liquid is absorbed.
While mixture simmers, line muffin tins with paper liners.
Heat oven to 450°, then fill muffin tins 3/4 full with mixture.
Top each cup with the remaining bread crumbs.
Place in hot oven for 5 to 8 minutes until top bread crumbs brown a bit.
Beat cream cheese, brown sugar and flour together until smooth.
Add eggs, one at a time, nuts and vanilla.
Set aside.
Mix cornstarch, sugar and salt in a saucepan.
Blend with 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Then add remaining water.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture boils.
Remove from heat, add remaining ingredients.
Makes 1 1/3 cups of sauce.
Serve on plain sheet cake or spice or etc.
Wash clams and cover in salted water.
Soak 15 minutes.
Drain and rinse.
Discard water and repeat.
Combine cake mix, melted butter and egg.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Place marshmallows on top and return to oven about 3 minutes until marshmallows puff up.

Preheat oven to 350°. Lightly coat an 8 x 8 baking dish with butter-flavored cooking spray. In a large mixing bowl, stir together soy flour, whole-wheat flour, Splenda, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. In a medium mixing bowl, combine canola oil, vanilla extract, egg whites, applesauce and water. Pour applesauce mixture into the flour mixture and stir just until well combined. Pour the brownie batter into a baking dish. Bake until edges spring back when you touch them gently (the center will be soft), about 15 minutes. Allow the brownies to cool and then cut into 12 pieces.
Beat egg yolks; add sugar, flour and baking powder.
Add nuts, dates and vanilla.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Bake in square pan; cut into squares while warm.
Put in a bag with powdered sugar and shake.
Preheat oven to 450.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl. Toss well.
Arrange potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
Sift flour, salt and soda.
Cream sugar and margarine; add eggs.
Add dry ingredients, buttermilk, nuts and bananas.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour in greased loaf pan.
Toss together.
Mix 1 cup salad dressing and 1 cup sour cream and add.
Combine sugar and water in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Pour sugar mixture into a 4 1/2-quart freezer container.
Stir in fruit juices and freeze until firm.
Remove from freezer several hours before serving (mixture should be slushy).
Stir in ginger ale.
Garnish with fruit slices.
Yield:
30 cups.
Melt butter
with
onion.
Mix	with all other ingredients, except
cracker
crumbs.
Put in 8 x 8-inch baking dish; sprinkle cracker crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Place 1 cup tomatoes in bottom of casserole. Cover with 1/3 of the bread crumbs and 1/4 cup cheese, then onion. Add remaining tomatoes, crumbs, cheese and onion. Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cook blueberries, sugar and water for 15 minutes.
Put berry mixture in square pan.
Sprinkle with corn flakes.
Pour butter over flakes.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Serves 4.
Insert 2 slices of almond into each date. Wrap with 1/3 slice bacon. Secure with toothpick. Bake at 350° until bacon is cooked.
Combine cream cheese and milk, stirring until spreading consistence.
Spread 1 scant teaspoon of cream cheese mixture on each slice of bread and roll tightly.
Wrap each rollups with bacon, securing with a toothpick.
Place rollups on a broiler pan; bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes, turning if necessary to prevent over browning.
Garnish with parsley, if desired.
Yields approximately 4 dozen.
Preheat oven to 225°.
Combine popcorn and nuts.
In saucepan, mix sugar, butter and corn syrup.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Cook until mixture turns caramel colored, about 280°. Remove from heat, stir in vanilla.
Place popcorn in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Carefully pour mixture over popcorn mixing well.
Turn out onto counter.
Quickly break into pieces.
Store in tightly covered container.
Yields 9 cups.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease a 12-inch pie plate or square dish is fine.
Mix Bisquick, water and beans.
Spread in dish.
Layer remaining ingredients on bean mixture, hamburger, salsa and cheese (in that order).
Bake 30 minutes.
Top with sour cream, lettuce, black olives, onions and diced tomatoes. Delicious!
Mix orange juice, sugar, lime juice and mint.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients; drop by spoonfuls in hot grease.
Fry until golden brown.
Mix in order as given.
Bake in greased iron skillet at 425° until done.
Cream butter; add sugar, vanilla and water.
Mix well.
Add flour and salt.
Mix well.
Add crushed nuts.
Shape into bite size balls.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet for 8 to 10 minutes at 325°.
When cool, roll in powdered sugar.
Melt butter in saucepan; add sugar, cocoa and milk.
Bring to a boil.
Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla, oats and peanut butter; mix well. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Cool.
Cook squash until tender; drain and mash.
Add cheese to squash while squash is hot.
Add all other ingredients to squash mixture.
If desired, saute onions and bell pepper in oleo until clear, then add to squash mixture.
Put mixture into buttered casserole dish and top with Ritz crackers.
Dot with butter or oil.
Put into preheated 350° oven and bake for 30 minutes.
Combine shortening, sugar and eggs. Add jam and mix well. Sift together dry ingredients and add alternately with buttermilk. Pour into layer pans and bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Boil chicken until done.
While chicken is boiling, mix Veg-All, cream of chicken soup and cheese.
When chicken gets done, let cool, then tear apart and add to vegetables.
Mix together; cover with cheese.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes. Serve with rolls.

recipes.t: Second Best Casserole In The World
d: Boil chicken; skin and debone.
Cut meat into bite size pieces.
Cook noodles in chicken broth; drain.
Combine chicken, noodles and remaining ingredients.
Put bread crumbs on top.
Pour melted butter over top.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Mix and let stand for 2 hours; then drain.
In medium saucepan, heat water and margarine.
When it starts to boil add flour.
Mix well.
Remove from heat.
Add eggs one at a time.
Pour into slightly greased 9x13 inch glass dish. Bake at 425° for 35-45 minutes.
Spread filling (recipe to follow) on top of crust.
Add Cool Whip on top of filling.
Drizzle with chocolate sauce.
Melt first 4 ingredients until smooth.
Add Rice Krispies and peanuts.
Press into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cut into squares.
Nougat - Step I:
Combine 3/4 cup sugar, 2/3 cup syrup and 1/4 cup water in 1 1/2-quart pan.
Stir over medium heat until sugar dissolves;
boil to 238° on candy thermometer.
Pour over beaten egg whites, beating constantly until slightly cooled, about 5 minutes.
Spoon into well-buttered bowl and make well in center. Let stand.
Cream sugar and Crisco. Add eggs and mix well. Add soda, salt, vanilla and sour cream; mix well. Gradually add flour using enough to make dough stiff. Chill overnight.
Bake at 350° until light brown, 8 to 12 minutes.
Cut up hard-boiled eggs.
Put all ingredients, except eggs, in blender.
Blend on high, adding pieces of eggs, one at a time. Blend until pudding is smooth and free of any lumps.
Cool in refrigerator and eat cold.
(Also great for freezing into popsicles.)
Brown
seasoned meat.
Make macaroni and cheese according
to directions
on
box.
Lastly,
combine
browned meat, macaroni and soup.
Pour into a casserole dish.
Lay slices of cheese over top. Heat
in
oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Let cool and enjoy.
Boil chicken, onions, salt and pepper until done.
Take chicken off bone; chop this up small.
Put back in broth.
Add remaining ingredients; cook real slow.
You can add cooked rice, but watch closely, because it will stick.
We add small diced potatoes.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Combine onion, ham, broth, water, sausage and potatoes.
Cook until potatoes are fork tender but not mushy.
Add bacon, garbanzo beans, black pepper, salt, and garlic butter.
Simmer for 30 to 35 minutes or until garbanzo beans are tender.
Stir occasionally. Makes 6 servings.
Put fruit in pie pan. Sprinkle with sugar.
Blend flour, salt, sugar, baking powder and egg.
Sprinkle over fruit.
Melt margarine.
Pour over top. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Grease 9 x 13 inch pan.
Place bread in pan as a liner in bottom.
Sprinkle cheese and sausage over.
Mix eggs, milk, salt, pepper and mustard.
Pour over bread, sausage and cheese.
Chill overnight.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
In medium saucepan, melt butter in water. Stir in dry frosting mix until smooth.
Heat over low heat for five minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in nuts.
Drop mixture by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Let stand until firm.
Combine sugar, corn syrup, water and salt in a 2-quart heavy saucepan.
Cook and stir over high heat until sugar is dissolved. Continue cooking without stirring over medium heat until syrup reaches the hard ball stage (255°).
Wipe away any sugar crystals that form on sides of pan.
Cook about 5 or 10 minutes after it boils.
Mix first 8 ingredients well. Place in ovenproof casserole. Garnish with almonds. Bake in 350° oven (uncovered) about 10 minutes or until warm. Serve warm with toast squares or crackers.
Completely cook chicken in Miracle Whip about 8 minutes.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat until cheese is melted.
Serve over hot cooked rice, if desired. Serves 4 to 6.
Fry bacon; drain and crumble.
In 2 tablespoons of bacon drippings, cook potatoes, onion, green pepper and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Pat mixture in bottom of skillet and cook 20 minutes until bottom is brown.
Combine flour, nuts and butter.
Spread in a 9 x 12-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Cool.
Gradually add granulated sugar to eggs mixing until well blended.
Stir in pumpkin.
Add combine dry ingredients; mix well. Spread batter evenly into lightly-oiled wax paper lined 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake at 350° for 14 minutes or until cake begins to pull away from sides of pan.
Loosen sides immediately; invert onto towel sprinkled with powdered sugar.
Carefully remove wax paper.
Roll up cake and towel starting at narrow end; cool on rack.
Butter Pyrex casserole.
Cover bottom of 8-inch square baking dish with chilies and top with cheese.
Pat hamburger in bottom of pan.
Salt and pepper it.
Slice onion thin over hamburger.
Put potato tots over onion.
Then spread soup over all.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Beat together until smooth.
Bake in two 8-inch layer pans or a 9 x 13-inch oblong pan at 350° for 40 minutes.
Frost immediately.
Work the shortening, peanut butter, sugar and eggs together with a spoon until fluffy and creamy, then add flour and baking powder.
Mix together real good, roll into balls and press on cooking sheet with a fork.
Put in oven at 375° until done.
Makes about 76 cookies.
Brown hamburger, drain off fat.
Add onions and cook until tender.
Stir and add remaining ingredients.
Heat until hot. Serve on bun, or as a coney sauce.
Bake cake in 3 layers following box directions. Cool.
Combine the remaining ingredients, except vanilla and cook until thick. Add vanilla. Cool slightly. Spread filling between layers. Frost with caramel frosting and garnish with plumped prunes.
In a blender combine banana, pineapple juice, sugar, and orange juice concentrate.
Cover and blend until smooth.
Pour into large freezer containers.
Stir in the 1 1/2 cups water and lemon juice.
Apply seal and freeze for six hours or until firm.
Crush graham crackers; cover the bottom of an 8 x 10-inch pan. Mix the softened margarine and 2 slightly beaten eggs.
Gradually add 1 cup of powdered sugar.
Spread the mixture over the crushed crackers.
Drain the pineapple and spread over the egg mixture. Cover the pineapple with Dream Whip.
Cover the Dream Whip with graham crackers for the top layer.
Chill and serve.
Melt butter and sugar and then add beaten egg yolks.
Add dry ingredients with milk.
Put in pie shell and bake at 325° for 45 to 60 minutes.
Put everything except cheese in food processor and mince.
Add cheese, then process.
Serve with French bread, Triscuits or crackers.
These muffins would be good on a holiday brunch menu.
Spray 9 x 13-inch casserole with Pam.
Spread 1 package of crescent rolls into casserole.
Top with thin slices of cheese (Swiss and Muenster).
Place potatoes and onion in a steamer over boiling water; steam until the potatoes are tender.
Remove skins and mash potatoes with cooked onion, yogurt, chives and beaten egg.
Spoon into a nonstick casserole dish.
Bake in a 350° oven for 20 minutes or until top is lightly brown.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix peas with mayonnaise and eggs.
Place cubed potatoes in baking dish.
Add enough to cover bottom of pan.
Sprinkle with chopped onion.
Sprinkle 1/2 package of Lipton soup mix.
Put pork chops on top of mixture.
Sprinkle chops with rest of soup mix.
In saucepan, heat mushroom soup and milk until warm.
Pour over pork chops and potatoes.
Cover with foil; bake for approximately 1 to 1 1/2 hours in a preheated oven at 300°.
Dissolve raspberry Jell-O in 1 cup boiling water.
Stir in cherry filling.
Pour into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Chill until partly set.
Dissolve lemon Jell-O in the other cup of boiling water. Beat cream cheese and mayonnaise together; gradually add lemon Jell-O.
Stir in undrained pineapple.
Chill until partly set. Fold Cool Whip and marshmallows into lemon mixture.
Spread on top of cherry mixture.
Top with nuts; chill until set.
Pack cucumbers in jars of course.
Wash good.
While filling jars put in some dill, a few pickling spices and alum.
Mix water, vinegar and salt.
Heat and pour over pickles while hot and seal. These are easy fixed and we all like them.
Cut the onion, tomato and avocados in rough chunks.
Mash them in bowl with a sturdy knife or fork, then add the remaining ingredients.
Thaw and drain spinach.
Place in greased casserole in alternate layers, the spinach, onion and mushrooms, adding a few shakes of salt and pepper as you go, then top this with the cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix thoroughly 1/2 cup soup, hamburger, onion, egg, bread crumbs, parsley and seasonings.
Press firmly into a 9-inch pie pan.
Bake for 25 minutes at 350°.
Spoon off fat.
Frost with potatoes.
Top with remaining soup and cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes, or until done.
Garnish with bacon.
Combine all ingredients and cook 20 minutes after boiling starts.
Seal while hot.
Stir flour, soda and spices
together.
Combine sugar, pulp, half of flour mixture and milk.
Add remaining flour, melted butter, vanilla and raisins.
Spread softened butter on bottom and sides of 1-quart baking dish.
Pour batter into dish and spread with a spatula.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Serve hot with whipped cream.
Place yams in baking dish and top with pineapple.
Sprinkle brown sugar and cinnamon over pineapple.
Use small amount of reserved pineapple juice to dissolve sugar; dot with butter.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes at 375°.
In a bowl, combine eggs, salt and baking powder.
Beat gradually, adding sugar and vanilla.
When mixture is thick and lemon colored, fold in sifted cake flour and coconut.
Bake in a jellyroll pan, 10 x 15 x 1-inch, which has been greased and the bottom lined with waxed paper and greased.
Bake in a hot oven (400°) for 12 to 13 minutes.
Turn out onto a towel that has been sprinkled with confectioners sugar.
Quickly remove the waxed paper and trim off the crisp edges.
Roll the cake, rolling the towel in the cake.
Let stand for 20 minutes; unroll.
Frost with a chocolate frosting or Coconut Whipped Cream.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt. Blend shortening and peanut butter in mixing bowl.
Gradually add brown sugar, creaming until light and fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla; beat well.
Blend in dry ingredients gradually; mix thoroughly. Shape into balls, using a rounded teaspoonful for each.
Roll balls in granulated sugar; place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for 8 minutes.
Top each cookie with a candy Kiss, pressing down until cookie cracks around edge.
Bake 2 to 5 minutes longer, until golden brown.
Yields about 36.
Grease 10 x 15-inch jelly roll pan.
Line with crescent roll strips.
Layer with meat, potatoes and cheese.
Combine eggs, milk and spices.
Pour over the top.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Combine sugar, butter, cocoa and milk.
Boil 1 1/2 minutes. Remove from heat and add remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper and let cool.
Store in airtight container.
Brown ground pork.
Then add each ingredient.
Stir after adding each ingredient.
Bring sugar and vinegar to a boil.
Pour over remaining ingredients.
Cook chicken breasts; cool and cut into chunks.
Mix mushroom soup, chicken soup, evaporated milk, mushrooms, chicken, celery, green pepper, pimento and almonds.
Put into casserole dish and cover with Chinese noodles.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cream vanilla, margarine, sugars and eggs.
Add flour, oatmeal, soda, baking powder and salt.
Fold in mashed bananas and nuts.
Spread batter in greased 11 x 15-inch cookie sheet pan. Bake at 350° until slightly browned and springs back to touch. Remove from oven and glaze.
In large saucepan, heat all ingredients to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Makes 10 servings (about 1 cup each).
Pound breasts slightly and dredge in flour mixed with seasonings.
Melt margarine in skillet; brown chicken on both sides.
Add 1 cup wine, cover and simmer 1/2 hour or until tender.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cut bread into 1-inch slices and lay in pan.
Beat eggs with milk, sugar, salt and vanilla.
Pour over bread.
Cover with foil and refrigerate.
Next day, uncover and dot with butter.
Bake at 350° until puffy and brown.
Serve with syrup.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Add milk, seasoning and cheese to slightly beaten eggs.
Turn mixture into greased baking dish.
Place in pan of hot water and bake in moderately slow oven (325°) for 20 to 25 minutes or until firm.
Remove from oven.
Let stand 3 minutes and unmold onto platter.
Serve with tomato sauce.
Peel and cut potatoes into cubes wash and drain. Put into a large pot. Add water, milk, salt, pepper and butter. Cook until done or tender. Add cheese and soups, stir until cheese is melted.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine graham cracker crumbs, sugar and margarine; mix well.
Pat onto bottom of 9 or 10-inch spring-form pan.
Set aside.
Mix all ingredients together in bowl and bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix and heat.
Pour over pork barbecue.
Boil water, lard, sugar and raisins until lard forms on top. Put soda in enough water to dissolve.
Add to mixture.
Add nuts and flour.
Bake at 350° until done (45 minutes to 1 hour).
In large bowl, combine oil, lemon juice, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper.
Add lamb cubes; turn to coat in marinade. Cover.
Refrigerate 2 hours or overnight.

recipes.t: Miss June'S To Die For Chocolate French Silk Pie
d: Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add melted chocolate, cocoa powder and vanilla; blend well.
Add 1 egg at a time, beating for 10 minutes after each addition (total 30 minutes).
Pour into shell and chill at least 4 hours.
Garnish with Cool Whip and toasted sliced almonds, if desired.
Saute onions in butter.
Add soup and milk, stirring to blend. Add other ingredients and heat; do not boil.
Boil chicken breasts until done, saving broth.
Chop onion, celery, and bell pepper.
Melt margarine, saute onion, celery, and bell pepper.
When vegetables are cooked until almost done, stir in bread crumbs and stir until moist.
Mix the soups together. Spray 2 1/2
or 3 quart casserole dish.
Put half of bread crumbs and vegetables in bottom of dish.
Put soups and chicken on top of this.
Put rest of crumbs on top.
Pour broth over all of it. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine first 3 ingredients in a large saucepan, bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and cook for 5 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.
Combine butter and next 4 ingredients in a large bowl, stir in cauliflower, 1 cup cheese, onion, chopped green pepper and tomatoes.
Spoon into a greased 13x9x2 inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Add remaining 1/2 cup cheese and bake 5 additional minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drip by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.

Soften
cream
cheese
to
room temperature and combine with drained
pineapple
and 1/2 cup pecans and green onions. Roll into
ball
and

Mix together corn, beans, soup, onion and cheese.
Pour into casserole dish.
Crumble crackers over the top, then pour melted butter over crackers.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine candies, sugar and water; bring to a boil.
Add Certo. Boil 1/2 minute.
Pour into sterilized jars.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Roll dough into small balls and place on cookie sheet.
Flatten each one with fork.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes at 325°.
Makes 30 to 40 cookies.
Mix oleo, brown sugar, corn syrup and pecans.
Spray 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add mixture in pan.
Prepare cake mix and pour over pecan mixture and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Great with ice cream!

Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine dry ingredients.
Add sour cream, eggs, corn and oil; stir to mix. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until center springs back when touched. Pour melted butter over corn bread.
Beat eggs.
Add ginger, nutmeg and cloves.
Mix with 2 quarts orange juice and lemon juice.
In punch bowl, put chunks of ice cream.
Slowly pour ginger ale down sides of bowl.
Gently stir in juice and egg mixture.

Mix in alternate layers cucumbers, salt and ice. Let stand for 3 hours. Drain, combine sugar, vinegar and spices. Heat to a boil. Add cucumbers and let them get hot. Pack, sterilized jars. Let syrup mixture continue boiling. Pour over cucumbers and seal. Makes about 6 pints.
Brown beef in Dutch oven in cooking oil.
Add 3 cups hot water, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for about 20 to 30 minutes (until beef is tender).
Add onion, bouquet sauce, bouillon cube and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer until onion is tender (about 10 minutes).
Shake cold water and flour in covered container; stir into beef mixture slowly.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute.
Prepare noodles or rice according to package directions.
Serve beef over the noodles or rice.
Place meat in a bowl with the next 3 ingredients.
Marinate 1 hour.
Heat margarine and oil in skillet. Stir in meat and sear. Add bouillon, coffee and water.
Simmer, covered, for 30 minutes. Blend flour in 1/2 cup water. Stir in skillet and thicken.
Serve over noodles or rice.
Skim excess fat from broth.
Add enough water to broth, if necessary, to measure 1 cup.
Mix flour and cold water until smooth.
Gradually stir into broth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until gravy is smooth and thickened.
Season with salt and pepper.

Melt margarine and cocoa together. Remove from heat. Stir in sugar and eggs. Mix well. Add flour, salt, nuts and vanilla. Mix well. Spoon into greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes. Sprinkle marshmallows on hot cake and cover with Chocolate Frosting when cake is cool.
Cook sweet potatoes until tender.
Cool and peel.
In large bowl, mash.
Add marmalade, sugar, orange juice and extract.
Beat until smooth.
In separate bowl, beat egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold into potato mixture.
Coat a 6-cup casserole with nonstick spray.
Add mixture; sprinkle with almonds.
Bake at 350° until puffy and set, about 40 minutes.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Put cherry pie filling in pan and crushed pineapple over that.
Sprinkle sugar over the pineapple, then yellow cake mix. Dot the top with 2 sticks margarine. Sprinkle pecan pieces over top of butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Boil one chicken; skin and debone it.
Cool and tear into bite size pieces.
Cook spaghetti in chicken broth saved from boiling chicken (add water if necessary).
Drain most of broth off spaghetti, but save it.
To spaghetti add chicken pieces, olives, pimentos (optional) and Cheez Whiz.
(I use an 8-ounce jar of regular Cheez Whiz and an 8-ounce jar of mild Mexican Cheez Whiz. You can use all of one if you want.)
Mix all together in a large dish.
This makes a lot.
Mix together soy sauce, oil, mustard, ginger, pepper and garlic.
Add chicken strips to mixture.
Marinate 1/2 hour, stirring frequently.
Place chicken and mixture in a shallow baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Baste every 10 minutes.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Add eggs and mix well.
Stir in bananas.
Sift dry ingredients and add to mixture.
Fold in pineapple, coconut, cherries and nuts.
Makes 3 loaves of bread. Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until done.
This will freeze good.

recipes.t: Outrageous Chocolate Chip Cookies(Yields About 2 Dozen)
d: Heat oven to 350°.
Beat sugars, margarine, peanut butter, vanilla and egg in medium bowl with wooden spoon until creamy and well blended.
Mix in flour, oats, baking soda and salt.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls, about 2-inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool 1 minute before removing from cookie sheet.
Remove stems from mushrooms and save for other uses.
Brush melted butter over mushroom caps, coating thoroughly.
Stir together remaining ingredients until well blended.
Place mushrooms, cavity side up, on large rimmed baking sheet.
Evenly mound filling into each mushroom, pressing it in lightly.
Broil about 6 inches below broiler until bubbly and lightly browned (about 3 minutes).
Serve warm with napkins.
Makes 10 stuffed mushrooms.
Can be doubled, tripled, etc., as is necessary.
They are so good, they won't last long.
Mix all ingredients well and pour into greased jelly roll pan. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Cool 5 minutes.
Use teaspoon to dip small portion and form small balls. Roll in powdered sugar.
Layer in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Mix in taco seasoning with sour cream.
Smash avocados; season with garlic salt.
Grate the cheese.
Spread ingredients in order as shown, then chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Mince garlic fine; add all other ingredients.
Cook sausage.
Drain well and crumble.
Spread each slice of bread with butter.
Cut into cubes.
Place bread cubes in a greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with sausage and top with cheese.
Mix together milk, sugar and salt; crumble into this mixture the yeast.
Stir until yeast is dissolved.
Stir in egg and shortening.
Mix in first with spoon, then by hand the flour.
Add flour in 2 additions, enough to make it easy to handle and soft as possible.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Let rise until double, punch down, turn over and let rise again.
Cut dough into pieces the size of walnuts.
Form into balls, roll each ball in melted butter, cinnamon, sugar and nuts.
Place 1 layer of balls in well-greased 9-inch pan.
Sprinkle with raisins.

Let rise 45 minutes.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.

Add meat and brown.

Preheat oven to 375°.
In large bowl of electric mixer, at low speed, cream peanut butter and vanilla.
Combine sugar and salt. Gradually add to peanut butter, creaming after each addition until fluffy.
With mixer at medium speed, add eggs gradually.
At low speed, blend in milk and beat until mixture is smooth.
Strain into unbaked pie shell.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, or until filling is set in center when pie is gently shaken.
Mix all ingredients.
Add milk to make batter to desired thickness.
Heat cooking oil or meat grease in a 9-inch pan. Sprinkle dash of corn meal in oil to prevent sticking.
Pour batter into pan and cook at 400° to 450°, about 30 minutes, until done.
Prepare spinach, tearing leaves into bite-size pieces and placing in a salad bowl. Add eggs, mushrooms and bacon.
Slice frozen muffins.
Put ingredients into separate cups or dishes.

Let children make their on pizza by spooning on sauce, cheeses and pepperoni. Put assembled pizza on cookie sheet and broil 2 to 3 minutes.
Let cool briefly.
Serve and enjoy.
May use pastry dough.
Cream the butter and sugar. Stir in carrots and egg. Add flour, baking powder, salt and rum flavoring. Drop on greased baking sheet. Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Frost immediately with confectioners sugar and orange juice mixed to a spreading consistency.
Brown ground beef and drain thoroughly.
Combine remaining ingredients and add ground beef.
Bring to a light boil, stirring occasionally.
Lower heat to a low simmer and cook for 45 minutes.
1. Place apples in heavy saucepan.
Add water to cover. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Mix well.
Use for marinating meat or as a barbecue sauce.

Drain and reserve syrup from pineapple.
Cut each pineapple slice in half; set aside.
In medium size bowl, mix brown sugar, water, cornstarch, vinegar, horseradish and reserved syrup from pineapple; set mixture aside.
Cut pork sausage meat into 1/4-inch slices.
With sharp knife, make a few slashes in each cocktail frankfurter.
In a 12-inch skillet over medium heat, cook sausage slices, a few at a time, until well browned, removing slices as they brown to paper towels to drain well.
Keep warm.
Pour off fat from skillet.
Sift in bowl flour, baking powder, salt and soda.
Add 1/2 cup nuts (optional).
Blend (in order) egg, milk, unpeeled orange, dates, shortening and sugar.
Blend well then add to dry ingredients.
Bake in greased loaf pan at 350° for 50 minutes. Slices better next day.
Serve with cream cheese mixed with powdered sugar and orange juice to taste.
Brown ground beef and drain off fat.
Let cool.
Set aside. Dice the green pepper and onion; set aside.
Wash lettuce and break into bite-sized pieces.
Add cheese, onion and green pepper to lettuce; mix.
Mix beans with ground beef separately.
Cook ground beef.
Add flour and 1/4 to 1/2 cup water.
Add chopped cabbage, onion, salt and pepper.
Cook 20 minutes, stirring often.
Take off heat.
Add sour cream.

Mix sugar, Crisco and eggs.
Sift in dry ingredients.
Add milk in.
Roll dough into balls (golf ball size).
Place on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Top with optional confectioners sugar and nuts.
In large serving bowl (clear one looks pretty), layer all vegetables.
All ingredients should be chopped or shredded. After all vegetables are in put a layer of mayonnaise over them, making sure to cover all vegetables.
Sprinkle sugar over mayonnaise and top with a layer of shredded cheese and crumbled bacon.
Let sit overnight and mix well before serving.

recipes.t: Spinach, Gorgonzola And Walnuts Over Fettuccine
d: Heat oil in large skillet.
Add garlic and cook over low heat 5 minutes.
Add spinach and cook over medium heat until limp, about 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in cheese and nuts. Add fettuccine and toss well to melt cheese into spinach and pasta.
Season well with pepper.
Makes 2 servings.
Sprinkle steaks with salt.
Press into cracker crumbs on both sides.
In a large frypan, brown coated steaks in butter, cooking about 5 minutes on each side.
Serve hot.
Makes 4 servings.
Drain cherries, reserving juice.
Cream butter and sugar; add egg yolks, sour cream and reserved juice.
Sift together flour, baking powder and baking soda and add to creamed mixture and mix well.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into batter.
Add cherries and nuts.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes in 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Mix ingredients
and
pour into well-greased casserole, 11 3/4 x 1 3/4-inches.
In a small bowl of mixer, beat cheese, milk and extract until well blended and fluffy. Stir in raisins.
Using ice cream scoop or 2 spoons, shape mixture into 4 balls.
Place on cut sides of pear halves.
Sprinkle with almonds. Serve at once.
* Can use lemon, strawberry, chocolate, orange, or any cake mix you desire; it's always good!

Add onions, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, red pepper and oil.
Cook until onions are tender.
Next add tomatoes (in juice), kidney beans and chili powder.
Simmer for 1 hour, stirring frequently.
Cream shortening and sugar and add eggs.
Dissolve baking soda in water.
Combine with salt, spices and molasses.
Add alternately with flour.

Cut in desired shapes.

Mix Coca-Cola and ketchup together.
Pour mixture over chicken.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer.
Let simmer until chicken is tender.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill in refrigerator for 3 to 4 hours.
Serve with salsa chips.
Combine all but the last 2 ingredients in a casserole.
Mix the corn flakes crumbs with 1/4 cup melted butter and spread over the potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.

Do not overcook. Drain at once in colander. Cool, peel and slice potatoes 1/4-inch thick into large flat pan.
Set aside.

Mix butter or oleo with cake mix (reserve 1 cup).
Put remaining mixture into 13 x 9 x 2-inch oblong pan, pressing all in bottom and 1/2 inch up edge.
Spread pie filling over the crust.
Blend chopped nuts and the reserved mixture. Sprinkle over top.
Bake 45 minutes.
Serve with ice cream.
Boil chicken until done.
Cut up in cubes.

Prepare noodles according to package directions.

Add spaghetti sauce. Bring to boil.
Remove from heat.
In 9 x 13-inch pan, layer sauce, noodles, cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with sauce.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top. Cover dish with foil and bake for
1 hour.
Let stand for 5 or 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot applesauce and add the remaining ingredients.
Mix well and put in refrigerator to chill.

Trim all fat and membrane from meat.
Cut meat into 1-inch cubes.
Put all ingredients in Dutch oven (covered).
Bake at 300° for 4 to 5 hours.
Check after 3 1/2 hours; if too dry, add water. After 4 1/2 to 5 hours use potato masher.
Meat should look like a spread.
Serve warm on bread.
Especially good on party rye.
Melt butter in sauce pan, add lemon juice, vinegar, catsup and Worcestershire sauce. Add salt, pepper, tabasco and red pepper to taste. Bring to boil. Pour over meat to be barbecued.
Saute onion and celery.
Add to bread and seasonings.
Add half of soup and water mixture.
Make into balls and bake 30 minutes, covered, at 350°. Add rest of soup mixture.
Bake, uncovered, 10 more minutes.

Remove from heat and add other ingredients.
Stir until well mixed.
Drop with teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Let set until hardened.
Store in container.
Cream the oleo and 1 cup brown sugar. Add 1 beaten egg and mix well. Add the flour.
Spread on jelly roll pan like pie crust. Beat 2 eggs and pour or brush evenly over crust.
Sprinkle 1 cup brown sugar over entire crust. Sprinkle the pecans on top. Bake at 350° until set and brown.
Pour liquid smoke over brisket; sprinkle both sides generously with celery, onion and garlic salts.
Wrap brisket in heavy foil and refrigerate overnight.
Cook peas according to package.
Pour into serving bowl; cover and set aside.
One 12 inch deep sided frying pan with lid.

Juice may be used without the sugar, particularly if you like a tart lemon flavor.

Chop fruit, and mix to your taste.
Mix eggs (well beaten), sugar, spices, salt and pumpkin.

Arrange top crust and seal.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serve hot in wedges.

cheese for topping.

Mix all ingredients together thoroughly with wet fingers. Roll into balls.

Mix cream cheese, milk and pudding mix with mixer and spread on cake.

Drain pineapple and spread over pudding mixture.

Sprinkle with nuts.
Store in refrigerator until ready to serve.

Cook hamburger meat.
Add sauce.
Mix the Italian seasoning, cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese.
Layer, starting with sauce and make sure noodles are covered.
Pour 1/4 cup water over mixture. Cook at 350°, covered, for 45 minutes, then uncover and cook for another 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Serve with crackers.

recipes.t: Apple Pie(1994 2Nd Place Perry County Fair Apple Pie Contest)
d: Mix sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in large bowl. Stir in apples.
Add lemon juice.
Pour into 9-inch unbaked pie crust.
Place top crust over filling.
Overlap crust one-inch beyond pie plate and fold and roll top edge under lower crust edge, pressing on rim to seal.
Cut slits in top crust for steam to escape.
Roll reserved pastry about 1/16-inch thick on lightly floured surface.
Cut into desired shapes.
Brush one side of pastry shapes with water.
Place shapes, moist side down, on edge and top of pie.
Mix egg yolk and one teaspoon water; brush over pie.
Bake in preheated 425° oven for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat and bake for approximately 30 minutes more, until crust is golden and apples are tender when tested with toothpick or cake tester. Remove from oven and cool.
Serves 8.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in greased 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Combine ingredients in order given.
Whisk until well blended. Refrigerate at least 12 hours before serving to let flavors blend.
Dressing is thin.
Add more mayonnaise if you want a thicker dressing.
Yield: About one quart.
Mix all together and top with buttered crackers.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.
*Italian Roma tomatoes also work well; split in half lengthwise.
Mix crackers margarine and sugar and press into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan.
Set aside.
Let Sherbet and ice cream soften and mix together.
Spread over the crust and freeze.
Mix sugar, lemon juice and butter together and cook on low heat until dissolved. Add a little of the hot mixture to 2 egg yolks.
Mix well and pour back into saucepan with other hot mixture.
Bring to a boil and cook one minute.
Cool thoroughly and spread over ice cream.
Serve with dollop of whipped cream and lime slice.
In medium bowl, toss sliced steak and cornstarch; set aside. In small bowl, blend water, steak sauce, soy sauce and garlic powder.
Set aside.
In an old skillet burn the brown sugar.
It will be bubbly and black looking on the top.
When it gets burnt pretty good add 1 1/2 cups hot water to the sugar.
Be careful and remove the skillet from the heat before adding the water.
It will still bubble over - so be careful.
Cool.
Cok onions and garlic in oil until tender.
Remove from heat. Add tomatoes and cornstarch.
Stir to dissolve.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened and translucent.
Add beans and basil.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Thaw and squeeze spinach dry. Add rest of ingredients.

In a bowl mix turkey, egg, thyme, milk and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well. Fold in instant potatoes. Take a heaping spoonful of mixture and roll in the palms of your hands to make balls. Add enough olive oil to the bottom of a frying pan to coat it. Arrange meatballs in pan and brown on all sides, turning frequently. Add turkey balls to your favorite sauce.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients; simmer about 10 minutes.
Serve with cheese straws while hot.
Delicious.
Beat eggs; gradually beat in sugar and oil.
Combine dry ingredients.
Alternate zucchini and dry ingredients into egg mixture.
Mix.
Stir in nuts and vanilla.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Makes 2 loaves.
Grease and flour pans.
Brown chops in frying pan and season.
Mix catsup and dry mustard together and spread on chops.
Combine vinegar, water and sugar; pour over chops.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
Wash the broccoli and cauliflower in cold water. Cut into bite sized pieces. Toss in olive oil. Sprinkle with garlic salt and lemon juice. Add in the olives.
Mix together.
Top with corn flake crumbs or crushed potato chips.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine sugar and oil.
Mix well.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Chill several hours or overnight.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan in preheated oven for 1 hour at 375°.
Cut in squares.
Cook zucchini for 10 minutes in salted water and drain.
Place in greased baking dish.
Melt butter.
Add flour and blend in tomatoes, green pepper, onion, brown sugar, bay leaf and cloves. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour over zucchini.
Top with crumbs and dot with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In large bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk and water. Add pudding mix and beat well.
Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped topping.
Layer pudding mixture, vanilla wafers and bananas until you have used up all the pudding and bananas.
Top with whipped topping.
Mix together and store in refrigerator at least overnight.
Remove stems from mushrooms.
Wipe caps and slice.
Saute mushrooms in butter with onion until golden.
Prepare asparagus (cooked) as usual; cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon butter and blend in flour.
When lightly browned, add cream.
Heat slowly, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Add sauteed mushrooms and onion; keep warm. Drain asparagus; place in dish.
Top with mushroom sauce.
Add a sprinkle of paprika, if desired.
Serves 8.
Cook noodles according to package.
Drain.
Cool in a single layer on wax paper.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Combine meat, eggs, bread crumbs, Mozzarella cheese, onions, oregano, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Fill each shell with 2 tablespoons meat. Spread a thin layer of sauce in the bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan. Put shells with the open side down in a single layer.
Cover with sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes 36 shells.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Beat in softened cream cheese and Sprite.
Chill until just beginning to set.
Add Cool Whip, salad dressing, sugar and vanilla.
Drain pineapple and add nuts and pineapple to jello mixture.
Chill until firm.
Lightly mash shrimp.
Add mayonnaise, catsup, horseradish, salt and m.s.g.
Blend well.
Stuff celery stalks.
Chill 1 hour. Cut in bite-size pieces.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat.
Blend in melted chocolate and vanilla; stir in flour and chopped nuts.
Pour batter into greased 8 x 8-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Test with toothpick.

Chop cabbage and onions. Break up noodles (reserve flavor packets for dressing). Toast noodles, seeds and nuts in a dry teflon pan until lightly browned. Cool. Mix ingredients together just prior to serving and tossing with dressing.
In cruet or bottle, combine all ingredients. Mix well, then chill. Serve on taco salad or Indian tacos. May add dry taco seasoning or Tabasco for extra zip.
Brown hamburger with onion in large fry pan.
Boil egg noodles for 10 minutes.
Drain.
Add soup and water to hamburger.
Add green beans and juice.
Mix in noodles, salt and pepper.
Pour in casserole dish, cover top with Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until cheese melts.

Cook sugar, vinegar and spices for 20 minutes. Drop in fruit a few at a time and cook until easily pricked with fork. Pack in hot sterilized jars. Add syrup to within 1/2 inch of top. Seal. Makes 6 pints.
Mix together first 8 ingredients and allow to rise.
Then cut dough into 12 pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball.
Make a 1-inch hole in the center of each ball, using a floured finger to form a ring shape.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 20 minutes.
Take eggs and add flour until it's a thick dough.
Meanwhile, boil the chicken and all remaining ingredients.
Roll out dough as thin as possible.
Cover with flour, then roll into a tight roll and put in the refrigerator.
Take out chicken, debone and put back into pot.
Take out roll of dough and slice into 1/4-inch sections.
Drop each noodle in pot one by one after unrolling them so they don't stick together.
When noodles turn white they are done.
Simmer for half an hour.
Melt and spread in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Let cool.

recipes.t: Gram'S Butternut Cookies(Note:  These Are The Cookies We All Remember.)
d: Mix all together except egg white and nuts.
Spread into two buttered pans, about 1/3-inch thick.
Brush with egg white and cover with nuts.
Bake at 350° until slightly golden at edges. Cut before it cools completely.
Make day before. Place in 9 x 11-inch pan in order listed.
No substitutions (no Miracle Whip or imitation bacon).
Refrigerate.
Mix together oleo, brown sugar and eggs.
Add rest of ingredients and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add the eggs.
Sift flour, soda, baking powder, salt and spices.
Mix the coffee and molasses.
Alternately add coffee mixture and flour mixture to the creamed mixture.
Roll to 1/2-inch thickness and cut.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Boil eggs; slice in half.
Beat egg yolks, mayonnaise, mustard and cheese until well blended.
Fold in finely chopped olives. Stuff eggs.
Refrigerate until party time.
Makes 24 stuffed eggs.
Spread biscuits on bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread sour cream over biscuits.
Brown hamburger with onion, Italian seasoning to taste, salt and pepper to taste.
Drain and pour over sour cream.
Add tomato sauce and top with Mozzarella cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix pie filling, pineapple and strawberries with juice and let chill.
Just before serving, add bananas and mix together.
Whip the cream; beat in honey gradually.
Stir in vanilla. Fold in remaining ingredients.
Chill.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Pour cabbage in bottom of dish.
Mix soup and milk together and pour on top of cabbage.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs and then butter.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Pound chops; salt and pepper both sides.
Beat egg(s).
Dip pork chops into flour, then egg, then bread crumbs, covering both sides.
Fry in hot oil until brown and crispy on both sides.
Put chops in roasting pan with water and a pat of butter on top of each pork chop.
Cover and bake about 1 hour at 350°.
Then uncover and bake for 30 minutes more.

recipes.t: Mrs. Clark'S Lemon Cheese Cake Filling
d: Mix all together in saucepan.
When mixture begins to boil, add the dissolved cornstarch and let cook until thick.
Let cool a few minutes before putting on any white cake layers.

Mix
egg,
meat
and
bread crumbs.
Shape into 4 dozen balls. Brown
meatballs
on
broiler
pan
under oven broiler turning once.
Place in large saucepan or Dutch oven.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over meatballs.	Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally to coat evenly.
Chill fruit, fruit juice, grenadine and 7-Up.
At serving time, combine crushed pineapple and strawberries in a punch bowl. Add pineapple juice and grenadine.
Slowly pour in chilled 7-Up. Add ice cubes.
Garnish punch bowl with curls of orange rind. Makes about 30 servings.

Beat with mixer until well blended. Pour into ice cream freezer container.
Add milk to fill the container.
Freeze according to manufacturer's directions.
Brown meat and onion in large skillet; drain.
Stir in water, catsup, mustard, salt and pepper.
Bring to boil.
Stir in rice. Cover; remove from heat.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Fluff with fork.
Top with cheese.
Cover; let stand for 3 minutes or until cheese melts.
Makes 4 servings.
In large skillet melt butter over medium heat.
Add mushrooms, onions, garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook until mushrooms are tender. Add green beans.
Cook 5 to 7 minutes or until heated through. Stir in cheese.
Serve hot.
Yields about 10 servings.
Cook ham as desired and set aside. Save ham broth.
In small strainer rinse raspberries, drain well.
Place berries in large mixing bowl. In small mixing bowl combine sugar, cornstarch and salt.
Add sugar mixture to berries.
Stir gently to coat berries.
Boil chicken in salted water; debone.
Pour chicken broth over Doritos to wet.
Layer Doritos in casserole.
Place chicken, except 1 cup, over Doritos.
Saute onion in margarine until tender.
Add soups and cup of chicken.
Pour on top of chicken. Add cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese melts.

Heat shortening in a saucepan.
Add onion, beef and salt. Cook slowly for 5 minutes occasionally.
Stir in chili powder, flour, tomatoes and water.
Cover and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours.
Stir occasionally.
Add more water, if needed.
Place chicken in a large baking dish.
Season with salt and pepper.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain the pineapple; reserve 2 tablespoons liquid.
Cream sugar and cream cheese until fluffy.
Beat in bananas and eggs.
Stir in baking mix and nuts.
Do not beat.
Pour into a greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes or until done.
Cover with foil the last 15 minutes.
Defrost spinach and squeeze out extra moisture. Mix eggs and cottage cheese. Add spinach to egg mixture. This is the filling.
Spray small casserole dish with Pam.
Place jalapeno peppers on bottom and side of dish.
Beat eggs (like preparing for scrambled eggs).
Pour over peppers and top with Cheddar cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until set.
Serve warm.
Combine cake mix, mandarin oranges, eggs and oil.
Beat 2 minutes at high speed of electric mixer; reduce speed to low and beat 1 minute.
Bake in 3 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool in pan 10 minutes. Remove and cool completely.
Put prepared stuffing in an 8-inch square pan.
Shred chicken and put on top of stuffing.
Layer on chopped broccoli.
Mix the mayonnaise, soup and cheese; pour on top of broccoli.
Crush Ritz crackers and put on top.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix all ingredients; bake, covered, 45 minutes at 350°.

Cook meat and grind.

Put in jars.
Cold pack 30 minutes or pressure to 10 pounds and turn off.
Heat oven to 350°.
In medium saucepot, cook pork chop, onion and peppers in olive oil over medium-high heat 7 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in remaining ingredients.
Transfer mixture to an 11 x 7-inch baking or casserole dish.
Bake 30 minutes or until beans are tender.
Makes 8 servings.
Mix and sift flour and baking powder.
Beat egg yolks, then add sugar and beat until thick.
Add water, lemon rind and lemon juice.
Stir in flour and then blueberries.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Turn into greased pudding mold and steam 1 hour over rapidly boiling salted water.
Serve with nutmeg or lemon sauce.
Makes approximately 6 servings.
Mix sour cream, cream cheese and sugar. Add balance of ingredients.
Mix well with mixer at medium speed.
Pour into graham cracker shell and bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes. Allow to cool, then top with cherry or strawberry pie filling, if desired.
Peel squash and slice.
Place in kettle with lemon juice, peel and pineapple.
Bring to boil.
Lower heat and simmer, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
Add pectin and peach jello and bring to boil. Stir in sugar and ginger at full rolling boil, stirring constantly. Sustain boil until the mixture jells.
Remove from heat; skim off foam.
Allow mixture to cool for 5 minutes.
Skim and ladle into hot sterilized jars.
Wipe jar rims; cover quickly with flat rings; screw bands tightly.
Invert jars 5 minutes, then turn upright. After jars cool, check seals to make sure they are sealed.
Mix together and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Top with cooked bacon strips.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in greased casserole dish and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Saute onion, celery and green pepper in oleo.
Cook broccoli as directed.
Drain.
Add mushroom soup, garlic powder and grated cheese.
Mix together with cooked rice and bake 30 minutes at 350° in buttered casserole.
Sift together the sugar, flour and baking powder.
Add milk and egg.
Beat until smooth.
Add apples.
Drop heaping teaspoons full into hot fat (1 1/2-inch deep).
Leave in fat 4 minutes or until brown.
Drain and roll in a mixture of sugar and cinnamon.
In bowl with mixer, blend cream cheese and 1/4 cup milk until smooth.
Add remaining milk and pudding mix and beat at low speed for 2 minutes.
Alternately layer pudding mixture and fruit into 4 parfait glasses.
Chill until served.
Quick and easy.
Whip the cream and set aside.
Beat the egg whites.
Slowly add 1/4 cup brown sugar, white sugar and salt to the eggs.
Beat until stiff.
Fold cream, egg mixture, vanilla and liquor together.
Freeze, covered, in 4 to 6 goblets.
Combine first 8 ingredients.
Toss well.
Fold in mayonnaise. Cover and chill at least 2 hours.
Garnish with parsley and cherry tomatoes if you like.
Sometimes I boil an extra egg and slice it thin and long over salad in bowl.
Chill until ready to serve in lettuce lined salad bowl.
Cook shells, drain.
Rinse with cold water, drain well, put in medium bowl.
Put oil and garlic in container of blender or food processor, process until garlic is pureed.
Add parsley, oregano, basil, salt and pepper.
Process until parsley is finely chopped. Pour dressing over shells and toss to coat.
Add salami, cheese and scallions, toss again.
Refrigerate until serving time.
Cook for approximately 1 hour, or until thickness desired, in pot without lid.
Makes 7 pints.
Beat egg whites until very stiff.
Gradually add sugar to stiff egg whites, then add baking powder and vanilla.
Continue beating mixture at least 3 minutes; set aside.
Crush crackers and walnuts thoroughly (a food processor with plastic blade works well); combine.
Fold the cracker mixture into the egg white mixture.
Spread into an 8-inch pie pan, greased with butter. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool.
Top with whipped cream.
Blend cream cheese and milk in blender until creamy.
Add sour cream, green pepper and onion.
Blend.
Fold in dried beef and heat in a 350° oven for 10 minutes or until bubbly.
Serve hot with chips for dipping.
Can be prepared ahead and frozen.
In blender container, combine ingredients; blend until smooth. Serve over ice.
Garnish as desired.
Store, tightly covered, in refrigerator.
Stir before serving.
Mix together soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic.
Simmer in saucepan.
Cut chicken into 1-inch chunks.
Dip chicken in beaten egg, then dip chicken into flour.
Fry the coated chicken nuggets in oil until browned.
Dip chicken nuggets into soy sauce mixture, then bake them in 325° oven for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle chicken with sesame seed, if desired.
Serve with rice and whatever sauce remains.
Prepare outdoor grill for barbecuing.
Meanwhile, peel carrots; cut each carrot lengthwise in half.
Cut each unpeeled potato lengthwise into 6 wedges.
Cut each onion lengthwise in half.
In 12-inch skillet over high heat, in 3/4-inch boiling water, heat carrots, potatoes and onions to boiling.
Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp; drain.
Add olive oil, salt, pepper and marjoram to vegetables in skillet and toss to coat well.
Salt lightly on both sides of meat with the garlic, seasoned salt and Cajun seasoning.
Sprinkle both sides with onion flakes. Coat thoroughly both sides with teriyaki sauce.
Coat thoroughly just one side with the soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce.
Put steaks side by side in airtight container and shake.
Turn over every hour for four hours.
Pour marinade over steaks on grill; cook slowly until tender and serve.
Stir together first 5 ingredients in a large bowl.
Gently stir in blackberries until sugar mixture is crumbly.
Spoon fruit mixture into a lightly greased 11-inch by 17-inch baking dish. Cut 1 piecrust into 1/2-inch wide strips, and arrange strips diagonally over blackberry mixture.
Sprinkle top with 1 tablespoon sugar.
Bake at 425° for 45 minutes or until crust is golden brown and center is bubbly.
Serve with ice cream if desired.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Cook chicken in boiling water until tender.
Save stock. Debone chicken and cut into small pieces.
Mix onion, soups, sour cream, broth and green chiles in a bowl.
Grease a 2-quart casserole and place a layer of torn tortilla pieces on the bottom. Add a layer of soup mixture, then chicken pieces, then grated cheese.
Repeat this process one more time, ending with cheese. Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 45 minutes.
Broil chicken until brown.
Turn and brown other side.
Place broiled chicken in Pyrex dish.
Sprinkle with onion (if desired). Mix soup and milk together and pour over chicken.
Cover with foil and bake at 325° for about 1 hour.
Set oven to 425°.
Place margarine or butter in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Place pan in the oven about 3 minutes or until margarine melts.
Stir together egg and milk.
Dip pork chops in egg mixture.
Coat with stuffing mix.
Place chops on top of melted margarine in pan.
Bake 20 minutes.
Turn.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes more or until pork is no longer pink.
Beat concentrate for 30 seconds.
Blend in ice cream and whipped topping.
Whip until smooth.
Pour into crust.
Freeze at least 4 hours.
top with additional whipped cream.
Put the oats in bowl; set aside.
Put oleo, sugar, chocolate and milk in pan; boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add peanut butter; stir until dissolved.
Add vanilla.
Pour all over oatmeal; stir until oatmeal is all covered.
Put waxed paper on cookie sheets; drop by spoonful.
Set in cool place to harden.
Bring salt, butter and water to a boil.
Turn burner off and sift flour in.
Beat vigorously until it rolls.
Cool slightly and add unbeaten eggs, one at a time and beat thoroughly until creamy and smooth.
Drop by teaspoons onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Lower heat to 350° and bake for 10 more minutes.
Do not open door while baking.
Cool, slit sides and fill with prepared coconut pudding or your favorite pudding.
Combine all ingredients in pint jar.
Mix well and let set at least 6 hours before using.
Great on lettuce leaf salad or spinach.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Lightly coat a 5 x 9-inch loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray.
In a large bowl, mix oil and sugar.
Add the buttermilk and beaten eggs, stirring until smooth.
In another bowl, combine the remaining ingredients and add to the liquid mixture, stirring just until the batter is moistened.
Don't overmix it.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Yields 18 1/2 slices.

In skillet, heat olive oil and half of minced garlic for 2 minutes over medium-high heat. Add broccoli and seasoning. Saut until broccoli turns limp; cool. Slice bread and add butter with remaining garlic to each inner side. Spoon broccoli mixture on bottom half of bread, followed by half of cheese. Repeat. Put top half of bread onto the mixture and loosely wrap in foil. Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted. Set aside 10 minutes. Slice and serve.
In blender, mix all ingredients thoroughly; keep refrigerated. Yields 1 3/4 cups or 28 servings, 1 tablespoon each.
Beat ingredients 4 minutes. Pour into well greased and floured tube pan. Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
In a 4 to 5-quart pan, over medium heat, cook onions in oil until limp and lightly browned, stirring often.
Add chicken broth, beans, tomato paste, spices and herbs.
Cover, bring to boil over high heat; reduce to simmer until beans mash easily, about 3 1/2 hours.
(Soaking beans overnight can reduce cooking time to 2 1/2 hours.)
Uncover and boil beans on high until reduced to about 5 1/2 cups, about 30 minutes, stirring to prevent scorching.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix softened butter and cream cheese until smooth.
Gradually add the flour to form a pastry dough. Line tart tins with tart size paper tartlet cups.
Mix the remaining ingredients for filling.
Place squash strips into a greased baking dish.
Dot with butter.
Sprinkle with salt and paprika.
Pour milk over all of this.
Cover and bake at 350° until squash is tender.

Place graham crackers in a 9-inch square Pyrex dish, bottom and sides (don't crush). Put 1 1/2 cups milk and cream cheese in blender; blend well, then add instant pie filling. Blend until it begins to thicken. Pour in crust and spread evenly, then pour cherry pie filling over that.
Chill until set or cold.
Combine the first 3 ingredients to the onion, celery, pepper and mushrooms. Mix the vinegar, oil, sugar, salt and pepper and add to bean mixture. Cover and refrigerate. Keeps well.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease two baking sheets.
In mixing bowl combine flours, baking powder and salt.
In blender combine peanut butter and milk.
Blend until smooth.
Pour into dry mixture and blend well.

Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead lightly.
Roll out 1/4-inch thick and cut into 2-inch squares.
Place on baking sheet, about 1-inch apart.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Cool and dice.
Add eggs, onion, pickles and celery.
Mix together with salad dressing, salt, pepper and mustard.
Refrigerate; garnish with paprika and egg slices.

Bring sugar and corn syrup to a boil.
Add peanuts; stir constantly and cook until light brown.
Remove from heat.
Add baking soda and salt.
Pour mixture onto waxed paper.
Break into pieces when cooled.

Add ingredients in the order listed.
Water should be warm (105° to 125°).
Select white bread and push "start."
Cut peeled eggplant into 1/4-inch slices.
Dip each slice in eggs and crumbs.
