Place layer of eggplant in buttered baking dish.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese, oregano and Mozzarella cheese.
Cover well with some sauce. Repeat until ingredients are gone.
Top last layer of sauce with Mozzarella cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1/2 hour. "Enjoy."
Mix salt, pepper and flour together, then sprinkle lightly over chicken.
In a skillet with butter, brown the chicken on all sides.
Pour barbecue sauce (your favorite brand) over chicken; lower heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Remove cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix hot water and margarine in bowl.
Stir in stuffing mix, pepper, half the pineapple and syrup.
Spoon stuffing evenly on chicken; roll tightly.
Secure with toothpicks. Place in 9-inch square pan with any remaining stuffing in center.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook frozen vegetables as package directs.
Drain and cut up any large pieces.
Combine creamed corn, cheese, corn and soup.
Fold in the cooked vegetables and mushrooms.
Pour into a 13 x 9-inch dish.
Bake, uncovered, 25 to 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine soup, paprika and pepper.
In a greased 2-quart oblong dish (2 x 4 x 5-inch), arrange potatoes in overlapping rows.
Sprinkle with the cheese.
Spoon on soup mix over the cheese.
Cover with tinfoil; bake 40 minutes in a 350° oven.
Uncover and bake an additional 10 minutes or until potatoes are tender.

Mix last 3 ingredients and pour over first 4 ingredients and allow to marinate at least one hour.
Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate overnight before serving with fresh vegetables.
Brown meat and drain.
Saute cut up celery and onion with meat until glazy.
Add cooked rice, soup and peppers.
Cook about 4 minutes.
Put in a casserole dish and top with sliced olives.
Cut up nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.

Cover and remove from heat.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Pound chicken breasts quite thin. Divide stuffing, spooning into one end of each breast.
Roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Roll in flour.
Brown in margarine in skillet.
add wine and water.
Cover; simmer 15 to 20 minutes, turning twice.
Blend cheeses and oleo. Stir in olives and chives. Chill for easier shaping. Form in ball. Chill thoroughly. Before serving, sprinkle nuts over ball. Serve with crackers.
Spread ribs, meaty side up, in roasting pan. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Arrange lemon slices on ribs and brown, uncovered in 450° oven for 45 minutes.
Melt chocolate and butter over hot water.
Stir to blend; cool.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add sugar 2 tablespoons at a time, beating until thickened, about 5 minutes with mixer.
Blend in chocolate mixture.
Add flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon; blend.
Stir in vanilla and pecans.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased baking sheet.
Bake in moderate oven (350°) until cookies feel set when lightly touched, 8 to 10 minutes.
Store in tightly covered container.
Makes about 36 cookies.
Trim
off
large leaves of broccoli.
Remove tough ends to lower
stalks; cut up and mix with other ingredients.
Put in baking dish and bake uncovered in 350° oven for 25 minutes or until tender.
Garnish with lemon slices if desired.
Mix sweet potatoes, 1/2 cup margarine and sugar.
Beat in eggs and vanilla and put in a buttered casserole dish.
Top with brown sugar, nuts, flour and 1/4 cup margarine, all mixed together.
Grate lightly the peel of both fruits.
Squeeze fruit; put peel and juice in large pan.
Add citric acid, water and sugar.
Bring to a full boil.
Let stand for 24 hours.
Strain into jars.
When ready to use, dilute this "syrup" with three parts water.
Put all ingredients in a covered jar and shake vigorously until well blended.
Makes 1 cup.
Use with either greens or fruit salad.
Wash your squash; cook and drain, then mash squash.
Mix in grated cheese, seasoning, milk and pepper.
Put in casserole dish. Bake at 325° for 20 to 25 minutes or until cheese is bubbling on top.
Pour apple pie filling into a 13 1/2 X 8 3/4 x 1 3/4 baking dish.
Pour dry yellow cake mix on top and sprinkle with cinnamon. Blend slightly and pour pecans over this.
Place pats of margarine over entire top of mixture and bake at 350 degrees for 25 - 30 minutes or until golden brown.
In saucepan combine white sugar and cornstarch.
Cook until thick.
Add vanilla and salt.
Pare apples, slice and add to cooked mixture.
In another bowl, combine crumbs mixture, flour, oatmeal, brown sugar and melted butter.
In a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan, put in 1/2 of the crumb mixture, then add cooked mixture and top with other half crumb mixture, spreading evenly.
Add 1 cup water throughout.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes.
Sift corn meal, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar together. Combine egg, oil and milk; add to dry ingredients.
Mix until smooth.
Pour into greased 9-inch square pan, 10-inch iron skillet or 12-muffin tin.
Bake at 425° for 20 to 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Brown beef and onion; drain. Add remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes.
Drain salmon; remove skin and bones.
Flake salmon with a fork; add cream cheese, lemon juice, onion, salt and liquid smoke. Stir well.
Chill mixture several hours or overnight.
Shape salmon mixture into a log.
Combine pecans and parsley; stir well. Roll salmon log in pecan mixture and chill several hours. Yields one 10-inch log.
Combine oats and buttermilk.
Let the mixture stand for 1 hour.
Stir in the eggs, sugar and butter.
Add the flour mixture and stir until it is just combined (will be lumpy).
Fold in the raisins.
Spoon batter into greased and floured muffin tins.
Bake in preheated hot (400°) oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 18 medium or 12 large muffins.
In a skillet, saute 1/2 onion in about a tablespoon of oil. Cook for 2 minutes and add garlic.	Cook 2 minutes more and add chicken, taco mix, and cumin.
Mix well, set aside.
In a blender, add the rest of the onion and the can of enchilada sauce.
Blend until fully mix. In Crock Pot-insert, pour about 1/2 cup sauce on the bottom of the pan and begin building casserole.
Start with sauce, then put on tortilla, then a layer of chicken mixture, then a layer cheese. Repeat this pattern until finished.
Pour the rest of the sauce evenly over the top and sprinkle a little cheese on the top just before serving.
A Great dish if you are busy all day.
If you don't have a Crock Pot, you can cook this in a dish. Follow the same procedure except cook in the oven at 350° until bubbling and casserole is completely hot.
Hope you enjoy, we have!
Brown salt pork in a large fry pan.
Chop onion, green pepper and celery; put in the pan.
Add rest of ingredients.
Heat slowly until hot, stirring as needed to keep from sticking.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine sugar, chocolate milk and corn syrup.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring once in a while.
Cover with lid and turn heat
down for 3 minutes.
Uncover and cook until it forms a soft ball in a cup of cold water, about 10 minutes. When candy forms soft
ball,
remove from heat and stir in 1/2 stick
of butter
or
margarine.
Stir
just
enough
to
melt butter.
Let cool
until
able
to
touch
bottom of pan.
Add vanilla; beat well.
Add nuts.
Drain pineapple syrup into measuring cup, reserving pineapple chunks.
Add enough water to syrup to make 1 cup liquid.
Pour into medium skillet.
Add carrot strips, curry, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over medium heat 10 minutes or until tender.
Stir in pineapple chunks and cook, covered, a few minutes to heat through.
Measure cold water into small bowl.
Sprinkle gelatin over cold water.
Let stand 1 minute.
Add sugar to the mixture.
Stir until gelatin dissolves.
Pour boiling water into medium bowl. Stir in gelatin mixture.
Combine milk, vanilla and almond extract.
Stir milk mixture into gelatin mixture.
Divide mixture between four serving dishes.
Refrigerate until set, about 3 hours.
Pare and slice kiwis.
Arrange slices and strawberries over each dessert.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine all ingredients, except bread crumbs.
Place in a greased casserole dish and top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Yields 6 servings.
Sift dry ingredients in large bowl.
Mix remaining ingredients and pour into center of dry ingredients.
Stir until well mixed. Pour into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Steam rutabaga until tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients and serve.
Makes 4 servings.
Makes 60 calories per serving.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Combine berries and cornstarch in medium bowl; toss lightly to coat.
Add pourable fruit; mix well. Spoon into 1-1/2-quart or 8-inch square baking dish.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, baking powder and salt.
Add milk, butter and concentrate; mix just until dry ingredients are moistened.
Drop six heaping tablespoons of batter evenly over berries; sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake 25 minutes or until topping is golden brown and fruit is bubbly.
Cool on wire rack.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Makes 6 servings.
Just before serving, fill crust with berries.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and top with whipped cream.
Serve.
In 2-quart casserole, mix soup, water, soy sauce, green onions, vegetables, turkey and rice.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until hot.
Stir and sprinkle French fried onions over turkey mixture.
Bake for 5 minutes or until onions are golden.
Bake Jiffy cake, as per directions, in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cool.
Place drained pineapple on cake.
Slice banana onto pineapple layer.
Mix cream cheese with 1/2 cup milk.
Using 2 1/2 cups milk, add instant pudding and to that stir in cream cheese mixture.
Spread pudding and cream cheese over banana layer.
Top with Cool Whip and nuts.
Refrigerate.
Combine dry ingredients in mixing bowl and mix thoroughly. Beat eggs and whip oil and milk and applesauce.
Add dry ingredients to liquid ingredients until moistened, then add raisins and blend.
Fill muffin tins, greased or with papers, 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Remove from muffin tin immediately.
You can freeze muffins for later use.
Cut fish in bite-size pieces.
Mix flour, salt and pepper. Coat each piece.
In large frying pan, cook bacon until crisp. Remove bacon from pan and reserve.
Cook onion and fish in bacon fat over medium heat until lightly browned.
Reduce heat and mix in tomato juice, mustard, parsley and garlic powder.
Simmer until sauce thickens slightly, 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream.
Serve over hot cooked rice or toast points. Crumble bacon and put on top of each serving.
Serves 6.
Boil chicken breasts for 1 1/2 hours with 2 tablespoons of butter and salt.
Let cool; debone and skin breasts.
Save 1 1/2 cups of broth.
Mix all 3 cans of soup with broth; mix well.
Melt stick of margarine; add to stuffing until moist.
Layer stuffing, chicken, then soup.
Repeat until all is used.
Top with stuffing. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Mix chicken, 1 cup cheese, 1 can soup, 1/4 cup onion and sour cream. Spread on tortillas and roll up. Arrange in two layers in baking dish. Mix 1 can soup, milk and 1 cup cheese. Pour over rolled tortillas, covering thoroughly. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook and drain macaroni.
While warm, add the French dressing and refrigerate until cool.
Add remaining ingredients.
Stir to mix.
Cover and refrigerate several hours.
More dressing may be needed.
Precook broccoli until about done.
Arrange in flat baking dish.
Place cooked chicken, cut into chunks, on broccoli.
Mix other ingredients (except potato chips) and spread over chicken and broccoli.
Top with crumbs, if you want.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
If this has been chilled, it takes about 45 minutes to 1 hour to heat.
Serve over rice.
Cook 8 ounces spaghetti in 4 quarts boiling, salted water for 10 minutes, until tender.
Drain salmon; remove skin and bones.
Flake fish.
Dice 2 of the eggs and add to fish.
Add celery, mayonnaise, pickle and lemon juice.
Mix.
Remove thin circle of peel from top half of apple.
Core. Place apples in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Add water, lemon juice and vanilla. Sprinkle apples with cinnamon and sugar substitute.
Cook on High in microwave for 3 1/2 to 4 1/2 minutes or until apples are tender.

recipes.t: Baked Ham Slice With Apple Rings
d: Gash fat in ham slice to prevent curling.
Mix brown sugar and spices; rub 1/4 of mixture into 1 side of ham.
Put slice, sugar side down, in shallow baking dish.
Peel and core apples; cut in 1/2-inch slices.
Arrange around ham.
Sprinkle apples and ham with remaining sugar mixture.
Heat juice to boiling and pour over all.
Stir together flour, sugar and baking powder.
Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cereal and milk.
Let stand about 5 minutes.
Add egg and applesauce.
Beat well.
Add flour mixture, stirring only until combined.
Put batter into muffin pans that have been coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes. Yield: 12 muffins.
In large mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs one at a time beating after each.
Add preserves and vanilla.
Add dry and wet ingredients alternately beginning and ending with flour.
Mix just enough to wet all of flour.
Do not overbeat.
Pour in well greased and well floured tube pan.
Bake at 325° about 1 1/2 hours. Cool on rack 15 minutes.
Remove from pan and wrap in foil to keep moist.
Mix together and put in a greased casserole (shallow).
Cover top with layer of Swiss cheese (not the holey kind).
Mix
1/2 cup Ritz cracker crumbs in slightly less than 1/2 cup melted butter and sprinkle over top.
Bake 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Combine first 6 ingredients in large roasting pan.
Combine oil, brown sugar, Worcestershire and garlic salt.
Pour over first 6 ingredients and toss to coat.
Bake in 250° oven for 1 1/2 hours, stirring frequently.
Brown noodles in hot fat (Spry), stirring constantly.
Add rice and remaining ingredients.
Simmer 30 minutes, until all liquid is absorbed.
Great with pork chops or chicken.
Mix all ingredients together; cover and put in refrigerator until chilled.
Remove from refrigerator and roll into 1 inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press down each ball with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Chop shrimp and scallions.
Cut pork, chicken and beef into small strips.
Heat wok with 2 tablespoons oil.
Add shrimp, pork, chicken and beef.
Stir-fry.
Remove.
To wok, add water.
Add noodles.
Cook until soft (3 to 4 minutes).
Add seasoning (from noodle package), the meat, shrimp, spinach and scallions.
Cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Serve hot.
Serves 2 to 4.
Amount of noodles in recipe may be doubled or tripled.
If so, add an additional 3/4 cup water for each package of noodles.
Prepare pie crust according to package directions for two crust pie using 9-inch pie pan.
Pour enough oil in a large pot to cover bottom.
Brown pork and remove from pot.
Add flour and brown.
Add all ingredients.
Stir well.
Cover and simmer 1 hour.
Mix everything but chops.
Put in 9 x 12-inch pan.
Lay chops on
top.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover with foil.
Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
Serve with mashed potatoes. Serves 4.
Blend in enough vegetable oil to get potatoes moist.
Let stand.
Add onion, celery, pickle juice and vinegar.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Keep and serve warm.
Dredge meat in flour, salt and pepper mixture.
Brown slowly. Add remaining ingredients; simmer 5 minutes.
Add onions.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 75 minutes.
Place oil, onions and green pepper in frying pan to saute. Salt and pepper to taste.
Take out of pan and place in a large bowl.
Put ground beef in frying pan and brown; drain.
Put this into the bowl.
Add Luck's pinto beans (throw away the fat) and the tomato sauce to the bowl.
Add hot sauce if desired.
Let stand for 30 minutes.
Place in casserole dish.
Mix the Jiffy mix according to directions and pour on top of casserole.
Bake at 400° until brown, about 20 minutes.
In skillet over medium heat, brown meat and onion; cook until done.
Pour off drippings.
Stir in corn, tomato sauce, rice, steak sauce and pepper.
Cut tops off green peppers and stuff; arrange in a 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 40 minutes.
Prepare rice according to directions.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole or baking pan.
Top with onion rings.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Serves 8 to 10.
Place chicken in 12 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix orange peel, juice, onion and bouillon granules.
Sprinkle chicken with salt, pepper and paprika.
Pour orange juice mixture over chicken.
Cover and bake at 375° for 50 minutes.

Heat oven to 350°. Grease and flour a large cookie sheet. Beat egg whites and salt until soft peaks form. Add sugar gradually, beating well after each addition. Beat until stiff and glossy. Beat egg yolks and vanilla until thick and lemon colored. Add to egg whites and fold in gently but quickly. Fold in flour. Press through a pastry tube or cookie press, with large plain tip, into strips 2 1/2 inches long onto prepared cookie sheet. (If you don't have a pastry tube or cookie press, shape rounded teaspoonfuls of batter into strips.) Bake 8-10 minutes or until set and very lightly browned on the bottom. remove from sheets and cool on racks. Store in tightly closed tin box.
Makes 3 dozen.
Mix thoroughly and boil 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Boil tomatoes until soft; strain through a sieve.
Add vinegar, sugar, cayenne pepper, black pepper, cloves, mustard and salt.
Boil down until it is 1/4 of its bulk and add cinnamon. Bottle, seal and process.
Makes 4 to 5 pints.
Boil sugar, cocoa, milk and butter together over medium heat for one minute.
Add cereal, peanut butter and vanilla.
Stir fast.
Drop on waxed paper to harden.
Cook broccoli in microwave as directed on package or on High setting (for fresh)
until tender.
Add margarine, salt and orange juice and heat in microwave until margarine is melted.
Top with toasted slivered almonds.
In small bowl, beat together egg white and water.
Stir in pecans, stirring until all surfaces are moistened.
Mix together sugar and remaining ingredients, sprinkle over pecans and mix well to coat all sides.
Spread on lightly greased or foil-lined cookie sheet and bake in preheated oven at 300° for 30 minutes.
Stir about halfway through baking time to assure crispness and even drying.
In a large saucepan, combine sugar, milk and margarine.
Bring to a boil while stirring.
Remove from heat; mix in the chips. Stir and melt.
Add the oatmeal and mix well.
Drop dough from spoon onto a waxed paper lined tray.
When cooled they are ready to enjoy.
In a small mixing bowl, beat cream cheese and butter until smooth.
Beat in marshmallow cream.
Fold in whipped topping. Serve with fruit.
Store in refrigerator.
Yield: about 4 cups.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in casserole bowl.
Top with 1 roll of Hi Ho or Ritz cracker crumbs (35 crackers), 1/2 cup slivered almonds and 1/2 cup margarine.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
In a large bowl, beat egg yolks and sugar until thick and pale yellow.
Beat or fold in Mascarpone until thoroughly incorporated. Mixture should be completely smooth.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into Mascarpone mixture.

Combine Espresso and brandy. Dip ladyfingers very quickly into coffee-brandy mixture, one at a time, and line the bottom of a 13 x 9-inch rectangular dish. Spread half of the Mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers and sprinkle with powdered cocoa.
Dip more ladyfingers into the Espresso-brandy and make another layer.
Cover with Mascarpone and sprinkle with cocoa.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Just before serving, peel some chocolate into curls with a carrot peeler and sprinkle over the cake.
Place all ingredients in a large bowl and mix thoroughly.
Let stand 1/2 hour.
Shape into medium-size meatballs.
Fry gently in oil, until slightly browned, or place on foil-covered cookie sheet for 1/2 hour at 350°.
Gently place in your own hot spaghetti sauce and cook on medium-low heat for 1 hour.
Blend together cocoa, cornstarch and sugar.
Add milk, a little at a time.
Cook slowly until thickened.
Remove from heat. Add vanilla and butter.
Stir gently, until cool and thick enough to spread.
This will frost 2 layers.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and rinse. Place in a 2 1/2-quart salad bowl.
Add turkey, celery, onion and green pepper.
Toss to mix.
Combine dressing mix, sour cream, salad dressing and garlic salt.
Add to pasta mixture and mix well.
Sprinkle with almonds and paprika.
Garnish with pepper ring and tomato slice, if desired.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Cook linguine according to package directions. Add broccoli for last 4 min. of cooking time. Drain.
Mix dry pudding with pineapple.
Save about 2 tablespoons for dissolving gelatin.
Add nuts.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Dissolve gelatin in pineapple juice.
Mix into salad.
Chill.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Lightly spoon flour into a dry measuring cup.
Level with a knife.
Combine flour and sugar in bowl; cut in butter with a pastry blender or 2 knives until mixture is crumbly.
Add almonds; toss well.
Combine apple and Amaretto in a bowl.
TOSS WELL.
Spoon apple mixture into an 8-inch square baking dish or 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with crumb mixture.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Prepare and bake mix using package directions for a 13 x 9-inch cake pan.
Mix cream cheese and whipped topping in a bowl. Spread over cooled cake.
Combine pudding mix and milk in a bowl.
Mix well. Spread over cream cheese mixture. Top with remaining 8 ounces whipped topping. Chill until serving time.
Yields 18 to 20 servings.
Boil water.
Add to gelatin.
Stir until dissolves.
Add tomato sauce and vinegar; stir.
Chill slightly.
Add vegetables. Pour into individual serving dishes or 8 x 9-inch pan.
Chill until set.
Serve over bed of lettuce.
Cook ground beef and drain.
Add sauce.
Cook noodles.
Blend eggs, Ricotta and 1 cup Parmesan.
Alternate layers, starting with meat sauce, noodles, Ricotta mixture and meat mixture.
Repeat. End with noodle layer.
Top with Mozzarella cheese and remaining Parmesan cheese.
Makes 4 bread loaf pans.

Brush the dough or crust with a little olive oil to the edge. Spread tomato sauce over the dough to within 1/2-inch of the edge. Distribute Mozzarella slices over the tomato sauce and season with pepper.
Arrange basil leaves over the Mozzarella, reserving a few garnish if you wish.
Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Carefully slide the pizza in the oven and bake for 6 to 8 minutes or until the bottom if crisp and browned and the top is bubbling.
Garnish with the reserved basil leaves, if desired.
Yield:
one 12-inch pizza.
Brown the meat with the onion.
Mix together all ingredients except the noodles.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Add noodles.
Mix 3/4 into the casserole and spread the rest evenly over the top. Bake 15 minutes longer.
In large bowl, combine taco sauce, mustard and lime juice; mix well.
Add chicken, turning to coat; marinate for 30 minutes.
In large heavy skillet, melt butter until foamy.
Remove chicken from marinade; fry until browned on all sides, turning frequently.
Add remaining marinade; cook about 5 minutes longer, until chicken is fork-tender.
Remove chicken, boil marinade 1 minute and spoon over chicken.
Place 1 tablespoon sour cream on top of each piece; top with lime segment.
In a large soup kettle, melt the butter.
Stir in flour; heat and stir until smooth.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add potatoes and onions.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients; stir until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cream shortening, sugars, eggs and vanilla together.
Blend in chocolate chips.
Gradually add in flour on medium speed of mixer.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool for 25 minutes, then cut into squares.
In large bowl, mix first seven ingredients.
Add eggs, water and pumpkin.
Beat thoroughly.
Pour into 1 pound coffee cans, filling cans about halfway.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Beat egg in medium bowl.
Mix in bread crumbs, chili sauce, salt, onion, garlic powder, ground beef and celery.
Shape into 30 small balls about 1-inch in diameter.
Melt Crisco in large skillet on medium heat.
Add meatballs and brown on all sides. Continue cooking until done, about 12 minutes including browning. Warm barbecue sauce while meatballs cook.
Serve meatballs on wooden picks to be dipped in warm sauce.
Slice cake and place on bottom of 9x13 pan.
Prepare Jello and pour over cake.
Chill until set.
Slice bananas over cake and Jello.
Prepare pudding.
Spread over bananas.
Let set 5-10 minutes in refrigerator. Spread Cool Whip over pudding. Refrigerate.
In a large soup pot, cook roast.
When done, remove roast and add diced onion, celery and cubed potatoes to broth.
When potatoes are almost done, add soups.
In the meantime, shred up roast and add to pot.
Simmer for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together well (until all cream cheese is worked in).
Place on plate, form ball and refrigerate.
Can be rolled in chopped nuts or parsley before serving.
Mix all ingredients together and beat to stiff peaks, 4 minutes over boiling water.
Sprinkle chopped nuts over top if you like.
With a stiff brush, scrub mussels with running cold water to remove sand or beards.
In a 5-quart Dutch oven or saucepot, over medium heat, in hot oil, cook onion and garlic until tender.
Stir in tomatoes with their liquid, wine and basil.
Then heat to a boil over high heat.
Add mussels and once again heat to boiling. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until mussels open, about 5 minutes.
Serve with bread and salad.
Mix flour, sugar, cocoa powder, salt and baking soda.
Add water, oil, egg, vinegar and vanilla and pour in a large 8 x 14-inch cake pan. Bake at 325° for 30 to 40 minutes or until done.
Mix well.
Bake in a large skillet or muffin pan sprayed with vegetable cooking spray.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes or until done.
Combine first three ingredients and then add milk.
Fold in the Cool Whip and nuts.
Pour into a prepared graham cracker crust and freeze overnight.
Just before serving, remove from the freezer and let stand at room temperature for about 30 minutes.
Brown hamburger and onion; drain.
Pour spaghetti sauce into hamburger.
Mix well.
Pour in baking dish.
Mix cream potatoes as directed on box and layer on top of hamburger mixture.
You can sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Work first 6 ingredients together real good.
Make a hole in flour, then add buttermilk (enough to take up all the flour, but enough to knead a little bit).
Then put out on pastry sheet. Knead just enough to flatten with hand.
Don't overwork.
Then cut and bake at 425° until light brown.
When taken from oven, put butter on top and cover for 6 minutes.
Serve.
Cream shortening and sugar, blend in eggs.
Add milk and vanilla.
Mix real good, add dry ingredients.
Mix in nuts and chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoon full on greased cookie sheet. Bake at 375 degrees for 10 - 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Layer the bottom of the unbaked pie shells with the nuts. Then mix all the ingredients and pour onto the pecans in the pie shell.
Bake in a 300° oven for 45 minutes.
The edges will become firm and the middle will look soft, but it will thicken when it cools.
Use a 9 x 12-inch baking pan.
Quarter cabbage and cut off core.
Boil over medium heat in salted water until tender.
(Do not overcook.)
Pour into colander and cool.
Mix all dry ingredients. Place cabbage leaves on chopping board and cut out middle stem. Make layers of cabbage leaves, dry mixture and drizzle 1/4 cup olive oil.
Continue making layers, ending with dry ingredients and olive oil.
(Make 4 layers.)
Cover with tinfoil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Can be made the day before, placed in refrigerator and when cold, cut into squares.
When ready to serve, warm in 400° oven for 30 minutes.
Can be eaten cold.
Cook turkey, onions and pepper until done, stirring constantly.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil. Cover. Reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serves 4.
Counts as 3 proteins, vegetable and 1 bread.
Boil to small ball stage in 3-quart pan.
Beat with mixer until mixture cools a little.
(Starts to cool to side of pan somewhat.)
Add nuts (optional).
Pour into an 8 x 8-inch or 9 x 13-inch pan if recipe is doubled.
Place Canadian bacon in a greased 9 x 13-inch dish.
Place a chicken breast on each piece of Canadian bacon and top with a 1/2 slice of bacon.
Bake for 1/2 hour, uncovered, at 350°.
Remove from oven and cover with mushroom soup and sour cream mixed together.
Bake for 30 minutes more at 350°.
Serve with chopped green onions.
Heat oil in large frying pan or Dutch oven.
Add vegetables, mushrooms, garlic and bell pepper.
Stir, cover and cook for 3 minutes.
In a bowl, combine meat, eggs, salt and pepper and cheese.
Stir into the vegetable mixture.
Pour into a 3-quart casserole dish and bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Top with Parmesan cheese and bake for 5 minutes longer.
Yield: 4 to 5 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spread pie filling in the bottom of a 9-inch square pan.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Combine dry cake mix, nuts and melted butter.
Sprinkle over pie filling.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes until golden brown.
Serve with ice cream, whipped cream or serve with warm coffee cream.
Brown beef and drain.
Add remaining ingredients with beef and put in crock-pot.
Cook 4 to 6 hours.
Mix ingredients and pour into a prepared unbaked 9-inch pie shell.
Have oven preheated to 450°.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Lower temperature to 350° and bake another 25 minutes or until custard is mostly set and crust is browned.
Break the cauliflower into its flowerets, cutting the bigger ones in halves or quarters so that all the pieces are about 1/2-inch in size.
Put the oil in a soup pot along with the garlic, salt, pepper and the cut-up cauliflower.
Stirring gently, cook over medium heat until the vegetable bits are well oiled and flavored.
Add the tomato paste, hot water, the potato slices and 2 teaspoons salt and bring to a boil.
Break the pasta into 1 or 2-inch lengths as you put it in the pot.
Continue boiling until the pasta is well cooked, has absorbed some of the water and the cauliflower, garlic and tomato have lent their flavors to the pasta.
Before serving discard the garlic clove.
Serve with a sprinkling of Parmesan cheese.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Drain and set aside.
In one bowl, mix cream cheese, cottage cheese and sour cream. Cook noodles.
Alternate noodles and cheese mixture in a 13 x 9-inch casserole.
In 4 cup glass measuring cup, combine sugar and corn syrup. Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Add peanuts and cook 4 minutes.
Add butter and vanilla; cook 1 minute.
Quickly fold in baking soda. Spread on greased cookie sheet to cool.
Break into pieces.
Combine chicken, water, vinegar, bay leaf, garlic, pepper and soy sauce in a medium to large saucepan.
Bring to a boil; cover and lower heat.
Cook until chicken is done and a small amount of broth is left.
Add the oil and brown the contents of the pan, if desired.
(Cooking time is 45 to 60 minutes average.)
Serve over rice.
Add soup, milk and seasonings to potatoes and water. Serve with bacon sprinkled on top.
Heat, but do not boil.
Add melted butter to sugar.
Add eggs and mashed potatoes. Combine dry ingredients and add alternately with buttermilk.
I refrigerate these for several hours (even overnight).
Roll 1/2-inch thick; cut and deep fry.
Heat sugar, vinegar, and oil until sugar is dissolved and pour over kraut mixture. Refrigerate. The longer it sets the better it tastes.
Spread caramel topping on bottom of crust.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Refrigerate.
Stir pudding mixes into milk in medium saucepan.
Stirring constantly, cook on medium heat until mixture comes to full boil.
Remove from heat.
Cool 5 minutes, stirring twice.
Pour into crust.
Place plastic wrap on surface of filling.
Refrigerate 3 hours or until set.
Garnish with Cool Whip.
Store leftover pie in refrigerator.
Makes 8 servings.
Crush vanilla wafers; add butter. Press into a 13 x 9 inch pan. Melt in microwave for 1-1/2 minutes;
marshmallows and orange juice. Add cream cheese and cool whip. Pour into crust.
You may top with cherries.
Combine the boiling water and Jell-O.
When congealed, add the salad dressing immediately. Beat until double.
Blend into the Jell-O mixture the cottage cheese, onion, celery and salt and pepper.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.
Mix gelatins in large bowl; add hot water, stirring until gelatin is dissolved.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into lightly greased 6-cup mold.
Chill until firm.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Cut shortening and flour as you do for pie dough.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add eggs, sugar, salt and sour cream.
Mix and add with flour and shortening.
Refrigerate overnight.
Place yeast in warm water.
Cream sugar with melted butter in large bowl.
Add beaten egg.
Add dissolved yeast to creamed mixture, then add flour and stir until mixed.
Bake by dropping spoonfuls into well-greased muffin tins.
Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes.
The batter does not need to rise to bake or to refrigerate.
Place in airtight bowl and keep refrigerated.
Will last several days.
Use as needed.
Melt oleo in heavy skillet; add rest of ingredients, except Rice Krispies and coconut.
Stir constantly over medium heat until thick.
Remove from heat and cool.
Add Rice Krispies; make into small balls and roll in coconut.
"A favorite holiday treat of ours!"
Pour vanilla pudding powder over fruit. Let sit overnight. Add cut up bananas before serving.
Soak ingredients for 2 to 3 hours.
Wrap pineapple in 1/2 slice bacon.
Microwave 1 minute, turning as needed, until done. Use lean bacon for best results.
Brown meat and onions.
Stir to separate meat; add taco season.
Layer beans, peppers, chips and meat mix, ending with cheese.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Slice 3/4-inch layer off top (the lid) of bread.
Hollow out loaf, leaving 1/2-inch thick bread shell.
Brush inside of loaf and underside of lid with salad dressing.
Layer half the lettuce, meat, Mozzarella, meat, tomatoes, meat, Cheddar cheese and remaining lettuce.
Firmly pack down and replace the lid.
Cut sandwich in wedges to serve.
Wrap unsliced loaf well and refrigerate.
Try adding onions, mushrooms and peppers.
Combine mayonnaise, flour, eggs and milk until blended.
Stir in crabmeat, Swiss and onions.
Pour mixture into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
In casserole bottom melt margarine.
Pour in some favorite stuffing mix.
Save some for top.
Add zucchini chunks and carrots. Mix sour cream, cream of celery soup and chopped onion.
Pour over zucchini and carrots.
Top with remaining stuffing mix.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Put ingredients in a large pan and boil 10 minutes.
Put in jars and seal.
For fried okra, rinse thoroughly.
Roll in meal and fry as you would any fried okra.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a cookie sheet with margarine. Let dough thaw and rise until double in size.
Roll dough out flat.
Beat eggs; add oregano and Parmesan cheese.
Spread 3/4 egg mixture all over flattened dough.
Top with shredded cheese and pepperoni slices.
Roll up like a jelly roll; seal edges and ends (be sure they are sealed).
Place on greased pan and spread rest of egg mixture over top.
Bake 30 minutes or until brown.
While hot, brush with margarine on top and sides.
Serve hot.
Peel, core and slice apples and place in a baking dish.
Mix flour, oats and sugar.
Melt oleo and mix with dry.
Spread mixture over apples.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Beat until creamy, oleo and sugar.
Add flour and eggs alternately.
Add salt, mace, lemon juice and grated lemon rind. Mix.
Pour in greased and floured angel food cake pan.
Bake two hours at 325°.
Wash chicken and pat dry.
Spray a cold, large skillet with nonstick spray coating.
Heat skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken to skillet.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until no longer pink, turning once during cooking.
Transfer chicken to serving plates.
Cover to keep warm.
In a large saucepan, combine sugar, cocoa and salt.
Stir in hot water and butter, bring to a boil.
Add the milk, maple flavoring, vanilla and 8 marshmallows.
Heat through, stirring occasionally, until marshmallows are melted.
Ladle into mugs and top each with a marshmallow.
Yields 4 servings.
Boil pasta and drain.
Add pepperoni, olives, green peppers and onion.
Add dressings and mix well.
Let chill for about one hour before serving.
I prefer to let set overnight.

recipes.t: Bagna Cauda(Garlic, Oil And Anchovy Sauce)
d: Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the garlic.
Cook briefly, stirring, without browning.
Add the wine and cook until reduced by half.
Add the butter, a little at a time, beating rapidly with a wire whisk.
Stir in the anchovy, season with pepper and serve hot. Yield:
about 3/4 cup.
Mix brown sugar, white sugar and corn syrup in a large pan; bring to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Immediately add peanut butter.
Stir until peanut butter is dissolved.
Add corn flakes and peanuts.
Stir until well coated.
Boil chicken 1 1/4 hours with 1-inch water, covering them. Cool; debone chicken.
Place chicken in large buttered casserole dish.
Mix 3 soups and pour over chicken.
Place finely chopped onion over this.
Add stuffing.
Slowly drip batter over this; add broth from chicken.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 60 minutes.
This is a meal in itself.
Saute bacon until crisp, drain well.
Saute garlic and onions until wilted and add tomatoes.
Stir and cook until liquid is reduced by 1/2, approximately 1 hour.
Pour into chafing dish, add bacon and cheese.
Serve when the cheese has melted.
Keep warm for dipping with Fritos or Doritos.
Heat together 6 cups water and 4 cups sugar.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix all together.
Freeze.
When ready to serve, remove and break up with fork until mixture is like mush.
Add 3 quarts ginger ale.
Serves 40 to 50.
Slice angel food cake crossways into three parts.
Spread layers with apricot jam and stack.
Cover entire cake with Cool Whip.
Garnish top of cake with peach slices.
Chill until ready to serve.

recipes.t: Taco Frijoles Para Los Ninos(Bean Taco For The Little Ones)
d: Place chips on bottom of individual serving bowls.
Place beans in individual bowls.
Top with lettuce, cheese and onion.
Sprinkle with salsa pequin, if desired.
Serve hot.
Makes 8 servings.
Wash okra and drain well.
Remove tip and stem.
Cut into 1/2-inch pieces.
Add egg to okra and toss to coat.
Combine cornmeal, salt and pepper.
Dredge okra.
Deep fry in hot oil at 375° until golden brown.
Let cream cheese soften at room temperature.
Add juice from minced clams until mixture is the right consistency.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix first 3 ingredients and bring to a boil in a deep dish pie pan.
Work Crisco into the flour as if making biscuits.
Then work in the iced water, making a dough for dumplings and crust.
Flour the board and roll the dough out with rolling pin.
Roll thin, then cut in 1-inch strips all across the board.
Have the berries boiling and drop dumplings all across the pan, dipping the juice over the dumplings and making sure to cover good.
Then roll a top crust while berries are still boiling.
Place cover on pie.
Cover the top with butter and then sugar.
Place in oven and brown the top, being careful to not let burn.
1st Layer:
Mix and press into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° until very light brown.
Cool.
Soften cheeses to room temperature; blend well.
Mix with paprika.
Cover and refrigerate until firm enough to mold into a ball.
Roll in finely chopped nuts.
Cover and refrigerate until needed.
In a large saucepan, combine the cubed potatoes, peas and onions and Italian dressing.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in sour cream; blend well.
Serve warm, garnished with fresh mint.
Melt shortening in large skillet; brown meat on all sides. Stir in consomme, wine, soy sauce, garlic and onion salt.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 1 hour or until meat is tender.
Blend cornstarch and water; stir gradually into meat mixture.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Serve over rice or noodles.
Heat milk to lukewarm. Dissolve yeast.
Mix together first 6 ingredients.
Let rise until double in bulk.
Turn out on lightly floured board and knead in remaining 5 ingredients.
Set aside 1/3 of the dough.
Divide remaining dough in three equal parts and roll each in a strip about 12 inches long.
Braid.
Put on greased baking sheet.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cut buttered bread into crouton size pieces.
Stir eggs and milk together in a large bowl.
Mix all the remaining ingredients in with milk and egg mixture.
Pour into a buttered (or spray with Pam) 9 1/2 x 11-inch baking dish. Refrigerate overnight.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes at 350°.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add 7-Up.
Chill until thickens. Drain pineapple juice (save).
Fold pineapple, marshmallows and bananas in jello.
Put in pan.
Chill until firm.
Place all ingredients (except Bisquick, oil and milk) in crock-pot for 5 to 6 hours on low.
Drain thoroughly in colander. Save and cool liquid.
Debone chicken and cut into small pieces. Thicken liquid with flour and water paste.
Add chicken and vegetables.
Pour into oblong baking dish.
Preheat oven to 450°. Make biscuits with Bisquick, oil and milk.
(Knead 2 minutes, then cut.) Place on top of chicken and bake 15 to 20 minutes or until biscuits are golden brown.
In large bowl, combine pineapple chunks, mandarin oranges, grapes and kiwi slices.
Set fruit aside.
Add water to reserved pineapple juice to make 1 cup liquid and combine with orange juice, honey and lemon juice.
Pour over fruit mixture.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serves 6.
Mix the wine, butter and garlic together and pour over the shrimp.
Sprinkle with paprika and parsley flakes.
Bake in a 350 degree oven for about 6 to 7 minutes.
Be careful not to overcook the shrimp.
The shrimp is done when it turns pink.
Boil potatoes in jackets; cool.
Peel potatoes and grate.
Mix with other ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix all together.
Put in a large roaster.
Cover and bake at 250° for 3 hours.
Wash and bake sweet potatoes until almost fork-tender (about 45 to 50 minutes).
Cool.
Scoop potatoes out of skins and mash, there should be about 2 cups.
Mix potatoes and remaining ingredients until smooth.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° until knife inserted in center comes out clean (50 minutes). Garnish with whipped cream.
Makes 1 (9-inch) pie; preparation time: 45 minutes; cooking time: 1 1/2 hours.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
In medium saucepan, combine the first 4 ingredients.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture begins to bubble.
Remove from heat; cool slightly.
Set aside.
Melt butter and chocolate.
Add sugar and milk.
Keep heating and stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Remove from heat.
Stir in oats, nuts and vanilla.
Allow mixture to cool to medium warm. Roll teaspoonfuls into balls.
Place on waxed paper lined cookie sheets. Chill until firm.
Makes about 6 dozen.
Mix hamburger, salt and onion in pan.
Saute until brown.
Add cubed potatoes, mixed vegetables and tomato sauce.
Cook for 45 minutes.
Stir often.
Combine soup and 1/4 cup water.
Add 1 cup noodles, tuna, celery, cashews and onion; toss lightly.
Place in ungreased 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining noodles over top. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Serves 4 to 5.
Mix the first 2 items and let stand overnight.
Mix ingredients (except marshmallow cream) and bake at 350° for 30 minutes in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread marshmallow cream on cake as soon as you take from oven.
Drizzle frosting over marshmallow cream.
Cool and cut into small pieces.
Very rich.
Combine sugar, oleo, salt and milk.
Bring to a full boil (rolling) and boil over low heat for a full five minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add melted chocolate and Marshmallow Creme.
Add nuts and vanilla; stir until well mixed. Pour in a greased 9 x 13-inch dish.
Cool for several hours. (Melt chocolate slowly; it burns easily.
Use heavy pan.)
Cook and drain vegetables.
Mix all ingredients and put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with mixture of 1/2 cup melted butter or margarine and crushed Ritz crackers.
Bake in a 350° oven for 20 minutes.
Brown meat and spices; drain.
Add tomato sauce, paste and sugar.
Simmer about 1 hour on low.
Chop chicken into small pieces.
Crush chips.
Add all other ingredients, except cheese.
Mix together; pour into baking dish. Top with cheese and bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until cheese is melted good.
(Can use Velveeta cheese.)
Mix flour, sugar, butter, baking soda and salt in large bowl. Make a well in the center and add egg and buttermilk. Mix well. Blend in caraway seed and currants.
Knead until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes.
Form into 2 round balls and place on buttered cookie sheet.
Brush with beaten egg.
Bake in 375° oven until well browned.
Cool before cutting.
Pour oil over crackers and mix well.
Blend dry ingredients and mix with crackers.
Put in airtight container and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat
oven to 350°.
In bottom of unbaked pie shell, sprinkle
tablespoons flour and then sprinkle 2 tablespoons sugar.
On top of this arrange the finely sliced apples.
Pour on top 3/4 cup sugar.
Then sprinkle with cinnamon.
Over this pour sweet cream.
Then dot with butter.
Bake for 45 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Blend condensed milk, milk and water.
Add peach pulp and lemon juice.
Freeze.
This makes 2 quarts.
Saute onion.
In oblong baking dish, mix tuna, onion and pepper.
Pour in soup and water.
Cook noodles until tender. Drain and add to tuna mixture.
Top with crumbled bread and shredded cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Place sliced onions in bowl.
Boil next 4 ingredients and pour over onions.
Soak overnight.
Drain well and add 1 1/2 cups salad dressing and 2 teaspoons celery seed.
Chill several hours.
Add 3 cups boiling water to Jell-O.
Mix well.
Add orange juice concentrate.
Add pineapple and oranges.
Mix.
Put in refrigerator and let set up.
Mix pudding (dry) with Cool Whip. Spread on top of set up Jell-O.
(Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese if desired.)
Combine all ingredients. Cook over low to medium heat until cheese is melted. This is hot and delicious.
Microwave chicken breasts on High 2 minutes.
Microwave broccoli until about half done.
Layer broccoli in 9 x 9-inch casserole dish.
Top with chicken breasts and pour soup mixture over chicken and broccoli.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Five Minute Chili (Meatless)(Quick And Tasty With Very Little Fat.)
d: Put all together and heat 4 or 5 minutes.
Serve with corn bread.
Fix Dream Whip as directed.
Blend cream cheese with 1/2 cup of powdered sugar.
Mix cream cheese mixture with Dream Whip and spread over graham cracker crust.
Then dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add frozen strawberries.
Stir until thick.
Pour over cream cheese and Dream Whip mixture and chill.
Mix cake mix, margarine and buttermilk together, then, in separate bowl, mix food coloring and cocoa.
Fold into cake mixture with spoon.
Put soda and vinegar in cup; mix, then add to cake mixture with spoon.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.; cut both layers in two, making 4 layers.
Shell and devein the shrimp, leaving fantail on.
Combine all remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Dip shrimp in mixture; place in shallow pan in single layer.
Pour remaining sauce over shrimp. Broil 6 to 8 minutes 3 inches from heat.
Makes 4 servings.
Brown hamburger and onions until done.
Drain away all grease. Place into a casserole dish that is very deep.
Add all the remaining ingredients.
Bake at 400° until it bubbles.
Turn oven down to 375° and bake for 45 minutes.
Put 1/2 lettuce into bowl.
Add layer of celery, onion, bell pepper, peas and eggs.
Top with remaining lettuce.
Cover with mayonnaise, spreading to sides of bowl.
Sprinkle with cheese and crumbled bacon on top.
Mix salad dressing and seasonings in a large bowl until well blended.
Stir in potatoes and onion to coat.
Divide potato mixture evenly among six 12-inch square pieces of foil.
Seal each to form packet.
Place on grill and grill, covered, for 40 minutes or until done.
Makes 6 servings.

recipes.t: Delicious Dairy Dip(Great For Fresh Fruit!)
d: In a small mixing bowl, combine cream cheese, sour cream, sugars and syrup; beat until smooth.
Chill.
Serve with fresh fruit.
Mix all together.
Chill for several hours or overnight before serving.
Saute diced medium onion and mushrooms.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Combine hamburger, soup, sour cream, onion and mushrooms. Cook egg noodles as directed on package.
Drain and combine with hamburger mixture.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Cook carrots with 2 tablespoons of cinnamon and drain.
Add honey and lemon juice; toss with 1 teaspoon of cinnamon more.
Mix in saucepan the pudding, sugar, milk and butter.
Cook to soft ball stage.
Take off and stir in peanuts.
Beat until starts to thicken.
Drop from teaspoon on waxed paper.
Cut medium head of cabbage in strips.
Place in large skillet; cover with water and simmer until tender.
Do not overcook.
Fry bacon cubes in another large skillet.
Remove all but 3 tablespoons of drippings.
Add approximately 2 tablespoons of flour and enough water from cabbage to make a gravy.
Add sugar and vinegar to make a sweet sour taste that pleases you.
Add salt and pepper.
Drain cabbage and add to gravy mixture.
Simmer for a few minutes.
Beat egg, vanilla and sugar.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat into first mixture.
Add apples and nuts.
Bake in 9-inch square pan for 30 minutes at 350°.
Beat heavy cream; add pineapple.
Top pie just before serving.
Dissolve soda with hot water.
Mix other ingredients in order. Drop by teaspoons on baking pan about 3-inches apart.
Bake at 325° for 15 to 25 minutes.
In a medium bowl with electric beater, cream butter and sugar; beat in salt and lime juice.
Add flour and stir until blended. Chill, covered tightly, until firm enough to handle.
Shape into two 4-inch long rolls.
Wrap in Saran.
Chill until firm.
Remove 1 roll at a time.
Cut crosswise into 1/8-inch slices.
Use a wide metal spatula to place 1-inch apart on ungreased cookie sheets. Sprinkle with sugar/lime rind mixture.
Bake at 375° approximately 6 to 8 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack.
Makes 5 dozen.
Brown hamburg; add onion and celery.
Cook until tender, not brown.
Put in casserole.
Add rice, bean sprouts, mushrooms and juice on both.
Add tomatoes and seasoning.
Bake at least 1 hour or longer at 325°.
Fry hamburg and onion in a large pan.
Add water, onion soup mix, tomatoes and vegetables.
Bring to a boil.
Add orzo and cook until pasta is done.
Saute pepper and onion in oil until brown.
Add hamburger; cook 5 minutes or until brown.
Add tomatoes (not drained, but chopped), water, rice and seasonings.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Serves 5.
In medium bowl, combine nondairy creamer, egg, onion, mustard, salt and pepper; set aside.
In large bowl, mix corned beef, sauerkraut, ground beef and bread crumbs.
Add reserved egg-onion mixture and mix with hands until thoroughly combined.
Pat 1/2 of mixture into prepared pie shell.
Sprinkle cheese evenly over top; cover with remaining mixture and sprinkle with chopped parsley, if desired.
Bake at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Serve at once or bring to room temperature; cover with plastic wrap and freeze up to three months.
If frozen, to serve, partially thaw in refrigerator and bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes until heated throughout and bubbly.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Have everything at room temperature and mix all together, except caraway seed.
Cover and let set in a warm place for one hour.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes. (Takes a while, but it's worth it.)
Pour into a buttered dish and top with caraway seed, if desired.
Refrigerate with cover on, spread and enjoy.
Place potatoes in crock-pot (only fill 2/3 full).
In saucepan, melt butter; add onion.
Steam until clear, then add flour stirring constantly on medium heat.
Add milk and simmer until sauce begins to thicken; remove from heat.
Add 1 1/2 cups of cheese.
Cook on low 14 to 16 hours.
Best when done the night before.
Place remainder of cheese on top.
Serve when melted.
Sprinkle paprika over meat, cut in strips and let stand 10 minutes.
Cook meat and garlic in oleo until browned.
Add onions and peppers.
Cook until wilted.
Add beef broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Blend cornstarch, water and soy sauce.
Add to meat mixture.
Cook until thickened.
Serve over rice.
Mix all ingredients together in a shallow casserole dish. Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. Then uncover and cook for another 10 minutes.
Cut tips off chicken wings.
Halve remaining chicken wings. Combine Lipton soup mix, bread crumbs and caraway seed.
Beat egg with beer or water.
Dip chicken in egg mixture, then soup mixture, coating well.
Place in shallow baking pan and drizzle with butter.
Bake, uncovered, 30 minutes or until tender.
Combine all ingredients except cheese.
Cook at 350 degrees for 15 minutes.
Stir, sprinkle on cheese and bake for 20 more minutes.
Mix ingredients in order of listing.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Mix soy sauce, garlic and salad oil together.
Pour over steak; let stand 1 hour.
Pour into frypan.
Allow meat to brown thoroughly on all sides.
Add pepper, onion and celery; cover. Cook 5 to 10 minutes over low heat.
Stir in cornstarch dissolved in water; stir until thickened.
Add tomatoes; cover.
Cook 5 to 10 minutes longer or until meat is tender.
Serve over boiled rice.
Cook rice as package directs.
Cook broccoli.
Put in a large casserole dish.
Add soup, broccoli, chicken and cheese.
Mix well.
Sprinkle grated cheese on top and bake at 325° for approximately 30 minutes.
Serve with tossed salad.
Use a soft white cloth to tie your spices in.
Put spice bag and garlic to taste in bottom of quart jar.
Begin with a layer of pickle in jar, then a layer of sugar; continue in this manner until jar is completely filled and firmly packed.
Add tarragon vinegar, put a top on jar and begin shaking and turning the jar often until all sugar has dissolves.
Wait at least 24 hours before putting in refrigerator.
Usually takes 2 to 3 days for pickles to become crisp-firm.
Cook garlic and onions in oil until tender.
Add vegetables and bay leaf.
Add salt, pepper and a little oregano.
Bring to a boil and simmer 30 minutes.
In a medium size baking dish, spread refried beans.
Combine sour cream and taco seasoning mix for next layer.
Mash ripened avocados with guacamole mix and spread.
The other ingredients may be added for the remaining layers.
Dip is better if allowed to chill for a few hours.
Serve with taco chips.
Mix chocolate cake mix according to directions.
Pour into greased 7 x 11-inch pan.
Bake 20 minutes.
Brown meat.
Add taco seasoning according to directions. Spoon on roll.
Add sliced tomato, lettuce and cheese.
Serve with corn chips.
In Dutch oven, brown beef, breaking up pieces with spoon.
Add onions, garlic, water, basil, salt, pepper and potatoes.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes or until potatoes are almost tender.
Add peppers and tomatoes.
Simmer 10 minutes or until all is tender.
In 13 x 9-inch pan, melt oleo and brown sugar.
Combine 1 cup sugar, flour, baking powder and milk.
Pour over melted ingredients.
Spoon on fruit.
Cook at 325° until browned. Cinnamon or sugar may be added to fruit if desired.
Combine assorted greens, pineapple and green pepper, toss lightly.
Place in lettuce-lined bowl.
Arrange fruit salad on top. Serve with dressing.
Serves 8 to 10.

Cut margarine or butter into baking mix; refrigerate 30 minutes. Mix sausage and green chili; let stand to room temperature. Divide dough in 1/2; roll each piece to a large rectangle 1/4-inch thick. Spread meat chili mixture over dough; roll up as a jelly roll. Wrap in plastic wrap and freeze for 1 hour. Remove from freezer and slice to 1/3 inch thickness. Freeze until ready to use. Remove from freezer and place on baking sheet. Bake in 400° oven for 20 minutes. Serve hot.
Place all ingredients in a small bowl.
Mix until smooth. Makes 1 serving as part of midday meal.
Supplement as required.
In skillet over medium heat,
brown
meat and cook onion until done.
Pour off drippings.
Stir
in
corn, tomato sauce, rice, steak sauce and ground
pepper.
Set aside.
Cut tops off peppers; remove
seeds.
Spoon
meat
mixture
into
peppers. Arrange in 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking
pan.
Bake
at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until peppers are done.
Arrange peaches in a shallow, greased baking dish.
Blend remaining ingredients until crumbly.
Sprinkle over the peaches. Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Combine flour, salt and alum.
Mix with boiling water. Add oil and mix well.
Add food coloring as desired.
Knead with flour to stiffness desired.
Keep covered when not in use.
Brown and drain sausage.
Beat eggs; add milk, salt, pepper and mustard.
Place bread crumbs in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Crumble sausage over bread.
Add cheese and mushrooms.
Pour egg mixture over top.
Refrigerate 8 to 10 hours.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Mix graham crackers and melted margarine; line 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cream together cream cheese, sugar and vanilla.
Dissolve together jello, boiling water and lemon juice; cool.
Add jello mixture to cream cheese mixture, then fold in 1 large can Milnot evaporated milk (whipped).
Pour over graham cracker crust. Sprinkle a few graham cracker crumbs on top.
Soften cream cheese (room temperature).
After adding water to Jell-O, work in cream cheese until blended.
Add other ingredients and chill.
Use Bundt pan or mold.
Make a graham cracker crust by combining the graham cracker crumbs, sugar and melted butter and pat into a 9 inch pie plate. Bake at 300° for 12 - 15 minutes.
Cool.
Partially thaw the lemonade and combine with the sweetened condensed milk.
Fold in Kool Whip and pour into a graham cracker crust.
Chill for at least one hour.
Can be garnished with a lemon cartwheel.
In a medium bowl mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Then stir in the onion.

recipes.t: Cream Cheese-Olive Dip Or Spread(Heloise'S Recipe)
d: Mix cream cheese with mayonnaise.
Stir in pecans, olives, olive liquid and pepper.
It will be a little mushy but will thicken in the refrigerator. The spread will keep for weeks.
It makes a great spread for crackers or finger sandwiches.
(Also, low calorie cream cheese and mayonnaise can be used with good results.)
Melt stick of oleo; add crushed Ritz crackers.
Place crackers in bottom of oblong baking dish.
Layer drained beans and corn. Mix soup, sour cream, Cheddar cheese, onion and salt.
Spread over beans and corn.
Bake for 45 minutes at 350°, uncovered.
Boil ham for 1 to 2 hours.
Separately cook macaroni until tender and drain.
Remove ham from broth and cut up in small pieces, put back into broth.
Add the macaroni, tomato juice and pepper to taste.
Serves 6.
Can freeze.
In medium skillet, brown ground beef; drain.
Blend in soup mix and sour cream.
Add chili powder to Ro-Tel that has been beaten until smooth.
Heat through, but do not boil.
Add salt to taste.
Combine apple juice, flour, cinnamon and salt.
