Mix mayonnaise and butter.
Add cheese, onions, garlic and olives.
Split French bread lengthwise.
Spread half of mixture on each half of bread.
Place each half with butter side up on baking sheet in oven.
Bake at 350° until topping is crusty or until cheese melts.
Bring milk and lard to the boiling point but do not boil. Stir in sugar and salt; let cool to lukewarm.
Beat eggs and add to the milk.
Soak yeast cake in 2 tablespoons warm water and keep warm.
Sift and measure the flour.
Can add onion, green chilies, Mexican tomatoes and chili beans.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Stir in brown sugar, lemon juice, garlic and hot sauce.
Remove from heat.
In large skillet, heat oil over medium heat.
Fry wings, turning occasionally for 10 minutes or until brown and very well done. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Keep hot, or bake wings in a single layer at 450° for 25 minutes.
In skillet, melt 1/2 the butter, add garlic and onion, cook until golden.
Add spinach, cover pan, cook until spinach is heated through.
Meanwhile, cook noodles.
Drain and return to pot.
Toss with remaining butter, spinach mixture, Parmesan and cream until all are blended and heated through.
Serve immediately.
Mix all ingredients well.
Pour into medium-size greased casserole dish.
Bake uncovered, 30 minutes, at 350°.
Mix together chicken broth, refried beans, and tomatoes. Bring to a boil.
Shred chicken breasts, and add to the soup.
Cut flour tortillas in strips and bake at 350° until slightly browned. Place soup in individual bowls, top with cheese, then place tortilla chips on top.
Mix and store.
One serving is 3 teaspoons of mixture to 1 cup of boiling water.
Break florets into small pieces; add onion and cheese.
Dice bacon and fry until crisp; drain well and add to broccoli mixture. Combine mayonnaise, vinegar and sugar, stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Pour over vegetables.
Chill.
Combine milk and lime juice.
Add slightly beaten egg yolks. Pour into pie shell and bake 10 minutes.
Make meringue by beating egg whites and cream of tartar and gradually adding sugar.
Cover pie with meringue, spreading to edges over crust.
Bake at 325° until lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Boil the squash and onion in water until tender; drain.
Next add the cornmeal and egg.
Continue stirring and add the milk and cheese, if you prefer.
Drop the patties into hot grease, preferably in an iron skillet.
Cook just the same as you would any other type of patty.
Cook on low or medium.
Brown and drain on a paper towel.
Boil chicken breasts and debone; cut into small pieces.
Saute chopped onions in Wesson oil.
Add chicken and heat until piping hot.
Season with salt and pepper.
Thaw tortillas.
Fill with chicken and onions and roll up.
Stick with a toothpick to hold together.
Fry in hot grease.
Serve with Roy's Best of the Bayou picante sauce.
Serves 6.
Mix first 7 ingredients; pour in casserole.
On top, put strips of Swiss cheese and almonds.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 more minutes.
Sift together flour, 1 cup sugar and baking powder into small mixer bowl.
Measure egg whites, salt and cream of tartar into large mixing bowl.
Beat with electric mixer at high speed until very soft mounds begin to form.
Beat 1/2 cup additional sugar into egg whites, a tablespoon at a time.
Continue beating until very stiff, straight peaks form when beater is raised.
Do not underbeat.
Toss vegetables. Mix together mayonnaise, lemon juice, sugar and salt. Combine with vegetables. Best if refrigerated overnight.
Mix well.
Put small amount cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 60 minutes until bubbly.
Cook pasta; drain and rinse with cold water. Combine cooled pasta, spinach, tomatoes, artichokes and cheese in a large bowl; toss gently.
In casserole dish place a layer of potatoes (cut into pieces). Then add chopped onion, salt and pepper to taste.
Then add melted butter.
Chop the ham and add to this.
Pour mushroom soup on top of ingredients and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix margarine, powdered sugar and 1 cup flour together and pat in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
While baking, mix rest of ingredients together on low speed.
Pour on hot crust and continue baking for 20 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar while warm.
Cut when cool.
Mix
all dry ingredients until dry buds form.
Add egg. Roll into balls, place on cookie sheet, flatten.
Bake at 375° for 7 minutes.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Add sifted ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Drop by spoonfuls on greased cookie sheet and bake for 12 to 15 minutes in 400° oven.

Chop cabbage and carrots. Mix together and stir in vinegar, sugar and mayonnaise. Salt and pepper to taste. Cover and refrigerate up to 48 hours before serving. Stir every 12 hours if possible. Great with fish or chicken. Serves 6.
Cook chopped onion slightly.
Add beef and brown until fairly done.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Add garlic salt.
Blend in package of chili seasoning.
Add tomato paste plus three cans water.
Stir until blended.
Fold in beans and cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes.
Reduce heat to simmer and cook as long as desired.
I usually let it simmer at least an hour and a half.

recipes.t: Lime Molded Salad(Nice On Buffet Table)
d: Mix jello, boiling water and pineapple.
Chill until firm. Fold in sour cream.
Pour into mold.
Chill 3 hours or more. Serves 8 to 12.
Mix together all ingredients except bacon.
Top with bacon slices.
Bake for 3 hours uncovered at 300°.
Cook noodles as directed on package and drain well.
Toss noodles, cream cheese, and butter together in pan.
Beat together in blender, eggs, sugar, milk and apricot nectar.
Turn noodle mixture into a buttered baking dish and pour egg mixture over the top.
Sprinkle with topping mix.
Bake 350° for approximately 45 minutes.
Can be done ahead and refrigerated all day.
Grease and lightly flour Bundt pan.
Mix together cake flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
Drain pineapple, saving syrup.
Add pineapple syrup to dry
mixture; add eggs, oil and vanilla.
Beat for 3 minutes.
Stir in pineapple, carrots and nuts.
Bake at 325° for about 1 1/2 hours.
Cool 10 minutes in pan before unmolding.
Frost with cream cheese glaze.
Sift flour, salt and soda together.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and bananas, beating until light.
Alternately add flour and milk.
Beat after each addition until smooth.
Add nuts.
Pour batter into greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, or until done.
Remove from pan; cool on rack.
Marinate meat overnight.
If desired, partially cook peppers of your choice and onions, then bake or fry over meat.
Mix all ingredients, except marshmallows, in electric mixer. Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Add marshmallows on top and bake for another 10 minutes.
Take chicken off the bone.
Mix soup and juice in a bowl and in a separate bowl mix melted margarine and stuffing mix.
In casserole dish, layer stuffing mix (reserve some to put on top), then chicken.
Pour soup and juice mixture over chicken, then top with stuffing mix.
Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Place all ingredients in blender container.
Blend at high speed until creamy.
Serve with chips, crackers and fresh vegetables.
Mix all ingredients except steak. Soak meat in mixture for 2 hours or longer, turning periodically. Remove from liquid and broil indoors or on barbecue.
Use mixer on medium speed to mix Crisco and brown sugar.
Add egg and vanilla.
Continue to mix until well blended.
Add drained pineapple to mixture; then add flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Bake 8 to 9 minutes at 400° on lightly greased cookie sheets.
While cookies are warm, glaze with confectioners sugar and pineapple juice, mixed together to make thin glaze.
Makes approximately four dozen.
Mix lemonade (thawed) with condensed milk and vanilla flavoring.
Fold in Cool Whip; stir until mixed well.
Spoon mixture into crust.
Makes 1 pie.
Double for 2 pies.
Keep chilled.

recipes.t: Cream Vegetables With Meat And Pasta
d: Boil chicken; break in strips.
Set aside.
Saute onion and bell pepper until tender.
Cook rotini until tender.
Drain well. Steam mixed vegetables and drain.
Salt and pepper chicken, using garlic salt if desired.
Dip chicken in melted margarine and roll in bread crumbs.
Place in baking dish.
Break up bacon over chicken.
Pour soups over chicken.
Cover and cook in oven on medium heat (350°) for two hours or until tender.
Squeeze a little lemon juice over chicken, if desired.
Fry four slices of bacon until crisp.
Place on a paper towel to drain.
In the bacon fat, brown 1/2 cup chopped green pepper until soft.
Mix together a can of cream-style corn, the bacon (crumbled), green pepper, 3 teaspoons chopped pimentos, a slightly beaten egg and 1/2 can French fried onion rings.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Use remaining onion rings as topping.
Mix all ingredients and store in refrigerator.
Eat and enjoy.
Mix ham, pork, milk, egg and oatmeal or bread crumbs and make into balls.
Arrange in baking dish.
Combine brown sugar, vinegar and water and pour over balls.
Bake 1 hour in medium oven at 350°.
Mix ground chuck, tomato juice and seasoning together.
Add the cheese which has been cubed.
Spread on bread slices and top with strips of cheese.
Put on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brown the hamburger and 1 onion.
Add chili powder to taste; drain any grease after completely browned.
Add the brown sugar, ketchup and barbecue sauce.
Add some more chili powder, if needed.
Mix and simmer.
Add the pork and beans.
Simmer for about 10 minutes.
Add the last onion; simmer for a couple of minutes.

recipes.t: Peerless Rice-Paddy Pie(In Honor Of Stallion, "Alex Miles")
d: Whip the whipping cream; set aside.
Mix the cream cheese and the sugar until smooth.
Add in the sweetened strawberries and mix by tossing lightly.
Set aside.
In a mixing bowl, combine the first five ingredients.
Put this mixture in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.	Sprinkle with dry cake mix and drizzle with melted margarine.
Top with walnuts.
Bake at 350° for one hour or until knife comes out clean.
Serve with ice cream or Cool Whip.
Layer in order given.
Arrange fruit on top of any ready-to-eat cereal to represent a funny face.
(Use bananas for ears or eyes, apple or pineapple for whole face, strawberry for nose, raisins for eyes or beard, peach slice for mouth.)
Serve with milk.
Rehydrate potatoes according to package directions.
Drain well.
With a fork or wire whisk, beat eggs, soft cream cheese and milk in a large bowl until blended.
Stir in potatoes, Parmesan and pepper.
Pour into lightly greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish or shallow 10-inch round casserole.
Bake in preheated 350° oven 35 to 40 minutes, until set and lightly browned.
Let stand 5 minutes before cutting.
Serve as a main dish or cut in small squares for party appetizers.
Reserve 1/3 cup flour to dredge pecans.
Put in blender sesame seed, milk, onion and parsley.
Blend slightly.
Pour into bowl and mix remaining ingredients well. Place in shallow casserole and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°. Grease and flour a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Beat all ingredients, except raisins, in large bowl on medium speed for
1 minute, scraping bowl constantly.
Stir in raisins.
Pour into pan.
Bake
until wooden pick comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes.
Remove
from
pan; cool before slicing.	Makes one 9-inch loaf.
Mix filling ingredients.
Fill buttered buns with mixture. Wrap in aluminum foil and refrigerate.
Just before serving, heat at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.

In large bowl combine Ricotta, spinach, 1 cup Mozzarella, 1/4 cup Parmesan, egg, parsley, onion powder, pepper and garlic powder. Combine spaghetti sauce and water.	Spread 1 cup sauce in an ungreased 9 x 13 baking dish and stuff uncooked manicotti with spinach mixture.
Arrange over sauce.
Pour remaining sauce over manicotti and sprinkle with remaining Mozzarella and Parmesan. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes or until heated through.
Yield:
6 to 8 servings.
Can be done on stove top or with microwave.
Melt oleo.
Mix with sugar.
Add eggs, vinegar, vanilla and coconut.
Add milk, mixing well.
Stir in meal and mix well.
Pour in unbaked pie shell. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until firm.
Combine all ingredients.
Form into two long rolls. Refrigerate overnight.
Slice into thin rings and bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375° until lightly browned (5 to 7 minutes).
Makes about 75 wafers.
Bring to boil the first 4 ingredients.
Boil about 20 minutes or until ball forms in cold water.
Take off stove and add next 3 ingredients.
Beat until creamy.
Add nuts (pecans or walnuts) if you like for nutty fudge.
Beat yolk and add with milk to pumpkin mixture.
Beat egg white and fold carefully into mixture.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 450° a few minutes, then bake at 350° until done.
Mash 1 cup sliced peaches.
Add water and cook 5 minutes.
Mix sugar and cornstarch; add to fruit mixture.
Cook until thick and clear.
Add lemon juice, butter and salt.
Allow mixture to cool completely.
Arrange remaining fruit in cooled pie shell.
Pour cooled glaze over fruit.
Chill thoroughly.
Top with whipped cream.
Drain fruit. Slice bananas into large bowl. Add fruit, marshmallows and mayonnaise. Refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Soften gelatin in cold water.
Dissolve in boiling water. Blend in sour cream, salad dressing, vinegar, salt and pepper. Chill until partially set; whip until fluffy.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Pour into 5-cup ring mold; chill until firm. Garnish with tomatoes or cheese or pineapple or orange slices. Serves 6.
Melt oleo.
Add sugar and stir.
Add milk and heat until fairly warm (not hot).
Add marshmallows.
Bring to a slight boil. Remove from heat and add chocolate and nuts.
Place in buttered jelly roll pan.
Mix together and chill for 4 hours.
Drain fruits.
Serves 8.
Melt chocolate chips, cream cheese and evaporated milk over low heat or in microwave.
Add walnuts.
Microwave syrup and sugar until it comes to a boil.
Add peanut butter; stir until dissolved.
(I put in microwave for about 1 minute more.)
Pour over Rice Krispies.
Spread evenly into buttered 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt chips for only 2 to 3 minutes in microwave.
Spread over the warm Rice Krispie layer.
Spread cream cheese on tortilla.
Top with another tortilla (sandwich).
Cut two tortillas in slices (like a pizza) and place on platter.
Place cup of picante in middle of platter for dipping.
This makes an excellent last minute dish, especially when unexpected company arrives.
Saute pepper and onion in oleo.
Drain the squash and while still hot, add ingredients.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Set oven to 350°.
Have a 13 x 9-inch baking dish on hand.
Use 1 tablespoon of olive oil to grease the pan.
In pan, heat the remaining oil and saute onion over medium-low heat for 15 minutes. Add olives and saute an additional 5 minutes.
Set aside.
Cut dough in half and roll out a piece to fit the bottom and sides of the pan.
Press into the pan.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese.
Place uncooked spinach into Parmesan cheese.
Scatter the onion/olive mixture over the spinach and sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup of Parmesan cheese.
Roll out remaining dough and place on top.
Make 6 to 8 holes in top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is brown.
Serve at once.
Pare eggplant and cut into 1/2-inch slices.
Cook in boiling water with 1/2 teaspoon salt until tender (about 15 minutes). Drain well.
Mash the eggplant into small pieces.
Add onion and bell pepper.
Stir gently.
Add eggs, milk, bread crumbs, cheese, salt and pepper.
Spoon into 1 1/2-quart greased casserole dish. Combine margarine and cracker crumbs.
Sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Brown ground chuck and onion in a frying pan.
Add Worcestershire sauce, tomato sauce and barbecue sauce.
Stir well. Sprinkle oregano over mixture.
Heat thoroughly.
Pour mixture into a casserole dish.
Sprinkle grated cheese over mixture and top with quartered biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes, or until biscuits are brown.
Boil the first five ingredients 5 minutes.
Gradually add milk. Boil and stir continually until firm ball forms in small bowl of water.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla.
Crush cookies in food processor or blender.
Set aside.
In medium bowl, cream together butter, cream cheese and powdered sugar, beating with electric mixer until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Combine soy sauce, ginger and garlic.
Add beef strips and toss.
Set aside while preparing vegetables.

Combine first 3 ingredients. Set aside 3/4 cup of crackers. Press remaining crumb mixture into an ungreased 13 x 9 x 2 baking dish. Set aside. Combine sweetened condensed milk, orange juice concentrate and Mandarin oranges. Mix with mixer. Fold in Cool Whip. Spoon mixture over crust and sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture. Cover and freeze until firm.
Crust:
Melt margarine, mix with flour and add 3/4 cup pecans. Pat out in pie pan.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Take out of oven. Let cool completely.
Bring to a boil; simmer for 15 minutes.
Can and seal.
Have your jars and lids good and hot.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add 7-Up.
Chill until syrupy.
Fold in fruit and marshmallows.
Let congeal.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix together apple filling, water and granulated sugar in a bowl.
In another mixing bowl, mix together all the dry ingredients.
Fold the two together and spoon into a square baking dish that has been sprayed with nonfat cooking spray.
Bake about 30 to 40 minutes, until set and golden brown on top.
Mix well all ingredients.
Place vegetables in a small colander or strainer; drain well. Beat together cream cheese and lemon juice until smooth.
Stir in vegetables and pepper.
Serve on crackers or mini bread sandwiches.
Yield: 2 cups.
Let rhubarb stand in water for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain.
Mix rest of ingredients together.
Add rhubarb.
Mix and bake in 2 single crusts for 30 to 35 minutes at 400°.
This recipe is great for using up leftover cabbage rolls. Cabbage and meat mixture left over from cabbage rolls.
Cook noodles (1/4 package) drain and add to mixture.
Fry cabbage first and add beef mixture.
Fry on low heat.
You can add hot or sweet peppers.
Add 1/2 jar of chicken gravy to mixture.
Serve and Enjoy!
Bake cake in 2 layers according to package directions.
Simmer raspberries, sugar and water on medium heat until thick and total volume is reduced by half.
Whip cream with vanilla and powdered sugar and add 1/2 coconut.
Layer the cake with raspberry sauce, then 1/4 cup whipped cream mixture.
Place next cake layer on top and repeat process.
"Ice" the cake with the remaining whipped cream and sprinkle the remaining whipped cream on top.
Butter 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Line with whole graham crackers. Mix pudding and milk.
Blend in Cool Whip.
Pour 1/2 of pudding mixture over crackers.
Alternate, ending with crackers on top. Refrigerate 2 hours before frosting.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water and allow to cool.
Mix rest of ingredients.
Stir into cooled gelatin.
Put in mold and chill.
Dissolve Jell-O in water; add relish, nuts and celery.
Chill.
Drain and flake salmon.
Add cheese, lemon juice, onion, horseradish, liquid smoke and salt; mix well.
Chill 2 or 3 hours or overnight.
Shape into log.
Chill 2 or 3 hours.
Sprinkle pecans on wax paper.
Roll log in pecans.
Chill until ready to serve with crackers.
Cut potatoes into small portions.
Boil for 30 minutes.
Drain all water and pour into large mixing bowl, then add butter and mix on low until butter has melted.
Slowly add Pet milk and turn up speed to medium.
Add salt and pepper.
Beat until creamy and smooth.
You will need a 9 x 13-inch pan sprayed with nonstick spray.
Cook squash until tender.
Mash and mix with 1/2 cheese and 1/2 cracker crumbs.
Top with remaining cheese and crackers.
Dot with margarine and bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Pour boiling water into Jell-O.
Add frozen orange juice. Add crushed pineapple with juice.
Let stand in fridge until it starts to jell or coats a spoon.
Mash bananas; mix in Jell-O and fold in Cool Whip or whipped cream.
Pour into oiled mold or a 9 x 13 pan or pour into nice glass bowl.
Chill firm.
Best if made day before.
Preheat oven to 400°.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over moderate heat until it is broken into small pieces and is no longer pink.
Drain and mix with parsley and 1/2 cup of Parmesan cheese, scallions and lightly beaten eggs.
Set aside.
Melt butter in a large skillet and saute mushroom caps briefly, rolling them around in the pan.
Cool.
Divide mixture among mushroom caps, mounding it slightly.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in a large lightly buttered pan at 400° for 10 minutes.
Melt butter, stir in flour.
Gradually add half-and-half, stir until thickened.
Add Parmesan; cook and stir until smooth.
Fold in crabmeat, heat 3 minutes, stir occasionally.
Toss fettucini with sauce, sprinkle with parsley.
Serve immediately.
Serves 4.
Cook squash and onion, then drain.
Add salt, pepper, egg, chicken soup and dressing mix.
Then mix all ingredients and add cheese on top.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Mix jello and hot water.
Add orange juice, then add all the other ingredients.
Refrigerate for a few hours before serving.

In large bowl, combine the flour, cinnamon, salt and baking soda. In another bowl, beat the eggs, sugar, pumpkin and oil. Stir into dry ingredients just until moistened. Fold in chocolate chips. Pour into 2 greased 8 x 4 x 2-inch loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes before removing from pans to wire racks. Yield: 2 loaves.
In skillet in hot margarine, cook garlic for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in soup, milk and cheese.
Heat to boiling.
Add chicken.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Toss with fettuccine.
Garnish with cherry tomatoes and fresh parsley, if desired.
Makes 4 servings.
Melt chocolate in boiling water.
Cool.
Cream margarine and sugar until fluffy.
Add egg yolks one at a time beating well after each one.
Add melted chocolate and vanilla.
Mix well. Sift together flour, salt and baking soda.
Add alternately with buttermilk to the chocolate mixture.
Beat well each time.
Beat until smooth.
Fold in egg whites.
Pour into 3 deep 8 or 9-inch cake pans, lined on bottom with wax paper.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cool.
Frost tops only.
Melt cheese
with
milk.
Add taco sauce.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add ground beef to cheese mixture.
Keep warm and serve with nacho chips.
Separate cauliflower and broccoli into florets.
Cut carrots into 2 to 3-inch pieces.
Into a casserole dish, that has been sprayed with vegetable oil, place vegetables evenly.
Slice butter into several "pats" and place on top of mixture.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour, or until tender.
Mix thoroughly the ham, pork, pepper, cracker crumbs, eggs, pineapple juice and onion.
Arrange 2 slices of pineapple along each side of a greased Pyrex loaf pan.
Put ham mixture into loaf pan, pressing against the pineapple slices to hold them in place. Cut remaining pineapple slices into fifths and place on top of ham loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours.
In mixing bowl (using a wooden spoon) or in the large bowl of an electric mixer, cream the butter and shortening together until well-blended and soft.
Then beat in sugars in turn, beating well after each until fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well each time, then beat in vanilla.
Cream oleo and sugar until creamy.
Add eggs, beating well. Blend in potatoes and vanilla.
Combine flour, cocoa and baking soda.
Add alternately with milk, blending well after each addition.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until cake tests done. Cool.
Frost with your favorite frosting.
Make jello and cool.
Drain pineapple, mix with cottage cheese and nuts.
Add to cooled jello then stir in the whipped topping and refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients and stuff opossum with it.
Sew up opening with large needle and coarse thread.
Roast in oven roaster on wire rack at 350° until tender and richly brown.
Cut tomatoes in 1/2-inch thick slices.
Mix flour, salt and pepper.
Dip tomatoes in mixture, covering both sides.
Fry slowly in small amount of hot fat until browned; turn and brown other side.
Mix all together.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In bowl, combine milk and lemon juice. Mix well. Stir in the pineapple, cranberry sauce, marshmallows, pecans
and food coloring, if desired. Fold in the whipped topping. Spoon into a 13 x 9 x 2 inch baking dish. Freeze until firm, 4 hours or overnight. Cut into squares. Yield: 12-16 servings.
Butter sides of a heavy 2 quart saucepan.
In it combine sugar and milk.
Heat and stir over medium heat until sugar dissolves and mixture comes to a boil.
Then cook to soft-ball stage (234 degrees).
Remove from heat; add remaining ingredients and stir until blended.
Pour into buttered 9x9x2-inch pan.
Score in squares when warm, cut when firm.
1st Layer: 2 cans (drained and blended) Trappy's jalapeno pinto beans.
In a large pan, combine all ingredients.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Remove lid and simmer an additional 5 to 10 minutes.
Saute onion and green pepper in butter or margarine.
Then add remaining ingredients.
Follow instructions on jello box, then fold in whipped cream. Stir in remainder of ingredients; place in fridge for 2 1/2 hours. Serve on lettuce leaf.

recipes.t: Hilda'S Boiled Custard Peach Ice Cream
d: Beat all ingredients, except peaches.
Cook on low heat until it's showing thickness, stirring all the time.
When custard is done, add peaches.
Put into ice cream freezer and freeze or you can put in the freezer.
Boil chunks of duck breasts until tender; discard water. Cook rice as directed on package. Brown sausage and onion. Mix all ingredients; pour in greased pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut up 1 chicken into small pieces and salt and pepper it. Place rice in bottom of Dutch oven.
Add 1 can of mushroom soup, 1 can of water and stir.
Place chicken pieces on top of rice and soup.
Cook on High for 15 minutes.
Then cook on Medium-Low setting for 25 minutes.
Let stand for 15 to 20 minutes before serving.
Serves 4.
Combine chicken and all ingredients. Mix gently. Place in casserole dish.
Mix. Shape into bar. Wrap in foil. Freeze until firm.
Makes 1 serving. Exchanges: 1 milk, 1 fruit, 1 bread, 1 protein and 1 fat.
Put sugar, syrup and water on stove to boil.
Beat egg whites until very stiff.
Let syrup cook until it forms a hard ball when dropped in cold water.
Pour slowly into egg whites, beating constantly with mixer.
Add vanilla and beat as long as possible. Drop by spoon on wax paper.
Set bowl in hot water if candy begins to harden.
(May add nuts.)
Combine zucchini and salt; let stand 15 minutes.
Rinse in cold water and drain well.
Saute onion in butter until tender. Add zucchini.
Cook, stirring constantly until all liquid is absorbed.
Stir in sour cream and pepper.
Cook squash and onion in slight amount of water until tender. Mash.
Add other ingredients; sprinkle with crumbs and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine the first 8 ingredients.
Fold in apples, nuts and raisins.
Spoon into a well-greased cake pan or a 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes or until cake tests done.
Serves 16 to 20.

Section oranges, removing seeds. Save extra juice and make up to 1 cup with concentrated orange juice. Mix flour and sugar; add 1 cup orange juice and cook until boils. Let boil a few minutes and add butter and stir in. Cool to room temperature. Stack rounds with sections, between and over top with sweetened cream. Serve at room temperature.
Place pineapple and juice in pan.
Bring to a boil; add lime Jell-O and dissolve.
Fold in cheese.
Cool slightly; fold in whipping cream.
Chill and cut in squares.
Combine sugar and cocoa in a 2-quart boiler.
Stir in milk and butter.
Cook until mixture comes to a rolling boil; stir well. Continue to cook on high for 1 minute.
Remove mixture and stir in vanilla.
Add oats; mix thoroughly.
Add coconut and nuts (optional).
Drop by teaspoon onto waxed paper.
Place in refrigerator to set.
Brown
chicken	that
has
been
sprinkled
with Tony's seasoning.	The more you use, the spicier the chicken.
Remove chicken
from skillet.
Saute chopped onion and bell pepper in chicken
grease
(2 tablespoons).
Place chicken back in skillet. Pour
tomatoes
over
chicken.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to avoid sticking.
Serve over hot yellow rice.
Cream sugar and margarine; add eggs and lemon extract.
Mix. Add flour and baking powder.
Mix together.
Add nuts and raisins last; mix well.
Put in a greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 275° for 1 hour and 45 minutes.
Combine brown sugar, orange juice and mustard.
Mix well. Spoon over ham, shoulder roast, (pork) etc.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine sour cream and margarine.
Fold in flour.
Fill greased muffin tins three-fourths full.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes.
Makes 18 biscuits.
Combine sweet potatoes, salt and 1/2 cup boiling water in saucepan; simmer, covered, for 15 minutes or until tender.
Pour off all but 1/4 cup stock; dot with butter.
Combine orange juice, corn syrup and brown sugar.
Blend well.
Pour over sweet potatoes.
Simmer, basting frequently for 15 minutes.
Combine undrained pineapple, whipped topping and pudding mix. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Cut cake lengthwise into 3rds.
Spread 1/3 pudding mixture over each layer of cake, ending with pudding on top.
Chill 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with sliced almonds.
Serves 12.
Brown ground beef in skillet; drain excess fat.
Add soup and seasonings, simmer about 5 to 10 minutes to blend flavors, stirring occasionally.
Serve on buns.
Drain pimentos and chop parsley.
Combine with dressing in a large Ziploc bag; add mushrooms and toss to coat.
Chill.
Mix all ingredients. Pour into greased casserole.
Top with 1/2 cup of grated Cheddar cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes. May serve with crackers.
Mix sugar, salt, milk and egg together.
Cook until thick. Let cool.
Add vinegar and peanut butter.
Cut up bananas and pour dressing over them.
Sprinkle with peanuts.
Mix well and pour over all ingredients.
Put in a crock or covered dish.
Let stand in the refrigerator.
"The longer it stands, the better it is."
Put the bacon pieces in pan and fry until almost done.
Then add all other ingredients, except hamburger meat.
I add that about 30 minutes before soup is done.
You may also add carrots, English peas, corn or any other vegetable you would like, but if you add extra vegetables, you will also need to add extra liquid. Cook about 1 1/2 hours.
In small pan over low heat stir together honey and peanut butter until smooth.
Remove from heat; add cocoa powder and blend well.
Add remaining ingredients.
Press into greased 9 x 9 x 2 inch pan.
Chill until firm.
Cut into 36 squares.
Cook peas; drain.
Mix ingredients and chill.
Boil chicken, debone and retain broth (1 1/2 to 2 cups). Prepare rice with equal parts water in 2 to 3-quart pan.
Melt margarine and mix in flour.
Add broth slowly, stirring constantly, then melt cheese in the sauce.
Defrost broccoli and cut into small pieces.
Bring water and salt to a boil; add rice.
Cover and remove from heat.
Let set for 5 minutes.
Melt butter in skillet; saute onion and celery until tender.
In a large mixing bowl, combine rice, celery and onion with remaining ingredients.
Pour into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In large bowl, mix sugar and butter.
Beat in egg and molasses.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Roll dough on well-floured board.
Cut into desired shapes.
Place on greased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cool.
Decorate as desired.
Makes about 15 (6-inch) cookies.
Mix in pan; turn to boil. Boil 1 minutes; turn off. Add Maple and vanilla.
Combine pineapple juice and pudding mix in bowl; mix well.
Add banana, pie filling and undrained pineapple; toss to mix.
Pour into serving bowl.
Chill until set.
May substitute any fruit juice for pineapple juice.
Yield:
10 servings.
Mix water, sugar, Karo and cornstarch together.
Cook until thickened.
Add Jell-O and mix well.
Cool and pour part in bottom of baked pie shell.
Leave strawberries whole and pour remainder of mixture over strawberries.
Garnish with whipped cream.
Mix all ingredients until well blended.
Serve with Hawaiian bread.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease 9-inch square pan.
In medium bowl, beat butter until creamy.
Stir in sugar and brown sugar. Add flour, salt and baking soda.
Stir until mixture is crumbly. Set aside 1 cup of crumb mixture for top.
Press remaining mixture into pan.
Stir lemon juice into apricot preserves.
Spread into pan, leaving a 4-inch border around all edges.
Sprinkle preserves with remaining 1 cup crumb mixture.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until browned.
Bake cake mix in a 13 x 9-inch pan.

Combine applesauce and soda in a small bowl. Cream butter with sugar in large bowl. Stir in egg, cinnamon, salt, allspice and cloves. Blend in applesauce mixture. Mix in flour and raisins. Pour into greased 5 x 9 loaf pan or use smaller pans. Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes. Cool 10 minutes in pan on rack.
Take out of pan and cool on rack completely.
Melt margarine over medium heat.
Add flour.
Slowly stir in 2 cups of milk.
When slightly thickened, slowly add rest of milk, chicken granules, broccoli and cheese.
Stir until smooth and thick.
Enjoy!
Mix fruit cocktail, juice and all, with pudding until pudding is thick.
Mix in Cool Whip.
Add well drained pineapple and marshmallows.
Mix and refrigerate.
Mix all ingredients together.
Roll in wax paper and refrigerate.
Cool and slice.
Combine all ingredients.
In a medium saucepan, simmer 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Serves 5.
In bowl combine all ingredients.
Divide meat mixture into 4 hamburger patties.
Sear 5 inches from hot coals for 2 minutes. Turn and cook for 6 minutes for medium done.
Serve hot, topped with avocado, onion, lettuce and tomato.
Top with cheese cracker crumbs rolled in 1/2 stick melted margarine.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cut boneless venison into thin, small steaks.
Sprinkle with garlic and onion salt; pound well.
Roll in flour and brown meat in skillet.
Alternate layers of meat, cream of mushroom soup and sliced onion in a casserole.
Add 1 soup can of water over all. Cover and bake 2 hours at 300°.
Boil broccoli 10 minutes until tender.
Drain.
Cook ziti 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain.
Saute garlic in olive oil in large skillet until lightly browned.
Add broccoli; cook 1 minute.
Add ziti, cream and Parmesan and cook 2 minutes, tossing well.
Spoon into 9 x 13-inch Pyrex pan and top with Mozzarella.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Mix crushed Lorna Doones and melted margarine.
Spread on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake for 15 minutes at 350°.
Peel 5 to 6 peaches or apple slices into small slices and place in bottom of Pyrex dish.
Melt margarine; add sugar and flour.
(This will be dry and crumbly.)
Sprinkle over fruit and pat down.
Bake in a 350° oven for 1 hour.
Crumble 1 1/2 slices of toasted bread into crab meat and combine ingredients with milk blended with mayonnaise.
With other 1 1/2 slices of toasted bread, grate and sprinkle over top of casserole.
Dot butter on top. Put in stove and cook until warm through.
Serve.
Heat slowly in double boiler.
Dip balls in this mixture.
Combine the sugar, milk, half and half, whipping cream and lemon rind.
Add lemon juice and beat well.
Fold in egg whites. Add food coloring, if desired.
Pour into freezer can of 1 gallon hand or electric freezer.
Let ripen at least 2 hours.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Add rest of ingredients; simmer 1 hour.
Cream sugar and margarine; add one egg at a time.
Add milk, corn meal, vinegar, lemon juice and salt.
Pour into crust.
Cook 10 minutes at 375°, then reduce heat to 325° and cook 40 minutes more.
Pour mixed ingredients over chicken.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
(Turn or shake chicken to make sure all chicken pieces are coated.)
Place chicken in baking dish and bake at 300° about an hour or can be grilled.
(Discard marinade, do not cook chicken in the mixture.)
Mix all juices as directed on package. Next, mix all ingredients together. Refrigerate until ready to use. Add 1 quart of ginger ale. Yields 2 gallons.
Mix juice and milk together.
Add other ingredients.
Put in a pie shell and chill.
Makes 2 or 3 pies.
Mix together butter and shortening.
Beat in 1 1/2 cups sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Sift together flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt.
Blend into creamed mixture.
Shape rounded teaspoons of dough into small balls.
Combine 3 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon; roll balls in sugar/cinnamon mixture.
Place 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheet. Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
(Be careful, they burn easily!!) Remove from baking sheet; cool on racks.
Makes approximately 6 dozen.
Cook pasta; drain.
Put in saucepan.
Stir in olive oil on low-medium heat.
Add package dressing.
Stir in veggies.
Heat until veggies are tender.
Serve.
* Will leave some leftovers for sandwiches.
Mix everything together.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour in a greased casserole dish.
Serves 4 to 5.
Combine brown sugar, beaten egg, water and vinegar in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil; remove from heat and add vanilla. Let cool.
When ready to serve (or just before) slice and cut up bananas into bite size pieces.
Pour sauce over bananas and top with chopped peanuts.
Melt butter in frying pan.
Add cleaned shrimp.
Saute 5 minutes.
Add Creole sauce and water or stock and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve on hot platter in ring of boiled rice.
Brown ground beef or turkey and drain.
Add garlic, onion, celery, cabbage, water and potatoes; season with salt and pepper. Cook until tender.
Add about 1 cup of sour cream.
Serve with salad, rye bread and butter.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Prepare Basic Biscuits, rolling dough about 1/4-inch thick.
Using a sharp knife or pizza cutter, cut dough into narrow strips, 1/2-inch wide.
Cut strips into 3-inch sticks.
Dip sticks into melted butter and roll in mixture of Parmesan cheese, oregano and garlic salt.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet, about 3/4-inch apart.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes about 3 dozen sticks.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add tomato sauce and chili mix to ground beef.
Spread cream cheese in bottom of 9 x 13-inch ovenproof dish.
Spread chili mixture over cream cheese.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes in a 350° oven, or in microwave until "bubbly".
Serve with tortilla chips.
In bottom of long, ungreased cake pan, mix the cocoa, brown sugar and water.
Sprinkle the marshmallows over this.
Pour the cake batter over this (prepared according to package directions). Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes. Serve warm with ice cream or Cool Whip.
Bake cake in layers as directed.
Prepare our creamy white frosting mix as directed, except dissolve 2 teaspoons powdered instant coffee in the hot water before adding to the dry mix.
In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of Triscuits crumbs, honey, raisins, peanut butter and dry milk.
Shape into one-inch balls. Roll balls in Triscuits crumbs.
Serve immediately or store in refrigerator.
Yield:
5 dozen.
Form ingredients into a ball.
Chill; roll in chopped pecans. Refrigerate until serving.
Blend together the first 6 ingredients.
Shape the dough into walnut size balls.
Dip in reserved egg whites.
Roll in chopped walnuts.
Place on cookie tray; press thumb in center.
Bake at 325°.
When cool, fill centers with apricot jam.
Drain green beans and corn.
Put green beans in a long casserole dish and spread corn on top.
Mix together sour cream, soup and salt and spread on top of beans and corn.	Mix cheese, butter and crackers.
Put on top and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Put brown sugar in top of double boiler.
Add cubed bread. Combine eggs, vanilla, salt, milk and raisins.
Pour mixture over bread.
Don't stir.
Cook for 1 hour in double boiler (undisturbed).
When done, turn upside down on serving dish.
In large saucepan, combine first 6 ingredients.
Bring to boiling.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
In 6-quart Dutch oven, in 2 tablespoons oil, brown roast. Spoon off fat.
Stir in mushroom soup, onion soup mix and 1 cup water.
Cover; simmer 2 hours, turning occasionally.
Add vegetables.
Cover; cook 40 minutes or until roast and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove roast and vegetables to platter.

recipes.t: Oatmeal Cookies With Chocolate Covered Raisins
d: Heat oven to 375°.
Beat butter and sugars until creamy.
Add eggs, milk and vanilla; beat well.
Add combined flour, baking soda and salt; mix well.
Stir in oats and chocolate covered raisins. Drop by rounded tablespoonful onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 minutes.
Cool 1 minute on cookie sheet, then remove.
Pack cucumbers in jar and pour over, after boiling, vinegar and water.
Put in each jar dill, grape leaves, garlic, pepper and alum.
Cap and seal.
(Green tomatoes, bell pepper and sliced onions may be added too.)
Add dry ingredients to mixer bowl.
Whisk to blend.
Cut cold shortening and butter into small pieces and add to bowl.
Mix on stir for 1 minute until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Continue on stir while adding the 3/4 cup of cold buttermilk.
Mix just until moistened.
Form dough into a ball and turn out onto lightly floured board.
Knead 5 to 6 times and roll out to 1/2-inch thick.
Cut into 2 inch rounds.
Arrange biscuits on greased baking pan.
Brush with 1 tablespoon buttermilk.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Yield:
16 biscuits.
Mix eggs, oil and baby food well, then add remaining ingredients.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Toothpick should come out clean.
Place all ingredients in blender, except strawberries.
Blend on high speed until well mixed, about 30 seconds.
Garnish each shake with 1 strawberry.
Soak wheat in water a few minutes.
Squeeze dry between palms of hands.
Chop onions, parsley, mint and tomatoes very fine.
Add wheat, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Serve on fresh lettuce.
Serves 6.
Combine cola and barbecue sauce.
Pour into skillet.
Add chicken and bring just to boiling.
Cover, reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Serves 4.
Mix all together and put in casserole and sprinkle top with bacon crumbs.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes, covered. Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Add minced onion, taco sauce and stewed tomatoes.
Simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Add meat mixture to shells and arrange lettuce, cheese and tomatoes.
Toss lightly. Serve at once.
Yields 6 servings.
Bake cake; make pudding as directed.
Cool them both.
In large bowl, break cake in small squares and layer it in bowl. Then pour 1/4 Schnapps over cake.
Make 1 layer of pudding, 1 layer of pie filling and layer of whipped cream.
Sprinkle with coconut and pecans (crushed).
Then repeat layers and refrigerate until served.
Hope you enjoy.
Cream sugar and butter together; add remaining ingredients and mix together.
Pour into 2 greased and floured loaf pans.
I use milk chocolate chips, baby M&M's and toffee pieces.
Combine dry ingredients, stir in nuts.
Add rest of ingredients (oil, bananas, eggs and pineapple).
Stir until moistened.
Spoon batter into 2 greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pans.
Bake for 1hour or until done.
Cool 10 minutes in pan, then put on rack to cool.
Bake at 350°.

recipes.t: Do-Ahead And Chill Chocolate Angel Torte
d: Combine sugar and cornstarch in a medium saucepan; mix to blend.
Stir in Carnation and water.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture begins to thicken.
Stir a small amount of hot mixture into egg.
Return egg mixture to saucepan.
Continue cooking until mixture just comes to a boil and thickens.
Stir in vanilla and chocolate.
Cover surface of filling with wax paper; chill.
Slice cake horizontally, making three layers.
Fill and frost cake layers.
Sprinkle nuts over top of cake.
Chill several hours before serving.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Put 12 eggs in pan; break yolks.
Put chopped onion and pepper on top of eggs and salt and pepper.
Add mushrooms, sausage and cheese.
Pour over whipped cream.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Uncover and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Let stand 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut and serve.
Combine cherries, raisins and bourbon.
Cover and let stand overnight.
Drain fruit and reserve bourbon.
Preheat oven to 275°.
Cream butter and sugars until light.
Add egg yolks, a little at a time, and mix well.
Combine 1/2 cup flour with the nutmeg, baking powder and chopped pecans.
Set aside.
Add remaining flour and bourbon alternately to the butter mixture, beating well after each addition.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into the batter.
Then fold in soaked fruit and pecan flour. Turn into a greased 10-inch tube pan that has been lined with greased waxed paper.
Bake for 3 1/2 hours.
Cool before removing from pan.
Combine ingredients in an electric blender or with the potato masher.
Delicious with pita bread, as a dip, or as a sandwich on whole wheat bread.
Sprinkle onion soup mix on roost beef. Bake according to directions.
Keep drippings for sauce. Make regular gravy with cornstarch. Stir into roast beef. Put in crock pot to keep hot. Put on buns.
Melt butter and marshmallows; add Rice Krispies and vanilla. Press mixture into a 9 x 13-inch buttered pan.
Melt chocolate chips and pour over the top.
Let set in refrigerator for awhile.
Grind crackers to make crumbs and combine with melted margarine. Press into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix all ingredients.
Stuff in peppers and wrap in foil.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix the first 6 ingredients; form into a ball.
Roll in fine cut parsley.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Serve with crackers.
Cook bacon in large skillet until crisp; remove to paper toweling to drain, then crumble.
Cook beef in fat remaining in skillet until no pink remains.
Add onion; saute just until tender. Combine beef, onion, catsup, salt, brown sugar, mustard and vinegar in a 3-quart baking dish.
Partially drain all the beans, add to baking dish, stir gently to mix.
Sprinkle bacon on top. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Makes 8 servings as a main dish.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Cream together the butter and sugar. Stir in the eggs, molasses and vinegar.
Sift and add dry ingredients.
Mix until well blended.
Form the dough into 3/4-inch balls by rolling dough in between your palms.
Bake on a greased cookie sheet for 12 minutes.
In glass pie plate, layer kraut and cheese.
In separate bowl beat biscuit mix, milk, mayo, eggs and chili sauce.
Slowly pour over meat and cheese and allow to soak in.
Makes own crust.
Bake at 325° until puffed and brown on top.
Prepare gelatin according to the recipe on the box.
Divide in half.
Place other half in serving bowl and refrigerate until set. Refrigerate other half until thick.
I use the quick-set recipe on box being careful to remove all remaining ice cubes.
Place cereal in large bowl and set aside.
In small saucepan over low heat, melt caramels with water, stirring until smooth. Add almond extract and stir.
Pour over cereal, stir until all pieces are coated.
Spread on wax paper or lightly greased pan to cool.
Separate pieces while cooling.
Store in airtight container. Makes 4 cups.
On each flour tortilla, place sour cream down center, chunks of chicken, salsa, onions, cheeses, peppers and more salsa (as desired).
Roll side of tortilla up and secure with a toothpick. Place burritos on a baking sheet and broil in oven for a few minutes, until burritos begin to brown and crisp.
Serve.
Good with Spanish rice.
Blend all ingredients on low speed.
Turn mixer to high speed and beat until fluffy and of proper consistency.
Mix and bake corn bread according to directions on package. Cool and crumble the corn bread.
Meanwhile, cook the sausage, crumbling as it cooks.
Drain.
Chop pickles, tomatoes, onion and cucumber.
Stir in sausage and all but 1/2 cup crumbled corn bread. Mix well.
Use reserved corn bread to decorate the top.
Also garnish with green pepper strips.
Makes about 6 servings.
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly and add eggs, one at a time. Mix well.
Add dry ingredients and milk alternately.
Add melted chocolate, vanilla and nuts.
Mix well.
Bake in a 7 1/2 x 11 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch pan at 350° for about 25 minutes.
Cut in strips or squares while warm and dust with powdered sugar.
Cook noodles and drain.
Melt butter in hot noodles in a large bowl.
Once butter has melted, add beaten eggs, sugar and cottage cheese.
Stir well.
Add all other ingredients.
Bake in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°
or until noodles turn golden brown.
Allow to cool somewhat before serving.
Good either warm or cold, as a side dish or dessert.
In a large frying pan or Dutch oven, cook the meat and vegetables over medium heat until the meat is browned and the vegetables are tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the V-8, catsup, sugar, vinegar and Worcestershire and simmer, uncovered, over low heat for 2 hours.
The mixture will resemble spaghetti sauce. (Remove lid during last 30 minutes of cooking if it seems too thin.)
Sauce keeps well and freezes well.
This dish can be used on cocktail rolls as an hors d'oeuvre or piled on hamburger buns for lunch.
Drain raspberries carefully in fine strainer.
Don't push pulp through strainer.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Place a disposable coffee filter in a strainer over a medium bowl.
Pour raspberry juice into filter.
Should have 1/2 cup clear juices.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Parboil ribs about 15 minutes.
Put in baking pan.
Pour sauce over and bake slowly in a 350° oven until done.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
Mix crumbs, nuts, sugar, cinnamon and butter.
Set aside.
Prepare cake mix according to directions.
Pour half the batter in pan.
Sprinkle half the crumbs over batter.
Cover with remaining batter. Sprinkle the rest of crumbs over top.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and process until smooth.
Makes 1 tall glass.
Preheat gas grill on high for 15 minutes.
Lightly garlic salt both sides of ribs.
Put ribs on grill.
Close lid.
Rotate ribs frequently.
Saute bacon and chopped onion in bacon fat.
Do not drain. Mix all ingredients and cook on very low heat (in heavy bottom pot or kettle) for about 1/2 hour.
Very good with pork chops, ham or fried chicken.
Makes 5 servings.
Mix egg, sweet potato, sugar and shortening in a bowl; beat until smooth.
Stir in enough flour to make a dough stiff enough to turn onto a floured surface.
Knead a few times; then roll out 1/2-inch thick.
Cut with a biscuit cutter or jar lid and bake on an ungreased baking sheet at 350° for about 15 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time; add
flavorings.
Sift all dry ingredients together and add alternately
with
sour
cream to first mixture.
Bake at 325° for one hour.
Mix cake mix (save 2/3 cup), margarine and 1 egg until moist. Press flat into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 350° until lightly browned.
Mix sugar, remaining eggs and vanilla together.
Add corn syrup and 2/3 cup dry cake mix.
Lightly stir in pecans.
Pour this filling over browned crust.
Return to oven. Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Let cool and cut into bars.
Saute onions and mushrooms in butter.
Arrange onions and mushrooms in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with Swiss cheese, then the bread.
Mix soup, milk and Worcestershire.
Pour over top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake uncovered 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients, except cheese, in food processor or blender.
Puree until smooth.
Stir in cheese.
Yields 1 cup.
Drain juice into saucepan and heat until boiling.
Stir in both pkgs. of jello.
Set aside to cool.
Add water and coke. Chill until partly thickened.
Fold in pecans, cream cheese, pineapple and cherries.
Spray jello mold with non-sticking spray.
Cut asparagus into 1-inch lengths.

Cook until barely tender. Make a cream sauce of margarine, flour, milk and seasonings. Arrange alternate layers of asparagus, sliced cooked eggs, cream sauce and cheese in greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Sprinkle with buttered crumbs.
Bake in a moderate oven, 350° for 30 minutes. Serves 6.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
In a large bowl, combine cake mix, 1 cup of oats, cheese and 6 tablespoons of margarine at low speed until crumbly.
Reserve 1 cup of crumbs for topping.
To remaining crumbs, blend 1 egg.
Press into prepared pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Cook pasta according to package, rinse and drain.
In large bowl, mix all ingredients; toss, chill and serve.
Mix 2 packages of softened cream cheese with mayonnaise, dill weed and chopped onions.
Bake crescent rolls at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Spread out on a cookie sheet or pizza pan; let cool.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix mushroom soup with milk; reserve 1/2 cup of the mixture. Mix remaining soup mixture wit rice, mushrooms (including liquid) and half of the onion soup mix.
Pour into oblong baking dish, 11 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch.
Place chicken breasts on top.
Pour reserved soup mixture over chicken breasts; sprinkle with remaining onion soup mix.
Cover and bake 1 hour; uncover and bake 15 minutes longer.
Makes 4 servings.

Slice eggs in half lengthwise; remove yolks and set whites aside. In a small bowl, mash yolks with a fork. Add the mayonnaise, pickle relish, mustard, garlic salt, Worcestershire sauce and pepper; mix well. Stuff or pipe into the egg whites. Refrigerate until serving. Makes 2 dozen.
Mix together lettuce, cauliflower, broccoli and peas in a large bowl.
Blend together salad dressing, dressing mix and sugar; mix into vegetables.
Top with bacon bits and shredded cheese.
(Other vegetables may be used if desired, such as green pepper, cucumber, carrots, celery or tomato.)
Cream
shortening,
margarine and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Fold in flour, 1 cup at a time.
Add baking powder with last cup.
Blend well. Add pineapple
and
milk.
Beat 3 minutes.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Chicken Filling:
Cook chicken with salt, savory, garlic, onion and 4 cups water.
Take off broth, remove chicken bones and break meat into 1-inch pieces.
Cook a few minutes more.
Strain broth and reserve 3 cups.
Toast the English muffin.
Place on a plate.
In a skillet, fry the bacon until crisp.
Drain on a paper towel.
Reduce the heat.
Break the egg into the skillet; cook to desired firmness. Slide egg onto the muffin.
Crumble the crisp bacon over the egg. Pour excess fat out of the skillet.
Heat pizza sauce and pour over egg.
Sprinkle cheese over all.
Combine all ingredients and let set several hours.
Melt morsels in double boiler, stirring constantly to smooth consistency.
Add peanuts and chow mein noodles and mix well. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper until hardened.
Store in airtight container.
Does not need to be refrigerated.
First Layer:
Mix flour, margarine and nuts. Pat in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Blend all in blender and pour over salad of fresh spinach, mushrooms, boiled eggs and bacon.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Pour pie filling in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Add pineapple. Sprinkle cake mix over pineapple.
Pour margarine over cake mix. Add coconut.
Sprinkle pecans over.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour. Yields 15 pieces.
Mix and decorate with grapes.
Serves 20 people.
Cut butter into small bits; reserve 2 tablespoons for on top. Dissolve soda in hot water.
Stir in molasses.
Pour in unbaked shell.
Mix dry ingredients: flour, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, baking powder and soda.
Spread mixture into shell.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Reduce to 350° for 25 minutes or until the center is firm.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons mix (reserved) on top.
Bake 10 minutes.
Serves 8.
Sprinkle yeast on warm water; stir until blended.
Stir in 2 teaspoons of sugar; set aside.
Combine cottage cheese, onion, dill weed, baking powder, 2 tablespoons of sugar and eggs.
Mix well.
Add yeast mixture and mix well.
Add flour to make a stiff dough.
Knead on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic. Place dough in greased bowl; turn to bring greased side up. Cover; let rise in warm place until doubled (1 to 1 1/2 hours). Punch down.
Turn onto floured surface; knead a few times.
Divide in half.
Shape into bread pans and let rise until doubled.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Remove from pans to rack.
Brush tops with butter.
Place oil in skillet, about 1-inch.
Let it get hot.
Cut small hole in center of biscuits with salt shaker lid.
Drop into oil.
Turn when brown.
Brown other side.
Drain on paper towel. Roll in sugar, powdered sugar or cinnamon.
Makes 20 donuts and 20 holes.
Melt butter; blend in flour.
Add milk all at once.
Cook and stir until thick and bubbly; cook and stir 1 minute more.
Remove from heat.
Add ham, onion and mustard.
Chill well.

Saute onion in oleo and add rice and uncooked broccoli.

Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes or until a pick comes out clean when inserted in cake.

Place on top of meat.
Pour remainder of broken-up tomatoes and juice on top.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper as desired.

Add sugar and vanilla.

Add soup; simmer 10 minutes.

Put ingredients in layers.
Lettuce in the bottom and peas on top.
Spread 1 pint mayonnaise on top.
Sprinkle with 1 or 2 tablespoons sugar.
Cover with Romano or Parmesan cheese.
Garnish with crumbled bacon or Bac*Os.

Spoon over chicken.
Shred cabbage medium fine.
Saute onion in oil in large pot. Add cabbage and saute lightly.
Add wine, vinegar, sugar and apple.
Cook 35 minutes or until cabbage is wilted.
Freezes well.
Mix and bake at 325°.
Bring ingredients to a boil; cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, after it boils.
Remove from heat and add powdered sugar. Beat until creamy.
Chop and combine vegetables, salt and sugar.
Cook until it begins to thicken; add vinegar and spices.
Cook until it becomes a thick sauce and seal.
Combine cheese, flour, paprika and pepper.
Add beaten egg whites and shape into small balls.
Roll in cracker crumbs.
Fry in hot oil at 375°.
Drain.
Serve hot.
Yield:
8 servings.
Combine the first 3 ingredients in a saucepan; cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Set aside.
Saute onion in butter until tender.
Stir onion, soup, milk and broccoli into rice.
Spoon into a greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch dish; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Combine all ingredients in a large mixing bowl, stirring to blend.
Beat at medium speed for 5 minutes (700 strokes by hand), scraping sides of bowl frequently.
Take the hard roe of shad; season with salt and pepper.
Roll in flour.
Immerse in beaten eggs.
Roll again in bread crumbs or corn meal.
Fry in enough fat to cover.
Fry slowly.
Shad roe has a tendency to pop.
Drain on paper toweling.
Serve with tomato sauce and lemon slices.
Melt caramels in water in saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth; set aside.
In a large bowl, mix cereal and nuts. Pour melted caramels over and mix well.
Pat entire mixture into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle chocolate and butterscotch chips over cereal mixture.
Place in a 200° oven until soft. Spread melted chips; cool and cut into bars.
Cut lobster into bite size pieces and cook slowly in butter to start color.
Do not cook too long or too fast or it will be tough.
Remove lobster meat.
Add flour, mixed with seasoning, to fat in pan, adding cream and top milk slowly.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add lobster and bread, torn into small pieces.
Pour into greased casserole.
Top with a few buttered crumbs and bake until bubbly and delicately browned.
Mix together sugar, flour and cinnamon.
Add oil, eggs, vanilla and pumpkin.
Pour into a greased tube pan and bake for 1 hour at 325°.
Let cool completely.
Coat chicken breasts in the melted butter.
Roll in bread crumbs mixed with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in a shallow pan for 1 hour in oven at 350°.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise.
Scoop out pulp, leaving 1/8 inch thick shells.
(Save pulp for another use.)
Brush with melted butter; broil 6 inches from heat until crisp.
Place cut side up on ungreased baking sheet.
Sprinkle with garlic salt and cheese.
Broil 30 seconds or until cheese melts.
Top with bacon and chives.
Yield: 8 servings.
Combine flour, salt and pepper.
Dredge pot roast in seasoned flour and brown in fat in Dutch oven.
Pour off drippings. Dissolve bouillon cube in hot water.
Add bouillon, bay leaves, garlic salt, marjoram and basil to meat.
Cover tightly and cook slowly 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until meat is tender.
Remove meat to hot platter, discard bay leaves and thicken cooking liquid with flour for gravy.
Mix together grated cheese, mayonnaise, celery and onion.
Mix together Ritz crackers and melted butter.
Grease casserole. Place vegetables on the bottom, cheese mixture next, then spread crackers and butter mixture on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Prepare the first four ingredients in salad bowl.
In blender, place the remaining ingredients and mix for 1 minute.
Store left over dressing in refrigerator.
Keeps well.
Put a layer of wafers in baking dish.
Add a layer of fruit to which sugar has been added, then add nuts to which margarine has been added.
Make another layer of each.
Chill 4 hours.
Unmold on cold platter.
Top with whipped topping and cherries.
Blend cream cheese and mayonnaise.
Add olives, olive liquid and nuts.
This should be soupy but thickens up after chilling. Excellent spread on small slices party rye bread, toast or bagel rounds or crackers.
In pot, melt margarine.
Put flour and pepper in margarine and blend.
Add milk and stir until margarine mixture is melted.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Cook macaroni as directed.
Put macaroni in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Put cheese mixture over macaroni.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix sugar and oil in blender.
Add remainder of ingredients. Blend.
Chill.
Very good.

recipes.t: Lemon, Lime And Cottage Cheese Salad
d: Mix the Jell-O with the hot water; dissolve and let cool.
Mix with the cool Jell-O the following: cottage cheese, crushed pineapple, mayonnaise, milk and pecans.
Refrigerate this overnight and you will enjoy it the following night.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Spoon filling into pastry shell.
In a bowl, combine flour and brown sugar.
Cut in butter until mixture is crumbly. Stir in nuts. Crumble over pie filling.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes or until top is golden and filling is bubbly. Remove to wire rack to cool. Makes 8 servings.
Fry ground beef, onion and celery until celery is tender.
Put in bottom of 2-quart casserole dish.
Layer corn and soups, then top with Tater Tots.
Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Heat oven to 400°.
In 9-inch square baking pan, melt butter in oven (3 to 5 minutes).
Meanwhile, in medium bowl, combine all ingredients except milk.
Stir in milk just until moistened.
Turn dough onto lightly floured surface; knead 10 times or until smooth.
Roll dough in 12 x 4-inch rectangle.
Cut into 12 (1-inch) strips.
Dip each strip into melted butter.
Place in same pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly browned.

recipes.t: Country Ham Steak With Glazed Apples
d: In 10-inch skillet, melt butter until sizzling.
Stir in brown sugar and mustard.
Add apples.

Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until apples are crisply tender (5 to 7 minutes). Place ham steak in same skillet, arranging apples on ham steak. Cover; continue cooking until ham steak is heated through (5 to 7 minutes).
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in greased 9-inch square pan.	Bake for 30 minutes.
Cut into squares and serve.	Good hot or cold.
Makes 8 servings.
Line pan with 1/2 crushed wafers.
Cream powdered sugar and butter; add beaten eggs and beat.
Repeat.
Beat in vanilla and pour mixture over wafers.
Whip cream; add sugar and pour over first mixture.
Pour pineapple over that and sprinkle rest of wafers over top.
Let stand in cool place 12 hours.
Brown rice in oil.
Add tomato sauce, water and spices; bring to a boil.
Let boil for 20 minutes, then cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed.

Chop dates, raisins, and candied cherries. Crush graham crackers. Slightly toast pecans with a little butter then grind or chop. Melt marshmallows with butter in double boiler. Mix all ingredients together (you will have to mix with your hands). Line a box with wax paper; butter wax paper and pack cake into box. Refrigerate. (Will keep a long time in refrigerator.)
Reserve 1/2 of chopped beef.
Mix all ingredients and roll into a ball.
Then roll in remaining half of beef.
Chill for 1 hour.
Serve with crackers.
Mix ingredients and spoon into hot grease for cooking.
Cream the
cream
cheese,
butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add
eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add
vanilla
and almond extract.
Add flour; blend well but do
not overbeat.	Bake in a 10-inch tube pan at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Layer bacon, lettuce, tomato, broccoli and onion in order listed in large, glass salad bowl.

Sift flour. Make big hole in middle and put all ingredients in hole. Add buttermilk. Mix with hands to make a stiff dough. Roll out and cut with cutter; don't roll too thin. Bake at 425° until done, but not too hard. Brown lightly with oven on broil.
Press crescent rolls into a 13 x 10-inch casserole dish, bringing up sides to hold liquid (like pizza).
Sprinkle sausage over bottom, on top of the crescent roll layer.
Add hash browns and cheese.
Combine eggs, milk, salt and pepper and mix well. Pour over top of all.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 45 minutes, when eggs are set and top is browned.
Dissolve jello in 1 cup water.
Add remaining ingredients and stir well.
(Optional:
1 quart ginger ale when ready to serve.)
Place fruit in 8 x 8-inch baking dish. Combine flour, sugar, oats and walnuts. Mix butter until crumbly; sprinkle evenly over fruit. Bake at 425° for 15
to 20 minutes or until golden. Serve with ice cream, if desired. Prep time: 5 minutes. Cook Time: 20 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Coat shrimp lightly with flour.
Melt margarine in large skillet on medium heat.
Add shrimp; cook and stir 5 minutes or until lightly browned, turning frequently.
Mix chili sauce, parsley, lemon juice, mustard and pepper.
Pour over shrimp; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; simmer 5 minutes.
Cook squash in a small amount of water until tender; drain and mash.
Combine margarine and stuffing mix; stir well.
Place 1/2 of stuffing mixture in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Combine squash, onions, sour cream and soup.
Mix well.
Pour over stuffing layer.
Top with remaining stuffing.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Yields 10 to 12 servings.
Combine all ingredients in a 2-quart baking dish.
Top with cheese.
Cook at 350° for about 30 to 35 minutes.
Serves 4.
Slice a large X on bottom of each tomato.
Immerse into boiling water 15 seconds.
When cool, peel off skin.
Slice tomatoes into 1-inch chunks, letting seeds fall out.
Alternate layers of potatoes, green pepper and onion in greased 2-quart baking dish.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over potatoes.
Cover and bake in oven at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are done.
With the back of a wooden spoon, press eggs through a strainer into a small bowl; add the 1/4 cup butter and mix well.
Stir salt, Cayenne, Worcestershire and celery seed into egg mixture.
Shape egg mixture into 3/4-inch balls and chill in the refrigerator 1 hour.
While egg mixture is chilling, prepare bread crumbs.
Heat oven to 375°.
Place bread crumbs and the 2 tablespoons butter in a pie plate or shallow pan; place in oven and bake 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until crumbs are lightly browned.
Remove plate from oven and cool.
Roll egg balls in the prepared bread crumbs to coat thoroughly.
Makes 16 to 18 balls.
On large round cookie tray, layer in order listed.
Should be made a day ahead.
Mix graham crackers and nuts. Cook bits over low heat until melted.
Mix all other ingredients together with melted bits.
Put in buttered pan, then in refrigerator until hard enough to eat. You may add anything to recipe, like coconut instead of nuts. Enjoy.
Combine meat, bread crumbs, eggs, onion and seasonings and mix lightly.
Shape into medium meatballs.
Brown in margarine.
Put in casserole and combine preserves and barbecue sauce.
Pour over meatballs.
(Cover dish.)
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cream sugar, shortening and eggs until light.
Sift together flour, nutmeg, cinnamon and baking soda.
Add to egg mixture, then add the rest of the ingredients.
Add 1/4 cup of milk, if necessary.
Coat fruits with part of the flour.
Drop by teaspoonful on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° until light brown.
Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toss with chicken and celery.
Add grapes; mix.
Spoon into cooked and cooled pie shell.
Tastes best if chicken mixture is chilled before serving in pie shell.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Add rice and cheese. Saute onion in oleo and add to mixture.
Pour into greased casserole dish and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Melt butter in deep 10-inch or 12-inch casserole dish at 350°. Remove from oven keep warm.
Stir together in large bowl, sugar, flour, baking powder and salt.
Add milk, beat until smooth.
Set aside.
Mix together soy sauce, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, garlic and mustard.
Place chicken in a bowl and pour sauce over all.
Cover and marinate in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Remove chicken from marinade; discard marinade.
Sprinkle chicken with pepper; grill until chicken is cooked through and tender, about 6 to 8 minutes on each side.
Makes 4 servings each with 130 calories (1.5 g fat and 76 mg cholesterol).
Combine all ingredients and blend.
Place chicken in glass baking dish.
Add ingredients.
Cover and chill overnight, turning often.
Place skin side down on cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Turn and bake 30 minutes longer.
Serve hot or cold.
Saute onions and celery until tender.
Add tomatoes; sprinkle parsley flakes over top.
Add fish on top.
Simmer for 10 minutes, turn over, and simmer another 10 to 20 minutes until flaky.
Place unpeeled potatoes in 3-quart pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil and cook until potatoes are just tender when pierced, about 20 minutes.
Drain well.
When cool enough to handle, peel and cut into 1/4-inch slices.
In a greased shallow 2-quart casserole, arrange half of the potato slices.
Top with half of the bacon and onion.
Stir milk into sour cream.
Spread 1/2 of this over the bacon and onion, then half of the cheese. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Repeat layers.
Sprinkle top with croutons and drizzle butter over all.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 to 45 minutes.
Slice bananas into blender.
Puree until smooth (1 1/2 cups). In saucepan, combine 1/2 cup pureed bananas, 1/3 cup sugar, 1 egg and chocolate.
Heat until chocolate melts.
Cool.
Cream remaining 1 cup sugar with shortening until light and fluffy.
Add rum extract and remaining 2 eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Combine dry ingredients.
Beat with creamed mixture alternately with remaining bananas.
Blend in chocolate mixture. Bake in 2 greased and floured 9-inch round cake pans in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes until done.
Cool 10 minutes in pan. Invert on wire rack to cool.
Cut slice in top of cake.
Put cut side up and frost with Rum Fudge.
Frost sides and top.
Garnish cake with banana slices.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Mix all together and beat until smooth.
Do not overbeat or it will have air bubbles.
May use food processor which does not make air bubbles.
Cook the onion in small amount of oil until tender.
Combine potatoes, onion and egg; mix well.
Drop by spoonful in hot skillet.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Brown on both sides. Serve hot.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake at 425° to 450° for 20 minutes. Pan can be lined with wax paper.
Mix all ingredients, except bread dough in a large bowl.
Roll dough flat, about 1/4-inch thick.
Spread spinach mixture on the dough and roll in a jellyroll style.
Pinch edges together and make several fork pierces in the top.
Place on oiled baking sheet.
Bake at 350° to 375° for about 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients together.
Bake at 350° until brown.
Combine ingredients; spread on bread, making desired sizes and shapes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Dump applesauce into pan.
Dump pineapple into pan.
Spread dry cake mix over this.
Melt margarine and pour on top of cake mix. Sprinkle nuts over butter.
Do not stir.
Bake for 1 hour.
Top with whipped cream.
Mix soups, sour cream and chicken breasts together in casserole dish.
Cover with cracker crumbs.
Pour oleo over top and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine ingredients and mix well.
Place in oven-safe casserole.
Dot with 2 tablespoons of butter and bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Serve warm on crackers.
Use ungreased 9 x 12-inch (approximately) pan.
Layer ham, bread and cheese.
Beat 6 eggs with 2 cups milk and pour over ham mixture.
Drizzle with melted butter.
Refrigerate overnight.
Bake uncovered at 325° for 1 hour.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
Cut chocolate into small pieces.
Add chocolate, nuts, dates and cherries to flour mixture.
Beat eggs with mixer until foamy.
Add sugar gradually, beating until eggs are thick and light.
Add flour mixture; mix well.
Turn mixture into greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cool and slice.
Brown bacon, remove from pan and
reserve
2 tablespoons bacon drippings.	Saute onion and pepper until slightly tender, pour into
large skillet or Dutch oven.	Add
corn,
tomatoes, bacon and 2 tablespoons bacon drippings.	Add
garlic,
pepper and salt. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes, adding
okra
(if
desired) for the last six minutes.
Stir lightly twice during cooking.
Layer bottom of 9 x 13-inch dish with crushed tortilla chips. Put 2 cans tamales over chips.
Follow with diced onion and black olives.
Pour 2 cans chili with beans over mixture.
Top with grated cheese.
Serve with sour cream.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and serve with your favorite vegetables, crackers or bread.
Saute garlic in oil for just a few minutes.
Fry potatoes, carrots and onions in oil and garlic until vegetables are tender. Add sausage and broccoli.
Steam for 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain and serve.
Mix in pimento, celery, bell pepper and onion, chopped.
Saute onion in butter until soft.
Stir in flour and water. Cook over low heat until thickened.
Blend in shredded Velveeta. Combine sauce and broccoli.
Add eggs; mix gently until blended. Put in casserole and top with cracker crumbs.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Open milk and put in large bowl into freezer.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add marshmallows and dissolve.
Take off heat and add chopped cabbage, walnuts and pineapple.
Whip evaporated milk until thick, then fold into jello mixture.
Refrigerate.
Mix all of the ingredients together with a wooden spoon.
Bake at 325° to 350° for 1 hour and 10 to 15 minutes.
Let cool 15 minutes.
Makes 1 Bundt cake or 2 large loaves or 3 medium loaves or muffins.
Pound chicken or veal to about 1/4-inch thickness.
Sprinkle with pepper and dust with flour.
Heat oil and brown meat until golden.
Remove from pan and add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil; simmer until reduced to half.
Add meat and heat through. Time will vary according to thickness of meat.
Be sure juices run clear if using chicken.
Very good served over linguine or fettucine.
Makes 4 servings.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Place first five ingredients in a bowl and mash with a fork. Stir until well blended.
Divide in half.
Shape into 2 smooth balls.
Roll one in parsley-chive mix and the other in chopped nuts.
Roll in plastic wrap and chill 2 or 3 days for best flavor.
Have at room temperature before serving with crackers or toast points.
Melt margarine and saute the onions.
Blend in flour.
Add undrained clams and Worcestershire sauce; cook for 15 minutes on low heat.
It will thicken.
Remove from heat and cool.
Place chocolate in empty coffeepot.
Place coffee and orange peel in brew basket.
Prepare coffee using 3 cups water.
Serve hot with whipped topping.
Makes 4 cups.
Brown hamburger and onion or onion soup mix.
Layer zucchini and then hamburger; add soup and repeat.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Serves 4.
Mix the ingredients and pour into churn.
Fill to line with milk.
Churn until frozen.
Saute onion and bacon until onion is tender.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Heat until bubbly, stirring well.
Serve warm with corn chips.
Yield:
about 3 1/2 cups.
In large bowl, combine eggs, sugar, milk, salt, melted butter, vanilla, flour, baking powder, nutmeg and cinnamon.
Heat vegetable oil until hot, about 370°.
Drop by teaspoonfuls into hot oil; when brown on all sides, remove from fat and sprinkle with sugar or glaze.
(Doughnuts will turn themselves.)
Place beets, onion and red pepper in saucepan.
Add salt, horseradish, vinegar and sugar.
Cook 20 to 25 minutes.
Put at once into sterilized hot jars and seal immediately.
In a large bowl, stir together soup and mayo until smooth. Fold in turkey, celery, red pepper, onions, parsley and pepper. Cover and refrigerate.
Makes 5 cups.
Combine broth, onion, potatoes and dill in saucepan. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend mixture in blender or food processor until smooth.
In a saucepan, melt margarine. Blend in flour, salt and pepper. Add the milk. Cook and stir until mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Stir in the blended potato mixture. Cook and stir until soup is heated through.
Makes 3 or 4 servings.
Brown celery in butter. Add shrimp and cook until shrimp have turned pink. Add rice and soy sauce. Mix thoroughly (do not add salt) and cook for about 5 minutes stirring every few minutes. Serve.
Heat oven to 350°.
In a medium saucepan, combine chocolate chips and butter; cook and stir over very low heat until chips are melted and smooth.
Add sweetened condensed milk; mix well. Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup; level off.
In medium bowl, combine flour, nuts, chocolate mixture and vanilla; mix well.
Shape 1 tablespoonful (use measuring spoon) of dough around each candy kiss, covering completely.
Place 1 inch apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes.
Cookies will be soft and appear shiny, but become firm as they cool.
Do not overbake.
Remove from cookie sheets; cool.
Saute onions in butter.
Blend in flour.
Add water.
Stir in salt, Cheez Whiz and broccoli.
Add well beaten eggs.
Bake 40 minutes at 325°.
Mix all dry ingredients together.
Cream the butter or shortening; gradually add brown sugar and beat well until light and fluffy.
Add beaten egg and blend well.
Add the dry ingredients alternately with the banana pulp, a little at a time, beating after each addition only until smooth.
Pour half the batter into a greased or lined 8-inch square cake pan.
Melt chocolate chips in a saucepan and spread over batter.
Cover with remaining batter and bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.
Frost with Butter Frosting.
Combine flour, walnuts and brown sugar in bowl.
Cut in butter or margarine until particles are fine.
Press into bottom of greased 8 x 12 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 400° for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Cool.
Melt oleo in pan.
Add in layers, all other ingredients in order.
Do not mix.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Grease a bundt pan.
Place orange marmalade around pan (use more if you'd like).
Sprinkle with nuts.
Combine brown sugar and cinnamon.
Separate biscuits. Dip in melted butter then in sugar mixture.
