Stand biscuits on edge in pan spacing evenly.
Sprinkle with remaining sugar and melted butter.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes until brown. Cool 5 minutes and then invert on serving plate.
A tube pan may be used instead of a bundt pan.
Mix ingredients together and put in 9-inch baked pie crust, cooled.
Cover with whipped topping.
Cut round steak into narrow 2-inch strips.
Slice onion and then cut slices in half.
Brown round steak and onion with garlic. When browned, add just enough water to cover meat (approximately 1 1/2 to 2 cups).
Cover and simmer for 2 hours, checking occasionally to make sure it has enough water.
Add cream of mushroom soup and stir until smooth.
Add sour cream and again stir until smooth.
Serve over cooked egg noodles.
If desired, you may add a large can of sliced mushrooms to the stroganoff.
Cook cauliflower in chicken broth.
Add other ingredients and simmer for 10 minutes.
Fast and scrumptious.
Combine soup, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, ginger and garlic powder.
In 3-quart oblong baking dish, arrange chicken. Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Spoon off fat.
Spoon soup mixture over chicken.
Bake 30 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear.
Sift sauce; serve with rice if desired. (Skin can be removed from chicken before baking.)
Makes 4 servings.
Combine chicken, celery, green pepper, pimento, water chestnuts and rice in bowl; toss lightly to mix.
Spoon into buttered 3-quart baking dish.
Combine soup, mayonnaise, onion, lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce in bowl; mix well.
Add 1/3 of the soup mixture to chicken mixture; mix well.
Spoon remaining soup mixture over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Yield:
12 servings.
Mix and press on cookie sheet (one with the edging).
Prick top of the ground chuck and bake at 400° for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350°.
Continue for 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut into squares and put on rolls.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat egg whites (at room temperature) at high speed of an electric mixer until foamy; add salt. Gradually add sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until stiff peaks form.
Fold in vanilla, chocolate morsels and pecans into beaten egg whites.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto aluminum foil-lined cookie sheets.
Place in oven and immediately turn off heat.
Do not open oven door for at least 8 hours.
Carefully remove from aluminum foil.
Yields about 3 dozen.
Partially cook bacon.
Drain; reserve 2 tablespoons drippings. Set bacon aside.
Cook onion and garlic in drippings until tender, but not browned.
In bowl, combine egg and tomato sauce; stir in breadcrumbs, mushrooms and onion.
Mix parsley, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper.
Add meat; mix well.
Divide into 4 parts. Place 2 strips bacon side by side on waxed paper.
Cut slice in half crosswise.
Place 2 1/2 slices at one end of bacon slices, overlapping slightly.
Pat 1/4 of meat mixture evenly over bacon; roll up jellyroll style, starting at narrow end.
Place rolls, seam side down, on rack in 12 x 7 x 2-inch baking dish.
Repeat with remaining bacon and meat.
Bake in oven about 40 minutes for medium doneness.
Cube bacon and fry crisp.
Add vinegar and water.
Thicken with flour and sugar mixed.
Add potatoes and onions.
Heat slowly.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Cook and drain broccoli, put into 1 1/2-quart casserole dish. Top with chicken that has been removed from the bones.
Mix the mayonnaise, both soups, evaporated milk, lemon juice, cheese and curry powder.
Pour this over the chicken and broccoli.
Mix stuffing mix with margarine (melted) and sprinkle this on top of the casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Saute onions in butter until transparent.
Add clams with juice and crushed crackers.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Serve hot with crackers.
Fry ground beef and drain.
Boil squash until tender.
Don't overcook.
Drain.
Simmer bell pepper and onion until tender. Layer in order listed in large baking dish the ground beef, soup, squash, onion, pepper, sour cream and shredded cheese.
Mix butter and crackers and put on top.
Bake at 350° until bubbles.
Bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Add broccoli. Cover, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Saute onion in butter in a Dutch oven over low heat about 10 minutes or until tender.
Add flour, stirring until smooth; cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add milk and bouillon cubes.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until mixture is thickened.
Add broccoli, cooking water and pepper. Simmer 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Yields 9 cups.
In a double boiler melt the butter.
Add flour and stir until smooth.
Add milk and stir until smooth and slightly thick.
Add Rotel and cubed Velveeta; stir until melted.
Add spices or picante and heat through.
Mix together.
Add sherbet by large spoonfuls.
Press dough over a large cookie sheet, sealing edges.
Bake at 375° for 7 minutes or until golden.
Cool.
Put 2 cups of sugar in frying pan, then add milk.
Pan should be on medium heat.
Add vanilla flavoring.
Heat and stir until it comes to a low boil.
Put a drip in a cup of cold water.
If it forms a hard ball in the water, then it's ready to add peanut butter slowly.
Could use from 3/4 to 1 cup.
Then add margarine. On low heat, stir until cloudy.
Then put in an 8 x 10-inch container.
Mix cucumbers, onions and salt; let stand for 1 or 2 hours. Rinse and drain well.
Let stand for 5 hours longer.
Drain, but do not rinse.
Boil vinegar, water, sugar and spices for 3 minutes.
Add cucumbers and onions and simmer 10 to 20 minutes (do not boil).
Pack into jars and seal at once.
In large (8-quart) pan, mix sugar, syrup, soda and water.
Boil until mixture bubbles freely.
Then place the thermometer in, and don't let it touch the bottom of the pan.
Next add the whipping cream slowly all around in the pan (don't pour it all in one place).
Let this boil to the hard boil stage (260°).
Do not stir. Pour out onto marble slab or heavily buttered cold platter.
When cool enough to handle, pull until creamy white and holds its shape (about 20 minutes).
Cut with scissors and put in dish to cream. Be sure to butter your hands and remove all rings.

recipes.t: Cherry Glazed Chicken Breasts Stuffed With Wild Rice
d: Sprinkle chicken breasts lightly with salt, paprika and garlic powder.
Cook rice and after cooking add almonds.
Place stuffing in the center of each chicken breast.
Roll and secure with toothpicks or skewers.
Roll stuffed breast lightly with flour. Melt butter in pan you will cook breasts in.
Roll stuffed breasts in butter.
Bake in 325° oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Baste with Cherry Glaze 2 or 3 times during last 45 minutes of baking.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Reserve.
Slice and fry sausage in skillet.
Coarsely crumble sausage.
Remove sausage from drippings.
In drippings, add onion and celery and saute.
Add mushrooms, almonds, water chestnuts, soup, water, cooked rice and sausage.
Mix and bake covered 45 minutes at 1 hour at 350°.
This recipe is enough for 16 to 20 chickens.
Cut up unpeeled squash.
Cook until tender; drain and mash. Add margarine and mix well.
Add all other ingredients.
Mix well. Pour into casserole dish and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes or until golden brown.
Saute onion in butter for several minutes.
Remove from heat, blend in flour gradually.
Add broth, milk, and pepper stirring until smooth.
Add broccoli and Velveeta.
Cook on medium heat 7-9 minutes or until soup is slightly thickened.
Prepare cake mix as directed on box.
Add 1 1/2 cups crushed Oreo cookies and bake as directed in 2 round pans.
Let cakes cool, then cut in half to make 4 layers. Whip the cream with 3 tablespoons sugar and fold in 1 1/2 cups Oreos and spread between layers.
Keep refrigerated.
Layer in bowl in order.
Top with Miracle Whip (approximately 1 to 1 1/2-inches thick).
Sprinkle about 1/2 cup sugar on top. Cover with Saran Wrap.
Refrigerate for 24 hours.
Take a 9 x 13-inch pan. Layer cherry pie filling, crushed pineapple and cake mix. Slice butter and layer on top of cake mix. Sprinkle nuts on top. Bake at 325° for 1 hour or until brown on top.
Place 1/2 of the raw sliced potatoes in the bottom of a casserole dish.
Next, place sliced onions, place hamburg evenly over these 2 ingredients.
Put other half of potatoes on top. Pour tomato soup evenly over top.
Place 2 or 3 pats of butter, salt and pepper to taste over.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Cook tomatoes with salt for 30 minutes. Skim off sediments. Chop garlic, onions and peppers in processor (not too fine).
Add to tomatoes at the end of 30 minutes.
Cook another 30 minutes. Ready to can.
Combine sugar, flour and nutmeg; cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add nuts.
Arrange yams and peaches in a 1 1/2-quart casserole; sprinkle with sugar mixture. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with marshmallows.
Broil until lightly browned.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook mixed vegetables until tender-crisp and then drain.
Add rest of ingredients.
Mix well and refrigerate.
Better if made 1 day before using.
Melt 4 tablespoons margarine and stir in flour, salt and pepper to make smooth paste.
Drain liquid from asparagus and add enough milk to make 2 cups.
Stir liquid into flour paste and cook slowly, stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in pimentos, parsley and almonds.
Cover bottom of 1 1/2-quart casserole with half of asparagus (reserve 6 or 7 tips for garnish), eggs and cheese; repeat and cover with cracker crumbs.
Garnish with asparagus tips.
Melt remaining butter and pour over top.
Bake at 425° for 20 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, mix together all ingredients.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes. Can be served warm, at room temperature, or cold.
Mix the dressing, preserves and soup mix together.
Pour over cut up chicken and bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours, uncovered.
Sauce good over rice.
Mix all but last ingredient and place in a casserole.
Top with bacon.
Bake for one hour in a 325° oven.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour (in lightly greased floured pan). Turn oven down to 300° and bake 20 minutes more.
When bread is taken from oven, rub top with butter.
Combine all ingredients, folding in mayonnaise last.
Place mixture in pie plate and sprinkle with a little extra cheese. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
(We usually microwave for about 5 minutes.)
Combine all ingredients except potato chips.
Spoon into a greased 2-quart casserole.
Top with potato chips and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Beat eggs, vanilla and oil together.
Sift flour, sugar, soda and salt.
Add to egg mixture.
Add apples and nuts.
Mix well. Bake in 3 layers at 325° for 40 minutes.
Mix and bake at 350° to 400° for 45 to 60 minutes.

recipes.t: Chicken Rosemary(Recipe From The Club Meeting'S Herbal Luncheon)
d: Dust chicken pieces with flour and saute in butter until tender and light brown.
Add chicken broth, rosemary, mushrooms and wine.
Turn into casserole pan and bake about 30 minutes, uncovered, at 350°.
Drain sweet potatoes and slice into mixing bowl.
Add pineapple without draining and salt.
Stir to mix.
Pour into buttered casserole.
Cover top with bits of butter, then with marshmallows.
Bake at 300° until marshmallows are browned.
Brown sausage; drain.
Add potatoes and tomatoes; cook over medium heat 5 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Beat eggs and 2 tablespoons water.
Pour over ingredients in skillet; cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes or until egg mixture is set in center and cheese is melted.
Uncover; let stand 5 minutes before cutting into wedges.
Mix the first
4 ingredients.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the franks or the hot dogs (cut into quarters) and simmer until heated.
Keep warm in a chafing dish or crockette.
Great appetizer!
Melt milk chocolate chips and shortening over hot water, stirring until mixture is smooth.
Pour 1/2 of melted chocolate into an 8-inch square pan.
Spread evenly.
Refrigerate until firm (about 15 minutes).
Combine caramels, butter and water and melt. Stir until mixture is smooth.
Stir in peanuts.
Pour into chocolate pan.
Spread evenly.
Refrigerate until tacky (about 15 minutes).
Top with remaining melted chocolate and spread evenly. Return to refrigerator and chill until firm (about 1 hour).
Cut into squares and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Mix together the first 5 ingredients.
Add water and vanilla. Beat until fluffy.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes.
In a saucepan melt butter or margarine.
Add brown sugar and water.
Stirring constantly, heat to boiling.
Add drained, cooked carrots and simmer 5 minutes or until carrots are tender.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Mix together cabbage, sugar, onion, green pepper, salt and pepper and set aside.
Mix vinegar, oil, celery seed and mustard together and boil for 5 minutes.
Pour over cabbage mixture and do not stir!
Let stand refrigerated overnight, remove and stir well. Stays fresh for 8 to 10 days.
Cream the shortening and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Add milk and flour alternately.
Put in greased and floured tube pan. Bake in a 325° oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes without opening oven door.
This makes a very large cake.
Cream margarine and sugar together in bowl.
Add eggs and bananas, mixing well.
Sift flour and soda together into batter, blending thoroughly.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Cook shells per package directions.
Drain.
Cool in single layer on waxed paper or aluminum foil.
In a large bowl, combine cheeses, eggs, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper.
Fill each shell with about 2 tablespoons of cheese mixture.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on bottom of rectangular pan (13 x 9 x 2-inch).
Place filled shells, open side down, in single layer in pan.
Cover with remaining sauce.
Sprinkle with additional Parmesan cheese, if desired.
Cover with foil; bake at 350° for about 35 minutes, or until hot and bubbly.
Fills about 36 shells.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Grate squash and onion (I cut up the onion).
Place in mixing bowl.
Add to this the egg, salt, pepper and flour; mix well.
In a thick boiler (I use Club aluminum), put in enough cooking oil to be about 3/4 to 7/8-inch deep.
The oil should get hot.
When it is hot, use small spoon and drop small amounts of the ingredients in.
Usually it takes about 6 or 7 fritters.
When these are brown, turn over to brown the other side.
Take out of oil; place on paper toweling to get rid of excess oil.
Begin the cooking process over until all the mixture is used.
Serve hot.
Mix first 3 ingredients well and add sauce.
Layer in buttered dish the noodles, meat and sauce (heated) and cheese.
Cook at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Mix together the flour, white sugar, baking powder, 1 tablespoon cocoa and salt.
Mix only until smooth.
Add milk, shortening, vanilla and nuts.
Spread into a greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Mix together brown sugar and 2 tablespoons cocoa and sprinkle over batter.
Pour 1 cup boiling water over batter. This forms sauce in bottom of the pan as pudding is baked. Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix flour with enough water to make a stiff dough.
Form dough into a ball and knead about 10 minutes.
Place in bowl and cover with additional water.
Let stand 30 minutes or overnight.
Knead dough with hands under water to wash out the starch.
Pour off the starchy water and cover with more water.
Continue washing until water is almost clear.
You now have concentrated protein to make the steaks!
Mix rice and corn; sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Pour over 1 can of tomato sauce, 1/2 cup water, onion, green pepper, and ground beef.
Sprinkle again with salt and pepper.
Add second can of tomato sauce and 1/4 cup water.
Cover with strips of bacon. Cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake another 30 minutes longer until bacon is crisped.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix bread crumbs, cheese and spices; set aside.
Beat eggs and oil, set aside.
Melt butter in pan; flour chicken, dip in egg mixture, then dip in bread crumb mixture.
Fry gently on moderate heat, browning on both sides.
Cook about 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Split Pea And Ham Soup(Total Cooking Time:  75 To 85 Minutes)
d: Combine all ingredients in a 4-quart microwave casserole. Cover.
Use Cook cycle and cook 70 to 80 minutes or until peas are tender.
Remove ham hock from soup; cool until ham hock can be handled and meat cut from bone.
Add meat to soup.
Discard peppercorns and bay leaf.
Stir.
Use Cook cycle and cook 5 minutes or until heated through.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Heat 1 1/2 teaspoons oil in skillet over medium heat.
Saute onion until translucent, almost tender, approximately 3 minutes.
Add caraway and dill.
Cook briefly. Remove from heat.
Transfer to bowl.
In food processor, blend tofu, salt, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon oil and tahini until smooth. Fold into sauteed vegetables.
Pour into pie crust and bake 20 to 30 minutes.
Mix sugar, butter and Pet milk.
Cook until thick.
Add the marshmallows, chocolate chips and pecans.
Cook until thick.
Spread almonds in a single layer in shallow pan.
Bake at 300° for 15 minutes, stirring often until almonds just turn brown. Combine softened cream cheese and mayonnaise; mix well.
Add remaining ingredients.
Blend, cover and chill overnight.
Form cheese mix and shape into 2 pine cones on serving platter. Beginning at narrow end, press almonds at a slight angle into cheese mixture in rows.
Continue overlapping rows until all cheese is covered.
Garnish with pine sprigs.
Serve with crackers.
Mix oil, chocolate and granulated sugar.
Blend eggs in, one at a time, until well mixed.
Add vanilla.
Stir flour, baking powder and salt into oil mixture.
Chill dough overnight.
Heat oven to 350°.
Drop teaspoon of dough into confectioners sugar (1 box only) and coat well.
Place 2-inches apart on greased baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Don't overbake.
Makes 6 dozen.
In a 2-quart baking dish, arrange potatoes, onions and green pepper.
Top with pork chops.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt and pepper.
Combine soup and milk.
Pour over all.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Cook in microwave for 5 minutes or until soup starts bubbling.
After soup starts boiling, cook for another 15 minutes or until pork chops and vegetables are tender.
Turn baking dish halfway around after 5 minutes of cooking.
Let stand about 5 minutes.
Cut chicken into thin strips.
Cook until done in a small amount water.
Add onion.
Cook until transparent.
Add cut up broccoli and next 3 seasonings; cook about 5 minutes.
Add 1 1/2 cups water with chicken bouillon cubes dissolved.
Cook 1 minute. Stir cornstarch into cold water.
Gradually add to chicken and broccoli.
Cook 1 minute.
Serve over steamed rice.
Makes 2 big servings.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add flour and sugars.
Melt margarine and let stand to room temperature.
Add to sugar mixture and blend well.
Add chopped nuts and chocolate chips.
Pour into pastry shell.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°. Place sliced apples in greased baking dish. Combine cake mix, sugar, cinnamon and butter until clumpy. Pour over top of apples. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cook ground chuck and onion.
Add tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, salt and powders.
Mix well; simmer for 10 minutes.
Fold in crushed chips.
Spoon onto bottom half of bun.
Top with lettuce, cheese, tomatoes and top half of bun.
Sift dry ingredients in bowl.
Gradually stir in water.
Add fresh vegetables, shrimp, etc.
The batter will be thin. Deep fry until golden brown.

Place chicken cubes and green pepper pieces in shallow dish. Drain pineapple, reserving 1/2 cup juice. Set pineapple aside. Combine reserved pineapple juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, liquid smoke, garlic powder and ginger.
Pour over chicken and green pepper pieces.
Stir to coat. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Boil potatoes in jackets; cool and cut in cubes.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove and crumble over potatoes.
Add onions to hot bacon drippings and fry until tender.
Mix vinegar, salt, pepper, sugar, celery seed and water; bring to a boil.
Stir in egg yolk quickly.
Remove from heat; add potatoes and bacon.
Put in casserole and keep warm to serve.
Mix cucumbers, peppers, onions and salt and let stand 30 minutes; drain.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over cucumber mixture.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Fill jars and seal.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift sugar, soda, flour and salt together into bowl; add eggs, oil and vanilla.
Mix well.
Add apples and nuts; stir until mixed well.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Peel and split pears, remove the core.
Allow the Roquefort cheese and the butter to soften to room temperature.
Add mix to creamy texture.
Fill the pear; mix enough cream into the cream cheese with a light whisk until it will pour, adding a pinch of salt.
Place the pears on a bed of lettuce and pour mixture over them.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika.
Chill 1/2 hour before serving.
Serves 8.
Thoroughly combine sugar and cocoa in a 4-quart saucepan; stir in milk.
Bring to a bubbly boil on medium heat, stirring constantly.
Boil to 234° (soft ball stage) on candy thermometer. Bulb of the candy thermometer, boil until a small amount dropped in a half cup of cold water forms a soft ball.
Remove from heat; add margarine and vanilla.
Beat, by hand, until fudge thickens and loses some of its gloss.
Quickly add pecans and spread in a lightly buttered platter or a lightly buttered 9-inch square pan. Cool and cut into squares.
Melt butter in a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Add crushed graham crackers. Add chocolate chips and coconut.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Cover with condensed milk.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix ingredients; store in an airtight container.
To serve, add 1 1/2 tablespoons of mix in a cup of hot water.
Place thawed broccoli on bottom of a greased 11 x 7-inch pan. Place chicken on top.
Mix together soups, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Pour over chicken, completely covering.
Sprinkle cheese over soup mixture.
Combine butter and bread crumbs.
Sprinkle over cheese.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes, until hot and bubbly.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cut first 3 ingredients until it resembles coarse meal.
Add milk and stir.
Place on a floured board and knead 10 minutes. Roll between waxed paper, 12 x 8-inches.
Spread preserves to 1/2 inch of edges.
Fold sides to center and pinch ends together. Place on a greased baking sheet.
Cut 1 1/2 inches toward center, 1 inch apart, 1/3 way through.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Peel eggplant and cut into small pieces.
Boil in salted water until tender.
Drain well.
Mash and stir in other ingredients. Mix well.
Drop by teaspoon onto well-greased griddle.
Fry on both sides until golden brown.
Cream the cream cheese, butter and sugar; add vanilla.
Add flour 1 cup at a time alternately with eggs.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Skillet:
In skillet over medium heat, in hot oil cook chicken 10 minutes or until browned on all sides.
Spoon off fat.
Stir in soup, pepper and thyme.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover; simmer 35 minutes or until chicken is fork-tender, stirring occasionally. Oven:
Substitute 1 tablespoon melted margarine for oil.
In 12 x 8-inch baking dish arrange chicken skin side up.
Drizzle with margarine.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Spoon soup, pepper and thyme over chicken.
Bake 20 minutes more or until chicken is fork-tender.
Stir sauce before serving.
Skillet cook time is 45 minutes; oven cook time is 60 minutes.
Boil chicken until tender; remove skin and debone.
Cut in small pieces.
Cook wild rice according to directions on box. Saute chopped onion, green onion, celery and bell pepper in oleo; mix with chicken.
Alternate rice mixture and chicken in casserole dish.
Add mushroom soup on top.
Add mushrooms and juice.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Boil chicken until done and remove from bone.
Cut into small pieces.
Place on bottom of a casserole dish.
Combine chestnuts, sour cream, water, and soup.
Spread over chicken.
Crush crackers and spread them over the soup mixture.
Melt butter and drizzle it over the crackers.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 - 35 minutes.
Press hamburger into pie pan.
Press up on to edge.
Lay cheese on top of hamburger. Spread tomato paste on top of cheese. Bake in a 350° oven until hamburger is done (about 25 to 30 minutes).
Mix and cover in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Refrigerate overnight. Before baking, cover with 1 cup crushed corn flakes mixed with 3 tablespoons melted butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.t: Believe It Or Not Cookies(Made Without Flour)
d: Mix all ingredients lightly until evenly blended.
Do not overmix.
Roll in small ball; put on ungreased baking sheet. Press flat with fork.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
When cool, roll in powdered sugar.
Makes 100 cookies.
Absolutely delicious!
Mix sugar and dry gelatin in saucepan.

Add milk, syrup, chocolate and margarine and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until candy reaches 238° on candy thermometer or a few drops tested in cold water form a soft ball which flattens on removal from water.
(Candy will be much thicker than ordinary candy.)
Remove from heat; add vanilla and cool 15 minutes.
Beat until thick; stir in nuts and spread on buttered pan.
If candy is not hard enough, chill for an hour or so.
Marinate in Good Seasons Italian dressing.
Add raw spinach for filler and color if needed.
Sprinkle with a little Feta cheese.
Shred red cabbage; slice apples, peel onion and spike with cloves and add all other ingredients to large pot, adding enough water to keep cabbage from burning.
Bring to boil, stirring occasionally.
Add more water if necessary and simmer on low heat until cabbage is done.
Cream butter and sugar in mixing bowl.
Add egg and molasses; beat well. Sift together dry ingredients; gradually add to creamed mixture.
Mix well. Chill dough 1 to 2 hours.
Roll into 1 1/4-inch balls and dip in sugar.
Place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for about 10 minutes or until set and surface cracks.
(Cookies will be chewy.)
Cool on wire rack. Yields approximately 4 dozen.
Mix all ingredients together and pat into a greased 10 x 13-inch glass dish.
Mix water, vinegar and salt.
Sift dry ingredients and add to the boiling vinegar, water and salt.
Stir constantly.
Cook until flour is well done.
If you like, add a little nutmeg.
If mixture becomes stiff become the flour is done, add a little hot water. Pour into baked pie shells.
Mix all ingredients and form into a loaf. Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Roll deer meat in flour.
Fry in vegetable oil at a slow fry. Sprinkle in salt and pepper to suit you.
Sprinkle in Italian and oregano seasonings (small amounts).
Sprinkle in a pinch of sage. Add 1 cup fresh diced onions.
Fry at low temperature under lid until brown and tender.
Boil cabbage until leaves are wilted; separate leaves.
Mix all other ingredients and mold into egg-size balls.
Place each on a cabbage leaf; wrap and fasten with toothpicks.
Brown lightly in a greased skillet.
Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add a small amount of water if necessary.
You may serve with tomato sauce or plain. Serves 8 to 10.
Mix all ingredients together with blender on high speed until thick and creamy.
In mixer with flat beater, mix first 6 ingredients.
Let yeast mixture proof until foamy.
Add to dry ingredients along with buttermilk.
Mix until well blended and turn out onto well floured board and knead into a nice smooth ball.
Roll out to 1/2-inch and cut with cutter.
Place on well-greased sheet pan.
Allow to rise 3 to 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cook until a nice golden brown (approximately 20 minutes).
Wonderful buttered with a slice of Smithfield ham!
Bet you can't eat just one!
Mix all ingredients well in bowl.
Chill overnight.
Form into 8 patties.
Fry slowly until brown on each side.
*Fruit may be fresh or frozen (thawed and drained).
Line a deep dish pizza pan or a 13 x 9-inch pan with crescent rolls.
Crumble browned, drained sausage over rolls.
Cook hash browns and spread over sausage.
Sprinkle cheese over potatoes. Break eggs; add milk.
Beat and pour over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Sift dry ingredients and mix.
Combine milk and oil.
Add to dry ingredients.
Stir until moist.
Drop from tablespoon on top of bubbling broth, or stew.
Cover tightly.
Bring to a boil and then reduce heat.
(Do not lift lid.)
Simmer 12 to 15 minutes. Makes 5 servings.
Pour 1 cup boiling water over gelatin and stir.
Mash sauce with fork until mushy.
Combine all ingredients and allow to set.
Bring to boil the water and salt; set aside to cool.
Beat the eggs.
Beat with the shortening and sugar until fluffy.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to the egg mixture alternately with the milk until the batter is smooth.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake in a 350° oven for 50 minutes.
Mix
graham cracker crumbs and Ritz cracker crumbs with melted margarine.
Press	into
x 9-inch glass casserole. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes and cool.
Mix ice cream with milk and pudding.
Pour
over crust.
Top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle crushed Heath bars on top.	Freeze.
Mix butter, flour, sugar and salt until crumbly.
With floured fingers, press 2 cups crumb mixture onto bottom of pan, reserving remaining mixture.
Bake at 350 for 10-12 minutes.
Combine potatoes, egg, onion and parsley.
Shape into round cakes about 3/4-inch thick.
Brown cakes on both sides in hot Crisco.
Serve hot with eggs for breakfast.
Cook the chickpeas with salt for 20 minutes in the pressure cooker (or until peas are soft).
Drain chickpeas.
Combine with other ingredients in blender.
Blend until creamy.
Mix all together and chill.
Serve with Fritos.
Makes about 2 cups.
Combine all ingredients, except fish and pecans.
After mixing these items, stir in fish.
Chill in a fish mold, or shape into a log after rolling in pecans.
Serve with cocktail rye squares or crackers.
Let cheese soften.
Mix all ingredients together and roll in pecans.
Place chocolate morsels in top of a double boiler; bring water to a boil.
Reduce heat to low; cook, stirring occasionally, until chocolate melts.
Remove from hot water; let cool completely. Stir in rum.
Combine egg whites, cream of tartar and salt in a small mixing bowl; beat at medium speed of an electric mixer until foamy.
Add 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating at high speed until stiff peaks form.
Cover; set aside.
Mix all ingredients and fry in hot skillet, turning once. Easy to make.
Even squash haters will like it.
* Such as garlic, pepper, etc.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling
water;
let cool.	Combine soup, mayonnaise and pepper;
stir
into gelatin mixture.
Add remaining ingredients, mixing well.
Pour into a lightly oiled 4-cup mold; chill until firm.
Yield: 8 servings.
Mix Jell-O and water and let set until partially jelled.
Mix in other ingredients.
Top with pecan halves and chill until completely jelled.
Mix Tang and pineapple juice with vanilla pudding until well blended.
Fold in fruit; chill thoroughly.
Serve with whipped topping.
About 30 minutes before serving:
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large, shallow baking dish in oven, melt butter or margarine. With pot holders, remove dish from oven; stir in lemon juice.
Dip fillets in mixture, turning to coat both sides.
Scrape, wash and slice carrots.
Cook with some water in saucepan until tender.
Drain.
Mix mayonnaise, horseradish and onion and add to cooked carrots.
Mix bread crumbs and melted butter.
Spread on top of carrots.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until brown.
Mix all together (can be divided to make different flavors). Roll in chopped nuts and chill.
Cream together sugar, oleo and Crisco.
Add eggs and mix well. Add flour, 7-Up and extract.
Mix well.
Bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350° in greased and floured tube pan.
Marinate meat 1 or 2 days before smoking.
Keep meat in cooler at	32° to	40°
while marinating.
*Equals 2/8 of a cup + 1 tablespoon.
Soften margarine and cheese.
When soft, mix with flour and add salt and red pepper.
Mix well.
Add Rice Krispies.
Make in small balls and mash flat.
Bake at 325° for 15 to 20 minutes. Let cool and store in airtight container.
(Makes approximately 35.)
Sift flour, sugar, soda, cocoa and salt into large bowl. Combine mayonnaise, cold water and vanilla in small bowl; mix well.
Add to flour mixture; mix well.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Use your own frosting mix or serve with Cool Whip.
Remove one end from each of four 1-pound cans (the kind used for canned fruits and vegetables); rinse cans, dry and grease well.
In a large bowl, combine the graham and all-purpose flours, soda and salt.
Stir in yogurt, molasses, raisins and walnuts; mix well.
Divide batter evenly between cans.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 1 hour or until a wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in cans 10 minutes; then turn out and stand loaves upright on a wire rack to cool completely.
Cut loaves crosswise to make thick or thin slices as you prefer.
Makes 4 small loaves.
Cook pudding mix as directed on package, using 1 1/2 cups pineapple juice for the liquid instead of milk.
Cool.
When cooled, fold in fruit.
Put into a glass serving bowl.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in 9 x 12-inch cake pan.
Add pie filling and
pineapple.
Smooth as it is mixed.
Dump cake mix on top
of
fruit.
Dot
with remaining butter.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Combine flour, ginger, soda, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Set aside.
In large mixing bowl beat oleo or other shortening with electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds to soften.
Gradually add the 1 cup of sugar and beat until fluffy.
Add eggs and molasses and beat well.
Stir dry ingredients into beaten mixture. Shape into 1 1/2-inch balls (1 heaping tablespoonful dough each). Roll in 2 tablespoons sugar and place on ungreased cookie sheet 2 1/2 inches apart.
Bake at 350° about 11 minutes or until light brown and still puffed.
(Do not overbake.)
Let stand for 2 minutes to cool.
Makes 24 (3-inch) cookies.
Brown hamburger with onion.
Add soups and sour cream; simmer at least 30 minutes.
Serve hot over noodles or rice.
Freezes well.
Serves 6.
Combine vegetable soup, 1/2 cheese, sour cream, pepper and 1 can Durkee onions.
Pour into 1-quart casserole.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 30 minutes.
Top with remaining cheese and onions. Bake, uncovered, 5 minutes longer.
Brown meat; add onion and cook until tender.
Drain off liquid. Stir in milk and cheese.
Stir until blended.
Add corn, soup and pimento.
Season with salt and pepper.
Pour into 2 quart casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mixture may be divided into 2 (1 1/2 quart) casserole dishes and can be frozen.
Serves 6.
Cook macaroni and mix all together, adding salad dressing or mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Use 1/2 to 3/4 to marinate pork tenderloin at least 4 hours before cooking.
Cook on grill for 20 to 25 minutes or to 160°.
Prepare pudding mix, plus brown sugar.
Allow pudding to cool 5 minutes, then add marshmallows.
Add crushed pineapple and oranges (both drained).
Allow mixture to cool.
Cut chicken (boneless) into 1-inch cubes.
Soak 2 hours in eggs.
Bread chicken with combination garlic powder and bread crumbs.
Brown in oil in skillet.
Place in 9 x 9-inch baking dish, layering chicken with cheese.
Pour broth over all.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes until cheese browns.
Drain pineapple.
Mix ingredients and let set.
Mix well with mixer; serve warm.
Layer each of the ingredients beginning with lettuce. Let these ingredients set overnight in the refrigerator.
Combine all ingredients; stir well.
Store in an airtight container.
Yields 7 cups mix.
To cook, see the next recipe.
Mix all ingredients together and chill.
Apples will not turn brown if tossed in lemon juice before mixing into salad.
Mix first three ingredients. Set aside.
Put potatoes in bottom of casserole dish, then cheese next, last pour mixture evenly over cheese.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Last 10 minutes uncover to brown top.
Place the oats and butter in a bowl and pour on the coffee. Let stand 20 minutes.
Stir in the sugars and eggs. Mix well.
Add flour, salt and soda.
Stir in spices.
Bake in a 13 x 9 greased baking pan at 350° for 45 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add vegetables and garlic. Stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes or until tender. Remove vegetables from pan.
Add remaining oil and chicken to pan.

Stir-fry 4 minutes or until tender. Reduce heat. Stir in vegetables and remaining ingredients; simmer 1 minute, stirring occasionally. Serve over the cooked rice. Sprinkle with crushed red pepper flakes.
Pour milk in large bowl; add pudding mix.
Beat until well blended.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in Cool Whip and half of the cookies.
Place 1 tablespoon cookies in cup.
Fill cups 3/4 full with pudding mixture.
Top with remaining cookies.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Prepare cake mix as package directs. Pour 2 cups batter into greased 9 x 13-inch pan and bake 15 minutes.
Mix in order given. Add the 3 egg whites, beaten stiff.
Fold into the cake batter and bake at 350°.
Frost with Seven Minute Icing or Chocolate Frosting.
Cream together sugar, margarine and syrup.
Cut cherries in half.
Make creamed mixture into walnut-sized portions.
Make a thumbprint hole in each and place a cherry half inside.
Then work into a ball and chill.
Mix above items well, except shrimp sauce.
Shape into log and chill.
When serving, pour cocktail sauce on top.
Serve with crackers.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg.
Mix all together and bake at 350° about 1 hour.
Add 1/2 coconut, if you like.
Peel and boil potatoes until done.
Blend together potatoes, margarine, salt, pepper, onion bits, sour cream and 1 cup cheese. Top with remaining cheese and bacon bits.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes in greased casserole dish.
Saute vegetables in butter for 10 minutes.
Add broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Cut cheese into cubes, add to broth mixture. Stir until cheese melts.
Add milk and chicken.
Season with pepper to taste.
Heat to simmer.
Never boil.
Pour beans in bowl. Drain pineapple and pour pineapple into bowl. Cut meat into cubes. Pour into bowl. Add barbecue sauce in bowl. Mix well. Pour into baking dish. Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Split sandwich	buns
in
half.
Heat margarine, grated onion, mustard
and salad dressing in saucepan.
Spread dressing on buns. Place
slice
of
ham
and Swiss cheese in buns. Wrap in aluminum foil.
Heat in a 350° oven for 20 minutes.
Cook broccoli using package directions for 1/2 time; drain. Slice tomatoes 3/4-inch thick.
Reserve 2 tablespoons cheese. Combine remaining cheese, broccoli and onion in bowl; mix well. Arrange tomatoes in shallow baking pan.
Spoon broccoli mixture over tomatoes.
Sprinkle with reserved cheese.
Broil 7 to 8 inches from heat source for 6 to 8 minutes or until cheese is bubbly and tomato slices are heated through.
Drop teaspoonfuls on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle on sugar.
Combine first 7 ingredients.
Cool to lukewarm.
Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water.
Add syrup mixture.
Blend in eggs. Gradually add flour mixture until smooth.
Add enough flour to make a stiff dough.
Place in a greased bowl, cover and let rise until doubled.
Knead a little.
Divide into 2 loaves and let rise again in pans until doubled.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Grease 8 x 8 x 2-inch dish.
Brown meat and drain.
Mix sour cream, salad dressing, cheese and onion.
Keep this.
Mix Bisquick and water until dough forms.
Put in dish 1/2-inch high up sides of dish.
Layer beef, tomatoes and green pepper.
Spoon over sour cream mixture.
Bake 25 or 30 minutes at 375°.
Makes 5 or 6 servings.
Combine corn syrup and peanut butter; mix well, then add to the vanilla ice cream and 2/3 cup peanuts.
Pour 1/2 of mixture into pie shell, then drizzle and swirl chocolate syrup over ice cream mixture.
Finish pouring rest of ice cream mixture into shell, then drizzle and swirl chocolate syrup over top.
Sprinkle a few chopped peanuts over that to make it look pretty.
Freeze until real firm (at least 4 hours).
Let stand for 5 to 10 minutes before slicing.
Yields 1 scrumptious pie!
Combine
molasses,
soda and water and	pour
into
pie shell. Rub together flour, shortening,
sugar
and
cinnamon. Sprinkle on top of molasses, soda and water	mixture.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° until filling is a rich
brown, about 35 minutes.
In large bowl, combine sugar and flour.
Set aside.
In heavy saucepan, combine butter, Crisco, coffee and cocoa.
Stir and heat to boiling.
Pour over flour and sugar.
Add buttermilk, eggs, soda and vanilla.
Mix well at high speed on mixer.
Pour into well buttered jelly roll pan, 17 x 11-inch.
Bake 20 minutes in 400° oven.
In food processor, grind fine the peel. With motor running, add sugar and blend; mix well.
In a large bowl with electric mixer, cream the butter and sugar mixture (a little at a time) until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time.
In a bowl, add and sift dry ingredients. Add to butter mixture alternately with buttermilk.
Pour into two buttered and floured loaf pans. Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Will keep 4 days wrapped.
Peel, core and slice large, overripe cucumbers.
Soak cucumbers in lime and 1 gallon water for 24 hours.
Wash; soak in ice water for 2 hours.
Boil cabbage heads until leaves look transparent, then remove from head and allow to cool.
Cut thick vein out so leaf won't split when cooking.
Mix together the following ingredients: ground beef, Italian sausage, rice, onion, garlic, salt and pepper. Form mixture into hot dog shapes just large enough to fit each cabbage leaf.
Place rolled mixture into cabbage leaf and roll, tucking sides as you go, then place into deep pot.

When a row is complete, top it with sauerkraut, and so on, until pot is full. Now, pour your tomato sauce over top, fill pot with water (enough to cover cabbage rolls), cover pot with lid and cook 2 to 4 hours.
In a pan, melt margarine and add cocoa and water.
Bring to a boil.
Pour over flour and sugar mixture while hot.
Add milk, eggs, soda, vanilla and cinnamon.
Bake in a greased jelly roll pan for 15 to 20 minutes at 400°.
Cook rice in bouillon with onion, celery and green pepper added.
Seed, wash and cut up chili peppers.
In buttered casserole, put a layer of rice, 1/3 of the sour cream, 1/3 of the chilies and 1/2 of the Jack cheese.
Repeat layers.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
The last 5 minutes, cover with Cheddar cheese.
Boil chicken breasts until done, cool and remove chicken from bones.
Cut or shred chicken to make approximately 4 cups. Discard skin.
In large pot, melt butter; add mushrooms and saute 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper until smooth.
Slowly stir in chicken broth, continue to stir until flour is mixed in. Slowly stir in table cream and whipping cream.
Drain pimentos from juice in jar and add pimentos to the mixture.
Add cooked chicken and sherry.
Continue to cook over low heat until thickened.
Serve over cooked rice (or noodles).
This recipe can be prepared the night before and refrigerated.
To warm, just add a little milk to thin the mixture out if needed.
Mix first 4 ingredients and shape mixture into bite size balls; brown.
Add pineapple juice to oil and cook slightly over low heat. Add a mixture of cornstarch, soy sauce, vinegar, water and sugar. Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Add meatballs, pineapple chunks and green/red pepper.
Cook for about 3 minutes, until heated through.
Enjoy!
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease 2 large baking sheets.
In large bowl, sprinkle yeast over water.
Stir until well blended and yeast is dissolved.
With spoon, gradually stir in sugar, salt and 3 1/2 cups flour until dough is soft and slightly sticky.
Turn dough onto floured table or board.
Knead.
Turn 1/4; repeat. Knead 5 to 7 minutes adding another 1/2 cup flour if needed until dough is smooth and elastic.
Dough should not stick.
Cut dough in half and cut each half into 6 equal size pieces.
With floured hands, roll one piece of dough back and forth between palms of hands to form a dough rope.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a medium bowl, combine cream cheese, onions and dill weed.
Unroll crescent roll dough onto a greased pan.
Don't separate dough.
Press dough into an 8 x 11-inch rectangle pan.
Spoon crabmeat lengthwise along center of dough. Spoon cream cheese mixture over crabmeat.
Fold long edges of dough over cream cheese mixture, slightly overlapping edges. Pinch together to seal.
Place seam side down on baking sheet. Lightly brush top of dough with egg yolk.
Cut slits in top of dough.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes or until golden brown and flaky. Cut into 1-inch slices and serve warm.
Toss apples with lemon juice.
Combine with chicken, celery, walnuts and raisins, adding just enough mayonnaise to hold salad together.
Refrigerate before serving.
Put milk, rice, and salt in bowl and bake at 350° until almost thick.
Then stir in sugar and vanilla.
Bake few minutes longer. Raisins may be added if desired.
Total baking time will be 2-3 hours; rice needs to be stirred every 15-20 minutes while baking.
Make meatballs to your taste; set aside.
In 2-quart casserole dish, mix ketchup, water, olives and onion.
Add meatballs.
Put in microwave on High for 15 minutes, then set microwave on Roast for 30 minutes.
Besides making great meatballs, it makes a great gravy for boiled potatoes or rice.
Melt butter and mix with graham cracker crumbs.
Cover bottom of pan with 1/2 of this mixture; meanwhile, have Dream Whip and milk mixing.
When whipped, add sugar and then cream cheese.
Mix well.
Pour 1/2 mixture over crumbs; then spoon both cans of cherry pie filling over cream.
Top cherries with remaining half of whipped cream mixture.
Then sprinkle remaining half of crumbs over pie for topping.
(Strawberries, peaches, blueberries or pineapple can be substituted for fruit filling.)
Mix the first 5 ingredients together.
Grease a 10 x 13-inch baking dish.
Line with chips.
Top with 1/3 meat mixture and 1/3 cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with cheese.
Pour chicken broth over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
If using fresh potatoes, place in a pan; cover with water and cook, covered, for 25 to 35 minutes or just until tender.
Drain; cool slightly.
Peel and cut into chunks.
Place cooked or canned sweet potatoes in 2-quart baking dish.
Roll chicken pieces in melted butter; season with salt, pepper and Tony's.
Roll in crushed potato chips.
Place in baking pan and bake uncovered at 350° for 1 hour.
Barbecue chips add extra flavor.

recipes.t: Pork Tenderloin With Honey Mustard Sauce
d: You will need 1 large 14 x 20-inch Reynolds oven cooking bag.
Grate onion.
Peel potatoes and grate them.
Combine onion and potatoes; rinse, and drain in a sieve; squeeze out excess liquid. Put in a bowl and stir in egg, flour, 1/2 tsp. salt and 1 T. pepper.
Heat about 1/4-inch of oil in a large frying pan.
Drop about 2 T. batter making several pancakes at a time.
Cook until golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes a side.
Drain on paper towels.
Cook broccoli until tender-crisp (5 to 7 minutes).
Drain well. Spread in 9 x 13-inch dish or pan.
Melt 1/4 cup margarine.
Add flour and cook to smooth paste.
Add next 4 ingredients.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Spread over broccoli.
Melt 6 tablespoons margarine in hot water.
Pour over stuffing and toss until evenly moist.
Spread over sauce.
Bake at 350° until stuffing is slightly brown, about 20 to 30 minutes.
Mix together the peanut butter, mashed bananas, butter, brown sugar and eggs with an electric mixer on medium speed.
Sift together the flour with the baking powder.
Add to the peanut butter-banana mixture.
Mix on low speed just until blended.
Stir peanuts and chocolate chips into batter.
Spread into a greased 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Cool completely in pan on a wire rack.
Cut into bars.
Combine cornstarch and water in a saucepan; stir well.
Add raspberries.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Cool.
Drain pineapple; grate zucchini.
Mix in order given.
Bake in greased and floured Bundt or tube pan at 325° for 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes in pan, then finish cooling on a rack.
Mix all ingredients and pour into a greased casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix butter, sugar and salt until light.
Add eggs, sour cream, soda and flour; mix.
Pour into greased muffin tins.
Sprinkle with nutmeg and sugar.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cut 2 lemons in thin slices and freeze in blocks of ice.
When ready to serve.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Pour over ice.
Then add ginger ale or 7-Up.
Bake pie crust at 350° for 8 minutes.
In a bowl, mix rest of ingredients (except cheese).
Add to pie crust.
Top with cheese. Bake for 40 minutes.
Combine corn oil, lemon peel and juice, mustard, sugar, garlic salt and tarragon in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients.
Toss gently.
Chill before serving.
Boil the rice and cool. Dissolve the jello in the water and juice. Let set until partly set, then whip.
Add pineapple or fruit cocktail and sugar.
Fold in the whipped cream and add rice. Refrigerate until ready.
Shred the cabbage and fill quart jars, pressing cabbage down tightly in jars.
Add 1 tablespoon salt and 2 tablespoons vinegar to each jar.
Put on lids and rings; tighten.
Let set 2 weeks before using.
Mix ingredients.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Crush graham crackers.
Combine with 1/4 cup of butter that has been melted.
Spread in bottom of bread pan.
Chill.
Remove stems from mushrooms; set caps aside.
Chop stems. Combine stems, zucchini, onion and water.
Cook, stirring constantly over medium heat until vegetables are tender.
Drain. Stir in cheese.
Stuff caps with mixture.
Place in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes or until caps are tender.
Serve warm.
Put frozen lemonade and orange juice with ReaLemon juice in punch bowl.
Put in ice cubes or block of ice.
Pour 7-Up over this.
Add lemon, orange or rainbow sherbet on top for added zip.
Crush vanilla wafers to fine crumbs.
Add next 4 ingredients, mixing well. Form into balls and roll each in flaked coconut. Freeze. Serve frozen.
Yields 6 dozen.
Roll chicken with ham and Swiss and secure with toothpicks. Roll in flour mixture.
Dip in egg.
Roll in bread crumbs.	Heat oil and saute to brown.
Add water (1/2 cup) and 1/2 cup wine. Cover and cook 10 minutes longer until done.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add eggs and blend.
Add food coloring and water, then cocoa.
Blend in buttermilk and add flour and salt.
Gradually add vanilla and beat until mixed.
Mix vinegar and soda and stir in last.
Do not beat.
Pour into 2 greased and floured 9-inch pans.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until done.
Cool and frost with white icing.
Mix all ingredients together.
Prep yeast by adding to the 1 1/2 cups of warm water and sprinkling a teaspoon of sugar on top. Add to flour mixture.
Mix well but do not overmix.
Make into rolls.
Can be baked immediately or let rise.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Melt together margarine, oil, marshmallows and caramels.
Mix together popcorn, salted peanuts and M&M's and pour over first mixture.
Press mixture into greased Bundt or tube pan and cool. Remove from pan to serve.
Preheat oven to 400°.

Grease a deep dish pie plate. Brown ground beef and onions in skillet; add seasonings, then spread in the pie plate. Sprinkle the green chilies on top. Mix the Bisquick, milk and eggs until blended. Pour over the meat mixture in the pie plate. Bake for 25 minutes, then remove from the oven and sprinkle with cheese. Return to oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Saute celery and onion in butter.
Combine all ingredients in a 2 quart casserole dish.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Mix with celery, green pepper and French dressing.
Toss well and marinate several hours or overnight.
Just before serving, mix remaining ingredients and fold into macaroni mixture.
Serves 8 to 10.
Mix all the ingredients and pour into a pastry shell.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until firm.
If using canned sweet potatoes; drain liquid before mashing.
If using fresh sweet potatoes, peel, cut into small pieces and cook until soft.
Drain and mash.
A pat or two of butter adds flavor.

recipes.t: Pork Chops With Mushroom Gravy(Quick, Easy And Delicious)
d: Sprinkle pork chops generously with garlic salt and pepper. Brown chops in Teflon frying pan.
No oil added (use a little Pam spray before browning).
Add soup and milk.
Stir well and mix into pan drippings.
Turn pork chops over.
Cover and let simmer 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with mashed potatoes.
Mix butter, basil, rosemary, celery salt and garlic salt.
Dip chicken in butter mixture. Mix crumbs and cheese. Roll chicken in crumb mixture. Place in buttered baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining butter and crumb mixture over top if desired. Cover. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Combine ingredients; refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Serve with Wheat Thins or cut up veggies.
Melt over double boiler the butter and chocolate chips.
Add marshmallows and coat.
On a long sheet of waxed paper, sprinkle powdered sugar.
Pour mixture on waxed paper and sprinkle top with powdered sugar.
Shape and refrigerate.
Slice when ready to eat.
Mix all together in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In medium size bowl, combine chicken, apple, celery, nuts and grapes.
In small bowl, combine mayonnaise, lime juice and honey; blend well.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon dressing over chicken salad and toss to coat.
Serve on bed of leaf lettuce with croissants.
Beat eggs lightly; add flour and sugar.
Melt butter and chocolate; add egg mixture and blend.
Put in walnuts and vanilla and pour into a 9-inch pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes. Can be topped with vanilla ice cream while warm.
Dice shallot and mix with cream cheese, sausage and pepper. Remove stems from mushrooms and fill with mixture. Place stuffed mushrooms in glass baking dish. Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix first 6 ingredients and pour into an ungreased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle the dry cake mix over all.
Drizzle the melted margarine over this.
Top with the chopped nuts.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Layer all the ingredients, ending with cheese and bacon bits.
Mix pie filling, pineapple and Eagle Brand milk.
Stir in lemon juice, food coloring, pecans and coconut.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Chill.
Mix pudding, butter and milk together and boil for one minute. Add sugar, vanilla and nuts.
Put in square pan to cool.
Cut.
Slice apples and set aside.
Melt caramels in water and layer apples with caramel sauce alternately in pie shell.
Combine cinnamon, nuts, flour and sugar.
Cut in butter until crumbly; sprinkle over apples.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs lightly in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients and blend well.
Roll into walnut size balls.
Transfer to baking sheet.
Bake until golden, about 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
Spinach balls can be partially baked for 10 minutes, cooled and frozen.
Reheat thawed balls in 350° oven for 10 to 15 minutes before serving hot.
Makes about 6 dozen.
Cook vegetables slowly with milk, until well done.
Mash with potato masher.
Add cheese.
Season and serve at once.
Place hash browns in greased baking dish.
Layer sausage (crumbled), grated cheese and chopped onions.
Pour in milk and whipped eggs over sausage mixture.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Melt butter in baking dish.
Mix flour, sugar and milk together.
Pour into baking dish.
Add pie filling.
Do not stir. Bake at 350° for one hour or until golden brown.
Mix Jell-O with water and sugar.
Add 7-Up.
Measure 2 1/2 cups (set remainder aside) and pour into a 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Chill until slightly set.
Add cantaloupe and chill until firmly set.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour into 2 1/2-quart casserole. Cover and bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Pour sherry over cut fruit and let stand overnight in refrigerator.
Cream butter, sugar and eggs.
Sift flour, soda and cinnamon 4 times.
Add flour to butter, sugar and eggs.
Add fruit and nuts.
Drop on well-greased cookie sheet.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 300°.
Marinate meat in pickle marinade for 3 days. Cook slowly at 350° for 2 to 3 hours in marinade. May add water. Meat should be cut into medium sized pieces.
Mix cucumber and salt.
Let set for 4 hours.
Drain well.
Mix cucumbers and all other ingredients in dishpan.
Cook for 20 minutes.
Pack in pint jars while hot enough to seal.
This is good with hot dogs or beans.
(Be sure to drain salty water out as good as you can.)
Mix all ingredients.
Pour in oblong pan and bake at 350° about 30 minutes.
Add ingredients together and cook until rhubarb is tender. Add strawberry jello and stir until dissolved.
Store in refrigerator.

Boil ribs until tender and done. Drain and place in baking dish. Bake at 350 degrees for 5 minutes. Mix all other ingredients in saucepan, stirring often on medium heat until onions are tender. Brush sauce on ribs and bake for 20 minutes longer. May need to brush on more sauce. Bake 8 to 10 minutes longer. Bake uncovered 10 minutes or until ribs have soaked up sauce.
In a bowl, sift together flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add to this the egg, sweet milk and nutmeats.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into bread tin and bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Wash potatoes.
Do not peel; slice 1/4-thick.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch glass pan.
Place potatoes in layers.
Mix butter and oil; brush over slices.
Pour remaining ingredients in pan.
Sprinkle spices.
Bake at 400° for 25 to 30 minutes.
No need to cover. Too easy to taste so good.

Pare cucumbers and cut in thin slices. Cut onions into thin slices. Alternate onions and cucumbers in baking dish. Sprinkle each layer with flour, salt and pepper. Then pour the ketchup or chili sauce over all. Dot with butter. Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes or until tender.
Lightly mix all ingredients except cheese and chips.
Pour into 8 x 8 baking dish.
Sprinkle with cheese then chips.
Bake at 300 degrees for 30 minutes.
Cream together sugar, margarine and milk until smooth.
Chill until firm.
Place 1 teaspoon mixture in palm of hand.
Gently pat and form an even layer large enough to cover a cherry.
Place cherry (with stem) in center and mold mixture to cover cherry. Place on foil-lined cookie sheet.
Repeat with remaining cherries. Chill until firm.
Melt chocolate in double-boiler.
Holding cherry by stem, dip into melted chocolate.
Cool on foil sheet.
Remove stem and cover with a dot of chocolate.
Blend with ice in blender.
Melt margarine; stir in flour.
Slowly add milk to make a white sauce.
(I use microwave as does not scorch.)
Fry bacon and remove.
Saute onions in bacon drippings.
Add potatoes, bacon, onions, cheese, salt and pepper to heated milk mixture.
Return to microwave; heat thoroughly.
Remove; add sour cream.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix together stuffing and melted butter and put 1/2 mix in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix soup, milk, chicken, peas, onion and pepper. Pour over mixture in pan and cover with remaining crumb mixture. Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Mix together in large bowl all ingredients except 1/2 stick margarine and corn flakes.
Put in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt 1/2 stick margarine and mix with corn flakes.
Put over top of mixture.
Bake uncovered 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
May divide in half and freeze until ready to bake.
Combine all ingredients in a bottle; shake well.
Refrigerate.

Mix all (except flour) with a spoon as long as possible, then knead in flour with the hands until sufficient flour is used to make a delicate dough. Roll out thin, cut with cookie cutters and bake in a quick oven (375° to 400°) for 7 to 10 minutes; less for thin cookies. Keep ingredients in a cool place until mixed.
Brown beef, bacon and onion; drain.
Add all other ingredients, except beans; stir well.
Add beans and mix well. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 20 to 24 servings.
Put onion and garlic in food processor and chop until fine. Saute onion and garlic in oil in large pan until translucent (don't burn).
Add fresh beans and stir.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 10 to 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes (with juice), salt and pepper to taste.
(If you want, you may add a little tomato sauce to make it thicker.)
Cover and cook on low heat for at least an hour, depending on how hard or soft you want the green beans to be.
Or you can bake in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Stir occasionally. Add water, if needed.
Mix flour mixture together.
Combine cream cheese, bacon, onion and pepper; mix well. Separate crescent rolls into 2 rectangles and pinch seams together. Spread cheese mixture on each rectangle.
Roll up, starting at longer side, and seal end of roll.
Cut each roll into 16 slices. Place slices cut-side down on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve warm.
In blender, blend basil, garlic, olive oil and parsley.
Mix in nuts, then the cheese.
Serve over pasta.
In a 4 to 5-quart Dutch oven, cook ground beef, onion and garlic, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add cabbage until wilted.
Add remaining ingredients; cook 25 minutes.
Serve over cooked rice or noodles. Makes 4 servings.
Cook squash and drain.
Mix the remaining ingredients, using 3/4ths box of croutons and 1/2 of the melted butter.
Top with remaining croutons and drizzle butter over all.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
Saut onion in oil and garlic until transparent (about 5 to 10 minutes).
Add tomatoes, spices, salt and pepper; bring to a boil and add green beans.
Turn to simmer and cook until beans are tender.
Layer the ingredients as they are listed.
Drain pineapple. Mix syrup with sugar and flour.
Alternate layers of cheese and pineapple.
Pour syrup over all.
Bake for 40 minutes in a 350° oven.
Good with baked ham.
Place pork chops in casserole pan.
Salt to taste.
Mix all other ingredients in small saucepan and heat just enough to melt butter.
Pour over pork chops; cover and cook at 375° for 45 minutes.
Chicken can be used in place of pork chops.
Crumble and brown hamburger in fat.
Drain off excess fat. In a separate pan, add all remaining ingredients and heat thoroughly.
Add to hamburger.
Serve over buns.
This can be increased to serve a large crowd and is fast and easy.
*Use 2 or 3 different types of greens, depending on the season, iceberg, curly leaf, romaine, Boston, bibb lettuce, spinach leaves, etc.
Mix together like a sponge first 8 ingredients; let rise 20 minutes.
Add to sponge the carrots (raw), parsley, basil and flour.
Knead; let rise until double in bulk.
Form into 2 loaves. Let rise again.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Soften cream cheese and blend in vanilla.
Sift sugar and cocoa together and gradually add to cream cheese.
Blend thoroughly.
If too stiff to spread, add milk or cream, one teaspoon at a time until desired consistency is reached.
Mix first 6 ingredients and shape into small balls and fry in Crisco until brown.
Bring 5 remaining ingredients to boil.
Add cooked meatballs and simmer 30 minutes before serving.
In large bowl combine corn, kidney beans, onion, green pepper and cheddar cheese.
Sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon of the "Poultry Magic" over each chicken breast.
In a hot skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter, add onion. Cook about 5 minutes and onion browns.
On medium heat, continue cooking 5 to 6 minutes, until onion is caramelized.
Put onion in another container.
On high heat add 3 tablespoons butter.
Dredge the seasoned chicken through flour.
Cook about 1 to 2 minutes per side or until golden brown.
Remove chicken.
To pan add 1 cup bouillon to deglaze pan, stirring and scraping pan bottom.
Stir in caramelized onion and return browned chicken.
Stir in remaining bouillon and "Poultry Magic" and bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, about 20 minutes or until sauce thickens.
Serve with rice.
Drain all juices from fruit.
Mix milk with Cool Whip.
Mix sugar with cream cheese.
Mix all together and refrigerate.
Fry hamburger and onions until slightly brown.
Fry bacon and break into small pieces.
Mix tomato soup, mushrooms, mushroom soup and tomato juice.
Season with salt, pepper and a little sugar. Put in alternate layers in 9 x 13-inch baking dish the hamburger, cooked spaghetti, liquid mixture, bacon and cheese.
Cover with a few crumbled Ritz or saltine crackers.
Bake about one hour at 350°.
Save a little cheese to put on top.
(Be sure to drain spaghetti well after cooking.)
Blend peanut butter, sugar and water.
Mix in Bisquick mix. Drop by small teaspoonfuls onto lightly greased cookie sheet. Flatten with fork.
Bake in a 400° oven about 8 minutes.
Makes 6 1/2 dozen.
Separate eggs.
Add sugar to egg yolks.
Add cream and milk. Beat egg whites stiff.
Fold into liquid mixture.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Combine first 3 ingredients and press into 9 x 13-inch pan, lightly brown.
Cool completely.
Melt 1/4 cup butter.
Add coconut and 1/2 cup chopped pecans.
Cook over low heat, stirring often until coconut is golden brown.
Cool completely.
Combine cream cheese and condensed milk, beat at medium speed with an electric mixer until smooth.
Fold in whipped topping.
Layer 1/3 each of cream mixture, caramel sauce and coconut mixture over crust.
Repeat process twice.
Cover and freeze until firm.
Cook spaghetti, drain and set aside.
Slice onions and mushrooms.
Cut the pound of bacon in half then in half again; set aside.
Saute the onions and mushrooms in margarine, remove and set aside.
In same frying pan cook bacon until almost done (not crisp).
Drain bacon grease.
Add onions and mushrooms to bacon. Add oregano, spaghetti, half and half and stir over medium heat. Add Parmesan cheese.
Mix well.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes and remove. Serve with a salad and garlic bread.
In a large casserole dish lay 1 layer of dried beef.
Wrap turkey cutlets in bacon and lay on dried beef.
Mix cream of mushroom soup and sour cream well.
Then spread over meat. Refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 275° for 3 hours, uncovered, or until very brown and crispy on top.
Serve with dried parsley and steamed fresh broccoli.
Makes a nice company dinner.
Dissolve pudding mix in pineapple.
Mix well.
Add coconut, marshmallows and fold whipped topping into mixture.
Refrigerate overnight and enjoy!
Mix all ingredients except Chinese noodles.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place Chinese noodles on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.

Cream together shortening, sugars and egg. Add flour, soda and cream of tartar. Mix well. Add vanilla and coconut. Mix. Roll dough in walnut size balls. Dip tops in water and then sugar. Place on cookie sheet, sugar side up. Bake at 350°until golden brown.
Pour half and half into large bowl.
Add pie filling mix.
Beat with wire whisk until well blended, 1 minute.
Let stand 5 minutes. Fold in whipped topping and crushed cookies.
Spoon into crust. Freeze until firm, about 6 hours or overnight.
Remove from freezer and let stand 10 minutes to soften before serving.
Store any leftover pie in freezer.
Combine all ingredients in a 4-quart Dutch oven; bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook and drain sausage; cut celery up fine.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in casserole dish and grate cheese over top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl and whisk until thoroughly blended.
Pour into a lidded container and refrigerate for up to a week.
Shake before serving.
Mix together eggs, sugar, oil, zucchini, sour cream and vanilla.
Sift together and add dry ingredients.
Grease and flour two large loaf pans (or five mini loaf pans).
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to one hour.
Shred tomatoes, peppers, onions, and cabbage together.
Soak in salt water 3 hours, then drain.
Cream together first 6 ingredients.
Combine flour, cream of tartar and baking soda.
Add flour mixture to creamed mixture.
Add cereal, nuts and chocolate chips.
Form into 1-inch balls.
Arrange on cookie sheet.
Press with fingers.
Bake at 300° for 10 minutes. Aloha from Hawaii.
Grease baking sheet and set aside.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour, then lower heat to 300° for 1 hour.
Layer cooked chicken and cooked broccoli in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Mix the chicken soup, water and mayonnaise and pour over chicken mixture.
Next, add shredded cheese and bread crumbs.
Mix and form into balls.
Melt 1/2 block paraffin with a small package of semi-sweet chocolate drops.
Use a double boiler.
Dip balls in chocolate.
Place on rack to cool.
In a medium bowl combine crumbs, 2/3 cup mincemeat, meat, egg, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Shape into 1 1/2-inch meatballs.
In a large skillet, brown meatballs in oil; remove as browned.
In same skillet, cook onion and green pepper until tender.
Add remaining mincemeat, curry and ReaLemon.
Mix well.
Return meatballs to skillet.
Cover; simmer 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with rice.
Brown meat and drain.
Dump in crock-pot.
Add all other ingredients, except cheese.
Cut up cheese in chunks and drop in pot.
Cook on low until melted.
Serve with large corn chips.
In top of double boiler, melt margarine.
Add onion and celery.
Saute until tender.
Place over boiling water.
Add creamy peanut butter and flour; blend well.
Stir in beef bouillon and lemon juice.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. When serving, garnish with chopped peanuts.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put in a baking pan.
Cook at 400°.
Combine 2 cups white flour and next 7 ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix well.
Heat water and oil to 120° to 130° and add, blending at low speed until moistened.
Beat 3 minutes at medium speed.
Stir in remaining flour to make a firm dough.
Knead for 5 minutes.
Place in a greased bowl.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Punch down; sprinkle cornmeal on surface and roll dough to 1/2-inch thickness.
Cut into 3-inch circles.
Place muffins on ungreased cookie sheet.
Cover; let rise to double.
Handle carefully.
Bake on griddle at 325°, cornmeal side down, for about 8 minutes on each side.
Cool on rack.
Split with fork, toast and serve.
Mix pudding and pour in greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Take one large can of peaches, drain juice and save.
Arrange peaches on top of cake batter.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and 5 to 6 tablespoons of peach juice.
Spread on top of peaches.
Bake at 350° in oven for 50 to 60 minutes.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar on top when cool.
Combine caramels and 1/3 cup milk over low heat; stir until melted.
Combine cake mix, 1/3 cup milk, margarine and nuts. Press half of mixture into greased 13 x 9-inch pan. Bake 6 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven and sprinkle chocolate pieces on top. Pour on caramel evenly.
Crumble remaining cake mixture on top and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool and cut into bars.
Mix cranberry juice and apple cider or apple juice. Just before serving, add ginger ale.
Blend in blender at high speed.
Refrigerate.
Pare and slice potatoes; place in a medium-sized casserole dish.
Lightly salt and pepper potatoes.
Mix soups and milk.
Fry pork chops until brown.
Drain chops and arrange on top of potatoes.
Pour soup mixture on top of chops.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Cook soup according to package directions.
Add vegetables and seasonings; cook for 10 minutes.
Add ground beef, breaking it up into small pieces.
Cook for about 30 minutes until meat and veggies are done.

recipes.t: Better Than Anything Cake(Heavenly Or Sinful, You Make The Call)
d: Mix cake mix according to directions and bake in a 9 x 15-inch pan.
See box for baking time.
Remove cake from oven when done and immediately poke holes all over the cake with the end of a wooden spoon.
Pour the jar of caramel sauce all over the cake and then do the same with the sweetened condensed milk.
Let cake cool in refrigerator.
Spread Cool Whip on top of cake and top with broken Skor bars.

recipes.t: Chicken In Tomato And Onion Sauce
d: Heat oil in pan.
Add chicken pieces and brown.
Remove from pan.
Drain fat from pan.
Add butter and sliced onion; cook until tender.
Add undrained, chopped, mashed tomatoes, soup mix, soy sauce and 3/4 cup water and heat through.
Place chicken in ovenproof dish and pour sauce over.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Remove chicken.
Pour sauce in saucepan.
Stir in blended cornstarch and 1 tablespoon extra water; stir until sauce boils and thickens.
Pour over chicken.
Crush crackers coarsely into a large bowl.
Add tuna, onion, salt, pepper, green peppers, egg and milk.
Blend well and form into four individual loaves.
Place loaves in greased, shallow baking dish.
Brush with melted butter.
Bake in oven for 30 minutes at 375°.
Heat soup and sliced eggs.
Pour over loaves placed on a platter.
Can be made into one large loaf.
Microwave peanut butter, chips and margarine one minute on High.
Place cereal in plastic bag; mix with first mixture and add 2 cups powdered sugar.
Toss to coat.
Cream the first 5 ingredients together and set aside.
Take your frozen shrimp and boil as directed on package.
Rinse thoroughly in cold water and the cut into small pieces.
You can also use canned shrimp.
For best results, chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Beat eggs at high speed for 5 minutes.
Gradually add sugar. Stir in flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
Stir in pumpkin and lemon juice.
Spoon into greased and floured 15 x 10 x 1-inch pan.
Top with nuts.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Turn out on towel; sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Starting at narrow end, roll towel and cake together.
Cool.
Unroll for filling.
Cream sugar, oleo until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla and yolks, one at a time, beating until fluffy.
Sift flour, corn meal and soda.
Add alternating with sour cream.
Beat egg whites and salt together until peaks form.
Fold gently into batter.
Bake in well greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Saute the onion and carrots in the oil until tender. Add the water and chicken bouillon; cook 10 to 15 minutes. Cook and drain the noodles, then add the noodles and thawed broccoli to the water. Bring to a slow boil, then add the garlic salt, milk and Velveeta cheese. Heat slowly until cheese melts.
Toss all ingredients except Fritos and dressing, which should be added at serving time to each salad.
This will keep leftovers fresher.
Cream butter and sugar. Add eggs and beat well. Add dry ingredients. Drop onto greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Mix apples
with
1/2 cup sugar and lemon juice.
Place in graham cracker pie shell.
Boil chicken.
When done, debone.
In boiler of chicken stock, add Velveeta cheese.
Start with 1/2 pound and add more to your taste.
When melted, add noodles.
When done, serve.
Can be refrigerated and warmed up.
Melt margarine in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch Pyrex baking dish. Sprinkle crumbs over margarine and stir.
Add layers of chocolate chips, pecans, butterscotch chips and coconut.
Pour the milk over top and bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Cool in pan and cut into bars.
Melt oleo; mix with crumbs.
Beat Dream Whip with milk until stiff.
Add sugar and cream cheese; mix well.
Pour one half of the crumbs into dish.
Add one half of the Dream Whip mixture. Then add pie filling.
Add remaining Dream Whip mixture.
Top with remaining crumbs.
Put the chicken
in a bag with flour and seasonings and shake well.
Heat
the butter and oil in a heavy skillet until quite hot, and
brown
the
chicken thighs well on both sides. Transfer to a
piece
of
foil
or
absorbent
paper.
Add the onions to the
skillet
and brown very well, using additional butter and oil if
needed.
Return
the chicken thighs to the pan with
the broth
and	the
additional paprika and simmer, covered, until the
chicken is just tender, about 20 minutes. If the broth is absorbed, add more.
Transfer the chicken to a hot serving dish. Add
the sour cream to the pan off the heat and stir into
the pan juices.
Heat 1 minute.
Pour over the chicken thighs. Sprinkle the lemon rind on top.
Crush garlic clove and saute with olive oil.
Add tomato paste and simmer 15 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, basil, parsley, applesauce, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 40 minutes.
Add Romano cheese.
Combine all ingredients and refrigerate overnight.
Mix together ingredients and marinate tenderloin.
Scrub potatoes under cold water.
Dry with a paper towel. Pierce each potato twice with a fork.
Place 1-inch apart on a paper towel in the microwave oven.
Microwave at High (100%) until center is slightly firm, 10 to 12 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes. Cut potatoes in half lengthwise.
Scoop out inside, leaving small amount next to outer skin.
Add margarine, parsley, cheese, sour cream, salt and pepper.
Mash well with a potato masher or electric mixer.
Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Place stuffed shells in a 2-quart oblong baking dish (microwave-safe).
Top with chopped green onions.
Sprinkle with paprika; just a few sprinkles on each.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave at Medium heat (70%) until heated through, 4 to 5 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix sugars and melted oleo; put in eggs, soda, vanilla and flour.
Then cream in Crisco.
You may need to add a little more flour.
Roll in small balls and place between wax paper; press with bottom of a glass.
Bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 350° until light brown.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix meat, 1 1/3 cups of instant potatoes (dry), egg, salt, pepper, onion, catsup and milk.
Spread in ungreased pie pan (9 x 1 1/2-inch).
Bake, uncovered, for 35 to 40 minutes.
Prepare remaining instant potatoes as directed on package for 4 servings.
Top baked meat loaf with mashed potatoes; sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 3 to 4 minutes longer, or until cheese melts.
Makes 4 or 5 servings.
Cook spinach per package directions.
Drain.
Combine with drained artichoke hearts.
Saute chopped onion in chopped oleo. Add sour cream, artichoke hearts and spinach.
Season with celery seed.
Put in casserole; cover with grated Parmesan cheese. Sprinkle with paprika.
Heat in 325° oven for about 20 minutes.
(I sometimes make in advance and refrigerate until ready to heat 25 or 30 minutes.)
Cream butter, sugar and eggs; add flour, baking powder, salt, milk and vanilla.
Mix well and reserve 1 cup of batter.
Melt candy bars; add to reserved batter.
Mix with other batter and pour into greased and floured pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until done.
Frost with Fudge Icing.
Mix pineapple, flour and sugar.
Add cheese and put into casserole dish.
Mix cracker crumbs and melted margarine.
Spread on top.
Bake at 325° for about 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Combine cake mix, egg and 1/3 cup butter or margarine.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 18 minutes. Spread marshmallows over crust while still hot.
In double boiler, place corn syrup, peanut butter chips, 1/4 cup butter or margarine.
Cook until smooth.
Add Rice Krispies and peanuts. Immediately spread over marshmallows using back of spoon.
Cool; cut into squares.
In a mixing bowl combine oil, vinegar, sugar, 1/4 teaspoon salt, dash of pepper and seasoning packet from noodles.
Stir to dissolve seasonings.
Stir in broken noodles, cabbage, chicken, onion and sesame seed.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Before serving, stir in almonds and garnish with green pepper rings.
Serves 8 to 10.
Spread rolls in pie pan.
Press seams together to form flat crust.
Bake until light brown.
Brown hamburger and drain.
Add taco seasoning.
On baked crust, layer crushed taco chips, hamburger, cottage cheese, hamburger, chips and cheese.
Bake until cheeses are melted.
Bake at 350°.
Mix together all ingredients, except butter and chicken.
Dip chicken in butter and then into crumb mixture.
Bake for 1 hour at 300°.
