Mix all ingredients together and make out into small balls. Melt semi-sweet chocolate bits and a small piece of paraffin in a double boiler.
Dip balls into chocolate mixture and place pecan half on top of each.
Yields approximately 6 dozen.
Beat fruit cocktail in large bowl.
Pour in 1 cup coconut, eggs and cake mix.
Blend.
Pour in 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan.
Top with brown sugar over batter.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes or until toothpick comes out dry.
While cake is still hot, mix in small pan the butter, sugar and cream.
Boil until margarine is melted.
Add rest of coconut.
Pour over hot cake. Cool and serve.

Preheat oven to 350°. Prepare a well-greased Bundt pan. Remove biscuits from tube, separate and cut into quarters; set aside. Mix together white sugar and cinnamon. Roll biscuit quarters into sugar mixture and then place into Bundt pan. Sprinkle nutmeats over all. Melt oleo and brown sugar in saucepan. Bring to a boil just enough to dissolve sugar. Pour sauce over biscuits and bake for 35 minutes. Remove and let stand 10 minutes. Turn out onto a large plate.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Mix.
Add combined milk, margarine and egg.
Fold in 2 teaspoons sugar and berries.
Spoon in greased muffin pan 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Cut up the tough end of the broccoli and cook along with the rice in the bouillon.
When half done, add the rest of the broccoli pieces and finish cooking.
Mix all ingredients and serve on rye or wheat bread.
Heat oil in skillet, saute shrimp, garlic and green peppers 5 minutes.
Stir in ginger, salt, pepper, chicken broth and beans. Cover and simmer 6 to 8 minutes.
Combine cornstarch with cold water, stir into shrimp
mixture and simmer 1 minute longer. Serve on bed of steaming hot rice.
In a large bowl, mash enough berries to equal 3 cups.
In a saucepan, combine the sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in the mashed berries and water; mix well.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Cook and stir for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat; add food coloring if desired.
Pour into a large bowl. Chill for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mixture is just slightly warm.
Fold in the remaining berries.
Pile into pie shell.
Chill for 2 to 3 hours.
In a small mixing bowl, whip the cream until soft peaks form; sprinkle pudding mix over cream and whip until stiff.
Pipe around edge of pie or dollop on individual slices.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Melt cheese in top of double boiler over boiling water. Combine the horseradish, mayonnaise, Tabasco sauce and chopped chives.
Stir into melted cheese.
Pour into jar.
Cool.
Cover and let stand in refrigerator 24 hours.
Makes a generous pound of cheese spread.
Chop pears, onions and peppers.
Soak in water.
Heat sugar and vinegar.
Pour over mixture.
Seal jars.
Heat lids and rings.
Melt chocolate and butter.
Beat egg yolks.
Add sugar, milk and vanilla.
Add chocolate mixture.
Beat again.
Add coconut and nuts.
Bake in an unbaked pie shell at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Top with meringue.
Cook in saucepan on low heat until thick and tender.
This is do your own thing recipe.
Melt margarine in 3-quart saucepan over low heat.
Add marshmallow cream and chocolate chips.
Stir until smooth.
Add corn flakes and peanuts; toss until well coated.
Drop rounded tablespoonfuls of mixture onto waxed paper or cookie sheet and cool.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
In a medium saucepan, over very low heat, melt chocolate and shortening.
Remove from heat and add sugar, egg, flour, salt and vanilla.
Stir well.
Pour into a greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan and sprinkle with chopped nuts, if desired.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 12 minutes or until cookies test done. Remove from oven; cool in pan and then cut into 2-inch squares. Makes approximately 16 squares.
Place bananas in baking dish.
Roast 15 minutes.
Cool. Process bananas, sugar and rum.
Puree.
Add cream.
Process until fluffy (approximately 2 minutes).
Can be made up to 4 hours ahead.
Cover.
Chill.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add crushed pineapple, strawberries, bananas and walnuts.
Pour half of mixture in a pan and refrigerate until firm.
Spread with sour cream and pour remaining mixture over sour cream.
Chill until firm.
Put drained peas in 9 x 12-inch casserole.
Saute onions, celery and pepper in butter.
Add to peas.
Add rest of ingredients.
Top with bread crumbs.
Cook at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir together the first 5 ingredients.
Mix egg and milk; add to flour mixture.
Stir until batter is smooth.
Pour oil into deep skillet to a depth of 1-inch (fill pan no more than 1/3 full).
Heat over medium heat to 375°.
Saute onions, bell peppers and celery.
Mix everything together in rice cooker and stir often.
"The hotter, the better."
Sausage or shrimp may be added for variety.
Mix together.
Press into 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 3 or 4 minutes.
Let cool.
Remove casings from Italian sausage and brown.
Remove from pan.
Drain off fat.
Add 1/2 cup water to pan.
Add onion, garlic, eggplant, carrots, basil and oregano.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables; stir.
Slowly pour in milk and cook until the sauce thickens a little, 5 to 10 minutes.
You may add more flour for thicker sauce.
Season with pepper (optional) and serve over pasta.
Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Place sliced potatoes in cold water.
Before using, drain and dry on paper towel.
In 3-quart greased "with butter" casserole, layer potatoes with cheese, onion, salt and pepper.
Top with remaining cheese.
Beat eggs with milk and Ranch dressing and pour over top of potatoes and bake until tender.
Dot with butter.
Cut slice from top of bread; remove center, leaving a shell. Cut removed bread into bite-size pieces.
Save.
Brush inside of shell with 3 tablespoons margarine.
Place on cookie sheet with cubed bread.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.

Fry the garlic and onion. Add the chicken, carrots and the cabbage. Set aside. Boil the chicken broth then add the rice noodles until it is cooked. Then add the vegetable mixture and stir until almost dry. Arrange on a platter and serve.
Beat butter and sugar at medium speed with electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add 1/2 cup corn syrup and egg yolks, beating well.
Gradually stir in flour, cover and chill for 1 hour.
Melt 1/4 c. butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat, stir in powdered sugar and 3 tablespoons corn syrup.
Cook, stirring often until mixture boils.
Remove from heat and stir in pecans.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Shape mixture by 1/2 teaspoon fulls into 1/4 inch balls.
Place 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Beat egg whites until foamy and brush on dough balls.
Bake at 375° for 6 minutes.
Remove from oven and place pecan balls in center of each cookie.
Bake 6 to 8 more minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool 5 minutes on baking pans.
Remove to wire racks to cool completely.
Freeze if desired and serve.
Place wok over high heat.
When wok is hot, add 2 tablespoons oil.
When oil is hot, add chicken and garlic.
Stir-fry until chicken is opaque (4 minutes).
Remove from wok.
Add 1 tablespoon of oil to wok.
When hot, add onion and green pepper.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return chicken to wok.
Add Sweet and Sour Sauce and pineapple chunks.
Stir until liquid boils and thickens (about 1 minute).
Serve over bed of rice.
Mix all ingredients.
Spoon into 9-inch pie plate or 3-cup shallow baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve with assorted crackers, veggies or pita triangles.
Bring water to a boil and add red hots, stirring until melted. Add jello and stir to dissolve.
Add lemon juice, then applesauce. Pour into any type pan to jell, 13 x 9-inch preferred.
Top with whipped cream or serve plain.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Heat two 9-inch cast-iron skillets or heavy cake pans. (You need sturdy pans that can hold and conduct heat.)
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray 9 x 13 pan with Pam.
Stir together the cake mix and milk until moistened.
Pour into pan. Pour the pie filling evenly over the top.
Most of the fruit will sink to the bottom.
Bake 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with walnuts and bake 20 minutes longer until nuts are toasted.
Press graham cracker crust into bottom of 8 x 8-inch square pan.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until fluffy.
Add vanilla. Fold in whipped cream and marshmallows.
Spread into pan and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Serve topped with cherry pie filling.
Makes 9 to 12 servings.
Brown ground beef.
Chop onion in ground beef and drain well. Mix pork and beans with ground beef; set aside.
Mix Jiffy mix, egg and milk together.
Stir enough to moisten well.
Pour ground beef and pork and beans into casserole dish.
Pour corn bread mixture over beef and bake until golden brown for about 35 minutes at 350°.
Will serve 4.
Break up cake into egg size pieces in large serving bowl.
Add fruit and juice, then prepare pudding mix made with only 2 cups milk (rather than 3).
Mix lightly.
Arrange a small amount of fruit on top.
Top with Cool Whip.
This is good with fresh strawberries.
Mix and let jell.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine sweet potatoes, egg, butter and sugar.
Turn into an 8 x 8-inch casserole dish.
Cut off edges of bread and cut into cubes.
Dip cubes into melted butter and place in rows on top of marshmallows and pineapple layer.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Mix all together lightly and place into casserole dish.
Bake 1/2 hour at 350°, then add 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese and 1 cup crushed potato chips.
Bake another 1/2 hour and serve.
Heat corn oil in skillet over medium heat.
Add onion; saute, stirring frequently until tender.
Stir in zucchini, squash, salt, basil leaves, pepper and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer about 20 minutes or until tender.
Makes four 3/4-cup servings.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over medium heat until no longer pink; drain on paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine 1 3/4 cup of cheese and the next seven ingredients; fold in potatoes. Spread half into a greased shallow 3 qt. baking dish.
Top with sausage and remaining potato mixture.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Uncovered; bake 10 minutes longer or until heated thoroughly.
Serves 10-12.
Combine all ingredients in large bowl.
Mix well and chill.
Mix flour, sugar, milk, eggs and oil together.
Pour into a greased 13 x 15-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
In large heavy skillet, saute chopped onion in oil.
Add the mixed, cubed meat; fry 30 minutes.
Stir in sauerkraut, drained and crumbled bay leaf.
Simmer covered for 1 1/2 hours, until meat and sauerkraut are tender.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Just before serving, stir in the sour cream.
Place potatoes in pan and add water.
Steam in oven at 350° for about 10 minutes or until potatoes begin to get tender, then add salt, sugar and creamed butter after mixing well.
Pour this over potatoes and cook in oven for 30 minutes or until syrup is thickened.
The potatoes will have a glazed look.
Don't overcook!
Cook over medium heat the sugar, milk and salt to soft ball stage.
Remove from heat.
Stir in peanut butter, butter, vanilla, coconut and chopped nuts.
Wait 5 minutes.
Beat with spoon until spreading consistency.
Spread over 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix well and store.
Use 2 coffee measures to 1 cup hot water.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease an 8 x 4-inch loaf pan and set aside. Cream the butter.
Gradually add 1 cup sugar, beating at medium speed until well blended.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
In separate bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to sugar mixture alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Stir in lemon rind.

Dredge blueberries in 2 teaspoons flour. Fold into batter. Pour batter into prepared loaf pan. Bake at 350° for 55 to 60 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Combine 1/3 cup sugar and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Heat until sugar dissolves.
Pierce top of bread in several places with a wooden pick or long fork tines.
Pour lemon juice mixture over warm bread and let it soak in.
Cool bread in pan for 30 minutes. Makes 1 loaf.
Mix sugar and Karo together in heavy saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Add crunchy peanut butter.
Pour over corn flakes in a large bowl.
Toss to coat.
Spoon in small pieces on waxed paper.
Cook noodles according to directions.
While cooking, combine soups and milk; add chicken, peas, salt, pepper and mushrooms. Drain noodles and stir in.
Pour all in a 9 x 13-inch dish sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Combine jello and pineapple.
Heat until mixture simmers. Add sugar, apricots and softened cream cheese.
Continue heating, stirring occasionally, until cheese melts.
Remove from heat; chill until mixture mounds when dropped from spoon.
Whip chilled evaporated milk until stiff peaks form; fold into apricot mixture. Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill until firm.
Top with chopped nuts.
Serves 15.
Chop onions; brown hamburger and onions.
Drain.
Mix in chili beans and mixed vegetables.
Cook on low heat for 1 hour.
Spray 9 x 9-inch baking dish with Pam.
Mix all ingredients together in a bowl.
Pour into baking dish.
Bake at 425° until brown.
Melt butter in baking dish.
Mix together flour, egg and milk. Pour over butter.
Dissolve sugar in peaches.
Add vanilla; pour on top.
Bake at 350° or until lightly browned.
Combine chili sauce and refried beans in saucepan over medium heat until well blended.
Spread on tortilla shells.
Add remaining toppings of choice and bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Combine all ingredients, except pimientos, in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Separate beans with a fork.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 6 to 8 minutes or until beans are tender-crisp.
Add pimientos and heat 1 minute.

Sift together dry ingredients. Cut in butter to dry ingredients until mixture is like coarse crumbs. Combine egg and milk; add to dry ingredients all at once, stirring only to moisten. For big biscuit style, spread dough into a greased 8 x 1 1/2-inch round pan, slightly building up dough around edges. Bake at 350° for 15 to 18 minutes or until golden brown. Remove from pan. Cool on rack about 3 minutes. Serve with strawberries and whip cream. Makes 1 shortcake.
Mix sugar and oil; add 3 eggs.
Mix well.
Add carrots and pineapple; add dry ingredients (sifted together).
Bake in a well greased and floured pan at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix the first 5 ingredients and cook until thickened.
After cooling, stir in 1 1/2 cups coconut. Top with beaten egg whites. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup coconut on top. Brown in a 400° oven about 8 or 9 minutes.
Cook ground chuck and onion in a large skillet. Add taco seasoning, tomatoes, tomato sauce and nacho cheese soup.
Let simmer for 10 minutes.
In casserole dish, add crushed chips. Pour hot mixture on top of chips. Stir well.
If too dry, add about 1 cup water or tomato juice. Top with cheese and microwave 5 minutes.
Brown chops.
Place chops in baking pan with remaining ingredients.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 1 hour.
Brown and drain hamburger.
Mix with all other ingredients. Cook on simmer until thoroughly cooked and flavors blended (about 45 minutes).
Stir frequently.
Thicken with 3 tablespoons flour and cook an additional 30 minutes.
Serve on bread or buns.
Use no salt.
Saute onion and green pepper in margarine until transparent.
Add water and bouillon cubes.
Bring to a boil to dissolve cubes.
Add rice, parsley and pepper.
Bake in a deep 2-quart casserole, covered, for 3/4 to 1 hour or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Oven should be at 350°.
Remove from oven, flake rice with fork, replace cover and let steam for 10 minutes before serving.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a shallow pan, stirring well. Place roast in dish (pan).
Cover and marinate 3 to 4 hours in the refrigerator, turning occasionally.
Remove roast from marinade and place on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.
Insert meat thermometer at an angle into thickest part of meat.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° until thermometer registers 170° (2 1/2 to 3 hours) total cooking time.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together and put in casserole dish.
Bake for 30 minutes or until heated through.
Beat
cream cheese with milk until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients, blend.
Press small amounts into candy molds. Remove from
molds
and
air
dry at room temperature, 4 to 6 hours. Store in airtight containers.
Yields 4 dozen.
Cream powdered sugar, butter, salt and almond flavoring until light and fluffy.
Stir in flour.
Shape dough into 1 1/2-inch balls.
Roll cookies in finely chopped almonds.
Place on an ungreased baking sheet about 2-inches apart.
Make a depression in the center of the cookie with thumb.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 16 minutes or until edges are lightly brown.
Fill depression with 1/4 teaspoon raspberry jam or enough to fill center.
Melt white confection baking bar in double boiler; drizzle over cookie.
First Layer:
Melt over hot water butter and cocoa.
Add powdered sugar, egg and vanilla.
Set aside.
Mix together crumbs, nuts and coconut.
Press into 9 x 13-inch pan and chill.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice. In large skillet, heat corn oil over medium heat.
Add green pepper (cut into 1-inch squares), onion (cut in thin wedges) and garlic.
Stir-fry 2 minutes or until tender-crisp.
Remove from skillet.
Stir-fry pork, half at a time, for 3 minutes. Return all pork to skillet.
Brown meat, onion, bell pepper and garlic in pot.
(Drain grease if necessary.)
Add rest of ingredients and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for an hour, covered.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Prepare cake mix according to package directions. Spoon into paper lined muffin tins, filling 3/4 full. Mix the softened cheese, egg, salt and sugar together until light and fluffy. Add the chips.
Drop by teaspoon into each cupcake. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes; check for doneness.
Makes about 2 dozen cupcakes. Frost with favorite icing, if desired.
Mix ingredients and bake in oblong cake pan at 300° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Cover with small marshmallows when removed from hot oven.
Prepare brownies according to package directions.
Bake. Allow to cool.
Melt oleo in large pan.
Place sliced onions on top of oleo. Pour rice on top.
Add beef consomme and water.
Place chicken pieces on top and season.
Pour mushroom soup over all.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour at 400°.
Remove foil and bake 30 minutes.
In a large bowl combine the first 4 ingredients.
Set aside. In a small bowl combine mayonnaise, sour cream and vinegar; mix well.
Pour over chicken mixture.
Toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
(Wonderful on croissant rolls.) Recipe can be cut in half.

recipes.t: Mrs. Sallie E. Nunnally'S Chess Pie
d: Melt the cup of butter.
Beat the two eggs thoroughly.
Add the melted butter to the eggs and beat.
Add the two tablespoons of water and the cup of sugar. Beat until all ingredients are mixed well. Pour the mixture in the pie crusts.
Bake at 325° for approximately 20 to 25 minutes, until the mixture is "set."
Reserve some cheese; mix all other ingredients.
Put in a baking dish and top with reserved cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook until done; let cool.
Debone.
Add enough salt to broth to suit your taste.
Add 1 teaspoon yellow coloring.
Cut tomatoes into fourths, about two-thirds of the way down. Put a leaf of lettuce on a plate and place tomato on top.
Set aside.
Mix tuna (drained) and mayonnaise together.
Add eggs and onions.
Carefully fill tomatoes with tuna salad.
Serve with crackers.
Great for the summer.
Mix first five ingredients together until smooth.
Add oats, flour, soda and salt.
Mix well.
Put in nuts and chocolate; mix just enough to blend.
Spread batter into a cookie sheet.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Mix peaches with 1 cup of the sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Set aside.
Put butter in 9-inch square pan and place in oven to melt.
In a mixing bowl, combine remaining sugar, flour, baking powder, salt and milk.
Blend with spoon until smooth and pour over melted butter (do not stir).
Top with peaches (do not stir).
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until golden brown.
Serve with a pitcher of sweet cream or ice cream. Serves 9.
Melt butter in heavy pot and saute onions and parsley.
Blend in flour, cream and cheese until cheese is melted.
Add remaining ingredients and gently fold in crabmeat.
May be served fancy in chafing dish with Melba toast or in patty shells or just warm with crackers.
Serves 8.
Pour milk and eggs into bowl
Add cut up chicken pieces and soak for 15-20 minutes.
Mix flour, salt, and pepper.
Roll chicken in the mix.
Heat oil in a frying pan and cook chicken until done.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brown beef and onion. Drain well. Stir in seasoning mix, water and olives. Simmer 5 minutes.
Combine sugar, flour and cinnamon; toss with apples.
Pour into 9-inch square pan.
Drain and chop artichoke hearts.
Add mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese and chopped green chilies.
Mix thoroughly and put into baking dish. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes until brown around the sides. Serve hot or cold.
Cook liver in simmering water for 10 minutes.
Drain and chop fine.
Blend liver and remaining ingredients to smooth paste. Cover and refrigerate.
Cover and cook 5 to 6 pound hen until tender; remove and debone.
Cook spaghetti in broth; may need to add water and do not drain.
Saute peppers and onions in butter for 45 minutes on low heat.
Add this to spaghetti; add peas, also juice from peas.
Add chopped chicken and Ro-Tel.
Add cheese in hunks; place in greased casserole dish.
Place in hot oven about 350°; cover until cheese melts.
Combine all ingredients in slow cooker; stir to blend.
Cook on low for 4 hours.
Yields 8 servings.
Mix instant potatoes with water and salt.
Blend eggs into cooled potatoes.
Slowly add the flour.
Dip a tablespoon into salted, boiling water to get it hot.
Use hot spoon to chop off a 1/2 tablespoon of dough and drop it into the hot water.
Keep doing this until all dough is used up.
Let the dumplings boil until all are expanded and look spongy and are floating.
Take out with slotted spoon and toss with butter.
Use in soups, stews, casseroles, etc.
Mix shortening and sugar well; add eggs; add milk and flour. Then add all of the spices and coffee.
Mix well; add raisins and nuts.
Bake in round layer pans at 325° until done.
Heat water to boiling.
Remove from heat and add instant potatoes; mix.
Add to the rest of the ingredients and mix well. Shape into patties.
Roll in a mixture of 1 cup flour and 1 cup cracker meal.
Fry in cooking oil in skillet until golden brown. Drain on paper towel.
In a mixing bowl, combine bread cubes and 1 cup cracker crumbs.
Stir in broth, eggs, salt, celery, onion, chicken and mushrooms.
Spoon into a greased 2-quart casserole.

recipes.t: Banana Cake With Peanut Butter Icing
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Set aside.
In a small bowl combine bananas and buttermilk; set aside.
In bowl, mix peas, onion, celery and pepper.
In serving bowl, place lettuce to cover bottom.
Place 1/2 the pea mixture on top of lettuce; sprinkle 1 teaspoon sugar over that.
Cover with another layer of lettuce pieces,
then rest of pea mixture. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon sugar over top.
Empty mayonnaise on top and spread evenly.
Place cheese on top of mayonnaise, covering it evenly.
Empty bacon bits on cheese and spread evenly.
Decorate with celery leaf, if desired.
Cook pasta; set aside.
Cut up chicken; stir-fry with some garlic and parsley.
Mix together the milk, bouillon, cornstarch and margarine; add to chicken.
Pour over pasta.
Mix together and press into oblong pan all but chocolate chips.
Melt chips and pour over other mixture; spread evenly. Let cool and cut into squares.
Combine and pour into buttered casserole dish. Bake 35 to 40 minutes in a 350° oven.
Lay chicken in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place cheese on top.
Mix soup with 1/2 can water; cover chicken.
Mix stuffing with butter and water according to package directions.
Place on top of casserole and cover with foil.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix mustard, lime juice, garlic, soy sauce and lime peel until well blended.
Reserve 1/2 cup of the mustard mixture for serving with cooked chicken.
Grill or broil chicken 15 minutes or until cooked through, turning and brushing occasionally with remaining mustard mixture.
Serve with reserved 1/2 cup mustard mixture.
Melt butter in heavy pan.
Break vermicelli into small pieces; saute in butter until golden brown, stirring constantly.
Add rice; keep stirring until rice is well coated, 2 to 3 minutes. Add boiling chicken broth and salt.
Cook, covered, on medium-low heat for 20 minutes, until liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with fork. Serves 8.
Beat the first five ingredients together.
Add flour, sifted with salt, cinnamon, ginger, allspice and soda.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl; beat at medium speed of an electric mixer until well blended.
Pour mixture into freezer can of electric freezer (or hand-turned).
Freeze according to manufacturer's directions.
Let ripen at least 1 hour (if you can wait!).
Yields 5 quarts.
Work first 6 ingredients together to form a smooth paste.
Add toffee chips.
Roll a spoonful of dough between the palms of hands. Flatten with bottom of glass or cookie press.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet for 25 minutes at 325° until golden brown.
Wrap raw oysters with bacon (Sizzlean is better).
Place in pan.
Cook in oven under the broiler.
When done on first side, turn over.
Seasoning comes from bacon.
Cook chicken and debone.
Cut into bite size pieces and put in bottom of greased casserole.
Mix soup and sour cream and spread over chicken.
Sprinkle crushed crackers over soup.
Pour melted margarine over crackers.
Sprinkle poppy seed on top.
Bake at 325° about 30 minutes.
Process cheese and butter in a food processor until blended.
Add flour, salt and paprika; process until mixture forms a ball, stopping often to scrape down the sides.
Add cereal and almonds; process until blended.
Stop twice to scrape the sides.
Shape dough into 1 inch balls.
Place balls about 2 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Flatten each ball in a crisscross pattern with a fork dipped in flour.
Bake at 350° for 12 -14 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove to wire racks to cool.
Store in an airtight container.
Grind or chop all vegetables together.
Put on salt; stir and set aside for 5 minutes.
Drain off excess water.
Add sugar, vinegar and water.
Put in hot jars and seal.
In saucepan, melt butter; add flour, salt, milk, cream cheese and Cheddar cheese.
Cook and stir until sauce boils.
Remove from heat.
Cook broccoli until crisp/tender.
Combine broccoli and cheese sauce; pour into casserole dish.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan for 40 minutes at 300°.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl and chill.
Use for sandwiches or with crackers.
Will also stuff 8 tomatoes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place fruit in a buttered 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Cut crusts from bread slices and cut each slice into 5 fingers.
Place the bread fingers over peaches.
In a bowl, mix sugar, flour, egg and butter.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Serves 4 to 6.
Heat oven to 400°.
Grease pie plate, 9 x
1 1/4-inch.
Mix chicken, zucchini, tomato, onion and cheese.
Spoon evenly into pie plate.
Beat remaining ingredients 15 seconds in blender on high speed, 1 minute with wire whisk or hand beater or until smooth.
Pour evenly over chicken mixture.
Warm shells slightly to prevent cracking.
In each shell, place chicken, a sprinkling of cheese and 1 tablespoon picante sauce.
Roll and place in greased baking dish.
Continue with each roll.
Pour remaining picante sauce and spread cheese evenly over dish.
Bake at 400° until cheese is bubbly, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet. Add onion; saute until tender (not brown), 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic.
Add tomatoes, vodka and red pepper; break up tomatoes with side of spoon.
Cook until sauce is reduced by 1/3 and thickened, 15 minutes.
Stir in cream; simmer, stirring (do not allow to boil) 5 minutes. Season with salt.
Drain all the fruit (reserve juice).
Chop all fruit and cut cherries in halves.
Mix all together in a large mixing bowl. Sprinkle instant pudding mix over fruit.
If fruit seems too thick, add some of the reserved juice. Chill.
Melt butter.
Add flour, sugar and salt to make a paste.
Add cheese until it melts.
Remove from heat.
Add sour cream to beans.
Top with corn flakes and butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook celery in a little boiling water until crisp done, about 8 minutes.
Mix celery with water chestnuts which have been drained and thinly sliced.
Add chicken soup and diced pimento. Place in a one-quart casserole.
Toss breadcrumbs with almonds and melted butter.
Sprinkle over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until hot.
Serves 6.
Heat oven to 350°.
Oil pan and sprinkle coconut and pecans over a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix cake mix according to box.
Pour over coconut and pecans.
Mix all ingredients and sprinkle on top of batter.
Bake in 375° oven for 45 to 50 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Combine pancake mix, 3/4 cup brown sugar and cinnamon.
Add banana, milk, egg and oil; mix well.
Spread into prepared pan.
Combine nuts, 1/4 cup brown sugar and margarine; sprinkle evenly over batter. Bake about 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Yields 12 servings.
Mix first 5 ingredients and form ball.
Roll in pecans and refrigerate.
Brown smoked, sliced sausage in a skillet and drain well on paper towels.
Arrange lettuce on a large serving dish and top with vegetables and sausage.
Add Feta cheese.
Pour dressing over salad and serve.
Total preparation and cooking time:
15 to 20 minutes.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Form into a ball and cover with dried beef.
Combine cabbage, bell peppers and salt; let set for 1 hour, then drain.
Combine with remaining ingredients; mix well and cook for 40 minutes, stirring frequently.
Make a paste of 1/2 cup flour and 1 cup cool water to which is added some of the hot relish mixture to prevent lumping; add this to mixture, stirring rapidly until thick.
Place in hot jars and seal.
Process filled jars in a hot water bath for 10 minutes.
Yield: 6 to 8 pints.
Saute green pepper in margarine.
Add spaghetti, Ro-Tel, pepper and onion to cooked chicken.
Stir well until melted.
Add peas and mushrooms.
Place in 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, bake at 325° for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Feeds 10 people.
Freezes well.
Mix all together and put in a 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine syrup, sugar and butter in saucepan and bring to a boil.

Reduce heat and add peanut butter, stirring until melted. Pour peanut butter mixture over Rice Krispies in a large bowl. Stir until well mixed and spread into greased 9 x 13 inch pan and press down lightly and cool, cut into bars.
Cover raisins with water and cook 5 minutes. Drain.
Combine sugar, flour and salt.
Add to raisins, along with sour cream, egg yolks (that have been beaten good) and oleo. Cook very slowly, stirring, until mixture thickens.
Add vanilla.
Pour into baked pie shell. Top with meringue and brown.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg, milk, soda, baking powder and flour in small amounts until dough is stiff enough to roll. Roll out or cut in shape desired.
Bake at 300° until lightly colored.
Slip skins; cook insides and bring to a boil.
Rub out seeds. Add skins and pulp together.
Mix in other ingredients and place in pie shell.
Put crust on top.
Bake in 400° oven until crust is brown, 45 minutes.
Beat all ingredients in a deep bowl with a fork.
Pour into heated, nonstick frypan.
Brown on one side; turn carefully and brown the other side.
Also good for a light meal in the evening.
Roll into little fingers.
Bake at 325° for 14 to 16 minutes. When cool, roll in confectioners sugar.
Brown beef and onion.
Add chilies.
Heat through.
Add soup and milk to meat and heat through.
Put thin layer of sauce in bottom of baking dish.
Put each tortilla into sauce and cover with sauce.
When bottom of dish is covered with one layer of tortillas, sprinkle layer of cheese.
Keep layering until sauce and tortillas are used.
Sprinkle top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.

Mix oil and sugar. Add eggs and vanilla and beat well. Sift all dry ingredients together and add to sugar mixture. Add oats and nuts and mix well. Dough will be stiff (use hands). Shape into rolls and wrap in waxed paper. Chill in the refrigerator. Slice 1/4-inch thick and bake on ungreased baking sheet for 10 to 15 minutes at 350°. Yield: about 60 cookies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease large baking dish.
In skillet, cook sausage, onion and vegetable until sausage browns and vegetables are soft.
Pour off fat; stir in soup.
Divide dough into 6 equal parts.
On floured surface, roll out 1 part to a 6 inch round.
Spread mixture in skillet on 1/2 of round.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Fold over and pinch sides together.
Place on baking dish.
Brush with egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Cream together shortening and sugar until fluffy.
Add egg, then molasses.
Mix together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Add to creamed mixture.
Last, add water.
Bake in 8-inch square pan approximately 30 to 35 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Combine all ingredients and beat 2 to 4 minutes.
Pour into a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes in a 350° oven.
Crumble 1/3 of the cake into the bottom of a large bowl.
Add a layer of pudding, then cherries, pineapple, Cool Whip and then top off with pecan pieces.
Repeat the process again ending with Cool Whip and pecans.
Place all ingredients into stew pan and put on slow fire. Stir occasionally and cook until fish is ready to fall to pieces. Serve hot.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour BOTTOM ONLY of a 9 x 5 loaf pan.
In a small bowl, beat cream cheese until light and fluffy.
Add 1 egg and blend well.
Set aside.
Lightly spoon flour into a measuring cup; level off.
In large bowl, mix together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Stir in apple juice, margarine and beaten eggs.
Fold in cranberries and nuts.
Spoon half of batter into prepared pan.
Spoon cream cheese mixture evenly over batter.
Top with remaining batter. Bake at 350° for 65 to 75 minutes or until top springs back when lightly touched.
Cool 15 minutes.
Remove from pan and cool on wire rack.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water and allow to jell slightly.
Mix in sherbet thoroughly.
Add drained pineapple and oranges.
Mix well. Refrigerate until firm.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt.
Blend in shortening. Stir in egg.
Add enough boiling water to orange juice and rind to measure 1 cup.
Stir into flour mixture.
Add blueberries and nuts; stir gently.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake for 60 minutes.
Makes 1 loaf.
Melt oleo in 9 x 13 x 6-inch ovenproof dish.
Heat water and sugar until sugar melts.
Cut shortening into flour until particles are like fine crumbs.
Add milk and stir only until dough leaves side of bowl.
Turn out on floured board into ball or rectangle about 1/4-inch thick.
Roll like jelly roll, slice into 16 slices, 1/2-inch thick.
Place fruit on bottom of prepared dish, then put dough slices over fruit.
Pour sugar syrup over rolls.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Halve potatoes lengthwise and slice into 1/2-inch thick strips.
Put margarine and olive oil in bowl.
Add potatoes, tossing to coat well.
Arrange potato strips in single layer on nonstick baking sheet.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake in preheated 450° oven for 30 to 40 minutes.
Combine ingredients in a shallow bowl or bag.
Melt butter and shortening in pan.
Place chicken skin side down.
Cook, uncovered, 30 minutes.
Turn chicken; cook, uncovered, 30 minutes more.
Combine all ingredients in blender; blend.
Keep in refrigerator.
Spray a large skillet with nonstick cooking spray.
Over medium heat, cook chicken in skillet 8 to 10 minutes until browned and no longer pink, turning.
Remove from skillet; keep warm.

Beat and mix well the egg yolks, lemon juice, rind and butter; set aside. Mix sugar, flour and salt. Measure milk. Whip egg whites. Add sugar mixture alternately with the milk. Fold into beaten egg whites. Pour into 8-inch square pan. Place this pan in a pan of water. Bake for 45 minutes in 350° oven. Pudding will be in the bottom of pan. Turn over when served and
top with Cool Whip.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Beat egg and milk together.
Stir in melted butter.
Mix all together.
Bake in 8 x 8-inch pan at 425° for 25 minutes.
Bake in slow oven for 3/4 hour.
Preheat oven to 350.
Mix flour, baking powder, and sugar together using a fork.
Cut in shortening until it has the consistency of cornmeal.
Add cheese.
Stir in buttermilk all at one time until just blended.
Do not overmix.
Drop by tablespoonfuls (or use an ice cream scoop) onto a well-greased baking sheet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
Bake pie crust and let cool.
Place chopped strawberries in pie crust.
Combine all other ingredients in boiler and bring to a boil.
Pour into pie crust.
Place in refrigerator.
Add Cool Whip or whipping cream when ready to serve.
Saute onion and bell pepper in oleo.
Add soups, tomatoes, seasoned shrimp or crawfish and parsley.
Bring to a boil, then add raw rice.
Mix well.
Bake in a 350° oven, covered, for 1 hour. Stir (with a fork) after first 30 minutes.
Finish baking.
Peel potatoes.
Boil and mash with butter and cream cheese. Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into a buttered casserole dish and refrigerate mixture overnight.
Bake the next day in 350° oven for 50 minutes.
Serves 4.
Peel and slice apples into greased 10-inch pie pan.
Cover with 1/4 cup sugar.
Cream butter, 1/2 cup sugar and beaten egg.
Add dry ingredients; mix.
Spread over fruit.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix first 6 ingredients by hand.
Don't use mixer.
Will be very thick.
Add chocolate chips.
Pour into well-greased and floured Bundt pan or tube pan.
Bake 60 minutes in 350° oven. Cool upright at least 25 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to moderate 350° (175°C) if you use shiny metal cookie sheet.
Or, heat to 325° (165°C) for dark metal sheet. Cream together thoroughly the shortening, sugar and vanilla.
Beat in eggs.
Beat chocolate.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Measure milk; blend in dry ingredients with milk.
Add nuts.
Chill 3 hours.
Form 1-inch balls.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Place on greased cookie sheet, 2 or 3 inches apart.
Place cookies in center of oven.
Bake for about 15 minutes.
Cool cookies slightly.
Remove from the cookie sheet with turner; place on racks or paper toweling to cool.
Combine eggs, brown sugar, milk, pumpkin, salt and spices. Cook in double boiler until thick, stirring constantly.
Beat egg whites; add sugar and beat until stiff.
Soak gelatine in cold water.
Stir into double boiler.
Chill until pumpkin mixture is partly set.
Fold in egg white mixture.
Pour in pie shell and chill until set.
Garnish with whip cream.
Grate cheeses together.
Mix eggs and picante sauce together. Put 1/2 of cheeses in bottom of Pyrex dish (oblong).
Put the egg and picante mixture on top of cheese.
Cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut in squares and place each piece on Doritos or tortilla chips.
Brown ground beef, onions, salt and pepper in a skillet. Drain.
Pour meat mixture into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Makes 2 gallons.
It is good hot.
I omit the ginger ale.
Beat eggs with a spoon in a 2-quart pan.
Add sugar, butter and dates. Cook slowly for 10 to 12 minutes on a low fire.
Remove from heat and cool. Add Rice Krispies and nuts.
Shape into small balls. Roll in shredded coconut.
Mix pecans and coconut.
Put in bottom of pan.
Mix cake according to box directions. Pour over pecans and coconut.
Mix sugar, cream cheese, butter and vanilla.
Spoon over cake mix. Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
Soften active dry yeast in warm water.
Scald milk in sugar, salt and butter; cool to lukewarm.
Mix in 2 cups flour, yeast, eggs, cardamom and fruit.
Add enough remaining flour to make a stiff dough.
Knead on floured surface; place in a greased bowl and grease top of dough.
Cover.
Cream all ingredients, but only half the nuts.
Chill for 2 hours.
Roll into 1-inch balls and then roll balls into remaining nuts to coat.
Keep chilled.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix ingredients and roll or drop small amount on a greased cookie sheet.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes (until set and not brown).
Remove from cookie sheet and roll in confectioners sugar.
In a large mixer bowl, combine softened cream cheese and sugar.
Beat with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until fluffy.
Reduce mixer speed to low and gradually add whipping cream, milk, peach nectar or orange juice, lemon juice, vanilla and apple pie spice.
Beat until ingredients are combined.
Stir in the chopped peach.
Freeze the ice cream mixture in a 1 or 2-quart ice cream freezer, according to manufacturer's directions. Makes about 1 quart.
Combine cream cheese, sugar and peel; mix until well blended. Unroll dough from cans and lay on floured surface.
Overlap long edges to shape into a rectangle (13 x 7-inch), pressing all edges together to seal.
Spread rectangle with cream cheese mixture (3/4 of mixture, save 1/4 for icing).
Roll up dough, starting at long side, roll up (jelly roll fashion).
Cut or slice 1-inch pieces. Lay on cookie sheet on cut side about 2 inches apart.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cut up chicken.
Add and mix all other ingredients together.
Mix ingredients and put in freezer.
Serve semi-frozen.
Great for Christmas or Thanksgiving dinner.
Mix all ingredients and pour into an unbaked pastry shell. Bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until center of pie is firm when shaken.
Cook and stir ground beef; drain off all fat.
Add spaghetti sauce to meat and mix well.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix Ricotta cheese, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese, parsley flakes and oregano.
In an ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan, layer 1/4 each of noodles, meat sauce, Mozzarella cheese and the cottage cheese mixture.
Repeat 3 times.
Add meat sauce over top and sprinkle (cover well) with Parmesan cheese.
Bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Drain peas.
Rinse with cold water and drain well. Add chopped celery and onion. Combine oil, vinegar, mayonnaise, salt and cayenne pepper.
Mix well.
Pour over peas.
Stir gently. Allow to chill in refrigerator several hours or overnight.
Saute pepper in butter until tender.
Blend in flour.
Add milk and stock.
Cook until smooth.
Add cheese, pimento and soup. Cook spaghetti in broth and drain.
Add sauce and chicken.
Pour into casserole.
Sprinkle with additional cheese.
Bake at 250° to 300° for 45 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Cook bacon completely, but not crispy.
Cook greens for about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients; stir thoroughly. Makes approximately 4 servings.
Cream together powdered sugar, evaporated milk and peanut butter.
Mix in cream cheese, half of dry peanuts and Dream Whip. Once all mixed, pour into pie shell of your choice.
Sprinkle remaining dry peanuts on top.
Freeze for 2 hours, then refrigerate until ready for use.
Serve with chocolate syrup and Cool Whip.
In a large bowl, combine mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Mix well.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Refrigerate several hours.
Serves 6.
Grease (Crisco) a 9x13 baking dish.
Peel and slice potatoes. Make a layer of potato slices, top with velveeta cheese and 4 tsp butter on cheese.
Repeat layers.
Mix milk and flour together. Pour over layers.
Cover and Bake at 350 - 400 degrees for 1 1/2 hours or until potatoes are tender.
Cook beef with onions.
Prepare tortilla and assemble one at a time.
Fry tortilla in hot oil for a few seconds on each side. Dip into 1 can of heated enchilada sauce and remove immediately. Place on a plate and put olives, cheese and meat mixture on tortilla.
Roll up and place seam side down in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
When all enchiladas are in baking dish, cover with remaining sauce.
Sprinkle top with grated cheese, olives and raw chopped onions.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Sift the first 3 ingredients.
Add egg, margarine and rest of ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet. Sprinkle coconut on each cookie and level with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Combine vinegar, sugar, oil, salt and pepper; add to other ingredients. Set in refrigerator overnight, then drain and serve.
Melt sugar over low flame until sugar is golden brown.
Add butter.
Add nuts and stir until nuts are covered.
Pour into well buttered dish.
When cold, break into pieces.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water; chill until it starts to jell.
Mix together cream cheese and confectioners sugar until smooth.
Whip Milnot until it peaks; slowly add cream cheese mixture and gelatin.
Mix cracker crumbs with margarine, reserving 1/4 cup.
Line a cake pan with rest of crumbs.
Pour in cream cheese mixture.
Sprinkle with rest of crumbs.
Chill.
Crumble Oreos; set aside.
Fold together the remaining ingredients.
Layer as follows: pudding, Oreos, pudding, Oreos, etc., for a total of 4 or 5 layers.
End with one inch of Oreos on top.
(These may be ground fine in a blender so as to resemble dirt.)
Optional: Add gummy worms to layers.
Mix all ingredients together and spread on a baked Lazy Daisy Cake.
Place under the heated broiler in oven until it bubbles. Delicious!
Mix jello with 1 cup boiling water and set aside to cool. Beat Milnot until stiff and set aside.
Cream sugar and cream cheese together.
Add cooled jello to whipped Milnot, then cheese mixture and vanilla.
In mixing bowl, combine all dry ingredients.
In small bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Mix dry with moist ingredients, stirring until all are moist.
Brown chicken in melted margarine.
Remove chicken from pan. Drain pineapple, reserving juice. Combine brown sugar, cornstarch and salt in skillet.
Gradually add vinegar, soy sauce and pineapple juice.
Stir. Cook over medium heat until thick.
You may need to add about 1/2 cup water. Add pineapple, green pepper, onion and chicken.
Cover and simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Cook broccoli; drain.
Saute onion and shrimp in butter until tender.
Add broccoli; simmer 5 minutes.
Add cheese soup and rice.
Put mixture in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine onion, green pepper and crumbled ground beef in a plastic container and microwave on High for 6 minutes.
Drain and place in a 2-quart container.
Add tomato sauce, tomatoes, beans, salt, pepper, chili powder and dry mustard.
Cover and microwave on High for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring halfway through cooking. Standing time is 10 minutes.
Cooking time is 16 to 18 minutes. Serves 4 to 8.
Combine first 5 ingredients; set aside.
Dip chicken in salad dressing; dredge in bread crumb mixture.
Place chicken bone side down in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan coated with cooking spray. Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes or until tender.
Yields 6 servings.
Saute onion and garlic in margarine over medium heat until soft.
Add meat and brown.
Add flour, salt, pepper and mushrooms. Cook 5 minutes.
Add soup and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. Stir in sour cream.
Heat thoroughly.
Sprinkle with parsley. Serve with noodles.
Mix first 7 ingredients together, then add remaining ingredients.
Mix thoroughly, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Mix cake mix, butter, banana and egg until well blended.
Stir in chocolate or butterscotch bits.
Drop by teaspoonful on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a saucepan, combine sugar, water, cream of tartar and butter.
Bring to a boil, add cinnamon and continue to boil for approximately 4 minutes stirring constantly.
Crush the saltine crackers and put in a 9 inch unbaked pie crust.
Pour mixture from saucepan into crust and sprinkle extra cinnamon over top.
Bake for 40 minutes or until done.
Measure all ingredients except flour into a small bowl.
Beat until mixture is soft and well blended.
Add flour and mix to a stiff dough.
Measure by level tablespoonful.
Roll each measure of dough into a small ball, placed on ungreased cookie sheets.
Press down lightly with fork.
Bake in 350° oven for 10 to 15 minutes or just until very lightly browned.
Remove from oven and serve warm. Also very good reheated.

recipes.t: Fresh Peach Pie(Variations For Strawberry And Blueberry)
d: Cook sugar, water and cornstarch until thick.
Remove from stove and add peach jello.
Cool.
Add peaches and stir until coated and thickened.
Put into prebaked pie shell.
Add Cool Whip or topping.
Grease a 9 x 11-inch oblong pan with margarine.
Mix first three ingredients by hand.
Press into bottom of pan.
Cook the almonds and sugar over low heat, stirring constantly, until sugar is melted and almonds are coated.
Cool and break apart.
Store at room temperature.
Soak beans overnight.
Add all ingredients and cook very slow until tender in enough water to cover the beans.
Add any other spices to suit your taste.
Boil chicken until done.
Save broth.
Melt butter.
Mix with stuffing and seasonings.
Mix both soups with broth.
Cook mixed vegetables in separate container with grated cheese.
In greased casserole, layer dressing mix, chicken and soup.
Repeat, ending with dressing mix.
Bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Place 6 slices buttered bread, buttered side up, in large baking pan.
Place 1/2 sausage that has been cooked and drained and 1/2 cheese over bread.
Beat eggs and milk together.
Pour 1/2 of this over sausage mixture.
Place other 6 slices of bread on top, rest of sausage, cheese, milk and eggs.
Push down with hands.
Make the day before and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Top should be crusty brown.
Pour milk into ice trays and freeze until almost frozen at edges.
Put ice cold milk into cold bowl and mix with cold beaters at high speed until fluffy.
Add sugar and your favorite flavor Kool-Aid; whip until stiff.
Pour into a 9-inch pie pan that has been lined with vanilla wafers; piling high.
Freeze until firm 3 to 4 hours.
Salt and pepper tomato slices.
Dip tomato slices into beaten eggs, then into flour.
Drop into deep hot oil; let fry until golden brown.
Makes about 2 dozen.
Serve alone or with meal.

recipes.t: Ice Cream And Rice Chex Dessert
d: Brown 1 package slivered almonds in 2 tablespoons margarine. Melt 1/4 cup butter/margarine; add remaining ingredients. Put 1/2 mixture in bottom of 13 x 9-inch pan.
Add 2 quarts ice cream.
Cover with other half of Chex mixture.
Freeze.
Heat oven to 400°.
Combine ham, potatoes, margarine, salt, pepper and milk, in a large saucepan, with just enough water to cover ham and potatoes.
Cook until potatoes are done.
Add flour and water to thicken.
Add 1 cup of cheese and pimiento; stir until well-mixed.
Cook hamburger according to taco seasoning directions.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan layer the crushed chips, meat, refried beans, sour cream, cheese and finally sprinkle on the tomatoes and/or olives. Put in 350° oven until cheese is melted.
Bring to a boil and continue to boil for 5 minutes the water, sugar, cloves and cinnamon sticks.
Add tea bags and brew for 10 minutes.
Remove tea bags and add orange juice, pineapple juice and lemon juice.
Better next day after refrigerated.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Spray bottom of 9 X 13 pan. Combine pumpkin, milk, eggs, sugar, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl. Pour into pan. Sprinkle dry cake mix evenly over pumpkin mixture, top with pecans. Drizzle with melted butter over pecans. Bake 50-55 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool and serve chilled. Top with cool whip when serving.
Crumble half of cake and layer half of the ingredients in order listed.
Continue layering, beginning with last half of cake and ending with Cool Whip.
Garnish with nuts, coconut, cherries, etc.
Be sure to use punch bowl.
It makes a large quantity.
Add all ingredients together.
Simmer for 1 hour.
Salt and pepper to taste.
You can add hot sauce, if desired.
This can be frozen.
Mix water with jello; then add pie filling and pineapple.
Let jell in fridge.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, sugar and vanilla and spread over top of jello mix.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup chopped pecans on top.
Store in refrigerator.
Mix all ingredients in the order in which they are listed. Stir thoroughly.
Press into a greased loaf tin and bake in a 350° preheated oven for one hour.
Combine cracker crumbs and margarine; press into 1 1/2-quart oblong Pyrex dish.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Cream the cheese and milk.
Gradually add sugar.
Spread mix over graham cracker crust.
Sprinkle pecans over cream cheese mixture.
Whip cream with vanilla.
Spread over pecans.
Chill.
When cold, spread cherry pie filling on top.
Chill overnight.
In skillet, brown chops.
Pour off fat.
Add remaining ingredients. Cover; cook over low heat 45 minutes or until tender. Yields 4 servings.
Add salt, pepper and garlic powder to flour and cornmeal.
Coat gator strips with the mixture.
Deep fry in vegetable oil.

recipes.t: San Francisco Oyster Loaf Ala Chase
d: Cut lid off bread.
Hollow out loaf.
Clean the oysters and dredge in flour or cracker meal.
Place oysters in frying pan with the olive oil and simmer on both sides until done, approximately 6 minutes. Butter inside of loaf.
Place oysters in loaf.
Replace lid and bake in a 325° oven for 10 minutes.
Add and season with remaining ingredients to taste, especially the lemon which brings flavor to its peak. Serves 4 to 6.
Mix together syrup, sugar, cornstarch, salt and add water slowly and cook until clear.
Add Jell-O; stir until dissolved. Cool and add berries.
Pour into pie shell.
Chill, then add Cool Whip on top.
Melt butter with boiling water in a small saucepan.
Stir in flour and salt; cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture leaves sides of pan in a smooth ball.
Remove from heat and cool.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Drop mixture by heaping spoonfuls about 2 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° for 40 minutes.
Cool. Cut top off cream puffs and fill with sweetened strawberries.
Top with whipped cream.
Replace tops and garnish with whipped cream and whole strawberries.
Yields 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Layer apples in the bottom 8 by 8 inch square of baking dish.
Combine water, cinnamon and salt, sprinkle mixture over apples.
Work together the sugar, flour and butter until crumbly. Spread crumb mixture over apples.
Bake uncovered about 40 minutes.
Serve warm.
Combine potatoes, margarine and seasonings; mix well.
Place in 1-quart casserole.
Top with Marshmallow Creme.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
On a large round serving plate, place lettuce in the center. Around the lettuce, place the onions, sliced tomatoes, radishes, cucumbers, celery and carrots. Serve with a Curry Dip.
Combine pineapple with juice and soda; mix well.
In large bowl, combine cake mix and remaining ingredients.
Add pineapple mixture.
Beat at medium speed for 4 minutes.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes. Do not under bake.
Cool in pan
for 15 minutes.
Remove from pan, finish cooling on rack.
Heat oven to 400°.
Mix crumbs, oregano and garlic.
Dip eggplant slices in butter, then in crumb mixture.
Place in single layer on sprayed jelly roll pan.
Spread evenly with sauce. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook potatoes with skins on; salt lightly.
Put cold water on them to hasten cooling to handle.
Peel and cut into cubes.
Mince bacon; fry until crisp.
Combine onion, vinegar, water, sugar, salt, pepper and mustard; heat.
Add potatoes, bacon and parsley. Heat slowly and mix to flavor potatoes.
Bring large pot of water to a boil.
Add pasta; cook until tender.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
While pasta cooks, spray a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray.
Heat over medium-high heat.
Add pork.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir often. Remove from skillet.
Spray skillet again.
Add bell pepper and carrots.
Stir over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes until veggies are crisp and tender.
Stir in corn and scallions.
Mix remaining ingredients until well blended.
Stir into skillet.
Bring to a boil.
Boil 30 seconds or until thickened and clear.
Stir in pasta and pork.
Cook until heated through.
Bring pineapple (not drained) to boil.
Add jello; stir well. Let mixture cool.
Add buttermilk.
Let cool.
Let Cool Whip soften.
Stir in last.
Sprinkle top with chopped nuts.
Mix together at high speed for 5 minutes.
Peel, pit and mash avocados in medium size bowl, with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Combine sour cream, mayonnaise and taco seasoning mix in another bowl.
Mix cornstarch in cold water.
Add remaining ingredients. Cook on medium heat to desired thickness.
Yields 1 1/2 cups.
Mix flour, salt, pepper, paprika, thyme and onion.
Set aside. Melt margarine in a shallow baking pan in a 400 degree oven. Remove baking pan from oven.
Dip chicken pieces in buttermilk, then in flour mixture.
Place in buttered pan and turn to coat with butter.
Bake in 400 degree oven for 30 minutes.
Turn chicken. Bake another 30 minutes or until tender.
Beat eggs and sugar.
Soak gelatin in water, put over flame until boiling.
Add nutmeg.
Pour over sugar and eggs slowly.
Mix well.
Beat cream until stiff and add rum.
Fold in egg yolk mixture.
Pour into shell and chill.
Sprinkle with shaved chocolate.
Mix cake mix, 2 eggs and butter together.
Press into a 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Mix with beater the cream cheese, powdered sugar, 2 eggs and pecans.
Spread on cake.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Shred carrots to make 4 cups.
Stir in raisins and salt.
If your raisins are too hard, steam them for 1 minute in the microwave.
Spread even coat of olive oil on each piece of bread. Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine all above ingredients in a bowl and mix.
Spread a generous amount of topping on each piece of bread and bake in oven for 15 - 20 minutes.
In large pot, combine everything, except catsup.
Boil until water is gone.
Drain and discard grease.
Add catsup and simmer about 30 minutes.
Makes approximately 1 gallon.
Put ribs in pan, season and bake at 450° for 20 minutes. Take ribs out of pan and put sauerkraut and remaining ingredients in.
Place ribs on top of sauerkraut and bake at 350° for 1 1/2
to 2 hours.

Start the oven at 300°. Add salt to egg whites. Beat until eggs are frothy. Beat in sugar, about 2 tablespoons at a time. Add vanilla. Gently stir in coconut, corn flakes and chocolate. Drop by teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet. Bake for 20 minutes. Makes 3 1/2 dozen.
Place macaroni in microwave bowl, layering with butter and cheese.
Pour milk over mixture.
Microwave on High 3 to 4 minutes, stirring several times.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix well and spread into cake pan. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cook tortellini; drain and add spinach, cheese and ham.
Toss with dressing.
Melt chips over hot water and add remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Let dry and store in airtight container.
Make cake according to package directions. When cool, spread crushed pineapple on top of cake.
Mash potatoes, vanilla extract, sugar, margarine, eggs and orange extract together; set aside.
Cut oranges in half and remove pulp (do not use veins).
Mix into potato mixture and place in orange shell.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Remove and put marshmallows on top, place 1 cherry on top and return to oven at 350° until top is melted and lightly brown.
Combine all ingredients, except cheese, potato chips and almonds.
Place in a large rectangle dish.
Top with cheese, chips and almonds. Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Slice potatoes thin.
Line bottom of dish.
Slice onion over potatoes.
Shake Krazy salt over.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over this.
Keep adding layers to make amount you want.
Add milk to dish.
Dot generously with butter.
Cook at 325° for 1 hour.
May add peppers.
Makes it pretty as well as adds flavor.
Pour pie filling into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix all other ingredients together until well mixed.
Sprinkle over top of pie filling.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except chili powder and paprika.
Shape and roll into this.
Preheat oven to 425°.
In a 2-quart saucepan, combine the rhubarb, cornstarch, salt and 1 cup of the sugar.
Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until the mixture boils and thickens.
Pour the rhubarb mixture into the unbaked pie shell.
Bake 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350°.
Mix all ingredients. Cover and refrigerate to blend flavors about 1 hour. Serve with crackers.
Stir until cool
and
drop
on
waxed paper or put into lightly buttered dish until fully cooked.
Put butter and margarine on stove and let it melt.
Put flour in bread tray and sprinkle cinnamon over it.
Mix eggs and sugar in a bowl and stir and beat until smooth.
Then pour this into the flour.
Add melted butter and margarine.
Mix good until real stiff.
Roll out dough real thin and use a saucer to cut out the tea cakes.
Sprinkle sugar on top and cook.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large pitcher, stirring to dissolve sugar.
Add club soda just before serving.
Serve over ice.
Makes about 1 quart.
While flank steak is partially frozen, slice into 1/4 x 2-inch strips. Allow to completely thaw.
Heat oil in a large skillet until almost smoking.
Sear steak on both sides.
Add onion, garlic, tomatoes, bell pepper and herbs.
Simmer, covered, for 1 hour, adding water if liquid boils off. Add mushrooms and wine. Continue to simmer until mushrooms are cooked. Serve with white rice.
Serves 6 people.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place in layers in greased 9 or 10-inch square baking dish apples, sugar and dry cake mix.
Pour melted margarine over top of cake mix.
Bake for 35 minutes.
Let Cool Whip stand at room temperature.
Drain juice from fruit; mix pudding.
Put some of each on each layer of cake.
Save a few for top layer.
This will fill a large punch bowl and costs about $15.00.
Make cake and let cool.
Combine cake mix, fruit cocktail with syrup, 1 cup coconut and the eggs in large mixing bowl.
Blend, then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch pan and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Saute first three ingredients.
Place in 2 qt. casserole dish. Add next 3 ingredients.
Blend until mixed.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake 45-55 minutes at 350 degrees.

recipes.t: Romanian Cabbage Soup With Bacon(Ciorba Teraneasca)
d: You will
need a large soup pot.
Chop up one slice of bacon, and fry it in a heavy stewpan until the fat runs.
Fry the onions in the fat until they are golden.
Add the peppers and fry them, too.
Remove the stewpan from the heat.
Layer the cabbage and the rest of the bacon into the soup pot.
Season between the layers with salt, pepper and the herbs.
Pour the water over it all and bring to a boil.
Mix butter, parsley, onions, garlic powder and celery salt. Cut bread into 1-inch slices, cutting to bottom crust but not through.
Spread butter mixture on each slice.
Wrap in heavy-duty aluminum foil.
Heat over hot coals for about 20 minutes.
Turn often during heating.
Reserve 3 strawberries.
In blender, put in remaining strawberries, banana, milk, yogurt and honey.
Cover; blend at medium-low until thick and smooth.
Pour into chilled glasses; sprinkle with nutmeg.
Garnish with strawberry.
Soften butter.
Add remaining ingredients except confectioners sugar and mix together well.
Pour into greased pan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Sprinkle confectioners sugar on top of brownies while they are still hot.
Pour tomatoes in a large roasting pan over stove.
Cut garlic into tiny pieces and add to pan.
Add mushrooms.
Salt and pepper a whole dressed snapper.
Place in roasting pan.
Pour sauce over fish and bake at 350° for 40 to 60 minutes or until fish flakes easily.
Baste every 15 minutes with sauce.
Remove fish and thicken sauce with flour.
Add Worcestershire.
Serve over hot rice.
Spread out the nachos in a single layer on a baking sheet. Cook the onion with the meat until no pink remains, but do not brown.
Add tomato sauce and seasoning; combine well.
Place a spoonful of meat mixture on each chip and sprinkle grated cheese over all.
Place under preheated broiler for 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese has melted.
Sprinkle tomato and lettuce over all. Serve at once.
Shred these ingredients medium fine.
Mix all together and let stand 1 hour.
Make syrup for cole slaw and let cool.
Heat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients except nuts; stir just until moistened.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into greased 8 x 4-inch loaf pan.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes.
Check with toothpick.
Cool 10 minutes.
Remove from pan.
In a large nonstick Dutch oven, heat the oil on medium heat. Add chicken. Cook until lightly browned, turning once, about 8 minutes.

Transfer to a plate and keep warm. Add bell pepper, onion and jalapeo pepper to pan. Cook for 5 minutes. Stir in rice. Saut for 1 minute. Add the broth, water and tomatoes with liquid. Break up tomatoes with a spoon. Return chicken to pan.
Mix all ingredients until well blended.
Serve hot. (Hamburger or sausage may be added.)
In large bowl, mix unflavored gelatine with sugar.
Add boiling water and stir until gelatine is completely dissolved, about 5 minutes.
Stir in cranberry juice.
Chill, stirring occasionally, until mixture is consistency of unbeaten egg whites, about 45 minutes.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Mix ingredients in a large bowl.
Then serve with fresh vegetables.
Mixture is best made day before and refrigerated overnight.
Start with cold oven.
Cream butter, Crisco and sugar together.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each addition.
Add flour and milk alternately, mixing well.
Add flavoring and mix well.
Grease and flour tube pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Frost with Cream Cheese Icing.
Cream oil, sugar, milk, vanilla and egg.
Slowly add and stir in flour, salt and soda.
Stir in M&M's, but do not overstir.
Add cookie dough to baking sheet (1 tablespoon for larger cookies) and bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes or at 350° for 12 minutes.
Combine ground beef, soup mix and sour cream.
Add bread crumbs or oatmeal if too runny.
Form into loaf.
Place in skillet and cover with tomato soup.
Cover and cook on medium heat for 50 minutes or until done.

Put chicken in bottom of baking dish. Cut up boiled eggs on top of chicken. Mix can of cream of chicken and can of chicken broth. Pour over chicken. Mix flour with partly melted butter. Mix in milk and pour over chicken. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes, until golden brown.
Dissolve cherry gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in the lemonade concentrate.
Add cold water and cranberry juice cocktail.
Place 2 trays of ice cubes or a molded ice ring in a large punch bowl.
Pour punch over ice.
Pour in chilled ginger ale.
Yields 25 servings.
Brown together beef, garlic, onion and celery, then drain. Add remaining ingredients and simmer 30 to 35 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, milk, thyme and parsley.
Fill mushroom caps with cheese mixture.
Bake in oven at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix together and cook on medium heat until vegetables are tender.
Cook rice, milk and margarine in top of double boiler, stirring occasionally for 1 hour. Stir eggs, sugar, extract and a dash of salt in buttered 2-quart casserole.
Pour hot mixture into egg mixture and stir well.
Place casserole in pan of hot water in oven.
Stir coconut in after 15 minutes at 325°.
Pudding is done when knife comes out clean.
Mix gravy and broth in crockpot until smooth.
Stir in chicken, vegetables and mushrooms.
Cover and cook on low 4 hours. Stir in peas; mix sour cream and flour.
Stir into chicken. Cover and cook on high 20 minutes.
Mix Bisquick and milk until just moistened.
Drop spoonfuls onto chicken mixture.
Cover and cook on high 45 to 50 minutes until dumplings are done.
Makes 4 servings.
Make crisscross, deep vertical cuts in zucchini and slice in thick 1/4-inch slices which will yield quarters.
Sift flour and mix with fruit and nuts.
Mix sugar and butter well and add eggs and flavoring. Add fruit and nuts until mixture is smooth.
Put into a greased tube pan.
Put into a cold oven and bake at 225° for 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Beat egg whites until stiff. Put aside.
Combine sugar, syrup, water and salt in a 3-quart pan.
Bring to a boil, 252°, using a candy thermometer, if available.
If not, drop a little of the mixture into cold water.
If it forms a hard ball, it is ready. Remove from heat and begin to pour in a fine stream into stiffly beaten egg whites.
Beat on high speed with electric mixer until mixture holds its shape and loses its gloss.
Add 1 teaspoon of vanilla and walnuts.
Spoon out on waxed paper and let cool (approximately 2 hours).
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan. Cream the butter and sugar with electric mixer in large mixing bowl until light and fluffy.
Add 1 egg; beat well.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups flour and salt until well blended.
Reserve 1 cup of mixture by spooning lightly in measuring cup; set aside.
Press remaining crust mixture into prepared pan.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Boil whole head of cauliflower for about 20 minutes, or until tender.
Do not overcook.
Take it out of the water and drain it well.
Using two forks to handle it works best.
Place the cauliflower on the center of the serving plate with the stem side down.
If it does not sit straight, you may have to cut the stem some.
Mix mayonnaise and mustard in a cup, and "frost" the cauliflower with the mixture.
Remove the lid from a jar of cheese whiz and microwave it until it is hot.
Pour the cheese whiz over the cauliflower.
Sprinkle top with creole, and Voile!
Serve while hot.
Saute celery and onion in about 2 tablespoons butter in skillet on low heat.
Place bread crumbs in a shallow bowl; set aside.
Combine mayonnaise, water and lemon juice.
Stir well.
Dip fish in mayonnaise mixture.
Dredge in bread crumbs.
Place fish on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 450° for 17 to 20 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork. Yields 8 servings (197 calories and 24% fat per serving).
Mix ingredients together well. Pour into greased and floured tube pan and bake at 325 until done approximately 45-50 minutes. Cool 10 minutes. Remove from pan.
Cook rice on medium heat.
As rice begins to swell and absorb water, continue to add more water, stirring often.
Sample rice to determine when it is soft and done.
When done, fill pot full with hot water, stirring well.
Strain in colander and serve.
Cook green beans al dente.
Melt butter over medium heat; do not brown.
Add diced tomatoes and toss.
Add chicken stock and wine.
Let boil.
Add cheese and al dente green beans.
Add salt and pepper.
Toss with fettucine.

In a heavy saucepan, cook at a simmer the lentils and chicken stock.

Dissolve yeast in water.
Add the sour cream, egg, sugar, salt and 2/3 cup flour; beat until smooth.

Press over bottom and up sides to form crust. Seal perforations.
Put on sausage and potatoes; top with cheese. Beat eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Pour into crust.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over all.
Bake in a 375° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cook clams, garlic and parsley in butter.
Add remaining ingredients and cook 10 minutes on low heat.
Stir occasionally. Pour over cooked linguine noodles.

recipes.t: Easy Breakfast Casserole(Mix The Night Before And It Works Well!)
d: Crumble bread into a 9 x 13 baking dish, greased.
Crumble and sprinkle sausage over bread.
Add cheese.
Mix well eggs and milk.
Add salt, mustard (if desired) and dash of pepper.
Pour over mixture.
Add green pepper and onion (optional).
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, cream shortening, butter, sugar and lemon peel.
Add eggs and lemon juice, mixing well.
In a separate bowl, sift together 1 1/2 c. flour, baking powder and salt.
Blend into creamed mixture with milk.
Toss blueberries with 2 Tbsp. flour.
Gently fold into batter.
Pour batter into a greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3 in. loaf pan and bake for 50 to 55 minutes, testing for doneness with a toothpick.
Remove from pan and cool on a wire rack.
Yields:
1 loaf of bread.
Arrange in layers in salad bowl: lettuce, cauliflower, diced onion, Miracle Whip, Parmesan cheese, sugar and crumbled bacon. Chill for 24 hours.
Stir before serving.
Yield: 8 to 10 servings.
Unroll dough:
pat into 10 1/2 x 8-inch rectangle on baking sheet; seal seams.
Combine cheese, egg yolk and sugar; beat until smooth.
Spread on dough to 1/2 inch of edges; sprinkle with cinnamon (may add 1 or more of the optional items).
Fold in thirds lengthwise, seal edges.
Combine egg white and water, brush over top.
Bake at 350° approximately 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
You also need toothpicks to hold bacon around chestnuts.
Cook shrimp (according to directions).
Break bread into pieces, size of a quarter.
Break cheese into bite size pieces. Arrange shrimp, bread and cheese in several layers in a greased 2-quart casserole.
Pour melted margarine over.
Beat eggs.
Add mustard and salt to eggs, then milk.
Stir and pour over casserole.
Let stand at least 3 hours (or overnight, covered, in refrigerator).
Bake for 1 hour at 350°, covered.

Mix rice with soup and water in 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Sprinkle 1/2 package of onion soup mix.
Cover rice with chicken. Top with remaining onion soup mix.
Cover pan tightly with foil. Bake at 250° for 2 1/2 hours.
Grease potatoes well and bake in a 400° oven for 45 minutes or until soft.
Split lengthwise; scoop out center into mixing bowl and set shells aside.
Add butter, sour cream, salt, pepper and cheese to potatoes and mash until well mixed.
Mound into shells. Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° until lightly browned on top.
May be frozen after filling and baked for about 40 minutes when ready to use.
Combine ingredients.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350° in a 9 x 13-inch pan.

Spread on bottom of cake pan wrapped in aluminum foil.
Mix eggs and milk; dip chicken.
Place in pan; cover with corn flakes.
Put a little square of butter on top of each chicken piece.
Cover pan with foil.

Melt butter in a large skillet.
Brown livers.
Push livers to one side.
Add mushrooms; cook and stir until mushrooms are light brown.

Sprinkle with salt and Worcestershire sauce.
Reduce heat, cover tightly and simmer for 5 minutes, or until livers are done.
Serve with scrambled eggs. Makes 2 to 3 servings.
Mix and drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes or until light brown.

Add crackers and stir thoroughly.

Mix for another 30 seconds.
Sift flour, salt and baking soda together.
Slowly add flour mixture to sugar mixture, stirring slowly.
Increase speed; beat a little longer.
Add chocolate chips.

Add onion, margarine and garlic.
Place mixture in heavy pot.
Smother mixture until done. Place buns and beaten eggs in bowl until soaked, then add to eggplant mixture and add crab meat, shrimp, green onions, parsley and seasoning.
Mix well.
Place in 1 to 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.

Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.

Bring to boiling; let boil for 6 minutes, stirring all the time.
Take off heat and add cream of tartar, salt, baking soda and vanilla.
Stir until foamy and pour over popcorn.
Spread in cookie sheet after mixing well and coating corn.
Bake at 200° for 1 hour.
Boil the water, cloves and cinnamon 5 minutes.
Add tea bags for 10 minutes and remove.
Add the remaining ingredients.

Chill.

Cover and cool.
Spread angel food cake with raspberry jam and cut into small pieces.
Place 1/3 of cake into a glass bowl and sprinkle with sherry wine.

Pour into pie crust and bake at 325° to 350° for 45 minutes.

Combine all ingredients; mix well.
Cover and place in refrigerator for 1 hour before serving.

Set aside.

Blend in eggs.

Mix first 6 ingredients and place chicken on top.

Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.

Stir in raisins and nuts.

recipes.t: Portuguese Sweet Bread (Pao Doce)(Makes 5 Large Round Loaves)
d: Bring milk to a boil, dissolve yeast in warm water.
In a large bowl, sift flour, salt, and sugar.
Add butter and mix well. Add the beaten eggs, lemon extract, and yeast and mix well. Knead dough for 20 minutes, gradually adding milk as needed. Knead until no dough sticks to your hands.
Let rise in a pan until it doubles in size.
Push down, then shape into 5 round balls and place each in a greased pan.
Let rise until double in size.
Brush tops with whole beaten egg.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
In a large dutch over or stainless steel pan, brown Beef until browned on all sides.
Then pour Water over meat.
Add Onions, Mrs. Dash and Salt.
Cook on medium heat for one half hour.
Cut all vegies to bite size and add to above ingredients.
Cook one more hour on low.
Combine butter, brown sugar and molasses and beat until creamy.
Add pumpkin and egg.
Mix flour and seasonings together. Add dry mixture to pumpkin mixture and beat until smooth.
Grease muffin pans or use muffin cups.
Fill 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° approximately 15 minutes or until toothpick is clean.
Simmer first 7 ingredients 1 hour.
Add ham and heat well. Can be kept hot in crock-pot and frozen also.
Melt
margarine
in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Sprinkle crumbs in pan.
Add
each
ingredients in a layer, pouring condensed milk on last.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Dissolve 1 package of gelatin in 2 cups boiling water.
Add raspberry flavoring.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan; chill until firm.
Soften unflavored gelatin in 1/2 cup cold water.
Heat cream and sugar in pot until hot, but not boiling.
Remove from heat. Add vanilla and cream cheese; blend until smooth.
Cool.
Pour over first layer.
Chill until firm.
Dissolve remaining gelatin in 1 cup boiling water.
Stir in blueberries and flavoring.
Cool.
Pour over cream cheese layer; chill until firm.

Wrap each breast in bacon and place in pan.
Mix sour cream and soup; pour on top.
Bake at 275° for 3 hours (time and temperature may be adjusted.)
In medium saucepan, heat oil.
Saute bell pepper and onion for 2 minutes.
Lower heat and add paprika and taco seasoning.
Stir well.
Add can of beans and mash with potato masher.
Add 1/3 cup water.
Cover and simmer for 8 minutes on low heat.
Add picante sauce and serve in shallow round bowl.
Top with both cheeses and heat in microwave for 3 minutes.
Top with sour cream and serve with chips.

Toss gently.
Place in 8-inch square baking dish; set aside.

Cut in butter until mixture resembles a coarse meal.
Stir in oats and pecans.
Spoon mixture over apples.

Spoon in dessert dishes; top with ice cream.

up onions, peppers and tomatoes in bacon grease.

most

at

thickness

as
it
will
stick

Fold in raisins and oatmeal.
Drop by level tablespoons onto greased cookie sheet 1 inch apart.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Beat eggs until light.
Add brown sugar, butter and other ingredients.
Blend well.
Put in well-greased baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes; stir.
Cook 15 minutes longer.
In one bowl mix Dream Whip by package until it peaks.
Add cream cheese and mix well.
In second bowl, melt butter and pour in graham cracker crumbs.

Turn omelet and bake 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut to serving sizes and serve warm.

In a large saucepan cook beef and onion over medium high heat, stirring often to break up meat, until slightly browned, 5 to 10 minutes.

Stir in all remaining ingredients. Heat to boiling.

Add mangos and chili peppers and bring to a boil.
Cook for 20-30 minutes until mangos look clear or glassy. Gently stir mixture occasionally to avoid sticking to the bottom of the pot.

Mix well and add cheese until it is melted.
