Now crunch 1/2 bag of chips and put in bottom of a 13 x 9-inch pan, then layer 1/2 of chicken on top and then 1/2 of cheese sauce on top.
Then repeat with other 1/2 in same order.
Sprinkle top with chips and Cheddar cheese. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
On waxed paper, coat stew meat with flour; reserve leftover flour.
In a 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat, in hot salad oil, cook meat, a few pieces at a time, until well browned on all sides, removing pieces as they brown.

Add potatoes and carrot chunks.
Over medium heat, heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in frozen peas.
Cover and simmer 5 to 10 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Serve with dumplings or noodles. Makes 8 to 10 servings.

recipes.t: Sun-Maid Raisin Nut Cake(Our Family Christmas Cake Since 1936)
d: Cream butter with brown sugar.
Add molasses, beaten eggs and buttermilk, in which the soda has been dissolved.
Mix and sift the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and cloves.
Add to this dry mixture the Sun-Maid raisins (cut in pieces) and walnuts (coarsely chopped).
Combine dry ingredients with the first mixture.
Bake in 3 layers in moderate oven at 350° for about 25 minutes.
When cool, cover with your favorite icing.
I use Caramel Icing.
Cream butter and flour.
Mix egg yolks, sugar and baking powder.
Beat egg whites stiff; save to last.
Add to mixture fresh coconut (grated), red and green cherries, red and green pineapple, white raisins and nuts.
Add juice of fresh orange; add egg whites.
Bake in 275° oven for 30 minutes per pound.
Cook spinach according to package directions.
Drain well. Add cream cheese and 1/2 stick butter.
Mix well.
Melt second 1/2 stick butter.
Mix with bread crumbs.
Sprinkle mixture on top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Brown beef.
Add onion, garlic, celery and bell peppers.
Add rest of ingredients and cook for 2 hours.
Add spaghetti sauce mix.
Mix sugar, cocoa and hot water.
Bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes.
Add milk and heat almost to boiling.
Serve.

recipes.t: Beef And Cheese Foldover(One Dish Meals)
d: Brown meat and onion; drain.
Stir in barbecue sauce; set aside.
Heat oven to 375°.
Unroll crescent dough into 4 long rectangles on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Overlap long sides; firmly press perforations and edges to seal.
Pat to form 15 x 13-inch rectangle.
Spread meat mixture lengthwise in a 4-inch wide strip, down center of dough to within 1-inch of ends.
Top meat with cheese slices.
Fold shorter sides of dough 1-inch over filling.
Bring long sides of dough rectangle over filling, overlapping edges; pinch edge to seal.
Sprinkle with sesame seed. Bake at 375 ° for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Serves 6.
*To cut down calories, heavily grease pan and dust with flour. Works out well.

recipes.t: Cantaloupe Soup(The Blender At Its Best)
d: Remove seeds from cantaloupe and cube the pulp.
Place pulp and cinnamon in electric blender and puree.
Combine orange and lime juices and stir into the puree.
Chill and serve in chilled soup bowls.
Garnish with mint sprigs.
Serves 5.
Combine ginger ale, orange juice
and marshmallows and melt over low heat. Cool.
Combine juice, egg yolk, flour, sugar and butter; cook until thick.
After cool, add Cool Whip.

Add to salad.
Melt the margarine in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
In a bowl, mix well the cottage cheese, eggs, onion, broccoli and cornbread mix.
Pour in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake in oven at 375° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Place a layer of bread crumbs, asparagus and soup in casserole dish. Top with layer of bread crumbs. Dot with butter. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine chicken pieces, soups, pimentos and seasonings in saucepan.
Heat until bubbling and hot.
Line a large Pyrex casserole dish (that has been sprayed with Pam) with chow mein noodles.
Pour hot chicken/soup mixture over noodles.
Top with grated cheese.
Place in 350° oven until cheese is golden brown.
Cut tenderloin into 8 pieces; place each piece between 2 pieces of plastic wrap or waxed paper and flatten to 1/2-inch thickness.
Sprinkle with lemon pepper.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook pork for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until no longer pink and juices run clear.
Remove to a serving platter and keep warm.
Move oven rack to lowest position.
Heat oven to 450°.
Grease cookie sheet or 12-inch pizza pan.
Mix baking mix and water. Beat vigorously 20 strokes.
Turn onto floured surface.
Knead about 60 times or until no longer sticky.
Press into 13-inch circle on cookie sheet; pinch edge, forming 1/2-inch rim, or press in pizza pan.
Cook about 1/2 hour until slightly thickened.
Flavor should be "sweet and sour".
Flatten the chicken breasts with wooden mallet and season with salt and pepper.
Roll the strips of cheese in the ham slices and place in the center of the flattened breast.
Fold the edges over one another and press tightly.
Dredge them with flour and dip into beaten eggs.
Coat well with bread crumbs.
Chill until ready to fry.
Cook at 325° in deep fat for 10 minutes.
Serve.
Any desired combinations of sherbets can be used.
Combine whipped cream, sugar, cookies and nuts.
Spread about 1/3 of mixture into 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Spoon sherbet over this layer. It is easier to do if the sherbet is fairly soft.
In large bowl, mix dry ingredients.
Mix last 3 ingredients and pour over all dry ingredients.
Bake at 225° for 1 1/2 hours, stirring every 15 to 20 minutes.
In saucepan on very low heat, mix butter, heavy cream, parsley, sherry and garlic powder until smooth.
Add egg yolks. Remove from heat and pour over fettucini.
Top with Parmesan.
Prepare cake mix in a 9 x 13-inch pan by package directions, adding 1 teaspoon of flavoring and 1 package of frozen coconut. Mix together powdered sugar, milk and water.
Pour over cake immediately after taking from the oven.
Allow cake to cool. Spread with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle other package of coconut. Sprinkle with pecans.
Brown meat in small amount of oil in skillet.
Add onions and stir in chili pepper.
Transfer into crock-pot.
Stir in tomatoes and beans.
Cook on low all day.
Yummy!
Sift flour, sugar, cocoa, soda, cream of tartar and salt into mixing bowl.
Drop in shortening and add 2/3 of milk, then vanilla and beat.
Add eggs and beat.
Add the remaining 1/3 of milk and beat.
Bake at 350°.
Mix sugar, butter and egg whites; slowly add flour and sour cream.
Add beaten egg yolks.
Mix and pour into stem cake pan. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Press cracker crumbs with 1 stick melted margarine into a 9 x 12 x 2-inch pan. Set aside.
Mix all together (except eggs) and put 1/2 of mixture in bottom of casserole dish.
Slice all the eggs.
Use as the middle layer and then add the rest of mixture on top of this.
Top with a cup of crushed cornflakes and 1 stick of butter.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 35 minutes.
Cook noodles for 3 minutes and break into small pieces.
Chop or grate cabbage.
Mix drained noodles, cabbage, nuts, chicken and peas in a large bowl.
Mix flavor packages, oil, vinegar and sugar.
Pour over cabbage mixture and blend together.
Top with sunflower seeds and chill.
Makes a lot.
Rinse wheat in water until water is no longer cloudy.
Soak for 5 minutes.
Squeeze dry by cupping hands and pressing between palms of hands.
Use food processor to pulsate parsley to save time or chop fine on cutting board.
Chop onions, mint leaves and tomatoes very fine.
Place vegetables in a large bowl; add wheat, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and mix well.
Serve with fresh small grape leaves or place salad on romaine lettuce leaves used as scoops.
Serves 6.
Work flour and shortening together, then work in sugar to a crumbly mixture.
Add beaten egg yolks.
Pinch off small amounts of this dough so that when it is rolled, it is about the size of a small walnut.
After it is rolled between the hands, flatten slightly to about 3/4 of an inch thick.
Make a small indentation in the center with finger large enough to hold a small amount of tart jelly.
Brush each cookie with slightly beaten egg white and sprinkle with finely chopped nutmeats and sugar.
Put in refrigerator for about 1 hour.
Bake in slow oven (250°) for 20 minutes, then gradually increase heat to 300° and bake about 40 minutes.
Mix soups, Ro-Tel and milk; bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and pour into casserole dish.
Add crumbled tortilla chips and diced chicken; mix well.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until heated thoroughly.
Remove from oven and add grated cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes more, uncovered, or until cheese melts.
Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
Mash cranberry sauce and add lemon juice and blend.
Pour into a 1-quart refrigerator tray or 1 (9 1/2 x 5 x 3-inch) loaf pan. Soften cream cheese.
Add sugar and mayonnaise.
Mix well.
Add pecans and whipped cream.
Spoon cheese mixture over cranberries. Freeze until firm.
To serve, cut into slices and serve on lettuce.
Makes 8 servings.
Heat 1 cup of the grape juice just to boiling point.
Add the gelatin; stir until dissolved.
Remove from heat.
Add other cup of grape juice (ice cubes may be added for quick cooling).
Wash and let grapes dry.
Place grapes in the bottom of a bowl or in individual dessert glasses.
Pour thickened gelatin mixture over the grapes.
Chill until firm.
Yields 4 servings.
Melt 1 cup sugar and corn syrup.
Add milk, then add rest of sugar.
Cook on low temperature until it forms firm ball (245° on thermometer).
Add vanilla, butter and nuts.
Pour on buttered wax paper or foil.
Cut spareribs into 2-inch sections.
Place in large bowl, add remaining ingredients.
Mix with spareribs and marinate for 6 hours.
Cook in 300° oven in the marinade sauce until tender.
Add some water when needed.
Brown under broiler flame.
Garnish with sweet and sour sauce (Duck Sauce or Saucy Susan).
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix all of the
ingredients
together.
Slice rolls and remove some of the center from
the rolls to make room for the filling (save and freeze for
later
use
when
you need bread crumbs). Fill each
roll
with
approximately
tablespoons filling (more or less,
depending
on
size
of
rolls).
Wrap individually in foil and
refrigerate or freeze until ready to use.
Then place on cookie
sheet
and heat thoroughly in 300° oven until hot through (about
to 30 minutes, depending on whether or not they are frozen).
Serve with salad and dessert for a light meal. Leftovers can be reheated.
Grind together the cranberries, orange and apples.
Add the pineapple juice to the gelatin and hot water.
Mix other ingredients together and allow to set in refrigerator until solid.
Mix bean, onion and pepper together in bowl. Mix the vinegar, oil and sugar together and mix with beans. Let set overnight before serving.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Stir in remainder of ingredients. Pour in shell.
Bake in 300° oven for 55 to 60 minutes or until custard is set and knife inserted comes out clean.
Serve hot. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs one at a time and beat well. Add milk alternately with sifted dry ingredients.
Add grated rind or lemon.
Bake in loaf pan 350° for 1 hour.
Cool 5 to 10 minutes.
Mix sugar and juice of 1 lemon and pour over bread.
Let stand 1/2 hour then remove from pan.
Makes 1 loaf.
Simmer all ingredients for 15 minutes on medium.
Combine sugar, oil and vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix well.
Stir in flour, cocoa, cinnamon, baking powder and salt. Cover.
Refrigerate for 2 hours or longer.
Lightly grease baking sheet; set aside.
Place confectioners sugar in a small bowl. Shape dough in 1-inch balls.
Roll in confectioners sugar.
Place 2 inches apart on baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 11 minutes. Cool on rack.
Dissolve yeast in warm water and set aside. In a large bowl, mix flour, sugar and baking soda.
Cut in shortening.
Add buttermilk and yeast, mixing well.
Cover dough and chill 2 hours. Place dough on a floured cloth.
Roll out and cut with a biscuit cutter.
Place in pan and set aside until dough reaches room temperature. Brush with melted butter and bake at 325° for 10 to 15 minutes. Makes 36 rolls.
Mix all ingredients and pour in one 9-inch pie crust.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Dilute soup with juice from peas to make 1 can.
Layer in casserole dish.
Cover with soup.
Top with salt and pepper, butter and cheese.
Sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix together and serve over or with fruit.
Mix dry ingredients together.
Add eggs, butter and vanilla. Cook over medium heat until thick, stirring often.
Pour into pie shells.
Top with whipped cream.
Place 9 bread slices in a single layer on bottom of slightly greased 13 x 9 pan.
Top with cream cheese slices.
Place remaining bread slices on top.
Whisk together eggs, milk, syrup and cinnamon.
Pour over bread.
Cover and chill 8 hours.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Lightly cover with foil after 20 minutes.
Mix all except nuts in large bowl.
Beat well.
Add pecans and stir.
Bake 50 or 60 minutes at 350°.
Brown and drain meat. Add all other ingredients and simmer for 1 1/2 hours. Serve over fritos with sour cream and grated cheese.
Combine first 9 ingredients.
Coat fillets with cooking spray; dredge in breadcrumb mixture.
Place fillets on a broiler pan coated with cooking spray; bake, uncovered, at 400° for 20 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Serve immediately.
Yields 4 servings.
Pat rounded teaspoonful of filling on crackers.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Broil under broiler until bubbly and lightly brown. Serve at once.
Grease a cookie sheet.
Beat egg whites, vanilla and salt until soft peaks form.
Gradually add sugar, beating until stiff peaks form.
Fold in coconut.
Drop from a teaspoon 1 1/2 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake in 325° oven for about 20 minutes.
Cool on a wire rack.
Makes about 20 to 24.
Cook noodles in
boiling,
unsalted water until tender. Drain. In a large bowl
stir together the soup, milk and sour cream. Add celery,
mushrooms, pimiento and parsley.
Stir in cooked noodles
and ham;
turn
into
a
quart
casserole. Combine cracker crumbs and melted butter and sprinkle over the casserole. Bake, uncovered, for 30 to 35 minutes at 375°.
Mix all ingredients in bowl.
Brown pork chops in shortening; remove from skillet and season.
Pour off some of the drippings.
Add rice, green pepper, onions, chicken broth and thyme; stir.
Place pork chops on top. Cover and cook in frypan at 275° for 30 minutes or pour into a 3-quart casserole and bake 1 hour at 325°.
Serves 6.
Mix
sugar and flour in saucepan.
Pour in water.
Stir to thicken over medium heat.
Should be like gravy consistency.
Stir in vinegar or lemon juice to your own taste.
Serve hot over your favorite white or yellow cake.
Cook broiler, water and salt until tender; cool.
Remove skin and bones.
Chop.
Add rest of ingredients.
Mix all together and store in refrigerator.

With electric mixer, cream butter and sugars. Beat in egg and extracts. Sift together the flour, soda, baking powder and salt. Gradually add to mixture. Stir in pecans. Roll into 1-inch balls. Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 9 to 11 minutes or until set. Cool for 3 minutes on cookie sheet before removing to rack. Makes about 6 dozen.
Mix the first 6 ingredients together.
Dip chicken pieces in butter, then in crumb mixture.
Place chicken in foil-lined roasting pan (use a rack if you have one).
Dot chicken with extra butter.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until brown.
Serves 6 to 8.

Cover potatoes and onion with water. Cook 5 minutes. Add pimento and cook 1 minute more. Drain and set aside. Melt margarine. Add flour, cheese, salt and milk. Stir until smooth. Add potatoes to this cheese sauce, then pour into a casserole dish. Top with buttered bread crumbs. Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Blend onion sauteed in margarine with soups and tomatoes as it heats.
Add deboned chicken (cut into chunks) and Fritos.
Stir until mixture is blended with chips.
Pour in baking dish and top with cheese.
Heat 20 minutes at 350° or until cheese bubbles. Freezes well, omitting cheese.

recipes.t: Lois Ann Beason'S Chicken Breasts In Sour Cream
d: Arrange chicken breasts in a shallow baking dish.
Sprinkle with salt and coarse grind pepper.
Cover with mushrooms.
Combine undiluted soup, sherry and sour cream.
Stir until blended.
Pour over chicken, completely covering it.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours or until done.
Clean chicken cutlets the day before and season with salt, pepper and garlic so that the chicken will soak up the seasonings. The following day, crush the potato chips and place them in a bowl.
Beat the eggs in another bowl.
Dip the chicken cutlets in eggs and then in the potato chip crumbs until they are fully covered.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes, then check with a fork to see if done inside.
If not, let cook a little longer.
While chicken is baking, cook spaghetti according to directions on package.
Heat spaghetti sauce.
Combine sauce and spaghetti and serve with chicken cutlets.
Mix until crumbly the powdered sugar and peanut butter.
Put in bottom of baked pie shell, saving 2/3 tablespoon of mixture for top of pie.
Combine cornstarch, sugar, milk, salt, egg yolks, butter and vanilla.
Cook until thick.
Cool some.
Pour on top of crumbly mixture in pie shell.
Beat egg whites with sugar for meringue. Cover top of pie.
Sprinkle reserved crumbly mixture on meringue and brown in oven at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Combine pancake mix and salt; stir in club soda until smooth. Separate onions into rings.
Dip a few rings into batter to coat. Drain off excess.
Heat oil to 375°.
Fry onion rings, a few at a time, 2 to 3 minutes, turning once.
Drain.
Season with salt.
Mix all ingredients together and cook.
Makes 6 round waffles. Can be frozen.
Combine oil, eggs, sugar and vanilla.
Combine all dry ingredients and add to sugar mixture.
Add apples and chopped nuts.
Bake in 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 40 minutes.
Top with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Dressing:
Make the night before.
Combine oil, sugar, vinegar and beef packet from Ramen noodles.
Combine pudding mix and milk.
Beat until well blended, 1 to 2 minutes.
Chill for 5 minutes.
Fold in remaining ingredients. Spoon into dessert cups.
Chill.
Serves 6.
In a 30 cup percolator basket, place sugars, tea and sticks. In the bottom of percolator, put juices and water.
Perk and enjoy.
In small bowl, combine corn, milk, onion, green pepper, salt and pepper.
Put 1/2 of corn mixture into quart casserole dish. Layer half the cheese and half the bread crumbs.
Layer remaining corn and cheese.
Mix remaining crumbs with melted butter and cover corn and cheese with crumb mixture.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Marinate chicken pieces in sugar and soy sauce.
Beat eggs with a little milk, dip chicken in milk and roll in cornstarch. Fry in oil over low heat.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Place a little water in a pan and place first batch of fried chicken in it. Sprinkle cashews and chopped green onions over chicken.
Place in oven to keep warm as chicken fries.
Continue layering in this manner.
Mix lemon Jell-O, crushed pineapple, bananas and marshmallows. Let stand until firm. Cook sugar, pineapple juice, flour and egg until thick and cool.
Spread over Jell-O mix. Mix Dream Whip and spread.
Melt margarine in skillet over medium heat.
Beat eggs.
Add cheese torn in pieces.
Add milk, salt and pepper.
Mix well. Pour into skillet and cook until soft done.
Drop on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Frost with orange icing.
Place string beans in boiling salt water.
Cook 7 to 8 minutes.
Add drained mushrooms 3 minutes before the end of cooking time, just long enough to heat them through.
Drain beans and mushrooms.
Season with additional salt and pepper and a lump of butter, if desired.
Thaw potatoes for 45 minutes.
Combine melted butter with 2 cups crushed cornflakes; set aside half of them for topping. Combine all ingredients and pour into greased 3-quart baking dish. Top with buttered cornflakes.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mix all ingredients
together.
Place in casserole dish and cover with grated cheese
and
potato chips.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Boil raisins in the water for 5 minutes; let cool.
Cream the sugar and shortening.
Add eggs.
Add dry ingredients to flour, then add to creamed mixture.
Add raisins, nuts and vanilla.
Put in refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet. Bake 10 to 15 minutes at 350°.
Spray 9-inch round pan with Pam.
Open biscuit tube.
Place biscuits in 9-inch round pan.
Sprinkle grated cheese and bacon bits on biscuit dough.
Place in oven and bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Fry bacon and pour off fat.
Add onion and brown.
Add to mixture of beans.
Mix syrup, catsup and mustard together.
Add to beans. Bake for 2 hours at 325°.
Wonderful!
Brown beef and drain.
Add taco seasoning, tomato paste, one can of water (use tomato paste can) and corn.
Put in casserole dish and cover with cheese.
Prepare cornbread according to directions and pour on top.
Bake according to box directions.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add the rest of ingredients and simmer for 2 hours.
Peel eggplant and slice into 1/4-inch slices.
Soak in water and then dredge in flour.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Combine 2 eggs and milk; whip.
Dip eggplant into egg and milk mixture and into crumbs.
Place oil into skillet, heat oil.
Fry eggplant on both sides.
Place in casserole.
Coat chicken legs with dressing and bread crumbs.
Arrange chicken on round microwave-safe plate, spoke fashion with meaty portion towards outer edge of plate.
Combine all ingredients except nuts and preserves.
Mix well and chill.
Mold into ring.
Cover with chopped nuts.
Fill center with strawberry preserves.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Put 1/2 of potatoes in greased baking dish.
Combine salt, pepper and flour; sprinkle part of this over potatoes.
Dot with butter.
Repeat this procedure.
Measure soup and add enough milk to make 2 cups.
Pour over potatoes.
Cover; bake for 30 minutes. Remove cover and bake until done.
Cheese may be added the last 15 minutes of baking.
Broil lamb chops 4 inches from coals about 8 minutes on each side, basting with mixture of other ingredients.
Combine all ingredients and roll into walnut-size balls.
Roll into smaller balls if used as cocktail meatballs. Bake on cookie sheet with sides at 450°.
No need to turn balls.
Boil and mash sweet potatoes.
Blend in well beaten egg yolks, melted butter, salt and milk. Fold in well beaten egg whites. Butter a ring mold or Bundt pan. Place nut halves around in bottom of pan and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Cover with sweet potato mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Turn upside-down in large plate. Let stand 5 minutes, then remove pan.
Fill ring with buttered green peas or green limas.
Mix cream cheese, green chilies, black olives and picante sauce.
Smooth mixture on tortilla.
Roll up tortilla and secure with toothpick.
Refrigerate.
Cut into 1-inch pieces.
Serve with picante sauce.
(Great for parties!)
Peel eggplants; cut into 1/2 inch slices.
Dip in egg and dredge in matzoh meal.
Place in a single layer on lightly greased baking sheets.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Turn eggplant slices and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Layer 1/3 of eggplant slices in a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with 1/3 each of Mozzarella cheese and spaghetti sauce; repeat layers twice. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and bake, uncovered, at 325° for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Yields 8 servings.
Mix together flour, baking powder, sugar and butter with a fork to make coarse crumbs.
Set aside 1 cup of crumbs.
In a separate bowl, mix well the eggs, milk and vanilla.
Mix in dry crumbs with a fork.
Pour into a greased 12 x 18-inch pan.
Top with cherries (pie filling), then the reserved cup of crumbs. Sprinkle with cinnamon, brown sugar and walnuts.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Pour on syrup and bake 10 minutes more.
Mix all together and bake in loaf pan for 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Mix beef, onion, bread crumbs, egg, salt, pepper and 1/2 cup ketchup until well blended.
Make into loaf; mix and pour remaining ingredients on top of loaf.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Mix meal and flour in bowl. Add buttermilk and mix thoroughly.
Add beaten egg, onion and yeast mixture.
Mix good and drop by teaspoon into hot fat.
Cook until golden brown.
Serve hot with fish and French fries.
Let cheeses stand at room temperature until softened.
Place in mixer bowl with Worcestershire sauce.
Beat on medium until well mixed.
Roll mixture into a ball; roll in chopped nuts and then chill.
Steam cabbage and saute in margarine.
Melt cheese and milk; pour over cabbage.
Place bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Mix apples, sugar and raisins.
Let stand 1 hour.
Stir often. Sift flour, nutmeg, cinnamon, salt and soda together.
Add dry ingredients to apple mixture.
Mix by hand.
Then add vegetable oil, vanilla and egg whites.
Mix by hand.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes. May be served plain, with Cool Whip or frosted as desired.
I never had a failure with this recipe.
I have used many variations including chocolate chips.
It stays moist and freezes well.
Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with Keebler Club crackers.
Melt oleo in pan.
Add sugars, milk and graham crackers. Boil at least 5 minutes.
Spread over Club crackers.
Spread another layer of Club crackers over this.

Beat shortening at medium speed with electric mixer until fluffy. Add sugars, beating well. Add eggs, beat until blended. Combine flour and next four ingredients; gradually add to sugar mixture, beat after each addition. Stir in coconut, cereal, vanilla, and pecans. Drop by tablespoons onto baking sheets. Bake at 350° 10 minutes or until golden. Yields 4 1/2 dozen.
Combine all ingredients and pour into greased 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle top with sugar, cinnamon and chopped nuts. Bake in 350° oven for time recommended on cake mix instructions.

The night before serving, bake cake in a 13 x 9 inch baking pan according to package directions. Cool; cut into 1 inch cubes. Pour pudding mix into a bowl, add milk and Kahlua; mix well. Leave Heath bars in wrappers and pound with a hammer to crush.
In a very large glass bowl or a trifle bowl, layer, in order:
half of cake cubes, half of pudding mixture, half of whipped topping and half of Heath bars.
Repeat layers.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Makes 12 to 14 servings.
First, tear cake up in small pieces in a 9 x 13-inch pan. Spread out.
Blend a little hot sauce with the mustard.
Add the mustard mixture and cheese to the remaining hot sauce; stir over low heat until cheese melts.
Add and stir in the tarragon.
Good on cauliflower, asparagus and green beans.
Yield:
1 1/2 cups.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large mixer bowl, on low speed, combine cake mix, 1 egg, margarine and 2 teaspoons spice until crumbly.
Press onto bottom of 15 x 10-inch jelly roll pan.
In large mixer bowl, beat cream cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in Eagle Brand, 2 eggs, pumpkin, 2 teaspoons spice and salt; mix well.
Pour over crust.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until set.
Cool.
Chill; cut into bars.
Store in refrigerator.
Makes 48 bars.
Place sliced sweet potatoes in a greased baking dish.
Combine the next 5 ingredients.
Drain apricots, saving 1 cup juice. Combine sugar mixture and juice; cook on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Arrange apricot halves on the potatoes and pour sauce over all.
Place a pecan half in the center of each apricot half. Drizzle the 2 tablespoons melted butter or oleo on top.
Bake 25 minutes at 375°.
Mix the first 4 ingredients in pan and bring to a boil.
Boil for 1 1/2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Add oatmeal and vanilla. Drop by teaspoons on waxed paper.
Let set until firm.
Mix together. Pour into pie shell. Bake 350°for 45 minutes.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add egg and sift dry ingredients together.
Add remaining ingredients with dry mixture to sugar and eggs.
Pour into a greased 5 x 9-inch loaf pan.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Cook cake according to directions on box.
Cool cake completely.
Punch holes (with knife, etc.) in cake and pour Eagle Brand milk and creme de coconut over cake.
Put Cool Whip and coconut on top of cake.
Combine gelatin, sugar and water in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve sugar and gelatin.
Remove from heat and stir in strained apricots.
Set aside to cool.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Add tomato paste, garlic powder, oregano and water.
Mix until smooth.
Then add eggs; mix well. Add cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Mix first 6 ingredients and put into 9 x 13-inch dish.
Bake, covered, 20 minutes at 350°.
Melt margarine with Cheez-Its and spread on top.
Bake uncovered 15 minutes more.
In saucepan bring water and salt to a boil, add macaroni and cook until tender.
Drain and set aside.
Melt butter over moderate heat in small saucepan.
Add flour and cook, stirring until the mixture froths and foams.
Add the milk all at once and stir until thickened.
Pour sauce into a large mixing bowl and stir in macaroni, diced ham and 1 1/2 cups of the cheese.
Pour into prepared casserole dish. Top with bread crumbs, remaining cheese and melted butter.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, peppers, pineapple, onion and salt.
Roll into a ball and roll in chopped pecans.
Garnish with peppers or cherries.
(If you wish to freeze, cover with plastic wrap.) Uncover to thaw on rack so it will not get soggy.
Serve on any kind of crackers.
Brown beef in skillet with salt, pepper and onion powder.
Be sure to remove excess fat.
Put cooked beef in a casserole dish. Next, layer sliced potatoes (peeled or not, thin to medium slices), then layer with veggie of your choice.
Top with cream of whatever soup and about 1/2 cup water.
Bake in conventional oven until potatoes are soft (about 1 hour) or microwave until potatoes are done (15 minutes).
Serve with dinner rolls.
Crush chips in bag.
Toss together all ingredients, except tortilla chips.
Refrigerate.
Before serving, mix in chips and enough dressing to wet.
Heat oven to 350°.
Cream shortening, sour cream, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Spoon cookies onto sheet.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar.
Bake 8 minutes.
Mix peaches and sugar thoroughly.
Set aside 10 minutes.
Stir Sure-Jell with water in saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir mixtures together until sugar is completely dissolved and no longer grainy, about 3 minutes.
Pour into plastic containers; cover.
Let stand at room temperature 24 hours.
Jam is now ready to use.
Store in refrigerator or freeze extra containers.
Thaw in refrigerator.
In a medium saucepan, combine carrot, celery and onion; add chicken broth.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until vegetables are done.
Cook macaroni; drain.

Cook celery in chicken broth or a chicken flavored bouillon cube, plus 3/4 cup water, for 5 minutes. Combine cooked macaroni, celery, broth, celery soup, mushrooms, chicken or turkey, parsley and Worcestershire sauce.
Add salt if needed.
Pour into greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with bread cubes; dot with butter.
Bake in moderate oven at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 8.
Combine all in 1 1/2-quart casserole. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Brown stew meat in skillet.
Combine meat and all other ingredients in a greased 3-quart casserole dish.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours, until vegetables are tender and meat is done.
Combine all ingredients with wire whip or in your blender. This is much cheaper than buying condensed milk.
Store in refrigerator.
Yields 1 1/3 cups or the same as one can of condensed milk.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In 13 x 9-inch baking pan, arrange chicken.
In small bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Brush on chicken.
Bake uncovered 45 minutes or until chicken is done. Makes about 4 servings.
Melt butter in 3-quart saucepan.
Add herbs and celery. Season.
Simmer gently for five minutes.
Add meat; stir well. Add gravy and stir.
Cook for five minutes.
Put in casserole.
Bake at 275° for 5 hours.

In large stockpot, heat chicken stock (reference other recipe). Sweat onion, celery and carrots. Cut into 1-inch cubes. Add sweated vegetables to chicken stock. Return cooked chicken pieces to the soup. Heat to boiling. Reduce heat to simmer. Add noodles (or rice) and cook until tender. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Mix as usual.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Cook potatoes until almost done. Add ham and flour.
Then add grated or chopped boiled eggs.
Salt and pepper to taste. Add water so that it has a good consistency.
Brown and drain hamburger.
Stir in tomato paste, onion and seasonings.
Mixture will be thick.
Cook over low heat 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Place biscuits in a greased muffin tin, pressing to cover bottom and sides.
Spoon about 1/4 cup meat mixture into biscuit lined cups and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 400° for 12 minutes or until golden brown.
Combine cream cheese and milk.
Add remaining ingredients. Blend well.
Spoon into ovenproof dish.
Sprinkle with toasted sliced almonds.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Serve piping hot with crackers or rye bread.
Mix all ingredients, but the fish.
Marinate fish for a couple of hours in this mixture.
Place fish in grill basket 4 to 6 minutes per side, basting once.
Mix together 1 cup brown sugar, 1 cup flour and 6 tablespoons margarine to a crumb texture.
Set aside.
Cream together 1/2 cup margarine and 1 1/2 cups light brown sugar.
Add egg.
Beat.
Add buttermilk and vanilla.
Beat.
Add 2 cups flour and soda.
Beat. Pour in greased and floured pan; top with the reserved crumbs. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until center springs back to touch.
Mix ingredients and drop on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool on rack.
Cream the shortening, margarine and vanilla. Add milk and sugar alternately. Blend until smooth.
Dissolve yeast in warm water. Add all other ingredients except flour. Add 1 cup flour. Mix well. Add remaining flour. Put in warm place and allow to rise 1 hour.
Stir down and place in buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole. Let rise 40 minutes. Bake 40 minutes at 350°. While warm, brush with melted butter and salt.
Spread mustard on both sides of chicken; sprinkle with pepper. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 4 hours.
Melt butter; stir in lemon juice, garlic salt and tarragon.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place chicken on grill.
Baste with sauce.
Grill 50 to 55 minutes, until done, turning and basting every 10 minutes.
Yields 4 servings.
Bring chicken to a boil and cook until done.
Add chicken base (amount depends on how much you need to enrich the stock).
Bring to a boil and taste.
Add noodles and let them cook until almost done.
Add corn and cook until done.
Eggs can be large diced and added at the end for a garnish.
Enjoy!
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine cake mix, eggs and margarine.
Spread in pan; bake 20 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Pour applesauce over cake.
Combine oats and brown sugar until crumbly.
Sprinkle over applesauce.
Return to oven; bake 20 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool.
Cut into squares.
Mix all together and pour into a large pan or oblong 14 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish or 2 small ones.
Cook spaghetti; while warm, cut in cheese.
Chop onion fine, celery and pepper, pimento and tomato; add to spaghetti, then seasoning to taste.
Cream together 1 cup sugar and shortening. Add eggs, one at a time, and beat well.
Combine 2 cups flour, soda and salt. Combine buttermilk and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk mixture.
Combine pecans and 1 tablespoon flour.
Stir pecans and apples into mixture.
Pour into greased and floured 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Combine 1 1/2 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle over batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook cabbage for 15 minutes; drain well.
Combine flour and sugar and add to tomatoes with remainder of ingredients.
Bring to boil and stir slightly.
Place in casserole in alternate layers (tomatoes last).
Bake in 375° oven until bubbling, about 30 minutes.
Set oven low, 250°.
Pare, quarter and core the apples. Combine the sugar and cinnamon.
Put a layer of apples in the bottom of a bean pot; sprinkle a little of sugar mixture over them.
Continue layering apple quarters and sugar mixture.
Pour enough cider over the apples to cover them completely.
Cover bean pot.
Place pot in oven and bake 2 to 3 hours or until apples are tender.
Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Blend oleo, brown sugar, sugar and pudding. Add eggs and vanilla flavoring; mix well. Add flour and baking soda; blend well. Add chocolate chips. Bake at 350° about 10 minutes.
Mix Dream Whip as per instructions on box.
Add instant vanilla pudding and peanut butter.
Place in pie shell and sprinkle with chopped nuts or chocolate chips.
Refrigerate.
In blender, puree berries, granulated sugar and 2 tablespoons liqueur; reserve 3/4 cup. Pour remainder into pie plate.

In a 1-quart microwave dish, combine apple, carrots, brown sugar, margarine and water. Cover tightly. Microwave on 100% power (High) 7 to 8 minutes or until carrots are tender, stirring several times during cooking. Let stand 2 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Blend first 6 ingredients in top of double boiler.
Cook over rapidly boiling water, beating until mixture stands in peaks. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and beat until thick enough to spread.
Mix Jell-O, hot water and Pet milk until Jell-O is dissolved. Add other ingredients and put in bowl or pan. Let set. Mix after it has partially set.

Saute mushrooms in butter until tender. Add flour and stir until smooth. Add milk and seasonings. Cook until thickened, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Blend half of sauce with the chicken and the other half with the cooked spaghetti. Bank spaghetti on bottom and around edges of shallow greased baking dish. Pour chicken mixture into center. Sprinkle with cheese. Brown under broiler or in hot oven. Makes 4-6 servings.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Shape into 18 meat balls. In saucepan, brown meat balls; cook over low heat for 5 minutes. Pour off fat.
Stir in soup and water.
Heat; stir now and then. Makes about 3 1/2 cups.
Peel and mash potatoes. While potatoes are still hot, add other ingredients. Pour into unbaked pie shell and bake at 350° until set and browned.
Recipe can be doubled for 2 pies.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift dry ingredients (except sugar). Work butter into flour mixture.
Add sugar, mix in.
Put yolks into sour cream and beat well.
Mix into flour mixture.
Knead dough until smooth.
Roll 2/3 dough on floured surface.
Put into cookie sheet (one with 3/4 to 1 inch edge works best).
Spread with pie filling.
Roll rest for top crust.
Cut for lattice top. Brush crust with egg whites. Bake in oven till golden.
Chop cucumbers, onions and pepper.
Drain all the juice that you can, then sprinkle turmeric over all this.
Set aside 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix vinegar, sugar, celery and mustard seed.
Cook until boiling, then pour over cucumber mixture.
Cook 1 hour.
Put in jars and seal.
Cook on high until starts to boil, then turn down to 3, stirring every now and then.
Remove stems from mushrooms.
Finely chop 1/4 cup stems. Cook and stir chopped stems, onion and pepper in margarine in skillet over medium heat until tender.
Remove from heat; stir in crumbs and basil.
Spoon crumb mixture loosely into mushroom caps; place on baking sheet.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes or until hot.
Cream shortening and sugar together until creamy.
Add egg and beat well.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with sour cream.
Add nuts and flavoring.
Drop by teaspoons on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 40 cookies.
Combine pancake mix, corn meal and salt; mix well.
Add milk and mix well.
Dip each frankfurter in batter; coat well.
Fry in fat heated to 365° until golden brown.
Turn to brown evenly. Serve immediately.
If desired, insert popsicle sticks.
Makes 10.
Fill a 9 x 13-inch cake pan with bread slices. Layer sausage and cheese over bread.
Beat eggs and add milk.
Pour over bread, sausage and cheese.
Let set in refrigerator overnight. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Good for a ready breakfast for company or Christmas morning.
In 1-quart casserole dish stir in all ingredients except chow mein noodles.
To bake:
Bake, uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle chow mein noodles on top, bake another 5 to 8 minutes and serve.
Mix Raisin Bran, sugar, flour and soda in a large bowl.
Add mixture of eggs, buttermilk and oil; mix well.
Store in covered container in refrigerator and use as desired.
Fill muffin tins 2/3 full and bake for 15 minutes at 400°.
Beat egg lightly in bowl with a whisk.
Add the flour, half the milk, salt and pepper.
Stir in remaining milk.
Let batter stand for an hour.
Coarsely grate the cheese and stir half of it into the batter.
Grease an 8-inch Pyrex pie plate; pour the batter into it and bake in a preheated 425° oven for 30 minutes or until puffed and brown.
Scatter remaining cheese on top and bake just until it is melted.
Cut into 24 narrow wedges.
Mix well oleo, 1/3 cup cocoa, eggs, sugar and flour.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cook 30 minutes or until done.
While hot, spread with marshmallow cream.
Ice with the following immediately:
confectioners sugar, margarine, vanilla, cocoa and Pet milk.
Sprinkle nuts on top.
Mix butter and sugar.
Add all other ingredients.
Pour into a greased Bundt pan.
Bake at 325° to 350° for 1 hour.
Dissolve sugar in water.
Add the Kool-Aid mix, pineapple juice and ginger ale. Chill and serve over ice.
Mix dry cake mix, softened butter and 3 eggs until moist. Pour into greased and floured cake pan.
Chop celery and onions fine; simmer in butter until soft. Beat eggs.
Mix all ingredients together.
Salt and pepper to suit taste.
(Mash potatoes with milk.)
Heat on stove top, stirring constantly, until desired consistency or bake at 300° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Brown roast in small amount of oil over high heat.
Place roast in Dutch oven over low heat.
Mix remaining ingredients together.
Pile sour cream mixture on top of roast.
Simmer slowly 2 1/2 to 3 hours, basting frequently with gravy.
In a large mixing bowl, beat sugar, butter (must be very soft but not melted), eggs and almond extract on low just until mixed. Beat on high speed for 5 minutes, scraping bowl occasionally.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder and salt.
On low speed, add flour mixture alternately with milk, mixing just until blended.
Fold in chocolate chips.

Carefully pour batter over pecans.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 40 minutes or until cake tests done. Cool 20 minutes in pan before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

Cut into halves and place in bowl.

Drain and add to artichokes.
Pour sour cream into skillet with butter and blend well.
Add Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper to taste.
Add parsley.
Pour over artichokes and mushrooms.
Top with bread crumbs and bake in a 350° oven for 1/2 hour or until bubbly.
Beat well and bake in 3 well floured cake pans at 350° until done.
In skillet, cook sausage and onion until meat is browned. Drain off fat.
Stir in tomato sauce, basil, oregano and salt. Cover and simmer about 10 minutes. Spread desired pizza crusts with meat mixture. Top with shredded cheese.
Bake as directed in crust recipe. Sprinkle with 1/3 cup snipped parsley, if desired.

Set aside.

Add artichokes and pour into pie shell.
Cover top with the other pie shell and bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Mix well and turn into greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut beans into 1-inch pieces.
Cook for 20 to 30 minutes on medium-high in salted water.
In frying pan, saute onion, celery, pepper and garlic in butter until tender.
Drain beans.
In large bowl, add beans, other vegetables and basil and stir.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix together soup, flour, milk and onion.
Pour over potatoes and cabbage.
Place browned pork chops on top and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Combine onions, parsley, vinegar, oil, mustard, garlic and thyme.
Place beef chuck shoulder steak in plastic bag.
Add marinade, spreading evenly over both sides.
Close bag securely and marinate in refrigerator for 6 to 8 hours, turning at least once.
Pour off marinade.
Discard.
Place steak on rack in broiler pan so surface of meat is 3 to 4-inches from heat.
Broil 18 minutes to desired doneness, turning once.
Carve into thin slices to serve.

Stuff mushroom caps with shrimp mixture.

Separately combine sugar, cornstarch and salt. Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Gradually add to chocolate mixture. Stir in coconut and pecans.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Cool for several hours.
Strain broth in which chicken was stewed.
Measure 1 quart broth into a saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Combine flour and water; stir in some of the hot broth.
Cook until thickened, 15 to 20 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Put all ingredients except hot dogs in skillet; bring to a boil.
Add hot dogs and simmer for 10 minutes.

Place chicken breast in 9x13 inch pan, sprayed with Pam.
Slice potatoes 3/8 inch thick and place in pan.
Place sliced onion rings on chicken.
Sprinkle liberally with Tony Chachere's.
Pour Italian dressing over all. Cover with foil and bake at 475 degrees for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Brown ground beef and
onion.
Add tomato soup, water, seasoning, corn and green pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Cut up dates.

Cook over low heat until it boils.
Add pecans.
Cool.
Bake potatoes.

Cut baked potatoes in half, lengthwise.
Remove the potato from the skin, leaving skin whole.

Using a spoon, put potato mixture back in skin, leaving a hollow place in center.

Top with remaining cheese.
Heat in oven or microwave just long enough to melt cheese on top.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour and baking powder.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with coconut milk and vanilla.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans and bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool cake completely and split cake layers.
Spread Sour Cream Coconut Filling between layers and on top of cake.
Cook rice according to directions.
Cook peas until heated through; stir together.
Add handful of bacon bits and serve warm.

corn
syrup,
sugar
and
water until hard crackle stage.
Remove
from
fire,
add
salt and vanilla (if nuts are unsalted
add
1 1/2 teaspoons salt).

Pour on greased cookie sheet and press thin as possible, with 2 greased spoons.
Cool
and
break into small pieces.

Mix together the chicken, onion, salt, pepper, milk, cream cheese, margarine and croutons.
Flatten each triangle; fill with chicken mixture.
Wrap crescent roll around filling.
Bake on cookie sheet for 20 minutes.
Melt butter in heavy pan over low heat.
Add onion and cook until tender, stirring occasionally.
Add flour and stir.
Whisk in clam juice.
Increase heat and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Add half and half and return to a boil, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Add 3/4 pound of crab meat, wine and seasoning.
Simmer about 3 minutes.
Brown beef and garlic in oil.
Add, then cover and simmer 20 minutes the tomato paste, tomatoes, salt, pepper and oregano. Cook noodles according to directions on package.
In an 11 x 7-inch dish, alternate layers of noodles, meat sauce, 12 ounces cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese.
End with Mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Blend all and pour over raw spareribs.
Let sit for awhile. Cook on barbecue over medium heat.
One small head fresh broccoli (about 1/2 pound) may be substituted for frozen spears.
Divide into spears and cook 3 to 4 minutes before using.

Put sugar, salt and corn syrup into a large pan; bring to a boil and boil to firm ball stage, 245°, stirring occasionally. Gradually add milk and butter slowly, so that the mixture does not stop boiling at any time.
Continue to cook rapidly, stirring constantly to medium ball stage, 242°.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and nuts.
Stir well.
Scrub and trim zucchini.
Grate them by hand or in a processor; toss in a bowl with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and let sit 20 minutes.
Squeeze out moisture.
Beat egg whites in small mixer bowl on high speed until stiff. Beat egg yolks on high speed for 1 minute.
Add corn, salt, pepper and flour.
Beat on low speed until blended.
Add beaten whites; fold in on lowest speed.
Add oil in frypan.
When hot, drop the batter by spoonfuls.
Fry both sides until brown.
Serve hot with syrup.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour pan(s).
Cream butter, sugar and eggs using a mixer.
Add remaining ingredients and mix on low until blended.
Turn into pan(s) and bake until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, about 1 hour.
Cool 10 minutes.
Makes one 9 x 5-inch loaf or two 5 5/8 x 3 1/8-inch loaves.
Combine corn meal, flour, milk, eggs, salt, soda, corn and jalapeno peppers in a bowl; mix and set aside.
Saute ground beef, onion and bell pepper until lightly browned; drain thoroughly and set aside.
Thoroughly grease a 10 1/2-inch iron skillet.
Pour half of corn meal batter into skillet.
Sprinkle evenly with beef mixture, then cheese.
Pour remaining batter over top.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until golden brown.

Gently stir in drained fruits.
Pour into a 9-inch square pan.

Cut into squares to serve. Store in freezer.
Mix all together.
Cook in crock-pot for 8 hours with lid off.

Add spinach, Cheddar cheese, mushrooms, salt and nutmeg.
Cover and chill overnight.
(If you wish, you can bake and serve the same day.) Next day, spoon into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° until set, about 45 minutes.
Brown and drain off grease.
Add oleo, onion, pepper, mushroom and tomato soups.
Simmer 45 minutes and stir often.
Boil, bone and cut chicken into pieces.
Saute onion and bell pepper in oleo.
Heat soups, chili seasoning, Ro-Tel tomatoes and chicken broth.
Add sauteed onion and bell pepper.

Soak tortillas in small amount of broth.
Tear into sixths or eighths. Put layer of tortillas, layer of chicken, soup mix, grated cheese and repeat another time with cheese on top.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
Cover casserole with foil.
Wrap each spear of asparagus with a slice of Prosciutto from stem to just below the tip.
Divide among four plates and set aside.

Preheat oven to 425°. Prepare pastry. Sprinkle bacon, cheese and onion in pastry-lined pan. Beat eggs slightly and beat in remaining ingredients. Pour in pie pan. Bake 15 minutes. Cook and drain broccoli. Cook rice.
Combine broccoli with soup, cheese, rice, onion and celery.
Pour into casserole dish.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20
minutes.

Spread in an 8-inch layer pan lined with Saran Wrap.
Spread with remaining Cool Whip and sprinkle coconut on top and sides.
Put cherries and pineapple tidbits on top.

Mix together very well.
Spread it evenly at the bottom of a rectangular crystal dish or baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until light brown.
Set aside to cool.
Mix above ingredients, folding in sour cream last.
Place in baking dish and bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.
Serve with crackers.
Stir yeast, water, milk and sugar in 2 1/2-quart crock or other nonmetallic bowl until yeast is dissolved.
Stir in flour until a smooth batter forms.
Let stand loosely covered in a warm place for 3 to 5 days.
Stir down occasionally.
Store loosely covered in refrigerator.
Mix all together in casserole and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

Serve hot.

Combine egg yolks and milk.
Thoroughly mix in cold water.
Mix thoroughly with flour mixture.
Cook over medium low heat until slightly thickened.

Add vanilla.
Cool to lukewarm.

When frozen, pack well.

Add salt, margarine, grits, eggs, Tabasco sauce and cheese.
Stir well.
Bake in a greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle on paprika before baking.
Bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients except the cookies together in a large mixing bowl.
Beat on low and gradually increase speed.
Beat on high speed for several minutes until the mixture is consistent. Line a bowl, pie shell or flowerpot with crushed cookies.
Pour the mixture into the bowl so that the cookies surround the mixture.
Chill for an hour.
Serve cold.
Melt butter; add flour	to
smooth paste.
Add milk and cook until thick.
Add
grated
cheese
to cooked macaroni and sprinkle with more cheese and
a
dash of paprika.

Bring to boil.

Stir together flour and baking powder.

Add to meat and gravy with bean sprouts and water chestnuts.

Beat cheese until smooth.
Add pineapple, 1 1/2 cups pecans, onion, bell pepper, salt and sauces.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, 3 tablespoons sugar and salt.
Cut in butter or margarine until consistency of cornmeal.
Pack into bottom and 1-inch up the sides of a 9-inch spring-form pan or 9-inch square pan.

Mix to smooth batter. Pour into paper lined cake pan, 8 x 8 x 2-inch and spread batter with topping.
