Mix sugar and flour together.
Add to fruit and cheese mixture.
Spread mixture in an 8 x 11-inch or 9 x 12-inch casserole dish.
Spread crushed Ritz crackers over top.
Pour melted butter over all.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Let cool and serve.
This dish is good hot or cold.
Chop pork chops into cubes and brown in 2 tablespoons oil. Cut up vegetables into cubes.
Mix browned pork, vegetables, mushroom soup and water until well blended.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour or until vegetables are tender.
In small bowl, stir together mayonnaise, parmesan, sugar, mustard, anchovy paste, Worcestershire and garlic.
Gradually stir in lemon juice.
Cover and chill several hours or overnight.
In medium salad bowl, toss lettuce with dressing.
Sprinkle croutons over top.
Serve immediately.
Makes 6 servings.

In a small bowl, stir together 1 tablespoon of the mustard with the olive oil, pepper, tarragon and salt. Spread mixture over the top and sides of meat. Let stand 15 minutes at room temperature or refrigerate up to 4 hours.

recipes.t: After Dinner Mint Pie(A Luxurious Frozen Dessert That'S Quick And Easy.)
d: Combine crumbs and margarine; reserve 1/2 cup for topping. Press remaining crumb mixture onto bottom of 9-inch spring-form pan or pie plate. Chill. Gradually add milk to Marshmallow Creme, mixing until well blended. Add extract and food coloring; fold in whipped cream. Pour into pan; freeze until firm. Sprinkle with remaining crumbs or garnish with mint, if desired.
Drain salmon, remove skin and bones.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Form into four patties.
Pan fry in small amount of vegetable oil until browned on both sides.
Mix eggs, sugar and milk until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook until thick.
Cool, then add one large can Pet milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Finish filling gallon freezer with milk.
Brown beef; drain. Add dry egg noodles, water and salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce simmer until noodles are done, then add vegetable soup. Continue to simmer until done.
Grease loaf pan and set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large mixing bowl combine butter, orange juice and rind, dates, sugar and egg.
In a separate bowl combine remaining ingredients. Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients and stir just until batter is moist and uniform.
Bake 50 minutes or until done.
Mix in large saucepan and boil 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in 1 cup peanut butter and 4 cups uncooked oats.
Mix well with spoon.
Add 2 teaspoons vanilla.
Drop onto wax paper with tablespoon to cool.
Saute oleo and onions.
Add water and noodles; bring to a boil.
Add broccoli and garlic powder.
Cook until noodles and broccoli are done, about 15 minutes.
Cool and add milk and cheese.
Return to burner and stir until cheese is melted.
Cook on low until ready to serve.
Brown hamburger, adding onion when about halfway done.
Cook until onion is tender.
Drain about 1/2 of liquid; add flour, salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Cook for about 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add soups and water.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat and add sour cream; let reheat to serving temperature.
Serve over cooked egg noodles.
Cook tomatoes, onion, salt and pepper, cayenne and sugar for 15 minutes.
Melt butter; blend in flour.
Add milk gradually. Gradually add tomato mixture to milk mixture, stirring constantly. Serve.
Combine 1/2 cup sugar and water.
Bring to a boil; stir until sugar dissolves.
Boil, covered, over medium heat, for 5 minutes. Beat egg whites until stiff; gradually add remaining 1/4 cup sugar. Slowly pour hot syrup into whites; beat constantly until mixture has cooled.
Pare and puree kiwi fruit to measure 3/4 cup. Gradually beat lemon-lime soda, kiwi fruit puree and lime juice into egg white mixture.
Partially freeze.
Spoon mixture into chilled mixer bowl and beat with chilled beaters until mixture is light and foamy.
Return to freezer until firm.
Brown beef, onion and green pepper.
Add 2/3 can of the tomato sauce and 2/3 of taco seasoning.
Season with pepper and simmer until well blended.
Set aside 1/2 cup of chips and 1/4 cup cheese.
In 3-quart casserole, layer rest of ingredients twice in the following order:
taco chips, stewed tomatoes, meat mixture, fresh tomatoes, beans, tomato sauce and cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes, covered. Bake uncovered another 5 to 8 minutes.
Serve with bottled hot sauce.
Serves 10 easily.
Cook
potatoes	in
water
and	mash
with milk or used leftover
mashed
potatoes.
To
the
potatoes, add bread (cut into
cubes), 2 eggs, parsley and broth.
In tablespoon butter cook
celery
(that
has
been diced), onion and parsley until soft (saute or in microwave).
Add to filling mixture.
Butter ovenproof
casserole
dish;
put mixture into dish and bake at 350° or until brown on top for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Chocolate Cake With Cream Cheese Filling
d: Mix together the first 10 ingredients.
Cream together remaining ingredients (except chocolate chips).
Use half of the chocolate cake batter; spoon out the cream cheese and half of the chocolate chips.
Spread over the top of the cake batter and pour rest of the batter over the top and top with chocolate chips. Bake at 350° for approximately 45 minutes.
Brown hamburger with onions.
Add salt and pepper.
Drain grease.
Add taco seasoning and simmer.
Bake potatoes and cut in half lengthwise.
Scoop out center of potato, leaving 1/4 inch around edges.
Place potatoes in baking dish and sprinkle with cheddar cheese.
Add about 2 Tbsp. seasoned hamburger and top with mozzarella and cheddar cheese.
Sprinkle on onion, chives, and bacon bits.
Heat until cheese is melted and serve with sour cream.
Mix thoroughly. Form small flat cakes.
Broil until brown. Serve with sauce.
Place marshmallows, pumpkin, spices and salt in saucepan. Heat over low flame stirring until marshmallows are melted.
Cool. Stir in half of the whipped cream. Carefully fold in remaining cream.
Pour into pie shell. Chill until firm.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix oleo, flour and pecans together.
Press into pie shell (oblong pan).
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until light brown. (Let cool.)
Wash scallops, cut in 3/4-inch pieces.
Poach in boiling water 3 minutes.
Drain and cover with cold water.
Cook shrimp in boiling water and lemon, bay leaves and whole cloves 5 minutes. Drain and cool in cold water.
Clean shrimp and cut in half lengthwise.
Melt 1 1/4 pounds butter; add flour.
Cook 8 to 10 minutes, do not brown.
Add scalded milk and stir until thick and smooth.
Clean lobster, remove bones and intestinal vein from tail. Cut in chunks.
Saute lobster in butter until lobster is hot.
Add shrimp and paprika; saute until seafood is done, about 3 minutes. Heat scallops to boiling.
Remove from heat; drain.
Add all seafood to sauce.
Incorporate wine.
Season lightly with salt. Garnish with parsley.
Can be served in patty shell or toast, etc. Makes 50 portions.
Mix pudding and milk together.
Add Cool Whip.
Make layer of crackers, then pudding.
Repeat this until you have a layer of crackers on top.
Put frosting on top layer of crackers. Wonderful.

recipes.t: Outback Steak House Ranch Salad Dressing
d: Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl. Mix well. Cover bowl and chill dressing for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cook macaroni until almost done (bakes easier this way).
Beat egg together with milk and set aside. Layer grated cheese and macaroni in 2 quart casserole dish. Repeat layer.
Pour milk and egg mixture over layered macaroni and cheese.
Place pats of butter on top of mixture and sprinkle bread crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for one hour.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine all ingredients except buttermilk in large bowl.
Mix well.
Add buttermilk; mix well.
Knead on a floured surface. Place in a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 400° for 45 minutes.
Mix sugar, milk and oleo in pan.
Bring to rolling boil for 1 minute.
Remove and add chocolate chips.
Stir to spreading consistency and ice brownies.
Spread dessert topping on bottom of crust.
Pour milk into large bowl.
Add pudding mix.
Beat with wire whisk 2 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in Cool Whip and chopped toffee bars. Spoon into crust.
Freeze 4 hours or until set.
Let stand at room temperature 15 minutes or until pie can be cut easily.
Pour stock and heat in covered pot.
Cook onions slowly in skillet in butter until transparent.
Cool 15 minutes.
Add salt, sugar, flour and vermouth in pan.
When mixed well, add to stock. Simmer in pot 1 hour.
Mix the first 5 ingredients.
Combine mayonnaise, wine vinegar and sugar and let stand at room temperature.
When ready to serve, pour on the dressing and mix.

Cook potatoes until tender. Remove skins and slice potatoes. Put in buttered baking dish. Add sauteed onion and green pepper, pickles and cheese. Crisp fry bacon. Crumble and put on top. Place in 350° oven and heat long enough for cheese to melt. This can be made ahead of time.
First Layer:
Combine flour, oleo and pecans.
Mix well and spread into dish.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes at 375°.
Let cool completely.
Skin, trim and clean the camel, lamb and chickens.
Boil until tender.
(Be sure your pot is large enough.)
Cook rice until fluffed.
Fry nuts until brown; mix with rice.
Hard boil the eggs and peel them.
Then stuff the chickens with eggs and rice.
Stuff the lamb with five of the chickens and some rice. Stuff the camel with the lamb and more rice.
Broil in large oven or near a gas flame until brown.
Spread the remaining mixed rice on a large tray and place the camel on top.
Place the remaining stuffed chickens around the camel.
Decorate rice with boiled eggs and nuts.
And don't worry if there are more guests than you've expected, the recipe serves 80 to 100.
Thaw bread dough and let raise.
Roll each loaf out on cookie sheet.
Spread approximately 1 tablespoon mustard on each loaf. Layer alternately ham, cheeses, salami and pepperoni.
Overlap middle section and pinch ends together.
Pour melted butter on top and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Bake at 350° uncovered 30 minutes.
Peel and stone avocados; cut into cubes.
Combine avocados and onion in a medium size bowl.
Toss gently to mix well.
In a small bowl combine oil, lemon juice, scotch, sugar, salt and pepper; mix well.
Pour over avocado mixture.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
To serve, place orange sections on lettuce, pile on avocado mixture in center.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients except flour together and cook over low heat until vegetables are tender.
Add flour mixed with a little water until smooth.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine 1 1/2 cups cheese, both soups, onion and evaporated milk into saucepan and place on medium heat.
Stir occasionally. Heat until all ingredients are mixed well and cheese is melted.
Cook 3/4 c. whipping cream and 7 1/2 squares of chocolate in a heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly, until chocolate melts and mixture is smooth.
Pour into a large bowl.
Whisk together remaining 3 cups of whipping cream, 9 yolks, 3/4 c. of sugar and 1 1/2 tsp. vanilla until sugar dissolves and mixture is smooth.
Whisk 1 1/2 c. of egg mixture into chocolate mixture until smooth.
Cover and chill remaining egg mixture.
Pour chocolate mixture evenly into 9 (8 oz.) custard cups; place cups in a 13x9-inch pan.
Add hot water to pan to a depth of 1/2 inch.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes or until almost set.
(Center will be soft.) Slowly pour remaining egg mixture evenly over custards and bake 20 to 25 more minutes or until set.
Cool custards in water in pan on a wire rack.
Remove from pan; cover and chill at least 8 hours. Sprinkle each custard with 1 Tbsp. brown sugar; place custards in a pan.
Torch top of custard with hot flame until sugar melts.
Let stand for a few minutes to allow sugar to harden.
If you do not have a torch you can use the broiler; 5 1/2 inches from heat (with electric oven door partially open) about 2 minutes.
Brown hamburger; drain off fat.
Cook noodles; in casserole dish, combine cooked noodles, margarine, milk, soup and cheese sauce.
Add meat; mix well.
Microwave for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
Cook and mash squash.
Mix all ingredients together in greased baking dish.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes, then at 350° for 35 minutes.
Using a sharp knife, remove the layer of skin from ham, leaving a thin layer of fat to keep the meat juicy while baking. Score the surface of the ham in diamond pattern without cutting into the meat.
Place a whole clove in center of half the diamonds.
Brush top of ham with Dijon mustard and place in roasting pan.
Cook meat in oil until lightly browned.
Mix in onion, salt, pepper and rice; cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Place cabbage in casserole.
Pour meat mixture over it.
Do not stir. Cover and bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cream the cream cheese, Miracle Whip and milk.
Spread on dinner size plate about 1/4 inch thick.
Spread 2/3 bottle cocktail sauce on top.
Sprinkle shrimp on top of that.
Dip into with your favorite kind of crackers.
Combine sugar, flour and salt.
Blend together with egg substitute in top of a double boiler.
Cook, uncovered, over boiling water, stirring constantly until thickened.
Reduce heat and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, continuing to stir.
Remove from heat; add vanilla and nutmeg.
Spread a small amount of custard on bottom of a 1 1/2-quart bowl or casserole.
Add a layer of wafers, sliced bananas, custard, wafers, sliced bananas and ending with custard to make 3 layers.
Place marshmallows on top and bake at 450° for 3 to 4 minutes until marshmallows are slightly brown. Serve warm or room temperature.
Makes 8 servings.
Place 1/2 of beans in a 2-quart casserole. Top with 1/2 of onions; repeat. Combine catsup with sugar and pour over onions. Sprinkle bacon over top. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Saute onion, bacon and mushrooms until done.
Add drained green beans to pan.
Melt butter in mixture and heat through.
Brown the meat, onions and peppers.
Drain the fat.
Add the milk, enchilada sauce and 2 soups.
(It works better if you combine all this before you add it to the pan.)
In a Pyrex casserole, alternate the tortilla chips, meat mixture and a little cheese twice, ending with the bulk of the cheese on the top. Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Boil the sugar and water until stringy. Dice the green pepper, onion and celery; toss with the sugar mixture and sauerkraut. Refrigerate overnight.
Put all ingredients and 4 cups water in kettle. Bring to boil and then simmer, covered, 2 hours or until tender. Serve plain or deep-fry.
*Available in Chinese section of supermarkets.

recipes.t: Cheese Souffle(Recipe Originated With Joanne Hall, Kokomo, Indiana)
d: Melt cheese and butter in pan.
In large bowl, break bread. Beat egg yolks and the rest of the ingredients together with bread. Then add melted cheese and butter mixture.
Beat egg whites and fold into mixture.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes until browned. Serves 6.
Add all vegetables to broth and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Substitute vegetables as desired.
Serves 6. Preparation Time:
30 minutes.
Mix and bake cake according to package directions adding almond extract and 1/2 of the coconut.
After baking and while still hot, poke holes in top of cake with fork and pour a can of cream of coconut over the top.
Cool completely and cover cake completely with Cool Whip and remainder of coconut.
Combine pineapple chunks, grapefruit sections, orange sections, cherries, peaches and warm orange marmalade slightly. Remove from heat and mix with Southern Comfort.
Pour over fruit and mix well.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine water, sugar and Jell-O in pan.
Bring to a boil. Stir until dissolved.
Remove from heat.
Stir in baby food and pineapple.
Combine cream cheese and milk until smooth.
Mix with Jell-O.
Add nuts.
Pour into a 9 x 12-inch dish and chill until solid.
Press the first 4 ingredients (mixed) in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for about 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool and crumble in pan for crust.
Mix
together the soups, steak and mushrooms.
Place in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake, covered, for 2 1/2 hours at 325° or longer.
Add
ounces
sour
cream to meat mixture. Serve over cooked noodles.
Preheat oven to 350° (325° for glass dish).
In a 13 x 9-inch cake pan, melt margarine in oven. Sprinkle crumbs over margarine. Pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over crumbs.
Top with remaining ingredients.
Press down.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly brown.
Cool.
Chill, if desired. Cut into bars. Store loosely covered at room temperature.
In a bowl, dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in strawberries, pineapple, bananas, and nuts.
Pour half of mixture into a 13 x 9 x 2 in. dish.
Refrigerate for 1 hour or until set. Set the remaining gelatin mixture aside.
Combine the sour cream, sugar, and vanilla; mix well.
Spread over the chilled gelatin. Spoon remaining gelatin mixture over top.
Chill overnight.
Yield: 12 - 15 servings.
Beat eggs; stir in remaining ingredients.
Place into 2 loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Drain fruit.
Save juice from the pineapple and fruit cocktail.
Mix juice with instant pudding.
Stir until thick. Pour over fruit.
Add sliced bananas and cherries.
Chill.
Slice sausage in quarter slices.
Brown on both sides.
Drain off fat.
Add other ingredients.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Serves 5 to 6.
Cook sausage, stirring as to blend.
Saute jalapenos in this until changes color.
Add cheese, stirring constantly to melt cheese and mix well.
Pour in shallow dish and cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In saucepan, combine sugar, flour and salt.
Stir in undrained pineapple, sour cream and lemon juice until thoroughly blended.
Cook and stir until mixture thickens and bubbles; cook and stir 2 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir a moderate amount of hot mixture into egg yolks; return to hot mixture, stirring constantly.
Cook and stir 2 minutes more. Spoon hot mixture into cooled pastry shell.
Spread meringue atop pie, sealing meringue to edge of pastry.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes, or until golden.
Cool before cutting.
Put 1 cup water in pot.
Add cubed pork and start browning. When pork turns light brown, add sausage and brown until dark brown.
Remove excess grease from pot.
Brown onions.
Add green onions and bell pepper.
Cook down.
Add 4 cups water.
Add seasoning and bring to a boil.
Add rice and stir until water becomes thick.
Cover and put fire as low as possible.
Wait 10 minutes and turn rice over (do not stir) from the bottom of the pot.
Re-cover.
Wait 10 minutes and turn over again.
Turn fire off.
Let sit 5 minutes and serve.
Cook all the ingredients except Cool Whip over medium heat until thick.
Cool in refrigerator for 2 hours. Fold in 1 cup Cool Whip.
Store in refrigerator.
Brown chops and set aside.
Pour rice into pan where chops were browned.
Stir constantly until golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Add bouillon water; simmer over low heat until liquid is gone, 20 to 25 minutes.
Lay chops on top of rice for the last 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except Tater Tots in large casserole dish. Cover with 1 layer of Tater Tots.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix together the first 2 ingredients and then spread on large platter.
Layer on top of that mixture the remaining listed ingredients in the order given.
Refrigerate.
Serve with taco chips.
Saute onion in oleo in skillet.
Stir in flour and dry mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
Add milk.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Stir in cheese until melted.
Alternate layers of potatoes, celery, ham, green pepper and cheese sauce in 9 x 13-inch pan until all ingredients are used, ending with cheese sauce.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cover and refrigerate until used.

recipes.t: Sweet 'N Sour Cabbage And Kielbasa Saute
d: In 10-inch skillet, heat oil.
Add kielbasa and onions and saute until browned.
Add cabbage and stir thoroughly.
Add remaining ingredients and cook, stirring occasionally, until cabbage is tender and liquid has evaporated.
Makes 2 servings.
Make cake according to package directions.
Pour into rectangular pan and bake.
Cool and cut in half.
Make pudding, using 2 1/2 cups milk per package.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Drain.
Add pinto beans, tomato sauce, salt, pepper and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Spray baking dish with Pam.
Pour meat mixture into baking dish.
Cook squash and onion in a small amount of salted water until tender; drain.
Add bread or cracker crumbs (reserving 1 tablespoon for top), cheese, egg, salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons margarine.
Spoon into greased casserole.
Top with remaining crumbs; dot with 2 tablespoons margarine.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until brown.
Yield:
4 servings.
Saute onions and garlic over low heat.
Add turkey hamburger to saucepot.
Cover.
Stir frequently until meat is lightly cooked and separated.
Add chili powder, tomatoes and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Uncover; add drained kidney beans to sauce.
Cook slowly about 30 minutes.
Add tomato puree with a little water if mixture is too thick.
Tastes better when cooked in advance (24 hours).
Cook potatoes until fork-tender.
Drain and cool slightly. In a large bowl, combine potatoes and all other ingredients; toss gently to mix well.
Sprinkle paprika on top.
Cover.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours for best taste.
Prepare pudding mix according to directions, using only 1 cup milk.
Blend in 1 1/2 cups whipped topping and 1/4 cup pecans. Spoon into pie shell.
Decorate with remaining 1/2 cup whipped topping and additional nuts.
Chill at least 1 hour.
Serves 6.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Divide macaroni and cheese into two parts.
Layer 1/2 macaroni, then 1/2 grated cheese in 2-quart buttered baking dish.
Repeat with second layer, finishing with cheese.
Dissolve the mustard and salt in 1/4 cup milk.
Beat eggs; stir in mustard mixture and rest of milk.
Pour over macaroni and cheese.
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife stuck
comes out clean.
Mix well together.
Cook at 350° for 45 minutes.
Melt 1 stick margarine and pour into an oblong pan.
Mix all chips and crushed wafers.
Pour condensed milk over mixture.
Mix. Pour into pan.
Cook at 350° for 30 minutes, until golden.
Cool and cut into squares.
Beat cream cheese, gradually adding milk.
Beat until smooth. Add lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, salt and pepper. Add shrimp and stir in cream cheese mixture.
Chill.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups dip.
Peel and cut up eggplant.
Then boil until they are done enough to mash up.
Remove from the boiling water and mash the eggplant.
Then add cream of chicken soup, onion (chopped), eggs, salt, pepper, cornbread (crumbled), light bread and sage to your taste.
Mix well.
Slice raw cauliflower thin.
Combine with other ingredients. Serve in salad bowl.
Salt to taste.
Chill overnight.
Brown chopped onion and rice in hot oiled pan.
Add water and bouillon.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes.
Turn off.
Add Cheddar cheese.
Serve with meat, vegetables and rolls.
In skillet, cook bacon or ground beef.
Use meat drippings to cook onion and bell pepper.
Drain.
Add all ingredients.
Bring to boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix
all
dry
ingredients
together.
Add
milk and egg whites, beaten stiff.
Set in pan of water and bake in moderate oven for 50 minutes.
Take out of pan of water last 5 minutes.
Place cooked broccoli in greased casserole.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over broccoli.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup sharp, grated cheese over top.
Top with 3/4 cup fresh bread crumbs. Melt 1 tablespoon margarine and dribble over top.
Bake until bubbly, approximately 35 to 45 minutes at 350°.
Bring cream cheese and braunschweiger to room temperature. Combine half of the cream cheese with remaining ingredients except nuts. Mix well.
Spread in mold and chill for several hours. Unmold.
Frost with remaining cream cheese.
Garnish with chopped nuts.
Serve with crackers or a party loaf bread.
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly.
Mix in beaten eggs.
Sift dry ingredients and add to creamed mixture alternately with sour milk.
Add almonds and vanilla flavorings.
Pour into 3 greased 8-inch pie pans.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon sugar on top of each. Bake at 350° about 25 minutes.
Place cream cheese in a bowl and stir until very smooth.
Add all remaining ingredients and stir until thoroughly blended. Transfer to serving bowl and garnish with sliced olives, if desired.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
Place chocolate chips, peanut butter chips and the peanut butter in 2-quart dish in microwave, uncovered, on Medium until melted, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir until smooth.
Mix in marshmallows and peanuts until evenly coated; spread in buttered square 8 x 8 pan.
Refrigerate until firm, at least 1 hour; cut into bars.
Sprinkle chicken with seasoned salt; place in crock-pot on high.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over chicken.
Cook for 3 to 4 hours, stirring occasionally.
Serve over cooked rice. Enjoy!
Cook spinach in the bouillon.
Puree in food processor with oysters.
Add enough milk to make 1 quart of soup.
Serves 4.
Mix together and shape into loaf.
Place in casserole and pour over it a syrup made of 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup vinegar and 2/3 cup water.
Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Baste with syrup 3 or 4 times.
Bake chicken at 350° for 30 minutes; drain juice off the chicken.
Add the noodles.
Mix water and soup; pour over the chicken.
Sprinkle spices from the noodle packs over the chicken. Bake for 30 minutes in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
If the noodles are not tender, cook a little longer.
Combine all ingredients.
Keep refrigerated.
This recipe makes enough to keep extra on hand.

recipes.t: Old Fashion Pumpkin Pie Filling Or Sweet Potato
d: Beat all ingredients well.
Pour into 9-inch deep dish pie shell.
Bake at 425°
for 15 minutes.
Reduce oven to 350° and bake
45 minutes more until knife inserted comes out clean.
Cool.
Have turkey at room temperature.
Rub inside and out with salt.
Preheat oven to 475°.
Bring water and tea to gentle boil and let steep; add sugar. Remove tea bags, pour into 1 gallon container.
Add Ocean Spray cranberry juice concentrate.
Fill remainder of container with cool water.
Serve hot or cold with lemon wedge or cinnamon stick.
Combine eggs, bean sprouts, meat or seafood, onion, salt and pepper.
Mix together lightly. Melt 1 teaspoon butter in 6-inch skillet.
Pack 1/2 cup of mixture into skillet.
Cook until set and brown on edges.
Turn and brown on other side.
Boil first 3 ingredients one minute.
Remove from heat.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Press into greased pan.
Cut into squares.
Cook beans according to package directions.
Add meat and all ingredients and simmer together for about 4 hours.
Smash several beans on the side of the pan.
Combine sugar, cornstarch, lemon rind, juice, egg yolks and milk in a heavy saucepan; cook over medium heat until thick, stirring constantly.
Stir in butter and cool mixture to room temperature.
Stir in sour cream and pour into pie shell.
Cover with whipped cream and garnish with lemon twists.
Store in refrigerator.
Combine ingredients. Drop in spoonfuls on buttered pan or cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Add 7-Up and ice ring just prior to serving.
Combine ingredients as listed.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Salt and pepper fish.
Arrange pepper slices and onion slices over fish.
Mix chicken broth, lemon juice and basil.
Pour mixture over fish.
Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Sift flour, baking powder and salt into mixing bowl.
Add egg and creamed corn, mix well.
Heat corn oil in skillet.
Drop corn mixture by tablespoons into hot corn oil and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Makes 18.
Bake cake in 2 layers.
Put one layer, broken in pieces, in bottom of bowl and add 1/2 pie filling, 1/2 crushed pineapple and 1/2 nuts.
Repeat with second layer of cake.
Add cherries last. Refrigerate.

Melt butter in skillet and cut up onion. Cook until the onion is tender. Add soups; stir until smooth. Add 1/2 cup of milk. Debone chicken; layer chicken, rice and soup mixture. Top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook and take chicken off bone.
Reserve 2 cups broth.
Cut chicken into pieces and place in bottom of baking dish.
Melt margarine and pour over chicken.
Mix together dry ingredients and mix well with milk.
Pour over chicken.
Heat soup and broth to the boiling point and pour over all.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes its own crust.
In a large canner container, add zucchini, water and lime. Soak, weighted down, overnight. Drain and wash well.
Cover with clean water. Let stand for 2
hours and drain.
In a large pan, put water.
Cut potatoes, carrots and onion up. Put into pan.
Cut sausage up.
Lay on top of vegetables.
Quarter cabbage and put on top.
Bring water to boil.
Cook until done. Place on large platter.
Serve.
Put salt and pepper to season. Add butter to season also.
Mix well.
Make into walnut size balls, mash down and put on a cookie sheet.

Mix everything together and bake in a greased pan at 325° for 35 minutes or until brown.
Wash and dry chicken or hens.
Sprinkle inside with salt, pepper and/or nutmeg.
Place chicken or hens on rack, breast side down, in shallow pan.
Stuff cavities with apples.
Roast at 350° for about 45 minutes (35 minutes for hens) or until juices run fairly clear when pierced.
Turn chicken (hens) upside down.
Brush with melted butter.
Fold ham and cheese slices around chicken. Roast at 400° for another 20 to 35 minutes or until chicken is tender and nicely browned.
Sprinkle lemon juice over chicken and toss well.
Add celery, Miracle Whip, almonds, onion and salt and mix thoroughly.
Just before serving, stir in croutons or sprinkle them on top.
Mix together bread crumbs, cheese and spices.
Melt margarine. Dip wings in melted margarine and roll in bread crumb mixture. Place in greased shallow pan or cookie sheet.
Make sure sides of wings are not touching.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring until it crumbles and is no longer pink.
Remove sausage, and drain on paper towels, reserving 1 tablespoon drippings in skillet. Whisk flour into hot drippings until smooth; cook, whisking constantly, 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk, and cook, whisking constantly, 5 to 7 minutes or until thickened and bubbly. Stir in sausage, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately over biscuits.
Mix together eggs, lard and milk, then your dry ingredients. Bake at 350°.
Put all into pot and cover with water.
Cook until meat is tender.
Meat will be very sweet.
You can use the stems and leaves of fresh beets also.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Bake cake as directed in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan; cool.
Take half of cake; break into pieces.
Put in large bowl, layer with half pudding, half pineapple, half cherry pie filling, half bananas, half coconut and half Cool Whip. Repeat layers.
Top with nuts.
Chill and serve.
Peel, chop into cubes, then boil squash until tender.
Saute onion in butter in a frying pan.
Add sausage; cook until completely browned.
Add cooked squash to sausage mixture.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix together and put into 8 x 8-inch pan.
Refrigerate.
Soften cream cheese; mix all ingredients.
Let firm in refrigerator, then roll in coconut.
Thaw the blueberries well; drain off syrup and save.
Sift together the dry ingredients.
Measure the blueberry syrup. There should be about 1/2 cup.
If not, add water to complete the measure.
Line greased Bundt pan with nuts.
Quarter biscuits and roll in cinnamon and sugar.
Put in greased pan and sprinkle nuts on biscuits.
Melt butter, brown sugar and water.
Boil 2 minutes and pour over biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add soup and salsa to beef.
Set aside.
Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with 2 large tortilla shells. Layer with 1/2 beef mixture.
Sprinkle 1/2 of the cheese, then put the other 2 shells on top.
Put remaining beef on top of the shells.
Bake for about 30 minutes at 300°.
Top with remaining cheese and let melt (you could use chicken instead of beef).
Mix flour, sugar and margarine with hands.
Pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Spread with thick layer of peanut butter while warm.
Melt chocolate chips with water and syrup.
Spread.
Cool and cut.
Heat oven to 350°.
In large skillet, cook and stir celery, onion and green pepper in butter until onion is tender.
Stir in tuna and remaining ingredients.
Steam carrots just until tender.
Transfer to serving bowl and keep warm.
Combine orange juice, sugar and margarine in a saucepan and heat almost to boiling point.
Dissolve cornstarch in water; stir in and cook until clear and thickened.
Add ginger. Pour over carrots.
Preheat oven to 400.
Coat large nonstick skillet with cooking spray.
Place over medium high heat until.
Add chichen, cook 4 minutes on each side (or until browned).
Place chicken in an 11 x 7 inch baking dish coated with cooking spray.
Combine hot sauce and next 4 ingredients:
Pour over chichen.
Bake, uncovered, at 400 for 25 minutes.
Boil raisins and water 10 minutes.
Drain and cool; add enough water to make 2 cups liquid.
Add sugar, margarine, flour, soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves and add raisins last.
Bake in greased 9 x 13 pan in slow oven about 40 to 45 minutes.

Grease 1 1/2-quart rectangle glass dish. Line the bottom (not the sides) with chocolate wafer crumbs. Cream butter and confectioners sugar, adding the egg and bourbon. Spread this mixture on crumbs. Cover and set in the refrigerator for an hour. Whip cream with sugar and add vanilla. Fold in chopped pecans and spread this mixture on top of mixture. Cover with more crushed wafers. Let stand in the refrigerator, covered, for overnight. Cut in 8 pieces.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add flavorings.
Add beaten eggs.
Add a little flour and whipping cream until flour is gone.
Pour into a greased and floured mold.
Bake at 325° in cold oven for about 1 1/2 hours.
Mix flour, salt and shortening together.
Add vinegar to milk. Blend all together.
Roll on floured board.
Makes a double crust.
If you figure out what to do with these ingredients, please let Mac know.
Thank you.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add 1 tablespoon orange rind. Add eggs, one at a time, flour, salt, soda, buttermilk, dates and pecans.
Bake in a greased and floured tube pan for 1 hour and 20 minutes in a 350° oven.
Melt chocolate with margarine in saucepan over very low heat, stirring constantly until smooth.
Remove from heat.
Blend in sugar, eggs, salt and vanilla; beat well.
Stir in coconut.
Drop from teaspoon onto greased baking sheets.
Leaving 1 1/2 inches between.
Bake at 325° for 15 minutes.
Cool on racks.
Makes about 3 dozen.
Brown ground beef, onions and green bell peppers.
Drain; add chili beans and tomato sauce.
Simmer and serve hot.
Drain pineapple and oranges.
Mix cottage cheese, Cool Whip and Jell-O (dry) together.
Add fruit.
Serve immediately.
Combine the juices and lemonade.
Put a block of ice in a punch bowl.
Add the juices and club soda.
Serves 35.
Saute bacon in skillet until crisp.
Remove bacon and drain on paper towels.
Add rice to bacon dripping remaining in pan and cook until browned.
Add onions and cook until golden.
Add bacon and remaining ingredients.
Cover and cook until rice is tender.
More liquid may be added in the form of tomato juice or beef or chicken stock.
Serves 4.
Cook broccoli and onion until broccoli is done and cooked down.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Add rest of ingredients and cook until cheese melts.
Serve warm in chafing dish.
Serve with chips.

About 30 minutes before serving, in medium saucepan over medium heat in 1/2 cup boiling water, heat first 3 ingredients to boiling. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until apples are tender (for chunky applesauce) or 12 to 15 minutes for smoother applesauce.
During last minutes of cooking time, stir in sugar. Makes about 4 cups.
Do not dilute soups.
In a bowl, dice up some chicken.
Add rice and soup mix and put in casserole sprayed with Pam.
Dot with butter.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Dissolve jello and salt in hot water.
Add vinegar, grated onion and pepper.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Chill until firm.
Drain and rinse beans.
Brown ground beef.
Drain excess fat. Add beans, tomatoes, tomato paste, onion, pepper, chili powder and water.
Simmer 45 minutes.
Season ribs on one side.
Place in baking pan.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Turn ribs over; season liberally.
Sprinkle red pepper flakes to personal taste (medium to hot depending on amount).
Return to 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Pour excess fat from baking pan.
Turn ribs again.
Apply red pepper flakes in light dosage (also liberal amount of Lea & Perrins).
Return to oven at 325° for 30 minutes.
Turn ribs for last time.
Apply liberal amounts of Lea & Perrins.
Return to oven at 325° for 30 minutes.
Apply more Lea & Perrins and warm up before serving (if you like juicy ribs).
Wash and grate squash.
Add eggs and flour, sifted with salt, pepper and baking powder and sugar.
Mix well and add melted butter. Drop from tablespoon into 1-inch salad oil hot enough to brown bread cube in one minute.
Turn once.
Makes about 12 fritters.
Delicious serves with fried chicken.
Melt caramels with water in saucepan over low heat.
Stir until sauce is smooth.
Pour over cereal and nuts.
Stir well. Press into greased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle chips over top.
Place in 200° oven for 5 minutes.
When chips are melted, spread to form frosting.
Cut into bars.
Prepare a 9-inch square baking pan by tearing a piece of aluminum foil about 36 inches long and folding it over to make a long piece 3 inches wide.
Place around the inside of the baking pan to make the pan 3 inches tall.
Or, use a 12 to 15-cup baking pan with a flat bottom and 3-inch sides.
Mix the first 3 ingredients together in pan; bring to a boil. Simmer well for 2 minutes.
Add vanilla.
Mix this into the remaining ingredients which have been put into a large bowl.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper.
Cool.
Mix pudding and milk.
Fold in Cool Whip.
Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with graham crackers.
Pour 1/2 of pudding mix over graham crackers.
Do another layer of graham crackers and pour rest of pudding mix.
Top with layer of graham crackers and put icing on. Put in refrigerator for 5 or 6 hours before serving.
Layer in a large bowl or other large container in order given. On top of bacon, spread Miracle Whip dressing, just as you would frost a cake.
Sprinkle granulated sugar over Miracle Whip.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Stir first before serving.
If desired, tomato chunks may be added before serving.
Place sliced tomatoes in a buttered 13 x 9 casserole.
Cover with onions.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and lemon pepper.
Top with grated cheese and crushed crackers.
Dot with butter.
Bake, covered, for 45 minutes at 400°.
Bake, uncovered, for an additional 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients well and refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 375.
Mix shortening, sugars, egg, and vanilla.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Drop by rounded teaspoonful 2 inches apart on ungreased baking sheet.
Bake 10 minutes.
Remove immediately from baking sheet.
In large bowl, combine eggs, milk, vanilla, sugar and salt. Mix until well blended.
In a small bowl, mix flour and baking powder.
Stir flour into egg mixture until smooth; set aside. Stack 2 slices of bread sandwich style.
With sharp knife, remove crust from bread.
Repeat with other breads.
Spread thin layer of jelly or jam on each bread.
Cut sandwich into quarters; dip doughnuts into batter.
Fry in oil or shortening.
After browned, sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Put all in glass dish, crock or enamel pan.
Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon salt.
Let sit 2 hours.
Bring syrup to boil, then let cool.
Melt butter; add apples.
Cook 5 minutes.
Combine flour, curry powder and salt.
Stir into apples.
Add milk slowly.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Add shrimp.
Serve over hot fluffy rice.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs and beat.
Mix the baking soda in the applesauce and add to the first mixture.
Sift the dry ingredients together and add to the mixture.
Beat until well mixed.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 8-inch cake pans.
Bake at 350° until done.
"Great to take places, congeals real firm."
Make shells according to directions.
Then lay out on wax paper to cool.
Brown hamburger; add salt, pepper, garlic powder and oregano to taste.
Drain grease and set aside.
Add cottage cheese, Mozzarella cheese, mayonnaise and egg; stir well.
Stir in hamburger.
Saute together ground beef and onion; drain.
Add remaining ingredients (except tortilla chips and shredded cheese); mix well.
Heat water, beans, onion and garlic to boiling in 2-quart saucepan.
Boil 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover and let stand 1 hour.
Add just enough water to cover beans and add salt.
Heat to boiling; reduce heat and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
(Add water if necessary!)
When done, mash beans and top with crumbled bacon. Great for burritos or nachos.
Can be frozen for later.
Heat oven to 400° and grease a 10-inch pie plate with shortening.
Cook and stir over medium heat the onions, ground sirloin and pepper until brown.
Pour meat mixture into pie plate after draining any fat.
Spread meat mixture evenly in pie plate. Put milk, eggs and baking mix in blender and blend on high 15 seconds (or use egg beater or wire whisk).
Pour mix into pie plate.
Bake 25 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Top with tomato slices and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 5 to 8 minutes longer or until knife inserted inc enter comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix beans, sugar, sauce and onion in 2-quart casserole dish. Top with bacon slices.
Bake at 350° for 2 hours, uncovered, until beans are deeply browned.
Beat eggs and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add flour; mix well.
Add milk and vanilla.
Pour into pie pan lightly greased with butter.
Sprinkle nutmeg on top.
Bake about 50 minutes at 350° or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Flour settles to bottom during baking to form a very light crust.
Drain, rinse and squeeze dry sauerkraut.
Mix all together and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Boil chicken breasts.
Remove skin and debone chicken breasts. If using boneless chicken, do not boil!
Fry in nonstick pan in margarine or butter (enough to coat pan) or white wine.
Mix together soups and white wine.
Add chicken pieces and simmer. Simmer at least 1 hour.
The longer you can simmer the chicken, the more tender the chicken will be!
(It will melt in your mouth.)
Combine
dry
ingredients
thoroughly
and
set
aside. Whisk remaining	ingredients
(except
bananas
and
vanilla wafers) in a 6 to 8 cup microwave container.
Add dry ingredients and whisk all ingredients thoroughly.
Cover with plastic wrap, leaving
a small vent.
Microwave for 6 to 8 minutes or until thick, stirring each minute.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Melt butter in large Dutch oven, saute green pepper and onion.
Stir in chicken, mushrooms, pimento, soup, milk, garlic powder and salt. Drain spaghetti and add to mixture, toss.
Pour into greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan or baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 10 minutes longer or until cheese melts.
Mix and bake cake according to package direction.
While cake is baking, mix sweetened condensed milk and caramel ice cream topping.
While cake is hot, make holes in cake with a large fork, then pour mixture over the cake.
Let cool.
Top with Cool Whip. Sprinkle over that the crushed Butterfinger bars and pecans.
Mix all ingredients except cheese.
Pour into baking dish. Bake at 400° for 1 hour.
Remove from oven; top with cheese. Return to oven and allow cheese to brown.
Put potatoes in greased 2-quart casserole; pour over mixture of soup, milk, salt, pepper and onions.
Season and trim fat from chops; brown in skillet on both sides.
Put on top of potatoes. Cover and bake at 375° for 1 hour or until done.
Beat together oleo, brown sugar, egg and honey until smooth. Add flour, soda, salt, cloves, cinnamon and ginger.
Stir until well combined.
Divide dough into balls (approximately 24).
Dip balls into granulated sugar and place 3 inches apart on baking sheet.
Bake until tops are crinkled and just firm, 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool completely.
Store in airtight container.
Bake at 375°.
Cook diced potatoes and onion until done.
Add all other ingredients and simmer on very low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring frequently, making sure it doesn't stick or scorch.
Dissolve soda in hot water.
Mix all ingredients.
Drop by spoonfuls onto greased pan.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Lower heat to 300° for 5 minutes.
In pitcher, combine water, juice concentrate, ReaLemon and sugar; stir until sugar dissolves.
Chill.
Just before serving, add ginger ale.
Scoop sherbet into glasses.
Pour in juice mixture.
Melt butter and mix with dressing.
Line dish with the mixture.
Save some to sprinkle on top.
Mix the 4 remaining ingredients and pour into the dressing lined pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Melt butter in heavy 2-quart saucepan; stir in milk and sugar. Bring to full, rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Continue boiling over medium heat until mixture reaches 234° or soft ball stage, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
Remove from heat and stir in chocolate pieces until melted.
Add Marshmallow Creme and nuts, stirring until well blended.
Pour into well-greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cool at room temperature.
Cut into squares.
(If fudge is too soft, chill.)
Makes about 3 pounds.
Peel and cook potatoes.
Mix with electric mixer.
Add stick of oleo and softened cream cheese.
Mix well.
Add sour cream, a little at a time, to get the desired consistency of mashed potatoes.
Put in baking dish, dot with oleo and sprinkle with paprika.
Heat in oven until lightly browned.
Can be prepared a day ahead.
Mix all ingredients together but corn flakes and butter.
Pour in a 13 x 10-inch pan.
Stir together corn flakes and butter. Spread topping over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until potatoes are done.
*Currants can be used instead of raisins.
In a small pan, sprinkle gelatin over water.
Let stand 1 minute.
Stir
over low heat until dissolved.
Stir in 1 cup cream. Bring
to a boil.
Pour into blender. Add chocolate and process until
chocolate
melts.
Add
1/2 cup cream, eggs and vanilla.
Continue	until well blended. Pour into bowl.
Chill until thick, about 30 minutes.
Dissolve
jello
in boiling water.
Chill until mixture begins to thicken
and
is
firm
to touch (1 to 1 1/2 hours). Whip jello until fluffy.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Pour into mold or baking dish.
Place chilies under broiler.
Roast until blistered, remove and place in damp cloth.
Peel and remove seeds and veins from chilies. Fill chilies with cheese strips; roll in flour.
Beat egg whites with salt until stiff.
Fold in beaten egg yolks.
Dip floured chilies in egg mixture.
Fry in deep hot fat until golden brown.
Remove from
grease; place on towel to drain.
Serves 6.
Cream the butter, sugar and eggs.
Add flour and baking powder.
Pour into a single round, greased cake pan.
Drain and slice apricots; pour on center of cake batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine butter and sugar; cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs and sour cream.
Combine next 5 ingredients.
Add to batter and mix well.
Pour into a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Brown hamburg and onion in a large skillet.
Sprinkle in some parsley flakes.
Drain hamburg and place in a 2-quart casserole. Cover with cream-style corn, then cover with mashed potatoes. Sprinkle with parsley leaves.
Top with cheese (optional).
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating mixture until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla, anise and nuts.
Add flour sifted with baking powder and salt.
Mix well. Knead like bread.
Shape into 6 to 7 loaves.
Brush top of loaves with 1 beaten egg.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven; cut diagonally into small pieces.
Return to oven.
Toast until light brown.
Combine crushed graham crackers with melted butter until well blended.
Pat down firmly to
form crust in bottom of well greased 9-inch spring pan, making sure
edges
of
the
pan are sealed. Beat eggs well.
Add
cream
cheese
and
beat
until mixture is smooth.
Next, add 1
cup sugar, lemon juice and the flour.
Beat until all ingredients
are	well
mixed.
Add sour cream, vanilla and 4 tablespoons sugar.
After mixture has been well blended, pour into spring
pan
with
the
graham
cracker crust.
Bake at 375° for one
hour	or
until
outer edges have turned brown. Cool, then remove sides and refrigerate. Cake is at
its best after
being
refrigerated	overnight
or
longer. Before serving,
cake may	be
topped
with
prepared
cherry, blueberry or pineapple pie filling.
Serves about 15.
Toss cabbage, peppers, celery and onion together.
Heat sugar, vinegar, salt, celery seed, mustard seed and oil together; cool. Add to cole slaw.
Combine green beans, green peas, celery, green pepper, onion, pimento, vinegar, oil, sugar, paprika, salt and pepper in bowl; mix well.
Chill for 24 hours to several days.
Drain before serving.
Yield:
10 servings.
Let zucchini, onion
and salt stand overnight; drain and rinse with cold
water.
Add
all
ingredients
to zucchini and onion. Cook 30 minutes.
Seal in hot clean jars.
Brown bacon, hamburger and chopped onion in saucepan.
Then add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Bake at 300° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix together and form into a ball.
Serve with crackers.
Boil, then reduce to a simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, uncovered. Makes 5 servings.
Use chopsticks or a fork to separate rice grains.
In a small bowl, combine the eggs, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt and pepper. Set aside.
Heat wok and add oil around the rim (this seals the wok and heats the oil quickly).
Add shrimp, bacon, and green onion.
Immediately add rice and stir-fry over high heat; after a few minutes, the grains will separate.
While stirring rice, pour in egg mixture.
Stir-fry one minute.
Serve rice in a warm Chinese bowl to retain heat during serving.
Serves 6.

In a large saute pan, with a lid, add the oil. Heat the oil over medium heat. When the oil is hot, add the clams. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and saute for 6 to 8 minutes. Add the onions, garlic and wine. Continue to saute for 2 minutes or until the shells completely open; discard any shells that do not open. Add the pasta. Season with salt and pepper. Continue to saute for 2 minutes. Add the parsley and mix well. Serve on a large platter. Drizzle with olive oil and serve. Yield: 4 to 6 servings.
Cut bacon in half while in the package. Set aside.
Mix Bisquick with eggs, milk and spices. Stir in shrimp last. Separate cold bacon slices.
Put 1 spoonful of mixture on the end of 1/2 slice of bacon. Roll up individually. Brown in skillet in hot oil. Serve hot or cold.
Boil dandelion blossoms, water and sugar together 15 minutes. Cool.
Add yeast and sliced lemon.
Let stand 5 days; strain and let stand 5 more days.
Put in gallon jugs and put a balloon on top until it quits working, then cork.
Combine softened cream cheese, granulated sugar, vanilla and nutmeg, mixing until well blended.
Mash 3/4 cup strawberry slices; stir into cream cheese mixture.
Whip cream with confectioners sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold into cream cheese mixture. Fold remaining strawberries into cream cheese mixture.
Spoon into pie crust.
Chill overnight.
Mix together in bowl the flour, cinnamon, soda, salt and ginger.
Cream shortening, sugar, eggs and molasses in separate bowl.
Add sour milk and raisins.
Stir until mixed well.
Add dry ingredients.
Drop by tablespoon onto greased baking sheets.
Bake in a 350° oven for 12 minutes.
Cream sugar and butter thoroughly.
Add beaten eggs.
Sift together flour, soda and spices.
Add to egg mixture.
Add milk and bourbon; mixing well.
Add nuts, citron and candied cherries. Drop on greased cookie sheet and bake in moderately slow oven (325°) for 25 minutes.
These are wonderful for eggnog or Tom and Jerry parties.
Yields six dozen cookies.
Thaw broccoli and by hand squeeze out water.
Mix all ingredients well with a wooden spoon.
Use a well-greased oblong pan (9 x 13-inches).
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serve hot.
Cook grits in 3 cups water.
Let cool or may be cold.
Add other ingredients and bake at 375° until done.
Place 20-inch sheet of foil on baking sheet; brush with margarine.
Lay pieces of meat in center.
Combine next 7 ingredients and spread evenly over meat.
Mix A.1. and cornstarch and pour over meat.
Fold foil to seal tightly.
Bake 2 hours in 375° oven.
Mix and put in baking dish.
Cook until thick.
Add 6 slices fat-free cheese.
Cut 30 ounces potatoes into baking dish.
Cover with ingredients and bake at 425° for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender.

Fry bacon. Drain grease. Crumble into small pieces. Saute onions in bacon grease. In another pan, put potatoes, carrots and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil until potatoes and carrots are soft. Add bacon, onion, 1 cup milk and soup. Cook until hot, but do not boil. When all is hot, add shredded Cheddar cheese.
Cook macaroni as package directs; drain.
Mix ingredients together using only 1/2 of the grated cheese. Reserve 1/2 (or rest) of the grated cheese for top.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle top with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly and crusty.
Heat oven to 375°.
Note:
Do not preheat oven until you are ready to slice cookies.

recipes.t: Grits Casserole A La Donna Ford
d: Cook grits until medium consistency.
While grits are cooking, brown sausage.
Grate cheese.
Beat the eggs slightly.
Fry sausage until done.
Drain real well.
In a crock-pot, add all ingredients, except chips.
Heat until all is mixed well. Serve hot with chips.
Preheat oven to 200°.
Lightly oil a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with oil.
Place popcorn in oiled pan and keep popcorn warm in oven while preparing peanut butter syrup.
In a large saucepan, combine brown sugar, peanut butter, corn syrup, water, oil and salt.
Bring to a boil, stirring frequently.
Stir in baking soda and quickly pour syrup over popcorn.
Gently stir until popcorn is well coated. Bake at 200° for 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Stir and let cool.
Break into clusters.
Store in airtight container.
Makes 12 cups caramel corn.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Add cold water, vinegar, mayonnaise, salt and pepper.
Blend with rotary beater.
Pour into refrigerator tray.
Quick chill in freezing unit until firm, about 1-inch from edge, but soft in the center, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Flatten biscuits.
Brown ground beef in skillet and drain. Put pizza sauce on biscuits and top with ground beef and then both cheeses.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes or until done.
Dip choplets in soy milk mixture, then in bread crumbs.
Place in skillet with small amount of olive oil.
Fry until brown; turn choplets over.
Place sliced onion on top of choplets.
To the broth, add the George Washington seasoning and enough water to make 1/2 can.
Pour over choplets.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer until onion is tender.
(Green pepper can be added with the onion.) Delicious.
Combine and refrigerate for 2 hours the ground cranberries and sugar.
Prepare Dream Whip.
Fold in marshmallows.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Combine the two mixtures and add crushed pineapple and pecans.

recipes.t: Barbecued Beef Ribs(Los Angeles Times Cookbook)
d: Arrange beef ribs on rack in baking pan.
Saute onion and garlic in oil until golden.
Add mustard, tomato puree, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, hot pepper sauce, barbecue spice and salt.
Simmer about 15 minutes.
Strain.
Brush barbecue sauce generously over beef ribs, covering them thoroughly.
Bake at 375° to 400° for 45 minutes, basting frequently with sauce until beef ribs are tender and well done.
Store any remaining sauce, covered, in refrigerator.
Cream oleo
and
sugar, add 1 egg at a time.
Add 3 cups flour, flavoring and pecans.
Add 1 cup flour to chopped fruit, then add to mixture.
Makes two cakes, baked in angel food cake pans.
Bake
at 250° until done.
After 1 hour put pan of water under cake.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt chocolate chips, unsweetened chocolate and butter together.
Cool 10 minutes.
Stir in sugar. Add eggs and vanilla, beating by hand until blended.
Stir in flour, baking powder and salt that has been mixed together.
Fold in nuts and white baking chocolate.
Pour into a greased 9-inch square pan.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes until they test done.
Cool. Sift powdered sugar over before cutting into 24 bars.
Blend together the first 3 ingredients; roll into small balls. Melt the last 2 ingredients over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Use small pitcher or creamer to pour chocolate.
Pour a little chocolate into tiny paper cups.
Drop in small peanut butter ball.
Pour more chocolate on top.
Let stand until hard. These freeze well.
Let fish defrost (block) just long enough so that you can cut it into 4 or 5 pieces.
Place in casserole with enough oil on the bottom of the casserole to keep from sticking at 400°
for about 15 to 20 minutes.

Prepare the fettuccine according to package directions. Meanwhile, combine cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, margarine and milk in a saucepan. Stir over low heat until smooth. Combine with hot cooked noodles. Add cooked small shrimp or imitation crab or lobster meat to the sauce to make a delicious seafood alfredo.
Cook potatoes in boiling salted water for 15 minutes or until tender; drain well.
Meanwhile, saute garlic and green onion in butter for 2 minutes or until softened.

Bake 25 minutes.
Crumble 2 tostada shells on each of 6 salad plates.
Layer half each of the chicken pieces and Mexican Coleslaw on crumbled tostadas.
Top with cheese, remaining chicken and coleslaw, olives and orange wedges.
Sprinkle with chili powder.
Top with taco sauce.
Yields 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients in a large pan with a lid; use a whisk to mix.
Insert meat, making sure all meat is covered.
Replace lid to pan and place pan in refrigerator at least 24 hours.
Prepare meat before sauce.
Cut off all fat and sinue.
Drain beets, reserving juice.
Mix sugar, salt, vinegar, water and beet juice in a small saucepan.
Heat until sugar dissolves.
Peel eggs.
Put beets and eggs in a bowl.
Cover with the liquid and refrigerate for several days.
Separate eggs.
Place egg yellow in saucepan along with sugar and milk.
After adding milk, fill 1/2 can with water and pour into mixture.
Bring to rapid boil.
Stir constantly.
Boil until thick and creamy.
Add extract.
Remove from heat.
Slice bananas. Place vanilla wafers in pan and layer bananas.
Repeat once and pour sauce over it.
Place egg white in bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons sugar and beat until fluffy.
Place over pudding.
Refrigerate until cool.
You can not eat just 1 bowl!
Cut vegetables and cover with water in large pot.
Boil 30 minutes.
Cover, lower heat and simmer until soft.
Try pepper, garlic or bouillon cube to season.
Melt margarine. Add eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Cook slowly until eggs begin to set. Add cream cheese.
Mix lettuce, broccoli, onions and oranges. Brown nuts and noodles (crushed) in butter. Put nut and noodle mixture over lettuce mixture just before serving.
Brown the ground beef.
Drain and rinse meat. Salt and sprinkle on chili powder.
In Dutch oven, layer meat, sliced onions, potatoes and carrots.
Finish with onions.
Pour the tomatoes over layers. Bake, uncovered, until potatoes and carrots test tender. Great with cornbread!
Beat all ingredients together until light and fluffy.
Tastes like whipped cream.
Cook potatoes in boiling, salted water 10 minutes and drain. Melt margarine; stir in flour, mustard, salt and pepper.
Add milk gradually while stirring.
Cook over low heat until smooth and thickened.
Arrange potatoes, tuna and onions in alternate layers in greased 2-quart casserole dish.
Pour sauce over and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Grate cabbage and sprinkle 1/2 cup sugar on top.
Bring to boil, salt, mustard, celery seed, oil, vinegar and 1 tablespoon sugar.
Pour over cabbage.
Cover and refrigerate.
In heavy skillet melt butter or margarine.
Stir in rest of ingredients.
Toss until nuts are coated.
Place in single layer on 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1 baking pan.
Bake in 300° oven for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often till nuts are brown and crisp.
Makes about 4 1/4 cups.
Saute onions and mushrooms in butter.
Add soup and milk; stir.
Remove from heat.
Add the egg and mayonnaise.
Stir in stuffing, then fold in crabmeat.
Pour mixture into greased baking dish.
Top with shredded cheese.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. This is very rich and will serve small portions to 5 or 6.
Double the recipe for a larger group.
Slice mushrooms; saute in 2 tablespoons margarine until golden.
Remove mushrooms and reserve.
Add remaining margarine to pan; brown chicken well.
Sprinkle with Beau Monde during browning.
Add mushrooms; sprinkle with tarragon.
Pour wine over chicken.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Spoon sour cream into pan juices; sprinkle with green onion to serve.
Serve with rice.
Place butter in a baking dish in oven to melt.
Mix flour, milk and 1/2 cup of sugar; set aside.
Pour 1/2 cup of sugar over peaches.
Pour flour mixture over butter in baking dish.
Do not stir.
Last, pour fruit on top.
Do not stir.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Boil chicken 1 hour.
Cut cooled chicken into cubes and line a 9 x 13-inch baking dish with the chicken.
Add the soup, milk, salt and pepper to the chicken, then add the dressing.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Remove foil and bake 10 minutes or until brown.
Combine chicken, vegetables and water to cover in a saucepan. Cook chicken until tender.
Remove and chop chicken into pieces; set aside.
Combine rice with broth in a saucepan.
Cook just until rice is tender.
Season to your taste.
Beat egg yolks and lemon juice; whisk a small amount of hot liquid (soup) into egg mixture. Then whisk egg mix back into soup.
Add chicken.
Heat just to serve.
Cream butter and sugar in mixer bowl.
Blend in eggs, vanilla and bananas.
Add flour and salt alternately with sour milk, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in baking powder and soda. Pour into greased cake pan.
Bake at 375° for 25 minutes.
Cool completely.
Frost with whipped cream.
Garnish with cherries. Refrigerate.
Saute onion in butter.
Add flour and blend well.
Stir in milk and cook for several minutes, stirring constantly until it comes to a boil.
Turn off heat.
Add cheese, salmon, salt and pepper and mix well.
Place mixture in greased casserole and top with biscuits.
Bake in 425° oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix eggs, baking powder, salt, mayonnaise, lemon juice and hot sauce.
Add cleaned shrimp.
Let stand for 1/2 hour to soak all flavorings.
Prepare flour, seasoned fish fry and baking powder. Roll shrimp into this mixture and fry in frypan.
Thoroughly mix ingredients.
Roll into long roll and place in refrigerator to chill well.
When ready, slice and bake 8 to 10 minutes in 350° oven.
Preheat
oven
Grind almonds to a coarse cornmeal like
consistency.	Melt
butter
in a small pan over low heat until clear.
Add all other ingredients to the butter and heat until the mixture is well blended.	Drop by teaspoons onto a Teflon
cookie
sheet
about
5 inches apart.
Bake only one sheet at
a
time, for about 5 minutes or until the now spread out wafers are a light golden brown.
Remove the pan and let it cool for about 30 seconds before beginning to take up the first wafer. A
Teflon
spatula works well here.
Roll up as soon as the
wafer is
manageable,
leaving
the hole through the roll about	3/4 inches in diameter. Roll with the crunchy side out. This
must
be done
quickly,
but
if the mixture becomes too brittle, put the pan back into the oven to soften wafers again. When
rolls	are cool and hard, dip each end into melted chocolate and
fill
with unsweetened whipped cream, using a pastry bag that you
can
make of	waxed
paper if you don't have one already.
Saute onion, ground beef and peppers.
Add enchilada sauce, 1 can chicken soup.
Cut tortillas in strips and line casserole with them.
Add layers of meat mixture and cheese.
Sprinkle top with cheese.
Bake in oven at 350° for 20 minutes.
In mixing bowl, thoroughly stir together the flour, sugar, salt and baking soda.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients.
Combine egg, bananas, oil, undrained pineapple and vanilla.
Add all at once to dry ingredients, stirring until well blended.
Pour the batter into the greased and floured fluted tube pan (Bundt pan).
Bake at 350° for 65 to 70 minutes.
Cool on rack.
Put homemade vanilla frosting or Cream Cheese Frosting on it.
Wash
raisins in hot water and drain.
Cream shortening with sugar,
then
add
beaten
eggs
and milk.	Combine with oatmeal and
raisins; mix well.
Add flour, sifted with soda, salt	and cinnamon.
Beat thoroughly.
Drop onto greased pans and bake about 12 minutes in a 350° oven.	Makes about 3 dozen medium-sized cookies.
Mix first 3 ingredients together, Bake in a lightly greased 9 x 9 inch pan at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done.
Cool and crumble in large bowl. Stir together rest of ingredients and add crumbled bread, mix well.
Keep refrigerated
overnight. This dish keeps for 3 or 4 days. Optional, top with grated cheese and /or crumbled bacon.
Cut potatoes and sausage into bite size pieces.
Place all ingredients in a large pot or Dutch oven and cook on low heat until potatoes are done (about 25 or 30 minutes).
Serve with rolls or cornbread.
Blend all ingredients, except ham.
Spread mix on ham slices, roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Cut into thirds.
Chill for 1/2 hour.
Mix sugar and cinnamon in bowl.
Spread 1 tablespoon of butter on each slice of bread.
Sprinkle sugar-cinnamon mixture on bread. Bake for 5 minutes at 400°. Top with nuts or raisins.
Serve with a glass of milk.
Makes 2 servings.
Cook onion and pepper in shortening until tender.
Add ground beef and brown.
Add tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes. Add pinto beans and seasonings; simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve with warm cornbread.
Mix first 2 ingredients.
Add eggs, one at a time and blend. Add remaining ingredients, beat smooth.
Pour in floured, greased tube pan and place in cold oven.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a 2-quart baking dish, toss together the apples, granulated sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice.
In a large bowl, combine flour, oats, brown sugar and salt.

Preheat oven to 350°. Grease an 8 x 11-inch glass baking dish. Mix together eggs, flour, salt, milk, chiles, Cheddar and Jack cheeses. Pour into prepared baking dish. Bake in preheated oven 35 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes before cutting in squares.
Place chops on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Slice potatoes over top of chops to cover.
Slice cabbage over top of potatoes to cover.
Slice onions over top of cabbage.
Mix mushroom soup with only enough water to rinse can out.
Pour over all layers in dish.
Add salt and pepper. Cook 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until chops are tender.
Saute one large onion in microwave for three minutes with 2 to 3 tablespoons of water.
Cut up raw or frozen asparagus.
Microwave with 1/2 cup water for 7 to 8 minutes until tender.
Puree in blender.
Add puree, chicken bouillon cubes, 3 cups water and 2 cups of cut up pieces of asparagus and sauteed onions.
Cook until asparagus are done.
Add light oleo and skim evaporated milk.
Heat until starting to boil.
Stir often, as will stick and burn.
Mix flour in 1 cup water until smooth.
Add to soup until slightly thickened.
Add light Velveeta cheese.

Thaw spinach; drain well by squeezing water out with hands. Divide spinach equally into bottom of two unbaked pie shells. Sprinkle 1/2 cup of each cheese (Mozzarella, Cheddar, Swiss) into each pie shell.
Mix eggs, milk, Worcestershire sauce and onions with wire whisk in a bowl.
Pour egg mixture evenly into pie shells.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350° and bake for an additional 15 minutes.
Let cool 10 minutes before cutting.
In a medium saucepan, melt margarine over low heat.
Add chocolate and stir just until melted.
Remove from heat; stir in sweetener and vanilla.
Add cream cheese and beat until smooth. Stir in nuts.
Spread mixture in a buttered 8-inch square pan. Cover and refrigerate until firm.
Cut into 1-inch squares. Store in an airtight container in refrigerator.
Yields 64 squares of fudge.
Combine tuna, celery, raisins and green onion in a small bowl. In a measuring cup, stir together mayonnaise, lemon juice, curry and salt.
Fold in tuna mixture.
Toast English muffins. Immediately spoon tuna mixture on muffins.
Top each sandwich with slice of cheese.
Broil for 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese melts. Serve hot, garnish with celery leaves.
Makes 4 sandwiches.
Place 4 of the bread slices in bottom of buttered baking pan. Mix mayonnaise with fish and vegetables and 1 can of soup.
Spread evenly over bread.
Cover this with balance of bread and pour over it the eggs and milk, which have been well mixed.
Let stand at least 4 hours or overnight.
Bake 20 minutes in a 325° oven. Remove from oven and spread remaining can of soup, cheese and sprinkle with paprika.
Return to oven to finish baking, 45 to 50 minutes.
Dump in a 9 x 13-inch cake pan, but do not mix.
Sprinkle with coconut and chopped nuts.
Bake at 350° about 1 hour.
Combine flour, 1 cup sugar and salt.
Dissolve cocoa in water. Add with mixture to milk and cook in double boiler until thickened.
Add egg yolks.
Remove from heat and add vanilla. Pour into cooled pie shell.
Beat egg whites with 3/8 cup sugar until fluffy.
Spread over filling.
Bake at 300° until golden brown.
Yield: 6 servings.

Grate, grind or chop the peeled carrots,add the chopped pimentos or chopped red pepper.Add the chopped parsley. In a mug put about 1/3 to 1/2 cup of salad vinegar. Add honey one Tbsp. at a time until the mixture is sweet to your taste,be sure to stir this mixture all the time,then add a dash of salt and pour over the veggies. Let it chill in the refrigerator overnight or for several hours to blend flavors.

With electric mixer, cream together butter, salt, vanilla and powdered sugar until light and fluffy. At low speed, add flour and oats until just mixed. Form dough into large or small canes. Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Place cherry halves on canes and bake in a preheated 325° oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until lightly golden brown.

Beat cream cheese, egg yolks, heavy cream, egg, pepper and salt until smooth and blended. Cut bacon in 1-inch pieces and cook until lightly browned and crisp. Arrange the bacon in the pie shell. Pour cheese mix over bacon and bake in preheated 400° oven for 20 minutes. Reduce heat to 350° and bake 10 minutes longer or until puffed and golden brown. Let stand a few minutes and serve hot. Serves 4 to 6.
Boil sugar in quart of water until melted.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Cool both liquids.
Mix with other liquids.
Add ice to serve.
You can break this down to the amount you need.
Serves 100.
Line bottom of rectangular pan with beef.
Roll chicken with bacon slice, skewer with toothpicks.
Lay on top of beef.
Mix soup and cheese.
Add 1/2 soup can of water, mix and pour over chicken.
Cover with foil and bake 3 hours at 325°.
This is excellent served with rice pilaf.
Combine sugar, milk, chocolate, corn syrup and salt in saucepan.
Stir over medium heat until chocolate melts and sugar dissolves.
Cook to 234° or until a little dropped in cold water forms a soft ball.
Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Add butter.
Cool to lukewarm without stirring.
Add vanilla.
Beat until thick and no longer glossy.
Quickly stir in nuts.
Pour into buttered 8 to 9-inch
square pan.
When set, cut into squares.
With electric mixer, beat ham and cream cheese together until smooth.
Stir in pineapple, green onion and honey.
Spread 1/4 cup ham mixture on each tortilla to within 1/2-inch of edges.
Roll up each tortilla starting from one edge.
Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate 2 to 8 hours before serving.
In a large saucepan, bring water to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Add drink mix, sugar and coffee; stir until dissolved. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
In a bowl, combine sugar, flour, cinnamon and allspice.
Add the peaches and blueberries; toss gently.
Line pie plate with bottom crust.
Add the filling.
Dot with butter.
Top with a lattice crust.
Brush crust with milk.
Sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar.
Bake at 400° for 40 to 45 minutes or until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly.
Cool.
Season shrimp in shell with salt, black pepper, red pepper and garlic powder.
Put shrimp in hot oil or butter and stir until all shrimp turn pink.
Add onions, celery and bell pepper.
Mix well; cook, covered, for 15 minutes.
When done, using slotted spoon, move shrimp to platter.
Serve juice in small bowls.
When eating, suck on shrimp first, then peel shrimp.
Can be dipped in juice or dip juice with French bread.
Serve with green salad.
Delicious! If real hungry, double recipe.
Soften yeast in water; pour milk over cornmeal, salt, sugar and shortening.
Cool.
Beat in eggs and 2 cups flour.
Add yeast and mix well.
Stir in flour.
Cover and let rise until double in bulk, about 1 hour.
Stir down; spoon into greased muffin cups.
Fill about 1/3 full.
Cover and let rise until double in bulk.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 400°.
Brush with melted butter.
Makes about 2 dozen.
In saucepan, bring water and butter to the boil until all butter is melted.
All at once, add flour and salt; beat until mixture forms a ball that leaves the sides of the saucepan.
Cool slightly.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly after each addition.
Spread pastry mixture onto an ungreased jellyroll pan or cookie sheet.
Bake in 400° oven for 35 minutes.
Remove from oven; pierce bubbles with fork while hot.
Cool completely.
Lay out sweet potato slices in a buttered baking dish or pan. Mix remaining ingredients, except butter, and pour over potatoes. Dot with butter.
Place in oven and bake for 35 minutes at 350°.
Boil noodles in salted water until tender; drain.
Set aside. Melt butter or margarine in a Dutch oven or heavy pot.
Fry coarsely chopped cabbage in butter until lightly browned.
Cut Spam into 1/2 inch cubes and add to cooked cabbage.
Cook 5 minutes longer.
Mix in boiled noodles and add pepper to taste.
Brown and crumble sausage in skillet.
Drain well.
Return to stove and add stick of butter.
Stir until melted and mix with sausage.
Add Cheez Whiz and combine with sausage.
Place English muffin halves on cookie sheet and top with sausage mixture.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook
meats and other ingredients; add 2 cups water.
When ready, add mashed potatoes and put in crusts.
Peel onions. Cut a slice off top and bottom so onions sit flat in a baking dish, just big enough to hold them.
Combine stock, wine, salt, pepper, rosemary and thyme.
Pour over onions, cover with foil and bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Turn onions over and bake 30 more minutes.
Pour off liquid, sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and return to oven for 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve immediately.
Mix soup, margarine and Cheez Whiz in a large saucepan and heat until well blended.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour. Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Brown meat.
Add onions, pepper, sauce, beans and Tabasco. Add water if it seems dry.
Simmer, for taste.
Cook over medium heat until thickened.
If not all used, stores a long time in refrigerator.
Cook yolks of eggs, lemon
juice and mustard in double boiler until thick.
Cool.
Add this mixture to the whipping cream.
Add fruit and put in refrigerator for 6 hours.
Do not freeze. Serves 8.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Lightly oil a baking pan large enough to hold 4 catfish in a single layer.
Rub cut side of garlic into pan. Combine beaten egg and milk in shallow dish.
Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and seasonings in another dish.
Dip each fillet into egg mixture and roll in Parmesan mixture; coat completely. Arrange fillets on baking pan and drizzle remaining oil on top. Bake 20 minutes until fish is flaky.
Remove the stalks, tips and tough outer leaves of the artichokes. Keep the artichokes in cold water and lemon juice until ready for cooking (this will prevent them from turning black).
Place artichokes in a pan (in which they fit tightly). Add all the other ingredients with just enough water to cover. Bring to a boil.
Cover the pot and let simmer over reduced heat for a few minutes.
Uncover the pot and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes.
Place in serving dish.
Serve hot or cold.
Makes 6 servings.
Serve with Fontana Candida, the light, sophisticated wine of Rome.
Heat
oil in uncovered wok or pan.
Add next 4 ingredients; stir-fry 1 minute.	Add remaining ingredients; cover and cook until
beans
are
crisp-tender (5 to 7 minutes).
Serve immediately.
Serves 4.
Combine first 3 ingredients.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Cool. Cream the powdered sugar, cream cheese and 1 cup whipped topping.
Spread on crust.
Combine pudding and milk until firm.
Pour over mixture.
Spread whipped topping over pudding.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Brown the ground beef and drain the fat, then add in the onions, peppers, salt, pepper and garlic.
Add mashed tomatoes and a can of tomato sauce or tomato juice and bring to a boil.
Add in rice and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
Add more tomatoes or juice, if necessary.
In frying pan, combine first 3 ingredients.
Brown thoroughly and drain.
Combine tomatoes, sauce, paste and meat mixture in large pot.
Mix well and cook for 10 minutes on medium heat.
Stir in oregano, bay leaf and garlic salt.
Cook sauce, uncovered, on low for 30 minutes.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine and mix dry ingredients.
Add and mix lightly remaining ingredients.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan (spray with Pam first).
Bake 25 minutes.
Cream shortening and butter; add sugar, egg and almond extract.
Then add flour, salt and baking powder.
Fold in cherries and coconut.
Drop by teaspoonful on greased baking sheets.
Flatten slightly.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes. Makes 3 dozen.
Mix all ingredients together; roll out on floured board and cut cookies.
Bake at 325° to 350°.
Check for doneness after 15 minutes.
Spread butter or margarine on bread. Place in 13 x 9 x 2-inch greased baking dish.
Set aside.
Cook sausage until brown, stirring to crumble; drain well.
Spoon over bread slices; sprinkle with cheese.
Combine eggs, half and half (may substitute whole milk) and salt; mix well and pour over cheese.
Cover and chill overnight.
Remove from refrigerator 15 minutes before baking.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook both puddings and jello with 3 cups of water until thick.
Cool. Add Cool Whip and mandarin orange slices.
Spread bread with butter.
Place in greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch casserole.
Crumble sausage into skillet.
Cook, stirring to keep it in small pieces until no longer pink.
Lift with slotted spoon. Spread over bread.
Sprinkle cheese over sausage.
In bowl, combine eggs, half and half and salt.
Mix well and pour over cheese. Cover and chill overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Remove casserole from refrigerator at same time letting stand 15 minutes to come to room temperature.
Bake strata, uncovered, until set, about 45 minutes.
Let stand a few minutes before cutting into squares. Makes 8 to 12 servings.
Preheat oven to 325°.
In large bowl, beat eggs until foamy, then beat in flour, sugar and brown sugar until well blended. Blend in melted butter.
Stir in chocolate chips and walnuts. Pour into pie shell and bake at 325°
for 1 hour.
Pour butter, sugar and milk in pan.
Heat to boiling.
Remove from heat.
Combine Quaker oats and vanilla.
Pour mixture from pan over oats.
Stir well.
Add cocoa and peanut butter.
Mix well.
Spoon onto wax paper on a cookie sheet.
Put in refrigerator for 1 hour or until firm.
Spread pudding on cooled cake.
Top with drained pineapple and then Cool Whip.
Garnish with cherries and nuts.
Keep chilled.
