Pour soda and boiling water over dates and raisins; set aside. Cream butter and sugar.
Add vanilla, then egg.
Beat well.
Add flour and mix.
Pour in fruit mixture, water and pecans.
Mix and bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes in 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
In a skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat.
Saute squash and onion until crisp-tender.
Remove from heat; stir in chilies, crackers, salt and pepper.
Spoon into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes. Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Cook macaroni, rinse and drain.
Combine all ingredients and toss.
Add mayonnaise and mix.
Refrigerate for 1 hour; serve.
Reserving half of noodles and nuts, mix all ingredients in casserole dish.
Sprinkle remaining noodles and nuts on top.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 350° about 30 minutes, or until heated through.
Cream the butter, sugars, egg yolks and water.
Add flour, soda, baking powder, salt and vanilla.
Put on greased cookie sheet and pat out thin.
Sprinkle with chocolate chips.
Beat 2 egg whites until stiff; add 1 cup brown sugar.
Spread over cookie dough.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix flour, margarine and pecans together for crust; pat into a 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Let cool.
Cream together powdered sugar and cream cheese; fold in half of the Cool Whip whipped topping.
Spread over cooled crust.
Beat together pudding mix and milk for 2 to 3 minutes, stir in vanilla.
Spread over cream cheese layer, then spread the remaining half of the whipped topping over the butterscotch layer.
Top with a few additional chopped pecans.
Refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours or overnight before serving.

Mix dry ingredients and cut in shortening as per pie. Mix in eggs. Put half in bottom of 9 x 13 cookie sheet. Top with pie filling. Sprinkle with remaining dough. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until browned.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Steam broccoli, onion and pimento in 2-quart casserole dish sprayed with nonstick spray.
In blender or food processor, combine the rest of the ingredients.
Pour over broccoli.
Bake 35 minutes or until knife comes out clean.
Mix together.
Chill overnight in the refrigerator.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add onion, vinegar and salt. Chill until mixture begins to set.
Add cucumber and mayonnaise. Garnish with pimentos or tomato slices.
Combine.
Spread over chicken pieces.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Blueberry Crumb Bake With Tangy Yogurt Cream
d: Heat oven to 400°.
Butter a round 10-inch baking dish.
Toss blueberries with lemon zest.
In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of flour with the sugar.
Using your fingertips, cut in butter until it resembles coarse meal.
Set 1 1/2 cups of the mixture aside for the crumb topping.

In a small bowl, lightly beat the egg. Stir in the yogurt and lemon juice. Add to the dry ingredients in the large bowl and stir briefly until blended. Fold in 1 cup of the blueberries. Spread the batter in the dish and scatter the remaining 1 1/2 cups of blueberries on top. Sprinkle the reserved crumb mixture over the blueberries.
Set the dish on a cookie sheet and bake for about 1 hour.
Serve warm with the Yogurt Cream on the side.
Sprinkle fryers with salt, pepper and paprika.
Fry until brown in one cube margarine.
Place in casserole dish(es).
Brown sliced mushrooms.
Add flour, broth, rosemary and sherry; cover and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Add egg and mix.
Sift together flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and soda and stir into egg mixture.
Stir in apples, nuts and vanilla.
Pour into greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Trim crust from bread and flatten with a rolling pin.
Mix cream cheese, egg yolks and 1/2 cup sugar.
Spread with cream cheese mixture and roll each slice of bread like a jelly roll.
Dip in melted butter and roll in mixture of 1/2 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Place on a cookie sheet and freeze.
Prepare noodles according to package directions.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In medium skillet, brown meat and drain well.
Add onion, green pepper and sauce; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat.
In 9 x 13-inch baking dish, layer noodles, sauce and Velveeta cheese.
Repeat layers, ending with Velveeta cheese.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Mix altogether in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Bake cake mix according to directions.
Prick with fork.
Mix cream of coconut and Eagle Brand milk together and pour over cake. Spread with Cool Whip and coconut when cool.
Sift together in a large bowl 2 Kings 4:22, Jeremiah 6:20, Leviticus 2:13, Amos 4:5 and 1 Chronicles 9:9.
Add Judges 5:25, 1 Samuel 14:25 and Judges 4:19.
Beat until smooth.
Add Jeremiah 17:11.
Beat for 5 minutes by hand; add 1 Samuel 30:12.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
(Find the ingredients by looking up the Bible verses.)
This mixture may be made in advance and kept in a covered jar in the icebox.
It can be used over any fresh, canned or frozen fruit.
Cook raisins and water until water is gone.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cool all ingredients.
Roll into 1-inch balls, then roll in sugar.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Beat eggs.
Combine with all ingredients.
Pour into greased casserole.
Bake, covered, thirty minutes at 350°.
Uncover and bake a few minutes longer.
Mix all ingredients except chips in a bowl with lid.
Store in refrigerate overnight, then 30 minutes before serving, add the corn chips and stir to mix well.
Put fruit cocktail and water in large saucepan.
Add jello and cook until dissolved.
Cool.
Add cottage cheese and Cool Whip and stir until well mixed.
Refrigerate until set, about 6 hours or overnight.
Brown beef and onion together.
Drain off fat.
Place beef and onion in large kettle and add other ingredients.
Let simmer for about 2 hours.
In small saucepan, cook and stir butter and brown sugar over low heat until brown sugar melts and mixture bubbles.
Remove from heat and add pecans.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Prepare pudding mix according to package directions for pie filling.
Cool slightly.
Pour over butter and brown sugar mixture.
Chill 4 hours or until firm.
Just before serving, garnish with whipped topping.

recipes.t: Creamed Eggs And Medium White Sauce
d: Boil eggs and let cool.
Slice eggs.
Melt 1/2 stick butter in saucepan. Stir in enough flour to make thick.
Add approximately 1 1/2 cups milk. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Stir together until thick. Add cheese.
If this does not get thick, you may have to mix more butter and flour together for thickening.
Use your own judgement.
Layer eggs in baking dish.
Pour sauce over eggs. Continue to layer until gone.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Turn into greased 13 x 9 pan and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and pour onto griddle on low heat.
Makes 9 to 10 pancakes.
Place bottom crust in 8-inch pie pan.
Spread diced potatoes evenly over bottom crust.
Sprinkle minced onion over potatoes. Spread pieces of pork evenly on top of potatoes and onion.
Season to taste.
Cover with vented top pie crust and bake at 350° for 1 hour.

recipes.t: Pumpkin Layer Pie(Low Sugar For Diabetics)
d: Mix cream cheese, 1 tablespoon milk and Equal until smooth. Stir in whipped topping and spread on crust.
Pour 1 cup milk into bowl; add pudding mix and beat with mixer until blended (1 to 2 minutes).
Stir in pumpkin and spices and mix well.
Spread over cheese layer.
Refrigerate 3 hours.
Garnish with Cool Whip.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Blend in eggs and vanilla; mix well.
Sift together flour, salt and baking soda. Mix into sugar mixture until well blended.
Chill 2 hours.
In small bowl beat cream cheese and pineapple until combined. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. roll in 1 inch balls.
Roll in coconut.
Refrigerate overnight or 6 hours.
Serve.
Combine all ingredients in a medium saucepan, stirring until well blended.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour, uncovered, stirring occasionally.
Cut whole breasts in half.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper in bowl.
Combine bread crumbs, garlic powder and cheese.
Dip chicken in eggs, then coat with crumbs.
Melt butter and oil in skillet.
When butter foams, add chicken.
Cook over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden.
Add Marsala.
Cover skillet and reduce heat.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
If sauce looks too dry, add more Marsala.
Turn chicken several times.
Melt margarine in rectangular baking dish.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs over melted margarine.
Sprinkle coconut, then fruit.
Cut dates in small pieces and mix with a small amount of flour to keep them from sticking together.
Sprinkle dates, then nuts over mixture.
Press lightly with hands to level.
Pour milk evenly over top and bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Bring sugar, butter and milk to a boil; boil 5 minutes. Add Hershey bar, marshmallow cream and chocolate chips; beat well. Add nuts. Pour into large buttered cookie sheet; cool. Cut into squares.
Mix cake and bake in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Cool.
Cut half of cake in cubes; reserve other half for another dessert.
Dissolve Danish dessert in 3 1/2 cups cold water.
Bring to boil 1 minute, stirring constantly until thick and clear.
Cool.
Add strawberries.
Spread over cake cubes in pan.
Mix pudding, milk and sour cream until smooth.
Spread over strawberries.
Top with Cool Whip.
Garnish with almonds.
Mix 2 cups of crushed graham crackers, 1/2 cup of sugar and 1/4 cup of melted butter.
Spread in pan.
Bake 10 minutes in 350° oven.
Take out and pour on 1 (14 ounce can) of sweetened condensed milk (if you like gooey bars, add another can).
Sread 2 cups of coconut over milk.
Bake 10 minutes in 350° oven.
Turn off oven.
Spread 1 package of chocolate chips over bars and let chocolate melt in oven.
When melted, spread evenly.
Grind together raisins, prunes and carrots.
Mix this with all the ingredients and bake at 350° until done, 30 to 40 minutes.
Shred
cabbage
fine.
Salt
and
pepper to taste.
Cut apples in slices and add to cabbage.
Heat fat in frypan.
Add a
little boiling water to the cabbage and cook in the frypan until tender. Sprinkle with flour.
Add sugar and vinegar and cook a bit longer. Serve hot.
Sprinkle meat strips with salt and pepper.
Brown in oil.
Add onion, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder. Cover and cook 1 1/2 hours on low heat.
Turn heat to medium, add bell pepper.
Cover and cook until tender, about 30 minutes. Serve over rice.
Using plenty of flour, roll out 1 loaf bread dough into oblong (rectangular) shape.
Mix oregano with beaten eggs.
Brush surface of bread dough with egg mixture.
Sprinkle half of the sausage over surface of bread dough.
Sprinkle half of each of the cheeses over the sausage.
From the long side of bread dough, roll the dough over until it meets the edge of the other long side.
Bring the ends of the roll together to make a circle and press edges closed to hold in melted cheese.
Brush top of roll with egg mixture.
Repeat process for second loaf.
Add more eggs and oregano, if needed.
Bake each on greased cookie sheet (or similar) at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cook all together 20 minutes.
Put in jar and seal.
Cut steak into serving pieces.
Heat oil in skillet and brown steak pieces.
Remove steak from skillet and drain.
Place carrot and onion in bottom of slow cooker.
Place steak on top.
Sprinkle salt and pepper.
Place tomatoes on top.
Pour broth over layers. Cover.
Cook on low for 6 hours.
If you use a more tender meat, such as rib eye steak or rump roast, cooking can be shorter.
Serve over rice, potatoes or noodles.
Serves 4.
Soften in microwave the butter and margarine.
Do not completely melt.
Add sour cream and stir well.
Add flour and mix well.
Spoon into 1 3/4-inch muffin tins and bake at 350° for about 20 minutes until golden.
Makes 3 dozen.
Saute onion slightly in margarine.
Add soup and milk.
Mix in cheese, broccoli, rice and water chestnuts; simmer 10 minutes. Pour into a large, greased casserole dish.
Bake 1 hour at 325°. (Mixture should be creamy, not dry.) Casserole can be made a day or two ahead or frozen for later use.
Mix
syrup,
oleo
and sugar;
bring to a boil.
Boil 6 minutes
(until thread forms when dropped from spoon).
Remove from
heat.
Add
cream
of tartar, soda and salt.	Stir until well mixed.
Pour over popped corn; stir until all kernels are coated.
Place
in container that can be placed in oven.
Bake 1 hour at 200°, stirring often.
Keep in airtight container.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Remove to paper towels, crumble and set aside.
Drain all but 2 tablespoons of drippings.
Saute onion and celery in drippings, until onion is lightly browned.
Add potatoes and water.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in corn, milk, sausage, dill and bacon.
Cook until the potatoes are tender, about 30 minutes.
Makes 4 (6 ounce) servings.
Place potatoes in large salad bowl.
Separate eggs.
Chop whites and add to potatoes with onion.
Toss gently.
In another bowl, mash yolks with mayonnaise, cream, vinegar, sugar, mustard and salt.
Pour over potatoes and stir to coat.
Cover and chill. Yields 16 to 20 servings.
Mix sauce ingredients and simmer 5 minutes.
Pour over wings and toss lightly to coat.
Bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Thaw bread dough.
When thawed, break half the loaf into small pieces and place in well-greased pie plate.
Melt margarine in saucepan, adding dry pudding, brown sugar, cinnamon and milk. Bring just to a boil.
Pour over broken pieces.
Add walnuts or pecans, if desired.
Break up remaining bread dough and place on top.
Let rise to top of pan and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until brown.
Invert on plate and serve warm.

recipes.t: Mexican Pork Or Beef Chile Verde(Microwave)
d: In 2-quart casserole dish, combine onion and garlic.
Cover. Microwave High 2 minutes.
Stir in meat in cubes, flour, salt and pepper.
Add tomatoes and green chiles.
Stir to break up tomatoes.
Cover.
Microwave High 5 minutes.
Stir.
Reduce power. Cover for 30 minutes.
Stir.
Microwave uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until meat is tender.
Serve with warm tortillas.
Serves 4 to 6.
Total Cooking Time:
57 minutes.
Mix all ingredients well.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until done.
Let cool.
Soak chicken in beaten eggs at least 2 hours, better if overnight.
Roll the chicken in bread crumbs.
(I use the Italian seasoning crumbs.)
Brown pieces in skillet in butter or oleo. Place chicken in baking dish.
Do not pile chicken on top of pieces, just one layer.
Add mushrooms, including juice.
Cover container with foil and bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Uncover and put a slice of cheese on each piece.
Put back in oven until cheese melts.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Stir flour and cocoa together; set aside.
In saucepan, melt margarine and shortening.
Mix in sugar, eggs and vanilla; stir until smooth. Blend in flour-cocoa mixture and nuts.
Spread in greased pan. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen 2-inch bars.
Mix all ingredients together and shape in meat loaf shape. Brown top and bottom in frying pan (you can also make individual 1/4 pound loaves).
Add 1 can whole tomatoes with some chopped celery.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Blend above into coarse crumb mixture and press firmly into bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes at 350°.
Cut meat into serving sizes.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Dip meat into 1/4 cup milk, then coat with flour, salt and pepper mixture.
Brown meat on both sides in oil.
Remove to shallow baking dish.
Blend 2 tablespoons flour into oil in skillet.
Stir in milk and soup.
Pour this mixture over meat in baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, 1 1/2 hours in 350° oven.
Melt chocolate chips in microwave; add icing and nuts, pour into cake pan and refrigerate.
Mix dry cake mix with 1 egg and 1/2 cup of oil (makes crunchy bottom layer).
Reserve 1 cup of this mixture and pat out in pan. Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven.
Beat cream cheese, sugar, lemon and egg until light and soft.
Spread this over baked layer and sprinkle with reserved mixture.
Bake at 350° for another 15 minutes.
Allow to cool, then cut into squares.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a casserole.
Mix bread crumbs and butter and sprinkle over top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until browned.
Serves 4.
Simmer until brown.
You may use a crock-pot and cook for several hours.
Yields 5 to 6 dozen.
Cook 1 cup of dry rice in 2 cups of water.
It's better if it stands a little and dries out a bit after cooking, so make the rice early in the day and let it stand then.
In a heavy skillet, brown 4 or 5 slices of bacon until crisp.
Remove the bacon and turn down the heat.
Slightly beat 3 or 4 eggs and pour them in the hot bacon drippings (after removing the bacon).
Add the rice and 3 or 4 cut up green onions.
Mix it all together.
Add the bacon and if you have leftover pieces of pork, beef or ham, chop into small pieces. Last but not least, add soy sauce until the rice is as brown as you like it.
Stir well and simmer on low heat, 15 to 20 minutes, then serve.
Mix sour cream and cream
cheese.
Add
the rest of the ingredients to taste.
Thaw potatoes a little.
Then mix all ingredients and bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Mix all except sour cream.
Pour half of mixture in pan and let congeal.
Spread sour cream on this add remaining half of mixture and let congeal.
Put all ingredients into crock-pot and cook 8 hours.
Before serving, juice may be thickened with flour or cornstarch.
Serve over rice or buttered cooked noodles.
Spread cream cheese on 8 or 9-inch plate.
Add rest of ingredients as listed one by one in layers on plate.
Top with cheese.
Eat with nacho chips.
In a saucepan, pour in cream of chicken soup and water; cook until boiling. Add remaining ingredients. Put in a baking dish and bake for 20 minutes at 350°.
Melt 1 stick margarine and mix with the 2 cups graham cracker crumbs.
Pat mixture firmly in the bottom of an 8 x 11 x 2-inch pan.
In large mixing bowl, mix cream cheese and Cheddar cheese using fork.
Add pepper, garlic salt, onion salt, chopped onions and parsley.
Mix well.
Shape into ball or small log.
Roll in finely chopped pecans and sprinkle generously with paprika.
Wrap in foil and store in refrigerator a day before using.
Serve on crackers. Freezes well.
In skillet, over medium heat, heat chicken in margarine.
Cook chicken 10 minutes or until brown on both sides.
Stir in soup, water and pepper.
Heat until boiling.
Add in broccoli and reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes or until chicken and broccoli is fork-tender.
Boil raisins
and water for 4 minutes.
Cool, add other ingredients.
Mix well.
Fill Number 2 cans half full. Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Mix last 5 ingredients well.
Add the rest of the ingredients and stir or toss to blend.
Refrigerate for several hours before serving.
In a 2-quart casserole, combine all the ingredients except for the croutons. Cook at Medium-high heat 9 to 10 minutes.
Stir twice. Crumble croutons over chicken mixture to form a crust. Continue cooking 4 to 5 minutes.
Melt butter.
Add milk and heat to lukewarm (105° and 115°). Place yeast in a bowl.
Add milk mixture and stir until yeast is dissolved.
Add salt, anise, fennel, cardamon (if used), syrup and rye flour.
Mix.
Add about 3/4 of all-purpose flour.
Knead until dough is soft.
Cover and let rise in warm place for 45 minutes. On lightly floured surface, knead dough until smooth and satin, adding flour as needed.
Roll out to long roll and cut into 12 even pieces.
Form pieces into oblong rolls.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet.
Let rise about 35 minutes.
Bake at 450° for 15 to 18 minutes or until golden brown.
Pour over cucumbers.
Mix and serve.
Very good and low in calories.
Rub garlic halves around a saucepan and discard.
Pour wine and lemon juice into pan and place over low heat.
When liquid is hot, add the cheese cubes and stir until they melt and mixture is blended.
Add cornstarch mixture, pepper and cayenne.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes or until mixture thickens.
Do not allow to boil.
Stir in Kirsch and beat for 1 minute.
Pour cheese mixture into fondue pot over low heat.
Serve with bread cubes.
Makes 6 servings.
Cut frankfurters into 1-inch pieces.
Set aside.
Heat to boiling, chicken broth and water in a heavy saucepan or Dutch oven.
Add macaroni, basil, salt and black pepper.
Return to boiling.
Cook, uncovered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in frankfurters, vegetables and onion.
Simmer 5 minutes longer until macaroni is tender, vegetables are cooked and water is almost all absorbed. Fold in sour cream and mayonnaise.
If used, garnish with chopped fresh green parsley, chives or green peppers before serving.
Arrange slices of potato in rectangular dish, this may require a couple of layers, depending on the size of potatoes.
Cover dish with plastic wrap and microwave on High 4 minutes.
Rotate and microwave another 4 minutes.
When potatoes are cooked, top with grated onion.
Sprinkle with jalapeno; add bacon and cheese. Season very well with salt and pepper.
Microwave on High 2 minutes, uncovered.
Serve.
Mix sugar, cocoa and salt.
Mix well. Add melted butter.
Mix well. Add eggs, vanilla and milk.
Mix well.
Bake at 400° for 10 minutes. Turn to 325° for 25 minutes.
In saucepan, melt butter.
Add remaining ingredients.
Let simmer 10 minutes.
In large bowl add sauce to wings.
You may preboil the wings or use wings frozen.
Put in refrigerator for 2 to 3 hours.
Cover baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes at 375°.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together sugar and cocoa.
Add margarine, water and vanilla.
Beat with electric mixer on low speed until combined.
Beat on medium speed for 1 minute more. Cool for 20 to 30 minutes or until spreading consistency.
Mix all ingredients and pour into a greased and floured bundt pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Check often with toothpick.
If you don't add pecans, you don't have to flour pan.

recipes.t: Italian Casserole(Can Be Frozen; Easy To Make.)
d: Cook and drain macaroni.
Saute sausages, mushrooms and onion in skillet.
Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange layers of macaroni, sausages, mushrooms and onion in two-quart casserole dish.
Top with cheese slices.
Make second layer.
Top with marinara sauce.
Bake in a 375° oven about 30 minutes or until cheese melts.
Serves 6.
Brown onion and garlic in butter in large skillet.
Add meat and brown.
Add salt, pepper, flour and 1 can of soup.
Heat for 5 minutes, covered.
Add other can of soup and heat 10 minutes, covered.
Stir in sour cream and mushrooms (optional) and heat through.
Combine all ingredients and cook slowly for three hours. Place in pint or quart jars.
Soften yeast in lukewarm water.
Pour hot water over sugar and shortening; cool to lukewarm.
Add 1/2 cup flour; mix thoroughly. Stir in softened yeast, half of remaining flour and egg; beat thoroughly.
Add enough flour to form a soft dough.
Turn out on lightly floured board; let rest 5 or 10 minutes.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Place in greased bowl, turning once to grease top.
Cover; let rise until double in bulk.
Punch down; grease top.
Cover with damp towel and refrigerate.
When ready to bake, shape into rolls and place in a well-greased pan.
Let rise until double.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Brown the beef in your microwave on High (approximately 5 to 6 minutes).

In microwave safe dish, crumble beef and drain any fat. Add onion, green pepper, salt and pepper to taste, chili powder, crushed tomatoes, tomato paste and kidney beans and microwave on High for approximately 23 to 25 minutes.
Dish into bowls and serve.
Enjoy!
Combine all ingredients, except bacon, parsley or nuts; form into a ball.
Roll in bacon, parsley or nuts.
Refrigerate.
Can also be used to fill cherry tomatoes.
Heat oven to 325°. Coat a roasting pan with cooking spray.
Season steak accordingly.

Dredge in flour. Brown in skillet. Add onions, 4 teaspoons flour and juice from canned apricots. Place in baking dish and bake at 350° for about 45 minutes. Thirty minutes into baking, put apricots on top of steak and return to oven.
Mix buttermilk baking mix, 1/2 cup sugar and 3 tablespoons cocoa in greased 8-inch square baking dish.
Stir in milk and vanilla until well blended.
Sprinkle evenly with remaining 1/3 cup of cocoa and 1/2 cup sugar.
Pour hot water evenly over top.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 40 minutes or until top is firm.
Dust with confectioners sugar.
Serve at once in dessert bowls with the sauce spooned over cake.
Makes 6 servings.
Good.
Cook noodles; add olive oil to prevent them from sticking together.
Brown ground beef, onion and bell pepper. Drain fat from meat by putting in a strainer and "washing" meat with hot tap water.
Put meat back in skillet once drained and add mushrooms, sauce, oregano, salt and pepper.
Spray large pan with Pam.
Layer sauce first, noodles second, cottage cheese, then Mozzarella and/or Cheddar.
Start over with sauce.
Continue until pan is full.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brown ground beef in pan; drain.
Stir in seasoning mix, water and olives; simmer 5 minutes.
Separate crescent dough into 8 triangles.
Place triangles in ungreased 9 or 10-inch pie pan; press over bottom and up sides to form a crust.
Sprinkle 1 cup corn chips over bottom of crust.
Spoon meat mixture over crust and crushed corn chips.
Spread sour cream over meat mixture; cover with cheese.
Sprinkle remaining chips over top.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
If desired, serve in wedges topped with shredded lettuce and avocado slices. Refrigerate any leftovers.
Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Cook vegetables, potatoes and cabbage in three cups water until soft.
Add tomato juice and canned beef.
Simmer a short time to blend flavors.
Mix first 5 ingredients with mixer.
Place in buttered dish. Top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar and beat again. Add oil, vanilla and zucchini. Add dry ingredients and raisins or nuts.
Pour into 2 well-greased and floured loaf bread pans or four 3 1/2 x 7 1/2-inch pans. Bake at 325° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Test with toothpick to be sure it is done.
Place sour cream in microwave to soften.
Unwrap cream cheese and remove from aluminum foil wrapping and place in microwave to soften.
Mix sour cream and cream cheese in a large bowl.
Add in olives, jalapenos and garlic; mix well.
Using a rubber scraper or similar instrument, spread some of the mixture onto a tortilla, leaving approximately 1-inch of the tortilla free from the mixture around the circumference of the tortilla.
Starting at the bottom of the tortilla, fold the edge into the center of the tortilla; next, fold the opposite edge into the center of the tortilla.
Now fold the top half of the tortilla onto the bottom half of the tortilla and press gently to make sure the filling is squeezed to, but not out of the ends of the tortilla shell; set aside.
When finished with the tortillas, wrap tightly in plastic and place in refrigerator for several hours to stiffen (can be made a day in advance).
Before serving, slice folded tortillas on a bias into quarters.
Arrange pieces on platter in a geometric design of your choice and garnish plate with thin strips of red, green and yellow bell peppers amongst the killers.
Sift meal, flour, salt and soda 3 times.
Add the milk and beaten egg yolk, melted margarine and lastly, beaten egg white. Pour small amount into piping hot, greased corn stick pans and bake in hot oven (425°) for 15 minutes.
Serve hot and with a generous amount of margarine.
Yields 8 to 10 sticks.
In a saucepan, combine sugar, tartar and water; stir as mixture heats until sugar dissolves.
Wipe away any sugar crystals that may form on the side when dripped from a spoon.
Using a long, sharp pin, dip pecan halves, one at a time, into glaze and place on a buttered dish.
Work fast for glaze hardens rapidly. Dates, almonds, Brazil nuts, Malaga grapes, orange sections and even violets may be treated in this way.
Heat and stir sugar, syrup and 1 cup water in a heavy 3-quart saucepan until sugar dissolves.
Cook over medium heat to soft ball stage (234°).
Add nuts and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Cook to hard crack stage (305°), stirring often.
Remove from heat.
Quickly stir in butter and soda.
Pour at once onto 2 well-buttered 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch pans, spreading with spatula.
If desired, cool slightly and pull with forks to stretch.
Break up when cold.
Makes 1 1/2 pounds.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Dip chicken in mixture of melted butter, pepper sauce and vinegar.
Put in baking pan.
Sprinkle with 1 package dry dressing mix.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Cook orzo until al dente.
Melt butter; fry onion, pepper and frozen peppers.
Sprinkle with soup mix powder.
Mix with orzo.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Drain peaches, reserving 1/2 cup liquid. Arrange peaches, cut side up, in an 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan.
Add reserved liquid.
Combine sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle evenly over peaches.
Mix sugar with sour cream.
Stir into other ingredients.
Mix all ingredients together and pour into pie crusts.
Top with Cool Whip.
Place in refrigerator overnight or several hours. Makes 2 pies.
Boil peaches, sugar and pineapple for 15 minutes.
Remove from stove.
Add jello and stir well and put in jars.
Seal in hot water bath 10 minutes or turn jars upside down overnight.
Heat oil in large kettle, then brown meat on all sides.
Spoon off fat.
Stir in mushroom soup, onion soup mix and 1 cup water. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook 2 hours.
Add vegetables, cover and cook 45 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Remove meat and vegetables.
Stir together flour and remaining 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Gradually stir into soup mixture and thicken, stirring constantly.
Garnish with fresh parsley, if desired.
Dissolve the jello in the sugar and water.
Add cream cheese, pineapple and baby food.
Blend until smooth.
Fold in Cool Whip. Pour into mold and refrigerate.
Combine blueberries, 1 cup sugar and 1/4 cup water in a medium saucepan.
Cook over low heat until berries are soft, about 15 minutes.
Combine cornstarch and 3 tablespoons water in a small mixing bowl.
Stir well.
Add cornstarch to blueberry mixture. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Set aside to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, pour 1 1/2 cups of very hot water. Add salt, butter and honey; stir until melted.
Dissolve yeast in 1 cup of warm water and then add to other ingredients.
Add flour, mixing well after each cup is added.
Dump dough onto a floured board and knead 10 minutes.
Grease a large bowl with butter. Place dough into buttered bowl and turn once to coat entire surface of dough.
Place wet cloth on top and allow to rise for 1 1/2 hours.
Test dough by pressing with finger; when hole remains in dough, punch down.
Turn onto work table.
Divide into 4 parts. Place each into a greased loaf pan.
Let rise again about 1 hour. Bake 45 minutes in a 350° oven.
Mix all fruit together.
Sprinkle instant pudding 1 box at a time.
Chill before serving.
If desired, use sugar-free puddings and lite fruit.
Mix well.
Pour into uncooked pie shell.
Bake about 1/2 hour or until set in the middle at 350°.
In large pot, bring chicken stock to boil.
Add vegetables. Cover and simmer 10 minutes, or until they are tender.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Blend in flour; cook 1 minute.
Gradually add milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add cheese; stir until melted.
Stir cheese sauce into vegetables.
Cook over low heat until thoroughly heated.
Do not boil.
Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Melt margarine and add to crumbs and place on pie plate in dish, 11 x 8 or 12 x 9.
Combine sugar, egg and lemon in double boiler.
Cook until thick.
Allow to cool and add pecans, raisins and mayonnaise. Spread onto bread; makes 2 dozen sandwiches.
Bake ribs.
Salt and pepper 1 1/4 hours, uncovered at 350°. Mix all other ingredients and pour over baked ribs and bake 1 hour more, uncovered.
Serves 4.
Mix all ingredients in usual manner.
Put soda in hot applesauce to dissolve it and add to batter.
Add all ingredients into a Dutch oven with lid; mix.
Cook, covered, in 300° oven for 3 hours.
Do not peek! Serve on hot rice or noodles.
May use sour cream, if desired.
Combine first 5 ingredients in a large bowl; toss well and set aside.
Combine sugar and next 7 ingredients and stir well.
Pour over cabbage mixture and toss gently.
Cover and chill 1 hour. Serves 8.
Dissolve Jell-O in water, add pineapple and pie filling.
Stir and congeal.
Beat cream cheese until smooth.
Gradually add sugar. Blend in sour cream.
Spread over top congealed mixture.
Top with nuts.
Mix all together like pie dough.
Put half on bottom (pressed down) on cookie sheet with sides.
Add prepared apricot filling or other fruit.
Enough to cover the dough, don't over do it.
Put rest of dough on top.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Brown onion and celery in margarine.
Combine all ingredients and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Rinse chicken and pat dry.
Arrange in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix together soup and sour cream.
Spoon mixture over chicken.
Drizzle water over chicken mixture in dish.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Combine mayonnaise, ginger and salt.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover and chill.
Mix all ingredients, except sharp cheese.
Cook in oven for 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Add sharp cheese; cook until melted.
Combine ingredients and pour into pie shells.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Mix the first 4 ingredients together; sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Microwave for 5 to 7 minutes.
Set aside grated carrots, cherries and nuts.
Combine dry ingredients and sift into a large bowl.
Add oil, carrots and vanilla; stir by hand until well done, then beat for 3 minutes. Add nuts and cherries.
Bake in greased and floured angel cake pan for 1 1/4 hours.
Melt margarine.
Cook onion and celery until tender.
Mix with bread crumbs and cornbread crumbs.
Add spices.
Pour soup over mixture and mix all ingredients well.
Pour enough chicken broth over mixture until desired moistness.
Spread in pan and bake at 350° for 30 minutes or stuff in turkey and roast.
Serves 12.
Brown meat in large skillet; drain.
Add taco sauce; simmer. Melt cheese with milk to make cheese sauce.
Add more milk if needed for desired consistency.

Peel potatoes and cut into quarters. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Boil for 20 minutes or until tender. Drain potatoes and mash with sour cream, cream cheese and chives. Grease large casserole dish, add potato mixture and sprinkle with grated cheese and paprika. Bake at 350 degrees for 35-40 minutes. Can be frozen before baking for up to 3 months.
Sprinkle peppers on well-greased 9-inch square pan; cover with cheese.
Pour eggs over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until firm.
Cool and cut into 1-inch squares.
Combine all ingredients in covered shaker and shake until well blended.
Pour in tall glass and relax!
Blend oil, eggs, sugar and vanilla flavoring.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and cinnamon.
Combine mixture.
Fold in nuts and apples.
Bake in a tube pan 1 hour and 20 minutes at 325°.
Pour morsels and milk into Pyrex dish and cook on High 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in vanilla and nuts.
Let cool before cutting.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water.
Stir in raspberries and applesauce.
Gel.
Put a layer of sour cream or nonfat yogurt on top before serving.
In large bowl, mix together Cool Whip, pineapple and softened cream cheese.
Sprinkle with pudding mix.
Lastly stir in drained cooled wheat and mix well.
Refrigerate.

recipes.t: Milwaukee German Toffee(To Make About 4 Pounds)
d: Use heavy pot, like pressure cooker.
Butter an 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
In a 2-quart saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, water, cornstarch, butter and salt.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, to 256° on candy thermometer (above 200° on meat thermometer) or until firm.
Remove from heat and add vanilla.
Pour into pan.
When cool enough, pull taffy until satiny and hard.
Butter hands if taffy is sticky.
Put into long strings.
Cut into pieces and wrap.
Serves 6.
In a flat Pyrex dish, put a layer of broccoli and turkey. Prepare sauce by mixing remaining ingredients except bread crumbs and margarine.
Pour sauce over broccoli and turkey.
Top with bread crumbs and margarine.
Make at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Can be made ahead and heated.
Drain spinach thoroughly; set aside.
Saute onion in butter in a large saucepan until tender and add flour, stirring until smooth.
Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add milk and stir in spinach, salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Makes about 1 quart.
Empty one envelope Shake 'n Bake into its plastic shaker bag. Add Parmesan cheese and oregano.
Place chicken breasts in the bag, one at a time, and coat.
Precook cornbread and cool.
Precook 1 cup water, 1/2 stick butter, 1 chopped onion and 1/2 cup celery.
In extra large pan, mix (by hand with a whisk) chicken, soups, eggs and seasonings. Add cornbread, milk and toast.
Add precooked items while slightly warm.
If dry, add another can of broth and milk. This makes two large casserole dishes. Cook at 350° until middle is firm.
Time varies depending on size of dish.
A clean knife test will work. This can also be prepared ahead of time and frozen.
Mix all ingredients in a crock-pot.
Stir often until the cheese is melted.
For crust, add flour, sugar, pecans and melted oleo together and bake in 13 x 9-inch pan for 25 minutes at 350°.
Let cool and crumble in same pan or one of equal size.
Reserve 1/2 cup. Spread 2 cans of pie filling over crumbled crust.

Beat together cream cheese, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Stir in 1/4 cup cereal, chocolate chips and raisins. Cover and chill several hours or overnight. Shape into ball. Roll into remaining cereal to coat. Serve with apple or pear wedges, unsalted crackers or graham crackers. Can make up to 3 days ahead.
Combine Parmesan cheese and oregano and set aside.
Cut each potato lengthwise into 8 wedges.
Dip into egg white and dredge in Parmesan cheese mixture.
Place fries on a baking sheet coated with vegetable cooking spray.
Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Wash and cut up strawberries.
Mix oranges and pineapple with strawberries.
Beat pudding, buttermilk and Cool Whip until thick. In large dish, layer fruit, then pudding.
Top layer will be fruit.
Prepare 1 box yellow cake mix as directed on the box.
Bake in a 1 x 13 x 22-inch jelly roll pan for 25 minutes at 350°.
Let cool.
Mix the pudding, milk and cream cheese with a mixer.
It will be thick.
Fold in 9 ounces of Cool Whip.
Place in refrigerator to set up a little.

Place rest of ingredients of the cake in the following order: spread pudding mixture on the cake thickly, sprinkle well drained pineapple over pudding, sprinkle chopped pecans over the pineapple and sprinkle coconut on top. Place the cake in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
You may freeze the cake for a later day.
Just thaw and serve.
Cook spaghetti and combine all ingredients, except part of cheese.
Place in casserole dish and top with remaining cheese. Heat in 350° oven.
Cook rhubarb, sugar and water until tender.
Remove from heat. Add jello.
Put in hot jars and seal.
Place broccoli in baking dish.
Top with sliced chicken. Sprinkle with cheese.
Combine chicken soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder.
Pour this over chicken and cheese. Sprinkle bread crumbs on top with additional cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Serve with yellow rice.
Brown hamburger and onion together. Add remaining ingredients; mix well. Simmer for 1 hour.
Mix yellow cake mix, 1/3 cup oleo and 1 egg in 9 x 13-inch pan for 12 to 18 minutes at 350°.
When baked and while still hot, put 3 cups mini-marshmallows on top.
Then add following topping: heat corn syrup, 1/4 cup oleo, peanut butter chips and vanilla. Heat until smooth, stirring constantly.
Then add rice crispies and salted peanuts.
Spread over marshmallows.
Tastes like a Payday candy bar.
Drain salmon, reserving liquid; remove skin and bones if desired.
Flake salmon with fork.
Dissolve bouillon in boiling water in a bowl.
Add salmon liquid, milk, egg, parsley and onion; mix well.
Add salmon, stuffing mix and cheese, mixing well. Place in 2 greased 10-ounce custard cups or casseroles.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serve with vegetable sauce if desired. (Vegetable sauce can be found in the Soup, Salads and Sauces section of this cookbook.)
Combine pineapple, sour cream and pudding in bowl.
Beat at medium speed until blended.
Spoon mixture into crust.
Top with whipped topping.
Cover and chill at least 3 hours.
Cook broccoli until tender; drain.
Mix together soup, egg, onion, cheese and salt and pepper.
Pour over broccoli.
Cover with bread crumbs.
Pour on melted butter.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
In a large bowl, beat eggs and then add all remaining ingredients.
Mix thoroughly and pour into lightly greased glass baking dish (13 x 8-inch).
Bake in 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes, or until set and lightly browned.
Cut into squares.
Serve hot or cold.
Can be frozen and reheated.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Lightly grease a 10-inch pie plate. Set aside.
In bowl, beat cream cheese, sugar, cream, brandy extract, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg until creamy.
Stir in Toll House semi-sweet morsels.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheet; chill 5 minutes.
Roll into balls and roll in the nuts.
Makes 3 dozen balls.

recipes.t: Memories Chicken Salad (Caf Memories In Iuka)
d: Boil chicken breasts until tender, then shred.	Mix chicken with remaining ingredients and serve with fruit on lettuce leaf and croissant.
Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in hot water; add lemon juice and rind.
Chill until partly set.
Whip canned milk until stiff, then add Jell-O.
Pour into glass baking dish in which crumbs are on bottom.
Put crumbs over top.
Set in refrigerator overnight.
Mix together.
Serve on 6 split English muffins.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Slice like pizza.
Serve hot.
Layer bread cubes, sliced sausage and shredded cheese in a casserole.
Beat eggs.
Add milk and seasonings.
Pour over casserole and refrigerate overnight.
Bake one hour at 325°.
Mix sugar, flour and sweet milk and add beaten egg yolks. Cook in a double boiler until thick. Pour over layer of bananas, then top with wafers. Brown at 400°.
Place apples in 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Add enough water to cover apples.
Mix first six ingredients to a crumbly stage. Sprinkle on top of apples.
Bake in oven at 350° until browned.
Sift together the flour, sugar, baking soda and cinnamon. Add oil, then add the beaten eggs and the salt.
Beat batter; it will be thick.
Fold in chopped walnuts, carrots and raisins (optional).
Grease pan with margarine.
Bake at 350° in a 13 x 9-inch pan for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or in a 10 x 4-inch pan for 40 minutes.
Combine sugar and flour.
Add sweet potatoes, melted margarine and water.
Mix well.
If needed, add more water to make mixture moist.
Roll into small biscuits.
Bake at 400° until brown.
Melt butter with milk in microwave.
Add dry ingredients; stir in beaten eggs.
Pour over bread.
Cook in microwave for 9 to 12 minutes.
Mix turkey, cereal, herbs and onions and form into 4 patties. On a nonstick pan sprayed with Pam, fry until browned.
Sprinkle on the cheese.
Cover and cook until the cheese is melted.
Salt and pepper hash browns.
Cream together the sour cream, butter, onion, milk and soup.
Mix creamed mixture with potatoes and place in casserole. Top with grated cheese and corn flakes. Drizzle 1/4 cup melted butter over top. Bake 45 to 60 minutes at 350°.
Place steak in large Pyrex dish.
Layer onion, carrots and potatoes on top.
Heat soup with margarine and pour over casserole.
Cover and bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Cream the first 4 ingredients together.
Then add all other ingredients.
Grease 9 x 13-inch pan.
Level the dough evenly with a spoon.
Bake in 350° preheated oven for 30 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Bars are real chewy and moist.
Mix the first 5 ingredients altogether; pat down in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat the eggs, powdered sugar and cream cheese together for 5 minutes.
Pour the mixture over the first mixture in the pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour.
May add chocolate chips, if you wish.
Mix all ingredients in a large glass bowl.
Put into jars with tight covers.
Refrigerate for 2 weeks before using.
These will keep for 2 years in the refrigerator.
(A gallon sun tea jar works well if you have a glass one and enough room in the refrigerator.)
Mix cornmeal, bacon drippings, salt and green onions.
Pour enough boiling water to stick mixture together without being too dry or mushy.
Form into oval cakes and fry in bacon drippings in skillet, about 3 minutes on each side.

Slice 2 of the eggs into 1 1/2 qt. casserole. In a sauce pan melt butter, blend in flour, 1/2 tsp. and dash pepper. Add milk all at once. Cook, stirring constantly until mixture thickens and bubbles. Cook sausage: drain. Stir sausage and corn into sauce, pour over eggs. Slice remaining eggs: arrange atop mixture. Sprinkle with bread crumbs. Bake at 375 degrees for 20-25 minutes.
Mix in order.
Let stand overnight.
Put mixture in a 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Put all ingredients into a 10 x 10 x 3-inch Corning baking dish.
Add 1-inch of water.
Cover with lid.
Cook at 300° for 3 hours.
Sift together flour, baking powder, soda, salt and cinnamon. Add sugar, oil and eggs (mix well).
Add carrots, drained pineapple and nuts.
Turn into 8-inch layer pans (greased and floured).
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cool in pan, then turn out and cool on wire racks.
Spread layer top and sides with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Sift flour, salt and baking powder together.
Use fork to mix in shortening.
Then add cold water and vinegar.
Mix well.
Makes 2 pie crusts.
Mix together Cool Whip and sour cream.
Add remaining ingredients.
Refrigerate.
Mix cake as directions indicate on package.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool cake.
Then mix cream cheese and milk together until cheese dissolves.
Add instant pudding and mix until thickened.
Pour this over cake.
Next, pour drained pineapple on cake and top with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Mix broccoli, onions, mushrooms, pepperoni and dressing.
Let stand for 2 hours.
Toss in lettuce and top or toss with cheese.
Pour this mixture in a casserole dish and top with topping. Use Pam in dish first.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Grease a 9 x 13 baking pan.
In a large bowl, mix jalapenos and creamed corn.
Beat in the baking soda, salt, sugar, and eggs (beating well).
Add the buttermilk, oil, cheese, and cornmeal.
Mix well.
Pour the batter into the greased pan and bake for 35 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve it hot with butter!
Pour egg into a 6-cup buttered casserole.
Heat corn and milk; gradually stir into beaten egg.
Add salt, breadcrumbs and cheese; mix thoroughly.
Bake, uncovered, in a 325° oven for 30 minutes.
Pour in cooled pie crust and top with low-fat Cool Whip.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add beaten egg yolks.
Continue to beat, adding milk and hot potatoes, sifted flour with baking powder and beaten egg whites.
Bake.
Makes 6 layers.
Combine flour, pecans and butter in bowl; mix well.
Press into 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Cool.
Mix banana pudding mix with crushed pineapple.
Then add other ingredients, leaving the whipped topping to be added last. Refrigerate.
Boil crabs for 10 minutes.
Turn heat off; let crabs soak in seasoned water for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cool crabs and pick, saving "roe" if fortunate to have "she crabs."
(The more crabs, the better.)
Scald the turtle with boiling water and the hard shell.
Clean well with lime, then season with salt, black pepper and garlic. Sprinkle with capers and Worcestershire sauce and let stand for 1 to 2 hours.
Chop onions, tomatoes and sweet pepper.
Saute these ingredients in oil and butter.
Add turtle and allow to brown, then pour on 2 cups of warm water and steam until tender.
Quarter potatoes and add to stew.
Let simmer until gravy thickens.
Add sherry just before serving.
Serve piping hot.
Layer in greased casserole onions, cheese and bread.
In a separate bowl, mix egg, milk, salt and pepper.
Pour mixture over the top.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour into tube pan.
Put into icebox for 24 hours.
Mix thoroughly; shape dough into 2 1/2-inch logs and place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 17 minutes.
Roll in powdered sugar while still warm.
Cream shortening; gradually add sugar, beating well.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition.
Stir in apple and bananas.
Combine flour, soda and salt.
Add to creamed mixture, stirring just enough to blend.
Spoon batter into greased and floured pan.
Bake for 1 hour.
Cool in pan 10 minutes.
Cool completely on wire rack.
Brown the meats; drain.
Heat tomatoes and cheese together until cheese melts, then add this to the meat mixture.
Add hot sauce to taste.
Serve over tortilla chips.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Mix spaghetti sauce, season and ground beef.
Add a dash of oregano or to your taste; let simmer.
Boil spaghetti until tender.
Mix spaghetti sauce and spaghetti; take half and pour into casserole dish.
Top with Mozzarella and Cheddar cheese.
Add the rest of the mixture; top with Mozzarella cheese and Cheddar cheese.
Place in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes, then serve.

Preheat oven to 350°. Place butter in a 13 x 9 inch pan, put in oven to melt butter. Remove from oven and sprinkle crumbs over butter, pressing down with a fork. Sprinkle coconut over crumbs, add a layer of chips and one of almonds. Drizzle condensed milk evenly over top. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool before cutting.
Brown sausage and drain well.
Grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan and line bottom of pan with crescent rolls, firmly pressing perforations to seal.
Sprinkle sausage and Mozzarella cheese over dough.
Combine eggs and milk and pour over sausage and cheese. Bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Put Cheddar cheese on top and bake 10 minutes longer.
Cook chicken until thoroughly done and falls off the bone.
Do not chop or grind chicken.
Just cut into bite size pieces. Amounts of mayonnaise, pickle cubes, salt and pepper will vary to suit the taste of the cook.
Brown meatballs in olive oil.
Remove.
Saute onion and garlic in oil.
Add meatballs.
Pour on tomato sauce.
Simmer in sauce about 3 hours.
(Add 3 bay leaves.)
Tremendous!
Bring Karo, sugar and water to a boil.
Drop in peanuts.
Cook until peanuts are done (they will pop and turn darker).
Put in soda, salt and vanilla.
Pour on buttered plate; cool about 30 minutes and break.
Saute onion, chili and shortening.
Add tomato juice and garlic salt.
Mix all ingredients into melted cheese.
If too thick, add more tomato juice.
Serve hot with corn chips.
Thaw loaves of bread.
Place in greased pan (9 x 13-inch) in small chunks.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over bread.
Let rise for 30 minutes.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Turn out on wax paper while hot.
Press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Heat oil in a skillet.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drop by tablespoon into skillet. Fry until golden brown, approximately 1 minute on each side.
Serves 5 to 8.
Beat cream cheese, milk and vanilla in medium bowl on low speed until smooth.
Gradually beat in powdered sugar, 1 cup at a time, until smooth and of spreading consistency.
Frosts a 13 x 9-inch or fills and frosts two 8 or 9-inch cake layers. Refrigerate any remaining frosting.
Heat oven to 375°.
Combine flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Cream butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs until light and fluffy.
Add flour mixture alternately with milk.
Beat well after each addition.
Stir in oats, raisins and nuts.
Mix well.
Drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake 12 to 15 minutes.
Cool on wire rack.
Makes about 5 dozen.
Brown pork chops, leaving drippings in pan.
Add both soups and let simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve with any rice or potato.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Cukes And Onions
d: Peel
cucumbers
and slice very thin.
Place in a glass bowl. Peel
onion;
slice
very thin and separate into rings. Add to bowl with the cucumbers.
Add sugar, water, vinegar and vegetable oil.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add dill weed. Stir
and let stand at room temperature at least 1 hour before serving.
Combine all ingredients. Serve on shredded lettuce.
Soak beans overnight. Drain water off in morning.

Add fresh water and boil gently about 1/2 hour. Drain. Cut salt pork into 4 pieces. Add beans, salt and remaining ingredients to bean pot. Cover. Cook all day at 300° (at least 8 hours for best results). Add water if necessary.
Great for a picnic!
Freezes well.
In large bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk and water. Add pudding mix; beat well.
Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in Cool Whip. Spoon 1 cup pudding mixture into a 2 1/2-quart glass serving bowl. Top with 1/3 each of the wafers, bananas and pudding.
Repeat layering twice, ending with pudding.
Chill thoroughly.
Garnish as desired.
Refrigerate.
Bring water to a boil.
Stir in rice.
When rice is cooked, remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Beat eggs, crush onion rings.
Combine all ingredients and pour into pie shell.
Bake at 325° for about 20 minutes until brown.

In a bowl, combine cabbage and green pepper. In a jar with tight-fitting lid, combine remaining ingredients; shake well. Pour over cabbage mixture just before serving; toss to coat. Serve with a slotted spoon. Yield: 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Let stand at least 2 to 3 hours.
Deep fry at 350°.
Serve with mustard/shoyu sauce, if desired.
Grease bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan and sprinkle marshmallows on the bottom.
Combine strawberries and gelatin and set aside (use the syrup and don't add water to the gelatin).
Combine
pectin
with 1/4 cup of the sugar.
Mix applesauce and spices in large bowl.
Add pectin mixture gradually to
fruit, stirring
vigorously.
Set
aside
for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir
remaining
sugar gradually into fruit mixture until sugar is dissolved, about 3 minutes.
Pour into plastic containers; cover.
Let stand at room temperature 24
hours. Spread is now ready to use.
Store in refrigerator up
to
3 weeks or freeze extra containers up to 1 year.
Thaw in refrigerator. Makes about 5 (1 cup) containers.
Mix all together and serve.
Combine all ingredients well. Roll into balls and place on greased sheet pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
*Dried minced green onion can be used as a substitute.
Heat first 4 ingredients in saucepan until well mixed.
Add milk, vanilla and salt.
Cook until thick.
Serve over ice cream.
Mix sugar, eggs and shortening.
Add dry ingredients alternately with tomato soup.
In a medium sized saucepan, bring raisins, water and butter to a boil.
Stir in cornstarch mixture and cook, stirring constantly, until thick.
Remove from heat and stir in walnuts, lemon peel, juice and vanilla.
Cool completely.
Thaw puff pastry for 20 minutes and unfold.
On a lightly floured surface, roll each sheet to a 9 x 15-inch rectangle, then cut into 3-inch squares.
Put about 2 teaspoons of filling in the center of each square; moisten corners of pastry with water and bring together to make a four cornered puff.
Press firmly to seal.
Bake on a cookie sheet in a preheated 400° oven for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Unbaked puffs may be wrapped tightly in plastic wrap and frozen until ready to bake.
Makes 30 puffs.
Cook ingredients until tender.
Tiny shell macaroni, 1/2 package.
Add not too long before other ingredients are done.
Heat oven to 350°.
Place frozen bread in bread pans and let thaw.
Do not let rise, just thaw.
Scramble sausage in a skillet until browned.
Shred cheese(s).
Pinch bread into 3 to 4 separate sections (each loaf).
Butter hands and press flat and stretch dough until about 6 inches across.
Add sausage 4 to 5 tablespoons each on pressed dough.
Add cheese about 1/3 cup each.
Fold over to make a pastry like fold.
Bake on a cookie sheet for 20 to 30 minutes.
Brown short ribs on all sides in oil.
Pour off drippings. Season with salt and pepper.
Add water, bouillon, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and the onion slices.
Cover tightly and cook slowly for 2 hours or until meat is fork-tender.
Pour out cooking liquid to measure 1 1/2 cups.
Use water if needed.
Thicken the liquid for gravy.
Serve with mashed potatoes.
Combine first 2 ingredients in top of a double boiler.
Bring water to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cook until chocolate is melted.
Remove from heat; set aside to cool.
Mix all ingredients together and serve on spinach salad.
Boil sweet potatoes, peel and mash, then add margarine, syrup, white sugar, flour and seasoning.
Bake in 9-inch crust.
Cook at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cream Crisco, margarine, sugar and salt for 7 minutes. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each.
Add flour and milk alternately, beginning and ending with flour. Fold in flavoring. Bake in greased and floured tube pan for 1 hour and 45 minutes at 325°.
Start in COLD oven and do not open door while baking.
Cool on rack and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
In 3-quart saucepan, cook onion and celery in butter until onion is tender.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper.
Add milk all at once.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Stir in spinach and cheese. Cook and stir until cheese is melted.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs lightly in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients and blend well.
Roll into walnut sized balls.
Transfer to baking sheet.
Bake until golden, about 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
Brown hamburger.
Layer bottom of casserole dish with tortilla strips, hamburger meat, tomatoes, beans, onion and cheese.
Mix soups together with small amount of water and spread over top of casserole.
Begin layering again and end up with cheese on top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or microwave on High for 10 minutes.
In a
large bowl, thoroughly mix 2 cups flour, dry milk solids, sugar, salt and undissolved yeast.
Add margarine.
Boil sugar and water 5 minutes.
Add chocolate, salt and the cornstarch dissolved in cold water.
Stir until smooth.
Cook 3 minutes.
Cool.
Add vanilla.
Store in a jar in refrigerator.

Thoroughly mix the gelatin, sugar and salt in a saucepan. Beat together the egg yolks, lime juice and water; stir into the gelatin mixture. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, just until the mixture comes to a boil.
Remove from the heat; stir in the grated peel.
Add the food coloring sparingly to give a pale green color.

Chill, stirring occasionally, until mixture mounds slightly when dropped from spoon. Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form; gradually add 1/2 cup sugar, beating to stiff peaks. Fold the gelatin mixture into the egg whites; fold the whipped cream.
Pile into the pastry shell.
Chill until firm.
Spread with additional whipped cream and edge with grated lime.
In the large bowl of an electric mixer, cream shortening, granulated sugar and brown sugar.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat until blended.
Add flour.
Sprinkle baking soda and salt over top.
Beat until no traces of flour can be seen.
With a wooden spoon, work in oats and coconut.
Brown meat, green peppers and onions. Combine all ingredients in slow cooker for 4 to 6 hours on low.
Cut flowerettes from broccoli.
Layer broccoli, raisins, onion, bacon and water chestnuts in bowl. Combine remaining ingredients and pour over salad.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cook carrots until tender; cool.
Combine all ingredients. Marinate at least 12 hours.
Drain.
Brown beef and onion.
Drain off fat.
Stir in flour, salt and garlic.
Add milk and softened cream cheese.
Cook and stir until bubbly.
Add moderate amount of hot mixture to beaten egg. Return to mixture in skillet.
Cook until thickened, 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in broccoli.
Set aside.
Lightly grease 2 loaf pans.
Put salt, molasses, oil and oats in a large bowl.
Add boiling water.
When the mixture is lukewarm, add eggs and yeast; let stand until yeast is dissolved, then add flour.
Stir and let stand 20 minutes (no kneading).
Turn out on floured board; knead and cut into 4 equal parts.
Put 2 parts in each bread pan.
Let rise until doubled in bulk.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
In skillet, cook beef, celery and onion until meat is browned and vegetables are crisp and tender.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, salt, beans, gravy mix and 1 cup water.
Simmer to thicken and blend flavors.
Whip potatoes according to directions.
Spoon in mounds over meat.
Top with paprika and shredded cheese. Cover.
Heat until cheese melts.
Serves 6.
Add all ingredients to the macaroni.
Serves 6.
Place all of the ingredients in a microwave-safe bowl and microwave on High power for 1 minute.
Stir and microwave for 1 additional minute.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.
First, brown bread crumbs in a nonstick frying pan over medium heat.
Stir constantly; pour into a bowl.
Set aside for later use.
Clean cauliflower.
Cut into small flowerets.
Cover bottom of 4-quart pot with olive oil.
Add garlic and cauliflower. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cook, covered, over medium heat 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir often.
Add chicken broth.
Turn heat to high; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add sherbet.
Allow to cool and thicken.
When mixture is thick, add pineapple, oranges and bananas. Fold in whipped cream.
Let set several hours or overnight.
Melt butter; stir in sugar.
Cook and stir over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add milk; bring to a boil.
Cool to room temperature. Beat in powdered sugar until like fudge.
Stir in nuts; pour in buttered 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan.
Chill until firm.
Grate cheese in blender.
Mix all ingredients together and form into a ball.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Wrap and refrigerate to set. Better overnight.
In large punch bowl, combine sugar and water.
Stir until sugar is dissolved.
Add lemon juice, orange juice, pineapple juice, grape juice, tea and grapefruit juices.
Mix well (chill thoroughly).
At serving time, stir in ginger ale and garnish with orange slices studded with whole cloves, lemon slices and cherries.
Preheat oven to 375°. Mix all ingredients and pour into pie shells. Bake 30 minutes or until light brown.
Cook bacon crisp. Add onion and seasonings to bacon grease. Simmer for a few minutes. Add potatoes and crumble bacon on top. Serve hot.
Blend together first 3 ingredients.
Then mix in lard like pie dough.
Add eggs, vanilla or lemon flavoring and buttermilk with soda. Roll out and cut.
Do not prick the pastry shell before baking.
Partially bake the pastry shell in a 450° oven for 5 minutes; remove from oven and cool on rack.
Brown meat and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Add onion and green pepper.
Simmer 30 minutes and then drain off any excess grease.
Next, add tomato and mushroom soup.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Add macaroni and beans with meat mixture in casserole dish.
Top with grated cheese and place in oven at 350° for about 15 minutes or until cheese melts. Serves 8.
Combine all ingredients; bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes.
Thicken with 1/4 cup cornstarch, dissolved in 1/2 cup water.
Bring to boil again.
Seal in jars, 6 or 7 pints.
I make this at Christmas time and use it for gifts.

Cook broccoli in water in a covered saucepan or microwave until crisp-tender; drain. Place broccoli in a greased 11 x 7 x 2-inch (2-quart) baking dish; set aside. Combine chicken, soup, mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese and curry powder; spoon over broccoli. Top with bread cubes and butter. Bake chicken casserole, uncovered, at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until heated through. Chicken casserole serves 4.
Boil on low heat until soft ball forms in cold water.
Beat until smooth.
Pour into pan and let cool.
Cut into very small pieces.
Candy is very rich.
Mix all ingredients, except coconut. Form into balls and roll in coconut.
Mix first 3 ingredients and press into 9 x 13 glass pan. Spread ice cream over Cocoa Krispie mixture.
Spread hot fudge over ice cream.
Sprinkle peanuts on last.
Freeze overnight. Serve frozen.
Pour cherries and pineapple in cake pan.
Stir in coconut. Pour cake mix on top of mixture.
Slice butter in pats and place on top of cake.
Bake at 350° for about 35 to 40 minutes.
Microwave whole cauliflower in a covered casserole dish for 10 minutes. Mix together the mayonnaise, grated cheese and mustard in a small bowl.
Pour on cauliflower and microwave on High for 3 minutes, uncovered.
Mix well and put into a loaf pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour or more.
Cook cauliflower and/or broccoli in a small amount of boiling salted water.
Cover until crisp-tender. Drain well. Remove from pan.
Melt 1/4 cup margarine in the same pan.
Stir in flour. Add milk all at once.
Cook and stir until mixture is very thick and begins to bubble.
Add cheese and sour cream.
Cook and stir over low heat until cheese is melted. Stir in ham, mushrooms and cooked vegetables.
Turn in a 2-quart casserole pan. Combine bread crumbs and 1 tablespoon melted margarine or butter.
Sprinkle atop casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 40 minutes.
Makes 6 servings.
Combine ingredients.
Drop by tablespoonfuls into hot fat, about 3/4-inch deep.
Turn each puff when brown on one side, 3 to 5 minutes required.
(These may also be fried in deep fat.)
Blend all ingredients in blender.
Chill overnight and enjoy.
Brown meat and drain.
Mix next 3 ingredients for chili.
In separate pan melt cheese, then add cream.
Then add to chili. Serve over Doritos.
Top the taco (chili sauce) with shredded lettuce and chopped tomatoes.
Top salad with Thousand Island dressing.
Puree basil, nuts and garlic.
Mix in cheese.
Add oil while machine is running.
Toss into any textured pasta.
Sprinkle top with cheese if desired or extra nuts.
Beat eggs lightly, mix all ingredients well.
Bake at 325°F for about 45 min.
Put foil over top if crust gets too dark.
Wash squash and cut in half, lengthwise.
Remove seeds and string fiber.
Sprinkle with salt.
Dot with butter.
Add one tablespoon of honey or syrup to each half squash.
Place in a baking pan in oven at 375°.
Bake until tender about 45 minutes. Baste occasionally with the butter-honey mixture.
After squash has browned, which will take 30 minutes, add a little water to the pan. Cover for remainder of baking period.

Unroll crescent rolls, separate into 8 triangles. Fit triangles into a 9-inch pie plate, pressing edges together to seal. Combine chopped ham and next 4 ingredients, spoon into pie plate. Cut remaining 3 triangles into thin strips; arrange over mixture. Bake on lower oven rack at 325 degrees for 1 hour. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Prepare macaroni according to package directions; drain. Combine soup, milk and cheese.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until cheese is melted.
Mix macaroni, cheese sauce, luncheon meat and green pepper.
Pour into 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Brown ground beef and onion.
Add all other ingredients and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer until done.
Heat to boiling 7-Up and drained pineapple juice; dissolve jello with this.
Pour into square or rectangle container.
Mix cottage cheese, Cool Whip, pineapple and almost all nuts (leave a few to sprinkle on top).
Mix with jello and chill.
Break up or slice cake to fit bottom of trifle rifle bowl (or glass bowl).
Brush liberally with chocolate liqueur.
Cover with 1 layer of fruit and drizzle with sludge.
Spread on whipped cream. Repeat layers until top of bowl is reached.
Drizzle chocolate sauce on top.
Chill for several hours or overnight.
Chop peppers and onion fine.
Cover with boiling water and let stand 10 minutes; drain.
Cover again with hot water and let come to boil.
Let stand 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain dry and add salt, vinegar and sugar.
Cook for 15 minutes and pack in hot jars. Process in water bath can at 212° for 10 minutes.
Drain crab meat and combine with other ingredients.
Mix well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Good with crackers, chips or vegetables.
Mix all ingredients and pour into a baking dish.
Cook for 10 minutes at 375°.
Lower temperature to 350° and bake 45 minutes longer.

Cream margarine, sugar and vanilla. Sift flour with cocoa and salt. Blend dry ingredients into creamed mixture. Add pecans and mix well. Shape into balls. Place on cookie sheet. Bake at 325° for 25 minutes. While, warm, roll in powdered sugar.
Mix well and pour into greased loaf pan.
Cover top with ketchup and bake, uncovered, in preheated oven at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Saute in pan.
When cooked, stuff into partially cooked large rigatoni.
In baking dish, put layer of rigatoni and cover with spaghetti sauce over all.
Put in oven at 350° for 30 minutes to consume.
Pour half the cooking wine in bottom of casserole dish.
Put chicken, artichokes, olives, onion, garlic and oregano in and then add the rest of the wine.
Cover and bake at 375° for 1 hour. Garnish with Romano cheese.
Put over your favorite pasta.
Cook on low in crock-pot 4 hours or 2 hours at 325° in oven.
Mix all together and cook until it forms a soft ball when tested in cold water.
Add nuts and beat until creamy.
Soften and mix together.
Make into 2 or more rolls.
Roll in chili powder or Parmesan cheese.
Mix dry pudding and Tang gently with fruit mixture.
Chill. May be used as salad or dessert.
Thaw pie crust for 10 to 20 minutes in pan.
Prick sides of crust thoroughly with a fork.
Dot bottom and sides of thawed pie crust with butter.
Sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Bake in preheated oven at 425° for 8 to 13 minutes or until golden brown. Cool, then cut into pieces for serving.
Mix all ingredients in saucepan.
Heat until cheese melts and corn is tender.
This recipe can be doubled easily and kept warm in a crock pot.
Prepare spaghetti by directions on package.
Mix ground beef, onions and salt; cook until well done.
Drain; set aside.
Brown onions in margarine.
Add to remaining ingredients. Pour into casserole dish.
Cover and bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Stir in next 5 ingredients; heat until bubbly; pour into 2-quart casserole dish.
Cut biscuits in half to form 20 half circles.
Place cut side down around edge of casserole.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes, until biscuits are golden brown. Refrigerate any leftovers.
Serves 4 to 6.
Drain pineapple well, maybe overnight.
Mix with mixer, all ingredients.
Roll into ball.
Roll into crushed nuts.
Serve with favorite crackers.
Soak beans overnight in water, salt and pepper.
Keep water over the top of beans.
Stir and discard bean pieces which float to the top.
Cover with fresh water.
Boil 1 hour; drain.
Return beans to kettle.
Add all ingredients and water to cover beans. Simmer several hours.
Stir occasionally (too much stirring causes beans to get mushy).
Always keep enough water in kettle.
Eat as is or add to chili, refried, etc.
Cream butter, gradually adding sugar.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolks.
Blend well.
Gradually add flour and mix well.
Fold in nuts.
Pat half of batter into greased 8-inch square pan.
Spread with filling.
Cover with remaining batter. Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Cool and cut into 1-inch squares.
Mix flour, brown sugar and salt.
Add to milk and butter. Cook until thick.
Add beaten egg yolks.
Cook about 15 minutes longer until real thick.
Remove from heat and add vanilla and 1/2 cup granulated sugar.
Pour into baked pie shell and top with meringue.
Combine butter, sugar and 1/2 cup almonds in heavy 3-quart saucepan.
Heat slowly to boiling point.
Boil gently until 305°, stirring constantly.
Pour into large buttered sheet pan sprinkled with 1/2 of chocolate chips.
Spread with spatula.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup almonds.
Cool and turn over and put rest of chocolate chips and almonds.
Place under broiler until chips melt.
Spread chocolate chips and rest of almonds.
Peel and quarter the white potatoes; boil them until tender. Put cooked potatoes in a large bowl.
Mash potatoes until smooth, then mix them with butter, sugar, salt, lemon and vanilla.
Add eggs, milk and baking powder; beat until smooth.
Add more sugar, if desired.
Pour mixture into pie crust shells and sprinkle lightly with grated coconut.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven until done.
Combine all ingredients except eggs and peas, then carefully fold in eggs and peas.
Place on crisp lettuce leaf and arrange quarters of tomatoes around.
Mix melted oleo and brown sugar.
Let cool.
Add beaten eggs and vanilla.
Sift flour, soda, baking powder and salt and add to first mixture.
Add chocolate chips, coconut and nuts.
Bake in greased 9 x 13-inch pan at 350°.
Sprinkle 3 tablespoons graham cracker crumbs in 9-inch pan. Set aside.
Soften gelatin in 1/2 cup water.
Bring 3/4 cup juice to boil and stir in gelatin.
Beat cottage cheese smooth.
Add egg yolks, skim milk, lemon juice, sweetener, vanilla and salt.
Beat well.
Blend in gelatin at low speed.
Chill.
Stir occasionally until thick, but not set, about 1 hour.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form, then fold into gelatin mixture by hand.
Spoon over crumbs in pan.
Sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.
Add pineapple tidbits on top.
Chill overnight in refrigerator.
Crumble cornbread.
In separate bowl, mix beans, corn, tomatoes, onions, peppers, cheese, and bacon.
Mix in layers of vegetable mixture.
Mix sour cream and picante sauce together. Combine with cornbread and vegetable mixture just before serving.
Cook vegetables in large covered saucepan in chicken broth until almost tender (10 to 15 minutes).
Do not drain.
Set aside.
In another bowl, gradually add cream of potato soup; mix thoroughly.
Blend water in cornstarch (in small cup).
Pour into potato soup mixture.
Mix together, then pour all white mixture into vegetables and broth.
Cook and stir until thick and bubbly (on medium heat).
Melt margarine in a large nonstick skillet coated with cooking spray.
Add cabbage and next 4 ingredients; cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with caraway seed; cover and cook 1 minute.
Yield:
5 cups.
Contains 39 calories per 1 cup serving.
Melt butter in heavy skillet.
Stir in sugar, egg yolk and dates.
Cook and stir over low heat 5 minutes or until mixture is thick.
Remove from heat.
Stir in lemon juice, peel and nuts. Cool.
Drop or roll into balls and roll in powdered sugar. Delicious!!
I double this recipe.
Cream sugars and shortening.
Add egg, flour and all other ingredients; blend.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Combine ingredients.
Put equal amount in two 9-inch square pans that have been sprayed with Pam or Cooking Ease.
Bake at 350° (preheated) for 35 minutes.
Chill in icebox and cut in bite-size pieces.
Serve as hors d'oeuvres.
Yields 180 bite-size squares.
Mix all ingredients. Marinate overnight. Cook over medium heat in a saucepan for 30 minutes. Serve in a bowl with small amount of sauce; keep warm. Serve with toothpicks.
Brown onion and ground beef.
Add green pepper, taco seasoning and tomatoes.
While meat mixture is cooking, cook noodles.
Rinse and drain noodles.
Put noodles in buttered baking dish.
Add sour cream and 1/2 cup grated cheese.
Mix together.
Pour meat mixture over noodles and cover with remaining cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Let set until solid in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix eggs, sugar and oil; beat well.
Sift dry ingredients together.
Add to first mixture.
Stir in zucchini, nuts and vanilla.
Bake in two loaf pans at 325° for 1 hour.
Turn out of pan.
Cook rice as directed on box. Brown onion in oil on medium heat.
Add chicken and cook until tender.
Add salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Add eggs.
When eggs are cooked, add rice and reduce heat.
Add 2 to 3 more tablespoons soy sauce and serve.
Combine the softened cream cheese with the fresh dill. Spread on the thin slices of smoked salmon and roll up jelly-roll fashion.
Chill.
Just before serving, cut the rollups into slices about 1/2 inch thick.
Melt chocolate and margarine over low heat or in double boiler. Take off burner and add sugar, eggs, flour and salt mixed together and vanilla, stirring after each addition.
Add nuts last.
Bake in a 7 x 9-inch greased pan for 25 minutes at 350°.
Finely chop the pepper, onion and celery.
Flake the crabmeat. Combine all together, except for the cracker crumbs.
Place in a buttered baking dish.
Cover with bread crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Soften cream cheese and add Marshmallow Creme to blend. Add orange
juice
and	orange peel until well blended.
Good with chunks
of cantaloupe, honeydew melon, pineapple, apple, banana, grapes, strawberries, etc.
Stir well.
Let stand
in
freezer
at
least
hours (overnight is preferable).
Make into small balls and place on wax paper.
Put back in
freezer
and freeze for about 1 hour. Melt 12 ounce chocolate chips with 3/4 of one bar of paraffin. Dip balls by toothpick into chocolate mixture and place on wax paper.
Keep in freezer until set good.
Shake well in jar.
Cut ends off the zucchini.
Cut zucchini lengthwise.
Do not pare the zucchini.
Scoop out pulp.
Cook (boil) pulp, bread crumbs, salt, pepper, onion and eggs for 5 minutes.
Spoon into zucchini shells.
Dot with butter.
Sprinkle on cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut eggs in half.
Remove yolks, mash and mix with the remaining ingredients.
Fill white with the mixture and serve.
Mix together and pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with Pepperidge Farm dressing.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients; pour into casserole dish. Top with roll of crushed Ritz crackers. Pour melted margarine over top. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Butter two large casseroles.
Heat oven to 325°.
Crush crackers into crumbs.
In skillet saute mushrooms with 2 tablespoons butter.
In bowl mix soup, mushrooms and light cream. Put 1 fish fillet on bottom of each casserole.
Add a layer of mushroom sauce, then a layer of crumbs.
Continue layering seafoods in casseroles with a layer of sauce and crumbs between each.
Finish each with crumbs.
Cut remaining butter into thin pats and place on top.
Bake casseroles in a water bath for a little more than an hour.
This dish may be frozen.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease square pan, 8 x 8 x 2-inches. Place peaches in pan.
Mix remaining ingredients and sprinkle over peaches.
Bake 30 minutes or until topping is golden brown.
Serve warm and if desired, with light cream, ice cream or hard sauce. Makes 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 325°.
In large bowl, beat eggs at high speed until foamy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in flour, sugar and brown sugar until well blended.
Beat in softened butter.
Stir in walnuts and chocolate chips.
Pour into pie shells.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes or until knife inserted halfway between edge and center comes out clean and top is golden brown.
Cool on wire rack. Serve with Cool Whip or ice cream, if desired.
Combine all ingredients putting seven up in last.
Note:
Save some of crumb mixture for top.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Gradually add in sugar while beating, then add baking powder and vanilla.
Beat well on slow speed and fold in crumbs and nuts.
Press out into greased pie plate.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 35 minutes.
Cool for 20 minutes.
Serve topped with whipped cream, Cool Whip or vanilla ice cream.
Boil shells and let cool.
Finely dice onion and pepper. Brown hamburger and sausage in frying pan while sauteing onion and pepper at same time.
Drain grease from hamburger and sausage, onion, and peppers.
In mixing bowl combine Ricotta cheese with hamburger, sausage, onions, and peppers.
Mix together.
Add salt and pepper to taste to the mixture.
Stuff large shells to capacity with mixture.
Add 1/4 inch sauce to cover bottom of casserole dish.
Place shells side by side, filling dish.
Cover shells with light coating of red sauce.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Remove dish and cover with Mozzarella cheese. Bake uncovered for 10 minutes, let cool for 15 minutes.
Serve.
