Mix Dream Whip as directed on box.
Add all other ingredients and chill for 1 hour.
In large saucepan, cook broccoli in 1 cup water with bouillon cubes.
Bring to a very low boil; reduce heat to medium-low and cook about 7 minutes or until broccoli is tender.
Put milk, cheese cubes and flour in a blender.
Process on medium speed.
Add milk mixture to cooked broccoli mixture.
Add cream.
Cook, stirring frequently, over medium heat until mixture is thickened.
Reduce heat.
Simmer about 10 minutes.
Add sugar gradually to creamed butter.
Beat in eggs and jam. Alternate flour, allspice with buttermilk.
Add nuts, raisins and coconut.
Bake in well greased pan at 300° for about 40 minutes.
Cook bacon; drain and chop up.
Saute onion in bacon fat; drain.
Combine eggs, milk, cream cheese, bacon and seasonings. Pour into pie crust.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 35 minutes.
If you like, add more cheese, mushrooms, crab meat or vegetables.
Makes 1 pie.
Serves 8.
Preheat broiler.
In a bowl, combine catsup, brown sugar, lemon juice, vinegar and Worcestershire sauce.
Brush zucchini pieces lightly with cooking oil.
On 4 long skewers, alternately thread beef, potatoes and zucchini.
Brush with catsup mixture. Broil the kabobs 4 to 5-inches from heat for about 20 minutes. Turn once and brush occasionally with sauce.
Serve kabobs on rice.
(Can be cooked on grill.)
Makes 4 servings.
Saute first 5 ingredients for 6 minutes.
Add broth and bring to a boil.
Add noodles.
Cook until all ingredients are absorbed, about 7 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6 as a side dish.
Combine sugar, margarine, beaten egg and dates in a boiler. Cook over low heat, stirring often, until thick.
Cool, then pour date mixture over Rice Krispies and chopped nuts.
Stir to mix well.
Take small amounts and roll between hands to form finger shapes.
Roll fingers in Angel Flake coconut.
Yields approximately 1 dozen.
Mix meal, flour, sugar, eggs and buttermilk thoroughly.
Add melted shortening.
Pour into loaf pan to within 1-inch of top. Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Brown and drain meat; add onion.
Spread half of the potatoes and carrots in a baking dish and cover with half of the meat and onion mixture.
Season to taste.
Cover with half of a can of condensed tomato soup.
Layer remaining ingredients in same order, topping with remaining half can of soup.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Serves 8.
Stir sugar, salt, 1 1/2 cups of water and oil together.
Add oats and flour with more water if necessary to make a moist dough. Roll very thin on Pammed cookie sheets.
Cut into squares and prick with a fork.
Bake until light brown in a 300° oven.
Watch carefully as crackers around the edges will brown first.
Remove these as they brown.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan; set aside.
In a large bowl, cream the shortening, butter and sugar.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating thoroughly after each addition.
In another bowl, sift the flour and baking powder.
Add the flour in small batches to the creamed mixture alternately with the milk, beginning and ending with the flour.
Cook pudding by directions.
Then add extracts and 1/2 of the coconut.
Cool and top with Cool Whip and the rest of the coconut.
Pick cooked chicken from bone in large chunks; place in pan. Mix the sour cream and soup together; pour over chicken.
Cook stuffing according to directions, using chicken broth in place of water.
Drop over chicken mixture.
Bake for 25 minutes at 350°.
Stir together and serve.
Mix sugar and egg yolks.
Cream oleo and shortening together. Combine both mixtures.
Mix buttermilk and soda; add alternately with flour.
Beat slowly; add coconut and pecans.
Fold in well beaten egg whites with sugar added to egg whites; add vanilla.
In large bowl, stir together the flour, cinnamon and baking soda.
In another bowl, cream the sugar, oil and eggs. Stir in carrots, then add this mixture to the dry ingredients.
Bake in 3 (9-inch) round pans or in a 9 x 13 pan.
Spread refried beans in shallow dish.
Mix sour cream with taco seasoning and spread over beans.
Top with cheese, tomatoes and black olives.
Use tortilla chips for dipping.
Cook sausage over medium-high heat in large skillet, stirring frequently until no longer pink.
Remove from heat and add the cole slaw mix, ginger, garlic, pepper and salt; mix well. Transfer to colander to drain; cool 15 minutes.
Assemble egg rolls as directed on wrapper package, using 1/3 cup sausage mix for each roll.
To cook in a wok, Dutch oven or fryer, add oil to 3-inches deep and heat to 375°.
Fry 4 at a time for 3 minutes or until golden; drain on paper towels.
Serve with your favorite dipping sauce.
Yields 18 to 20 appetizers.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together all-purpose flour, whole bran cereal, Parmesan cheese, snipped chives, baking powder, salt and Italian seasoning.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients.
In a small mixing bowl, combine egg, skim milk and cooking oil.
Add all at once to flour mixture.
Stir just until moistened (batter should be lumpy).
Spray 12 muffin cups with nonstick coating.
Divide batter evenly among muffin cups.
Bake in a 400° oven for about 20 minutes or until golden.
Remove from pan; serve warm.
Yield:
12 muffins.
Bake potatoes and let sit and cool.
Cut lengthwise and hollow out with a spoon.
Set shells aside.
Boil sugar, water, raisins and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add cloves, cinnamon, shortening, soda, flour and fruits.
You may vary the amount of citron to your taste.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Cube cheese and put in crock-pot on low.
Brown meat.
Add meat and salsa to cheese.
When melted, serve with tostito chips.
Sift flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Cream margarine, white sugar, brown sugar and vanilla.
Mix these together and add corn flakes and coconut.
Bake in 350° oven for about 14 minutes.

recipes.t: Braised Chicken Breasts With Mustard Sauce
d: Remove
skin
from chicken breasts.
Place on a rack in an electric
frying pan or in frying pan on top of stove.
Add 1 cup water
to
frying
pan.
Cover
and
cook on high until breasts are
almost
done.
Remove
breasts
from frying pan. Heat
grill. Place
breasts on very hot grill for 10 minutes. Turn often and baste with honey/lemon mixture.
Place on a bed of wild rice and top with 3 tablespoons of Mustard Sauce.
Melt butter; add bread cubes and onion and brown lightly. Then combine all ingredients and spoon into a casserole dish. Sprinkle fine bread crumbs on top and bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Place pork chops on pan. Smear 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of minced garlic on each pork chop. Cover each pork chop with a thin
layer of cheese, then sprinkle Mrs. Dash. Broil pork chops until cooked, but be sure to frequently check to ensure moist pork chops.

Form sausage into 12 patties; brown on both sides. Cook noodles in boiling water as directed on package. Drain and mix with 2 tablespoons pork fat. Spoon the noodles into buttered 11 3/4 x 7 1/2 x 1 3/4-inch rectangular dish. Mix sauerkraut with brown sugar and celery seed. Place on top of noodles. Place sausage on top. Pour beef broth over all and sprinkle top with buttered bread crumbs. Place, uncovered, on rack in large electric skillet preheated to 400°. Bake for 1 hour. Have skillet covered and vents closed. Yields 4 to 6 servings.
Cook bacon until crisp; drain.
Set aside 1 tablespoon drippings.
Crumble bacon; set aside.
In same skillet, brown sausage; drain off fat.
Stir together flour, baking powder and salt.
Add milk and eggs; beat until smooth.
Spread reserved bacon drippings in a 10 x 6 x 2-inch baking dish.
Place sausage pieces in dish; sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
Pour batter over all.
Bake uncovered at 400° until set, 30 to 35 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Soften cream cheese and gradually add sour cream.
Beat with mixer until creamy, then add taco mix.
Spread mixture in a glass pan.
Top with lettuce, cheese, peppers, onions, olives and tomatoes.
Serve with Doritos chips.
Combine honey and peanut butter with dry milk powder; mix well.
Chill thoroughly.
Shape into 1 1/2-inch balls.
Roll in coconut.
Yields 36 candies.
Fry bacon.
Remove bacon; leave 3 tablespoons of grease in pan.
Add onion; cook until lightly browned.
Add remaining ingredients and a dash of pepper.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer 1 to 2 minutes.
Top with crumbled bacon.
Serves 6.
Mix together 1 egg, melted butter and cake mix.
Pat this mixture down in a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar.
Add dry ingredients to egg mixture. Mix well and fold in apples, vanilla and nuts.
Top with coconut. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Use a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Drain fruit.
Put 1/4 cup juice and marshmallows in medium saucepan.
Heat on low heat until marshmallows melt.
In large mixing bowl, soften cream cheese with a little whipping cream. Whip the remaining cream.
Add salt and melted marshmallows to the cream mixture.
Fold in whipped cream and fruit.
Spoon into four (No. 2) cans.
Cover with foil and freeze.
Make meat balls; cook in large pot with sauce.
Drain sauerkraut and mix with onions and sour cream.
Spread the mixture in the bottom of a 9 X 13 pan.	Evenly distribute the corned beef and Mozzarella cheese over the top.
Top with broken bite-sized bits of rye bread.
Drizzle the entire dish with melted butter and bake in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes.
Serves 8.

recipes.t: Lemon Herb Baste For Cornish Hens
d: Brush mixture on hens while grilling for a delicious lemon flavor.
Brown ground chuck, onion and garlic; cool.
Add Mozzarella cheese, bread crumbs, parsley, egg, salt and pepper.
Spoon enough sauce to cover bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Stuff cooked shells and place in pan.
Cover with sauce and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes or until hot.
In medium bowl, combine ground beef, bread crumbs, onion, salt and eggs; mix well.
Shape into 3/4-inch balls.
In a large skillet, brown meatballs in oil, turning occasionally.
Drain. Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to coat meatballs with glaze.
Serve warm in chafing dish.
Makes 48 meatballs.
Cook scallops in margarine for 5 minutes.
Cut bacon into 2-inch pieces.
Arrange bacon and scallops alternately on skewer. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
To bake, insert skewers in uncooked potato halves, so they will stand upright.
Bake at 475° for 20 minutes.
Serves 4.
Wash mushrooms, remove stems and chop enough to make 1 cup. In a saucepan, cook mushroom stems, onion and garlic in margarine until tender.
Stir in bread crumbs and cheese.
Spoon mixture into mushroom caps.
Arrange caps in a 15 x 10 x 2-inch pan.
Bake at 425° for 8 to 10 minutes or until heated through.
Heat olive oil and saute onion until translucent.
Add tomatoes and water.
Bring to a boil and add salt, pepper, garlic powder and basil.
Bring to a second boil and add rice and stir.
Reduce to low heat and cover.
Cook until liquid is absorbed, 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in Parmesan cheese before serving.

recipes.t: Orange Wild Rice With Raisins And Apples
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
In mixing bowl, combine cooked rices. Gently toss together raisins, almonds, parsley, zest, apple, oil, orange juice, salt and pepper with combined rices.
Place mixture in casserole.
Cover with foil; heat thoroughly for 20 minutes.
Mix first 8 ingredients and pour in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan. Sprinkle with cake mix.
Drizzle melted butter over top.
Top with nuts.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 25 minutes.
Serve cold with whipped cream.
Layer first 6 ingredients in order listed in a large salad bowl.
Combine salad dressing, sour cream and dressing mix; mix well.
Spread over top of vegetables, sealing to edge of bowl. Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired. Cover tightly and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Toss gently before serving.
Yield:
12 to 15 servings.
Place cut up chicken in 9 x 12-inch pan.
Mix soup, milk, vegetables and onion in saucepan.
Heat until blended and vegetables are slightly cooked.
Pour over chicken.
Melt margarine and pour over cornbread stuffing.
Add 1 cup chicken broth and stir well.
Spread over chicken mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Place all ingredients in a screwtop jar.
Shake well.
Store in refrigerator.
Empty envelope of gelatin into blender.
Add lemon juice, onion slices and boiling water; cover blender and blend at high speed for 40 seconds.
Add mayonnaise, paprika, dill and salmon. Cover and blend at high speed briefly.
Add cream, 1/3 at a time, and blend after each addition.
Blend 30 seconds longer.
Pour into 4-cup mold which has been lightly coated with salad oil. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Unmold.
Saute bell pepper, onion, garlic and squash in 1 tablespoon oil.
Add mushrooms.
Remove. Add sausage and saute; drain and discard remaining grease.
Pour Hunt's in skillet and add all of the ingredients.
Serve over spaghetti and top with Mozzarella cheese.
You may also layer spaghetti, sauce and cheese and bake in oven at 350° until cheese melts.
Steam carrots until tender; drain.
Over medium heat combine in skillet the butter, sugar, lemon juice and salt.
When bubbly add carrots and parsley.
Remove from heat.
Stir until carrots are coated.
Serve immediately.
Stir ingredients together until lemonade mix is dissolved. Just before serving, add 1 quart of ice cubes and 1 to 2 bottles of sugar-free 7-Up or ginger ale.
Cook raisins in water for 10 minutes.
Add butter; let melt, then cool.
Add egg, flour, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon, baking soda, allspice, cloves and salt.
Pour into ungreased cookie sheet with edges.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 400°.
Lightly grease 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie plate. Mix crabmeat, cheese and onions.
Place in pie plate.
Beat remaining ingredients until smooth (15 seconds in blender on high speed or 1 minute by hand).
Pour into pie plate.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Mix crushed pineapple and instant pistachio pudding in a bowl. Add Cool Whip and mix well with spoon.
Add nuts, if desired. Decorate with sliced pineapple and cherries.
Put in refrigerator to cool.
Put pork chops in casserole dish, then add a layer of potatoes and then a layer of onion.
Salt and pepper, then add cream of chicken soup.
Bake at 375° for about 45 minutes to an hour.
Mix all ingredients together.
Make into balls.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes or overnight.
Then dip in chocolate.
Brown sausage (Deans or Owens); drain.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, cover bottom with 8 slices of bread, cut in cubes.
Sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese.
Add drained sausage.
Mix eggs (beaten) in milk and mustard and pour over sausage.
Cover with Saran Wrap and refrigerate overnight.
In morning, top with can of mushrooms (drained) and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Serves 6 to 8 people. Serve with fruit and pastries.
To yolks, add ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Replace yolk mixture in whites.
Beat eggs slightly in a bowl.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Pack mixture into a greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for about 40 minutes.
Unmold onto hot platter.
Garnish with parsley and hard-cooked egg segments.
Yields 8 to 10 servings.
Contains 191 calories per serving.

recipes.t: Faye And Hildy'S Celery Seed Dressing
d: Put all ingredients in blender and blend.
Mix together, sprinkle with sugar or Sweet 'N Low to taste. Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate for at least an hour.
Beat eggs and add sugar.
Add milk and crackers, then coconut and vanilla.
Cook until thick.
Mix together all ingredients, except dry cake mix, pecans and melted butter.
Line pan with wax paper.
Pour mixture in pan.
Sprinkle yellow cake mix on top (dry).
Sprinkle pecans on that.
Pour melted butter on top.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Turn upside-down.
Take paper off and let cool.
Combine jello with boiling water.
Add the cool water.
When cool and jello-like, fold in the remaining ingredients.
Mash
sweet
potatoes
and
mix in all the ingredients. Bake until
firm and browned on top.
Then add topping and let cook for 15 minutes on 375°.
Mix eggs, sugar, syrup and butter.
Beat together well.
Add oatmeal and coconut, stirring together well.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes at 350°.
This is a rich pie very much like pecan.
Pie is done when filling is set.
Preheat oven to 350°, butter a 10 inch spring form that is 2 inches high.
Work the flour, hazelnuts, butter, sugar, egg, 1 egg yolk, cinnamon and lemon zest to a dough.
Press 3 quarters of the dough into the bottom and sides of the pan.
Fill with jam.
Roll out the remaining dough 1/4 inch thick, cut into strips, criss-cross them over the filling, brush with 1 egg yolk.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Cool and serve.
Mix the sugar, eggs and oil.
Sift together the cinnamon, salt, soda and flour.
Add to the first mixture. Stir in the rhubarb.
Mix and pour into a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Sprinkle on 3 tablespoons brown sugar and 1 tablespoon cinnamon. Bake at 350° for 45 to 55 minutes.
Mix cream cheese, Miracle Whip and ketchup together with mixer.
Add onion and shrimp.
Blend all ingredients; serve with crackers or vegetables.
*You can use bacon (crumbled up), Canadian bacon or ham.
Peel potatoes or leave on skins.
Cut each potato into wedges (4 each).
In mixing bowl, combine oil, salt, garlic powder and pepper.
Add cut-up potatoes; toss to coat.
Wrap potatoes in heavy foil.
Seal edges tightly.
Grill packet on medium to hot grill about 35 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
These can also be cooked in the oven.
Mix the top ingredients in a bowl and use this mixture in place of your usual milk when making biscuits.
When your biscuits are done, sprinkle with powdered sugar while hot.
Note: Fresh rhubarb is best!
If frozen rhubarb is used, defrost prior to adding to filling.
Canned rhubarb must be drained first and isn't as good.
Brown hamburger, drain grease.
Cook hamburger with the taco seasoning mix according to package directions.
Line a 13 x 9-inch baking pan with the refried beans.
Layer the hamburger, onion, salsa and cheese over the refried beans.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Mix olives and sour cream and top the baked mixture. Serve with nachos.
Melt together oleo and cream cheese.
Add soup and onion; mix together until smooth.
Put 1/2 of potatoes in a greased pan and pour on half of the sauce.
Sprinkle the rest of the potatoes and add the remainder of sauce.
Top with 1 cup grated Cheddar cheese. Bake at 325°, covered, for 1 hour.
Mix ingredients together and roll chicken.
Bake in lightly buttered pan for 1 hour at 350° until brown.
Butter sides and bottom of pan.
Cook 10x sugar, oleo and evaporated milk.
Stir constantly.
When it starts to boil, boil for 3 minutes.
Remove from stove and add peanut butter, Marshmallow Creme and vanilla.
Stir and pour in pan.
Cool completely.
Cut and enjoy!
In 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat, cook livers, green pepper, celery and garlic in butter until vegetables are tender, stirring often.
Stir soup mix, water and hot pepper sauce into skillet.
Heat to boiling; stir in rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover; simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender.
Makes 6 servings.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add cranberry sauce.
Use fork or wire whisk to dissolve cranberry sauce in jello mixture. Add pineapple, undrained.
Stir to blend.
Let jello chill.
Dust roast with flour and brown.
Put into large Dutch oven and surround it with potatoes, carrots and the green beans.
Slice onions over the top and cover with both cans of the soup, which have been mixed together with 1/2 can of water to blend.
Bake at 325° for 3 hours, or until done.
In a bowl, blend cream cheese and Miracle Whip.
Stir in raspberries, pineapple and pecans.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour in 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Freeze 8 hours.
To serve, set out 15 to 20 minutes.
Cut and serve.
Serves 12 to 18.
Mix first 3 ingredients together.
Press into 13 x 10-inch dish.
Bake at 300° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Do not overbake!
Cool. Mix next 3 ingredients and spread over cooled pretzel mix.
Stir together remaining ingredients; put mixture in the refrigerator to chill for 10 minutes.
Pour over top of dish and refrigerate.
All ingredients can be substituted for low calorie products.
In a mixing bowl, pour water over oatmeal and allow to stand 10 minutes. Add sugars and butter, stirring until the butter melts.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Sift flour, cocoa, soda and salt together.
Add to batter.
Mix well. Stir in half of the chocolate chips.
Pour into a greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle top of cake with walnuts and remaining chips. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Cook rice as directed.
Put in casserole.
Blend 2/3 cup Cheddar cheese, peppers and sour cream.
Put remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until thick.
Add rice, can of broth (and enough water to make 2 cups), 2 tablespoons butter or oleo and onions.
Cook according to rice directions.
Mix with cream of chicken soup; salt and pepper to taste.
Pour into casserole.
Top with chicken breasts; salt and pepper chicken.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine Jell-O pudding, egg yolks and milk in saucepan.
Cook and stir over medium heat until mixture comes to a full boil. Remove from heat.
Arrange layer of vanilla wafers on bottom and sides of 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Add a layer of banana slices and of pudding.
Continue layering wafers, bananas and pudding, ending with pudding.
Stir boiling water into gelatin in bowl for 2 minutes or until dissolved.
Mix water and ice to make 1 1/4 cups.
Stir into gelatin until slightly thickened.
Remove any remaining ice.
Stir in whipped topping until smooth.
Refrigerate 10 minutes or until mixture will mound.
Spoon into crust.
Refrigerate 4 hours or until firm.
Garnish with additional whipped topping, if desired.
Drain corn, reserving 1/4 cup liquid. Sift together flour, baking powder, salt, parsley flakes and paprika. Combine eggs, melted butter and liquid from corn.

Mix well. Add to dry ingredients all at once and stir until smooth. Fold in drained corn. Drop batter from a tablespoon into deep fat heated to 375°. Fry, a few at a time, until golden brown on all sides.
Remove from fat.
Drain on paper towel. Keep hot while frying remaining fritters.
Cook macaroni; drain and rinse with cold water.
Drain again. Brown meat; drain off fat.
Add taco seasoning and mix well; cool. In large bowl, mix macaroni, green pepper, onions, cheese, tomatoes, lettuce and seasonings; chill.
Just before serving, stir in seasoned meat, French dressing and chips; toss lightly. Makes 8 to 10 servings.
Mix all ingredients in a 1-gallon Ziploc bag.
Marinate in bag several hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Lift from marinade and grill over charcoal grill.
(Based on Iranian cooking with yogurt!)
Mix first 5 ingredients.
Spread in a 9 x 12-inch pan (sprayed with Pam).
Sprinkle yellow cake mix over pumpkin.
Add pecans. Dot top with oleo.
Bake at 250° for 50 minutes.
Mix margarine, cloves, mashed garlic, salt, celery seed and black pepper together.
Set aside.
Boil 30 minutes all ingredients together.
Pack in pint jars. Process for 20 minutes in pressure canner.
Yield 6 to 7 pints. Tastes just like real pineapple.
Mix together with reduced calorie Ranch dressing.
Prepare the cake mix and bake in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish according to package directions.
When done, remove from oven and while still hot, poke holes in cake with end of wooden spoon. Pour sweetened condensed milk, then caramel topping into holes. Spread entire cake with whipped topping.
Sprinkle crushed candy bars on top of cake.
Refrigerate cake until serving time.
Cake can be frozen.
Mix all ingredients except Ritz crackers and margarine.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch dish.
Mix crushed crackers and margarine and cover top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine sugar, milk and marshmallows in a saucepan.
Cook and stir until sugar and marshmallows melt.
When bubbles cover entire surface, boil and stir over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Beat in butter, salt, chocolate bits and vanilla until chocolate bits are melted.
Add nuts, if desired.
Spread into buttered 9 inch square pan.
Chill until firm.
Cut into 64 squares and enjoy.
Cook sugar, Karo, milk and peanuts until 240°; remove from fire.
Add remaining ingredients; stir good and spoon out on foil.
Mix all ingredients, except peanut butter and oatmeal.
Stir well.
Cook for 1 minute.
Remove from heat.
Add peanut butter and oatmeal; mix well.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper.
Have cheese at room temperature. Mix cheese, onion, Worcestershire sauce and Accent until blended.
Add 1/2 cup pecans and 1/4 cup parsley.
Shape mixture into ball.
Place in bowl lined with waxed paper.
Chill overnight.
Slice cucumbers and onions.
Sprinkle with salt and let stand 6 hours.
Drain.
Mix sugar and vinegar.
Dissolve, then add sour cream.
Mix and pour over vegetables.
Let stand 24 hours.
Bring to boil until clear and thick and bubbling.
Cook for about 5 minutes, then add 2 to 3 cartons of clean, fresh, cold strawberries.
Put in prepared pie crust.
Just before serving, top with whipped cream.
Place sugar, oil and pumpkin in large mixer bowl and beat well at medium speed.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Sift flour, baking powder, soda, cinnamon and salt together and fold into batter.
Stir in nuts and raisins.
Pour into greased and floured 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/4 hours or until done.
Do not open oven door under 1 hour.
Let cool slightly in pan before turning onto cake rack.
Hard boil eggs; remove 1/2 to 2/3 yolks.
Chop remaining yolks and whites.
Add chopped olives.
Mix in mustard and salad dressing to taste.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar, vinegar and mustard.
Boil this, stirring constantly, on low heat until thick.
Chill.
Then add real Kraft mayonnaise dressing.
Mix dressing with sliced, cooked potatoes, 8 boiled chopped eggs, celery and onion.
Drain potatoes and mash well.
Add vanilla, flour, margarine, egg and sugar.
Make small balls and put a marshmallow in center of each ball.
Roll in coconut.
Place on greased baking dish and bake in 350° oven for 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix together first 7 ingredients. Put in large pan. Melt butter. Mix with potato chips. Spread on top. Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Combine last 5 ingredients.
Pour over cereal and stir.
Cook 2 hours at 200°.
Mix ingredients and pour over crackers.
Bake at 200° for 1 hour.
Stir every 20 minutes.
Combine all ingredients. Spoon into buttered shallow 3-quart casserole. Bake at 350° until bubbly (about 1 hour).

Cream shortening until fluffy. Gradually add sugar and cream cheese making sure mixture is smooth. Beat in egg yolk, vanilla, and flour. Use a cookie press or chill until firm, roll and cut with decorative cutters. Decorate for the holiday. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Yield 3-4 dozen.
Cream butter with 7/8 cup of sugar.
Add well beaten egg, then the milk and vanilla.
Mix the dry ingredients together and add alternately to the milk mixture, beating thoroughly.
Saute the veggies in bacon drippings.
Mix the soup and the milk and evaporated milk together and heat; add the sauteed veggies and heat through; don't boil.
Serve in big soup cups. Makes 3 large soup cups or 4 small ones of chowder.
Crumble bacon atop each as you serve the soup.
Combine instant tea powder and the cold water; stir until the tea is dissolved.
Add sweetener, orange juice and lime juice. Mix thoroughly.
Chill.
Serve over ice in tall glasses.
Makes 6 servings.
Garnish with orange slices and fresh cranberries.
Mix first six ingredients together and pat one-half of mixture into 9 x 13 pan.
Melt caramels with evaporated milk. Pour over crust.
Sprinkle nuts and chocolate chips over caramel mixture and top with remaining crust mixture.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Dissolve Jello in 2 c. boiling water.
Add the cherry syrup plus enough cold water to make 1 1/2 c.
Put in the refrigerator to thicken.
When partially set, add the cranberry sauce, cherries, cut in half, and the nuts, apples and marshmallows.
Mix well.
Refrigerate until set.
This keeps well and can be made ahead.
Grease a 9 x 13 x 2 1/2-inch casserole dish.
Cook noodles; drain well.
Make layer of noodles, layer of sauce, 1/2 cottage cheese, 1/3 of the nuts, layer of spinach, layer of Mozzarella and Parmesan, layer of sauce and layer of noodles.
Repeat.
Top with cheese and nuts.
In a large mixing bowl, sift together the flour, salt, baking powder, cinnamon and nutmeg.
In a small bowl, whisk together the eggs, oil and orange juice and add to the flour mixture.
Before the flour and liquid ingredients are completely combined, fold in the blueberries, stirring gently.
Fill well-greased muffin tin about 2/3 full.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes 12 muffins.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium heat.
Add chicken, onion and pepper.
Cook and stir until chicken is done.
Add broth and tomatoes; bring to a boil.
Stir in rice and cover.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Let stand 3 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix all ingredients well.
Refrigerate for several hours before serving.
Vegetable may be changed to your favorites.
Mix rice, water, juice and salt just to moisten in pan, then bring to quick boil.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Add marshmallows, fruits and nuts.
Cool to room temperature or in fridge.
Fold in the cream.
Chill at least 1 hour.
To make pizza crust:
Spread rolls on greased jelly roll pan. Bake crust according to package directions.
Combine all ingredients and cook until veggies are tender, about 1 hour.
Mix wet ingredients and add to mixed dry ingredients.
Let rise for 1/2 hour.
Spoon into 375° deep fat oil.
Cook until golden brown.
Remove and serve.
Makes 30 hush puppies.
*Hot peppers chopped into batter makes them good.
In crock-pot, put all ingredients except wine.
Mix together well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 8 to 10 hours.
During last hour of cooking, add wine and stir.
Serve over egg noodles or rice.
In a saucepan, cook mushrooms and green pepper in butter until pepper is tender. Blend in soup. Gradually stir
in milk.
Add chicken and pimento.
Heat, stirring now and then. Serve in patty shells or on toast.
Soften cream cheese to room temperature.
Combine all ingredients, except bread.
Beat until well blended.
Chill until fairly stiff.
Spread on pumpernickel rounds.
In saucepan, cook green pepper and celery in oleo until crisp. Stir in soup, water and soy sauce.
Add vegetables and chicken; heat through.
Serve with rice.
Brown meat and onion; drain.
Grate cheese; set aside.
Mix corn bread batter.
Heat greased iron skillet.
Put half batter in skillet, then add browned beef with onions.
Sprinkle cheese on top of this.
Add remaining batter.
Cook approximately 1 hour. Be careful not to let cheese touch sides of skillet or it will stick when turned out.
Cook meat; mix taco season package in meat.
Mix both cans of chili.
Heat oven to 350°.
First put some chips on bottom of pan. Make sure you mix chili with meat, then put meat with chili on top of chips.
Put more chips on top.
Lightly brown meat; drain off grease.
Add onion and peppers and cook with meat for about 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour into greased casserole dish; cover.
Bake 45 minutes.
Last 15 minutes remove lid and spread desired amount of cheese on top.
Mix graham cracker crumbs with melted margarine and press lightly into a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Dissolve yeast in 1/2
cup
warm
water.
Add
remaining ingredients.
Leave at room temperature for 24 hours.
Feed 3/4 cup sugar, 3 tablespoons instant potatoes and 1 cup warm water. Leave out 12 hours.
Use 1 cup starter for baking and put 1 cup back in refrigerator.
Mix together very gently and place in a greased casserole. Sprinkle with grated cheese or cover with spaghetti sauce and meat.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Serves 12.
Fill pot half full of water.
Add salt to Worcestershire sauce and margarine.
Add sausage; boil 5 minutes.
Add potatoes; boil 5 minutes.
Add onions; boil 5 minutes.
Lift strainer and check potatoes and onions for tenderness.
Add corn; boil 5 minutes.
Add shrimp boil and hot sauce; let come to boil.
Remove vegetables after draining and place in a large container.
Add medium size shrimp (1/2 pound per person); boil 3 minutes.
Remove and serve. This is good for a family gathering.
Combine seasonings with butter.
Rub butter seasonings onto chicken.
Bake in slow 300° oven 1 1/4 hours.
Serves 4.
Melt butter with corn syrup in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat.
Add brown sugar and stir to dissolve.
Cook syrup to hard ball stage.
To check, drop some syrup into cup of cold water and when it forms a firm ball it is done.
Takes about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add baking soda, stirring to blend.
Pour over popcorn; stir to coat evenly.
Blend brown sugar, oleo, salt and Karo together and boil 8 minutes.
Take pan off heat and add baking soda and butter.
Into very large mixing bowl, pour mixture over 6 quarts popped corn. Peanuts or pecans can be added to popped corn.
Mix thoroughly. Bake on 2 cookie sheets at 200° for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
M - M - M - M - Good.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl cook ziti until just barely tender; drain and place in a large bowl.
Mix the Ricotta and 1/2 of Mozzarella cheese with ziti.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch pan. Cover bottom of pan with 1/2 spaghetti sauce.
Spoon the ziti mixture into pan.
Cover with remaining sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and top with remaining Mozzarella.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes until lightly brown.
Put oil in frypan.
Brown chicken about 10 minutes each side. Take out of pan. Stir onion in and cook until tender.
Blend in soup and water.
Return chicken to pan and spoon soup mixture over chicken.
Cover and cook about 30 minutes or until tender. Serve with noodles.
Cream butter and cheese.
Add sugar.
Add small amount of flour then 1 egg over and over until used up.
Place in cold oven at 350° for 1 hour.
Put hamburger, soup mix, crackers and barbecue sauce in mixing bowl.
Beat egg in separate bowl.
Mix together with hands until well mixed.
Put in baking pan.
Put in oven at 375° for about 30 to 45 minutes, or until light brown.
Mix ingredients in heavy, 2-quart saucepan, then stir and cook over low heat until sugar dissolves.
Then add pecans and stir and cook to a full, all-over boil.
Then boil slowly about 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until candy reaches soft ball stage (234°).
Remove from heat and beat until candy thickens, but still looks shiny.
Boil cured ham hocks until tender.
Remove ham hocks from boiler.
Add collard greens to liquid in boiler.
Put ham hocks on top of greens.
Then put bacon drippings in and bring to a boil. Simmer on low heat until tender.
Add a pinch of salt and chopped onion.
Melt butter in saucepan, add flour and mix well.
Add milk and cook until creamy sauce forms, stirring constantly.
Add seasoning, ketchup and crabmeat.
Cook for 2 minutes. Add egg and cheese and mix well until cheese melts.
Grind tomatoes, celery, onions and peppers through food chopper. Sprinkle with salt and let stand overnight.
Drain.
Add brown sugar, mustard, cinnamon and vinegar.
Mix all together. Mix well and put in jars. Requires no cooking and will keep.
This is a very good relish.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat eggs well.
Add remaining ingredients.
Fold in apples (mixture will be thick).
Spread in pan.
Bake 45 to 60 minutes or until toothpick stuck in middle of cake cakes out clean.
Serve with vanilla ice cream or frozen yogurt.
Makes 10 to 15 servings.
Drain pineapple.
Reserve 3 tablespoons of the juice.
Mix reserved juice with 1/2 cup of water, soy sauce, cornstarch, vinegar and pepper flakes.
Set aside.
Cook and drain peas thoroughly.
Mix together other ingredients very thoroughly.
Carefully combine with peas. Chill and garnish with more dill or chives.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Wash berries until blue color is gone. Drain peaches; lay on paper towel.
Set juice aside.
In small bowl, combine flour, sugar and cinnamon.
Cut in margarine.
Set aside.
Make muffin batter, substituting juice along with liquid for correct amount.
Pour into greased 8-inch pan.
Cut peaches in half.
Press into batter, fat-side up.
Sprinkle berries on top. Add flour/sugar/cinnamon mixture over top.
Bake 25 minutes or until golden brown.

Dice ham in a medium size bowl; add sour cream a little at a time so you will not get too much. Add chopped cream cheese and picante sauce. Mix ingredients well. Spread on flour tortillas and roll up. You may cut in half or leave whole.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add applesauce and beaten egg. Mix and sift dry ingredients.
Add nuts and combine the 2 mixtures.
Bake in loaf pans 45 to 60 minutes at 350° to 375°.
Combine all ingredients and chill for several hours before serving.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Add package of taco seasoning mix and about half of taco sauce.
Simmer.
Put tortilla chips on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan, then ground beef mixture.
Layer cheese on meat.
Then add lettuce, onion and tomato.
Mix remaining taco sauce and 1/2 of bottle of Zesty Italian dressing and pour over salad.
Cream cheese, chilies, sour cream, picante sauce and ham together.
Spread on flour tortillas and roll up into a roll. Place in Saran Wrap and place in refrigerator to cool, then cut in pieces and serve.
Combine sugar, 1/2 cup butter, salt and water.
Bring to rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Slice cooked yams 1-inch thick.
Slice apples 1/2-inch thick.
Carefully arrange yams and apples in alternate layers in steam table pan.
Pour over with syrup.
Top with melted butter. Bake in 375° oven for 1 hour until apples are tender.
May garnish with coconut.
Grease 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan and a small loaf pan.
Place large marshmallows 2 inches apart in pan.
Mix sugar, flour, soda and salt together.
Add mashed bananas, shortening, buttermilk and vanilla.
Mix thoroughly.
Add unbeaten egg whites and mix thoroughly.
Stir in chopped nuts. Carefully spoon over marshmallows in greased pans.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes, according to pans used.
Mix all ingredients together and let sit in refrigerator for 2 to 3 hours before serving.
Really better made a day ahead.
In skillet, over medium-high heat, in 2 tablespoons hot oil, stir-fry chicken until no longer pink; remove.
Set aside.
In same skillet, in remaining 1 tablespoon oil, stir-fry vegetables and garlic until tender-crisp.
Place rolls in 9 x 13-inch ungreased pan; press into pan for crust.
Fry sausage; pour off grease.
Add onion and fry until tender.
Mix eggs, milk and cheese with seasoning.
Add sausage mixture.
Pour into pan lined with rolls.
Bake at 350° about 25 minutes.
In mixing bowl, blend all ingredients until smooth.
Pack into small, oiled bowl.
Chill overnight.
Unmold and garnish with fresh parsley.
Yields 3 pounds.
Mix together ingredients until well blended.
Split 1 package hot dogs lengthwise, making sure not to cut completely through the hot dogs.
Spoon some of the barbecue mixture into each hot dog and place in a flat pan, slightly touching each other.
Pour any remaining sauce over the hot dogs.
Bake 30 minutes in a 375° oven.
Put water and vinegar in 10-gallon pot.
Place a layer of crabs on an elevated platform in the pot.
Sprinkle each layer generously with seasoning mix.
Put lid on pot and steam about 25 minutes.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add egg and vanilla.
Then add vinegar
and dry ingredients.
Beat.
Roll into balls size of walnuts.
Press
down
with
bottom of glass.
Dip glass in water or sugar
to prevent sticking.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Heat honey and peanut butter.
Quickly add carob and then all the seeds, coconut and fruit.
Pour into greased 8 x 8-inch pan and refrigerate until it hardens.
Cut into squares and keep refrigerated.
Yields 25 squares.
Blend all ingredients except
the walnuts and turn into a shallow greased casserole
dish.
Top
with
the walnuts and bake 20 minutes at 350°.
Serve with a selection of crackers.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat eggs until fluffy.
Add milk, salad oil and lemon juice.
Add this mixture to flour mixture and blend.
Pour 2 inches of oil into a large, heavy skillet and heat.
Dip chicken pieces into batter and drop into hot oil.
Reduce heat to medium and fry about 45 minutes, turning frequently to brown all sides of chicken.
Remove chicken to platter.
Pour most of oil from skillet.
Add amount of milk desired for gravy, heat, stirring brown particles from bottom of skillet.
Mix sugar, sour cream and vanilla in a large pot.
Stir and bring to a boil.
Boil 3 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in roasted pecans.
Stir until liquid is absorbed.
Pour onto waxed paper; separate so pecans will dry without sticking together.
Allow to dry.
Store in airtight container.
Combine softened cream cheese and shredded Cheddar cheese.
Mix until well blended, add remaining.
Mix well.
Chill overnight. Shape into ball.
Roll in fine chopped nuts.
Blend shortening, sugar and eggs.
Add flour, baking soda, cream of tartar and salt. Mix well.
Roll mixture into balls.
In sandwich bag shake together the 4 tablespoons of sugar and 2 teaspoons of cinnamon.
Place balls into bag and shake.
Put balls on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Melt butter, blend in flour, salt and pepper.
Gradually stir in broth.
Heat and stir until thick.
Add all other ingredients. Serve over pastry shells.
Cook, peel and chop shrimp into small bite size pieces, enough to make 2 cups; set aside.
Mix chili sauce, Worcestershire sauce, horseradish (found in the dairy products at most grocers) and lemon juice.
Place cream cheese on platter.
Mix shrimp into sauce and pour over cream cheese.
Chill.
Serve with your favorite crackers.
Melt
margarine
in casserole dish and add to remaining ingredients.
Bake at 350° until set.

Mix all ingredients except chicken and cheese in casserole dish. Place chicken on top and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done. Remove and add grated cheese over top of casserole. Return to oven until cheese melts.
Grind the cranberries, orange and orange peel.
Add the sugar and mix well.
Let stand overnight.
Mix the Jell-O and water. When half set, add to cranberry mixture.
Then add remaining ingredients.
Pour into mold and set in refrigerator until completely set.
Mix dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Cream sugar, oil and eggs until well blended.
Gradually add dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Stir in apples and nuts.
Pour into greased and floured Bundt cake pan.
Bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes in a cold 350° oven.
Top with glaze.
Season salmon.
Cover with capers, lemon juice and vinegar. Spread with sour cream.
Arrange slices of lemon on top, sprinkle with seasoned salt and paprika.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes.
Serves 4.
In a 10-inch skillet over medium heat in hot oil, cook mushrooms and green onions with garlic until tender and liquid is evaporated, stirring often.
Stir in mixed vegetables, tomatoes, half and half, cheese and basil.
Add spaghetti.
Heat through, stirring occasionally.
Mix flour, margarine and pecans together.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 375° until light brown. Cool completely.
In a 9-inch pie pan, mix sugar and graham cracker crumbs.
Mix in butter.
Press mixture firmly and evenly against sides and bottom of pie pan.
Set aside in refrigerator.
Combine all ingredients except pie shell.
Blend well with electric mixer.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake in preheated oven at 400° for about 30 minutes or until golden and puffy.
Top with whipped cream.
Mix all ingredients in large pot over medium heat just until starts to boil, stirring frequently.
Reduce heat and simmer for about 1 hour.
Mix rice, ground beef and onion.
Steam cabbage in pot of hot water.
Drain and gently remove leaves.
Put tablespoon of mixture on leaf and roll.
Place in casserole dish.
Add tomato sauce and 1/2 cup water.
(Use water that cabbage was steamed in.)
Cover and bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Combine sausage, eggs, stuffing mix and sage.
Mix thoroughly. Shape into balls.
In dry skillet, brown all sides and drain on paper towels.
Drain fat from skillet.
Add catsup, chili sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, vinegar and water; stir well.
Return meatballs to skillet; cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Refrigerate or may be frozen.
When ready to serve, reheat.
Mix beef, salt, pepper and A. 1. sauce together.
Form a loaf. Place on a rack over a pan with a small amount of water.
Cover with foil.
Bake at 350° until done.
Remove from oven and let cool.
Prepare gravy lite, using double the amount of water called for.
Add vinegar, bay leaf, garlic powder and mushrooms.
Simmer until mushrooms are tender.
Remove from heat.
Crumble meat into the gravy mix.
Stir in the milk and continue to stir until milk is dissolved.
Place 1/2 cup cooked noodles on plate.
Pour meat mixture over all.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Stir
all ingredients together.
Place in casserole and bake 30 to 45 minutes at 350°.
In a 1 to 2-quart pan, sprinkle gelatin over water; let stand for 5 minutes to soften.
Heat over medium heat for 30 seconds or until mixture begins to simmer.
Remove from heat.
In a small mixer bowl, beat eggs on high speed for 2 minutes or until slightly thick.
Slowly beat in sugar, liqueur and gelatin.
In a large mixer bowl, beat cream until it mounds softly.
Add egg mixture and fold in to blend.
Pour into a 1-quart mold or into individual serving dishes.
Refrigerate for 3 hours or until mold is set. Unmold onto serving plate or serve from individual dishes.
Garnish with fresh sliced strawberries and mint, if available.
Sprinkle servings with toasted almonds.
Mix all ingredients together and shape into a ball.
Roll in chopped walnuts and place cherry on top.
Garnish with parsley and serve with assorted crackers.
The cheese ball freezes well.
Cook the pasta according to the package directions.
Drain well.
Pour the pasta into a large bowl and quickly add the margarine, heavy cream and about half of the Parmesan cheese.
Toss until well mixed.
Serve immediately topped with pepper and the remaining cheese.
Serves 5 to 6 people.
Stir together soup, cheese, milk, mayonnaise and eggs.
Pour over broccoli.
Sprinkle cracker crumbs over top.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In kettle, combine cranberry juice and pectin.
Bring to full, rolling boil.
Stir in sugar.
Bring again to boil.
Boil hard, uncovered, 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in lemon juice.
Skim off foam.
Pour into hot, sterilized jars. Cover with hot wax or water seal.
Combine all ingredients and beat with a hand mixer until thoroughly mixed.
Pack into covered crock and refrigerate.
Combine potatoes, celery, eggs, pimiento and seasonings.
Add combined salad dressing and mustard; mix lightly.
Chill.

Spread 1/2 can enchilada sauce in 3-quart oblong baking dish. Set aside. Combine chicken, 1 cup cheese, chilies and onion. Spread about 1/3 cup mixture along one side of tortilla. Roll jelly roll fashion and place seam side down in dish. Pour remaining 1/2 can of enchilada sauce over enchiladas. Sprinkle remaining 1/2 cup of cheese on top. Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Cook in crock-pot for 1 hour.
Add hot dogs.
Put bacon in saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil.
Drain bacon; dry on paper towels.
Saute bacon in heavy skillet for 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove all but 2 tablespoons fat.
Add onions and garlic.
Cook until onions are transparent.
Add potatoes, stock, tarragon and salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender, but not mushy, and liquid is absorbed.
Add vinegar and oil and toss lightly. Sprinkle with parsley; serve hot.
Serves 6.
Mix all juices at least 3 hours before.
Pour ginger ale just before serving.
Pour over ice or sherbet.
Mix all ingredients together in crock-pot except whipping cream.
Heat until cheese is melted, stirring occasionally.
Add whipping cream to mixture 1/2 hour before serving.
Stir.
Serve over Fritos or tortilla chips.
Put fruit and nuts through food chopped, then mix with orange juice and honey.
Press well together and let stand in cool place for 24 hours.
Shape into balls and roll in grated sweet chocolate, coconut or chopped nuts.
Melt
margarine,
then	add
sugar.
When
syrupy,
add peanut butter.
Peanut
butter burns easily, so keep stirring over
low heat.
Place cereals, pretzels and nuts in roasting and
baking pans.
(I
use top and bottom of roasting pan and two
x 13-inch pans.) Pour melted mixture over cereals; mix well.	Bake in	a
oven
for
a
couple of hours, until cereals
are dry and crispy.
While baking, mix every 30 to 45 minutes.
Cream shortening and sugar, add eggs and beat well.
Sift all dry ingredients together and add to mixture alternately with bananas.
Stir in nuts.
Bake in well-greased loaf pan for 40 to 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Remove from pan and cool.
Mix thoroughly 1/2 cup soup, beef, bread crumbs, onion, egg and salt.
Shape firmly into an 8 x 4-inch loaf; place in shallow baking pan.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Blend remaining soup, water and drippings.
Heat; stir occasionally. Serve with meat loaf.
Makes 6 servings.
In a small saucepan, cook spinach over low heat without adding water.
In a skillet heat oil.
Add onion and chilies.
Fry for 3 or 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in crab meat and turmeric.
Cook 1 minute.
Stir in spinach and cook 5 minutes over low heat.
Add salt.
Sprinkle with lime juice and serve immediately with rice.
Yields 4 servings.
Cook carrots in salted water until tender; drain.
Place in a greased, 1-quart casserole.
Put apples on top.
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Dot with butter.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes.
Mix sugar with eggs, then add milk.
Stir in flour with the salt and baking powder.
Add nuts.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.

Cube six cups potatoes. Top off each cup with water, and pour one by one into soup kettle. Slice 1 carrot, 1 stalk celery, and diced 1 onion. Put in cup and top off with water and put in soup kettle. Cook until tender. Add 2 chicken bouillon cubes and simmer until dissolved. Add 1 cup condensed, 1/2 stick butter, and salt and pepper to taste, bring to simmer, serve.
Saute garlic, onion and bell pepper in oil until tender-crisp. Add rice and brown slightly.
Add tomatoes, then liquid.
Add 1 teaspoon chili powder and salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to boil, cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until done.
Dump all the ingredients into crock-pot.
Cover and set on high.
Cook for 6 to 8 hours.
Test for doneness and stir a couple of times.
Prepare pastry.
Sprinkle bacon, cheese and onion in pastry lined pie plate.
Beat eggs slightly; beat in remaining ingredients.
Pour egg mixture into pie plate.
Cook uncovered in 425° oven for 15 minutes.
Reduce oven temperature to 300°.
Cook uncovered until knife inserted halfway between center and edge comes out clean (about 30 minutes).
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Mix
the
sugar, raisins, water, oleo and cinnamon in a pan and
bring to a boil.
Add the soda dissolved in 1 tablespoon
hot water.
Slowly
boil
5 minutes (watch closely; it will
boil over).
Remove from heat.
Add the chopped nuts and cool.
Sift the
flour	and
baking
powder into mixture; mix well.
Spread into
greased and floured pan.
Bake 25 minutes at 350°.
Cut vegetables into pieces.
Put in chopped onions.
Break bacon into small pieces.
Cut cheese into cubes.
Then add all ingredients together; mix well.
Line a 9-inch pie plate with pastry.
Mix the sugar, flour, nutmeg and salt; add to beaten eggs.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in rhubarb; dot with 1 tablespoon butter.
Bake at 400° for 40 to 50 minutes, or until pie is "set" and lightly browned.

recipes.t: New Year'S Black-Eyed Peas And Sausage
d: Fry bacon.
Drain grease, leaving 2 tablespoons in pan.
Add celery, green pepper, onion and garlic to the bacon drippings and saute until onion is clear.
Transfer to Dutch oven and add peas, water, salt, pepper and tomato.
While bringing peas to a boil, fry sausage and drain well.
Add sausage to peas and simmer for 40 minutes or until desired thickness of broth.
In medium saucepan, combine 1 cup water, butter and salt. Bring to boil, then remove from heat.
Add flour and cayenne pepper all at once and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until dough is smooth.
Return to low heat and stir continuously for 5 minutes or until the mixture pulls away from the sides and forms a ball.
Flake salmon, discarding bones.
Combine salmon, bread crumbs, chopped onion, oleo, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Combine milk and egg.
Shape into a loaf and bake at 350° in a greased loaf pan for 35 to 45 minutes.
If desired, serve with cheese sauce.
Beat eggs until thick and fluffy.
Mix sugar and oil; beat into eggs.
Mix together flour, cinnamon, soda and salt.
Add to the egg mixture.
Stir in walnuts.
Peel and core apples; slice into greased pan 9 x 12-inch.
Pour batter over apples.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Ice with cream cheese icing.
Cook cranberries in 1 cup of water. Add 1 cup of sugar. Cook 5 minutes or until cranberries split.

Place liver in a strainer. Let cold water run over liver to wash it until it's clear. Place oil in skillet. Heat it slowly. Mix milk and egg; beat well. In another bowl, mix flour, salt and pepper. Place liver in milk mixture, then dip well in flour mixture. Place in hot oil. Turn stove to medium or lower. Cook until liver is brown on both sides, then place your sliced onions on top. Add 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer 1/2 hour. Turn over once while it steams.

Mix first 5 ingredients and let stand while making the crust. Pour mixture into pie crust. Sprinkle with nutmeg. Bake until a knife comes out clean. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes. Then at 325° for 45 minutes.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Arrange buttered bread crumbs on the bottom.
Top with grated cheese, then the meat.
Blend milk and seasonings; pour evenly over bread, cheese and meat.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
Sausage or ham may be substituted for bacon.
Mix all ingredients together and refrigerate until ready to use.
Cook butter in skillet until melted.
Sprinkle in flour.
This makes a paste.
Add broth; stir all together.
Add sour cream. This will be thick and creamy.
Cut
each
wing
at
joint to make 3 pieces, discard the wing tips.
Place
wings
in shallow container.	Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour	over
wings,
reserving 1/4 cup.
Cover and refrigerate
8 to 10 hours, turning occasionally.
Put wings in shallow baking dish and drizzle the reserved 1/4 cup over them. Cook at 350° for 1 hour.
Step 1:
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Add oil, egg yolks, cold water and vanilla or lemon.
Beat well.
Preheat oven to 450°. Brush the potatoes all over with oil. Prick them in several place on all sides with a fork. Place in a baking dish. Bake until tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Cut vegetables up in large bowl.
Marinate in Kraft free Italian dressing (small bottle).
Salt and pepper to taste.
Keep in refrigerator.
In a small saucepan, melt oleo.
Pour into a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan; spread evenly by tilting.
Sprinkle crushed vanilla wafers evenly over oleo.
Arrange nuts and fruits over crumb mix and press down gently.
Mix sweetened condensed milk and other milk and pour evenly over top.
Bake in 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until set.
Cool; cut into squares.
Makes 60 squares.
Mix well.
Drop by teaspoonfuls into hot fat (375°) and fry until golden brown.
This makes about 2 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large saucepan sprayed with Pam or other pure vegetable cooking spray, over low heat, melt chocolate chips and butter. Stir occasionally until well blended.
Remove from heat.
Add baking mix, sweetened condensed milk and egg. Stir well. Stir in walnuts. Spray Pam on bottom and sides of a 13 x 9-inch baking pan or dish.
Pour brownie mixture into dish.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes.
Cool slightly, then cut into squares.
In a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish, mix soup, milk, soy sauce, pepper, beans and 1/2 can onions.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until hot.
Stir.
Sprinkle remaining onions over bean mixture. Bake 5 minutes or until onions are golden.
Serves 6.
Cook potatoes, covered, in boiling salted water until tender. Drain and mash.
Stir in butter and spoon into a greased 9-inch pie plate.
Spread over bottom and up sides, building up sides with a spoon to form a crust.
Arrange vegetables in bottom of potato crust.
Sprinkle with cheese.
In a small bowl, combine eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Pour over cheese and sprinkle with bread crumbs or wheat germ.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Melt chocolate and oleo over low heat; set aside to cool.
Mix sugar and eggs until slightly fluffy.
Add chocolate, oleo, flour, baking powder, salt and vanilla.
Mix well.
Last, add walnuts. Bake in a 9 x 9 x 2-inch pan in a preheated 300° oven.
Bake 30 minutes.
Cool in pan; cut into squares.
This recipe may be doubled, if so desired.
Cream the cheese, sugar and milk until fluffy; spread on bottom of pie shell and set aside.
Combine sugars, pumpkin, oil and eggs.
Mix until well blended.
Add flour, soda, salt and spices.
Mix well.
Stir in walnuts.
Pour into well-oiled loaf pan.
Bake at 350°
for 65 to 70 minutes.
Cut a pocket in each chop.
Or use butterfly chops.
Season cavity with salt and pepper.
Combine sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and chopped nuts.
Shake biscuits in this mixture (cut biscuits in quarters before shaking in the mixture).
Arrange in angel cake pan.
Boil brown sugar, oleo and 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon.
Pour over biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Fry tortillas in oil until soft.
Place some cheese and onion in each shell and roll.
Place, seam side down, in lightly greased cake size pan.

recipes.t: Sweet And Sour Chicken And Rice
d: Cut up chicken into cubes.
Put in skillet and cook until chicken is no longer pink.
Add all ingredients and cook on low heat. Boil rice and mix rice with chicken mixture.
Remove membrane from seeds.
Wash and pat dry.
Place in a 9-inch glass pie plate.
Add remaining ingredients.
Microwave on High for 8 to 10 minutes until slightly toasted, stirring 4 to 5 times.
Beginning with lettuce, layer each ingredient on top of the other in oblong dish.
Spread the mayonnaise over the layer of hard-boiled eggs.
Sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese on top of mayonnaise.
Add bacon bits if desired.
Cover and set in refrigerator overnight before serving.
Break the cauliflower and broccoli into small flowerets into a bowl.
Cut up onion
real
fine
and
then
add chopped tomatoes. Mix together the
mayonnaise, sour cream, sugar and vinegar.
Pour over vegetables.
Mix well and chill.
Dissolve coffee and cinnamon in hot water.
Mix all ingredients together with a hand-held mixer until desired spreading consistency.

Break broccoli into florets and chop some of the stems into small pieces. Mix broccoli, raisins, pecans and onion in a salad bowl. Refrigerate. Mix mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar in a bowl. Let stand, covered, in the refrigerator overnight. Pour dressing over the salad just before serving.
Mix egg whites, sugar, crumbs, pecans and coconut.
Stir by hand.
Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Bake in a preheated 325° oven until glossy and set, about 25 to 30 minutes.
Do not overbake. Serve warm with whipped cream.
Split muffins.
Mix all ingredients and spread on 12 muffin halves, then cut each muffin half into eight.
Broil or freeze (then heat).
Flour chops and brown in a small amount of hot oil in skillet. Mix rest of ingredients and pour over chops. Cover and simmer for 1 hour or until fork tender.
In a bowl, combine the potatoes, ham, cheese, mayonnaise, egg, mustard and pepper; mix well.
Add enough of the flour to make a stiff mixture.
Chill.
Shape into 1 inch balls; roll in cornflakes.
Place on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 25-30 minutes or until heated through. Serve hot.
In small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of the apple juice and the cornstarch; mix well.
Set aside.
In large skillet or Dutch oven, combine remaining apple juice, syrup, cinnamon, margarine and salt; mix well.
Bring to a boil.
Add potatoes; stir to coat well. Return to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes or just until potatoes are tender.
Stir cornstarch mixture into potato mixture; cook and stir over medium-high heat until bubbly and thickened.* Pour into ungreased 8-inch square (1 1/2-quart) baking dish; cover tightly with foil.
Refrigerate up to 24 hours.
Pour all ingredients into a pint jar with a tight lid.
Shake well, until mixed.
Set in refrigerator for a few days (the longer, the better).
This thickens with age.
Use on fruit, cole slaw or just over lettuce.

recipes.t: Sweet Potato Pie(Makes 8 Servings. Prep Time: 15 Minutes.)
d: Bake potatoes in microwave, allowing about 5 minutes per potato to cook.
When soft, let cool and peel into measuring cup.
Use about 3 cups of potatoes.
Put stick of butter on top and put back into microwave and melt butter into potatoes.
Add dash of salt, cinnamon and sugar and blend with mixer.
Add eggs and mix well. Mix in vanilla.
Add condensed milk and blend well.
Stir in coconut (optional) and blend.
Pour into 3 frozen pie shells and bake in 350° oven for about 30 to 35 minutes or until center is set.
Cream butter, cream cheese and sugar until light and fluffy. Add sugar and flavorings.
Beat well.
Add eggs, one at a time; beat well after each addition.
Stir in flour.
Spoon mixture into greased 10-inch tube pan.
Bake at 325° for about 1 1/2 hours.
Place potatoes, onions, eggs and parsley in a greased casserole or baking pan.
Pour dressing over potato mixture and mix to coat all.
Heat oven to 350° and cook for 30 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Preheat covered barbecue grill to 300°.
Move coals to side and place pan large enough to catch all drippings under the grate. Wash and pat dry bird.
Blend herbs and butter to a paste. (Experiment with whatever herbs you like or, better yet, fresh herbs!)
Separate the skin from the breast from the back.
Insert paste and rub between the skin and meat.
Grill for 10 minutes per pound.
Fresh cooks faster!
Turkey is so moist and tender!
Cook bacon and onion about 10 minutes.
Combine with rest of ingredients and pour into greased 2 quart casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.

recipes.t: Pineapple Or Any Other Fruit Pie
d: Stir all above ingredients together.
Pour into 2 baked pie shells.
Let set overnight in refrigerator.
Mix dry ingredients, add milk and bring to boil.
Pour beaten egg yolks in and cook until it thickens.
Add extract, coconut and vanilla.
Pour into 9-inch baked pie shell.
Beat egg whites for meringue.
Sprinkle coconut on top.
Brown in oven.
Mix all ingredients in small bowl.
Add to 1 1/2 cups of water and 1 pound cooked hamburger.
Simmer for 10 minutes just as you would packaged seasoning.
Combine juices and water.
Stir until thawed, add 2 trays ice cubes.
Just before serving, carefully pour the ginger ale and club soda into bowl.
Makes 25 servings.
Mix together tomato paste, sugar, salt, garlic and Worcestershire sauce and spread thinly on muffins. Sprinkle cheese over tomato mixture. Top with pepperoni.
Rub chicken breasts with poultry seasoning.
Saute in butter and cook, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
Remove to a buttered casserole dish.
Cover with the ham and a slice of cheese on each piece of chicken, parsley and thyme to taste.
Pour heavy cream over all and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes at 350°.
Then broil for 5 minutes until light brown.
Serve with Wild Rice Sausage Bake.
Place batter in pan; then add nuts.
Then add syrup.
Bake in a 350° oven for 35 to 40 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and chill well (may be chilled overnight).
Make into balls the size of walnuts.
Put on cookie sheet.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 350°.
Serve hot or cold.
Can be frozen.
Heat oven to 350°.
Coat 8 inch square baking pan with vegetable cooking spray, set aside.
In mixer bowl beat milk and prune puree to blend thoroughly; add flour, sugar, 2 tablespoons of cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Beat just to blend thoroughly. Spread evenly in pan.
In small bowl,
mix brown sugar and the remaining 1/4 c. cocoa powder.
Sprinkle evenly over top.
Bake in center of oven about 45 minutes until cake is springy to the touch.
Cool 15 minutes on rack.
Brown, drain and crumble hamburger with onion and garlic added.
Cook noodles.
In skillet, mix meat, corn, soup, tomato sauce and chili powder and simmer 5 to 10 minutes.
Layer the noodles, cheese, meat sauce and Parmesan cheese twice.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix cheese, bacon bits, mayonnaise, olives and onions.
Spread 1 tablespoon over each bread slice.
Broil until cheese melts, 1 to 2 minutes.
Layer in casserole.
Pour beer on top.
Bake at 325 degrees for 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until ready to serve.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg yolks, one at a time, mixing well.
Stir in jam, add flour which has been sifted with spices, alternately with sour cream and ending with flour.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites.
Bake in four 9-inch layers in 350° oven until center springs back when pressed with finger.
(May also be baked in a tube pan.)
Frost with Never Fail Frosting.
Put chicken in a shallow pan.
Sprinkle salt and pepper on top.
Inset lemon in cavity.
Bake, breast up, at 350° for 1 hour, breast down at 350° for 1/2 hour and breast up at 400° for 1/2 hour.
Mix ingredients.
Spray casserole dish with Pam.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Boil 4 to 6 large chicken pieces until chicken falls off bones. Use the 2 quarts water to boil chicken in.
Cut up onion and place in with chicken.
Season with salt, pepper and 1 sprig of thyme. Add okra, cut in cubes.
Add tomatoes.
At this point you can add shrimp, crab or sausage or leave it with just the chicken.
Boil slowly for 3 hours.
To be eaten with rice.
Mix well honey, lemon juice mustard and salt.
Barbecue chicken over medium hot coals and brush generously with glaze mixture.
(Sometimes I marinate in a Ziploc bag in mixture for an hour before barbecue.)
Cook chicken until fork tender.
Brush often with honey glaze.
Heat milk and butter; add cracker crumbs.
Add other ingredients, except butter.
Take out stem of mushrooms; fill with stuffing.
Dip mushrooms in butter.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Knead and make into small balls. Place pecan on each ball to flatten.
Bake at 350° for about 14 to 16 minutes.
Fry sausages in 1/2 cup oil for 5 minutes.
Remove from pan and slice when cool.
In same oil that sausages were cooked in, add sliced onions and peppers.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Add tomatoes and sausages and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste (garlic salt and parsley may also be added to taste).
Mix all ingredients together, knead lightly. Ready to use or eat!
In large bowl, combine yeast, water and teaspoon of sugar. Add mixture of eggs, oil and buttermilk.
Combine all dry ingredients in a second bowl and add them to the liquid.
Fry pancake batter as desired.
Mix cake mix, 1 egg and butter together.
Press into greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Cream sugar, cheese and 3 eggs together.
Pour on top. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix flour, butter and sugar.
Pat into bottom of a 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Mix ingredients together and beat until smooth and creamy. Bake at 350° until done.
Place hash browns in a greased 9-inch microwave-safe dish. Microwave, uncovered, on high for 4 minutes or until thawed.
Press onto botom and halfway up the sides of rhe dish.
Microwave, uncovered, on high 3 minutes, sprinkle with cheese, ham and broccoli.
In a bowl, beat the eggs, milk and seasonings.
Pour over the ham mixture.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave at 70% power for 10-12 minutes or until set.
Let stand for 5 minutes before cutting.
Yield:
4-6 servings.

Brown ground chuck in skillet; drain well. Add onions, garlic salt, pepper and water. Cook until dry. Layer meat, olives, cheese and sliced tomatoes in bottom crust. Repeat, then cover with top crust. Make 3 or 4 holes near center of top crust with a fork to help vent the pie. Cook at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Mix sugar, flour, vanilla and egg together.
Put fruit in bottom of pan.
Pour egg mixture over it.
Add butter and cut in pieces.
Cover with dough.
Brown chicken in a little oil in a large Dutch oven.
Drain oil and add all other ingredients and stir well.
Cover and cook slowly until chicken is done.
Serve with unsalted rice.
Cream butter and shortening.
Add brown sugar and white sugar. Add one egg at a time.
Beat until well creamed.
Add flour, salt, baking powder and vanilla, then add nuts.
Blend well. Place mixture in greased and floured 10-inch tube pan and bake at 325° for one hour.
Test for doneness.
Unwrap approximately 60 caramels.
Microwave with 3 tablespoons of water in a glass mixing bowl, stirring constantly, so caramels don't stick or burn.
Add Rice Krispies, 1 cup at a time, while stirring.
Pat mixture into a glass casserole, after spraying with Pam.
Mix all ingredients, except Club crackers, and boil 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Line a 9 x 13-inch pan with Club crackers; pour 1/2 mixture over crackers.
Add layer of Club crackers; pour mixture over crackers.
Add another layer of Club crackers.
Then top with Topping.
Remove strings from pea pods and cut diagonally in half.
Mix oil, sugar, vinegar and soy sauce in large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients; toss to coat.
Serve immediately.
Mix sugar, eggs and raisin mixture.
Sift flour and other ingredients.
Mix into creamed mixture.
Pour into greased and floured cookie sheet.
Bake 25 minutes at 375°.
Pour strawberry soda into ice cube trays; freeze.
Boil sugar and water for 5 minutes; add fruit juices and chill.
Drain peas.
Dice tomatoes, onions and cheese.
Tear lettuce into small bits.
Mix with salad dressing and serve.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water and add apricots, marshmallows and crushed pineapple.
Let set.
Cook together last 6 ingredients; let sauce cool and then fold in 1 cup whipped cream. Spread over Jell-O.
You can put grated cheese or coconut on top.
Boil potatoes with skins on.
Do not overcook.
Cool until you can handle them.
Peel and salt while still warm.
Mix other ingredients thoroughly.
Add to diced potatoes.

Add chocolate which has been melted.

Stir in nuts.

Pour 1 cup sauce in a 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Layer chicken and top with remaining sauce. Sprinkle with cheeses.
Bake for 45 minutes, or until thoroughly cooked.
Serves 8.

Combine all ingredients.
Mix very well and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Add flour and eggs and mix everything.

Drop from teaspoon onto greased baking sheet and bake in 375° oven for 12 to 15 minutes.

Quickly stir in chocolate and nuts.
Turn into buttered 8 x 8-inch pan, spreading 1 inch thick.

Chop cucumbers, peppers and onions.

Boil for 20 minutes.
Seal in pint jars which have been sterilized.

Pour into 9-inch square or 11 x 17-inch pan, greased bottom only.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until top springs back when touched in center.
Serve warm or cool, plain or with whipped cream or frosting.

Spray a 2-quart casserole with Pam or oil with margarine.
Alternate layers of sweet potato mixture and marshmallows, ending with marshmallows. Bake 30 minutes at 350°.

Combine cream cheese, instant jello and sugar. Add whip cream to soften and sugar to taste.
Prepare pudding according to instructions. Layer cream cheese mix on bottom and pudding on top. Top with chocolate or strawberries as desired.
Place in freezer for 45 minutes to allow to set.

Add next 3 ingredients and cook 6 minutes more.
Add jello and stirring, continue to cook until it is dissolved.

Slice the bananas.
Wash and clean the berries.
Layer the banana slices and berries in a dish.
If desired, add yogurt or milk and sprinkle with brown sugar.

Layer in casserole dish (approximately 9 x 13-inch).

Preheat oven to 400°.
Spray 8-inch round cake pan with nonstick spray.
Unroll dough; form 14 x 10-inch rectangle.

recipes.t: Moo Goo Gai Pan(Chinese Chicken And Mushrooms)
d: Skin and bone chicken breasts.
Slice across breasts into 1/8-inch slices.
In a medium bowl mix chicken, soy sauce, sherry, cornstarch, ginger, sugar and garlic powder.
Set aside.
Thinly slice mushrooms.
Cut each green onion crosswise into 3-inch pieces.
In a 12-inch skillet or wok over medium-high heat in 1/4 cup hot salad oil, cook mushrooms and green onions, stirring quickly and frequently until mushrooms are tender (about 2 minutes).

With a slotted spoon, remove mushroom mixture to bowl. In same skillet or wok, over high heat, in 3 tablespoons hot salad oil, cook chicken mixture, stirring frequently and quickly, until chicken is tender (about 2 or 3 minutes).
Return mushroom mixture to skillet and heat through.
Serve over rice.
Layer tortillas, chicken mixture and cheese 3 times.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes.

Rub mixture on both sides of steak.

Great cubed for fondue or other dipping.
Cook vegetables, celery and onions.

Place half of vegetables in dish, half of cheese and half of mayonnaise.
Start over with rest of vegetables, cheese and mayonnaise.

Stir in the water and flour mixture; cook until thickened and bubbly.

Simmer 5 minutes.
Serve over hot, cooked rice.

Combine remaining ingredients except oil and stir into dry ingredients.
Drop by tablespoons into hot oil (375°).
Fry until golden brown turning once.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

Pour into greased pan.

Set aside.
Blend cottage cheese in blender or food processor until very smooth; slowly add milk while continuing to blend.
Add chicken soup to cheese/milk mixture.
Blend; add mixture to cooked, undrained vegetables. Microwave until heated thoroughly (about 3 minutes) without boiling.
Add salt and pepper.

Combine cherry filling and extract.
Alternate layers of pudding, crumbled cookies and filling in 6 parfait or dessert dishes.
Garnish with topping.

Season with salt and pepper.

Mix until thoroughly blended.
Add ground beef.
Mix gently but thoroughly. Line a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan with foil.
Press in the beef mixture.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Put the oatmeal in a medium bowl.
Pour boiling water on the oatmeal and let stand while preparing the rest of the ingredients.
Cream butter and sugars (brown and granulated) until fluffy.
Sift the dry ingredients (flour and cinnamon), then add them to the butter and sugar mixture.
Pour in the vanilla and the oatmeal.
Stir until well blended.
Pour into 2 (9-inch) layer pans or one 12 x 9 x 2-inch utility pan.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes or until done.

Add milk; mix until partially blended.
Place margarine over top.

Add vanilla; beat until smooth.
Add pecans; mix well.
Pour into 8 x 8-inch buttered dish.
Chill in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Cut into squares.
Brown together onion, green pepper, hamburger and rice.
Add salt, pepper, tomato sauce, water and mustard.
Bring mixture to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes.
Boil the water out of the green beans.
Place in a casserole dish and pour the mushroom soup over beans (add 1/4 cup water to can of soup).
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Place onion rings on top and brown.

Add the mandarin oranges and crushed pineapple; add nuts.

Cover and freeze.
Remove from freezer 15 minutes before serving.
Cut into squares.

Pour 1 can of tomato sauce and 1/2 can of water over the layers.

Cover with a layer of seasoned meat.
Pour remaining can of tomato sauce and 1/4 can of water over casserole.
Top with bacon strips. Cover; bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.

Dice onions and celery in small pieces.
Melt oleo (margarine) in a large pot.
Saute onions and celery.
Combine French onion soup, beef consomme soup and sliced mushrooms with sauteed onions and celery.

Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours, uncovered. Stir every 30 minutes.

Mix remaining ingredients and pour over olives.
Cover and refrigerate 10 to 12 hours; shake olives occasionally to coat evenly.

Mix flour, salt and pepper together. Coat chicken pieces with flour mixture.

Shred cabbage in a large bowl.
Place chopped onion and green pepper on top of cabbage.
Sprinkle sugar evenly on top.
Bring oil, vinegar, mustard, celery seed and salt to a boil.
Pour over cabbage while hot.
Don't stir.
Refrigerate, covered, at least 4 hours (better if refrigerated overnight).
Stir mixture and drain before serving.
Cook butter, water and chopped broccoli for 3 minutes, remove pan from heat, then add Velveeta and Minute rice.
Cover pan and let set for 4 minutes.
Add cream of celery soup.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Roast 40 minutes per pound.
With a sharp knife, cut 10 or more one-inch deep holes in top surface of ham; press garlic slivers and pinch of black pepper in each hole. Place roast on rack in open pan.
Rub surface with sherry and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Roast 40 minutes per pound or until meat thermometer is 185°.
Pour off fat and combine with 2/3 cup sherry; thicken with cornstarch for sauce.
Slightly mix ingredients together.
Prepare whipped topping.
Mix with 1 cup of milk as directed on package in small mixer bowl.
Measure 2 cups of the prepared whipped topping and set aside.
Add 1 cup milk and chocolate pudding mix to remaining topping in bowl.
Blend and then beat at high speed for 2 minutes.
Spoon into pie shell.
Put can of tomato sauce and enchilada mix in pan and mix. Heat over low fire.
Brown beef and onion over low fire in skillet.
After sauce heats 10 minutes, add to the beef, just enough to be slightly soupy (to your preference).

Distribute liquid into jars.
Seal.

recipes.t: Warm Brie Salad With Hazelnut Vinaigrette(4 Persons)

Mix together soup, mayonnaise and eggs.
Stir into broccoli.
Add cheese; mix well.
Melt butter and mix with crackers.
Add cheese, then crackers on top as crumbs. Bake at 350° for 30 to 50 minutes.
Brown beef and onions; drain.
Add taco seasoning, beans and tomato sauce and simmer five minutes.
Press dough in a 9 x 13-inch pan and up the sides one inch.
Brush on oil and sprinkle corn meal over dough.
Pour meat sauce over dough and bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes and cook until melted.
Cut into cubes.
Top with shredded lettuce, chopped tomatoes, taco sauce and sour cream.

Combine the next 9 ingredients and pour on top. Sprinkle with Old Bay seasoning.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Let sit 10 minutes.
Serve.
Whip together the milk, cream cheese and Cool Whip. Fold in pie filling, pineapple and nuts. Refrigerate.

Place fruit in a foil pan or make your own pan with heavy duty foil.
In a bowl, stir together honey, butter and 1/2 tsp. cinnamon.
Spoon over fruit and toss to coat fruit.

Add flour and make a roux. Stir and add chicken broth and 1 can cream of chicken soup (add water, broth or milk if this is too thick).
Add remaining ingredients and stir.

Put uncooked biscuits on top.
Bake at 350° until brown.

Add chicken and celery.
Let chill for 1 hour.

Add other ingredients.

Remove from heat. Add sugar, eggs, butter and vanilla. Mix well until eggs are cooked in hot rice. Add milk and raisins. Return to low heat, stirring continuously for about 5 minutes.
Pour into serving dish.
Sprinkle with nutmeg and brown sugar.
Mix in bowl by hand.
Bake 8 to 12 minutes at 350°.
In a pot (not iron), saut okra, onions, celery and garlic until done or all the stringiness is gone from the okra.

cookie

are
dry.

ingredients
