Delicious!
Place broccoli in lightly greased 1 1/2-quart casserole dish. Put chicken on top of broccoli.
Combine the remaining ingredients, except cracker crumbs, stirring well.
Spoon mixture over chicken; top with crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes, or until bubbly.
In a large saucepan, combine refried beans, picante sauce and taco seasoning mix.
Stir over medium heat until thoroughly heated.
Garnish with sour cream and serve with tortilla chips. Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Sift first four ingredients into bowl.
Cut in shortening until size of small peas.
Stir in egg; add milk, tablespoon at a time, until roughly forms into soft dough.
Form into 1-inch balls. Wet balls in beaten egg, then roll in sesame seed.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Flatten balls a little.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Heat some oil in
a cast-iron skillet.
Cut tomatoes in thick slices.
Dip in bread
crumbs,
then
in
beaten egg and milk, then back in crumbs
again.
Fry until tender and golden brown, topping with cheese during last few minutes of cooking.
Brown ground chuck in skillet and drain off fat; cool.
Add remaining ingredients.
Mix all ingredients.
Spread on split semi-hard rolls or buns.
Bake at 350° for about 10 minutes, until bubbly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.t: Josephine'S Recipe For Out Of This World Pie
d: Measure sugar and cornstarch into saucepan; mix well.
Add pineapple with its juice; mix well so no lumps form.
Stir in pie filling and food color.
Use a wooden spoon; stir gently to avoid mashing the cherries.
Cook over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil and is well thickened, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in dry gelatin.
Let cool.
Put all ingredients into a buttered baking dish; stir well and bake 1 hour in a moderate oven.
Serve with cream.
It is not necessary to cream the sugar and butter for the cake.
Heat oven to 350°.
Allow vinegar and milk to clabber while mixing remaining ingredients (except soda) in order.
When ingredients are well blended, dissolve soda in clabbered milk. Stir into flour mixture.
Spread in greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan. Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until top springs back when touched lightly.
Cool in pan on wire rack before cutting.
Stir sherbet and orange sections into jello and chill thoroughly.
Place asparagus and water in a 8 x 8 x 2-inch microwave dish. Cover with plastic wrap.
Turn back one corner to vent.
Cook on High for 7 to 9 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Let stand, covered, while cooking sauce.
Grease pan.
Put in oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Bake at 350°.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a 10-inch pie pan.
Layer bacon and cheese in pan.
Beat together the milk, mayonnaise, eggs, Bisquick, salt and pepper until smooth (15 seconds in blender on high or 1 minute with hand beater).
Pour into pan.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes.
Garnish with lettuce and tomatoes.
Mix together diced chicken, soup, sour cream, chilies and flavor in saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until boiling.
Fry tortillas in oil
until flexible.
Place 2 heaping tablespoonfuls chicken mixture on each tortilla.
Place in casserole.
Top with cheese and onion.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° about 30 minutes.
Melt margarine. Add flour and milk. Thicken to make sauce. Add cheese to create cheese sauce.
Layer in a 9 x 13-inch pan in the order given.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.

Prepare corn muffin mix according to directions except with milk instead of water. Pour batter into mini-muffin pan with 24 cups. Fill to 3/4 full. Cut each wiener into 4 bite size pieces. Place one piece in each filled muffin cup. Bake at 375° for about 15 minutes.
Brown 1 pound ground beef in frypan.
Season with garlic, salt and pepper to taste.
Add tomato soup and simmer 5 minutes.
In second pan, cook egg noodles as directed on package.
Drain.
Add 1 cup chopped onion and cottage cheese.
Layer alternately in casserole dish beginning with noodle mixture and ending with meat mixture (about 2 layers of each).
Top with grated cheese and bake in a 350° oven until onion is tender and cheese is melted. Freezes well.
Serves 8.
Cut in together flour, oleo and nuts.
Press into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Let crust cool.
Mix cream cheese, sugar and Cool Whip together and spread onto cooled crust.
Mix milk and both packages of pudding together and spread onto cheese mixture.
Cool 6 to 8 hours.
Top with Cool Whip (optional).
Serves 10.
Brown sausage; drain and crumble.
Saute onion and garlic with sausage.
Add black-eyed peas, tomatoes, water, chili powder and salt.
Simmer for 25 or 30 minutes.
Blend cottage cheese and yogurt in blender to remove all curds. Add skim milk to thin if necessary.
Blend in coconut extract. Combine mixture with drained fruits.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Saute onions in butter until tender.
Add mushrooms, reserving a few slices.
Saute for a few more minutes.
Cream butter, sugar and flour together until it forms little beads.
Add cream and yolks.
Mix very well.
Roll out on floured board as thin as desired.
Cut with cookie cutter.
Dip in unbeaten egg whites; sprinkle with mixture of cinnamon and sugar. Place a few chopped nuts on top (optional).
Bake at 350° about 10 minutes or until light brown.
Mix together sugar, vanilla, almond flavoring, oil and milk. Add eggs and poppy seeds.
Blend in flour, salt and baking powder. For 1 loaf, bake 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350°.
For 6 mini-loaves, bake 35 minutes at 350°.
For 12 muffins, bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool and glaze with confectioners sugar, milk and vanilla or almond extract.
Make jello as directed.
Add can of cranberries.
Allow to chill and set slightly.
Add balance of ingredients and mix well. Pour into mold and let set.
Put 1 tablespoon of butter and salt into water and bring to boil.
Add macaroni.
Use just amount of water that when macaroni is done, it won't have to be drained.
Watch closely.
Add 1/4 of the cheese to macaroni quickly.
Mix well until cheese melts. Melt butter; add to milk and stir into macaroni so it won't be dry.
(Add more milk, if needed.)
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and poke rest of cheese cubes into macaroni.
Sprinkle paprika on top.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour or until it bubbles.
Mix together the first 5 ingredients well; do not brown meat. Spread meat mixture into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Spread with tomato sauce.
Place Mozzarella cheese on top.
Top with oregano, basil, seasoned salt and Parmesan cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 60 minutes.
Nice served with tossed salad and Italian bread.
Heat jelly and mustard together to boiling point. Put in fondue dish and keep hot. Provide skewers for people to dip the bread cubes into the fondue.
Cream the butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time. Alternate dry ingredients with liquid.
Bake in greased pans at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix eggs, flour, sugars and milks in blender; pour into pie shell.
Sprinkle top of pie with cinnamon and dot with butter. Bake at 375° for 30 minutes, then at 350° until center is set, about 10 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Melt margarine in 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan in oven. Mix Bisquick, paprika, salt and pepper; coat chicken. Bake 35 minutes.
Turn chicken.
Bake 15 minutes or until done.
Rinse beans twice.
Place in at least 4-quart heavy pot.
Add water, ham and sausage.
Place on medium heat.
While beans are soaking and warming, chop onions.
Add to pot.
When the mixture boils, reduce and cover.
Stir every 20 to 30 minutes for 3 hours. Then, with a wooden spoon mash about 1/4 of the beans against the side of the pot.
Forty minutes after mashing beans, add cayenne pepper (not too much).
Cook 30 minutes more while cooking rice. Serve over rice.
Vegetables cook away to nothing.
The mashed beans thicken sauce.
Even better the next day.
Brown chicken.
Add water and cover.
Simmer.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Combine brown sugar and cornstarch. Add pineapple juice, vinegar, soy sauce and salt.
Pour over chicken.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Add pineapple, green peppers and onion.
Cook 5 minutes.
Serve over rice.
In pan, fry hamburger; set aside.
Peel potatoes, cut into small pieces and boil with macaroni.
(When it is finished boiling do not drain water.)
Add onion, chili, stewed tomatoes, salt to taste and chili powder to taste, then add fried hamburger.
The longer you let it simmer the better, at least 30 minutes.
Add water as needed.
Goes really good with Nana's cornbread.
Simmer all ingredients together for 1/2 hour.
Layer in casserole dish with shredded Mozzarella cheese and cooked bacon (any amount).
Bake at 350° until cheese melts, approximately 15 minutes.
Put all ingredients in large pan and cover with water.
Cook, covered, over low heat.
Add water as needed.
After approximately 6 hours, take bones out of meat and break meat up.
Then cook with lid off into thick mixture for 1 to 2 hours.
Serve over corn chips and add the following as desired:
grated cheese, chopped onion, shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, diced avocados and hot salsa.
Serves 12 to 14.
Combine cream cheese and marshmallow cream.
Stir about 30 strokes, or until mixed well.
Chill about 1 hour before serving. Dip fresh fruit into fruit dip.
Combine first 8 ingredients in 1 1/2-quart casserole dish. Blend 1/4 cup cracker crumbs with 2 tablespoons butter and sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Serves 6.
Mix marinade, marmalade, garlic, dry mustard and ground ginger in a bowl. Put pork tenderloins in gallon-sized Ziploc and pour marinade in bag and close. Marinate several hours; overnight is best.
Cream butter. Add brown sugar and cream well. Blend in flour (mixture may be crumbly).
Press into bottom of ungreased 13 x 9-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine all
ingredients in food processor. Blend until well mixed. This is a very pungent dressing, but good on spinach salad. (Note: Don't expect anyone to kiss you after eating this dressing!)
Remove mushroom stems.
Place mushrooms, round side down, in a shallow baking dish.
Cut cherry tomatoes in half.
Combine all ingredients.
Spoon into a lightly greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix baking soda and water together.
Beat in eggs.
Dump in cake mix and pumpkin pie mix.
Beat all together.
Pour in greased 9 x 13-inch greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Put the zucchini in a colander or on towels to drain off the moisture.
Combine the remaining ingredients.
Add the zucchini and mix well.
Pour into lightly oiled 2-quart casserole dish. Bake in 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes.

Brown beef and drain. Mix all ingredients together except for potatoes. Put in a casserole dish. Spoon potatoes around top of casserole. Sprinkle a little chili powder on top of potatoes. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until potatoes are slightly brown. Serves 4 to 6.
Whip egg whites until foamy.
Add salt and cream of tartar and continue to whip until they hold a point and are not dry.
Add 1/2 cup sugar slowly, then the extract.
Add flour, remaining sugar and nuts.
Bake in an ungreased pan for 30 to 40 minutes in a 350° oven.
Beat eggs; add to corn.
Add salt, pepper, flour, cream and butter.
Grease 2-quart casserole.
Pour in mixture.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Melt butter in a small pan.
Set aside.
In a separate pan, warm milk.
Stir cocoa and boiling water together to make a paste, then mix in melted butter.
Combine sugar, cornstarch and salt and add to warm milk.
Add the cocoa-butter mixture and egg.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until thickened, 15 to 20 minutes. Don't let mixture boil.
Remove from heat and mix in remaining butter and vanilla.
Cook frozen broccoli for 10 minutes; drain it.
Melt butter and mix to Ritz crackers that should be crushed; set aside.

In a large bowl, mix together onion, cream of celery soup, beaten eggs, Parmesan cheese, mayonnaise, salt and pepper, then add broccoli. Pour mixture into a greased casserole and top with moistened crumbs.
Bake in a 350° oven for 40 to 45 minutes.
Bake uncovered.
When top is light brown, it's done.
Melt 1/2 cup of the butter and mix with egg, cocoa, vanilla, crumbs, coconut and sugar.
Press into a 9 x 9-inch pan.
Add all ingredients together.
Beat well.
Bake in Bundt pan at 350°.
Boil potatoes in jackets until fork-tender.
Cool.
Peel and grate.
Melt oleo over low heat.
Stir in cheese.
Add mixture to potatoes along with sour cream, onion, salt and pepper.
Turn into a greased, shallow 3-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with paprika. Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes or until heated through.
Cut into squares to serve.
Makes 10 servings.
Combine marshmallow cream, sugar, milk, butter and salt in
a 2-quart saucepan.
Bring to a full, rolling boil, stirring constantly.
Continue
to boil over moderate heat, stirring constantly,
for
minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in chocolate and
vanilla.
Beat
until
smooth.
Spread
into a greased
pan. Sprinkle
with a few peanut butter chips.	Melt the rest of the peanut butter chips and spread over the fudge. Chill in refrigerator until firm.
Put candy in a bowl and microwave for 2 minutes.
Take out and stir.
If not melted completely, put back in microwave for 15 second intervals until all melted.
Take out and stir in peanut butter and nuts (any amount you want).
You can add marshmallows if you want.
Stir quickly until all melted.
Pour out on waxed paper or in pan.
Let stand until firm.
Cut into squares.
Easy and good!
In saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch; mix well.
Add corn syrup, water and orange rind.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in almond extract, raisins, nuts and cranberries.
Cover and cook until cranberry skins burst, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Dot with butter.
Allow to cool; do not stir.
In a small saucepan, cook garlic cloves and rosemary in hot oil over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes or until garlic is soft (avoid burning).
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Let oil mixture cool.
Stir lemon juice, pepper and salt into oil.
Wash the chicken thoroughly; pat dry with paper towels. Season body cavity with salt.
Twist wing tips under the back. Place chicken, breast side up, on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.
Cut five slits randomly in the chicken skin.
Insert the five cloves of garlic under the skin.
Brush chicken with some of the oil mixture.
Insert meat thermometer into the center of one of the inside thigh muscles.
Roast at 375° for 1 1/4 to 1 3/4 hours or until thermometer registers 180°.

Mix pie filling and pineapple together in an ungreased 9 x 13-inch cake pan. Sprinkle dry cake mix over this. Add melted butter over cake mix. Add coconut and nuts. Bake at 350° for 1 hour. (I put a brown bag over the cake for a little while, or it will get too brown before it gets done.)
Into bowl, put crushed pineapple; do not drain.
Add pudding. Mix well and add Cool Whip.
Mix thoroughly.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Sprinkle top with graham cracker crumbs.
Let chill.
Mix all ingredients. Pour into pie crust.
Add taco seasoning mix, water and olives to browned and drained ground beef.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Layer the following into pie crust:
refried beans, Doritos, ground beef mixture and sour cream, Cheddar cheese and more crushed Doritos.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Crunch up Oreo cookies and put in bottom of large oblong cake pan.
Melt butter and pour over cookies.
Mix up and pat to make the crust.
Sort and rinse beans.
Cook until tender.
Cook ground beef in skillet.
Drain off fat.
Add cooked beef and remaining ingredients to beans; stir.
Cook until flavors are mixed.
Can be frozen.
Very good.
Break bread into small pieces; place in well-greased baking dish (9 x 13-inches).
Cut cheese into cubes and sprinkle over bread.
Sprinkle ham or bacon over cheese, then pour margarine over ham or bacon.
Beat eggs with mustard, salt and milk, then pour over casserole.
Chill in refrigerator overnight.
Bake, uncovered, in preheated oven for 1 hour or until firm.

Using a lard can, put apples that have been cored, quartered and peeled in can. Pour sugar on top, covering apples. Place lid on can and let it sit over night. Cook apples next morning for 3 hours, or until apples are tender. Remove from stove. Using a potato masher, mash apples while adding cinnamon and ground cloves. Pack into hot jars and seal.
Brown meat and onion and drain.
Add everything else but cornmeal.
Cook until done.
Mix cornmeal and a little water. Stir in and cook 20 minutes longer.
Mix all ingredients in blender on medium speed until smooth. Sprinkle parsley and chives in just before finishing to give a pretty color.
Combine softened cream cheese and Cheddar cheese, mixing until well blended.
Add pimiento, green pepper, onion, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and seasonings.
Mix well.
Chill.
Shape in one ball or smaller balls.
Roll into nuts.
Bring raisins, water and lemon juice to a boil and boil for 5 minutes.
Mix the sugar and flour and stir into boiling raisin mixture. Cook until clear and thick.
Stir in the margarine and blend until melted.
Pour into unbaked pie shell and cover with top shell. Bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
*Recipe found in Vegetables Section of this book.
Peel onion and remove enough center layers to make a pocket. Mix sausage, most of cheese, garlic, pepper, salt, egg and corn. Divide evenly and fill pockets in onion.
Sprinkle remaining cheese and all the margarine over the onions.
Place onions in 9 x 13-inch pan and pour in water.
Bake 30 minutes at 375°.
Open cans of asparagus and drain.
Put asparagus into an 8 x 8-inch casserole dish.
Slice eggs on top of asparagus.
Make cream sauce by melting butter, then add flour and milk mixture to medium heat.
Stir until thick.
Add cheese.
Once cheese is melted in sauce, pour sauce over eggs and asparagus.
Top with crushed crackers.
Bake at 400° in oven until hot.
Serves 4 to 6 people.

Mix first 5 ingredients together. Put half the batter in a greased skillet. Put half of the green chillies and half of the grated cheese on top. Pour rest of the batter over that. Then put the rest of the green chilies and cheese on top. Bake at 400° for 40-45 minutes.
Cook the first six vegetables separate in a little water. When almost soft, drain.
Have it all ready before adding to boiling tomato juice.
Add 1/2 cup sugar, 1 teaspoon chili powder and salt to taste.
Cold pack for 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients together.
Drop by teaspoon on cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Do not overbake.
This is a soft and moist cookie.
Heat soup.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Dissolve gelatin in water and stir into soup mixture.
Let cool.
Blend in mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Chill until slightly set.
Add celery, onion, olives and shrimp.
Mix well.
Lightly coat inside of fish mold; put an olive slice for the eye.
Size should be 6 or 8 cups.
You could also use a ring mold.
Chill until firm. Unmold on bed of greens.
If using ring mold, fill center with parsley sprigs or parsley and whole shrimp.
Cook hamburg in oil; add onion and cook until tender.
Add remaining ingredients and cook on simmer 30 minutes or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Tear bread into small pieces.
Mix together with other ingredients in a food processor.
Drop mixture onto cookie sheet from spoon.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Prepare cake mix as directed on box.
Pour in long pan like sheet cake and bake.
Mix together caramel topping and milk. Punch holes in cake and spread over baked cake.
Frost cake by mixing cream cheese, Cool Whip and sugar in mixer.
Spread over cake.
Sprinkle with sprinkles.
Set oven at 350°.
Combine first 6 ingredients; let stand 5 minutes.
Add onion and meat; mix well.
Line a loaf pan (8 x 5 x 3-inch) with bacon across the width of pan.
Pack meat mixture into pan.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Remove from oven; invert meat loaf onto baking sheet and lift off pan.
Raise oven temperature to very hot (450°); return meat loaf to oven for 10 minutes to crisp bacon. Makes 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients.
Spray glass cooking dish with vegetable spray and pour in dish.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Cook broccoli; chop and set aside.
Melt butter in large, heavy pan.
Add mushrooms and onion; saute until tender.
Add flour and stir until bubbly.
Gradually add 1 1/2 cups milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Add cheese and stir until smooth. Add remaining milk.
Add broccoli and heat thoroughly.
Combine and mix all ingredients, except last 3 items.
Pinch off small amount and roll into bite-size balls.
Place on cookie sheets and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine and mix last 3 items and bring to boil; simmer for 30 minutes, until sauce is slightly thick.
Place sauce in large chafing dish and add meatballs.
In a deep casserole, layer the ingredients (do not pack beef). Pour juice over.
Bake at 325° to 350° about 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Quick Sock It To Me Cake Iii
d: Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix together cake mix, sugar, oil, eggs, pecans, and vanilla.
Fold in the sour cream.
Put half the batter in a bundt pan.
Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the batter in the pan.
Pour remainder of the batter on top.
Bake for 70 minutes until cake tests done.
Cut center out of rolls.
Melt margarine in saucepan.
Add bread pieces, canned chicken and chicken soup.
Fill holes with chicken mixture; spread remaining mixture across top of rolls. Bake at 400° until brown, 10 to 15 minutes.

Cream butter well with sugar. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Mix in flour and baking soda alternately with the buttermilk until blended. Stir in lemon peel and lemon juice. Spread in greased and floured 10 x 4-inch tube pan. Bake 1 hour in a preheated 325° oven.
Drain pineapple juice and add flour.
Cook and stir constantly until thick.
Cool.
Whip cream and combine to cooled thickening. Add crushed pineapple and pour into cooled pie shells.
Sprinkle with chopped pecans.
Chill and serve.
Cover cookie sheet with foil.
Lay saltines on foil.
Melt and boil butter and brown sugar for 3 minutes.
Pour over crackers and spread.
Bake at 375° for 5 minutes.
Remove and cool one minute. Pour chocolate chips evenly over top; let soften and spread. Refrigerate to set.
Break up and serve.
Cream butter; add sugar.
Add egg yolks.
Add milk and flour, then flavorings.
Roll nuts, coconut and raisins in flour and add to mixture.
Fold in egg whites.
Bake in four layers in moderate oven until done.
Make a cream sauce by blending butter with flour and salt. Stir in milk; cook until thickened (use rounded tablespoonful measure in this recipe so your sauce will be thick).
Set aside until cold.
Drain salmon; take out skin and bone.
Add slightly beaten egg, lemon juice and the white sauce to the salmon.
Place in refrigerator to chill for at least an hour, then shape into croquettes.
Roll in fine cracker crumbs and fry in hot fat.
Drain on paper towels.
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt.
Add beaten eggs.
Combine juice of 3 oranges, melted butter and enough boiling water to make 1 1/2 cups of liquid.
Add liquid to flour mixture.
Add walnuts and cranberries.
Makes 3 loaves.
Let stand in pans for 20 minutes before baking.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to an hour.
In the order listed, place the water, oil, honey, molasses, salt, rye flour, bread flour and yeast in the baking pan of a bread machine.
Place the pan in the machine and bake the bread according to the manufacturer's directions for a plain loaf. Makes 1 (1 1/2-pound) loaf (16 slices).
Thaw potatoes.
Mix first 7 ingredients and place in 9 x 13-inch buttered casserole.
Sprinkle cornflakes on top and drizzle with oleo.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes to 1 hour.
Cover potatoes and onion with water; cook until tender.
Do not drain.
Mash slightly, leaving some lumps.
Add rest of ingredients and salt and pepper to taste.
Additional sweet milk may be added if more broth is needed.
Cook until hot and serve.
Grate and mix with light Miracle Whip.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Grease a shallow 2-quart baking dish with nonstick spray.
In a 10-inch skillet, cook onions and ground beef until meat loses red color.
Drain off excess fat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Spread meat mixture in baking dish.
Cover with undiluted soup and top with single layer of frozen Tater Tots.
Bake for 45 minutes.
In a medium-size bowl, put pineapple with juice.
Add drained cans of peaches, fruit cocktail and strawberries.
Add vanilla pudding mix and orange juice.
Mix all well and chill well.
Mix all ingredients together and spoon over chicken in baking dish.
This will be enough sauce to do 2 chickens.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
In skillet, brown beef.
Stir to separate meat and pour off fat.
Add soup, sour cream and seasonings.
Cook over low heat 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve over noodles.
Beat margarine at medium speed with a mixer until creamy.
Add cake mix, eggs and water, beating until blended.
Stir in brickle chips and pecans.
Drop cookies by tablespoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes until edges are brown.
Makes 48 cookies.
Cut up Cauliflower into bite size pieces.
Mix together with frozen peas, shredded cheese and 1/2 jar bacon bits.
Mix ranch dressing according to direction.
Then pour over salad and mix well.
Let sit overnight.
(May substitute 1 Broccoli for Cauliflower.)
Garnish liberally with love and keep cool until it sparkles. If you have followed God's cookbook in preparing your marriage, your home is ready now!
Day 1:
Combine starter and peaches (only one can of juice). Let set 10 days, stirring each day!
Slightly butter 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Butter bread and chop into cubes.
Cook sausage and chorizo and drain.
Place bread cubes in dish.
Cover with chorizo and sausage.
Add 1 cup cheese.
Add eggs and milk, beaten together.
Pour over bread and sausage.
Cover and let set overnight.
Before baking, add 1/2 cup grated cheese and chopped green chilies.
Bake in 350° oven for 35 to 45 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Combine soy sauce, bourbon and sugar.
Mix well.
Marinate pork in mixture for 2 to 3 hours.
This can be baked in marinade, uncovered, at 325° for 1 hour.
Turn meat halfway through.
Slice on diagonal.
Or this is wonderful cooked on grill.
Serve with horseradish sauce or Rothschild Raspberry Salsa.
Boil potatoes until soft, mash.
Put potatoes and all ingredients into crock-pot.
Cook on low until heated through.
Can be made the night before and put in crock-pot the next day to heat up.
Cube eggplant and put in pot with water to cover.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Drain and place in greased baking dish.
Peel, seed and grate 3 cups zucchini.
Mix eggs, sugar, salt, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, Wesson oil and flour.
Then add zucchini, coconut and nuts.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour.
Makes 3 loaves.
Cream shortening.
Add sugar gradually.
Cream until well blended.
Add 1 egg.
Beat until mixture is light and fluffy. Sift flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk and vanilla.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch cake pan.
Cover with washed and drained blueberries.
Sprinkle top with sugar.
Dot with butter.
Bake in a 350° oven for about 1 hour.
Beat egg. Combine with Ricotta and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cover bottom of casserole dish with sauce. Add a layer of rice. Add a layer of Ricotta.
Add sauce and a layer of Mozzarella and some Parmesan. Repeat until all ingredients are used.
Put sauce on top and sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbly.

Brown sausage. Beat eggs; add milk and salt. Grease 13 x 9-inch pan. Spread sausage in bottom of pan. Next layer bread cubes. Top with Cheddar cheese. Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until center is done. Makes 6 servings.
You may use bacon or ham instead of sausage.
Mix butter and sugar.
Add eggs, then add cake mix and sour cream.
Then add flavoring, flour and milk.
Bake at 350°
about 1 hour and 10 minutes in tube pan.
As soon as you remove from pan, pour a real thin glaze of icing.
I like to do this while the cake is still hot, therefore most of the glaze is absorbed into the cake.
Mix all ingredients.
Add M&M's.
Drop by teaspoon on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° until lightly browned, about 10 minutes.
Crumble sausage and fry in large skillet.
Stir while cooking. As soon as all pink color of meat disappears, push meat to one side and brown potato cubes slightly in sausage drippings.
Stir potatoes and sausage together.
Sprinkle flour.
Add milk; cook and stir until slightly thickened.
Pour into 2-quart casserole. Sprinkle cheese and paprika over top.
Cover with lid or foil and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes.
Serve hot.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Recipe can be refrigerated for later.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a shallow dish.
Dip fish in milk and dredge in cornmeal mixture.
Place in a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan and drizzle with butter.

Top with the remaining 1/4 cup cheese and sprinkle with the bread crumbs.

Continue to bake for 20 to 25 more minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

Heat oil in large skillet.
Brown chicken.

Cook until desired consistency.

Slice when cold.

Add spaghetti to skillet and sprinkle with Romano cheese, salt, pepper and monosodium glutamate.
Using large spoon, stir spaghetti being careful not to cut it.
Continue until heated and be careful not to let butter brown.
Put all ingredients in blender.
Chill before using.
Cut beans lengthwise.
Chop onions.
Combine all ingredients in a heavy saucepan.
Cook, covered, for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Cook broccoli until tender; drain and put into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Combine soup with milk, stirring until smooth.
Pour half of soup mixture over broccoli.
Sprinkle grated cheese over soup layer; add remaining soup.
Top with buttered bread cubes; bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until lightly browned. Yield:
6 servings.
*Stew chicken. Strain and save broth.
Remove skin and bones and break meat into pieces.
Place on bottom of a 9 x 12-inch greased glass pan.
Saute mushrooms in a little of the broth.
Mix mushrooms, soup and sour cream together.
Place on top of chicken. Mix stuffing with 1/2 pound melted butter or margarine and 1 cup broth.
Place on top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until dressing is browned.
Brown beef in 2 tablespoons cooking oil.
Salt to taste.
Cook until tender.
Add celery, peppers and onions.
Combine all ingredients, except cheese, in a large bowl.
Mix lightly.
Put in casserole and bake until tender.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° until cheese is melted.
Spray small casserole with Pam.
Add sliced eggplant, mushrooms and 1/3 cup grated cheese, mixed together.
Sprinkle basil over ingredients or other herbs and spices to suit your taste.
Cover with spaghetti sauce (add more basil, if desired). Add remaining cheese.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serves 4.
Spoon 1/4 of dip over each tortilla, spreading to edges. Sprinkle each with 1/4 of chicken.
Roll up.
Place seam side down on a plate or flat dish.
Cover with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Cut each roll into six 1-inch pieces.
Serve with salsa.
Makes 24 appetizers.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt, then cut in butter to make crumbles.
Add dried fruit, ginger and lemon peel, mixing well.
Add buttermilk.
On a lightly floured board, knead dough 6 turns, then place on greased baking pan (12 x 15-inch) and shape into an oval loaf.
Using a floured knife, cut across loaf in triangles to form pie shaped slices.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes or until top is brown.
Melt butter.
Blend together sugar and eggs; add butter.
Stir in buttermilk, soda, cornmeal, flour and salt.
Bake in a 9 x 9-inch pan at 350° for 30 minutes.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Chill until partially set. Beat until fluffy.
Fold in berries.
Gradually beat sugar into egg whites; beat until mixture stands in peaks and sugar is dissolved.
Fold egg whites and whipped cream into gelatin mixture.
Pour into cooled baked pastry shell.
Chill until set. Top with whipped cream.
Garnish with sliced strawberries.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix sugar, flour and 1/2 stick margarine (melted); mix well. Add well beaten eggs; mix well.
Add milk and flavoring; mix well. Pour into unbaked pie crust.
Dot with remaining margarine. Sprinkle with nutmeg, if desired.
Bake at 325° for about 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Busy Day Fruit Cobbler(A Juicy Cobbler, Southern Style)
d: Place
fruit
in
greased 8 x 8-inch pan.
(If fruit is very juicy, mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch with each cup juice.) Cream shortening
and
sugar.
Mix in egg.
Add flour and milk alternately;
mix until smooth after each addition.
Pour over fruit in pan.
Bake in 375° oven for about 30 minutes.
Cut in squares.
Serve warm with cream or whipped cream, if desired.
Combine all of the ingredients in a 8 x 12-inch casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until set.
Cover with 1 cup bread crumbs.
Wash okra.
Leave small amount of stem on okra.
Pack into sterilized pint jars, standing on end to get as many okra pods in jars as possible.
For hot pickles, add 1 pod of hot pepper to each jar.
For dill pickles, add sprig of dill weed to each jar. Boil vinegar; add 1/4 cup to each jar.
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt to each jar.
Finish filling jar with boiling water.
Seal jars while hot.
Ready to eat in about 2 weeks.
Heat 2 c. water and 1 c. milk.
Soften yeast in warm water; let set.
Combine sugar, oil and salt in large bowl; add hot milk; then add cold water.
Add eggs that have been whipped a little. Add yeast and mix.
Add between 7 and 9 c. flour, until a stiff batter.
Spread a large quantity of flour and pour out batter. Knead dough for about 7 minutes. Put into a greased bowl and let rise until doubled.
Punch down and turn over.
Let rise 30 minutes.
Turn out and shape into rolls or loaves and let rise double.
Bake at 375° until golden brown.
Brush with butter.
Heat butter in large pan and saute the meat until it becomes light brown on all sides.
Add the salt, pepper, carrots, celery, parsley and the water or beef sauce and then lemon juice.
Boil it for 2 hours.
Let the meat cool and cut it in pieces.
Put the pieces in the pan again and warm the pieces for awhile.
Pour the gravy through the colander.
Make the gravy thicker by adding 2 teaspoons of flour.
Serve the meat with rice or sauteed mushrooms.
Peel and seed squash. Dice into pieces. Cook in saltwater until soft and tender. Drain off water.

Pure squash or beat with mixer. Mix flour and sugar together. Add to mixture. Beat on low speed. Add eggs, milks and vanilla; mix well. Pour into unbaked pie shells. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until set.
Drain fruit.
Reserve juices.
Combine juices and stir well. Set aside 1/2 cup juices.
Combine butter and sugar.
Stir until smooth.
Add reserved juice, brandy and spices.
Stir until blended.
Combine fruit in 12 x 8 x 2-inch dish.
Pour brandy mixture in.
Microwave on High 10 to 12 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Stir twice.
Sift flour, cocoa and salt together; set aside.
Cream sugar and shortening together.
Blend in eggs and vanilla.
Add soda to cold water; stir well.
Add alternately with dry ingredients to creamed mixture, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Blend thoroughly after each addition.
Beat 2 eggs slightly and pour into a well of flour mixture (flour, sugar, baking soda, salt and cinnamon).
Add oil, apples, nuts and vanilla.
Mix.
Pour batter into a 15 x 9 1/2 x 2-inch greased pan.
(I use lasagna size foil pans.)
Sprinkle topping on cake.
Put in cold oven.
Set oven at 325° and bake for 50 minutes.
Combine dates and water; bring to boiling.
Simmer 5 minutes. Cool. Set aside 2 tablespoons of date mixture for frosting.
Beat in egg, sugar, butter and milk.
Stir together flour, salt, baking powder and soda.
Add to egg mixture.
Stir in nuts.
Drop from teaspoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool.
Mix together the ingredients.
Form loaf in pan (catsup on top).
Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.

In a large saucepan cook cauliflower in a a small amount of water for 6 to 7 minutes until crisp and tender. Drain well. In a medium saucepan saute bell peppers and mushrooms in butter for 2 minutes. Add flour and gradually stir in milk. Bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted. Add pimentos and salt. Place half of the cauliflower in a greased 2 quart
baking dish. Top with half of sauce. Repeat layers. Bake uncovered at 325 degrees for 25 minutes or until bubbly. Sprinkle with paprika if desired.
Mix all ingredients.
Freeze 6 to 8 hours.
Place a scoop of slush into a glass of ginger ale.
Great for parties!
Beat whipping cream and confectioners sugar until stiff.
To 2 cups of frosting stir in several drops of yellow food coloring and 1/2 teaspoon almond extract.
To 1 cup of frosting, add red food coloring and 1/2 teaspoon rum extract to make pink.
Stir until dissolved.
Add and stir into first mixture.
Pour into Tupperware ring or 2 small bowls and let set in refrigerator overnight.
Brown first 4 ingredients in skillet; place in crock-pot.
Add remaining ingredients to crock-pot.
Stir and cook 2 hours on low. May add hot pepper to taste.
Fry the onion in oil.
Add remaining ingredients.
Saute onions in oleo.
Mix all ingredients together and sprinkle 1/2 cup corn chips on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
Make rice according to package.
When done mix in ground beef, egg and seasonings.
Arrange peppers in baking dish.
Fill each with ground beef mixture.

recipes.t: Three Bean And Corn Bread Casserole
d: Heat oven to 425°.
Mix all ingredients except Corn Bread Topping; pour into ungreased baking dish, 13 x 9 x 2-inch. Prepare Corn Bread Topping; spoon evenly over bean mixture to within 1 inch of edges.
Bake until topping is deep golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes.
Cream the margarine, shortening and sugars.
Add vanilla and eggs.
Combine flour, soda, salt and oatmeal.
Add to sugar mixture.
Stir in chips.
Chill dough before baking.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes.
In Dutch oven brown roast in shortening.
Combine onion soup mix with 2 cups of water.
Pour over roast; simmer, turning occasionally for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until tender.
Or after browning, put into crock-pot until almost tender, then add potatoes and carrots.
Blend flour and water.
Stir into drippings where roast was browned and make gravy.
Serves 6.
Combine in bowl the first 3 ingredients and let stand until the moisture is taken up.
Add 1 egg and beat well.
Sift remaining ingredients and add.
Stir until combined.
Grease muffin tins and fill 2/3 full.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes before removing.
Yields 12 to 15 (2 1/2-inch) muffins.
Cook chicken.
Remove from bones and chop.
Mix well all ingredients and place in casserole dish.
Cover with another cup of Ritz crackers (crushed).
Bake about 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix and toss with lettuce.
Cook and drain noodles.
Cut pork into thin strips.
(Throw in the bones, too.)
Heat 2 large skillets.
Put 1 tablespoon butter into 1 skillet and add the meat.
Brown slightly.
Add the onions. Add the beans.
Cover and cook until the beans are done.
In second skillet, melt the rest of the butter until hot.
Add the cooked noodles.
Cook until crisp and brown.
Turn over and brown other side.
When noodles and meat are ready, remove half the noodles to a bowl.
Take half the meat and add it to the noodles in the pan. Put the noodles from the bowl into the other pan with the meat. Mix each pan to combine.
You now have 2 pans of stuff.
Enough to feed a crowd.
Mix egg yolks, margarine and milk together.
Mix sugar and flour together.
Add the two mixtures together in medium saucepan. Cook until thickened.
Coconut is optional.
Pour into 2 baked pie crusts or 1 deep-dish baked crust.
Combine first 5 ingredients into 3-quart pan.
Cook over medium heat until sugar dissolves.
Add cashews and coconut. Increase heat to high.
Stir constantly until mixture becomes light brown.
Remove from heat.
Cook 4 cups celery, diced fine in 2 cups water until tender, about 18 minutes; drain and save 1 cup liquid.
Saute 1/2 cup minced onions in 1/2 cup butter over low heat.
Drain 1 1/2 cups oysters.
Add enough celery liquid to oyster liquid to make one cup.
Mix well 4 quarts lightly packed, day old bread crumbs with 2 teaspoons poultry seasoning, 1 tablespoon salt and pepper.
Then combine dry ingredients with liquid onions and oysters; blend well.
Put cheese in double boiler.
Melt and add rest of the ingredients.
Pour into containers and serve.
Boil potatoes until done.
Refrigerate until cold.
When cold, peel and dice in small squares.
Dice boiled eggs.
Mix Lorna Doone cookie crumbs with melted butter.
Press crust into bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix pudding and milk until thick. Blend softened ice cream.
Pour on crust.
Chill until firm.
Before serving, spread Cool Whip and sprinkle with crushed Heath bars.
Slice large mushrooms and leave small ones whole.
Cut onion in half, then into long, thin strips.
Melt butter with soy sauce. Add remaining ingredients.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until onion is almost clear.
Place hash browns on bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix soups and sour cream and pour over hash browns.
Cover top with French fried onion rings.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In large bowl beat peanut butter and butter until smooth.
Add sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Beat until creamy.
Blend in flour and salt.
Stir in one cup chocolate morsels.
Spread in ungreased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until edges begin to brown.
Sprinkle remaining chocolate over cookie layer.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Spread evenly over top.
Cool completely.
Cut in 1 1/2-inch bars.
Makes about 48 bars.
Beat eggs and oil. Add all other ingredients and mix together. Put in slightly greased 10-inch glass pie pan. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. Knife should come out clean when cutting.
In a pan heat milk, chicken base, white pepper and Worcestershire to a simmer.
Do not boil.
In a pan melt butter; stir flour in and cook, stirring 2 minutes until flour is incorporated.
Stir in warm milk and cook, stirring until sauce is thickened.
Place crabmeat in a shallow 1 1/2 or 2-quart buttered casserole and sprinkle first with lemon juice, then with Parmesan cheese.
Cover with white sauce.
Sprinkle grated Cheddar over the top.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 20 to 25 minutes until heated through and bubbly.
You may substitute crawfish tails for the crabmeat.
Makes 6 servings.
May add pecan pieces, if desired.
Brown ground beef in a soup pot; drain. Add all other ingredients and bring to a simmer. With lid on, simmer for 4 hours. Serve with sour cream and cheese.
Melt over hot (not boiling) water the chocolate morsels; stir until smooth.
Remove from heat.
Stir in marshmallows, nuts and sunflower seeds.
Spread in foil-lined 8-inch square pan.
Chill until firm.
Mix hash browns and oleo.
Add salt, pepper, soup, cheese, sour cream and onions.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Boil the potatoes
until tender. Cool and grate.
Saute the onion and add
with
all
other
ingredients to the grated potato. Season to taste.
Top
with crushed corn flakes. Bake at 350° for approximately 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Put the first 3 ingredients in a pan over low heat.
Let boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add the remaining ingredients.
Stir until melted.
Pour into a greased pan and let cool.
Mix all ingredients well and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Take out and mix well again and return to refrigerator for another 24 hours.
Shape into loaves and bake on broiler pan at 160° for 8 hours, turning after first 4 hours.
After it cools, you can slice it and freeze it in sealed bags.
Bake 55 minutes at 350°.
Soak beans overnight or use quick cook method on package. Drain off 1/2 the water after cooking.
Add remaining ingredients to cooked beans.
Put in a casserole dish and cover to bake.
Bake for 3 hours at 350°.
Let stand covered for 30 minutes before serving (to thicken sauce).
Serves 8 to 10.
Slice rolls in half; spread half of mixture on each side. Layer ham, beef and cheese.
Spread a little of mixture on top. Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
In a nonstick skillet, spray nonfat cooking spray generously. Saute beef or turkey, onion, mushrooms, garlic powder and dry mustard over medium-high heat until meat is browned and onion is tender.
Combine mayonnaise, yogurt and beef broth and add to beef mixture.
Cook over low heat 15 minutes.
Serve over hot noodles. Serves 4.
Place ham on rack in a shallow roasting pan.
Bake at 325° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Slice to serve.
Mix the first 4 ingredients well.
Place the remaining ingredients in saucepan and heat to rolling boil.
Mix cabbage and dressing.
Add 1/2 cup red wine vinegar.
Marinate three days in refrigerator before eating.
Keep in refrigerator in airtight container up to 3 weeks.
Bake at
for 20 minutes.	Grease cookie sheet and lay in wax paper.
Mix eggs, sugar, pumpkin, flour, spice and nuts in a bowl.
Stir
and pour in pan and bake.
Place a tea towel on counter
top
and sift powdered sugar on towel until its very white.
When
pumpkin
bread is done, place on towel and roll
up while
it's
very warm.
Let set.
Roll up until cold.
Unroll. Spread cream cheese filling and roll up again. Slice and enjoy.
Sprinkle vanilla wafer crumbs evenly in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Set aside.
In a small mixing bowl, beat egg yolks with fork.
Beat in milk and cooking oil.
In a large bowl, stir together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Add egg mixture to flour mixture all at once.
Stir mixture until blended, but still slightly lumpy.
In small mixer bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form. Carefully fold egg whites into egg-flour mixture.
Leave a few fluffs of egg whites.
Do not overmix.
Lightly grease waffle maker.
Cook; do not lift lid while baking.
Makes 3 or 4 (9-inch) waffles.
Place 12 crackers on uncoated paper plate.
Spread 1/2 teaspoon tomato paste on each cracker.
Top each with 1 slice pepperoni, 1 teaspoon shredded cheese and sprinkle with basil.
Mix all ingredients except vanilla in medium saucepan and cook over medium-high heat until it comes to a full boil; stir constantly. Continue to stir and boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla. Set aside to cool.
Make 2 pie shells and bake them.
Mix jello and water together first, then add all ingredients. Chill.
Beat cream cheese, butter and vanilla until fluffy. Gradually add sugars and beat until just combined.
Stir in chips. Cover and refrigerate 2 hours.
Place mixture on plastic wrap and shape into a ball.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Just before serving, roll in pecans.
Serve with graham crackers.
Eggs, sour cream and butter should be at room temperature.
Coarsely chop onions.
Boil onions in salted water.
Add butter to liquid; stir until melted.
Add white sauce to onion mixture.
Serve hot.
Serves 8 people.
Mix flour and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour in a greased casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until set.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Place bread slices on baking sheet and bake 8 to 10 minutes until golden on each side.
Rub one side of the toasted bread with garlic and drizzle with a little oil. Arrange a few slices of tomato over each slice of bread.
Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with basil.
Drizzle tomatoes with more oil.
Serve while warm.
Serves 8.
Saute until soft in the margarine the celery, onion and carrots. Add broth and milk, reserving 1/2 cup milk.
Combine flour and cornstarch in a bowl. Stir milk. Add soda and cheese last. Cook over low heat until cheese melts, stirring constantly. Serves 6 to 8.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Add beans; mix well. Place 6 tortillas in casserole pan.
Layer ground beef mix, cheese and remaining tortillas in casserole.
Mix soup and Ro-Tel in bowl.
Pour over tortillas.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix sugar and oil.
Mix flour, soda and cocoa.
Add to sugar and oil alternately with buttermilk.
Heat coffee to a boil and add to mixture last.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Butter a small casserole dish and put in drained green beans. Slice hard-boiled eggs on top.
Pour a mixture of mushroom soup and milk that has been heated.
Place in 325° oven for about 20 minutes.
Mix jello, sugar and pineapple.
Cook 5 minutes.
Cool.
Whip cream cheese (softened) and 1 cup cold water together.
Add pineapple.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Mix Cool Whip in.
Pat in molds and refrigerate.
Brown beef and drain off excess fat.
Add sauce and water; simmer about 10 minutes.
Combine remaining ingredients, except noodles, for filling.
Pour about one cup of sauce on bottom of 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Combine the first 4 ingredients and cook 10 to 15 minutes, covered.
Do not drain.
Combine the next 3 ingredients and cook for sauce.
Add broth and cheese.
Combine all and heat until really hot, stirring to prevent scorching.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Peel and cube eggplant; cook until tender.
While eggplant is cooking, saute onion, bell pepper and celery in oleo.
Mash eggplant, leaving water in the eggplant.
Add crumbled cornbread and egg to mixture.
Add onion, celery and bell pepper.
Place in greased casserole.
Top with cheese.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
In greased 6-cup souffle dish, combine Ritz crackers, cheese and mushrooms.
In medium bowl with electric mixer at medium speed, beat together eggs, milk, onion powder, parsley and poultry seasoning.
Pour over mixture in souffle dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until puffed and lightly browned.
Serve hot.
Combine first 3 ingredients; press into a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 20 minutes or until lightly brown.
Cool completely.
Melt 1/4 cup margarine. Add coconut and 1/2 cup chopped pecans.
Cook over low heat, stirring often until coconut is golden brown.
Cool.
Make pie crust.
Either your own or pie crust mix.
Cut pie crust with cutter and line muffin tins.
Put teaspoon of jam on pie crust and then large tablespoon of batter mix on top.
Bake until golden brown at 300° to 350°.
Wash lentils.
Drain.
Cover with vinegar and tomato juice. Let soak for 2 hours.
Brown beef cubes and chopped onion.
Add spices; add to lentils and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours, adding hot water as necessary.
Freshness and quality of the spices makes a lot of difference, so check the flavor and correct the seasoning 15 to 20 minutes before serving.
Wash apples; peel very thin.
Core, slice and place in shallow baking dish.
Mix together white sugar, spices and 1/4 teaspoon salt; sprinkle this and lemon juice over apples.
Blend flour, brown sugar, dash of salt and margarine until crumbly.
Sprinkle over apples; pat down gently with back of spoon.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Store in tightly covered container.
To serve, dissolve 1 tablespoon of mixture in cup of hot water.
Yields 8 cups.
Heat oil in a 4-quart heavy, covered kettle.
Add lamb and garlic; cook until meat is browned.
Add boiling water; cover and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add carrots, celery, onion, potatoes, salt, pepper and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer until all is tender.
Mix flour and cold water into a smooth paste.
Stir into hot stew. Keep stirring until thickened.
Serve with a garnish of chopped parsley.
Stew tastes better next day or two days later.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Serve with beef.
Mix crumbs with melted butter.
Reserve 1 cup; press remainder onto bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate.
Set aside.
Fry bacon until crisp and cut small.
Remove from pan.
Fry pork until golden brown.
Remove from pan.
Saute onions until soft.
Drain clams, saving juice, then chop clams fine.
Add to clam juice enough water to make 3 cups.
Bring to a boil and add potatoes, browned pork, onions and bacon.
Simmer until potatoes are done, about 15 minutes.
Blend flour to a smooth paste with cold water, add to the potatoes, stirring until it boils and thickens.
Add clams and seasonings.
Add the milk and add slowly to hot clam mixture.
Add 2 tablespoons butter when done.
Serves 6.
In a large serving bowl, combine the first seven ingredients. Let stand at room temperature for up to 1 1/2 hours.
Cook linguine according to package directions; drain.
Toss with cheese mixture.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately.
Stir all ingredients. Serve with crackers or chips.
Beat eggs well.
Add sugar slowly, while beating.
Fold in dates and nutmeats.
Bake in buttered cake pan for 60 minutes at 325°.
Serve with whipped cream.
Combine eggs, sugar and oil; mix well.
Stir 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon juice and baking soda into pulp.
Combine flour, salt and spices.
Add to egg mixture alternately with persimmon mixture, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in walnuts and raisins. Spread in greased and floured oblong pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool for 5 minutes.
Combine first five ingredients and mix well.
Make small size (1-inch diameter) meat balls and fry in small amount of oil (if necessary) evenly on all sides.
Drain on paper towel.
Layer each ingredient, beginning with the lettuce.
Cook jumbo shells according to package directions; drain.
Cool on paper.
Brown beef and pork in skillet; drain.
Combine meat, eggs, bread crumbs, Mozzarella cheese (if desired), onion, oregano, salt and pepper.
Fill each shell with 2 tablespoons.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on bottom of 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Place shells open side down, in a single layer in the pan; cover with sauce.
Cover with aluminum foil; bake at 350° about 45 minutes. Fills 36 shells.
Makes 10 to 12 servings.
Mix Cool Whip, cottage cheese and crushed pineapple.
Add pecans and chopped cherries (save some for garnish). Add dry jello. Stir well. Chill.
Will need a 2 quart casserole dish.
Put sausage in large pot.
Cover with water at least 1 inch over top of sausage.
Boil about 30 minutes.
Remove sausage from broth; put into a bowl and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours or overnight. Strain through a tea strainer to remove all of the fat.
Put broth in pot.
Add cabbage, cut into wedges.
Place sausage on top and cook until done.
Season to taste.
Cook chicken until it comes off the bone easily.
Cool and debone.
Put pieces into baking dish (9 x 13-inch).
Pour cream of chicken soup and broth over chicken.
At this point, you can put into refrigerator or freezer.
Mix flour, buttermilk and oleo; pour over chicken mixture.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Brown ground beef.
Once beef is brown, mix all other ingredients in a skillet.
Bring to a boil.
Cover the bottom of a casserole dish with the Doritos.
Pour in other ingredients.
Top with the Cheddar cheese.
Put in oven at 350° until cheese melts. If you wish, you may top with salsa and sour cream.
Serves 8 to 10 people.

Cut cheese into pieces. Chop the peeled chiles and the peeled tomato; add the other ingredients. Cook in the top of a double boiler, stirring occasionally. Serve hot with Fritos, tostados or crackers. This mixture should cook or rather melt down, about 3 hours. If possible, serve in a chafing dish or in some utensil over hot water.
Fold each of the ingredients into the Cool Whip.
Cool to enhance the flavor.
Maraschino cherries placed on the top add a festive touch at Christmas.
Mix onions and salmon.
Let stand for 30 minutes, then add other ingredients.
Deep fry until golden brown.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Pour oil into 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Tilt pan until bottom is covered with oil.
Put remaining ingredients into pan; stir with a fork or spoon until blended (about 2 minutes).
Scrape sides and spread batter evenly in pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.
Cooled cake may be sprinkled with powdered sugar. Use a knife to loosen cake from sides, cut and serve directly from pan.
Store leftover cake, loosely covered.

recipes.t: Festive Pumpkin Or Sweet Potato Bread
d: Sift first 9 ingredients together.
Cream the sugar and oil in a large bowl.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.

Blend 1/3 cup water and pumpkin or sweet potato in bowl. Add pumpkin or sweet potato mixture alternately with dry ingredients to sugar mixture, blending well after each addition. Stir in raisins and nuts. Pour into 2 small greased and floured loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bread tests done.
Boil the shrimp in their shells with the celery leaves, pickling spices and 1 tablespoon salt for 5 minutes.
Drain shrimp and clean.
Place shrimp in covered container with a mixture made from the remaining ingredients for 24 hours.
Serve on toothpicks with pineapple cubes, green peppers and cheese cubes.

recipes.t: Bountiful Cream Of Broccoli Cheese And Clam Bisque
d: Microwave broccoli, onions, broth and salt, covered, 20 minutes.
Put aside 6 cooked broccoli flowerets for garnish. Puree broth mixture in food processor for a count of 20 seconds. Uncover.
Cut orange slices into small pieces.
Use 1/2 cup of your flour to keep your knife clean.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs; beat until very light.
Sift flour, salt and soda; add alternately with the coconut and nuts.
Add orange candy to creamed mixture.
Add vanilla.
Drop by small teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes, or until light brown, at 350°.
Makes 5 dozen cookies.
Saute ingredients in pan.
Be generous with lime juice.
Put over any kind of pasta (linguini or angel hair pasta).
Wash sweet potatoes, cover with water and partially cook until just tender enough to be pierced with a fork.
Do not over cook. Drain well and set aside.
Combine the oil or butter, brown sugar and juice and rind in a small saucepan.
Heat to boiling and cook for 2 minutes.
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them in half lengthwise.
Place sweet potatoes in a shallow 8 inch square pan. Pour syrup over them.

for 3 days before cooking.
Then cover with foil or use a
cooking bag and bake in oven or smoker at 325° until thermometer reaches 180° to 185°.
Saute onion and garlic in butter over medium heat.
Stir in meat and brown.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper and mushrooms.
Cook 5 minutes.	Stir in soup.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Stir in sour cream.
Heat.	Serve over noodles.
Dip dove breasts in soy sauce.
Wrap with 1/2 slice of bacon and secure with a toothpick if necessary. Place on grill or in the oven (350°) on a rack in a pan.
Cook for approximately 30 minutes or until the breast is tender.
Put cake pieces into 9 x 13 x 2-inch pan.
Drizzle jello over top.
Let set for a few minutes in refrigerator.
Pour prepared pudding over this and add slices of banana over top.
Frost with Cool Whip.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Cook noodles according to package directions; drain noodles.
Rinse with cold water.
Mix Ricotta, egg, parsley and 1 cup Mozzarella in a bowl; set aside.
Mix. Bake in muffin pan at 450° for 10 minutes.
Makes 6 good size rolls.
Rinse tuna in colander 1 minute; let drain 1 minute.
Combine tuna with next 5 ingredients and toss gently.
Combine mayo, lemon juice and dill.
Toss gently with other combined ingredients. Cover and chill for 1 hour or until serving.
When ready to serve, spoon into halved pita pockets.
Use celery leaves to garnish. Makes 6 servings.
Great for picnics, summertime entertaining or lunch anytime!
Melt 1/4 cup butter.
Stir in 1/4 cup flour.
Add chicken broth, stirring constantly until mixture thickens.
Lower heat and add cheese.
Stir until cheese melts.
Remove from heat.
Stir in chicken, carrots and the pimento.
Spread in shallow 2-quart casserole.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Melt 1/4 cup butter.
Add seasoned stuffing mix and mix well.
Spread over chicken mixture. Bake for 30 minutes.
Serves 8 to 10.
Boil chicken in salt water; cool and debone.
Take 1 1/2 quarts broth from chicken and boil vermicelli in it.
Do not drain.
Saute bell pepper, celery and onion in margarine; add this to vermicelli along with Ro-Tel tomatoes, chicken and cheese. Heat until cheese is melted.
Bake in casserole dish at 350° until bubbly.
Mix cake mix, jello, oil, milk and eggs and beat until well blended.
Put in 1/2 package frozen strawberries, 1/2 cup pecans and 1/2 cup coconut.
Bake in three greased and floured cake pans. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool cake on wire racks.
Place paper towel on a microwave-safe plate.
Arrange tortilla chips on Bounty-lined plate.
Sprinkle with cheese, olives and pepper.
Microwave at 50% (Medium) for 2 to 5 minutes or until cheese melts, rotating plate once or twice.
Makes 4 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Saute pork, celery and onion.
Mix all ingredients together in roaster pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In a medium bowl, place chicken.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with lemon juice and let set for 5 minutes.
Reserve 1 teaspoon taco seasoning mix; set aside.
Combine remaining taco seasoning mix, chicken, beer and chiles in a large skillet.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes or until mixture is thickened.
Remove from heat; stir in salsa.

recipes.t: Cole Porter'S Three Fruit Cole Slaw
d: In a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients except the mayonnaise.
Cover and chill.
Just before serving, stir in the mayonnaise.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine dry ingredients.
Add nuts and mix.
Combine slightly beaten eggs with remaining ingredients.
Pour all at once into dry ingredients.
Blend lightly.
Bake in 2 well-greased and floured loaf pans at 350° for 1 hour.
Brown the flour with the bacon drippings until brown and thick.
Add the salt and pepper.
Mix well and add milk, cooking and stirring until desired thickness.
Sop with biscuits.
Mix oleo, flour and pecans.
Pat into 9 x 13-inch pan and bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Combine sugar, cream cheese and 1 cup topping.
Mix pudding and cold milk; spread over cream cheese mixture in pan.
Spread rest of whipped topping over mixture and refrigerate.
Mix and refrigerate.
Add vodka to mix or serve as Virgin Mary.
Adjust spices to your own taste.
Layer in large oblong pan the refried beans, ground beef cooked in taco seasoning mix, green chiles, black olives, cheese and taco sauce.
Bake for 20 minutes in oven at 425°.
Stir in one cup of sour cream.
Serve with Doritos or nachos.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
Mix all ingredients until stiff.
Form into patties.
Dip in chocolate; place on wax paper to set.
Cook and drain spinach and set aside.
Melt butter; add all spices.
Drain oysters and blot with towel.
Combine butter mixture with drained spinach.
Add bread crumbs and oysters and stir gently.
Place in a greased casserole and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Then uncover for 15 minutes.
Serve with Melba toast for appetizer.
Line 8-inch square baking pan with foil.
Combine sugar, Marshmallow Creme, milk, butter, Kahlua and salt in 2-quart saucepan.
Bring to rapid boil, stirring constantly for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add all chocolate.
Stir until melted.
Add nuts and vanilla.
Turn into pan.
Refrigerate until firm (overnight).
Cut into squares.
Keep in refrigerator until desired use.
Drain liquid from salmon and remove skin and bones.
Add next 5 ingredients.
Mix well.
Add cream cheese.
Chill overnight. Form into a ball and roll in chopped nuts and parsley.
In large frying pan, saute butter, onion, green pepper and mushrooms.
Broil ground veal steaks until brown on both sides. Serve on a toasted bun topped with the sauteed mixture.
Season to taste.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored.
Add water and continue beating until very thick.
Gradually add sugar and extract.
Sift flour with salt 3 times.
Fold in egg yolk mixture a little at a time.
Beat egg whites until foamy and then add cream of tartar.
Beat until real moist and glossy looking.
Fold this into first mixture.
Bake in ungreased pan at 325° for 1 hour. Remove from oven, invert pan and completely cool before removing from the pan. cut into 3 layers and fill with the filling.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In large skillet, heat oil.
Cook zucchini and mushrooms in oil until zucchini is tender-crisp, about 5 minutes; remove from heat.
Stir in tomato sauce, seasonings and 1/2 can French fried onions.
Pour into greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Mix all ingredients and pour into buttered baking dish. Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour.
Cook tapioca according to directions on box.
Do not use milk. Use the juice from the oranges and pineapple. Then enough water to equal 3 cups.
Cool.
Combine ingredients and form into loaf.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add pineapple and oranges. Pour into a 9 x 13-inch dish or larger.
Put in refrigerator until set.
Mix sour cream with mayonnaise and spread over congealed Jell-O mixture.
Sprinkle marshmallows and cheese on top of mayonnaise and sour cream mixture.
Keeps a week in refrigerator.
Mix all ingredients in 1/2 gallon container.
Pour into 2 sterilized wine bottles.
Cover, cork and store in a cool dry place for 30 days.
Serve as you like.
Makes approximately 1/2 gallon of Kahlua (coffee brandy).
Beat eggs well; add sugar, then add milk.
Pour into pie crust and cook on 450° for 25 minutes or until done.
I do not use flavoring, you can add some if you like.
Mix first 4 ingredients and place in tortilla.
Roll up and place in 13 x 9-inch pan.
Pour sauce over and add more shredded cheese on top.
Serve with gucamole, sour cream and picante sauce.
Place potatoes and water in a 2-quart microwave-safe casserole; cover.
Microwave on High for 12 to 15 minutes or until tender, stirring after 8 minutes.
Drain.
Mix remaining ingredients until well blended.
Stir in potatoes.
Refrigerate 1 hour.
Drain, reserving marinade.
Arrange potatoes on skewers.
Place on grill over hot coals.
Grill, covered, 6 to 8 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden brown, brushing occasionally with reserved marinade and turning after 4 minutes.
(Spraying the grill rack with nonstick cooking spray helps keep potatoes from sticking.)
Cover bottom of dish with Tater Tots and cook on 350° for 10 minutes.
In a skillet, brown ground beef.
Drain fat and add broccoli and steam.
Put on top of Tater Tots.
Mix in a bowl together soup, milk, 3/4 of cheese and 1/2 can of onion rings. Cook for 25 minutes.
Top with rest of cheese and onion rings. Stick back in oven until cheese is melted.
Melt butter.
Stir in 2 eggs and apple juice concentrate.
Add bananas.
Mix flour, salt, soda and wheat germ; add to banana mixture.
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
The dressing will look very thick, but it covers a whole salad.
The salad is best when served ice cold.
Croutons or baked pieces of pita bread are good with it.
Mix all ingredients together and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Mix all ingredients and serve.
Put all together.
Mix well.
Bake 1/2 hour at 350°.
Cream the sugar, oil, salt and cinnamon. Add eggs, one at a time.
Add the cooked carrots and nuts. Add dry ingredients.
Bake at 350°.
Cook sausage over medium heat until well browned; drain.
Stir in the onions and also brown.
When completed, open can of rolls and stretch the dough until thin, without splitting or tearing.
Mix first 6 ingredients together.
Make into thick patties and brown in skillet.
Combine mushroom soup and water.
Bake at 350° for 35 or 40 minutes.
Cook and stir onions and garlic in oil in 3-quart saucepan over medium heat until onions are tender.
Stir in water, lentils and salt.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 1 hour.
Stir in spinach, lemon peel and lemon juice.
Cover and simmer until spinach is tender, about 5 minutes.
In a bowl, combine water, sugar and yeast.
Set aside for about 5 minutes, or until bubbly; then add yogurt, margarine, egg, herbs and onion.
Set aside.
Make meat filling ahead of time by frying together ground beef, onion, salt and pepper and chili. Add water for sauce.
In electric skillet, combine ring bologna (chopped bite size), kidney beans (don't drain) and stewed tomatoes (don't drain). Boil rice.
Add to mixture. Add chili powder; salt to taste. Simmer on low about 20 minutes.
Mix this all together well and brush over chicken. Serve with rice or noodles.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix all ingredients together and shape into a ball. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Serve with assorted crackers.
Butter bread on one side and dice into 1/2-inch cubes.
Grate cheese.
In 2-quart buttered casserole, alternate layers of bread and cheese (4 layers).
Mix rest of ingredients.
Pour over bread and cheese.
Refrigerate overnight and bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Take an unbleached muslin bag, put some sweet fresh hay in bottom of the bag; add the ham and put hay firmly all around ham. Tie the bag and hang in dry place.
Ham treated in this manner will keep for years.
Mix together.
Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Mix first 6 ingredients together and spread on flour tortillas.
Roll tightly and chill.
Heat oven to 325°.
Butter and flour two 7 x 5-inch loaf pans. In medium bowl, sift flour, baking powder and salt; set aside. In large bowl, with electric mixer, beat butter until creamy.
Add sugar and orange peel; beat until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add sour cream and orange juice alternately with flour mixture.
Blend in fresh cranberries.
Pour into prepared pans and bake for 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean.
*Low-fat cream cheese and reduced fat mayo may be used, results are delicious.

Combine margarine and cream cheese in microwave oven until soft. Combine with spinach, artichokes, black pepper and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Stir well. Spoon into a lightly greased casserole dish. Sprinkle with bread crumbs. Bake at 325° for 30 minutes.
In saucepan, combine cider, spices and lemon juice. Cover and heat over medium-low heat for 30 minutes. Strain.
Garnish with lemon slices.
Brown hamburger and sausage; drain.
Add cheese to meat.
Add remaining ingredients.
Spread on party rye bread.
Place in 350° to 375° oven about 10 minutes, if not frozen.
May be frozen first and baked as needed.
Put chicken in bottom of oblong casserole dish.
Tear tortillas in pieces and place on top of chicken.
Melt butter in saucepan; add onion and cook until tender.
Add soup and tomatoes and let come to a boil.
Pour over chicken and top with cheese. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In bowl of electric mixer, beat eggs until light and lemony. Add flour, baking powder, cottage cheese, Jack cheese and melted butter.
Blend smooth, then stir in chilies.
Pour mixture into buttered 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes until top is browned and center appears firm.
Measure flour; mix with butter and powdered sugar until smooth.
Spread this with fingers in ungreased 8 x 8-inch pan. Bake for 25 minutes.

Mix liquids and butter; add potatoes and onions and cook until done. Mix cracker crumbs, flour and seasonings. Add to potato and onions mixture. Add red and green peppers after you have chopped and sauteed briefly in butter; mix well. Bring to a boil; add cream (or milk) and corn. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. This makes 2 or more quarts.
Drain salmon and remove bones, if any.
Mix all ingredients and form into patties.
Fry on both sides until golden brown.
Spread broken tortilla chips in bottom of casserole dish. Pour chili over chips.
Top with cheese, onion, olives and/or peppers.
Bake until warmed through.
Serve with sour cream and lettuce.
In a large skillet, heat oil.
Add chops, 3 at a time; brown well on both sides.
Remove and set aside.
Add green peppers and onions; saute for 3 minutes.
Remove and set aside.
Stir in flour; cook and stir for 1 minute.
Blend in onion soup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder and salt.
Bring to boiling point.
Return chops to skillet; spoon sauce over chops.
Cover and simmer until tender abut 1 hour.
Stir in tomatoes, sauteed green peppers and onions.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes longer.
Rub seasoned salt into roast.
Brown lightly.
Add water; cover and simmer until tender (2 to 2 1/2 hours).
Remove meat from juice to cool.
Measure 2 cups meat juice.
Add tomato sauce and beef stew mix.
Add brown sugar.
Simmer for 20 minutes. Shred meat and add to sauce.
Makes delicious sandwiches.
Serves 8 to 10.
Salt and pepper pot roast; brown on all sides in 1 tablespoon oil.
Mix the rest of the ingredients together and pour over roast.
Cover and bake at 300° for 3 hours.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Soak tomato slices in mixture of lime and water for 24 hours. Remove tomatoes from lime water and soak in clear water for 4 hours, changing water each hour.
Remove from water.
Mix sugar, vinegar and allspice (tied in gauze cloth loosely).
Put tomato slices and sugar mixture together and bring to boil.
Remove from heat and let stand 24 hours in solution.
Cook gently 1 hour, then seal in hot jars.
Heat oven to 400°.
Cut margarine into flour, sugar, baking powder and salt until mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Stir in 1 egg, the currants, orange rind and just enough half and half so dough leaves side of bowl.	Turn dough onto lightly floured surface and knead lightly ten times.
Roll 1/2-inch thick.
Scrub and cut up new potatoes, with skins on.
Cook until tender; drain well.
While potatoes are still hot, add Ranch dressing.
Put in serving dish.
Top with Cheddar cheese and bacon bits.
Serves 6 to 8 people.
Mix all ingredients.
The thinner the batter, the lighter the hush puppies.
Drop into hot grease and brown both sides.
Mix together and place in pie crust.
Freeze.
Cook pie shell as directed; set aside.
In skillet, brown ground beef.
Drain excess oil off.
Add onion, salt and pepper to taste.
Place in cooked pie shell.
Cover with American cheese. Place in oven at 150° until cheese has melted.
Heat margarine, milk and water to lukewarm.
Add sugar, salt and yeast.
Mix thoroughly.
Add flour until dough is no longer sticky.
Let stand until dough has doubled in bulk.
Press down; knead and roll into small balls.
Let the dough rise again and bake at 400°.
Layer broccoli and chicken in 9 x 13 x 2-inch dish.
Mix together other ingredients (soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and cheese).
Pour over chicken and broccoli.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Top with Pepperidge Farm mix and melted margarine.
Return to oven and brown.
Preheat oven to 350°; grease shallow 1 1/2-quart or 8-inch square baking dish.
Set aside.
Line a large cookie sheet with aluminum foil, dull side up. Spray with Pam.
Break crackers into small sections at the perforations.
Lay crackers close together (within 1/8 to 1/4-inch).
In a medium saucepan, bring the margarine, sugar and flavoring to a rolling boil, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Pour mixture over crackers.
Sprinkle with pecans.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in 350° oven.
Remove immediately and sprinkle with chocolate chips, if desired.
Cool on wire rack.
Break into sections; store in refrigerator.
Brown meatballs and add to sauce.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt margarine in casserole dish. Combine all ingredients in dish with melted margarine.
Bake, covered, for 1 hour at 350°.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
Use red wine glasses with a large bowl.
Heat water in glasses in microwave.
Make one drink a a time.
Place the Cointreau and sugar in the glass and swirl, then flame, caramelizing the sugar. Add coffee.
Add rest of liquor.
Top with whipped cream, sugar and chocolate jimmies.
Makes 1.
Turn off the lights when flaming; a great show and a great drink!
Mix baking mix and 1/2 cup water until soft dough forms.
Beat vigorously 20 strokes.
Gently smooth into ball on floured cloth. Knead 5 times.
Roll into 14 x 11-inch rectangle.
Place on lightly greased cookie sheet.
Pour oil 3/4 inch in deep frying pan.
Grate potatoes in wooden bowl.
Add salt, pepper, egg and cinnamon.
Mix all ingredients, except corn flakes and applesauce.
Add corn flake crumbs, a little at a time, until slightly firm.
Make sure oil is good and hot.
Spoon batter in oil.
Keep turning until golden brown.
Serve with applesauce and sprinkle with sugar.
Mix corn, Jiffy mix, eggs, butter, 1/2 sour cream and 1/2 grated cheese.
Pour into 2-quart casserole.
Spread top with remaining sour cream, then remaining cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 45 minutes.

recipes.t: Mary Lou Lange'S Spaghetti Sauce For 100
d: Brown and drain ground beef.
Combine all ingredients; simmer. Use with 15 pounds of spaghetti noodles, 10 loaves French bread, 3 bags salad and 2 quarts of salad dressing.
In medium saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar, salt and spice. Bring to a boil.
Put cucumbers, onions and peppers in alternate layers in 1-quart jars.
Pour boiling liquid over all.
Seal and refrigerate.
Mix first 6 ingredients, blending until smooth.
Add remaining ingredients.
Stir just until mixed.
Put into 12 muffin tins sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 17 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, except pork loin, in a jar and shake well, making sure all is well blended.
Pour over pork loin and cover.
Refrigerate overnight.
Turn pork several times.
Place meat, fat side up, on rack in a greased shallow roasting pan; reserve marinade.
Roast in a 325° oven for about 3 hours.
Baste pork with marinade several times while roasting.
Marinade forms very dark crust on roast.
This is one of my family's favorites.
Melt butter; add sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Beat well with spoon.
Add coconut, then buttermilk. Pour into 2 unbaked pie crusts.
Bake at 350° for about 1 1/2 hours or until golden brown.
Mix all ingredients (except crust).
Cook until thick.
Pour over crust.
Beat 4 egg whites, stiff.
Add 8 teaspoons sugar, two at a time.
Spread over filling.
Bake until egg whites are brown.
Cut stem ends off tomatoes and hollow out, leaving 1/4 to 1/2-inch thick shells.
Discard seeds.
Chop tomato pulp and tops. Set aside.

Halve, seed, peel and cut the avocado into chunks. Combine the chunks, cottage cheese, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper sauce in blender or food processor until mixture is smooth. Stir in chopped tomato.
Makes 16 (2 tablespoon) servings of dip.
Melt over hot water the milk, chocolate chips and oleo.
When melted, add marshmallows and peanuts.
Mix together.
Press in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill.
Prepare jello and let stand until it starts to thicken. Grind and dice rest of the ingredients.
Add sugar to ground cranberries, oranges, apples and celery (finely chopped).
Add all ingredients to jello and chill.
In skillet, brown the meat and onion; drain fat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Place in a greased 2-quart casserole.
Top with potatoes.
Combine soup and milk; pour over potatoes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Yields 2 to 3 servings.

Melt butter, then add onion and bell pepper. Cook on medium heat for 20 minutes. Add Ro-Tel tomatoes and cream of mushroom soup. Bring to a boil. Lower fire to medium heat and let cook for 20 minutes. Add crawfish and cook for 15 minutes or until crawfish is tender. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In a large mixing bowl, cream the shortening, butter and sugar.
Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each one. Add the flour, alternating with the 7-Up.
Add the flavorings and bake in a greased tube pan for 1 hour and 20 minutes at 350°.
Combine all ingredients except oil.
Divide into 4 portions forming each into a patty.
Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil over high heat, reduce heat to medium and add patties.
Cook, turning once, until browned, about 3 minutes on each side.
Serve on warmed platter with a seafood sauce.
Yield: 2 servings of 2 patties each.
Combine all ingredients except the pecans and cook at a low temperature until the sugar is dissolved.
Then boil until the soft ball stage is reached.
Add pecans.
Stir until it just begins to harden.
This candy hardens very quickly once it has started to thicken in the pan.
Quickly drop by spoonfuls into 2-inch patties on wax paper.
Let stand until firm.
Cook broccoli 4 minutes.
Drain.
Place in buttered casserole. Place grated cheese on broccoli.
Add milk and cream of mushroom soup.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Place onion rings on top and bake 10 minutes more.
Serves 8.
