Remove all visible fat.
Place roast in slow cooker.
Combine soy sauce, bouillon and spices.
Pour over roast, add water to almost cover roast.
Cover and cook over low heat for 10 to 12 hours or until meat is tender.
Remove meat from broth, reserve broth, shred meat with fork and serve on hard rolls or French bread.
Dip into broth.
In 4-quart saucepan over medium heat, cook beef, onion and garlic until beef is no longer pink, stirring occasionally to break up meat.
Drain.
Add beans, salsa, chili powder and oregano.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve topped with cheese.
*I use Jif brand peanut butter.
If unavailable, use another brand, but add several tablespoons water to mixture.
Peel orange.
Remove seed and skin.
Combine sugar, shortening, orange, orange juice, eggs, soda, salt and flour in a large mixing bowl.
Mix well.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls on and ungreased baking sheet.
Bake at 350 degrees until lightly brown. Remove from oven and cool slightly.
Transfer cookies to rack to cool completely.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spread pineapple in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Place pie filling on top of pineapple.
Sprinkle dry cake mix over; sprinkle nuts over the cake mix.
Cut up oleo over all.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Saute first three ingredients in saucepan.
Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer one hour.
Mix all ingredients together and place in pie crusts.
Freezer several hours until firm.
Color half of frosting red and half yellow.
Pile coconut and green food coloring in sandwich bag and work coloring in for lettuce.
Frost bottom half of 1/2 vanilla wafer with yellow and half red.
Sandwich wafers with grasshopper cookie in between and coconut for lettuce. Boil water (1/2 cup water and 1 tablespoon sugar).
Cool.
Brush on top of top wafer.
Sprinkle with sesame seed.
Spray a 9 x 13 casserole dish with pam spray and line dish with crescent rolls.
Layer on top of rolls, sausage then cheese. Mix eggs and milk and pour over cheese.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Bake in preheated oven at 350 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes.
Divide nuts and morsels in 2 unbaked pie shells.
Over this pour mixture of margarine, eggs, sugar, syrup and vanilla.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes; may take less time.
Combine 2 cups raisins, 3 cups boiling water and 2/3 cup sugar and boil 10 minutes.
Add cornstarch, mixed in a little water, 1 egg, nutmeg and butter.
Cook until mixture thickens.
Put into unbaked pie shell and add top crust.
Bake at 425° for 10 minutes, then reduce heat to 400° and continue baking until crust is brown.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, preserves and cinnamon. Combine soda and buttermilk; add to mixture, then add flour.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cook carrots and yams until tender.
Drain.
Mix with other ingredients.
Layer in a baking dish with brown sugar between layers.
Add water.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until apples are tender.
Remove cover and continue baking until top is golden brown.
Serves 8 to 10.
Combine eggs, sugar, peanut butter and vanilla.
Blend well. Add dry ingredients and mix only until mixture is smooth.
Spread into greased large baking dish.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Bake at 350° for 23 minutes.
On a large microwave-safe plate, arrange 8 to 10 tortilla chips or as many as will fit in one layer.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon salsa in center of each chip.
Top with a few pieces of tomatoes and sprinkle with cheese.
Repeat until all tortilla chips are topped, making 4 plates in all.
Microwave each plate on High for 1 minute or until cheese is melted.
Remove plate carefully as it may be hot.
Top each nacho with about 1 tablespoon sour cream.
Serve immediately.

recipes.t: Crock-Pot Meal To Serve Over Noodles
d: Cut meat in pieces.
Mix other ingredients.
Pour over meat. Bake 1 1/2 hours at 350°.
Serve over noodles.
Can cook in crock-pot on low for 8 to 10 hours.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Prepare rice according to package directions.
Spread rice in a buttered, shallow 1- 1/2 quart baking dish.
Arrange asparagus over rice.
Top with chicken.
Blend soup, sour cream, milk, lemon juice and 1/2 cup of cheese.
Add salt and pepper.
Spread over chicken.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Combine dry mustard with vinegar in glass bowl (do not use aluminum).
Mix well and let stand for about 1 hour.
Mix sugar and flour together.
Combine all ingredients in double boiler or nonstick pan and cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes or desired thickness.
Makes about 2 cups.
Keeps in refrigerator for months.
Great to make the night before.
Blend cream cheese on low of electric mixer.
When well blended add flour, salt, cocoa and half of sugar.
Separate egg whites and yolks.
On low speed, blend whipping cream, egg yolks and kahlua. Blend well; mix cream cheese mixture.
On high speed in another bowl beat egg whites with remaining sugar until stiff.
Fold in cheese mixture.
Cover bottom of pan with aluminum foil.
Grease sides of pan.
Make crust of graham cracker and margarine.
Pat 1/2-inch thick into bottom of pan.
Spoon in cheese mixture into crust.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours.
Pare and cut potatoes in strips.
Grease a cookie sheet and place potatoes on the sheet, arranging them so they do not touch. Brush with melted butter. Sprinkle salt, paprika and sesame seed over the top. Bake for 1 hour at 350°.
Turn, if you wish. Serves 6.
In small bowl, combine refried beans and chilies; spread on serving plate.
Combine sour cream and taco seasoning; spoon bean mixture, spreading evenly.
In another bowl, mash avocados; stir in lime juice and salt.
Spoon evenly over sour cream mixture. Cover; chill 3 hours.
Mix dry ingredients.
Add buttermilk, Crisco, jam and eggs; mix well.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes, or in 2 (9-inch) pans for 15 to 20 minutes.
Blend wet ingredients.
Fold in dry ingredients. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Brown ground meat and drain off excess grease.
Brown bacon and onions.
Combine all ingredients in crock-pot and cook slowly 3 to 4 hours.
*Important to use escarole as it will not wilt.
Cream sugar and cheese together; add vanilla and milk. Dissolve gelatine in boiling water; add cold water.
Set aside. Let cool but not set.
To the cream cheese mixture add Cool Whip, pineapple and nuts.
When gelatine is cool, add to mixture.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch dish and refrigerate.
Wash and stem grapes.
Put in glass bowl.
Top with sour cream and sprinkle with sugar.
Chill for several hours before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 1-quart baking dish.
Place 1/2 of cheese in baking dish and cover with chilies. Pour eggs over cheese and chilies. Add the stewed tomatoes.
Top with remaining cheese. Bake for 30 minutes or until cheese is bubbly and slightly brown.
Mix all ingredients with milk until stiff enough to drop into hot oil or grease. Fry until golden brown.
Combine all ingredients, mixing well.
Let fish marinate in sauce 30 minutes to 2 hours or longer.
Broil fish, basting with marinade.
Makes 2 1/2 cups sauce.
Brown pork chops on stove top.
Place a layer in deep baking dish, top with sliced onion rings and top that with tomato soup. Repeat until dish is full, usually 4 to 5 layers.
Bake uncovered at 475° until mixture bubbles, then reduce heat to 350° and bake 1 hour, covered.
Serve with baked potatoes; use juices for topping.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease cookie sheet lightly.
Sift flour, baking soda and baking powder.
Work margarine and peanut butter with spoon until creamy; gradually add brown sugar substitute, continue working until light.
Add regular sugar substitute and egg; beat well.
Mix in dry ingredients thoroughly. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto lightly greased heavy-duty aluminum foil; flatten with tines of fork.
Bake about 8 to 10 minutes.
Combine soup, oil, vinegar, sugar, mustard and pepper.
Pour over hot carrots.
Add chopped celery, onion and green pepper. Keeps up to 3 weeks in refrigerator.
Place broccoli in casserole.
Spread tuna over the top.
Add one-half can of the mushroom soup, the stuffing mix and then the rest of the soup.
Top with Cheddar cheese and bake in a 350° oven for one hour.
Serves four.

Cook chicken; let cool. Take off the bone. Cook noodles in broth of chicken. Saut bell pepper in butter. Add enough flour and milk to make a white sauce. It should be thick but not lumpy. Melt cheese in this mixture while it is hot. Then add cream of mushroom soup. Combine all ingredients and place in a large casserole dish. Top with corn flake crumbs. Bake at 350° until bubbly hot.
Cook rice, coffee and butter in a double boiler for about 25 minutes.
Combine all ingredients, except cinnamon; pour into a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Set casserole in pan of warm water.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Turn off heat; let stand in oven for 30 minutes.
Serve warm with whipped cream.
Use melon baller. Scoop flesh from cantaloupe and honeydew into balls and set aside.
In a large glass bowl, combine sugar, lime juice, lemon juice, orange liqueur and lime zest.

Stir well to dissolve sugar. Add cantaloupe balls, honeydew balls, strawberries and grapes. Toss gently. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour to blend flavors, stirring once or twice.
Spoon fruit mixture into serving bowls or hollowed out melon halves. Serve immediately.
Beat eggs; add oil and carrots.
Sift cake mix, pudding and cinnamon.
Mix all together.
Bake in 3 round cake layers at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut wings at all joints. Throw away wing tips. Place wings on paper towels to absorb all water.
Soak rice in hot water for 1/2 hour; drain well.
Spread in big shallow pan to dry a little, about 1 hour.
Cook bacon until crisp; crumble and set aside.
Add rice to drippings and cook until rice is lightly browned.
Add crumbled bacon, beef broth, tomato sauce, green pepper, onion, garlic and cumin seed.
Cover; cook over low heat, stirring now and then, until rice is done and liquid absorbed, about 30 minutes (add extra water if needed).
Brown ground meat in large frying pan, breaking it up as it cooks.
Drain fat.
Add onion and bell pepper.
Saute with meat until tender.
Add tomato juice, salt, pepper and garlic powder. Add salsa in amount necessary to make spicy for your taste.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Add rice and olives.
Stir, cover and remove from heat.
Let stand, covered, at least five minutes before serving.
Make dough.
Spread on pizza pan.

Cover with onions, which have been sliced and fried in oil, and garlic, pepper and salt. Lay on top of dough slices of fresh tomatoes with a few pitted ripe olives and a few filleted anchovies (washed of salt).
Add several strips of pimentos.
Bake in hot (400°) oven for 1/2 hour.
Mix all ingredients together in saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir often to mix cheese.
Serve immediately.
Delicious!
Tear bread into small bite-size pieces.
Add and mix all ingredients together.
Pour into buttered baking dish.
Bake about 30 minutes or until done at 350°.
Can be served hot or cold. Fresh fruit garnish makes it more tempting.
In a large mixing bowl, with an electric mixer, blend ingredients at high speed for 2 minutes.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch cake pans and bake in preheated oven at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool and frost with Caramel or 7 Minute Icing.
You will need 1 pan, size 12 3/4 x 9 x 2-inches (or approximately).
Grease mold with mayonnaise.
Heat tomato soup and cream cheese until softened.
Add mayonnaise while still warm, then add rest of ingredients.
Gelatine is last to be added.
Refrigerate overnight.
Remove from mold when ready to use.
Serve with crackers.
Soften gelatin in cold water.
Wash and cap strawberries.
Add sweetener.
Press 1 1/2 cups strawberries through strainer.
Add food coloring.
If desired, add lemon juice and bring to boil. Remove from heat and soften gelatin, stirring to dissolve. Chill until mixture begins to thicken.
Fold in remaining whole strawberries.
Spoon in cooled pie shell.
Refrigerate until set. Garnish with whipped cream.
Put first 4 ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix well with pastry blender, fork or mixer.
Mix until mixture is like small peas.
In small bowl, beat together vinegar, egg & water.
Combine with the flour mixture until it is blended well.
Divide into 5 portions and shape into flat patties.
Wrap well in plastic or foil. Refrigerate or freeze.
Will keep in refrigerator a week or months in freezer.
Mix mayonnaise, milk, seasoned salt and pepper.
Mix well; set aside.
Mix cauliflower, broken up in small pieces, onion, peas and celery in a bowl.
Add mayonnaise mixture and mix well.
Set in refrigerator and chill.
Pour butter over topping ingredients and crumble over potato mixture.
Bake 35 minutes in 350° oven.
Brown hamburger and onion.
Add rest of ingredients.
Cover with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Mix all of the ingredients and bake 15 minutes at 350°.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Serve with goldfish crackers.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Combine rest of ingredients and fold in macaroni.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes in a 2 1/2-quart baking dish.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all of the dry ingredients in a bowl.
Make a well in the center.
Add eggs and oil.
Stir well until moistened.
Stir in strawberries and pecans.
Pour batter into 2 lightly greased loaf pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Mix all ingredients together; pour over steak.
Marinate overnight or as long as you wish.
We marinate it for up to 2 days.
Cook and drain squash.
Melt oleo in casserole dish.
Stir in Stove Top cornbread stuffing.
Set aside 1 cup of stuffing and oleo.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix sugar, flour, eggs, soda and pineapple (and juice) with mixer on low speed.
Then add nuts. Pour into a 9 x 12 inch greased pan and bake for 40 minutes.
Stir together brown sugar, cream cheese and margarine with spoon.
Put frosting on cake while cake is still hot.
Sprinkle with nuts.
Put the ingredients in the order shown in crock-pot.
Turn on high until it starts to boil, then turn to low for 4 or 5 hours. Or, leave on low all day.
Brown ground beef, onion, salt and pepper in skillet.
Drain off grease and put in a slow cooker.
Then add cheese, tomato sauce and chiles.
Mix until cheese is melted.
Serve warm.
Dip in your favorite chips.
Flatten chicken breasts with palm of hand.
Combine flour, salt and pepper and dust breasts on both sides.
Saute full side down in butter and oil for 5 minutes, shaking the pan to prevent sticking.
Turn the chicken and add champagne.
Cook for about 15 minutes until chicken is done and champagne is reduced by half. Remove to heated platter and keep warm.
Add the cream to the pan juices and cook until thickened.
Add sauteed mushrooms and pour sauce over the chicken.
Serves 6.
Mix first 2 ingredients together and use to dust a greased 10-inch tube pan.
Mix butter and other flavoring with milk in a large mixing bowl.
Add remaining ingredients and beat for 20 minutes.
Pour batter into pan and place in a cold oven.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Heat oil in wok or skillet over high heat.
Add garlic and cook a few seconds, then add frozen vegetables and stir frequently until warmed through.
Cut chicken into 1/2 x 2-inch strips.
When vegetables are barely cooked, add chicken and stir until it becomes opaque.
Stir in teriyaki sauce and serve over hot rice.
Combine
coconut,
apricots
and
milk	in
large bowl. Cover. Refrigerate
at least 4 hours or overnight.
Roll into balls using
scant tablespoon.
Place on wax paper and refrigerate. Melt almond
bark and dip balls using a fork and swirl the top with a toothpick.
Combine all ingredients in a large iron skillet; cover and cook on medium heat until vegetables are almost done.
Remove lid; reduce heat and cook until thick.
*Try shoulder and rib chops, approximately 2 1/2 pounds.
Mix all ingredients together.
Marinate in refrigerator for 2 days.
Fry in butter or margarine the green pepper, pimentos and onion.
Add potatoes, ham, salt and paprika.
Continue frying until browned.
Cut artichoke hearts in half.
Blend artichokes with eggs, crab meat or pepperoni, salt, pepper and cheeses. Pour into pie crust.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until set. Serve warm or cold.
Heat oven to 350°.
Arrange sweet potatoes in ungreased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish.
Season with salt. Spoon caramel topping on potatoes. Bake, uncovered, 25 to 30 minutes, basting occasionally with caramel topping in pan.
Makes 4 servings.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in a 13 x 9 x 1 3/4-inch baking pan.
Pare potatoes; roll in butter to coat well.
Sprinkle with seasoned salt.
Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour.
Remove pan from oven; turn potatoes.
Add chicken broth.
Bake 1 hour longer, turning several times.
Makes 8 servings.
Beat together margarine, sugar and eggs. Add pineapple and coconut. Mix and pour into pie shells. Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Put apple pie filling on bottom of 8-inch square cake pan. Mix remaining ingredients.
Spread mixture over top of pie filling. Sprinkle lightly with cinnamon.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
In a large skillet cook and stir brown sugar, margarine or butter and vinegar over medium heat for 1 or 2 minutes.
Add onions.
Cook, uncovered, over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes or until onions are glazed and tender, stirring often.
Set aside.
Cook sausage until pink is gone.
Add seasonings.
Spread on rye bread and bake at 350° for 10 to 15 minutes.

Add vanilla pudding to milk in bowl. Beat at lowest speed just until blended, about 30 seconds. Blend in pumpkin, spice and 2 cups Cool Whip. Pour into pie shell. Chill until set, at least 4 hours. Garnish with remaining Cool Whip and pecan halves. Enjoy.
Arrange apple slices in an 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Mix together the Equal, flour and cinnamon.
Cut in margarine until well blended.
Sprinkle flour mixture over apples.
Sprinkle lemon juice over all, then pat until firm on top.
Microwave on High, uncovered, 15 minutes.
Turn dish every 5 minutes.
Let stand 15 minutes.
Serves 16.
Contains 123 calories per serving.
In a large kettle, place kielbasa and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, lower heat and simmer for about 2 1/2 hours.
While kielbasa is cooking, in a large skillet, saute onions until clear; add sauerkraut, applesauce*, salt, pepper and tomato sauce.
Simmer for about 20 minutes.
When kielbasa is done, cut into 2-inch pieces and add to sauerkraut.
Also, add about 1 cup of water that kielbasa was cooked in.
Continue for another 15 minutes.
Serve with boiled potatoes (quartered) and bakery fresh pumpernickel bread.
Cook spinach; drain well.
Fold sour cream, soup mix, water chestnuts and spices into spinach.
Bake for 30 minutes, uncovered, at 325°.
Top with grated cheese for the last 10 minutes of baking.
Serves 6.
Cut margarine into mix making sure its mixed thoroughly. Place pie filling in 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle cake mix over pie filling.
Bake at 350° until golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Serve hot or cold.
Wash and cook apricots in water as directed on package.
Put the cooked apricots through a food mill, or puree them, about 3/4 cup at a time in a blender (or use a food processor).
Add sugar and salt.
Stir and cook 4 to 5 minutes over moderate heat.
Add Cognac or apricot brandy to taste.
Serve over puddings, or plain cake.
Makes approximately 1 1/2 cups sauce.
Boil cream until it is reduced to 2 tablespoons.
Remove from heat; stir in Grand Marnier and chocolate.
Return to low heat to melt chocolate.
Whisk in butter.
When mixture is smooth, pour into bowl; refrigerate 1 hour.
When mixture is firm, shape into 1-inch balls.
Roll balls in cocoa.
Store truffles, covered, in refrigerator.
Let truffles stand at room temperature 1 hour before serving.
Combine all ingredients and bake in 9-inch unbaked pie shell at 325° for 45 minutes.
Have ribs sliced at joints.
Rub split garlic cloves into meat.
Baste with sauce and broil until done.

recipes.t: Medallions Of Pork With Riesling Sauce
d: Season pork with salt and pepper.
Coat in the flour; shake off excess.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic and saute until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Transfer to bowl.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter in same skillet over medium-high heat.
Add pork and saute about 4 minutes per side.
Transfer pork to plate. Add onion mixture, Riesling, raisins, vinegar, green peppercorns and herbs to same skillet and boil until sauce thickens, about 4 minutes.
Add pork to skillet to heat through.
Divide pork among plates.
Add 1/4 cup butter to sauce in skillet and whisk just until melted.
Mix in pine nuts.
Spoon sauce over pork.
To the sour cream, add the soda, then add sugar and eggs. Beat well.
Sift 1 cup flour, salt and baking powder.
Add sweet milk and extract.
Beat well and then add enough flour to make a soft dough that can be handled.
Roll and cut, fry in deep fat and roll in powdered sugar to which a little cinnamon has been added.
Brown pork.
Add water.
Cover, simmer until tender.
Drain pineapple.
Reserve liquid.
Combine sugar and cornstarch.
Add pineapple syrup, vinegar, soy sauce and salt.
Add to pork.
Cook and stir until thick.
Add pineapple, green pepper and onion. Cook 2 or 3 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Combine grated apples with sugar in heavy pan.
Slowly bring to boil.
Soften gelatin in applesauce.
Add to cooked apple mix. Bring to full boil for 15 minutes.
Stir constantly.
Remove from heat.
Add nuts and vanilla.
Beat eggs and sugar together until fluffy.
Then add the remainder of the ingredients, lastly the pecans.
Pour in unbaked 9-inch pie shell.
Bake for 10 minutes at 450°; 35 minutes at 350°.
Grease large casserole dish.
Slice eggplant thin.
Do same to onion.
Alternate eggplant, tomato sauce and cheese in layers until all ingredients are gone.
Bake in 350° oven for about 45 minutes.
Recipe will make a large casserole.
May be cut in half.
Use 1 can soup and 16 oz. sour cream or 2 cans soup and 8 oz. sour cream or 2 cans soup and 16 oz. sour cream, depending on how much you want to make.
Place all ingredients in saucepan.
Simmer for 1 hour.
Serve (use cocktail picks).
Coat pork chops with mixture of paprika, salt, pepper, ginger and flour.
Brown in lard in skillet.
Add pineapple juice and vinegar.
Sprinkle with brown sugar.
Simmer for 40 minutes. Yield: 6 servings.
Place sugars, water and butter in a pan over high heat.
Boil for 2 minutes or to soft ball stage.
Remove from heat and add pecans and vanilla.
Beat until mixture becomes creamy and begins to sugar on sides of pan, then drop by spoon onto waxed paper to cool.
Lightly grease a 7 inch ring mold.
Sprinkle cornflakes in bottom of mold.
Mix sausage, onion, bread crumbs, parsley and egg.
Pat meat mixture into mold.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 15 minutes.
Drain and bake another 15 minutes or until done. Invert mold onto heated platter, garnish with fresh parsley.
Fill center with scrambled eggs if desired.
Sausage ring may be refrigerated or frozen before baking.
Thaw and heat as directed.
In large saucepan, warm milk.
When milk is warm, add salt, yeast and 1 1/2 cups flour.
Stir until yeast is melted.
Put aside and let rise for 1 hour.
When 1 hour is up, add the eggs, sugar, melted butter, lemon and orange peels.
Stir in well with hand, not mixer.
When everything is mixed in, begin adding flour slowly until it makes a soft nonsticky dough.
Knead well.
Put aside to rise 3 to 4 hours.
When well risen, knead again.
Shape into braids or loaves.
Wash and dry chicken; crush garlic, ginger, pepper and salt. Combine with cinnamon, turmeric, cloves, vinegar and butter.
Rub this mixture all over chicken and allow to stand for 30 minutes. Place chicken in roasting tray together with margarine and cook in moderately hot oven for 1 1/2 hours, basting occasionally.
About 20 minutes before serving, preheat broiler.
Blend hash, sour cream or yogurt, relish and horseradish. Set aside.
Place halved buns, cut side up, on cookie sheet.
Spread each half with some mustard.
Spread one side of each bun with hash mixture.
On the other side, lay a tomato slice, topped with a slice of cheese. Broil until cheese is bubbly, then serve at once.
Serve with French green beans, salad, pears and cookies.
Put peaches and butter in 2-quart baking dish. Mix remaining ingredients in blender on high for 15 to 20 seconds. Pour over peaches and butter.
Bake at 350° until golden brown.
Using a meat grinder, grind up eggs, pickles and bologna.
Add sugar and Miracle Whip; mix well.
Store in refrigerator until well chilled.
Spread on bread and enjoy!
Combine all ingredients, except pasta.
Simmer for 2 hours. Add pasta until heated through.
Serve hot with cornbread and salad.
Can add any vegetables that you like.
Peel and pit avocado.
Mash thoroughly.
Stir in lime juice, green chiles, cumin, garlic salt and Italian dressing.
Mix with wire whisk until smooth.
Stir in additional Italian dressing as needed to make the right consistency.
Makes about 1 1/2 cups dressing.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add syrup and salt; beat well.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
Add pecans.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes.
Saute quickly in a pan (preferably on gas, high heat), stirring often.
In medium bowl, beat cream cheese until light and fluffy.
Add condensed milk.
Blend thoroughly.
Stir in lemon juice and vanilla.
Pour into crust.
Chill 2 to 3 hours.
Top with chilled cherry pie filling before serving.
Place first 5 ingredients in large pot and bring to boil. Simmer until vegetables are tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, brown hamburger and drain fat.
When vegetables are tender, add cooked hamburger and undrained kidney beans.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes and add chili powder to taste (depends on how hot you like it).
Preheat oven to 350°.
Sift flour, sugar, salt, soda and cinnamon.
Add other ingredients in large bowl and stir thoroughly.
Pour mixture into 9 x 13-inch greased and floured (or Pam sprayed) glass Pyrex.
Can also put into Bundt pan that has been Pam sprayed.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Test by toothpick. Allow cake to cool before icing.
You will need an 11 x 13-inch baking sheet.
Cream butter.
Gradually add sugar; cream thoroughly.
Add eggs and cocoa, alternately.
Add flour, sour milk and vanilla. Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
In a large pan, crumble corn bread and top with beans, then tomatoes, peppers, onions and bacon.
Set aside.
Clean carrots well.
Slice and cook.
Combine remaining ingredients and cook until thick.
Pour over cooked carrots. Cover and let stand a few minutes before serving.

Cut chicken wings into 3 sections; discard wing tip section. In a large, resealable plastic bag or shallow glass container, combine remaining ingredients. Reserve 1 cup for basting and refrigerate. Add chicken to the remaining marinade and turn to coat. Seal bag or cover container; refrigerate for 4 hours, turning occasionally.
Drain and discard marinade.

Boil water and steep tea 5 minutes. Add sugar, lemon juice, vanilla and almond extract to tea. Add the water and stir well. Freeze. Remove from freezer in time to allow it to become slushy at serving time.
Cook or steam zucchini in boiling salted water, until just tender.
Drain.
In microwave casserole dish (1-quart size), melt 4 tablespoons of butter or margarine.
Add carrot and onion and cook until tender.
Stir in 2 1/4 cups stuffing cubes, soup and carrot/onion.
Mix into zucchini dish, stirring gently.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter or margarine.
Add remaining 1 1/4 cups stuffing cubes to butter and toss gently.
Sprinkle cubes on casserole.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 40 minutes, uncovered. Makes 6 to 10 servings.
In a bowl, mix cracker crumbs, garlic powder and Season-All. In separate bowl, beat egg and water with a fork.
Cook
onion and sausage balls in skillet until onion is tender and sausage is lightly browned.
Drain off excess fat. Add
next 4 ingredients.
Heat to boiling, cover, reduce heat and
simmer 20
minutes.
Add
peas
and pimientos, cover and simmer 5 to 10 minutes longer.
Serves 4 to 6.
Mix Jell-O and cream cheese with boiling water until dissolved.
Smooth with an electric mixer.
Add in remaining ingredients and stir with a spoon.
Add Ragu sauce to cooked beef.
In greased 13 x 9-inch pan, layer 3 noodles, beef sauce, cottage cheese and Mozzarella cheese. Make 4 layers.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.

recipes.t: Spaghetti With Tomatoes And Goat Cheese
d: Cut tomatoes into chunks; add olive oil, garlic, hot pepper flakes, capers and salt to taste. Stir to blend. Cook pasta in salted water until al dente. Tear basil leaves into small pieces. Drain pasta and toss with goat cheese in a large bowl. Transfer into saucepan and saute 2 minutes on medium-high until garlic is released. Add basil and tomatoes. Toss and serve.
Brown meat; drain.
Mix all other ingredients; pour in unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Can use ham, shrimp or bacon in place of hamburger meat.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Cool slightly.
Stir in cranberry sauce, drained pineapple, celery and nuts.
Pour into mold or bowl, which has been rinsed out with cold water first. Chill in refrigerator until firm, overnight.
Remove from mold or brown and put on a chilled plate.
Put a dab of mayonnaise on top.
Tear cakes into pieces and place in oblong dish.
Mix cream cheese and condensed milk together until smooth.
Dribble almost all of this over cake.
Mix strawberries with remaining mixture and dribble over cake.
If wanted, sprinkle pecans over this. Refrigerate for about 4 hours.
Top with Cool Whip and pecans. Refrigerate until serving.
Mix together the first 7 ingredients for vinaigrette.
Set aside.
Have cheese and butter at room temperature.
Mix together and blend well.
Add other ingredients and blend well.
Run through cookie press.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 375°
for about 12 minutes.
Brown first 3 ingredients together in skillet; drain.
Add next 6 ingredients to beef mixture.
Simmer 45 minutes.
Top with cheese.
Boil sugar and milk 3 minutes.
Add peanut butter and marshmallow.
Mix thoroughly.
Put into 8 x 8-inch pan until set.
Put the oil in a large skillet.
Turn the heat to medium.
Add chicken.
Stir.
Cover the skillet.
Cook about 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini, green peppers, onion and celery to the skillet.
Stir gently until the vegetables are coated with oil.
Cook until the chicken and vegetables are hot.
Put the lid on the skillet.
Turn the heat to low.
Cook about 5 minutes.
Cook until the zucchini is tender and firm.
If the mixture gets dry, add a little water.
If there is liquid in the skillet, cook with the lid off.
Add black and red pepper.
Stir gently.
Cut cheese and place on top, if desired.
Cream butter or oleo and sugar until fluffy.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Drop on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Let set 5 minutes, then dust with powdered sugar, about 2/3 cup.
Mix cake mix, eggs, salt, orange extract and applesauce. Next, mix fruit with flour. Add dry ingredients with batter.
Bake at 275° for 2 hours and 45 minutes or until done.
Cover and store 1 month before eating.
Mix ham, milk, corn and soup in 3 qt. saucepan. Heat to boiling, stirring occasionally; reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sprinkle with onions.
Bring sugar, milk and margarine to a boil.
Boil 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add white chocolate morsels and marshmallow cream.
Mix well.
Remove 1 to 1 1/2 cups of
mixture and set aside.
To remainder of mix, add flavorings and food coloring. Mix well and pour into 9 x 13 buttered pan.
Drop white chocolate by spoonfuls on top of the orange.
Swirl through with a knife. Chill and cut with knife.
Combine first four ingredients.
Add water until desired consistency.
Season with garlic and black pepper to taste. Simmer until heated through and well blended.
Doubles well.
Combine above ingredients.
Bake in small tube pan for 1 hour at 350 degrees.
Stew chicken; bone and cut into small pieces.
Cook macaroni, cheese, pimentos, peas and mushrooms.
Melt butter in saucepan and add flour and 2 cups of chicken broth.
Cook until thick and add to chicken mixture.
Mix thoroughly and place in buttered baking dish.
Cover with bread crumbs.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
The last 10 minutes, add grated cheese and cook until melted and bubbly.
Cook broccoli in salted water until tender; drain.
Cook chicken breasts and cut into bite sizes.
Arrange broccoli in greased baking dish, 9 x 11-inch.
Place cooked chicken on top. Sprinkle cheese on top.
Combine bread crumbs and melted butter; sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Melt chocolate and butter in saucepan over very low heat, stirring constantly.
Cool slightly.
Beat eggs, sugar and vanilla in a large mixing bowl on high speed for 10 minutes.
Add flour, beating just to blend.
Stir in walnuts.
Spread in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 375° for 35 minutes.
(Do not overbake.) Cool in pan; then cut into squares.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix mushroom soup and milk; reserve 1/2 cup of mixture.
Mix remaining soup mixture, the rice, mushrooms (with liquid) and half the onion soup mix.
Pour into an ungreased 11 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Place chicken breasts on top.
Pour reserved soup mixture over chicken breasts; sprinkle with remaining onion soup mix.
Cover with foil; bake 1 hour. Uncover; bake 15 minutes longer.
(Can use whole chicken, cut up.)
Mix all ingredients well. Chill.
Place cubed venison in a large pot with plenty of water and let it boil while preparing vegetables.
Add vegetables, salt and pepper.
Cook until meat is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Add 2 tablespoons of browned flour and 1/2 cup of water; stir until thickened.
Mix all ingredients; pour into pie shells. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Dice up the potatoes and the onions.
Cook in a quart of water until done.
Then add 1/2 gallon of milk, then the parsley flakes and Cheez Whiz.
Salt and pepper to taste.
You may add leftover mashed potatoes if you have them.
Stir well for about 15 minutes.
Melt butter; saute garlic and green peppers.
Slowly add flour.
Add milk, one cup at a time.
Slice Velveeta and add, stirring until it melts.
Add chicken broth, broccoli and carrots. Simmer.
Do not boil.
Salt and pepper to taste.
Place bacon
in
9-inch
pie plate.
Cover loosely with microwavesafe paper towel.	Cook on High 3 minutes.
Drain off fat, reserving
tablespoon in small custard cup; set aside. Stir pepper and mushrooms into bacon; cover and cook on High 2 minutes.
Combine chocolate chips, margarine or butter and corn syrup in medium size saucepan (stir over low heat until melted and smooth). Remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla and sugar.
Add Rice Krispies, mixing lightly until well coated.
Spread in 9 x 13-inch pan. Chill until firm.
Cut into squares.
Store in refrigerator.
Line bottom of dish with crumbled crackers.
Saute onions in butter until transparent.
Pour over crackers.
Mix egg, milk and cheese; pour over onions.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook onion in bacon drippings until tender.
Add all of the other ingredients; put into casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Pour evaporated milk into large metal bowl and place in freezer until ice crystals form along edge of bowl, minimum of 30 minutes.
Chill electric mixer beaters at the same time.
Remove bowl and beaters from freezer.
In large skillet, over medium-high heat, cook and stir steak, mushrooms and onion in margarine until steak is browned and vegetables are tender.
Reduce heat to medium. Add flour; cook and stir 1 minute. Add water and bouillon; cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.
Stir in sour cream; heat through (do not boil). Serve over noodles.
Combine all ingredients except crackers and mix well.
Pour over crackers and make sure all are coated.
Place in sheet pan and cook in warm oven 20 to 30 minutes.
Store in airtight container and enjoy.
Roll bread out to 10 x 15-inch.
Mix butter, seasoned salt, parsley flakes and oregano.
Spread some on bread.
Cover surface with 3 1/2 ounce package sliced pepperoni.
Add cheese.
Roll up like jelly roll and spread some butter on top.
Bake on cookie sheet at 350° for 30 minutes.
Brush on remaining butter mixture after it comes out of the oven.
Place cucumbers,
garlic,
pepper,
onion
and	dill in large mouth quart jar.
Bring to a rolling boil water, vinegar and salt. Pour over cucumbers
and seal.
Ready for use after 6 weeks.
Combine Jell-O and sugar.
Add water; stir until dissolved. Add remaining ingredients.
Blend well.
Chill and serve.
Combine all ingredients, except Fritos and dressing.
Add Fritos and dressing when ready to serve.
Slice onions into rings and saute with butter until clear and soft.
In 9-inch casserole, layer 1/3 of soup, then onions, then cheese, making 3 layers.
Spread cracker crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes, until browned.
Mix together egg yolk, sugar, flour, baking powder, hot water and vanilla. Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into batter. Put in a greased cookie sheet. Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Boil jalapeno peppers in water in a small saucepan until peppers soften.
Drain.
Pour whole tomatoes, jalapeno peppers, garlic salt and onion in blender until well blended.
Use for a dip with chips or top on your favorite food.
Enjoy!
Be careful, it may be hot.
If so, add more tomato.
Pour butter in large 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Layer other ingredients.
Place Saran Wrap, then aluminum foil over baking dish.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cut green beans in bite size pieces; boil until tender.
Drain green beans and set aside.
Crush crackers in a paper bag with rolling pin or other utensil.
Melt butter or margarine in pan (can use same pan as the green beans).
Put crackers in melted butter or margarine and toss to warm on low heat.
Then add in the green beans and serve.
Mix all vegetables together.
Season with salt, pepper and 1 teaspoon Crisco.
Add a small amount of ketchup and boil until thick.
Cook noodles and keep them warm.
Add Parmesan cheese, Ranch dressing and sour cream to noodles and mix.
Garnish with Parmesan cheese and serve.
Combine first 3 ingredients, then add the rest except for pecans.
Pat chopped nuts onto the outside of the balls.
Makes 2 balls.
Take about 1 pound firm fresh or salt water fish fillet; cut in small bite-size pieces.
Place in a pot with 1 pound of fresh peeled tomatoes, cut in chunks.
If fresh tomatoes are not available, canned tomatoes may be used.
Add 2 small onions (halved and sliced) and 2 to 4 small white potatoes (peeled and cut in small pieces).
Flavor with thyme, parsley, salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer slowly for 4 to 6 hours.
Carefully add sherry or rum pepper to taste.
Mix all together in Ziploc bag or container.
Add 4 chicken breast halves.
Turn occasionally.
Marinate for at least 2 hours to overnight, whichever you prefer.
Best done on gas grill. Great done under broiler 10 minutes each side.
Bring the can of pineapple to a boil and add box of Jell-O; mix well.
Let cook and add 1 cup buttermilk and mandarin oranges with juice; mix well.
Fold in Cool Whip; put in covered dish and let set overnight in refrigerator.
You may add nuts and/or miniature marshmallows.
Cook potatoes in small amount of salted water; drain and refrigerate until cool. Chop potatoes coarsely. Mix well with remaining ingredients. Bake in 1 1/2-quart dish at 350° for 30 minutes.
Scald milk.
Remove from heat and let cool.
Stir in eggs, cheese and seasoning.
Divide mixture between two bowls.
Add bacon to one mixture, crabmeat to the other.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Arrange tartlet shells on greased baking sheet.
Fill 14 shells with bacon mixture and 14 with crabmeat mixture.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Serve warm.
Makes 28 appetizers.
Combine sweet potatoes, butter and brown sugar.
Beat egg yolks; add salt, cinnamon and mace.
Mix thoroughly.
Add walnuts and milk.
Beat egg whites until stiff; fold in and pour into pie shell.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 375° and bake 25 minutes longer or until firm.
Cool.
Top with whipped cream if desired.
Cook all ingredients but the soda to soft ball stage, then add soda and mix well.
It will be foamy.
Pour over popcorn.
Soften margarine in microwave; add sugar.
Add eggs.
Put extract in milk.
Add flour and milk to margarine and sugar, alternating.
Bake in a 9 x 12-inch pan for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Top with strawberries or peaches.
Yields 6 or 7 loaves.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes. Combine first 4 ingredients in large bowl; dissolve and carefully add beaten eggs.
Check temperature of mixture; if warm (around 100°), then add yeast, 1/4 cup warm water and sugar which have been combined.
Beat in half the flour (whole wheat or white). Work in remainder of flour.
Turn out on board floured with white flour.
Knead at least 10 minutes (board side will be "blistered" when kneaded enough).
Let rise to almost double; bake.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Dip chicken into melted margarine, then roll in crumb mixture.
Place in shallow pan and drizzle with remaining margarine.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Serves 4.
In a 3-quart pot with cover, cook beef in 1 cup water for 1/2 hour, then add chicken breast with spinach and other ingredients. Add water as needed.
Cook for 45 minutes.
Usually served over rice.
Serves 4.
Combine dates and milk.
Cook until thick in microwave.
Cook 3 minutes; stir.
Cook 3 minutes more; stir.
Add pecans. Spread on crackers.
Bake at 350° for 8 minutes.
Cool and frost.
Prepare rice according to package directions; set aside. Drain pineapple, reserving 1/4 c. juice
Blend
pineapple juice with 1/3 c. soy sauce, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, pepper, garlic powder, and 1/2 c. water; set aside.
Mix together and chill.
Dig in with raw vegetables.
Cook cranberries and 1 1/2 cups of water until popped open. Add sugar and simmer for 8 minutes.
Dissolve jello in boiling water; add 2 cups cold water.
Chill until thickened.
Add cranberries, pineapple and walnuts.
Pour into greased mold.
Combine all ingredients except pecans in a bowl and refrigerate.
Stir in pecans just before serving.
Mix together mayonnaise, sour cream and sugar.
Place everything in a glass bowl in the order given; do not stir. Should be done the day before; cover.
Combine all ingredients, mixing with a fork.
Form into 7 or 8 thick patties.
Coat both sides with finely crushed saltine cracker crumbs on waxed paper and fry in skillet with minimum hot Crisco until lightly browned on each side.
Cook broccoli and onion until tender; drain.
Add soups and simmer a few minutes.
Add rice and cheese.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Prepare
cake mix per box directions.
Add food dye and paste made
from the cocoa and vinegar.
Mix well and bake as directed on cake box.
Frost with favorite frosting.
Mix
sugar, Karo syrup and milk together
in
saucepan. Place over lowered heat until mixture begins to
thicken.
Add vanilla. Pour
onto waxed paper and roll into a
long
roll. Roll in chopped pecans.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add egg, vanilla and nuts, then add milk.
Mix in flours.
Drop by teaspoonful on a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Melt butter in saucepan over low heat.
Add flour and stir until smooth.
Add cheese and cream.
Cook until thickened, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in crabmeat, salt and pepper.
Beat egg yolk lightly with sherry and add to crab mixture.
Chill until serving time.
Just before serving, spoon into canape shells.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 5 to 10 minutes until top is bubbly.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Have child do the squishing.
Have child form into a loaf and plop into a shallow baking pan.
Squirt some more ketchup on top and bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes while Mom puts her feet up.
Set the table.
Don't forget the napkins.
Salt and pepper meat. Brown on both sides in a large skillet. While meat is browning pour beef broth in slow cooker. Reserve 2 Tbsp. broth.
Mix with cornstarch. Pour mixture and wine into slow cooker. Stir well. Add meat. Cook 7 to 8 hours on low. Use gravy over rice or potatoes.
Cook squash until tender.
Drain.
Add soup, sour cream, pimentos, onion, 1/3 stuffing and water chestnuts.
Mix.
Put one third of stuffing on bottom of pan.
Pour mixture in pan. Add remaining stuffing on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves about 8.

Cook beef with onions, stirring frequently. Add to remaining ingredients (EXCEPT cheese) in a large bowl. Turn into 9 x 13 pan or 3-quart casserole dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray. Top with cheese. Bake for 20 minutes in a preheated 375° oven. Serves 8 to 10. Can freeze. Can do ahead.
Heat margarine and olive oil.
Add garlic which has been put through press.
Cook until garlic is cooked.
Add shrimp.
Add pepper and salt heavily as salt has to penetrate shrimp shell. When shrimp are done, add vermouth and lemon juice and cook about 2 minutes.
Beat the three eggs in a large bowl and hot noodles, milk, cheese, salt and pepper; mix well.
Put in large casserole dish. Put butter on top in 1 teaspoon pieces.
Sprinkle with paprika and bake at 350° until brown on top, between 45 minutes and 1 hour.
Cut lettuce into salad size pieces. Cut tomatoes and toss together. Mix with Miracle Whip to desired creaminess. Salt and pepper to taste.
Place crushed vanilla wafers in large bowl.
Add chopped cherries, pineapple, pecans and raisins.
Mix well using hands. Beat eggs, sugar, milk and salt together.
Pour over fruit.
Mix well with hands.
Place in greased tube pan and press down with hand.
Wet hand before pressing, it will not stick to cake.
Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Cool 15 minutes before removing.
Heat broth to boiling.
Add rice and turn down heat; cover for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a small, nonstick pan or wok on medium heat, put butter or oil, carrots and onion and cook until onion is translucent.
Take out onion and carrot.
Scramble 1 egg; add onion and carrot back to egg and add cooked rice.
Cook over medium heat about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce, if desired. Serve hot.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 1 large loaf or 2 small loaves.
Empty tuna into buttered baking dish.
Add cracker crumbs. Pour egg and milk mixture over tuna and crackers.
Cover with grated cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Tear cake into bite-sized bits into 13 x 9-inch oblong pan. Mix hot water and jello; pour over cake.
Then pour pudding over cake (cherry pie filling).
Top with Cool Whip.
You can multiply this to make as much as you need.
Put tomatoes in large, stainless steel or crockery container with salt.

Toss well. Let stand 3 hours. Drain, but do not rinse. In large pan, put 1/2 gallon vinegar with 8 cups sugar. Heat to boiling. Add all vegetables. Return just to a boil and simmer 10 minutes only. Fill jars. Seal and process for 10 minutes in hot water bath. Do not boil (instead, bring to a good simmer; turn off heat and allow jars to sit with lids covered, for only 10 minutes).
Combine all ingredients in saucepan and simmer until sugar dissolves.
Mix ingredients together.
Pour into a 1-quart casserole. Sprinkle with cinnamon and dot with butter.
Bake 1 hour at 325° until set.
Can be served warm or at room temperature.
Can be refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place fruit in buttered 8 x 8-inch dish.
Cut crusts from bread.
Cut each slice into 5 strips. Place over fruit.
In a bowl, beat egg, flour, sugar and butter. Pour over bread.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes until golden brown.
Add salt and spices to water.
Add lemon juice and onion. Bring to a boil; add salmon.
Lower the heat and poach very gentle, allowing 10 minutes per pound.
Cook macaroni. Brown ground beef. Combine all ingredients except onions. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Uncover and put onions on and continue to bake for 5 minutes longer.
Measure first four ingredients into sifter.
Set aside.
Rinse raisins with boiling water to plump them.
Drain.
Set aside with walnuts.
Mix and roll out and cut with a small biscuit cutter.
Put a date into each and fold over.
Bake at 375° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Brown sausage and drain.
Spread rolls over pizza pan, sealing seams.
Layer sausage, potatoes and cheese.
Combine eggs, milk and pepper.
Pour over pan.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes or until set.
In a large bowl mix the flour, yeast, salt and herbs.
Add the olive oil and water and mix until a dough is formed.
On a floured surface knead the dough until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover with a towel and set in a warm place to rise.
When the dough has doubled in size, about 30 minutes, punch it down and divide it into 16 pieces.
Roll each piece into a 12-inch "snake."
Cook spinach and drain well. Combine spinach, sour cream and onion soup.
Put in a greased casserole.
Sprinkle with Pepperidge Farm crumbs (mashed until fine) with Parmesan cheese. Cook in a 350° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine soup mix with breadcrumbs.
Dip chicken in soup mixture, coating well.
Place in lightly greased large shallow baking pan; drizzle with butter.
Bake, turning once, for 10 minutes, or until tender.
Makes about 2 dozen nuggets.
Pour hot water on yeast cakes; let cool.
Add 2 cups flour; let rise 20 minutes.
Add eggs and the 4 cups flour (add 1 cup bran, if desired).
Mix well.
Can be refrigerated.
Take out after 1 1/2 hours.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 15 minutes.
Place marshmallows and orange jello in bowl and pour boiling water over.
Stir until dissolved.
Mix cream cheese and salad dressing until smooth.
Add pineapple.
Then mix with the marshmallow mixture.
Whip the cup of cream and fold into mixture. Pour into 9 x 13 glass dish and chill.
When set, top with 6 ounce red jello, prepared as directed on box.
Chill until set. Cut into squares and serve.

Prepare Mock Hollandaise Sauce. Set aside. Bring 6 cups water to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to low. Carefully break 1 egg into small dish and slide egg into water. Repeat with remaining eggs. Simmer, uncovered, about 5 minutes or until yolks are just set.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease cookie sheets.
Combine butter, sugars, egg and vanilla; beat until well blended.
Combine flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt.
Add to butter mixture; mix well. Stir in oats and raisins.
Drop by tablespoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake in upper third of oven for 12 to 15 minutes. Remove from cookie sheets; cool on wire racks.
Makes 3 dozen.
Mix sugar, oil, flour, applesauce and spices, then add raisins, nuts and gumdrops.
Mix well.
Bake 2 1/2 hours in a greased and floured tube pan at 275°.
Place a pan of water under cake and steam will make it moist.
Test for doneness.
In bowl, combine bananas, oats and milk; set aside.
In large bowl, cream sugar and margarine until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine all ingredients, adding alternately with banana mixture.
Spoon into 2 greased loaf pans.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Contains 18 slices per loaf, 180 calories a slice.
Cook onion and hamburger; add salt and pepper, bell pepper and seasoning mix, tomatoes (chopped a little), tomato sauce and chili beans.
Let simmer for 30 minutes.
Pour into 2-quart casserole. Sprinkle cheese on top with corn chips.
Bake 20 minutes.
Put sugar, corn syrup and water in heavy pot and let come to a boil.
(Use medium heat throughout.)
Add peanuts when mixture starts to boil.
Cook until peanuts start popping and smell parched and sugar is medium brown in color, about 20 minutes. Remove from heat immediately and add baking soda.
Stir quickly. Do not beat.
Pour on a large buttered cookie sheet.
Let cool and break in small pieces.
Mix first five ingredients and pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cut soft butter into cake mix.
Add nuts and crumble on top of pumpkin mixture.
Bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Cook macaroni and drain.
Chop tomato and boil eggs.
Mix everything with mayonnaise.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Sift flour with baking powder and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with milk.
Add flavoring and mix well.
Fold in well beaten egg whites.
Bake in layers at 375° for 25 minutes, in nonstick pans, or well-greased, floured pans.
Peel and cube potatoes.
Boil in lightly salted water just until tender.
Do not overcook.
Turn off stove.
Drain potatoes and immediately return them to the hot pot.
Set on hot stove eye that is turned off.
Pour in amount of canned milk needed for beating.
Do not disturb potatoes.
Add 1 large spoonful of mayonnaise and the butter to the undisturbed potatoes.
Let set until milk becomes lukewarm (this is important).
When milk is warm, mash potatoes slightly; add salt and pepper to taste.
Beat with an electric mixer until smooth.
Combine tuna, condensed soup, peas, celery, onion, milk and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl, mixing thoroughly.
Spoon half of tuna into a 1-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with half of crushed potato chips.
Spoon remaining tuna mixture into casserole. Sprinkle with remaining potato chips.
Cook, uncovered, in microwave oven for 10 minutes at High, or until thoroughly heated. Rotate casserole one-quarter turn once.
Makes about 6 servings.
Rinse raisins in hot water; drain. Chop raisins with food chopper or knife. Blend in peanut butter and honey. Form into 1-inch balls. Roll in nuts.
Shred lettuce onto bottom of 9 x 13-inch dish.
Sprinkle with onions, celery and water chestnuts.
Break peas apart and sprinkle over all and add shredded cheese.
Combine sugar, cheese, salt and garlic powder, mixing well.
Sprinkle veal on both sides with lemon juice, then salt and pepper.
Dust lightly with flour.
Heat butter in large skillet and saute cutlets over moderately high heat for 4 minutes on each side, until lightly browned.
Remove to a warm platter.
On each cutlet, place 4 spears of asparagus and one crab leg.
Top with Hollandaise sauce.
Serve immediately.
Blend sugar and flour.
Add oleo, then add eggs, pineapple and coconut.
Mix well.
Pour into 2 unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 325° about 1 hour.
Freezes well.
Peel and slice 6 large apples.
Arrange in 6 x 10-inch greased baking dish.
Mix together first 5 ingredients and spread over sliced apples.
Pour Crisco oil over all.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes in 325° oven.
Beat margarine at medium speed with an electric mixer. Gradually add sugars, beating well.
Add egg substitute and vanilla; mix well.
Combine flour, baking soda, salt and oats. Gradually add to margarine mixture, mixing well.
Stir in raisins.

recipes.t: Broccoli Rice Salad(First Place Salads, 1994 Rice Contest)
d: Combine bacon, broccoli, onion, raisins and rice.
Mix well. Combine mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar in a small jar.
Mix well and pour over broccoli mixture immediately before serving.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine all ingredients in skillet.
Place approximately a 2 pound chicken in skillet, cover and let simmer 45 minutes.
Roll chicken and cheese up in a crescent roll. Place in a cake pan. Heat soup and milk until smooth. Pour around crescents and cook in oven until crescents are brown. Sprinkle with cheese when done.
Combine honey, vinegar, spices and cinnamon.
Boil 10 to 12 minutes.
Strain.
Return cinnamon to spiced syrup.
Drain 1/2 of the syrup from the peaches.
Add peaches to spiced syrup and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add wine.
Store in covered glass dish in refrigerator.
Leave about a day before using.
More peaches may be added without reheating the syrup.
Line an 8 x 8 x 2-inch pan with plastic wrap.
Place corn syrup and milk in a 2-quart saucepan set on a medium-low heat burner. Add chocolate, stirring constantly, until chocolate is melted, then remove from heat.
Stir in the vanilla and the sugar with a wooden spoon until the mixture is smooth.
Spread the mixture in the pan previously prepared.
Using a teaspoon, drop the peanut butter onto the fudge.
To marbleize, use a knife to swirl the peanut butter through the fudge.
Chill 2 hours or until firm. Invert onto cutting board and remove the plastic wrap.
Makes approximately 25 (1 1/2-inch) squares.
Wash and peel asparagus; cut diagonally into 1-inch pieces. Heat oil in a heavy saute pan.
When very hot, add the asparagus and stir-fry for 2 minutes, stirring constantly with a large spoon.
Add the seasoned salt, salt and pepper, stirring another 30 seconds.
Pour in chicken broth and soy sauce.
Cover; cook 1 minute longer.
Remove from heat.
Add the chicken and mix. Transfer to a serving platter.
Cover; refrigerate until serving time.
Just before serving, add the vinegar and toss until well blended.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all dry ingredients (flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and nutmeg).
Combine and add to dry ingredients the beaten eggs, eggnog and vegetable oil; stir fast until combined.
Stir in the pecans and apricots.
Divide batter into 2 greased 8 x 4 x 2-inch bread pans.
Bake in a 350° oven for 55 to 60 minutes, or until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean.
Cool in pans for 15 minutes before removing breads to cooling rack.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Chill.
Makes 3/4 cup of sauce.
Preheat
oven
to
Grease and flour 12-cup Bundt pan or 10-inch tube pan and set aside.
Beat butter and sugar in large bowl with electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add poppy seed filling and beat until blended.
Beat in egg yolks, 1 at a time, beating
well
after
each addition.
Add vanilla and
sour
cream and beat
just
until
blended.
Stir
flour, baking soda and salt until
mixed, add to poppy mixture gradually, beating well after each
addition.
Beat
egg
whites in separate bowl with electric mixer
until
stiff
peaks
form. Fold beaten egg whites into batter.
Spread batter evenly into prepared pan.
Bake 50 to
60 minutes
or
until
cake tester inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool
in pan on wire rack 10 minutes.
Remove from pan and
cool
completely
on
rack. Dust with confectioners sugar just before serving.
Yields 14 to 16 servings.
* Sour cream is for top of soup in bowl.
Brown ground sausage.
Slice and boil the squash and onion. Combine with 1/2 cup milk into a casserole dish.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake in a 350° oven until cheese is melted.
Cook carrots only until still a little crisp, not soft. Cook remaining ingredients and pour over carrots.
Do not stir.
Cook 35 or 40 minutes at 350°.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Combine all fruit and marshmallows; add to jello.
Chill until thickened; spread on sour cream.
Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Put sugar, salt, milk, margarine and peanut butter in medium saucepan and bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to low and cook 3 minutes, stirring often.
Remove from heat.
Stir in oatmeal and almond extract.
Stir until slightly cool.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on waxed paper and chill until cool.
Makes 2 dozen.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice.
Add egg to milk.
Mix flour and sugar and shake with pineapple juice.
Add to milk and cook over medium heat until thickened.
Set aside to cool.
Drain fruit cocktail and mix with pineapple tidbits and marshmallows in a large bowl.
Add cooled mixture.
Fold in whipped cream and set in refrigerator overnight.
In large bowl, mix onion, garlic, mushrooms, ground beef, bread crumbs and basil until combined well.
Sprinkle salt and pepper on this.
Shape into 12 meatballs.
Brown ground beef and drain.
Add diced tomatoes, soup, beans, celery, onions and parsley.
Mix together.
Add chili seasoning.
Cook at least 30 minutes.
Combine beef, onion, bread, 1/2 cup of the water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper and nutmeg in large bowl; mix well.
Shape into 4 patties.
Cook patties in hot oil in large skillet until browned. Stir in gravy and 1/4 cup of water.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until cooked through.
Drain pineapple well and reserve the juice.
Combine juice, boiling water and gelatin.
Chill slightly.
Combine in pineapple, sour cream and cranberry sauce.
Chill for 2 to 3 hours.
Combine water, sugar and salt in medium saucepan.
Bring to a full boil.
Stir in rice.
Cover; remove from heat.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Add chips and coconut to hot rice and stir until chips are melted.
Cover and chill.
Fold whipped topping into rice mixture.
Pour into waxed paper-lined 8-inch square pan or 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Cover and chill until firm, about 1 hour. Remove paper and cut into squares.
Brown beef, onion and celery.
Add remaining ingredients, except noodles.
Bake, covered, for 1 hour.
Sprinkle with noodles and bake 30 minutes longer.
Bake at 350°.
Shred crab meat.
Discard any shell.
Cut peeled eggs in half lengthwise.
Remove yolks and mash or put through ricer.
Add rest of ingredients to taste, except paprika, and mix well.
Stuff each egg half with mixture and sprinkle with paprika.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled before serving.
Can substitute shredded shrimp.
Cream the sugar with cream cheese.
Stir in mayonnaise.
Fold in cranberry sauce, pineapple, nuts and whipped cream.
Pour into a 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan and freeze. Cut in slices, then squares to serve.
Place chicken in a large baking pan.
Peel and cut potatoes in quarters lengthwise.
Cut quarters in half again.
Place potatoes in between chicken.
Sprinkle herbs over all.
Slice onion and place on top of potatoes and chicken.
Drizzle the oil on top. Bake for 1 hour at 375°, turning chicken and potatoes after first 1/2 hour.

recipes.t: Cream Cheese Potato Soup(Ready In 1 Hour Or Less.)
d: In a Dutch oven, combine the water and boillion. Add the cream cheese; cook and stir until cheese is melted. Stir in remaining ingredients. Simmer, uncovered for 18-20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Preheat
oven
Sift together first 6 ingredients. Combine pumpkin, sugar, milk and eggs in bowl.
Add dry ingredients
and
butter.
Mix
only until flour is moistened. Stir in nuts.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Rinse broccoli to thaw.
Drain well. Mix together all ingredients.
Bake for 45 minutes in a greased preheated cast-iron skillet.
Combine ingredients and add mayonnaise and sour cream. Mix thoroughly and chill. Serves 10 to 12.
Mix Dream Whip by instructions on package; set aside.
Cream sugar, cream cheese and vanilla.
Combine with Dream Whip.
Mix melted margarine with cracker crumbs.
Alternate layers, starting with crumbs, then pie filling, then cheese mixture.
Blend all together.
Roll into 25 balls.
Roll in sugar. Press with fork to flatten.
Bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 350°
for 10 minutes.
Saute onion and mushrooms; add soup, cheese and broccoli in a casserole dish.
Top mixture with crumbled toast and sprinkle with butter.
Cook at 350° for 30 minutes.
Pat out crescent rolls in 9 x 13-inch pan to make crust.
Bake as directed; let cool.
Top with room temperature cream cheese, buttermilk dressing and dill weed.
Spread over cooled crescent rolls.
Top with chopped vegetables, then grated cheese.
Chill 1 hour.
Serves 24.
Combine water, butter, salt, nutmeg, pepper and sugar with carrots.
Simmer, covered, 8 to 10 minutes, or until tender-crisp. Stir in lemon juice and parsley before serving.
Dissolve the jello in the hot water.
Mix milk, Miracle Whip, jello, hot water and vinegar and refrigerate.
When it is set to the consistency of egg white, add the remaining ingredients.
Fry hamburger; drain.
Add sauce mix to meat.
Cook spaghetti or noodles until done.
Mix all together and season to taste.
Mix brown sugar with flour.
Add egg yolks and sweet milk. Add butter.
Cook until thick and put in vanilla.
Put mixture into 8-inch baked pie shell and top with meringue.
Drain the foul, wash it and put in a small pan.
Add salt, 1 cup of water and let cook until it boils.
Pour mixture into bowl, add lemon juice, onion, parlsey and oil.
Mix well.
Measure sifted flour; add soda and salt.
Sift again.
Melt chocolate in boiling water; cool.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add yolks, one at a time, beating after each.
Add chocolate and vanilla.
Add flour mixture alternately with buttermilk, beating after each addition until smooth.
Beat egg whites to stiff peaks.

Press into pan flour, powdered sugar and butter and bake in 350° oven 15 minutes in glass pan in oven at 325°.

Spread over top of crust and bake in 350° oven 35 minutes.
A double recipe fits in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Mixture is single recipe.
Brown pine nuts in butter till lightly browned.

Preheat oven to 400°.
Shape bread dough into balls, 6-8 inch diameter circles.
Fill with meat mixture and fold dough over meat into a rectangle shape.
Pinch seams together. Brush bottom of a 2 inch jelly roll pan with melted rendered butter (no salt). Place meat pies on tray and bake 20 mins on bottom rack until golden brown.
Raise to top rack to lightly brown.
Remove from tray and brush with butter from tray.
In a large mixer bowl, combine cake and pudding mixes.

Beat on low speed of mixer for 30 seconds.
Beat on medium speed for 5 minutes, scraping bowl frequently.
Pour into greased and floured Bundt pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Cool in pan 10 minutes. Remove to rack and pour glaze over cake while still warm.
Mix and add to first mixture.
Stir once daily for 6 to 8 days. This will keep up to 1 year.
While cake layers are baking, put into mixing bowl the sour cream, sugar and coconut.

Mix sugar with flour and salt; stir in milk until smooth.

Arrange skin side up in baking dish.

Mix well.
Spoon over chicken. Bake at 350° for 60 minutes, basting frequently with sauce.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In 9-inch square or 9 x 11-inch baking pan, arrange turkey tenderloins.

Blend well.

Pour in batter.

Roll out about 1/4-inch thick; cut into rounds or fingers. Bake in moderate oven until golden brown, for about 20 minutes. These biscuits keep well stored in airtight tins.
(GE)

Layer remaining ingredients in order listed. Serve with large tortilla chips.

Sift the flour, sugar, salt and baking soda. Blend in the shortening, bananas and eggs or egg whites.
Fold together quickly and do not overmix. Spoon or pour into greased and floured pan. Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.

Loosen edges and cool on rack or cool completely in pan. Glaze with confectioners sugar and water mix.

Place chicken in the dish and roll in margarine.

Melt butter in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Place chicken breast halves in dish.

Add chicken.

In large shallow roasting pan place popcorn and nuts.
Place in 250° oven while preparing glaze.

Stirring constantly, bring to boil over medium heat.
Without stirring, boil 5 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in vanilla and baking soda.
Pour over warm popcorn and nuts.
Stir to coat well.

Store in tightly covered container.
