Bring to a boil.
Add salt.
Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are cooked.
Put entire mixture through a sieve or puree in an electric blender.
Return to a saucepan and add milk.
Beat in egg yolks.
Serve with a teaspoon of butter and croutons in each bowl.
Combine sugar, cinnamon, milk and water.
Cook on slow heat until it forms a soft ball. Pour out on waxed paper and separate.
Place chicken in square metal pan sprayed with Pam.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour mixture over chicken.
Bake for 40 minutes at 400° (uncovered) or until done.
Serve over egg noodles.
Garnish with sliced lemons, if desired.
Combine first 6 ingredients and simmer until potatoes are tender.
Add remaining ingredients and heat thoroughly.
Heat oven to 375°.
In large skillet, brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Stir in tomato sauce, corn, water (optional) and seasoning mix.
Heat mixture until hot and bubbly; reduce heat and simmer while preparing crust.
Separate dough into 10 biscuits; flatten slightly.
Dip each in milk; dip in cornmeal.
Arrange 7 biscuits around sides and 3 in the bottom of 9-inch pie pan; press biscuits to form crust.
Sprinkle crust with 1/2 cup of the cheese. Spoon hot meat mixture over cheese; sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes or until crust is deep golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Makes 8 servings.
Melt chocolate over low heat; stir in sugar, milk, vanilla and mace.
Mix well.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth and thickened.
Excellent over pound cake, sponge cake, bread pudding or ice cream.
Makes 2 1/2 cups.
Mix well and serve.
Layer broccoli and chicken in baking pan.
Heat soup, mayonnaise, milk and sherry.
Pour over layers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and paprika.
Serve over rice. Serves 6 to 8.
Brown meat; then layer everything in a greased casserole in order given.
Bake at 275° for 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Combine cream cheese, sugar and juice in a small bowl; stir well and set mixture aside.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Add cream cheese mixture to apple mixture; toss gently.
Cover and chill.
Toss again before serving.
Serve in lettuce lined bowl. Serves 6 to 8.
Split potatoes and wrap in tinfoil. Bake until done. Scoop out inside and mix with butter, cheese and bacon bits. Replace in shell and sprinkle with cheese. Broil until cheese melts.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter and mix all ingredients. Roll into balls and place on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350°.
Makes about 4 dozen.
Cut chicken into bite size pieces.
Saute onion in butter in a large saucepan.
Add soup, milk and green chiles and blend well on top of stove or in microwave at Medium.
Roll tortillas with chicken and 1/2 the cheese and set side by side in casserole.
Pour sauce over top.
Work down in between.
Sprinkle with cheese. Bake, uncovered, 30 to 40 minutes at 350° or microwave 20 minutes on High.
Serves 8.
Mix first 7 ingredients together well.
Put in unbaked 9-inch pie shell and cut margarine up and place all over top.
Cover with strips.
Bake in 425° oven.
Check in 20 minutes and bake until done (heat may need to be lowered after 20 minutes).
Cook onion and celery in butter until tender.
Combine with potatoes, bread crumbs, eggs, parsley and seasonings.
Mix thoroughly.
Bake at 375° for 45 minutes in covered dish.

recipes.t: Luscious Flan(Pleases Eye As Well As Palate)
d: Sprinkle 1/4 cup sugar in a heavy saucepan; put over medium heat.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sugar melts and syrup is light golden brown.
Pour syrup into six 6-ounce custard cups.
Let cool.
Boil chicken breasts, set aside.
Boil mixed vegetables and drain.
In a bowl mix vegetables, soups and deboned chicken with 1 cup of reserved chicken broth.
Pour in casserole dish.
Mix powdered sugar, softened cream cheese, softened margarine, salt and milk until smooth.
Add pecans and coconut.
Spread over cake layers.
In large skillet, generously cover bottom with olive oil. Saute garlic salt and fresh garlic.
Add chopped chicken.
Cook, stirring, 15 minutes.
Add chopped red pepper.
Stir and cook 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix together tapioca pudding, vanilla pudding, orange extract and the 3 cups of water.
Let stand for 10 minutes so tapioca gets soft.
Cook until thick.
Boil for 1 minute.
Cool.
Add Cool Whip, pineapple and oranges.
Stir until blended good. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a large bowl, combine ingredients.
Blend together and chill (can be made ahead).
Cook beef and onion until done. Spoon into baking dish.
Stir in taco mix, tomato sauce and corn.
Sprinkle on cheese.
Sift flour, measure and sift two times.
Cream margarine and Crisco.
Add sugar and cream well.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating after each.
Add flour and milk alternately.
Begin with flour and end with flour.
Add flavoring.
Beat at slow speed. Bake in greased tube pan at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Start in cold oven.
This does not use baking powder.
May use 2 teaspoons vanilla instead of almond.
Heat oil; add onions and green peppers.
Cook until soft.
Add ground beef, salt, black pepper and chili pepper.
Cook until browned.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste and 4 cups tomatoes and 1 teaspoon sugar.
Cook together 15 minutes on medium heat.
Break spaghetti into pieces and cook according to directions on package. Do not overcook.
Drain and add to sauce mix and put into casserole.
Put into oven at 350° for 20 minutes.
Fry cabbage "slowly" in 1 stick butter (should take about 1 hour on low). Be careful not to burn, light brown is okay.
While cabbage is cooking, make noodles.
Season pork chops with salt and pepper.
Brown on both sides in a skillet.
In a 9 x 13-inch pan, layer the vegetables and pour soup over.
Remove chops from pan, remove fat from skillet and add water to rinse and scrape particles from bottom of skillet.
Pour this over vegetables.
Sprinkle with thyme.
Place chops on top. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
If chops get too brown during cooking, cover with glass lid or foil.
Soften cream cheese.
Add chili and mix well.
Heat in microwave or on stove.
Serve with corn chips.
Cook noodles in boiling water until tender; drain.
Combine noodles, drained tuna, mayonnaise, vegetables and salt.
Add soup, milk and cheese.
Bake at 425° about 20 minutes.
Cream sugar and margarine.
Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Sift remaining ingredients together and blend into mixture.
Form into rolls; wrap in waxed paper.
Refrigerate overnight.
Slice and bake at 350° for 8 to 12 minutes.
Combine kraut, onion and parsley; toss until well mixed. Spread dressing on each slice of bread.
Top 8 slices of bread with corned beef, cheese and kraut mixture; top with remaining bread.
Lightly butter both sides of sandwiches.
Grill slowly until cheese melts and bread browns.
Bring chicken broth and water to boil.
Add pasta and cook 5 minutes.
Add spinach and simmer 5 minutes longer.
Mix the ground meat, cheese and garlic and drop from teaspoon into soup.
Simmer 7 minutes until no longer pink inside.
Stir in 3 cups of vegetables and simmer until done (onion, carrots, celery, zucchini).
Blend the first 4 ingredients 5 minutes in mixer.
Spread over crumbs made of graham cracker crumbs and melted butter.
Mix and pat in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Refrigerate.
Cut 5 bananas in 1/2 pieces.
Layer in pan.
Next, layer pineapple.
Spread with Cool Whip.
Garnish with coconut, maraschino cherries and chopped nuts. Refrigerate overnight.
Heat soup and water to boiling point.
Add Jell-O.
When mixture is partly set, add remaining ingredients.
Pour into molds. Chill until set.
Makes 8 molds.
Remove husks and silks from corn.
Rinse corn and pat dry.
Cut corn from cobs (about 3 cups); to cut corn from cob:
with very sharp knife, first cut, just barely take the top of the kernels, second cut, take about half-way of kernels and third cut, use blade of knife and scrape down to cob.
This gets the milk out of corn. Place butter in 2-quart casserole; microwave at High for 55 seconds, until butter melts.
Add corn, 1/4 cup water and sugar, stirring well.
Cover with heavy-duty plastic wrap.
Cook on High 8 to 9 minutes or until corn is tender, stirring after 4 minutes. Shake 1/2 cup water, salt, pepper and flour in pan until flour is blended smooth.
Stir into corn, mixing well.
Cook on High 3 minutes or until mixture slightly thickens.
Mix all ingredients together and let set till dry onions are limp and no longer crunchy. Use for fish topping or anything else you like to use tartar sauce on.
Brown and drain beef. Add onion, tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, oil, cinnamon, cloves, salt, raisins with stock and green olives. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Mix and put in freezer.
Blend sugar and Crisco.
Add egg which was beaten slightly to sugar and Crisco.
Add sour milk.
Sift together soda, cornmeal, flour and salt.
Stir into mixture.
Pour into a greased pan and bake for 25 minutes at 350°.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs then cream again.
Add bread and pineapple including juice from can.
Pour into buttered dish and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Halve eggplant lengthwise.
Hollow out center.
Cook sausage; drain.
In a large bowl, mix sausage, eggplant centers, tomatoes, squash, onion, salt and pepper.
Mix well.
Stuff into eggplant shells.
Spoon 4 tablespoons of tomato sauce over each.
Mix bread crumbs, oregano, egg and remaining tomato sauce.
Spoon over eggplant.
Cover with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours. Serves 6.
Combine all ingredients in a 2-quart pan or slow cooker. Simmer for 45 minutes.
Add more milk, if needed.
Add salt to taste.
Serves 6 to 8.
Soften gelatine in cold water.
Add sugar, pineapple juice, vinegar, salt and green coloring.
Chill until slightly thickened, then add pecan meats, India relish, pineapple and olives.
Pour into molds or a flat serving dish which has been rubbed with oil. Chill until firm and serve.
Unusual!
Combine sugar, flour, salt, soda, baking powder,
cinnamon and Wesson oil.
Beat 2 minutes.
Add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes.
Fold in apples and nuts.
Bake in a tube cake pan for 45 to 50 minutes in a 350° oven.
Combine
mushroom
soup
and
1 cup of broth and put in bottom of	pan.
Add
half
of
stuffing
on top of soup.	Add chicken on	top of stuffing.
Put chicken soup with other cup of
broth on chicken.
Add the remaining stuffing on top.
You can
use frozen broccoli, if desired, on top of chicken.
Bake with aluminum foil on pan at 350° for 50 minutes.
Serve.
Cook squash and onion together.
Drain; mash well.
Drain again.
Melt margarine in 9-inch baking dish.
Pour melted margarine into squash.
Mix all ingredients well except cracker crumbs.
Pour in casserole dish.
Top with cracker crumbs.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes or until firm and top is brown.
Grind pears, peppers and onions in food chopper or processor. Add all the ingredients to the vinegar and sugar.
Boil 30 minutes.
Put in jars and seal.
Mix all ingredients except the chocolate bits and beat for 3 minutes.
Fold in bits and pour into a greased and floured Bundt pan.
Bake at 325°.
After 1 hour check with cake tester.
Bake until batter does not stick to tester.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan.

Bring water to a boil in large pot. Add potatoes to water along with chicken stock base, salt and pepper. Cook 12 minutes or until potatoes are about half-done. Add Cheddar cheese soup and simmer 10 minutes. Melt butter or margarine in a heavy saucepan. Add flour and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 3 to 4 minutes. Do not brown. Whisk flour mixture into the potato mixture and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer an additional 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in half and half and heat to serving temperature. Do not boil. Serve with chives, bacon bits and parsley.
Defrost pie crust. Butter 1 large baking pan.
Line bottom and sides of pan with two of the pie crusts.
Pour peaches into bowl. Mix all ingredients.
Squash peaches and mix until flour is mixed well.
Pour into pan and cut the two crusts you have left into strips. Cover top and bake at 375° for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Brown meat; drain.
Add spices and simmer 5 to 10 minutes. Then add tomatoes, V-8 and rice.
Cook until rice is done.
You may add more V-8, if desired.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy.
Add egg and vanilla; mix thoroughly.
Add dry ingredients which have been sifted together alternately with sour cream.
Blend well.
Fold in nuts.
Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes at 400°.
Cool and top with golden butter glaze.
Brown onion in butter.
Add chicken, carrots, bean sprouts, corn and seasonings.
Cook on simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Cool completely.
Wrap 2 tablespoonfuls of mixture in each egg roll skin and seal edges.
Place in deep fryer until browned.
Melt margarine and mix with other ingredients and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Combine the first 5 ingredients.
Place in 9 x 13-inch pan and top with bacon.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour to 45 minutes.
Separate yolks from whites.
Beat whites until light; add salt and beat until stiff and dry.
Beat egg yolks until thick and lemon colored; add milk and pepper.
Fold egg whites and baking powder into the yolks.
Melt butter in frying pan; pour in egg mixture and heat slowly until omelet has set.
Put in a 325° oven for 30 minutes, or until omelet browns on top.
Serve immediately with Spanish sauce.
Yield:
5 servings.
In pan bring 1 cup pineapple juice to boil.
Take off heat and add Jell-O.
Mix real good, then add Sprite.
Mix pineapple, cranberries and pecans.
Mix and pour into 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Chill until set.
Stew peaches with 2 or 3 cloves.
Simmer other ingredients 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour over peaches.
Store in refrigerator.
Roll out crescent rolls and press in jelly roll pan, pressing seams together.
Bake for 10 minutes at 375°.
Let cool.
Mix cream cheese, mayonnaise and Ranch mix; spread on cooled crescent crust.
Add vegetables, making sure you press them into the cream cheese mixture.
Top with grated cheese.
Refrigerate overnight.
Cook and drain beef.
Saute onions, pepper and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook 15 minutes.
Serve on rolls.
Mix sugar, mustard, cornstarch and a pinch of salt in a heavy saucepan. Add egg yolk and mix well.
Heat coffee cream to near boil. Add to egg mixture and mix well.
Place over medium heat and stir until thick.
Slowly add vinegar, beating constantly. Serve warm over meat.
Mix lime jello with 1 cup of hot water and 1/2 cup of cold water.
Put into pan to set.
Do the same with the cherry and orange jellos.
Chill in the refrigerator.
Mix sugar, pineapple juice and 1/4 cup water in saucepan; let come to a boil.
Mix with lemon jello.
Let set on counter until it jells.
Mix the Dream Whip and milk.
When thoroughly whipped, add lemon jello mixture. Cut lime, cherry and orange jellos into small cubes.
Fold into whipped mixture and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Use broth from chicken.
Throw in chicken and other ingredients.
Cook until thick.
Pour hot water over Jell-O; add pineapple juice and while still warm.
Add marshmallows and cheese.
When cool, add pineapple and nuts.
When it begins to thicken and congeal, fold in whipped cream.
Chill.
Prepare pan by buttering bottom and sides of 9-inch square pan.
Dice marshmallows.
Set aside.
Mix evaporated milk, sugar and salt in saucepan.
Heat mixture over low heat until it just boils, then cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly with wooden spoon.
Remove from heat.
Stir in marshmallows, chocolate chips, nuts and vanilla.
Stir until marshmallows melt.
Pour in pan. Cool.
Cut in squares.
Melt
oleo in soup pot.
Add onion, carrots and celery. Saute until
soft.
Add
flour
and
cornstarch.	Cook
until bubbly. Add broth and milk and make a smooth sauce.
Add soda and cheese. Garnish with parsley before serving.
Put flour, 1 1/2 cups sugar, cocoa, soda and salt into an ungreased 13 x 9 x 2-inch metal baking pan.
Stir with a fork to mix.
Form 3 wells in the flour mixture. Pour oil into one well, vinegar in the second and vanilla in the third.
Pour cold coffee over all ingredients and stir with fork until well mixed.
Do not beat.
Combine remaining sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over batter.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Combine cream cheese, egg and salt.
Beat until smooth.
Add chocolate and butterscotch chips; set aside.
Mix flour, soda, salt, cocoa and sugar.
Add oil, vanilla and water.
Beat together until smooth.
Combine first 4 ingredients.
Bring butter, water, shortening and cocoa to boil.
Pour over flour mixture and mix well.
Add eggs, buttermilk and vanilla.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cook macaroni. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Add tuna, peas, onions, cheese and salt to taste.
Blend in enough mayo to make creamy.
Saute onion in oil until tender.
Add ground beef.
Cook until brown, stirring until crumbly.
Add tomato sauce and seasonings; mix well.
Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes or until heated through.
Cook macaroni.
Drain.
Chop eggs.
Mix mayonnaise and Ranch dressing. Mix all ingredients with macaroni.
Chill in refrigerator or serve warm.
Serve with Ritz crackers.
Prepare stuffing according to package directions.
Spread in 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with layer of chicken.
In large saucepan melt butter.
Blend flour and seasonings.
Add cool broth.
Cook and stir until mixture thickens.
Stir small amount of mixture into eggs.
Return to hot mix.
Pour over chicken. Bake at 325° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes to set. Cut in squares to serve with pimento mushroom sauce.
Serves 12.
Mix together and chill.
Beat eggs until foamy.
Add other ingredients.
Pour into unbaked pie shells.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Cream sugar, shortening and eggs until light and fluffy. Combine dry ingredients, then add alternately with milk, beating well.
Beat in bananas and vanilla.
Pour in greased and floured pan (9 x 13 x 2-inches).
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Brown meat. Drain.
Stir in tomato sauce and seasoning mix.
Simmer 5 minutes. Unroll dough.
Press onto bottom and sides of ungreased 12-inch pizza pan.
Prick bottom and sides with fork.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown. Cover crust with meat mixture and cheese.
Continue baking until cheese begins to melt.
Top with remaining ingredients. Serve with sour cream, if desired.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Spread cream cheese on bottom of a platter.
Cover with the chopped onions.
Sprinkle Worcestershire sauce over the onions. Mix ketchup, horseradish and Tabasco and spoon over the layered ingredients.
Top with the crab.
Sprinkle a little lemon juice over crab.
Finish off with chopped parsley.
Serve with crackers. Delicious!!
Mix the cream cheese, sugar and yolks together.
Cut crusts from the bread and roll
the bread thin.
Spread the slices with the cream cheese mixture.
Roll up bread.
Dip each in melted oleo, then roll in the cinnamon and sugar mixture.
Bake for 10 - 15 minutes at 400 degrees.
Cut in half.
Serve plain or with sour cream.
You can freeze these to cook later.
Combine all ingredients.
Let stand 15 minutes.
Line 9-inch pie plate with pastry.
Add filling.
Add top crust.
Flute edges.
Bake at 400° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Serve warm.
Shred cooked chicken breasts in a baking dish.
Saute onions and celery.
Mix celery soup, chicken soup, celery and onions. Pour on top of chicken.
Mix Stove Top stuffing according to package directions.
Top chicken mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Beat cream cheese until fluffy. Add vanilla, lemon juice and condensed milk and mix.
Pour into graham cracker crust. Chill 2 hours.
With scoop, form 6 ice cream balls.
Place on wax paper-covered tray; cover and freeze several hours or until very firm.
Cook hamburger meat and drain.
Add spaghetti sauce, sugar and mushroom soup.
Cook for 10 minutes on medium.
Pour in casserole dish cooked noodles and sauce.
Then put cheese all in the casserole.
Cut in 1-inch strips.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Drain fruit cocktail, oranges and cherries.
In a large bowl, mix fruit cocktail, oranges and cherries.
Add sour cream, chopped walnuts, marshmallows and coconut.
Mix until all is blended. Place in another dish.
Cool in refrigerator for 2 hours and serve.
Beat eggs; add salt and pepper to taste and a pinch of garlic. Open chilies and clean seeds from them.
Spread in the bottom of well buttered 8 x 8-inch Pyrex baking dish, alternating cheese and chilies in layers.
Pour eggs over and bake 40 minutes at 350°. Cut into one-inch squares or smaller.
Mix pudding and pineapple well. Add remaining ingredients. Mix. Refrigerate.
Season chicken with salt, pepper and paprika.
Combine egg and milk.
Dip chicken in egg mixture.
Drop into paper bag with flour.
Shake to coat.
Place in hot oil in heavy deep skillet. Cover.
Fry at 350° to 400° until brown.
Serves 4.
Mix ground beef, rice and onion together.
Stuff it inside peppers.
Pour jar of spaghetti sauce in pan.
Add 1/2 jar of water.
Add peppers and cook at medium heat for 2 to 3 hours.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes. Makes 1 qt.
Place tofu on paper towel, changing paper towel until most of water has drained out.
Put tofu in bowl and mash with fork or potato masher.
Grind roasted sesame seed and add with rest of ingredients to tofu.
Mix well.
Use as dressing on boiled vegetables.
Serves 4 to 6.
Dissolve yeast in 1/2 cup water.
Measure sugar, salt and shortening; add 1 1/2 cups warm water in a large bowl.
Beat in yeast and eggs.
Add 2 cups flour and beat until smooth.
Stir in enough flour to make soft dough and mix well.
Place in a greased bowl; cover and let rise until doubled (about 1 1/2 hours).
Punch down, cover tightly and refrigerate.
(Dough keeps 3 to 4 days.) Remove dough from refrigerator.
Shape rolls.
Let rise until doubled (about 45 minutes).
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Brush top with butter.
Makes 24 servings.
Brown meat and leave juice in meat.
Add diced onion and pepper.
Let simmer 5 to 10 minutes, then add remaining ingredients, preferably tomatoes first.
Also, add 1 cup of water. Cook for about 2 hours and remove lid for the last 45 minutes for thicker chili.
Fold together blueberries and 2 tablespoons flour.
Set aside. Mix remaining ingredients and add floured blueberries.
Put into muffin cups (may use liners and put 1/2 cup mixture into each). Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Cook potatoes
and onion in enough water to cover, with salt and pepper, until
almost done. Add milk and butter. Cook until done, stirring
often. Can be thickened with cornstarch, if desired.
Heat oven to 425°.
Place potatoes on a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden brown, stirring once.
Mix all ingredients but stuffing and nuts.
Empty into a greased 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with stuffing and nuts. You may drizzle top with melted margarine.
Bake at 350° for approximately 1 hour.

recipes.t: Very Good And Easy Zucchini Cheese Quiche
d: Beat eggs until foamy.
Add cheese, zucchini, Bisquick and margarine.
Mix thoroughly.
Mix soda, baking powder and milk and pour into zucchini mixture.
Mix well and pour into buttered, 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into bowl.
Make a well and add Wesson oil, egg yolks, water and maple flavoring. Beat until smooth with electric mixer using medium speed for one minute.
In a large bowl, add cream of tartar to egg whites.
Beat with electric mixer until whites form very stiff peaks on high speed for 3 to 5 minutes.
Do not underbeat.
Pour egg yolk mixture gradually over beaten egg whites, gently folding with rubber spatula, just until blended.
Add nuts.
Do not stir.
Pour into ungreased 10 x 4-inch tube pan.
Bake 55 minutes at 325°, then increase to 350° for 10 to 15 minutes longer or until top springs back when lightly touched.
Turn pan upside-down and cool.
Let hang until cold.
Remove and frost with the following.
Combine all ingredients except Coca-Cola and marshmallows in large bowl; blend at low speed.
Beat one minute at medium speed; add Coca-Cola and blend well by hand.
Stir in marshmallows.
Pour batter into a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Melt butter in heavy skillet over low heat.
Add chopped onion and saute until onion is transparent.
Stir in whipping cream. Mix well.
Now, stir in Parmesan cheese.
When this is mixed well, add cooked peas.
Continue to cook over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Serve over fettucini noodles.
You can use broccoli, shrimp, etc. instead of peas.
Mix the flour, buttermilk and oil together in a bowl until mixture becomes a dough.
Sprinkle occasionally with flour as you knead this a few times.
In another bowl, mix the sugar and sweet potatoes together.
Press dough in the center and add sweet potatoes to this.
Begin kneading the dough until well mixed. Roll or pat out to desired thickness.
Cut biscuits.
Bake in oven oven at 450° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Mix softened cream cheese and Cool Whip.
Mix the drained fruits and mix all ingredients together.
Garnish, if desired, with halved cherries.
Store in refrigerator.
Mix together the first 6 ingredients.
Float orange slices on top. Add cherries.
Crust:
Mix flour, sugar and oleo until crumbly and press into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until lightly brown.
Cream shortening; add sugar, vanilla and orange rind.
Add milk alternately with dry ingredients.
Drop by teaspoons onto baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix together well; form into loaf and bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Combine Jell-o, pineapple (juice included), 1 cup water and 2 Tbsp. sugar in saucepan. Dissolve Jell-o and cook until mixture comes to a boil. Set aside to cool completely.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Cut potatoes in slices like French fries and place in large bowl with other ingredients.
Toss well and place on a nonstick baking sheet and bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.t: Guyanese Garlic Pork(Traditional Christmas Breakfast Dish)
d: You will also need 2 large airtight glass jars (Mason jars ideal).
Pull each biscuit out to about 6-inches long.
Dip in melted butter and roll in mixture of nuts, cinnamon and sugar.
Bake in 425° oven for 8 to 10 minutes.
Combine salmon, cracker crumbs, egg, onion, parsley and pepper.
Blend well.
Shape into patties.
Fry over medium heat.
Mix lemon juice and milk.
Add fruit (drained) and fold in topping. Put in icebox until set, about 30 minutes.
Simmer ham and sausage in 3 1/2 quarts of water.
Cook for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Remove ham and sausage and cut up. Return to water.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Cook and drain spinach.
Use either a 9 x 13-inch baking pan or a jelly roll pan/cookie sheet approximately 1 inch deep.
Spray bottom of pan with Pam before you begin to layer sheets of filo dough.
You will layer 10 to 12 sheets of filo dough, making sure you brush butter on top of each new sheet.
Keep a damp cloth over the filo dough so it does not dry out.
After you have layered your last sheet of dough, spread your cheese/spinach mixture.
Now begin laying the next 10 to 12 sheets of filo dough, again brushing butter on top of each sheet.
Be sure to cut off excess dough and score or cut into squares before baking.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cheese/spinach mixture:
Mix together the eggs, drained spinach, cheese, salt, pepper, dill, garlic and onion.
Mix cake according to directions.
Cream the cream cheese with sugar.
Beat in egg.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop 1 rounded teaspoonful of mixture in each cupcake paper.
Top with cake batter.
Bake as directed on cake box.
Heat oven to 325°.
Cream together eggs, margarine and sugars; sift together flour, soda and cream of tartar.
Mix into cream mixture.
Form into rolls (logs).
Wrap in wax paper and refrigerate.
Slice and bake in a moderate oven for 10 to 12 minutes.
Bake on lightly greased pan.
Beat several minutes and bake at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes in middle of oven.
Grease, flour and line 9 1/2 x 13-inch cake pan with wax paper.
After it is baked and cooled, lift cake out of pan onto oblong serving tray.
Cut lengthwise through the middle. Lift carefully with both hands under top part.
Put icing in the middle and replace the top.

Completely dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Combine cold water and ice cubes to make 1 cup. Add to gelatin; add soy sauce and lemon juice. Stir in the 3 tablespoons of boiling water and let dissolve.
Let cool to room temperature.
Pour dissolved gelatin into a medium bowl. Whip the cream.
Fold in whipped cream and mashed berries.
Pour into a wet mold and chill 12 hours.
Slice carrots and cook in water.
Drain.
Mix brown sugar, butter, water, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Pour over carrots.
Heat and serve.
Warm syrup and sugar, then add butter and melt in sugar.
Beat eggs good and then add them and flour to syrup mixture.
Add ground or chopped peanuts and vanilla. Pour in pie crust and bake.
Dissolve Jell-O in hot water.
Add pineapple and orange juice concentrate.
Stir well and chill until partially set.
Fold in apricots.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan.
Beat pudding mix and milk. Fold in whipped cream.
Spread on firm Jell-O.
Chill and serve.
Reserve 2/3 cup Mozzarella cheese for top layer.
Combine in bowl: soup, milk and pepper; set aside.
In another bowl, mix spinach, egg and Ricotta cheese; mix well.
In bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking dish, spread 1/2 cup soup mixture.
Arrange 4 noodles on mixture.
Top 1/3 soup mixture, 1/2 spinach mixture, 1/2 Mozzarella cheese and 1/2 chicken.
Repeat layers, ending with noodles.
Top with reserved 2/3 cup Mozzarella cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Cover.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until bubbling. Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
Preheat 10-inch iron skillet.
Mix all ingredients and blend well.
Pour batter into preheated skillet and bake for 30 minutes at 400°.
Mix all ingredients in a microwavable container.
Cook on High until hot and cheese is melted.
Eat with your favorite corn chips.
Chop all vegetables finely.
Mix with cooked spaghetti and chill.
Note:
Any kind of pasta may be used in place of spaghetti.
Cook potatoes in jackets until tender.
Peel and shred. Combine potatoes with sour cream, 1 cup of cheese and remaining ingredients except paprika.
Turn into buttered 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese and paprika.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Beat egg yolks with the sugar.
Add milk gradually, salt, then coconut and stiffly beaten whites.
If desired, mix 1/2 tablespoon cornstarch with the sugar and use only 2 eggs.
Fill shell and bake 30 minutes at 300°.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Mix barbecue sauce, onion and seasoning in baking dish.
Place ribs in sauce.
Roast, covered, for approximately 2 hours, until meat is done.
For quicker cooking, can be cooked in oven bag; cook approximately 1 1/2 hours.
Cook, peel and dice potatoes.
Slice cheese in strips.
Chop onion.
Fry bacon crisp and crumble.
Combine first 4 ingredients. Place in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Top with bacon.
Bake 1 hour at 325°.
Serves 12.
Mix together and put in pie crust.
Chill about 2 hours.
Melt butter.
Stir in Cheez Whiz.
Mix well with other ingredients.
Pour into greased casserole.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Melt chocolate and butter. Add eggs and sugar after beating together. Stir in remaining ingredients. Bake in buttered 8 or 9-inch square pan at 350° for 25 minutes.
Crust:
Combine flour, potatoes, milk and margarine or butter and set aside.

Cook rice. Combine cooked rice with milk, salt, sugar, eggs, vanilla and pineapple. Pour into 1 1/2 quart baking dish. Sprinkle with cinnamon. Cover with foil. Place on bottom of oven, watch so it doesn't burn. Cook about 30 minutes at 350 degrees or until done.
Mix all ingredients in large bowl.
Dissolve 2 scoops of the mix in 1 cup of boiling water for instant hot chocolate.
Yields 50 servings.
Boil potatoes until fork-soft.
Cool potatoes until you can comfortably peel them.
While you slice potatoes in large container, fry bacon pieces and boil eggs.
Drain peas
and
add
chopped pickle, cheese and grated onion. Mix together with enough mayonnaise to moisten.
Serve on crisp lettuce leaf.
In heavy saucepan, mix sugar and cornstarch.
Separate egg yolks from whites, putting yolks in mixture.
Add milk, small amount at a time, with egg and sugar until thin.
Then add rest of milk.
Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly, so not to stick, until thick.
In a large bowl, combine whipped topping, gelatin and cottage cheese. Fold in oranges.
Chill until serving.
Makes 100 servings.
Combine all ingredients and refrigerate until ready to serve. Can be used on baked potatoes or fish.
Fry garlic, onion and chili peppers until lightly brown.
Add meat and brown.
Add water, tomato sauce, chili powder and cumin powder.
Cook for 30 minutes.
Cook longer for better flavor. Last, add oats to thicken.
Separate the fiber from pumpkin seeds. Do not wash the seeds. Add the margarine or oil and the salt to the seeds.
Spread in shallow pan and bake at 250° about 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes, until crisp and brown.
The listed amounts are just an idea.
You may vary the amounts of any of the ingredients to suit the dish and amount needed.
Mix all ingredients together well.
Shape into a ball.
Cook and chop up 4 chicken breasts.

Add cream of chicken and mushroom soup, then, mix chicken ala king, chopped small onion, Cheddar cheese (grated) and chicken broth to mixture for moisture. Place in casserole and top with can of dried onion rings.
Bake in oven at 350° until bubbles through and through.
Cook celery and onion in butter until tender, not brown.
Add chicken broth and seasonings.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Slowly add soup and cheese.
Add spaghetti and let stand for 1 hour.
Add chicken and olives.
Crumble goat cheese coarsely and stir into cottage cheese. Spread should be slightly lumpy.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Heat oil in saucepan.
Add garlic and onion and green pepper.
Saute until onion in translucent being careful not to brown.
Stir in tomatoes.
Simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Add jalapeno.
Cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate, covered, if to be kept overnight. Pile cheese mixture onto plate.
Drizzle salsa around it to form a red pool around creamy cheese.
Surround with additional fresh chopped tomatoes and green peppers if desired.
Serve with crackers or chips.
Place 4 slices of bread, butter side down, in oblong baking dish.
Place a slice of cheese on each piece.
Top cheese with the cooked sausage.
Beat the eggs, milk and salt together.
Place remaining 4 bread slices, butter side up, over the sausage.
Pour eggs over all.
Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
Saute onion and mushrooms in butter. Add remaining ingredients except for rice. Bring to a boil. Add rice.
Cook, uncovered, for 20 minutes until liquid disappears.
Partially defrost the fish so that fillets can be easily separated.
Pour oil into a skillet.
Add chopped onion and cook over medium heat about 5 minutes.
Add the other ingredients, except for the fish, and cook about 5 minutes.
Add the fish; cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until done.
Mix shortening, sugar and egg thoroughly.
Stir in pineapple. Measure flour by dipping method or by sifting.
Stir together flour, soda, salt and nutmeg and blend.
Mix in nuts.
Chill at least one hour.
Heat oven to 400°.
Drop rounded teaspoonfuls of dough about 2 inches apart on lightly greased baking sheet.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes or until no imprint remains when touched lightly. Makes about 5 dozen cookies.
Cook vegetables until tender and blend flour into milk. Simmer 10 minutes.
Garnish with paprika and parsley.
Add salt to taste.
Serve with garlic bread and tossed salad.
Shape in ball. Roll in pecans.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into a buttered casserole.
Bake in oven at 350° until set.
Heat oil and cook the chicken pieces in it until they are golden brown, turning frequently.
Add onions; cook a few minutes longer.
Add garlic, tomatoes, basil, salt and pepper.
Cover pan and cook gently until chicken is done and tomatoes are cooked to a sauce.
Stir occasionally.
Continue cooking for about 45 minutes. Add wine.
Cook another 15 minutes.
Serve with Italian Rice and a green salad.
Mix Veg-All and soup together and pour into a casserole dish. Mix flour, milk and melted butter together.
Pour over the soup and Veg-All mixture.
Bake 45 minutes at 400°.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Cook onion and green pepper in boiling, salted water until tender, then drain.
Combine first 6 ingredients in saucepan.
Cook about 20 minutes over medium heat until it comes to a boil.
Stir occasionally and continue cooking until mixture forms a small ball in cold water. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla and stir until mixture begins to lose its gloss.
Drop small portions onto waxed paper.
(Put foil under waxed paper to keep it from sticking to your countertop.) Work fast, keeping saucepan over a warm surface, if it seems to harden too fast.
Let pralines cool before removing from waxed paper.
Combine the mayonnaise, Creole seasoning, dill weed and paprika.
Mix well and set aside.
Combine chicken, bell pepper, celery, onion, and relish.
Toss to mix.
Add flavored mayonnaise and mix well.
Makes about 6 servings.
Wash beans until all bubbles disappear.
Mix beans, salsa and chopped vegetables in large bowl.
Season to taste with Old Dutch dressing; mix well.
Let marinate 1/2 hour.
Delicious!
Bring pineapple and juice, sugar and water to a boil.
Add jello and cream cheese.
Stir until cream cheese is dissolved. Chill until it starts to set.
Add cool Whip and mix thoroughly. Sprinkle nuts over top.
Combine meat, salt, pepper and onion; mix well.
Brown in skillet.
Add red beans, corn, spaghetti, tomato juice and chili powder.
Simmer for 30 to 45 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar; add eggs 1 at a time.
Add flour sifted with mace.
Pour in greased 9-inch tube pan and bake 1 hour beginning in cold oven.
Can be baked as sheet cake with butter icing for teas.
Combine flour, baking powder, sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa and salt. Stir in milk, vanilla and shortening.
Pour into greased 8-inch baking pan.
Peel and slice potatoes thin.
Mix onion, cream of mushroom soup and milk.
Layer potatoes with butter.
Add salt and pepper. Lay pork chops on top.
Cook for 1 hour at 350°.
Defrost patties.
Crumble 4 patties in 9 x 13-inch dish.
Salt and pepper.
Top with margarine and 1/2 of cheese.
Repeat layers. Pour half and half over mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix first four ingredients.
Marinate chicken wings in mixture for as long as possible.
If cooking a lot of wings, double recipe.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Layer lettuce, celery, green pepper, onion and peas. Spread mayo over all. Sprinkle sugar over mayo. Sprinkle cheese. Top with bacon. Refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours before serving.
Line a 10-inch skillet with 4 lettuce leaves.
Set aside. Peel a 1/2-inch wide strip around center of each potato.
Layer potatoes and next 3 ingredients over lettuce leaves.
Add water and sprinkle with sugar, salt and pepper.
Dot with butter.
Mix together chicken, soup and vegetables. Pour into baked pie crust. Sprinkle grated cheese on top of chicken mixture. Crumble Ritz crackers on top. Bake at 350° until hot, about 20 minutes.
Drain pineapple, save juice.
Mix sugar and flour together. Add pineapple and cheese.
Put in buttered casserole dish.
Cover top with crushed Ritz crackers.
Melt butter; add pineapple juice. Pour over casserole.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Bring margarine, cocoa and water to boil.
Pour over sugar and flour.
Mix eggs, buttermilk and soda and add.
Pour in 9 x 13-inch greased and floured pan.
Bake at 300° for 40 to 45 minutes.
Mix all together in blender.
Beat well for 5 minutes.
In double boiler, melt sugar and butter in milk.
Dissolve cornstarch in a little water and add to hot milk.
Stir until thick, remove from heat and add rum.
Combine and pour over 8 qt. popped corn.
Bake at
250° for 1 hour.
Mix together dressing mix and mayo. Drizzle dressing over peas and cauliflower.
Let stand overnight and mix together before serving.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in lemonade.
Add cold water and cranberry juice cocktail, chilled.
Pour over ice in punch bowl.
Slowly pour in ginger ale, chilled.
Makes 12 cups.
Sprinkle pecans evenly in 9 x 9-inch pan.
In saucepan, combine brown sugar and butter.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Boil for 7 minutes.
Pour hot mixture over nuts.
Sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Cover so chocolate chips melt.
Spread chocolate evenly.
Slice when warm or refrigerate and break into pieces.
Peel and core apples.
Slice apple in quarters.
In a pan add water and apples.
Cook over low heat.
Lightly mash apples; add cinnamon and stir.
Serve chunky warm or cold.
Heat strawberries and jello together; let cool.
Mix instant pudding, milk, sour cream and Cool Whip together.
Place in dish a layer of wafers, layer of pudding and then layer of strawberries. Put another layer of wafers and strawberries; top with pudding. Keep cool!
Cook until thick.
Cool; pour over slaw.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans.
In a large mixer bowl, beat the sugar, butter, eggs and vanilla for about 5 minutes.
Add water, whole wheat flour, cocoa, baking soda, salt, ginger and white of orange rind.
Beat until blended.
Pour into pans.
Bake 28 to 33 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes.
Remove from pan. Cool completely.
Can be eaten plain or with a white frosting. The more adventurous might try a coconut frosting.
Combine all together and cook for 1 hour.
Drain fat and cover top with ketchup and brown top.
If using cheese, brown top after adding catsup.

Cook hamburger and drain. Add taco seasoning, peppers, mushrooms and onions and cook until mixed well (about 5 minutes. Cover bottom and sides of baking dish with tortillas. Layer meat mixture, cheese, and salsa. Top with tortillas and layer again. Bake in 350° oven cheese is melted.
Cook until thickening.
Pour into cooked, cool pie crust.
Combine milk, bread, onion, egg and salt.
Add hamburg.
Form into patties (will be very moist).
Brown in a skillet, then put into a casserole.
Pour soup over the meatballs.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Mix shrimp, garlic, chili sauce and hot sauce.
Cover and refrigerate for several hours.
Cut bacon slices into halves. Cook bacon until limp; drain.
Wrap each shrimp with a bacon piece; secure with a toothpick.
Set oven to broil.
Broil until bacon becomes crisp.
Mix all ingredients together.
Pour in a greased and floured 13 x 9-inch pan and bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes or until done.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In an 8 x 12-inch baking pan, melt butter.
In large bowl or in blender container, combine 1 cup sugar, flour, milk and baking powder.
Mix well.
Pour mixture over butter in baking pan; do not stir.
Arrange peaches on top.
Chop cabbage into small pieces.
Drain French-cut green beans.
Bring water to a boil.
Add bouillon cubes, cabbage, onions, celery, green beans and tomatoes.
Cook (in large pot) until cabbage is tender.
This soup is called "Negative Calorie" because you will burn more calories making and eating this soup than are contained in the soup.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in cranberry sauce and undrained pineapple and finely chopped water chestnuts.
Stir in with coarsely chopped walnuts.
Pour into mold and chill until firm.
In covered pan, bring beans to boil until skins start to crack.
Drain.
Add water to cover beans.
Add garlic.
Heat large knife on fire until hot.
Bang and fold salt pork until it becomes a paste texture, keeping knife hot.
Add salt pork to beans.
Add black and red pepper.
Dash of salt is optional.
Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add rice to beans.
Cook 25 minutes.
Place pretzels in bottom of a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt oleo and 3 tablespoons sugar and pour over pretzels.
Bake at 400° for 8 minutes.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese, rest of sugar and Cool Whip and spread over pretzels.
Mix jello according to directions on box. Let partially jell.
Add apples and pecans.
Pour over casserole mixture and refrigerate to set.
Mix all ingredients well.
Spray muffin tins with Pam.
Bake at 375° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Melt margarine in a small nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and basil; saute 2 minutes or until lightly toasted; set aside.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan; cook over medium heat until cheese melts, stirring often.
To serve, transfer dip to a chafing dish.
Serve warm with tortilla chips.
Yield:
5 3/4 cups.
Mix first 3 ingredients and cool.
Add remaining ingredients. Refrigerate until set.
Mix melted margarine and pretzels in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 10 minutes at 400°.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese and sugar.
Add Cool Whip and put over cooled pretzels.
Heat pineapple juice to boiling and dissolve jello in juice.
Add frozen strawberries and cool until starts to gel.
Pour over pretzels.
Fry bacon in skillet; remove and drain.
Saute onion and green pepper in two tablespoons drippings.
Add mushrooms, hominy and remaining ingredients to skillet.
Simmer for a few minutes, until cheese is melted, stirring often.
Put mixture in baking dish and top with crumbled bacon.
Bake at 350° for at least 20 minutes, until bubbly.
Dissolve sugar in boiling water.
Stir in orange juice and next 3 ingredients.
Pour mixture into a large, plastic container, then freeze until firm.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill overnight.
Serve with your favorite vegetables or chips.
Mix together; add enough flour to make a stiff dough.
Roll out each time for 1 layer at a time.
Cut out with a pie pan.
Put in a greased pan and bake.
Will make 5 layers of cake.
Put cooked apples or apple butter between layers.
Cook pasta according to package directions, rinse and drain. Mix together.
Refrigerate several hours before serving.

recipes.t: Pacific Northwest Barbecue For Salmon, Steelhead Or Trout
d: Salmon/steelhead fillet or steak, cut out fins.
In Dutch oven, brown meat with garlic and chopped onion. Drain off grease.
Drain and coarsely chop the tomatoes.

Reserve juice. Add tomatoes, juice, picante sauce, cumin, salt and pepper to meat mixture. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Add corn and beans. Cover and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes. Serve with additional picante sauce.
One dish dinner needs only a pan of cornbread or nacho chips.
Fry sausage until done.
Pour off oil.
Add pepper and water, onion, tomatoes and paste.
Let simmer for 20 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook until done.
If it's too thick, add water until desired consistency.
Serve hot over rice.
Mix everything together, except the flour and soda.
Boil 5 minutes.
Cool.
When cool, add the flour and soda, sifted together.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes in 350° oven.
Layer ingredients in order given in a large pot.
Simmer on low for 1 to 2 hours, according to amount you have in pot.
Do not overcook.
Do not let potatoes go to mush.
Meat will flavor the whole pot of vegetables.
When potatoes are tender, it is ready! Serve with cornbread.
Very convenient and very good!
Sprinkle sugar, water, cinnamon and nutmeg over apples in loaf pan.
Mix oleo, flour and brown sugar together and top apples. Bake at 325° for 50 minutes.
Stir together mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar.
Stir in broccoli, and grapes.

Mix dry ingredients with 1/2 cup water to make a smooth paste. Add paste slowly to 1 1/2 cups boiling water, stirring constantly until the mixture is thick and bubbly (approximately 10 minutes). Remove from heat and stir in eggs.
Heat wieners in hot water.
Score through center.
Add 1/2 slice of cheese.
Dip tortilla in hot fat.
Place wiener in tortilla and add sauce.
Roll up and secure with toothpick. Deep-fry until crisp.
Serve with refried beans.
Pour hot water in blender with gelatin.
Blend.
Add pineapple and blend for 3 minutes.
Add sweetener and flavorings.
Slowly add powdered milk.
Blend well, pour into 9-inch pie pan.
Sprinkle with cinnamon, refrigerate.
Saute celery and onion until tender.
Mix with other ingredients, adding broth until desired consistency is reached. Bake, uncovered, 45 minutes in 350° oven.
Fold crabmeat into white sauce.
Roll into round cake shapes. Dip into egg and milk mixture, roll in "Shake and Blend" flour. Roll in Italian flavored bread crumbs.
Deep fry until brown.
Boil chicken and remove from broth and bone.
Skim fat from broth.
Add next 8 ingredients plus oregano.
Cook until potatoes are tender.
Add vermicelli noodles.
Cook on low for 1 hour.
Add water to broth as needed.
Serve with Parmesan cheese.
Peel and slice carrots. Place in saucepan with water and salt. Cook on medium heat until almost done. Add sugar, butter and ginger. Simmer until most of the liquid is gone.
Serve hot.
Cream butter, sugar and egg together until fluffy.
Mix in vanilla.
In separate bowl, stir together flour, soda, baking powder and salt.
Add to creamed mixture alternately with sour cream.
Stir in dates and nuts.
Drop by a rounded teaspoonful onto greased baking sheets.
Bake in a 400° oven for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove immediately to wire racks and let cool.
Spread with frosting. Makes about 3 1/2 dozen.

Melt butter in saucepan over low heat. Remove from heat and add sugar and mix well. Stir in eggs, then sift dry ingredients into mixture. Mix in chocolate chips and nuts. Cook in a greased 13 x 9-inch pan for 30 to 35 minutes at 350°. Cool in pan and cut when cooled.
In a food processor, smoothly puree fish, adding eggs one at a time.
Pour in cream with motor running.
(If using a blender, smoothly puree fish and eggs; scrape container sides.
Add cream with motor running.)
If making ahead, cover and chill up to 3 hours.
In saucepan, combine soup, milk, onions and mustard.
Cook and stir until smooth and heated through.
Remove from heat.
Stir in cheese until melted.
Pour 1 cup of sauce into each of two 10 x 6 x 1 1/2-inch baking dishes.
Break 6 eggs into sauce in each casserole.
Carefully spoon remaining sauce around eggs.
Stand bread slices around outside edge of casseroles.
Bake in a 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes, until eggs are set.
Garnish with parsley.
Dice the cabbage and onions.
Dice sausage.
In skillet, brown sausage.
Add cabbage and onions to sausage.
Season with soy sauce and a pinch of pepper.
Cook all ingredients until cabbage is cooked.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Stir in brown sugar.
Cook and stir 2 minutes.
Cool to lukewarm.
Put in mixing bowl.
Add sugar and vanilla.
Beat until of spreading consistency.
Put on cool cake.
Cook noodles and drain according to directions on box.
Mix with celery and bell pepper (diced), pickles, tuna and Miracle Whip.
Salt as needed.
Better served chilled.
Mix yeast, water and 1 cup flour; set aside.
Beat eggs well; add flour, mixing thoroughly.
Add yeast mixture, cheeses and pepperoni.
Pour mixture in a greased (spray with Pam) Bundt pan. Let rise 1 hour.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except for Swiss or Cheddar cheese and broccoli.
Add well drained broccoli and mix well.
Make into balls using ice-cream scoop (this can be frozen at this time).
Bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove and add cheese (if you like, you can also add cracker crumbs or onion rings at this time).
Place back in oven and bake until cheese is melted.
I usually make half of mine with Cheddar and half with Swiss cheese.
You can also make this into a casserole instead of the balls.
Makes 12.
Spray 9x13-inch glass baking dish with non-stick spray.
Put bread in pan.
In a bowl, whisk eggs, add mustard and stir, then add milk and pepper and stir.
Pour over the bread.
Top with chopped ham, onion, green pepper, and cheese.
Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours or over night.
Cook ham hock until soft.
Trim off all fat.
Cook all vegetables separately.
Mix together with cubed ham.
Heat and serve.
Good luck!
Heat cheese soup and cream cheese until soft; add bacon, spinach and all other seasonings.
Hollow out a loaf of round rye bread.
Put spinach dip (hot) into loaf for serving.
Cut the bread you hollowed out into pieces for dipping into dip.
Cook pasta as directed; drain and let cool.
In large bowl, combine pasta and cut up vegetables.
Pour dressing over pasta combination.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving to marinate.
Drain cherries; add juice and milk until thick.
Fold in cream, cherries and nuts.
Pour in pie shell and chill!

recipes.t: Low-Fat Chicken And Rice Soup(Serves 6 To 8)
d: Combine broth and uncooked rice. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 40 to 45 minutes. Stir in onions and carrots and cook for 5 more minutes. Combine
milk, flour and pepper. Stir into rice mixture.
Cook and stir until slightly thickened and bubbly. Cook and stir 1 minute more. Stir in sherry. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives before serving.
Cube raw potatoes.
Place in saucepan.
Add butter.
Add remaining ingredients and pour over this just enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil; lower heat and cook until potatoes are done.
Above all, don't disturb, stir or mix.
Let potatoes soak up flavor and juices which will thicken to nice consistency.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place on greased cookie sheet and flatten slightly.
Cookies should be about 5-inches in diameter.
Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Makes a huge amount.
Drain vegetables and mix.
Bring last three ingredients to a boil.
Pour over vegetables; refrigerate.
Heat soup and large cream cheese together, then beat until smooth.
Add gelatin (softened first in 3 tablespoons water).
Add celery, mayonnaise, green onions and crab.
Pour into mold. Chill.
Pour boiling water over oats.
Let stand 20 minutes.
Beat butter until creamy.
Gradually add sugar and beat until fluffy. Blend in vanilla and eggs.
Stir in oats.
Sift together flour, soda, salt and spices and add to creamed mixture.
Mix well.
Pour into greased and floured 9-inch square pan.
Bake in preheated oven at 350°
for 50 to 55 minutes.
Do not remove from pan.
Sprinkle soda on dates; pour hot water over.
Cream the butter and sugar together.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Mix flour and salt; add to egg mixture.
Stir in date mixture; mix well.
Drop from a spoon onto greased cookie sheet.
Bake in a 350° oven until brown.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Blend in relish, chill until partially set.
Beat together cream cheese and sour cream.
Blend in cottage cheese and nuts.
Fold cream cheese mixture into gelatin.
Pour into a 4 cup mold.
Chill until set.
Unmold on bed of lettuce.
Place the unpeeled bananas in a shallow baking pan.
Bake the bananas in a 325° oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until a fork will pierce the bananas easily.
To serve, make 2 lengthwise slits, 1/2 to 3/4-inch apart, through the peel of each banana.
Remove the peel between the slits.
Sprinkle each banana with a little lemon or lime juice and a little brown sugar.
Top each banana with a few finely chopped peanuts.
Makes 4 servings.
Combine and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Combine first 8 ingredients.
Add chicken breasts.
Coat well and refrigerate overnight.
Remove chicken and roll in cracker crumbs.
Arrange in shallow pan.
Pour 1/4 of margarine over chicken and bake at 1 hour at 300°.
Spoon rest of margarine over chicken and bake 45 minutes more.
Bring Carnation milk, sugar, margarine and salt to boil and boil 4 1/2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from stove and pour over the Marshmallow Creme, nuts, chocolate and chocolate chips.
Stir with large spoon continuously until all chocolate is melted.
Add vanilla.
Pour into buttered pans and refrigerate until firm.
Combine all ingredients and cook over low heat until cheese is melted and mixed well.
Serve with tortilla chips.
Peel pears and crush enough to make 8 cups.
Combine crushed pears with the other ingredients.
Simmer until thickened.
Put in hot jars and seal.
Chop beef in very small pieces.
Brown meat with onion, carrots, peppers and celery.
Scramble eggs very dry.
Add this mixture together with cooked rice.
Then, add remaining ingredients.
Mix cottage cheese, jello and pineapple.
Add Cool Whip. Sprinkle with ground nuts.
Chill.
In freezer container, dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Stir in the cold water and sherbet until combined.
Freeze for 4 hours or until set.
Remove from freezer 45 minutes before serving.
For each serving, place 1 cup of slush mixture in a glass; add 1/3 cup ginger ale.
Yields 8 servings.
Mix together and keep refrigerated.
Dice bacon and fry until crisp.
Set aside.
Shape beef into tiny balls.
Cook in bacon fat until brown.
Remove.
Slice onion and dice pepper.
Cook until lightly brown.
Add beans, tomato soup,
chili powder, macaroni, salt and Accent.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Grate cheese.
Add and stir until cheese melts.
Add bacon and meat balls.
Simmer 15 minutes. Serves 6.
Delicious with corn bread.
Dissolve gelatin and salt in boiling water.
Blend in sour cream, mayonnaise, lemon juice, onion and horseradish; chill until thickened.
Fold in salmon and dill weed.
Spoon into mold.
Chill until firm at least 3 hours.
Unmold.

Cook 3 minutes longer.
Serves 6.
Toast and butter bread.
Break bread into casserole dish.
Mix all ingredients and add to bread.
Bake at 350° until done (about 1 hour).
Mix and bake cake according to package directions.
Punch holes in cake.
Combine 1 1/2 cups sugar and 1 cup Pet milk. Bring to a rolling boil.
Boil for 1 minute.
Stir in marshmallows and coconut.
Spread over hot cake.
Bring 1/2 cup Pet milk, 1 1/2 cups sugar and butter to a full boil boiling for 1 minute.
Then add chocolate chips and almonds and spread over coconut mixture.
Cut 1-inch thick slices from top of pineapple, leaving green leaves on top.
Reserve top.
With curved knife, cut out fruit from shell, leaving 1/2-inch wall.
Cut fruit into cubes, removing any fibrous core.
Place olive in curve of each shrimp; skewer with plastic pick.
Place pineapple cube on pick.
Stir together sour cream, curry powder and salt.
Place in custard cup in pineapple shell.
Cover with reserved pineapple top.
Attach shrimmp and pineapple cubes in spiral design to shell of pineapple.
Serve immediately or cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Serves 6.
Place 4 chicken breasts (halved and boned, 8 fillets) in mayonnaise coated casserole dish.
Cover with slices of Swiss cheese.
Mix 1 can cream of mushroom soup with 1/4 cup sherry or wine; pour over chicken and cheese.
Cover top with bread crumbs or croutons and dot with butter.
Bake at 325 degrees for 3/4
to 1 hour.
Melt marshmallows, oil and margarine; pour over other ingredients.
Press into Bundt or angel food pan (greased).
Let set 1 to 2 hours.
Turn out on tray.
Line pan with pastry and brush with egg whites, beaten. Combine eggs, vanilla, sugar and salt.
Add milk; mix well.
Pour in pie crust.
Sprinkle nutmeg on top.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes at 350°.
Brown hamburger.
Season with salt, pepper, garlic powder and oregano to your taste.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Combine 1/2 of mixture to cooked spaghetti.
Cook beef until tender; add chopped vegetables.
Add 1 tablespoon of cornstarch, dissolved in 1 cup of cold water.
Add 1 teaspoon of salt and a dash of black pepper.
Start with a good portion of love, stir in a few smiles and one or two good belly laughs.
Add a pinch of each: understanding, cheerfulness, compassion, a prayer or two or three and honesty.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Beat eggs; add all the other ingredients.
Stir in broccoli.
Top with 1 stick margarine. Sprinkle 1 stack Ritz crackers on top.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Arrange jams in 1 1/2-quart casserole.
In medium bowl combine orange juice and cornstarch; stir until cornstarch is completely dissolved.
Blend in brown sugar and butter.
Add walnuts and pour over yams.
Microwave at High (10) for 10 to 12 minutes.
Arrange marshmallows on top and microwave at High (10) for 1 to 2 minutes. Rotate casserole 1/4 turn after 45 seconds.
Total Microwave Cooking Time:
11 to 14 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Let raisins stand in boiling water; drain.
Combine raisins, carrots, apples and walnuts.
Divide equally into three individual molds.
Dissolve gelatin in hot water; add cold water.
Pour over mixture in the molds.
Chill until firm.
Serve on crisp lettuce leaf.
Yield:
3 servings.
Carbohydrate 11 g, protein 1 g, fat 4 g, calories 84.
One serving = 1 fruit exchange, 1 fat exchange.
Combine all ingredients until well blended.
Form into a ball. Chill.
Cook carrots until just tender.
In a covered 2 1/2 to 3-quart dish, break up spaghetti and add 4 cups water with about 1 tablespoon oil.
Place in microwave for 10 minutes on High.
Pour into colander and rinse with cold water. Leave draining while preparing sauce.
In a bowl thin the mayo with the dressing.
Add remaining ingredients, except peanuts.
Toss to coat with dressing.
Add the peanuts just before serving.
Makes 4 servings.
Fill a 9 x 13-inch greased baking dish 1/2 to 3/4 full with cooking apples.
Mix 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon; sprinkle over apples.
Mix brown sugar, cooking oats, flour and melted margarine in amounts stated, then press and place over apple mixture.
Bake in a 350° oven until brown.
If desired, can serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Mix dry ingredients and cut in shortening.
Add milk and yeast.
Cover and refrigerate until cold.
Roll out on floured surface and cut out.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes.
Toss potatoes and green beans together.
Combine vinegar, onion, salt, sugar and dill.
Pour over potatoes and toss to coat evenly.
Cover and chill to blend flavors.
Add chopped eggs, sour cream and pimento and toss lightly.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix gelatin (water and pineapple juice to equal 2 cups) and pour into a 9 x 13 x 2-inch dish.
Add pineapple and blueberry filling.
Let congeal in refrigerator.
Combine other ingredients and spread over congealed mixture, chill and serve.
Keep refrigerated.
Add all together.
Pour into graham cracker crust and chill overnight.

recipes.t: Florida Raisin Pie(Miami Senior High Home Ec. Class, 1944)
d: Add juices, water, sugar and salt to raisins.
Cook together 5 minutes.
Moisten cornstarch in a little water and add to hot mixture, stirring constantly.
Cook until thick, always stirring. Cool.
Fill 9-inch unbaked pie crust and adjust top crust.
Bake at 425° for 15 minutes and then 350° for 25 minutes.
Sift together flour and salt.
Work in the shortening, using fingertips, 2 knives, a fork or special pastry blender.
The mixture should be of the consistency of coarse meal.
Take care not to work it to a smooth greasy paste.
Add water to make a dough that will just hold together, mixing lightly.
This amount is sufficient for a double crust pie.

Cook 4-5 c rice. Slice thawed chicken into edible pieces or thaw and peel shrimp. Cook meat in oiled wok or other pan thoroughly; set aside. Beat eggs, cook with oil in scrambled fashion; set aside. Fry vegetables in oil until desired tenderness; set aside.

Into a large bowl half filled with cold water, coarsely shred potatoes and small onion. In a colander lined with a clean towel or cheesecloth, drain shredded potatoes and onion. Wrap potatoes and onion in towel. Squeeze towel to remove as much water as possible. In the same large bowl, beat eggs. Add the shredded potatoes and onion, flour, salt and pepper. Toss together until well mixed. In 12-inch skillet over medium heat in hot salad oil, drop mixture by scant 1/4 cupfuls into 4 mounds. With pancake turner, flatten each mound to make a 4-inch pancake. Cook until golden brown on one side. This is about 4 minutes. Turn and brown on the other side. Remove to paper towel-lined cookie sheet to drain. Keep warm. Repeat to make about 12 more pancakes, stirring mixture occasionally. Garnish with parsley sprigs or sour cream.
Melt caramels, butter, milk and flavoring in top of a double boiler.
Dip marshmallows in mixture of cereal and nuts.
Put on wax paper to dry.
Shred cabbage.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Layer cabbage, sauerkraut, ground beef, onion, rice, tomato soup, salt, pepper and Parmesan cheese.
Layer until pan is full.
Pour a can of water over the top.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Fry bacon until crisp and remove from skillet.
Crumble; set aside.
In bacon drippings, blend in flour.
Slowly add milk, stirring to make a smooth sauce.
Add salt, pepper and chopped onion.
Cook spinach following directions.
Add cream sauce and let simmer until thick (5 to 8 minutes).
Serve and top with crumbled bacon.
Cook broccoli; drain water, then add other ingredients.
You may refrigerate until needed.
Then bake in an uncovered, greased 8 x 8-inch dish for 30 minutes at 350°.
Mix
all
ingredients well.
Add a little more water or broth, if
needed,
to make a thick soupy consistency.
Add a can
of cream of chicken soup.
Pour into a greased casserole dish and bake at 350° for 1 hour or until brown.

recipes.t: Cornish Game Hen Flambe("An Elegant Dinner - Easy")
d: Remove giblets and discard.
Season inside of hens with salt and pepper.
Cut bacon in half and lay across hens.
Put flour into large bowl.
Mix oil and milk together, then pour into flour while mixing with a spoon.
Add more flour or milk, if needed, to get a stiff, not sticky dough.
In large bowl, beat eggs lightly.
Add remaining ingredients except bacon and cheese.
Mix well. Press into 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Top with bacon.
Bake for 60 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven.
Place cheese slices on top and continue baking until cheese is slightly melted, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Boil cleaned potatoes until tender.
Remove skin and mash potatoes.
Mash mixed potatoes and yogurt.
Cut jalapeno pepper into two halves.
In a skillet, warm the oil and add pepper.
This makes a sizzling sound.
Add this to the potato-yogurt mixture. Add salt and mix again.
Wash cilantro, dry and mince.
Add cilantro to potato mixture.
Refrigerate or serve at room temperature.
(Substitute cut tomatoes or peeled, grated cucumbers for the potatoes.
Or use steamed bell pepper, omitting jalapeno pepper.)
Cook spaghetti (or use leftovers).
Wash, drain and cool.
Add cut-up vegetables, cut rather small.
Add Salad Supreme seasoning and Italian salad dressing.
Marinate overnight.
Make gelatin according to the package.
Drain pineapple, use it as part of the water for the gelatin.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Grind cranberries and orange.
Add celery and add sugar to this.
Let stand until sugar is well dissolved.
Then add this to the gelatin and add the walnuts.
Mix all the ingredients together and put in casserole dish. Mix 1 roll Ritz crackers with 1 stick melted margarine and sprinkle over mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix ingredients together.
Divide into 2 parts.
Shape each part into a roll.
Roll in wax paper and chill overnight.
Slice thin and bake at 350°.
Drain cooked raisins.
Mix together the remaining ingredients and blend in raisins.
Beat well.
Pour in unbaked pie shell. Bake at 325° for 25 minutes.
Spread butter on bread.
Sprinkle lightly and evenly with oregano, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Cover with grated Mozzarella cheese.
Beat egg.
Add rest of ingredients and mix.
Grease large sheet pan.
Bake at 350° for 15 to 17 minutes (no longer, cake will not brown).
Remove cake from oven; wait 1 minute and spread with peanut butter (the heat from the cake will melt peanut butter and make it easier to spread).
Refrigerate until cake is cooled.
Melt chocolate and spread on top of peanut butter.
Score chocolate while still soft (for size of cuts).
Refrigerate.
Mix eggs, milk, sweetener and salt together.
Pour into an already made pie shell.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Beat first 6 ingredients together until smooth.
Dip vegetables in tempura batter and cook in hot oil until brown.
Cream margarine.
Add egg yolk, sugar and vanilla and beat well.
Sift dry ingredients and add to the creamed mixture.
Then cut cherries and add to the mix.
Next, add chopped nuts, chocolate chips and coconut.
Use hands to mix and form a ball. Then pat onto cookie sheet.
I use a rolling pin to flatten out even.
Bake 20 minutes on ungreased 10 x 15 x 1-inch cookie sheet at 375°.
Cool, then cut into squares.
Cook hamburger
or
sausage until done; save 1/3 to 1/2 of the grease.
The
grease is the secret to good gravy sauce. Mix flour and
milk
mixture and make a roux.
Add to meat and grease.
Cook until
the
thickness
is what you want and has turned lightly brown.
Season
to
taste.
You can add to the flavor with chicken bouillon cubes.
Serve over biscuits.
Combine crushed Oreos and melted oleo.
Pat into a 10-inch pie plate or square pan.
Melt chocolate in 1 tablespoon oleo.
Add sugar and milk.
Cook until thick; cool.
Place coffee ice cream over crust.
Add cooled sauce.
Add Cool Whip and sprinkle with nuts on top.
Serves 8 to 10.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Core apples; pare a thin slice of peel from the stem end.
Place apples, pared side up, in a shallow 2-quart baking pan.
In a small bowl, combine raisins, walnuts, 3 tablespoons apple juice and 3 teaspoons of cinnamon.
Spoon an equal amount of mixture into apple cavities.
Combine 1 cup apple juice and remaining 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon.
Pour over apples. Dot tops with butter.
Bake, covered, until apples are tender, 30 to 40 minutes.

Combine soup, milk, pepper. Arrange alternate layers of potatoes, onions, cheese and soup. Dot with butter, sprinkle with paprika. Bake covered at 375° for one hour. Uncover, and bake for another 15 minutes.

Sift together flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and baking soda. Combine margarine, sugar substitute, vanilla and egg until creamy. Add flour mixture and applesauce alternately to creamed mixture.
Fold in raisins and bran cereal.
Drop on nonstick cookie sheet 1-inch apart.
Bake 15 minutes at 375°.
In a skillet, cook sausage until browned; drain off fat. Separate crescent dough into 8 triangles; place in ungreased 12-inch pizza pan with points toward center.
Press over bottom and up sides to form a crust; spoon sausage over crust.
Sprinkle with potatoes; top with Cheddar cheese.
In a bowl, beat eggs, milk, salt and pepper; pour into crust.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over all.
Bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
Let Crisco melt (not hot).
Remove from heat.
Add sugar and 2 teaspoons mint extract.
Knead; may add drops of water.
Divide and add colors.
Roll in balls and use fork or glass to flatten.
Drain beans.
Cut onions, peppers and pimentos into thin strips.
Mix together.
Mix oil, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper. Pour over beans and leave overnight.
Stir and serve.
Melt margarine and cool.
Add brown sugar and vanilla and beat in eggs, one at a time.
Sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Add to sugar mixture, stirring well, then add chocolate chips and pecans, mixing well.
Bake in a 13 x 9-inch greased and floured pan at 350° for about 25 minutes (underbake).
Cool and cut into squares.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease casserole dish and layer meat, potatoes, carrots, celery and onions.
Sprinkle with salt. Combine soups.
Spoon on top of casserole.
Top with ginger ale. Cover and bake for 3 hours.
Mix well and chill at least 2 to 4 hours.
A great complement to summer's hot dogs and hamburgers.
If cake mix has pudding in it, omit the instant pudding and use 3 eggs instead of 4 and 1/3 cup oil instead of 1/2.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube or a 12-inch Bundt pan.
Sprinkle nuts over bottom of pan.
Mix rest of ingredients. Pour over nuts.
Bake 1 hour.
Cool and invert over plate.
Prick top and spoon and brush glaze on top and sides.
Allow cake to absorb glaze slowly.
Repeat until all glaze is used.
Melt butter in large heavy skillet over medium heat. Add all ingredients except parsley and French bread. Cook about 10 minutes; add parsley. Serve with toasted French bread. Yield: 4 servings.
Mix ingredients well and fry on a greased griddle.
When starts to bubble, turn pancake over.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Roll out half of dough and line 9-inch buttered pie pan.
Saute peppers and ham in oil 3 minutes; season with pepper.
Whisk 2 eggs and Ricotta in large bowl.
Spread mixture in pastry shell.
Pat spinach dry.
Sprinkle on top. Sprinkle saute mix over spinach and top with Mozzarella.
Add basil.
Roll out remaining dough and cover pie.
Trim edges.
Cut 4 vents and brush top with beaten egg.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes or until golden brown.
Set 20 minutes and serve.
Chop peppers (do not remove seeds).
In large pot, combine peppers (with seeds), mustard, vinegar, salt and sugar.
Bring to a boil.
Combine 1 1/2 cups water with 1 1/2 cups flour (I use a quart jar and add 1 ice cube to flour/water mixture and shake well).
Add to other ingredients.
Bring to a boil; boil 5 minutes (STIRRING CONSTANTLY).
Pour into hot jars (canning jars, following canning directions).
Boil crushed pineapple and sugar for 5 minutes; cool.
Bake cake according to directions.
While still hot, spread cooked pineapple on top.
Sprinkle instant pudding on top of pineapple "dry."
Cover cake with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with pecans and coconut.
Good!
Drain pineapple; place juice in a small saucepan. Add to the juice the sugar, flour and egg. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth and thickened. Let cool.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks one at a time.
Add 2 cups flour to baking powder alternately with orange juice.
Save 1 cup flour to mix with fruit.
Beat egg whites and add last with coconut.
Bake at 325° for approximately 2 hours.
Make 2 cakes in tube pan or 2 loaf cakes.
Mix all ingredients together (except egg whites) and beat well.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour into a buttered casserole and place in a pan of hot water.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
This has been a long time favorite.
Heat soup, cream cheese, milk and butter.
Mix in hash browns. Bake at 350°
for 30 to 35 minutes.
Sift together flour, sugar, soda, salt, cinnamon and allspice. Combine eggs, pie filling and oil; add vanilla.
Stir in flour mixture and mix well.
Stir in dates and nuts.
Pour into greased and floured pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Add boiling water to package of jello and stir well.
Add cold water and pineapple juice.
Chill until partially set, about an hour.
Add remaining ingredients and chill until firm.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Melt butterscotch and chocolate pieces in double boiler. Cool.
Add remaining ingredients.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on wax paper covered cookie sheet.
Place in refrigerator to set, about 2 hours.
Makes 2 to 3 dozen.

Heat oven to 350°. Grease bottom and sides of a 9 inch springform pan. Melt chocolate morsels and margarine in a large saucepan over low heat; cool slightly. Stir in oats, flour and brown sugar. Mix well. Press firmly onto bottom and 1 inch up side of pan. Bake 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan at 325° for about 1 hour.
Place potatoes on bottom and up sides of 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Bake, uncovered, at 400° for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, crumble beef in large bowl.
Cook on High 4 to 5 minutes; stir halfway through cooking time.
Drain well.
Stir in broccoli, 1/2 can Durkee onions, soup, milk, 1/2 cup cheese and spices.
Cook, uncovered, on High 6 minutes; stir halfway through.
Add tomatoes; spoon into potato lined casserole.
Cook, uncovered, on High 8 minutes; top with remaining cheese and onions.
Cook on High 1 minute.
Fry or bake pork chops, then spread them in a long casserole dish.
Put 1 slice of onion on each chop, then 1 whole tomato and a slice of bell pepper.
Spoon 1 tablespoon of rice on each chop. Pour juice from can of tomatoes over each chop.
Season to taste. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Makes a complete meal!!
Melt jello in two cups of boiling water.
Add cranberry sauce and mix well; add crushed pineapple (with juice) and chopped nuts. Mix well.
Add 1/2 cup cold water and mix.
Pour into bowl.
Heat oil and butter in skillet.
Dredge veal scallops in flour and sprinkle with salt and pepper on top.
Cook 2 minutes on each side on medium-high heat.
Remove from skillet; keep warm.
Prepare cake mix according to package, adding pudding mix and sour cream.
Add chocolate chips and nuts.
Pour into greased tube pan.
Bake using cake mix directions.
Cool and frost with chocolate fudge frosting.
Mix all ingredients together.
Marinate at least 2 hours.
All day works great!
Cook on grill, using marinade as baste.
In large bowl, cream oleo and sugars. Add eggs, milk and vanilla. Beat well. Combine dry ingredients and mix well.
Add to creamed mixture and mix well. Stir in water; mix until smooth. Pour in floured 13 x 9-inch pan. Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 350°. Dust with powdered sugar.
Butter a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix soup, rice and water in pan. Place raw chicken on top and sprinkle 1 package dry onion soup mix on top.
Cover with foil.
Cook for 2 hours at 350°.
Drain and flake salmon, removing skin and bones.
Combine salmon with cream cheese, lemon juice, onions, horseradish, salt and liquid smoke; mix thoroughly.
Chill several hours.
Combine pecans and parsley.
Shape salmon into an 8 x 2-inch log.
Roll into nut mixture.
Chill well.
Serve with crackers.
Dissolve gelatine in water.
Heat soup to boiling and pour in gelatine.
Take off heat; cool and stir in mayonnaise and remaining ingredients.
Pour in mold and refrigerate.
Melt the first 2 ingredients over low heat; set aside. Combine the rest and add to chocolate mixture.
Pour into a 9-inch pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 23 minutes (will be shiny on top).
Blend sugar, mustard and salt together in mixer bowl.
Add vinegar and mix at medium speed.
Slowly add oil.
Continue beating for 10 minutes.
Add celery seed, grated onion and food coloring.
Mix well.
Store in refrigerator.
Keeps well for several weeks.
Very good dressing for fruit or any salad.
Mix all ingredients together and serve fresh and chilled.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; drain. Alternate layers of macaroni and Cheddar and cottage cheese in greased 2-quart baking dish, beginning with macaroni and ending with cheese.
Melt the 1/4 cup butter in a saucepan; stir in flour to make a smooth mixture.
Blend in milk gradually.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Cook until sauce has thickened, about 2 minutes.
Add salt and pepper.
Pour sauce over macaroni and cheese.
Mix bread crumbs, if used, with melted butter. Sprinkle over macaroni and cheese.
Casserole may be covered and refrigerated at this point, if desired.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
If refrigerated, increase baking time by 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the first 6 ingredients.
Gently fold in blueberries.
Combine yogurt and buttermilk; stir into dry ingredients just until moistened.
Fill greased or paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full.
Bake at 400 degrees for 18 to 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes before removing from pan to wire rack.
Blend the first 3 ingredients well.
Chill for several hours. Shape into ball.
Roll in pecans and parsley. Wrap well and refrigerate.
Fry wings until brown and set aside.
Mix all other ingredients and toss in wings.
Brown hamburger meat and remove fat. Place in a pot and cook with vegetables and bouillon cubes for approximately 1 hour. Cover pot while cooking.
Trim steak of all fat and quickly dip into cold water.
Drain, but do not pat dry.
Apple Pam to a skillet; sear the steak on both sides over high heat.
Lower the heat to cook as desired, adding a little extra water as necessary.
Place the cooked steak on a warm serving platter while preparing the sauce.

recipes.t: Chop Suey Casserole Or Hamburger Hash
d: Brown ground beef, onion and celery; add soups, rice and soya sauce and water.
Bake for 1/2 hour in a covered casserole dish. Take cover off and top with chow mein noodles.
Continue cooking 1/2 hour, uncovered.
Serve hot.
Measure butter, dates and sugar into medium saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture becomes a soft paste.
