Remove from heat.
Add cereal and nuts, mixing thoroughly.
Portion by level measuring tablespoon onto waxed paper.
Shape into balls.
Let stand until set.
Makes about 3 1/2 dozen.
Cream and blend the Crisco, sugars, vanilla, eggs and cottage cheese.
Mix flour, baking powder, cocoa and soda and add to first mixture.
Mix well.
Chill for 1 hour.
Roll in balls, then in powdered sugar.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Melt butter, milk and cheese.
Drain corn.
Add garlic salt and peppers.
Bake until bubbly, 350°.
I substitute whole kernel corn for the Shoepeg when I don't have the Shoepeg and it's very good also.
Brown beef with pepper and onion.
Cook noodles until tender; add cream cheese and sour cream.
Layer beef, noodles and Ragu in a baking pan.
Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake 30 minutes until hot.
Serves 6 to 8.
Combine all ingredients in large saucepan.
Heat ingredients to boiling.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, until cabbage is crisp and tender.
Toss occasionally while heating for 5 minutes.
Cook, stirring until thickened.
Pour over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, stir together all ingredients except bread.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and combine well.
Assemble sandwiches and serve.
Cream butter; add next 3 ingredients and egg yolk.
Beat until light; add flour.
Mix well.
Wrap dough in waxed paper and chill. Make into 1-inch balls.
Dip into lightly beaten egg white.
Roll in almonds.
Grease cookie sheet.
Press center and fill with raspberry jam.
Bake at 300° for 20 minutes.
Cook applesauce, sugar and vinegar for 15 minutes.
Add gelatin and cook 5 minutes longer.
Cream the margarine, shortening and sugar together.
Whip 3 minutes to blend.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Alternately add flour, baking powder and milk to egg mixture.
Beat after each addition.
Add lemon, butter and vanilla flavorings.
Beat well.
Pour into floured and greased Bundt pan.
Bake at 325° for
1 hour.
Mix all together.
Sprinkle with 1/2 cup bread crumbs and 3 tablespoons melted butter.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch pan at 325° for 1 hour.
Make sure 1 hour.
Saute onion in 1/4 cup of oil.
Add carrot and simmer until the oil becomes nice and orange.
Add red pepper powder and sour cream.
Add salt to your liking.

recipes.t: Grilled Halibut, Cod Or Salmon Steaks
d: Place fish in a shallow baking dish.
Combine remaining ingredients and pour over fish.
Cover dish and refrigerate for 30 minutes, turning once.
Remove fish, reserve marinade for basting. Place fish on lightly oiled grill, 4 to 6-inches from moderately hot coals.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes or until fish flakes easily. Serves 4.
Mix first 4 ingredients to a smooth mixture and spread on tortillas.
Roll up and wrap in Saran Wrap.
Refrigerate.
When ready to use, slice like pinwheels and bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Mix sauce, brown sugar, onion and water
mixing bowl and set aside to warm to room temperature.
Bake at 275° for 1 1/2 hours.
Put toothpick or fork in middle. It's done when toothpick or fork comes out of cake clean.
Combine sugar and boiling water.
Stir and cool.
Add bananas and remaining ingredients.
Mix and freeze.
Take out 30 minutes before serving and use a knife to make into slush.
Makes 1 gallon and keeps frozen well.
Cover meat with water, 1 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon of pepper.
Simmer until tender, about 2 hours.
Remove meat.
Save broth.
Melt butterscotch morsels in microwave or double boiler.

Add peanut butter and almonds which have been toasted with a brushing of margarine. Drop by teaspoonful on waxed paper and let set. This makes a large batch which can be frozen for an indefinite period.
Cook macaroni, then add Italian dressing and chill 1/2 hour. Add mayo, olives, onions, salt, pepper and cheese.
Chill until needed.
Mix everything together and freeze in Tupperware.
Thaw until slushy and add 2 bottles ginger ale.
Cook the spaghetti in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain.
In a small skillet, heat the oil.
Add the garlic and quickly saute until garlic begins to brown.
Place spaghetti in a serving bowl.
Add the garlic and oil; toss.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serves 4.
In a plastic bag,
combine
corn
meal, flour, salt and pepper.
Cut okra into
1/2-inch slices and pour buttermilk or milk over okra and toss.
Place okra in plastic bag and shake. In a skillet, heat oil
and
add
okra.
Fry on moderate heat, turning frequently, until crispy
and
brown.
Drain
on paper towels.
Serve immediately.
Mix sour milk with soda.
Add sugar, salt and the softened yeast.
Add well beaten egg and margarine.
Add enough flour to make a firm dough.
Knead until smooth.
Let rise in warm place until double.
Punch dough down and shape into small balls.
Place in greased baking pan 1 inch apart.
Cover and let rise until double.
Bake in 425° oven for 20-25 minutes.
Makes 24 rolls.
Put milk, rice, sugar, lemon rind and salt in pot and simmer approximately 1 hour.
When rice is cooked, remove from stove and add the eggs, sugar and vanilla which have been mixed together. Stir constantly for 2 minutes.
Pour into serving dish and cool. When cool, refrigerate.
Place cooked ham on bottom of 9 x 13 pan.
Spread 2 cups cheese over ham. Add cooked noodles over mixture.
Add cream of mushroom soup mixed with 1 can of milk.
Put remaining cheese over top and bake in oven at 350° for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Pour in greased baking pan and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Put chocolate pieces, broken candy bar, Marshmallow Creme, butter and nuts into bowl.
Combine evaporated milk and sugar in saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to boil; cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and pour over other ingredients. Stir until chocolate has melted and mixture is smooth and glossy. Pour in ungreased 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Cool and cut into squares.
Whip cream cheese with milk.
Add rest of ingredients and mix.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix all ingredients, except crackers and cheese.
Place in ungreased 3-quart casserole dish.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with topping (crackers and cheese).
Bake, uncovered, in oven until cheese is melted.
Prepare mix as package directs for pudding. Fold in Cool Whip, miniature marshmallows and banana slices.
Line bottom and sides of a 10 x 6-inch baking dish with wafers.
Pour in pudding mixture. Garnish as desired.
In a large skillet over medium heat, brown meat in oil.
Drain. Sprinkle onions over meat.
Combine tomato sauce, picante sauce, cumin, oregano and garlic.
Pour over meat and onions.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer gently about 2 to 2 1/2 hours, adding green pepper during last 15 minutes of cooking.
Begin checking meat for tenderness after 1 hour and 45 minutes of cooking.
Remove meat to serving platter; keep warm.
Reserve 1/2 cup oyster liquid.	Season oysters with salts and peppers; frizzle in their own juice until slightly curled.	Set aside.
Melt butter in saucepan.
Add flour; blend.
Add onions; stir until onions are cooked.
Add oyster liquid.
Add milk 1 cup at a time, stirring constantly.
Cook about 10 minutes.
Add oysters.
Check for additional seasoning.
Sprinkle onion on top just before serving.
Serves 6-8.
Beat egg and set aside.
Mix together remaining ingredients. Refrigerate until cold.
Shape into balls; roll in crumbs, then in beaten egg.
Deep fry in fat until brown.
Mix beans, tomatoes, pepper and onion in a large bowl.
Right before serving, add corn chips and toss with dressing.
Combine water, butter, sugar and salt in a saucepan.
Heat to boil.
Add flour all at once, then over low heat beat with wooden spoon about 1 minute or until a smooth, thick dough.
Remove from heat.
Continue beating 2 minutes to cool slightly.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each until mixture has satiny sheen. Stir in raisins.
Drop heaping measuring tablespoons about 2 inches apart on greased sheet.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 to 35 minutes or until doubles.
Remove to wire rack.
Cool.
While still warm, spread frosting.
Makes 20.
Work fast and mix everything together. Add Cool Whip last. Refrigerate and serve.
Mix all ingredients, except avocado and Doritos.
Heat in a large pot (do not boil).
In a 13 x 9-inch casserole or cake pan (or large bowl), shred lettuce.
Then
add
the
rest of the ingredients in the order listed.
Cook beef for 2 1/2 hours, adding water as needed.
When the beef is tender, drain and shred. Add remaining ingredients and heat. Serve on a bun. Makes 6 sandwiches.
Makes 2 regular loaves.
Bake at 350° for about 40 to 50 minutes.
Slice squash and cook with onion (just to crisp; drain, if necessary).
Mix chicken soup, sour cream, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Melt butter and pour over 1/2 package of dressing.
Save some to sprinkle on top.
Place dressing in bottom of casserole dish.
Add squash and onions.
Top with sour cream mixture. Sprinkle with reserved dressing and Parmesan cheese, if desired. Bake at 350° until hot through.
Mix all ingredients.
Drop by spoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in a 350° oven for 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients except apples together in a large bowl and beat for 10 minutes on medium speed.
Grease tube pan.
Put 1 layer of batter, then one layer of apples and repeat this by making the top layer batter.
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Last 1/2 hour, cover with foil.
Mix together, sugar, flour, salt and soda.
Add melted butter, buttermilk and eggs.
Mix well and stir in pecans, dates and orange rind.
Pour into tube pan and bake 1 hour at 350°.
Pour sugar over shredded cabbage and let stand for several minutes.
Combine other ingredients in saucepan; bring to a boil. Pour boiling mixture over cabbage; let stand overnight before using.
This will keep for at least 10 days.
Store in a covered dish, but not a metal container.
This is very good with ham for a buffet dinner.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Don't overbake!

In medium bowl stir boiling water and jello together for at least 2 minutes. Stir in cold water. Refrigerate about 1 1/4 hours or until slightly thickened. Reserve a few oranges for garnish if desired. Gently stir in remaining oranges into thickened gelatin. In a separate bowl beat cream cheese and sugar with a wire whisk until well blended. Gently stir in 2 c. whipped topping. Spoon into large serving bowl, cover with gelatin mixture. Refrigerate 2 hours or until firm. Garnish with remaining whipped topping and reserved oranges.
Warm honey and oil in a saucepan until easily blended. Dissolve baking soda in buttermilk and add to the honey and oil mixture.
Beat eggs and add, in order, the remaining ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cool completely before slicing.
Beat egg white until stiff.
Gradually add vanilla and brown sugar.
Fold in pecans by hand and coat well.
Place on cookie sheet with pecan bottoms flat side down.
Bake at 225° for 30 minutes.
Mix thoroughly 1/4 cup soup, beef, bread crumbs, egg, onion, salt and 1/8 teaspoon each:
pepper, sage and thyme.
Shape firmly into 6 mini meat loaves in a skillet.
Brown loaves in shortening.
Pour off fat.
Stir in remaining soup and seasoning and water.
Cover; cook over low heat 20 minutes or until done. Stir occasionally.
Serves 6.
Squeeze the juice from 4 of the lemons, limes and oranges; pour into a gallon container.
Thinly slice the remaining fruit and set aside for garnish.
Add water and sugar to juices and mix well.
Chill garnish and serve on ice with fruit slice garnish.
Boil beans.
Stir 1/2 teaspoon sugar and salt while boiling. Cook 5 to 7 minutes; leave crispy.
Drain under cold water. Combine shallot, vinegar and salt.
Drizzle in olive oil; add beans and cilantro and toss to coat.
Sprinkle sesame seed on top.
Slice onions and separate into rings.
Saute until tender in 1 stick butter.
Place in casserole dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Melt other stick of butter and mix with crushed Ritz crackers.
Sprinkle buttered cracker crumbs over onions and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix well, bake at 350° until done.
Soften gelatin in water.
Bring cocoa, coffee, salt, sugar, milk and cold water to a boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat; add gelatin.
Cook until slightly thickened.
Beat the cooked mixture until smooth.
Beat cream.
Add vanilla.
Fold whipped cream into cooked mixture.
Pour into pie shell and top with nuts or shredded chocolate chips.
Mix all ingredients (except pie crust) together.
Place in a 10-inch pie plate.
Place top crust on.
Bake at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes, then slice.
Mix filling ingredients in the order given.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 350° in a preheated oven for 45 minutes to one hour or until knife inserted in center of pie comes out clean. Cool before serving.
Makes two pies.
Mix vanilla wafers, 2/3 cup peanuts and butter.
Put in 9 x 12-inch baking pan.
Bake for 10 minutes at 350°.
Arrange a layer of potatoes, layer of onion and another layer of potatoes in casserole.
Mix water and cream of mushroom soup; pour over layers of onion and potatoes.
Top with buttered bread crumbs.
Cook at 300° for 1 hour.
Yield:
8 servings.
Fry ham in bouillon soup until brown on one side.
Turn over and add honey on top of ham.
Continue to add enough bouillon soup to keep it from being dry.
Add coffee at the end of cooking. When all is done, there should be a brown sauce for top of ham.
Peel, quarter and core apples.
Wrap each piece in a roll. Press dough around apple to seal. Bring to a boil.
Mix orange juice, sugar and butter.
Place dumplings in ovenproof dish.
Pour juice mixture over dumplings and bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes. Serve with vanilla ice cream.
It's delicious!
Boil the turtle meat for 20 minutes.
Melt butter in a pot and cook the sliced garlic until browned.
Coat the cooked turtle meat with flour and add it to the pot along with the onion.
Cook the meat until browned.
Pour in the stock in which the turtle was boiled.
Simmer for several hours or until the meat is tender. Add potatoes, stir in the soup and cook an additional 30 minutes.
About 40 minutes before serving cut half of cheese into 6 slices; shred remaining cheese.
Make a 2 1/2-inch horizontal cut in meatier part of each chicken breast half to make a deep pocket. Place 1 slice of cheese in each.
On waxed paper, combine flour and salt.
In bowl, mix egg and milk; on another sheet of waxed paper place cornmeal.
Dip each chicken breast into flour, egg mixture and then in cornmeal.
In 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, in hot oil, brown chicken on both sides about 5 minutes; remove to plate.
To same skillet, add salsa, taco sauce and 1/3 cup water over high heat, heat to boiling.
Arrange chicken in sauce, reduce heat to low, simmer uncovered 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese and cook until cheese melts.
Serves 6.
Has 480 calories per serving, 22 grams fat, 147 mg. cholesterol and 1405 mg. sodium.
Put plastic wrap in bottom of bowl.
Smash lime sherbet on bottom and sides (rind).
Soften raspberry sherbet and mix with chocolate chips (fruit and seeds).
Put mixture in middle of bowl. Cover with plastic; freeze.
Turn upside down.
Put warm rag on bottom of bowl, remove bowl and slice.
Use warm water to dip knife for slices.
Preheat oven to 225°.
Tear dried beef into pieces and cover bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Wrap chicken with bacon and lay on top of the dried beef.
Salt and pepper to taste. Mix mushroom soup and sour cream.
Pour over chicken and sprinkle with paprika.
Cover with foil and bake at 225° for 2 hours. Uncover and bake one more hour.

Empty package of shredded cabbage and carrots into a large bowl. Add pepper and onions. In medium saucepan, combine sugar, oil, vinegar, celery seed, salt to taste and parsley flakes. Stir together over medium heat until sugar is dissolved. Pour hot dressing over cabbage. Cover and let stand overnight in the refrigerator. Yield: 8 servings.
Cook and debone chicken.
Mix stuffing direction from box with melted butter or margarine (reserve 1/3 dressing for the top).
Mix all ingredients together and put in greased casserole dish.
Cover with reserved dressing.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Combine all ingredients.
Pour in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Beat eggs in small bowl. Add raisins and vanilla and mix. Refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Combine sugar, water and vanilla in glass baking dish. Microwave, covered, on High for 5 minutes or until mixture boils. Peel and core pears; cut into halves.
Place in hot mixture. Microwave on High for 2 minutes.
Microwave on Medium for 5 minutes until pears are tender.
Cool.
Combine mint patties and cream in a small glass bowl; microwave on Medium for 2 minutes or until mints are melted.
Mix well.
Drain pears; place in serving dishes.
Top with chocolate mint sauce.
Serve with whipped cream or Cool Whip.
Yields 4 servings.
Combine canned chicken stock, cream of chicken soup and 2 cups water; set aside.
Cook all other vegetables and chicken until very tender; cut in small pieces.
Puree all vegetables and chicken breast in blender.
Add pureed vegetables and chicken breast to stock.
Simmer on low flame 1/2 hour.
Serve with garlic crackers or corn muffins.
Mix all together.
Pour over fish and marinate 30 minutes in refrigerator (if there is any leftover sauce from marinade, if you wish, boil it and use over the cooked swordfish).

Soak whole cucumbers in salt brine in crock (1 1/4 cups salt and cold water to cover). Let stand 3 days. On days 4 to 6, rinse daily with clear water. On the seventh day, cut in very thin slices and boil in a solution of 5 cups water, 3 tablespoons alum and 2 1/2 cups vinegar. Drain and cover with hot spiced vinegar made as follows: 3 pints vinegar and 7 pounds sugar and tie cinnamon and cloves in cheesecloth bag. Drop in solution. On days 8 to 10, reheat vinegar and pour over pickles. On eleventh day, seal in jars, covering with hot spiced vinegar. Makes 10 to 12 pints.
Mix everything except rice and pork chops.
Reserve 1 cup of liquid mixture; mix rice with remainder.
Place in casserole with meat on top.
Cover with remaining cup of liquid.
Bake 1 hour covered at 350°.
Uncover and bake another 15 minutes.

Heat oil; add carrots and stir 3 minutes. Add 1 cup water, sugar, vinegar and salt. Boil, covered, until carrots are tender. Blend and add cornstarch, 1/4 cup water and soy sauce and add to carrots. Stir and continue cooking 2 to 3 minutes until mixture thickens. Serve hot.
Combine tomato sauce, onion, water and beef bouillon; pour over roast in a deep casserole or baking dish.
Cover and bake 3 to 4 hours at 350°.
Turn roast over several times while it is baking.
Mix in small mixer bowl.
Spread on 12 English muffin halves. Quarter.
Broil about 5 minutes until browned.
If not wanting to use right away, freeze on flat pan.
Store in freezer bags.
Beat egg, sugar and salt until fluffy.
Blend in pumpkin. Sift together the dry ingredients.
Fold into egg mixture.
Add margarine and mix well.
Drop by heaping tablespoonfuls into greased frying pan.
Turn when golden, watching carefully. Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Can be served with dinner or as a dessert.
Mix first 4 items until smooth.
Then mix next three items. Bring to full boil.
Stir constantly.
Cool and refrigerate.
Vary sugar and/or vinegar to suit taste.
Combine sugar, butter and syrup in small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Pour syrup mixture into 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Place 6 slices of bread on top of syrup.
Top with remaining 6 slices of bread.
Gently stir together all ingredients and serve.
Makes about 2 cups.
If you use 2 pound ground meat, double your ingredients.
Boil 10 medium potatoes (diced).
Cover with water to 1/2 of the pot.
Boil until soft.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add milk almost to top of pot.
Bring to a boil again.
Mix about 2 tablespoons flour with a little milk to make a paste.
Pour into potato mixture.
Bring to a boil to thicken it.
Add 1/2 pint sour cream and dill weed, cut up fine.
Heat through; don't boil.
Add 3 tablespoons vinegar.
Mix tuna and cream of mushroom.
Boil noodles until tender. Mix noodles, tuna and soup together.
Put in casserole dish.
Bake at 350° until brown around the edges, approximately 20 minutes.
Mix mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder in a 2 1/2-quart bowl.
Add rice, pepper and shrimp; toss.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Spoon onto lettuce lined dish.
Garnish with cherry tomato halves and parsley.
Put the tomatoes and onion in a saucepan; bring to a boil. Add margarine, sugar, salt and oregano.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes.
Add bread and stir.
Pour into a 1 1/2-quart lightly greased casserole dish.
Top with grated cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 20 minutes or until cheese is melted.
In large skillet, crumble sausage.
Cook sausage, onion and celery until sausage is no longer pink.
Stir in pecans; cook until sausage is lightly brown.
Pour mixture into large roasting pan to mix.
Add corn, mushrooms, butter, sage and fruit.
Stir well until blended.
Stir in eggs, then mix in the cornbread.
Add broth and stir to mix.
Beat the eggs and add to mixture.
Let set for 15 to 20 minutes to absorb the liquid.
If moister dressing is desired, add more broth.
Bake in same roasting pan or transfer to two 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pans.
Bake in 400° oven for 30 to 40 minutes or until crusty brown on top.
Boil chicken breasts until tender; shred. Put shredded chicken in pot with chicken broth and water; add celery, carrots and onion. Season with garlic salt and pepper.

Bring to a boil. Make noodles by adding egg, oil, milk, salt and pepper to flour. Mix until not sticky. Roll dough on floured surface to about 1/4 inch thick. Cut into strips. Add to chicken broth. Cook on medium heat for 20 minutes.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add egg yolks and beat well.
Add flour, salt and lemon juice, rind and milk.
Blend well.
Beat egg whites until stiff; fold into lemon mixture.
Pour into pie shell. Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Cool and top with Cool Whip. Serves 8.
Sift dry ingredients together into bowl.
Mix together eggs, milk and oil.
Add, all at once, to dry ingredients and stir just to moisten.
Turn into greased 8-inch cake pan and bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Or, cook in glass pan in microwave on 50% power for 3 minutes; turn for last 3 minutes (6 minutes total).
Cook broccoli according to directions on package.
Cook soup and milk on medium heat until smooth. Drain broccoli after cooking and put into 1-quart buttered casserole dish.
Pour soup mixture on top. Crumble 1/2 package Ritz crackers and put on top of soup. Dot crackers with 1/8 stick margarine. Bake until golden at 375°, about 45 minutes.
Put 1 can French fried onions on top about 5 minutes before taking out of oven.
Have cured ham and fresh pork ground together.
In large bowl, to ground meat, add crackers and mix.
Add eggs and salt; mix.
Add milk until mixture will absorb no more.
Shape into loaf.
Put in roasting pan; pour water around loaf to about 1/2-inch.
Cover. Bake 3 hours at 325° to 350°.
Check about halfway through. May need to add water.
Cook cake according to directions in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cool. Mix next 3 ingredients together.
After cake is cool, spread pineapple over the cake, then spread the cheese/pudding mixture evenly over the pineapple.
Spread Cool Whip over next and scatter chopped nuts over all.
Drain pineapple; add marshmallows.
Mix cherries, sugar, salad dressing and cream cheese.
Mix well.
Fold in whipped cream.
Add nuts and coconut, if desired.
Chill and serve.
Soak gelatin in water.
Soften butter in top of double boiler. Add sugar, quartered marshmallows and egg yolks.
Take off stove; add gelatin.
Cool.
Add whipped cream and egg whites (beaten stiff).
Pour over peaches.
Line pan with vanilla wafer crumbs, saving a little for top of filling.
Let stand in refrigerator.
Cook broccoli 5 minutes and drain.
Mix everything.
Pour in 13 x 9-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle topping and dot with butter.
Bake at 350°.
Will serve at least 12 to 15.
Generously butter 12-cup ring cake dish; sprinkle with sugar to coat.
Spread half of pie filling in dish.
Mix remaining ingredients (including rest of filling).
Beat 3 minutes with mixer.
Pour into dish.
Cook at Medium 12 minutes, rotating every 3 minutes.
Increase power to High for 1 to 8 minutes or until cake springs back when lightly touched and begins to pull away from sides.
Let stand 10 minutes.
Invert onto serving plate. Let cool completely before slicing.
Makes one ring cake.
Bake the cake in a 9 x 13-inch pan.

In bottom of punch bowl or very large bowl, break cake into larger than bite size chunks (use only 1/2 the cake at this point), then layer half of the pineapple and juice, half of the pudding, half of the bananas, 1 can of pie filling, half the nuts and half the coconut.
Spread with 1 carton of whipped topping.
Repeat the above.
Garnish with cherries, nuts and, if you want to be fancy, chocolate curls.
Serves 25.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Blend ingredients in large bowl.
Beat at medium speed for 2 minutes.
Chop nuts in chopper until fine. Mix in batter.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan until brown. Cool in pan for 15 to 20 minutes.
Make sure egg whites are beaten.
Add other ingredients and fold in Cool Whip.
Pour over graham crackers (crushed) or try corn flakes or Grape-Nuts or bran flakes; anything you want for crunchies.
Freeze for 24 hours.
In a 12-inch stove top or electric skillet over medium heat, brown beef with onion, green pepper, 1/2 teaspoon salt and pepper. Remove meat mixture from skillet and drain fat.
Reduce heat to low.
Melt butter.
Spread potatoes over butter and sprinkle with remaining salt.
Top with beef mixture.
Remove seeds and seams from peppers; boil 5 minutes.
Brown meat and onions.
Add rice and tomato juice.
Simmer until thick; season.
Stuff peppers with meat mixture.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Sift together cake flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in vanilla.
Add dry ingredients alternately with buttermilk, beating well after each addition.
Add egg whites; beat at medium speed 2 minutes.
Pour batter into three waxed paper-lined 9-inch round cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Reduce heat to 325° and bake 25 more minutes or until cake tests done.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Spread Vanilla Filling between layers of cake.
Top with Orange Butter Frosting.
Brown hamburger with onion until onion is tender; drain.
Stir in remaining ingredients; mix well.
Bring to a boil; cover and reduce heat.
Simmer 40 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Rub roast with salt and pepper.
Put in large roasting pan; put in oven, turning to brown, for 20 to 30 minutes.
Remove roast; lower oven to 250°.
Scatter sauerkraut around roast.
In a bowl, mix the apples, onion, sugar, mustard and caraway seed.
Sprinkle this mixture over sauerkraut and drizzle wine over top.
(Can be refrigerated at this point and roasted later or next day.)
Cover and roast at 250° for about 4 hours, or until tender.
Moisten with more wine if it becomes dry.
Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.
Serves 4 to 6 people.

recipes.t: Pasta With Sun Dried Tomatoes And Pine Nuts
d: Saute garlic in olive oil.
Add herbs.
Remove from heat.
Add sun dried tomatoes.
(Cut tomatoes in 1/8-inch slices.)
Toss lightly with cooked pasta.
Top with pine nuts.
Serve with Parmesan cheese.
Melt margarine and white chocolate in double boiler.
Mix dry ingredients in a big bowl.
Add melted white chocolate and mix until coated.
Spread on wax paper to harden.
Break into pieces.
Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in pineapple juice; add eggs.
Cook in double boiler until thick.
Cool.
Whip milk until stiff.
Add cooled Jell-O mixture; blend.
Pour into graham cracker crusts. Chill.
Mix well.
Serve as is or frozen.
Cover bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch pan with marshmallows. Prepare cake mix according to directions.
Pour over marshmallows. Crush strawberries and mix with dry gelatin.
Pour this over batter.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Mix together rhubarb, orange juice, sugar and honey.
Simmer about 10 minutes until tender.
Remove from heat.
Stir in strawberries.
Cover and chill.
To serve, spoon fruit mixture over shells and add topping.
Combine all ingredients and spread on crackers.
Put onion and bacon in skillet and cook until glossy.
Remove from heat, add eggs, sour cream and stir.
Add salt and caraway seed to taste.
Brown round steak in large skillet in small amount of fat. Drain.
Add rest of ingredients and simmer until tender (1 to 2 hours).
May need to add a little water and stir occasionally to keep from sticking.
Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cut when cool.
Should be golden brown.
In 2-quart saucepan, saute onion in oil over low heat.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer for 15 minutes.
Keeps up to 2 months in refrigerator.
Yields 2 1/4 cups.
Cook
squash and onion together until tender and cooked down. Mash
cooked
squash
and add sour cream, soup and salt and pepper.
Melt 1 stick of margarine and herb stuffing.
Mix first 3 ingredients.
Add hominy.
Put in 9 x 13-inch casserole.
Top with crushed Fritos.
Bake 35 minutes at 350°.
Crumble Fritos and cover bottom of casserole dish.
Chop onion; cook in small amount of oil.
Add ground beef.
Brown and drain.
Add other ingredients except cheese.
Bring to a boil. Remove from heat.
When cool, add 2/3 cheese.
Pour in casserole dish.
Use remaining Fritos on top of meat mixture and remaining cheese on Fritos.
Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes.

recipes.t: Ground Meat And Vegetables With Bean Paste Over Noodles
d: Heat 5 tablespoons oil in preheated wok.
Stir-fry onion until fragrant.
Add ground meat; stir-fry until thoroughly cooked.
Add bean paste; stir-fry until fragrant.
Add water, cornstarch, sesame oil and sugar.
Bring to boil.
Cook until thickened.
Cook noodles by boiling water, adding noodles, bring to second boil and cooking over medium heat, about 4 minutes.
Drain noodles; place in bowls (individual).
Top with shredded vegetables and meat topping. Serve hot.
Mix well in bowls.
Serves 2.
Add yeast to warm water and sugar (1 teaspoon).
Let stand 5 minutes.
Mix together the ingredients.
Marinate the chicken 2 hours or overnight.
Drain and broil 4 minutes (each side) or grill until done.
Top with Monterey Jack cheese.
Melt, then top with chopped onion and tomato.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix together sugar, cocoa and flour in large bowl until no lumps remain.
Stir in melted butter.
Mix in eggs, one at a time, until smooth.
Stir in milk and vanilla. Pour mixture into pie shell.
Boil carrots until just tender (8 to 9 minutes).
Layer onion, carrots and green pepper in a large bowl.
Heat remaining ingredients to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Cool slightly. Pour over vegetables.
Cover and place in refrigerator for at least 8 hours.
They will keep about 1 week.
Pick, clean and wash
beans.
Put
in
Dutch oven large enough to hold
all
ingredients.	Place remaining ingredients in oven and let simmer for 4 hours, adding water as needed.
Put potatoes in casserole dish.
Add salt, pepper and pats of margarine on top.
Cover and microwave on High until potatoes are done.
Stir occasionally.
Combine peas, celery, lettuce and red onion in bowl. Mix juice from peas with mayonnaise and pour over pea mixture. Top with cheese and bacon bits.
If fish fillets are large, cut into 5 or 6 serving pieces. Arrange fish in ungreased square baking dish 8 x 8 x 2-inches. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Top with onions and tomato slices. Sprinkle with lime juice, oil and parsley.
Cover and cook in oven at 375° for 15 minutes.
Uncover and cook until fish flakes easily with fork, about 15 minutes longer.
Garnish with lime wedges, if desired.
Makes 5 or 6 servings.

recipes.t: One-Bowl Trifle Chocolate Oatmeal Jumbles(Makes 2 Dozen Cookies)
d: Heat oven to 350°. Place spread in large microwavable bowl. Cover loosely with waxed paper. Microwave on HIGH (100%) for 30 seconds or until melted; cool slightly. Add remaining ingredients. Stir until well blended (dough will be very stiff). Drop dough by level 1/4 measuring cupfuls 2-inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets; flatten slightly. Bake 13 to 17 minutes just until set. (Do not overbake. Centers will be soft.) Let stand on cookie sheets 1 minute. Using wide spatula, transfer to wire racks. Cool completely.
Cook broccoli; drain and set aside.
Blend soup and cheese. Blend mayonnaise with milk and stir into soup.
Place broccoli in baking dish and cover with sauce.
Sprinkle with cracker crumbs and butter.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until bubbly.
Wash cucumbers and cut in sticks.
Cover with boiling water and let stand 4 to 5 hours.
Then drain and pack into six pint jars.
Cream butter and sugar in bowl.
Beat in eggs, one at a time. Add milk alternately with wafer crumbs, mixing well.
Stir in coconut, pecans and vanilla.
Pour into prepared tube pan.
Bake at 275° for 2 1/2 hours.
Yields 16 servings.
Chop onions.
In large pan, melt butter and
cook onions until golden, but not brown.
Add enough flour to absorb butter, about 4 to 5 tablespoons.
Add chicken broth, 1 1/2 cans water and wine gradually while stirring well to avoid lumps.
Add more water or broth to taste and consistency; salt and pepper.
Simmer fifteen minutes until bubbly.
Pour in individual serving bowls.
Place a slice of fried or toasted crunchy French bread and sprinkle generously with grated Swiss cheese.
Broil until brown.
Serves 6.
Mix and form into ball and roll in coconut.
Chop almonds and toast at 350° for 3 to 5 minutes.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup on bottom of well-greased tube pan.
Set aside almonds and chocolate chips.
Measure remaining ingredients into mixing bowl. Blend.
Beat at medium speed for 4 minutes.
Stir in chocolate chips and almonds.
Pour into pan and bake at 350° for 70 minutes or until cake pulls away from sides of pan.
Cool in pan 15 minutes.
Remove and finish cooling on rack.
Garnish with whipped topping.
Mix grease, lye and 1 quart water the night before and stir hard.
In the morning, add salt, 20 Mule Borax and 1 quart water. Boil 5 minutes, then leave on medium heat for 1 hour.
Set off the stove to cool.
Cut in any size cake desired and dry.
Age improves lye soup.
Cream sugar and butter.
Add eggs, one at a time; beat well. Add flour, one cup at a time.
Beat well after each addition.
Add flavorings and mix well.
Cut fruit in small pieces and mix with coconut and nuts.
Pour batter over fruit and nut mixture and mix well.
Bake in tube pan.
Start baking at 300° for 45 minutes. Then turn down temperature to 275° for 1 1/2 hours.
This cake can be frozen.
Flour and pan-fry chicken breasts in a small amount of oil until brown. Drain and set aside. Cook rice as directed on package. Don't overcook.
Mix chicken soup with 1 soup can of water. Spoon rice into a 10 x 13-inch baking dish.
Lay chicken breasts on rice. Add about half the soup on this layer, then put broccoli on fillets.
Add rest of soup and top with cheese. Bake in a 350° oven for about 35 minutes.
In a mixing bowl dissolve yeast in water.
Stir in Bisquick, egg and the tablespoon of sugar.
Mix well.
Turn dough onto surface, dusted with extra Bisquick and knead gently 20 times. Place in center of greased 15 1/2 x 12-inch baking sheet.
Roll out to 14 x 9-inch rectangle.
Mix well and bake at 400° for 20 to 30 minutes in lightly greased pan/skillet, etc.
Grease a large Bundt pan (cake pan).
Layer frozen rolls in pan. Mix cinnamon with sugar and pour over rolls.
Layer one at a time chopped nuts, brown sugar and pudding mix.
Slice margarine and place around the rolls.
Cover pan with cloth and set in warm draft free place overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes. Invert pan over serving dish and let stand a minute so syrup will cover cake.
Decorate with cherries on top if desired.
Best served while warm.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In large frying pan, brown ground beef with onion, salt and pepper; drain.
Stir in sour cream.
Separate crescent dough into 2 large rectangles.
Place rectangles in ungreased 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Press over bottom and 1/2 inch up sides to form crust.
Spoon hot mixture into crust.
Top with cheese slices.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes, until deep, golden brown and crust is no longer doughy.
Refrigerate any leftovers. Makes 5 to 6 servings.
Mix jello.
Fold in all ingredients and chill until firm.
Mix cake mix, eggs, milk and margarine together.
Bake 3 layers at 350° until done.
Mix cream cheese, granulated sugar and powdered sugar until smooth and creamy.
Add 8 ounces Cool Whip. Grate frozen Hershey bars into frosting mixture.
Mix well and frost layers.

recipes.t: Morgan'S Korean Kal-Bi Ribs(From Morgan'S Restaurant, Bellevue, Wa)
d: Run all of the ingredients
in	blender for a minute or two. Combine flavors for 24
hours.
Marinate
to 5 pounds beef short ribs (or chicken pieces) at least overnight.	Grill meat or barbecue until
brown,
or	under broiler quickly.	(I use the crock-pot to cook meat, then brown on the grill.)
Drain pineapple juice and add water to equal 2 cups of liquid. Then dissolve Jell-O by boiling and add the pineapple, cream cheese and marshmallows to melt.
Cool.
When cool, add the cream and put in a 13 x 15-inch pan and chill.
Boil potatoes until done.
Slice the potatoes very thin. Place in a 2-quart casserole or a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Alternate layers of potatoes, grated cheese and soups, mixed with milk. Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish top with more grated cheese and sprinkle with parsley.
Bake in a 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Brown ground beef and onion; drain.
Add taco seasoning.
Mix well.
Layer tortillas, meat mixture and cheese in round casserole dish, ending with tortillas and cheese.
Bake in 350° oven for 15 minutes or for 5 minutes in microwave.
Serve with chopped tomato, shredded lettuce and sour cream.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Mix all ingredients together.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Blend well.
Eat with apple slices, pears, strawberries, etc.
Mix Crisco, eggs and sugar.
Mix in buttermilk, extract and vanilla.
Stir in flour, soda and salt.
Bake at 350° for 7 minutes.
Heat water, broccoli, ham, carrots, celery, onion and salt to boiling in 4-quart Dutch oven.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Gradually stir milk into baking mix in small bowl (mixture will be lumpy).
Stir into ham mixture.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Remove from heat; stir in cheese.
Cover and let stand until cheese is partially melted (5 minutes).
Stir before serving.
Makes 6 servings.
Thaw garlic bread.
Open the split halves and place on baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
While bread is baking, mix shredded Cheddar cheese, green onions, dill and mayonnaise (do not use Miracle Whip).
Mixture will be thick; you can add more mayo if desired.
Take bread from oven and spread mixture evenly on top of both sides (will be a nice thick layer).
Shake paprika on top. Place in broiler for approximately 3 to 5 minutes until nice and bubbly.
Watch it doesn't burn!
Cut into slices and enjoy!

recipes.t: Chicken Rice Pilaf(Djaj Mah Ruz M'Falfal)
d: Cook chicken in the water until tender.
Remove from liquid, debone and set aside.
Save the liquid.
Place almonds, pine nuts and butter in a saucepan.
Turn heat to low.
Stir, browning the nuts to a golden color.
Drain rice and add to the nuts.
Stir on low heat for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces, broth, salt and pepper.
Bring to boil on high heat.
Lower heat, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve on a platter with a sprinkle of cinnamon on top.
Bake potatoes until done.
While still
hot, cut in half lengthwise and scoop out potato, leaving skins intact.
Mix potato with butter, sour cream, 1 1/2 cups of the cheese and onions.
If necessary, thin with more sour cream.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Place mixture back in skins.
Top with remaining cheese and reheat until cheese melts.
Stir together first 4 ingredients.
Add remaining ingredients. Cover and chill.
Makes about 8 cups.
In a medium saucepan, combine the flour and brown sugar.
Stir in the milk; cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly.
Cook and stir 1 minute more.
Remove from the heat. Gradually stir about 1 cup hot mixture into egg yolks.
Return all to the saucepan.
Bring to a gentle boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat; stir in butter and vanilla.
Cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.
Fold in the whipped cream.

Stir the cornmeal into the boiling water with the salt and sugar. Stir 1 minute. Remove from fire. Add butter. Beat well and add eggs. Beat well. Add milk, beating again. Pour into greased 8 or 9-inch baking pan (Pyrex). Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Delicious!
Preheat oven to 400°.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and vanilla in a mixing bowl.
Melt butter.
Combine butter and milk to the rest of ingredients and mix well.
Pour into dish and bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven at 400°.
Beat egg; stir in milk and oil.
Add rest of ingredients.
(Batter will be lumpy.)
Fill 12 muffin cups about 3/4 full.
Bake until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Brown meat in salt (no oil or shortening).
Drain on paper towel.
Spray casserole with Pam.
Layer zucchini slices (unpeeled), 1/2 of meat, onion slices, tomato chunks and croutons. Repeat layers.
Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake, covered, at 375° for 40 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350° and grease
13 x 9-inch pan.
Beat cake mix (save marbling pieces),
applesauce,
water, oil and eggs together.
Pour 1 1/2 cups	of
batter into smaller bowl; add marbling
package and beat.
Pour
yellow batter into pan. Put mounds of chocolate mixture on
top and marble.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle on top.
Bake
at 350° for 33 to 38 minutes.
Cool completely.	Serve with
Cool Whip or applesauce.
Mix dry cake mix, pie filling and lemon juice and beat well. Pour in a jelly roll pan.
Do not spray pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
When cool, frost with Cream Cheese Frosting.
Season meat and coat sides with flour.
Brown in oil.
Add liquid from tomatoes plus 1 3/4 cups water to it.
Add cut-up onions and Worcestershire sauce.
Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours. Cut green peppers into strips and add to meat.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add whole tomatoes to gravy and simmer 15 minutes more. No extra seasoning is needed for gravy.
Serve over rice.
Dip chicken breasts into beaten eggs; coat with bread crumbs. Heat oil in a frying pan on medium heat.
Add coated chicken and brown lightly on both sides.
Remove from pan and place in a baking dish, topping each breast with a slice of Mozzarella cheese.
Mix together remaining ingredients in a saucepan and cook until mixture gets hot and thickens.
Pour over chicken and bake in a 350° oven for 25 minutes.
Serve over angel hair pasta.
Combine all ingredients, except ham.
Spread cream cheese mixture evenly on one side of each ham slice.
Roll up and secure with wooden pick.
Cover and chill.
Carefully slice each roll into 1/2-inch pieces.
Serve with toothpicks.
Yield: 4 dozen.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Wash mushrooms.
Remove stems and mince finely.
Mix egg yolk with cream cheese.
Add onion and minced stems.
Stuff mushroom caps with mixture.
Place on cookie sheet and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake 10 minutes.
(May be made ahead of time.)
Put one large and 1 small jello in bowl and 2 cups of steaming hot water.
Add strawberries.
Let it jell and put on top of mixture.
Refrigerate overnight.
Heat sour cream.
Add sugar, melted margarine and salt and stir to dissolve.
Cool to lukewarm.
In a large warm bowl, add 1/2 cup warm water and sprinkle yeast into water.
When dissolved, add sour cream mixture, then eggs and stir in flour.
Put batter in refrigerator overnight.
Divide into 4 parts.
Roll each section into round circle on floured surface.
Cut into pie shaped wedges.
Roll into crescent rolls.
Put on greased baking sheet and let rise in a warm place until double in bulk.
Bake at 375° for 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Cook ground chuck in medium skillet over medium heat until browned.
Drain and pat dry with paper towels.
Wipe skillet with paper towel.
Return meat to skillet and stir in tomatoes, water, garlic and Italian herb seasonings.
Cover and bring to boil. Reduce heat; simmer 20 minutes.
Cook noodles according to package directions omitting salt and fat.
Drain well and set aside.
Cook spinach according to package directions omitting salt and fat. Drain well and squeeze excess moisture from spinach.
Combine spinach and next 4 ingredients.
Stir until well combined.
Set aside.
Place half of cooked noodles in a 12 x 8 x 2-inch baking dish coated with cooking spray.
Top each half each of cottage cheese mixture and American cheese.
Spread half of meat mixture. Repeat layers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
Melt chocolate and butter (I use microwave).
Combine powdered sugar, milk and vanilla.
Pour hot chocolate mixture over and beat until spreading consistency.
If more liquid is needed, use a few drops of hot water.
Makes enough frosting for 10 x 14-inch pan or 2 layers.
Mix up whatever amount you need and pour the dressing over according to your own taste.
Place cooked and drained broccoli in baking dish.
Mix in chestnuts.
Add cheese to top of mixture.
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons melted butter over mixture.
Mix crumbs with remaining butter and sprinkle on top.
Bake in oven at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix sugar, butter and cream cheese together.
Add your choice of listed fruits.
Shape into eggs.
Let dry for a while.
Dip into dipping chocolate or roll in chopped nuts.
To form dough, mix together flour, Crisco and milk.
Spread out on floured surface and roll out.
Sprinkle dough with sliced apples, cinnamon to taste and apple pie spice.
Roll dough with apples inside to form a jelly roll effect.
Slice up dough and lay sideways in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix first 6 ingredients and let stand.
Make dough by combining flour, 2 eggs and water.
Roll out and place in a 9-inch pie pan.
Fill with ham mixture and top with crust.
Beat 1 egg and brush on top of pie.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Use as many of the ingredients as desired for the salad.
Mix as you would any other salad.
Add spices to coffee.
Boil 5 minutes; strain.
Add sugar and chill.
Serve in glasses, containing little cracked ice and top with cream.
Dust with additional cinnamon.
A large platter works better than a bowl.
This way you can display each ingredient and the presentation is excellent.
Remove core of lettuce and break in 3-inch pieces and place on bottom of platter.
Combine sugar, sour cream, milk, butter, corn syrup and salt in heavy 2-quart saucepan.
Stir over moderate heat until sugar is dissolved and mixture reaches a boil.
Boil over moderate heat 9 to 10 minutes to 238°, soft-ball stage.
Remove from heat and allow to stand until lukewarm (110°), about an hour.
Add vanilla and beat until mixture just begins to lose its gloss and hold its shape. Quickly stir in walnuts and turn into oiled pan.
Let stand until firm before cutting.
Makes 1 1/2 pounds.
Dissolve jello as directed (1/4 cup less water).
Add sugar and cool.
Then add apples, bananas and pineapple.
Let set up in refrigerator.
Boil 1/2 cup pineapple juice, 1/4 cup sugar, flour and beaten egg, stirring all the time.
Let mixture get cold. Prepare Dream Whip; fold into cold mixture and spread over jello. Sprinkle with nuts.
Cut artichokes and swiss cheese into fourths.
Combine mayo and parmesan cheese.
Add other ingredients.
Place one piece artichoke on bread.
Spread mixture over artichoke and top with swiss cheese.
Put under broiler until hot and cheese melts.

Cut a round circle in the bread and hollow out. Set aside. In a large bowl, beat cream cheese until smooth. Stir in the clams, clam juice, onion, beer, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, red hot sauce, salt and pepper until well blended.
With 2 sheets of aluminum foil large enough to cover loaf, fill loaf with cream cheese mixture and seal tightly with foil.
Bake at 350° for 3 hours.
Cream margarine and cheese together, then add other ingredients and mix well.
Roll into long rolls and refrigerate several hours.
Slice into thin rounds and place on slightly greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes or until edges brown.
May be frozen and baked later.
Mix eggs and oil.
Combine buttermilk and soda.
Add this to eggs and oil.
Stir in flour, cornmeal and salt.
Add corn, onion, peppers and cheese.
Bake in a 400° oven until done.
In greased 2-quart baking dish toss shells, tuna and celery. In blender mix mayonnaise, milk, parsley and green onions until smooth.
Pour over tuna mixture; toss to coat.
Bake in preheated 400° oven 15 minutes or until bubbly.
Chop cranberries, apples (cored and peeled) and oranges (peeled) in food processor.
Prepare jello according to package directions.
Combine all ingredients; let set.
(Will take about 18 hours to jell.)
In a large bowl,
break
up
lettuce,
cauliflower
and bacon. In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, cheese and sugar. Add the dressing to the lettuce mixture and mix well.
Put
cucumbers, onions and chili peppers in salad bowl. Stir together
ingredients
and pour over vegetables in bowl. Store in refrigerator until ready to eat.
Mix pumpkin, eggs, oil and water. Set aside.
Mix flour, sugar, pumpkin spice, soda, salt, nuts, nutmeg and cinnamon. Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients slowly.
Mix well.
Place into greased and floured loaf pans (2).
Bake at 350° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cook cake as directed on box.
After cake is cool, tear cake into pieces, then layer all ingredients in a large bowl and top with Cool Whip and nuts.
Mix water and sugar.
Bring to a boil for 2 minutes.
Place marshmallow cream in bowl and pour hot syrup into cream.
Beat until the mixture loses its gloss.
Add nuts, vanilla and salt. Drop by spoonfuls on waxed paper.
Coat bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate with vegetable cooking spray and line with tortillas.
Set aside.
Cook ground chuck in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until browned, stirring to crumble.
Drain and pat dry with paper towels.
Combine meat, chilies, onion and cheese.
Stir well.
Spoon mixture into prepared dish.
Coat bottom and sides of an 8-inch pie plate lightly with butter.
Brown meat and onion.
Drain.
Add remaining ingredients; heat thoroughly.
Chop tomatoes, onions, and peppers very fine. Then add sugar, salt, and vinegar.
Add spices tied in a cheesecloth bag.
Cook slowly uncovered for 2 hours until thick. Remove spice bag.
Pour into hot, sterilized jars and seal.
Makes 4 pints.
Mix together sugar and flour.
Add egg yolk, then gradually add milk and stir.
Add lemon flavoring and coconut.
Cook over medium heat until thick.
Stir slowly while cooking.
Pour in baked pie crust and add meringue.
Sprinkle with coconut and brown in oven.
Place chicken in single layer in a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Combine soup, soup mix, sour cream, lemon juice, dill and mushrooms; pour over chicken.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 1 hour.
In a large skillet over medium-heat in hot oil, toss sliced cabbage until well coated and slightly wilted.
Add apple, wine, sugar, salt and pepper.
Over high heat, heat to boiling.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, tossing occasionally until tender-crisp.
Yields 4 servings.
Cook vegetables as directed on package and place in greased casserole.
Mix onion, celery, cheese and mayonnaise and spread over vegetables.
Melt butter, then put in crumbled crackers; sprinkle over casserole.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
In food processor, mince artichoke hearts, also jalapeno peppers.
Combine all ingredients in ovenproof bowl; mix, then smooth top of mixture.
Bake, uncovered, until edges are brown at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve with blue corn chips.
Prepare rice according to directions. Thoroughly combine all ingredients together and put into 2 pans that are 12 x 20 x 2-inches. Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Makes about 50 servings.
Soak bread crumbs
in
milk.
Add other ingredients and stir well.
Pour in a pan and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Cook sugar and milk over medium heat for approximately 10 minutes.
Do not stir.
Add butter, whiskey and pecans.
Whip until mixture hardens.
Drop by spoonfuls on wax paper.
Mix first 5 ingredients together and drop by spoonfuls into hot oil until brown.
Turn over and brown on other side.
Sprinkle powdered sugar over them and serve.
Combine potatoes, onion and water in heavy saucepan.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
In heavy skillet, melt butter; add flour.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Stir mixture slowly into potatoes; cook and stir until thick.
Add cheese and seasonings.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Heat oil in 4-quart pot.
Add onion and garlic. Stir until onion softens.
Stir in next 5 ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Add pasta.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, 8 to 10 minutes until pasta is tender.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vinegar.
If desired, garnish with pepper strips.
Good accompanied with corn bread.
Pour boiling water over rice and let set for 3 minutes. Combine all ingredients well and pour into 9 x 13-inch greased baking dish.
Bake for 1 hour at 350° (or until sides are brown and top begins to brown).
Put bananas, eggs, and honey in a blender and blend until smooth.
Add orange juice, milk and cinnamon and blend again. Pour into tall glasses and serve.
Cook rice.
Saute onion, celery and pepper.
Mix all together. Put cheese on top.
Put jalapeno to taste.
Put in hot oven until cheese melts.
Mix ingredients and bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Cool and cut into strips.
Combine sugar and water.
Boil to soft ball stage (236°); pour slowly, beating constantly, onto egg whites.
Add flavoring. Continue beating until icing holds its shape when dropped from spoon.

Combine coconut and margarine. Reserving 2 tablespoons coconut mixture, press remainder firmly on bottom and up side to rim of 9-inch pie plate; chill. In large bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk, ReaLemon, fruit cocktail, almonds and cherries; mix well. Fold in whipped topping.
Pour into prepared crust. Garnish with reserved coconut and additional fruit if desired. Chill 4 hours or until set.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Brown beef
and saute with onions.
Add both sauces and mix well.
Boil noodles until done.
Drain and rinse well.
Brown meat in skillet; drain and add rest of ingredients. Simmer 30 minutes in the skillet or cook in crock-pot for 1 hour.
Mix and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour at 350°.
Combine first
ingredients
in
large
bowl and toss well. Cover and
refrigerate at least 30 minutes. Add cashews and noodles; toss again.
Serve on lettuce.
Serves 6.
Combine milk, cream, salt and pepper in a large heavy kettle. Heat over medium heat until milk is scalded.
Cook syrup, butter and sugar for 5 minutes.
Add vanilla and baking soda.
Stir well.
Pour over popcorn and mix well.
Put in 2 baking pans and bake at 250° for 1 hour.
Stir every 15 minutes.
Cook chicken breasts and remove from bone.
Place in casserole dish and pour mushrooms over chicken.
Mix cream of chicken soup with sour cream.
Spread over chicken.
Melt margarine and mix with Ritz crackers and poppy seed.
Sprinkle over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix well.
Pour into unbaked pie shell and bake at 375° for 45 minutes to 1 hour until knife blade comes out clean.
Ovens vary so you may want to lessen the heat.
Sprinkle ribs with garlic salt.
Make sauce with remaining ingredients and pour over ribs.
Bake in deep pan at 350° for 2 1/2 hours.
Mix together all ingredients in large bowl.
Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
Mix all ingredients and put in casserole baking dish.
In a dutch oven or large pot, heat oil over medium heat.
Add carrots, onion, potato, sweet potato and garlic.
Cook, stirring until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add broth and split peas.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, partially covered, until vegetables are tender and peas have broken down, about 40 minutes. Season with pepper.
Meanwhile, in a small skillet, cook bacon until crisp, 3 to 5 minutes.
Transfer to a plate lined with a paper towel.
Ladle soup into bowls and garnish with bacon and croutons.
Slice large ripe tomatoes in 1/2-inch rounds or wedges and place in a large, flat pan or dish one layer deep.
Sprinkle generously with salt, coarsely ground pepper and crumbled oregano. Carefully pour oil so that tomatoes are just covered.
Place in refrigerator until ready to serve.
Allow at least 1 hour to marinate.
Place all ingredients in crock-pot.
Cook on low heat setting for 4 to 6 hours.
Serves 8 to 10.
Melt first 3 ingredients together.
Add vanilla, then peanuts. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper lined cookie sheets. Chill.
Fix stuffing according to directions.
Mix milk, soup and chicken.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Place 1/2 stuffing in bottom of pan.
Pour soup and chicken over stuffing and place remaining stuffing on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 350°.
Butter 8 or 9-inch glass pie plate or round baking dish.
Spread shoestring potatoes evenly over bottom of pan. Makes 4 indentations into potatoes, down to bottom of dish, each about 1 1/2-inches across.
Carefully break 1 egg into each indentation.
Bake at 350° for 3 to 10 minutes; add cheese and parsley.
Return to oven and bake until cheese melts and eggs are set.
Cut into 4 wedges and serve immediately.
Mix sugar, cocoa and cornstarch.
Add egg yolks, beating thoroughly.
Add milk, gradually, while mixing.
Cook mixture in a double boiler until it thickens, stirring constantly.
Add butter and vanilla.
Pour into a baked pie shell.
Top with meringue. Bake at 325° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Brown hamburger and onion; drain.
Add seasoning, water and beans; mix well.
May need to add a little more water.
Fry tortillas a few seconds on each side in hot oil.
Divide meat mixture on tortillas and roll up.
Place, seam down, in well-greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Mix together 2 cans soup; spread over enchiladas.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cook macaroni by directions on box and drain.
Add margarine to cooked macaroni.
Beat eggs and milk together.
Pour egg and milk mixture over cooked macaroni.
Sprinkle grated cheese over macaroni and stir it into the egg and milk mixture, saving some to sprinkle on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes or until mixture is firm.
Mix all ingredients into large kettle and cook until tender. Season with oregano, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Heat oven to 325°.
Grease 10 x 1 1/2-inch pie pan.
Mix apples and spices; turn into pan.
Beat remaining ingredients, except Streusel, until smooth, 15 seconds in blender on high or 1 minute with hand beater.
Pour into pan.
Sprinkle with Streusel.
Bake until knife inserted in center comes out clean, 55 to 60 minutes.
Slowly add the crumbled cream cheese to the sugar and mayonnaise.
Add crushed pineapple and the cherries.
Whip heavy cream and fold into the mixture.
Freeze in trays or in 8 x 8-inch pan.
Cut in squares and serve on lettuce.
Serves 6.
Fry in shortening or bacon grease until potatoes start to brown.
Cut up into thin slices a Polish sausage.
Add to ingredients in pan.
Cover and let cook until potatoes are golden brown.
Defrost the bread dough until soft enough to pull off and roll into small balls.
Arrange approximately 48 small balls in a 9 x 12-inch greased pan.
Wash and cut cucumbers into slices about 1/4-inch thick.
Mix cucumbers and salt.
Let stand overnight.
In the morning, drain and press out all the juice possible. Rinse once in cold water. Combine vinegar, sugar substitute and spices. Boil 1 minute. Add cucumbers and simmer 5 minutes.
Pack cucumbers into clean, hot sterile jars to within 1-inch of top. Fill jars with hot liquid to top.
Seal tightly.
Makes about 12 pints.
Cucumber Slices:
46 calories per pint.
Pour hot water over oats and let stand.
Cream white and brown sugars and oil.
Beat eggs into creamed mixture.
Add flour, cinnamon and salt into oats; beat well.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Don't use mixer.
Sprinkle coconut on top of cake before baking.
Cream butter, sour cream and sugar until light and fluffy. Sift plain flour and baking soda together.
Add flour to mixture alternating with the eggs.
Add flavor and bake in Bundt or tube cake pan for 1 1/2 hours at 325°.
Mix mayonnaise, sour cream, parsley, onion flakes and dill in a bowl.
Cut dried beef into small pieces and fold into mixture. Cut rye bread into chunks.
Dip the bread!
Combine egg, salt and vinegar in bowl of food processor, fitted with steel blade. Pulse just to blend.
With processor running, very slowly add the oil until the mixture emulsifies (or thickens). Add sour cream and chives.
Pulse again just to blend.

recipes.t: Barley With Monterey Jack One Dish Dinner
d: In a large saucepan, cook barley in 3 tablespoons butter, stirring for 2 minutes.
Add 4 cups water and salt.
Bring liquid to boil and simmer, covered, for 45 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Let cool.
Mix tomatoes, half and half, scallions, olives, mushrooms and chili peppers, 3/4 of the cheese, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Combine well and transfer to a baking dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese and bake at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Serves 8.
Mash cheese.
Add well drained clams.
Moisten with clam juice to proper consistency.
Add lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce. For color, add chopped parsley.
Serve cold with crackers or potato chips.

recipes.t: Quick-Haluski With Cabbage And Low-Fat Cottage Cheese
d: Chop cabbage; boil until tender.
Boil shells as per directions on box and drain.
Melt oleo; drain cabbage and add to oleo.
Combine shells
with cabbage, then add 1 carton of low-fat cottage cheese.
May be topped with dry or chopped fresh dill.
Blend marshmallow cream and orange juice with rotary beater. Stir in salad dressing and vanilla.
Makes 1 1/2 cups.
For fruit salads.
Place chicken and broccoli in bottom of 1 1/2-quart casserole dish.
Sprinkle with salt.
Combine remaining ingredients and spread over chicken and broccoli.
Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes.
Makes 4 servings.
Melt oleo and blend in flour until stiff mixture.
Beat eggs and white sugar until fluffy.
Add oleo-flour mixture and beat again.
Blend in white Karo and maple syrup and water.
Add to egg mixture along with chopped pecans.
Save a few half pecans to garnish top of pie.
Bake in uncooked pie shell about 1 hour at 350°.
Mix first 4 ingredients.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Add flour, salt and pepper to the yeast, sugar, oil and warm water.
Mix well.
Knead 5 minutes.
Let rise 30 minutes.

In top of double boiler, melt morsels over boiling water. Stir in sweetened condensed milk. Remove from heat. Stir in cereal and peanuts. Drop by teaspoons onto waxed paper lined baking sheets. Chill 2 hours or until firm.
Store at room temperature in loosely covered container.
Makes about 2 pounds or 48 candies.
Mix liquids together.
When ready to serve, add sherbet. Serves 50.
Blend sugar, wine and oil well.
Add flour gradually, stirring until a wet, but not sticky, dough is formed.
Take small pieces and form into rings.
Dip one side into sugar.
Bake, sugar side up, on cookie sheet for 20 minutes at 350°.
Bake German chocolate cake according to directions on box in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Poke holes in cake using the handle of a wooden spoon.
Make lots of holes, but don't overlap.
While cake is still warm, pour Eagle Brand milk over cake.
Then pour caramel topping over cake.
Let set in the refrigerator to cool.
Crush 3 Heath bars; sprinkle over top.
Cover with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle 3 more crushed Heath bars over Cool Whip.
Combine all ingredients except soup and milk.
Place in baking dish and form a loaf.
Mix soup and 1/2 can milk.
Pour over meat loaf and bake in 350° oven for 1 hour.
Is very good with potatoes placed around meat and some of the soup mixture poured over them also.
Process oats in a blender or food processor until ground.
Beat butter and sugars at medium speed with an electric mixer until fluffy.
Add eggs and vanilla; beat until blended.	Combine ground oats, flour and next 3 ingredients.
Add to butter mixture, beating until blended.
Stir in chocolate and pecans.
Drop dough by tablespoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake at 375° for 7-8 minutes or until golden brown; remove to wire racks to cool. Yield:
6 dozen.
Bake cookie dough 8 to 10 minutes. Mix cream cheese, powdered sugar and Cool Whip. Spread on cookie dough while still warm. Add fresh fruit.
Grind cranberries; add sugar.
(Let set for 1 hour.)
Add marshmallows to Cool Whip.
(Let set for 1 hour.)
Drain pineapple.
Mix all together.
Put in glass bowl.
Spread the 2 packages of crescent rolls on a large baking sheet to make crust.
Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Cool.
Mix cream cheese, Miracle Whip, horseradish and pepper.
Spread on cooled crust.
Top with vegetables and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Keeps well.
It can be made a day ahead of time. (Doesn't take many veggies.)
Combine in crock-pot. Cook all day on low or in oven at 250° for 5 hours.
Butter bread and place in bottom of 9 x 13-inch casserole dish. Top with bacon (can substitute sausage or a vegetable) and cheese. Mix eggs, milk, salt and mustard.
Pour into dish.
Cover and let set in refrigerator overnight.
In the morning, mix cornflakes and melted butter.
Pour on top of casserole.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour. Makes 8 to 12 servings.
Combine 1 cup sugar and margarine; cream until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour with milk and vanilla to creamed mixture, beating well.
Drain cherries.
Combine juice, wine and cornstarch.
Add lemon juice, salt and allspice.
Cook and stir until clear and slightly thickened.
Add butter and cherries.
Serve warm with baked ham.
Line sides and bottom of serving bowl with sponge cake.
Warm milk.
In a small mixing bowl, mix together the cornstarch, sugar, egg and vanilla; mix until creamy.
Pour into warm milk; stir to boiling.
Pour over prepared layer; sprinkle shredded dark baking chocolate on top.
Allow to cool at room temperature, then put in refrigerator.

recipes.t: Texas Company Eggs Sunday Rest Meal
d: Whip eggs and milk.
Scramble until they just hold their shape, soft and a little runny.
Spread eggs in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
While hot, spread with sour cream.
Top with cheese and bacon.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 20 minutes or until hot.
Boil sweet potatoes until done.
Peel and cool.
Cut lengthwise.
Put in 9 x 12-inch baking dish.
Mix all other ingredients until melted.
Pour over potatoes.
Cook at 375° for 40 minutes.

Slice chicken into chunks and fry in tbsp of butter with garlic pepper seasoning salt and cook thoroughly. Set aside with 3 cups cooked broccoli well strained, cook 1 pound of your favorite pasta. * Sauce = melt one stick butter on medium heat, then add cream cheese and melt. With wire whisk slowly stir in milk and then add parmesan cheese and pepper. Heat till well blended then combine chicken, broccoli, pasta and sauce. Yummy!
Mix ingredients together and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes or until beets are softened.
Mix everything together. Chill in refrigerator before serving.
In large fry pan,
brown meat in butter.
Add mushrooms and onion; continue
browning
until
tender.
Add
remaining ingredients except wine.
Simmer,
stirring
frequently, until sauce thickens.
Add red wine; continue simmering for 15 to 20 minutes until meat is
tender.
Serve over buttered noodles or rice.
Parboil yams and then peel.
Cut in thick slices.
Place in baking dish.
Mix all dry ingredients.
Cover yams with mixture. Dot with margarine.
Put lemon juice over yams.
Pour water in. Cut 1/2 orange in slices.
Place on yams.
Other 1/2 of orange squeeze over yams.
Bake at 400° for 35 to 40 minutes or until yams are tender.
Syrup is thick, baste after.
Yields 6 servings. Eat with love from the kitchen of Shirley Murden.

In saucepan, combine pie filling mix and sugar. Gradually blend in lemon juice and water until smooth. Stir in egg yolks. Bring to a full boil over medium heat. Boil 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add lemon peel and pour into baked pie shell. Top with Meringue, sealing well at edges.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes. Cool 2 hours before serving.
Makes 6 servings.
Blend flour, sugar, soda and salt. Add to mixture oil, eggs and buttermilk and mix well. Add raisin bran. Cover tightly. Bake as needed at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Combine flour, ginger, soda, cinnamon, cloves and salt; set aside.
In a large mixing bowl beat margarine with an electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds to soften.
Gradually add the 1 cup sugar, beat until fluffy.
Add egg and molasses; beat well. Stir dry ingredients into beaten mixture.
Shape into 1 1/2-inch balls (1 heaping tablespoonful dough each).
Roll in the 2 tablespoons sugar and place on ungreased cookie sheet, 2 1/2 inches apart.
Bake in a 350° oven abut 10 minutes or until light brown and still puffed (do not overcook).
Let stand for 2 minutes before transferring to rack to cool.
Makes 24 (3-inch) cookies.
Mix water and sugar together in a large pan.
Heat until sugar is dissolved; set aside to cool.
In a large container, mix pineapple, orange and lemon juices; add cooled sugar water mixture to Jell-O (dry); mix well.
Add bananas (that have been mashed thoroughly); mix well and freeze until ready to use.
Combine first four ingredients in mixing bowl.
Heat last three ingredients to 110° to 115°, warm to touch.
Pour liquid mixture over flour mixture.
Blend at low speed for one minute. By hand, stir in 1 cup additional whole wheat flour and 4 to 4 1/2 cups all-purpose flour.
Knead on floured surface about 5 minutes. Place dough in greased bowls; cover and let rise 45 to 60 minutes until doubled in bulk.
Punch down dough; divide in half.
Shape each half into a loaf shape.
Place in two 9 x 5-inch greased loaf tins.
Cover loaves; let rise 30 to 45 minutes until light and double in size.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes until loaf sounds hollow when tapped.
Remove from pan; cool on rack.
Slice when cool.
Mix in heavy pan and stir with wooden spoon.
When this begins to boil fast, time for 8 minutes.
Remove from heat and add chocolate chips and Marshmallow Fluff.
Stir until chocolate and marshmallow are blended.
Add walnuts.
Pour into a 14 x 9-inch pan. Spray pan with Pam before emptying the fudge into pan to set.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly and drop by spoonful onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake 7 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.
You may brush with melted butter while still warm.
Yields
8 to 10 biscuits.
Season flounder fillets with garlic salt and white pepper. Coat fillets with flounder and then beaten egg.
Next, fry fillets in skillet, using vegetable oil.
Cook fillets for about 3 minutes on each side.
Place flounder fillets on a serving plate.
In the same skillet, add butter, lemon juice, salt, pepper and garlic. Mix until blended and pour on top of fillets.
Beat eggs slightly and add everything else except nuts and mix. Add nuts in with mixture. Pour into pie shells. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Use either red or green peppers.
Remove seeds from peppers; blend peppers in blender.
Use vinegar for liquid.
Mix in sugar; bring to rolling boil and add Certo.
Bring to full boil again, stirring constantly for 4 minutes.
Skim off foam.
Pour into jelly jars.
Heat oven to 400°.
Spray a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan with nonstick spray.
Dip chicken in margarine, then coat with remaining ingredients.
Place in prepared pan.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, or until tender.
In a large, heavy bottom pot, fry ham, onion and green pepper in canola oil over medium high heat for 5 minutes.
Add cabbage, chicken broth, red pepper flakes, bay leaf and parsley.
Stir. Bring to a boil.
Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until cabbage is tender.
Drain and rinse black-eyed peas.
Add peas to pot; stir and simmer, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
In covered blender container at high speed, blend all ingredients until smooth.
Pour mixture into chilled 12 ounce glasses.
Serve milkshakes with large straws.
Cut cake into 1-inch cubes.
Prepare pudding with milk.
Place cake and marshmallows in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour prepared pudding over top, completely covering cake. Chill at least 1 hour. Cover top with Cool Whip.
Combine graham cracker crumbs and melted margarine.
Pat in bottom of pan.
Soak first 3 items in salt water overnight.
Drain well.
Add chopped celery and remaining ingredients.
Mix well; bring to full boil and can hot.

Sift together flour, cinnamon, allspice and cloves. In a separate bowl, add soda to buttermilk. In a third bowl, cream shortening and sugar. Add jam and mix well. Add milk and flour mixtures alternately to creamed mixture, blending well after each addition. Stir in nuts. Pour into a greased and floured Bundt pan. Bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/4 hours or until done.
Add 1
cup coconut to cake mix.
Mix and bake according to directions	using
a 9 x 13-inch oblong pan.
While cake is hot, punch
holes in cake.
Combine Eagle Brand milk and cream of coconut.
Pour
over
cake.
Frost when cool.
Combine Cool Whip, pecans and coconut.
Refrigerate.
Brown chops
on
both
sides in small amount of cooking oil; drain off any fat.
Mix remaining ingredients.
Pour over chops. Simmer
minutes
or until fork-tender.
Serve with white rice or noodles.
Cream butter and sugar until fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix all ingredients with mixer. Spread on muffin halves. Quick freeze. Remove and cut in quarters. Freeze in plastic bags until ready to use. Broil for 5 minutes or until just browned and bubbly.
Dissolve jello in hot
water;
add
cranberry
and beat until smooth.
Add orange
juice.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Add celery and apple.
Pour in 9 x 13-inch pan or mold. Half a recipe would fill an 8 x 8-inch pan.
Serves 10 to 12.

recipes.t: Cheesy Onion Bake With Toasted Rounds
d: Grate the cheese and mix with the onion, mayonnaise and cracked red pepper.
Bake in a covered baking dish in a 225° to 250° oven for about 25 minutes.
Using an electric knife, thinly slice the French breads into rounds.
Lay the slices on a cookie sheet and lightly brush with melted butter.
Sprinkle with coarse ground black pepper and bake 20 to 25 minutes in 300° oven.
Serve the hot cheesy onion bake as a dip with the toasted rounds.
Mix hamburger, pork, eggs, chopped onion, green pepper and milk together.
Add bread crumbs to form a patty.
Brown patties in a little oil until browned on both sides.
Remove patties.
Add water to juice and thicken with flour water to make gravy.
Put patties back in gravy and let simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In a small bowl, stir together oat bran, flour, baking soda and salt.
In a separate large bowl, cream the butter or margarine with sugar and vanilla extract. Beat in egg whites. Gradually add oat bran mixture and mix well. Stir in chocolate chips and nuts.
Drop from a level tablespoon onto cookie sheets sprayed with nonstick vegetable spray. Bake at 375° for 10 minutes or until golden.
Cream the cream cheese, sugar and peanut butter.
Stir in milk and whole container Cool Whip.
Put in pie crust.
Freeze 4 to 6 hours.
Top with crushed peanuts or grated chocolate.
Combine first 3 ingredients, mixing well.
Combine eggs and next 3 ingredients.
Add to sugar mixture, stirring well.
Add coconut.
Pour into pastry shell and bake at 350° for 35 minutes or until filling sets.
Yield: One 9-inch pie.
Cook meal, sugar, salt, shortening and milk in a saucepan until thick (like cereal).
Cool to lukewarm.
Add yeast that has been dissolved in warm water.
Add eggs and beat.
Add flour to form soft dough.
Knead.
Cover and let rise.
Punch down.
Roll out and cut with biscuit cutter.
Brush with butter.
Let rise. Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
In mixing bowl, combine sugar and cocoa.
Add eggs and corn syrup.
Stirring constantly, mix a little hot milk into cocoa mixture.
Gradually add more milk until all milk is used, stirring constantly, until mixture is smooth, thickened and coats the spoon. Pour into molds, ice cube tray, paper cups, etc., and freeze until stiff.
Add sticks.
Freeze thoroughly.
Combine rhubarb, water and sugar in a 2-quart microwavable bowl; cook, uncovered, 8 minutes.
Add pudding mix.
Cook 1 minute.
Serve warm.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Stir in milk, sugar, salt, shortening and 2 1/2 cups of the flour.
Beat until smooth.
Mix in remaining flour to form soft dough.
Turn dough onto lightly floured board; knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. Place in greased bowl; turn greased side up.
Cover; let rise in warm place until double, about 1 1/2 hours.
In a large skillet, brown pork in fat.
Add 1/4 cup water; cover and simmer until tender (about 1 hour).
Drain pineapple, reserving syrup.
Combine sugar and cornstarch.
Add pineapple syrup, vinegar, soy sauce and salt.
Add cornstarch mixture, pineapple, green pepper and onion rings to skillet.
Cook (continue stirring) over medium heat until mixture thickens. Cover and simmer 5 minutes longer.
Serve over cooked rice. Makes 6 servings.
In large pot, brown meat, pepper and onion; drain.
Add chopped cabbage, Ro-Tel and tomatoes.
Add cheese soup.
Cook about 2 hours on slow heat or simmer.
Good served with cornbread.
Serves 6 to 8.
Cook squash until tender; set aside.
Add cream of chicken soup to stuffing mix and mix.
Add 1 to 2 soup cans of water (mixture should be slightly soupy).
Add squash.
Place in greased baking dish; dot with margarine.
Bake in a 350° oven until golden brown and firm to touch.
Mix first 3 ingredients together well. Put into an 8 x 12-inch Pyrex dish.
Bake 20 minutes at 300° or until golden brown.
Let cool.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Combine crumbs with sugar and butter. Press on bottom of 9-inch pan.
Mix milk and pudding mix together.
Beat 1 to 2 minutes or until well blended.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in Cool Whip. Gradually stir in 1 cup of crushed wafers.
Spoon into serving dishes.
Top with remaining crushed wafers.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
This will make 8 servings.
Peel
and
slice eggplant 1/4 inch thick; sprinkle with salt and
let stand 15 minutes.
Blot off moisture with paper towel. Fry
eggplant in olive oil until lightly brown or soft to
touch. Saute
ground beef with onion and garlic; salt and pepper slightly.
Add
tomato
sauce
and
cook
for about 30 minutes. Layer
eggplant, then beef mixture and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Use 8 x 10-inch casserole to layer eggplant. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in square pan.
Sprinkle brown sugar in pan.
Arrange pineapple and cherries over sugar mixture.
Mix cake as directed on label.
Pour batter in pan. Bake for 50 minutes.
Turn upside-down on cake plate.
Peel avocados and break into chunks; do not smash.
Add sour cream, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
Mix well, but don't smash the avocados.
Strain a jar of salsa to remove liquid.
Add strained salsa to avocados and mix.
Serve with warm corn tortillas or tortilla chips.
In
a 10-inch Dutch oven heat margarine until sizzling. Add corn, sugar, salt and water.
Fry for 6 minutes.
Cook asparagus until just barely tender; drain. Add butter. Arrange in shallow buttered baking dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Over this pour egg and milk blended together.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and oregano. Dot with butter.
Sprinkle lightly with more cheese. Bake for 30 minutes at 375°.
Blend with ice in blender.
Pour into cocktail glasses. Yield:
8 to 10 servings.
Put butter and marshmallows together in a pan over low heat until melted.
Stir in popped corn and beat well.
Press into a tube cake pan and let cool.
Combine first 2 ingredients, then add the next ingredients except for the butter.
Stir into seafood mixture.
Spoon into a 6 x 10 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Combine 1 cup breadcrumbs with melted butter.
