Sprinkle over seafood mixture.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
In a large pot, saute onion and pepper in oil for one to two minutes; add tomatoes, okra and cabbage.
Stir well.
Add water; and on high heat, bring to boil.
Reduce heat to medium, cover pot and cook 30 to 45 minutes.
Add salt to taste.
Stir occasionally. Great with corn bread.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
Cook sugar, syrup and water to hard ball temperature.
(Will form a ball when dropped in glass of cold water and "clink" when tapped against side.)
Beat into the egg whites, pouring in very slowly.
Add vanilla and chopped nuts. Beat until stiff.
Brown hamburger meat; salt and pepper to taste.
Cut cabbage coarsely.
Chop onion.
In a 3-quart casserole dish, add 1/3 of the cabbage, 1/2 of the hamburger meat and 1/2 of the onion. Layer these.
Add 1/3 of the cabbage and the last 1/2 of the hamburger meat and the last 1/2 of the onion and the remaining 1/3 of the cabbage.
Pour tomato soup over the top.
Do not stir or mix.
Cover and bake in 350°
oven for 40 to 60 minutes.
Combine soup, 1/2 cup cheese, onion, salt and milk.
Add potatoes and mix well; put in greased baking dish.
Top with 1/4 cup cheese and bake at 350° until potatoes are tender, about 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Cook ground meat in a skillet; drain.
In an oblong baking dish, spread refried beans on bottom; spread the meat on top of beans.
Spread Old El Paso salsa over meat; sprinkle cheese.
Bake for approximately 30 minutes at 350°.
Let cool.
Spread the sour cream over top and garnish with black olives.
Serve as a meal with tortillas or as a dip with nacho chips.
Peel apples and slice thin.
Bring to rolling boil all ingredients except apples.
Add the apples, stirring carefully to cover with liquid.
Cook on medium to medium-high until apples are transparent.
Remove apples with slotted spoon, leaving juice to continue cooking until slightly thickened.
Pour over apples and allow to cool before serving.
Arrange bread slices in greased baking dish. Cover bread with browned, drained sausage.
Mix together beaten eggs, mustard and milk.
Pour over sausage.
Sprinkle cheese on top and cover with undiluted soup.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Cook together until veggies are cooked; add chicken.
Cook this in a 5-quart stew pan.
Eat with cornbread.
Brown bacon, hamburger and onion.
Mix in other ingredients. Bake 1 1/2 hours or put in crockpot and cook on high for 2-3 hours.
Blend catsup gradually into cream cheese.
Add salad dressing, onion, horseradish, Worcestershire sauce and Tabasco; blend thoroughly.
Fold in shrimp; chill at least 1 hour.
Makes 2 1/2 cups.
Fry chicken in butter until white on the outside.
Take chicken out and saute broccoli and cauliflower in remaining butter.
When thawed, mix in broccoli cheese soup and milk.
Heat until simmering, then pour chicken back in and cook for about 10 minutes.
In large stewer, brown hamburger; drain.
Add water.
Bring to a boil.
Add all ingredients.
Stir well, until mustard is dissolved.
Lower heat and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
*Individual pieces (i.e. breasts, thighs) may be used.

recipes.t: Dietetic "3 Minute Delite" Poppy Seed Cake
d: Sift dry ingredients; add liquids and mix until smooth.
Add 1 can poppy seed filling and/or 1 cup of chopped nuts (optional). Beat well on medium speed for 2 minutes.
Use a 10-inch tube pan. Do not grease pan.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until tested done.
Cool cake before removing from pan.
Saute onion in 1 stick of margarine; add to other ingredients. Bake at 425° for 30 minutes.
(Dot with butter before baking.) (This tastes better if it is made in a long dish so it will be thin.)
Mix 1/2 cup bread crumbs, 1/2 cup milk, 1 egg and 4 tablespoons ketchup together.
Make into balls in pan.
Mix all together in a 1 1/2 quart casserole. Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours. Stir once during baking.
Combine all ingredients in a slow cooker.
Cover and cook 4 to 6 hours on low heat.
Serves 8.
Mix mayonnaise and spices, then mix with remaining ingredients.
Toss and serve.
Place pork chops in shallow baking dish.
Cover with apple slices.
Pour apple juice on top.
Sprinkle with cinnamon; cover and bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Take off cover and bake 15 more minutes.
Serve and enjoy!
Mix together the flour, sugar and melted margarine; set aside. Cook the zucchini with lemon juice until tender.
Add the sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg; cook 1 more minute, then add 1/2 cup of the flour mixture that was set aside.
Grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Take 1/2 of the flour mixture; pat down into pan.
Put zucchini mixture on top.
Top with remaining flour mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Enjoy!
Tastes like apple pie.
Bake cake mix as directed.
While cooling, mix vanilla pudding as directed, adding cream cheese.
Layer strawberries on cake.
It is best to slice strawberries.
Next, pour pudding and ice with strawberries.
Serves 12.
Combine all ingredients and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Mix all ingredients.
Bake in a casserole dish in a 350° oven for 45 minutes.
Wash beans and place in a large kettle. Cover with the 2 quarts of cold water.

Simmer for 3 minutes and then allow to soak for 1 hour. Add ham, salt, pepper, bay leaves, carrot and celery. Cover and simmer for 3 1/2 hours. Add onion during the last 1/2 hour. Mash beans slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mix all ingredients together.
Stir in mayonnaise; salt and pepper to taste.
Mix ingredients well. Shape into loaf. Prepare sauce to pour over before baking.
In a 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish, place first 3 ingredients and microwave on High for 1 minute.
Stir well.
Add cereals, pretzels and nuts, mixing to coat.
Microwave 5 to 6 minutes, stirring after 3 minutes, until evenly toasted.
Yield: 2 1/2 quarts.
Drain pineapple, reserving juice. Add cold water to juice to measure 1 cup.
Stir boiling water into Jell-O in large bowl until completely dissolved. Stir in measured liquid.
Refrigerate until slightly thickened. Stir in whipped topping until smooth. Stir in pineapple, oranges, marshmallows and coconut. Spoon into mold. Refrigerate 3 hours or until firm.
Makes 10 servings.
Mix ingredients together.
Bake
in
a greased, floured tube pan at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.
Mix together.
Marinate 20 minutes to 2 hours.
Great on chicken, pork or shrimp.
Put flour and sugar in large bowl.
In pan bring to boil butter, shortening, cocoa and water.
Pour over flour and sugar; mix well.
Add buttermilk, vanilla, cinnamon and soda.
Mix well and pour batter into greased and floured sheet pan.
Bake for 20 minutes at 400°.
Make small meatballs with hamburger, onion, bread crumbs, salt, egg, tomato sauce and garlic powder.
Shape into balls.
Sift together flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Work shortening with a spoon until fluffy and creamy.
Add sugar gradually, while continuing to work with a spoon until light.
Add eggs and beat well.
Add flour mixture alternately with the bananas, a small amount at a time, beating smooth with a spoon after each addition.
Turn into a greased loaf pan, 9 x 5 x 3-inch.
Bake in a 350° oven for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together and pour in baking dish.
Bake 15 minutes.

recipes.t: Curried Herring With Dill(This Recipe Sounds Odd, But It'S Consistently A Hit!)
d: Combine all ingredients except herring and mix well.
Add the herring and refrigerate until it is time to serve.
Great with pumpernickel bread.
Serves 25 to 30 people as hors d'oeuvres. Keeps indefinitely in refrigerator.
Sprinkle cubed cheese and onion over potatoes.
Place pimento, garlic salt and parsley on top.
Put bread cubes over top of casserole.
Pour margarine over top.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Mix dry ingredients with wet.
Bake at 450° for 15 minutes. Serves 1 dozen.
Grease casserole dish.
Beat 8 eggs and milk with seasonings. Pour over croutons and cheese.
Fry and drain meat and crumble over casserole.
Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
Bake covered 350 for 30 minutes.
Remove foil and bake additional 15 minutes.
Mix well and
let
rise 1 hour and work down.
Let rise another hour and
work
out
into
either 6 loaves of bread or about 6 dozen
rolls.
Bake
at 350° for 1/2 hour for rolls or 45 minutes for bread.	Grease top after baking with lard.
Prepare the night before serving.
Use large bowl that can be covered tightly.
Break lettuce and cauliflower into bite size pieces.
Dice onion.
Layer in this order: lettuce, onion, bacon and cauliflower.
Combine the remaining ingredients and spread on top.
Cover tightly.
Mix well just before serving.
On wax paper, mix flour, 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, half of the pepper and half of the rosemary.
Coat chicken in flour mixture; shake off excess.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken; saute 5 minutes or until just cooked, turning once.
Place on platter.
Dredge pork chops in mixture of flour, salt, dry mustard and garlic powder.
Brown in oil in large skillet.
Place browned pork chops in crock-pot.
Add can of soup.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours (high for 3 1/2 hours).
Mix all ingredients together and bake for 40 minutes at 375 degrees.
Cook broccoli in boiling water until not quite done.
Mix mushroom soup with 1/2 cup milk and add onion juice.
Place layer of broccoli in casserole dish, layer of bread crumbs, layer of mushroom soup mixture and layer of cheese.
Repeat, making 2 layers.
Top with buttered crumbs and Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray glass pan, 9 x 13-inch or 2-quart.
Spread crescent rolls across bottom and sides of pan. Brown hamburger and 1/2 an onion in pan.
Drain.
Mix together.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, covered.
Sprinkle chops lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in large skillet.
Cook pork chops on high heat 4 to 5 minutes each side. Transfer to plate.
Cover.
Keep warm.
Add shallots and thyme to skillet.
Cook 1 minute.
Add Port wine, chicken broth and cherries to skillet.
Bring to boil.
Cook until reduced by half, about 3 minutes.
Return pork chops to skillet.
Cook until meat is heated through.
Sprinkle with parsley when serving.
Cut ends off cucumbers and pack in a gallon big-mouth jar. Cover with vinegar and let set for 6 weeks.
Drain crab meat.
Chop eggs. Blend all ingredients. Serve as stuffing for tomato on lettuce leaf.
Top with slices of avocado and sprinkle with paprika.
Serves 8 or 9.
Heat sugar, Crisco, honey and molasses in pan until shortening is melted.
Cook over low to medium heat and stir to prevent scorching or crystallizing.
In 8-cup measure, place the broccoli, carrot, onion and water. Cover with plastic wrap and microwave on High for 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Place the tomatoes, onions, bell peppers, and cucumbers on a serving platter.
In a bowl, whisk together the olive oil and vinegar.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour the vinaigrette over the vegetables.
Crumble the feta over the salad, sprinkle the olives and oregano over the top, and serve immediately.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine all ingredients; mix well.
Shape into cakes.
Fry in shortening (or oil) until done, browning on both sides.
Drain on paper towels.
Melt margarine and add flour.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Do not brown.
Stir in milk, salt and pepper.
Cook until smooth and thickened.
Combine drained macaroni with white sauce.
Pour into 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Top with cheese.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Place under broiler for a few minutes if a browner crust is desired.
Serves 8.
Brown smoked sausage in skillet.
Place all ingredients together in an electric rice cooker.
Cook just as you would cook rice.
When the bell rings on rice cooker the jambalaya is ready. Yields 6 to 8 servings.
In a 9 x 5-inch dish, dissolve the raspberry Jell-O in the hot water; add the grape juice.
Add the pineapple and chopped pecans. Chill until set.
Combine the cream cheese and Cool Whip and spread over Jell-O mixture.
Sprinkle nuts over top and chill.
Mix separately from cake.
Pour this mixture over unbaked cake mix.
Bake 50 minutes at 350°.
Toast bread.
Break into cubes and turn into 8 1/4 x 1 3/4-inch ovenware dish.
Add hot milk.
Let stand 15 minutes. Beat together eggs, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and sweetener until light.
Add apples and raisins into bread mixture. Place into shallow baking pan.
Fill with water.
Bake at 350° until knife inserted in center comes clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Serve warm or cold.
Serves 8.
Saute in butter; onion, garlic, celery, parsley and bell pepper.
Add shrimp and cook 10 minutes.
Combine cheeses, half and half and flour.
Cook macaroni according to package directions; rinse and drain.
Add tuna, eggs, pepper and celery to suit your taste.
Add salt and pepper.
Mix and sprinkle chopped tomato on top for garnish.
Refrigerate.
Cook sausage in large skillet until light in color.
Remove from pan, leaving all sausage drippings.
(With fork, tear up sausage and reserve.)
To drippings, blend in flour, salt and pepper (to taste).
To this add milk slowly, stirring.
When mixture begins to thicken, add sausage.
Delicious over homemade baked biscuits or crunchy buttered toast.
Cook chicken; save broth.
Mix all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes.
Serve over fluffy rice.
Combine all ingredients in large baking pan and bake at 300° for 3 hours.
Brown hamburger.
Add onion, pepper and rest of ingredients. Simmer for 30 minutes; serve on rolls.
Bring to boil all ingredients.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
Brown meat and onion in large skillet; drain fat.
Stir in water, catsup, mustard, salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice; cover.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese; cover.
Let stand until cheese melts.
Put soda in
buttermilk
and let stand 3 minutes.
Cook all ingredients,
including
buttermilk,
to
soft ball stage. Cool and beat
until creamy.
Pour into buttered pan or plate. Cut into squares
when set.	Nuts, coconut or other flavorings may be added.
In medium skillet, melt butter; stir in soup mix and parsley blended with water.
Add fish.
Simmer, covered, 10 minutes or until fish flakes.
Makes about 4 servings.
Layer casserole dish with chicken, chips and cheese.
Mix soups and Ro-Tel in saucepan; heat to boiling.
Pour half over layer.
Make another layer of chicken, chips and cheese.
Pour remaining soup mixture on top.
Top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbling hot.
Cream butter and Crisco together.
To butter and Crisco, add sugar until creamed.
Add eggs, one at a time and beat well. Alternately, add flour, milk and water.
Beat well.
Pour in floured and greased tube pan.
Bake at 300° for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes longer.
Put pan in cold oven; set temperature and do not open door while baking.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Mix all ingredients and form into small balls.
Bake on a rack in a shallow pan for 20 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix semi-sweet chocolate chips, chopped nuts, marshmallow, margarine and vanilla.
In a 3-quart saucepan, mix sugar and milk.
Cook over medium high heat; stir constantly. When mixture boils, continue cooking 6 minutes.
Stir constantly. Pour ingredients in bowl; stir until chips dissolve and mixture is smooth.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch buttered pan.
Let set 6 hours or overnight.
Refrigerates well.
Let stand at room temperature for easy cutting.
Cream the cream cheese until soft and smooth.
Slowly blend in sugar; add melted chocolate and other ingredients.
Press into well-buttered shallow pan; refrigerate until firm.
For softer fudge, blend in 1 teaspoon milk.
Brown ground beef and soup.
Place on bottom of casserole dish, then drain green beans and put over meat mixture.
Add mashed potatoes, then top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Serves 4 to 6 people.
Heat oil in large pot.
Add chopped onion, celery and carrot. Cook 2 minutes.
Add cauliflower; cover.
Cook 15 minutes.
Add broth and bring to boil 5 minutes.
In a large heavy saucepan, melt the margarine.
Add the onion and cook, uncovered, until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the beef broth and water and bring to a boil, about 4 minutes.
Add peas and potatoes.
Adjust heat so that the mixture bubbles gently, cover and cook for 30 minutes, or until the peas and potatoes are tender. Remove from heat and cool 10 minutes.
In an electric blender or food processor puree the soup in 5 batches, whirling each batch about 15 seconds.
Return to the pan, set over low heat and bring to serving temperature, stirring often.
Add pepper.
Serves 4.
Crust:
Mix together Zwieback crackers, butter and sugar. Line bottom of cheese cake pan (9 1/2 x 3-inch).

recipes.t: Linguine With Shrimp Scampi And Broccoli
d: Melt 1/2 butter in oil and saute shrimp for 2 minutes.
Put aside.
Put 1/2 butter, 2 cloves garlic and olive oil in.
Add broccoli, wine, parsley and pepper.
Mix together, then add shrimp.
Serve over cooked linguine.
Melt shortening and mix with sugar, add eggs one at a time. Add flour, nuts and chocolate chips.
Batter will be sticky! Spread in a greased 9 x 12-inch pan.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes at 350°.
Let cool before cutting.
(These don't cut too neatly!)
Over low heat, saute squash and onions until tender-crisp. Salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in shrimp soup and water chestnuts.
Place in greased casserole and sprinkle with buttered crumbs on top.
Bake at 350° until hot and bubbly.
Cut the pork chops off the bone in small pieces.
Put in pot and fry.
Get the link sausage, slice thin.
Put aside until the pork is done, then fry the sausage.
Get out of pot and drain most of the grease, leave enough to fry the onion (cut up in small pieces), green onion (cut in small pieces) and bell pepper (cut in small pieces).
When that is done, add the meat and fry a few minutes more, then add the rice and fry about 10 minutes all together; then add spice, salt and pepper.
Add water and cook until it is done.
Combine the boiled potatoes, celery and red onion; set aside. Separately combine the last 3 ingredients and add to potatoes; toss to coat.
Chill.
Serves 4 to 6.
Cook broccoli and drain.
Add rest of ingredients and bake in 1-quart casserole at 350° for 30 minutes.
Stir together juice of lemon, egg yolks and salt; cook until thick.
Cool.
Prepare pineapple, grapes and marshmallows.
Now stir lemon mixture into the whipped cream.
Stir into fruit mixture.
Refrigerate for 24 hours.
This salad is not to be tasted or eaten before time is up.
Set oven at 350°.
Saute onions and celery with Tabasco until soft.
Drain tuna and shred.
Mix in mayonnaise, bread crumbs, half and half, 1 cup cheese, pepper and almonds.
Stir in onions and celery mixture, spoon into 3 to 4-quart casserole and top with remaining cheese.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Serve hot with crackers.
Peel and slice apples thinly into a 9-inch (2-inch deep) pie pan (or glass layer cake pan).
Mix sugar (1/2 cup) and cinnamon and sprinkle over apples.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into bowl.
Add orange juice (or milk), egg, water and melted butter (or margarine).
Mix until smooth with wooden spoon.
Pour over apples.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour or until done.
Put potatoes, onions and celery in a small amount of water. Cook until tender.
Add 2 cups corn, ham, milk and soup.
Stir well while heating.
Simmer ground beef, water and vinegar for 30 minutes.
Add catsup, mustard, sugar, salt and onion.
Cook on low heat for 30 minutes.
Serve on hot dogs or hamburger buns.
Mix all ingredients.
Spray iron skillet with nonstick buttery flavored Pam.
Bake at 450° about 30 to 40 minutes or until golden brown.
Blend together eggs, oil, and sugar until creamy.
Add flour, a small amount at a time, blending well after each addition. Batter will be stiff.
Fold in apples, coconut, and pecans.
Place in greased and floured 10 inch tube pan;
bake at 350 degrees about one hour or until wooded pick inserted in center of cake comes out
clean.
Cool in pan for 30 minutes; remove cake.
Mix all dry ingredients together.
Gradually add sour milk or buttermilk.
Put into prepared pan and bake for 30 minutes at 375°.
Take dressing mix; pour in sour cream, onion, basil and oregano.
Mix well.
Stir in cooked spinach; chill 1 hour.
Serve with raw vegetables or any type of wheat crackers.
Saute onion, green pepper and garlic in oil.
Add 3 tablespoons of flour until it gets brown.
Throw in everything except meat. Cook for 20 minutes.
Take bay leaves out and reheat for 5 minutes more.
Then add meat.
Meanwhile, have your rice cooked to mix in when done cooking.
Chop prunes.
Add to chopped nuts with brown sugar, flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix.
Fold into well beaten eggs.
Spread in greased 9-inch square pan.
Bake at 325° for 25 to 30 minutes. Cool in pan for 5 to 10 minutes.
Cut into 25 pieces.
Roll in confectioners powdered sugar, if desired.
Combine pineapple, lemonade, lemon juice, powdered punch, sugar and raspberries in a large container.
Add enough water to make 2 gallons.
Place in freezer and freeze.
About 2 hours before serving, remove from the freezer.
Using a potato masher or pastry mixer, "slush it," then mix in the pop.
Brown the meat; drain and set aside.
Blend mayonnaise, milk, eggs and cornstarch until smooth.
Stir in the meat, grated cheeses, onion, salt and pepper.
Turn into the pie shell.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Melt caramel topping, combined with 1/4 cup flour.
Combine remaining ingredients except chocolate chips and pecans in mixing bowl.
Press half of crumbs into bottom of greased 13 x 9 pan. Bake 10 minutes at 350°.
Remove from oven.
Sprinkle chocolate chips and pecans and spread caramel topping on cooked crumbs. Sprinkle remaining crumbs on top.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes longer or until golden brown.
Chill 1 to 2 hours.
Place spices in a spice ball or bag.
Combine all ingredients. Cover and simmer at least 45 minutes.
Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Stir until smooth.
Cook 4 to 5 minutes until thickened.
Add 1 teaspoon vanilla stirring until smooth and glossy.
Serve hot.
Makes 1 3/4 cups.
Cream butter.
Add sugar and beat well.
Add whipping cream, eggs and flour (alternately).
Mix well.
Add vanilla.
Bake in a greased and floured Bundt pan in a cold oven at 325° for 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Asparagus Casserole(An Extra Easy Side Dish)
d: Empty the drained asparagus into an ovensafe casserole dish. Spoon soup evenly over asparagus.
Bake at 350° until mixture bubbles, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Add cheese and bake another 15 minutes.
Grease a 9 x 13 casserole dish.
Spread chicken on bottom of dish.
Mix celery, soup, water chestnuts, mushrooms and mayonnaise together.
Pour over chicken.
Mix stuffing with melted butter. Spread over chicken mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Makes 12 servings.
Drain the peach syrup into a saucepan.
Add sugar, vinegar and spices and boil 5 minutes.
Add peaches and simmer 5 minutes. Allow fruit to stand in syrup overnight.
Serve chilled.
Partially bake pie shell.
Sprinkle all of the Monterey Jack, half of the Cheddar and the chilli peppers in shell.
Beat remaining ingredients together and add to pie shell mixture. Sprinkle remainder of Cheddar on top.
Bake at 325° for 40 minutes, or until crust is brown.
Preheat oven to 450°.
In a mixing bowl, stir together flour, baking powder, rice bran, apple fiber and salt.
Or you could do this in a food processor.
Add milk all at once; stir until ingredients are just combined.
If you are doing this in a food processor, pulse the machine a few times just until dough is combined.
If the dough seems a little dry, sprinkle on a tablespoon of water and work it in.
Place chicken in bottom of pan with broth and pepper.
Mix flour, baking powder and milk.
Pour over chicken.
Melt margarine and pour over flour mixture.
Bake in a moderate oven until crust browns.
(I like to use 2 cups of chicken broth as it makes more gravy.)
Roast and peel peppers.
Slit them down the center, lengthwise and fill with both kinds of cheese.
Seal and roll in flour. Continue until all peppers are done.
Separate eggs and whip whites until medium peaks form.
Mix together dry ingredients.
Add eggs and beat well.
Add cream, butter, flavorings and yeast.
Allow dough to rise, work down and allow to rise a second time.
Drop by spoonfuls into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Combine 3/4 cup sugar with cornstarch and lime peel in medium saucepan and mix well.
Add lime juice and stir until smooth. Blend in half and half and butter.
Place over medium heat and stir until mixture thickens and starts to boil.
Remove from heat and let cool, stirring occasionally.
Fold in sour cream.
Turn into pie shell.
Combine whipping cream and sugar.
Whip until soft peaks.
Spread atop pie.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in skillet; add garlic.
Lightly saute. Add cubed tomatoes and juice from can; cook 1 minute.
Add wine, salt, fresh black pepper, basil and oregano.
Cook over moderate heat for 10 minutes.
Heat remaining olive oil in a separate skillet.
Saute shrimp for 1 minute, turning once.
Sprinkle with red pepper flakes; remove from heat.
Spoon shrimp and pan juices into a large baking dish.
Crumble Feta cheese over shrimp.
Pour tomato sauce over all.
Just before serving, bake 10 to 15 minutes in a 400° oven until sizzling.
Serve over cooked linguine.

Combine rhubarb, sugar, flour and lemon rind; mix well. Blend in honey. Put the pie crust in a pie pan and fill with mixture. Put top crust on and seal edges. Bake at 450° for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 350° and continue baking for 35 to 45 minutes.
Melt butter in skillet.
Add summer squash, onion, salt, pepper and tomatoes.
Cook, covered, for 10 to 15 minutes or until squash is tender.
Sprinkle with cheese and soy sauce, if desired.
Crush cookies with a rolling pin or in blender until you have 2 cups.
Mix with cinnamon and 1/2 cup melted butter.
Press into bottom and sides of a 9-inch spring-form pan.
Chill.
Beat sugar with eggs until light and fluffy; add cream cheese gradually, beating well after each addition.
Melt the chocolate and add to the egg mixture, along with vanilla and sour cream, beating constantly.
Add melted butter and mix well.
Pour mixture into chilled pie dish and bake at about 350° for 45 minutes.
Chill overnight.
Serves 20.
Boil chicken. Saute mushrooms in butter.
Place chicken in casserole dish.
Pour soup over the chicken. Sprinkle with cheese and top with mushrooms. Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Boil clean unpeeled potatoes and eggs together until potatoes are to desired firmness.
Cool potatoes and eggs in cool water until comfortable to handle.
Rub the peeling off potatoes using fingers (faster than with knife!).
Remove eggshells from eggs. Dice or mash eggs and potatoes in large bowl along with rest of ingredients and mix well.
Chill (or serve room temperature) and serve.
Even better the next day!
Mix flour and shortening together with hand pastry blender. Beat egg in separate container and add water and beat together. Add this mixture to dry ingredients.
Melt butter in skillet.
Saute garlic and add pasta and cheese.
Mix on low heat until cheese is melted.
Serve on plate and top with your favorite sauce.
Heat oven to 375°.
Grease 13 x 9-inch pan.
In medium saucepan, combine the first 4 ingredients (raisins, milk, etc.) Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, just until mixture begins to bubble.
Remove from heat; cool slightly and set aside. Beat margarine, sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Add remaining ingredients; blend until evenly mixed and crumbly.
Reserve 2 cups.
Press remaining mixture onto bottom of prepared pan. Spread raisin mixture to within 1/2-inch of edge.
Sprinkle with remaining oat mixture; pat lightly.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Cool; cut into 1 x 2-inch bars.
Makes 4 dozen.
Drain beets, reserving liquid.
Add enough water to beet juice to make 2/3 cup liquid.
Combine cornstarch and pepper in saucepan.
Add liquid and vinegar.
Stir until smooth.
Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and boils.
Boil 1 minute, stirring.
Add sliced beets and sugar.
Heat through.
In large skillet, blend soup mix with water.
Boil and continue boiling, stirring for 1 minute until thickened.
Add chicken.
Cut into strips and add partially thawed and drained vegetables (ex. broccoli, cauliflower and carrots).
Cook, uncovered, stirring frequently for 5 minutes or until chicken is done.
Serve over hot rice.
Chop all together.
Add 1/2 cup salt to vegetable mixture. Let stand 2 hours.
Drain off juice.
Mix 6 cups of sugar and 1 teaspoon celery seed.
Mix all; put in jars unsealed.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain. Place in a 3-quart slow cooker.
Mix together the vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, then slowly add the olive oil.
If the sauce is too thick, add some water.
Serve with asparagus, salad or your favorite vegetable.
Sift together flour, baking powder and salt.
Add shortening, brown sugar, eggs, vanilla and milk.
Beat until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Stir in oats.
Drop from teaspoons onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake in preheated moderate oven (350°) for 12 to 15 minutes.

Boil first 3 ingredients together for 3 minutes. Dissolve jello in 1 cup hot water. Add to mixture. Put into freezer to thicken. Whip cream to a peak, then beat in cream cheese and add to jello. Mix all. Refrigerate overnight.
Heat sour cream in top of double boiler, until slightly yellow around edges.
Soften yeast in water, let stand 5-10 minutes.
Put butter, suger, and salt in a large bowl, immediately pour sour cream over ingredients in boel and stir until butter is melted. Cook to luke warm.
Blend 1 cup flour into sour cream mixture beating until smooth, stir softened yeast, and add to flour mixture, mixing well.
Add 1 cup of remaining flour and beat until smooth.
Thoroughly beat in eggs and remaining flour.
Cover bowl and refrigerate 6 hours or overnight.
Divide dough into 4 parts. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into a round (1/4 inch thick).
Cut each round into 12 wedged shape pieces.
Roll up beginning at the wide end.
Place rolls on greased sheets with points underneath.
Curve into crescents.
Let stand in warm place 1 hour.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Makes 4 dozen.
Cook broccoli in boiling, salted water until tender; drain. Arrange stalks in greased 11 1/2 x 7 1/2 x 1 1/2-inch Pyrex baking dish with flowerets facing outward.
Place chicken on top of broccoli.
Combine soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder. Pour over chicken.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Combine crumbs and butter.
Sprinkle over dish.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Garnish with pimento strips.
Serves 4 to 6.
Crumble uncooked chuck in bottom of 8 x 8-inch casserole.
Add onions, cheese, salt and pepper.
Mix soup and milk; pour over top.
Add Tater Tots on top and bake in a 375° oven for 1 hour, or until Tater Tots are brown.
Shape meatball mixture into balls.
Brown in a skillet, then drain off grease.
Place in crock-pot.
In a large 10-inch glass pie plate, melt margarine; set aside. In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs, one at a time, with a fork. Add sugar; stir well.
Add flour; stir well.
Add flavoring and stir.
Add milk; mix and pour into pie plate.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes; turn down to 300° and bake 30 more minutes.
Cool at least 2 hours before cutting.
Mix all ingredients together.
Place in jello mold.
Chill. Serve with crackers.
Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup; level off.
In large bowl, combine 2 cups flour, sugar, salt, yeast, cinnamon, and lemon peel; blend well.
In small saucepan, heat water, milk and butter until very warm (120° to 130°).
Add warm liquid and egg to flour mixture.
Blend at low speed with electric mixer until moistened; beat 3 minutes at medium speed.
By hand stir in 3 to 4 cups flour until dough pulls cleanly away from sides of bowl. Stir 1 cup raisins into dough.
On floured surface, knead in 1 to 2 cups flour until dough is smooth and elastic with blisters under the surface, about 10 minutes.
Place dough in greased bowl; cover loosely with plastic wrap and cloth towel.
Let rise in warm place until light and doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Brown turkey with onions and add to a large kettle with the other vegetables and juice.
Cook until the vegetables are tender. Water or chicken broth may be added if too thick.
Freezes well. I use zucchini, carrots, potatoes, green beans, onion, peas and celery.
Squeeze moisture from vegetable. Combine all ingredients except vegetable. Beat until smooth. Fold in chopped vegetable. Pour into greased 13 x 9-inch casserole dish.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 1 hour.
Dissolve jello in water.
Add frozen strawberries.
Let stand until firm.
Combine all ingredients down to cloves on low speed of mixer, then on high until well blended.
Stir in nuts and raisins.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes or until done.
Combine all ingredients.
Serve with fresh vegetables...cucumbers, carrots, celery etc or with chips as a dip.
Mix first four ingredients together.
Bring to a boil.
Let cool.
Mix altogether.
Spread into 2 loaf pans, greased.
Bake slowly at 275° for 2 hours.
Mix all ingredients and roll into small balls.
Press top with fork that has been dipped in flour to prevent sticking.
Bake in 350° oven until lightly browned on top, 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool.
In frying pan, melt butter.
Stir in olive oil, lemon juice, scallions, garlic, salt and pepper.
Place shrimp in the frying pan.
Toss around until coated with mixture and slightly pink.
You will also need 1 Reynolds| Pot Lux| cookware, 8 x 8-inch pan.
Brown chicken breasts in butter, then place in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Mix the soup, sour cream and mushrooms; pour 1/4 of this mixture over the chicken breasts.
Make a layer of asparagus spears.
Cover with 1/2 Parmesan cheese.
Add remainder of soup mixture; cover with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, uncovered.
Peel and slice vegetables.
Place roast and vegetables in slow cooker.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add water.
Cook until roast and vegetables are tender.
Peel off skin of eggplant.
Slice into medium slices, a little less than 1/4 inch thick.
Place in a colander and let drain for a few hours.
Dip slices in flour, then into batter of eggs, salt, pepper, minced garlic, Romano cheese and chopped parsley. Dip slices into bread crumbs, then into flat dish lined with waxed paper.
Use wax paper between each layer.
After all slices are breaded, place in refrigerator for at least 4 - 5 hours or preferably overnight.
Mix in order given and drop by teaspoons 2-inches apart onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake in a hot oven 7 to 10 minutes. Remove from oven. Cool 1 minute before taking from the pan.
Mix buttermilk and pudding. Fold in Cool Whip.
Add fruit and nuts. Refrigerate.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Mix all dry ingredients in mixer bowl using dough hook.
Blend well.
Mix oil and 1 cup of water and pour into the dry ingredients and blend. Add warm water until dough is wet, but stiff.
Mix on high until dough leaves sides of bowl.
Cover bowl and let dough rise to double in size.
Punch down and knead 2 to 3 minutes.
Form rolls by pinching off 2-ounce pieces.
Place on lightly oiled baking sheet.
Let rise until doubled in size.
Bake at 400° for 20 to 25 minutes, until lightly browned.
Drain juice from clams and pour over vegetables.
In small pan, add enough water to cover vegetables.
Simmer until tender.
Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, peas and ham.
In a small bowl, mix the flour, parsley, salt and pepper into soup.
Pour over potato mixture and blend well.
Pour into an 8 x 8-inch baking dish sprayed with butter-flavored cooking spray.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes.
Serves 6.
Layer in a large bowl the lettuce (broken up in bite size), sliced onions, cut up cauliflower and bacon bits.
Sprinkle the sugar.
Spread the Miracle Whip. Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese. Cover tightly and refrigerate 4 hours to overnight. Toss before serving.
Salt and pepper roast and brown well.
Add all ingredients and roast in oven at 325° for approximately 2 1/2 hours or until done. For best results, use a cooking bag.
Leftover juices make an excellent gravy.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease 9 x 13 pan.
In a large bowl, combine cake mix, pie filling and eggs.
Beat 2 minutes.
In small bowl, combine sugar and cinnamon.
Pour 1/2 cake batter in pan. Sprinkle 1/2 sugar mixture on batter.
Add remaining batter and sprinkle with remaining sugar.
Bake 35 minutes or until done.
Cover the green peas with hot water to which the sliced onion has been added and cook until the peas can be mashed.
Mash the peas and add the one pint of hot water.
Blend the margarine and flour and cook a minute or so with constant stirring, but do not brown.
Add the peas, then the milk and cream.
Season to taste with salt and white pepper and allow to boil up once.
Strain and serve.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Beat white sugar, eggs, Crisco, brown sugar, salt and molasses well, then add sour milk, soda, cinnamon, flour, applesauce, baking powder and allspice.
Beat thoroughly.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 50 minutes in loaf pan.
Top with whipped cream to serve.
Melt butter.
Add sugar and heat slowly, stirring until sugar is dissolved.
Stir in crumbs, cereal and chopped nuts.
Press half of crumb mixture into bottom of a 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan, reserving remaining mixture for topping.
Heat undiluted orange juice.
Add marshmallows, stirring until they are melted.
Cool until mixture begins to thicken, then whip until light and fluffy. Whip cream and fold into orange mixture.
Pour orange mixture over crumb layer.
Top with remaining crumbs.
Freeze until firm. Serves 15.
Heat oven to 275°.
Grease a 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 x 1-inch pan with shortening.
Mix snacks and nuts in large bowl.
Beat egg whites, orange juice, sugar and cinnamon in small bowl, using wire whisk or hand beater until foamy.
Pour over snack mixture and stir until evenly coated.
Spread in pan.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes until light brown and crisp.
Cool; store in airtight container.
Yields about 10 cups snack.

recipes.t: Cranberry Pork Chops(Easy, Tasty And Festive)
d: Brown chops in bacon drippings; season with salt and pepper. Meanwhile, mix remaining ingredients in a bowl.
Place chops in a baking dish, spread with cranberry mixture and cover.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven for about 1 hour.
Serve with baked sweet potatoes.
Serves 4.
Mix all together. Fold in egg whites.
Pour into 3 greased and floured 9-inch pans. Bake at 350° for about 35 minutes or can bake in oblong baking pan for 45 minutes.

Line 8 x 8 x 2-inch or 9 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan with foil, extending foil over edges of pan; butter foil. Set aside. Stir baking pieces and condensed milk in heavy, large saucepan over low heat just until pieces are melted and mixture is smooth. Remove from heat. Stir in lime peel and lime juice. Stir in 1 cup Macadamia nuts; spread mixture evenly into the prepared pan. If desired, sprinkle a few coarsely chopped Macadamia nuts on top. Cover and chill for 2 hours or until firm. Lift fudge from pan using edges of foil. Peel off foil. Cut into pieces. Store in airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week or in the freezer for up to 2 months. Makes 2 1/2 pounds (64 servings).
Combine all ingredients and put in ungreased baking dish. Dice American cheese on top.
Add crushed potato chips.
Bake at 400° until bubbly.
Put all ingredients in blender and mix well.
Chill for 1 hour.
Cook rice as directed.
In skillet, saute onion, peppers, squash, carrots and broccoli.
Add cubed, cooked chicken or pork. Add all of mixture to rice.
Use a little soy sauce for flavor. Really good!

Pour the boiling water over the oatmeal. Let stand 20 minutes. Mix the margarine, white sugar, brown sugar, eggs, flour, soda, cinnamon, salt and vanilla. Add oatmeal. Mix and bake in 9 x 13-inch greased pan 30 minutes in 350° oven.
Mix well; top with slivered almonds.
Bake at 375° for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with buffet bread or crackers.
Mix dough; divide into two loaves.
Wrap in wax paper and put in refrigerator for 2 or 3 hours or it can be frozen.
Slice thin and bake at 325° until light brown.
Set out a small baking dish.
Wash carrots and scrape.
Cook whole carrots 15 to 25 minutes or until just tender.
Meanwhile, combine brown sugar, water and margarine in small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until sugar is dissolved.
Drain carrots and place in baking dish.
Cover with sugar mixture.
Bake at 350° about 10 minutes or until carrots are completely glazed.
Baste occasionally.

recipes.t: Seasoned Oyster Crackers For Snacking(Just Like Potato Chips, It'S Hard To Eat O
d: Shake all ingredients together in a brown paper bag.
Let stand in brown paper bag for 24 hours.
Store in tins or tightly sealed containers.
Cream together butter and sugar.
Add eggs and molasses.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to butter mixture alternately with water.
Spread onto 2 jelly roll pans, 11 x 16-inch.
Bake in 350° oven for 25 minutes.
Frost and cut into squares.
Roll into 1-inch balls.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Makes about 40 to 45 cheese balls.
Put country style spareribs in roaster (as many as you want). Add salt, lemon pepper, onion flakes and water.
Place lettuce and onions in a salad bowl; set aside.
In a skillet, fry bacon until crisp.
Remove bacon; set aside.
In the drippings, combine all remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Immediately pour over salad.
Crumble bacon and add to salad; toss well.
Serve immediately.
Yields 4 servings.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Remove half of fat.
Add onion, vinegar and sugar.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Drain beans, reserving 1/2 cup liquid.
Add reserved liquid to beans and vinegar mixture. Heat through and serve hot.
Yields 4 servings.

recipes.t: Jumbo Shrimp In Spicy Wine Sauce
d: In a frying
pan,
saute
the shrimp in olive oil for 1 minute,
sprinkle
with
jalapeno
and red pepper flakes.
Add lemon juice
and
wine
to	pan
and cook shrimp, covered over medium heat
for
more
minutes or until shrimp turns pink. Remove shrimp
to a serving bowl.
Strain the sauce and reduce it over
high	heat
to make 1/2 cup.	Pour sauce over shrimp. May be served hot or cold.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix butter, eggs, sugar, lemon juice and vanilla together. Mix together the flour, baking powder, fruits and pecans.
Add this to butter mixture.
Pour into tube pan.
Place in a cold oven; bake at 250° for 2 1/2 hours.

Preheat oven to 350 F. Mix dressing and chiles in a blender until smooth. Transfer to a small bowl, chill. Combine flour and taco mix in a shallow dish, mix well. Stir in oil until mixed well. If using wings remove tips first. Coat chicken with mixture on all sides. Place on slightly greased cookie pan. Bake for 15 minutes, turn over and bake an additional 15 minutes, or until chicken is tender. Mix parsley in with ranch dressing. Use dressing as a dipping sauce.
Preheat oven to 350°. Peel apples and slice thinly.
Put into saucepan with water and raisins. Cover and cook 15 minutes until soft.
Cut bread into fingers and arrange half in a pie dish, buttered side down.
Cover with apple mixture, then bread butter side up. Top with sugar and spices. Bake 20 minutes.
Sift together first 5 ingredients.
Add milk, oil and vanilla. Mix until smooth.
Stir in nuts.
Pour into greased 8 x 8 x 2-inch baking pan.
Combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over batter.
Bake at 350° for about 45 minutes.
In a large boiler, heat peanut butter, Karo and sugar over medium heat until warm.
Stir in Rice Krispies.
Stir until Rice Krispies are mixed in well.
Place on buttered sheets.
Cut and serve.
Process all ingredients in a blender, stopping to scrape down sides.
Pour mixture into chilled glasses.
Mix together mayonnaise, cheese, onions, garlic powder and pepper.
Toss with potatoes and put in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan. Crumble 1/2 pound cooked bacon.
Cover casserole with bacon and sliced green olives.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Peel and cut potatoes and carrots.
Salt and pepper chicken. Arrange chicken in casserole dish.
Place potatoes and carrots in dish around chicken.
Then add cream of chicken and cream of mushroom soups on top of ingredients.
Bake at 375° for 1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Sausage With Cabbage, Sweet Potatoes(Makes 4 Servings)
d: Stir chicken broth and mustard in deep 12-inch skillet. Add sweet potatoes and onions. Reduce heat to medium. Cover and cook about 5 minutes until potatoes are tender, stirring occasionally. Add smoked sausage and cabbage. Cover and cook 15 minutes longer, stirring once or twice until potatoes are tender and cabbage is crisp-tender. Stir in apples. Cover and simmer 3 minutes until apple is crisp-tender.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Mix all ingredients together and put into a greased and floured tube pan.
Bake for 1 1/2 hours.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Mix all ingredients just before serving.
Line cupcake pans with liners.
Place a vanilla wafer in bottom of each liner.
In small bowl, beat cream cheese, sugar, eggs, lemon juice and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Fill the liners 3/4 full with cheese mixture.
Bake in a preheated 375° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until set.
Top each with spoonful of filling and 1 teaspoon nuts.
Chill.
In food processor (you can skip dicing steps), process peppers, salt, garlic, oregano and cumin on "momentary" until finely chopped.
Quarter onion.
Add to mixture and dice.
Add 1/2 cup V-8 (hot) and tomatoes (quartered) and process until diced.
Add vinegar and cilantro.
Process briefly.
Yields 2 cups.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl.
Add powdered sugar until mixture is stiff enough to work with.
In 4-quart saucepan, combine soup, milk, cheese, garlic powder and pepper.
Add broccoli and carrot.
Heat to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Cover; cook over low heat for 5 minutes or until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally.
Serves 3 to 4.
Use double boiler.
Beat egg yolks.
Add sugar and mix.
Add flour and cocoa.
Mix.
Add milk and water.
Cook until thick. Stir occasionally.
When thick, add vanilla.
Pour into baked pie shells.
Beat egg whites.
Put on top of pie.
Bake at 375° until golden.
Makes 3 pies or 2 deep dish pies.
Boil potatoes until soft.
Peel and slice.
Mix all ingredients together in large bowl and bake at 350° for 1 hour (uncovered).
Mix all together and put in refrigerator.
Sift dry ingredients in bowl.
Beat eggs and add the milk and stir into dry ingredients. Mix well.
Add the sliced apples.
Drop batter by spoonfuls into hot oil and fry.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease well a baking sheet.
Place vinegar in measuring cup; add enough evaporated milk to vinegar to make 1 cup.
Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs and vanilla, blending well.
Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
Add milk mixture and dry ingredients alternately to creamed mixture, stirring well after each addition.
Stir in chopped nuts
Cook, drain, rinse and cool spaghetti.
Combine all ingredients in a screw-top jar.
Cover tightly and shake vigorously to blend well.
Store covered in refrigerator. Shake well before using.
Brown beef and drain well.
Place all ingredients in crock-pot.
Cover and cook on low for 12 to 15 hours.
Spray inside of double grocery bag with Pam.
Combine brown sugar, margarine, salt, cream of tartar and white syrup for 3 minutes on stove or 2 minutes in microwave.
Remove from heat and add soda.
Stir.
Mix all ingredients together and serve.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.
Roll in butter and then into sugar and cinnamon mixture.
Grease bottom of 9 x 2 x 13-inch pan.
Spread diced chicken on bottom.
Spread Stove Top evenly over chicken, then cheese and then pour mixture of soup and milk over stuffing and cheese. Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes at 350°.
Let cool for 10 minutes. Serve.
Mix Crisco, sugar and eggs; add applesauce.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to mixture.
Dredge raisins and nuts in flour and fold in.
Bake in greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan for 1 hour at 350°.
Combine chocolate and peanut butter chips in a large glass mixing bowl.
Microwave on High until melted.
Blend in remaining ingredients in order listed. Spread in a 9 x 13-inch dish.
Let stand at room temperature before cutting.
Cook fettucine according to directions.
Melt margarine in a large pan; saute onion, bell pepper and celery until golden.
Stir in soups, garlic and sherry.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in sour cream and crawfish.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve over cooked fettucine.
Serves 6.
Cook onion in butter until soft; blend in flour and salt. Cook bacon and drain.
Gradually add sour cream to first mixture, stirring constantly.
Heat to boiling; add corn.
Bring to boil; fold in 1/2 cup crumbled bacon.
Turn into serving dish; garnish with remaining bacon.
Can be fixed ahead and cooked in 350° oven for about 20 minutes or until hot.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in skillet.
Add chicken; cook until browned.
Remove chicken.
Add broth, 1/2 cup water and broccoli. Stir.
Heat to a boil.
Stir in rice and cheese.
Top with chicken; cover.
Cook on low heat for 5 minutes or until cooked through.
Gently stir until cheese is melted.
Grease a 10 x 6-inch baking dish.
In 2-quart saucepan over high heat in 1-inch boiling water, heat broccoli and 1/2 teaspoon salt to boiling; cover and cook 10 minutes.
Drain.
Set aside.
Make mashed potatoes as directed. Stir in mustard, egg and tuna; shape and roll in butter and bread crumbs. Bake in preheated oven at 450° for 10 to 15 minutes. Serve with mushroom or tomato sauce.
In the top of a double boiler, stir together cocoa, sugar and salt.
Gradually add boiling water.
Place over direct heat and boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add milk and cinnamon sticks and place over boiling water.
Stir and heat 10 minutes. Remove sticks and stir in vanilla.
Beat with a wire whisk to froth milk.
Serve immediately.
Yields 4 servings.

recipes.t: Heyward'S Good For What Ails You Salad(Makes Enough For A Dozen People)
d: Mix fruit and sprinkle with lemon juice to prevent darkening. Serve in a large glass bowl.
Good for Potluck suppers.
Crumble Oreo cookies and place in bottom of a 9 x 9-inch container.
Pour chocolate syrup on top.
Dip out desired amount of ice cream and spread on top of chocolate.
Flatten chicken breasts (place between 2 pieces of plastic wrap and use rolling pin to flatten to uniform thickness).
Dredge breasts in flour with oregano, pepper and salt; shake off excess. Lightly brown in olive oil and butter.
Drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Saute mushrooms in remaining oil; remove from skillet. Pour over breasts.
Add lemon juice, chicken stock and Marsala to skillet and simmer.
Add about 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into 1/4 cup water and add to the skillet mixture.
Stir constantly until becomes thick and smooth.
Add 2 tablespoons butter and stir in.
Pour sauce over chicken and mushrooms.
Keep warm until you serve and garnish with lemon slices.
Mix all above ingredients and pour into an unbaked pie shell. Put top crust on.
Bake at 300° for 90 minutes.
Cook beef and onion until meat is browned; drain well.
Stir in tomato sauce and sauce mix; cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Spoon into a lightly greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Top with sour cream; sprinkle with cheese.
Unroll crescent rolls and place on top of cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 20 minutes.
Makes 8 servings.
Cook brownies.
Crumble half of brownies in bottom of trifle bowl.
Layer 1/2 crushed Butterfingers, layer vanilla pudding, then layer Cool Whip.
Repeat layers using chocolate pudding.
Top with Cool Whip.
Cut up fruit and sprinkle with Equal.
Add peanuts and marshmallows.
Stir in mayonnaise.
When served with nachos, this is a complete meal for 2.
Heat marshmallows and milk in top of double boiler over boiling water.
Stir until melted.
Cool thoroughly.
Mix creme de menthe and creme de cocoa and most of the Cool Whip.
Fold into cooled marshmallow mixture.
Pour into crust.
Chill until firm.
Beat butter until soft.
Gradually add sugar and milk alternately.
Divide into several sections, coloring and flavoring as desired (rum, orange, cherry, almond, mint, etc. perhaps a very small amount of vanilla as well).
Chill until good and cold.
Cook the spaghetti as directed and drain. Saute the onion and green pepper in butter until tender. Combine spaghetti, onion and pepper, soup, pimento, chicken and half of the cheese.
Pour into casserole dish. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 20 minutes.
Brown hamburger with onion. Combine rest of ingredients. Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
In large bowl, dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Stir in cold water.
Refrigerate until slightly thickened.
Fold in the whipped topping and 2 cups strawberries.
Pour into crust. Refrigerate for 3 hours or until set.
Garnish with the remaining strawberries.
Yield: 8 servings.
Use a small roaster with lid.
Place all ingredients in roaster.
Cover and bake at 350° for 4 hours.
Serve over rice or noodles, if desired.
Serves 6.
Brown hamburger with garlic salt, then drain.
Add oregano; simmer for 30 minutes.
Combine cottage cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Cook noodles, then arrange in pan with alternate layers (meat, cottage cheese mixture and Mozzarella cheese ending with Mozzarella on top).
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook cabbage in boiling water until tender, about 10 minutes. Drain.
Cook bacon until crisp.
Stir in vinegar, sugar and salt. Heat and pour over cabbage.
Serve.
Stir milk into well beaten eggs.
Add flour and beat until smooth.
Stir in fat and mix until well blended.
Cut up fruit or vegetables (see following).
Add to or dip in fritter batter.
Drop into hot fat (375°) and fry until brown.
Drain and serve hot with syrup or gravy.
Yields 12 to 15 small fritters.
Mix ingredients and place in 8 x 11-inch pan.
Sprinkle grated cheese on top, cover and bake 45 minutes at 325°.
Cream peanut butter, oleo, 10x sugar and flavoring.
Mix well. Will be thick.
Roll into balls.
Melt chips and paraffin in double boiler.
Dip balls into chocolate with toothpick.
Always place on foil.
Chop bacon and fry until crisp.
Remove from drippings.
Chop onion and pepper and cut okra into 1-inch pieces.
Add to bacon drippings and stir-fry until onion is transparent.
Add seasonings and tomatoes and cook about 5 minutes longer.
In medium bowl, beat cream cheese with electric mixer until smooth.
Beat in pizza sauce, green onion and oregano. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Use Mozzarella cheese sticks, celery, carrots or wheat crackers for dipping.
Mix together the sugar, water, turmeric and mayonnaise.
Add celery and onion.
Cook rotini.
Put in colander and drain.
Run cold water over.
After cold, add dressing.
Pour all ingredients over ice into punch bowl.
Stir and ladle into cups.
If recipe is doubled you do not need to double the strawberries.
In 9 x 13-inch pan, cut up apples.
Cover with brown sugar and cinnamon which have been combined.
Combine in a bowl the Bisquick, white sugar and oats.
Cut into this one egg.
Put this mixture on top of the apples.
Slice 1 stick of margarine over the top.
Bake at 350° for 40 to 45 minutes or until sides are bubbly.
Heat oil to 400°.
Recommend that you use enough oil to cover wings in deep fryer or electric skillet.
Carefully place in oil. Cover.
Mix beans, sugar, mustard
and
ketchup
in baking pan. Cook bacon in frying pan.
Crumble bacon; add to above mixture along with grease.
Lay remaining bacon
on top of beans.
Lay onion in middle of pan.
Bake at 350°, uncovered, for 2 hours.
Melt margarine in a 9 x 13-inch Pyrex dish.
Sprinkle rice over margarine.
Place chicken on the rice.
Season with salt and pepper as you like.
Spoon the undiluted soup over the chicken and rice.
Pour the water over all.
Cover with foil; bake at 350° for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Place all ingredients in pot with just enough water to cover. Cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
If there is too much liquid, remove cover and cook until most of it is evaporated.
Yields 4 servings. Good served with rice.
Roast pecans 10 to 12 minutes at 300°.
In large saucepan, combine remaining ingredients.
Cook on high approximately 2 minutes, or until forms soft ball in water.
Remove from heat. Add pecans and stir by hand until sugared.
Pour out on wax paper and separate.
Crumble yeast; add sugar, salt and water.
Beat in egg.
Add 1/2 of the flour and beat.
Add 1/2 of the butter and the other 1/2 flour.
Let rise to double original size.
Punch down, cover and place in refrigerator.
Dough may be used as needed for rolls. Keeps about a week.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Sift dry ingredients together 3 times. Mix eggs, sweetener and fruit liquid.
Beat at top speed of mixer until fluffy and thick (about 10 minutes).
Decrease speed; add applesauce and beat 3 minutes.
Carefully fold in dry ingredients. Drop by teaspoons onto lightly greased cookie sheet.
Place 1/4 almond on each cookie.
Bake about 10 minutes.
Cookie will spring back at light touch when done.
(May be placed under broiler to give deeper finish.)
Cut up the vegetables and mix together.
Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream and Ranch dressing and add to the vegetables.
Mix peanut butter and 1 cup sugar together.
Add beaten egg and mix well.
Add 1/2 teaspoon vanilla.
Drop by spoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet.
Press flat with a fork.
Bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
While the cookies are cooling, melt chocolate over low heat.
Melt butter in chocolate.
Remove from heat and add hot water.
Then add confectioners sugar gradually, until icing is thick enough (you may not need to use all the sugar).
Add vanilla. Spread icing on top half of the cookies.
Place plain cookies on top of iced cookies to make sandwiches.
Makes about 1 1/2 dozen.
Combine water, cauliflower, potatoes, celery, carrots and onion in a large pan; boil for 5 to 10 minutes or until tender.
Set aside.
Melt butter in separate pan over medium heat.
Stir in flour.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in milk.
Return to heat and cook until thickened.
Stir in vegetables with cooking liquid, then stir in cheese until melted.
Use salt and pepper to taste.
Melt butter; add onions and broccoli.
No need to drain broccoli first.
Cook thoroughly over low heat.
Add mushrooms and soups and cook until well heated.
Add cheese and almonds.
This is good served warm with chips or use leftovers on toast for dinner.
Serve over baked potatoes.
Boil 2 chicken breasts until done.
Remove; cool.
Cook spaghetti in same water.
Drain.
Melt margarine.
Add soups, mushrooms, sour cream and garlic powder (if desired) to taste. Cut chicken into bite size pieces.
Add chicken and spaghetti. Mix well.
Pour into greased casserole.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Stir together and pour over chopped cabbage, green pepper, celery and carrots.
Let set overnight.
Bring sugar, milk and oleo to a quick boil (do not scorch). Cook for 6 to 9 minutes at 225° to 230° on thermometer.
Add marshmallow cream and butterscotch morsels.
Stir to melt and blend well together.
Remove from heat and add vanilla.
Mix and marinate for a couple of hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Cook in saucepan on high heat with lid on.
Bring to a boil and then lower heat.
Cook until tender, about 45 minutes. Skim off fat.
Bring mixture to a rapid boil and add vinegar or juice from pineapple with 1/2 cup vinegar and pineapple.
Taste sauce and adjust seasonings.
Add 2 to 4 tablespoons more sugar, if desired.
Add remainder of juice from pineapple can.
Make a paste of cornstarch and water and add to boiling mixture.
Boil until thickened, then lower heat to simmer.
Add pineapple chunks.
Place lid on pan and simmer until served.
Yields 6 servings with some leftover.
Leftovers taste better the second day.
Serve with rice.
Cream first 4 ingredients well.
Roll frozen bananas in mixture.
You can cut bananas in half and insert popsicle stick in each.
Bananas pops may be rolled in chopped peanuts, if desired. Freeze.
Cut crust off bread and cut into cubes; set aside.
Combine milk, eggs, salt, mustard and pepper.
Lightly combine together milk mixture, bread crumbs and ham or sausage.
Pour mixture into 8 x 8 x 2-inch glass dish, greased lightly.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Bake in preheated 325° oven about 1 hour or until knife inserted comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before serving.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease 10-inch tube pan or Bundt pan. Combine cake mix and all ingredients in large bowl and beat well. Pour into pan.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes or until tester shows it's done.
Cool for 10 minutes and turn out of pan.
Glaze with 1 cup powdered sugar and enough hot water to pour.
Pour over cake while cake is hot.
Beat eggs.
Add oil and vanilla; mix in about 1/4 of dry ingredients.
Fold in apples, nuts and remainder of dry ingredients, sifted together.
Bake in greased tube pan lined with wax paper.
Bake at 325° for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Blend and mix to a paste the first two ingredients.
Round into a ball and divide in two.
Put into two long strips on ungreased baking sheet.
Then mix the butter, water and almond.
Bring to a boil.
Remove from heat.
Add flour and sugar.
When smooth, add eggs, one at a time, beating well.
Divide in two and spread evenly over pastry.
Bake 1 hour in 350° oven.
Do not underbake.
Makes 2.
Combine ingredients in saucepan; bring to boiling.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Strain; pour into heated punch bowl.
Float orange slices on top.
Makes 8 servings.
A cheerful pick-up on a blustery day!
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix all ingredients, breaking up potatoes if necessary.
Put in 2-quart casserole dish.
Bake 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Drain pineapple; measure syrup and add water to make 1 1/2 cups.
Combine liquid, butter, pineapple, soy sauce, ginger and salt in saucepan.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice, carrots and chives.
Cover.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Cook noodles according to package.
Meanwhile, in a saucepan, cook onion in butter until tender.
Stir in flour, soup and milk. Cook until thick and bubbly.
Stir in tuna, pimiento and drained noodles.
Turn mixture into a casserole dish.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake uncovered at 375° for 20 minutes.
Drain pickles.
Slice.
Return to jar.
Bring mixture to a boil, pour over pickles.
Let cool and refrigerate.
Cream together oleo, white sugar and brown sugar.
Stir in egg, peanut butter, salt, soda, vanilla, flour and oats.
Spread in oblong pan.
Do not grease.
Put in oven and turn on heat at 350°.
Bake 20 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Let cool for 1 hour and then spread with Betty Crocker chocolate frosting.
After frosting, mix the Icing.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add egg, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla.
Combine flour and baking soda and blend into mixture. You may add anything at this time.
Example: M&M's, raisins, chocolate chips, nuts, etc.
Drop by teaspoon onto lightly buttered cookie sheet and pat slightly.
Bake at 375° for 7 to 9 minutes until lightly browned.
Fry bacon till crisp.
Chop into small bits.
Add some of bacon grease to potatoes.
Saute onion, celery in remaining grease.
Then mix with potatoes and bacon.
Add water to skillet with vinegar and sugar.
Don't make it too sweet!
Simmer for a few minutes. Add a bit of cornstarch to thicken.
Combine with potato mixture and stir.
Mix together in saucepan the egg, sugar, dates and butter. Simmer on top of stove, approximately 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Let cool one minute.
Add Rice Krispies.
Stir until thoroughly mixed.
Shape into balls.
Roll in chopped nuts.
Mix well by hand.
Do not use blender.
Spoon over the strawberries or peaches.
Sprinkle nutmeg on lightly.
Enjoy.
Beat margarine, shortening and sugars until blended.
Add eggs and vanilla. Beat until blended.
Add flour.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet. Bake 12 minutes at 350 degrees.
Cook pineapple, sugar and salt.
Boil 10 minutes.
Add to Jell-O and refrigerate until at least soupy.
Fold in cheese and whipped cream.
Refrigerate.
Bake cake mix according to package directions in three 8-inch layers.
Cool.
Take sweet milk, 3/4 cup sugar and 1 tablespoon vanilla flavoring and pour this over each layer as you ice them (prick with fork).
Pick over crabmeat to remove shells.
Add all other ingredients except bread crumbs and toss lightly.
Shape into cakes, roll in bread crumbs and fry quickly in hot fat.
Makes 6 to 8 cakes.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Cut in margarine. Beat eggs and milk together, then add date crystals to soften. Stir egg mixture into flour mixture; blend well.
Turn dough onto lightly floured board and pat to 3/4-inch thick.
Cut into 12 scones; place on greased baking sheet.
Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar.
Bake at 425° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Brown onions in oil; add ground beef.
Stir with fork until brown.
Add all but beans.
Stir well and add beans.
Put in casserole dish; bake at 400° in oven approximately 30 minutes.
Cook Serrano peppers in a cast iron skillet on high heat 10 minutes or until blackened, turning peppers.
Combine Serrano peppers, tomatoes and next 7 ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Drain and cool.
Add to spaghetti, chopped onion, bell pepper, diced tomato and cucumber.
Marinate with Italian seasoning.
Add salad seasonings.
Cover; refrigerate.
Serve cool.
Butter sides of 2-quart saucepan and place first 4 ingredients in.
Cook; stir constantly until sugar dissolves and mix comes to a boil.
Cook to hard ball stage (250°) without stirring.
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form.
Gradually beat in gelatin until stiff peaks form.
Pour hot syrup slowly over egg white mixture. Beat constantly at high speed until soft peaks form and mixture starts to lose its gloss.
Stir in nuts and coconut.
Drop by teaspoon on waxed paper.
In a large saucepan, combine 1 cup milk, sugar, chocolate and cinnamon.
Cook and stir over medium-low heat until chocolate is melted. Gradually stir in remaining milk. Cook and stir until milk is very hot, almost boiling, but do not boil.
Gradually stir 1 cup of hot mix into eggs, then return all to saucepan. Cook and stir for 2 minutes over low heat.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla. Beat with beater until frothy.
Pour into mugs and top with whipped cream.
Makes 6 (8 ounce) servings.
Combine mandarin, pineapple and lime juice and chill thoroughly.
To serve, pour fruit juice mixture into chilled bowl with mandarin Ice Ring:
Carefully pour in carbonated water, swirl gently to mix.
Float scoops of sherbet on top.
Serves 10 to 12.

Preheat oven to 400°. Using 3-inch Cut-N-Seal, cut 6 circles from cheese slices on Cutting Board. Cut each circle into quarters using My Safe Cutter. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate. Cut the remaining scraps of cheese into small pieces and place in Classic 2-Quart Batter Bowl.
Lightly brown meat and butter in a large skillet.
Season with 1 teaspoon salt and crushed pepper.
Meanwhile, thinly slice onion and pepper.
Add to pan.
Stir in rice.
Saute, over high heat, until rice is lightly browned.
Add tomatoes, mustard and remaining salt.
Mix well.
Boil and simmer 5 minutes, uncovered.
Combine crumbs, sugar and butter.
Press firmly in bottom of cake pan.
Chill.
Beat cream cheese with sugar and 2 tablespoons milk until smooth.
Fold in half of Cool Whip.
Spread over crust. Arrange fruit in even layers.
Using milk, prepare pudding as directed.
Pour over fruit.
Chill overnight.
Before serving, cover with remaining Cool Whip.
Different fruits may be used in place of pineapple (3 sliced bananas, 4 cups sliced peaches or 2 pints strawberries).
Cream Crisco, sugar and egg together.
Dissolve soda into applesauce and add.
Sift flour, cinnamon and cloves with part of flour.
Add to the first mixture.
Add enough flour to make a fairly stiff batter (amount depends upon the thickness of the applesauce).
Pour into a greased loaf pan.
Bake in a moderate oven at 350° for 50 to 60 minutes.
Spoon ice cream onto pie crust.
Place crumbled cookies over ice cream.
Combine pudding mix, sugar and milk in bowl.
Blend with mixer on slow speed for 1 minute.
Fold in carton of Cool Whip.
(Save a tablespoon for dollop.) Place Heath crunches over topping and a dollop of Cool Whip for garnish.
Chop the first 3 ingredients fine.
Mix the water, sugar and salad dressing together.
Pour dressing over cabbage.
Mix well. Better if sits overnight.
Mix Jell-O and water.
Use a 2-cup container.
Pour in cran-orange and enough water (I use orange juice) to make 2 cups. Add to Jell-O plus the celery and nuts.
Pour into mold and enjoy a couple of hours later.
Heat oven to 425°.
Mix all ingredients except crackers.
Top each cracker with 1 tablespoon of the crabmeat mixture.
Place on a cookie sheet.
Bake 10 minutes.
Makes 36.
These hot and spicy appetizers are fast and easy enough to make as a snack during halftime.
Enjoy!
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time; mix by hand. Add vanilla.
Combine dry ingredients; sift into above mixture. Add milk, a little at a time.
Add nuts.
Grease pan.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes in a 10 x 15-inch pan.
While still hot, spread Marshmallow Creme over top.
Let cool.
Frost with chocolate frosting.
Brown ground beef in pan.
Drain.
Crumble beef and mix with remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Put in a greased casserole and bake 1 hour at 350°.
It is better looking if you sprinkle some grated cheese on top before baking.
Freezes well.
Boil slowly until a ball can be formed in cold water.
Heat oil in large pot. Peel and slice garlic and add to oil. Immediately add tomatoes and tomato puree. Do not brown the garlic!

Stir once. Cover and simmer sauce for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The sauce will turn from a bright red to more of an orange color when it is done. Serve over pasta with grated peccerino romano cheese.
Using a small casserole flat dish, layer these ingredients in order of the letters PROMPT.
Grease dish well with butter and begin layer with, potatoes, uncooked rice, chopped onion, raw ground beef, pepper and salt.
Top with tomato sauce.
Bake 400° for 30 minutes.
Top with shredded cheese if desired before serving.
This is an easy and quick recipe.
Mix all ingredients
and pour into baking dish.
If too dry, add a little chicken
broth.
Bake	at
350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
Slice squash; place a layer.
Sprinkle with flour, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle grated cheese and diced onions.
Repeat 3 or 4 layers.
Boil for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and add Certo.
Boil hard for 1 minute.
Ladle into hot jars and seal.
Immediately invert jars for 5 minutes, then turn up right (helps to seal). About 1 hour later, shake jars to mix peppers before completely set.
Great with cream cheese and crackers.
Yields about 6 to 8 half-pints.
Mix first 8 ingredients together.
Add salt and pepper.
Pour into a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Melt margarine and mix with crushed crackers and spread on top of vegetable mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Boil pineapple and jello until dissolved.
Cool.
Mix buttermilk and Cool Whip.
Mix all together; chill and serve.
Cream butter and sugar until smooth and creamy.
Add the vanilla and water.
Beat well.
Gradually add flour and salt until well blended.
Add pecans and beat until well mixed. Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Brown meat and onion; drain.
Add spaghetti sauce mix and tomato sauce.
Simmer 12 to 15 minutes.
Pour into large casserole dish.
Drop spoonfuls of sour cream on meat and cover with grated Mozzarella cheese.
Saute onions in oil until transparent and thoroughly cooked. Add broth and black pepper.
Simmer 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 ovenproof casseroles or bowls.
Top each with a slice of toasted French bread.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Place in oven or under broiler until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately.
Yields 6 servings.
Boil chicken.
Melt butter and blend in flour, salt and pepper. Add chicken broth and cook until mix thickens.
Add heavy cream. Stir in cream and wine in pan.
Put all broccoli crosswise.
Pour mix over it.
Put chicken in dish.
Sprinkle cheese over ingredients and bake at 350° for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Mix all together.
Keep in refrigerator.
Very good with vegetables or chips.
Melt butter in 9 x 13 pan.
Pour graham cracker crumbs over butter.
Pour Eagle Brand milk over graham crackers.
Then layer remaining ingredients.
Press lightly into milk.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes or golden brown.
Crumble cookies and add milk.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch pan . Mix cheese, Cool Whip and sugar.
Spread this on the crust.
Mix chocolate pudding and milk; spread on top.
Cover with cookie crumbs.
Refrigerate.
Soak poppy seeds in milk for 2 hours.
Then sift together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Cream butter with vanilla.

Add sugar gradually, creaming until fluffy after each addition. Beating only until smooth after each addition, alternately add dry ingredients in fourths, poppy seed/milk in thirds to creamed mixture.
Cook broccoli as directed on package; drain.
Melt margarine and saute onion until tender.
Add rice, soup and cheese to the onion.
Stir in the drained broccoli and blend all ingredients. Pour into a greased casserole and sprinkle top with paprika.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes or until bubbling.
Serves 6 to 8.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar, melted margarine, buttermilk and vanilla.
Add coconut last.
Pour into unbaked pie shell.
Put into preheated 375° oven.
Bake 10 minutes.
Then lower heat to 300° and bake for approximately 30 minutes or until set and begins to brown.
Cut broccoli and cauliflower in bite-size pieces.
Toss vegetables with bacon.
Mix sugar, vinegar, onion and mayonnaise. Pour on vegetables and toss.
Add raisins and stir well. Refrigerate 2 hours before serving.
Soak raisins for half a day in 2 cups of water.
Bring to a boil after soaking.
Add remaining ingredients except corn starch. Thicken with cornstarch with a bit of raisin juice.
Makes 2 pies.
Combine all ingredients; mix well.
Store in airtight container.
Makes 3 cups of dry mix.

Combine chocolate and water; bring to a boil, and stir until chocolate melts. Cool; stir in vanilla and set aside. Cream shortening; gradually add sugar, beating until light and fluffy. Add egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add chocolate mixture; beat until blended. Combine flour, soda and salt; add to creamed mixture alternately with buttermilk, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Beat egg whites (at room temperature) until stiff peaks form; fold into batter. Pour batter into 3 greased and floured 9 inch round cake pans. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool in pans 10 minutes; remove from pans, and cool completely. Spread coconut-pecan frosting between layers and on top and sides of cake. Garnish with pecans, if desired.
Mix ingredients well and pour into 2 separate iron skillet and bake at 350° until brown.
Mix shortening, sugar and pumpkin.
Mix egg and vanilla.
Stir in rest of ingredients.
Drop by tablespoonful on cookie sheet. Bake at 375° for 10 minutes.
Sift first 3 ingredients into bowl.
Add shortening, sugar, 1/2 cup milk, extracts and 1 egg.
Beat 2 minutes on low speed. Add 1/4 cup milk and 2 eggs.
Beat 2 minutes on low speed. Pour into greased layer pans and bake at 375° for 25 to 30 minutes. Yields 2 (9-inch) round layers.
Brown beef.
Place potatoes and onion in large buttered baking dish.
Add beef.
Mix soup and little milk until smooth and add to meat and potatoes.
Mix together.
Combine tomato sauce, salt, pepper and sugar.
Pour over top of mixture.
Dot with butter. Cover and bake at least 1 1/2 hours, uncovered.
Place cheese on top.
Return to oven until cheese melts, about 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
In a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish alternately layer beans and onions.
Combine soup, milk and marjoram.
Pour over beans and onions.
Sprinkle top with cheese. Bake uncovered for 20 - 25 minutes.
In blender, add 2 1/2 to 3 cups chipped ice, pineapple juice, 3 tablespoons cream of coconut and 1 tablespoon pineapple.
Mix well. Then add 2 1/2 to 3 ounces of rum (size of blender, cap of lid).
Mix crab meat, seasoning, salt and baking powder.
Mix egg and mayonnaise; add to crab mixture.
Make into 8 cakes and fry until browned.
Saute the onion, celery and green pepper in a large skillet or wok.
Cook and stir until the onion is tender, about 3 minutes, using medium-high heat.
Stir in the rice, the soup base and soy sauce.
Cook on low heat, stirring frequently, for 5 to 7 minutes.
Mix first 5 ingredients and shape into balls.
Brown in skillet and pour off accumulated fat.
Mix other ingredients. Place meat balls into a baking dish and cover with soup mixture. Bake 20 minutes in 350° oven.
Serves 6.
Combine Bisquick, milk and cheese until soft dough forms. Beat vigorously 30 seconds.
Drop dough by spoonfuls on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 450° for 8 to 10 minutes or until biscuits are golden brown.
Combine butter and garlic.
Brush over biscuits while warm.

Heat brown sugar and water. Boil 3 minutes. Remove from heat; add vanilla and margarine. Mix well. Pour a little hot mixture into eggs. Put egg mixture back into pot. Heat together until thickens. Pour into unbaked pie shell. Add pecans. Bake at 350° until browned.
Butter a 2 1/2-quart casserole. Check oysters for shell pieces.
Layer
crushed
crackers,	oysters,
butter, salt and pepper, about
or 3 layers. Pour any oyster juice over top. Scald milk.
Pour over all. Bake in hot oven at 400° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Insert
knife in center;	should come out clean, like a custard
pie. This can be doubled easily; use a larger casserole.
Mix graham crackers and oleo in 14 x 9 x 2-inch pan for crust. (May use pre-made graham cracker crust.)
Cream Crisco, sugar and egg.
Add buttermilk, vanilla and chopped nuts.
Sift flour, soda, salt and cocoa.
Chill 1 hour. Grease sheets.
Bake at 400° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Have all cheeses at room temperature.
Grate or cut fine American and sharp cheese.
Cream all in electric mixer.
Add garlic salt and Worcestershire sauce while mixing.
Chill several hours or overnight.
Make into 3 or 4 balls.
Roll in chopped nuts or in parsley.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Preheat oven to 325°.
Remove seeds from chilies and dice. Combine grated cheeses and chilies.
Put in buttered, shallow 2-quart casserole dish.
Beat egg whites until stiff.
In another bowl, combine egg yolks, milk, flour, salt and pepper and mix until well blended.
Gently fold egg whites into egg yolk mixture and then pour over cheese mixture.
Using a fork, ooze it through the cheese mixture.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Arrange tomatoes on top and then bake an additional 30 minutes.
Mix lightly, except save 1 cup noodles for the top.
Put in a greased 9 x 9-inch pan and bake at 375° for 45 minutes.
Mix well; shape into ball or log.
Wrap in wax paper and chill (may be frozen).
To serve, roll in chopped pecans or parsley.
Cook cabbage in enough water to cover; cook for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Mix remaining ingredients and place on cabbage leaves.
Roll up and secure with toothpick.
Wrap rolls in foil and place in baking pan.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Simmer all ingredients (put spices in a cloth, if desired) for 20 minutes. Remove spices and serve hot. A few red hot candies may be added to each cup, if desired.
Grease 10-inch tube pan with 2 tablespoons of butter. Sprinkle pan with 1/4 cup of sugar.
Set aside.
Melt butter in skillet.
Saute onions, celery and mushrooms. Pour over torn toasted bread.
Add browned hamburger, eggs, seasonings and chicken broth.
Mix together well.
Stuff turkey or chicken or place in greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake 1 to 1 1/2 hours at 350° until top is brown.
Serves 12.

recipes.t: Broiled London Broil With Purple Plum Sauce
