d: Score the steak quite deeply with a sharp knife all the way down its length on the diagonal, about every 1/2-inch.
Turn steak around and repeat, scoring in opposite direction, so score marks become little squares.
In large pitcher, combine all except lime or lemon slices; refrigerate to chill.
To serve, pour into tall glasses with ice cubes.
Top with lemon or lime slice.
Also, a stalk of celery may be added to each drink.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Melt butter in 8 to 9-inch baking dish. Add sugar to blackberries and lemon juice.
Let come to boil. Add muffin mix and milk.
Stir until well blended.
Spoon into baking pan with butter (don't stir).
Spoon hot blackberries and juice evenly over batter (do not stir).
Bake 35 to 45 minutes or until golden brown.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix together the first 5 ingredients and pour into large baking dish.
Arrange pieces of chicken on top.
Sprinkle with parsley flakes, paprika and dot with butter.
Bake at 325° for 2 hours, uncovered, or until tender.
Add a bit more water if necessary; do not salt.
Soups have plenty of salt in them.
Serves 8.

Prepare rice as directed on package. In a large skillet, saute mushrooms, green peppers, onions and shrimp. Shrimp will turn pink. Add soup to the rice and stir. Add shrimp mixture to rice and soup. Stir and transfer to a well-greased 2-quart baking dish. Sprinkle with stuffing mix. Bake at 350° uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes or until heated through. Serves 6.
Saute celery; add chicken and cook until chicken turns white, then brown.
Combine all ingredients to mix, except for cornflakes.
Place in an 8 1/2 x 11-inch greased baking dish. Sprinkle with cornflakes and bake for 45 minutes at 350°.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease jelly roll pan.
Mix brown sugar, butter and eggs until well blended.
Sift dry ingredients and add to sugar mixture; mix well. Add chips and pecans. Spread in prepared pan.
Bake at 350° for approximately 25 minutes.
Let stand for several minutes before cutting into squares.
Mix soups, onion, pepper, chili powder, garlic and tomatoes. In a buttered casserole, layer tortillas, layer chicken, layer soup and layer cheese.
Continue to layer in order until all ingredients are used, ending with cheese.
Bake at 375° for 30 minutes.
Serve over rice or plain.
Freezes well.
Mix first 5 ingredients and blend with hamburger.
Shape into small t-bone 1 to 1 1/4-inch thick.
Douse with Worcestershire sauce on broiler pan.
Broil 5 minutes on each side.
Combine crumbs and butter, press firmly on bottom and up side of 9-inch pie plate.
Chill.
In large mixing bowl, beat cheese until fluffy, gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk, then juice concentrate until smooth.
Fold in whipped cream.
Pour into crust.
Chill 2 hours before serving.
Garnish with fresh orange slices and whipping cream, if desired.
Store in refrigerator.
Beat egg, add buttermilk and mix.
Set aside.
Shake together flour, parsley, pepper and paprika.
In another bag, shake together cornflake crumbs and cheese.
Drop chicken in egg mixture, the flour mixture, back in egg mixture then the cornflake mixture. Take chicken and press down in cornflake mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Makes 4 servings.
Brown ground beef in skillet. In separate pan, saute onion and green pepper in the margarine until tender.
Meanwhile, cook spaghetti as directed on package and drain.
Put spaghetti in a shallow pan.
Add ground beef to drained sauteed onion and green pepper.
Add spaghetti sauce.
Pour on top of the spaghetti. Sprinkle top with Mozzarella cheese until lightly covered.
Bake at 350° for about 30 minutes until cheese is lightly browned.
Let stand for 10 minutes.
You may add extra Ragu and Mozzarella cheese if needed.
Saute zucchini, onion and tomatoes in olive oil.
Add corn, salt, pepper and garlic salt.
Cover with shredded Cheddar cheese. Cover with lid and simmer for 20 minutes.
Total liquid for jambalaya should be 8 gallons, including sauces, soup and water.
Soften gelatin in 1/4 cup cold water.
Combine chocolates and 1/2 cup water; stir over low heat until thick and blended.
Remove from heat.
Add gelatin and stir until dissolved.
Beat egg yolks with 1/2 cup sugar until light.

Add chocolate mixture, salt and vanilla extract and cool in refrigerator to room temperature. Gradually beat 1/2 cup sugar into beaten whites; fold into chocolate mixture and pour into cooled pastry shell.
Chill until firm.
Whip the heavy cream until stiff and add 1 tablespoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract.
When ready to serve, use the heavy whipped cream as topping for the pie.

Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). In a 1-quart casserole dish, combine mushrooms, onion, garlic, green pepper, Italian seasoning, seasoning salt, pepper and parsley. Pour water and butter over mixture; cover. Bake in preheated oven for 40 to 45 minutes.
Dissolve jello in hot water.
Add and mix the rest of the ingredients with the jello.
Chill until set.
Mix all ingredients until soft dough forms; beat vigorously 20 strokes.
Combine eggs, milk, salt and dry mustard.
Pour over bread. Top with butter.
Refrigerate overnight, covered.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Serves 6 to 8.
In a skillet, brown sausage.
Drain and discard the drippings. In a large mixing bowl, combine sausage and remaining ingredients; mix well.
Mix all ingredients together and put in a crock-pot which has been greased with 2 tablespoons shortening.
Cut several strips of cheese and put on top.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Cook 3 to 4 hours on low.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease baking dish.
Crumble bread into crumbs.
Mix all ingredients; pour into baking dish.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Sift the first 3 ingredients 2 or 3 times.
Put in bowl the egg plus enough milk to make 1/2 cup.
Beat and combine with dry ingredients.
Drop into liquid 1/2 tablespoon at a time.
Bake or cook 10 minutes.
Wash chicken.
Take a fork and punch a couple of holes in each one.
Place in baking dish.
Pour a bottle of Italian dressing over the chicken.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cover with aluminum foil; marinate overnight. Bake at 350° until a golden brown (about 1 hour).
There will be enough dressing for 2 salads.
Mix the first 4 ingredients; cook until thick.
Cool; pour over sliced strawberries in a cooked pie shell or a graham cracker crust.
Mix flour, curry and mustard; blend into butter.
Add other ingredients; bring to boil and simmer 2 hours.
Serve over London Broil.

Mash half of the banana and cube the other half. Blend all the ingredients; pour into the pie shell. Bake at 375° for 45 minutes until crust is golden and filling is set. Let cool at least 2 hours before cutting.
Saute the first 4 ingredients.
Add shrimp and crab meat.
Mix together spaghetti and serve warm.
Serve with Greek salad.
Mix sugar, water and cornstarch and boil until thick, stirring constantly.
Stir in jello.
Place sliced fruit in a cooked pie crust.
Spoon mixture over fruit and chill for several hours.
Top with Cool Whip.
Cut sweet potatoes in halves or quarters; place in baking dish.
In a small saucepan, bring to boil brown sugar, water, salt and butter.
Pour over sweet potatoes.
Bake at 350° about 30 minutes, basting occasionally.
Blend all ingredients in a bowl with a beater until fairly smooth.
Amounts of salsa and sour cream may be increased to suit taste and/or to increase smoothness.
Heat sugar, corn syrup and milk to a boil on medium-high and boil 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter and butter.
Beat by hand until cool and pour onto buttered platter. Don't try to make fudge on a rainy day; it won't set properly.
Sprinkle nuts onto well greased pan.
In a saucepan, melt butter.
Add brown sugar.
Stir constantly for 7 minutes.
Pour mixture over nuts immediately.
Top with chopped chocolate.
Let chocolate melt; then spread over batter with a table knife.
Place pan in freezer about 20 minutes.
Then cut into squares.
Store in refrigerator.
Beat together eggs, flour, salt, and pepper.
Coat ribs with this batter and brown on all sides in fat.
Cover and cook slowly for 45 minutes.
Pour off drippings.
Drain pineapple and reserve juice.
Stem and seed peppers and cut into one-inch squares.
Add peppers and pineapple to meat.
Cover and cook slowly for 10 minutes.
Add enough water to reserved pineapple juice to make one cup liquid.
Mix cornstarch, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, and pineapple liquid.
Cook, stirring until thickened.
Pour over meat mixture and cook slowly for five minutes.
Serves three or four.
Butter casserole dish; arrange alternate layers of potatoes, onions, cheese and margarine.
Sprinkle each layer with salt and black pepper.
Pour cheese sauce over all; add more cheese if you like.
Sprinkle with generous amount of paprika.
Cover and bake 1 hour at 375°.
Remove cover and bake 15 more minutes.
Blend pudding mix with corn syrup.
Gradually add evaporated milk and egg, stirring to blend.
Then add pecans.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake at 375° until top is firm and just begins to crack, about 40 minutes.
Cool at least 3 hours.
Mix all ingredients together in order listed except the cheese.
Pour half of the batter in greased baking dish then half the cheese sprinkled on the batter.
Add the rest of batter and cover with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° about 45 minutes or until done.
In a large saucepan, cover sweet potatoes with water; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until just tender.
Drain and cool slightly.
Peel and cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Alternate layers of potatoes and apples in a 9 x 13 x 2-inch baking dish.
Pour orange juice over potatoes and apples. Mix brown sugar, ginger and cinnamon, then sprinkle over potatoes and apples.
Dot with butter.
Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 35 to 45 minutes or until apples are tender.
Saute green onions in melted butter in large skillet or wok until tender.
Add cabbage and carrots.
Saute 4 minutes or until crisp-tender.
Stir in salt and pepper.
Can use oil instead of butter, if desired.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour into a greased casserole.
Bake at 325° for 30 to 45 minutes.
Layer all ingredients in casserole dish.
Cook in oven at 350° for 15 to 20 minutes or microwave approximately 5 minutes.
Cut Velveeta into cubes and chop
onion.
Put all ingredients into a double boiler and cook until all cheese cubes are melted. Remove from heat.
Keep stirring until there is no film on top. Dip tortilla chips and enjoy.
Refrigerate when not using.
Can be served warm or cold.
Drain pineapple.
Reserve liquid.
Add cold water to liquid to measure 1 cup.
Stir boiling water to jello in large bowl.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Stir in measured liquid.
Refrigerate about 1 1/4 hours.
Stir in Cool Whip with whisk until smooth. Refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Stir in rest of ingredients and chill for about 4 hours.
Yields 10 servings.
Blend cream cheese and sugar.
Fold cream cheese mixture into Dream Whip mixture; pour on cool crust.
Spread blueberries on top.
Let cool good; then enjoy.
Soften yeast in lukewarm water.
Pour milk over sugar, salt and shortening; cool to lukewarm.
Beat in half of flour and beaten eggs.
Stir in yeast, raisins and rolled oats.
Add enough flour to make a stiff dough.
Turn out on lightly floured board. Knead until satiny, about 10 minutes.
Round dough into ball and place in greased bowl.
Cover.
Let rise until double or 1 hour. Divide dough into 2 parts.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.

recipes.t: Hot Chocolate Fudge For Ice Cream Topping
d: Melt the oleo, salt and chocolate.
Stir in the condensed milk, powdered sugar and vanilla.
Bring to boil for a few minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.

Coat a 12-c. muffin pan with nonstick cooking spray. In a small bowl, combine the melted butter, parsley, garlic, and salt; mix well. On a lightly floured surface, roll the bread dough into a 12 inch square. Spread the parsley mixture over the dough, leaving a 1/2 inch border on the top and bottom edges. Roll dough tightly, jelly roll fashion, starting at the bottom edge. Pinch to seal the edge. Cut the roll of dough into 1 inch wide slices. Place each slice flat side down into a cup of the muffin pan. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size. Preheat the oven to 400°. Bake the rolls for 9 to 11 minutes, or until golden. Remove from the pan and serve warm.
Cream butter and shortening gradually.
Add 2/3 cup powdered sugar and flavoring, beating until light and fluffy.
Gradually add flour and mix well.
Stir in chopped pecans.
Combine all ingredients, except Top Ramen and sugar, together in large bowl.
Break up the Top Ramen noodles, but don't cook. Mix the noodles with the sugar.
Toss into salad.
Bake cake and crumble small amount in bottom of tall glass bowl.
Layer pineapple, pudding and cherry pie filling; start over with rest of cake and layer again.
Top with Cool Whip.
Garnish with nuts, coconut and cherries.
Makes enough for large group.
Mix all ingredients, except nuts.
Add nuts just before serving.

Fill 9-inch pie pan 2/3 full of peeled and sliced apples. Combine 1 tablespoon sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over apples. Mix together 1 cup sugar, flour, nuts, butter, vanilla and egg. Spoon this mixture over apples and pat down.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Top with whipped cream to serve.

recipes.t: Quick And Easy Spicy Hot Dogs
d: Mix all of the ingredients.
Marinate in the refrigerator for 24 hours.
Transfer to a fondue pot and serve bubbling.
Recipe will feed several.
Pour milk over biscuits; let set until milk is absorbed. Beat sugar, eggs and vanilla; add to bread mixture. Pour into a greased 3-quart baking dish. Bake at 400° for 45 minutes or until set.
Have Cheddar cheese at room temperature.
*White beans or limas may be used.
Mix all together.
Bake at 350° until it sets, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Brown onion in hot shortening; add meat and rice.
Cook slowly until rice is golden brown.
Add tomatoes, water and seasoning. Stir well and pour into greased casserole.
Cover and bake at 400° for 30 minutes, then remove cover and bake 15 minutes longer. Serve at once from casserole.
In a medium saucepan, pour whole bottle of chili sauce and jar of grape jelly.
Over low heat, stir occasionally until jelly melts.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine meat, finely chopped onions, bread crumbs, salt and pepper.
Form into small balls and place in a deep baking dish.
Pour sauce mixture over meatballs, making sure all are covered.
Bake 35 minutes.
In casserole dish, place half of the potatoes, half the cheese and 1/2 the margarine.
Then add remaining potatoes, cheese and margarine.
Top with soup.
Bake at 400° for 40 minutes.
Cook chicken in a skillet until done.
Mix mayo, sour cream, cumin, mustard, salt and pepper. Stir and add chicken; mix.
Add shredded cheeses and mix.
Place 2 spoonfuls on a tortilla shell. Roll up and place in baking dish. Spoon salsa over and sprinkle with Mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes. Serves 6 to 8.
Simmer ingredients in skillet 20 minutes.
Add consomme and water.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Stir before serving.
Serves 4.

recipes.t: Banana-Raisin Cookies(Low-Fat; No Sugar Except From Fruit)
d: Preheat oven to 375°.
Combine all dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
(Batter should be a little stiff.)
Drop by teaspoon onto a nonstick or lightly greased cookie sheet and flatten slightly.
Bake for about 15 minutes.
Put oatmeal into boiling water and let stand.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add oil; add oatmeal mixture and all other ingredients.
Mix well as you go along.
Add bread flour until you get a stiff workable dough.
Knead well.
Let rise.
Knead again and shape into loaves.
Let rise and bake at 350° until done (approximately 20 to 25 minutes).
Sprinkle yeast over lukewarm water.
Add 2 teaspoons honey. Leave to "work" while preparing dough.
Warm whole-wheat flour by placing in oven (250°) for 20 minutes.
Combine molasses with 2/3 cup water.
Combine yeast mixture with molasses mixture.
Stir this into warmed flour, add salt and wheat germ and finally 1 1/3 cups water.
(Dough will be sticky.)
Butter loaf pan.
Turn dough into pan.
Smooth dough in pan with spatula which has been held under cold water.
Sprinkle sesame seed over top of loaf.
Leave to rise to top of pan in warm, draft-free place.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until crust is brown and sides are firm.
Set pan on rack to cool for about 10 minutes, then remove.
Cool completely before serving.
Cream butter, peanut butter and sugars.
Add egg and vanilla. Beat well.
Add dry ingredients.
Shape into balls; roll in sugar and place on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes.
Place Hershey's Kiss or star in center of each cookie while hot.
Serves 48.
Combine eggs, sugar, salt and butter in a saucepan.
Heat to a boiling point.
Boil 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Cool.
Stir in graham cracker crumbs and marshmallows.
Spread in a greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Chill.
Melt chips and peanut butter at low speed. Add vanilla.
Spread over crumb mixture.
Refrigerate.
Cut into 3 dozen bars.
Melt shortening in large skillet.
Add onion, green pepper and beef; brown lightly.
Add tomatoes with juice to mixture in skillet.
Add kidney beans, chili powder, salt and pepper; mix well.
Pour into a 2-quart casserole.
Top with cornbread mixture and bake in 350° oven for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Mix walnuts with egg white until well coated and sticky to the touch.
Mix together sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle over walnuts, tossing until sugar mixture completely coats walnuts.
Spread on ungreased baking sheet for 20 minutes, stirring once.
Cool.
Store in tightly covered container.
Makes 2 cups.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla. Stir together flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt.
Stir into egg mixture.
Combine beans, potatoes, bacon grease and salt in pressure cooker.
Cook for 1 hour on medium-high heat.
Let steam escape before removing lid.
Simple and easy to prepare.
Mix over stove the light brown sugar, sugar and butter.
Cook until it comes to a boil that can't be stirred down.
Cook an additional 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add 1 (12 ounce) jar peanut butter and marshmallow cream.
Stir and mix thoroughly. Pour onto greased cookie sheet.
In large saucepan or Dutch oven, bring vegetables and water to boiling; reduce heat and simmer about 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add kielbasa and bean soup.
Heat thoroughly.
Makes 6 generous servings.
In a 2-quart casserole dish, layer thinly sliced potatoes, onion, frozen vegetables and chicken.
Pour in broth and soup. Cover with pie crust or biscuits.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes.
Combine potatoes, onions, water, salt, garlic salt, oregano and pepper in a large saucepan.
Cover; bring to a boil, then simmer until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Mash potatoes slightly.
Add milk and butter.
Heat thoroughly.
Serve.
Hm good.

Follow directions on package of hollandaise sauce for the sauce. Heat slices of Canadian bacon. Poach eggs. Split open the muffins and toast them. Put English muffins on plate; place a piece of Canadian bacon on muffin; place poached egg over bacon (upside down); cover with sauce.
Melt butter in saucepan and cool.
Mix stuffing, cheese and parsley together.
Dip boned chicken in melted butter and then in stuffing mix.
When all are coated, place in 9 x 12-inch dish or pan and sprinkle balance of stuffing mixture on top.
Drip small amount of butter on top, also.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 45 minutes. Serves 6.
Mix all ingredients well.
Put mixture in refrigerator overnight.
Roll out on floured board and cut like biscuits.
Bake at once for 20 minutes at 375°.
Mix with fork.
Bake 25 minutes at 350° in a jelly roll cake pan.
Cool.
Frost with Bakery Frosting.
Combine and melt cream cheese and soup.
Add all other ingredients.
Stir and chill to serve.
Flour enough to handle easily, maybe 8 to 9 cups.
Lard piping hot.
The rolling pin was a great big log, real heavy, and the cookie cutter was a saucer.
The doughnuts were not rolled as thin as cookies.
Melt margarine in square or oblong baking pan in a 350° oven. Mix milk, flour and sugar in mixing bowl.
Pour into melted margarine; do not stir.
Add flavoring to 1 large can of fruit (or fresh or frozen, sweetened to taste).
Pour into dough; do not stir.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 45 minutes, until browned.
Very good!
Cream butter and cream cheese.
Slowly add sugar and egg yolk. Beat until fluffy.
Add flour and vanilla.
Chill dough at least 1 hour.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls and place on greased cookie sheet.
Gently press a pecan half or cherry in center of each ball.
Bake at 325° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Yields approximately 4 dozen.
Grease bottom of a 9-inch spring-form pan.
Prepare cake mix as directed on package; pour batter evenly into spring-form pan. Bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Carefully place 2 cups water in a pot, then place pot on stove and cover.
Turn on heat to high.
Water is ready when bubbles form.
Melt the first 3 ingredients in a pan, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla, coconut and oats.
Mix thoroughly. Drop by spoonfuls on waxed paper.
Refrigerate.
Combine ingredients in saucepan and simmer 15 to 20 minutes. Serve hot.
Serves 6.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl, tossing gently to mix. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
Mix all together and cover with crushed potato chips.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
* Turkey sausage may be used instead of pork sausage.
In a 12-inch skillet, heat the oil and stir in the curry powder until blended.
Add the onions; when it's sizzling, add the broth and cabbage.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, until slightly wilted, about 2 minutes.
Add more liquid if needed. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, an additional 6 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with peanuts and serve.
Put dry Jell-O in bottom of bowl.
Add fruit cocktail; stir. Add mini marshmallows, any amount you want.
Add cottage cheese and Cool Whip.
Mix and let stand to set.
Mix before serving.
Melt together morsels and peanut butter over hot water (not boiling) or in a microwave for 1 minute and stir.
If not long enough, give it another 30 seconds to 1 minute.
When melted, stir in Chinese noodles.
Mix well and drop on wax paper by teaspoon. Let harden.
Cream the shortening and sugars.
Separate eggs; add yolks to mixture.
Mix flour and baking powder.
Add alternately with coffee.
Add nuts and jimmies.
Beat egg whites; fold into batter. Put into greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Done when toothpick comes out clean.
Boil cider and spices for 15 minutes.
Add honey, juices and orange peel.
Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
Make pie shell using your own recipe.
Pare, core and quarter apples, then halve each quarter.
You should have about 7 cups of apples.
Place in a large bowl.
Beat all ingredients together.
Pour into graham cracker crust.
Refrigerate.
May be frozen.
*May add additional jalapenos if desired or if a hot salsa is needed, add 1 Scotch bonnet pepper.
Butter one 2-quart casserole dish. Preheat oven to 350° (175°C). In a mixing bowl, combine the sweet potatoes, sugar, vanilla extract, eggs and cream. Blend well and spread evenly in casserole dish.
Sift together first 5 ingredients.
Stir in 1/2 cup chopped nuts.
Add 1/2 cup milk and 1 teaspoon of vanilla.
Blend slightly and stir in 3 tablespoon of melted butter.
Put in an 8 x 8 x 2-inch greased pan.
Beat shortening and gradually add sugar.
Beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs.
Beat until thick and lemon colored.
Combine dry ingredients and add alternately with bananas.
Blend in fruit, raisins and nuts.
Pour into a 9-inch tube pan.
Bake at 350° for 60 to 70 minutes.
Cool and spread with glaze.
In large mixing bowl, combine condensed milk and water.
Mix well.
Add pudding mix and beat until well blended.
Chill 5 minutes.
Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon 2 cups pudding mixture into 4-quart serving bowl.
Top with half the cake cubes, half the strawberries and half the remaining pudding mixture.
Repeat layering, ending with pudding mixture.
Garnish with strawberries. Chill at least 4 hours.
Brown ground beef; drain.
Stir in seasoning packet from noodles, soy sauce and cooked broccoli.
Cook noodles, using package directions.
Add to ground beef mixture.
Mix well; cook until heated through.
Serve with additional soy sauce.
Prepare macaroni according to package directions; drain. Combine macaroni, celery, onions, crabmeat and eggs.
Blend mayonnaise and French dressing.
Toss macaroni mixture with dressing; chill.
Serve on lettuce.
Yields 8 servings.
Place potatoes in lightly greased 11 x 7 x 1 1/2-inch baking dish.
Sprinkle with rosemary and pepper.
Combine with milk and gravy mix; pour over potatoes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 400° for 30 minutes or until tender.
Yields 6 servings.
Break up the cinnamon sticks and put them in a "tea ball" along with the cloves.
Put the water in a large pot (should be at least a six-quart size) and bring to boil, boiling for three minutes.
Turn off heat; put in the tea bags and "tea ball" containing the whole cloves and broken cinnamon sticks.
Let tea steep for 30 minutes.
Remove the tea ball and bags; pour in the sugar, stirring until dissolved.
Add pineapple juice and lemonade; stir.
Heat until brew is hot enough to drink.
Slice potatoes, eggs and lettuce.
Blend dressing and pour over vegetables.
Garnish with sliced tomatoes. Serves 4.
Slice top off bread.
Scoop out inside of bread.
Cut bread which was scooped out into bite size pieces.
Set aside.
Squeeze out spinach.
Combine with all other ingredients to make dip. Spoon dip into bread.
Chill until ready to serve or if desired, wrap in aluminum foil and heat at 200° for 2 hours.
Serve with bite size bread pieces and fresh vegetables.

recipes.t: Baked French Toast With Blueberry Sauce
d: Slice bread into 12 to 14 slices about 3/4-inch thick.
Place on a 10 1/2 x 15 1/2 x 1-inch cookie sheet.
Whisk egg, milk, baking powder and vanilla together and slowly pour it over the bread, turning to coat the bread completely.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours or overnight.
Boil sliced zucchini and onions in salted water until barely cooked.
Drain.
Place in buttered casserole dish.
Add cheese, salt and pepper.
Beat egg and milk.
Pour over zucchini.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
To potatoes, add egg, onion, salt and pepper.
Mix well. Shape in 6 patties . Dip in flour, then brown slowly in butter, about 5 minutes on each side.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix Jell-O and boiling water to dissolve.
Mix plain gelatin with cold water.
Add plain gelatin to hot gelatin; stir to dissolve.
Stir all ingredients into Jell-O mixture.
Chill in refrigerator until set or firm.
May also add chopped apple and nuts to this.
Mix peanut oil, soy sauce and sugar together in a large pan. After the sugar is dissolved, add chicken
parts.
Bring chicken in sauce to a boil, stirring occasionally.	Cover
and cook
for about 45 minutes or until wings are
tender.
Remove chicken from sauce and place on serving tray.
Chop
the stems of
green onions
and
mix together with 1/4	cup
chopped peanuts.
Pour sauce over chicken and sprinkle with
onion and peanut mixture.
Prepare pie crust.
Place chipped apples into crust.
Combine sugar, cinnamon, salt and melted margarine.
Add beaten egg.
Pour over chipped apples.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serve with ice cream.
Place preceding ingredients in your slow cooker in order given.
Stir until mixed, then cover and cook on low heat overnight or 10 to 12 hours.
Can be baked 1 hour or longer.
Sprinkle gelatin over water in small mixing bowl.
Place in pan of hot water.
Heat until dissolved.
Add ginger ale; stir. Add peaches. Chill until it begins to thicken.
Spoon into pie crust and chill until firm.
May be served with low calorie whipped topping.
Equals 1 fruit, 1 bread and 2 fats.
Dissolve the Jello and gelatin in 1 1/2 cups boiling water. Add 1 cup ice cubes.
Add lemon juice and chill until partially set.
Add remaining ingredients.
Pour in 9x13 pan.
Chill until set.
Melt butter in a 9 x 13 inch pan.
Dip chicken in butter and arrange in pan.
Place a slice of cheese on top of each piece of chicken.
Sprinkle dry stuffing mix over chicken and cheese.
Mix soup and milk.
Pour over top of stuffing mix.
Bake at 375° for 40 minutes.
Soften ice cream; add can of lemonade and stir until well mixed.
Slice cake in 2 or 3 layers.
Spread with ice cream in between layers.
Ice with remainder of ice cream mixture.
Serve immediately, topped with strawberries or return to freezer.
Let set out 10 to 15 minutes before serving.

In food processor, chop green onions, cilantro and cheeses. In large bowl, layer the green onions, diced tomatoes, diced avocados, cheeses and salsa; sprinkle with Lawry's seasoned salt. Marinate in refrigerator overnight.
Toss before serving with chips.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake in a Bundt pan for 45 to 50 minutes at 350°.
Place all ingredients in an ovenproof, covered bowl and cook at 250° for 4 1/2 to 5 hours.
Place margarine in 2-quart casserole. Microwave at High until melted, 1 to 2 1/2 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice, garlic and salt. Add shrimp; toss to coat.
Cover.
Microwave at High until shrimp is pink, opaque and tender, 4 1/2 to 7 minutes, stirring twice.
Mix all together, adding the margarine last.
Bake at 325° for 1 1/2 hours, stirring three times while cooking.
Serve with favorite topping.
In a pan combine soup and milk.
Bring to a boil, stirring often.
Remove from heat and add cheese, mayonnaise and salt. Stir until cheese melts.
Blend in sherry.
Add shrimp, noodles, onions and mushrooms.
Mix well and turn into casserole dish. Bake, covered, 25 minutes at 350°.
Uncover and add a bit of shredded cheese on top.
Bake 10 minutes more.
Beat all but corn with eggbeater.
Stir in corn.
Pour into well-buttered casserole.
Set in a pan of water.
Bake at 375° for 1 hour.
Cook lamb for 1 3/4 hours.
Let the lamb cool until the fat rises to the top.
Then scrape the fat off and take the meat off of the bone.
Add onions, carrots, celery, salt and pepper to the lamb and cook for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and cook the stew for another 3/4 to 1 hour, until the potatoes cook down and thicken the stew.
Serves 8.
Mix all together, except last 2 ingredients.
Mold into a loaf pan.
Cook for 1 hour.
Mix together mushroom soup and tomato sauce.
Heat.
Pour over meat loaf and cook for 30 minutes.
Brown pork chops; then add cabbage and peppers.
Steam 10 minutes.
Then add rest of ingredients.
Add salt to taste. Cover and cook on low heat for 3/4 hour.
Cook macaroni and cheese according to directions on the box, adding the butter, milk and cheese.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Chill before serving.
Mix margarine, curry powder and brown sugar and pour over fruit.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.
Goes well with ham or chicken.
Mix the butter and molasses in a saucepan and melt over low heat.
Cool to room temperature.
Stir together all dry ingredients in a large bowl; set aside.
Stir the egg into the molasses mixture and gradually stir in the flour mixture.
Cover and chill one hour or until dough is easy to handle.
Divide dough into 12 portions. On a lightly floured surface roll each piece into a 10-inch rope. Cut the ropes into 1/2-inch pieces.
Place the pieces 1/2-inch apart on ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350 for 10 to 12 minutes or until edges are firm and bottoms are lightly browned.
Cool on paper towels.
Mix ground beef, egg, onion and salt.
Prepare meatballs and set aside.
Mix in large saucepan chili sauce, lemon juice and grape jelly.
Add meatballs.
Simmer 1 to 2 hours.
(To reduce the fat in the sauce, you may cook the meatballs first in the microwave and drain; then add to sauce and simmer until heated through.)
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water; chill until thickened. Stir in remaining ingredients.
Pour into lightly greased mold or individual molds.
Chill until firm.
Serves 6.
Season raw shrimp with salt, pepper and cayenne pepper (to taste) and set aside.
Melt margarine.
Add onions, celery, bell pepper and garlic.
Cook slowly in uncovered heavy pot until onions wilt.
Add shrimp and let simmer, stirring occasionally, 30 minutes.
Dissolve cornstarch in water.
Add to mixture.
Cook 30 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Mix first 4 ingredients together and add lemon juice and mix. Place in unbaked 9-inch pie shell.
Bake at 450° after putting butter on top.
Cover with strips and then bake.
Check after 20 minutes.
Temperature adjustment may be necessary.
Bake until done.

Using a meat mallet or rolling pin, pound each beef cutlet to 1/4-inch thickness. Sprinkle garlic salt on both sides of each cutlet. Pour flour onto a pie plate or shallow bowl and coat each cutlet. Refrigerate until most of the flour has been absorbed (10 to 20 minutes). Pour buttermilk into a shallow bowl or pie plate. Dip each cutlet into buttermilk, then dredge each in another coating of flour, shaking off excess. (Reserve remaining gravy for making gravy.) Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 of the steaks and cook until golden brown on both sides, about 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a serving platter. Repeat with remaining 2 steaks, adding remaining oil as needed. Stir remaining flour into skillet. Stir in broth, milk, salt and pepper with a wire whisk. Cook, stirring constantly over high heat until thickened. Pour over steaks and serve. Makes 4 servings.
Into 8 ounce glass, measure first 3 ingredients.
Gradually add enough club soda to fill glass 3/4 full; stir until sugar is dissolved.
Add chocolate ice cream; stir.
Serve with spoon and straw.
Heat oven to 350°.
Spray muffin pans with nonstick spray. Mix first five ingredients together.
Use enough mustard to stick ingredients together.
Melt almond bark and chips; stir in peanuts.
Drop by spoonfuls onto waxed paper.
Cool.
Press rolls into a 13 x 9-inch baking pan.
Mix all other ingredients together.
Pour on top of crescent roll dough.
Bake at 375° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Let set 5 minutes.
Cut into 1 1/2-inch squares and serve hot!
Thaw peas and drain well.
Add rest of ingredients and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Toss lightly and refrigerate.
Mix sugar, oleo, syrup and salt.
Bring to boil.
Boil for 2 minutes.
Remove from stove.
Add soda; stir well.
Spray Pam on inside of large brown sack.
Put popped corn into sack.
Pour syrup over the popcorn.
Stir well.
Cook in microwave on Full power for 1 1/2 minutes.
Take out.
Shake well.
Cook 1 1/2 minutes more.
Shake well.
Cook for 30 seconds.
Shake.
Open bag.
Let cool.
Mix Oreos and 1/3 cup of melted butter and press in 9 x 12-inch pan and freeze.
Mix softened ice cream with instant coffee; spread over Oreo mixture and freeze.
In saucepan, mix chocolate squares or cocoa, 1/3 cup sugar, 2 tablespoons margarine and Pet milk.
Cook until thickened.
Cool and put on top of ice cream mixture.
Cook water, sugar, cornstarch, jello and Karo syrup until thickened, then cool.
Slice or quarter strawberries into a 9-inch baked pie shell.
Pour cooled, thickened mixture over strawberries.
Refrigerate.
Top with Cool Whip when serving. Yield:
6 servings.
Make cake as directed on package and use a 13 x 9-inch pan. After cake cools, poke all over top of cake and pour Kahlua over it.
Let stand overnight.
Combine 1/4 cup soup with remaining ingredients except oil. Shape into patties.
Heat oil in large skillet and brown burgers on both sides.
(Drain excess fat.)
Combine remaining soup with 1/2 cup water.
Pour over burgers and cook over low heat about 20 minutes, turning occasionally and stirring sauce as needed.
Add water as needed to sauce if it becomes too thick.

Melt margarine in saucepan. Add syrup and sugar. Bring to a boil and boil 3 minutes on stove top. Add soda and salt and stir. Pour over popcorn in brown grocery sack and shake or stir in large bowl. Microwave 1
1/2 minutes. Stir or shake. Microwave for another 1 1/2 minutes. Spread on cookie sheet to cool.
Put bacon, potatoes and onion in baking dish.
Add butter, milk, salt and pepper.
Bake at 350° until potatoes are tender.
With mixer blend cream cheese, sugar and vanilla.
Add pecans. Wash and slice Granny Smith apples to serve with dip.
Mix all ingredients together and chill for an hour.
Take out of refrigerator; roll in nuts.
Chill until ready to serve.
Combine all ingredients in bowl.
Form meatballs.
Place 8 to 10 on paper towel-lined plate.
Cover with paper towel and microwave 3 minutes on High.
Preheat oven to 300°.
Cream margarine, sugars and egg yolk until light and fluffy.
Combine flour, cinnamon and salt.
Add to beaten mixture and continue beating until blended.
Spread into ungreased jelly roll pan.
Beat egg white until just foamy.
Spread evenly on top of dough.
Sprinkle with nuts and press in lightly. Bake 40 minutes.
Cut into squares while still hot.
Add water to cook.
Cook until all vegetables are tender.
Add beef broth, if desired.
Combine all ingredients
in
top of double boiler.
Cook over low heat,
stirring frequently, until cheese melts.
Serve warm with taco chips.
Yield:
About 1 1/2 quarts dip.
Preheat oven to 425°.
Meanwhile, place pizza crust on pizza pan or baking sheet.
Mix tomato sauce and taco seasoning.
Spread over crust.
Dot with beef; sprinkle with chili peppers and cheese.
Bake in 425 °oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until meat is cooked and cheese is melted.
Sprinkle with lettuce, tomato and corn chips.
Serves 4.
Make Jell-O as directed, less 1 cup cold water.
Add remaining ingredients, stir and chill overnight.
Stir well before serving.
Beat eggs and sugar together.
Slowly add oil.
Add remaining ingredients, mixing until blended.
Spread batter in greased 7 x 11-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool and cut into squares.
Sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Saute onion until soft.
Add zucchini, salt and pepper.
Cook 5 minutes.
Toss with cheese before serving.
Combine egg, sour cream and buttermilk.
Sift together the flour, soda, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Add dry ingredients to liquids.
Mix until batter is lumpy; add coconut and extract but don't overbeat.
Spoon batter onto hot griddle.
When done, place on plate and sprinkle with flaked coconut.
Serve with cream of coconut (takes the place of syrup).
Makes 8 to 10 pancakes.
Boil 5 quarts water. Drop noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and rinse thoroughly.
Fry onions in 4 tablespoons oil until brown.
Add all other ingredients.
Stir in gravy and mix.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Drop from teaspoon onto ungreased cookie sheet.
Press a crisscross on each cookie with a fork dipped in water.
Bake at 350° for 10 to 12 minutes until golden.
Cool on cookie sheet about 1 minute before removing.
Alternate layers of green beans and onion rings in a 2-quart casserole, ending with onion rings on top.
Blend together soup and milk.
Pour over vegetables.
Blend slightly. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 portions.
Mix all ingredients and pour in an unbaked pie shell.
Bake at 300° for 45 minutes.
Combine all ingredients except pecans and butter; mix well and put into heatproof serving dish.
Saute pecans in the butter and sprinkle over top of cream cheese mixture.
Bake at 350° for about 15 to 20 minutes or until warm, but not runny.
Serve with corn chips.
Cook milk and sugar slowly, to a soft ball stage.
Add orange rind.
Cook for a few minutes more.
Add margarine and pecans. Stir to coat all pecans.
Turn out on waxed paper and separate.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease a loaf pan lightly with some shortening.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten eggs, mashed bananas and lemon juice until well blended.
Mix all dry ingredients together.
Add to shortening/banana mixture.
Mix until well blended.
Add nuts and lemon zest if desired.
Pour into greased loaf pan.
Bake 350° for 45 minutes.
Cool 5 minutes. Remove from pan.
Following is both basic dough and feeding.
Dissolve gelatin in boiling water.
Add cold water.
Chill until consistency of unbeaten egg white.
Combine next 6 ingredients and mix well.
Fold fruit mixture into gelatin mixture.
Pour into slightly oiled 10-cup ring mold.
Chill until set.
Unmold on lettuce leaves.
Fill center of ring with mayonnaise and garnish with orange slices, if desired.
Makes 20 servings.
Brown beef, add onions and cook until tender.
Add tomatoes mixed with chili powder, cumin, garlic and kidney beans.
Simmer for 1/2 hour (at least).
Add cracker crumbs just before serving.
Remove fat from chicken and cube.
Place cubed chicken in bottom of crock-pot.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook on high for at least 2 hours or until chicken is done, stirring occasionally.
Let the poppy seed soak in the buttermilk in refrigerator overnight.
Cream the shortening with the sugar well.
Add the eggs one at a time and beat until light and fluffy.
Add flour, baking powder, soda and salt together.
Add alternately with the buttermilk mixture.
Blend in vanilla.
Grease Bundt mold well or angel food cake pan.
Pour into mold.
Bake for 1 hour at 350°. Cool in mold before removing.
Plain powdered sugar or a glaze may be drizzled over the cake when cooled.
Place all ingredients in pan and heat.
Serve with oyster crackers, plain or seasoned.
See recipe for Party Crackers.
Season chicken with garlic salt and seasoned pepper in large baking pan.
Mix syrup with barbecue sauce.
Pour over chicken and bake at 400° in covered pan for 35 minutes and then uncover and bake for another 35 minutes, basting until well glazed.
Pour milk into large bowl.
Add pudding mix; beat with wire whisk 2 minutes.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Gently stir in 2 cups Cool Whip.
Arrange 1/2 of the cake cubes into 3 1/2-quart serving bowl. Drizzle with 1/2 of the chocolate syrup.
Layer with 1/2 of the chopped candy bars and 1/2 of the pudding mix.
Repeat layers ending with pudding mix.
Refrigerate 1 hour or until ready to serve.
Garnish with remaining Cool Whip.
Sprinkle with additional chopped candy bars.
Makes about 12 servings.
Heat the water to a boil.
Remove from heat and add the remaining ingredients.
Stir until all blended.
Put back on fire and bring to a boil.
Place in greased 13 x 9-inch dish and bake, uncovered, at 300° for 1 hour or until set.
Cream margarine, Crisco and sugar.
Add egg yolks, beating one at a time, to creamed mixture.
Sift flour and soda three times; add alternately with buttermilk to creamed mixture.
Add vanilla, coconut and nuts to creamed mixture.
Beat egg whites to peaks and fold into mixture.
Pour into three greased and floured 9-inch cake pans.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix together butter, cheese, flour, salt and red pepper.
Add ice water and knead together.
Roll out to 1/4-inch thick.
Cut in strips.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Place on greased cookie sheet. Bake in 300° oven until browned.
Sprinkle again with red pepper while hot.
Cool thoroughly before storing in airtight container.
Beat all ingredients with rotary beater until smooth.
Grease a pan with butter.
Cook until light brown, like pancakes.
Turn and brown other side.
After, you can spread with jam, honey or sugar, or I put some apple or pineapple or peaches inside.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Place stick of margarine in a 2 1/2-quart baking dish and melt in oven while preheating. Meanwhile, combine dry ingredients.
Stir in 3/4 cup milk (batter will be thin).
Pour batter into center of melted margarine.
Pour pie filling into center of batter.
Bake about 50 minutes or until top is golden brown.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.
Combine first 5 ingredients.
Blend well, then beat 4 minutes at medium speed.
Turn into greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 to 50 minutes, or until done. Prick cake with fork or skewer, completely through to bottom of cake.
Thoroughly blend lemonade concentrate and confectioners sugar.
Gradually spoon glaze over cake until completely absorbed. Cool and cut into squares.

Cream sugar and butter together. Add eggs and beat well. Add flour, baking powder, soda and cinnamon. Then add buttermilk and vanilla. Mix well. This will be very thick and resemble cookie dough. Grease 8 cake pans. I used Pam spray and made 4 layers at a time. You can use either 8 or 9-inch pans. Divide the dough into 8 equal parts and then pat it into the pans.
Mix all ingredients and bake in a greased cake pan for 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.
In a saucepan, whisk together all ingredients.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Pour into small jars. Cover and refrigerate.
Yields 1 1/2 cups.
Mix cream cheese and chicken with hands.
Roll into big ball. Roll ball in bacon bits.
Place ball on cheese ball serving dish. Chill until firm.
Serve with Town House crackers.
Mix garlic in with the Butter Buds.
Pour over chicken.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Turn breasts 3 times.
Serves 4. Contains 150 calories per serving.
Stir lemon juice into peach pie filling.
Cut pie crust into strips.
Place filling in small casserole.
Place pie crust strips over.
Dot with butter; sprinkle with sugar.
Bake in 350° oven until crust is brown.
Thaw frozen bread, but do not let rise.
Sprinkle nuts in bottom of 9 x 13-inch pan, if desired.
Pinch sections of bread off and roll into balls about the size of quarters.
Roll the balls in the cinnamon-sugar mixture and place in pan.
Heat together the brown sugar, margarine, milk and pudding.
Pour the mixture over the dough balls.
Let the bread rise a couple of hours or overnight.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Invert immediately on a cookie sheet.
Heat 1 inch salted water (1/2 teaspoon salt to 1 cup water) to boiling.
Add broccoli.
Cover and heat to boiling.
Cook until stems are almost tender, 10 to 12 minutes; drain.
Place broccoli in ungreased 1 1/2-quart round casserole.
Heat oven to 400°.
Beat soup and milk with hand beater until smooth; pour over broccoli. Sprinkle with cheese.
Mix baking mix and margarine until crumbly; sprinkle over cheese.
Bake until crumbs are light brown, about 20 minutes.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
Brown meat; drain.
Add tomato sauce and 1/2 cup green peppers.
Cook over medium heat 5 minutes stirring occasionally. Add beans and 1/4 pound cheese cubes.
Cook until cheese melts. Remove from heat.
Dip tortillas in hot oil; drain on paper towels.
Fill each tortilla with a 1/4 cup meat mixture, then roll up.
Place seam side down in a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish.
Pour remaining mixture over tortillas.
Cover and bake at 350° for 20 minutes.
Top with remaining cheese.
Bake 5 additional minutes to melt cheese.
Remove and top with remaining peppers, cheese and tomatoes.
Makes 4 servings.
Brown turkey and drain any juices. Sprinkle flour over meat and mix well. Add sour cream and mushrooms. Cook over low heat until bubbly. Remove and serve with pasta. Serves 2 to 4.
Sprinkle pecans evenly in bottom of well-greased bundt pan.
In saucepan, combine
soup, enchiladas, sauce, milk and chilies; heat until bubbly.
Dip
tortillas, one at a time, in sauce until limp or place
in
warm skillet until limp.

recipes.t: Hildy'S Cheese Strada With Ham And Broccoli
d: Cut 12 doughnuts and holes from the slices of white bread. Fit the resulting scraps of bread (crust removed) in the bottom of a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Layer sliced cheese, cooked and drained broccoli and ham over the bread.
Arrange doughnuts and holes on the top, with doughnuts down the sides and holes in the middle.
Combine slightly beaten eggs, milk, onion, salt and mustard; pour over bread.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake, uncovered, at 325° for 55 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
Cream together Parkay, egg and brown sugar.

Add apples, pecans and raisins by hand.
Drop by teaspoon on greased cookie sheets.

Bake at 350° for 12 minutes.
Frost with cream cheese frosting or plain vanilla frosting.

Cook, stirring, until sauce is smooth and thick.

Test for doneness.

Mix first 8 ingredients and put in a 9 x 12-inch Pyrex dish. Add a little chicken broth if mixture seems dry.

Mix together before serving.

Bake in 300° oven until potatoes are light brown.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
In medium saucepan, saute onion, olive oil and bacon until golden.
Add crushed tomatoes, basil, salt and pepper.
Cook for 15 minutes.
Stir occasionally.
Boil chicken; remove skin and set aside with hard-boiled eggs. Save stock.
In wide pot (tall pot makes process take longer), bring okra to a boil.
After lowering heat, slowly add peanut butter, stirring constantly.
If sauce becomes too thick, add some of saved chicken stock, stirring constantly.
Add chicken and hard-boiled eggs to sauce and serve over white rice.
No seasoning necessary.
Saute onions until transparent.
Add beaten eggs to other ingredients.
Bake in a greased 7 x 10-inch pan at 350° for 35 minutes.
Let cool before cutting small squares.
Reheat on serving pan when ready to use.
Place first four ingredients in a bowl.
Scald with boiling water, stirring vigorously.
Add milk, eggs slightly beaten. Place bacon drippings in a medium size Pyrex bowl and heat in oven.
Pour hot drippings into mixture and stir.
Pour all into Pyrex bowl and bake 45 minutes to 1 hour in 425° oven or until brown on top.
Serve with spoon.
Delicious served with butter. Excellent with beef hash and gravy.
Serves 4.
Put everything in skillet.
Cook on medium heat for 1 1/2 hours.
Saute mushrooms in butter.
Line greased 9-inch square pan with spinach.
Mix salt, 1/4 cup melted butter and onion. Sprinkle over spinach.
Sprinkle on half of cheese.
Now spoon mushrooms on top of cheese.
Sprinkle with garlic powder and add second half of cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 30 minutes.
If you use a 9 x 13-inch pan, double the recipe.
Single recipe serves 4 to 6 persons.
Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Pare and slice potatoes into dish.
Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and thinly slice onion in a layer on top of potatoes.
Spread the ground beef in a layer over onions.
Season the ground beef.
Add beans and soup.
Cover and bake at 350° for 2 hours.
Spread cream cheese onto large microwave dish.
Pour chili over cream cheese; cover with Cheddar cheese.
Microwave until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Add lettuce, sour cream, tomatoes and olives.
Serve warm with tortilla chips for dipping.
Line 9 x 5-inch loaf pan with aluminum foil, extending foil above sides of pan.
Combine coconut and margarine.
Press firmly on bottom of prepared pan.
In large bowl combine remaining ingredients except whipped topping, mix well.
Fold in whipped topping.
Pour into prepared pan.
Freeze 6 hours or until firm. To serve, remove from pan, peel off foil.
Slice to serve.
Freeze leftovers.
Sift 1/2 cup flour, baking powder, salt and cocoa together. Cream 1 cup sugar, oleo and 2 eggs. Add 1 teaspoon vanilla. In large bowl, add dry ingredients. Stir well. Add nuts.
Combine all ingredients.
Place in a small greased casserole dish.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with crackers.
Mix all ingredients.
Store in airtight container.
Best if chilled overnight.
Brown hamburger; drain.
Add garlic, salt and pepper and tomato sauce.
Simmer while cooking noodles.
Mix sour cream, cottage cheese and onions together.
In a large casserole, make 2 or 3 layers of noodles, cream mixture and meat sauce, ending with grated cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Combine all ingredients and simmer 1/2 hour.
Serve in a fondue or heatproof dish over a candle warmer.
Soak beans in water overnight.
Cover ham with water and boil until tender.
Skim fat from broth.
Add beans, drained, then celery, onions, parsley and pepper.
Simmer all together until ham is well cooked, the beans soft and the whole well blended.
Serves 6.
Drain vegetables, reserving liquid.
Combine flour and soup mix in large skillet.
Add water to reserved liquid to measure 3 cups; stir into mixture in skillet.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir 1 minute.
Stir in vegetables and beef. Cover; cook over low heat about 10 minutes, or until heated through.
Makes 4 servings.
Cook spaghetti.
Wash, cook and dice chicken.
Saut pepper, celery and mushrooms in 1/8 pound of butter.
Make white sauce with 2/3 stick butter, flour, broth and milk.
Combine chicken, spaghetti, vegetables and pimento.
Pour sauce over chicken mixture.
Pour into casserole dish.
Bake 400 degrees for 1 hour or until light brown.
Slowly put into boiling water tapioca; stir this frequently. Boil 1/2 hour until clear.
Remove from heat.
Pour into hot mixture the jello; add sugar.
Let cool.
Mix in Dream Whip, bananas and miniature marshmallows.
Cut celery, cauliflower and broccoli ends into small pieces. Add drained pimentos, olives and cheese.
Mix together with mayonnaise.
Cover potatoes, onions and salt with water.
Bring to a boil for 5 minutes.
Drain.
Add pimento and place in a greased 8-inch baking dish.
Add pepper and cheese to white sauce and pour over potatoes.
Top with crumbs and dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until bubbly.
Serves 6.
Place uncooked rice in casserole dish.
Arrange chicken on top.
Pour on soups and water. Bake at 300° for 2 hours. Turn chicken after 1 hour.
In small bowl, crush Wheaties.
Add oats, coconut and chopped nuts.
In another bowl, add flour, baking soda, salt and baking powder.
Cream margarine and sugars.
Add eggs and vanilla.
Add dry ingredients and mix.
Add cereal mixture last.
Bake on greased cookie sheet at 325°.
Mix all ingredients together.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Pour in Bundt pan and bake 45 minutes.
Grease cookie sheet and top of bread, then let rise for several hours.
Cut dough in half.
Roll each section as thin as possible (12 x 15-inch).
Dissolve Jell-O in 1 cup hot juice from drained pineapple (add water to make 1 cup).
Add 1 cup frozen orange juice prepared as directed on can.
Let set until partially jelled.
Add fruit and chill.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease or spray with nonstick coating a baking dish, 13 x 9-inch.
Cut pork chops and zucchini into bite size pieces.
Fry pork pieces along with bones in ungreased pan until cooked.
Transfer meat into a deep pot.
Add zucchini, drained corn and tomato sauce.
Add enough water to cover ingredients and season to taste. Let boil on medium heat until cooked or until zucchini is soft enough to eat.
Pour over cornbread, if desired, when serving.
Combine all ingredients; chill thoroughly.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Serves 6.
Mix all together and put in casserole.
Crush potato chips and sprinkle over top.
Melt 1 stick of butter and drizzle over top. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Mash avocados and stir in garlic, lemon juice and mayonnaise. Spread into 8 x 12-inch pan.
Cover with 1/2 of sour cream.
Spread on salsa.
Cover with remaining sour cream.
Sprinkle on olives. Sprinkle on tomatoes.
Sprinkle on cheese.
Serve with nachos or Dorito chips.
Lightly toast the English muffins.
Spread pizza sauce on muffins and top with cheese.
Place zucchini and mushrooms on top. Put in the toaster oven or microwave until cheese is melted. Enjoy.
Boil tea bags in 2 cups water 5 minutes. Set aside. Boil sugar in 4 cups water 5 minutes. Combine with tea. Stir in lemon juice, vanilla and almond extract. Chill and serve on ice.
Cook hamburger and drain grease.
Add to large kettle with vegetable broth, 2 cans stewed tomatoes, whole tomatoes broken up, onion, veggies and garlic.
Then add water to cover contents in kettle and continue to add as needed during cooking. Add pepper, salt and rosemary if desired. Cook on medium heat for 2 hours stirring occasionally.
Cook potatoes and mash.
Mix with sugar and butter thoroughly. Wrap marshmallows with potato mixture.
Roll each ball in corn flakes.
Place in greased baking dish and bake for 20 minutes at 325°.
Add salt to egg whites and beat until foamy.
Add sugar 1 tablespoon at a time, beating after each.
Continue beating until stiff.
Add vanilla and fold in cereal.
Drop from teaspoon onto greased baking sheet.
Bake at 350° for 15 minutes.
Makes about 3 dozen cookies.
Heat oven to 250°.
Combine crackers and nuts on large greased cookie sheet.
Combine in saucepan, butter or margarine, sugar and corn syrup.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add vanilla and soda.
Pour over crackers and nuts.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
When done, put on wax paper to cool.
Break into pieces when cool enough to handle.
Bake at 325° approximately 3 hours, uncovered.
Combine marshmallows and pineapple in saucepan and cook over medium heat until marshmallows are completely melted.
Cool thoroughly.
Whip the cream and fold pineapple mixture into whipped cream.
Pour into graham cracker crust and chill several hours or overnight.
May be topped with more whipped cream and toasted coconut if desired.
Mix gelatin, sugar and salt in 2 1/2-quart saucepan.
Stir in milk and chocolate pieces.
Place over medium heat and stir constantly until gelatin is dissolved and chocolate is melted. Remove from heat; beat with rotary beater until chocolate is blended.
Stir in Kahlua and vanilla.
Chill, stirring occasionally until mixture mounds slightly.
Fold in whipped cream.
Turn into a 4-cup mold.
Chill until firm.
Unmold.
Garnish with chocolate curls.
Combine filling ingredients in order given.
Pour into unbaked pie shells.
Bake 15 minutes at 425°.
Reduce temperature to 350° and bake an additional 40 to 50 minutes or clean knife test. Makes two 9-inch pies.
Combine cream cheese, soup and pepperoni.
Spread on toasted muffins.
Put on a cookie sheet and broil for 5 minutes or until cheese browns evenly.
Cool for 5 minutes.
Serve.
Bring to a boil oleo, cocoa, sugar and milk.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat quickly and mix in peanut butter, oatmeal and vanilla.
Drop on wax paper on cookie sheet.
Melt chocolate and butter and mix in sugar, eggs, biscuit mix and nuts.
Spread in an 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 350°.
When cool, cut into 1 1/2-inch squares.
Makes approximately 1 dozen brownies.
In a large saucepan, saute onion in margarine until soft. Stir in flour, mustard, pepper and nutmeg.
Gradually add broth, cook, stirring constantly, until smooth.
Add milk, heat through. Remove from heat.
Add cheese, stir until melted.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.
Serves 4, approximately 3/4 cup each.
Cook broccoli and cauliflower according to directions (microwave if you have).
Drain, then add soup and Cheez Whiz. Pour into greased casserole.
Put onions on top.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
Cream butter, cream cheese and sugar in large mixer bowl until light and fluffy.
Add egg yolk, almond extract and orange juice and beat well.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt and gradually add to creamed mixture.
Stir in 3 cups of the coconut. Cover tightly.
Cream the sugar and butter.
Add eggs, flour, cornstarch and vanilla.
Mix until well blended and smooth. Add cream.
Make small balls about 1 inch in diameter, then roll about 9 inches long and twist into a figure eight.
Grease cookie sheet lightly and sprinkle with flour before putting roskette dough on the sheet.
Bake at 350° in preheated oven for about 20 minutes. While still warm, carefully remove from cookie sheet to cool. Makes about 5 dozen.
Mix all ingredients in large mixing bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Toss again before serving.

Cut eggplant in round 1/2 inch slices. Beat eggs, dip eggplant in egg then in bread crumbs. Coat completely and shake off excess crumbs. Slowly heat half of the oil in a a large skillet. Saute eggplant slices in oil until light brown on both sides, about 2 minutes per side. Drain eggplant on paper towel. Add more oil as needed to brown remaining eggplant. Preheat oven to 350 degrees. In a baking dish put eggplant then cover with ricotta cheese, spaghetti sauce, mozzarella cheese, Italian seasoning and parmesan cheese. Bake uncovered for 20 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes. Serves 4.
Remove mushroom stems.
Chop enough stems to measure 1/2 cup. Cook half of mushroom caps in 3 tablespoons of margarine over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Drain.
Repeat with remaining mushroom caps and margarine.
Brown and drain meat.
Melt cheese with meat over low heat. Add remaining ingredients and put in a teaspoon of meat and cheese mixture on rye bread.
Serve.
Can freeze for later use.
Mix vanilla wafers and margarine; press in bottom of pan. Set in icebox to chill.
Mix milk, eggs, salt, pepper and butter.
Then mix remaining ingredients except for a small amount of cheese.
Pour into 9 1/2 x 11-inch baking pan.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top and bake for 45 minutes at 375°.
Serves 4 to 6.
Have margarine and cheese at room temperature; whip until light and well mixed.
Add remaining ingredients.
Drop by spoonfuls on ungreased pan and press with fork dipped in flour. Bake 12 minutes at 350°.
Makes 60.
Mix all ingredients and refrigerate for 24 hours before serving.
Dissolve jello in boiling water.
Add mashed bananas, pineapple and juice and strawberries and mix well.
Refrigerate overnight and serve.
Dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add buttermilk, sugar and Crisco.
Stir to melt Crisco.
Sift in flour, soda and salt.
Beat until smooth and let stand 10 minutes.
Divide in half and roll out each half on slightly floured board fairly thin.
Cut each circle into 12 pie-shaped wedges.
Roll from wide end to point.
Put in greased pans and let rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 400° for 15 to 20 minutes.
Makes 24 rolls.
Mix thoroughly graham cracker crumbs, sugar and oleo.
Mix cream cheese with sugar and eggs.
Put graham cracker mix in loaf pan and spread with mixture.
Bake 15 minutes at about 350°. Cool.
Sift together the first 8 ingredients.
Combine shortening and bananas.
Beat shortening and bananas for 2 minutes.
Add egg; beat 1 minute.
Add dry ingredients alternately with milk.
Blend thoroughly after each addition.
Stir in pecans; spread well in greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 22 to 25 minutes.
Fillet fish, removing the skin.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes or squares.
Use a glass or crock container.
For each quart of fish, use 5/8 cup of pickling salt and cover with cider or white vinegar. Stir well.
Place the jar in the refrigerator for one week.
Stir thoroughly every day.
Rinse thoroughly in cold water and let stand in cold water for one hour.
Drain well, pack loosely in jar, using a layer of fish and layer of onion.
Over this pour a syrup of 1 pint vinegar, 1 1/4 cups sugar and 1 teaspoon pickling spice. Bring to a boil and let cool.
Remove spices.
Pour syrup over fish.
Seal and store in refrigerator.
Ready in 3 to 4 hours.
Mix Mexicorn with creamed corn.
Add remaining ingredients, except Parmesan; blend.
Pour into buttered 9 x 12-inch casserole; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Preheat oven to 325°; bake until firm, about 40 to 45 minutes.
Marvelous!
Saute
meat; drain fat.
Sprinkle with packaged seasonings. Blend
well.
Add
tomato
sauce and tomatoes, mixed in blender. Simmer
for
to 20 minutes, stirring frequently. In a
very lightly buttered 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, spread a thin	layer of	sauce, then a layer of quartered tortillas, chilies and cheese.
Repeat for a second layer.
Bake at 350° for 40 minutes. Serves 8.

recipes.t: Low Calorie Crust For One Pie
d: Mix flour and salt.
Pour vinegar, then oil, then milk into a small cup and add all at once to flour mixture.
Stir to blend. Then press into a ball.
Flatten slightly.
Roll out between 2 sheets of wax paper to fit an 8-inch pie plate.
Flute edges. Pour in filling and bake at 425° for 25 minutes.
Put butter, sugar and dates in large boiler.
Cook until thick and bubbly.
Mixture will make a ball when 1/2 teaspoon is put into a cup of cold water.
Remove from heat; add nuts, Rice Krispies and vanilla. Mix well.
Let cool.
Make into small balls.
Place on waxed paper.
Roll in powdered sugar.
Dissolve Jell-O in boiling water.
Add sugar and lemon juice. Stir and add frozen strawberries.
Stir well.
Fold in whipped cream.
Crumble cake in small pieces.
Place half in bottom of greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Pour Jell-O mixture over cake.
Place second layer of cake and pour remainder of Jell-O mixture. Refrigerate until set.
Saute onions in margarine until tender.
Stir in bread crumbs, sugar, salt and pepper.
Set aside.
Arrange half of the tomatoes in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Top with half of crumb mixture. Repeat layers.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Combine squash, onion, salt and sugar.
Simmer with small amount of water for 20 minutes.
Drain well.
Mash with potato masher.
Add eggs, melted butter, flour, milk and cheese.
Add seasoning salt to taste.
Bake in a buttered 1 1/2-quart casserole for 30 minutes at 350°.
Top with crumbs and bake 10 minutes more. It can be stored in a refrigerator for 2 or 3 days, unbaked. Freezes very well.
Makes 8 servings.
Combine tomatoes, cheese, vinegar, oil, pepper sauce, garlic and salt.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Makes about 3/4 cups.
Using a colander, thoroughly rinse the beans, removing all the juice.
In a mixing bowl, combine the beans, mayonnaise, onions and cucumbers.
Mix thoroughly and add pepper generously.
Salt to taste.
Chill for at least two hours (overnight is better).
Yields 4 (1/2 cup) servings.
Mix everything together but ham and cheese.
Put enough sauce in meat to make it red.
You can also add some onions.
Bake at 350° for about 1 hour or until meat is brown.
Sprinkle some Mozzarella cheese on top, Swiss and ham chunks.
Mix butter, powdered sugar, peanut butter and vanilla.
Form into small balls.
Melt chocolate chips with Crisco.
(I do it in the microwave.)
Put toothpick into balls and dip in chocolate to give the appearance of a buckeye.
Place on waxed paper. Refrigerate to harden.
Unroll crescent roll dough.
Place in a lightly greased 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan, pressing edges and perforations together to line pan.
Bake at 350° for 7 to 8 minutes until browned.
Cool and press down.
Mix all together and bake at 350° for 1 hour; the last 5 minutes sprinkle a small amount of grated cheese on top.
Very tasty.
Boil chicken breasts until done.
Reserve broth (1/4 cup). Skin and bone chicken.
Use kitchen scissors to cut into small chunks.
To remainder of broth, add potato, carrots and celery. Cook a while, then add peas and cook until tender.
Drain vegetables.
Melt margarine in pan.
Add flour and salt to make a sauce base, then slowly add reserved broth and milk.
Cook, stirring frequently, until sauce thickens.
At desired consistency, add chicken and vegetables.
Season to taste.
Cover with crust; slit the crust.
Bake at 375° until crust is brown.
Dissolve 1 package of Jell-O in bowl with boiling water.
Pour into greased 9 x 13-inch pan.
Refrigerate to set.
Bring milk to boil.
Add sugar.
Add the unflavored gelatin, dissolved in cold water.
Mix well.
Add sour cream and vanilla.
Mix well.
Cover first layer with sour cream mixture (1 1/2 cups).
Refrigerate until set.
Repeat with 3 packages Jell-O and boiling water. Alternate layers of Jell-O with sour cream mixture.
Let each layer set before adding the next layer.
Place apples in greased shallow baking dish.
Sprinkle with lemon juice.
Combine flour, oats, sugar, salt and cinnamon.
Add melted butter, mixing until crumbly.
Sprinkle crumb mixture over apples.
Bake in moderate oven at 375° for 30 minutes or until apples are tender.

Cut veal into thin slices, dip in beaten egg and then into the bread topping, Shake and Bake. Bake in the oven at 350° until done. Mix a brown gravy packet per directions and add a can of mushrooms. Salt and Pepper to taste. After the veal is cooked pour gravy mixture over the veal and serve with mashed potatoes.
Dial 662-5555 (Pizza Hut).
Clean chicken and dry.
Combine bread crumbs, cheese and parsley flakes; mix.
Melt margarine and add lemon juice; set aside.
Coat each piece of chicken in bread crumb mixture and place in baking dish.
Drizzle margarine and lemon juice mixture over each piece of chicken.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cook noodles to package directions.
Cool ground beef to warm. Mix meat, cheeses and sauce together.
Spray 9 x 13-inch pan.
Stir all ingredients together until sugar is pretty well dissolved.
Freeze.
Use one ice cream scoop per cocktail glass and add wine or 4% mixer to dilute.
Stir and serve.
Combine sugar, cornstarch and salt in medium saucepan.
Stir until well blended.

Add boiling water, stir until well blended. Put on stove and cook until mixture thickens, stirring constantly. Add chocolate and butter to mixture, continue cooking and stirring until chocolate and butter melts.
Remove from heat.
Add vanilla, stirring constantly. Let cool a little.
Spread over cake.
Cream oleo with sugar.
Mix all ingredients together.
Bake at 325° for 45 minutes.
Blend the oil and spices in a small bowl.
Rub mixture over the entire roast.
Place in shallow pan and bake at 350° for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until internal temperature is 155°.
Let stand for 10 minutes before slicing.
*If using raisins, soak in cool water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Boil sweet potatoes with skin on.
Peel and mash with fork (not mixer).
Add brown sugar, margarine and vanilla.
Spoon into hand; add marshmallow and spoon more in hand with marshmallow in middle.
Form a ball.
Roll in coconut.
Put in buttered baking dish in 425° oven for about 15 minutes.
Delicious!!
Cook and mash potatoes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and beat until fluffy.
If necessary add a little milk.
Layer in ungreased 2-quart casserole first 3 items.
Mix bread crumbs, cheese and butter; sprinkle on top of soup.
Bake uncovered one hour at 350°.
Brown ground beef.
Add celery and onion.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add soup.
Stir and pour into casserole dish.
Place chow mein noodles on top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Cut meat in bite size pieces.
Roll in flour and brown in oil. Brown onion in grease.
Mix sauce.
Add steak and onion to sauce.
Simmer for 2 to 3 hours in crock-pot, stirring often. Serve over rice.
Mix all together just before serving.
Mix all ingredients and serve.
Cook noodles and vegetables until noodles are done.
Bring Cheddar cheese, cream cheese and margarine to room temperature.
Add milk, onion, pimiento, Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce.
Beat until combined.
Cover and chill 4 to 24 hours.
Melt the chips, add noodles and nuts.
Drop on cookie sheet and place in refrigerator and cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Beat eggs well.
Add remaining ingredients; mix well.
Pour into a baking dish sprayed with Pam. Bake 45 minutes.
Fry hamburger and onion.
Add soup, sour cream and chiles. Put a little of the mix on bottom of a pan.
Put mixture by the tablespoonful onto the flour shell.
Roll up and put into pan. Pour sauce on top of enchiladas.
Add cheese.
Bake at 350° until bubbly.
Place breast between waxed paper and pound flat.
In pie pan combine crumbs, Parmesan, 1 teaspoon oregano, garlic salt and pepper.
In bowl stir together butter, parsley and 1/2 teaspoon oregano.
Spread herb butter on breast.
Add strip of cheese, fold and roll.
Drip in melted butter and roll in crumb mixture.
Place seam side down in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Drizzle remaining butter over. Cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
Bake uncovered 20 minutes at 425°.
Combine all ingredients and marinate for 2 hours.
Bake in shallow dish uncovered at 350° for 40 minutes.
Set oven at 400°.
Mix margarine, sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl.
With a knife, spread the mixture on one side of the bread.
Place the bread on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Toast in the oven for 8 minutes.
Cook to hard ball stage.
Pour over popped corn.
Mix good. Batter hands and make into balls.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl.
Pour into a 1 1/2-quart ungreased casserole dish.
Set casserole dish in a large baking pan.
Add hot water to pan to come about halfway up the outside of the casserole dish.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes.

recipes.t: Coconut Cake With Sour Cream Filling
d: Mix cake mix according to directions, adding 2 whole eggs. Bake in 2 layers.
When cool, split layers with knife or thread, making 4 layers.
Mix together coconut, sour cream and sugar. (Save enough coconut to cover the top and sides of cake.)
If possible, mix coconut and sour cream with the sugar the day before baking the cake.
After the cake has cooled and been sliced, spread the coconut mixture on each layer.
Stack layers, using toothpicks to hold the layers in place, then spread the top and sides of the cake with whipped topping and sprinkle with coconut.
Refrigerate 2 days before serving to improve the flavor.
Brown and drain meat; add onion and green pepper.
Cook until tender.
Add barbecue sauce, mushrooms and salt.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Cut bread in 1/2.
Scoop out center.
Place 6 slices of cheese in bottom.
Fill with hot meat.
Cover with remaining cheese.
Put top back on bread and wrap loaf in tinfoil.
Bake at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cream butter and sugar; beat in eggs, one at a time.
Beat in flour and half and half (alternate).
Add flavoring.
Cook in 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Double for two cakes; freeze one for later.
Mix all ingredients; reserve half of the cheese to sprinkle on top.
Pour into a greased 9 x 13 baking pan or dish.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Cut into squares.
Cook chicken tenders until done.
Pinch
the tendon off of each tender, being careful not to waste any meat.
Discard the tendons.
Cut tenders in 1/2-inch pieces.
Place tenders in bowl; cover and place in refrigerator while you prepare the other ingredients for the chicken salad.
Dissolve yeast in water.
Combine flour, salt, lemon rind, and 1/4 C of sugar in a large bowl.
Cut in margarine.
Combine graham cracker crumbs and margarine.
Press into 9 x 13-inch dish.
Mix confectioners sugar, cream cheese, softened and egg.
Spread over crust.
Add bananas, sliced, over cream cheese mixture and crushed pineapple, drained.
Top with Cool Whip. Sprinkle nuts on top.
Refrigerate.
Brown bacon slices and set aside.
Brown the hamburg and onion in part of the bacon fat.
Partially drain the Great Northern beans and mix with the pork and beans in a large casserole (5-quarts).
Add the hamburg and onion.
Season with remaining ingredients.
Bake 1 hour at 350°.
Put bacon slices across other ingredients for the last 15 minutes.
Line 8 x 8 dish with whole graham crackers.
Drain juice from cherries and set juice aside.
Spread drained cherries over whole graham crackers in dish.
Sprinkle sugar over cherries and set aside.
Take round steak pieces and lay them out.
Brush top side with melted butter.
Salt and pepper each one.
Layer onion and garlic on each side. Roll up each piece and stick with a toothpick to hold the roll.
Dip in flour and brown on all sides.
Take 2 cans of mushroom soup and either put in a baking pan with 1 can of water or in a crock-pot.
Place meat in receptacle.
When baking, cover with foil and place in a 350° oven for 1 1/2 hours.
Cook eggs and shred; set aside.
Start with well-chilled cooked rice.
Break up the rice into loose rice.
Oil wok and heat.
Put rice into wok and cook, constantly turning it.
Add salt, Accent, soy sauce, sesame oil, meat and vegetables.
Cook until done.
Serves 4.
Cream shortening and sugar.
Add beaten eggs and beat well. Add dry ingredients, beating well.
Add oatmeal, vanilla and nuts. Shape in rolls and wrap in waxed paper.
Place in freezer and bake as needed.
Slice 1/4 inch thick.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350° for 10 minutes.
Yields 5 dozen.
Cut chestnuts in
half;
place in medium hot oven until shells and inner	brown
skins
peel
off
easily.
Peel	the chestnuts and put
in
enough
water	to cover.
Add sugar and salt; boil until chestnuts are very tender.
Remove from heat; drain and mash or puree in blender with remaining ingredients. Can be garnished with whipped cream, fruit, etc.
Serves 6.
Mix ingredients together and stir until smooth.
Serve with all kinds of fruit (sliced bananas, apples, mandarin oranges and pineapple chunks).
Flatten crescent rolls out on cookie sheet and bake 10 minutes (cool).
Mix cream cheese, mayo, sour cream and dressing.
Mix together and spread on top of cooled rolls.
Top with choice of cut up veggies such as lettuce, broccoli, tomatoes, mushrooms and olives.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and cut into squares.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix ingredients by hand.
Form the balls the size of half dollars.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet, about 1 inch apart.
Bake for 35 minutes, or until brown.
Heat oven to 375°.
Beat egg, water, butter, oil, sugar, cinnamon and 1/2 the cake mix until smooth.
Add remaining cake mix, oats, raisins and nuts.
Blend and spread in two 9 x 9 x 2-inch square pans or a cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.
Combine all ingredients; chill and serve on lettuce.
Beat eggs and add remaining ingredients; cook until it starts to thicken.
Remove for heat and cool.
Brown the first 4 ingredients until tender; add all remaining ingredients except cheese.
Simmer for 1 hour on very low temperature.
Add Jack cheese to thicken, just before you serve. Top with chopped fresh onions, if desired.
Serves 6.
Cook sliced potatoes in 1/2-inch boiling salted water 10 minutes.
Drain and arrange in alternate layers with onions in a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Pour White Sauce over and bake, uncovered, in moderate oven at 350° for 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Serves 4.
Melt butter in small skillet.
Add green pepper and onion. Saute until tender.
In a mixing bowl, toss together zucchini, bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, salt and pepper.
Add sauteed vegetables and mix well.
Place the mixture in buttered 1-quart casserole.
Bake in preheated 375° oven for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Arrange tomato wedges on top of casserole and bake 5 additional minutes.
Sprinkle Cheddar cheese over tomatoes and continue to bake until cheese is melted.
Serves 6.

recipes.t: Blasted Mahi-Mahi With Tomatoes And Okra
d: Saut onion in oil in Dutch oven 5 minutes or until tender. Stir in tomatoes and remaining ingredients. Reduce heat and cook, stirring often, 10 minutes or until okra is tender.
Beat together eggs and milk; set aside.
Fry sausage and drain grease.
Place in casserole dish, then add grated cheese and bread crumbs.
Pour in egg mixture.
Cover with Saran Wrap.
Place in refrigerator overnight.
Next day, cook, uncovered, 45 minutes to 1 hour in 350° oven.
In a 9-inch pie pan, spread butter on bottom and sides.
Press pecan halves, rounded sides down, into butter.
Put brown sugar evenly over pecans.
Roll out enough pastry for lower crust. Place in pie plate over brown sugar and pecans.
Pare and slice apples.
Sprinkle apples with lemon juice. Combine flour, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and dash of salt; toss with apples.
Put apples in pie pan.
Roll out top crust and put over pie.
Pinch edges. Prick top of pie with fork.
Bake at 400° for 50 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Cool 5 minutes; invert and remove pie pan carefully. Serve warm or cool.
Cook noodles until almost done and drain.
Combine in saucepan the rest of the ingredients and heat until the bouillon cubes are dissolved.
After draining the noodles, pour the mixture over the noodles and cook until not soupy.
Brown meat until brown.
Put all other ingredients together and cook for 40 minutes.
Allow to stand for 1 hour and reheat.
Mix fruit, sugar and cinnamon and put in lightly greased casserole.
Mix brown sugar, flour, pecans, butter and Quaker oats and sprinkle over fruit mixture.
Bake at 375° for about 40 minutes.
In saucepan, heat cream of mushroom soup, Ro-Tel and cream of chicken soup.
Crumble the Doritos chips.
Layer the ingredients as follows:
chips, chicken and liquid.
Repeat layers; top with cheese.
Bake at 350° for 20 minutes in a casserole dish.
Saute zucchini and onion in margarine until tender (10 minutes).
Mix in seasonings.
In a 10-inch skillet over medium heat, in hot margarine, cook mushrooms, green onion and garlic until tender, stirring occasionally.
Add broth and shrimp; heat to boiling.
Beat eggs.
Add sugar, then sifted dry ingredients.
Drop by teaspoons on greased cookie sheet, no more than 6 at a time.
