Bake at 400° for 5 minutes or until lightly browned.
Roll into cone shape while hot (before rolling fill with Cool Whip and pineapple); fasten with toothpicks.
Brown meat with onion; drain.
Layer meat, beans and cheese on top of tortilla chips which have been spread on the bottom of an oblong baking dish.
Mix Ro-Tel with soup and pour on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for 1/2 hour or until cheese is melted.

Sprinkle the roast with 1 tablespoon flour. In a Dutch oven, brown the roast on all sides in half of the butter. Add the water, bouillon, onion, celery, salt and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour. Add carrots; cover and simmer 45 to 60 minutes longer or until meat is tender. Remove meat and carrots to a serving platter and keep warm. Strain cooking juices; set aside. In the same Dutch oven, melt remaining butter. Stir in remaining flour; cook and stir until bubbly. Add 2 cups of the cooking juices and blend until smooth. Cook and stir until thickened; add additional cooking juices until gravy has desired consistency. Yield: 6 to 8 servings.
In large saucepan, combine sweetened condensed milk, cocoa, vanilla and salt.
Mix well.
Over medium heat, slowly stir in water; heat through, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with whipped cream if desired.
Melt butterscotch morsels in a double boiler. Stir until all melted. Remove from heat and stir in cocktail peanuts and chow mein noodles. Drop by spoonful on wax paper and cool in refrigerator.
Pour melted butter into 9 x 11 x 2-inch pan.
Beat egg whites until foamy, gradually add sugar.
Pour sugar mixture over pecans; spread in pan over butter.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Cool.
Mix well.
Roll in small balls and press down slightly with a fork that has been dipped in water.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes. While still quite warm, roll in powdered sugar.
Mix all ingredients, except pickling spice and vinegar.
Pack into gallon jar, placing bag of pickling spice in center.
Pour vinegar over all.
Place a layer of plastic wrap over jar and seal with lid.
Every day, turn jar.
Do this for 30 days.
Then place in refrigerator and serve chilled.
Prepare brownie mix and bake according to package directions in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Prick top of warm brownies, using fork. Drizzle with coffee-flavored liqueur.
Let cool and crumble. Prepare pudding mix according to directions, omitting chilling.
Bring to a boil the sugar and Karo.
Boil 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove and add chunky peanut butter and butter.
Stir well.
Add Cocoa Puffs.
Stir.
Drop by spoonfuls on cookie sheet. Let cool and set.
Cut beef in thinnest possible slices.
Pound flour, salt and pepper into meat.
Cut into strips about 3 x 1/2-inch.
Dice onions and fry slowly until soft and just turning yellow.
Then add meat and saute until well seared.
Add tomato paste and enough beef stock to just cover.
Add soy sauce to taste.
Simmer until tender. Transfer to top of double boiler and add sour cream and mushrooms. Serve with rice.
Mix ground beef, salt, eggs, margarine and onion together. Shape in 2-inch balls and roll in flour.
Brown on all sides in the margarine.
Add 1 1/2 cups bouillon and the bay leaf.
Bring to boil, cover and simmer 1/2 hour.
Mix 1/4 cup flour with remaining bouillon until smooth.
Stir into mixture and cook, stirring gently, until thickened.
Good with mashed potatoes.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Let stand at least 2 hours (overnight is better).
Serve at room temperature.
Heat Presto cooker and brown pork.
Add onions and cook slightly.
Add potatoes, water, salt and pepper.
Close cover securely and place pressure gauge in place.
Cook for 5 minutes with pressure up.
Let pressure drop on its own.
Add milk, corn and butter and reheat.
Thicken chowder, if you like.
In a saucepan, saute the onion in butter.
Add corn, milk and spices.
Simmer for about 15 minutes.
Add clams with juice and cook about 5 more minutes.
Add salt to flour and sift.
Work in shortening with two knives until shortening is evenly mixed.
Stir and moisten into dough with water; pat into ball and chill.
Later cut off amount needed and roll out on a floured board with light, quick strokes to 1/8-inch thickness, working into circular form.
Blend gelatine, Sweet 'N Low and pineapple juice together in saucepan until boiling, while stirring constantly.
Then stir in the last 3 ingredients.
Pour in flat pan and refrigerate until set.
Cut into squares.
Oil a large platter or cookie sheets.
Combine sugar, Karo and water in heavy pan.
Stir until dissolved.
Bring to boil and wash sides of pan down; wash all sugar that sticks to sides of pan. Add peanuts when mixture reaches soft ball stage (235°).
When mixture begins to boil again start stirring.
Cook to hard crack stage (310°) and add soda, salt, butter and then vanilla and coconut.
Remove from heat first and stir well.
Spread as thin as possible on greased platter.
Run knife under brittle as soon as possible to let air beneath candy and platter.
As soon as candy is hard enough to handle, stretch in all directions.
Beat together first 4 ingredients.
Add flour, soda, cinnamon, salt, cloves and black walnuts (you may use other walnuts).
Pour into large greased jelly roll pan.
Bake in 325° oven.
Test after about 25 minutes.
Freezes well.
You may cut recipe in half and use 9 x 12-inch pan or make two pans from full recipe.
Mix ingredients.
Cut 3 to 4 pounds beef 3/16 to 1/4 inch thick.
Soak 24 hours.
Dry in food dehydrator until hard or what you like.
Place ingredients in casserole in order given.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 4 hours in a 250° oven.

Prepare shell macaroni according to directions. Drain and set aside. In medium saucepan, combine soup, milk and cheese. Cook and stir until cheese melts. Stir in remaining ingredients. Turn into a 2-quart baking dish. Bake at 325° for 30 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Put noodles in pot any size with water.
Let noodles boil for a minute or until done.
Put in rest of ingredients (does not matter which order put in).
Mix the first 6 ingredients together and place in casserole dish.
Spread crushed potato chips and grated cheese on top.
Bake in a preheated 400° oven for 20 minutes.

In nonstick skillet, warm oil. Sprinkle chicken with paprika. Add chicken to skillet and cook until golden on both sides. Remove chicken and cover loosely with foil. Add rice and onion to skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until rice is golden and translucent, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in broth, tomatoes with liquid, parsley and pepper, crushing tomatoes with a spoon. Bring to a boil. Return chicken to skillet. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in green beans. Cover and cook about 15 more minutes.
Mix graham crackers, sugar and melted butter well; line the bottom of a 9-inch spring-form pan and bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Boil potatoes in Jackets, peel and slice.
Brown bacon and onion to taste.
Make a sauce of flour, sugar, vinegar and water.
Mix altogether and fry.
Combine oil and seasonings in a bowl.
Add potatoes, stir to coat, and arrange in a single layer on an ungreased 15 x 10 inch pan.
Bake uncovered at 450° for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake 10 to 15 minutes or until crisp tender.
Serves 6.
In a small saucepan, bring first 3 ingredients to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes.
Pour 1/2 cup of syrup mixture into a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish.
Arrange potatoes in syrup.
Top with remaining syrup.
Bake in 350° oven, basting often, 20 minutes or until glazed.
Makes 12 servings.
Mix the first 5 ingredients together.
Spread on rolls.
Bake at 400° on cookie sheet for about 15 minutes, or until meat is cooked.
Remove from oven.
Place Mozzarella cheese on top.
Put back in oven until cheese is melted.
Mix together and place all ingredients in shallow baking dish. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes at 375°.
Remove from oven.
Allow to set 10 minutes before serving.
Combine last 5 ingredients for sauce and simmer for 1 hour. Spread shrimp in single layer in shallow ovenproof dish.
Cover with warm tomato sauce.
Sprinkle with Feta cheese.
Cook in 450° oven until shrimp are done.
It doesn't take long.
Serve with French bread or over orzo type pasta.
Combine all ingredients in casserole. Top with buttered bread crumbs, if desired.
Heat in oven at 375° until mixture is bubbly and hot, about 1/2 hour or so.
Place flour, sugar, baking soda and baking powder in the baking pan.
Sift cocoa powder into pan and stir all together. Add water, mayonnaise, eggs and vanilla to the pan; mix well until all the flour is moistened and batter is smooth.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool.
Place 1/2 cup of the frosting in a small bowl. Stir the food color into the frosting, a few drops at a time, until you like the shade.
Spread it neatly in the upper left corner of the cake to make a 4 1/2-inch square.
Arrange marshmallows in a circle on the blue frosting to make stars.
Preheat oven to 375°.
Grease and flour 15 x 10 x 1-inch jelly roll pan.
Cut bacon into 2-inch pieces.
Fry until crisp.
Remove bacon. Set aside.
Remove all but 4 tablespoons of drippings.
Dice potatoes, onion and celery.
Cook potatoes, onion and celery in Dutch oven having water about 2 inches above the vegetables. Cook until almost soft.
Add cauliflower while vegetables are cooking brown.
Add flour in drippings to soup.
Add bacon.
Cook over medium heat until thick.
Garnish with hard-boiled eggs.
Serve.

Dissolve jello in water. Beat cream cheese until fluffy. Stir in jello and stir until smooth. Stir in vanilla, oranges, pineapple, soda and pecans. Chill until jello mounds using a 13 x 9 x 2-inch dish. Fold in 3/4 of whipped topping. Refrigerate until set. Garnish with remaining topping.
In large bowl, mix gelatine with sugar.
Add boiling water and stir until gelatine is completely dissolved.
Add lime juice, food coloring and lime peel.
Cool mixture completely.
Stir in milk. Freeze 1 1/2 hours or until mixture is frozen about 1/2 inch around sides of bowl.
Cook sliced zucchini in boiling water until soft, drain.
Put in large bowl.
Saute carrots, onions and green peppers in butter (oil) until tender.
Add to bowl.
To bowl, add 1 1/2 cups stuffing cubes, sour cream and soup; mix.
Put in 2-quart casserole dish. Melt margarine.
Add remaining cubes.
Toss and put over top of casserole.
Bake 40 minutes at 350°.
Cream together the butter and brown sugar; stir in vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Keep refrigerated.
To serve, put 1 tablespoon of butter mix in a mug.
Add 1 ounce of dark rum and 6 ounces of water.
Stir and serve.
Brown beef with onions in Dutch oven.
Add taco seasoning, salad dressing mix, beans, chilies, hominy, stewed tomatoes and water.
Simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with taco chips and top with sour cream and sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Beat all ingredients with mixer for 5 minutes.
Pour into unbaked pie shell and bake 45 minutes at 325°.
Makes 1 large pie.
Rinse, stem and dry mushrooms.
Place on greased baking sheet. Combine ingredients.
I use a food processor.
Reserve 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese.
Spoon mixture into mushroom caps. Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake at 350° for approximately 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Mix pretzels, 3 tablespoons sugar and butter together.
Press into 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Beat together cream cheese and powdered sugar.
Fold in Cool Whip and marshmallows.
Spread over crust.
Add Jell-O to boiling water; stir to dissolve.
Add berries.
Pour over Cool Whip layer.
Refrigerate several hours or until firm.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt and pepper together 3 or 4 times.
Cut in shortening, then crumble with tips of fingers.
Add just enough sweet milk to make a very, very stiff dough.
Roll out on a well floured dough board about 1/8-inch thick.
Cut into strips or squares and drop into boiling stock in which chicken has been previously cooked.
The stock should be boiling madly when dumplings are dropped in; add milk to chicken stock for a richer gravy.
Lower heat and cook slowly about 20 minutes.

Cook noodles until done. Drain in colander. Set aside. Brown hamburger meat; drain in colander. Mix noodles and hamburger. Add pepperoni. Then mix pizza sauce and spaghetti sauce and put into glass baking dish. Add shredded cheese. Cover with foil and bake at 350° until cheese is melted.
Layer pan with crushed pineapple, then spread 1 can cherry pie filling, then 1 box cake mix (dry).
Cut 2 sticks of margarine evenly on top.
Sprinkle top with pecans and bake at 350° until done, 30 to 40 minutes.
Mix and store in refrigerator 5 days and freeze.
Boil chicken in water to cover for about 2 hours.
Bone and dice.
Let stock set.
Sift dry ingredients into a large bowl. Add everything else and stir with a spoon to mix well. Do no beat. Pour into a greased and floured Bundt pan; bake at 350° for about 1 hour.
Place unopened can of milk in pan of water (cover can).
Boil for 4 hours.
Remove from water and when cool enough to handle, open can and smooth caramel in crust.
Place in refrigerator until ready to serve.
Mix cake according to directions.
Bake as directed in greased 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Poke holes in warm cake and pour caramel topping on top.
Cool.
Top with Cool Whip and crumbled Heath bars.
Arrange steaks in greased baking dish.
Sprinkle with vinegar, salt, pepper and basil.
Bake at 375° for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Combine bread crumbs and cheese.
Spread over steaks; sprinkle with melted butter.
Return to oven and bake 10 minutes longer or until halibut flakes easily.
Serve 6 on a heated platter garnished with parsley.
Adjust oven racks so that one is in the middle.
Heat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour a 10 x 10 x 4-inch heart-shaped or round angel food cake pan with movable bottom.
Mix sugar and butter in a large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until crumbly. Add eggs, gradually, increasing mixer speed to high, and beat until mixture is creamy and pale.
Then add 2 cups of nuts. Reduce speed to low.
Beat in chocolate and vanilla, then cornstarch and baking soda.
Scrape down sides of bowl.
Add half the flour and sour cream.
Before fully blended, add remaining flour and sour cream.
Still at low speed, beat in milk just until blended.
Beat together the margarine, peanut butter and sugars.
Blend in eggs.
Add combined flour, soda and salt; mix well.
Stir in oats and 1/2 cup chocolate chips.
Place 1/2 dough onto 1 or 2 foil lined and lightly greased 12 or 13-inch pizza pan(s).
Spread dough within 1 inch of pan edge.
Sprinkle each cookie with the remainder of chocolate chips.
Bake at 325° for 20 to 22 minutes. Cool.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Spray shallow 2-quart casserole or 12-inch by 8-inch baking dish with non-stick cooking spray. Discard seeds from chiles.
Slice cheese into same number of pieces as there are chiles.
Place 1 slice of cheese in middle of each whole chile.
Arrange stuffed chiles in casserole.
In bowl, whisk eggs, flour, and milk until blended.
Pour egg mixture over stuffed chiles in casserole.
Bake 35 minutes or until top is golden brown and knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix 1 package dry dressing mix with 1/2 cup of mayonnaise and 1/2 cup of milk.
Add cream cheese and beat with electric mixer. Add Cheddar cheese and blend.
Cover and refrigerate overnight. Before serving, sprinkle with almonds or bacon bits.
Good with Ritz crackers or Wheat Thins.
Mix ingredients in 1 1/2-quart bowl.
Shape into loaf in center of 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Peel and slice 1/4-inch thick, 3 medium potatoes and 3 medium onions.
Peel and quarter lengthwise 3 medium carrots.
Mix 2 teaspoons dried parsley flakes, 1 teaspoon salt and dash of pepper.
Place vegetables in layers around meat.
Sprinkle each layer with part of salt mixture. Cover pan tightly with foil.
Bake in 375° oven (high moderate) for 1 hour or until vegetables are tender.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes more to brown meat.
Serves 6.
Drain and soak shrimp as label directs.
Beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in lemon juice.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Chill to blend flavors.
Garnish as desired.
Serve with crackers or fresh vegetables.
Yields 3 cups.
In a large bowl, combine corn oil, vinegar, sugar and salt. Add beans and onion.
Toss to coat well.
Cover.
Refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Makes 4 1/2 cups.
Mix cream cheese and pumpkin, then fold in cool whip. Mix together sugar and spice; add to cheese mixture. Pour into prepared shell. Refrigerate for 3 hours.
Break egg over apples in bowl.
Add oil, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and walnuts.
Mix well.
Add mixture of flours and baking soda, stirring just until moistened.
Spoon into greased 8 x 8-inch cake pan.
Bake in preheated 350°
oven for 40 to 45 minutes, or until tests done.
Let stand in pan for 10 minutes before slicing.
Yields 9 servings.
Mix all ingredients.
Put into a greased and floured spring form.
Bake slowly at 325 to 350°F for 1 hour.
Melt margarine.
Crush graham crackers with a rolling pin. Sift powdered sugar.
Mix margarine, graham crackers, peanut butter and sugar together in large bowl.
Spread mixture in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Melt chocolate chips and milk chocolate and pour on top of peanut butter mixture.
Refrigerate
1 1/2 hours.

recipes.t: Lisa'S Night Before Christmas Morning Breakfast
d: You will need a deep 2 to 3 quart covered casserole dish. This recipe you layer in the casserole dish.
Start with croutons, some butter, sausage, cheese and repeat until you are close to the top (about 1 to 1 1/2 inches from top).
In a separate bowl, mix eggs, milk, garlic salt, mustard and onion until well blended and pour over layered ingredients in casserole dish.
Cover and chill overnight.
Bake in the morning at 325°
for 1 hour.
Preheat
oven to 350° (325° for glass dish).
In a 13 x 9-inch baking dish, melt butter in oven.
Sprinkle crumbs over butter. Pour
Eagle
Brand milk evenly over crumbs.
Top with remaining ingredients.
Press
down
firmly.	Bake
to 30 minutes until browned lightly.
Cool.
Cut into bars.
Beat egg whites stiff.
Add sugar.
Continue to beat until very stiff (10 minutes).
Melt chocolate chips in double boiler and add to egg whites.
Add vanilla, chopped nuts and coconut. Drop by spoon onto wax paper on cookie sheet.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
Remove quickly from paper.
Cook rice and water; set and cool.
Prepare pudding as directed on package.
When cool, mix together with Cool Whip.
Put in fridge and let set.
Heat milk to 110° to 115°; remove from heat.
Dissolve yeast in 1/2 cup warm milk in small bowl.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Combine remaining milk, honey, shortening, salt and whole wheat flour. Beat at medium with electric mixer until smooth.
Gradually stir in enough all-purpose flour to make it stiff.
Heat a stemmed glass. Add sugar. Pour in strong black coffee to about 1 1/2-inches of the rim.
Stir well. Add Irish whiskey to within 1/2-inch of top.
Pour in cream over the back of the spoon to put a "head" on the contents.
Mix all ingredients except cracker crumbs.
Pour into a square, well-buttered baking dish.
Sprinkle top with crumbs and dot with butter.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Mix rice, water, celery and cream soups together in 9 x 13-inch pan.
Lay pieces of raw chicken on top.
Sprinkle 1 package of onion soup mix over the top.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake at 350° for 3 hours.
Do not peek!
Wash spinach thoroughly.
Remove stems.
Tear leaves into large pieces.
Cook in a small amount of boiling water 5 to 10 minutes or until tender.
Drain.
Place on paper towels and squeeze until barely moist.
Melt butter in a large skillet; saute onion and garlic until tender.
Stir in next 4 ingredients.
Add the spinach and cook over low heat until thoroughly heated. Sprinkle with paprika.
Serves 4.
Mix and serve.
Keeps well in fridge for several days.
Melt sugar, syrup and salt.
Remove from heat and add peanut butter and Rice Krispies.
Pat in container.
Melt butter and brown sugar, add milk, vanilla and beat in confectioners sugar and spread over mixture; chill.
Wash and cut fish in serving portions.
Put bread crumbs, salt and pepper in plastic bag.
Shake fish in seasoning and crumbs. Take fish out of bag and put in frypan of hot oil. Cook until tender; place on paper towel to drain.
In a large bowl, mix well the sugar, eggs and oil.
In another bowl, combine flour, cocoa, salt and baking powder.
Mix dry and moist ingredients a little at a time, until well blended.
Add nuts and mix well.
Spread in a 9 x 13-inch baking pan and bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 350°.
Store in airtight container.
Mix together; form into log.
Roll in parsley flakes.
Chill and serve with crackers.
Mix all items, except dinner rolls, and spread on rolls which have been opened up to form a rectangle.
Roll up like a jelly roll.
Place in refrigerator for about 15 minutes for easy handling.
Cook spaghetti; drain and rinse.
Cook meat; drain.
Chop into small fine pieces.
Pour spaghetti sauce over spaghetti; mix well. Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan; sprinkle meat over top.
Cover with cheese slices and bake for 1/2 hour at 350°.
Mix and bring sugar, corn syrup and water to 240°.
Add peanuts and continue to cook at 300°.
At this temperature, add soda, vanilla and margarine.
Have about 3 cookie sheets buttered and at this time pour your brittle on the cookie sheet and then pull with knife or fork to the thinness you want.
Let cool and store in cool place in Ziploc bags.
This makes about 2 1/2 pounds of brittle.
In a large mixing bowl, cream butter and 2 cups sugar until fluffy.
Add vanilla.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, baking powder, soda and salt; add alternately with sour cream, beating just enough after each addition to keep batter smooth.
Spoon 1/3 of batter into a greased 10-inch tube pan.
Combine cinnamon, nuts and remaining sugar.
Sprinkle 1/3 over batter in pan.
Repeat layers two more times.
Bake at 350° for 70 minutes or until cake tests done. Cool for 10 minutes.
Remove from pan to a wire rack to cool completely.
Yield:
16 to 20 servings.
Melt butter
in baking dish.
Mix all other ingredients in bowl
and pour the mixture into buttered baking dish.
Bake at 375° for 30 or 40 minutes.	Brown lightly on top.
Brown
sausage	in
large
skillet.
Drain, reserving 1 tablespoon	drippings
in
skillet.
If onions and chilies are used,
wilt
at this time.	Add rice-vermicelli mix.
Continue cooking
until
vermicelli	is
slightly
browned.	Add water, contents
of seasoning packet and tomatoes (chopped in blender or food processor).
Bring to a boil.	Cover; reduce heat and simmer 15	to 20 minutes or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Mix the dry ingredients first, add melted butter and sprinkle over potatoes.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
Chop all vegetables.
Soak overnight in 1/4 cup of salt.
Be sure water covers the vegetables.
In the morning, drain all the salt water off of the vegetables.
Place all spices in a cheesecloth bag.
Boil for 10 minutes in the vinegar (use a large pot).
Remove spice bag from vinegar.
Add sugar and mix well.
Add all vegetables.
Stir in well.
Bring to a boil, then turn stove off.
Cut chicken at joints.
Wash, then pat dry with paper towel. Heat oil in a deep skillet and brown chicken slightly over medium heat.
Add next five ingredients.
Bring to a boil uncovered without stirring.
Add onions, salt and pepper. Simmer 20 minutes allowing sauce to thicken.
Transfer chicken and sauce to an ovenproof casserole or baking pan and bake 10 to 15 minutes or until slightly brown in a 350° oven.
Mix ingredients together except cornflakes and butter.
Mix cornflakes and butter together and put on top of the other ingredients.
Bake 45 minutes at 350°.

recipes.t: Died And Went To Heaven Chocolate Cake
d: Preheat oven to 350°. Lightly oil 12-cup Bundt pan; dust with flour. Invert and shake out excess. In large mixing bowl, whisk together flour, granulated sugar, cocoa, baking powder and salt. Add buttermilk, brown sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla. Beat with electric mixer on medium speed for 2 minutes. Whisk in
hot coffee. The batter will be thin. Pour into prepared pan; bake for 35 to 40 minutes. Cool in pan 10 minutes.
Drain pineapple.
Reserve syrup, add water to make 1/2 cup. Dissolve Jell-O and sugar in 1 cup hot water.
Add syrup and lemon juice.
Chill until partially set.
Add fruits, celery and nuts. Chill in 5 cup ring overnight.
Serves 8 to 10.
Prepare pie crust according to directions for empty baked crust; cool.
In a small bowl, combine cream cheese and 1 tablespoon sugar.
Beat until smooth; spread into bottom of baked crust.
(I use half of strawberries.)
In a 1-quart saucepan, combine pureed berries, remaining sugar and cornstarch.
Cook over medium-low heat until mixture thickens and becomes clear; stir often (about 7 to 10 minutes).
Remove from heat.
Stir in remaining strawberries.
Let cool for 10 minutes, then pour into crust.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours, then serve with whipped topping.
Yields 8 servings.
Put cooked rice, milk, sugar and nutmeg in medium saucepan. Cook over medium heat for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until thick. Remove from stove. Add vanilla.
Let cool.
After cool, sprinkle with cinnamon and refrigerate.
No trouble at all.
Sweet as can be.
Never talks back.
He'll even help decorate the tree.
Cut meat in strips 1/2 x 1/4 x 4 to 6-inches long.
Mix all other ingredients and pour over meat.
Marinate overnight in fridge.
Drain meat and pat dry with paper towels.
Let meat cure in oven using pilot heat or lowest setting.
Turn oven off periodically.
Process until done.
Fry meat, salt and pepper to taste, drain.
Place generous amount of meat, onion, and cheese on each tortilla.
Roll up and place end side down in baking dish.
Set aside.
In saucepan, add flour, chili powder, tomato juice, salt, water and oil. cook until slightly thickened.
Pour over each tortilla.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes until cheese melts and warms up.
Put milk and butter in saucepan. Heat until butter melts, but do not boil. Add oysters and salt and pepper. Let get real hot, but don't boil. Serve with saltines.
Preheat oven to 450°.
Combine Wheat Chex crumbs and apples; mix well.
Pour apple juice over crumb mixture.
Combine biscuit mix, nutmeg and cinnamon; mix well.
Stir into crumb mixture; mix well.
Drop by spoonfuls onto buttered baking sheet.
Bake at 450° for 10 minutes.
Yields 16 to 18 servings.
Beat egg whites in large bowl.
Fold in sugar and beat until stiff.
Fold into custard mixture.
Place layers of cake, broken in bite size.
One layer of cake and one layer of custard until all custard and cake is used.
Leave in refrigerator overnight.
Unmold and frost with whipped cream.
Take a plastic bag and pour into it approximately 8 to 12 ounces of Worcestershire sauce.
Add garlic powder, onion salt, lemon pepper, paprika, Italian seasoning and seasoned salt (if desired).
Amounts are not important and depend upon personal preference.
Place roast in bag and marinate a minimum of 24 hours in refrigerator.
Bake uncovered at 375° for 1 hour and 20 minutes for medium to well done.
Combine oleo, egg and sour cream.
Add corn and Jiffy mix. Stir well.
Bake at 350° in a greased dish.
Let stand for 5 minutes.
Bake approximately 9 minutes in waffle iron.
Spray waffle iron with Pam every other time.
Heat oil in 10-inch skillet.
Mix zucchini, cheese, parsley, egg, salt and pepper; stir in baking mix.
Drop by rounded tablespoon into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown, about 1 minute on each side; drain.
Makes about 2 dozen cakes.
Sprinkle chicken over medium size dish.
Heat broth and soup together.
Pour over chicken.
Melt margarine; add milk and flour. Mix and pour over top of chicken mixture.
Bake at 325° until golden brown.
Mix and let come to a boil. Cook until tomatoes begin to change color.
Jar and seal. Delicious on peas or lima beans.
Peel and grate potatoes, onion and apple on coarse grater. Beat eggs lightly; add grated potatoes, onion and apple and blend well.
Add salt, flour and baking powder and mix thoroughly.
Pour 1-inch oil into skillet and heat.
Drop mix by tablespoons into hot oil.
Fry and brown both sides.
Serve hot.
Drain off any liquid before frying each cake.
Serve with sour cream or applesauce.
Makes 20.

recipes.t: Marquise Au Chocolat(Avec Une Sauce De Creme A L'Anglaise)
d: Melt chocolate in a double boiler; add a few drops of water if necessary to smooth out chocolate.
Let cool; meanwhile, beat yolks, sugar and butter until smooth and silky.
Add this mixture to the cooled chocolate; it should be smooth and thick, but not stiff.
Gently fold in the beaten egg whites, then pour into a small mold which has been lightly buttered.
Set the mold in a bowl of ice cubes and refrigerate until set, 4 to 5 hours.
Dunk the bottom half of the mold in hot water and the Marquise will slip out very easily.
Cut into wedges to serve.
Mix ground beef, onion, pepper and rice.
Stir over high heat until browned.
(Pour off excess fat.)
Add tomato sauce and remaining ingredients.
Mix well.
Bring to a boil quickly.
Cover tightly and let simmer for 25 minutes.
Combine paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, red pepper, white pepper, black pepper, thyme and oregano in shaker bottle; mix well.
Spray cast-iron skillet with nonstick cooking spray. Heat until very hot.
Sprinkle catfish filets with seasoning mixture.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes on each side.
May cook over hot coals on grill.
Yield:
2 servings.
Place undrained chilies in bottom of glass pie plate.
Grate cheese and sprinkled on top of chilies.
Beat eggs, milk and salt. Pour over cheese.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Serve with triscuits or tortilla chips.

Fill 9x13 pan with sliced apples. Spread sugar and cinnamon over apples, dot with butter and a dash of salt. Mix remaining ingredients together. Place on top of apples. Bake 375 degrees for 35-40 minutes.
Mix together potatoes, sugar, salt, eggs, oleo, milk, and vanilla.
Place in a well-greased baking dish.
Mix well brown sugar, flour, nuts and oleo.
For topping, place over potato mixture.
Bake at 325° until done.
(My oven heats so fast I can't use 350° for 30 minutes.)
Soften unflavored gelatin in 1/2 cup water. Set aside.
In a 3-quart saucepan, combine cranberries, sugar and wine or cranberry juice; heat to boiling, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat. Add lemon gelatin and softened unflavored gelatin. Stir until dissolved. Stir in remaining water.
Chill until mixture is partially set.
Fold in celery and walnuts.
Pour into greased 8-cup mold.
Cover and chill until set.
Place salmon in pint jars.
Leave 1/2 inch at top.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Cook in pressure canner for 90 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease and flour Bundt pan.
Mix all ingredients together until smooth.
Pour into cake pan.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes.
Remove from oven.
While hot, add glaze.
Allow to cool and remove from pan.
Arrange fillets in single layer.
Cover with plastic wrap. Cook in microwave on High 5 to 7 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork.
Let stand 5 minutes.
In 1-quart casserole, combine sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in pineapple juice.
Add green pepper, vinegar, soy sauce, onions and garlic.
Cook at High 3 to 4 minutes or until mixture thickens.
Stir twice.
Stir in pineapple chunks and almonds.
Arrange fillets on serving dish. Spoon mixture over fillets.

Combine first 4 ingredients in large bowl and mix until well blended. Blend flour, soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and baking powder into mixture on low speed until smooth. Add squash, carrots and nuts. Stir until well blended. Preheat oven to 350°. Bake 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours. Makes 2 loaves.
Cream margarine and sugar.
Add eggs and beat well.
Mix all ingredients together and add to butter mixture.
Add fruit, nuts and soaked raisins.
Mix well and drop on a greased cookie sheet. Make them small teaspoon drops.
Bake at 325° for 15 to 18 minutes.
Mix soup and water.
Use 1/2
of mixture to make up hamburger patties.
Make into 4 patties and brown on both sides.
Pour balance of soup mixture over patties.
Cover and let simmer for 25 minutes.
Cook until thick.
Remove from heat and add 1 1/3 cups coconut and 1 cup nuts.
Mix well and drop on wax paper.
Peel potatoes and slice into thin slices.
In a casserole dish, put potatoes, onion, milk and butter.
Season with salt and pepper. Mix everything together.
In microwave, cook 14 to 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
(Stir every 2 to 3 minutes while cooking.)
After potatoes are tender, add cheese and stir together. Cook 1 more minute in microwave (until cheese is melted).
Preheat oven to 425°.
Grease muffin cups.
Stir together flour and sugar in mixing bowl.
Beat egg in separate bowl; stir in milk, butter and banana.
Add liquid mixture to dry ingredients, stirring just until blended.
Batter will be slightly lumpy.
Fold in pecans.
Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes about 12 muffins.
Melt butter in pan.
Blend in flour, salt and sugar.
Stir until smooth.
Add milk and cook until thick.
Stir in corn and beaten eggs.
Bake at 350° until the knife comes out clean.
Cook and slice potatoes.
Saute mushrooms and onion in butter. Combine cottage cheese and sour cream.
In a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish, layer first potatoes with salt and pepper. Second, mushroom mixture.
Third, cottage cheese mixture, then Cheddar cheese on top.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes covered; uncovered, bake 15 minutes.
Add more cheese.
In small mixing bowl, beat egg and buttermilk.
Mix in all other ingredients and stir well.
Spoon batter into 6 paper-lined custard cups or microproof muffin pan, filling about half full. Cook 6 muffins at a time on High (max power) 2 or 3 minutes, or until no longer doughy.
Repeat twice.
Yields 18 muffins. Cooking time:
6 to 9 minutes.
Boil rice until tender.
Let rice stand, then drain.
Brown hamburger until done.
Dice up bell pepper and onion.
Add these and tomato sauce to hamburger.
Add hamburger mixture to cooked rice; simmer for about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Place the first 5 ingredients in mixing bowl.
In smaller bowl, make dressing with mayo, sour cream, curry powder, lemon juice and salt; pour over chicken mixture and toss.
Chill 30 minutes.
Yields 6 servings.
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs, one at a time.
Mix well. Add salt, vanilla and vinegar.
Fold in remaining ingredients and pour into pie shells.
Bake at 350° until well browned.
In a medium saucepan, over medium heat, melt butter and saute onion until golden; about 8 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and toss to mix it with the onion and coat it lightly with butter. Cover the pot, reduce heat to low and let steam 8 to 10 minutes; until just tender.
Spread the beans on a large platter (about 10 x 13-inches). Mix together the cream cheese, sour cream and taco mix; spread this on beans.
Spread taco sauce over top.
Cover with lettuce, then tomatoes and cheese.
Serve with round tortilla chips.
Can also use chopped onion, black olives, hot peppers, etc., on top.
Melt butter in a large pan.
Add onion, potatoes and carrot. Cover and cook over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Cook green beans in the microwave on high for 5 to 6 min. Toss walnuts on the beans. Mix all other ingredients together and pour over the beans and walnuts.
Set in refrigerator to cool for 2 hours and serve.
Serves 6.
Wash and remove outer skin from broccoli and cut into small pieces.
Mix sugar, cornstarch, oyster juice, chicken broth and ginger (a jar works great!).
Place broccoli pieces in pan with approximately 1/4 cup of water.
Cover and steam approximately 3 to 4 minutes until broccoli is tender, not too done!
Drain any excess water; toss in ginger and stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add sauce; stir again until broccoli is coated and remove to warm plate.
Chop cauliflower and broccoli into small pieces.
Add chopped eggs and chopped onion.
Drain water chestnuts and add to mixture.
Combine sugar, water and salt; cook down until a rich brown color.
Add 1 1/2 cups milk and cook and stir until sugar is dissolved.
Combine cornstarch, spice, remaining 1/2 cup milk and egg yolks; beat until well blended.
Add raisins to hot milk mixture and cook and stir until thick and cornstarch is cooked (about 3 or 4 minutes).
Pour into baked pie shell and top with meringue made with the 2 egg whites and brown in a slow 300° oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together.
Chill and serve with chips. This recipe will serve 4 people.
Saute onion and celery in butter.
Simmer remaining mixture 10 minutes, then add sauteed onion and celery.
Mix with cooked chicken and then bake an additional 10 minutes.
In a large skillet (or Pan), combine sausages and barbecue sauce; stir over medium heat until heated through.
Gradually stir in marmalade.
Serve warm.
Mix in order listed.
Sprinkle top with cinnamon and sugar mixture.
Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together, except tomato sauce.
Roll in small balls.
Put tomato sauce in large pan.
Bring to a boil.
Add meatballs.
Simmer for 1 1/2 hours in covered pan, stirring occasionally so meatballs don't stick.
Mix all ingredients well.
Chill and serve with fresh veggies, crackers or chips.
Combine first 4 ingredients in large bowl.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt and cocoa, then stir into sugar mixture.
Fold in chopped Snickers.
Spoon into greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Sprinkle with chopped Hershey bars.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool and cut.
Makes 2 1/2 dozen.
Heat oil in skillet.
Add chicken.
Stir until golden brown. Add taco seasoning and 2 tablespoons or so of water.
Add cilantro and simmer for 4 minutes.
Cover and set aside.
Divide and place chicken onto a half side of each tortilla.
Add green onions, cheese and a small amount of salsa if desired.
Fold over tortilla. Carefully place one folded tortilla in clean, dry skillet over medium heat.
Cover and let cook 5 minutes.
Carefully turn onto other side and heat 3 to 5 minutes until golden and ingredients are melted inside.
Repeat with other quesadillas.
Place milk, sugar, eggs and salt in top of double boiler. Place over boiling water; stir constantly until custard lightly coats spoon.
Do not overcook.
Soften gelatin in cold water and pour custard over it.
Stir until dissolved.
Add flavorings. Chill until partially thickened.
Stir frequently.
Fold in whipped cream.
Split cake in 2 layers.
Spoon filling between layers, on sides and top of cake.
Sprinkle with almonds.
Chill. Serves 16.
Mix ingredients thoroughly.
Form into balls.
Add more powdered sugar, if too sticky.
Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 375°.
In a large mixer bowl, lightly but thoroughly, combine the meats and crumbs; use your hands, if necessary.
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs and add the sour cream, onion, lemon juice and spices.
Mix well.
Pour over the meat mixture and blend.
In blender, blend cottage cheese, milk and pineapple juice. In a large bowl, combine cheese mixture and fruits.
Mix well. Refrigerate.

Saute onions in stick of butter until just translucent. Put layer of cracker crumbs in bottom of buttered 9 x 11-inch baking dish. Top with 1/2 of the sauteed onions. Dab 1/2 of mushroom soup over onions, then cover with remaining onions and the rest of the soup. Sprinkle light layer of cracker crumbs over onion/soup layers. Beat the milk and eggs together, then pour over the top of the onions. Finish with shredded cheese on top. Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes or until casserole is set and starting to lightly brown.
Peel and core apples.
Sift flour with 4 tsp. baking powder and 1/2 tsp. salt.
Cut in shortening.
Add milk.
Stir with fork to make soft dough.
Roll out on floured board. Cut dough into 6 squares about 4 inches.
Roll thin.
Put apple in center of each square.
Pour sugar in the core of each apple.
Fold dough up over apple.
Pinch edges together.
Place in baking pan.
Bring water, cinnamon, sugar and butter to a boil.
Pour over the dumplings. Bake 1 hour and 15 minutes in oven at 400 then for 30 minutes at 300.
Mix all together and chill.
Saute onions and mushrooms in butter. Add soup and water, then rice and seasonings; stir. Bake in greased casserole, covered, in a 350° oven for 45 minutes or 1 hour.
Cream the shortening and sugar.
Add remaining ingredients in order given; mix well after each addition.
Spread in a shallow, greased pan.
Bake at 350° for 18 to 20 minutes.
Do not overbake. Take out while soft and chewy.
In a bowl, combine pie filling, peel, juice and nutmeg.
Pour into greased 10 x 6 x 2 pan.
Combine flour, sugar and salt.
Cut in butter with fork; stir egg mixture (egg beaten with vanilla) into flour mixture until moist and crumbly.
Sprinkle over cherry mixture and bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
Serve with ice cream or topping.
Makes 6 servings.
Cook about 20 minutes until thick.
Combine first 4 ingredients in a large saucepan.
Cook over medium heat 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add pecans and continue cooking 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla. Place pecans individually on wax paper.
Cool completely.
Yields 2 cups.
Combine first 4 ingredients in saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until reduced to 3 cups (about 30 minutes). Strain mixture through sieve and discard solids.
Fry hamburger; drain and put in bottom of small casserole. Add beef soup.
Put about 2 inches of mashed potatoes on top.
Dot the top with buttered bread crumbs and bake at 350° for about 30 to 40 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Beat eggs well.
Add sugar, vanilla, cream and buttermilk. Stir and add flour, baking soda, salt, baking powder and nutmeg. Chill dough before rolling out.
Fry at 375°.
Salt roast; put in pan with water.
Simmer 3 to 4 hours until roast shreds easily.
During last hour, add your potato.
When it's done, mash potato and shred your roast together.
Add soup, chillies and chopped onion.
Place back on stove and heat just long enough to stir together.
Lightly brush each tortilla with butter, then place a scoop of beef mixture in each tortilla and top with a large spoon of sour cream and cheese.
Fold tortilla. Place in a large pan.
Spread rest of sour cream and cheese on top.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together, except Fritos.
Put in large casserole dish or 9 x 13-inch pan.
Crush Fritos and put on top of mixture.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
You will need 6 (8 ounce) jars.
Mix soup, milk and butter together and heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Add broccoli, wine and tarragon.
Bring to a boil and serve.
Layer carrots, peppers and onions in Tupperware. Mix remaining ingredients and pour over carrots. Marinate 2 days in refrigerator.
Stir together the oats, flour, baking powder, soda and salt; set aside.
With mixer at medium speed, beat peanut butter and margarine until smooth.
Beat in sugars until blended.
Beat in eggs and vanilla.
Add oat mixture; beat well.
Chill dough, if necessary; shape into 1-inch balls.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet, 2 inches apart.
Flatten with floured fork, making crisscross pattern.
Bake at 350° for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Mix all well.
Put into 2 1/2 to 3-quart buttered casserole. If too dry, add 1/3 cup water or tomato juice.
Bake, covered, at 350° for 45 minutes.
Saute vegetables with garlic in butter; remove garlic.
Add tomato paste and wine.
Simmer briefly but do not overcook vegetables.
May be prepared early in day.
When ready to serve, add additional wine to taste and heat thoroughly.
Serve with sliced tenderloin steak or other cooked beef.
In a saucepan, heat enchilada sauce.
While it is heating, spray or grease rectangular baking dish.
Heat oven to 350°.
Mix powdered sugar, shortening and softened butter together. Stir in flour.
Press in ungreased 18 x 26-inch bun pan.
Bake in 350° conventional oven and 325° in convection oven, until just golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Oven temperatures vary and you may need to adjust cooking time to your oven.
Cream together the butter or oil and honey.
Add eggs.
Sift dry ingredients together and add to creamed mixture alternately with milk.
Pour batter into 2 oiled 9-inch cake pans.
Bake for 35 minutes in oven
preheated to 350°.
Combine all ingredients, except chocolate chips.
Press into a greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes. Sprinkle immediately with chocolate chips.
Let stand 5 minutes. Spread chocolate evenly.
Melt butter in a large skillet; add celery and mushrooms. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes or until celery is crisp-tender, stirring often.
Add onions, rosemary, peas, chicken broth, salt and pepper.
Cook until thoroughly heated.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.
Combine sugar, water and butter.
When mixture begins to boil rapidly, add pecans.
Boil, stirring constantly, until mixture forms large bubbles on top and looks sugary.
Remove from fire. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto well buttered marble slab or platter.
Beat eggs and add to ingredients.
Mix well.
Bake in loaf pan at 350° for 1 hour.
If desired, sprinkle with brown sugar before baking.
Peel and slice potatoes.
Chop onions.	Alternate layers of potatoes and onions in greased 2 or 3-quart baking dish.
Season each layer with salt and pepper.
Mix mushroom soup, cream of celery soup and milk and pour over potatoes.
Place ham slices on top.
One-half cup of grated sharp Cheddar cheese may be added as topping instead of slices of ham.
Bake in 350° oven until potatoes are tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
Cut fish in 2 or 3 portions, according to size. Dip fish into beaten egg, then into bread crumbs.
Place coated fish in a well-greased, shallow baking pan. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Drizzle a mixture of melted butter or margarine and lemon juice over fish.
Bake in oven at 400° until golden brown. Allow 5 to 6 minutes for each 1/2-inch of thickness.
Makes 3 servings.
Freeze leftover portions.
Beat the cream cheese and Eagle Brand together. Add Cool Whip to mixture.
Pour 1/4 of this mixture into 1 crust.
Drizzle 1/4 of the caramel on top of each pie.
Melt oleo in skillet.
Add coconut and pecans. Stir until toasted.
Sprinkle 1/4 of the mixture on top of the caramel in each pie. Repeat each step using the remainder of the ingredients.
Place in freezer and serve frozen. This is very good to have on hand as an emergency dessert.
Wash broccoli.
Remove long leaves and tough pieces of stalks. Cut stalks lengthwise into quarters.
Place broccoli in large saucepan with 1-inch boiling salt water.

Cook for 10 to 12 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain broccoli well. Reserve cooking water. In a large saucepan, melt butter over medium heat and saute celery and onion until soft. Stir in flour, blending well. Combine reserved cooking water and milk.
Gradually stir into saucepan. Cook until mixture is slightly thickened and comes to a boil. Add cheese and stir until melted. Stir in tuna.
Serve hot over cooked broccoli.
Makes 4 servings.
Preparation time:
20 minutes. Cooking time:
15 minutes.
Chop beef into small pieces.
Mix rest of ingredients with beef and mix well.
Chill until serving.
Serve with bread or crackers.
Bake cake as directed on box.
Cool.
Divide in half. Prepare instant pudding as directed on box.
*If the button mushrooms are used, additional broth will be needed to cover and simmer them.
Mix together oil, rice wine vinegar, sugar, salt and spice packet.
Pour mixture over shredded cabbage.
Break up noodles on cabbage; add toasted sesame seed and mix well.
Chill before serving.
Heat oven to 350°.
Combine butter, peanut butter and brown sugar; beat until light and fluffy.
Add water, egg and vanilla; mix well.
Combine flour, cinnamon and baking soda.
Stir into butter mixture; mix well.
Stir in oats and raisins.
Drop by tablespoonfuls onto cookie sheets.
Bake in upper third of oven for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Remove from cookie sheets to wire racks.
Makes 4 dozen.
Melt cheese and mayonnaise in saucepan.
Put potatoes in bowl and mix with cheese. Add 3/4 cup bacon bits on top.
Bake in a 9 x 13-inch casserole. Cook, covered, at 350° for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine 3/4 cup granulated sugar, flour, 3 tablespoons cocoa, baking powder and salt. Blend in milk, butter and vanilla. Beat until smooth.
Pour batter into an 8 or 9-inch square pan or dish.
Beat eggs; add juice and sugar.
Cook in double boiler, stirring until thick and smooth.
Remove from fire.
Add butter and cool.
Add to fruit mixture and whipped cream.
Put in refrigerator for 24 hours before serving.
Combine cheese, chicken soup, sour cream, butter and onions. Spread mixture over potatoes.
Top with corn flakes.
Bake at 425 degrees for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Heat oven to 375°.
Mix dressing, flour, bouillon and pepper in saucepan; gradually add milk.
Cook, stirring frequently, over medium-low heat until thickened.
Add turkey and vegetables.
Cook until thoroughly heated.
Spoon into 8-inch square baking pan. Unroll dough and place over turkey mixture to cover.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Makes 4 servings.
Pour boiling water over dates and let set 10 minutes. Add remaining ingredients except chocolate bits and nuts.
Put chocolate bits and chopped nuts on top before baking.
Pour into greased and floured, large loaf pan, 9 x 14-inch.
Bake at 350° for approximately 30 minutes.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon corn meal in bottom of a 10-inch skillet (well-greased). Cook over medium heat until corn meal is slightly browned.
Combine corn meal, salt and soda.
Mix well. Add milk, corn, eggs and oil.
Mix well.
Pour 1/2 batter into skillet; sprinkle with cheese, onion, peppers and ground beef.
Top with remaining batter.
Bake in a 350° oven for 50 to 55 minutes. Makes 6 servings.
Mix well the milk, cheese, eggs, oleo, flour and sherry.
Add the vegetables.
Pour into a 9-inch greased pie pan.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
Soften sausage and cream cheese.
Blend together, then add other ingredients.
Refrigerate.
Serve on crackers.
In 8-inch square dish, spread pie filling.
In small bowl, mix together cake mix, butter, nuts and cinnamon until crumbly. Sprinkle evenly over cherries or in three rows so cherries are visible.
Cover with wax paper.
Microwave on Auto Cook 2 if you have the Automatic Cooking Cycle, if not cook on 20% power for approximately 11 to 15 minutes.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.
In a large heavy saucepan, put the sugar and evaporated milk. Bring slowly to a rolling boil.
Let boil for no longer than 8 minutes, stirring constantly, to keep from scorching.
Remove from heat and add the marshmallows, chocolate chips and butter or margarine. Stir until melted and well blended.
Add broken nutmeats and vanilla. Spread in large ungreased (at least 9 x 13-inches) pan.
When cool, cut into squares.
Makes a huge batch, about 4 to 5 pounds of fudge.
With a slotted spoon, dip cottage cheese from the carton into a large mixing bowl.
Dump into dry gelatin.
Mix well; add the drained fruits.
Dump in whipped topping and fold well.
Chill 1 hour or overnight.
This keeps well for 3 to 4 days.
Makes 6 to 8 servings.

Place cucumbers in gallon jar. Cover with a brine of 1 c. coarse salt and 11 c. boiling water. Cover jar and let set for two weeks. Pour off brine, rinse, and then cover with cold water to which Alum has been added. Let set for 24 hours. Pour off water. Cover with cold cider vinegar to which pickling spices have been added. Let set for 24 hours. Drain off vinegar but leave pickling spice. Add 3 c. sugar, let set for 24 hours, add 3 more c. sugar, let set for 24 hours, and then add 3 more cups sugar. This makes a juice to cover the pickles. Just leave pickles in the gallon jar and set on a shelf. Take out as needed to serve. These have a long shelf life and are very crispy.
Cook and drain broccoli.
Grease a 9-inch pie plate.
Spread cooked broccoli in pie plate.
Beat together sour cream, cottage cheese, Bisquick, margarine and eggs.
Pour in pie plate.
Top with thin tomatoes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 to 40 minutes.
When knife inserted in center comes out clean, it is done.
Serves 6 to 8.
Mix sugar and cornstarch together.
Grate lemon and wash from grater with cup of cold water.
Mix in sugar and cornstarch.
Add beaten egg yolks and pinch of salt.
Taste for sweetness and lemon flavor.
Stir while cooking.

Boil water, pineapple, and sugar. Remove from heat, add box of jell-o and stir thoroughly. Put in freezer, stirring occasionally until it starts to jell. Blend mixture and cream cheese. Mix in cool whip and add pecans. Refrigerate.
In large saucepan, melt butter and chocolate over low heat. Remove from heat.
Add remaining ingredients except confectioners sugar.
Blend well.
Spread in greased 13 x 9-inch pan.
Bake at 350° for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool; sprinkle with confectioners sugar.
Cut into squares.
Makes 36 bars.
Brown ground beef and onion until cooked.
Use an herb gravy packet and mix in with onion and meat.
Dice potatoes and boil for 20 to 25 minutes.
Mash with butter and milk.
Put meat, onion and gravy in medium sized casserole dish.
Add mashed potatoes on top of the meat.
Place oven on broil and brown top of pie.
Add eggs to other ingredients one at a time.
Bake in a large, long, greased cake pan at 350° for approximately 45 to 55 minutes or until knife comes out clean.
Brown short ribs in fat.
Add remaining ingredients except noodles.
Cover tightly and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours or until ribs are done.
Add noodles and cook 15 minutes longer or until noodles are tender.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.
Brown hamburger.
Drain liquid.
Add remaining ingredients and heat until cheese is melted.
Can be prepared in crock-pot. Serve hot with chips of your choice.
Combine sugar, peanut butter, milk and extract in a large mixer bowl.
Blend thoroughly.
Combine dry ingredients and gradually add to peanut butter mixture.
Pour batter into a greased 9 x 5 x 3-inch loaf pan.
Bake at 350° for about one hour and 10 minutes or until bread tests done.
Turn out of pan onto cooling rack.
Cool 10 minutes.
Makes one loaf.
With a sharp knife, cut beef across grain into thin strips, 1/8-inch thick.
Combine soy sauce, garlic and ginger.
Add beef; toss and set aside while preparing vegetables.
Heat oil in large frying pan or wok.
Add beef; toss over high heat until browned. Test meat.
If not tender, cover and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes over low heat.
Turn heat up; add vegetables to meat.
Toss until vegetables are crisp (about 10 minutes).
Mix cornstarch with water; add to pan.
Stir and cook until thickened.
Add tomatoes; heat through.
Add
to
green peppers
and hot peppers 6 cups sugar and 1 1/2 cups white vinegar.
Boil 9 minutes;
remove from stove. Add 1
bottle of Certo and green food coloring.
Stir.
Put in hot clean jars and seal.
To be eaten on cheese not toast.

Cook chicken. Take off bones and place in casserole dish. Moisten stuffing well with broth and place over chicken, leaving enough to top dish with. Boil chicken soup with broth and pour over chicken and stuffing.
Top with rest of dressing. Bake at 350° until it bubbles.
In large mixer bowl, beat cream cheese until fluffy.
Beat in Eagle Brand until smooth.
Stir in ReaLemon and vanilla.
Pour into crust.
Chill for 3 hours or until set.
Top with desired amount of pie filling before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers.
Combine the first 5 ingredients.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Cover; chill.
Makes 4 1/2 cups.
Boil beef in 5 cups water for 1 1/2 hours or until beef is tender, having added the onion, salt, bay leaf, allspice and cloves.
Cool 2 cups of hot juice.
Add gingersnaps; mix.
Stir in brown sugar.
Simmer 45 minutes or more.
In large skillet, brown beef; drain.
Add canned tomatoes and taco seasoning; simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 can French fried onions.
In bowl, combine cottage cheese, 1 cup Cheddar cheese and eggs.
Place 3 tortillas on the bottom of a greased 8 x 12-inch baking dish.
Overlap 6 tortillas around sides of baking dish.
Spoon meat mixture evenly
in dish.
Top with 3 tortillas, then with cheese mixture.
Bake, covered, at 350°
for 45 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Place remaining onions in center of casserole; bake, uncovered, 5 minutes longer. Before serving, arrange tomatoes and lettuce around edge of casserole.
Makes 6 servings.
Mix all of the ingredients together.
Sprinkle chicken with flour, salt and pepper and Accent.
Fry breasts in oil until light brown.
Cook asparagus and drain. Place in bottom of large casserole.
Place chicken over asparagus.
Place pasta into a boiling pot of water.
Lower heat and let simmer until pasta is al dente.
Beat together the eggs, sugar, salt, butter and syrup. Sprinkle pecan halves in unbaked pie shell.
Pour mixture over pecans.
Bake at 375° for 40 to 50 minutes.
Makes 1 pie.
Bring vinegar, sugar, salt and spices to a boil; pour over zucchini (sliced and unpeeled) and onions.
Let stand 1 hour. Cook 3 minutes.
Pack in hot jars.
Put lids on, and process in boiling water bath for 5 minutes.
Makes 6 or 7 pints.

recipes.t: Cream Cheese Tuna Balls And Hot Mustard Sauce
d: Heat oven to 350°.
In large bowl, combine 1 cup potato flakes, onion, salt and garlic.
Add tuna, cream cheese and eggs; mix well.
In a small bowl, combine corn flakes and 1/4 cup potato flakes.
Shape tuna mixture into 42 (3/4-inch) balls.
Roll in corn flake mixture.
Place tuna balls on ungreased cookie sheets. Bake at 350° for 20 to 25 minutes or until lightly golden brown.
Trim steak, cut into serving size pieces.
Place in a 9 x 13 pan, sprinkle with pepper and top with onions, mushrooms and tomato sauce.
Cover and bake at 325° for about 2 hours or until meat is tender.
Serve over noodles.
Mix pickles, olives, onion, celery and green pepper in food processor; drain on paper towels and squeeze.
Blend cream cheese with rest of ingredients.
Add the processed vegetables; mix well.
Cook 2 cups cranberry juice.
Add all ingredients except wine. Bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Remove spices, let cool.
Add remaining cranberry juice and wine. Heat and serve.
Delicious!!
Cook potatoes in water, vinegar and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Dice potatoes and eggs; add vegetables and bacon crumbles.
Mix Miracle Whip and salt.
Chill.
Makes 1 1/2 quarts.
Soften cream cheese to room temperature.
Add vanilla pudding, orange juice and chopped up fruit.
Roll into ball.
Roll cheese ball in nuts.

recipes.t: Pigs In A Blanket Apple Pie
d: Slice in narrow wedges 2 big Granny Smith apples.
Take biscuits; pull apart and use 2 layers of a biscuit to wrap each slice of apple.
Melt a stick of oleo.
Add cup of water, cup of sugar and 1 teaspoon of vanilla flavoring to the butter or oleo. Pour mixture over Pigs in a Blanket (or apples).
Sprinkle cinnamon sugar all over top.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
In large bowl, toss together green cabbage, onion and parsley. Place red cabbage in a small bowl.
Cook cabbage for 2 minutes in a large pot of boiling water. Drain under cold water.
While cabbage cooks, put the 2 cups of water in saucepan.
Sprinkle gelatin over top and let stand for 1 minute.
Place over low heat and stir 3 minutes or until liquid is almost simmering, gelatin granules are completely dissolved and mixture is clear.
Remove from heat and stir in sugar until dissolved.
Stir in lemon juice.
Mix oil and sugar; beat in eggs.
Stir in flour, cinnamon, salt, applesauce, baking soda and cocoa.
Pour mixture into a greased and floured 13 x 9 x 2-inch pan.
Stir in 1 cup chocolate chips.
Sprinkle on top with 2 tablespoons sugar, nuts and remaining chocolate chips.
Serve with whipped topping or ice cream if desired.
Boil water, add tapioca and simmer with lid for 25 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add sugar and dry jello.
Cool.
Add frozen strawberries and Cool Whip.
Pour in bowl and refrigerate.
Brown bacon and drain.
Saute ham and garlic in a little butter.
Add all ingredients except eggs.
Mix well.
Turn off the heat and pour eggs over and quickly toss to coat spaghetti mixture.
Add olives.
Combine vegetables, salt and pepper.
Mix oil, sugar and vinegar together
and pour over vegetables.
Allow to set a few hours.
Mix all ingredients together and bake in greased pans at 400° until brown, about 35 minutes.

recipes.t: Pineapple Topping (To Be Used On Cakes)
d: Cook until it looks clear. This topping is great between layers of white or yellow cake. Then top with Cool Whip or make a cream cheese icing for the top.
Mix soup and milk well.
Cook the chicken with celery and onion (salt and pepper).
Take off the bone.
Save the liquid, celery and onion.
Put chicken into a large Pyrex dish.
Pour mushroom soup, chicken soup and milk mixture over chicken.
Mix Pepperidge Farm stuffing (using liquid, celery and onion).
Mix the dressing according to directions.
Put dressing on top of mushroom mixture. Bake about 1 hour at 325°.
Homemade dressing can be used.
Cook and drain spinach.
Saute together green pepper, onion and oil for 5 minutes.
Mix Italian seasoning and garlic powder, then add to pepper, onion and oil mixture.
Add cottage cheese and egg whites to chopped spinach and mix with shredded Mozzarella cheese and Parmesan cheese.
Put salt and pepper and flour it real good.
Then put oil in pan and fry until it's done.
To pre-bake crust:
Preheat oven to 375°.
Place foil or waxed paper over crust, weight it down with dried beans or grains.
Bake for 15 minutes, remove foil and beans and bake 10 more minutes until lightly browned.
Remove from oven and cool completely. Place about 2 cups berries in food processor.
Add 1/3 cup sugar and puree.
Taste to adjust sugar; set aside.
Place remaining berries in the cooled crust and gently spread into place.
Put cornstarch into small saucepan and whisk in pureed berries.
Bring to boil, then lower heat and simmer, whisking frequently, until thickened (5 minutes).
Remove from heat and pour over berries in the crust.
Cool to room temperature or chill before serving.
Separate and unroll breadsticks.

Place 3 pepperoni slices in single layer over 1/2 of each breadstick. Fold remaining half of breadstick over top; seal end and twist. Place on ungreased cookie sheet. Combine cheese, Italian seasoning and garlic powder. Sprinkle evenly over each breadstick.
Bake in preheated 350° oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Serve with pizza sauce.
Makes 8 pizza sticks.
Halve each eggplant and scoop out the pulp, leaving a 1/4-inch thick shell.
Dice the pulp finely.
Heat oil in a skillet and cook onion and garlic in it until tender.
Add eggplant pulp and cook slowly until lightly browned and almost tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add tomato and Worcestershire and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in eggs and nuts and use to stuff eggplant shells. Top with bread crumbs.
Set in an oiled shallow roasting pans. Bake at 375° for 25 minutes or until shells are tender.
Serves 6.
Heat oven to 350°.
Blend soup and milk in large bowl.
Stir in cheese, onions, macaroni and beef.
Fold in eggs, if using. Pour mixture into ungreased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Cover tightly. Bake 30 minutes or until heated through.
Makes 4 to 6 servings.

Pour first two ingredients together and let stand for 10 minutes. Add rest of ingredients. Place in a greased 9x13 pan and bake 350 degrees for 25 minutes. This is a very moist and delicious cake it can be topped with a sprinkle of powdered sugar instead of frosting.
Heat oil in Dutch oven over medium heat.
Cook and stir eggplant, onion, garlic and parsley in oil until onion is tender, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the rest of the ingredients.
Heat to boiling.
Reduce heat.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, 15 minutes.
Put on spaghetti and top with Parmesan cheese.
Heat oil in a 6-quart pot.
Saute onion until brown.
Add beans, tomatoes, celery, ketchup, dry mustard and pepper.
Add chili to taste.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Can be frozen.
Serves 8.
Calories: 265.
Fat: 3 gm.
Chol. 0.
Preheat oven to 400°.
Cream together shortening, sugar, vanilla and flavoring.
Add egg.
Sift together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves and salt.
Add to first mixture and blend well.
Spread half in a buttered 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Cover with layer of jam or jelly.
Pat rest of dough on top.
Bake 25 minutes.
Cool.
Cut in bars.
Makes about 20.
Combine all ingredients; mix well by hand.
Put into pan and refrigerate at least 1 hour before cutting.
Prepare
jello according to directions on box.	When it starts to
congeal,
add pineapple, bananas and marshmallows. Refrigerate while making topping.
Combine mayonnaise, cheese, olives, pimientos and garlic in small baking dish.
Bake in 375° oven for 20 minutes.
Cream all ingredients except peanuts and chips.
Add peanuts and chips; mix well.
Drop on cookie sheet and bake 9 minutes at 350°.
Mix gelatine, sugar and salt thoroughly in a small saucepan. Add 1/2 cup of the water and place over low heat, stirring constantly until gelatine is dissolved.
Remove from heat and stir in remaining 1 cup of water and vinegar or lemon juice.
Chill mixture to unbeaten egg white consistency.
Fold in diced apples, chopped celery and chopped nuts.
Turn into a 4 cup mold or individual molds and chill until firm.
Unmold by slipping mold in warm water to the depth of the gelatine.
Loosen around edge with tip of a knife.
Place serving dish on mold and turn upside down. Shake holding serving dish on mold turned upside down.
Shake holding serving dish tightly to mold.
Garnish with fruit.
Cream butter and sugar, add hot applesauce.
Mix and sift dry ingredients and spices.
Add to the applesauce mixture.
Add nuts and chopped dates or raisins.
Pour into greased pan and bake at 375° 20-30 minutes.
Put
salt
and pasta in boiling water.
Cook until well done. Drain
pasta.
While pasta is still hot, add butter and Umeboshi. Mix
until
butter
is completely melted.
Decorate with parsley.
Mix apples, marshmallows, grapes, celery, walnuts and enough mayonnaise to moisten.
Refrigerate.
In pizza pan spread refried beans.
Mix cream cheese, sour cream and taco seasoning until smooth.
Pour over beans and spread.
Dice tomatoes, green peppers and olives.
Sprinkle cheese on top.
Serve with taco chips.
Combine all ingredients; mix well.
Pour into 9 x 13-inch pan; bake at 350° until done.
Heat soup and cheese until melted.
Add gelatin and stir until smooth.
Cool a bit, then add mayonnaise and vegetables.
Prepare lime solution with the 5 quarts water and the hydrated lime.
Wash cucumbers thoroughly and slice.
Soak cucumbers in lime solution for 24 hours.
Wash cucumbers in several waters to remove lime.
Cook milk and corn meal until thick.
Add butter, sugar and salt.
Dissolve yeast in warm water and let stand for 20 minutes; then add eggs and flour.
Combine with corn meal mixture and add enough additional flour (3 to 3 1/2 cups) to make a soft bun dough.
Knead on floured board.
Set covered in a warm place.
Let rise until full size.
Punch down and let rise again.
Then form into buns.
Rise and bake at 350° for 12 to 15 minutes.
Makes 2 dozen.
Mix green beans & corn, put in greased casserole dish.
Mix soup, sour cream, cheese, onions and salt, spread over beans and corn.
Mix melted butter with cracker crumbs & almonds.
Spread over casserole.
Bake for 45 minutes at 325° uncovered.
Can be mixed & refrigerated over night before baking.
Whisk together all ingredients, except chops.
Marinate chops in mixture in refrigerator for 1 to 2 hours.
Remove.
Broil or grill chops for 12 to 15 minutes.
Brush with marinade; turn once.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Grease well and flour a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking pan.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spices into large bowl of electric mixer.
Add shortening and applesauce; beat 1 minute at low speed, just to combine.
At medium speed, beat 2 minutes, constantly cleaning side of bowl with rubber scraper and guiding batter into beaters.
Add eggs; beat 2 minutes. Combine raisins and walnuts; fold into batter with rubber scraper. Turn batter into prepared pan.
Bake 45 minutes, or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean.
Let cake cool completely in pan on wire rack.
Frost as desired.
To serve, cut into rectangles.
Mix together mayonnaise, Durkee, mustard, cooking oil, Worcestershire sauce and boiled eggs.
Put mixture in beans and peas and mix well.
Heat in 375° oven until bubbly.
Add French onions.
Return to oven until onions are warmed.
Melt the butter and add the first four
ingredients together. Mix well.
Stir in 1 1/2 c. chopped nuts.
Bake 30 minutes on 350°. After cake is done, place marshmallows on top of hot cake and place back in oven to toast lightly.
Let this set up before adding second layer.
Cover hamburger with water and break into bits.
Add celery and onion and any other veggie you wish.
Potatoes tend to mush up.
Add can of beef broth and water to cover contents.
Add seasoning, salt, pepper and garlic salt, if you prefer.
Put in crock-pot.
Put in refrigerator overnight.
Skim any fat next day. Reheat and eat.
Makes a thick soup.

recipes.t: Crustless South Of The Border Quiche
d: Preheat oven to 400°.
Butter a 10 x 15 x 2-inch baking pan. In large bowl, beat eggs until slightly thickened; add flour and baking powder and blend well.
Add Jack cheese, Cheddar cheese, cottage cheese, chiles and butter; stir until smooth.
Pour into prepared pan and bake at 400° for 15 minutes.
Lower heat to 350° and continue to bake for 45 minutes or until quiche is set and lightly golden on top.
Allow to cool slightly, cut into 1 1/2-inch squares and serve hot or at room temperature.
In large bowl, cream sugar, powdered sugar and margarine until light and fluffy.
Add oil, vanilla and eggs; mix well. Stir in flour, baking soda, cream of tartar and salt until well blended.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight for easier handling.
Cut butter into dry ingredients until crumbly.
Press mixture over fruit.
Bake at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
Chop oranges, raisins, apples and cherries and put in large kettle.
Add remaining ingredients.
Cook for 30 minutes.
Then simmer and stir occasionally (covered).
If canning, cook in pressure cooker 15 minutes at 10 pounds pressure.
If not canning, cook additional 30 minutes.
Cut weenies and veggies into small pieces.
Saute in margarine.
Stir in flour.
Slowly add 1/2 cup milk, stirring constantly, to make a paste.
Add rest of the milk and stir. Remove from heat; add cheese.
Stir until melted.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Brown meat; drain.
Add peppers and onion; cook until tender.
Add remaining ingredients, except cheese; mix well.
Spoon half of meat and potato mixture into a 13 1/2 x 8 1/4-inch baking dish or 2-quart casserole dish.
Cover with half of cheese.
Top with remaining meat and potato mixture.
Cover with aluminum foil or dish cover.
Bake 45 minutes.
Uncover dish. Top with remaining cheese.
Let stand 5 minutes.
Serve with salad. Makes 12 servings.
Mix all ingredients except butter together.
Melt butter in 8 x 8-inch casserole dish.
Pour in mixture.
Bake in 350° oven for 45 minutes or until it starts to brown on top.
Cook or boil pared potatoes until tender; drain.
In a large bowl mash with a potato masher or beat with electric mixer on low speed. Add sour cream, cream cheese, 1 tablespoon margarine or butter, salt, pepper and thyme.
Gradually beat in enough of the milk to make smooth and fluffy.
Turn into a greased 1 1/2-quart casserole.
Cover with foil and chill up to 24 hours.
Brown ground beef and garlic.
Add tomatoes and seasonings. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Cook lasagna noodles according to directions on package.
After draining, cover with cold water until used.

Combine all ingredients except bacon in a 1-gallon zip-seal bag; marinate 24 hours in the refrigerator. Remove meat from marinade; lay in a greased baking pan and cover each piece with a strip of bacon. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes, then turn oven to broil and watch closely until browned.
Cut bacon into 1/2-inch pieces.
Cook in large kettle until crispy brown.
Turn often.
Remove bits of bacon and reserve.
Cook raisins for 10 minutes or until water has cooked down. Cool butter and sugar.
Add egg yolks and raisins.
Fold in egg whites.
Pour into pie shell.
Bake in slow oven (325°) for 40 minutes or until done.
Preheat oven to 350°. Mix first 6 ingredients by hand.
Bake 15 minutes at 350°. Turn down oven to 300° and continue baking 20 to 25 minutes.
Base:
Combine flour, brown sugar, coconut and 9 tablespoons melted butter.
Mix well and press into greased 28 cm x 18 cm x 1 cm pan.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
In an 11 x 15-inch cookie sheet, combine Chex, pretzels, nuts, crackers and Fritos.
In a saucepan, melt margarine, then add Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion salt, chili powder and, if desired, Tabasco sauce and dry onion.

Heat oil in saucepan. Add mushrooms and onions. Cook and stir on medium heat 5 minutes or until tender. Stir in rice, water and wine. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender. Stir in 1/2 cup of the cheese and half and half. Serve with remaining cheese. Makes 4 to 6 servings. Preparation time: 10 minutes. Cooking time: 25 minutes.
Cut corn from cob and add milk, salt and pepper.
Put butter in heavy skillet.
When hot, add corn.
Cook until tender, stirring occasionally.
Just before ready to serve, add beaten eggs and blend in well.
Serve hot.
Mix first 5 ingredients together as meat loaf, but press it into 8-inch pie tins.
Bake in oven at 400° for about 15 minutes, or until done.
Fill meat crust with mashed potato filling.
Shave cheese and place on top.
Place back into oven.
Bake, until cheese has melted, in oven at 375° to 475°.
Serve hot.
Cook dates, sugar and water until thick.
Stir often and blend in lemon juice and margarine.
Cool.
Cut zucchini into 1/4-inch thick strips, about 2 to 3-inches long.
In nonstick skillet, melt butter and saute zucchini, onion and garlic, stirring constantly.
Add tomatoes, salt, pepper and oregano.
Simmer until tender.
Turn into greased casserole dish. Cover with cheese and bake at 350° until brown.
In large pan, empty pork and beans.
Add enough water, about 2 cans.
Bring to a boil while preparing hamburger meat.
In a skillet, brown meat, onion and garlic.
When brown, add tomato sauce and chili powder.
Cook for a minute, then add to beans. Simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Saute green pepper, celery and pimiento in melted butter in a large skillet until tender.
Stir in parsley, Old Bay seasoning, mustard, hot sauce and red pepper.
Layer first 6 ingredients in a large salad bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, sugar and cheese.
Spread over other ingredients. Sprinkle with bacon bits.
Combine first 6 ingredients in a small bowl. Slowly whisk in oil. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare cake mix as directed, adding coconut flavoring and 2/3 cup coconut.
Bake as directed, using 9 x 13-inch pan.
Remove cake from oven.
Punch holes throughout and pour over the following mixture.
Mix water and milk to make 2 cups liquid.
Dissolve powdered sugar into this and add 1 teaspoon coconut flavor.
When cake is cool, frost with Cool Whip.
Sprinkle top with remaining coconut.
Whip sweet potatoes, then add sugar and cream.
Melt 3/4 stick margarine and marshmallows.
Add marshmallow mixture to cream mixture, then add eggs and vanilla.
Pour in greased 13 x 9-inch casserole dish.
Top with 3/4 stick melted margarine, 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup cereal or nuts.
Bake at 350° for 35 to 40 minutes.
Basic ingredient is cabbage or use whatever you have in your dehydrator, such as, onion, pepper, celery, carrot, radish, tomato, etc.
Add salt and pepper.
Secret is mayonnaise mixed with lime (fresh) juice.
Use your own taste buds!
Cut potatoes crosswise into 1/4-inch slices, taking care not to cut all the way through so that potato remains intact.
Place cut side up in a shallow pan coated with cooking spray.
Combine remaining ingredients, stirring well.
Brush potatoes with margarine mixture.
Bake at 400° for 1 hour or until tender and slices have fanned out.
Baste occasionally with pan drippings. Yield:
6 servings (90 calories per serving).
Brown ground beef and onion (salted), then drain.
Add water, oats, chili powder and catsup or catsup and Manwich.
Cook slowly 1 hour.
Mix and place in greased dish.
Bake at 325° for 30 minutes. Top with Cheddar and return to oven until cheese melts.
Crush Ritz crackers, reserving 1/2 cup crumbs.
Stir melted margarine into remaining crumbs and press into a 9 x 13-inch pan. Chill.
Combine all ingredients except yogurt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Boil 8 minutes without stirring.
Cool to room temperature.
Add yogurt; blend well.
Mix and beat 4 minutes.
Bake in 9 x 12 x 2-inch pan at 350° for 30 or 40 minutes.
Boil sugar, milk and dates until it forms soft ball in water. Remove from fire and let cool to lukewarm.
Add vanilla and nuts and beat until firm enough to form 1 or 2-inch roll.
Pour in wet cloth; tie each end.
Hang up and let remain until cold.
Then slice.
Clean carrots with vegetable brush; slice the fresh carrots (not too large).
Steam fresh carrots or drain canned carrots. Slice green bell pepper and onion into rings.
Combine with cooked carrots.
Combine all other ingredients and pour over vegetables. Let stand in refrigerator overnight.
This keeps very well.
Grate zucchini.
Add all ingredients.
Mix well.
Drop in hot pan with very little Crisco by heaping tablespoons.
Cook on medium heat.
Turn cake one time.
Makes about 8.
Truly delicious!
Put turkey breast in pan, skin side down.
Combine garlic, pepper, salt and rosemary in blender.
Add oil; chop all together. Spread 1/2 of mixture over turkey.
Bake on rack in roasting pan (300°) for 1 hour.
Put remaining mixture on turkey roast.
Finish baking at 300° until done.
Use juices from turkey to baste during cooking time.
In heavy pan (better iron skillet), brown until dark the 1 cup sugar, stirring constantly.
At the same time, mix 1/2 cup sugar, flour, salt, egg yolks and milk in saucepan.
Place over medium heat, stirring constantly until somewhat thickened.
Pour into burnt sugar and cook over low heat until smooth.
Add margarine and vanilla.
Pour into pie shell.
May add meringue.
Stirring both requires some coordination.
In a heavy pan, combine all ingredients; bring to boil.
Stir 2 minutes or until clear.
Remove from heat.
Cool.
This is good on cheesecake or as a cake filling layer.
In 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat, in 1 tablespoon hot margarine, cook half the chicken until browned, stirring often. Remove; set aside.
Repeat with remaining chicken.
Reduce heat to medium.
In same skillet, in remaining 1 tablespoon hot margarine, cook mushrooms and onions until vegetables are tender and liquid is evaporated, stirring often.
Stir in soup and sour cream.
Heat to boiling.
Return chicken to skillet.
Heat through, stirring occasionally.
Serve over noodles.
Sprinkle with parsley.
Makes 4 servings.
Preparation time:
15 minutes; cooking time:
20 minutes.
Remove chicken from bones and cut into bite size pieces. Spray a 7 x 10 x 2-inch pan with Pam and arrange drained green beans over bottom.
Place half of the boned chicken over green beans.
Top with whole crackers.
Cover the crackers with cheese slices; arrange remaining chicken over the cheese.
Combine soup, broth, onion flakes and 1/4 cup grated cheese.
Pour over chicken. Sprinkle casserole with cracker crumbs and mushrooms.
Drizzle with melted margarine.
Bake for 30 minutes at 350°.
This can be doubled for a larger casserole.
Coat large baking dish with cooking spray.
Layer half each of potatoes, onion and tomatoes in dish; sprinkle with half of salt, thyme and rosemary.
Repeat layers and drizzle with the olive oil. Cover and bake at 425° for 35 to 40 minutes or tender.
Sprinkle with parsley.
(If no fresh parsley, sprinkle with 1 tablespoon dry crushed before baking.)
